key: A Dance of Snowy Tides and Hoarfrost Groves
Song of the Welkin Moon Act I
0.comment: A Dance of Snowy Tides and Hoarfrost Groves
0.content:
A Dance of Snowy Tides and Hoarfrost Groves (also: Song of the Welkin Moon Act I, Welkin Moon Act I, Where the Moon Rises, Reunion Beneath the Moonlight, In the Shadows of Night): The first act of the Song of the Welkin Moon chapter and the Traveler's arrival in Nod-Krai. After a send-off in Natlan, the Traveler, Paimon and Ineffa sail north, feel kuuvahki for the first time and look for clues to the Traveler's crashed spaceship. They meet the Moonchanter Lauma of the Frostmoon Scions, learn the Fatui are hunting a "relic", and meet Columbina, whom the Scions call their goddess Kuutar. The Traveler and their sibling break into the sanctum holding the Moon Marrow, the Wild Hunt attacks, and in the end the Traveler agrees to carry the Marrow in their own body.

The act has three quests: Where the Moon Rises, Reunion Beneath the Moonlight, and In the Shadows of Night. It requires the Interlude Chapter's last act, Paralogism, and is followed by Elegy of Dust and Lamplight.

It introduces most of Nod-Krai's major local factions and people at once (the Ratnik Flins, the Frostmoon Scions, the Fatui under Marionette, Nefer's Curatorium of Secrets) and the region's central mystery: the three moons, the Moon Marrow, and the Traveler's memory of their crash.

Plot: The Traveler, Paimon and Ineffa leave Natlan after a farewell party and sail to Nod-Krai, where the Traveler feels kuuvahki, the moon's power, and recalls the same feeling from leaving their spaceship. They learn Varka is away, and meet Flins, the Frostmoon Scions' Moonchanter Lauma, Marionette of the Fatui, and Aino, who suggests the Scions' ritual to see the true past. Lauma explains the Three Moons and the Moon Marrow relic that the Fatui demand; the Traveler tells her they are a Descender. They meet Columbina, who is called Kuutar by the Scions, and then the Traveler and their sibling break into the relic's sanctum. The Wild Hunt attacks, the relic goes missing, and with Nefer's Curatorium hiring Jahoda, Lauma and Jahoda help the Traveler track it to the Fatui and recover it from Marionette. A phantom impersonating the sibling is exposed, and the Traveler agrees to carry the Moon Marrow in their own body while Lauma tells the Scions that the sky is fake.

In Natlan, Ineffa waits for the Traveler and Paimon outside the Stadium of the Sacred Flame, saying conditions for travel are good. Mualani, Kachina, Kinich and Ajaw arrive for a farewell party that Paimon had told them about, and Kachina invites Ineffa too. Unseen, someone watches and reports to Sandrone in Nod-Krai, who says it is about time she met the "variable" in person.

On the boat to Nod-Krai Ineffa says the moment she knew she had entered Natlan was when she could no longer sense the moon's power. At Nasha Town the Traveler feels a power in the land that matches how they felt when they left their ship after landing in Teyvat. Ineffa names it kuuvahki, the moon's power, a pure primordial elemental energy like Phlogiston or the Primordial Sea. The Traveler guesses it is the Light Realm power Yohualtecuhtin mentioned, and that their spaceship may be nearby, perhaps near a beach. Ineffa notes Nod-Krai is islands, so that fits many shores.

Following a kuuhenki (a local sprite and familiar of the Moon Goddess) around town, Ineffa explains Nod-Krai's past and present and Aino's "Boom and Blast Kuuvahki Cannon", used when the Wild Hunt grows too dangerous. At the Flagship the bartender Demyan says Varka has gone with his knights to Amsvartnir, in the north, where trouble had been brewing; he left lodging paid and a portion of Berries and Fried Meat for Ineffa to bring Aino. In the hallway Paimon bumps into Flins, a Ratnik who fends off the Wild Hunt at the northern graveyards and is in town to repair his lantern; the Traveler feels something is off about it. Lauma, a Moonchanter of the Frostmoon Scions, is handing out food; when the Fatui soldiers Oiva and Ognjen demand some, she still feeds them but warns that the Scions' kindness has limits. In the Adventurers' Guild branch the Traveler finds Marionette, the Seventh Harbinger, who gives a friendly warning not to interfere in Fatui matters; the Traveler realises the Fatui have been watching them.

Aino has never seen a spaceship and says she has taken apart most of Nod-Krai's machinery without finding anything alien. She suggests the Frostmoon Scions, who have a ritual to see the "true" past. On Hiisi Island Lauma speaks with the wildlife, explains the Scions' statues of their goddess Kuutar, and recognises the kuuhenki following the Traveler as a rare kind called a Luonnotar. In her library she tells of her people's origin in Hyperborea and the Three Moons: in the war with the Descenders only the Frost Moon stayed whole while the Eternal and Iridescent Moons shattered, their fragments falling on Nod-Krai, and the Fatui have pulled down parts of the Eternal Moon. A prophecy said the Moon Goddess would return. Oiva and Ognjen later give the Scions an ultimatum: surrender the relic and the location of their "Kuutar" in three days or the Fatui will cleanse the island. A scuffle drives them off. Lauma suspects the Fatui's "Kuutar" is the Harbinger Columbina. The Traveler admits they are the latest Descender; Lauma agrees to help, though the "Moon Marrow" can only be retrieved in a ritual when the moon is closest to Teyvat, about two months away.

The Traveler cannot sleep and walks out; following the Luonnotar's song they find a young woman in an underground flower cavern. She says she has been called Columbina and Kuutar but does not know her own name because she was born alone. The Traveler then meets their sibling outside; the sibling refuses to wait two months, uses Abyssal power to open a hidden staircase at the Kuutar statue, and the pair pass the sanctum's trials (a kuuvahki puzzle, weak monsters, moving statues) and its guardian. The sibling asks the Traveler to take the relic; afterwards the Traveler finds themselves outside, surrounded by the Wild Hunt, until Flins arrives and destroys them. The sibling has vanished.

The next day, overheard talk of the relic's theft leads them to Nefer's Curatorium of Secrets. The Traveler confesses to Lauma; she is not angry. Nefer notes that the Fatui have apparently called off their search. Through Lauma's manoeuvring, Jahoda is hired to find the relic. That night Lauma, her antlers grown, asks whether the sky is fake, which the Traveler confirms, and mixes her silver blood into medicine for Kapy's daughter Kaarina. The Traveler later brings Paimon and food to Columbina, who says the Frostmoon Scions once prayed to her for answers, that the Fatui also wanted only her power, and that she helped the Tsaritsa at the cost of much of her strength.

In the third quest, Lauma and Jahoda lead the Traveler to the Fatui site, using terminals and a ventilation shaft. Inside they find Vilemina, who left the Scions for the Fatui because she could no longer live a lie, and who took the Moon Marrow. Lauma admits she knew the truth about the sky. Vilemina cuts off her own antlers as the Scions' punishment for betrayal and says Marionette took the Marrow to Starsand Shoal. Marionette is confronted outside; her subordinates do not answer because the Wild Hunt is attacking. In the mist the Traveler hears the sibling's voice but realises it is a phantom, since they had been told the sibling found them still in their hypersleep pod, not that the two left the ship together as the voice claimed. Marionette extracts the Marrow from her robot Pulonia and tosses it to them. Flins arrives, learns the Wild Hunt has changed, and leaves to warn his superiors; Lauma later says animals fear him.
Back at the Curatorium, the Marrow can no longer be stored in the compromised chamber. Lauma offers to be its vessel, as a past Moonchanter had been for two days when the Scions' bloodline was strong, but she thinks she could manage five days at most. The Traveler convinces her to let them hold it, with Paimon arguing it is less dangerous than the Abyssal corruption they have already resisted. Nefer returns with medicine and learns of a phantom that can impersonate others. Lauma then tells the Scions the whole truth about the fake sky; some accept, some leave because losing faith felt like losing home, and some thank her for being closer to them. She asks the Traveler how she looks and says she feels she is "finally living on the bright side of the moon."

Smaller details. Dori runs a curios shop after the Fatui pulled down two Ancient Moon remnants; Katheryne is at the guild branch too. Ineffa stays with Aino, who had broken their agreement on snacks. Lauma tells Kapy not all Snezhnayans should be confused with the Fatui, while Kapy distrusts the Snezhnayan doctors. The Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau was built over one of the large moon remnants. Vilemina asks the Traveler to look after Lauma, and is later shown intending to spend her last night with the group, troubled that the other Scions refused to accept the truth. The Frostmoon statues were designed with Kuutar's likeness, and the Fatui have been defacing them except on Hiisi Island. Lauma says Kuutar left angry at the Scions' greed and has been reported on the island again.

Revelations: Nod-Krai's land carries kuuvahki, the same kind of power the Traveler felt on leaving their ship; the Traveler concludes their ship is somewhere in the region. The Fatui's "Kuutar" is Columbina. The Three Moons (Frost, Eternal, Iridescent) are tied to a war with the Descenders. The Traveler tells Lauma they are a Descender.

The sky above Nod-Krai is fake: Lauma has long felt the moon's power coming from a different direction than the moon she sees, and she tells the Frostmoon Scions at the end of the act. Phantoms of the Wild Hunt can impersonate people, including the Traveler's sibling, and the Wild Hunt has changed in nature. The Moon Marrow is now stored in the Traveler's body. Columbina says the Fatui, like the Scions, valued her only for her power.

Characters: Traveler and Paimon, accompanied by Ineffa at first, with Aino, Varka (absent), Flins, Lauma (central ally), Columbina (Fatui Harbinger and the Scions' goddess), Sandrone (the Harbinger Marionette, first seen being told of the Traveler's departure, then confronting them in person), Nefer and Jahoda; Vilemina, Demyan, Katheryne and Dori in minor roles. The Traveler's sibling appears in the sanctum scene and a phantom later impersonates them.

Consequences: The Traveler now carries the Moon Marrow and has Lauma, Nefer and Jahoda as allies, while the Fatui know them by sight. Lauma's revelation changes the Frostmoon Scions. The act sets up Elegy of Dust and Lamplight and the later acts that follow Flins and Columbina.

Placement: Song of the Welkin Moon Act I, added in version 6.0 (Luna I, 2025-09-10). It requires Paralogism, the final act of the Interlude Chapter, and is followed by Elegy of Dust and Lamplight and then A Nation That Doesn't Exist. Story order equals release order.

1.comment: A Dance of Snowy Tides and Hoarfrost Groves: Moon Marrow
1.content: In A Dance of Snowy Tides and Hoarfrost Groves the Moon Marrow is the "relic" the Fatui and the Traveler's sibling are looking for. It can be retrieved only in a ritual when the moon is closest to Teyvat. The sibling opens its sanctum early; it is later taken by Vilemina and Marionette. At the end of the act the Traveler stores it in their own body at Lauma's guidance.

2.comment: A Dance of Snowy Tides and Hoarfrost Groves: Hiisi Island sanctum
2.content: A hidden staircase at the statue of Kuutar on Hiisi Island leads to a sanctum with trials meant to deter unworthy visitors: a kuuvahki puzzle, a fight against weak monsters, a statue-moving puzzle, and a guardian. The Traveler and their sibling pass them together.

3.comment: A Dance of Snowy Tides and Hoarfrost Groves: Columbina meets the Traveler
3.content: The Traveler first meets Columbina in an underground cavern of blue flowers, following a Luonnotar. She turns the flowers red when she thinks the Traveler is a Fatuus, says she does not know her own name, and warns that the moon can be treacherous.

4.comment: A Dance of Snowy Tides and Hoarfrost Groves: Lauma's silver blood
4.content: Lauma shows the Traveler massive antlers, which she says occur once a century, and cuts her hand to mix silver blood into medicine for Kaarina. The Traveler sees healed scars from similar cuts and realises she has been treating others in this way. She asks them to keep it secret.

5.comment: A Dance of Snowy Tides and Hoarfrost Groves: Wild Hunt phantom
5.content: In the third quest a fog separates the Traveler from the others and a voice imitates their sibling. They see through it because it claims the pair left the ship together, which does not match what they remember being told. Lauma disperses the mist with her power.

key: A Finale Emberforged World Quest series
An Omen of Annihilation and the Final Entreaty
6.content:
A Finale Emberforged (also: A Finale Emberforged World Quest series, An Omen of Annihilation and the Final Entreaty, Little One's cleansing): In An Omen of Annihilation and the Final Entreaty (5.5), the Traveler and Paimon bring Little One to the central device in the Heart of the Sacred Mountain and offer both Golden Entreaties. Inside the light they are ambushed by a Primeval Source Dragon Mech while a voice remarks that such stories never end without an evil dragon. The Traveler is locked in a Laser Jail and falls in battle. Little One, alone, uses its dragon blood, and a calm voice offers guidance. Little One is shown the truth in a vision and briefly gains a mature dragon's form and speech. The speaker is Kukulkan, whom humans called the Sage of the Stolen Flame. He explains that the cleansing was a lie of omission and that he wants the Natlan Phlogistonization Array, Huitzilopochtli, activated to wall off the Abyss. Little One cancels the activation, refuses to put the Traveler and Paimon at risk and fights its way out. Back at normal size it helps the Traveler break the party out and defeat the Mech again. The Flamelord's Blessing is lifted.

Kukulkan's reasoning is that the Abyss will keep coming, that humans have not built a united defence in thousands of years, and that his faith in them has run out. His plan would convert Natlan to a land of phlogiston, with the old dragons ruling a "new world". He names the Chosen of Dragons as both the chosen dragon and the chosen human who brings it, saying the human's duty ends on arrival. The quest ends with Little One shrunk back down, the mark on its horn dimmed and cool, and the party leaving to celebrate with stew and cake.

The player controls an indwelled adult Little One for most of the middle of the quest and a trial Traveler in the two boss fights. The tutorial "Human and Saurian, as One!" appears when Little One joins the second fight, which introduces commanding Little One to break the Laser Jail and block the Mech's claw attacks. After the quest Titu has updated dialogue.

Plot: Entry. At the central mechanism the Traveler hears golden text telling the Chosen of Dragons to offer the Golden Entreaties and ignite the Sacred Flame. The two Entreaties are shattered, and their markings spiral together into a single inscription that emits a pulse of golden light. Paimon recaps their journey, including the fight with Och-Kan (who turned out to be Coco), before the party steps into the light.

The trial. The space is empty. A voice says: "Learn the truth and make your choice." The Primeval Source Dragon Mech appears. About a minute into the fight the Traveler is trapped by its Laser Jail and falls. Paimon is also locked up.

Little One. From Little One's viewpoint, it tries to open the cage, uses the power in its blood despite the Traveler's warning, and begins to be overwhelmed. A voice calls it Chosen of Dragons and guides the power so that it supports rather than devours it. Little One is shown a white void and awakens as a mature dragon able to speak. The speaker is Kukulkan.

Truth. Kukulkan shows Little One the Heart of the Sacred Mountain, where the first Pyro Sovereign shaped the Dragonborn, and tells his account: Xiuhcoatl was frozen in lava by the "reaver from beyond the skies", awoke when Nibelung descended, and was left lucid only in brief moments. Before his death he transformed the dragon city and created the Tzitzimimeh and Huitzilopochtli. The array would turn Natlan into pure phlogiston, so that the Abyss could never gain a foothold. Everyone in Natlan would die or give up their bodies. Kukulkan took Little One to the Tonatiuh and the Sacred City to show what had become of his people, and says he gave humanity extra time before losing faith.

Choice. Kukulkan asks Little One to confirm the activation three times. Little One remembers the Traveler and Paimon. If it confirms, the screen goes white; the narration describes a world where only "it" remains, pondering whether another choice existed. The route followed in the canon story is to cancel. Kukulkan tries to keep Little One with taunts (that the Traveler and Paimon do not care, that its power will vanish and its speech with it) but Little One says they matter to it and that if there is no path back to them, it will make one. It breaks through the golden obstacles to the cage and frees them.

The final fight. With the cage broken, Little One is again in adult form, helps the Traveler and Paimon, and the party defeats the Mech. Golden text says the Flamelord's Blessing has been dispelled, thanks the Chosen of Dragons for all they have done, and says it is hard to say, but "I love you". Little One returns to its normal size and faints; the volcano shakes. On the platform by Huitzilopochtli Kukulkan says he finally understands Xiuhcoatl's feelings and admits that if he truly wanted a dragon to activate the array, he should have raised it in the Sacred City to hate this world; he sent it to a human's side. On the surface the volcano only vents a little smoke and Little One wakes with the mark dim.

Details from the vision. Kukulkan changes into forms of Manqu and Bona to show off the transformation arts that phlogiston allows, and invites Little One to do the same. Little One declines. Kukulkan explains that Tonatiuh was once a cable to reach beyond the sky, later reconfigured, and that Och-Kan hid a Golden Entreaty there. The tower network that anchors Huitzilopochtli's coverage was mostly destroyed on Och-Kan's orders, but its fragments are enough. He says Xbalanque exploited Xiuhcoatl's one weakness, a modified pupil serving as Huitzilopochtli's control hub, and that both died; Xbalanque was reborn as the Pyro Archon.

Revelations: - The Sage of the Stolen Flame is Kukulkan, who also bears other names such as Waxaklahun Ubah Kan.
- The Flamelord's Blessing is the dragons' own bloodline mark on the horn. Kukulkan says it kills most unguided saurians, and that he chose a dragon and a human together to reach his goal, creating the legend on purpose; many humans have died for it.
- Huitzilopochtli is a Natlan-wide device built by Xiuhcoatl that would transform the land into phlogiston, leaving the survivors as phlogiston-based beings.

- Phlogiston is described as an information-carrying substance in which Iridescent Inscriptions can imitate any form.
- The Golden Entreaties are Huitzilopochtli's control hub, split in two between Kukulkan and Xbalanque and hidden through Och-Kan and the Tonatiuh.
- Kukulkan hoped to learn from Och-Kan how the one seated upon heaven's throne turned the Ley Lines into a girdle defending the planet and to merge the human and dragon races, but says human souls vary too much and are too fragile.

- Xiuhcoatl was steeped in the Abyss, and his last lucid moments produced Huitzilopochtli. Kukulkan says the dragons who gave up their bodies and sleep in the sealed Sacred City consume vast resources.
- The wording "Chosen of Dragons" covers both the chosen dragon and the chosen human who brings it; the human's part ends on arrival.

Characters: Little One (a whelp, briefly a speaking mature dragon), the Traveler, Paimon, and Kukulkan as the persuasive antagonist. The Primeval Source Dragon Mech is the boss.

Kukulkan combines sorrow, contempt for humanity's stagnation and a clear affection for Little One. The quest also mentions Och-Kan, Xbalanque, Xiuhcoatl and Nibelung only in his account. Paimon appears in cutscenes and as a trapped companion.

Consequences: Little One is no longer afflicted by the Flamelord's Blessing: the mark has cooled and dimmed. The party celebrates. The quest awards Adventure EXP, Primogems, Mora, Hero's Wit, Mystic Enhancement Ore and The Cornerstone of Stars and Flames. It also unlocks, with many other conditions, the farewell quest Someday, We All Must Walk Alone in In the Footsteps of the Chosen of Dragons.

Titu has updated dialogue after the quest.

Placement: Released in 5.5 as the finale of the Natlan world quest storyline for Little One. It follows Chronicler of the Crumbling City (whose last part is As the Burning Sun Sears Shadows), Path to the Flaming Peaks, Lost Traveler in the Ashen Realm and Between Pledge and Forgettance.

7.content:
Huitzilopochtli is the Natlan Phlogistonization Array, built from Xiuhcoatl's design at the Heart of the Sacred Mountain. In Kukulkan's account it would burn everything in Natlan and log its information into phlogiston, turning the land into a realm of primal flame that annihilates the Abyss when it approaches. Life would either die or become phlogiston-based, and ley lines and bodies would be gone. Its activation requires both Golden Entreaties and three confirmations to start or cancel.

Xiuhcoatl's control hub for it was one of his own pupils, which Kukulkan calls his only weakness. The sequence's name for the strike is Sweeping Skyfire.

8.content: Kukulkan offers Little One wisdom, power and a place as shaper of a new world in exchange for activating the array. He is open that the legend of the cure was a deliberate fiction and that the human was only a means. He is moved when Little One refuses, saying that it made the same choice he and Och-Kan once made.

9.comment: A Finale Emberforged: Primeval Source Dragon Mech
9.content: A guardian machine that fights the Traveler in the trial. It uses a Laser Jail to trap the active character, a charged beam and claw attacks. In the first fight Little One is an ally; in the second, Little One has grown and joins as an adult.

key: A Gifted Rose World Quest series
10.content:
A Gifted Rose (also: A Gifted Rose World Quest series, Affan's Golden Rose quests): A Gifted Rose is a five-part world quest series in the Great Red Sand, Sumeru, added in version 3.1. On the edge of Aaru Village, a lonely old man named Affan is trying to grow three stone-like seeds left to him by a dead neighbour, an exile the villagers call the "old ghost". With the Amurta researcher Sabbah, the Traveler and Paimon get the seeds to sprout and bloom as Golden Roses.

The series is a quiet, small-scale story about exile, being forgotten, and keeping a dead person's wish alive. It requires The Exile (World Quest Series) to have been completed. It has five quests, plus one follow-up Hidden Exploration Objective, and it runs over several in-game days because the plants need real-time days to grow.

The old man's garden belongs to Shafaqat, a former Akademiya researcher who was exiled to Aaru Village and died there. The story ties him to Sabbah, who is also an exile, so her arc from The Exile continues here.

Plot: **Prickly as Thorns.** Sabbah has mentioned a flower grower in the village. Affan is brusque, believing children come to mock him, then apologises. He originally had two nurseries; the western one was ruined by black corruption, which the Traveler recognises as the Withering and destroys. Affan thanks them with food (shawarma wrap, tahchin and beans) rather than much Mora, which worries Paimon, who wonders whether he gave away his own rations. Affan will say only that he is planting "a friend's wish".

**Long Day Ahead.** The seeds have not changed. Paimon suggests the soil is too dry and poor in nutrients, so the Traveler waters them. Affan reveals he is growing Golden Roses, which he calls much rarer than the Sumeru Rose, from seeds and a house left behind by "the old ghost". He says village parents use that name to frighten naughty children. As a child he was chased off with a hoe from the old man's garden, and he now wants to recreate that garden from memory. He also tells the Traveler about his own life: he never left the village, once nearly joined the Eremites as a newlywed, and eventually moved to the village edge where he felt more at ease.

**Can Stones Bloom.** Still nothing grows, and Affan fears he has been planting stones. After another watering he apologises aloud to the dead man. Affan then gives the dead man's name: Shafaqat, "Uncle Shafaqat". He had left Sumeru City young, built the house and garden, and grew trees and flowers that children loved to visit, until he turned reclusive. The notes Affan has gathered describe Shafaqat's exile from the Akademiya, the loss of his labs and books, estrangement from his daughter, and his plan to scatter Golden Rose seeds across the desert before dying. The Traveler proposes asking Sabbah, whom Affan had once driven away.

**Ballad of Days Gone By.** Sabbah and Affan meet at the nursery. She finds that the seeds are petrified. She weighs two explanations, long weathering (unlikely) or a Geo-rich breed forming its own stone shell, and points to the folk song that Shafaqat composed: "Blooming from the stone, the Golden Rose sang to me." The Traveler breaks the casings with blunt attacks and awakens the seeds with Dendro. When shoots appear, Sabbah says that Shafaqat's wish can now be fulfilled. She and Affan speak about being exiles, and Affan tells her he does not want to see a second "old ghost".

**Some People Never Fade Away.** On the day of the bloom Sabbah has already been visiting and reading Shafaqat's notes. The Traveler awakens the flowers with Dendro. As the roses bloom, Affan recites the last stanza of the rose song and says he has fulfilled the dead man's wish. Sabbah says Shafaqat has surpassed time through the roses and his folk song, that seeing his traces makes her feel she has crossed time, and that she can carry his regrets and live on for him. Affan and Sabbah agree to plant more Golden Roses together.

A follow-up Hidden Exploration Objective (its name is unofficial on the wiki) lets the Traveler collect Golden Rose Seeds found elsewhere, plant them in the nursery and awaken them with Dendro over two days. Affan wonders where the seeds came from and concludes that the seeds Shafaqat once scattered over the desert somehow found their way back. This is a wiki-recorded optional objective.

Gameplay note, labelled as such: the quest asks the player to apply Hydro, then break stone casings with blunt attacks and apply Dendro. The text does not change the lore.

Revelations: - "The old ghost" of Aaru Village was an exiled researcher named Shafaqat (Affan's elders say this was his name). He grew Golden Roses and wrote the village's rose folk song.
- Affan has been caring for Shafaqat's house and nursery, and sorting the notes he left behind, in order to carry out his wish that Golden Roses grow widely in the desert.
- The Golden Rose seeds are wrapped in a stone-like casing (Sabbah's analysis) and must be cracked open before Dendro can wake them.

- Shafaqat's notes say he once worked at the Akademiya, was exiled, and that his work was discredited and his name became a family taboo. He mentions a daughter he never saw again.
- Sabbah, herself exiled, sees his fate as what may await her. By the end of the series she decides to stay in Aaru and help Affan.

Characters: The Traveler, Paimon, Affan, Sabbah (an exiled Amurta researcher), and Shafaqat, who appears only through Affan's memories and his notes. Nahida's All Schemes to Know can be used on Affan and Sabbah to read their thoughts.

Consequences: Golden Roses bloom in Affan's nursery. Affan and Sabbah plan to grow more of them together. Affan has come to terms with the dead man's memory, and Sabbah, who had felt lonely in Aaru Village, says she feels less alone.

The village rose song, composed by Shafaqat and handed down by the older generation, is revived through the quest. Affan notes that some in his generation no longer know it.

Placement: Requires The Exile (World Quest Series), which comes just before it in the Great Red Sand. Released in 3.1. The five quests can only be done on successive days because the plants need time to grow.

11.content: Affan is an open-world NPC, an old man who lives alone at the edge of Aaru Village in a house left to him by the "old ghost". He is gruff at first, then warm, and tends a nursery where he tries to grow Golden Roses from seeds in his dead friend's notes. He mentions a late wife, a youthful wish to travel that never happened, and that he feels he belongs neither to the village nor anywhere else. The wiki has no profile text for him beyond his quests and dialogue.

12.comment: A Gifted Rose: Shafaqat, the old ghost of Aaru Village
12.content:
Shafaqat is known to the village as "the old ghost" and, to those who remember, "Uncle Shafaqat". According to Affan's elders he left Sumeru City young, built his house in Aaru Village and rarely left it for decades. His notes say he was exiled from the Akademiya, that his work was discredited, that he missed his daughter, and that he wanted Golden Roses to grow across the desert. He is dead by the time of the quest.

Children liked him when he was younger and asked for Ajilenakh Nuts and his stories, but by the time Affan met him he had become unfriendly toward children. His rose folk song says that the Golden Rose "sang to me" from the stone and that songs will surpass the singer and time.

13.content: In this series the Golden Rose is a rose breed that Shafaqat cultivated in Aaru Village. Its seeds are encased in a hard stone-like shell, which Sabbah thinks results from a strong affinity for Geo. Affan calls it more precious than the Sumeru Rose. The seeds can be kept dry for a very long time, according to the dead man's notes. Dendro awakens them after the shell is broken.

14.comment: A Gifted Rose: Sabbah in Aaru Village
14.content: Sabbah is an Amurta researcher living in exile in Aaru Village (first met in The Exile). In this series she examines Affan's seeds, finds the way to wake them, and says she identifies with Shafaqat because both were exiled. She chooses to stay and help Affan tend the roses and says she is less lonely as a result.

key: A Great Heart Fettered by Slender Chains
15.comment: A Great Heart Fettered by Slender Chains
15.content:
A Great Heart Fettered by Slender Chains (also: Everfrozen Earth snow giant quest): A Great Heart Fettered by Slender Chains is a Snezhnaya World Quest added in version 7.0. In a blizzard in the Everfrozen Earth, the Traveler and Paimon find a huge snow giant bound to the ground by chains of snow and ice. The chains can be broken only with help from a girl's shadow, who leads them through four small scenes from a house and its past. When all four are broken, the storm clears and the giant stands and walks away.

It starts when the player approaches the figure in the storm. It gives Adventure EXP, Primogems, Mora, Hero's Wit and Mystic Enhancement Ore as rewards (game-mechanics information), and the next quest in the chain is "Like a Labyrinth Imprisons Her Servants".

The tone is quiet and almost wordless. Much of the story comes from short remembered voices and the setting of the objects, rather than from the Traveler's conversations. It is a good short scene source for Snezhnaya's mix of fae, human memory and Prime Ice constructs.

Plot: In the blizzard the Traveler and Paimon see a huge silhouette, a snow giant held down by chains of snow and ice. Paimon wonders how to help. Each of the four chains is guarded by a seal that only a ghost-like figure, the shadow of a girl, can break, and every time she reaches one the Traveler has to clear the way and then break the chain itself.

Chain 1. A man-made Chimeric Horned Bear is nearby. After it is defeated, the shadow comes out from behind some crates and breaks the seal on the nearest chain, then the Traveler destroys the device that controls the chains.

Chain 2. The shadow cannot cross a gap, so the Traveler places a Launching Platform. She then runs toward a Prime Ice window, which the Traveler breaks with the Eye of Graeae's Fab-Vision. In a corridor guarded by Snegurochka statues she kneels behind crates, and two voices are heard. A compassionate voice says Lady Pavlina has ordered that the human girl must not meet "him", and calls this too cruel. A cold voice, identified as Pavlina, replies that it could get Donskoy killed: his spirit was damaged during the war and he needs a long peaceful sleep. The Traveler destroys the statues, and the compassionate voice shows a secret passage by which she might glimpse Donskoy while he sleeps. More statues trap her and are destroyed, and she breaks the seal.

Chain 3. A buried wooden house plays faint music behind frozen doors. The Traveler goes underground, melts walls of ice, and meets the shadow in a room with a gentle male voice, who is Donskoy, asking for a phonograph to be placed beneath the picture frame, on the larger chair and beneath the cabinet, with lines about one last dance and being put "in my place" if he does not return from battle. After the phonographs are placed correctly she packs up the phonograph, the ice on the door breaks, and she goes out to break the seal.

Chain 4. The Traveler builds a Snowball Launcher and sends a snowball through the Gate of the Sprouting Tsar's White Birch, then helps the shadow paint. An easel is empty until the Traveler places a Pale-Furred Wolf Construct and a Red-Bellied Plover Construct and sits on the chair: Paimon guesses she wants to paint a person surrounded by animals. A note found near the easel, "In Search of Inspiration", says animals that like warmth avoid Snegovik because of the cold, but ice sculptures and drawings of real animals might still fulfil his wish. The shadow paints, an ice wall breaks, and she goes to the last chain.

After all four are broken the snow giant wakes and slowly walks away. Paimon wonders where he went and how the girl is linked to him, and expects to meet him again.

Post-quest. At 18:00 in-game time the Eye of Graeae sends a message, "Regarding the giant figure by the sea...", saying people have reported a giant surrounded by ice and snow near the sea. The Eye compares data and thinks it may be the one chained in the canyon, and marks the area on the map as "Gigantic Figure by the Sea".

Revelations: - Pavlina has forbidden a human girl from meeting Donskoy, because his spirit was damaged in the war and he needs a long, undisturbed sleep.
- Donskoy's voice, in memory, speaks of a last dance and of leaving a phonograph "in my place" if he does not return from battle.
- Snegovik and Snegurochka statues help guard the places the shadow passes, and the shadow is afraid of them.

- The painting scene suggests that Donskoy wished for a portrait of a person with animals, though the quest only hints at this through a note and Paimon's guess.

Characters: - The Traveler and Paimon.
- The snow giant, who is probably Donskoy (inferred, not stated).
- The girl's shadow, who is unnamed.
- Pavlina, heard as the cold voice, and an unnamed compassionate voice who helps the girl.
- The Eye of Graeae, whose Fab-Vision breaks Prime Ice and who sends the later message.

- Chimeric Horned Bears and Snegurochka statues appear as guardians; the bear is described as a man-made (aberrant chimeric) monster.

Consequences: The giant is freed from his chains and leaves the canyon, and the blizzard ends. The Eye of Graeae's message sends the Traveler toward the coast and the next quest. No lasting change to named characters is shown within this quest.

Placement: Story order: a standalone World Quest in the Everfrozen Earth, before "Like a Labyrinth Imprisons Her Servants". Release order: version 7.0. It shares Pavlina and Snegovik themes with Hesperides of Love and Hate.

16.comment: A Great Heart Fettered by Slender Chains: Donskoy
16.content: In this quest Donskoy is a name spoken about and, in the page's attribution, a gentle male voice heard in a memory. The cold voice says his spirit was damaged in the war and that he needs long, peaceful sleep, so he must not be disturbed. The quest does not describe him directly, but the sleeping snow giant is very likely him.

17.content:
A Land Entombed (also: Ancient Investigation Journal quest): A Dragonspine world quest from Version 1.2. The Traveler finds an Ancient Investigation Journal and takes it to the researcher Stevens, who explains it belongs to an old expedition sent up the mountain by Mondstadt's aristocrats. The Traveler recovers the other two parts.

Stevens recalls an old annal, from before the Knights of Favonius existed, about a team sent by the aristocrats to investigate the mountain; the annals say almost nothing about what it found. Once all three journals are collected he concludes that very likely no member returned to Mondstadt, apart from possibly one man named Eberhart.

The quest is a small piece of history-mystery and a quiet pointer toward the ruined kingdom under Dragonspine. It unlocks only an achievement and a reward.

Plot: The Traveler and Paimon pick up a journal in the mountains and show it to Stevens at the camp. He asks them to find the two other parts, marks the sites, and after reading all three tells them an aristocrat-led expedition seems to have been lost, with Eberhart perhaps the sole possible survivor.

Stevens thinks the team investigated three sites. The Traveler finds the first journal at the secret chamber near the Entombed City's great door, the second in a cellar under the ice in the southwestern ruins (two Warming Seelie puzzles and a Ruin Grader guard it), and the third on a shelf in Starglow Cavern, behind a thin opening in the ice. Reading them, Stevens is taken aback and drifts into thought mid-sentence. He explains why the annals mention only the team's departure, and asks the Traveler to bring any other books they find in the mountains.

Stevens first jokes that "treasure" means a treasure trove of knowledge. After reading the journals he says some minor details still need straightening out but the overall picture is clear, and the quest description says the journals seem to point to some sort of conspiracy. He ends by wondering aloud where Eberhart went, since there is no record of his return to Mondstadt. Stevens' conclusions are his own reading of the journals and the annals.

The journals are Part I (the secret chamber by the Entombed City's ancient palace door), Part II (the cellar in the southwestern ruins) and Part III (Starglow Cavern); the order of collection does not change the dialogue. The last passage can only be reached by short or medium-height characters. The first two sites are puzzle rooms with Warming Seelie, so the "treasure" is mostly access to history.

Revelations: The journals suggest that the aristocrat-sent investigation team did not come back as a group, which explains the gap in the old annals. One member, Eberhart, may have survived, but his fate is unknown.

Characters: The Traveler, Paimon and Stevens.

Stevens is a history-minded researcher at the Dragonspine base camp who is enthusiastic about primary sources and promises compensation.

Consequences: Stevens gains valuable historical sources and rewards the Traveler. The quest grants the achievement Snow-Stored History. The Ragged Records are related but optional.

Placement: Released in Version 1.2 with the rest of Dragonspine's exploration content. It can be done in any order relative to In the Mountains.

key: A Lanternlit Ode to the Silver Moon
18.comment: A Lanternlit Ode to the Silver Moon
18.content:
A Lanternlit Ode to the Silver Moon (also: Lantern Rite 2026, Luna IV Lantern Rite event, The Realm of Clouds, The Realm of Rocks, The Realm of People, White Horse's Leisurely Journey, Odes of Lang: Zibai): A curious eclipse, a photograph and an exhibition of Chasm artifacts lead the Traveler to the first of Zibai's three Selves. The second, Zizhi, possesses people who voice wishes and shows the memory of Lang-Gan's destruction; the third, Ziqiao, is won over by a day's sightseeing with Zhongli's help. On Lantern Rite night Zibai awakens. The epilogue is a lighter tour of Liyue with the recovering adeptus.

The story quest was released with the Lantern Rite flagship event of Luna IV (30 January to 23 February 2026) and remains playable afterwards from the Quest Overview, under Event Quests, where it is started by enabling Focused Experience Mode. Players are recommended to have completed the Song of the Welkin Moon finale (True Moon) because the plot builds on the return of the Frost Moon and on events in Nod-Krai.

Zibai becomes a playable character in the same version, and continues in Liyue in later content; by Version 7.1 she is living at Baiju Guesthouse and appears in the Moonchase Festival event Silverwing in Pursuit of the Moon. The residence at Baiju Guesthouse begins in this quest's epilogue.

Plot: Act I, The Realm of Clouds: in Liyue Harbor for Lantern Rite, the Traveler hears about a partial eclipse and legends of the White Horse Adeptus, and at an antiques exhibition touches a broken jade token that carries them to a dream space where a woman tells them the way home. Zhongli explains that she is Zibai's First Deadly Self.

Act II, The Realm of Rocks: Zibai's Second Self, Zizhi, possesses Lu Xiangxiang, then Gaming, then Mountain Shaper. The adepti plan to force her out, and the Traveler wins her trust and sees the memory of Lang-Gan's destruction.

Act III, The Realm of People: Zhongli persuades the Third Self, Ziqiao, to take a day's tour of Liyue; she gives up her fragment, and on Lantern Rite night the Traveler and Zhongli revive Zibai.

Epilogue: amnesic Zibai tours Liyue with the Traveler and Paimon.

The four chapters are detailed in their own entries: Act I follows the antiques exhibition and the dream space; Act II the possession of Lu Xiangxiang, Gaming and Mountain Shaper by Zizhi; Act III Ziqiao's day in Liyue Harbor and the Lantern Rite revival; the epilogue Zibai's first days back, with the tea errand, Qiaoying and Qingce villages and Wangshu Inn.

Further details. Qiqi's recollection of Baizhu's patients and the stall's Xiao Lanterns frame the eclipse as a communal worry. At the exhibition Zhongli asks Yun Jin for opera lyrics in return for the silk painting, which he says is his own copy; Beidou buys a bronze war chariot for 90 million Mora to show Ningguang; the Six Ritual Jades set is missing two pieces; and the Traveler and Zhongli learn that Zhongli had helped the exhibition because he sensed Zizhi in a jade carriage. The adepti's reaction to the Selves is explained by Madame Ping: Zizhi seems to guide those she possesses to fulfil their own wishes, not to harm them. Mountain Shaper and Moon Carver were in Liyue Harbor because Rex Lapis had asked the adepti to keep watch. In Zizhi's prison the Traveler outruns the river of time, a symbol of the curse of time. In Act III Zhongli describes Ziqiao as the most free-spirited of the Selves and says she aided him in the Archon War a thousand years earlier before retreating to the mountains; she tells the Traveler at the end that she had decided to help from her first sight of Liyue Harbor. In the epilogue Paimon likens Zibai's three temperaments to a hot-tempered Pyro Slime, a mathematical Hydro Slime and a mischievous Anemo Slime. Lu Weng's gift of Sunglo Tea and the news that the guesthouse's old name stays close the epilogue.

Revelations: The White Horse Adeptus is Zibai, whom Lang-Gan worshipped as the God of Soil and Grain. According to Zhongli she died long ago, and Istaroth preserved the shards of her soul in her three severed Deadly Selves: Ziju (Heavenly Soul, Taiguang), held in the shadowmoon; Zizhi (Earth Soul, Shuangling), who slept beneath the Chasm; and Ziqiao (Human Soul, Youjing), who helped Zhongli in the Archon War.

The false moon: the shadowmoon is a projection that hung in the sky for thousands of years until the true Frost Moon returned. Zhongli says it is disintegrating bit by bit, appearing as a black shadow over the moon, and suspects that people's wishes trigger the bouts of collapse. He expects the mass release of wish lanterns at Lantern Rite to bring it down, which will open the cage around the First Self; that is the moment to act, and also the moment when everything could be lost. The First Self and the shadowmoon have merged, so when the shadow goes she will cease to exist unless the other two souls are gathered.

The memory of Lang-Gan, shown by Zizhi: Zibai taught the people to grow grain, spin and weave, build houses and cast bronze, and descended on festival nights to hear wishes. Then the moons darkened, two shattered, and a Celestial Nail appeared over Lang-Gan. Istaroth told Zibai that places tainted by the Abyss must be purified, that she was only an emissary and had no reason for guilt. Zibai said that, as their god, she would die among them. Her Jadelight Canopy held the Nail back, giving people time to flee; Zibai fell, Istaroth caught her and told her she had done enough, and split her soul into the Three Deadly Selves. The survivors, descendants of whom now live across Liyue, looked up at the one moon that remained. Zizhi says war had spread cursed remnants from the heavens over the earth, and that she wished she had given them a little more time.

Other revelations. Zhongli's idea that wishes trigger the shadowmoon's collapse is based on timing: the Traveler's vision began just as Linlang spoke of her own wish at the exhibition. The Moonchase Rite, an adeptal ritual in which Rex Lapis tried to contact the moon (reported by Ganyu from Cloud Retainer), is understood to have been an attempt to reach the White Horse Adeptus all along. The ancient poem found on the Chasm artifacts, called "Odes of Lang: Zibai", is an ode of blessing to the maiden of the moon, naming the Eternal, Iridescent and Frost moons and what she grants each: silk, fibre for cloth, and tools to divine one's fate; then farming, harvest and wine offered to her. In the epilogue Zibai recalls the god whose remains are sealed at Wuwang Hill, known in opera as Tao Dou, as Bune, god of the underworld, a name Paimon does not know.

Characters: Main: the Traveler, Paimon, Zhongli, Zibai (and her Selves Ziju, Zizhi, Ziqiao). Lu family: Lu Xiangxiang and her grandfather Lu Weng of Baiju Guesthouse. Others: Ningguang, Keqing, Lan Yan, Yelan, Gaming, Shenhe, Hu Tao and friends, Yun Jin, Beidou, Yaoyao, Qiqi, Baizhu, the adepti Cloud Retainer, Madame Ping, Xiao, Moon Carver and Mountain Shaper. Istaroth appears in a memory.

The 4-star Liyue characters who can be invited with Fortune Coins are Lan Yan, Gaming, Xiangling, Beidou, Xingqiu, Ningguang, Chongyun, Xinyan, Yanfei, Yun Jin and Yaoyao.

Consequences: Zibai is revived, confused and partly forgetful, with the temperaments of all three Selves. She takes a long-term room at Baiju Guesthouse, charged to the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor, and enjoys Liyue. Lu Xiangxiang decides to stay with the archaeological team. Mountain Shaper and Moon Carver are banned from Mt. Aocang for three days for the mint plan.

After the tour she is staying at Baiju Guesthouse, treats the Traveler and Paimon as her "guides", and appears in later Liyue content, including Silverwing in Pursuit of the Moon (7.1).

Placement: Released in Version 6.3 (Luna IV, 14 January 2026) as the story of the Lantern Rite flagship event (30 January to 23 February 2026). It requires the Prologue (Act III, Song of the Dragon and Freedom) and, for context, the Song of the Welkin Moon finale True Moon in Nod-Krai. After the event ends it is still available from the Quest Overview under Event Quests. In story order it follows the return of the Frost Moon and precedes Silverwing in Pursuit of the Moon (7.1).

Earlier Lantern Rite stories are Lantern Rite (2021, Version 1.3) and Fleeting Colors in Flight (2022, Version 2.4); the 2021 festival's lantern honoured Skybracer, and this one honours the White Horse Adeptus.

Gameplay: Game mechanics, not in-world fact. Four modes: Vigorous Brushstrokes (a runner stage collecting jade), Wishes Contended, Fortunes Won (combat for Charm Coins), The Moonlit Adeptus's Trail (the Traveler plays an adeptus fighting Zhanzhus in a storyteller's tale) and Bright Moon, Lantern Glow (placing Xiao Lanterns and trimming Auspicious Treasure Trees). Fortune Coins are spent in the Festive Shopping shop, to invite a companion (1,000 coins) and to obtain Yaoyao's outfit Rainlit Bamboo Reverie (1,000 coins; later sold in the Character Outfit Shop). Completing the story quests gives Primogems and materials. The story quest remains available after the event, though event gameplay does not.

19.comment: A Lanternlit Ode to the Silver Moon: Zibai's Three Deadly Selves
19.content:
Zhongli's account: Zibai severed the practitioner's Three Deadly Selves, impure aspects of mind, before she died. Istaroth preserved Zibai's shattered soul in them. Ziju (Heavenly Soul, Taiguang) was in the shadowmoon, Zizhi (Earth Soul, Shuangling) slept in the Chasm and possesses people who make wishes, and Ziqiao (Human Soul, Youjing) lived freely in the mountains. When all three souls were gathered Zibai could be restored.

Ziqiao is the most worldly and teases mortals; Zizhi is angry and sorrowful; Ziju is the closest to Zibai's own nature. After the revival Zibai shows all three temperaments in turn.

20.comment: A Lanternlit Ode to the Silver Moon: Memory of Lang-Gan
20.content: The destruction of Lang-Gan as seen through Zizhi: worshippers once lit lanterns at an altar like Chiwang Terrace and prayed to the maiden on the moon, who taught farming, silk and bronze; then the moons dimmed, a Celestial Nail appeared and Istaroth said the Abyss-tainted land had to be purified. Zibai interposed her Jadelight Canopy to give her people time, was caught as she fell, and her soul was split. The survivors looked up at the single moon left.

21.comment: A Lanternlit Ode to the Silver Moon: Odes of Lang: Zibai
21.content: The text on the Chasm artifacts, first called "An Ancient Poem". It praises a maiden descending from the Eternal, Iridescent and Frost moons who blesses silk, fibre and divination plants, teaches ploughing and sowing, and receives wine and a wish at harvest. Ziqiao (in character as the White Horse Adeptus) explains it to Yun Jin, and the people of Liyue Harbor recite it on Lantern Rite night as lanterns rise.

22.comment: A Lanternlit Ode to the Silver Moon: Lu Xiangxiang and the Lu family
22.content: A young archaeologist from a Qiaoying Village tea-growing family whose grandfather Lu Weng runs Baiju Guesthouse, named for the White Horse Adeptus who saved one of his ancestors. She helped excavate Lang-Gan relics in the Chasm, was possessed by Zizhi and overturned tables and injured two customers at Wanmin Restaurant, and recovered with no memory of it. Her family grounded her by making her raise a tea tree; Zibai replaces the seedling overnight and the family treats it as a miracle.

23.comment: A Lanternlit Ode to the Silver Moon: The White Horse Adeptus legends
23.content: Xingqiu lists the competing accounts: Hu Tao's reading as the Gold-Eyed Celadon Mare of the Eight Adepts; the elders of Qingce who say a white horse leapt from a spring and aided Rex Lapis in the Archon War; some Chenyu Vale tribes who call her the Daughter of Time; and the ancient texts that make her an emissary who carries wishes to the heavens. Madame Ping says the White Horse Adeptus always avoided the other adepti in the Archon War and she never knew why.

24.comment: A Lanternlit Ode to the Silver Moon: Moonchase Rite
24.content: Ganyu reports Cloud Retainer's understanding of the ritual that gave the Moonchase Festival its name. Before it became a festival it was an adeptal rite performed by Rex Lapis to communicate with the moon, which never answered. Seeing Keqing's photo of the dark spot on the moon, Cloud Retainer concluded that the Rite had been an attempt to reach the White Horse Adeptus all along.

25.comment: A Lanternlit Ode to the Silver Moon: Act I - The Realm of Clouds
25.content: Yaoyao and Qiqi are making Xiao Lanterns, and Qiqi mentions that Baizhu had patients injured walking in the dark when the moon vanished. The legend of Zhanzhu the Moon-Devourer, a toad that eats the moon, is told. The huge lantern this year honours the White Horse Adeptus, who legend says lived on the moon. Lu Weng of Baiju Guesthouse insists she is real: one of his ancestors, a young herb-gatherer, fell from a cliff and was rescued by the White Horse Adeptus, who told her about the moon and the kingdom of Lang-Gan. She lost track of time and returned to find her village in ruins after countless years, but it proved to be a dream: she woke at the foot of the cliff with a basket full of rare herbs and saw a white horse leap over the cliff above. He is quarrelling with his son, who wants to rename the guesthouse. At Third-Round Knockout the Traveler meets Xiangling, Hu Tao, Xingqiu and Chongyun, who show the photograph Lu Xiangxiang dropped, the moon being covered from its centre. She had been shouting about Lang-Gan treasure and the picture, wielded a shovel and was subdued by Shenhe. Ningguang, Keqing and Lan Yan at Yujing Terrace say the Chasm artifacts were all registered with the Ministry of Civil Affairs, that more such eclipses are expected, and that the picture shows the moon above Chiwang Terrace; Lan Yan adds that the ancient people of Chenyu Vale are said to have spoken to the heavens there. Baizhu says Lu Xiangxiang is in shock and will be sedated for two days. The Traveler goes to the exhibition on the ship organised by Linlang of Xigu Antiques, where they meet Beidou and Yun Jin, Zhongli (whose painting is a copy) and the broken token. After the dream space and the Traveler's return, Zhongli takes them to Mt. Tianheng to explain.

26.comment: A Lanternlit Ode to the Silver Moon: Act II - The Realm of Rocks
26.content: Yelan investigates Lu Xiangxiang's disappearance with the Traveler; she suggests checking Xiao Lantern stalls because people pray for wishes there. Gaming, who wished for apprentices for the Mighty Mythical Beasts, is approached by Lu Xiangxiang, who offers to be his apprentice. Time freezes, Zizhi tells the Traveler to leave, and then Lu Xiangxiang comes round and does not remember. Gaming becomes aggressive, trying to force Treasure Hoarders and then two disguised adepti to be apprentices. Moon Carver (Houzhang) and Mountain Shaper (Jiehu) recognise it as malign. Zizhi moves to Mountain Shaper, who goes to plant mint at Cloud Retainer's abode. The adepti (Cloud Retainer, Madame Ping, Xiao) debate whether to fight and decide to follow Cloud Retainer's plan. Zizhi eventually accepts the Traveler's wish to know her sorrow and puts them into her prison: an unending river of time (a chase sequence). After surviving it the Traveler sees the memory and Zizhi's last request that, if anyone ever raises a banner against the heavens, her name be put on its cloth. Back at Mt. Aocang Mountain Shaper returns to himself and Cloud Retainer scolds him for the mint; Xiao tells the Traveler he will not ask what Zizhi said.

27.comment: A Lanternlit Ode to the Silver Moon: Act III - The Realm of People
27.content: Two days later, at Mt. Aocang, the Geo pillar has fallen but only the Traveler can hear it. At Mt. Qingce the Traveler finds Zhongli weaving a Xiao Lantern and talking to Ziqiao, who shapes herself as a white horse. Ziqiao says she is not Zibai, reminds Zhongli that after he freed her from a painting she fought for him, helping to subdue Chenyu Vale and bring peace to Mt. Qingce, so their contract has been fulfilled, and invites a new offer. Zhongli proposes a one-day festive excursion with the Traveler and Paimon as guides. Ziqiao asks to start in Liyue Harbor, eats at Wanmin Restaurant, where Xiangling plays along with her claim to be the White Horse Adeptus, meets the now-recovered Lu Xiangxiang, discusses ambition and joy, hears Iron Tongue Tian and Yun Jin discuss the ancient poem and recites its meaning, meets Yanfei and Ganyu, jokes about the lateral gait of the giant horse lantern, has her photo taken with the Traveler and watches the sunset from Yujing Terrace. At sunset she pretends the day was dull to tease Paimon, then says she decided to help as soon as she saw the ordinary life of the city, thanks them, tells them to take what they need, and fades. Zhongli, who has been nearby, explains that a Deadly Self cannot survive long without the soul remnant that sustained it. At the Lantern Rite release the Traveler places the Human and Earth souls in a Xiao Lantern that Zhongli holds and lets it rise. Zibai's Jadelight Canopy appears and melts away to reveal the full moon, and Zibai awakens, her eyes briefly flashing the colours of her three Selves. She does not know where she is, then recalls that she was the Envoy of the Lunar Palace named Zibai, recognises Zhongli as the Lord of Geo, "Heaven's Star", and remembers the Traveler and Paimon as her guides.

28.comment: A Lanternlit Ode to the Silver Moon: Epilogue - White Horse's Leisurely Journey
28.content: Zibai, found in Wanmin Restaurant, mistakes Shenhe for the Crane Adeptus of mint planting and lectures her about self-cultivation. She wants to buy Sunglo Tea for Zhongli because Hu Tao has restricted him to discounted purchases after his expensive exhibition. Travelling in a lunar chariot of her own making she tells Paimon she was once an angel and then a moon envoy. A tea merchant, Fenglian, explains her bulk discount; Zibai extrapolates the pattern to a free twenty-one boxes and a loss for the seller, who suddenly has no stock. In Qiaoying Village she finds Lu Xiangxiang grounded with the task of raising a tea seedling and secretly transplants a full tea tree overnight, creating a "miracle". In Qingce Village she advises two children on planting rice and canola, citing the title the people of Lang-Gan gave her. At Wuwang Hill she meets Hu Tao and Zhongli, who says she was not from Liyue but perhaps will be. At Wangshu Inn she cooks Flavor of Spring for Xiao, returns the broken jade token to the Traveler and promises to make a trinket from it. At Baiju Guesthouse she takes a long-term room, charged to the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor.

key: A Long Day in the Mountains
29.comment: A Long Day in the Mountains
29.content:
A Long Day in the Mountains (also: Magic Mountain, Paradise, Hell, Judgment, Temple of Space chapter, Zeitlind's quest): A Version 6.5 world quest chapter set around Dornman Port and the Old Sanatorium Site on Windrest Peak, then inside the Temple of Space. A young woman named Zeitlind is searching for her older sister Hilda, who vanished from the sanatorium. A towering angelic Watcher, Nihilita, sends the Traveler to free the temple from his counterpart Melanta.

The chapter has four acts: Magic Mountain (the prologue), Paradise, Hell and Judgment. It is built around the Temple of Space, a place created by the God of Space, Asmoday, whose inhabitants have been terrorised since their Watcher Melanta took control. Zeitlind recovers her sister's belongings from the temple's districts. The trial ends with Melanta defeated and Zeitlind giving up her memories to open the way.

The theme is memory, will to live and what freedom means to a created being. It deals gently with grief and an absent sibling, which parallels the Traveler's own search for a lost twin. Melanta, who wants to "correct" others, is shown as hurt and jealous rather than simply cruel.

The wiki notes the title echoes the novel The Magic Mountain; the chapter uses a sanatorium on a mountain and otherworldly figures in the same way, but that is an observation from outside the game.

Plot: A man, Mann, warns people not to go up the mountain after seeing a ghost at the old sanatorium: a woman beside a grave with her own face. The Traveler meets Zeitlind, who is looking for her sister, and the red-sky Watcher Nihilita traps her and sends the Traveler to the Temple of Space. There the group helps the inhabitants, finds Hilda's belongings, and finally confronts Melanta.

**Magic Mountain.** In the north of Dornman Port, Mann and his dog Hauptmann tell of the encounter at the Old Sanatorium Site. At the graveyard Zeitlind says her older sister disappeared while staying there, and the grave turns out to be her sister's, though it looks like Zeitlind. The sky turns red, Nihilita appears and traps Zeitlind in cubes, and entrusts the Traveler with a juvenile Watcher, Dex. At the Temple of Space Zeitlind is freed. Istoria explains that after the God of Space vanished, Melanta took over and tormented the inhabitants. The group frees Josephus in the Memory Core, and Istoria reveals Hilda had been in the temple. A Domain Keeper steals Zeitlind's suitcase and scatters its contents across the three exhibition spaces.
**Paradise.** The Traveler and Zeitlind restore Luyang Academy, where people were turned into ink, Mahavaipulya Chamber, and the Desert Pavilion, where people were turned into sand. In each they recover an item of Hilda's: a photograph at Wangshu Inn, a stack of letters sent to Zeitlind from the sanatorium, and an amethyst brooch. Many inhabitants mistake Zeitlind for Hilda, and some knew her. Istoria says that to defeat Melanta they must construct the Path to the Heavens, which demands the sacrifice of memories.
**Hell.** Red cubes cast the group into the Apathic Interval, where those chosen for the temple must give up their desires. Dex and the Traveler break the Maranasati Caskets, rescue Istoria, Zeitlind and a man named Alara, and escape with three Deathmuse Shards without forgoing their desires. Paimon, curiously, was not drawn in.
**Judgment.** Istoria says Hilda once sacrificed her memories to make the Path and met Melanta herself; afterwards Melanta wrecked part of the Path. Istoria offers his own memories but is persuaded his knowledge is too valuable, and Zeitlind accepts the burden. The group crosses the Corridor of Nothingness, where the Traveler sees shared dreams of the sisters, and reaches the Atrium of Suchness. Melanta cannot account for the Traveler's sibling's fate and calls Nihilita a traitor. He loses the fight, accepts that all creations became free when Asmoday left, and admits his actions caused his own breakdown. Asked by Zeitlind why the sanatorium is cursed, he answers, then explains that he sought to correct others, admits envy of Nihilita's freedom and longing for his creator's approval, and self-destructs.

Details worth keeping: Istoria once discussed philosophy with Hilda to strengthen her will to live; Zeitlind tells him Hilda was badly hurt when her fiancé abandoned her; Melanta exiled a figure called Maukie and illusions of it trouble the rescue at Luyang Academy. Istoria explains the names of the two Watchers. Zeitlind says her epitaph should read "To be continued" and loses her memories upon returning to the surface. Back at the sanatorium the Traveler and Paimon help her begin anew and remind her that her sister is still somewhere out in the world.

Revelations: The Temple of Space is run by Watchers created by the God of Space, Asmoday, and one of them, Melanta, rules by fear.

Melanta says all creations were free the moment Asmoday left, and that Nihilita left because of that. Hilda, Zeitlind's sister, once went to the temple and sacrificed her memories to confront Melanta; her fate afterwards is unknown. Melanta also answers Zeitlind's question about why the Windrest Peak sanatorium is cursed.

Melanta could not explain the Traveler's sibling's fate when asked, which keeps that mystery open in this chapter. The chapter never states how Hilda left the temple or where she went.

Characters: The Traveler and Paimon; Zeitlind; Raumhilda (Hilda); Nihilita; Melanta; Dex; Istoria.

Mann and his dog Hauptmann; Josephus, Alara and Venipi among the inhabitants; Daozi, Bosch and Yoshitoshi at Luyang Academy; Calcerius, Okikuni and Yu Huangyi at Mahavaipulya Chamber; the Domain Keepers and the Punisher of Gomorrah as enemies.

Consequences: The temple is freed and Melanta is gone. Zeitlind loses her memories and starts over on the surface. The chapter leaves Hilda's whereabouts open.

The Temple of Space and the mystery of the Watchers are linked, through Melanta's words, to Asmoday's departure and the Traveler's sibling.

Placement: Released in Version 6.5 (Luna VI, 2026-04-08) as a world quest chapter. It starts near Dornman Port in Mondstadt and then moves to the Temple of Space. The wiki page lists no quest requirement.

key: Song of the Welkin Moon Act III
30.content:
A Nation That Doesn't Exist (also: Song of the Welkin Moon Act III, Welkin Moon Act III, Hidden in the Shadows, Special Operation, Everlasting As the Moon): The third act of the Song of the Welkin Moon chapter. With Rerir's body restored, the master of the Wild Hunt drains kuuvahki from Nod-Krai and attacks Columbina, and the Traveler and their allies are forced to hide and prepare. Nefer's ceremony shows Rerir's life as a Khaenri'ahn, and Arlecchino, a fellow Fatui Harbinger, opens a path to the last Moon Marrow, the Iridescent one.

The act has three quests: Hidden in the Shadows, Special Operation, and Everlasting As the Moon. It follows Elegy of Dust and Lamplight and precedes An Elegy for Faded Moonlight.

It shows Rerir, the Rächer of Solnari and one of the Five Sinners of Khaenri'ah, directly as an opponent too strong for the party, and it is the act in which the Fatui figures Sandrone and Arlecchino choose to aid the Traveler and Columbina.

Plot: After the Wild Hunt strikes Nasha Town's quarry and leaves it drained of kuuvahki, Rerir attacks Columbina. The Traveler and Columbina escape and are sheltered by Varka, while Nefer is hired to help. Columbina proposes finding the Iridescent Marrow, the last of three, to restore her power; Sandrone lets them into the Bureau and the Wild Hunt attacks it. Nefer's ceremony shows Rerir as a Khaenri'ahn who had proposed to Tholindis. Arlecchino rescues the Traveler and Columbina at Thunderclap Reef, opens a portal to the Marrow's domain, and her hands are corrupted by forcing the exit open.

After Rerir's physical form is restored, the Traveler and Paimon wonder what he wants. In Nasha Town the Ratnik Radimir says the Wild Hunt hit the quarry and Flins wants to see them. There Aino, Ineffa, Jahoda and Lauma note the area's kuuvahki is fully drained. Believing Rerir is hunting other kuuvahki-rich places, the group splits to check them, then regroups at Hiisi Island. Jahoda dares Rerir to appear, and the ground shakes; Lauma realises he is attacking Columbina. Lauma orders Jahoda to take Columbina away, but Rerir overpowers them and fires at Jahoda. Columbina shoves her aside and is grazed. She and the Traveler touch hands, and an explosion teleports them away. Rerir summons the Wild Hunt to find her.

Columbina tells the Traveler she cannot teleport them again. The Wild Hunt finds them; after they fight off ghouls, a Wolf's Gravestone slams down and Varka arrives, taking them to a secret base. He says he and his men were misled to Lake Amsvartnir, though he doubts Rerir could be in both places. Columbina proposes finding the last Moon Marrow, the Iridescent Marrow, so that with all three she can restore her power faster; she needs to visit the Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau and takes the Traveler. Varka introduces Nefer as the current owner of the Northern Intelligence Network. She refuses to work for free; Lauma offers payment and Jahoda asks her to take it from her own pay, and Nefer reluctantly accepts and asks Flins for the fragments of Rerir's heart. Aino and Ineffa will build decoys with Columbina's traces; Jahoda and Lauma go with Nefer.

At the bureau, Fevroniya and Ozerov threaten to call security until Sandrone lets them pass. Columbina asks for Arlecchino, whom Sandrone says has not been around since the facility was finished. Sandrone, annoyed by Columbina's past intervention but recalling her tea parties, agrees to help and has Pulonia ask Fevroniya to send a message to Arlecchino. The bureau shakes: the Wild Hunt attacks. Sandrone sends the Traveler and Columbina out by a secret passage while her landcruisers fight. Rerir arrives, no longer senses Columbina, and when Sandrone sets Pulonia on him he incapacitates it with a flick of the hands.

At the Curatorium of Secrets Nefer asks Jahoda to bring the "shady merchant" she met, who turns out to be Dori. Nefer calls in a favour for Dori's flower-shaped object, which Dori reluctantly lets her have for three days before she starts charging. Nefer then holds a ceremony using Rerir's heart fragments. Jahoda, Lauma and Nefer glimpse his past: a Khaenri'ahn under Irmin who had proposed to a woman named Tholindis, whose duty was to eliminate descendants of the Crimson Moon Dynasty and who did not tell her. They also see a glimpse of Tholindis' memory, and Nefer is puzzled how it came to be in Rerir's possession. The time runs out.

In the last quest the Traveler and Columbina are cornered by the Wild Hunt at Thunderclap Reef until the ghouls burn away: Arlecchino has come. At the bureau Sandrone repairs her landcruisers with Freminet's help while Lyney keeps Lynette away from the machines; one collapses when Lynette touches it. Arlecchino brings the pair to the secret base, where the others tense at who she is, and says she is present only on a personal level and can locate the Iridescent Marrow. On a peninsula between Silvermoon Hall and Hiisi Island she tells the Traveler she is a descendant of the Crimson Moon and learned of her past through Pierro. She agrees to Columbina's terms and opens a portal to the Marrow's domain, warning them to ignore the voices. Inside, the Traveler and Columbina retrieve it as riftwolves rush them and the exit seals; Arlecchino forces it open and her hands are corrupted by defying the Abyss. She declines the Traveler's offer to purify it, since that would destroy her hands. They share the power with Columbina and Arlecchino gives her the Marrow. Columbina hopes she will not be corrupted by the Abyss as Rerir was; Arlecchino says she intends to be, and suggests Columbina change her name once Rerir is dealt with.
Planning details. Nefer takes the job only under pressure from Lauma's payment and Jahoda's request that it come from her own pay. Aino and Ineffa's decoys are meant to draw the Wild Hunt away from Columbina. Columbina explains why they need Arlecchino's help, and Arlecchino agrees to the terms; the terms themselves are not spelled out in the summary.

The bureau's guards defer to Sandrone at once. Dori's flower-shaped object is lent to Nefer's ceremony in exchange for a favour. Lynette's contact with a landcruiser, and Lyney's attempts to keep her away from the machines, give the act a light moment between the fights.

Revelations: Rerir was a Khaenri'ahn under Irmin who had proposed to Tholindis, and whose secret duty was to kill Crimson Moon descendants. Arlecchino is a descendant of the Crimson Moon Dynasty and learned of it through Pierro. The final Moon Marrow is the Iridescent Marrow, kept in an Abyss-guarded domain reachable through a portal.

Columbina's strength is fading, and she believes holding all three Marrows will restore it much faster. Defying the Abyss corrupts Arlecchino's hands. Rerir has grown too powerful for the party and for Pulonia, and the quarry the Wild Hunt struck was left completely drained of kuuvahki.

Characters: Traveler and Paimon with Lauma, Jahoda, Aino, Ineffa, Flins, Varka, Nefer, Columbina, Sandrone (aiding), Arlecchino (aiding, with Lyney, Lynette and Freminet at the bureau), Dori, Pulonia and Rerir (antagonist).

Consequences: Columbina now holds the Iridescent Marrow, with its power shared to her, while Rerir remains at large. Arlecchino's hands are corrupted. The story continues in An Elegy for Faded Moonlight.

Placement: Song of the Welkin Moon Act III, added in version 6.1 (Luna II, 2025-10-22). It follows Elegy of Dust and Lamplight (Act II) and precedes An Elegy for Faded Moonlight (Act IV). Story order equals release order.

31.comment: A Nation That Doesn't Exist: Iridescent Marrow
31.content: The last of the three Moon Marrows. Columbina asks to find it to restore her strength faster. Arlecchino opens a portal to its domain on a peninsula between Silvermoon Hall and Hiisi Island; the Traveler and Columbina retrieve it, and Arlecchino's hands are corrupted in forcing the exit open.

32.comment: A Nation That Doesn't Exist: Rerir's past
32.content: Through Nefer's ceremony using fragments of his heart, the party sees that Rerir was a Khaenri'ahn serving under Irmin who had proposed to Tholindis, with a duty to eliminate Crimson Moon descendants that he hid from her. A memory of Tholindis appears among the fragments, which Nefer cannot explain.

33.comment: A Nation That Doesn't Exist: Arlecchino and Columbina
33.content: Arlecchino saves the Traveler and Columbina at Thunderclap Reef, says she is a Crimson Moon descendant who learned of it through Pierro, and helps them take the Iridescent Marrow. She tells Columbina to consider a new name after Rerir is dealt with.

34.content:
A New Star Approaches (also: Chapter I Act III, Liyue Archon Quest Act III): Chapter I Act III of the Archon Quest, set in Liyue. The Traveler is invited to the Jade Chamber, helps the adepti and the Qixing stop the sealed god Osial, and discovers that Zhongli is the Geo Archon, Morax, who staged his own "death" and hands his Gnosis to the Fatui.

The act has six quests: The Floating Palace, Equilibrium, Solitary Fragrance, Heart of Glaze, Turning Point and The Fond Farewell. It finishes the preparations for the Rite of Parting, brings the Qixing and the adepti into open conflict and then into cooperation, and ends with Zhongli's reveal and a hand-off to the Inazuma storyline.

The act is the payoff of the Liyue chapter. Rex Lapis' "assassination" in the Rite of Descension (Act I) turns out to have been Zhongli's own design, a test of whether Liyue can stand without a god. He reveals that the whole series of events, beginning with that supposed assassination, was his doing.

Plot: The Traveler and Paimon reach the Jade Chamber, join the Qixing and adepti against the ancient god Osial, and then find Zhongli at Northland Bank, where he reveals he is Rex Lapis and gives his Gnosis to Signora.

**The Floating Palace.** Ganyu has delivered Ningguang's invitation. The Traveler and Paimon look for a way up to the Jade Chamber at Mt. Tianheng; a mechanism there does not take them far enough. The Traveler recalls the Guizhong Ballista that Zhongli repaired during the cocogoat hunt in the previous act. Millelith guarding it clash with them because Paimon assumes a trap; Keqing arrives, learns they are Ningguang's guests, and explains how to reach the Chamber. She adds that the Millelith are there because someone repaired the long-derelict ballista in a single day.

**Equilibrium.** Paimon insists tradition demands a gift for Ningguang, so the pair gather ingredients for a tasty slime snack, rescuing a man, Meng Dan, from Treasure Hoarders along the way. After visiting Mingxing Jewelry and finding a guide, they ascend to the Jade Chamber. Ningguang accepts the gift, offers one in return and talks at length about gods, Archons and the Fatui. The Traveler takes a piece of "paper snow" from the Chamber's intel wall.

**Solitary Fragrance.** The paper snow leads them to ruins where the Fatui have been researching the Sigils of Permission. They then meet Zhongli at Dihua Marsh, where he asks for wild Glaze Lilies for the Rite of Parting. While looking for them the Traveler meets Ganyu again and learns she is one of the adepti, who has watched over Liyue Harbor since its founding 3,700 years ago; she shares her thoughts on Rex Lapis' passing. On return the harbor is in turmoil: the adepti and the Qixing are in open confrontation, and Ningguang has started cracking down on the Fatui. Felix tells Zhongli the Millelith are questioning the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor over its Fatui ties; Zhongli leaves to help Hu Tao and tells the Traveler to find Childe.

**Heart of Glaze.** Believing Childe has gone to the Golden House after the Exuvia and the Gnosis, the Traveler duels him there. Childe reaches into the Exuvia and finds nothing, then wrongly assumes the Traveler has the Gnosis. In the fight he draws on his Delusion and a monstrous transformation, and is beaten. He admits Signora's report on the Traveler was wrong. His fallback is to use the Fatui-copied Sigils of Permission to release Osial, an ancient god Rex Lapis sealed under the Guyun Stone Forest, although he dislikes involving bystanders.

**Turning Point.** The adepti and the Qixing join forces. Ningguang's replica Guizhong Ballistas are manned by Cloud Retainer, Mountain Shaper and Moon Carver, while Fatui reinforcements arrive through portals; Keqing leads the Millelith and the Traveler is blessed by Xiao, Ganyu and Madame Ping. The ballista volley fails to hurt Osial, who destroys the platform, and Xiao pulls the Traveler clear. Ningguang then sacrifices the Jade Chamber, dropping it on Osial to press him into the seabed.

**The Fond Farewell.** The Traveler finds Zhongli at Northland Bank with Signora and Childe. He is Rex Lapis, the Geo Archon, and he arranged his own apparent assassination as a test of whether Liyue could do without him. In return for an undisclosed goal he struck a "contract to end all contracts" with the Tsaritsa. Satisfied, he gives his Gnosis to Signora, and the two Harbingers leave.

After the battle the adepti and Qixing settle their differences and the Qixing hold the Rite of Parting, where the Traveler overhears rumours about the battle and the Fatui's involvement and hears the official story the Qixing have put out to explain Morax's demise. Keqing offers the Traveler a reward for stopping Osial; the Traveler only asks for help posting notices about their missing sibling. After talking with townspeople, the Traveler speaks to Zhongli about Liyue's future. Zhongli, aware of the Traveler's aim, says Inazuma is sealed and the Archon Baal has issued the Vision Hunt Decree, and he expects his own "death" to push her plans further. He tells the Traveler not to give up on finding a way in.

Structurally the act mirrors Act II: the first half is errands and courtesy (a gift for Ningguang, flowers for the rite), the second half escalates sharply. Childe's mistaken belief that the Traveler holds the Gnosis is the hinge, because it pushes him to the Osial plan. Zhongli's reveal recasts everything since the Rite of Descension as part of his test.

Revelations: Zhongli is the Geo Archon, Rex Lapis (Morax), and staged his own death.
