Back in the real world Nahida and Paimon have forgotten Rukkhadevata, but the Traveler remembers. Dottore then walks in, having put the Traveler and Paimon to sleep with a sound wave. He reminds Nahida she cannot fight him, but she threatens to destroy the Electro Gnosis, which could awaken Celestia. She agrees to give it to him on condition that he destroys his other segments, and he does. He then proposes trading information about "the skies of Teyvat being fake" for her Dendro Gnosis. The Traveler wakes at Gandharva Ville.

A Toast to Victory: Nilou's letter invites the Traveler to a feast celebrating Cyno's return to the post of General Mahamatra. The Traveler learns that Azar and the other sages were sentenced by Nahida to spend the rest of their lives in Avidya Forest cultivating wisdom, that Alhaitham refused an offer to be Grand Sage, that Dehya intends to leave Dunyarzad's service now the Eleazar cases are cured, and that Setaria plans to leave the Akademiya and keep studying for her people. Everyone now believes Nahida was always the Dendro Archon, so the Traveler keeps Rukkhadevata's memory secret in honour of her last wish. Nahida thanks everyone through the Traveler and then arrives at the feast in person.

Alhaitham's plan rests on assumptions about the Akasha: it has formidable computation, but Alhaitham is confident it cannot yet uncover a plan they are all working on together; the guards at Caravan Ribat must not learn that Cyno has stepped down; and a false order about Kusanali's escape empties the Akademiya of guards. The Traveler's work inside the Akasha divides into Nahida's own state of mind (self-doubt, then resolve) and the fight against Scaramouche, where Nahida uses the samsara loop and Sumeru's pooled knowledge.

The next day the Traveler asks Nahida about Fontaine and its Archon Focalors. She tells them that Irminsul records their sibling, who is not from Teyvat, as appearing suddenly in Khaenri'ah and then travelling Teyvat after the cataclysm, but with blurred records around the climax of the journey, which suggests someone is withholding information. She adds that the Fatui classed them as Teyvat's fourth "Descender", a visitor from outside, suspects the first to be the Heavenly Principles, and does not know the other two. She promises to help and hints she may appear in their dreams.

The act is built as a heist told in parallel strands: a political infiltration through the Akademiya, an Eremite and mercenary diversion in the Bazaar, and a mental operation inside the Akasha, all keyed to Jnagarbha Day because the Akademiya would be preoccupied. Dottore figures three times: in Tighnari's report of his visit to demand Haypasia, as the decoy at Port Ormos that draws the group away while the Fatui go after Haypasia, and finally as Nahida's negotiating partner. Several threads depend on side content in play: the wiki notes that To the Wise, The Unanswerable Problems and Sands of Solitude must be finished or advanced if started, in order to complete the act.

Revelations: Rukkhadevata made Nahida as her successor and is erased from Irminsul and from everyone's memory to cure the forbidden knowledge. Scaramouche was being turned into a false god. Dottore wants the Electro Gnosis and hints at the "false sky".

Rukkhadevata says Nahida was created from the purest Irminsul branch to be her incarnation in the next samsara, and that Irminsul can only be saved if she is erased from it, which removes every trace of her. Nahida connects the forbidden knowledge to King Deshret's time and to the cataclysm. Dottore offers information about "the skies of Teyvat being fake" and reasons that Nahida's Dendro Gnosis has no further use now that the Akasha is to be shut down.

Nahida reveals the Fatui's classification of the Traveler's sibling as the fourth Descender, and that Irminsul records the sibling as arriving in Khaenri'ah and travelling after the cataclysm. Alhaitham says he had never known of forbidden knowledge while working at the Akademiya and suspects the scholars and mercenaries who used it fell to its corruption, and that the Akademiya treated it as something else.

Characters: The Traveler, Paimon, Nahida, Alhaitham, Cyno, Dehya, Scaramouche and Dottore are the principals.

Supporting cast: Candace, Tighnari, Collei, Nilou, Kaveh, Dunyarzad, Azar and the other sages, Rahman, Setaria, Luxembarbo, Isak and Uday, Sheikh Zubayr, Haypasia, Viraf and Rukkhadevata's lucid consciousness.

Consequences: The Akasha is back in Nahida's sole control and the sages' access is revoked. Azar and the other sages are sentenced to live in Avidya Forest. Irminsul is restored and the forbidden knowledge is gone, but everyone except the Traveler has forgotten Rukkhadevata. Dottore leaves with the Electro Gnosis and has destroyed his other segments. Cyno resumes the post of General Mahamatra, and Nahida is regarded as the Dendro Archon from the start. The Traveler learns more about their sibling's records in Irminsul and is pointed towards Fontaine.

Placement: Chapter III Act V, following King Deshret and the Three Magi and preceding Caribert and Inversion of Genesis. Released in version 3.2. The wiki lists Adventure Rank 35 as the unlock requirement.

77.comment: Akasha Pulses, the Kalpa Flame Rises: Jnagarbha Day infiltration plan
77.content: Alhaitham's plan to free Nahida is timed for Jnagarbha Day, when the Akademiya is busy. He stages a betrayal and an attack on Azar to get the Traveler detained near a stable Akasha connection, while Nilou's performance and a false order about Kusanali's escape draw the guards away. Cyno confronts Azar at the Sanctuary of Surasthana, and Nahida takes the Akasha back and removes the sages' access.

78.comment: Akasha Pulses, the Kalpa Flame Rises: Rukkhadevata erased from Irminsul
78.content: Inside the Akasha, Nahida and the Traveler reach Rukkhadevata's lucid consciousness, who tells Nahida she was made from the purest Irminsul branch to be her next incarnation. To restore Irminsul Nahida must erase Rukkhadevata from it; she does, with regret. The forbidden knowledge vanishes and Sumeru dreams again, while Nahida and Paimon forget Rukkhadevata. The Traveler remembers and chooses to keep it secret.

79.comment: Akasha Pulses, the Kalpa Flame Rises: Dottore's bargain for the Electro Gnosis
79.content: After the fight in the Akasha, Nahida holds the Electro Gnosis. Dottore puts the Traveler and Paimon to sleep with a sound wave and negotiates; Nahida threatens to destroy the Gnosis, which could awaken Celestia, but chooses to give it to him on the condition he destroys his other segments. He agrees and does so. He then proposes trading information about the skies of Teyvat being fake for her Dendro Gnosis.

80.content:
Akitsu Kimodameshi (also: Test of Courage event, Haunted Tales, The Currents of Life, Akitsu Yuugei): The event opened with a three-part story and a co-op minigame. Ayato describes the contest as his idea, run by three parties: merchants funding it, the Kamisato Clan lending the grounds, and the Grand Narukami Shrine advising. Each party picked one object to find, one per round. The Traveler is partnered with a friend each round, while Arataki Itto secretly tries to scare contestants for practice and Shikanoin Heizou investigates a "ghost". The ending is gentle: the ghost is a lonely youkai, the festival is held, and Chizuru is persuaded to stay and enjoy it.

Requirements were Adventure Rank 30 and the Archon Quest part "Ritou Escape Plan". Rewards included Primogems, a Crown of Insight, the event weapon Toukabou Shigure (Sword) and the furnishing Kimodameshi Vivaciousness, via a currency called Courage Test Tickets. The gameplay modes were Leisurely Pastime (also playable in co-op) and the harder solo Shatterdark.

Plot: Part II, "Haunted Tales": Heizou asks them to keep quiet about what they saw, because he is investigating for a client left stranded on the beach. Round two's partners are Yoimiya, Sayu or Thoma. Itto then finds three small youkai, Youko, Kappa and Hitotsume Kozou, who explain that they are trying to hold a Mikawa Flower Festival. They built the Akitsu Yuugei game on the beach using nearly all their youkai power, inspired by a legend of the youkai Kamai Kenji and a human samurai. When the pair play Akitsu Yuugei with the veiled woman, her wish as winner is that they never cross paths again. The youkai say she is not one of them.

Part III, "The Currents of Life": the shrine maiden is missing when the third round is due, so Heizou becomes the Traveler's partner and investigates. The clues (a torn piece of black shade cloth, a smoke-blackened ball that smelled of fireworks, sleeping powder in the stones) suggest the "ghost" used props. Heizou concludes that she is a youkai born from an object, who is strong near her original body and weak away from it.

At the beach the woman gives her name as Hanyuuda Chizuru. She hid there waiting to fade, and was woken when the youkai built Akitsu Yuugei. She frightened visitors away so that the young youkai would not repeat the grief she watched in the Kamai and samurai story, and she trapped the thief who wanted the game's decorations. Heizou deduces her true form: the pair of hagoita once used by Kamai and the samurai. Yae Miko, who with the shrine maiden had arranged the vanished staff and the third object, reveals more of the story and Chizuru decides to attend. Itto announces he will organise the festival, and the finale is a festival on the beach with food stalls and a yo-yo fishing game.

Details of the contest: Dango Milk was supplied by a man named Tomoki and chosen by the funders; the second object was a fan chosen by the Yashiro Commission side; the hagoita was the Grand Narukami Shrine's pick, which Heizou works out is why Miko arranged things as she did. Ayato remarks in passing that the Traveler's help might yet be needed, but the quest does not say what he expected. In the festival scene Itto, Gorou, Yoimiya, Thoma, Ayaka, Sayu and Chizuru appear in small optional conversations.

Revelations: The "ghost" is Hanyuuda Chizuru, a youkai who grew from a pair of hagoita used by Kamai Kenji and a human samurai. She had watched their friendship end in regret and wanted to protect other youkai from the same grief. Yae Miko answers her by giving the rest of the tale: the samurai was Yanagibashi Takuto, founder of the Souran Isshin Art, which he developed while dueling Kamai; and five hundred years ago Kamai fought alongside Tominaga Masanari, third heir of that art, who carried a sword handed down from Takuto. Miko presents this as the resolution of Kamai's regret: friendships continue in new forms.

Ei, speaking in the Kazuha partner branch, recalls that Akitsu Hazura (the hagoita game) was loved by Makoto, that Hyakkiyakou once held the Mikawa Flower Festival, and that she and Makoto once attended. The youkai's version of the game is called Akitsu Yuugei because the original game was lost to time and they rebuilt it from a merchant's description.

Characters: Ayato proposed and watches over the event but leaves details to retainers. Itto, leader of the Arataki Gang, wants the contest to be fun for his gang and is scared by real ghosts. Heizou investigates, calmly and quickly. Yae Miko orchestrates the final round. Hanyuuda Chizuru is a kind, guarded hagoita spirit. Youko, Kappa and Hitotsume Kozou are small, eager youkai. Round partners (Ayaka, Gorou, Kazuha, Yoimiya, Sayu, Thoma) each get a short personal scene. Ei appears in the first round to comment on the games, not to scare.

Consequences: The unmasked ghost story ends with a festival held on the beach, organised by Itto with the youkai and the Yashiro Commission, and Chizuru joining it. Heizou goes to tell his client that "intent to steal" is a minor offence but cannot go unpunished. The wiki lists the event as part of the Mikawa Flower Festival event series.

Placement: Released in Version 3.3. The event required the Ritou Escape Plan part of the Inazuma Archon Quest; players who had not done Arataki Itto's story quest Act I could enter through a Quick Start. Release order and story order are the same; no other quest requires it.

81.content: Hanyuuda Chizuru is the name taken by the youkai in Akitsu Kimodameshi who haunts a beach near Chinju Forest. Her true body is a pair of hagoita once used by the youkai Kamai Kenji and a samurai, which have started to rot after hundreds of years. She can use youkai power near her body and little away from it, and frightens people with props such as shade cloth, fireworks and sleeping powder. She decides to attend the festival at the end.

82.comment: Akitsu Kimodameshi: Kamai Kenji and Yanagibashi Takuto
82.content: In the legend told in Akitsu Kimodameshi, the youkai Kamai Kenji welcomes a human samurai, Yanagibashi Takuto, to the Mikawa Flower Festival and proposes a duel every ten years. They became close friends over decades of drinking, travel and sparring; at their final meeting the samurai was sixty-five and too frail to finish a last game of Akitsu Hazura. Yae Miko later names Takuto as founder of the Souran Isshin Art.

83.content: Akitsu Yuugei is the brick-breaking minigame at the heart of Akitsu Kimodameshi. The player controls a bar to bounce a Skill-Ball into bricks, with elemental reactions giving special effects. In the story it was built by Youko, Kappa and Hitotsume Kozou as a symbol of friendship based on the lost game Akitsu Hazura (Haneasobi), a festival game played with hagoita.

84.comment: Akitsu Kimodameshi: Test of Courage rounds
84.content: The event's contest has three rounds, each a search in Chinju Forest for an item chosen by one organiser: Dango Milk, a fan, and a pair of hagoita. Contestants play in pairs; leaving early forfeits prizes; winning all three earns the Grand Narukami Shrine's grand prize.

85.content:
Alatus Chapter (also: Butterfly's Dream, Xiao's Story Quest, Alatus Chapter Act I): Alatus Chapter is Xiao's Story Quest, with one act, Butterfly's Dream. Near Wangshu Inn the Traveler and Paimon meet a masked man calling himself the adeptus Starsnatcher, who sells wishes for Mora. His sigil is attracting malevolent hilichurls, and Xiao, the last of the Yakshas, is the one quietly cleansing them.

The quest unlocks after Of the Land Amidst Monoliths at Adventure Rank 40. It is a light, mostly comic story that doubles as a short look at Xiao's karmic burden and at the memory of the Yakshas, ending in a small act of remembrance.

Plot: Outside Wangshu Inn the Traveler fights hilichurls radiating evil. A masked man, Starsnatcher, claims to be an adeptus and to grant wishes for faith, meaning Mora. A book at Wanwen Bookhouse about the Yakshas makes the Traveler and Paimon suspect he is a fraud. Following the evil aura, they find Xiao, who explains the trouble comes from his karma and lets them help cleanse a cavern. They then use an adeptal ritual to confront Starsnatcher, who turns out to be an ordinary man.

Starsnatcher's Sigil of Permission is the real reason the demons gather. Xiao asks the Traveler to take it from him without violence, using the adeptal art Dream Trawler. The ritual needs a censer, lamps and cold items, gathered from a shrine near the southern road of Mt. Tianheng and with Mist Flowers. At the shrine the Traveler meets Pervases, a junior student of the Yakshas. Starsnatcher turns out to be a fan of Xiao, repents, and leaves a letter, the sigil and returned money. Xiao orders a dish in memory of an old friend.

**The Master of Stars' Deception.** Two evil hilichurls near Wangshu Inn are killed by the Traveler, and a masked man drives off another pair while four followers stand by. He gives his name as Starsnatcher and asks what the Traveler wishes. The followers say he performs miracles but charges Mora. The Traveler says they are searching for a lost sibling, and he agrees to help if shown faith; the Traveler offers a tasty dish instead of Mora, and Paimon proposes checking Wanwen Bookhouse for a new cookbook.

**Glimmers of the Vigilant Yaksha.** At the bookhouse the pair see Starsnatcher buy the book Yakshas: The Guardian Adepti. Reading a copy, they learn that Rex Lapis appointed adepti as Yakshas to destroy demons formed from the wrath of dead gods, that the brutality wore on them, and that only one remained, the Conqueror of Demons, whom they recognise as Xiao. Back near the inn, Starsnatcher's group is menaced by more hilichurls; his Sigil of Permission fails to drive them off, and the Traveler defeats them. Paimon no longer believes him and has the Traveler follow the evil aura using Elemental Sight.

**The Purging of Evil.** The trail ends at Xiao, standing over three dead hilichurls. He admits that the evil gathering there is a consequence of his own karma, and dismisses the book as fan fiction that his fallen comrades would find insulting to cry over. He goes to cleanse a nearby cavern with the Bane of All Evil and reluctantly accepts the Traveler and Paimon as companions. Afterwards Paimon tells him about Starsnatcher; he does not know the name, is disgusted at the wish-granting, and is alarmed to learn of the sigil, which he realises is what has been gathering the demons. To confiscate it without violence he recalls the Dream Trawler, normally used to separate a soul from the body but able to call the spirits of others.

**Insights of Drifting Dreams.** At the shrine near Mt. Tianheng's southern road, its guardian Pervases appears in human form and then speaks through a statue. He explains he was the Yakshas' junior student and is using his Mortal Lingering art to see how Liyue fares on the anniversary of his death. Sensing Xiao's karmic burden on the Traveler and Paimon, he asks them to send regards to the Vigilant Yaksha and voices a last wish to taste Grilled Tiger Fish again. When the ritual is performed, Starsnatcher's spirit appears, thinking it a dream, is subdued, and begs the supposed adepti for mercy. When told that this is Xiao, he becomes a devoted admirer. He explains that his grandfather, a folklorist, told him tales of Xiao as a child. He found the sigil among his father's belongings, began dressing as an adeptus for fun and was later swayed by greed and attention. He swears never to act under falsehoods again.

**Aftermath at the inn.** Next day Verr Goldet tells the Traveler that Starsnatcher, who stayed under the name Wang Ping'an, has checked out leaving a sincere, apologetic letter. He has gone on a journey of self-reflection, returned the money taken from followers, and left trinkets and the sigil, feeling unworthy of it. The Traveler gives the sigil to Xiao, who surprises them by ordering Grilled Tiger Fish instead of Almond Tofu, in honour of Pervases. They leave him to eat in peace.

The tone is deliberately lighter than the Archon Quest: the demons are real and dangerous, but the antagonist is a repentant impostor, and the story resolves by trickery and talk rather than a boss fight. Xiao's reluctance to be accompanied, his bluntness toward Paimon's sympathy, and his private tribute to Pervases show how he handles grief, and the encounter with Pervases is the quest's only direct link to the living world of the Yakshas.

Revelations: - The demons around Wangshu Inn gathered because of Starsnatcher's Sigil of Permission, in addition to Xiao's own karmic burden.
- Starsnatcher was an impostor, a man named Wang Ping'an, who had inherited the sigil.
- Pervases, a junior student of the Yakshas, remains as a lingering presence at a shrine near Mt. Tianheng.

- The Dream Trawler can call the spirits of others, not only separate a soul from a body.
- Xiao calls the book Yakshas: The Guardian Adepti fan fiction, though Paimon finds it consistent with what he says about his karma.

Characters: Xiao (the Vigilant Yaksha), Paimon and the Traveler, plus Starsnatcher (Wang Ping'an), Pervases, and Verr Goldet at Wangshu Inn.

Starsnatcher's four followers appear as extras. Xiao is shown as solitary, blunt and weary, but willing to be helped.

Consequences: Wang Ping'an gives up wish-selling and returns what he took. Xiao regains the sigil and the demon gathering at Wangshu Inn ends. The Traveler gains a small personal glimpse of Xiao and the Yakshas.

Placement: Released in Version 1.3 as Xiao's Story Quest; requires Of the Land Amidst Monoliths (Chapter I, Act I) and Adventure Rank 40. It can be played at any point after that, independent of later story.

86.content: In Butterfly's Dream, Starsnatcher is a masked man near Wangshu Inn who passes himself off as an adeptus and sells wishes for Mora. He is really Wang Ping'an, a man who found a Sigil of Permission among his father's belongings and began cosplaying an adeptus out of fun before greed took over. After being confronted through a Dream Trawler ritual he repents, returns the money and sigil, and leaves on a journey of reflection.

87.comment: Alatus Chapter: Pervases and the Yakshas
87.content: Pervases appears in Butterfly's Dream as the guardian of a shrine near the southern road of Mt. Tianheng. He says he was the Yakshas' junior student, and uses his Mortal Lingering art to look in on Liyue on the anniversary of his death. His last wish is to taste Grilled Tiger Fish again, and Xiao later orders that dish in his memory.

key: Knights of Favonius potion shop event
88.content:
Alchemical Ascension (also: Alchemy and Business Operations, Knights of Favonius potion shop event): The Acting Grand Master, Jean, wanted the Knights to show ordinary people what alchemy could do and to learn how they responded. Lisa, in charge of the effort, opened a potion shop and enlisted the Traveler and Paimon. They grew herbs, brewed potions, priced them to the market and sold them, with supplies handled by the Knight Freda of the Logistics Company. Familiar characters dropped by with requests, Sucrose set alchemy exams, and the venture grew into a Teyvat-wide trade. It ends with Lisa and Jean thanking the Traveler.

The entry requirement was the Prologue Archon Quest Song of the Dragon and Freedom. The wiki recommends Masquerade of the Guilty and Eula's Story Quest Aphros Delos Chapter Act I first, for the best experience. The event is a management game with a light story attached.

Plot: Act I, Potions Most Potent: at Knights of Favonius headquarters Lisa explains the plan and recruits the Traveler and Paimon. At the ready-made shop they brew a first potion, sell the first batch and learn to watch market trends and cultivate herbs. Lisa introduces Freda, who says the Acting Grand Master ordered her to support the business. Act II, A Breakthrough in Craft: orders pile up, Paimon suggests Lisa hire more help, and Lisa and Freda propose improving brewing, cultivation and sales. Act III, International Markets: the Sumeru merchant Atefeh arrives and offers to sell the shop's potions across Teyvat if they become her regular supplier. They agree. Epilogue, A Job Well Done: once enough revenue is earned, Jean visits to thank everyone.

Beyond the acts, visitors arrive in sequence. Beidou and Eula appear together (they met at Dornman Port after a misunderstanding over an entry permit and then shared a drink); Diona and Venti look for cocktail ingredients for The Cat's Tail; Diluc arrives after Elzer of Dawn Winery briefed him on the shop's success; and Gorou and Kirara come on an errand, with Kirara advising Gorou as a consultant in exchange for his help promoting Komaniya Express. Sucrose arrives with alchemy exams at four levels named Nigredo Realm, Calx, Rubedo Imminent and Citrinitas Simulated.

In the epilogue Lisa says enough sales data has been collected for the Knights' research and invites the Traveler to keep running the shop if they like. Jean says she had already heard from other knights and wanted to thank the Traveler in person; she had worried Lisa, cooped up in the library, was bored and wanted to give her talents room. Lisa jokes about losing hair to stress and being due a vacation, and gives the Traveler a memento. Jean notes the public reaction was far better than expected and that potions could become a new revenue stream for Mondstadt. The epilogue triggers once revenue reaches 2,600,000 in cycles 24 to 29, or at the end of cycle 29. A merchant from Liyue named Deyou can be engaged through the Sales Expansion Contract; he says his trades keep losing money and he wants to prove himself to his father.

Revelations: Nothing in the event changes the wider story. Its new information is small: according to Sucrose, Jean's plan, discussed with Albedo, was not only to sell potions but to teach the public the principles and practice of alchemy, and public understanding of alchemical potions had grown as a result. Beidou and Eula hit it off after the Dornman Port misunderstanding.

Diluc tells the Traveler that Elzer only briefs him like this when he thinks the winery faces a real threat, and jokes that a business with full production and supply lines and orders from across Teyvat would be a rival in the wine trade. Business Correspondence letters from Kaeya, Candace, Lyney and Xingqiu also appear, though those characters do not appear in person.

Characters: Lisa leads the project and Jean sponsors it; Freda is the event-exclusive Logistics Company knight who supplies it; Atefeh (Sumeru) and Deyou (Liyue) are event-exclusive merchants; Sucrose sets alchemy exams. Potion-request visitors are Beidou and Eula, Diona and Venti, Diluc, and Gorou and Kirara. Paimon and the Traveler run the shop.

Freda is described as a knight who likes adventure, with brown hair, golden eyes and Knights of Favonius attire; she is excited to meet the heroes whose stories she has heard. Lisa calls the Traveler and Paimon her cuties and relies on them for the work. Gorou's visit shows that Watatsumi Island had no map of Mondstadt for him, so he had to scout on the job.

Consequences: The event leaves no lasting change to the main story. The Knights gain sales data for their alchemy research, Lisa says she is due a vacation, and Jean raises the possibility of potions as a new income source for Mondstadt. As gameplay rewards, the Traveler can earn the Polearm Dialogues of the Desert Sages and other items.

Placement: Released in Version 4.5 as a Flagship Event. Requirements were Adventure Rank 20 and the Prologue Act III Archon Quest. The wiki does not place the story on a timeline, so treat it as a light interlude with the Traveler and Paimon travelling together.

Gameplay: Game mechanics, not in-world fact. The event has three phases: Getting Started (from 14 March), Gaining Traction (from 16 March, after A Breakthrough in Craft) and Red Hot (from 18 March). Three systems drive it: Cultivating Ingredients, Concocting Potions and Selling Potions. The shop has fifteen Alchemy Levels, with upgrades such as cultivation area expansions and improved alchemy cauldrons bought from Freda. Operation Bonuses and shop decorations unlock later.

Rewards include 1,000 Primogems in total, a Crown of Insight and the Polearm Dialogues of the Desert Sages. The Artisans' Gift track pays out as revenue reaches thresholds from 50,000 to 2,000,000.

89.content:
During the Alchemical Ascension event the Knights of Favonius ran a public potion shop near Cider Lake, led by Lisa, to show off alchemical research and collect public feedback. The Traveler and Paimon operated it.

Freda of the Logistics Company supplied it; Sucrose later ran alchemy exams; Atefeh and Deyou distributed potions across Teyvat.

90.content: An event-exclusive Knight of Favonius from the Logistics Company who handled supplies for the potion shop. She says Jean ordered her to support the Traveler and Paimon, and she is excited to meet them.

91.content: Sucrose visits the shop to set four alchemy exams of rising difficulty. She tells the Traveler and Lisa that part of Jean's plan, discussed with Albedo, was to teach the public alchemy as well as sell potions.

92.content:
Alcyon Chapter (also: Linnea's Story Quest, Up! Toward Homecoming Wings, Spirit Envoy Championship): Linnea's Story Quest, set in Nod-Krai. The Traveler helps Linnea and her Jack Frost partner Lumi compete in the Spirit Envoy Championship, a tournament pairing people with animal companions. A rival, Celaeno, turns out to be Linnea's fae sister, and Linnea learns what kind of fae she is.

The chapter has one act, Up! Toward Homecoming Wings, made of three quests: The Championship Begins, Twice Upon a Gaze and Tread the Right Path. It was released in version 6.5 (Luna VI). The Traveler enters with Aguara, their former Tepetlisaur whelp companion, as the tournament partner.

Beneath the tournament, the story is about origins: why Lumi differs from other Jack Frosts, why Linnea has wings on her head, and whether a foreseen future can be changed. It also uses cameo competitors from other regions for lighter moments.

Plot: Katheryne mentions the Frostmoon Scions' Spirit Envoy Championship. The Traveler finds Linnea, who enters with Lumi. Over several rounds a mysterious fae, Celaeno, appears, Linnea faints and dreams, and she learns Celaeno is her sister. Celaeno explains their kind and Linnea's fate. In the semifinal Lumi grows huge and Linnea calms her. The Traveler wins the final.

The Championship Begins: at Nasha Town, Katheryne has no notable commissions but tells the Traveler and Paimon about the Spirit Envoy Championship, a Frostmoon Scions event meant to strengthen bonds between people and animals. It is normally closed to outsiders but this year has a large prize. The Traveler meets Linnea, an Adventurers' Guild advisor who lectures at Speranza, and her partner Lumi. Aguara asks to join. They sign up, meet Mualani and Itto with their own companions, and the draw begins.

Twice Upon a Gaze: over a meal at Speranza, Linnea tells the Traveler she thinks of it as home and reveals she is a changeling raised by humans, with wings on her head. She hopes to learn about Lumi's origins. During the tournament, Celaeno enters, her hat blows off to show she is fae, and Linnea faints after asking her questions. In a series of worsening dreams she sees Celaeno as her sister.

Tread the Right Path: confronted at the Flagship, Celaeno explains Augury Birds and the family history behind the swap. In the semifinal Lumi grows huge and is calmed by Linnea, who finds why Lumi differs. The Traveler wins the final and Celaeno bids farewell.

The Championship Begins: Katheryne explains that the rules were changed after a past entrant brought an extremely rare and powerful partner, so now only common animal species and their variants are allowed. Linnea is introduced teaching a class about food at Speranza and is delighted by Paimon. She tells the Traveler that Lumi was bullied for being different, and that she has tried ever since to learn what makes Lumi special. Mualani, who knows of Linnea from a visit to Natlan, and Itto, who brought pooled funds from his gang, arrive with their companions Mamala and Crimson Staff. In the first draw the Traveler faces Itto, and Linnea faces Ilze and her Floating Hydro Fungus Iku-Turso. Itto also sends Ushi against Aguara, which gets Aguara disqualified for using two companions. Linnea meanwhile wins, watched by someone with evident contempt.

Twice Upon a Gaze: Jurva cooks for them and says Linnea used to be the boss at Speranza before she grew up and left. Linnea says her parents are still alive and simply left the area, and that they supported her despite her unusual features. She remembers little of Lumi's earlier life, and of her own only a lullaby she believes was meant to discourage her from seeking her past; when she once travelled to the tundra, every instinct told her to leave. She is amazed at Aguara and Lumi being evenly matched, and bothered that she cannot predict their moves. Later the Traveler and Aguara beat Haniyyah and the Sumpter Beast Fluffy the Flower King, then Mualani in the quarter-finals. A new competitor, Celaeno, defeats Jahoda and her Chic Badger with her Radiant Bladehorn Haemus, and Linnea is shocked that a Radiant Beast is so docile. When Celaeno's hat is blown off, Linnea tries to question her; Celaeno walks away, finding the moment painful. Linnea faints and is carried to Lauma, who says she just needs rest. After waking she loses to Celaeno in the next match and, in a sequence of dreams, sees Celaeno ask her to return to the tundra one last time to say goodbye to their parents, explaining that what she dreams is actually the future. Aguara has picked up her scent and leads the group onward.

Tread the Right Path: at the Flagship, Linnea demands that Celaeno open the door. Celaeno warns that curiosity will lead to regret and tells her that Augury Birds are a rare kind of fae who foresee their own futures; fewer than five exist, counting both sisters. The Traveler recalls Vedrfolnir's words about an unchangeable fate. Their parents had Linnea live among humans, swapping her with a human child, so her abilities might be delayed. That child had a rare disease that only the fae could cure; her birth parents later came for her and they moved to Snezhnograd. Celaeno admits she first resented Linnea and had formed a bitter image of her, but changed her mind on seeing how much Linnea suffered not knowing. She also says she took in Haemus after it was separated from its parents. Linnea accepts her. In the semifinal the Traveler faces Viliana and her Snow Fox Gorynishche. Lumi grows huge while fighting Haemus, deflecting blades toward spectators whom the Traveler protects, until Linnea tugs her hat and shrinks her. Linnea realises Lumi differs because she consumes Geo, and hopes to find a Jack Frost with the same tastes. Celaeno sees her vision go blank at the moment Lumi's hammer falls and asks if Linnea defied fate. Linnea says a future being set does not mean she has to accept it. Before the final, the Little One, the Traveler's Saurian former companion, is seen watching from a cliff and has helped Aguara train, bringing Grainfruit. The Traveler wins and the quarter-finalists pose for photos; Celaeno wants to release Haemus into the wild. She promises to tell their parents how Linnea is doing and says her abilities will develop in time.

The cameo layer: Mualani finds Itto's group familiar until he mentions Kuki Shinobu, who had visited Natlan and the Flower-Feather Clan for their trials, where Chasca called her a natural. Itto serves for a time as a bouncer at the Flagship, scaring off a patron who demanded compensation from Paavo. Between rounds the Traveler, Linnea and the animals practise together, and the Traveler tells Linnea how they met Aguara; Linnea wishes to travel with Lumi one day, but not before she learns Lumi's past. Paimon suggests giving Aguara a title before the quarter-final. At the end, each finalist says something: the Traveler credits hard work and friendship, Celaeno wants to free Haemus, Linnea accepts whatever fate holds, and Viliana says she enjoyed her time in Nod-Krai. Celaeno tells Linnea to write if she wants to see her, and says she will give an address when she next comes to the tundra.

Revelations: Linnea is an Augury Bird, a rare fae who can foresee their own futures; she has an older sister, Celaeno.

Linnea was swapped with a human baby by her fae parents so her abilities would be delayed. Lumi differs from other Jack Frosts because she consumes Geo. All of this was revealed in 6.5.

Celaeno says fewer than five Augury Birds exist, counting herself and Linnea. The human child exchanged for Linnea had a rare disease that only the fae could cure, and was later reclaimed by her birth parents and taken to Snezhnograd. The Traveler's own question about fate echoes Vedrfolnir's earlier words.

Celaeno's vision of the semifinal ended where Lumi's hammer would have landed, which she takes as a possible sign that fate was defied; the quest does not state so for certain. The ending says Linnea's abilities are expected to develop fully later.

Characters: Linnea, the Traveler, Paimon, Lumi, Aguara and Celaeno.

Katheryne, Lauma, Jahoda, Jurva and Paavo (Speranza and the Flagship), Mualani and Itto (with Mamala and Crimson Staff), Ilze, Haniyyah, Viliana, Haemus and the Little One.

Kuki Shinobu and Chasca appear only in conversation. Vedrfolnir is referenced by the Traveler in discussing fate.

Consequences: Linnea learns her origin and reconciles with Celaeno, who promises to pass news to their parents and to give an address. Lumi's difference is explained.

The chapter leaves open what Linnea's coming abilities will mean and whether her fate can be changed. According to the wiki, Celaeno afterward appears as an open-world NPC at Snezhnograd (flagged there as needing verification).

Placement: Unlocked at Adventure Rank 40 after An Elegy for Faded Moonlight (Song of the Welkin Moon Act IV). The wiki says fully finishing the chapter also needs A Nocturne of the Far North (Act V). The event page recommends In the Footsteps of the Chosen of Dragons first. During the Luna VI event, players at Adventure Rank 28 who have finished A New Star Approaches could use a Quick Start. Released in Luna VI, 6.5, on 2026-04-08.

93.content: In version 6.5 the chapter was also a time-limited event, running from 2026-04-08 to 2026-04-28 (GMT+8), with extra rewards such as Primogems and materials for finishing it in that window. The story itself remains available.

94.content:
A tournament held by the Frostmoon Scions to improve human-animal bonds through training, with animals meant to cope with hardship and disasters. Traditionally closed to outsiders, it is open this time with a hefty prize. Entrants pair up with one companion animal; only common species and their variants are allowed, since a rare, powerful partner once entered. Using two companions gets a contestant disqualified.

Rounds shown include draws the day after sign-up, quarter-finals, semifinals and a final. Competitors include Itto, Mualani, Ilze, Haniyyah, Jahoda, Viliana, Celaeno, Linnea and the Traveler.

95.content: Per Celaeno, Augury Birds are a rare kind of Snowland Fae who foresee their own futures, and fewer than five exist. Celaeno says the foreseen future cannot be changed. Their parents had Linnea raised among humans to delay her powers.

96.content: Linnea's older sister, an Augury Bird from the Snezhnaya tundra. She competes with the Radiant Bladehorn Haemus and wears a hat that hides she is fae. She came to Nod-Krai resenting Linnea, but could not go through with it after seeing Linnea's distress.

97.content: Lumi is a Jack Frost fae from the northern tundra who was bullied for being different. In the semifinal Linnea understands that Lumi's difference is that she consumes Geo, and she hopes to find a Jack Frost with the same taste.

98.content:
All Fires Fuel the Flame (also: Chapter V Interlude, For the Same Land): All Fires Fuel the Flame is the Interlude Act of the Natlan chapter, a quiet aftermath story set after the Abyssal invasion. The Traveler and Paimon help Iansan treat three Flower-Feather Clan warriors who were broken by the fighting, and Capitano appears with medicine and a few grim admissions about Ronova.

The act has a single quest, "For the Same Land". It sits between The Rainbow Destined to Burn and Incandescent Ode of Resurrection, requires Adventure Rank 40, and is about recovery rather than battle: the cures for Abyssal Corrosion Syndrome, the unlikely help of Capitano, and the tribes gathering to forge the Traveler's Ancient Name.

The act also shows tribes cooperating beyond their rivalries (Iansan of the Collective of Plenty working in another tribe's territory) and explains where the Natlan cure for Abyssal sickness came from: a military doctor of Capitano's platoon.

Plot: After the invasion, Paimon suggests visiting the hard-hit Flower-Feather Clan. Iansan and Collective of Plenty volunteers are already there. Chief Mutota explains that warriors Atoco, Cochitta and Ocotlan were found in the wilderness traumatised after meeting Gosoythoth, the Abyssal rift called the Reaper of the Abyss. A treatment existed hundreds of years ago but its knowledge has been lost, and the Traveler's attempt to purify the corruption does nothing.

The three are treated one at a time. Atoco is brought round when the Traveler takes the form of his dead saurian companion Duarte and then jolts him back to his senses, after which Iansan tells him to accept the loss. Cochitta is persuaded to keep fighting after her young brother Cuallee turns up, and she kills a few stray riftwolves to regain her confidence. Ocotlan is the severe case: he sees the tribe as monsters, attacks his father Munay, and is only cured when Capitano arrives, names the condition as Abyssal Corrosion Syndrome and supplies the Draught of Lucidity. Afterwards the Traveler is summoned to the Stadium of Sacred Flame, where Xilonen, with the other tribes' champions, begins work on the Traveler's Ancient Name.

Detail: the Traveler and Iansan first move the afflicted to calmer settings under watch. Around Atoco's bonfire they learn the name Duarte; Izcalli says Duarte died four years earlier in an Abyssal attack, so the Traveler takes the form of a Qucusaurus. The ruse works until Atoco grows suspicious and the Traveler jolts him back to himself.

Mutota tells the Traveler that Cochitta's parents died fighting the Abyss, that she became a warrior after shielding her younger brother from a monster, and that the tribe celebrated her prowess until the invasion. Cuallee arrives with a toy weapon asking where the monster is. Mutota says some riftwolves fled north; a pack of three is found and Cochitta kills them with help. Ohtli and Itotia are heard praising the Traveler afterwards.

For Ocotlan, Capitano explains that mild cases can be cured by words or contact but a deeply entrenched hallucination needs the Draught, which leaves the patient with lasting migraines. Munay consents. Ocotlan recovers and says he had a vision of the tribe overrun. Capitano leaves extra medicine for other warriors.

At the Stadium, Mualani, Kinich, Ajaw, Kachina, Citlali and Ororon wait (Ajaw is flung aside by Kinich), and Chasca arrives, having heard that the Traveler helped her tribe. Xilonen is pleased at the turnout. The Traveler's deeds are to be told to the Pilgrim's Chronicle while the Traveler waits elsewhere; she also calls in Paimon, who is counted as a companion though not from Natlan. Paimon proves to have much to share. Xilonen returns the chronicle and says she will need it to forge the Ancient Name, after which the war may be ended.

Revelations: Capitano says he fled Khaenri'ah to Natlan with his platoon, saw the tribes fighting the Abyss, respected their resolve and sees a common enemy. The medicine was developed by Guthred, his second-in-command and a military doctor, who tested it on himself after several soldiers tried to kill each other and died soon after finishing it. Capitano says his goals do not match the Traveler's, that the souls of the land are not at peace, and that his work is not finished.

The Traveler asks about Mavuika's use of Ronova's power, which would mean she is marked for death. Capitano says Ronova caused his and his people's suffering, removes his mask and shows his true face, which shocks Paimon and the Traveler. He says the Ruler of Death can interpret the form of death or grant immortality as she wishes, and that before the final moment comes they must fight harder than ever.

Characters: Traveler and Paimon; Iansan (Collective of Plenty, the act's guide and caregiver); Mutota (chief of the Flower-Feather Clan); Capitano; Xilonen and the gathered Natlan champions. Minor named figures are the warriors Atoco, Cochitta and Ocotlan, Cochitta's brother Cuallee, Munay, Izcalli, Ohtli, Itotia, and the late saurian Duarte.

Consequences: Three warriors are restored, the Draught of Lucidity is available again with stock left for other fighters, and the Ancient Name project moves forward. Capitano emerges as an ally of convenience, not a friend. The next act, Incandescent Ode of Resurrection, follows.

Placement: Story order and release order match: The Rainbow Destined to Burn (Act IV), then this Interlude (5.2), then Incandescent Ode of Resurrection (Act V). It is a Chapter V quest set in Natlan.

99.comment: All Fires Fuel the Flame: Draught of Lucidity
99.content: A strong medicine for severe Abyssal Corrosion Syndrome, developed by Guthred, Capitano's second-in-command and military doctor. Capitano says it is only for the worst cases because the patient suffers chronic migraines afterwards. Ocotlan of the Flower-Feather Clan is given it in "All Fires Fuel the Flame".

100.comment: All Fires Fuel the Flame: Atoco, Cochitta and Ocotlan
100.content: Three Flower-Feather Clan warriors found traumatised after Gosoythoth's appearance in the Abyssal invasion. Atoco grieves the saurian Duarte; Cochitta, a renowned fighter whose confidence collapsed in the invasion, is rallied by her younger brother Cuallee; Ocotlan sees the tribe as monsters and is the severe case. All three recover during the act.

key: Song of the Welkin Moon Act IV
101.content:
An Elegy for Faded Moonlight (also: Song of the Welkin Moon Act IV): Act IV of Song of the Welkin Moon. Dainsleif and Albedo, with Durin, join the Nod-Krai allies. In a ritual the group views Rerir's past as a Khaenri'ahn Sinner. Rerir turns on Nefer, and in the final fight Columbina, helped by an alchemical array and Dainsleif, throws him through a moon gate out of Teyvat.

The act has three quests: All Is Foretold, Dance of Death: Serpent and Scorpion and Echoes of Fate. It follows A Nation That Doesn't Exist and precedes A Nocturne of the Far North. It was released in version 6.1 (Luna II).

The act is the resolution of the Rerir thread begun in Elegy of Dust and Lamplight. It also gives Nefer's backstory in a domain the group is pulled into and ends with a quiet conversation about the Lord-Artificer.

Plot: At the allies' secret base the Traveler reunites with Flins, who met Albedo and a young man introduced as Mini Durin. Varka brings Dainsleif. The group enters Rerir's past at the Curatorium, then is pulled into a desert domain where Rerir attacks Nefer. Afterwards the group prepares and fights him, and Columbina flicks him into a moon gate held by Dainsleif.

The allies gather and Dainsleif joins them. A ritual at the Curatorium shows Rerir's past with King Irmin and Tholindis, then drags the group into a desert domain showing Nefer's past, where Rerir attacks her. In the final fight Columbina, with Albedo and Durin's array and Dainsleif's help, throws Rerir out of Teyvat.

All Is Foretold: the Traveler arrives with Columbina and finds Flins in good spirits. Arlecchino appears only to accompany her friend and leaves to speak with Sandrone at the Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau. Varka introduces Dainsleif, whom Paimon describes as a Khaenri'ahn noble. Nefer, suspicious of a Khaenri'ahn who should not still be alive, joins them. Dainsleif asks for help investigating Rerir's past and explains how the Five Sinners came to be. The Traveler reports on Columbina and Arlecchino, and Columbina says that all three Moon Marrows in hand are still not enough to overpower Rerir. At the Curatorium Nefer says Dainsleif trusted the Traveler's group to keep the matter secret. With Jahoda and Lauma, they enter Rerir's past. Rerir carried out tasks for King Irmin until ordered to kill his own fiancee Tholindis. His next target, Frithr, was spared because Rerir had grown disillusioned. Dainsleif then asked him to help free his brother Vedrfolnir, imprisoned by Irmin for a bad prophecy, with Surtalogi, Rhinedottir and Hroptatyr. Vedrfolnir said he had not known the prophecy, though both had heard the same voice, and told Rerir to go to the Universitas Magistrorum, where Tholindis was in danger. He found her before a portal. She had learned the truth and fell in so he could live an ordinary life. Rerir, in despair, accepted the voice's offer of power in hope of reuniting with her.

Dance of Death: Serpent and Scorpion: the ritual seems to succeed, but Nefer finds the group in a desert. The domain shows her past: raised as an adopted child by Sinuhe, leader of the Shimti tribe, who unintentionally doomed it by taking water from a well of the Iab tribe. Later she went to Aaru Village, where Uncle Anpu arranged for the Sumeru Akademiya to invite her, but the Akademiya had not acknowledged her adoptive father's letter. She left for revenge on the tribes that killed her family. They reach a temple of Thoth, one of King Deshret's Seven Pillars. Ashru becomes an abyssal creature and grabs Nefer by the throat, and Rerir says she has seen too much. An attack from above interrupts him and the group is teleported out. Back in reality Nefer's chessbox shakes and she binds it with Dendro restraints.

Echoes of Fate: with Rerir restrained, the group prepares. When the seal breaks, Rerir expels Lauma, Aino and Flins and turns on Nefer. Albedo and Durin set up an alchemical array to siphon his power into Columbina, who overpowers him and opens a moon gate. Rerir believes she cannot hold both him and the gate, and she says someone else does. He sees Dainsleif keeping it open, and is flicked out of Teyvat. Nefer is temporarily blinded by the fight, and Lauma takes her for treatment. The following day the group celebrates at the Flagship. The Traveler then visits Columbina and Sandrone at the bureau, where a slightly peeved Sandrone gives them tea and a notebook to use as a coaster, then mentions the Lord-Artificer, Alain Guillotin, and asks the Traveler's opinion of his actions before saying they may do as they like and starting maintenance on Pulonia.

Rerir's tasks for Irmin are shown as a sequence ending with the order against Tholindis, after which he became disillusioned with Irmin's directives. The wiki summary says Nefer goaded Rerir into using his full power, which cost her sight for a time.

The act pairs two flashbacks, Rerir's and Nefer's, as parallel stories of loss and vengeance, and then closes with Sandrone raising the Lord-Artificer's past with the Traveler.

Revelations: Rerir's tragedy: he lost his fiancee Tholindis and accepted power from a voice. Rerir himself is cast out of Teyvat.

Dainsleif explains how the Five Sinners came to be; the free-Vedrfolnir operation involved Dainsleif, Surtalogi, Rhinedottir and Hroptatyr alongside Rerir. Vedrfolnir and Rerir heard the same voice. Nefer's past as an Eremite is shown.

Dainsleif is shown keeping the moon gate open and Nefer is suspicious of him, wondering how a Khaenri'ahn is still alive.

Characters: The Traveler, Paimon, Columbina, Dainsleif, Nefer, Flins and Rerir are the main figures.

Allies: Albedo, Durin (introduced as Mini Durin from Simulanka), Varka, Lauma, Aino, Jahoda, Arlecchino and Sandrone. Characters seen in Rerir's past include Irmin, Tholindis, Frithr, Vedrfolnir, Surtalogi, Rhinedottir and Hroptatyr; in Nefer's domain, Sinuhe, Uncle Anpu, Thoth and Ashru.

Consequences: Rerir is banished from Teyvat. Nefer is blinded for a time. The Traveler leaves the final conversation with Sandrone with the question of the Lord-Artificer's legacy unresolved, and the story continues in A Nocturne of the Far North.

Placement: Song of the Welkin Moon Act IV, after A Nation That Doesn't Exist and before A Nocturne of the Far North. Released with Luna II (6.1, 2025-10-22).

102.comment: An Elegy for Faded Moonlight: Rerir's past
102.content: In the shared ritual the group sees Rerir serve King Irmin, be ordered to kill his fiancee Tholindis, spare his next target Frithr, and help Dainsleif free Vedrfolnir. Tholindis falls into a portal to let him live a normal life, and Rerir then accepts a voice's offer of power.

103.comment: An Elegy for Faded Moonlight: Nefer's desert domain
103.content: In a domain born of the ritual, Nefer's past appears. She was raised by Sinuhe of the Shimti tribe, who unintentionally caused the tribe's destruction by the Iab tribe. After the Akademiya failed to answer her adoptive father's letter, she left it to avenge her family.

104.comment: An Elegy for Faded Moonlight: Moon gate banishment
104.content: Albedo and Durin build an alchemical array to funnel Rerir's power into Columbina, who opens a moon gate and flicks him into it. Dainsleif holds the gate open and Rerir is thrown out of Teyvat.

key: An Unwavering Culinary Dream World Quest series
105.content:
An Unwavering Culinary Dream (also: An Unwavering Culinary Dream World Quest series, Aranara cooking training, A Delicacy for Nara, Arapacati's four brothers): The series is five quests: the opener, Cooking, the Flavor of Nature (which finds Arachatora), then three that can be done in any order, Cooking, a Pleasant Memory (Arasaka), Cooking, the Aroma of Homecoming (Arapas) and Cooking, the Beauty of Sharing (Araphala), and finally A Delicacy for Nara. The tone is comic and tender: Aranara do not understand human tastes, so every Supreme Delicacy is a mild failure by human standards, but each one carries a memory of a golden Nara who once befriended them.

Underneath the jokes the series explains why the Aranara cook at all. The Golden Nara they call Nara Varuna taught them how humans eat and what a "brother" or "sister" is, and the four cooks are practising so that Nara can again enjoy a meal in Vanarana. The series also gives the Aranara's view of time (moons, seedlings, hibernation), of The Withering ("Marana") and of salt.

Plot: An Unwavering Culinary Dream. In Vanarana, Arapacati is nervous around the tall Golden Nara but trusts Arama, who vouches for the Traveler. She is upset: her big brothers have not come back, and the family cannot celebrate Festival Utsava without them. Paimon mistakes "missing" for a kind of seed, until Arapacati makes clear she knows where they are: they left for cooking training long ago. The four made so much smoke in Vanarana that she sent them away, scaring the other Aranara so much that some hibernated. She tells the Traveler to follow the rising pillars of smoke and, if a brother is acting strangely, to splash him with Dendro, since Aranara recover their senses from Dendro after touching strange mushrooms.

Cooking, the Flavor of Nature. Near Vissudha Field the Traveler heals a whimpering Arachatora with Dendro. He ate a strange mushroom because the Head Mushroom he meant to cook was in an area taken over by a Withering zone. He is certain mushroom dishes are the best food and wants to prove it to his brothers. The Traveler defeats two Ruin Sentinels, lowers the water in a cave, purifies the Withering zone and picks the Head Mushroom. Arachatora cooks it: the result is tasteless, tough and hard to chew, which baffles him because an earlier Nara visitor praised his cooking. He gives the Traveler the recipe for Mushroom Hodgepodge and says where the others are: near Gandharva Ville, Apam Woods and Devantaka Mountain.

Cooking, a Pleasant Memory. Arasaka is a timid cook who tends Zaytun Peaches near Avidya Forest and panics around tall Nara. His Supreme Delicacy needs the "taste of happiness", which he describes as white, crumbling like sand, and kept in a "hard bubble". He is too frightened of the crowds in Gandharva Ville to fetch it, and says a Nara with a bulge on his back had gone there. The Traveler finds the merchant Iaanesh, who laughs at the description and identifies it as sugar in a glass bottle. Arasaka tastes it and finds it is not as happy as the first time, then decides it must be shared with friends. He cooks peaches with sugar for the Traveler and Paimon, and the result is overwhelmingly sweet. He teaches them Selva Salad.

Cooking, the Aroma of Homecoming. Near Apam Woods the Traveler follows the smell of soup. Paimon drinks the unattended pot and tastes nothing; Arapas appears from underground, furious. He has been testing water from across Apam Woods and found a "Living Spring" that is the best, but the "Apshvaana" that live at its source bite. They turn out to be crocodiles. The Traveler fetches a new pot, and Arapas makes a plain, aromatic soup, rejects the idea of salt (land with salt is land without life, he says, and Aranara would shrink back into seeds) and repeats what a Nara visitor told him, that a soup needs only aroma. Persuaded that Araja and Arapacati approve of the Traveler, he promises to try a soup with taste and teaches the Masala Cheese Balls recipe.

Cooking, the Beauty of Sharing. At a camp near Devantaka Mountain the Traveler follows a trail of dropped Sunsettias to a cave, where Araphala is asleep. After Dendro wakes him, he panics (his sister warned that a bad Nara would make porridge of a sleeper). He explains Aranara hibernation: in grave danger they compress their memories and dreams into a seed that regrows when it is safe. He came to this place long ago with a golden Nara friend to gather the Unrivaled Fresh Fruits and has gathered fruit here ever since, hoping to eat it with them. A huge monster with Marana's aura, five Araphalas tall, appeared and he hid. The Traveler defeats the Ruin Drake. Araphala shares the fruit uncooked: for him finding better ingredients is the cooking, and travelling through the forest is the true training.

A Delicacy for Nara. Back in Vanarana, Arapacati scolds all four brothers: the forest is dangerous because of Marana, they quarrelled right after leaving, and each wandered somewhere risky. Arachatora may not pick mushrooms until Sunsettias have ripened ten times. Araphala and Arapas are told off for going far from Vanarana, and Arasaka for needing someone else's help to complete his training. Then she thanks the Traveler and explains why she and the others call each other siblings: Nara Varuna spoke about a sibling, said the Aranara should cherish family, and said sharing food is a happy thing. Arapacati asks the Traveler to join Festival Utsava and cook food only Nara can understand. The quest ends there.

Order. The first quest points to smoke pillars. Once Cooking, the Flavor of Nature is done the next three open together and can be completed in any order, and A Delicacy for Nara needs all three. Each cook's last line is some version of "now I only have to let them taste this". After the series each brother has a short line reflecting on his scolding: Arachatora dreads waiting for Sunsettias, Arapas wants to try cooking with Vanarana's water, Araphala hopes Arapacati calms down after some fruit, and Arasaka wonders how the taste of happiness could bring bitterness.

Dialogue details. Arachatora tells Paimon that when he ate bad mushrooms before, the Nilotpala Lotuses bloomed and closed twice before he recovered, and he does not know whether two days is long or short. He calls Arapacati his "younger sister" although they are not related. He says the Traveler can fight Marana because the Traveler could heal him with the power of Lesser Lord Kusanali. Araphala's leaf journal reads like a diary of seasons, while Arapas's leaf notes count frosts and record which water was "not acceptable". Iaanesh, a merchant whose family trades gems from Liyue for spices and travels between the Chasm and Sumeru, was left by his father in Gandharva Ville as a child and cannot now recall the friend he made there.

Revelations: - The four Aranara cooks are not related. Arapacati and the others adopted the words "brother" and "sister" after Nara Varuna spoke of a sibling with a mix of happiness and sadness.
- Aranara can fall into a stupor or fear after touching strange mushrooms, and recover through Dendro.
- Aranara hibernate when in grave danger, compressing memories and dreams into a seed that can regrow into an Aranara once it is safe.
- Nara Varuna taught the Aranara how humans eat, and sharing food is the reason the Aranara began cooking training.

- The Aranara treat Marana's spread as the great danger of the forest, and Araja warned them especially about faraway places.
- Aranara fear fire, because forest fires can raze entire forests, but the cooks train themselves to control flames.
- The Aranara measure time by moons, trees and seedlings, not days.

Characters: - **Arapacati**: the little sister of the group, fearful of tall Nara at first but in charge of the family. She sends the Traveler, gets angry when the brothers argue, and invites the Traveler to Festival Utsava.
- **Arama**: an Aranara of Vanarana who vouches for the Traveler and helps explain things to Arapacati.
- **Arachatora**: the mushroom cook. Gentle and formal, sure that the Head Mushroom is the best ingredient.
- **Arasaka**: the sugar cook. Anxious and prone to panic; believes in a "taste of happiness" tied to a friend.
- **Arapas**: the water and soup cook. Proud and short-tempered, with a firm view that soup needs only good water and aroma.
- **Araphala**: the fruit cook. Sleepy and easily frightened, but content that finding ingredients is cooking.
- **Iaanesh**: a merchant in Gandharva Ville who identifies sugar.
- **Paimon** and the Traveler, who taste each dish; Paimon says they are too plain or too sweet.

Nara Varuna never appears. Several cooks mention a Nara visitor who praised their food (Arachatora's mushroom, Arapas's soup) or shared a fruit trip (Araphala), and Arapacati identifies the one who taught them about family as Nara Varuna, the same golden Nara the Aranara remember in Varuna Gatha.

Consequences: All four brothers return to Vanarana before Festival Utsava, are scolded, and promise to do better. The Traveler receives recipes (Mushroom Hodgepodge, Selva Salad and Masala Cheese Balls), and Arapacati asks them to cook at the festival. The Aranara's idea of cooking changes a little: Arapas says he will try adding taste, and Arasaka learns that happiness depends on who you eat with.

Gameplay note, labelled as such: A Delicacy for Nara gives a Sumeru reputation reward of 20, and the series gives Primogems and other rewards.

Placement: Released in version 3.0 with Sumeru. It requires The World of Aranara, which sets up the Aranara and Vanarana. Story-wise it occurs while the Aranara are preparing for Festival Utsava, in the period around Varuna Gatha, but the quests do not give an exact order.

106.comment: An Unwavering Culinary Dream: Arapacati and her four brothers
106.content: Arapacati is an Aranara of Vanarana who calls Arachatora, Arasaka, Arapas and Araphala her big brothers. They are not related by blood or age, and she explains that the family bond is a choice inspired by Nara Varuna. The brothers went off for "cooking training" so they could make a Supreme Delicacy for Nara at Festival Utsava, but they never knew when to come home. Arachatora cooks mushrooms and is gentle and formal. Arasaka cooks with sweetness and is timid. Arapas cooks soups and insists on good water. Araphala loves fresh fruit and sleeps a lot. See the quest An Unwavering Culinary Dream for what happened to each.

107.comment: An Unwavering Culinary Dream: Head Mushroom
107.content: The Head Mushroom is the ingredient Arachatora has been watching grow in a cave near Vissudha Field. It is somewhat larger than a normal Shroom-Kin, and its habitat was taken over by a Withering zone. It must be freed from the zone before it can be picked. Cooked, it is tasteless and tough for the Traveler and Paimon, though very fragrant. Arachatora rewards the Traveler with the recipe for Mushroom Hodgepodge.

108.comment: An Unwavering Culinary Dream: The taste of happiness
108.content:
Arasaka's "taste of happiness" is sugar, which he first tried with a Nara friend near Gandharva Ville. He cannot name sugar and describes it as white, crumbling like sand, in a hard bubble. The merchant Iaanesh recognises it from this description and gives a bottle as a gift. Arasaka concludes that the taste is happier when shared with friends and teaches the Traveler Selva Salad.

Iaanesh remembers being left in Gandharva Ville as a child and making a friend who exclaimed over sugar in much the same way, though he can no longer remember the friend. The series never states that this friend is Arasaka's friend; that is left to the player to infer.

109.comment: An Unwavering Culinary Dream: Living Spring and the Apshvaana
109.content: Arapas insists soup needs the best water and has tested water throughout Apam Woods. His favourite is the cold, clean Living Spring at a river's source, guarded by "Apshvaana", which turn out to be crocodiles. He believes a soup should only smell good: salt would kill land and force Aranara back into seeds. The Traveler's first plain soup is aromatic but tasteless. He agrees to try adding flavour and teaches the Masala Cheese Balls recipe.

110.comment: An Unwavering Culinary Dream: Araphala and Aranara hibernation
110.content: Araphala is found asleep in a cave near Devantaka Mountain. He explains that Aranara hibernate in grave danger by compressing memories and dreams into a seed that can regrow when it is safe. He was hiding from a huge Marana-tainted monster (a Ruin Drake that the Traveler defeats). He believes finding the best ingredients, such as Unrivaled Fresh Fruit from strong trees, is the real cooking training.

111.comment: An Unwavering Culinary Dream: Nara Varuna in the cooking quests
111.content: In this series the Golden Nara called Nara Varuna is the one who taught the Aranara how Nara eat and what siblings are. The Aranara note that Nara Varuna looked happy and sad when speaking of a sibling, and ask the Traveler (also a Golden Nara) to share food with them in turn. Reading Nara Varuna as the Traveler's lost sibling is supported by the wider Aranara storyline, not stated in these quests.

key: A Brush of Seafoam and Crimson
A Gradient of Dreams and Ochre
Blue Longing of Heart and Moon
112.content:
Ancient Colors (also: Seymour's Story: Prologue, A Brush of Seafoam and Crimson, A Gradient of Dreams and Ochre, Blue Longing of Heart and Moon): Ancient Colors is a three-act Fontaine World Quest series added in version 4.0, listed in the Fontaine Reputation menu as "Seymour's Story: Prologue". The Traveler meets Mamere, a Melusine who paints, and her talking machine friend Seymour, helps repair him, and then discovers that a man named Jakob is trying to revive the buried heart of Mamere's "Father" beneath Merusea Village.

The acts are "A Brush of Seafoam and Crimson" (The Illusion's Finishings), "A Gradient of Dreams and Ochre" (There Will Come Soft Rains) and "Blue Longing of Heart and Moon" (Limner, Dreamer, and Robotic Dog). It has no listed prerequisite, begins near the Statue of the Seven at Elynas, and leads on to In the Wake of Narcissus by way of Initial Facts.

The tone stays gentle in the first two acts, with comic Eremites and village errands, and turns serious in the last quest, where the Traveler is trapped in Jakob's plan and then speaks to the dead being whose body Merusea Village sits inside. The series introduces the Narzissenkreuz Ordo plot from Seymour's side, as Ann of the Narzissenkreuz does from Ann's.

Plot: Act I, The Illusion's Finishings. In the wilds near the Statue of the Seven at Elynas the Traveler and Paimon find a Melusine named Mamere being harassed by Eremites (Irus, Kaykubad and Kaykaus) who want her paintings for Mora. The Traveler drives them off. Mamere thanks them by offering to paint for them and takes them to Merusea Village, the underground home of the Melusines. At her house they meet Seymour, her talking machine friend. She also says a gentle collector, Mr. Jakob, takes an interest in her art. The Traveler and Paimon help her gather "paint" nearby and see her prepare to paint.

Act II, There Will Come Soft Rains. Seymour has been damaged and Mamere's house ransacked. In the village the Melusine Serene gives the Traveler spare parts, saying the incident must be reported to Monsieur Neuvillette, and suggests asking villagers for more. After collecting four Strange Parts, the Traveler returns and Seymour is repaired. The mercenaries return, saying Jakob, whom they have not been paid by, made monsters appear; Virda of the Maison Gardiennage takes them to the Fortress of Meropide. The ground shakes, and Mamere, in pain, says her "Father" is suffering and begs the Traveler to take her back to where the paint was gathered.

Act III, Limner, Dreamer, and Robotic Dog. At a giant red stone, Jakob uses Abyssal power to restart its "heart" in order to gather its blood. He says he serves the Narzissenkreuz Ordo, not the Abyss Order, and that blood from the heart is what Mamere's "paint" really is. Jakob traps the Traveler in a barrier and calls rifthounds. Seymour holds them off, Jakob taunts him about failing to protect "Mary-Ann", and a Breacher Primus attacks the barrier and frees the Traveler. Jakob escapes. Mamere paints the Traveler and Paimon, and the Traveler is drawn into a pink space where Elynas, the being whose body this is, speaks to them. After talking, she thanks them for stopping her heart and asks them to pass a message to Mamere. Back in the world the stone is stone again and the quakes stop, and the Traveler delivers the message to Mamere and receives her painting.

Details. Mamere does not need Mora and would have given a collector a painting as a gift if he had not mentioned Mora. In Act II the Eremites admit that Jakob hired them to take the paintings and never paid a deposit. Seymour talks only to Mamere at first, then answers the Traveler. Mamere says she found him lying in a pile of junk. Jakob appears as a cliff-top onlooker commenting on the beauty of the place.

In Act II the Traveler can do small errands for villagers to earn parts: Cosanzeana wants a flower garden and says she is learning to be a florist. The earthquake and monsters came after Jakob activated arrays in nearby ruins that opened the way to a realm of beasts, in his own words.

Elynas's account in Act III. She says she was brought into being by her "Mother", floated lonely in cosmic darkness, was given siblings, then left a "world beneath the earth" with them. She found that the things she enjoyed hurt others, fell in this place and died. Later, a battle among many people, a Hydro spirit and metal animals took place within her body; an explosion wounded her and, from those wounds, small life (the Melusines) grew. She taught them to build homes. Jakob and another visitor came long ago to collect her blood; she says Jakob has something of the cold cosmos within him. Her message to Mamere: that her paintings are beautiful, that she is loved and that she should get along with her sisters.

Revelations: - Mamere's "paint" is the congealed blood of Elynas, whose body Merusea Village lies in, as Jakob and Elynas both say.
- Elynas's heart can only be restarted by Abyssal power; if revived, her body would crush and digest the Melusines in it.
- Jakob serves the Narzissenkreuz Ordo, wants "equality" and "liberation of the will", and mentions a "world-formula" and a coming moment.
- Seymour is linked to a person named Mary-Ann, whom Jakob says he failed to defend.

- Elynas can link to the Traveler's mind through her blood and says only two people have not feared it: the Traveler and Jakob.
- Her cells act like an immune system and attacked the barrier trapping the Traveler.

Characters: The Traveler, Paimon, Mamere, Seymour, Jakob, Elynas (as a ghostly Melusine in the pink space), the Eremites Irus, Kaykubad and Kaykaus, Serene, Cosanzeana, Virda, and other Merusea Village Melusines.

Consequences: Jakob escapes with enough blood for his plans, and the Traveler is left with Mamere's painting as a reward. The series ends with Seymour's story still open. Initial Facts brings Ann's and Seymour's storylines together, and In the Wake of Narcissus resolves Seymour's link to Mary-Ann. Rewards include Mamere's Painting and completion of "Seymour's Story: Prologue" in the Fontaine Reputation.

Placement: Released in 4.0 with Fontaine. The wiki infobox lists In the Wake of Narcissus as next. It runs in parallel with Ann of the Narzissenkreuz, and the two prologues feed into Initial Facts.

113.content: Mamere is a Melusine painter who lives in Merusea Village, has a quiet house away from the other Melusines, and does not want Mora for her paintings. She calls Seymour family and her best friend, and refers to Elynas as her Father.

114.content: Seymour is a talking machine found by Mamere in a junk pile. At first he speaks only to her, uses clipped, logical language and calls the Traveler by "Mr./Ms." He is damaged in Act II and repaired with four Strange Parts. Jakob says he failed to defend someone named Mary-Ann, a name that surprises Seymour.

115.comment: Ancient Colors: Elynas and the heart
115.content: Elynas is the dead being whose body holds Merusea Village. Jakob restarts her heart to take blood; the Traveler stops it, and Elynas thanks them because reviving would harm her children. In the pink space she shows herself as a ghostly Melusine and asks them to tell Mamere her work is lovely.

116.comment: Ancient Colors: Jakob in Ancient Colors
116.content: Jakob first appears as a polite art collector; later he sends the Eremites for Mamere's paintings, restarts the heart with Abyssal power and traps the Traveler. He insists he is not of the Abyss Order, and says the Narzissenkreuz Ordo seeks equality and the liberation of will. He uses Abyssal power to reverse the crystallisation. See npc.jakob-ingold for the full character.

key: This Life, Just Like a Light Trickle of Song
117.content:
Animula Choragi Chapter (also: Animula Choragi, Furina's Story Quest, The Little Oceanid, To Yesterday, Whither Should the Water Flow?, This Life, Just Like a Light Trickle of Song): Furina's Story Quest, set in Fontaine after the Archon Quest fallout of the Masquerade of the Guilty. The Traveler and Paimon take a Guild commission from a small amateur troupe whose director died and whose lead actress is ill. They coax Furina, who has sworn off acting, into helping. The troupe finishes the director's last play, The Little Oceanid, and stages it at the Opera Epiclese.

The chapter has one act, "The Little Oceanid", made of three quests: To Yesterday, Whither Should the Water Flow? and This Life, Just Like a Light Trickle of Song. It was released in version 4.2. It is a quiet, character-driven story about grief, guilt and what a person does with freedom after a long performance ends.

The troupe's loss and Furina's own are mirrored: the director vanished in the disaster Furina could not stop, and Furina has to decide whether she can stand on a stage again. The act ends with her choosing to return to acting on her own terms, now holding a Vision.

Plot: Lauwick, an amateur troupe member, asks the Guild for help: their director is dead and their lead actress Dulphy is ill. The Traveler suggests Furina, who refuses at first and then relents. The group finds the troupe's writer and lead actor, learns the director's story, and stages her unfinished play at the Opera Epiclese, with Furina directing, stepping in on stage, and receiving a Vision.

To Yesterday: at the Fontaine Adventurers' Guild, Katheryne points the Traveler and Paimon to Lauwick, who needs a replacement for his ill lead actress for the troupe's last show. The Traveler suggests Furina, now living in a modest home and mostly cooking macaroni. She declines, saying she has no interest in acting after playing Focalors for so long, but changes her mind and apologises to Paimon. She learns the troupe's director, Aurelie, was a victim of Marcel's plots. At their quarters the group meets more members and learns the troupe cannot finish Aurelie's script, The Little Oceanid, without its writer Pauleau and its lead actor Vilmant.

Whither Should the Water Flow?: the group finds Pauleau in Poisson, where the disaster struck. Navia arrives and tells Furina that the town is coping, though some still resent her. Furina admits she is still haunted by the rising water and by people dissolving, and does not know how to enjoy her new freedom. Pauleau finishes his ending, and the group goes in search of Vilmant.

This Life, Just Like a Light Trickle of Song: after a slime fight, Vilmant reveals why Aurelie sent the troupe out of the city: a merchant had offered sponsorship in return for selling drinks that proved to be Sinthe, and Aurelie refused it. Pauleau and Vilmant argue, and Furina points out they are using the play to vent. The Traveler collects Aurelie's diary from the Palais Mermonia with Sedene's help. Furina asks Neuvillette for the Opera Epiclese, and the performance goes ahead.

To Yesterday: Katheryne has Furina's new address. Dulphy, who insists she is able to perform, is seen arguing with Lauwick. Furina overhears and is dragged in. The troupe members Elain and Buraud are surprised to see her. Lauwick explains Vilmant took Aurelie's death hard and Pauleau is busy writing the ending.

Whither Should the Water Flow?: Navia says some in Poisson are still angry at Furina for failing during the prophecy; Furina had tried to claim the visitor in her place was an actor dressed as her. Furina takes a walk, then rests aboard Spina di Rosula's ship. Pauleau reveals Dulphy was abandoned by her parents and Lauwick was fostered, and that he loved Aurelie, who treated everyone as family and rejected him. Dulphy wants an ending that mirrors the director's life, but Pauleau argues it would be meaningless.

This Life, Just Like a Light Trickle of Song: Furina cannot fight without a Vision, so the Traveler faces the slimes alone. Vilmant explains he accepted the merchant's sponsorship without telling anyone, informed Aurelie after learning the drink was Sinthe, and kept quiet about it afterwards, which enrages Pauleau. Furina realises Aurelie wanted to build a shelter for them from the outside world and says the ending should be devoted to her. The diary shows what Aurelie met in her last moments and that she cared for them. Dulphy suggests billing the play under Aurelie's name instead of her own. Furina insists on the larger stage, and Neuvillette, glad to see Furina recovering, agrees; he asks if she would perform again, and she declines.

The performance: after rehearsals under Furina's direction with help from the Traveler and Paimon, Dulphy's illness flares before the finale. Furina takes her role for the final scene, which she finds ironic. Dulphy asks beforehand what makes the heroine Clio shine; Furina answers that it is her pure heart and her unbroken belief in the beauty of the world. At the curtain call Pauleau credits Furina by name as consultant, though she had asked not to be, and the troupe had known the plan. Backstage he tells her everyone's work is acknowledged; she says they should have asked her first. Paimon was meant to lower a prop Vision from the ceiling for the scene, but a real one appeared for Furina, who wears it in place of the gem at her waist. They check on Dulphy, who is delighted that it succeeded. Furina, still annoyed at the thanks, says she will return to the stage with new perceptions.

Revelations: Furina receives a Vision at the end of the play.

Furina is no longer the actress who played Focalors; she is unsure how to live free of the role but ends the act willing to act again. The director Aurelie, a victim of Marcel's plots, had tried to protect the troupe from a sponsor whose drink turned out to be Sinthe.

The chapter confirms the Poisson disaster remains a wound for survivors and that Furina is still partly resented there. Neuvillette tells Furina he is glad she is recovering and does not press her to return to a leading role.
