Characters: Furina, the Traveler, Paimon and the troupe led by Lauwick.

Katheryne, Navia, Sedene and Neuvillette appear in supporting roles. Troupe members: Lauwick, Dulphy, Elain, Buraud, Vilmant, Pauleau and the late director Aurelie (prose only).

The merchant who offered the sponsorship is described but not shown. Marcel is referenced as the author of the plots that Aurelie fell victim to; how she died is not shown.

Consequences: Furina decides to return to acting at her own pace. She now has a Vision, which she keeps on her waist. The troupe finishes the director's play and honours her.

Furina's guilt and fear of the disaster are not resolved by the chapter, only softened by finishing something for others.

Placement: Unlocked at Adventure Rank 40 after Masquerade of the Guilty (Chapter IV Act V). Released in 4.2 on 2023-11-08. Story order follows the Chapter IV finale.

118.comment: Animula Choragi Chapter: The Little Oceanid (play)
118.content: The play is the late director Aurelie's unfinished script for an amateur Fontaine troupe. Its writer Pauleau supplies the ending, and Dulphy plays the heroine Clio; Furina takes the role for the final scene. The troupe stages it at the Opera Epiclese under Aurelie's name.

119.content: At the end of the performance a real Vision appears for Furina in place of the prop Paimon was meant to lower. Furina wears it where the large gem sat on her waist.

key: If She No Longer Dreams of You
120.content:
Ann of the Narzissenkreuz (also: Ann's Story: Prologue, The Narzissenkreuz Adventure, Kingdom Through the Looking-Glass, If She No Longer Dreams of You): Ann of the Narzissenkreuz is a three-act World Quest series in Fontaine, added in version 4.0 and shown in the Fontaine Reputation menu as "Ann's Story: Prologue". A tiny Oceanid called Ann, who says she belongs to the Narzissenkreuz Adventure Team, asks the Traveler to be her "knight" in a fairy-tale rescue of a "Princess Lyris" from the "fell dragon Narcissus". Along the way the setting stops making sense, and the series ends by showing that the underwater kingdom of Annapausis is a dream-world kept by someone else.

The acts are "The Narzissenkreuz Adventure" (two quests), "Kingdom Through the Looking-Glass" (Ann's Story) and "If She No Longer Dreams of You..." (Mary-Ann's Story). It requires The Outlander Who Caught the Wind and is followed by Initial Facts and In the Wake of Narcissus.

The series is deliberately lighthearted at first and slowly turns melancholic: the adventure team's names, roles and shapes are all "storybook" assignments, and the Traveler's role in the story is to be an unplanned variable. It is the entry point to the Narzissenkreuz plotline that In the Wake of Narcissus resolves.

Plot: Act I. Near the Court of Fontaine the Traveler and Paimon are pulled into an underwater place, Annapausis, by an Oceanid named Ann who greets the Traveler as a "good knight". She explains a story: the kingdom was conquered by the fell dragon Narcissus, Princess Lyris sleeps in a high tower, and the Narzissenkreuz Adventure Team plans a "Reconquista". The Traveler helps team members Petit Chou (a finch-shaped Oceanid) and Al (a mallard-shaped one) and meets Jak, Colonel Kate and the water-hound Mori, all of whom behave according to the story however odd their shapes look. Narcissus's "evil minions" are tainted water phantasms that the team cannot hurt, so the Traveler fights them. The team recovers the Princess's lost treasure, and then offers to give up their forms and merge into a great bubble to carry the Traveler and Ann to the top of the tower.

Act II. Beyond the tower's portal lies a library and a corridor that seems to repeat. After three loops the Traveler obtains the Holy Blade of Narzissenkreuz, which turns out to be a toy wooden sword. A "Narcissus" fight follows against an Oceanid of Loch, but the Princess is not there. Ann panics. Investigating old notes and records nearby, the Traveler and Paimon find a picture book that begins "a long time ago... there was a Princess named Lyris", and reading it transports them to "the real Annapausis".

Act III. In a sunlit garden they meet Mary-Ann, who calls Ann by name, feeds a polite talking "dog" that is not Mori, and tells Ann that there is no Princess here. The Traveler reasons that the kingdom and adventure were "a story". Mary-Ann explains that she dreamed of a small, brave Oceanid and asks Ann to live for herself and see the real world, before the room floods and the Traveler and Ann are sent away. Ann, still wanting to rescue Lyris, remembers the Narzissenkreuz Ordo and sets off for it with the Traveler and Paimon.

Details of the early quests. The Narzissenkreuz Adventure begins at an underwater waypoint north-west of the Court of Fontaine. In the first quest the team's enemies are "Evil Fangs of Narcissus" and the "Four Divine Kings of Narcissus"; the last step has the Traveler fight Mori, the water-hound, after a misunderstanding (Mori calls them bad people before being calmed by Ann). Jak, who is introduced as a team member, objects when the others say "Kingdom" and mutters "Republic". In the second quest, inside Annapausis, the Traveler breaks "treasure" seals in the sky and enters the tower. A "magical fountain" is guarded by Mori, who mistakes a statue of the Princess for the real one; the real Princess is said to be in the tower.

When the tower seals are broken, Al and the others decide to give up their shapes to boost the Traveler to the top. They treat it as a return to the water and not a death: pure water can take other forms again.

In Ann's Story the corridor changes each loop (more enemies and stairs on each pass) and a hidden door to the sword room appears once triggered. The "Narcissus" fight differs from the standard boss: it uses a different moveset and can be attacked directly.

In the room of old documents the Traveler can read fragments that name Karl Ingold, Emanuel Guillotin, Basil Elton, the Institute of Natural Philosophy and Petrichor, a ship named Sponsian, and a Director who is an Oceanid. The documents point to an earlier orphanage, but this series gives no explanation.

Revelations: - The Narzissenkreuz Kingdom, Adventure Team and "Narcissus" were all story roles. The Traveler concludes there is no Narzissenkreuz Kingdom among the seven nations.
- The Holy Blade of Narzissenkreuz in this series is a wooden toy sword. Wielding it, the young heroes could defeat all foes in their tale.
- The "real Annapausis" is a sunlit garden kept by Mary-Ann, who says the Annapausis is "our tomb" and asks Ann to live for herself.
- Ann is told her birth was "a beautiful accident"; she is a being born into the story.
- Al, Petit Chou, Mori, Jak and Colonel Kate are Oceanid-born shapes, and Mori is not the same as the "dog" Mary-Ann keeps.

- Paimon realises the sealed tower still had enemies and Bubble Formations, which the Traveler reads as elements that had not been "written yet".
- The Narzissenkreuz Ordo is the next lead; Ann says she recalls it.

Characters: The Traveler, Paimon, Ann, Petit Chou, Al, Jak, Colonel Kate, Mori (the water-hound), the "Narcissus" Oceanid, and Mary-Ann. Lyris is spoken of but appears only as a statue and as the story's Princess.

Consequences: Ann leaves Annapausis with the Traveler and Paimon. The series opens the way into Initial Facts and then In the Wake of Narcissus, where the Narzissenkreuz Ordo, Jakob and Mary-Ann are explained. In the Fontaine Reputation list the series completes the prologue of Ann's story, and its achievements include "Hardships Experienced...", "And After That..." and "Ann in Wonderland".

Placement: Released in 4.0 with Fontaine. It requires The Outlander Who Caught the Wind. After Mary-Ann's Story the wiki lists Initial Facts next, which leads to In the Wake of Narcissus. Ancient Colors (Seymour's Story: Prologue) is a parallel prologue that joins in at Initial Facts.

121.comment: Ann of the Narzissenkreuz: Annapausis storybook roles
121.content: In the series Ann's friends act out a fairy tale. Petit Chou is a small finch-shaped Oceanid, Al a mallard-shaped one who says purpose defines essence, Jak a blue frog who mutters "Republic" when the others say "Kingdom", Colonel Kate a squirrel-like soldier, and Mori a water-hound who guards a statue of the Princess. They fight "villains" in Narcissus's name, but they are Oceanid-born and the series later shows the whole kingdom is a remembered story.

122.comment: Ann of the Narzissenkreuz: Holy Blade of Narzissenkreuz (toy sword)
122.content: The Holy Blade that Ann says can slay Narcissus is a wooden toy sword that children of the adventure team once played with. The Traveler obtains it in Ann's Story after the corridor loops three times.

123.comment: Ann of the Narzissenkreuz: The picture book of Lyris
123.content: In Ann's Story, a picture book near the old records starts a tale of a beautiful Princess Lyris and the dragon Narcissus. Reading it aloud, Paimon and Ann trade lines; Ann interjects remarks as if she were the Princess in the story ("I don't want this name") and then the surroundings change into "the real Annapausis".

key: The Spindrift Shall Never Return to the Sea
124.content:
Aphros Delos Chapter (also: Aphros Delos, Eula's Story Quest, The Spindrift Shall Never Return to the Sea, Chapter of Wave Foam): The quest has three parts. First, the Traveler fails to talk to Schubert and finds Eula fighting Fatui in the Stormbearer Mountains. Second, Eula coaches them in noble speech, then in "dignified" combat and movement. Third, the Traveler wins Schubert's trust with a formal manner and a gift, is led to a Fatui hideout, and exposes the plot with Eula's help. It also shows how hard the Lawrence name still makes life for Eula in Mondstadt.

The act is a character piece as much as a mystery: the Fatui plot is small (giving the Fatui a diagram of the northern wall and its patrol routes), and most of the runtime goes to Eula's manner, her reputation among townspeople, and the gap between her stiff, formal speech and her kindness.

Plot: **Shadow of the Past.** At the Knights of Favonius Headquarters, Jean tells the Traveler and Paimon that Schubert of the Lawrence Clan has been seen near Mondstadt's northern city walls. She hopes an outsider can approach him, given the hostility between the Knights and the Lawrences. Schubert takes offence at the Traveler's lack of etiquette, complains that the city is in disarray without noble guidance, and leaves. Amber suggests her friend Eula and says she is probably patrolling the Stormbearer Mountains. There the Traveler and Paimon are attacked by Fatui Skirmishers; a sniper on a tower fires on the Traveler, Eula parries the shot, climbs the tower and kills him. She scolds the Traveler for carelessness, Paimon calls her speech weird and she bristles, and once she understands their aim she offers to teach them, after returning to the city.

**Speech and Etiquette.** In the city Eula tries to teach noble speech. Paimon is confused, and when Eula approaches townspeople without asking them to take part, they react with hostility to a Lawrence. Paimon steps in by saying the Traveler is a fast learner. The second half of the lesson is on Dragonspine, where Eula teaches "dignified" fighting and travelling and the Traveler passes both trials. They then go to Good Hunter, where Eula orders Gebratenes Fleisch mit Sauerkraut as a gift; the group shares a meal, Eula says her uncle is probably camping outside Springvale, and it is explained that she is judged by her surname although she is kind.

**Through the Motions, to the Heart.** At Springvale Schubert is irritated but gives a second chance. The Traveler's formal speech and the roasted meat impress him, and he treats them as a trusted companion since he needs capable people. He takes them to a hideout that the Knights had cleared earlier and the Fatui have retaken, which confirms his collaboration. He introduces them to the Fatui agent Sergei, who is suspicious, and hands over a diagram of the northern wall and patrol routes. When the Traveler reveals themselves as the Honorary Knight, both men flee. Eula and two Knights arrest Schubert, and the two argue about right and wrong before she has him taken away. The Traveler and Eula clear the Fatui out and recover the diagram. Eula thanks them but asks them not to take her targets next time.

The set-up leans on Eula's habits: she has spent a long time tracking this Fatui group, finds them only when she hears fighting, and rebukes the Traveler as a way of expressing concern. Her lessons treat noble manners as a tool the Traveler can borrow. Because the wiki summary calls Schubert her uncle, the confrontation at Springvale is a family argument as well as an arrest.

The Chinese chapter name is the "Chapter of Wave Foam" (the act title speaks of foam that never returns to the sea), and the chapter's in-game description speaks of a noble crown forged in Mondstadt from the blood and tears of the common folk, broken when the west wind blew and leaving only small spindrifts, and asks where those spindrifts will go (it does not name the Lawrences, but the act follows one of their descendants). Quest names run Shadow of the Past, Speech and Etiquette, Through the Motions, to the Heart.

Revelations: - A Lawrence Clan member, Schubert, was collaborating with the Fatui and had given them information on the northern wall's defences; the Fatui had reoccupied a hideout the Knights had earlier cleared.
- Eula is a Knights of Favonius officer who is also a disavowed member of the Lawrence family; people in Mondstadt hold her family name against her.
- Eula is outwardly severe but acts to protect the Traveler and the city.

The Lawrence Clan's loss of status, and the way ordinary Mondstadters transfer their old grievance onto Eula, are the quest's main social revelation; it does not retell the clan's history, which belongs to the faction entry.

Characters: Eula (lead; patrols, teaches, arrests Schubert), Schubert (Lawrence Clan, Fatui collaborator), Sergei (Fatui contact), Jean (quest giver), Amber (recommends Eula and shares the meal), Paimon and the Traveler.

Townspeople in the city appear as the foil to Eula's lessons. Two unnamed Knights help make the arrest. The Fatui force consists of Skirmishers in the mountains and the group in the hideout.

Consequences: The Fatui plot against the north wall is stopped and Schubert is in the Knights' custody. The Traveler leaves with a better understanding of Eula; the quest does not resolve her standing in Mondstadt, and the townspeople's prejudice remains.

Placement: Released in Version 1.5. Story order is not numbered by canon. Unlocked after the Prologue's Act III "Song of the Dragon and Freedom" at Adventure Rank 40. It has only one act and is standalone among Mondstadt's story quests.

125.comment: Aphros Delos Chapter: Eula's Etiquette Lessons
125.content:
In "Speech and Etiquette" Eula teaches the Traveler to speak like a noble, first in the city and then, as a test of dignified conduct, in combat and travel on Dragonspine. Her formal lecturing confuses Paimon, and approaching townspeople without asking them to participate angers them because of her Lawrence background.

The lesson ends with Eula ordering roasted meat at Good Hunter as a present for Schubert, who is camping near Springvale.

126.comment: Aphros Delos Chapter: Schubert and the Fatui Hideout
126.content:
Schubert, a proud Lawrence who thinks Mondstadt needs nobles to run it, was passing the Fatui a diagram of the northern wall and patrol routes. He brings the Traveler to a hideout the Fatui reclaimed and introduces them to Sergei. When the Traveler reveals they are an Honorary Knight, Schubert flees and is arrested by Eula.

Schubert is called Eula's uncle in the wiki summary, which gives her argument with him its edge: she does not defend him, and he disputes her view of right and wrong.

127.content:
Apocalypse Lost (also: Memories of Gurabad, Apocalypse Lost World Quest series, Chessboard of Safhe Shatranj quest): Apocalypse Lost is a world quest series in the Desert of Hadramaveth, Sumeru, released in version 3.4. It has a single quest, Memories of Gurabad. Once the Traveler has placed all five chess pieces on the chessboard at Safhe Shatranj, the jinni Liloupar leads them through a vision of ancient Gurabad. She tells her own story of ruining her husband's line, and then goes into the city, leaving the Traveler her bottle.

The series is the end of the arc that began with Liloupar becoming the Traveler's jinni in The Dirge of Bilqis. The quest is an act of farewell: Liloupar says she wants the Traveler to witness her past and what she learned, and Paimon senses that it is a goodbye. It is followed in the desert by Her Foes Rage Like Great Waters....

Much of the quest's text is shaped by the Book of Nahum, which speaks of the fall of a tyrannical city. Quotations from it appear in the vision of Gurabad; this is a literary echo, not a plot element.

Plot: **Preparation.** The wiki lists five chess pieces: King Deshret's Pillar, Border Fort, Soulferry, Khaj-Nisut and Temple of Gurabad. Four are obtained during The Dirge of Bilqis, and the fifth, the Temple of Gurabad piece, while progressing through "The Falcon's Hunt" (as the wiki records). They must be put in the glowing platforms at Safhe Shatranj, in the Hidden Exploration Objective Chessboard of Safhe Shatranj, to begin Memories of Gurabad.

**Tremors and the first vision.** Liloupar senses tremors from deep underground, jokes that it was only a drill, and Paimon is not amused. After the first fight with primal constructs she says Gurabad is near. She jokes that a slot exists on her bottle for the chess piece, then admits she invented it and tells her master to simply hold her to it. A vision follows of a great cold city whose gate sits in the mountain wall. The Traveler's head hurts and Liloupar says "That's Gurabad over there. I remember it now." She promises Paimon food and Mora as thanks and says the Traveler will be given back.

**Why Gurabad.** She says she does not fully know why she must go, but wants the Traveler to witness her past and the lessons she learned. She describes the place as holding the memories of ghosts, broken dreams and the aftertaste of revenge.

**At Gurabad.** The chess piece teleports the party, a little off-target, to the first valley. Liloupar reveals Gurabad and asks the Traveler to clear new "tenants", the primal constructs. When the last wave is down, the shard of her soul merges with the bottle. The Traveler sees the brass-masked man speak, quoting the Book of Nahum, and then the city overwhelmed. Pomegranates burst and trampled, a red flood, soldiers' weapons and machines spilling Jinn without minds, the brass-masked king fleeing into Shirin's arms while she looks old and dim, and King Kisra turned into a dark monster. Liloupar says they are all her flesh and blood.

**Her account.** Ormazd was once her lover, and through her love he rose from shepherd to king. She believed he was more than mortal, but vanity and selfishness took him in the end. She punished him by handing down ruin from father to son across three generations. Her son Parvezravan wanted unlimited power, so she designed him machines run by the remains of Jinn spirits and inspired in a dream a colossal machine that swallowed and spat out manufactured goods. They brought wealth but robbed laborers of their lives and farmers of their property. The rich and lords wept in joy at the end of slavery, but she says this began an even crueller servitude. Poverty bred hatred and ambition; riches bred greed and ambition. Parvezravan forced Shirin, his sister and queen, to create misshapen Jinn without minds, and Liloupar says her suffering pleased and empowered her. Through this she fostered the flesh and blood of Shiruyeh, the brass-masked Khorramdin, whom the poor saw as an emissary of her mistress and a savior. He led them to justice and to death, and the earth swallowed city and followers alike. She says she did nothing wrong, but her children Shirin and Shiruyeh remain there, lonely.

**Farewell.** The power of darkness is growing in Gurabad and, she says, only a mother's power can face it. She thought she could use the dark abyss to punish what she hated, but it will now be her fate to go in and face retribution. She tells the Traveler a jinni chooses her master, and that their bond will not be easily severed. She whispers into the bottle, the Traveler comes to understand the ancient verses she recites, and then the bottle dims and falls silent.

Gameplay and labelled mechanics: after the quest, the viewpoint at Safhe Shatranj opens, the previously unreadable Nameless Tablets in the desert ruins become readable, and the jinni's bottle still gives the same gadget benefits though Liloupar has left it, according to the wiki. These are game notes.

Details in the vision: the brass-masked man's words are taken from the Book of Nahum and a flood of pomegranate juice is described turning the city's reservoir into a red sea that drowns the slaves first and then their masters. The text calls the juice the "joy of life and the joy of vengeance".

Revelations: - Liloupar, in her own telling, was the lover of Ormazd, mother of Parvezravan and Shirin, and the force behind the fall of his line.
- Gurabad's Jinn-driven machines were her gift to Parvezravan; the Jinn were created through Shirin's suffering, and Shiruyeh, the brass-masked king, led a revolt that ended with the city falling into a chasm.
- Liloupar's reason for returning to Gurabad is to face the darkness she says she once set on the city and to see her children.

- Gurabad was a city of slave labour that, in her account, became industrial through Jinn machines, a change she says worsened the poor's condition.
- Liloupar says she can be bound only by her own choice: the jinni chooses her master.

Characters: The Traveler, Paimon and Liloupar. Historical figures discussed: Ormazd, Parvezravan (called Kisra in the vision), Shirin of Gurabad, Shiruyeh (Khorramdin) and Nabu Malikata (her mistress).

Consequences: Liloupar leaves her bottle and goes into Gurabad. The Traveler learns her account of the city's fall. The desert tablets become readable and Safhe Shatranj becomes a viewpoint.

The wiki's Liloupar article records later events in other quests, including her emerging again from a dormancy. Those events are outside this quest and are not summarised here.

Placement: Requires The Dirge of Bilqis and The Fallen Falcon. The wiki lists the series after The Dirge of Bilqis and before Her Foes Rage Like Great Waters.... Released in 3.4. Despite being displayed as a chapter, it contains one quest.

128.content: In Liloupar's telling Gurabad was a great city of slave labour that became a city of Jinn-driven machines. It fell when the earth opened beneath it after a revolt led by Shiruyeh and after the darkness she had unleashed. The quest shows it as a ruined, cold city swallowed by a chasm that lies behind a wall in a desert cave. The vision and Liloupar's account do not agree with any other source on all points.

129.content: Ormazd was a shepherd who rose to be a king through Liloupar's love, in her account. She believed he was no ordinary mortal, but his vanity and selfishness showed him to be like other rulers. She says she punished him by ruining his descendants across three generations.

130.comment: Apocalypse Lost: Shiruyeh, the Brass Mask
130.content: Shiruyeh, called Khorramdin and the brass-masked king, led the poor and slaves of Gurabad in a revolt. The people saw him as the emissary of Liloupar's mistress and a savior; Liloupar calls him a gifted charlatan who led his followers to their doom when the earth swallowed them. She says he is her flesh and blood, and that he and Shirin remain in the ruined city.

131.content: Parvezravan is Liloupar's son. She says he wanted unlimited power and received Jinn-driven machines through her, bringing wealth and ruin. He forced Shirin, his sister and queen, to create mindless Jinn. In the vision, King Kisra appears turned into a dark monster and Shirin old and dim.

132.content:
Aranyaka (also: Aranyaka world quest series, Woodland Encounter, Festival Utsava): A four-part Sumeru world quest series from Version 3.0. The Traveler and Paimon meet a Forest Watcher named Rana, whose village's children keep vanishing and returning with no memory. After Rana is sickened by the Withering, the pair enter the dream world of the Aranara, forest spirits, and help them hold a festival and destroy an avatar of the Withering so that a Bija, a life-giving seed, can be made.

The series is a gentle story about memory, friendship and sacrifice. It introduces the Aranara, the Withering as the Aranara see it ("Marana"), Vanarana and the Fane of Ashvattha. It ends bittersweetly: the Aranara Arana gives up its memories of the Traveler and of Rana to save her, and Rana receives a Dendro Vision. No Archon Quest is required to start it.

The series' title echoes the Sanskrit Aranyaka ("Book of the Forest"), texts that revolve around ritual and sacrifice, which fits a story built around a festival that ends in a sacrifice.

Plot: Leaving Gandharva Ville, the Traveler and Paimon rescue a Forest Watcher named Rana from fungi and go with her to Vimara Village. The village's children have been vanishing and returning with no memory. After Rana is struck down by the Withering, an Aranara named Arana says she needs a Bija and sends the Traveler to Vanarana, the Aranara's dream-world village. There they win the Aranara's trust, help hold Festival Utsava, and finally destroy Marana's Avatar in Old Vanarana so a new Ashvattha tree can bear a Bija. The Bija wakes Rana.

Part I, Woodland Encounter: Rana guides the Traveler to Vimara Village, where the villagers Amadhiah and Alphonso explain the children's disappearances. The Traveler clears Withering Zones on patrol with Rana and helps thin a Spinocrocodile population, since a Forest Watcher also keeps the ecosystem in balance. The next day a boy named Iotham is chased by Eremites and then trapped in a Withering Zone in a cave. Rana rushes in despite having no Vision, falls gravely ill and vanishes, leaving traces of energy. Arana explains the cause and points the Traveler to Vanarana.

Part II, Dream Nursery: To enter Vanarana the Traveler must play the Rhythm of the Great Dream on a Vintage Lyre (obtained from Amadhiah). Arama, a Golden Nara, sets small tasks so the other Aranara lose their fear of humans, and the elder Araja explains that a Bija needs Festival Utsava, for which scattered Aranara must be gathered. The Traveler helps various Aranara in side stories (Agnihotra Sutra, An Unwavering Culinary Dream, Varuna Gatha), and Aranakula returns to tend the Vanarana nursery with Arakara. Back with Rana, Arana admits it had put the village children to sleep and removed part of their memories before returning them.

Part III, Nursery of Lost Dreams: After the festival, the Traveler and Arama take Vasoma Fruits to the weakened Fane of Ashvattha. The Ashvattha tree tells Arama to make the ultimate sacrifice, and since it is too weakened by the Withering to bear a Bija, a new tree must be planted. First Marana's Avatar, in the heart of Old Vanarana, must be destroyed.

Part IV, In the End, the Forest Will Remember: Arana, its memories wiped, takes the Bija to Rana, who wakes and invites it to travel with her.

The festival: the Traveler and Paimon visit many Aranara and each gives a flower as a token of friendship; all gather to play the Rhythm of the Great Dream together, and Arama weaves the flowers into a garland. Araja reveals he cannot leave Vanarana's dream because he is the "Tree of Dreams".

In Old Vanarana Arama shields the group from the Withering and the Traveler breaks three seals: reading three Inscriptions of Remembrance, burning seven Stone Pillar Seals, and defeating a Ruin Grader that Arama must bind. A hidden space below shows no Withering, and an Aranara named Aramuhukunda, whom the Traveler had met at the festival, unlocks the final seal. Marana's Avatar repeatedly moves its soul into new Withering Zones, which the Traveler clears before destroying the core. Arana is then brought to Old Vanarana and becomes the new Ashvattha sapling while Arama dives into the ground, and a Bija fruit forms once the Rhythm of the Great Dream is played again. The Withering is not entirely gone, only kept from forming significantly for the foreseeable future.

In Part IV (the quest titled "Hello," "Thank You," and the Final "Goodbye") Arana wakes with its memories wiped, correctly deduces what happened from the gaps, and is persuaded to bring the Bija to Rana in Vimara Village even though it cannot recall her. Rana invites it to journey with her to make new precious memories and fill the "void". A light appears in her chest and she receives a Dendro Vision. She says she will tell Tighnari and hopes to meet the Traveler again, stronger.

Smaller beats. On the night in the reserve camp the Traveler and Paimon gather firewood while Rana cooks curry, and she mentions that the Aranara were once visited by another gold-haired human, which interests the Traveler. At the start of Part II Paimon worries that playing the Rhythm of the Great Dream outdoors would attract Whopperflowers, so the Traveler fetches the lyre first. Early on, the Traveler tries to coax information from the village children with stories and learns nothing. After Varuna Gatha, Aranakula plants a Vasmrti in the Vanarana nursery to grow Viparyas, and says twelve more Vasmrti sit in nurseries outside the dream world. In Part III, Aramuhukunda sees that the Traveler means to destroy Marana's Avatar and unlocks the last seal so they can face it. The Withering Zones in Old Vanarana cannot be cleared by the usual branches, so Arama destroys one whole zone directly.

Revelations: The missing children were put to sleep by Arana, who removed part of their memories before returning them; the Aranara expect children to forget them when they grow up. The Withering ("Marana") harms Rana because she lacks a Vision. The cure, a Bija, can only come from a sacrifice: the Ashvattha tree must be replaced, and the Aranara who becomes the new tree loses its memories.

The Aranara fought invaders in the cataclysm, and Old Vanarana still holds ruin machines and riftwolves from that time. The identity of the "child of snow" and of the gold-haired human who once visited the Aranara is left open.

Characters: The Traveler, Paimon, Rana, and the Aranara Arana, Arama and Araja.

Rana is a Forest Watcher without a Vision, devoted to her duty and the village. Arana is the Aranara who first helps Rana and eventually sacrifices its memories; Arama, a Golden Nara, guides the Traveler through Vanarana and Old Vanarana; Araja is the elder and the "Tree of Dreams". Amadhiah, Alphonso and the boy Iotham are villagers. Tighnari is mentioned as a fellow Forest Watcher and is told of Rana's plans. Eremites and Fatui appear briefly as enemies. Other Aranara named include Aranakula, Arakara and Aramuhukunda.

Consequences: Rana is cured, receives a Dendro Vision and leaves on a journey with Arana, who has lost its memories of her. A new Ashvattha tree grows from Arama's sacrifice, and the Withering at Old Vanarana is cleared, though traces remain. The series opens the wider Aranara questline, including Varuna Gatha and the Vanarana nursery.

Placement: Released in Version 3.0 with Sumeru. Despite references to Archon Quest events through Chapter II and the Traveler's existing knowledge of the Fatui, no Archon Quest is required to start it.

133.content: In the Aranyaka series Rana, a Forest Watcher without a Vision, is struck down by the Withering, which the Aranara call Marana. Only a Bija can cure her. The Aranara Arana gives up its memories to produce the Bija; when it wakes it no longer recognises the Traveler and Paimon, but is persuaded to carry the Bija to Rana and then travels with her.

key: Song of the Welkin Moon Act IX
134.content:
As All Falls to Emptiness (also: Song of the Welkin Moon Act IX): Song of the Welkin Moon Act IX, set in Sumeru. A letter about Collei's warning dream sends the Traveler and Paimon from Nod-Krai back to Sumeru City, where Nahida has taken on Irminsul's overload and collapsed. With a barrier sealing Sumeru off, the Traveler helps scholars, Eremites and Nod-Krai visitors regroup, fend off Jinn and Fatui, find the sleeping Liloupar, and win the Seven Pillars' agreement to open Aaru.

The act has three quests: Where Flowers Awaken, A Divergence Leading to Oneself and Ancient Shadows Re-Emerge. It moves through Sumeru City, Caravan Ribat, the Desert of Hadramaveth, the Temple of Silence, Gurabad and the Mausoleum of King Deshret. Released in version 6.6 (Luna VII). It is the point at which the Nod-Krai-centred story returns to Sumeru.

The act follows the Akasha System plan: to restart the system that once cleansed Irminsul of forbidden knowledge, the allies need a replacement for the Dendro Gnosis that originally powered it. This brings back several characters and places from Chapter III, and Nicole and Nefer arrive from Nod-Krai to help.

Plot: Collei's letter and a dream warn the Traveler of trouble in Sumeru. Irminsul has stopped processing information, Nahida has taken over its work and collapses, and everyone is evacuated to Caravan Ribat. The allies plan to restart the Akasha System, the Traveler takes Nahida to Apep, and the Fatui and Jinn attack. After Liloupar is found and the Jinn pacified, the Seven Pillars agree to open Aaru.

Collei's letter and her warning dream bring the Traveler to Sumeru City, where Nahida has absorbed Irminsul's overload and collapsed and the population is moved to Caravan Ribat. The allies plan to restart the Akasha System and the Traveler takes Nahida to Apep. The Fatui and Jinn attack; Collei, guided by Nicole, calms the Jinn with a prayer of Nabu Malikata, and the Traveler finds Liloupar in Gurabad, who pacifies the Jinn. After Nefer's answer frees Thoth and his fellow Pillars and Cyno speaks for Hermanubis, the Seven Pillars agree to open Aaru.

Where Flowers Awaken: at the Nod-Krai Adventurers' Guild, Katheryne gives the Traveler a letter from Collei, which begins a flashback of a dream she had in which everyone in Sumeru City had switched identities and Tighnari did not know her. A voice, later revealed as Nicole's, tells her it is a premonition and that she should tell Nahida and the Traveler. In Sumeru City the Traveler finds the city evacuating to Caravan Ribat on Nahida's and the new Sages' orders. In the Sanctuary of Surasthana, Nahida hovers inside a Dendro field: something has stopped Irminsul recording and processing information, creating a bottleneck that disrupts the ley lines, and she has taken over Irminsul's work herself despite the strain. Wanderer finds the cause is not an attack from outside. The field fails and Nahida collapses, so the group decides to move her to Caravan Ribat. Meanwhile in the Great Red Sand, a hooded Fatui leader says disrupting Sumeru City is a necessary step.

A Divergence Leading to Oneself: at Caravan Ribat the Sages are introduced and Rukh Shah reports that civilians returning near Yasna Monument went mad and killed one another. A Ley Line Blossom nearby is dissected and shows Irminsul can still be reached from outside, leading to a plan to restart the Akasha System, which needs a substitute for the Dendro Gnosis that once powered it. The scholars will search the Temple of Silence's records, while the Eremites move civilians to Aaru Village. The Traveler takes Nahida to Apep in the Desert of Hadramaveth, who agrees to share her Dendro energy, says the Heavenly Principles seized Irminsul from ancient dragonkind, and senses Jinn behind the sandstorms. Nahida wakes briefly and sends the Traveler a flower-shaped key containing a message. At the Temple of Silence the Traveler and Paimon are attacked by Jinn and the Fatui and trapped by the hooded man, while at Aaru Village Collei, with Nicole's guidance, uses a prayer of Nabu Malikata to make the Jinn submit. Jeht and Benben free the Traveler; with Jeht they open the way to Gurabad and find Liloupar, who explains she fought the Abyss there until Gosoythoth's defeat in Natlan let her sleep, and who then pacifies the Jinn and stops the sandstorms.

Ancient Shadows Re-Emerge: the group reunites at the Temple of Silence. A barrier now encloses Sumeru; Nicole explains it is one of the ley lines' defences to isolate Irminsul. She tells Collei that the god remains Dottore injected into Collei came from Nabu Malikata. At the Mausoleum of King Deshret, Nefer answers Thoth's question with "time", which frees Thoth, Heryshaf and Sobek and restores their true forms. Cyno, as Hermanubis' representative, with Apep already helping Nahida, secures the Seven Pillars' agreement to open Aaru. Jebrael's soul is among the first to emerge.
The sequence depends on layered plans: the Akasha System restart, the move to Aaru Village, and the Traveler's private message from Nahida. The Sages named in the act are Naphis and the five others (Baladhuri, Alkindi, Firnas, Shakir and Rushd) with their titles in parentheses (Vahumana, Spantamad, Kshahrewar, Rtawahist and Haravatat). Cyrus bemoans an "invisible hand" steering events. Dori and her Jinni partner Plumpy defend Aaru Village's north gate with Tighnari and Collei; Baladhuri and Firnas report the southern line has collapsed before Collei's prayer ends the attack. Nefer asks whether the scholars can modify Aaru, and Naphis says they are heading to the mausoleum.

Nicole and Nefer come from Nod-Krai and arrive before the barrier seals. Faruzan bonds with Nicole over a squirrel sculpture Nicole creates from nothing; the others agree not to tell Faruzan about Nicole's angel identity for the time being. Cyno tells Collei that however many fragments she carries she remains herself.

The act reuses Chapter III material: Apep's Heart of Oasis and the Fire Seed, the Mausoleum of King Deshret and its Pillars, and Gurabad. Liloupar's account links the Abyss's retreat in Gurabad to Gosoythoth's defeat in Natlan. Jeht reports that she settled her old grudge against the Tanit elder Masseira, and Alhaitham links the Jinn's sudden movement to Gurabad. The Fatui hooded man says his reason for following Dottore is "friendship" and a shared wish to write rules for the world.

Revelations: Irminsul is blocked and overloaded, and Nahida is strained by it. The god remains inside Collei were Nabu Malikata's. The Heavenly Principles usurped Irminsul from ancient dragonkind. A barrier has sealed Sumeru.

Apep tells the Traveler that Irminsul was one of the things the Heavenly Principles took and repurposed from ancient dragonkind. Nicole reveals the god remains Dottore injected into Collei were from Nabu Malikata. Wanderer establishes the anomaly is not an external attack. Nahida's key says the statues of the gods hang inverted from the heavens, and that one alone is unique among them, with its location hidden.

Nicole explains the barrier is a ley line defence to isolate Irminsul from the world. Liloupar says she fought Abyssal forces in Gurabad until Gosoythoth fell, after which they quieted.

Characters: The Traveler, Paimon, Nahida, Cyno, Alhaitham, Collei, Tighnari, Liloupar, Jeht, Nicole and Nefer are the principals.

Supporting cast: Wanderer, Kaveh, Dehya, Sethos, Dori and Plumpy, Faruzan, Naphis and the Sages, Apep, Benben, Thoth, Heryshaf, Sobek, Shesepankh, Bennu, Jebrael, Cyrus, Rukh Shah, Mu'tasim, Katheryne, a hooded Fatui leader who calls himself Dottore's subordinate, and Dottore (referred to, not present).

Consequences: Sumeru is sealed by a barrier, Nahida is in a coma under Apep's care, and the Seven Pillars have agreed to open Aaru. Liloupar is awake and has stopped the Jinn. The allies go on to prepare Aaru for modification.

Placement: Song of the Welkin Moon Act IX, following True Moon and preceding Of Myriad Paths, Flux, and Dissolution. Released in version 6.6 (Luna VII, 2026-05-20). The wiki lists Adventure Rank 40 as the unlock requirement.

135.comment: As All Falls to Emptiness: Irminsul anomaly and the Sumeru barrier
135.content: Something prevents Irminsul from recording and processing information, which disrupts the ley lines. Nahida takes over its functions and collapses. Near Yasna Monument the anomaly drives civilians to violence, and abnormal Ley Line Blossoms appear. A barrier then closes around Sumeru, which Nicole says is a ley line defence to isolate Irminsul. The Traveler is unaffected by the Irminsul anomaly.

136.comment: As All Falls to Emptiness: Akasha System restart plan
136.content: Because Irminsul can still be reached from outside, Alhaitham and the others plan to restart the Akasha System, built to cleanse Irminsul of Abyssal forbidden knowledge. It needs a replacement for the Dendro Gnosis that once powered it. Scholars search the Temple of Silence's records while the Eremites move civilians to Aaru Village. The plan later turns to opening Aaru.

137.comment: As All Falls to Emptiness: Liloupar awakened in Gurabad
137.content: Searching for Liloupar, the Traveler and Jeht open the entrance to Gurabad at Safhe Shatranj and find her nearby. She says she fought the Abyss until Gosoythoth's defeat in Natlan ended its pressure there, then slept. Learning of Sumeru's trouble she pacifies the Jinn and ends the sandstorms.

138.comment: As All Falls to Emptiness: The Seven Pillars agree to open Aaru
138.content: In the Mausoleum of King Deshret the group meets Thoth, Heryshaf and Sobek. Nefer's answer to Thoth's earlier question, "time", is accepted as her own and frees all three. Heryshaf calls Shesepankh and Bennu. With Cyno speaking for Hermanubis and Apep already helping Nahida, the Seven Pillars agree to open Aaru. Jebrael emerges and passes to the ley lines as a Sacred Ibis.

139.comment: As All Falls to Emptiness: Collei's god remains and Nabu Malikata
139.content: The voice that has been guiding Collei turns out to be Nicole's. Under Nicole's instruction Collei recites a prayer written by Nabu Malikata to make the Jinn submit, and Nicole later reveals that the god remains Dottore injected into Collei were Nabu Malikata's. Cyno reassures Collei that she remains herself.

The Truth, Lost With the Rain
When All Return to the Waters
140.comment: As Light Rain Falls Without Reason
140.content:
As Light Rain Falls Without Reason (also: Chapter IV Act II, Like the Faint Moonlight of Yesteryear, The Truth, Lost With the Rain, When All Return to the Waters): The second act of Fontaine's Archon Quest. The Traveler and Paimon join Navia of Spina di Rosula in tracing the serial disappearances of young women, which prove to be people dissolved into Primordial Seawater and tied to the death of Navia's father Callas. The case ends in a trial that exposes the culprit, Marcel, after which the Oratrice Mecanique d'Analyse Cardinale returns a "Guilty" verdict against the Fatui Harbinger Tartaglia (Childe).

The act has three quests: Like the Faint Moonlight of Yesteryear, The Truth, Lost With the Rain, and When All Return to the Waters. It is a detective story set in the Court of Fontaine and Poisson, and it is where the Traveler learns that Primordial Seawater dissolves Fontainians and that an Oceanid can hold a dissolved girl's memories.

Its last beats set up the rest of Chapter IV: a machine verdict against Tartaglia that Neuvillette does not accept as truth, and Furina's visible agitation at it.

Plot: After the trial of Act I, the Traveler and Paimon dine at Hotel Debord with Navia, who distrusts the Garde and wants a fresh angle on the disappearances. That evening at the Fountain of Lucine the Traveler is drawn into a dream-like link with an Oceanid, a former girl who has lost most of her memory and asks for someone called Vacher. She asks that Vacher be told to forget her. Back in the real world the Traveler finds Navia, Silver and Melus fighting a swarm of unregistered clockwork meka, and Clorinde helps them. Navia works out that her Fonta at the hotel had been spiked with Primordial Seawater (it tasted salty, and Paimon drank it by mistake), and the Traveler and Paimon fully join her investigation.

Navia explains that three years earlier her father Callas, head of Spina di Rosula, was accused of killing his friend Jacques and chose to duel rather than stand trial, dying at Clorinde's hand. She believes the murder and the disappearances are linked. Vacher has no public records, and Neuvillette's case archives have nothing on him either. Rain on the day of the conviction and on the night of the murder suggests to the Traveler that the real killer may have dissolved into water. Melus reveals that Callas knew he was dying and had been fighting the Sinthe drink trade, which Navia now concludes was made with Primordial Seawater. Melus names three suspects (Florent, Thierry, Marcel). After talking to them and to Jacques' family, the Traveler concludes that Marcel, the only one wealthy enough to afford private meka, is the likely culprit.

When the authorities accuse Tartaglia of the disappearances, the Traveler infiltrates the underwater Sinthe production facility while Navia accuses Marcel in court. His arguments nearly succeed, until Navia names Vacher and he reacts. In the facility the Traveler finds proof that Vacher ran the experiments, plus a notebook of Vacher's lover Vigneire containing the name Marcel, chosen for a child they never had. Marcel is exposed as Vacher; he blames a system that laughed off his reports of people dissolving.

Details of the investigation. The meka bore no serial numbers, and Clorinde infers a rich or powerful private owner, since Gardemeks can only be operated by the Maison Gardiennage. Callas had banned Sinthe from his group, angering the sellers, and had turned one of them, Jacques, into an informant. Clothes were found at the scene of Jacques' death, suggesting a third party. Jacques' wife believes his superiors noticed his betrayal and forced him to kill Callas against his will. Callas had left his gun inside the banquet hall when he stepped out for air, which rules out a second gun. Thierry says the meka would be nearly impossible to modify in secret. Melus warns Navia not to storm the enemy headquarters, as that would amount to war.

At the opera house Tartaglia, charged with the disappearances, is willing to accept it if he can duel Clorinde again. Navia asks Clorinde to testify, and Clorinde confirms that as a champion duelist she could tell Callas wanted to die. Navia explains that Callas would not defend himself because that would have made her and Spina di Rosula the next targets. Marcel counters that he moved to Fontaine after the disappearances began.

To show that Primordial Seawater harms only Fontainians, Marcel drinks a large quantity before the court, noting that this denies him a way to join Vigneire in death. Neuvillette declares Tartaglia innocent of the disappearances, reviews the Traveler's evidence and feeds it to the Oratrice, which returns "Guilty" for Marcel. Then, to clear Tartaglia formally of the original charge, he runs that too, and the machine returns "Guilty". Tartaglia tries to escape with his Electro Delusion and the Foul Legacy Transformation, but Neuvillette leaps from his seat and knocks him out with a Hydro power. He apologises and promises to investigate personally. Furina says the verdict is right, shows agitation and leaves.

Afterwards Marcel asks to visit the Fountain of Lucine. He is pulled into the dream realm and meets an Oceanid with Vigneire's voice that is really the merged consciousness of the women he dissolved; it drowns him, and doctors record a panic attack. A few days later Navia, having held a belated memorial for Callas and made amends with Clorinde, visits his grave with the Traveler. Neuvillette is there and explains that he let the duel go ahead because he believed no innocent human would die for justice. He adds that he had foreseen the Oratrice might one day disagree with him.

Revelations: The disappearing girls were dissolved into Primordial Seawater, which turns Fontainians into water, and the Oceanids keep fragments of the people they were. Sinthe was made with Primordial Seawater. Marcel was really Vacher, who experimented on the victims, and Callas's duel was a deliberate sacrifice. Rain is repeatedly tied to the dissolving.

The Oratrice's "Guilty" on Tartaglia is the first time it differed from Neuvillette's own judgment. Neuvillette says Furina took the Prophecy seriously.

Characters: Navia leads the investigation, driven by grief for Callas. Melus, who had withheld some of Callas's secrets, and Silver fight alongside her. Clorinde, the Champion Duelist who killed Callas in the duel he chose and whom he asked to keep Navia safe, protects Navia. Neuvillette presides in court and holds to court rules despite doubts. Furina sits in the trial; Sedene lets the group into Neuvillette's office at Palais Mermonia. Marcel is the culprit. Tartaglia is accused and then found guilty by the machine.

Consequences: Callas's honour is restored and Navia reconciles with Clorinde. Tartaglia is apprehended by the Gardemeks; later acts of Chapter IV follow what happens to him. Neuvillette promises to look into the verdict himself.

Placement: Chapter IV Act II, added in version 4.0. It follows Prelude of Blancheur and Noirceur and precedes To the Stars Shining in the Depths. Story order equals release order.

141.comment: As Light Rain Falls Without Reason: Marcel and Vacher
141.content: In As Light Rain Falls Without Reason, Marcel, a wealthy man who moved to Fontaine after the disappearances began, is revealed to be Vacher, the man behind the dissolving of the girls. Marcel was the name his lover Vigneire picked for the child they never had. The Oceanid at the Fountain of Lucine that he finally meets is the merged consciousness of the women he dissolved together with Vigneire, and it drowns him.

142.comment: As Light Rain Falls Without Reason: Sinthe
142.content: A recreational drink popular in Fontaine around the time of Callas's trial. Navia concludes it was made with Primordial Seawater, and long-term drinkers showed signs of drug dependence that hurt their families. Callas banned it from his group.

143.comment: As Light Rain Falls Without Reason: Callas's duel
143.content: Three years before the act, Callas, head of Spina di Rosula, was accused of killing his friend Jacques and chose a duel over a trial. He kept fighting after he was hurt enough to lose, and Clorinde killed him. She says he asked her to keep Navia safe and that she could tell he wanted to die. Neuvillette later admits he let the duel proceed because he thought an innocent man would not die for justice.

144.content:
Astrolabos Chapter (also: Mona's Story Quest, Beyond This World's Stars, Astrology and the 50-Year Pact): Mona's Story Quest. A broke astrologer who knows the Traveler is not from Teyvat offers to read their fate if they help her reclaim a box her master left in Mondstadt. They travel from Liyue to Mondstadt, where the box's guardian turns out to be Klee, and Mona ends up renting a sealed laboratory.

The chapter has one act, Beyond This World's Stars, of three quests: Astrology and the 50-Year Pact, To Mondstadt and A Bewildering Fate. It was released in version 1.0 and unlocks at Adventure Rank 38 after Darknight Hero's Alibi (Noctua Chapter) and True Treasure (Trifolium Chapter).

The act is mostly comedy about Mona's lack of Mora against her confident astrology, with a thread connecting her to Klee's mother and her master's diary. The Traveler's sibling is the motive: Mona promises to look into the Traveler's destiny.

Plot: Outside Liyue Harbor Mona meets the Traveler and Paimon and says that, as a disciple, the Traveler can help her win a contest of astrology. She takes them through Liyue and over the Stone Gate to Mondstadt. There she names Klee as the guardian of her master's box, but the box holds only Klee's treasures; the real contents were a diary. Mona rents a sealed lab from Goth.

Astrology and the 50-Year Pact: Mona knows the Traveler is not of Teyvat. She wants to confront the guardian of her box to prove the power of astrology and thinks having a "disciple" helps. Before leaving she visits Mr. Zhu's inn, where he offers 20,000 Mora to find a ring a slime took. Mona first refuses, then agrees at the price. The Traveler uses leftover slime bait from the Darknight Hero's affair to draw the slimes, finds the ring and gives it back; Mona grabs the Mora, saying they must act the part of disciples.

To Mondstadt: at Wangshu Inn, Mona offers to treat them but is horrified at the cost; the Traveler and Paimon order many dishes while she asks for plain noodles. Her stomach betrays her. The Traveler cooks Golden Crab for her using a recipe from Huai'an, and she is delighted. On the road Tyler and some merchants offer them a ride, but Mona identifies them as bandits and defeats them herself. She says she reads Teyvat's people at a glance, whereas the Traveler is like an impenetrable fog to her.

A Bewildering Fate: in Mondstadt City, Klee arrives. Mona asks if her mother is Alice, then asks what she taught her; Klee knows only how to make Jumpy Dumpties. Klee remembers a fifty-year agreement and a box. The Traveler helps fetch it from Windrise, fighting Dendro slimes. Meanwhile Mona reads a diary that fell from Klee's bag. The box proves to hold only Klee's treasures, and the book is Mona's master's own diary, which she was told never to read. Klee flees. With no Mora or lab, Mona accepts help from Katheryne's commission board and dispels a Hydro seal on a house by astrology. The owner, Goth, rents it to her cheaply.

Details: Mona accepts Mr. Zhu's request after first refusing, and Paimon points out the contradiction. Mona claims she eats simple food so as not to be distracted. Mona wants to combine the box guardian's knowledge with her own work to read the Traveler's fate. At the box, Klee says she replaced the original contents with her own treasures. When the Traveler wonders if the guardian is Lisa, Mona does not pry. Paimon fears Mona will faint from hunger and suggests checking on her.

The contest Mona wanted with the guardian cannot happen, since Klee knows almost nothing of what Alice taught beyond Jumpy Dumpties. Goth expects to rent at the lowest possible price; Mona had hoped for the house for free, but the alternative is being homeless.

Revelations: The box guardian is Klee, and the box's original content was Mona's master's diary.

Mona is a friend of Klee's mother, per Mona's own question about Alice. She cannot read the Traveler's fate as she does others.

Mona was told never to read her master's diary and has now done so.

Characters: Mona, the Traveler, Paimon and Klee.

Katheryne and Goth in Mondstadt; Mr. Zhu, Yuhua and Huai'an in Liyue; Tyler and his bandit group.

Lisa is only wondered about by the Traveler. Alice is mentioned as Klee's mother.

Consequences: Mona now rents a lab in Mondstadt, though she can only look into the Traveler's fate later. Paimon suggests checking on her from time to time.

The act leaves her master's diary and the Traveler's fate unresolved.

Placement: Requires Adventure Rank 38 and both Darknight Hero's Alibi (Noctua Chapter) and True Treasure (Trifolium Chapter). The wiki notes Paimon reusing slime bait from the Darknight Hero story. Released in 1.0.

145.content: At the end of Mona's Story Quest she dispels a Hydro seal on an abandoned house with astrology. Its owner Goth then rents it to her at the lowest possible price, giving her a laboratory in Mondstadt.

146.content:
Autumn Winds, Scarlet Leaves (also: Chapter II Prologue, Inazuma Prologue, The Crux Clash, A Path Through the Storm, Follow the Wind): Autumn Winds, Scarlet Leaves is the prologue act of Archon Quest Chapter II, released in Version 1.6, and it is set in Liyue, at Liyue Harbor and Guyun Stone Forest. The Traveler wants to reach Inazuma, which is sealed off by storms and a strict isolation policy, and is sent to the Crux Fleet captain Beidou, who runs a tournament for fighters without Visions. The Traveler wins it, and in the process meets Kazuha, a wandering crew member who carries the Vision of a dead friend.

The act is a three-quest lead-in: A Path Through the Storm, The Crux Clash and Follow the Wind. It contains no Inazuman locations and no Electro Archon; its purpose is to set up the voyage (the prize is a berth on the Alcor) and to introduce Kazuha, who becomes a major figure in the Inazuma story.

Thematically it opens Chapter II's central question, what a Vision means and who it belongs to, through Kazuha's Masterless Vision, before the Vision Hunt Decree is shown directly in the next act.

Plot: Atsuko explains that besides the storm, outsiders face the Sakoku Decree and the authorities who would hunt them if found, but she cannot dissuade the Traveler and recommends Beidou. At the Alcor, anchored at Guyun Stone Forest, Beidou introduces a temporary crew member, Kazuha, and mistakes the Traveler for a tournament entrant. The Crux Clash is a martial contest for fighters without Visions. Its prize is a Masterless Vision supplied by Kazuha, who hopes the winner will reawaken it. The Traveler is not interested in the Vision, so Beidou adds a second option: the winner may choose the Vision or a ride to Inazuma on the Alcor.

At the arena, Zhuhan of the crew handles registration and is startled to see the Traveler who helped Liyue against an ancient god; the Traveler must prove they have no Vision. The first opponent, Jinyou, is easily beaten without elemental powers, and Beidou sends the Traveler straight to the semi-finals because so many new challengers now want to fight them. The semi-final opponent, Rongshi, is harder; he is not after the prize, only a worthy fight, and he accepts defeat humbly and asks for a rematch someday.

Nobody can say much about the finalist except that they are fast. Kazuha takes the Traveler somewhere quiet, reveals he already knows the Traveler can use elemental power without a Vision and, when the Traveler cannot explain how, tests them against slimes, and gives advice on the finalist's style and a little background on Inazuma and its Electro Archon.

On the day of the final the challenger does not appear, which annoys Beidou. Kazuha senses something is wrong, and the display box holding the Vision is empty. He offers to find it since it was his responsibility and goes with the Traveler to a Treasure Hoarder named Fei the Flyer, whom he had already identified. Fei says he had planned to win fairly but lost hope after seeing the Traveler beat Rongshi. He fights and loses. Kazuha threatens him with harsh punishment (breaking his arms under the law of the sea, branding him a thief), but when the cornered Fei still does not awaken the Vision, Kazuha lets him go and takes the Vision back.

Kazuha admits he had noticed the theft all along and had hoped Fei might resonate with the Vision, since gods usually grant Visions to those who show strength and resilience. He asks the Traveler to try, and the Traveler cannot either. Paimon asks why it matters so much to him. Kazuha explains that after the Raiden Shogun issued the Vision Hunt Decree, his friend, another Vision bearer who longed to face the Musou no Hitotachi, challenged the Vision Hunters to a duel before the throne and lost. Kazuha reached Tenshukaku as the duel ended and divine punishment was pronounced, snatched the dying Vision and fled, and has since kept it in the hope that it will awaken for someone, having heard rumours of Masterless Visions doing so.

Back at the arena, Zhuhan tells them that Ningguang has called Beidou back to Liyue Harbor because the tournament got out of hand; Kazuha explains that the thief was the Traveler's final opponent. Under the rules Fei is disqualified and the Traveler is declared champion. Kazuha warns that Inazuma will be harsher once they land, says the Alcor must resupply and will send word when it is ready, and goes off to travel Liyue in search of someone who can reawaken the Vision.

Details of the structure: the act has exactly three quests (A Path Through the Storm, The Crux Clash, Follow the Wind), and the first sets the tournament up while the second and third are the matches and the theft. The Traveler beats the first opponent without using any elemental power. Beidou, who has heard of the Traveler from Ningguang, is also the person who chooses to let the winner pick a voyage instead of the Vision.

Revelations: - The Vision Hunt Decree exists: the Raiden Shogun is confiscating Visions, and Kazuha's friend lost a duel before the throne opposing it and was struck down by divine punishment.
- Kazuha is a temporary Alcor crew member; the next act shows he is still a wanted fugitive, which keeps Beidou from lingering in port with him aboard.
- Masterless Visions, Visions whose bearers have died, are said to have reawakened for other people.
- Inazuma is hard to reach: a permanent storm, the Sakoku Decree, and pursuit by authorities.

- Kazuha already knows the Traveler can use elemental powers without a Vision; the Traveler cannot explain how.
- Beidou has been briefed on the Traveler by Ningguang, so the Qixing are aware of the Traveler's deeds.
- The tournament and its Vision prize are Kazuha's attempt to find a new bearer for his friend's Vision.

Characters: - **The Traveler and Paimon**: decide to go to Inazuma; the Traveler wins the tournament without a Vision.
- **Beidou**: captain of the Crux Fleet's flagship Alcor, who runs the Crux Clash.
- **Kazuha**: a temporary Alcor crew member who carries a dead friend's Vision.
- **Atsuko**: an Inazuman in Liyue Harbor, the only Inazuman the Traveler has met, who warns them about the trip.
- **Zhuhan**: crew member who registers tournament entrants.
- **Jinyou, Rongshi**: the Traveler's tournament opponents; Rongshi is a fighter who wanted only a challenge.
- **Fei the Flyer**: a Treasure Hoarder who steals the Vision.

Ningguang appears only by reference: her summons pulls Beidou from the arena at the end. The finalist the Traveler would have faced turns out to be Fei the Flyer, who never shows up for the match.

Consequences: The Traveler is champion and has a berth on the Alcor, which sails after resupplying. Kazuha keeps the Masterless Vision and sets out through Liyue to find someone who can reawaken it. The next act, The Immovable God and the Eternal Euthymia, begins with the sailing.

Kazuha does not travel with the Traveler at this point; he rejoins the Alcor and is aboard on arrival in Inazuma, where he is a wanted fugitive.

Placement: Released in Version 1.6 as the Prologue of Chapter II, before Inazuma opened in Version 2.0. It follows Chapter I Act IV, We Will Be Reunited, and leads into Chapter II Act I, The Immovable God and the Eternal Euthymia (Version 2.0). Story order and release order match.

Because the prologue came out in 1.6 and the rest of the chapter in 2.0, Kazuha and the Masterless Vision were introduced before Inazuma itself was playable.

147.comment: Autumn Winds, Scarlet Leaves: The Crux Clash
147.content:
A tournament held by Beidou at an arena in Guyun Stone Forest, where the Alcor is anchored, for renowned fighters without Visions. The prize is a Masterless Vision supplied by Kazuha; for the Traveler, Beidou adds a ride to Inazuma as an alternative. Entrants are registered by Zhuhan. The Traveler beats Jinyou and Rongshi, and wins the title when the finalist, Fei the Flyer, is disqualified for stealing the prize.

Beidou skips the Traveler past the first rounds because other fighters now want to face them. Rongshi enters only for the fight, not the prize.

148.comment: Autumn Winds, Scarlet Leaves: Kazuha's Masterless Vision
148.content: Kazuha carries the Vision of a friend who opposed the Vision Hunt Decree, lost a duel before the throne and suffered the Raiden Shogun's divine punishment. He offers it as the tournament prize in the hope that a new bearer will reawaken it. The Traveler and Fei both fail to resonate with it, so Kazuha keeps it. Later events in Inazuma decide its fate; this act does not.

149.comment: Autumn Winds, Scarlet Leaves: Fei the Flyer
149.content: A Treasure Hoarder who entered the Crux Clash intending to win, then stole the Vision after watching the Traveler fight. Kazuha traced him and the Traveler beat him. Kazuha threatens him with harsh punishment, partly to test whether pressure would awaken the Vision, then lets him go and takes the Vision back.

150.comment: Autumn Winds, Scarlet Leaves: Atsuko's Warning
150.content: Atsuko, the Inazuman the Traveler already knows in Liyue Harbor, tells them the storm is only part of the danger. Inazuma's isolation policy and the authorities who would pursue illegal entrants are the rest. She yields when the Traveler is determined and sends them to Beidou, whose seafaring experience may get a ship through.

key: Bantan Sango Case Files: The Warrior Dog
The Truth (Just About) Comes to Light
151.comment: Bantan Sango Case Files: The Warrior Dog
151.content:
Bantan Sango Case Files: The Warrior Dog (also: The Warrior Dog, Mystery of the Black Shadow, Stealthy Trail, The Truth (Just About) Comes to Light, Black Shadow case, Ubiquity Net event): Four case files unlock over several days. In each, Ryuuji marks camps in the wild; at some the Traveler fights Treasure Hoarders and other armed groups to free caged animals, and at others must sneak past the dog using a gadget, the Ubiquity Net, which Sango had made and which can catch small animals but is too weak for criminals. The final file explains the Hoarders' plan, introduces the dog's true name Kageroumaru, and ends with Kageroumaru accepting the Traveler as his ninken.

Requirements were Adventure Rank 30 and the Archon Quest "The Immovable God and the Eternal Euthymia". Rewards came from stages in Tatarasuna, Fort Fujitou, Inazuma City, Chinju Forest and Kannazuka, and included Primogems and the event's Kageroumaru reward.

Plot: Case 1, "Mystery of the Black Shadow": the first camp is guarded by the dog; Ryuuji places smoke and fireworks devices to help the Traveler sneak in. A second camp is held by Treasure Hoarders and other armed groups. Case 2, "Stealthy Trail": Ryuuji marks new camps from Sango's deductions and, as an example of her method, recounts an earlier theft case in which the thief was caught because he sold fresh Naku Weed; Sango had reasoned he would not leave Narukami Island because boat travel was policed under the Sakoku Decree. Case 3, "The Truth (Just About) Comes to Light": the leads run cold with only about half the animals found, and Ryuuji reports Sango's puzzling instructions to investigate odd places. Case 4, "Recognition": Sango sends the Traveler to meet Ryuuji, who has been scouting Yashiori Island, where the Hoarders have just left a camp of cages behind.

Ryuuji explains Sango's deduction: the Hoarders were stealing dogs to train as treasure-hunting hounds, after an earlier attempt to train weasels failed. The Traveler fights the returning Hoarders. The dog, who seems unwilling to attack them, leads the group to an old letter left by a ninken trainer, addressed to anyone who finds it, asking for someone to look after Kageroumaru, who was too weak as a young dog to be paired with a ninja yet grew strong through training. The trainer's pact instructions are crossed out. Kageroumaru then attacks in an old house, and the Traveler defeats him. Under the ninken custom Ryuuji describes, a dog must acknowledge a stronger master, so Kageroumaru now follows the Traveler.

Paimon extracts a promise that Kageroumaru will not replace her as best companion. Ryuuji asks why a dog would steal and then protect animals, and Sango answers with her hypothesis (see uncertainties). She tells the Traveler that praise will not earn a discount on future commissions, and says "sentimentality is the enemy of truth". The Ubiquity Net feedback goes to the friend who built it.

Revelations: Two separate groups were behind the disappearances: Treasure Hoarders who held animals in "Dens of Thieves", and the dog Kageroumaru, who kept animals in "Hiding Spots". Kageroumaru's past as a ninken trainer's abandoned pup is revealed only through the letter in the last file. The event itself offers no confirmed reason why he hid the animals.

Characters: Sango is the agency's detective who prefers to think rather than walk; her stance is that her "flesh is an accessory to her mind". Ryuuji is her polite, practical investigator whose skill is running errands, not stealth or combat. He admits being bested by the dog and gives it nicknames such as "Hat Dog" that Paimon dislikes. Katheryne relays the commission. Paimon is awed by the bounty and persuaded by the animals' plight. Kageroumaru is a masked dog who resembles the Komore Teahouse owner Taroumaru; Ryuuji warns that, unlike Taroumaru, nothing is known about him. Ryuuji also mentions Shikanoin of the Tenryou Commission, whom the agency met before and whom he thinks can follow Sango's reasoning.

Consequences: The animals are returned to their owners by Ryuuji, the Treasure Hoarders' dog-training plan is exposed, and the Traveler gains Kageroumaru as a reward item. Sango considers the case closed.

Placement: Released in Version 2.3 and set after the Inazuma Archon Quest chapter's Immovable God and the Eternal Euthymia, which is its only requirement. Not needed for any Archon Quest.

152.comment: Bantan Sango Case Files: The Warrior Dog: Kageroumaru
152.content: Kageroumaru is a scarred, masked dog introduced as the "Black Shadow" in the Bantan Sango Case Files event. He was a weak puppy overlooked when ninja chose ninken, then grew strong. He guards caged small animals and attacks intruders, and finally accepts the Traveler as his master after being defeated. The wiki lists Kageroumaru as an event reward.

153.comment: Bantan Sango Case Files: The Warrior Dog: Bantan Sango Detective Agency staff
153.content: In this event the agency is represented by Sango, a deductive-minded detective who stays behind and issues commissions, and Ryuuji, her investigator. Sango had a friend build the Ubiquity Net from records of Kamuna Onmyoudou.

154.comment: Bantan Sango Case Files: The Warrior Dog: Treasure Hoarder dog-training plan
154.content: In the final case file, Ryuuji says Sango deduced that the Hoarders planned to steal dogs to train as Treasure Hunting Hounds, after weasels proved too difficult to train. Their camps appear as Dens of Thieves in the event.

key: Battlefield of Dice, Cats, and Cards
155.comment: Battlefield of Dice, Cats, and Cards
155.content:
Battlefield of Dice, Cats, and Cards (also: Come Try Genius Invokation TCG!, Genius Invokation TCG introduction quest): The quest begins in Mondstadt's alchemy shop, where Sucrose has received a package of strange cards from a Sumeru scholar. Timaeus explains that they belong to a popular game and sends the group to The Cat's Tail. There Margaret's staff, the cat Prince and his translator Shuyun, arrange a tutorial with Diona and a three-duel test. The tone is comic and light, and it works as an in-world welcome to the game.

It requires Adventure Rank 30 and the completion of the Prologue's Act III, Song of the Dragon and Freedom. Its last scene leads straight into the next quest, A Guest From Liyue, which begins in the same place.

Plot: Timaeus and Sucrose are discussing a package Sucrose received, probably a thank-you gift from a Sumeru scholar who had studied in Mondstadt. It contains only cards, among them one showing Sucrose herself. When the Traveler and Paimon join, Timaeus explains that these are cards for Genius Invokation TCG, a game said to have been invented by an Akademiya scholar and now popular everywhere. He admits he has been reading a light-novel series based on it, and he has promised himself not to touch the game until his research is further along, so he recommends The Cat's Tail, where players gather to play and trade.

At the tavern Margaret mentions that more TCG players now come in and that she has put Prince, her cat, and Shuyun in charge of looking after them. Shuyun claims to understand Prince's meows and passes on his remarks, including lofty refusals to play himself. Margaret hands the teaching to Diona, who grumbles that the game encourages drinking yet agrees once Shuyun argues that it might actually help her campaign against Mondstadt's wine trade. Sucrose, Paimon and the Traveler have no proper deck, so Diona lends them a pair of character cards a customer left behind. She walks them through a first game, in which the player controls Diluc, covering dice, skills, elemental reactions and winning by defeating all of the opponent's characters. Sucrose and the Traveler then play a practice duel against each other, and Sucrose loses and takes it a little hard.

Shuyun explains that becoming an official player recognised by the Genius Invokation TCG Society requires beating three opponents; the practice duel counts toward the tally. Everyone starting out gets a free Casket of Tomes, which Margaret hands over. The Casket can sense other nearby Caskets, which leads the Traveler to a Knight of Favonius named Swan on duty at the city entrance. Swan agrees to duel and loses. Prince, via Shuyun, chooses the final opponent: Fischl, who is also a beginner with two wins. The Traveler beats her. Fischl gives the Traveler her own Character Card as a prize, and Sucrose, who has won two games herself, joins Fischl for a game. Shuyun then explains what official players get: a TCG Player's Handbook, access to Genius Invokation merchandise at The Cat's Tail and the Invitation Board for challenging friends.

Details. Timaeus summarises the light novel (published by Yae Publishing House in Inazuma) in which a young man in Sumeru finds a Casket of Tomes in his attic, releasing the soul of an ancient player called the Crocodile King, who once served King Deshret and was sealed away after losing to the Ibis King. Sucrose also remarks that Timaeus once asked for a deadline extension for "personal reasons". Margaret refers to Diona as "Little Diona". Sucrose mentions in passing that Margaret had earlier refused to sell her fur from The Cat's Tail staff for an experiment; the quest does not explain further. Shuyun says that all card cases in the game are called Caskets of Tomes, and Paimon's guess that each holds an ancient player's soul is a joke; the Caskets work through a mechanism invented by Sumeru scholars.

Other players in the tavern react to the Traveler before they are officially recognised: Gary, Belen, Makri, Nanaya Yuumi and Atra each say something about the game, for instance that Gary and Belen will duel the Traveler once the Traveler becomes an official player. Swan only duels because he calls himself a fellow TCG player, even though he is on guard duty. Fischl, speaking in her usual grand manner, addresses herself as Prinzessin and her bird Oz as her familiar, and Oz translates her bluster into plain meaning. After losing she blames the "cursed dragon" for hiding the threads of fate from her vision.

Characters: The Traveler and Paimon; Sucrose, an alchemist who gets involved through the package; Timaeus, her colleague, who introduces the game; Margaret, owner of The Cat's Tail; Diona, a bartender at the tavern who teaches the tutorial; Prince and Shuyun, the tavern's cat and his translator who run the TCG corner; Swan, a Knight of Favonius and opponent; and Fischl with her companion Oz, the final opponent. Diluc appears only as a character card.

Diona is the one who teaches the rules. She wants to "destroy Mondstadt's wine industry" because she dislikes drinking, which the quest plays for humour. Fischl is also learning the game, having won two duels before facing the Traveler.

Consequences: The Traveler becomes an official TCG player: the TCG mode opens, and the Traveler receives the Casket of Tomes, a tutorial deck and Fischl's Character Card. Quest rewards are 60 Primogems, 2 Hero's Wit, 20,000 Mora, the Casket of Tomes and a Beginner Player Badge. Completing it also grants the achievement Visible, Yet Invisible.

Rewards and achievements are gameplay content, not in-world fact.

Placement: Released in Version 3.3 together with the TCG's introduction. It requires Adventure Rank 30 and the Prologue's Act III, Song of the Dragon and Freedom. It is a self-contained comic quest and not part of the Archon Quests; the next quest, A Guest From Liyue, starts immediately after.

156.comment: Battlefield of Dice, Cats, and Cards: Genius Invokation TCG tutorial at The Cat's Tail
156.content: In Mondstadt, Genius Invokation TCG is taught and played at The Cat's Tail, where Margaret keeps a corner for players. To be recognised by the Genius Invokation TCG Society a newcomer must win duels against three opponents; each new player receives a Casket of Tomes, which senses other nearby Caskets and so helps players find each other. The tavern staff Prince the cat and Shuyun, his translator, oversee new players.

157.content:
Bedtime Story (also: Chapter IV Act VI, Vimara Village missing-person case): Bedtime Story is the sixth and final act of Chapter IV, the Traveler's Archon Quest chapter (version 4.7). A commission from Katheryne in Sumeru City asks for help finding a missing man from Vimara Village whom no one can name. Investigating, the Traveler and Paimon meet Dainsleif, who tells them about the Five Sinners of Khaenri'ah, and finally meet Caribert, Chlothar Alberich's son, whose residual consciousness is tied to the Loom of Fate.

The act has three quests: Cold Case Commission, Memories That Should Not Exist and World-Order Narration. It requires Adventure Rank 40. It resolves the missing-person mystery, explains what the Loom of Fate is, and gives the Traveler a conversation with their sibling that they will not remember.

The sibling appears inside Caribert's memory world and cannot touch the Traveler. The act closes Chapter IV on the sibling's loneliness, and the Traveler leaves with only a photograph as evidence.

Plot: **Cold Case Commission.** Katheryne in Sumeru City explains that Vimara Village jointly issued the commission and that the villagers can give only his general appearance. Bahram calls him very kind and always willing to help; Amadhiah says he accompanied the elderly and played with the orphans. The Traveler suspects he exists only in memory. Atossa describes him as the family she never had and notes that it was always dusk when they met.

**Memories That Should Not Exist.** Dainsleif lists the Five Sinners and says that if they had joined him they could have stopped the Vinster King; the Traveler reminds him of his promise to explain the voice. He believes the Loom of Fate is closely related to the Ley Lines. The next day he is agitated by the foreign memory. At the eye's location a new memory distracts him; sensing a disturbance in the Ley Lines he sends the Traveler away. The sibling tells Dainsleif that sending an army when the Twilight Sword was ready would have spelled its own demise, so they came alone; if he wants to talk, he must beat them first.

**World-Order Narration.** Caribert planned to say farewell to Atossa and leaves her a message instead.
