He says his father, Chlothar Alberich, told him he would become the Loom of Fate, but he was only used for its construction, died when it was set in motion at the age of eight, and is now residual consciousness within it; his adult form is imagined from his father's appearance. After he fades, the sibling shares a short conversation with the Traveler. The villagers found the sleeping Traveler at the outskirts and carried them to the village; Paimon says Dainsleif came to check on them, seemingly injured and with a lot on his mind. Caribert's last implanted memory has the villagers recall seeing him sleeping under the tree at dusk before his parents came and they all left together; they now remember his name, and Atossa hopes he will return one day. In the photograph Caribert urges the two to get along whatever happens.

Further details. A dozen earlier attempts at the commission had ended in failure. Dainsleif says the Sinners' failure to defend Khaenri'ah is something he will never forgive and always remember despite the erosion of his memories. The sibling explains that neither twin belongs in Caribert's space, which is why they are intangible, and that with Caribert gone neither will remember the reunion. They say Dainsleif hesitated to raise his sword against them, without which they might still be no match for him, and that at the end of their journey they reached the Sea of Flowers at the End. The Heavenly Principles have shown no activity in the five hundred years since the cataclysm.

Revelations: - The Sinner's voice belongs to Vedrfolnir, "the Visionary", Dainsleif's older brother and one of the Five Sinners of Khaenri'ah, alongside Rhinedottir, Surtalogi, Rerir and Hroptatyr.
- Dainsleif holds the other Sinners responsible for not defending Khaenri'ah when the cataclysm came.
- The Loom of Fate is a device whose primitive form creates and implants memories and whose full form creates Ley Lines and changes the world.
- Caribert, son of Chlothar Alberich, was used to construct the Loom and survives only as residual consciousness tied to it; he built the Vimara Village life for himself and calmed the hilichurls with a bedtime story.
- Dainsleif had carried the first Field Tiller's eye inside his body; a false memory implanted by Caribert let the Abyss Order obtain it.
- The sibling is rushing to finish the Loom before the Heavenly Principles awaken, which did not happen when the Divine Throne of Hydro was destroyed.

- The sibling misses the Traveler but struggles to face themselves as their war continues; the Traveler will not remember the talk.

Characters: The Traveler and Paimon, Dainsleif, the sibling, Caribert, Katheryne, Atossa, Bahram, Amadhiah and a Pyro Abyss Mage. The Five Sinners are named; Vedrfolnir is a voice rather than a speaker.

Consequences: Caribert says the Loom of Fate is completed. The Traveler's meeting with the sibling is erased from their memory but a photograph remains. Dainsleif, having lost the eye, is left injured and preoccupied after facing the sibling. Chapter V follows in Natlan.

Villagers recall Caribert as someone who left with his parents, and Atossa hopes he will return.

Placement: Chapter IV, Act VI (final act), released in 4.7. It follows Masquerade of the Guilty and precedes Flowers Resplendent on the Sun-Scorched Sojourn (Chapter V Act I). The Caribert act (3.5) showed Caribert as Chlothar Alberich's son in the sibling's memories; here he refers to that memory himself.

158.comment: Bedtime Story: Caribert and the Loom of Fate
158.content: Caribert, Chlothar Alberich's son, was used to construct the sibling's Loom of Fate and survives as residual consciousness tied to it. Through the half-finished Loom he created a false life in Vimara Village with memories implanted in the villagers, and gave the hilichurls a calming bedtime story. He explains that a fully unlocked Loom weaves Ley Lines and can change the world, and he fades away peacefully as the sibling arrives.

159.comment: Bedtime Story: Dainsleif on the Five Sinners
159.content: Dainsleif names the Sinner as his older brother Vedrfolnir, the Visionary, and lists Rhinedottir, Surtalogi, Rerir and Hroptatyr. He blames them for abandoning Khaenri'ah and says he will not forgive them, though his memories erode.

key: Beneath the Lunar Sea world quest
160.content:
Beneath the Lunar Sea (also: Beneath the Lunar Sea world quest, Curtain-Form Blackbody Containment Lab quest): A Frost Moon world quest from Version 6.7 (Luna VIII). A frightened kuuhenki and a crowd of moonglow jellyfish lead the Traveler and Paimon to a sealed, dragon-built facility beneath the Moontide Sea, the Curtain-Form Blackbody Containment Lab. Restoring its power opens the way to a hidden chamber with a great blue tree.

The quest is a short, mostly exploratory scene with almost no story revelation. Its practical effect is to unlock an Ancient Moon's Remnant (the Frost Moon's reputation-style monument) at the lab, and it ends with the Traveler loading the facility's map from a terminal.

Its lore value is atmosphere: it shows that the dragons' ancient moon works still lie buried in the lunar sea and still respond to Archaeolune Energy, and it plants the name of the lab that later terminal records connect to the dragons' work on hiding the moon.

Plot: Paimon spots a scared kuuhenki, and after the Traveler beats the monster harassing it, the creature guides them toward a cave. Jellyfish crowd into the cave too. Inside is a locked facility; the Traveler finds how to open it, gets the power back on and enters.

The kuuhenki leads the pair twice, each time after the Traveler defeats a hostile construct (a Precursor's Secret Source Matrix of Overseer Network). Paimon is uneasy that the place is hiding something, then reads the sign at the entrance, a Blackbody Containment "Generation Station", which she has never heard of. She decides a place like that must hold treasure.

Inside, a door to the Curtain-Form Blackbody Containment stays shut until an Ancient Moon Pearl is returned to its station. The Traveler frees trapped moonglow jellyfish, switches on a backup power generator and the Archaeolune-affinitive materials, and opens an energy barrier on the ceiling with Archaeolune Ripples. A lift lowers a storage chest but the pearl does not drop, so the Traveler must fire the pearl back to its station with a launcher to open the door.

Beyond the door is a large chamber with a huge blue tree. Paimon is struck that something so beautiful could be hidden under the lunar sea and wonders what the dragons did there. The Traveler activates the facility terminal, which loads the area map, and the quest ends. Gameplay notes: the early cave stretch has two optional exquisite chests; the rewards are Adventure EXP, 30 Primogems, Mora, Hero's Wit and enhancement ore.

Step order for reference: help the kuuhenki (defeat one construct), follow it, help it again (defeat another), follow it into the cave; at the gate return the Ancient Moon Pearl; inside, free the jellyfish (two constructs), power the generator and Archaeolune-affinitive materials, open the ceiling barrier with Archaeolune Ripples, launch the pearl; talk to Paimon; activate the terminal. The facility lies in the Moontide Sea area of the Frost Moon.

Revelations: No question is answered in the quest itself. It establishes only that a dragon-era installation survives under the Moontide Sea, that its machinery still takes Archaeolune Energy, and that it is guarded by constructs. Paimon does not know what the name means.

Terminal records at the lab, read outside the quest, describe a "Curtain-Form Blackbody Containment" that was tested during the early phase of Project Lunar Veil, an effort to hide the moon behind a veil. They tie the lab's work to the dragons' study of a black substance from the Stellar Blackbody, a creature from beyond the stars. These records are lore on the wiki's location page, not something the quest dialogue says. See quest.moon-gazing for the larger story.

One record describes the Curtain-Form Blackbody Containment as being tested while Ninnin, a young artificial lifeform raised by the researcher Lusalim, could barely speak; she let slip the words "Lunar Veil", which Lusalim took as the project's name. Another record says Blackbody Matter, the black filaments found on the hull of the spaceship Moongazer, reacts with Archaeolune Energy and can fuse with plants and animals, turning some blue creatures black. Neither record is cited by the quest, and neither explains why the lab was buried or sealed.

Characters: The Traveler and Paimon. The only other presences are a frightened kuuhenki, moonglow jellyfish and the facility's guardian constructs.

Paimon supplies all the dialogue: curiosity, treasure-hunting optimism and a growing sense that the place is hiding something. The kuuhenki are small creatures of Archaeolune Energy native to the Frost Moon.

Consequences: Completing the quest is required to unlock the Ancient Moon's Remnant at the Curtain-Form Blackbody Containment Lab, a Moontide Sea monument where Luna Sigils can be offered, and gives the map of the facility. No lasting change in the world or to any character follows.

Placement: Released in Version 6.7 (Luna VIII, 2026-07-01) with the Frost Moon map. It is part of the Frost Moon exploration content that accompanies the Moon Gazing series, and the wiki marks no formal prerequisite or next quest. In story terms it takes place after the Traveler has reached the Frost Moon and before or alongside the Moontide Sea events of Moon Gazing's second and third acts.

key: Between Pledge and Forgettance World Quest series
161.content:
Between Pledge and Forgettance (also: Between Pledge and Forgettance World Quest series, Little One's volcano pilgrimage quests, Rite of the Bold, Revelations from the Past): Between Pledge and Forgettance (5.0) is a three-quest Natlan world series: Lost in the Woods, Rite of the Bold and Revelations from the Past. The Traveler and Paimon free a hurt young Tepetlisaurus from a barrier, travel with it, and learn from the researcher Manqu that the red mark on its horn is the Flamelord's Blessing, a power that often kills or maddens saurians as they grow. A volcano pilgrimage with two tokens is the only known remedy. Chief Pacal of the Children of Echoes grants the first token after a duel, and the ruins of the Sage of the Stolen Flame yield the first Golden Entreaty after trials in which human and saurian must act as a pair. The series is tied to a deliberate design by the Sage that only the later Natlan quests expose.

The series opens the long Little One thread that runs through the Natlan world quests: Lost in the Woods is triggered by shining pillars after arrival in Natlan, Rite of the Bold is gated behind Shadows of the Mountains and Tale of Dreams Plucked From Fire, and Revelations from the Past follows automatically. Its murals are the first place the Traveler sees the Sage's pledge with Xbalanque and a vision of the fall of Xiuhcoatl.

The wiki's end-of-series recollection summarises it as the Traveler and Little One each enduring the test and obtaining one of the two Golden Entreaties. The second Entreaty comes from Lost Traveler in the Ashen Realm, and both are offered together in the finale series, A Finale Emberforged.

Plot: Lost in the Woods. Shining pillars scattered around Natlan pull the Traveler and Paimon into a strange space full of Rifthounds. After the fight, a dying giant saurian addresses golden words to a "Chosen of Dragons" and, as the Traveler reaches out, the Traveler's consciousness enters the beast's body (a Saurian Indwelling). Using it, the Traveler breaks a rock that holds a trapped saurian whelp. Paimon bandages its tail with a scarf, and the whelp agrees to travel with the party. The player names it; the default name is Little One.

Rite of the Bold. Manqu, a researcher of the Saurian Relics Association, warns the party that the red mark on the whelp's horn is the Flamelord's Blessing, which saurians no longer survive well in the modern age, and that the Wayob and the Night Kingdom reject such saurians. He suggests handing it to the Children of Echoes, but when the Traveler refuses to abandon a companion, he reveals a legend: a warrior must bring the saurian to the volcano carrying a token that was split in two. Chief Pacal and Manqu then explain the pilgrimage custom. Pacal waives the old rituals of feather, pelts, fifty victories and ninety-six gems and instead tests the Traveler and Little One in a duel, with his own saurian Uchu fighting beside him. Defeated, he gives them the Talisman of Waxaklahun Ubah Kan, a name of the Sage of the Stolen Flame.

Revelations from the Past. At the ruins entrance, Abyss-tainted Rifthounds attack. Placing the talisman starts the Sage's trial. The Traveler and Little One are split between two viewpoints in the ruins. They solve puzzles using colour-coded crystals, cross a lava stretch, and enter Catastrophe's Edge, where they fight off enemies from the Abyss. At the end they receive the first Golden Entreaty.

The ruins are guided by golden text addressed to the "Chosen of Dragons". In the Audience Hall a mural shows a dragon and a human each holding a golden ring. Manqu has already said the Sage believed humans could lead saurians to a better future than the dragons' age, perhaps from guilt at having stolen phlogiston secrets from dragonkind. The golden text says the pledge with Xbalanque was made at Catastrophe's Edge, and invites the Chosen to prove themselves there.

Rite of the Bold only starts after Manqu has been met and two in-game days have passed since Shadows of the Mountains and Tale of Dreams Plucked From Fire were finished. If the player has completed Lost Traveler in the Ashen Realm, a recollection plays during the later quests. In Revelations from the Past Paimon first wonders whether the golden text meant "chosen by the great Tepetlisaurus" and then whether the Sage himself is a dragon.

Revelations: - The Flamelord's Blessing is real and dangerous: in Manqu's account it is a power of the old dragons that modern saurians cannot withstand, and the pilgrimage is the only remedy.
- The Sage of the Stolen Flame and the first Pyro Archon each brought back one token from the volcano; whoever holds both can enter the cleansing fire. Pacal says the Sage seems to appear in tales from the tribal era to Ochkanatlan and beyond.
- The Sage's murals imply he was a dragon, and show the Sage and Xbalanque each holding a golden disc.

A mural showing a giant black dragon, a tree and a figure gives the Traveler a vision of Nibelung sunk into the Abyss, of the Irminsul nearly withering, and of the fall of the Sacred City of Tollan, where a giant dragon with pierced pupils and a tiny human fall together and a man later rises from the dragon's heart wreathed in flame. A voice says the vision is not meant for the Traveler.

In the final room golden lines show a split seal: the dragon's eye cut in two by a human's sword, one disc given to the "silver dragon" and one to the "resurrected corpse", one buried beneath a great monument and one swallowed by the headstrong one. A further vision shows Och-Kan lifting a disc before the empty throne of Ochkanatlan, and the two discs merge into one golden seal. The quest speaks only in the golden text; the identification with Kukulkan, Xbalanque, Xiuhcoatl and Och-Kan comes from the later quests and the wiki's annotations.

Characters: The Traveler and Paimon travel with Little One, a young Tepetlisaurus who speaks only in growls. Manqu of the Saurian Relics Association is the scholarly guide. Pacal, chief of the Children of Echoes, is jovial, strong and protective of guests. His saurian is Uchu. Titu is mentioned as someone who spoke highly of the Traveler. The Sage of the Stolen Flame (Waxaklahun Ubah Kan, later revealed as Kukulkan) appears only through golden text.

Manqu is formal and blunt, apologising often for clumsy phrasing, and wants the pilgrimage to succeed partly to prove that old inscriptions remain true. Pacal dislikes pushing guests into a fiery pit to test a theory, but accepts the Traveler after seeing the party's resolve and Little One's reaction.

Consequences: The Traveler holds the first Golden Entreaty and gains the avatar "Your Saurian companion!". Little One stays with the party. The second Entreaty comes from Lost Traveler in the Ashen Realm. Offering both is the next step towards the volcano (see Path to the Flaming Peaks and A Finale Emberforged). The series also opens the many Little One side quests in In the Footsteps of the Chosen of Dragons.

Rite of the Bold awards the achievement The Legend of the Legendary Heroes. In the wiki's quest chain Revelations from the Past leads on to The Road Ahead.

Placement: Released in 5.0 with Natlan. In story order Lost in the Woods usually comes first, Rite of the Bold after the party has spent time in Natlan, and Revelations from the Past last. The series connects directly to Lost Traveler in the Ashen Realm (the next chapter), Path to the Flaming Peaks, Chronicler of the Crumbling City and A Finale Emberforged, which resolve it.

162.comment: Between Pledge and Forgettance: Talisman of Waxaklahun Ubah Kan
162.content:
The Talisman of Waxaklahun Ubah Kan is the proof Pacal gives the Traveler after the duel in Rite of the Bold. Waxaklahun Ubah Kan is a name of the Sage of the Stolen Flame, whom later quests reveal to be Kukulkan. Pacal admits he cannot remember the long name. The talisman is placed on a platform at the ruins entrance to open the Sage's trial.

Pacal and Manqu recall that after Xiuhcoatl died and the first Pyro Archon was revived, the Sage and the Archon each brought back one volcanic token. Both are required to enter the cleansing fire.

163.comment: Between Pledge and Forgettance: Flamelord's Blessing
163.content:
The Flamelord's Blessing is the red mark on Little One's horn. In Manqu's explanation it grants strength, swimming speed or leaping, but is not the saurian's own power. It is the strength of the ancient dragons, which modern saurians cannot bear, so growth can kill them or drive them mad. The Wayob and the Night Kingdom refuse to accept saurians marked this way. The Flamelord is the Pyro Dragon Sovereign, Xiuhcoatl.

Pacal calls it more curse than blessing. The later finale quest shows the Sage's own account is more complicated: he says the mark proves the dragon bloodline is unchanged, and that the promise of removing it was a lie of omission.

164.comment: Between Pledge and Forgettance: Volcanic pilgrimage
164.content: The old pilgrimage required a warrior and saurian to be recognised by the saurian's tribal chief, who for Tepetlisauri is the chief of the Children of Echoes. The ritual tasks Manqu lists include a green quetzal feather, a stole of pelts, fifty victories for the tribe and ninety-six gems. Pacal drops them and fights the Traveler instead, with Uchu, in the duel grounds in the mountain behind the Stadium of the Sacred Flame. He warns that no one has returned from this road.

165.content:
Beyond Silver and Fine Gold (also: Nicole's treasure hunt, Nicole's Witch's Lodge series): A Version 6.6 world quest series about Nicole. After the Traveler and Paimon unlock her Witch's Lodge in the Witch's Garden, Nicole turns its rooms into a treasure hunt: each of four rooms hides three golden feathers and a chest, and each room opens a week after the last. Between the puzzles she tells stories about her angelic past, the Hexenzirkel and her friends.

The four parts are The Joyous Floating Island, The Silent Theater, The Lost Palace and The Forgotten Lighthouse. They require the earlier Witch's Lodge quest and must be done in order; the next room unlocks at 04:00 on the Monday after the previous one is fully explored, so the series takes four weeks. The tone is light and teasing, but several rooms turn serious about angels, gods and betrayal.

Structurally the series is a gift: Nicole, whose duty as an angel was to guide people to treasure, invents a way to do it for friends. The wiki's quest page itself notes that each room must be fully explored before the next opens.

Plot: Nicole invites the Traveler and Paimon to her lodge. She has built a room full of tricks and hidden three feathers in it; finding them reveals a treasure chest. A new room opens each week: a tea party where everyone shrinks, a studio of magic paintings, a shrine of angel statues and a tall study full of books that make stairways when Nicole speaks.

The Joyous Floating Island: Nicole explains she wants a place to have fun and feel useful at once. A door with floating teacups sends the pair into the Great Mage's Tea Party, where they are shrunk to teacup scale. They heat a giant teapot with Pyro, sweeten a cup with three sugar cubes (Nicole mentions Alice takes three, Anya one, Barbeloth none), fend off a statue of a Mandragora Nicole animates, and open the chest.

The Silent Theater: a studio of empty frames. Three paintings pull the pair into scenes Nicole narrates: the day she agreed to join the Hexenzirkel, a love-and-horror tale of a Princess of the Morning Star, and her admiration for Anya and the stories of Simulanka. When each is "restored", the chest opens.

The Lost Palace: Nicole is busy elsewhere (she is selling sculptures at a stall in Fontaine), so she leaves scrolls with riddle hints; the pair arrange statues to follow them. Afterwards Nicole shows them the shrine where she lived as an angel.

The Forgotten Lighthouse: the final room. Nicole tries to explain why she is embarrassed, tells a fragment of the story of the first time the mages challenged the Anemo Archon, and hides the feathers at the top of a study. Words spoken aloud become golden platforms, and the Traveler and Paimon climb to the feathers on the stairs she speaks into existence.

Details of the puzzles: in the tea room the teapot rises into the air to pour each cup and the feathers appear in sequence; in the theatre each emblem on a frame (a witch's emblem, a Domain emblem, the emblem of Simulanka) leads to a painting; in the palace the three scroll hints describe statue placements in plain riddles (a bird "walking the field", a creature in the valley, a choir that gazes toward the voice); in the lighthouse the platforms are words Nicole speaks aloud ("leave it to me", "let light shine the way ahead", "go up from here"). When Paimon complains that Nicole shouted, Nicole jokes about turning trinkets into turnips, then ends the quest with a teasing telling of a dark ending that Paimon objects to because "words are magic here."

Dialogue touches worth keeping: in the tea room the stone Mandragora statue begins to move stiffly, Nicole calls it a minor technical difficulty and turns it into a real Mandragora, then uses her burst when Paimon asks for help; in the theatre she says she did not attend her first Hexenzirkel tea in person and "concluded" Alice was punishing her for hesitating; in the palace she vows to chase a thief who stole her sculptures all the way to the Fortress of Meropide; and in the lighthouse she mutters that she hopes Alice never hears the story. The Silent Theater also mentions a painting of Simulanka with light novels from Yae Publishing House on the floor, and a cameo of Mr. Nine, her old Seelie friend, who is pushing her to read.

Revelations: Nicole is an angel, a being created to love all living things and to guide and enlighten. She says the angels' emotions were crude and that a successful mission gave them a joyous relief that was their strongest feeling. In her own words, completing the mission she is "burdened with" is why she is happy to guide others to treasure.

Alice was the only person in the Hexenzirkel who knew Nicole's true identity when Nicole first attended a tea party, and Nicole decided to join them only after talking to Alice privately inside Alice's head.

In the Silent Theater Nicole says the first angel's betrayal happened beneath an Irminsul bough. She tells, with the names withheld, that a star-wandering traveller visited the Princess of the Morning Star in a silver tree, taught her free will and love, and that the gods destroyed the lovers' home; the princess lost her power and wisdom and even her closest friends were cursed. She insists the story is true.

In the Lost Palace she says the shrine was her home when she was an angel and that she loved telling the other angels about life among humans, sending omens and guiding people to build civilisations. A statue in the lodge's studio, after the quest, has Nicole say she can reassure her "sisters" that humans now live comfortably.

In the Lighthouse she hints at a story about the first time the mages challenged the Anemo Archon, which she finds embarrassing; the Traveler hears only the fragment.

Characters: Nicole is the host. The Traveler and Paimon are the guests and the only voices besides hers. Alice, Anya, Barbeloth, Rhinedottir and Ivanovna of the Hexenzirkel, and an old Seelie friend, are mentioned but do not appear.

Nicole is playful, verbose and slightly self-congratulating, and she talks to herself aloud when she thinks no one is listening. She calls herself an expert at hiding things, enjoys making the pair work for treasure, and is at her most sincere when she mentions the Hexenzirkel and the angels. Paimon plays straight woman, delighted by every chest and wary of Nicole's pranks.

Consequences: Each part unlocks one more room of the Witch's Lodge and a chest; the Forgotten Lighthouse completes the series. Afterwards Nicole says there is nothing left to give for "a few hundred years". The lodge's rooms also gain small Nicole-only interactions (a Mandragora statue, a painting that burns away to show the witches around their table in Dodoco form, an angel statue, a bookshelf that leads to a Mora chest).

The other Hexenzirkel members are not shown reacting. The series is also notable as the time Nicole's past as an angel is told directly to the player rather than hinted.

Wiki-listed mechanics, kept brief: the Pyro Traveler is a trial character in the tea room, theatre and lighthouse; Nicole is a trial character in the tea party's early steps. The final Mora chest from the lodge bookshelf (200,000 Mora) is a post-quest interaction, found by observing the study's bookshelf as Nicole.

Placement: Released in Version 6.6 (Luna VII, 2026-05-20) alongside Nicole's debut as a playable character. It requires the Witch's Lodge world quest from Luna IV (6.3). It sits outside the Archon Quest chain and has no story effect on it.

166.content:
Beyond the Smoke and Mirrors (also: Chapter V Act III, Natlan Archon Quest Act III): Beyond the Smoke and Mirrors is the third act of Chapter V, the Natlan Archon Quest (version 5.1). Xilonen is asked to forge an Ancient Name for the Traveler, an outsider, and the search for help leads to the shaman Citlali and her missing tribesman Ororon, who turns out to be working with the Fatui Harbinger Capitano. The act ends as the Abyss attacks the whole nation and the Traveler learns of a dangerous backup plan.

The act has three quests: All Names are Noble, To Whence the Smoke Drifts and The Flickering Light Splits in Twain. It requires Adventure Rank 40. It follows Black Stone Under a White Stone and adds the Masters of the Night-Wind to the story's central cast.

Structurally the act pairs a gentle, comic search for an Ancient Name with a secret meeting in which the Traveler is offered an alliance by an opponent, then turns to a nationwide attack and a flashback through Ororon's memory that explains what the Fatui are doing in Natlan.

Plot: **All Names are Noble.** Two days after the previous act, the Adventurers' Guild and the Scions of the Canopy have been ordered by the Pyro Archon to share information and tackle Abyssal threats together, and Kachina has volunteered as a stationed warrior. She takes the Traveler and Paimon to Xilonen's workshop in the Children of Echoes. Xilonen had been told only that the Ancient Name was for a traveler and would be "quite difficult"; she is surprised to learn it is for an outlander and explains it should be impossible, since the Night Kingdom records only the deeds of Natlanese in Natlan. She chooses to treat it as a test of her skill. The first step is to be acknowledged by the Wayob, so they decide to consult Citlali, an expert on the Night Kingdom, though the Spiritspeaker Stone was broken in the rescue. Kinich agrees to deliver Xilonen's letter and tells them the person who rescued Capitano was Ororon of the Masters of the Night-Wind. After a wait, Citlali arrives and agrees to help if they help prove Ororon's innocence. She examines the Traveler's past, dispels residue of souls clinging to them from the Night Kingdom, and explains that the decision ultimately lies with the Lord of the Night, a Night Kingdom entity that uses the Sacred Flame's power against the Abyss. It is asleep, so they must enter its dream by trance.

**To Whence the Smoke Drifts.** Following Ororon's phlogiston trail from his last known location, Citlali tells them he is an orphan raised by the tribe. Her spell lets the Traveler and Paimon hear her private thoughts. When the party splits, the Traveler and Paimon are pulled into the Night Kingdom, where Ororon appears and Capitano speaks with the Traveler, explaining his goals and mistrust of Mavuika. He asks to meet again east of the Stadium and asks them to tell no one. Citlali finds and frees Ororon from a Fatui camp, though he is made to labour there. She asks why he saved Capitano; he says that otherwise they would have gone for her. The Traveler later tells Paimon, but not Citlali, about the meeting and meets Capitano again with Ororon. Capitano argues that Mavuika's plan may fail and that there is another plan that would cost dearly; he vanishes mid-sentence as an angry Citlali, suspicious since they were separated, arrives and discovers the meeting. At the Weary Inn Citlali becomes drunk, learns the Traveler heard her thoughts, and in private reveals her insecurity about being called old and that Ororon has an incomplete soul, which his tribe treated as a bad omen and tried to use as a vessel for Night Kingdom souls. The Traveler decides to ask Mavuika about the backup plan.

**The Flickering Light Splits in Twain.** The Abyss launches a nation-wide attack on the Masters of the Night-Wind, the Children of Echoes, the Collective of Plenty and many outposts. The Traveler goes to Mavuika, who confirms that the backup plan exists but would erase everything from the Night Kingdom, including history and culture, and might still fail without ley line repairs. She asks them to keep it secret and says she will join the defence. The Traveler helps rescue a caravan, while Chasca and Chuychu infiltrate a Fatui camp and learn the Fatui seek the "Source Mechanism". Citlali reports that Ororon has returned to defend the tribe; the replacement soul-stabilising gem she had Ifa deliver to him carried a spell that copied his memories into the old gem. His memories show Capitano's visit to Ororon, Tarko's suspicion, and Ororon's rescue of the wounded Capitano, and Capitano states that the only way to save Natlan is to reconstruct its ley lines. The group decides to inform Mavuika at once.

Further details. In All Names are Noble, The Traveler wonders whether all six Wayob would have to acknowledge them. Citlali reveals she arrived late because she had examined Ororon's home, where his Phlogiston Aphids were off and there were marks from Snezhnayan weapons. She is unsure why the Fatui would take interest in a young man in his twenties. Citlali was also unsure how to approach the Traveler without awkwardness; Xilonen apologises for not warning them that Citlali looks much younger than her title suggests.

In To Whence the Smoke Drifts, Capitano says he heard about the Traveler from Childe (Tartaglia) and wants them as an ally rather than an enemy. Paimon suspects he wants the Gnosis for the Tsaritsa, and the Traveler realises the backup plan involves the Gnosis; before Capitano can say more he disappears. Ororon later tricks the group with a powder that causes an illusion and says he acted in Natlan's best interests. A Fatuus named Kosterlitzky orders Ororon back to work in the camp. Citlali and the Traveler report to Coyopa, who tells Ororon to return once the Archon decides.

In the memory sequence, a local tribesman first warns Ororon about the Fatui, and Capitano later visits and asks why he lives alone and whether he knows Citlali. Ororon follows the Fatui to a camp, where Tarko spots him; Tarko becomes dizzy as souls from the Night Kingdom escape, and Capitano dispels them. Days later, when Mavuika wounds Capitano at the Stadium, Ororon senses a familiar soul trying to escape, realises the lead would be lost if Capitano died, and intervenes. Capitano admits he was looking into the Night Kingdom. In a second camp, Capitano says that rather than a net to stop the damage, the nation's ley lines must be rebuilt. Citlali is angry that Ororon cannot let go of the past, while the group notes that rebuilding like the Loom of Fate would affect everyone's memories.

Revelations: - An Ancient Name cannot normally be forged for an outlander, because the Night Kingdom records only the deeds of Natlanese done in Natlan.
- The Lord of the Night is an entity in the Night Kingdom that uses the Sacred Flame's power to repel the Abyss; it is asleep and can be reached only through its dream.
- Ororon's memories show Capitano intends to rebuild Natlan's ley lines, an action that would alter everyone's memories.
- Mavuika has a backup plan that would erase the Night Kingdom's contents, including history and culture; she asks the Traveler to keep it secret.
- Ororon has an incomplete soul and relies on a gem to stabilise it; his tribe once tried to use him as a vessel for Night Kingdom souls.

- Chasca and Chuychu's reconnaissance finds the Fatui defending civilians during the nationwide attack and searching for the "Source Mechanism"; their purpose is unclear.
- The Abyss attack hit the Masters of the Night-Wind, the Children of Echoes and the Collective of Plenty at once.

Characters: The Traveler and Paimon, Katheryne, Kachina, Xilonen, Kinich, Citlali, Ororon, Capitano, Mavuika, Mualani, Chasca, Chuychu, Iansan and Ifa; also Piltzin, Chanca, Coyopa, Tarko and Kosterlitzky.

Consequences: The Traveler now knows of both Capitano's proposal and Mavuika's backup plan. Ororon is brought home, though his standing with the tribe is unresolved. The group is left with the task of telling Mavuika what Capitano intends for the ley lines.

Xilonen's Ancient Name for the Traveler remains unfinished: the Traveler must be acknowledged by the Wayob, and Citlali says the decision lies with the Lord of the Night. The Traveler kept the Capitano meetings from Citlali, who discovered the second one by following them. The story continues in Act IV, The Rainbow Destined to Burn.

Placement: Chapter V, Act III. It follows Act II, Black Stone Under a White Stone, and precedes Act IV, The Rainbow Destined to Burn. Released in 5.1.

167.comment: Beyond the Smoke and Mirrors: Ororon and the Fatui
167.content: Ororon, a young man of the Masters of the Night-Wind raised as an orphan by the tribe, saved the wounded Capitano from Mavuika; he tells Citlali that otherwise the Fatui would have gone for her, while his memories show he also wanted to keep a lead on what Capitano knew. He lived alone and was found working in a Fatui camp. His soul is incomplete and stabilised by a gem delivered by Ifa. His memories show the Fatui leader's wish to rebuild Natlan's ley lines.

168.comment: Beyond the Smoke and Mirrors: Capitano's offer
168.content: Capitano, the first Fatui Harbinger, secretly meets the Traveler in the Night Kingdom and a second time east of the Stadium. He argues Mavuika's plan may fail and that she has kept a costly emergency plan hidden, which the Traveler realises involves the Gnosis, and he would prefer the Traveler as an ally. Mavuika later confirms the backup plan.

169.comment: Beyond the Smoke and Mirrors: Mavuika's backup plan
169.content: Mavuika confirms there is a backup plan to save Natlan that would erase everything from the Night Kingdom, including history and culture, and might fail if ley lines are not repaired. She prefers her present plan as the safest way to win and asks the Traveler to keep it secret.

170.comment: Beyond the Smoke and Mirrors: Ancient Name for an outsider
170.content: Mavuika asks Xilonen to forge an Ancient Name for the Traveler, which Xilonen first calls impossible since the Night Kingdom records only Natlanese deeds done in Natlan. The process requires the acknowledgement of the Wayob and the consent of the Lord of the Night, reached through a trance with Citlali's help.

key: Black Stone Under a White Stone
171.comment: Black Stone Under a White Stone
171.content:
Black Stone Under a White Stone (also: Chapter V Act II, Natlan Archon Quest Act II): Black Stone Under a White Stone is the second act of Chapter V, the Natlan Archon Quest (version 5.0). When Kachina fails to return from the Pilgrimage of the Sacred Flame and Mavuika cannot find her or her Ancient Name, the Traveler, Mualani and Chasca (later joined by Iansan) go into the Abyss-corrupted Night Kingdom to bring her back, while the Fatui Harbinger Capitano publicly challenges the Pyro Archon.

The act has five quests: A Decision, To Reclaim an Ancient Name, Echoes of Life, Into Eternal Night and Past and Future. It requires Adventure Rank 40. It deepens the picture of the Abyss's attack on Natlan, shows how an Ancient Name is tied to the Night Kingdom, and closes with Mavuika asking the Traveler to help save Natlan, followed by a short epilogue with Capitano.

The act is both a rescue story and a statement of Natlan's situation: the pilgrimage is in danger, the Sacred Flame is strained, and the Pyro Archon has spent part of her power. Mavuika's request to an outsider sets up the Ancient Name thread continued in the next act.

Plot: **A Decision.** After a short stay with the People of the Springs, Mualani and Tonina bring news that the group from the Night Warden Wars has returned. Kachina, the inexperienced member, fell in battle, and the Ode of Resurrection should bring her back. At the Stadium of the Sacred Flame, Mavuika enters the Sacred Flame to fetch her but emerges alone: neither Kachina nor her Ancient Name can be found. Tepexpan and Tamuin heckle Kachina's failure; Chasca and Mualani defend her, and Mavuika shuts the heckling down and suspends the pilgrimage until further notice. In the Speaker's Chamber she suggests the Abyss may have found a way to undermine the pilgrimage's rules. With the help of the Masters of the Night-Wind she can locate Kachina's Ancient Name, but a party must physically enter the Night Kingdom. Mualani, Chasca and the Traveler volunteer. The Fatui then arrive, led by Capitano, the first Harbinger, who accuses Mavuika of failing the oath made 500 years ago. They clash; Mavuika wounds him, and someone from the Masters of the Night-Wind produces a fog that lets him escape.

**To Reclaim an Ancient Name.** Entering the Night Kingdom physically needs a Spiritspeaker Stone. Chasca asks Wayna of the Huitztlan, who refers her to Vichama, experienced at navigating the Night Kingdom. He agrees if they afterwards help him find his friend Mallko. The party fetches rope and obsidian and learns why Vichama is downcast: injured on the eve of a pilgrimage battle, he got an exemption from the Pyro Archon, and his group was then overwhelmed in his absence. During the ritual he finds Kachina's name while the Traveler siphons and purifies Abyssal energy from him, but he cannot find Mallko's. The stone cannot be disconnected, so Chasca shatters it with her bow, and the Traveler manages to find Mallko's final memory, which Vichama is glad yet grieved to hear. Chasca's younger sister Chuychu, whose family adopted Chasca, quarrels with her over the risk but backs her. Wayna promises to explain the broken stone to Citlali.

**Echoes of Life.** At the Stadium the party learns Mavuika has clashed with Capitano and sacrificed some of her power. She shows them a chamber of keepsakes kept by Pyro Archons over the years and explains that after Tenoch united the tribes and saved Natlan, the first Pyro Archon laid down the rules still followed today. The ritual with Kachina's name begins and Kachina appears. She says an Abyssal entity attacked her, the Wayob helped her flee and hide, and she fears the Abyss is affecting the Wayob and blocking her return. Mualani promises to find her. Mavuika directs the party to an entrance to the Night Kingdom, and Iansan joins them. The ruins on the way belong to the civilisation of the elemental sovereigns, and the Abyss's presence has reactivated devices there.

**Into Eternal Night.** In the corrupted Night Kingdom the party meets the spirit of Mallko, who helps them while he still can. They find Kachina fighting riftwolves and escort her to her Wayob's totem. As they purify it, the Abyss Lector Comonqui arrives, having destroyed Mallko's spirit, and claims the Pyro Archon refuses to share "primordial" power. Mualani rallies Kachina and they drive it off. A spectral figure, Tupac, appears and recognises Mualani as embodying her tribe's Wayob; on touching him she is flooded with memories showing that the plan to save Natlan began during the cataclysm. As an earthquake closes the rift, Mavuika appears as a projection of her consciousness and breaks the Night Realm's ceiling, letting everyone out.

**Past and Future.** In the Speaker's Chamber Chuychu treats the party for Abyssal contamination and notes the Traveler seems immune; Paimon is also unaffected. Mavuika explains that after the cataclysm the tribes and Wayob were weakened, and a Wayob's choice of bearer shows its tribe is strong again. Three tribes had heroes (Kinich, Iansan, Xilonen); Mualani makes a fourth; two remain, and less than a year is left. The keepsakes carried traces of Contending Flame, which she burned for the emergency boost. At the Weary Inn the group celebrates Kachina's return, and Mavuika asks the Traveler to help save Natlan, promising to have Xilonen forge them an Ancient Name. Elsewhere Rezanov asks Capitano whether to take the Gnosis; Capitano refuses, honouring her win. An unnamed ally tells him Mavuika has not dispelled the fog.

Further details. The pilgrimage was suspended partly because production of Contending Fire is far from sufficient and the tribes have reached a breaking point; the pause also keeps each tribe strong against the Abyss. Kinich favours finding the remaining bearers; Mavuika answers that time should pass, because the Wayob chose them and it is for them to decide how the story ends. She tells Tepexpan and Tamuin that doubt should motivate a search for truth, not serve as a weapon, and they back down when invited to ask her directly. Chasca blames herself for not protecting Kachina; Wayna fears Citlali's anger over the broken stone; Iansan is quietly upset at how Mavuika managed her rescue.

Revelations: - During the cataclysm the Abyss crafted a specific disaster for each tribe; Natlan repelled it under the then-Pyro Archon but at heavy cost, and recovery has been slow.
- The Abyss has reached into the Night Kingdom and the Wayob, threatening the Ode of Resurrection and the pilgrimage's rules.
- After the cataclysm the tribes and their Wayob were weakened; a Wayob's choice of an Ancient Name bearer signals its tribe is ready, and the plan to save Natlan began during the cataclysm.
- Mavuika has burned the Archons' keepsake collection and spent part of her power; Contending Fire reserves are low.
- Capitano, the first Harbinger, has come to end the old order and, for now, will not take the Gnosis from a weakened Archon.

- Mavuika asks the Traveler for help and promises an Ancient Name; Act III shows that forging one for a non-Natlanese is considered impossible.

Characters: The Traveler and Paimon, Mavuika, Kachina, Mualani, Chasca, Iansan, Kinich, Chuychu, Wayna, Vichama, the spirit of Mallko, Comonqui, Tupac, Capitano, Rezanov, Tepexpan, Tamuin and Tonina.

Consequences: Kachina is rescued, the pilgrimage is suspended, and Mavuika is weakened. The Traveler agrees to help save Natlan and Xilonen is to forge them an Ancient Name. Capitano withdraws into Natlan's wilds.

The unnamed Masters of the Night-Wind member who covered Capitano's escape is identified as Ororon in Act III.

Placement: Chapter V, Act II. It follows Act I, Flowers Resplendent on the Sun-Scorched Sojourn, and precedes Act III, Beyond the Smoke and Mirrors. Released in 5.0.

172.comment: Black Stone Under a White Stone: Kachina's disappearance and the Night Kingdom rescue
172.content: Kachina fails to return after falling in the Night Warden Wars. Her Ancient Name is found by Vichama through a Spiritspeaker Stone, which Chasca destroys to protect everyone. In the Night Kingdom the Traveler, Mualani, Chasca and Iansan find her hiding from the Abyss, purify her Wayob's totem and escape with Mavuika's help. Mallko's spirit is destroyed by the Lector Comonqui after helping them.

173.comment: Black Stone Under a White Stone: Capitano and Mavuika's clash
173.content: At the Stadium, Capitano accuses Mavuika of breaking an oath made 500 years ago and promises a new era with new rules for Natlan. Mavuika lands a searing wound on his chest before a Masters of the Night-Wind member covers his escape in fog. Later he tells Rezanov he will not take the Gnosis from a weakened Archon.

174.content:
Blessings of the Frost Moon (also: Blessings of the Frost Moon (Part 2), Frostmoon Enclave library quest): Blessings of the Frost Moon is a World Quest in the Frostmoon Enclave on Hiisi Island, Nod-Krai (Version 6.0). Lauma, the Frostmoon Scions' Moonchanter, who understands all animal speech, needs help to pull a buried statue called the Lunar Semblance out of a Moon Mirror, a task her animal friends cannot manage. The Traveler works paired mechanisms with her while she directs them through a watching ibis. The statue ends up in the Scions' library. A second part, unlocked later, shows the finished Grand Library and Lauma's reasons for opening it to animals as well as humans.

Tone is gentle and humorous: a weasel thief and an ibis help plan the "heist", and a puffin supplies fruit. The quest is the clearest early statement of Lauma's character: she cannot switch off her ability to understand animals, finds peace elusive as a result, and treats humans and animals as sharing one nature.

Plot: Part 1. Lauma is arguing with a longplume ibis and a weasel thief about how to move the sealed Lunar Semblance. She explains to Paimon that her animal-speech is always on and cannot be controlled, so even in the forest she hears constant quarrelling, though she has grown used to it. The Traveler goes to the Moon Mirror, where the statue lies sealed by a previous Moonchanter. Two mechanisms in two places must be worked at the same time; Lauma takes one side, the ibis tells her where the Traveler is, and the Traveler takes the other. Once the path is cleared Lauma uses her power to pull the statue out. Animals then help carry it to the library. Lauma explains that the statue is crude and worth little as Mora, but is priceless to the Frostmoon Scions as proof that documents about it are reliable. She asks the Traveler to bring her any texts about the Frostmoon Scions to copy for the library.

Lauma pays the weasel thief one Mora more each time it helps her, and thanks the Traveler for easy mastery of the mechanisms. The weasel thief says the Traveler is the best treasure-hunter it has seen and wants to join future hunts. A puffin brings extra fruit for the Traveler and Paimon, and the Midsommar Berries on a plate are quickly eaten.
Part 2 begins automatically when the Frostmoon Enclave Meeting Point reaches level 5. Lauma, in the finished Grand Library, says she must still find places for bird stands, cushions and deposit boxes, which she wants artisans to help build. She describes her duty as Moonchanter as listening to everyone's troubles, with animals visiting at set times of day (badgers at dawn, ibises after sunrise, finches in flocks in the afternoon, rimehorn deer at dusk, weasel thieves at night) and humans coming less often and telling only part of their story. She explains that she renovated the library as a space where humans and animals can mix, hoping the animals' lack of judgment will encourage people to speak openly.

Post-quest dialogues after Part 1 (only the wiki's listed sets are summarised): the weasel thief, now over-eager, digs up buried boxes, wish-boxes and fossils and drops them in the library, so Lauma hires a second, older weasel thief to return them to their places. She also gives the Traveler a coin from the first weasel thief as a "deposit" on a promised treasure-hunting partnership, with a suggestion to leave dried lakkaberries by the pillow. She reflects that "human nature" and "bestial nature" are both just nature, that she imagines the world might be better if humans and animals could talk, and that some people reject nature and hunt animals who can speak their language. A puffin, an ibis and a rimehorn deer appear in small recurring scenes.

Revelations: - Lauma's understanding of animal speech is always on and beyond her control; she found it a joy at first and a burden later.
- A previous Moonchanter sealed the Lunar Semblance in a Moon Mirror.
- The Moon Mirror's seal can be undone by working paired mechanisms in two places at once.
- The Frostmoon Scions keep a library and Lauma wants it open to both humans and animals.

- Lauma carries the role of confidante for both animals and Scions, and says people hide their true feelings in a way animals do not.
- Lauma thinks about writing: she says that books on human and "bestial" nature are written by humans who cannot hear the animals' side.

Characters: Lauma, Paimon and the Traveler are the named participants. Animals shown include a longplume ibis, a weasel thief, a puffin, finches and a rimehorn deer. Lauma teases that the ibis learned its way of talking from a short girl with a metal arm and a hat, a reference to Jahoda.

Consequences: Completing Part 1 unlocks the Frostmoon Enclave Meeting Point and sets up the library renovation. The Lunar Semblance is placed in the library and its documented existence confirms several earlier texts for Lauma. Part 2, a short conversation, follows later when the Meeting Point is at level 5.

Placement: Released in Version 6.0 (Luna I, 2025-09-10) as part of the first Nod-Krai content. Part 2 is gated by Frostmoon Enclave Meeting Point level rather than story progress.

175.comment: Blessings of the Frost Moon: Lunar Semblance
175.content: A large, crudely carved stone statue sealed inside a Moon Mirror by an earlier Moonchanter. Lauma says it is worth little in Mora and carries no mystical power, but is a priceless historical relic of the Frostmoon Scions whose existence confirms several written accounts. Animals helped carry it to the Grand Library after Lauma pulled it from the mirror.

176.comment: Blessings of the Frost Moon: Grand Library of the Frostmoon Scions
176.content: Lauma renovated the library to be open to humans and animals alike, with furniture, bird stands, cushions and deposit boxes for animals. She hopes people who feel unable to speak openly will find it easier among animals that do not judge. She asks the Traveler to bring her any texts about the Frostmoon Scions to copy for its shelves.

177.content:
Bough Keeper: Dainsleif (also: Dainsleif Travel Log, Chapter I Act IV Prelude): Bough Keeper: Dainsleif is a Mondstadt world quest from Version 1.3 that works as the prelude to Chapter I, Act IV of the Archon Quests. Katheryne tells the Traveler about a tall blond stranger with an eyepatch. The Traveler and Paimon find him at the Angel's Share, where he introduces himself as Dainsleif and agrees to be commissioned for 500 Mora and three questions. He takes only work against the Abyss Order, and together they search the Temple of the Falcon, Wolvendom and Stormterror's Lair for an Abyss Herald without finding one. The quest ends at a trampled dandelion that the Traveler senses a link to their sibling through.

The quest is a world quest by category but is voiced and structured like an Archon or Story Quest, and it carries a unique emblem combining the two siblings' constellations. Unlike the earlier Archon Quests, which centre on a nation and its Archon, it is built around the Traveler's own search for their sibling.

Plot: The stranger first ignores the party, then relents when the Traveler says they are looking for a lost relative. He gives his name, Dainsleif, and agrees to join them in return for an advance of 500 Mora and three questions. The questions ask who was the key to ending the Stormterror crisis, who will defend Liyue Harbor after its god, and whether those with Visions or those without matter more to the gods. He says no answer is right or wrong and that he only wants to see the Traveler's attitude. He then states that he accepts only commissions concerning the Abyss Order, which he opposes, and that he is tracking an Abyss Herald to Mondstadt.

He leads the party to the abandoned Temple of the Falcon, where the Abyssal Traces domain is cleared of Abyss Mages and no Herald is found. Traces lead to Wolvendom, where Abyssal marks float over two bonfires, but Dainsleif judges them the work of mages without deeper Abyssal power. The last lead is Stormterror's Lair; the party fights more monsters near the Light Actuators and again finds no Herald.

At the Lair the Traveler senses something familiar on a nearby cliff. Dainsleif and the party climb to the top and find nothing out of place except a Ruin Guard footprint and a trampled dandelion. When the Traveler touches the dandelion, they recall their encounter with the unknown god and feel their sibling's presence. Dainsleif suggests the flower may carry a "scent" only the Traveler can recognise, urges patience, and tells them that at least they now know the sibling is still in this world, and that the journey to find them is what matters most now. He then leaves, saying they will meet again, since he has taken the 500 Mora and the three answers.

Scene order: the quest begins from Katheryne in Mondstadt City; the three inquiries (Lawrence, Wagner, Charles) follow, each NPC having an optional repeat line. The wait on the tavern's second floor is a short skip-forward. If the player picks the third option of the questions at least twice, Dainsleif remarks that the Traveler really is similar to their sibling; otherwise he says they seem different from the sibling. He never explains the remark, and the Traveler's question about it goes unanswered. The 500 Mora is only a storytelling device and is never actually deducted.

Revelations: - Dainsleif already knows that the Anemo Archon is Venti, the course of the Stormterror crisis, and Rex Lapis's Contract to End All Contracts. He says he knows everything he should.
- The Abyss Order has stayed away from the Traveler since the Stormterror incident; Dainsleif says they may have been under orders to avoid the Traveler's path.
- Abyss Heralds exist: more twisted Abyssal beings that command Abyss Mages.
- He describes the Abyss as chaos and destruction eating at the world's foundations, strong enough that even the Dragon of the East, a servant of a deity, could not resist its corrosion; its creatures want to overthrow a world ruled by archons.

- Dainsleif implies a long personal history with the Abyss ("some history") and with Old Mondstadt: he saw its ruins before the Dragon of the East fell or nested there, which puzzles Paimon, who thinks Dvalin's trouble began only hundreds of years ago. He tells her not to think too much about it.
- A former travelling companion, never named, once took him around Teyvat; that companion "no longer travels". He says he cannot remember his own favourite place because he merely followed this companion.
- The dandelion shows the Traveler that their sibling is still alive in the world.

Characters: - **Dainsleif**: tall, blond, one eye covered by an eyepatch, calm, formal and cryptic; takes commissions only against the Abyss Order.
- **Paimon**: calls him "Dain", worries about the payment terms and asks about his past.
- **The Traveler**: answers his questions and senses the familiar presence at the cliff.
- **Katheryne, Lawrence, Wagner, Charles**: supply the trail. Lawrence is a gate guard who shadowed the stranger and lost him; Wagner is the blacksmith the stranger asked about unfamiliar materials; Charles is the Angel's Share bartender who calls him a connoisseur who mixes his own drinks.

Katheryne's mention of the eyepatch prompts the Traveler to joke that the stranger is a distant relative of Kaeya; Paimon dismisses the idea. Lawrence prefers not to tell Jean, since she might overreact. Charles says the stranger ordered a bottle in advance, and Paimon assumes Diluc is watching him too.

Consequences: Dainsleif now treats the Traveler as a client and says they will meet again, which leads into Act IV. The Traveler learns their sibling is still in the world and meets the Abyss Order as an ongoing threat. Rewards include 60 Primogems, 38,100 Mora, some materials and the achievement Gears of Destiny.

Placement: Released in Version 1.3 as a world quest requiring A New Star Approaches. It is shown on the quest screen as Chapter I: Act IV - Prelude and leads into Archon Quest Chapter I, Act IV: We Will Be Reunited. It does not appear in the Archive's completed quest list, only in the quest overview Travel Log.

The route passes places tied to each of the Four Winds: Mondstadt City (the Lion of the South), the Temple of the Falcon (Falcon of the West), Wolvendom (Wolf of the North) and Stormterror's Lair (Dragon of the East). This pairing is an observation about the locations, not something the characters say.

178.comment: Bough Keeper: Dainsleif: Dainsleif's Three Questions
178.content:
At the Angel's Share, Dainsleif asks three questions as payment: who was the key to ending the Mondstadt crisis (Venti, the Traveler, or Mondstadt's united people); who will defend Liyue Harbor now that Rex Lapis has left (the adepti, the Liyue Qixing, or everyone in Liyue Harbor); and who matters more to the gods (those with Visions, those without, or perhaps neither). He treats the answers as showing attitude, not correctness.

The answers change only a single line of dialogue near the end, in which he compares the Traveler to the sibling. The fee of 500 Mora is not actually taken.

179.comment: Bough Keeper: Dainsleif: Abyss Herald Search
179.content: The hunt visits the Temple of the Falcon (an Abyssal Traces quest domain with Abyss Mages), Wolvendom (Abyssal spell marks over bonfires, guarded by mages and hilichurls) and the Light Actuators of Stormterror's Lair (more monsters). No Abyss Herald appears. Dainsleif says the Herald may already have left and that the Traveler will meet one eventually.

180.comment: Bough Keeper: Dainsleif: The Trampled Dandelion
180.content: On the cliff above Stormterror's Lair, Dainsleif notices a Ruin Guard footprint and stops by a crushed dandelion. The Traveler touches it, recalls the unknown god and feels their sibling. Dainsleif says the sibling is still in this world and tells them to keep the journey to find them in mind as the meaning behind their travels.

181.comment: Bough Keeper: Dainsleif: Dainsleif's Hints About His Past
181.content: In this quest he mentions a former travelling companion who no longer travels, earlier visits to Old Mondstadt, and unfinished tasks before he can return home. The quest does not say who the companion is. A character who has only completed this quest should treat these as unexplained hints; his full background belongs to his own entry.

key: In the Hall of the Sea King
182.content:
Canticles of Harmony (also: Petrichorror Dream, In the Hall of the Sea King, Prisoner in Shackles, Pharsalia's Rhapsody, Requiem, The Shadow Over Petrichor, Underwater Nocturne, The Last Day of Remuria): Canticles of Harmony is a five-part Fontaine World Quest chapter added in version 4.6, after Song of the Dragon and Freedom. The people of the town of Petrichor fall into a dreamlike state, and the Traveler and Paimon follow a strange talking cat, Osse, through the Faded Castle to the drowned Remurian capital to end the corrupted Symphony of the ancient empire of Remuria and send the stolen souls home.

The parts are Prelude "Petrichorror Dream" (The Shadow Over Petrichor), First Movement "In the Hall of the Sea King" (Underwater Nocturne), Second Movement "Prisoner in Shackles" (The Last Day of Remuria), Third Movement "Pharsalia's Rhapsody" (Gradus ad Capitolium, with two Golden Aqueduct Reconstruction sub-quests) and Finale "Requiem" (Fortune Plango Vulnera). It shows the story of Remuria and its ruin through the Traveler's dreams and the words of Osse, Scylla and Boethius.

Titles and music. The wiki notes that the chapter takes its parts from musical terms and compositions (the second part echoes "In the Hall of the Mountain King"; the third alludes to the Latin poem Pharsalia; Fortune Plango Vulnera is a movement of Carmina Burana). The quest is mostly concerned with ending a corrupted Symphony and giving the Remurians' trapped souls rest.

Plot: Prelude. In Petrichor the Traveler and Paimon meet a gang who say they are rescuing treasure from the "Dark Lord Remus" and are chased off. The town's people are dazed and speak as if in ancient times; a "Bellringer" falls unconscious. Este of the Daydream Club, who is unaffected, tells them of the legend of the Faded Castle. A glowing cat, Osse, calls himself Ouranides of Ouranopolis, a spirit-keeper of the ancient realm, and says the Symphony has taken the townsfolk's souls. He asks the Traveler to help him open a hidden path to the castle, and the Traveler collects harp strings, which Osse says are the Symphony's scores. The Ancient Score and an Ancient Autoharmonic Music Box are the quest rewards.

First Movement. In the Faded Castle Osse (called Monsieur Os) shows the Traveler a library and a stage, where they obtain a Blank Score and perform a play. The Traveler sees the memories of the God King Remus; Osse explains that Remurians were a stone-bodied race with Ichor for blood, that the Symphony was meant to weave fate, that Boethius was a noble Harmost who became a monster, and that Osse himself became a hunter of phantoms to oppose him.

Second Movement. Osse (identified as Cassiodor) and the Traveler enter the Sea of Bygone Eras. They free Scylla, a dragon prince who was sealed by Boethius at the Initium Iani, by breaking three seals. They meet a nameless golem who still guards a fortress and asks whether Remuria won, and lingering Remurian shadows and soldiers.

Third Movement. At the sunken capital the group reach the golden palace Domus Aurea. Scylla rebuilds the golden aqueducts with the Traveler, and they play the Symphony to open the gate. Boethius tells Cassiodor to join him and release the souls.

Finale. Cassiodor joins Boethius to trap Phobos in one body and urges the Traveler to destroy them both. Phobos reveals itself as the Symphony. The Traveler strikes; Cassiodor fades. The Traveler plays the Requiem, the souls return to the sea, and the Traveler comes back to Petrichor.

Prelude details. A stone shard found in the bandits' crates replaces the "treasure"; they were taking statues from the ruins. The Traveler dreams as the "Imperator" and sees a speaker prepare to sound the Symphony Phobos to break the "shackles of Fortuna".

First Movement details. Osse explains the library as an archive where ancient plays and scores were gathered. He says that, in the past, "he and I and many companions" dwelt in the castle when the nation was new. Pipes and books respond to the music box, and the Traveler solves musical puzzles to get the Blank Score.

Second Movement details. Cassiodor says Scylla, once a friend of the Sebastos, led dragonborn to Machimos and was sealed when the Initium Iani was shut. Scylla replies that the attack was part of Remus's secret plan. The Traveler meets a Remurian golem who recognises Dominus Cassiodor and remembers a war that Remuria lost. They also see a replay of Legio IX troops carrying off the loot from tribal lands, which Este opposes.

Third Movement details. Boethius meets Cassiodor and the Traveler at Domus Aurea and says he serves no god or king but "mighty Remuria". He accuses Remus of colluding with dragons and of attempting to destroy the Grand Symphony, and says he spent thousands of years weaving the broken melodies together. He asks Cassiodor to join him. Scylla declines to enter the palace, saying he is merely occupying a body of Ichor.

Finale details. After Phobos is destroyed Praetorian Golems execute Boethius's wounded form. Cassiodor says he is certain the people of the present will live normal, happy lives, quotes lines about water and soil, and asks the Traveler to play the Requiem. Scylla says Cassiodor's soul must have returned to the High Sea and notes that a new true dragon, Neuvillette, has been born, and that he may go seek an audience.

Revelations: - The Remurians were a stone-bodied race with Ichor for blood, made by Remus so they could resist fate.
- The Symphony Phobos was built by Remus from the wisdom of Sybilla and his own power, and became a war-guiding will that consumed Boethius.
- Osse is Cassiodor, once a Harmost of Remuria, later one who hunts phantoms and is called the Golden Hunter.
- Scylla, once Remus's friend, was lured into a trap and turned to stone by Boethius.
- Phobos is destroyed in the Finale; Cassiodor does not survive it.

- Cassiodor learns that Remus aimed to free everyone from the Symphony through his own sacrifice.
- The Traveler's dream shows Remus planning the ritual meant to defy the prophecy of ruin.
- Many Remurian souls remain bound beneath the sea; Cassiodor says they are held by their own obsession, and Boethius claims they are imprisoned.

Characters: The Traveler, Paimon, Osse (Monsieur Os, Cassiodor), Boethius, Scylla, Remus (in memories), Phobos, Este (human of the Daydream Club, and a Remurian golem), the "Bellringer", and bandits in Petrichor.

Consequences: Phobos and Boethius are gone and the souls are sent back to the High Sea; the Traveler ends the chapter in Petrichor. Cassiodor is no more and Scylla is free to roam the waters. The chapter's reward track is "Canticles of Harmony" in the Fontaine Reputation, and rewards include the Ancient Score and the Ancient Autoharmonic Music Box.

Placement: Released in 4.6. Requires Song of the Dragon and Freedom. It is the Fontaine chapter that explains the origin of Remuria and the Faded Castle.

183.comment: Canticles of Harmony: Osse and Monsieur Os
183.content: Osse is a white cat with a bronze collar and pendant who speaks in formal, archaic language, calls himself Ouranides of Ouranopolis and is later called Monsieur Os by Paimon. He turns out to be Cassiodor, a Remurian Harmost who stayed behind to keep the past from rising. He fades at the end of the chapter.

184.comment: Canticles of Harmony: Phobos, the Symphony of Remuria
184.content: Phobos is a vast Symphony that Remus wrote so people could resist fate; in the Finale it says it was Sybilla's wisdom joined to Remus's power. It answered everyone's wishes, including hateful ones, and devoured Boethius. Cassiodor and the Traveler destroy it together.

185.comment: Canticles of Harmony: Scylla in Canticles of Harmony
185.content: Scylla is a Hydro vishap prince who was Remus's friend, was turned to stone at the Initium Iani and is freed in Second Movement. He speaks in an old-fashioned way, calls the Traveler and Cassiodor "little ones", helps rebuild the golden aqueducts, and sends the souls back. He says his attack was part of Remus's secret plan.

186.comment: Canticles of Harmony: Este of the Daydream Club
186.content: Este is a human member of Petrichor's Daydream Club who is unaffected by the Symphony and who tells the Traveler about the legend of the Faded Castle. Osse suggests he is a descendant of a Remurian who followed Cassiodor, and a golem named Este appears in Second Movement in a memory of Remuria.

187.comment: Canticles of Harmony: Domus Aurea and the golden aqueducts
187.content: Domus Aurea is the golden palace of Capitolium, built from a giant ship to broadcast the Symphony through pipes and golden waterways. To enter it, the Traveler and Scylla restore the aqueducts in the two Golden Aqueduct Reconstruction sub-quests and sound the symphony.

188.content:
Carassius Auratus Chapter (Yoimiya) (also: Carassius Auratus Chapter, Yoimiya's Story Quest, Dreamlike Timelessness, Star-Pickers' Passage): Yoimiya's Story Quest. In Act I the Traveler helps the Naganohara fireworks maker shelter and ship out a fugitive who slipped into Inazuma, and reunites him with a friend who now serves the Tenryou Commission. In Act II Yoimiya leaves Inazuma for the first time and travels to Sumeru, hoping to see a meteor shower.

Act I, Dreamlike Timelessness, was released in Version 2.0 and has four quests: The Firework Girl's Strange Stories, Expectations Not to Be Betrayed, A Sliver of Hope and Together Under the Fireworks. Act II, Star-Pickers' Passage, came in Version 3.7 with three: The Seeker of a Meteor Shower, All Things Flawless and Pure, and A Flower that Blooms Across the Sky.

Both acts are about what a brief, bright thing is worth. Act I sets the Naganohara show against the Inazuman ideal of eternity; Act II turns the show into a trip in which Yoimiya hopes to find inspiration for a new firework, and instead finds herself carrying other people's wishes.

Plot: Act I: during the Sakoku Decree, Yoimiya hides a wanted man, Sakujirou, and arranges a boat for him while preparing a fireworks show. His old friend Keisuke of the Tenryou Commission is hunting him. Yoimiya stops the conflict with a duel and the two part on better terms. Act II: with the Sakoku Decree gone, Yoimiya travels to Sumeru. The Traveler and Nahida stage a dream meteor shower with the Aranara, which also helps a girl named Avin.

Act I. On the beach at Inazuma City, the Traveler and Paimon meet children hunting a prank-playing youkai, then Yoimiya, who is checking materials for an upcoming show. Her father, Ryuunosuke, is deaf since a workshop accident. Yoimiya is quietly hiding Sakujirou, an Inazuman-born old customer who smuggled himself back in and is wanted by the Tenryou Commission; she means to put him on a boat after the show. She and the Traveler gather fireworks and check on a boat with Kouichi, who has been questioned because any new vessel draws Tenryou attention. Yoimiya asks the Imatani couple in Konda Village about Sakujirou and learns he once quarrelled with their son Keisuke, now a Tenryou officer, over leaving Inazuma. The Tenryou raid the Naganohara house and Sakujirou escapes. At a blockade Yoimiya fights through, finds Keisuke and Sakujirou, and challenges Keisuke to a duel so that the two will talk. She wins, Keisuke lets Sakujirou leave and lights the firework the two once planned together, and Sakujirou sees it from his boat.

Act II. Now that the Sakoku Decree is lifted, Yoimiya tells the Traveler she wants to see Teyvat's greatest meteor shower, hoping it gives her an idea for a new firework. The Traveler takes her by ship from Ritou to Port Ormos in Sumeru. Nahida, who learns of the wish, says meteor showers cannot be predicted, and proposes creating one in a dream with the Aranara, giving the Traveler an Emberglow Leaf. In the city Yoimiya befriends Avin, a young girl in a wheelchair who longs to explore. When Avin goes missing, the group finds her, calls an Aranara with the leaf, and is led to Avin's Aranara friend. The shared dream restores Avin's ability to run and ends in a field of rising stars.

Act I details. The act opens lightly: children believe in the Great Mujina, and Yoimiya says they should not yet have to learn of the Vision Hunt Decree. Sakujirou says he left Inazuma to avoid responsibility but heartache brought him back. Yoimiya asks the Traveler about the wider world and, hearing of their search for a sibling, offers them a welcome and fireworks in Inazuma if they return. After the duel she gives Keisuke the finished firework that Sakujirou had ordered, so Keisuke sets it off; the Traveler watches from Amakane Island and is later given a slip for the golden firework Yoimiya made for them.

Act II details. Yoimiya asks her father to look after the shop and her mother while she is away. In Sumeru she buys Aranara carvings and quickly reads Avin's mood. Nahida warns the Traveler to get the story straight or Yoimiya will see through it, and Paimon is wary of the lie. Yoimiya admits she first wanted the trip for herself, but once people gave her wishes for the shower she felt bound to find one. Ahangar, a smith in Sumeru City, makes three lenses for a spotting device and mentions Urstone as the pinnacle of his craft. Avin's mother, Niousha, tells them Avin has been depressed since an illness; Avin tells them she used to run with an Aranara friend and fears forgetting. The Aranara Arapurva answers the leaf, deems Yoimiya trustworthy because her heart is pure and fierce like the sun, and leads them to Mawtiyima Forest, where the dream begins.

Act I: Keisuke tells Sakujirou not to throw his life away and promises help if he returns, expecting to be demoted for letting him go. Yoimiya says she does not mind her workload because she wants her customers happy. She leaves her father a note when she runs her errands.

Act II: in the dream Avin touches a great blue stone and meets her Aranara friend Arashani, then produces a lens from her own chest that Yoimiya uses to find the best place for the shower. Yoimiya says afterwards that she already knew it was a dream but is grateful for the effort. Avin leaves with her mother, one of them says they will come to Inazuma to see the show, and before sailing Yoimiya gives the Traveler another Aranara carving.

Revelations: Yoimiya shelters a wanted man at risk to herself and her family.

Ryuunosuke has been deaf since a workplace accident. Sakujirou, an Inazuman-born man, is wanted by the Tenryou Commission for leaving and returning during the Sakoku Decree.

In Act II, Nahida says no one has any precise idea when a meteor shower will occur, and they cannot be predicted. The meteor shower seen in the quest happens in a dream.

Characters: Yoimiya, the Traveler, Paimon.

Act I: Naganohara Ryuunosuke, Sakujirou, Kouichi, the Imatani couple (Saburou and his wife), Keisuke and Yoshitaka of the Tenryou Commission. Act II: Nahida, Avin and her mother Niousha, Ahangar, the Aranara Arapurva and Arashani.

Fayez, Azar, Layla, Alhaitham and Farid are mentioned or appear briefly in Act II.

Consequences: Act I: Sakujirou leaves Inazuma by boat and is reconciled with Keisuke. Act II: Avin regains confidence, and she or her mother plans to see the Naganohara show in Inazuma.

Placement: Act I unlocks at Adventure Rank 30 after Chapter II Act I, The Immovable God and the Eternal Euthymia, and takes place during the Sakoku Decree. Act II unlocks at Adventure Rank 40 after Chapter III Act V, Akasha Pulses, the Kalpa Flame Rises; the Imperatrix Umbrosa Chapter Act II, Transient Dreams; and the Aranara World Quest Dream Nursery. It was released in Version 3.7 and takes place after the Sakoku Decree has ended.

189.content: Act I of Yoimiya's Story Quest. Yoimiya hides a wanted man, Sakujirou, from the Tenryou Commission, and reconciles him with his friend Keisuke, a Tenryou officer, by challenging Keisuke to a duel and setting off a shared firework.

190.content: Act II of Yoimiya's Story Quest, set in Sumeru. Yoimiya wants to see a meteor shower; Nahida and the Aranara create one in a dream. A girl called Avin regains the ability to run in the dream and reunites with her Aranara friend.

191.content:
Caribert (also: Chapter III Act VI, Sumeru Archon Quest Act VI): Caribert is the sixth act of Chapter III, the Sumeru Archon Quest (version 3.5). Kaeya, unexpectedly in Sumeru, invites the Traveler and Paimon by letter to Djafar Tavern in Port Ormos, where Dainsleif tells him that his Alberich ancestors founded the Abyss Order. Dainsleif then leads them to a hut in Avidya Forest tied to the sibling's "Loom of Fate" operation, where a man calling himself Eide cares for a sick, masked hilichurl he names Caribert.

The act has four quests: Destined Encounter, Fortune-Mocking Pedigree, A Lamenter at Fate's End and Portended Fate. It requires Adventure Rank 35. It reveals the Abyss Order's founder, gives the first clear picture of how the Khaenri'ahns were cursed, and builds to a vision in which the Traveler sees themselves as their sibling.

The act is a quiet, character-driven interval after the main Akasha and Irminsul plot. It carries the sibling thread forward by following where the sibling and Dainsleif once travelled, and introduces the Chlothar and Caribert family tragedy that Bedtime Story (4.7) later returns to.

Plot: **Destined Encounter.** Masrur hands over Kaeya's letter, which was written so that delivery was guaranteed. At Djafar Tavern Kaeya has been drinking. Paimon expects him to be in Mondstadt, with Jean upset; he answers that he came to study Sumeru's spiced liquor. When the Traveler notes he is alone, he explains that as a boy he overheard Crepus discuss sending merchants to Sumeru, knew Khaenri'ah lay beneath it, and hid in the cargo before being caught. He says he knows little beyond books, that spending less time in Khaenri'ah left him caring less about it, and that he wonders whether his father wanted him to live happily in Mondstadt. After Dainsleif's announcement about the Alberichs, Kaeya says the conversation has become too serious and goes to meet a spice merchant. Dainsleif tells Paimon he does not know Kaeya well, and that while recovering he remembered the Loom of Fate operation the sibling mentioned when they travelled together in Sumeru. At the field in Avidya Forest he finds the surroundings familiar; after slimes appear he goes off alone to investigate the Ley Lines. Around the campfire the Traveler tells Paimon that they and the sibling used to look at the stars together and name worlds they wanted to visit, and that coming to Teyvat was the first time they had been separated.

**Fortune-Mocking Pedigree.** Eide fears the Traveler is from the Forest Rangers or the Akademiya. The Traveler recognises him as Khaenri'ahn from his features. He asks whether the Traveler believes in a god (the Traveler does not) and rants against the gods and their "gift" that ruined Khaenri'ah. Asked why some became hilichurls, he explains that one bloodline founded Khaenri'ah but all humans who rejected the gods were welcomed; the pure-blooded were cursed with immortality as the "greater sinners", the rest with the curse of the wilderness. He calls Caribert his illegitimate son with a woman from Mondstadt, born when he was dissatisfied with his life as a noble, and will not speak of the mother. He makes a medicine from Sumeru Rose and Kalpalata Lotus that needs the blessing of one of the Seven. It fails, so they prepare another batch, and fungi spawn while he makes fertilizer, which the Traveler repels.
