221.comment: Chapter IV: Masquerade of the Guilty: Meropide investigation
221.content: Neuvillette sends the Traveler and Paimon to the Fortress of Meropide under false charges to find Childe. They uncover the prison's hidden rules, the forbidden zone with its sluice gate, and Wriothesley's secret ship. The gate fails once and Neuvillette reseals it.

222.comment: Chapter IV: Masquerade of the Guilty: Disappearance case and Sinthe
222.content: Navia's investigation links her father's conviction and death to a ring that sold Sinthe made with Primordial Seawater and dissolved witnesses. The culprit, Marcel, is exposed as Vacher and later dies at the fountain. Neuvillette concedes he let Callas' duel proceed because he doubted anyone would die for justice.

key: Chapter ??: The Dream Yet to Be Dreamed
The Dream Yet to Be Dreamed
223.comment: Chapter ??: The Dream Yet to Be Dreamed
223.content:
Chapter ??: The Dream Yet to Be Dreamed (also: The Dream Yet to Be Dreamed, Khaenri'ah Archon Quest chapter): "The Dream Yet to Be Dreamed" is the announced title of the Archon Quest chapter centred on the fallen kingdom of Khaenri'ah. As of Version 7.1 it has not been released: there is no playable story, so nothing about its events is canon.

It is listed on the wiki as following Chapter VII (Snezhnaya) and preceding an unreleased Epilogue. Its chapter number is still shown as "??" in the game's own presentation, and its title was revealed through the Travail storyline preview.

Plot: No plot exists in released canon. Treat any story for this chapter as unknown and do not invent it.

The only substantive material is a short narration by Dainsleif in the Travail preview. It speaks, in general terms, of people who live content within a sheltered eternity versus those who dream of dreaming, hidden from the gaze of the gods, and of defying the world with a power from beyond. It names no events, places or outcomes.

Revelations: None have been released. Do not assume answers to open Khaenri'ah questions (such as its fate or the curse) come from this chapter.

Any link between the teaser and those mysteries is interpretation, not canon.

When portraying characters, keep them ignorant of this chapter's content: they may at most know the title and the teaser's general tone.

Characters: Dainsleif is the only figure tied to the chapter, as the narrator of the teaser. Participation of any other character is unannounced.

Consequences: Unknown: nothing has been released.

Placement: Intended to follow Chapter VII, whose latest act, A Rekviem for the Underworld, arrived in 7.1. It is the last chapter currently announced before the Epilogue.

key: The Dream Yet to Be Dreamed
224.comment: Chapter ??: The Dream Yet to Be Dreamed: The Dream Yet to Be Dreamed
224.content: The Dream Yet to Be Dreamed is the announced, unreleased final Archon Quest chapter about Khaenri'ah. As of 7.1 no story content exists, so characters must not state its events as known fact.

key: Chapter V: Incandescent Ode of Resurrection
225.comment: Chapter V: Incandescent Ode of Resurrection
225.content:
Chapter V: Incandescent Ode of Resurrection (also: Chapter V, Natlan Archon Quest, Natlan Chapter, Incandescent Ode of Resurrection chapter): Chapter V introduces Natlan: a land of Saurians and six tribes organised around the Stadium of the Sacred Flame, where the Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame produces Contending Fire, the fuel that keeps the Abyss out. The chapter's title is the name of Act V, and the travel log shows Acts I to V plus the Interlude as one block and Act VI as a Traveler chapter. Every act requires Adventure Rank 40.

Its arc: Act I introduces the tribes and the Pilgrimage; Act II shows the Pilgrimage failing and the Fatui Harbinger Capitano attacking Mavuika; Acts III and IV bring Capitano into an uneasy alliance and the Abyss's nation-wide invasion; the Interlude treats traumatised survivors; Act V ends the war and Capitano's quest; Act VI is the Abyss Order's attack and the sibling's reappearance.

The chapter is also the point at which the Traveler is given an Ancient Name, "Tumaini" (hope), forged by the Name Engraver Xilonen. It is the first such name given to an outlander. Thematically it keeps returning to sacrifice, memory and what a death means: the Ode of Resurrection lets bearers of Ancient Names be revived, so dying and being forgotten become the real stakes, and the Sacred Flame and Night Kingdom stand for the nation's shared memory and fuel. The Traveler's ability to purify Abyssal energy, first used on Dvalin in Mondstadt, is repeatedly decisive.

Release spread: Acts I and II in 5.0, III and IV in 5.1, the Interlude in 5.2, Act V in 5.3 and Act VI in 5.7. Threads that carry into later content: Capitano's Gnosis mission is cancelled, and the Doctor's research on Ancient Moon's Remnants in Nod-Krai is flagged.

Plot: Act I (5.0): the tribes, the Pilgrimage and Kachina's win. Act II (5.0): Kachina is lost in the Night Kingdom, Capitano attacks Mavuika, and the six-heroes plan is revealed. Act III (5.1): an uneasy contact with Capitano and the Abyss's nation-wide attack. Act IV (5.1): Capitano joins the alliance and the invasion costs lives. Interlude (5.2): survivors suffer Abyssal Corrosion Syndrome. Act V (5.3): Gosoythoth is destroyed and Capitano takes Xbalanque's seat. Act VI (5.7): the Abyss Order's attack on the tribes.

**Act I - Flowers Resplendent on the Sun-Scorched Sojourn (5.0).** See quest.flowers-resplendent-on-the-sun-scorched-sojourn. The Traveler befriends Kachina of the Children of Echoes and meets Mualani, Kinich and his companion K'uhul Ajaw. The Traveler cannot resonate with the Pyro Statue of The Seven. Kachina wins a place in the Night Warden War, and when the Abyss attacks the People of the Springs the Traveler purifies the fresh Abyssal wound of Atea, though her older contamination is too deep and she has only days left.

**Act II - Black Stone Under a White Stone (5.0).** Kachina falls in the Night Warden War but does not return when the Ode of Resurrection is sung. Mavuika suspends the Pilgrimage because Contending Fire is running out. Capitano, the First Fatui Harbinger, accuses Mavuika of failing an oath made 500 years ago and attacks her; she wounds him, but he escapes in a fog raised by a member of the Masters of the Night-Wind. A Spiritspeaker Stone ritual recovers Kachina's Ancient Name, and the Traveler, Mualani, Chasca and Iansan enter the Night Kingdom through a rift in old ruins and bring Kachina back. Mavuika burns the Pyro Archons' keepsakes to pull them out, and explains her plan: six heroes bearing Ancient Names are needed, four are known, and the remaining two must be found in less than a year. She asks Xilonen to forge a name for the Traveler.

**Act III - Beyond the Smoke and Mirrors (5.1).** Xilonen needs Citlali's help to approach the Wayob. Citlali agrees if they clear Ororon, who has been taken by the Fatui. In secret meetings Capitano tells the Traveler he wants them as an ally, doubts Mavuika's heroes will appear, and hints at a costly backup plan; Ororon's memories later show that Capitano means to rebuild Natlan's Ley Lines. The Abyss launches a nation-wide attack.

**Act IV - The Rainbow Destined to Burn (5.1).** Mavuika's group infiltrates Capitano's base and stops the Secret Source Mechanism. Ororon is attacked by the Khaenri'ahn soul Guthred but earns his Ancient Name, Bidii, as the fifth hero. The Lord of the Night, Yohualtecuhtin, speaks and explains the Night Kingdom's origin. Capitano reveals he is a Khaenri'ahn survivor and joins the alliance. The Abyss invades; the Scions of the Canopy fall, Chasca's adoptive younger sister Chuychu dies, and Chasca gains her name as the sixth hero. Mavuika declares a Night Warden War for everyone and destroys the rift.

**Interlude - All Fires Fuel the Flame (5.2).** The Traveler and Iansan help Flower-Feather Clan survivors who suffer Abyssal Corrosion Syndrome. Capitano supplies the Draught of Lucidity, unmasks his rotted face and names Ronova as the cause of his people's suffering. Xilonen begins the Traveler's name.

**Act V - Incandescent Ode of Resurrection (5.3).** The Traveler dreams of Capitano leading many souls. Xilonen finishes "Tumaini". Mavuika and the Traveler enter the Night Kingdom, are aided by fallen heroes, and destroy Gosoythoth, the Abyss's "Reaper". At the ruins of Ochkanatlan Ronova demands Mavuika's life; Capitano offers himself in her place, taking Xbalanque's seat and fusing with the Lord of the Night.

**Act VI - A Space and Time for You (5.7).** A Traveler chapter. The Abyss Order attacks every tribe; the Traveler meets Direidyth, who sees monsters invisible to others; Dainsleif and the Traveler break the Order's base at Ochkanatlan; the sibling reappears.

Further details by act. Act I: the Traveler and Paimon leave Fontaine from Romaritime Harbor with a photo taken by Charlotte, and farewells from Navia, Clorinde and Furina. They reach the Children of Echoes' canyon village and find Kachina abandoned by her would-be teammates before the Pilgrimage. Kinich says five people will earn the honour to fight in the war; Cival refuses to bend the rules for an outlander because Contending Fire is only produced by Natlanese fighters.

Act II: Mualani explains that in the Cataclysm the Abyss seemed to tailor its disasters to each tribe. Comonqui, an Abyss Lector in the Night Kingdom, taunts that the Pyro Archon hoards a primordial power. Tupac, a spirit, shows Mualani memories of the Cataclysm. In the aftermath Rezanov reports to Capitano that Mavuika has lost much of her power, and Capitano refuses to attack her while weakened.

Act III: Xilonen is startled to learn that the person she is working for is an outlander; the Night Kingdom records only the deeds of the Natlanese. Citlali's spell lets the Traveler overhear her thoughts, and she is embarrassed when she learns it. Ororon tells the Traveler he saved Capitano because otherwise the Fatui would have gone for Citlali. Ororon is, in Citlali's account, the tribe's only person with an incomplete soul, which his tribe regarded as a bad omen; an earlier ritual to use him as a vessel failed.

Act IV: the Lord of the Night says she is the Night Kingdom's builder from fragments of the old Ley Lines after the Descender's fight with the dragons, and that her kind, once called Angels, survives only in the form of Seelies. Capitano gives the history that he fled Khaenri'ah with his platoon to Natlan and learned about the Gnosis from Ayizu, chief of the Masters of the Night-Wind. Citlali confirms from the Lord of the Night that forging the Traveler's Ancient Name will cost Xilonen, the Name Engraver, her life; Citlali plans to use the Traveler's Descender status to delay Mavuika's death. The Lord of the Night creates the Pilgrim's Chronicle, which records the Traveler's deeds in Natlan.

Act V: at the party in the People of the Springs, Amina says Atea died after the attack. Ororon's ritual vision of Capitano names Guthred and the legendary hero Thrain. Tumaini's test in the Sulfurous Veins attracts too many souls and saves some, including Vichama, and a pair of Tepetlisaur souls who stay with Ayo. In the Night Kingdom Atea, Mallko, Vichama, Bona, Cocouik, Guthred and Chuychu help the Traveler. After Ronova's decision, Mavuika writes a letter for her sister Hine and burns it; the Traveler leaves the feathered crown they were given at a new monument to the fallen.

Act VI: Iansan's contest is cancelled when the Order attacks. The Traveler finds their sibling's Hibernation Chamber key, tells Mavuika that the sibling leads the Order, and fights the Order beside Citlali. Direidyth explains a sage told her of a doomsday only a Savior could stop. At the Ochkanatlan base the Iniquitous Baptist is Haden, Dainsleif's disgraced master, who claims the sibling re-wove Khaenri'ah's Ley Lines with the Loom of Fate. Dainsleif kills him repeatedly, and Haden admits the revival is unfinished and the attack was a ruse to harvest Dainsleif's memories. Direidyth and the Traveler realise they come from different points in time; as the Traveler decides what to do with the key, the sibling arrives, recognises Istaroth's hand in events, and says that Direidyth reaching them led them to abandon Khaenri'ah. The sibling explains the attack was a feint while Yohualtecuhtin let them weave the Atlas of the New World, holding New Khaenri'ah's Ley Lines.
Act IV and Act V rest on a detail of Ronova's curse: Capitano is immortal because of it, so his death forces a paradox; Ronova chooses to uphold the curse rather than break her rules, so Capitano may die and take the seat. Capitano's heart was altered to carry the souls of the Ley Lines.

Revelations: - Natlan's Pyro Archon, Mavuika, is a human who was already an experienced warrior before she ascended. She fights alongside the heroes and has spent much of her power to keep the Sacred Flame burning.
- The Night Kingdom is the nation's spirit realm built from fragments of the old Ley Lines by the Lord of the Night, Yohualtecuhtin, whose kind were once called Angels.
- The Fatui's Capitano is a Khaenri'ahn survivor of the Cataclysm who fought for Natlan 500 years ago. Ronova cursed him and his people with immortality in decay. He is the first Harbinger.
- Natlan's Ancient Name bearers are chosen by the Wayob; the six heroes are Kinich, Iansan, Xilonen, Mualani, Ororon and Chasca. The Traveler receives the outlander name Tumaini.
- The false sky is briefly exposed in Act IV.

- Mavuika used a power from Ronova, the Ruler of Death, through Xbalanque; the price was her death, which Capitano spares.
- The sibling leads the Abyss Order, re-wove Khaenri'ah's Ley Lines with the Loom of Fate into the Atlas of the New World, and says it is needed to face the Heavenly Principles as equals. Direidyth, whom Dainsleif believes to be a pure-blooded Khaenri'ahn, comes from a different point in time, and the sibling says Istaroth played a part in their meeting.
- Mavuika learns Capitano had the Tsaritsa end his Gnosis mission, and that the Doctor's subordinates are studying Ancient Moon's Remnants in Nod-Krai.

Characters: The Traveler and Paimon; Mavuika; the six heroes Kinich (with K'uhul Ajaw), Mualani, Iansan, Xilonen, Ororon and Chasca; Kachina; Citlali; the Fatui Harbinger Capitano; Yohualtecuhtin the Lord of the Night; Ronova; chiefs such as Pacal and Amina; and Wayna, who supplies the Spiritspeaker Stone. In Act VI Direidyth, Dainsleif, Haden and the Traveler's sibling.

Consequences: The war with the Abyss ends: The Natlanese honour the Traveler with a festival and a monument to the fallen. Capitano is gone, but Mavuika lives and the Lord of the Night is granted eternal life. Mavuika warns that Snezhnaya, with the Fatui, will be the next conflict. The Abyss Order's attack in Act VI leaves the sibling free with the Atlas of the New World.

Song of the Welkin Moon, set in Nod-Krai, follows, and Chapter VII is set in Snezhnaya. Mavuika's warnings point the Traveler towards Snezhnaya and name Nod-Krai as the Doctor's base.

Placement: Follows Chapter IV (Fontaine, with Act VI "Bedtime Story") and precedes the Nod-Krai content of 6.x and the Snezhnaya chapter (Chapter VII). Acts were released across 5.0 to 5.3, and the Traveler chapter, Act VI, arrived much later in 5.7.

226.comment: Chapter V: Incandescent Ode of Resurrection: Natlan's six heroes and the Ancient Names
226.content: Mavuika's plan needs six modern heroes who inherit the Ancient Names of past warriors: Kinich (Malipo), Iansan (Uwezo), Xilonen (Baraka), Mualani (Umoja), Ororon (Bidii, previously borne by Sanhaj) and Chasca (Vuka, previously borne by Menilek). The Traveler is given the outlander name "Tumaini".

227.comment: Chapter V: Incandescent Ode of Resurrection: Capitano's role in Natlan
227.content: Capitano is the first Fatui Harbinger and a Khaenri'ahn who fled to Natlan after the Cataclysm. He first attacks Mavuika for the Pyro Gnosis, then offers an alternative plan with the Source Mechanism, and finally joins the alliance. In Act V he sacrifices himself to Ronova's curse to spare Mavuika.

key: A Space and Time for You
228.comment: Chapter V: Incandescent Ode of Resurrection: Act VI - A Space and Time for You
228.content: Act VI is the Traveler chapter of Chapter V. The Abyss Order attacks all the tribes, the Traveler meets Direidyth, and the sibling reappears with the Atlas of the New World.

229.content:
Chapter VII: Everwinter Without Mercy (also: Chapter VII, Snezhnaya Archon Quest, Snezhnaya Chapter, Everwinter Without Mercy chapter): The four acts are Everwinter Without Mercy (7.0), Wraith's Nocturne (7.0), White Night, Like a Dream Upon Waking (7.1) and A Rekviem for the Underworld (7.1). The chapter requires Adventure Rank 18 and the Prologue's Act III. Its teaser quotes Dainsleif calling the Tsaritsa a god with no love left for her people, and the chapter answers that line from several angles. Snezhnaya's Archon Quest was originally numbered Act VI in the Travail preview and became Chapter VII after Song of the Welkin Moon was added.

The chapter has three threads that keep crossing. The first is the country: a winter that never lets up, Kresnik Kristall shortages, Project Stuzha, and ordinary people (a hunter, a ballerina, a singer) trying to get by. The second is the Fatui: the Harbingers Sandrone, Childe, Pantalone, Pulcinella and Arlecchino are shown as officials with duties and disagreements, and Director Pierro finally speaks with the Traveler. The third is the Curse of Death, which kills everyone in range whenever a technological breakthrough threatens Celestia, and which turns out to be the work of Ronova. Paimon's strange illness is the personal thread tying them together.

Structurally the chapter moves from outsider travelogue (Act I), through a closed-room mystery that is secretly a death-curse (Act II), to a court-and-politics act that reveals the Tsaritsa's reasoning (Act III), and ends with a war plan against a Shade (Act IV). Each act tightens the Traveler's alliance with the Fatui. As of the 7.1 cutoff the chapter is unfinished: no next chapter is named, and the Holy Soil threat that Act IV ends on is unresolved.

Plot: **Act I - Everwinter Without Mercy (7.0).** Columbina throws the Traveler and Paimon a farewell party on the Flagship before they head to Snezhnaya, where Paimon quickly falls ill. A gust of wind blows the Traveler off a bridge, separating them, and the Traveler meets the Eye of Graeae, an ancient device that recognises them as a Descender. Pierro, whom the Traveler does not recognise (Paimon later names him), watches over Paimon in a cabin and leaves. In the town of Sretomorozsk the hunter Alyosha explains Project Stuzha, and they expose a corrupt official hoarding Kresnik Kristall. In Snezhnograd the Traveler joins Sandrone at a troubled mine, rescues the trapped miners and creates the Exaiphanes Blade, meets the ballerina and Fatuus Odette (Signora's protégée, not a Harbinger), and is invited to join the Rokot.

**Act II - Wraith's Nocturne (7.0).** At the Korolevskiy Theater a rehearsal is followed by a snowstorm, and the people trapped inside begin dying, two a night. The group first suspects Odette, who admits she is Lelek, the thief who leaves threatening letters. The truth is that everyone is under the Curse of Death: some guests are revealed to be dead already, the "Alyosha" trapped with them turns out to be Ronova wearing his appearance, and the Traveler and Mitya strike her and escape. Everyone wakes with no memory of it until they gather and recall the shared "dream". Pierro has taken Paimon to the Armory Palace; there he explains Project Mistilteinn, the Curse, and the Fatui's goal of challenging the Heavenly Principles, and the Traveler sides with them to protect Paimon.

**Act III - White Night, Like a Dream Upon Waking (7.1).** The Tsaritsa returns from killing the storm-making monster. The Traveler is tested by Danica, attends court, and is told in private why the Tsaritsa collects the Gnoses and about the Third Descender's seal. Pierro unveils a memory-reading prism, and Sandrone and Pantalone propose using Vesna's small authority of Life as a counter to the Curse: Seals of Life, memory bubbles drawn from many people. A creature of the Ruler of Life steals seals from Northland Bank, and Rhinedottir appears and takes back the stolen power, only to be drawn into a meeting with the Tsaritsa.

**Act IV - A Rekviem for the Underworld (7.1).** See quest.a-rekviem-for-the-underworld: the Delusion experiment, Hroptatyr's notebook, and the battle that strips Ronova of her authority.

Further Act I detail. Columbina also relays a message from Sandrone, who left earlier for Snezhnograd, telling them not to cause trouble for her. After a bridge fall and a wrecked train, the Traveler uses "Fab-Vision" with Graeae to climb out of a cavern. The corrupt official Shishkin and the mayor are arrested by the Fatui representative Polonsky, who hints that Alyosha has the makings of a Rokot member. The train is pulled into a Shadow Realm without wind, light or elemental energy, where Graeae gives the Traveler a new outfit and weapons. At the mine in Svetloledovka the Traveler draws on an unusual power to form the Exaiphanes Blade, and later uses it to empower the Cryo Statue of the Seven in Snezhnograd. Odette helps buy Kristall using Fatui logistics. At a Veche session Project Stuzha passes with 61 percent support, narrower than before, while the merchant Chugunov, against expectation, votes against it. Alyosha, who is secretly a Rokot member along with the singer Vodyanitsa, formally invites the Traveler to join; members stay anonymous and work freely.

Further Act II detail. The victims on the first night are the merchants Soboleva and Torgov, and on the second Kulish and Rampana. A man named Shram, who has no ticket, turns out to be a ghost from the era of human-fae hostility that ended over 400 years ago, who died in the theater protecting his girlfriend; he leaves peacefully. A girl called Tonia is revealed to be dead: she recalls being ill with Frostblight and falling asleep at a show, and Chugunov, who knew, had projected his own dead daughter Iskra onto her. She gives her real name as Ptashka and leaves. Mitya has been dead the whole time without remembering it, and carries a red eye mark on his palm that the Traveler identifies as Ronova's. Ronova explains soul-ferrying, says angels' renovation of the theater's Ley Lines hinders her, and says a Descender's soul cannot enter the Ley Lines. Afterwards Chugunov shuts down the Iskra Manufacturing Plant, and Odette visits Signora's tomb and decides to go on as both ballerina and Fatuus. Pierro tells the group he drew Paimon down from Celestia to Khaenri'ah and presented her to Irmin, who took no interest; this implies she is at least 500 years old, though she remembers none of it.

Further Act III detail. Pulcinella's report to the Tsaritsa mentions corruption cases; Mitya says no existing technology can deal with the Ruler of Death. The Tsaritsa tells the Traveler her authority is "love", which she refuses to use because the love the Heavenly Principles granted was false. Pierro explains she records each day in a transcription prism that Irminsul changes cannot alter. Pierro introduces the Mirror of Remembrance (the Svetovid Stone) and Vesna reveals she bears the mark of Life; reviewing memories through it shows that Ronova had been "killing" without permission by exploiting a gap in the Heavenly Principles' monitoring while Rhinedottir resurrected the dead before the Shades could be caught. The Seal of Life program is obligatory for officials and nobles, voluntary for the public through Northland Bank. The Tsaritsa arranged the collection partly to draw Rhinedottir out, then offers her information about Asmoday and a meeting in seven days.

Additional Act III detail. Danica says her family has served the Tsaritsa for three generations and that the Tsaritsa let her travel as a mercenary, which Danica regards as an act of love. The thief at Northland Bank is a "False Horned Steed" created by the Ruler of Life. Pantalone cooperates in the vault, explaining that the bank combines human and fae traditions, and later gives Vesna a small lantern holding her returned power.

Additional Act I detail. The Eye of Graeae helps the Traveler in exchange for a later favour; its knowledge of present-day Snezhnaya is out of date, which is why the train runs off a cliff on derelict tracks (it and its passengers come through unscathed). Odette reacts badly to learning that the Traveler once duelled Signora before the throne, though Childe says the two were not on good terms.

Revelations: - Snezhnaya's goal under the Tsaritsa is to build enough power to face the Heavenly Principles, which have kept the nation at risk of a Celestial Nail as it grows.
- The Tsaritsa's authority is love; she rejects using it because the love given by the Heavenly Principles was not real.
- Ronova, the Ruler of Death, is behind the Curse of Death, which strikes whenever a technological breakthrough threatens Celestia.
- Pierro drew Paimon down from Celestia; she is at least about 500 years old and was once presented to Irmin of Khaenri'ah.
- Project Mistilteinn is an anti-Celestia weapon; its energy was making Paimon, a being of Celestia, ill.

- A crystalline seal in Zapolyarny Palace was left by the Third Descender before the Heavenly Principles killed them; it reacts only to the Gnoses and its contents are unknown.
- Vesna holds a small authority of Life, stolen by the Archangel in the Hyperborean era and kept by the first Vila.
- Ronova and Rhinedottir had been killing and reviving people within a loophole in the Heavenly Principles' monitoring cycles.
- The Pyro Gnosis burned with Irminsul in Sumeru (the Traveler's account); the Tsaritsa expects any remnant of a Descender to be ejected from the Ley Lines eventually.
- Act IV adds the Crimson Moon's connection to death and the Fatui's plan to create more Delusions.

Characters: The Traveler and Paimon; Columbina (farewell scene); the Harbingers Sandrone, Tartaglia (Childe), Pantalone, Pulcinella, Arlecchino and Director Pierro; the ballerina and Fatuus Odette (Lelek); the Rokot members Alyosha and Vodyanitsa; the researcher Mitya and guard Valeriy; Chugunov and the ghost girl Tonia (Ptashka); Danica and Vesna of the Tsaritsa's court; the Tsaritsa; Ronova, Rhinedottir and Naberius; Dainsleif (Act IV).

Consequences: Project Stuzha is put on hold once the Tsaritsa returns, easing the energy shortage. Project Mistilteinn is paused at the end of Act II until Ronova can be dealt with (the Tsaritsa confirms this in Act III), then released when she is stripped of her authority in Act IV. The Traveler becomes a trusted ally of the Fatui and gains unrestricted access to Zapolyarny Palace. After 7.1 completion, the Anomaly world quest series opens.

The Fatui plan to produce new Delusions with Arlecchino's help, and the House of the Hearth separates from Fatui affairs. Ronova's last act in Act IV threatens to unleash Holy Soil from a Nail of Retribution, a thread left open at the cutoff.

Placement: Requires the Prologue's Act III (Song of the Welkin Moon is the preceding quest in the travel log but was never named Chapter VI). Acts I-II released in 7.0 (2026-08-12) and Acts III-IV in 7.1 (2026-09-23).

230.comment: Chapter VII: Everwinter Without Mercy: Project Stuzha
230.content: Project Stuzha is the Tsaritsa's plan to lower energy use across Snezhnaya so that supply can go to crucial research. It caused a shortage of Kresnik Kristall, the fuel for stoves, and left towns like Sretomorozsk with closed businesses. A Veche vote kept it alive at 61 percent in Act I; it was put on hold when the Tsaritsa returned.

231.comment: Chapter VII: Everwinter Without Mercy: Curse of Death theater incident
231.content: When Mitya conceives a technological breakthrough, the Curse of Death kills everyone nearby, who then wake without memory of it. At the Korolevskiy Theater the curse became a closed-circle mystery with deaths each night, the ghosts Shram and Ptashka among the guests, and Ronova disguised as Alyosha. Odette is revealed as Lelek in the process.

232.comment: Chapter VII: Everwinter Without Mercy: Seals of Life
232.content: A Seal of Life is a bubble holding one meaningful memory from a person's life, made with Vesna's authority of Life. Enough of them could defy death. Officials and nobles were required to donate; the public could give voluntarily at Northland Bank. A creature of the Ruler of Life tried to steal them from the vault; the Tsaritsa froze it, and Rhinedottir let it escape, reclaimed the stolen Life power and restored the seals to their owners.

233.comment: Chapter VII: Everwinter Without Mercy: Project Mistilteinn
233.content: Mitya's research programme, described as an anti-Celestia weapon. Its energy made Paimon ill, and every breakthrough risks the Curse of Death. Paused at the end of Act II (confirmed by the Tsaritsa in Act III) and no longer restricted after Act IV.

key: An Ancient Sacrifice of Sacred Brocade
234.content:
Chenyu's Blessings of Sunken Jade (also: Chenyu Vale world quest series, Qiaoying of the Sacred Mountain, Floating Jade, Treasure of Chenyu, An Ancient Sacrifice of Sacred Brocade, Rainjade Rite quest): A Version 4.4 world quest series set in Chenyu Vale, Liyue. The Traveler meets the adeptus Fujin, who says the vale's water and soil are declining, which endangers Qiaoying Village's tea. They gather her scattered power, learn that the beast Lingyuan has been disrupting the land, and see the Rainjade Rite completed.

The series has three quests: Qiaoying of the Sacred Mountain, Floating Jade, Treasure of Chenyu, and An Ancient Sacrifice of Sacred Brocade. It requires The Outlander Who Caught the Wind and entering Chenyu Vale. It ends with the village promised a fresh tea batch for the coming Lantern Rite.

It doubles as local history: the mural, the boatman and Little Mao give differing tellings of how the Jademouth ring came to lie in the river, and the old friendship of Fujin and Lingyuan explains why the land is contested between a nurturing adeptus and a beast who remembers a wilder vale.

Plot: Fujin pulls the Traveler into an adepti realm and says Chenyu Vale is declining. In Qiaoying Village tea quality has been dropping. The Traveler seeks a technician, follows a golden carp (Fujin), explores a shrine with Little Mao, gathers Fujin's power from carp across the vale, and faces Lingyuan, who admits she caused the disruption. The Rainjade Rite is then performed.

Grandpa Lu mistakes the Traveler for Feiyun Commerce Guild envoys and blames the soil and water for worse tea. Uncle Luo blames a tea machine and scolds a worker, Jin. A taste test of cakes from an old batch and a new batch shows the new one tastes off. Luo sends for a Fontainian technician at Yilong Wharf, Hautemontagne, whom the Traveler finds with Little Mao. Fujin, appearing as a golden carp, confirms Lu is right: if the decline continues the village could be abandoned and the vale return to a barren state. A beast watches the party unseen. Mao leads the Traveler to a mural of an old war, then to the Jademouth, and a boatman named Bosu gives his account of how it got there. In the shrine caverns, the Traveler meets a Solitary Suanni nicknamed Bluey, who says the new tea leaves were better before and then vanishes.

Bluey turns out to be Lingyuan. Fujin needs her power back to perform the rite, and that power took the form of golden carp around the vale; the Traveler finds them all. Lingyuan interrupts, says she has the situation under control, warns Fujin away and leaves. Fujin is shocked that her former friend would unbalance the land: Lingyuan's disruption of the spirit veins let the miasma spread, and with full control of the mountain she could reshape the vale. After a fight, Lingyuan explains that as a beast she remembers everything while humans forget; the tea trees Fujin planted gave a taste she recalls and cannot find today. After Fujin and the white snake left, she wanted to return the vale to its original state, seeing it as subdued by humanity. Satisfied with the answers, she lets Fujin restore the vale. The effort sends Fujin back to her carp form to recover. Lingyuan wonders how the Traveler brought Fujin back, thanks them, and cannot yet say what she thinks of humans. Lu and Luo thank the Traveler and promise a fresh batch for the Lantern Rite.

Details of the middle quest: Little Mao contradicts Bosu's telling of the Jademouth. In Mao's version a bad god once tried to redirect the river to drown the Millelith, and a giant white snake and a carp disobeyed her orders, with the carp throwing jade into the river to pin it down and stop the flood. The mural shows a great war between two factions whose bloodshed turned the Bishui River red. Mao says the Jademouth was presumably thrown by an adeptus. The shrine is solved through puzzles after driving out Treasure Hoarders. The three tellings are not reconciled in the quest.

Revelations: Lingyuan, not the tea machine, is behind the soil and water problems. Fujin and Lingyuan were once friends. A beast remembers what humans forget, and that memory motivated Lingyuan's wish to restore the vale's old state.

Characters: The Traveler and Paimon; Fujin (adeptus, golden carp); Lingyuan (a beast called Bluey); villagers Grandpa Lu, Uncle Luo and worker Jin; Fontainian technician Hautemontagne; Little Mao; boatman Bosu.

Lu is the village elder who knows the land's history; Luo runs the tea workshop and is brusque with workers; Little Mao guides the Traveler through the Rainjade Rite and its sites.

Consequences: The vale's balance is restored, Qiaoying Village's tea can recover, and the villagers say they will help the Traveler in future. Fujin is left to recover as a carp, and Lingyuan remains in the vale, unanswered on humanity.

Placement: Released in Version 4.4 with Chenyu Vale. It requires The Outlander Who Caught the Wind. Its quests run in this order: Qiaoying of the Sacred Mountain, Floating Jade, Treasure of Chenyu, and An Ancient Sacrifice of Sacred Brocade.

235.comment: Chenyu's Blessings of Sunken Jade: Rainjade Rite
235.content: The Rainjade Rite is the ritual Fujin says is needed to drive the miasma out of Chenyu Vale. She does not explain how until the Traveler reaches the site. It requires her power, scattered as golden carp across the vale, and is performed after Lingyuan agrees not to stop it.

236.comment: Chenyu's Blessings of Sunken Jade: Lingyuan and Fujin
236.content: Fujin is the adeptus who made Chenyu Vale inhabitable and planted its tea trees. Lingyuan is a beast who disrupted the spirit veins because she remembered the vale's old taste and wanted to undo human influence. Their friendship and its break drive the series. See their own entries for fuller detail.

key: Chromatic Ode of Candies and Roses
237.comment: Chromatic Ode of Candies and Roses
237.content:
Chromatic Ode of Candies and Roses (also: Sabzeruz Festival event, Birthday Celebration Anecdotes, Give Her Surprises, Give Her Sweetness, Give Her Memories): The event story, told in three "gifts" (Give Her Surprises, Give Her Sweetness, Give Her Memories), follows a group of friends in and around Port Ormos and Pardis Dhyai who plan a candy-tower surprise, a Haft-Mewa feast and a Parade for the Dendro Archon without letting her find out. Alongside this, Candace's gem seems to show her events before they happen, a caravan is robbed, and Nilou disappears to learn an older version of the Dance of Sabzeruz from a Pari named Sorush. The mystery resolves into the legend of the first Sabzeruz Festival and ends with a successful Parade and a group photograph.

Players who gathered 800 Festive Fervor could invite Candace to the party. Requirements were Adventure Rank 20 and the Prologue Act III Archon Quest; the Archon Quest Akasha Pulses, the Kalpa Flame Rises and several Sumeru quests were recommended.

Plot: First Gift, Give Her Surprises. Paimon and the Traveler arrive in Port Ormos just before the Sabzeruz Festival and find Tighnari, Collei, Dehya and Candace whispering about a plan: a birthday surprise for the Dendro Archon, an idea Dehya had while talking with Dunyarzad. The plan is a candy tower, a Haft-Mewa feast after the Carriage Parade, and decorations, with Kaveh doing most of the design. Candace asks the Traveler and Paimon to help shop. She haggles hard with a food stall, then, with Paimon, notices she is acting oddly: she twice reacts before accidents happen (a stove explosion, a falling crate that she stops from hitting a small girl). She explains she has been seeing things moments before they come true since buying an unusual gem that morning. They ask Dori to trace the gem; Candace bargains Dori down with a promise of food, shelter, security and tax relief in Aaru Village.

Second Gift, Give Her Sweetness. Dori reports the ore came from a nameless desert ruin and was cut into two gems because it was cracked. Meanwhile a caravan carrying supposed fireworks was robbed in a remote desert path by people with an apparent ability to predict the route. Candace and the Traveler find the caravan crew (Yakup, Hizir, Aruj), and Yakup mentions a bandit with a green stone like Candace's. At Caravan Ribat Cyno takes over the case. Back in Port Ormos Candace has another vision and overhears a seemingly sinister plot, which turns out to be Kaveh and Alhaitham talking about the candy tower. Alhaitham suggests the visions may show the past, not the future. Faruzan helps Kaveh with a model of the Flower Carriage, and when Nahida unexpectedly appears the group scrambles to hide the plan, helped by Nilou drawing her away. Tighnari moves the meeting place to Pardis Dhyai.

Third Gift, Give Her Memories. Nilou, the dancer for the Parade, is missing. Cyno, Candace and the Traveler follow her trail out of the city to the Fane of Ashvattha, where they find her with Sethos and a Pari named Sorush, who is teaching her the original Dance of Sabzeruz. Sorush and her companions were behind the caravan attack; Sethos had talked her out of going further. Sethos, who owns the second half of the gem, explains it is a cracked Wedjat Eye. The group returns to finish the tower, the Traveler is chosen as the Knight of Flowers, and the Parade proceeds. Afterwards everyone celebrates, and Nahida has a group photograph taken.

Details. In the first act Dehya's desert mercenary style and Collei's nerves provide comic relief, and Layla (worried by deadline) is only heard of in the open world. The caravan crew's comic bickering hides that their cargo was not clearly fireworks. Cyno is told a second gem went to a young man in the desert and, in Act III, checks the original seller. In Act III Nilou had left a message with the Pari Rashnu, who fell asleep before delivering it, so no one knew where she was. Sorush calls the Traveler "my Yasnapati" and Paimon "Pale Floater". Candace plays the tanbur for Nilou's dance in the Parade, and Dunyarzad asks the Knight of Flowers (the Traveler) to hang decorations on the Flower Carriage at the Sanctuary of Surasthana.

Revelations: Sethos tells the legend. At the first Sabzeruz Festival, King Deshret and Lady Malikata (Nabu Malikata, the Goddess of Flowers) secretly prepared a banquet for their friend, leading her along a trail of candy to a lake where Deshret played an instrument and Malikata danced. Malikata gave her the Khvarena to protect the rainforest; Deshret gave her the Wedjat Eye, to record their shared moments. The Wedjat Eye was lost after the Khaenri'ah cataclysm and buried in the sands. Sorush adds that Kusanali made the Khvarena into a divine bird guarding the border between birth and death, until it shattered and gave rise to the Pari. The Eye still records scenes, but only resonates with people of Al-Ahmar, the descendants of King Deshret.

Candace fears that what remains in the cracked memory may be mostly grief, and the group agrees with Sethos placing both halves in the care of the Temple of Silence rather than giving them to Nahida straight away. Alhaitham later says he would only examine it if it were brought to the Akademiya for certification.

Characters: Planners: Dehya, Candace, Tighnari, Collei, Kaveh, Faruzan, Dunyarzad, Cyno, Nilou (the dancer). Others: Alhaitham (sceptical helper), Sethos, the Pari Sorush, Rashnu and Mihir, Dori (informant), and the caravan crew Yakup, Hizir and Aruj. Nahida is the target of the surprise.

Cyno, Kaveh and Alhaitham provide most of the humour; Sheikh Zubayr, Nevida and a gate guard named Rukn help trace Nilou. The Wanderer and Layla appear in the open world in ambient dialogue only.

Consequences: The Parade is a success: candy explodes over the Flower Carriage like fireworks. Afterwards a party at Pardis Dhyai ends with Nahida saying this will be her most unforgettable birthday and inviting the Pari to Sumeru City, which Sorush politely declines. The Wedjat Eye halves go to the Temple of Silence. Cyno takes over the caravan case and plans to watch it under cover of protection.

Placement: Released in Version 5.1 as a Flagship Event, set in Sumeru after Nahida's rescue and reinstatement as Archon, when the Akademiya supports the festival again. The wiki notes the Sabzeruz Festival had been marginalised under the Akademiya's earlier leadership. The three story quests were removed after the event.

Gameplay: Game mechanics, not in-world fact. Three mini-games unlocked in sequence: Rocking Carriage (steer the Flower Carriage and collect flowers), Interreflection of Reality and Dreams (help the Amurta Dastur Dharmakirti run dreamscape therapy for patients) and Shadow of the Knight's Blade (battle challenges that recreate the legend of the Knight of Flowers). Playing them earned Festive Fervor toward the rewards and Candace's invitation.

238.comment: Chromatic Ode of Candies and Roses: Wedjat Eye
238.content: King Deshret's birthday gift to Lesser Lord Kusanali (originally Rukkhadevata) at the first Sabzeruz Festival, intended to record shared memories. It was lost after the Khaenri'ah cataclysm, later cracked and cut into two gems, one bought by Candace and one by Sethos. It records past events, resonates with Al-Ahmar's people, and gives bearers vivid glimpses. Both halves go to the Temple of Silence.

239.comment: Chromatic Ode of Candies and Roses: Sorush
239.content: A Pari who calls herself noble and the Bloomguard of Khvarena. Elder Zurvan chose her to present the Dance of Sabzeruz to Lesser Lord Kusanali. She attacked the caravan with Mihir's thorns (and a sleepy Rashnu), then took Nilou to the Fane of Ashvattha to teach her the original dance.

240.comment: Chromatic Ode of Candies and Roses: Dance of Sabzeruz
240.content: The most important part of the Sabzeruz Festival, based on the Goddess of Flowers' dance. In this event Nilou learns the older form from Sorush and performs it in the Parade to Candace's tanbur playing.

241.comment: Chromatic Ode of Candies and Roses: Flower Carriage Parade
241.content: The festival procession in which Nahida rides the Flower Carriage, attended by an actor playing the Knight of Flowers. In this event the Traveler is nominated for the part by friends representing Darshans. Kaveh's candy tower bursts over the carriage like fireworks.

242.comment: Chromatic Ode of Candies and Roses: Haft-Mewa Feast
242.content: A festival feast with seven foods on the table. The friends plan one for Nahida after the Parade, and it is the setting of the post-Parade celebration.

243.comment: Chromatic Ode of Candies and Roses: Candace's visions
243.content: After buying a strange gem, Candace sees events seconds before they occur and anticipates a stove explosion and a falling crate. Alhaitham suggests she is seeing the past; later she hears faint voices she wonders were Al-Ahmar and Malikata. The gem is half of the cracked Wedjat Eye and only works for people of Al-Ahmar.

key: Chronicler of the Crumbling City World Quest series
244.content:
Chronicler of the Crumbling City (also: Chronicler of the Crumbling City World Quest series, Sacred City of Tollan quests): Chronicler of the Crumbling City is a Natlan world quest series in which the Traveler, Paimon and the Little One enter the Great Volcano and discover the buried dragon city of Tollan. A guiding voice speaking through old Secret Source machines helps them restore the city's power, cleanse Abyssal corruption, and obtain the permit needed to reach the Heart of the Sacred Mountain.

The series has three main quests: The Frozen, Rekindling Land, In Search of a Hidden Heart, and As the Burning Sun Sears Shadows. Each has sub-quests: two for the first, five for the second. Most of the story is told through machines that speak for the dead, and each time the voice uses a different borrowed name.

The tone is elegiac. The city is dark, the dragons who built it are gone, and the voice describes it as barely alive. The player work is to relight, cleanse and unlock it, not to learn the whole history. The history that does surface comes in fragments: a war between the surviving dragonborn and humans, the death of the original master of flame, and a trial that ended in farce.

Plot: **The Frozen, Rekindling Land.** The party falls into the pitch-dark space below the volcano. A stone figure that looks like a rolled-up creature activates and speaks, naming itself Ehecatl, a name taken from a list of the fallen 150 years after a war. It explains that the master of this place, the original master of flame, died in the war between the remaining dragonborn and humans, and that the city has been dying since. It asks the Traveler to activate a mechanism so the voice can light the city, showing the first Sacred City, Tollan, in ruins. Its power fails and it goes quiet. The Traveler then restabilises the two other Astral Assemblages (The Forsaken Sea of Wisdom and Sealed Site of Sacrifice), and a Secret Source Servant now announces itself as Amaru, once the guardian of the sealed Celestial Axis. The Axis descends through the clouds to a region infested by the Abyss. Amaru warns that the city is infested and says a permit is needed to reach the Heart of the Sacred Mountain.

**In Search of a Hidden Heart.** A larger Secret Source Servant that has no name and no knowledge of the party says it was a prototype made to help Lord Xiuhcoatl with record keeping and has been alone since his fall. It marks sites of Abyssal corrosion where data can be recovered as Phlogiston Units. Three of them are needed to power the Secret Source Dragon Idol guarding the entrance. In the Chamber of Deliberation, the voice returns under the name Awanyu to help obtain the permit (Once, the Sacred Seat of Judgment). Three parallel sub-quests clear corroded areas (the Calculation Array, Force Inversion and the Armament Workshop). In The End of the Road the Traveler gives the Dragon Idol the permit and three Phlogiston Units, and it dives into the pit, opening the way down.

**As the Burning Sun Sears Shadows.** The Traveler enters the huge space beneath the volcano, the Heart of the Sacred Mountain, which is infested with the Abyss. A voice tells the "Chosen of Dragons" that the power of blazing fire now rests within them. The party clears the Abyss, releases the Astral Assemblages, and destroys the Oozing Cores that try to flee.

Additional detail. The first guide says it can speak only as long as the city has enough phlogiston, and that it uses names from a list of the fallen. It tells the party that, because of an oath, only a "human" may activate the seals, and muses that history repeats itself in cycles of tyranny, revolt and revenge, comparing it to a staged play. Amaru tells them the fireballs (Astral Assemblages) cannot fight the Abyss directly: contact leads to mutual annihilation or corruption.

Records the Servant can read to the party once enough Phlogiston Units are recovered concern how Secret Source Servants were created, "humans and exceptional individuals thereof", and corrosion and physical conditions. The Servant also explains that Lord Xiuhcoatl excavated downward to make a stable experimental environment and there built the ultimate weapon against the Abyss, but the seal on it caused the deepest corruption.

In Once, the Sacred Seat of Judgment, a golden purification barrier rises in the Chamber. As it rises, the party sees shadows of dragon lords denouncing a prince in front of the Silver Prince, accusing him of delivering phlogiston to humans and of sheltering an escaped test subject (Och-Kan). Awanyu speaks scornfully of the assembly and says the denouncement was a power grab. The permit proves to be only a vessel that must be activated by an Iridescent Inscription at the top of a rising platform.

During the rise, Awanyu says that when the Abyss swallowed the Dark-Winged Lord and a Celestial Nail reshaped the world and its laws, the dragon race's old reach collapsed. He suggests the world might long ago have been cleansed by the flames of rebirth, asking the party whether they agree. He also says the Thirteen Lords and Three Princes withdrew their charges when the true king appeared, that the Three Princes later died fighting humanity, that ten lords fell when Tollan collapsed, that one remains in Chichen Uctokah and that one survives to the present day, in a form it would not have wished. After the permit is activated he vanishes again.

Gameplay notes (labelled as such, not lore): the Phlogiston meter does not decrease during parts of the third quest, and a Secret Source Beam Cannon with unlimited ammunition appears. Completing certain sub-quests awards achievements.

Revelations: - Tollan, the first Sacred City, lies inside the volcano and was once the seat of Lord Xiuhcoatl, the "original master of flame", who died in a war between surviving dragonborn and humans.
- The Heart of the Sacred Mountain (also named Huitzilopochtli by the Servant) was dug when Tollan was rebuilt; Xiuhcoatl built a weapon against the Abyss there, and the seal on it caused the worst corruption.
- The Abyss is invading Tollan, and ending it entirely might require bringing the mountain down.

- The guiding voice has used the names Ehecatl, Amaru and Awanyu. Ehecatl's name was taken 150 years after the war from a list of the fallen.
- The Chamber of Deliberation preserved a trial of a prince by the Thirteen Lords and Three Princes, as replayed by shadows. The speaker says the charges were pretext for taking authority.

Characters: The Traveler, Paimon and the Little One; the voice speaking as Ehecatl, Amaru and Awanyu; a nameless record-keeping Secret Source Servant; and shadows of dragon lords seen in the Chamber of Deliberation. Xiuhcoatl and Och-Kan are named but do not appear in person.

Consequences: Tollan's Celestial Axis is working again, the Heart of the Sacred Mountain has been entered and cleansed, and a voice addressing the "Chosen of Dragons" says the power of blazing fire now rests within them (Paimon feels a warm strength). The party is now at the heart of the volcano with the Abyss pushed back, setting up the next quests (An Omen of Annihilation and the Final Entreaty is listed after the third quest on the wiki).

Placement: Released in version 5.5. The series page lists Path to the Flaming Peaks before it and A Finale Emberforged after it. The first quest follows Nahuatzin's Leap according to its own infobox. It continues the Little One storyline that began in Lost Traveler in the Ashen Realm.

245.comment: Chronicler of the Crumbling City: Ehecatl
245.content: Ehecatl is the first name the guiding voice uses, speaking through a Secret Source mechanism that looks like a rolled-up statue. The voice says the name was assigned from a list of the fallen 150 years after the war, and that the real Ehecatl died long ago. It speaks in a formal, theatrical style, startles Paimon with a loud "Warggh", and says its long "exile" is running out. If Investigator of Ancient Ruins was done, Paimon realises this statue is the one Kimosi and Nzaya were looking for.

246.comment: Chronicler of the Crumbling City: Amaru
246.content: Amaru is the second name used, speaking through the Secret Source Servant that once waited on a proud, arrogant master who held the threshold of the sealed Celestial Axis until his death. The voice reactivates the Axis after the Astral Assemblages are restored and warns about the Abyss before the machine shuts down.

247.comment: Chronicler of the Crumbling City: Awanyu
247.content: Awanyu is the third name the voice takes, from a scribe of the Chamber of Deliberation. As Awanyu it is bitterly scornful of the Chamber's judges and of the dragon lords' "games of authority and power", and it leads the Traveler through the permit sequence before vanishing again.

248.comment: Chronicler of the Crumbling City: Secret Source Servant of Tollan
248.content: A very large, unnamed Secret Source Servant is the only intelligent one without a master. It describes itself as a prototype built to help Lord Xiuhcoatl record information, has lost records to Abyssal invasion, and cannot recall its own name. It explains that phlogiston powers Source Mechanisms and that a Dragon Idol needs three Phlogiston Units. It says no human has come this far down in at least 500 years.

249.comment: Chronicler of the Crumbling City: Heart of the Sacred Mountain
249.content: Guarded by a Secret Source Dragon Idol and requiring a permit, the Heart lies beneath fissures in the Sacred City, where corruption is deepest. The Servant says it was excavated when Tollan was rebuilt and also calls it Huitzilopochtli. The Traveler enters in the third quest and cleanses it.

250.content:
Cisoria Chapter (Chiori) (also: Cisoria Chapter, Chiori's Story Quest, When They Talk About Tonight): Chiori's Story Quest, set in Fontaine ahead of Fontaine Fashion Week. A rival designer, Uther, tries to ruin Chiori's boutique through a hired attack on her courier, press smears and withdrawn suppliers. With the Traveler and friends from across Fontaine, Chiori exposes his factory and still stages her show.

The chapter has one act, When They Talk About Tonight, released in Version 4.5, with three quests: Where Honed Blades Clash, Stained Spots and The Woven and the Cut. It is a lighter story about work, reputation and loyalty.

The act shows Chiori as a proud, practical businesswoman who is also supported by many people, including Kirara, Navia, Chevreuse, Charlotte and Lyney and Lynette, whom she has helped with their outfits and a show.

Plot: Kirara arrives late with Chiori's fabrics from Inazuma, having been attacked by bandits hired to target a courier with two tails. Uther, a rival designer, is behind it. Rumours that Chiori uses underground suppliers cost her customers, models and her accessory maker. She salvages stock into a new collection, then helps expose Uther's unsanitary factory and takes the fashion show.

Where Honed Blades Clash. At Chioriya Boutique, Chiori finishes a gown for a client, Laetitia, and explains why a designer must show new work each Fashion Week. Kirara arrives late and admits she was ambushed by bandits who had been told to target a two-tailed courier. Chiori recognises the instigator, Uther, and goes to his home; Chevreuse of the Special Patrol follows and explains that Uther is a known troublemaker who has been warned by the Maison Gardiennage. Chiori throws him out and arranges an escort for Kirara by the Special Patrol and Spina di Rosula.

Stained Spots. The next day customers cancel orders after rumours that Chiori's fabric comes from underground factories. Her accessory supplier, Wenger, withdraws, as do the models he had booked. The rumours came from minor tabloids, not The Steambird, which Charlotte tells the Traveler and Paimon she wants to help correct. Laetitia learns that Chiori covered the dress's extra cost herself and comes to defend her. The Traveler and Paimon find Chiori by the sea in the Liffey Region, where she tells them of her past. She decides to make the collection out of what is to hand, using sea finds for accessories and salvaging fabric from her ready-to-wear stock, and enlists Navia, Charlotte, Lyney and Lynette.

The Woven and the Cut. Chiori, the Traveler and Paimon tour Uther's factory at Fleuve Cendre, find a hidden lower level with unsanitary conditions and chemical treatments that would harm wearers' skin, and photograph it before being locked in. Chiori reveals that she and Uther were once partners. Uther confronts them with Clockwork Meka and a gun; Chiori parries his shot with her blade and defeats him. The fashion show succeeds, and Chiori gives the Traveler and Paimon a customised brooch.

Chiori's past, as she tells it: she was a troublesome child, her parents sent her to a master tailor when her needlework showed talent, she grew angry at having to flatter arrogant clients, and after a few incidents left Inazuma for Fontaine to start over and make her brand known across Teyvat. She goes to a cliff by the sea in the Liffey Region when upset, and Eloffe, who works at the boutique, knows this.

Uther and Chiori began as newcomer designers who wanted their own take on fashion. After repeated rejections Uther gave up before a Fashion Week; Chiori kept going and gained recognition. When she opened her shop Uther began to harass her. Chiori held back during the confrontation because of their old partnership. Navia and Charlotte each first react angrily on seeing the damaged display stock, Navia assuming vandals, until Chiori says she asked the Traveler to do it.

Chevreuse says Chiori's work benefits the Special Patrol, which means she often protects Chiori from people who resent her, usually the rich and powerful, though sometimes she must protect others from her. Chiori compares Navia's determination and courage to her own. After the show Chevreuse is anxious over the risks Chiori took, and Chiori notes that Wenger sent an apology she intends to answer in her own time. Chiori ends the night saying she will never bow or scrape to anyone, confident in her work, and that it is the loveliest night she has had in Fontaine so far.

Revelations: Chiori and Uther were once partners. Uther ran a factory at Fleuve Cendre with unsanitary conditions and chemical treatments harmful to wearers.

Chiori covered a client's dress cost from her own pocket and does not use cheap materials. She left Inazuma after conflicts with arrogant clients while apprenticed to a master tailor. The press campaign was bought: several tabloids were paid to print the same article at once.

Characters: Chiori, the Traveler, Paimon and Kirara.

Uther (rival), Chevreuse, Navia, Charlotte, Lyney, Lynette, Laetitia (client), Eloffe (shop assistant), Wenger (accessory supplier), Leeann and Weis (customers who cancel).

Spina di Rosula, the Special Patrol and the House of the Hearth support Chiori.

Consequences: Uther's factory is exposed and he is defeated. Chiori's boutique gets a new sign and her fashion show goes ahead successfully. Kirara is escorted safely out of Fontaine.

Placement: Unlocks at Adventure Rank 40 after Masquerade of the Guilty (Chapter IV Act V). Released in Version 4.5 and set in Fontaine around Fontaine Fashion Week. No later acts exist as of 7.1.

251.content: A rival fashion designer who once partnered with Chiori and later resented her success. He hired bandits to attack her courier, planted rumours that she used underground suppliers, and ran a factory with unsanitary conditions at Fleuve Cendre. Chiori defeats him and exposes the factory.

252.content: An annual event in Fontaine that gives designers wide exposure. Chiori says it helped make her name. In the Cisoria Chapter she builds her collection from salvaged stock after Uther's sabotage.

253.content:
Clink Clank Clash (also: Zip-Zap Spy-Bot Number 1): Clink Clank Clash was a limited-time Flagship Event in Version 6.0 (Luna I), played from 2025-09-12 to 2025-09-29, set in Nod-Krai. After the Traveler and Paimon settle in, they find the young inventor Aino and her robot companion Ineffa caught up in a crisis involving stray robots, Guild commissions and a suspicious "outsourced contract". It is a light, comic workshop story told through short event quests and four minigames.

The story is spread over six event quests, each unlocking a minigame or following on from one. Treat it as a canon side story that happened during an event, not something every Nod-Krai resident would mention.

Plot: Gaudenty's "outsourced contract" has Aino and the Traveler chase runaway recon bots with Moonlanes and kuuhenki; the Adventurers' Guild's Sarin has them field-test a self-defence device; Ginette needs her kuuvahki robots found and debugged, and the robots turn out to want to play with the Traveler and to defend them; Ineffa shows off Aino's stealth robot Zip-Zap Spy-Bot Number 1, built for a rescue of Aino's friends from the Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau. In the finale, Unwritten Rules, Gaudenty is caught trying to steal Ginette's robots with inside help; Sarin reveals he is a disgraced ex-Guild bounty hunter, not a Bureau representative, and the merchant Asikko, who claims Gaudenty owes him, takes him away.

Quest by quest, in play order:

- A Mysterious Outsourced Contract (Northern Training Ground, Lempo Isle). Gaudenty claims to be an expatriate representative of the Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau. He says a batch of recon bots has escaped the Bureau and offers payment in robot parts, not Mora. Aino, who wants the parts for research, accepts and plans to use Moonlanes and kuuhenki to reach the high-flying bots. This unlocks "Pursue and Strike! The Out-of-Control Flier!".
- An Adventurer's Woes. Sarin, Branch Master of the Adventurers' Guild in Nod-Krai, explains that adventurers there cannot count on local authorities for protection. His self-defence device failed, so he commissions Aino to adapt it to kuuvahki-rich surroundings by testing it in fights. Aino will not fight herself. This unlocks "Boom! Blast! Power Test!".
- Misplaced Creativity. Ginette has built robots that use kuuvahki to communicate at a distance, but they malfunction. She also admits she lost them while testing at varied kuuvahki concentrations. Aino prepares a device that gathers kuuvahki remnants to track them. This unlocks "Seek and Find! Machines on the Fritz!".
- New Idea and The Last Step of Testing. Ginette adjusts the recovered robots and asks the Traveler to watch how the others behave. The robots gather and appear to invite the Traveler to play. Ginette concludes her design works through the robots' interaction with one another. While recovering the last batch, the Traveler and Paimon are set upon by Oprichniki, and the robots help fight them.
- Backup Plans. Ineffa shows the Traveler and Paimon Zip-Zap Spy-Bot Number 1, a stealth robot Aino made from an abandoned cleaning bot bought on the black market. It exists because Krum-Clank 70% Sweet was stolen, and Aino wants to be able to slip into the Bureau and rescue her friends. This unlocks "Quietly Now! Sneaky Sneaking Sneaks!".
- Unwritten Rules. Gaudenty is caught trying to steal Ginette's robots, after Ineffa and Sarin warned her. Ineffa shows from repaired surveillance records that he had inside help at the workshop. Sarin says he is a former Guild member expelled for misconduct, then a bounty hunter who lost his Voynich Guild certification, and no real representative of anything. The merchant Asikko steps in, claiming the man owes him a debt, and takes Gaudenty away.
Details worth keeping straight:

- The "contract". Asikko says he got Gaudenty a subcontract from the Design Bureau, that Gaudenty failed at it and re-outsourced the work to Aino, and that Gaudenty then let decommissioned recon bots flood the black market. Gaudenty's own claim that the bots must not reach outsiders sits badly with that account.
- Asikko's notice. Ineffa points out that Asikko had posted a high price for any of Aino's creations, which could push greedy people into stealing. Asikko answers that he only praised the technology and backed it with his own money, and that anyone who oversteps is responsible for it. Ineffa admits she cannot logically refute this but asks him to withdraw the notice, since Aino treasures every robot companion. He agrees not to press Aino commercially.
- Ginette's robots. Asikko tries to recruit Ginette, hoping the combat skills the robots picked up could become a product. She explains that she wanted robots that gain a degree of intelligence through kuuvahki interaction, that in her system kuuvahki behaved more like emotion than logic, and that the robots fight to protect their favourite playmate, the Traveler. She compares them to children who will not take orders. Sarin warns that the Guild will step in if disputes are stirred up, and Asikko backs off.
- Ineffa's stance. Asked whether letting Asikko leave with Gaudenty is right, Ineffa says Nod-Krai has many unwritten rules in its shadows, that she does not agree with them, and that she only wants them kept away from Aino's life.
- Afterwards. Letti, another member of the Nod-Krai Adventurers' Guild, takes Gaudenty's place at the workshop on the Branch Master's behalf because Aino has not finished her research on the recon bots. Letti says the Moonlanes the Traveler built remain usable, the collected components need not be returned, and the Fatui side does not intend to hold them accountable.

Reward and framing details: completing the quests also granted Mora, Adventurer's Experience and Wanderer's Advice, and the event offered five tiers of Legion Morale rewards up to 1,000 (the Etherlight Spindlelute at 200 and a Crown of Insight at 1,000). The Glacial Moon Battle Pass carried four event missions. Letti's name is Finnish for "plait" or "braid" (wiki etymology note, not in-story).

Revelations: - Gaudenty is not a real representative of the Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau, according to Sarin; he was expelled from the Adventurers' Guild for misconduct and later lost his Voynich Guild certification.
- Gaudenty worked with an insider, whom Paimon calls "that receptionist", to try to steal from Aino's workshop.
- Asikko had posted a notice offering a high price for Aino's creations, which may have encouraged the theft.
- Ginette's robots fight to protect the Traveler, whom they treat as a favourite playmate.

Per Ineffa's account of Aino's backup plan, Aino's friends are somewhere the Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau guards heavily. The event does not say who they are beyond the theft of Krum-Clank 70% Sweet, and it does not show a rescue.

Characters: - Aino: a young inventor who runs the workshop, chooses jobs by how interesting they are, and waives extra pay when a task sounds fun. She wants the recon bot parts for her own research.
- Ineffa: Aino's robot companion, who explains Aino's projects in precise, analytical statements and handles the confrontation in Unwritten Rules.
- The Traveler and Paimon: the helpers who run the tests, recover robots and are treated as favoured playmates by Ginette's robots.
- Sarin: Branch Master of the Adventurers' Guild in Nod-Krai, who commissions the self-defence device and later exposes Gaudenty's background.
- Gaudenty: a self-styled Bureau representative and in truth a disgraced bounty hunter.
- Ginette: a Fontainian engineer-researcher whose robots communicate through kuuvahki.
- Asikko: a merchant from the black market with an unsettled debt claim on Gaudenty.
- Letti: a Guild member who appears only after the quest, in place of Gaudenty.

Event-only NPCs here (Gaudenty, Ginette, Asikko, Letti) have no detailed canon profiles; do not give them backstory beyond what is stated. The wiki lists Letti with no profile. The Frostmoon Scions are mentioned only as the owners of the territory around the Light-Bathed Platform in one challenge briefing.

Consequences: Gaudenty leaves in Asikko's custody, Asikko withdraws his commercial claim on Aino's work, and the Guild's contact at the workshop becomes Letti. Aino's research on the recon bots continues. No lasting change to Nod-Krai's politics is shown, and the event is not needed to follow the Archon Quest.

Gameplay: (Game mechanics, not in-world fact.) The event required Adventure Rank 20 and completion of the Prologue's Act III "Song of the Dragon and Freedom"; completing Song of the Welkin Moon Act II "Elegy of Dust and Lamplight" was recommended. Players earned Legion Morale from four minigames: "Pursue and Strike! The Out-of-Control Flier!" (riding Moonlanes with kuuhenki to shoot down rogue recon bots and collect Moonlit Particles), "Boom! Blast! Power Test!" (waves of enemies, recharging a self-defence device with kuuvahki energy), "Seek and Find! Machines on the Fritz!" (following kuuvahki remnants to find malfunctioning robots) and "Quietly Now! Sneaky Sneaking Sneaks!" (steering Zip-Zap Spy-Bot Number 1 past patrols to collect ID cards). The Catalyst Etherlight Spindlelute was the headline reward.

The challenge locations include Nasha Town, the Clink-Clank Krumkake Craftshop, the Light-Bathed Platform (Frostmoon Scion territory), Maroon Basin and the Barrowmoss Barrens. Enemies in the power tests include Oprichniki (Fatui) troopers, landcruisers and Radiant beasts.

Placement: Released in Version 6.0, "Luna I", with phases opening on 2025-09-12, 2025-09-14 and 2025-09-16. In story terms it is an optional side story set in Nod-Krai after the player has been introduced to the region. It has no confirmed place in the Archon Quest order.

254.comment: Clink Clank Clash: Zip-Zap Spy-Bot Number 1
254.content: Aino's stealth robot, built by modifying an abandoned cleaning bot bought on the black market. Ineffa says the testing platform simulates hostile environments so that Aino can check the robot's ability to stay hidden, and that it is meant to get into the heavily guarded Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau and rescue friends after Krum-Clank 70% Sweet was stolen. In the minigame it has blades for spinning attacks, a short dash, and can use kuuvahki bullets against patrolling mechanisms.

255.comment: Clink Clank Clash: Gaudenty and Asikko
255.content: Gaudenty poses as an expatriate representative of the Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau; Sarin says he is an ex-Guild bounty hunter who lost his Voynich Guild certification. He tries to steal Ginette's robots with inside help. Asikko, a merchant, claims Gaudenty owes him money and leaves with him after a tense exchange with Ineffa and Sarin. Letti, a Guild member, takes Gaudenty's place at the workshop afterwards.

256.content:
Colors of Emptiness (also: Crimson Cleansing, Blues of the Old World, Colors Out of Space): Colors of Emptiness is a short Nod-Krai World Quest series on Lempo Isle, added in Version 6.0. Two quests, Crimson Cleansing at the north end and Blues of the Old World at the south end of the Nothing Passage, can be done in either order. In each the Traveler and Paimon follow a glowing orb, red in one and blue in the other, that possesses objects and animals as it moves through a gorge once held by the Fatui. When both are done, Colors Out of Space begins: the orbs collide and the Traveler is flung through a strange ruined space. Nothing explains what the orbs are.

The series has no fixed antagonist and no named supporting cast. Its worldbuilding comes from leftover Fatui material in the passage and from the mystery of the orbs.

Plot: Crimson Cleansing. At the north end of the Nothing Passage the Traveler finds a red orb that is chasing a blue kuuhenki. The orb enters an inactive Landcruiser, forcing a fight, then looks for blue stones in a container; the Traveler removes them, and the orb moves on through a mole den, a recon bot and a blue patch of mist.

Blues of the Old World. At the south end a blue orb escapes from a circle. It rides a mole, activates Landcruisers, enters a goat that heads for a blue crystal, and leads the Traveler to a red patch of mist. A red kuuhenki appears from the crystal and creates a Moonlane.

Colors Out of Space. With both quests done, the red and blue orbs collide in front of the Traveler and a vortex pulls the Traveler into a purple space full of floating ruins. The Traveler must wait for the flight to end. Paimon was blown away by the explosion and had trouble flying back; she doubts the Traveler's account and urges them to leave, since they found no treasure.

If a player does only one first quest, its ending leads straight into the other; the wiki lists several Paimon variants depending on what has been started. Each orb leaves behind a permanent strong kuuvahki environment of its own colour as it travels.

Paimon's guess at the beginning is that the orbs are Seelie, who lead to treasure, so she is disappointed when they find none.

The kuuvahki barrier in the gorge was apparently a Fatui authorization-terminal system; notes found there record a dispute between two Fatui figures (see the Fatui notes entry). The quest rewards are typical for a world quest and the final quest also awards the achievement "Colors Out of Snezhnaya".

Revelations: - The Nothing Passage had been designated a Military Administrative Area under an imperial edict issued in the Tsaritsa's name, with intruders to be treated as hostile agents.
- Fatui officers left notes and barriers, including a kuuvahki barrier and an authorization terminal.
- The Traveler glimpses a space of ruins that Paimon has never heard of in Teyvat.

- Nothing in the series identifies the orbs or the space beyond them.

Characters: Only the Traveler and Paimon appear. Fatui members are mentioned through notes: Anton Zarkovich and V. A. Preobrazhensky, who argue in a note about an authorization terminal and an ID card.

Consequences: The series is self-contained and has no stated follow-up. It unlocks the Nothing Passage as open ground and grants the achievement "Colors Out of Snezhnaya".

Placement: Released in Version 6.0 (Luna I, 2025-09-10) and set on Lempo Isle in Nod-Krai. It has no required story prerequisite on the wiki.

257.comment: Colors of Emptiness: Fatui notes in the Nothing Passage
257.content: A weathered notice at either end of the passage says the area is a Military Administrative Area by decree of Her Majesty the Tsaritsa of Snezhnaya, under the Imperial Edict on the Strengthening of Order, and that unauthorised entry will be treated as espionage. A messy note addressed to Anton Zarkovich warns him not to lock the writer's people out with an authorization terminal and threatens him with consequences; it is signed V. A. Preobrazhensky and accuses Zarkovich of obstructing work because his own northern experiments have failed.

258.comment: Colors of Emptiness: Red and blue orbs
258.content: Two unexplained glowing orbs that move through kuuvahki-affected ground and inhabit objects or animals. They are tied to the colours red and blue of the kuuhenki and mist patches around them. Paimon initially suspects they are Seelie; this is never confirmed.

259.content:
Crystallina Chapter (also: Crystallina, Skirk's Story Quest, Whispers Betwixt Stars and Night, Sinister Undercurrent, All Devouring, Heart and Mind, Unbounded): The Crystallina Chapter is Skirk's Story Quest, released in Version 5.7. It has one act, Whispers Betwixt Stars and Night. After a nightmare in which something Abyssal stabs the Traveler, Skirk appears in Liyue, says part of the Traveler's soul has been taken, and agrees to help recover it if the Traveler helps her find the thief. The thief proves to be Skofnungr, an old friend of her master Surtalogi.

The act has five quests: Sinister Undercurrent, Special Training, All Devouring, Heart and Mind and Unbounded. Most of it takes place in dreams and in an Abyssal space reached through Skirk, so it is a character study of Skirk as much as a case to solve. It requires the Archon Quest Masquerade of the Guilty (Chapter IV, Act V) and Adventure Rank 40.

Its central questions are what Skirk is, why she cut herself off from feeling, and how she relates to her master's legacy. The Traveler is both her student for a short time and the person who helps her accept her own emotions, and the chapter ends with a farewell that hopes for a peaceful "reborn world" at the end of the Traveler's journey.

In it the Traveler sees Skirk's inner world, and it shows her origin on a distant planet, her training under Surtalogi and her entry into Teyvat with Alice's help. The chapter has no further acts as of 7.1.

Plot: The Traveler wakes from a dream in which an Abyssal being stabbed them, and Baizhu finds nothing physically wrong. Skirk joins them at Wanmin Restaurant, says part of their soul is damaged by Abyssal corrosion, and meets them at Guili Plains, where Rifthounds are collecting god remains. She believes a god-level entity is stealing sources of power, including the Stella Fortuna, and offers to help recover the Traveler's soul if they help identify it. She trains the Traveler in bladework, Elemental Skills and reasoning, and the Traveler enters her dreams and sees her burned village, her master Surtalogi and her entry into Teyvat with Alice's help. After three answered questions (she is from outside Teyvat but not a Descender, came to learn the source of her master's strength, and hides from Tartaglia so he finds his own strength) they follow the culprit into the Chasm, where Skirk is wounded and they retreat. In her inner world the Traveler helps her accept her suppressed emotions. Back in the Abyssal space the culprit, the Dark Shadow, is revealed as Skofnungr, a Khaenri'ahn friend of Surtalogi who grafted narwhal flesh into his heart. Skirk spares him by destroying his consciousness and leaves.

**Sinister Undercurrent.** The Traveler feels agitated and unwell. Paimon takes them to Bubu Pharmacy; Baizhu finds nothing physical and suggests a non-physical cause. Asleep, the Traveler stands in a foggy Abyssal realm and an Abyssal being stabs them in the back, but they wake unharmed. At Wanmin Restaurant, Paimon recognises the woman who sits down and orders wine as Childe's master, Skirk. She believes a piece of the Traveler's soul is damaged and bears the marks of Abyssal corrosion, and asks to meet at Guili Plains. Chef Mao later says only the Traveler and Paimon were at the table. At Guili Plains, Rifthounds are gathering god remains. Skirk says a possibly god-level entity is stealing sources of power across the world, including the Stella Fortuna, and offers to help recover the Traveler's soul if they help identify it. She takes them into the Abyss for safety and offers to mirror the Traveler's dreams.

**Special Training.** Skirk trains the Traveler in bladework, Elemental Skills and reasoning. When the Traveler sleeps they enter Skirk's dream, follow a strange being and see fragments of her childhood: a merchant ship arriving on her planet, her fascination with the outside, and the ship's people burning her village while her parents tell her to flee. Skirk explains that her powers are Abyssal but disguised as Cryo because of the laws of Teyvat. She notes that the Traveler uses and changes elements without a Vision, and urges them to forge their own path. A mock battle teaches that fighting means setting emotions aside: she exploits the Traveler's hesitation when their sibling is mentioned, then repeats the drill while they sort their feelings.
