Further dreams show her training under Surtalogi and with other disciples, and entering Teyvat with Alice's help. Afterwards she grants three questions. She is surprised that the Traveler saw her inner world and asks for secrecy, says she is from outside but not a Descender, says she came to Teyvat to find where her master's strength came from, and explains she hides from Tartaglia so he will find his own strength before they meet again.

**All Devouring.** In the Chasm domain, Skirk notices the attacks aim at her; a spike pierces her shoulder, but she crushes it and returns the stolen soul fragment to the Traveler. She reasons the thief wanted the Traveler's ability to purify Abyssal energy so as to draw power from her, asks how it came by the All-Devouring Narwhal's power, and realises it must know Surtalogi, calling him "The Foul". The entity is angered. Because Skirk is hurt and Paimon cannot defend herself, they retreat to Bubu Pharmacy, where Skirk meditates for two days. The strange being then draws the Traveler into her inner world.

**Heart and Mind.** The inner world appears as a shattered river, which the being says shows how she cut off her emotions and started over each time she met weakness. Going upstream, the Traveler relives her arrival in Teyvat, her motives and the fate of her people. The being reveals itself as her suppressed emotions. Skirk calls it weak; the Traveler answers that its ability to break through shows strength. She accepts it, and the Traveler offers to help against Surtalogi if the time comes. Back in the real world, Paimon brings snacks and Skirk warns that her power is now greater.

**Unbounded.** In the Abyssal space the fog has cleared and the culprit appears as the Dark Shadow. Skirk says those who long for Surtalogi's strength imitate him unconsciously. She wounds herself deliberately so the entity will absorb her power; its armour breaks and a Khaenri'ahn man is revealed. He names himself Skofnungr, a friend and follower of Surtalogi. He tells how he was a young heir cursed with an incurable illness and shunned until Surtalogi told him to fight for his life, and how, after the cataclysm and Ronova's curse, Surtalogi offered to lift the curse and left him a weakened narwhal. He grafted its flesh into his heart. Skirk offers him an alternative to death: destroying his consciousness to remove the stolen power, after which the curse of immortality will slowly restore body and mind. He accepts, hoping to wake in time to see her fight. Skirk then leaves, saying she and the Traveler may or may not meet again, but hoping for a reborn world of peace; Paimon proposes stargazing on the spot.

Detail on Skofnungr: he says Surtalogi quickly surpassed him and that he was embarrassed to spar him later; Surtalogi told him of his departure to the stars and that he would not return for many years. Skirk tells him that several hundred years have passed. After the deed, Skofnungr concedes that he has reached his peak and is glad others are helping Skirk reach her goals.

On the structure: the soul-theft case frames the act, but the real conflict is Skirk's. Training is used to move the Traveler into her dreams, and the culprit is defeated only after she stops separating her power from her emotions (she says she will need time to practise with her power no longer split by emotion).

The wiki summary says Skirk offers three questions "much like" she did with Tartaglia. Her lesson that a fighter must set emotion aside is later complicated by the discovery that doing so permanently was her own flaw. Skirk also asks the Traveler not to tell Paimon what they discussed.

Revelations: - Skirk is from beyond Teyvat but says she is not a Descender; she is "just a visitor passing by".
- Her powers are Abyssal; she disguises them as Cryo because of Teyvat's laws.
- Her own planet's people were attacked by the crew of a merchant ship and her village burned; she was a child at the time and her parents told her to flee.
- She came to Teyvat to learn where her master Surtalogi's strength came from, after entering with Alice's help.
- She avoids Tartaglia deliberately so he forges his own path.
- A Khaenri'ahn called Skofnungr, a friend of Surtalogi, grafted flesh of a weakened All-Devouring Narwhal into his heart and became the Dark Shadow.
- Surtalogi left Khaenri'ah for the stars after the cataclysm, and Skirk says it has been several hundred years.

- Skofnungr was condemned by an incurable illness as a child, was shunned by peers and family, and refused Surtalogi's offer to lift Ronova's curse because he wanted to grow stronger.
- The thief was a man in armour, not a nameless Abyssal monster; the god remains and the Stella Fortuna that Skirk said were being collected were part of the power-gathering she described.

- The Traveler's ability to purify Abyssal energy is treated as significant by Skirk.
- The being in Skirk's inner world is her suppressed emotions, which she had been dismissing as weakness.

Characters: - **Skirk**: the chapter's protagonist.
- **The Traveler and Paimon**: the victim of the soul-theft and their guide; Skirk asks the Traveler not to tell Paimon what they discussed.
- **Baizhu**: the physician at Bubu Pharmacy who first examines the Traveler.
- **Skofnungr**: the culprit and a Khaenri'ahn friend of Surtalogi.
- **Surtalogi**: Skirk's master, shown in memories; also mentioned by Skofnungr.
- **Chef Mao**: the Wanmin Restaurant chef who saw only two people at the table.

Alice appears only in Skirk's memories (of entering Teyvat). Tartaglia is discussed, not present, and Ronova is mentioned in Skofnungr's account.

Consequences: The Traveler's stolen soul fragment is returned. Skirk accepts her suppressed emotions, destroys Skofnungr's consciousness to strip his stolen power, and departs, with no promise to meet again.

Skofnungr is left alive but unconscious, with his curse expected to heal him slowly. Skirk's power is no longer split from her emotions, and the Traveler has pledged to help her against Surtalogi if the time comes.

Placement: Released in Version 5.7. It requires Masquerade of the Guilty (Chapter IV, Act V) and Adventure Rank 40, so it comes after the Fontaine Archon Quest in which Skirk first appeared. Story order and release order match. The chapter has no later acts as of 7.1.

During Version 5.7 a companion event of the same name ran from 2025-06-18 to 2025-07-08, giving Primogems, ascension and level-up materials and Natlan specialties for completing the quest in time, and offered a Quick Start for players at Adventure Rank 28 who had finished Chapter I, Act III (A New Star Approaches). The quest itself remains playable afterward; only the event rewards and Quick Start window were limited.

260.content:
A dreamscape inside Skirk, seen only by the Traveler. It appears as a shattered river, each break marking a time she shut out her emotions to start again. Memories line its banks: her planet burning, Surtalogi's training, other disciples, entering Teyvat. A strange being that guides the Traveler is her suppressed emotions. She is initially hostile to being seen, and the Traveler keeps the secret from Paimon.

Upstream, the Traveler reaches Skirk herself and persuades her to accept the being. She had forgotten her reason for seeking strength after severing her feelings.

261.comment: Crystallina Chapter: Skofnungr and the Dark Shadow
261.content:
Skofnungr is a Khaenri'ahn, friend and follower of Surtalogi, who wore the form of the Dark Shadow after grafting weakened narwhal flesh into his own heart. He was the soul-thief in Skirk's chapter. He was an heir with an incurable illness, was helped by Surtalogi, refused to have the curse removed after the cataclysm, and hoped to grow stronger. Skirk spares him by destroying his consciousness and leaving his immortality-curse to heal him.

He asked to be killed but accepted Skirk's alternative, hoping to wake in time to watch her fight Surtalogi.

262.content:
Skirk's lessons to the Traveler cover bladework, Elemental Skills and reasoning. They also include a mock battle in which the Traveler is told to fight without emotion, and a second round where they must finish while sorting through feelings.

She says the Traveler's ability to command elements without a Vision shows they need no approval from gods.

key: The Truth Is Also a Lie
263.content:
Cypressus Custos Chapter (also: Cypressus Custos, Ayato's Story Quest, The Firmiana Leaf Falls, New Shoots from Old Branches, The Truth Is Also a Lie, The Wind Settles): The Cypressus Custos Chapter is Kamisato Ayato's Story Quest, released in Version 2.6, with one act, The Firmiana Leaf Falls. Rumour says Kujou Kamaji of the Tenryou Commission and Hiiragi Chisato of the Kanjou Commission are to marry. Ayato, head of the Kamisato Clan and Yashiro Commissioner, suspects the match is a trap and, with the Traveler's help, spoils it.

The act has three quests: New Shoots from Old Branches, The Truth Is Also a Lie and The Wind Settles. It is a political story, not a combat one. It shows how Ayato works: quietly, through informants and public opinion, and with a wry sense of what a "wedding" between the Tri-Commission's houses really costs.

It follows on from the unsettled state of the Kanjou Commission after Hiiragi Shinsuke's imprisonment and from the Kujou Clan's loss of control after Kujou Takayuki's fall. Its resolution lets Chisato assert herself for the first time and leaves Ayato crediting the Traveler and Paimon's trusted standing with Kamaji and Chisato for making his plan work.

Plot: Leaving Tenshukaku, the Traveler and Paimon overhear Ippei and Shinnojou, who have been buying clothes for their masters and guess a wedding is coming. Shinnojou, who admires Chisato, is upset. At the Kamisato Estate they find Ayato playing chess with Thoma; Ayato confirms the rumour and says a marriage between members of the Tri-Commission deserves his personal respects. At the Kujou Estate Kamaji says Chisato proposed by letter first, but when he spoke to her she acted as though she had sent none, and they agreed anyway. Ayato finds this off, since he knows Chisato is not coy, and goes to the Hiiragi Estate. There he declines the clan representatives' hospitality, drinks Dango Milk with the Traveler, and explains that the Kanjou Commission is unstable with no replacement for Shinsuke, and some supporters of the Hiiragi would resent the match. He has a Shuumatsuban watch the representatives.

Chisato tells them Shinnojou burst in and begged her not to marry because it would harm the clan name, that Kamaji's reply was sudden, and that she did not send the letter. Ayato asks her to consider the marriage carefully. Outside Ritou he notes that a low-ranking officer objected while the higher-ups approved, and he sensed someone listening. An aide reports that Shinnojou has been taken away. Ayato says the plotters are clever and cannot be stopped until they show their fangs, because acting openly would cause public backlash.

In the caves near Araumi they find and free Shinnojou, whom Ayato tells to go into hiding. Matsuura confronts Ayato, accuses him of meddling and of trying to protect his power, and says the notices have gone public so the wedding is set. Ayato is unimpressed, having thought him sharper, and says he will reply soon. Ayato tells the Traveler he wants to see how the public reacts once his plan is known. He tells Kamaji they can still turn the situation around by changing Chisato from a burden into an asset. Kamaji, who admits he moved too fast, agrees. The Shuumatsuban find a Kanjou informant who listens to the crowds, and Ayato says the plotters will have no choice but to give in, as he has done this many times; he advises waiting two days and leaves.

Two days later everyone in Ritou is talking about Chisato. At the Hiiragi Estate Matsuura comes in, accuses the Traveler and Paimon of motives, and is scolded by Chisato for the plot. He goes to the other plotters, who decide Chisato is valuable to them. Chisato notes she has used authority for the first time. Matsuura returns, apologises, and asks the Traveler to accompany him to the Kamisato Estate. There he apologises to Ayato, who asks how he will correct the error and dismisses him after hearing, saying both knew this would happen. Ayato tells Chisato that what she faces now is what he, Ayaka and Kamaji each had to face. He tells Paimon he suspected from the start but understood their feelings. Thoma comes out afterward and chats with him. Ayato says the Traveler and Paimon helped greatly, as the trust Kamaji and Chisato placed in them made it easier to accept his plan.

The scheme works through the marriage's appearance: no one can openly oppose a union between two Commission heirs, so Ayato lets it go ahead in public and instead changes what it means. His principle, as the act shows it, is that if a plan has no ill consequences it can be allowed to stand, and that people with real strength act only when the other side commits.

Revelations: - Chisato never wrote the letter that Kamaji says started the engagement.
- Matsuura and other plotters, with Kanjou informants watching the city, pushed the marriage.
- Ayato uses public pressure and the Shuumatsuban to counter the plot, and says he has done this many times before.
- The Kanjou Commission is unstable with no replacement for Shinsuke, and the Kujou Clan is weakened, which is what the plotters exploit.

- Ayato says marriage within the Tri-Commission is important enough that he would personally visit.
- Chisato's authority is asserted for the first time in this act.

Characters: - **Kamisato Ayato**: the Yashiro Commissioner and chapter protagonist.
- **The Traveler and Paimon**: companions and trusted friends of Kamaji and Chisato.
- **Thoma**: Ayato's household retainer, who plays chess with him.
- **Kujou Kamaji**: Tenryou Commission figure, the supposed groom.
- **Hiiragi Chisato**: Kanjou Commission figure, the supposed bride.
- **Ippei and Shinnojou**: retainers of Kamaji and Chisato.
- **Matsuura**: plotter who threatens Ayato.

Ayaka and Hiiragi Shinsuke appear only by reference.

Consequences: The wedding plot fails and Chisato gains standing within the Kanjou Commission. Matsuura apologises to Ayato. Shinnojou is safe.

Placement: Released in Version 2.6. It requires Omnipresence Over Mortals, Reflections of Mortality and the World Quest Chisato's Letter, and takes place in the settled Inazuma after Chapter II. Story order and release order match. No later acts exist as of 7.1.

264.comment: Cypressus Custos Chapter: Chisato's engagement plot
264.content: A rumour of a wedding between Kujou Kamaji and Hiiragi Chisato that Ayato suspects is a trap. Chisato says she sent no letter. Matsuura and the other plotters publish the match and have Shinnojou abducted to silence objections. Ayato frees him, turns public opinion, and Chisato gains the upper hand.

265.content: A plotter behind the marriage plot, linked to Kanjou informants. He threatens Ayato, then, when the plan collapses, apologises to Chisato and to Ayato in person.

key: The Remains of the Past Day
266.content:
Diluvies Chapter (also: Diluvies, Neuvillette's Story Quest, The Remains of the Past Day, A Familiar Threat, Ever-Surging Memories, In a New Light): Neuvillette's Story Quest, set in the Court of Fontaine. A threatening letter targets the Melusine Kiara, and the Iudex personally investigates because a similar plot once destroyed two people he trusted. Using the Fountain of Lucine, he relives the story of the Melusine Carole and his friend Vautrin. The trail leads to a smuggler in Meropide, and Neuvillette learns that Fontaine now stands with him.

The chapter has one act, The Remains of the Past Day, made of three quests: A Familiar Threat, Ever-Surging Memories and In a New Light. It was released in version 4.1 and unlocked after Cataclysm's Quickening. It is a quiet investigation story about trust, loneliness and how an immortal Hydro Sovereign who chose to live as a human reads his own emotions.

The quest keeps one stance throughout: Neuvillette handles the case alone and quietly because he regards himself as an "outsider" by his position, and it ends with Wriothesley telling him that this is no longer true.

Plot: Neuvillette is investigating a threat to Kiara. The Traveler and Paimon join him, and Clorinde offers to guard Kiara. At the Fountain of Lucine he accidentally pulls the Traveler into a memory of Carole and Vautrin from four hundred years ago. The letter is traced to Esseim, a freed smuggler, and then to Domenico in Meropide. Wriothesley tells Neuvillette he has overthought the case, as people now trust him.

A Familiar Threat: Sedene asks Neuvillette to leave the case to others since he is Iudex, but he says that four hundred years ago hardliners opposed to his reforms exploited the Melusine Carole's identity to cause unrest, which ended in her suicide and the exile of Vautrin, the leader of the Special Security and Surveillance Patrol. He will not repeat that. He asks the Traveler and Paimon to come, leaving a note for Furina. Kiara hands over the letter. Neuvillette explains he is an outsider because of his role, and reminds Paimon he is the Hydro Sovereign. While reading old cases, he serves different waters to the guests. He explains that after his birth as a human he lost most of his memories and his connection to the Primordial Sea, and chose to become Iudex to organise his thoughts. He proposes visiting the Fountain of Lucine, where all Fontaine's water converges and strong memories and emotions can be sensed.

Ever-Surging Memories: at the fountain after sunset, Neuvillette's power draws the Traveler into the past. Carole is excited to explore the surface, while Vautrin tells her that her dream of coexistence between Melusines and humans is likely impossible. Neuvillette awards them the Medal of Peace, but Thibert and Suavegothe conspire against Carole. A mob forms, Carole sacrifices herself to prove her innocence, and Vautrin learns the truth from Rastignac, keeps it from Neuvillette and kills the culprits in revenge. Neuvillette tries Vautrin before the Oratrice Mecanique d'Analyse Cardinale; both judge him guilty by the rules despite the audience's sympathy, and Vautrin leaves. Back in the present, Neuvillette senses resentment against Kiara in the water regarding an old smuggling case. Navia arrives with Spina di Rosula's help, and the trail leads to Esseim at Café Lutece. Esseim confirms writing the letter on Domenico's orders, and Domenico is already in the Fortress of Meropide.

In a New Light: Wriothesley brings Domenico before them. In the infirmary Sigewinne shows them criminals wearing a badge based on the Medal of Peace; it is the symbol of the Mutual Aid Network, and its founder is revealed to be Vautrin. Domenico admits he wrote the letter out of revenge and used a sympathetic guard to send it. Wriothesley tells Neuvillette that the case showed Fontaine trusts him now. Neuvillette returns to the Court understanding himself a little better.

A Familiar Threat: four hundred years ago he had become Iudex with Carole, a Melusine, and Vautrin as trusted subordinates. Paimon proposes the Gardes, the Marechaussee Phantom or the Special Security, but he declines because he cannot be sure how far a conspiracy has spread. Kiara, who is roughly 400 years old and remembers Carole, insists on finishing her inspection duty with Eloffe at Chioriya Boutique, where she explains Melusines can see anomalies such as old bloodstains that humans cannot. Charlotte, who has been following to interview Neuvillette, promises to keep the case quiet and to ask colleagues at The Steambird for information. Clorinde arrives, asks why he is busy with a trivial matter, and promises to protect Kiara. The Traveler and Paimon help read case files. Paimon finds the office too quiet; Neuvillette admits few come to relax there and brings water. The water tastes the same to Paimon, which they conclude has to do with him being the Hydro Sovereign. He could ask other dragons about his origin, but they are far away and approaching them unannounced is risky. He has found that his emotions resonate with others without knowing why.

Ever-Surging Memories: Carole's first trip to the surface is the first flashback. She had spent the past twenty years in Merusea Village and wanted to cooperate with humans; the Melusines were brought to the Marechaussee Phantom for their perception. Citizens treated them with fear and blamed Neuvillette and the Melusines for strange incidents. Five years later Neuvillette gave them the Medal of Peace. Vautrin looked on Carole as his dead younger sister Illaria, whose dream had spread to him. At the trial Vautrin leaves saying her dream was naive. In the present, Neuvillette apologises for letting his emotions leak. After they get back, the case file notes Esseim was released for good behaviour.

In a New Light: Domenico had tried to incite a riot at the prison and failed. He says he first wanted revenge on Neuvillette but found nobody interested and the Mutual Aid Network against him, so he turned to the Melusines. The core values of the network are to help each other, promote justice and not resent just judgement. Carole's badge was lost in a fire, so the other medal went to Vautrin. Wriothesley adds that, from what he has read, Vautrin was disciplined and far from his courtroom behaviour, suggesting that by appearing resentful he made Neuvillette's justice look proper. Neuvillette declines tea to avoid staying long in the prison.

Closing: Clorinde sent Kiara to the Palais Mermonia because everyone wanted to protect her, but thought she would be uneasy with so many people defending her. Neuvillette is briefly rushed by memories from 500 years ago and recovers. Kiara, woken from sleep, says she met Carole in her dream and was glad to see their dream come true. Neuvillette reads Furina's reply to his note and remarks that he cannot understand how she thinks.

Revelations: Vautrin founded the Mutual Aid Network, whose badge is modelled on the Medal of Peace.

Carole, a Melusine who worked with Neuvillette and Vautrin, was destroyed by a conspiracy of hardliners 400 years ago; Vautrin avenged her and was convicted by Neuvillette and the Oratrice. Neuvillette also states he lost most of his memories and his connection to the Primordial Sea when he was born as a human.

The Fountain of Lucine holds strong memories and emotions that Neuvillette can tap with his power. The quest ends with the idea that Fontaine now trusts Neuvillette, a change from the era when people feared him.

Characters: Neuvillette, the Traveler, Paimon and the Melusine Kiara.

Sedene, Clorinde, Charlotte, Navia, Wriothesley, Sigewinne and Furina (through a note). Villains and subjects of the case: Esseim and Domenico.

In flashback: Carole, Vautrin, Rastignac, Thibert and Suavegothe. Eloffe is the shopkeeper whom Kiara inspects.

Consequences: Neuvillette ends the case with a clearer view of how he is regarded and new feelings to sort through. Kiara is safe. Domenico remains in prison.

The flashback explains why Neuvillette is cautious about delegating and why the Mutual Aid Network exists,.

Placement: Unlocked at Adventure Rank 40 after Cataclysm's Quickening (Chapter IV Act IV). Released in 4.1 on 2023-09-27.

267.content: Carole was a Melusine who became Neuvillette's subordinate about 400 years ago and hoped for coexistence between Melusines and humans. Vautrin led the Special Security and Surveillance Patrol and was a friend. After hardliners framed Carole and she died, Vautrin killed those responsible and was found guilty by Neuvillette and the Oratrice; he was exiled. The two had received the Medal of Peace.

268.content: A group of criminals in the Fortress of Meropide who wear a badge based on the Medal of Peace. Their values are to help each other, promote justice and not resent a just judgement. Per the wiki summary, Paimon works out its founder was Vautrin, who kept the second medal.

269.content:
Divina Vulpes Chapter (also: Divina Vulpes, Yae Miko's Story Quest, The Great Narukami Offering, Mysterious Urban Legend, Friendship in Writing, A Centuries-Long Dream, Banquet of Parting): The Divina Vulpes Chapter is Yae Miko's Story Quest, released in Version 2.5, with one act, The Great Narukami Offering. A new book, A Firsthand Guide to Summoning Spirits, spreads a wish ritual across Inazuma City and leaves some of its users acting strangely. Miko investigates with the Traveler, finds the cause is an old friend, the Daiyouko youkai Urakusai, and sees him and other spirits off with a final party.

The act has four quests: Mysterious Urban Legend, Friendship in Writing, A Centuries-Long Dream and Banquet of Parting. It mixes a ghost-story investigation, a publishing-house rivalry in which Miko has the Traveler help write a rival novel, and a gentle farewell. Miko's wit and her affection for the mortal world are in the foreground, and Ei is only mentioned.

The chapter follows the Sacred Sakura events of Transient Dreams: gnawing rifthounds stirred ancient memories along the tree's roots, and that is what woke Urakusai's spirit. It is the Story Quest where Miko is shown as she is among old friends and ordinary readers, not as the Guuji of the shrine.

Plot: In Hanamizaka two men argue about a wish ritual rumoured to make people rich. At the Yae Publishing House the editors say a new book, A Firsthand Guide to Summoning Spirits, is a sensation though it did not come from their print house, and readers who follow it begin to act oddly. At the Grand Narukami Shrine, Miko is visited by Katou Youhei, whose brother Shingo was refused by the swordmaster Domon, then beat Domon's best disciple and has behaved strangely since. In Konda Village Miko makes Youhei admit that he and his brother had performed the ritual together. The spirit, not Shingo, holds the sword skill. Salt thrown by the Traveler drives it out; it challenges the Traveler, loses and fades away contentedly.

Miko shrugs off the book until Kuroda reports that it is dragging down the publishing house's shares. At the house she has read it, admires the writing, and decides to answer with a novel of their own. She sends the Traveler to a nearby convention for ideas and waits at the Uyuu Restaurant with her print-house team. The Traveler writes chapters from their journeys through Mondstadt, Liyue and Inazuma, Miko approves and submits it on their behalf, and after three days it is a success.

Meanwhile Miko has found the book's author, Tomoyuki, a failed light novelist who had been possessed. Since the spirit sought him out, she reasons it can be called with the book's own method. Under the city she finds an underground chamber with a faded mirror and an unusual painting. Following her instructions, the Traveler thinks of wishes and is possessed. The spirit says it will bring ruin to Inazuma, then Miko and it laugh together: she recognises Urakusai, a powerful Daiyouko youkai and her friend.

Urakusai explains that when rifthounds gnawed the Sacred Sakura's roots, memories stirred along them; he heard Tomoyuki's pleas, possessed him and wrote the book so that other youkai spirits could enjoy a last measure of life and leave with no regrets, because he is fond of humanity and its aspirations. He concedes the contest and asks how Miko has been. She says she has always been content and that even Ei has changed. He asks for a "Hyakkiyakou" before they depart, and she promises one.

At the Grand Narukami Shrine Miko explains that the youkai would normally fly on their own but as spirits they need her help. She asks the Traveler to evacuate the area to avoid further possessions and to keep monsters off the Mt. Yougou road, since the concentrated youkai energy would rile them. They do so and perform the ritual, and people in Inazuma City follow the book's incantation without knowing. After the farewell Miko, asked if she is all right, asks for a meal. At the restaurant she is already inside eating a large feast, having played them. The invocations granted nobody's wishes, and she says she expects the next chapter of their novel soon.

Practical details: Takatoshi and Kiyoto start the rumour in Hanamizaka; Junkichi and Kuroda are the editors; Miko says she needs to see the Traveler's sincerity before helping with their own request, which is why she sends them to handle Shingo first.

Revelations: - The book was not a curse: a friendly youkai had it written so spirits could leave without regret.
- The wishes in the ritual were not granted; people were taken over by youkai spirits instead.
- The Sacred Sakura holds memories along its roots, which rifthounds disturbed.

- Urakusai is a Daiyouko youkai and an old friend of Miko.
- Miko says Ei has changed.

Characters: - **Yae Miko**: the Guuji of the Grand Narukami Shrine and owner of the Yae Publishing House.
- **The Traveler and Paimon**: assistants, the Traveler also writing the rival novel.
- **Urakusai**: a Daiyouko youkai and Miko's friend.
- **Katou Youhei and Shingo**: brothers who used the ritual.
- **Kuroda, Junkichi**: editors at the publishing house.
- **Tomoyuki**: failed light novelist who wrote the book under possession.

Domon appears only by reference. Ei is mentioned by Miko in passing.

Consequences: Urakusai and other spirits depart after a final ritual. The craze fades because the wishes are not granted. The Traveler's novel is a hit, and Miko expects further chapters.

Placement: Released in Version 2.5, together with Act II of the Raiden Shogun's chapter. It requires Transient Dreams as well as Omnipresence Over Mortals, and takes place after it. Story order and release order match. No later acts exist as of 7.1.

270.content: A powerful Daiyouko youkai and friend of Yae Miko. His memories stirred when rifthounds gnawed the Sacred Sakura. He possessed the novelist Tomoyuki to write A Firsthand Guide to Summoning Spirits so other youkai could enjoy life and leave without regret. He yields to Miko and asks for a Hyakkiyakou before departing.

key: A Firsthand Guide to Summoning Spirits
271.comment: Divina Vulpes Chapter: A Firsthand Guide to Summoning Spirits
271.content: A best-selling book whose incantation was said to grant wishes. In truth it lets youkai spirits possess the reader. The book did not come out of the Yae Publishing House's own printing and cut into its shares, so Miko answered it with a rival novel.

key: Warriors' Dreams Like Spring Grass Renewing
272.content:
Dracaena Somnolenta Chapter (Sangonomiya Kokomi) (also: Dracaena Somnolenta Chapter, Kokomi's Story Quest, Warriors' Dreams Like Spring Grass Renewing): Kokomi's Story Quest, set on Watatsumi Island just after the Vision Hunt Decree ends. The Traveler joins Kokomi for the Victory Feast and finds a rumour that the Fatui and the Tenryou Commission are plotting to restart the war. The rumour proves to be a plan by grieving Watatsumi soldiers, and Kokomi turns it into a new corps to defend the island.

The chapter has one act, Warriors' Dreams Like Spring Grass Renewing, released in Version 2.1, with five quests: Watatsumi Sightseeing, Rumors Abound, Her Secret, Victory Banquet and New Beginning.

Alongside the intrigue, the act shows Kokomi as a leader who never wanted the role, carries a heavy workload and relies on careful planning and the trust of Gorou and her people.

Plot: On Watatsumi Island the Traveler helps Gorou's soldiers destroy a Fatui ship and learns that rumours of a Tenryou and Fatui plot are circulating before peace talks. Kokomi investigates a Fatui camp, rests secretly in a cave, and holds the Victory Feast. A drunken soldier admits the rumours were fake and meant to restart the war. At the talks with Kujou Sara the soldiers expose the rumour, and Kokomi settles it and forms a new defence corps.

Watatsumi Sightseeing. Arriving for the Victory Feast, the Traveler and Paimon meet Gorou, who suspects a moored Fatui ship and lacks the men to destroy it. They help him. Gorou says the Resistance is now helping civilians, and mentions that some soldiers seem secretive. The Traveler talks to Denjirou, Arisawa, and Yoshihisa and Tsuneo, who believe the Tenryou Commission still collaborates with the Fatui. At Bourou Village a trader, Naruse, is accused of dealing with the Tenryou, and Kokomi arrives and reveals she has begun peace talks, with Sara representing the Tenryou and the Kamisato Clan arranging the venue.

Rumors Abound. The three clear a Fatui camp and find Tenryou goods, expired rations and bomb-making materials. Naruse's stolen goods are returned, but he is fined for planning to sell above the fair price, against Kokomi's temporary decree on price gouging. Kokomi tells the Traveler the original shrine honouring the Raiden Shogun stood near the island's Statue of The Seven, and relations soured after Baal slew Orobashi.

Her Secret. Kokomi is missing for a morning; a soldier points the Traveler to a cave south of the shrine where she is napping. She admits she never wanted to be a leader and finds the work heavy. She asks the Traveler to find a book to restore her energy and falls asleep as they read.

Victory Banquet. At the feast, Kabasawa points the Traveler to a strange soldier, Kouzen, who is drunk and tests their warrior's will. Beaten, he admits the rumours were false and that soldiers want war again because the sudden end made their comrades' deaths feel in vain.

New Beginning. Kokomi gives the Traveler a paper of possible scenarios and the talks begin on a small island off Kannazuka. When Sara mentions returning the Resistance to Tenryou control, Kokomi's guards reveal the rumour, nearly causing a clash. Two Tenryou guards admit they were approached by Fatui seeking a restart. Sara vows to hunt them down. Kokomi refuses to release command of her soldiers for now, and afterwards announces a new corps to protect the island instead of punishing the soldiers.

Details. Gorou says the soldiers have been unusually secretive. Yoshihisa and Tsuneo suspect the Tenryou and the Fatui still collude; Tsuneo discourages telling the Traveler, thinking they might have proposed the talks. Kokomi says the Kujou Clan's collusion seems unlikely given Kujou Kamaji's efforts to redeem the clan, but she still considers the possibility that the talks are a trap. Uchimura advises her to keep an open mind. Izumi Naki reminds Kokomi of a meeting with textile industry representatives, which Kokomi leaves for.

In the cave Kokomi admits that her bloodline made her leadership inevitable, and that she struggles to be the ideal leader. The Traveler finds petitions, an "energy" list and a military treatise.

Kouzen says it is too late to stop them. Kokomi tells the Traveler she wants the conspirators unharmed. At the talks, the guards Motosuke and Sue Yoshitaka say most of the Fatui left and the few that remained were Signora's forces wanting to settle a score with the Shogunate. Kokomi suggests Sara should not tip the Fatui off, so that they come to the Tenryou Commission and are captured together.

Kokomi explains that she is unwilling to give up command because of internal issues in the Tenryou Commission, and that the negotiations showed its leaders could not consistently protect Watatsumi. She tells the soldiers she apologises for not teaching them how to release their fighting will, and that she will punish any further insubordination. The act ends at the purple tree, where Kokomi thanks the Traveler, says she still has a long way to go, and asks them to stay with her a little longer.

Revelations: - The rumour of a Tenryou and Fatui conspiracy was invented by Watatsumi soldiers who wanted war to resume.
- Fatui remnants who stayed in Inazuma were Signora's forces seeking revenge on the Shogunate, according to the Tenryou guards.

- Kokomi never wanted to lead; her bloodline made it inevitable.
- Relations between Watatsumi and Narukami soured after Baal slew Orobashi, in Kokomi's account.

Characters: Kokomi, the Traveler, Paimon and Gorou.

Kujou Sara and the Tenryou guards Motosuke and Sue Yoshitaka; the soldiers Kouzen, Yoshihisa, Tsuneo, Matsuda and Uchimura; villagers Naruse, Denjirou, Arisawa, Kabasawa and shrine keeper Izumi Naki.

Kujou Kamaji, the Kamisato Clan, the Raiden Shogun (as Baal), Orobashi and Signora appear only in conversation.

Consequences: The war rumour is disarmed, peace talks conclude, and Kokomi forms a new corps to defend Watatsumi Island. Sara promises another investigation of the Fatui remnants.

Placement: Unlocks at Adventure Rank 40 after Omnipresence Over Mortals (Chapter II Act IV) and the Story Quest Reflections of Mortality. Released in Version 2.1. Set shortly after the Vision Hunt Decree is lifted. No later acts exist as of 7.1.

273.comment: Dracaena Somnolenta Chapter (Sangonomiya Kokomi): Watatsumi new corps
273.content: After the Vision Hunt Decree ended, some Watatsumi soldiers started a false rumour to push for renewed war. Kokomi, instead of punishing them, formed a new corps to protect the island, since the Tenryou Commission's leaders could not reliably do so.

274.comment: Dracaena Somnolenta Chapter (Sangonomiya Kokomi): Kokomi's cave
274.content: A cave near the shrine where Kokomi secretly rests. The Traveler finds her there napping, and she admits she never wanted to be a leader. The purple tree nearby is where she meets the Traveler privately.

275.content:
Draco Rubedo Chapter (also: Draco Rubedo, Durin's Story Quest, The Magic Known as Storytelling): The act has nine parts: five main quests and four "A Moment's Rest" interludes. It combines Mondstadt scenes (the library, Good Hunter, Dragonspine) with trips inside the book, where Durin's life is retold as a story. The central question is what happens to a character after "happily ever after", and the answer is that Durin must write the ending himself. It ends with his new outfit, a cure for the symptoms of disconnection, and a flight with Dvalin.

It is also the quest where the Hexenzirkel's quiet, long-running plan is shown: Barbeloth's astrology, Rhinedottir's alchemy and Alice's magic combined to give Andersdotter's son a future, with the Traveler cast as the "reader" and Durin as the "writer".

Plot: Alice sends the Traveler and Paimon to Durin at Starsand Shoal and gives them the unfinished Hexenzirkel book. Over several days they follow its clues through Mondstadt (the library, Venti, Good Hunter, Stormterror's Lair) and into the story world, where Durin's life appears as a tale. Durin collapses when people who do not know him take him for the evil historical Durin; the Wanderer, in Sumeru, explains that the world refuses to see him as a separate being. Albedo and the Hexenzirkel's plan lets him break out of the story by writing his own ending, with his mother's pen.

**A Mother's Last Wish.** Alice tells the Traveler and Paimon telepathically to meet Durin at Starsand Shoal, where he stands beside four slain Radiant Beasts. He briefly appears in his Denial of Darkness form, recognises them and returns to his Confirmation of Purity form. Durin says his power has been harder to control lately. Alice opens a book into a special space and explains it is the joint work of the Hexenzirkel witches; Andersdotter died before finishing her part and asked that Durin receive it, since only he could resolve it. Durin accepts the task and Alice gives them a magic ink bottle of Andersdotter's. The first clue sends them to the Mondstadt library, where Lisa (who once volunteered to teach Durin to read) helps them find books missing from the catalogue; the book then pulls them in. Inside, they find a Dodoco narrator and a dragon egg that hatches into a baby Durin.

**A Prophecy From the Past.** Next day, with Anemo energy pointing to Venti, Venti tells them to go to where the mages met and play a melody. Durin asks him why an author would leave a story unfinished; Venti says there are many reasons and that, knowing Durin's mother, it is not his place to pry. Back in the story, four witches in Dodoco form welcome the infant with gifts (a book, a slingshot and a sword), and Durin chooses one.

**Fate's Accursed Wiles.** At Good Hunter Durin is playing Genius Invokation TCG against Kaeya while Fischl and Klee watch. Durin then takes the Traveler to Stormterror's Lair and into the story, where the grown Mini Durin is shunned; they persuade him to open his heart. They think they are finished and go to Good Hunter, but Marjorie and Shuyun are suspicious of Durin, believing he is the Durin they remember from history, and the rest are confused why nobody knew him. Durin collapses from a burst of abyssal energy, which the Traveler purifies. Jean says Barbara found no issue and takes custody of the book, deciding to tell Albedo. Venti and Dvalin watch from afar, Venti saying the story is not over.

**Revelation Beneath the Stars.** Durin explains that when people forgot him he felt disconnected from his body and only reconnected when friends spoke his name. New clues lead to Sumeru City, where the Wanderer is returning a modified book to Katayoun. The Wanderer says that whenever he tried to write about Durin the text changed to the Durin of history, and, as a Descender unaffected by Irminsul's changes, he concludes the world refuses to accept this Durin as a separate being. He joins them in a simulated Sumeru in which he is a cat and Durin follows the path he took after Simulanka, and concludes the Hexenzirkel built a way for Durin to exist separately.

**The Solution of Fate.** Albedo summons them to Dragonspine, examines Durin and explains the witches' plan: it needs Barbeloth's astrology, Rhinedottir's alchemy and Alice's magic. In the book Albedo becomes a Simulanka resident and the Wanderer a cat. Destroying a heart fails with a bad ending; Alice's magic resets it. Durin decides to break out of the story. A flashback shows Andersdotter wanting her son to live happily in Teyvat; she knew the story had to end and chose that Durin write his own. A manifestation of his mother gives him her pen and he defies the original's fate in a climactic battle. Back in Mondstadt, he wears a freer outfit and Albedo notes his symptoms are gone.

Afterwards Alice tells the Traveler she chose them as reader so her magic could work. Barbeloth looks at the stars and no longer finds Durin's fate there, calls him a lucky child and then stops responding. Venti whispers that Durin may fulfil a final regret, and Durin flies with Dvalin and befriends him. A fragment of Andersdotter's consciousness says goodbye to Alice, pleased with how her child has grown, and Alice gives the Traveler a copy of the finished book.

Between main quests four "Interlude: A Moment's Rest" quests mark the passage of days; the wiki notes that the Story Quest cannot be completed in less than five days of real time, unlike earlier Story Quests. Each visit to the book covers a later stage of Durin's life, ending with his mother's pen.

Revelations: - Andersdotter wrote a story to bring her son's character into Teyvat, but died before finishing it; her last wish was that Durin write the ending.
- Durin was forgotten or mistaken for the evil historical Durin by people who did not know him; he felt disconnected until friends spoke his name.
- The Hexenzirkel prepared a solution (astrology, alchemy and magic) that lets Durin exist separately, and it works.

Barbeloth no longer sees Durin's fate among the stars after the story is completed; she calls him a lucky child.

Characters: Durin (lead), the Traveler and Paimon, Alice (guide and maker of the reader/writer arrangement), Andersdotter (remembered), Lisa, Venti, Kaeya, Fischl, Klee, Diona (mentioned), Marjorie and Shuyun, Jean, Barbara (examines him, offstage), Albedo, the Wanderer, Katayoun, Barbeloth, Rhinedottir (referenced), Dvalin.

Albedo is Durin's brother in this quest's wording; the Wanderer is the only character who explains why the world misreads Durin.

Consequences: Durin's disconnection symptoms are gone and he gets the outfit "Toward the Distant Horizon" as the chapter reward. He becomes friends with Dvalin. The Traveler receives a copy of the newly made book.

Placement: Released in Version 6.2 (Luna III) with an event period starting 2025-12-03; the chapter stays available. It requires Adventure Rank 40 and Act VI of Song of the Welkin Moon, "Melting Moonlight in the Morning Mist". During the event, Quick Start allowed access at Adventure Rank 28 after Chapter I Act III of the Archon Quest.

276.comment: Draco Rubedo Chapter: Draco Rubedo Chapter Event Rewards
276.content: The event bonus for completing the chapter within the window was 60 Primogems plus ascension and level-up materials and Nod-Krai specialties. The outfit "Toward the Distant Horizon" is the chapter's special reward.

277.content:
The book is the joint work of the Hexenzirkel witches. Andersdotter left her part unfinished and asked Alice to give the work to Durin. Reading it moves the Traveler, Paimon and Durin into a story world where he is a Dodoco-narrated baby, a shunned adult, and later a character in a replica of Sumeru.

The Traveler plays the "reader", Durin the "writer". Alice's magic only works if both roles are filled.

278.content:
Dreams, Emptiness, Deception (also: Dreams, Emptiness, and Deception, Chapter III Act III, Sumeru Act III): Dreams, Emptiness, Deception is Act III of the Sumeru Archon Quests. After the Sabzeruz Festival samsara ends, Nahida, speaking through Katheryne, plans with the Traveler to learn what the Akademiya's sages intend. Their plan to turn Setaria, Grand Sage Azar's secretary, is ambushed by the Fatui Harbinger Dottore, who traps Nahida's mind in the Akasha. The Traveler flees toward the desert, where Nahida's last clue sends them to the people of the Great Red Sand and to a meeting at Aaru Village with Alhaitham, Cyno, Dehya and Candace.

It has three quests: Like a Triumphant Hero, The Gaze From a Certain God and The Four at Loggerheads. The announcement text calls it the end of the Sabzeruz samsara, the path to saving the god in the desert stars, and a boast from the lord of the scarlet soil.

The act is where the Akademiya's collaboration with the Fatui first becomes certain, and where Nahida is lost to the Traveler until Act V. It is also where the desert-based allies of the later plan are brought together.

Plot: Like a Triumphant Hero: some time after the samsara, Nahida takes over Katheryne at the Adventurers' Guild and says she wants to resolve the sages before turning to Irminsul and the Withering. The sages avoid wearing their Akasha Terminals, so she cannot read them. She chooses Setaria, a desert-born prodigy who is troubled by the sages' work and by being unable to help her people. Nahida learns the speech habits of Setaria's acquaintances and the Traveler, when Setaria goes shopping, speaks through their minds one at a time, pretending to be King Deshret's followers. Setaria cracks, agrees to steal confidential papers, and plans to hand them over at the Akademiya the next night. The place is full of cheering people: Dottore, who calls himself the Doctor, reveals that he overheard through a listening device, that Setaria is imprisoned, and that the crowd has been given the belief that the Traveler saved the world. Nahida steps in and tells the Traveler to run, revealing the scope of her abilities to Dottore. The Traveler and Paimon now know the Akademiya works with the Fatui and look for Tighnari.

The Gaze From a Certain God: paid Eremites ambush them near Gandharva Ville, sent by a client called the Outcast. Collei is there, unable to patrol because of Eleazar; Tighnari has gone to Pardis Dhyai. At Pardis Dhyai, "Katheryne" has escaped Dottore but expects him to find a way to trap her. Haypasia offers to show what she saw, but the Traveler sees Scaramouche's memories. In a fight "Katheryne" is speared; touching fingers with the Traveler, she swaps bodies with them, and the Traveler sees Nahida's true body in the Sanctuary of Surasthana and Scaramouche in the process of becoming a god. Nahida leaves a last clue before her mind is trapped. Tighnari rescues the Traveler and stays at Pardis Dhyai to watch Haypasia.

The Four at Loggerheads: Alhaitham helps them escape at Caravan Ribat and accompanies them to Aaru Village, where Cyno, the General Mahamatra, ambushes them. A sandstorm drives them into the village chief's house, where Candace presides. Cyno says he put himself in exile after noticing data missing from material Azar had submitted and being refused when he tried to investigate; Alhaitham admits he was ordered to track the Traveler but did not accept the job. Riftwolves attack; the Traveler, Dehya and Candace drive them off. The chief, Uncle Anpu, explains that the Village Keepers, exiled Akademiya scholars, have vanished. A boy, Isak, asks for help finding his grandfather.

Like a Triumphant Hero in detail. Nahida has been posting commissions through Katheryne to watch the Traveler at work. She says she slept after the samsara and dreamed of a happy Sabzeruz Festival; Paimon remarks that this is how the festival should really be, and Nahida wonders whether the looks she gets are 'pity'. Dunyarzad is stable, but Eleazar can only be cured once Irminsul's Withering is dealt with. In planning, Nahida refuses to involve innocent students, reasoning that doing so would make her no better than the sages. Her description of Setaria uses a star-and-sun metaphor: Setaria was a bright star of the desert who was taken up by the Akademiya, saw the damage done, and covered her guilt. The Traveler, borrowing Nahida's power, possesses a series of people close to Setaria; one is a fortune-teller. Setaria's responses reveal that King Deshret's supposed resurrection is itself an Akademiya misinformation campaign. She calls Rima of the Corps of Thirty for help, and Rima too is taken over. Setaria finally agrees to work against the sages, though she says she knows little of the full project.

The Gaze From a Certain God in detail. The ambushers include a brigade leader who boasts of the highest commission rate in Sumeru and says their client is an outcast. In the fight at Pardis Dhyai, Katheryne's body is run through by a spear; Nahida indwells the Traveler, and the Traveler briefly occupies Nahida's real body and sees Scaramouche, who sees them in turn. Nahida's clue, "Even in a moonless night, a shower of starlight can still drown out illusions and lies", is read by the Traveler and Paimon as a pointer toward the Great Red Sand and its people.

The Four at Loggerheads in detail. Paimon recalls the Wall of Samiel as a protection against sandstorms. Alhaitham says he is still studying the capsule and suspects the Traveler of withholding something. At the village Cyno asks him to give up the Divine Knowledge Capsule; Alhaitham replies by questioning why Cyno is alone, since other matra do not know where he went. Dehya joins them and says she wanted to go home out of boredom. Candace asks them to explain, warns them not to fight in the village, and goes outside when growls are heard. Afterward Cyno and the Traveler meet privately: he explains that the Village Keepers were once shunned as useless until a scholar's glowing form shielded the whole village during an earthquake. The Traveler attributes this to the Dendro Archon, and Cyno is surprised to learn the Archon walks among people. Isak appears and Candace confirms his story.

Quest-level steps. Like a Triumphant Hero: talk to Katheryne; talk to Nahida elsewhere; gather information on Setaria's contacts; return to Nahida; wait until the next afternoon; carry out the plan in the market; follow Setaria; wait until the next night; meet Nahida; go to the Akademiya; and sort out the information. The Gaze From a Certain God: go to Gandharva Ville; defeat three waves of Eremites; find Tighnari; enter Pardis Dhyai. The Four at Loggerheads: go to Caravan Ribat; follow Alhaitham; go to Aaru Village; defeat two waves of rifthound whelps; exchange information with Cyno; talk to Candace; go to the chief's house.

Background details introduced. Setaria's genius earned her a place at the Akademiya, a rare chance for someone born in the desert; she takes a day off every ten days. Nahida's understanding is that the key members of the Akademiya, including Corps of Thirty guards, deliberately avoid wearing Terminals. Dottore's experiment tested what ideas can be put into the minds of Terminal users. The client who hired the Eremites is known only as the Outcast; Paimon wonders whether this means an outcast of the Akademiya, and the Traveler guesses it is the Doctor.

Name notes: the Wall of Samiel is the wall at Caravan Ribat that Paimon says blocks sandstorms; Aaru Village's chief is Uncle Anpu; Isak is the boy whose grandfather is a missing Village Keeper.

Revelations: - King Deshret's supposed resurrection is an Akademiya-run misinformation campaign, as Setaria reveals.
- The Akademiya is collaborating with the Fatui, and Dottore can use the Akasha to implant beliefs in a crowd.
- Haypasia's Paripurna Life vision shows Scaramouche's memories, not the Dendro Archon's.
- Alhaitham was assigned to track the Traveler; Cyno stepped down after discovering missing data and Azar refusing his request.

- While swapped into Nahida's real body at the Sanctuary of Surasthana, the Traveler sees Scaramouche in the process of becoming a god, and he sees them.
- The Village Keepers are exiled scholars who were protected by a green light at an earthquake, which Cyno takes as the Dendro Archon's work.

Characters: - **Traveler and Paimon**; **Nahida** (as Katheryne); **Setaria**; **Dottore**; **Tighnari and Collei**; **Alhaitham**; **Cyno**; **Dehya**; **Candace**; **Haypasia**, **Isak** and **Uncle Anpu**; **Scaramouche** (seen in vision).

Roles:
- **Nahida**: leads the plan and loses her mind to the Akasha.
- **Setaria**: the target of the pressure plan; imprisoned after being overheard.
- **Dottore**: sets the trap and pays the Eremites.
- **Tighnari, Collei**: the Forest Rangers in Gandharva Ville and Pardis Dhyai.
- **Alhaitham, Cyno, Dehya, Candace**: the four at loggerheads, who meet at Aaru Village.
- **Rima**: a Corps of Thirty member briefly possessed by the Traveler.

Consequences: Nahida is cut off from the Traveler and trapped; Setaria is imprisoned; the Traveler and Paimon are on the run from the Eremites and Fatui. They find allies in the desert and Isak's grandfather's disappearance becomes the next task in Act IV.

Tighnari remains at Pardis Dhyai watching Haypasia. Alhaitham's divided loyalties and Cyno's exile become central to the Act IV and V plan.

Placement: Released in Version 3.1. It follows Act II, The Morn a Thousand Roses Brings (3.0), and leads directly into Act IV, King Deshret and the Three Magi (3.1).

Act III is the third of five Sumeru acts in Chapter III. The quest "Dawn" at the end of Act II leads into its first quest.

279.content: A desert-born prodigy who serves Grand Sage Azar as his secretary. Nahida targets her because her talent got her out of the desert but also left her guilty about the sages' work and about her inability to help her people. She is overheard cooperating with the Traveler and imprisoned.

280.comment: Dreams, Emptiness, Deception: Dottore's Akasha Experiment
280.content: A crowd at the Akademiya gate is made, through Akasha Terminals, to believe that the Traveler has just saved the world. It is Dottore's experiment as well as a trap; Nahida shields the Traveler and reveals her abilities.

281.comment: Dreams, Emptiness, Deception: Nahida's Last Clue
281.content: After exchanging bodies with the Traveler, Nahida leaves the clue that a shower of starlight can drown out illusions and lies even on a moonless night. The Traveler and Paimon interpret it as pointing to the desert people.

282.comment: Dreams, Emptiness, Deception: Aaru Village Meeting
282.content: A desert village where the Traveler meets Candace, Dehya, Cyno and Alhaitham. Cyno and Alhaitham fight before Dehya and Candace mediate. The village's Village Keepers, exiled scholars treated as mad, have vanished.

key: Roll! A Sea of New Acquaintances
283.content:
Duel! The Summoners' Summit! (also: Summoners' Summit, King of Invokations Grand Prix, Commence! A Suspect Genesis, Roll! A Sea of New Acquaintances, Cards Out! Grievances Begone, Culminate! Chatter of Joyous Dreams, Card Snatcher): The event's four story parts follow a regional tournament each: Mondstadt (Kaeya loses the final to Timmie), Liyue (Hu Tao reaches the final), Inazuma (Sangonomiya Kokomi wins) and Sumeru (Cyno is named champion). The card backs turn out to be coded messages from Treasure Hoarders, and the Komaniya Express courier Kirara unwittingly carries them. In Sumeru, Kirara also delivers a long-undelivered parcel to Garvipidam, who with the late Gulab created Genius Invokation TCG. Gameplay modes were A Tour of Wonders, Zero Hour Invokation, Evermotion Mechanical Painting: Invoker and Heart of the Dice.

Requirements were Adventure Rank 32, the Ritou Escape Plan and the quest "Battlefield of Dice, Cats, and Cards"; recommended story quests were the Akasha Pulses Archon Quest, Mona's Astrolabos and the Raiden Shogun's Imperatrix Umbrosa Act II. Rewards included Primogems, a Crown of Insight and the weapon Ibis Piercer, bought with Invokation Coupons.

Plot: In Liyue the party is greeted by Baiwen, who invites Charlotte to meet Ningguang at Yujing Terrace because Charlotte's exclusive may have offended those behind the scenes. Kazuha joins them. They help Kirara find the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor, where Hu Tao is preparing for her final. She reveals that the suspect won a card back from Chongyun in a match, and the party goes to Wuwang Hill to find Chongyun and a missing child, Little Yu, while Ningguang explains that the treasure-chest card back is a rare item some players pay for as a luck charm. In Inazuma, at the Ritou tournament, the Traveler meets finalists and spectators including Ei, Yae Miko, Itto, Shinobu and Sara, then tells Kokomi what they have learned.

Kokomi works through the clues: the Card Snatcher's route matches Kirara's deliveries, every parcel she carries ends up in the same place in Sumeru, and the card backs are in her bag. She infers a group acted: other members already collected card backs and shipped them by Komaniya Express while the one the party followed was too slow to use it, so he stole once and traded after that. The Traveler agrees to escort Kirara to the delivery address.

In Sumeru Cyno joins them at Caravan Ribat. Kirara delivers the package to Dedebaba, who is waiting with Pabag and Papak, three Treasure Hoarders. When they grow suspicious of her and the party, a fight follows and they are defeated. They confess that the treasure-chest card backs are signals: when dirty with wet earth and wiped off, a hidden message summons hoarders for a worldwide heist. Some fellow hoarders became fans of the game and lost the card backs to other players, so the group tried to recover them all and send them back to reprint. Cyno takes them into custody.

Kirara then brings the Traveler, Paimon and Charlotte to Vimara Village for a separate parcel the company had long been unable to deliver. Zadith, Arezo and the village head Amadhiah help the party find the recipient, a scholar named Garvipidam. The sender, Gulab, had died; the package contains a letter, and the cinematic shows Gulab giving his friend a device he made to help players find opponents nearby. Garvipidam tells them that he and Gulab were childhood classmates who painted cards together while Gulab, who had Eleazar, was in hospital. In the letter's flashback Gulab calls the device his last gift, so that his friend could make new friends through the game.

Revelations: Genius Invokation TCG was created by two Akademiya scholars: Gulab, who became a Rtawahist Dastur but was bedridden with Eleazar and died, and his friend Garvipidam, who built elemental theory into the game. They developed it by painting cards during Garvipidam's hospital visits. Gulab left a final parcel with a letter, delivered late by Kirara. Garvipidam, who could not bear to play without Gulab, is moved by the letter and by the party's account of what the game has done for people.

The poster seen in Mondstadt of the game's "inventors" looks young; Kaeya doubts that it is an accurate portrayal, and Charlotte says almost nothing is known about the inventors.

Characters: Charlotte is the cheerful, persistent Steambird reporter; Kirara an Inazuman courier and youkai; Cyno a serious Matra general who is nevertheless eager to pun; Kokomi a patient strategist. Mondstadt's finalists are Kaeya and Timmie. Hu Tao writes rhyming verse before her final. Ningguang hosts a meal and shares intelligence. Eichendorff, Lennard, Huffman and Mika are brief Mondstadt bystanders.

Consequences: The Treasure Hoarders' plan is stopped by Cyno, Charlotte has her scoop, and Kirara is credited as the one who makes it possible. Garvipidam receives Gulab's gift.

Placement: Released in Version 3.7. Requirements were the Ritou Escape Plan and Battlefield of Dice, Cats, and Cards. The recommended Akasha Pulses Archon Quest, Mona's Astrolabos Chapter Act I and the Raiden Shogun's Imperatrix Umbrosa Chapter Act II could be skipped through the event's Quick Start.

284.comment: Duel! The Summoners' Summit!: The Card Snatcher
284.content: The "Card Snatcher" is the title Charlotte gives to a suspicious figure who took or traded for specific Genius Invokation card backs during the King of Invokations Grand Prix. He is one of several Treasure Hoarders collecting treasure-chest card backs, which secretly carry a signal for a hoarders' operation.

285.comment: Duel! The Summoners' Summit!: Gulab and Garvipidam
285.content: Gulab and Garvipidam are the Akademiya scholars who created Genius Invokation TCG. Gulab, a Rtawahist Dastur with Eleazar, died; Garvipidam moved to Vimara Village and stopped playing. Gulab's late parcel carried a letter.

286.comment: Duel! The Summoners' Summit!: King of Invokations Grand Prix
286.content: A multi-nation tournament for Genius Invokation TCG arranged through the Adventurers' Guild, with regional finals. An unofficial player tournament ran alongside. Cyno is named the Sumeru champion in the event's story.

287.content:
Dulciaria Structura Chapter (also: Dulciaria Structura, Escoffier's Story Quest, Treasured Above All, Shaped by Fame, Roasted by Flames, Ice-Frosted Endgame, Gateau Debord quest): Escoffier's Story Quest, set at Hotel Debord in the Court of Fontaine. Navia and the Traveler find the hotel's chefs in trouble: the current head chef, Savanna, drives them hard, and a chef has been injured. They ask Escoffier, the former head chef, for help. A cook-off over the legendary Gateau Debord follows, then a sabotage plot and a trip to a ruin where the cake's secret is buried.

The chapter has one act, Treasured Above All, of three quests: Shaped by Fame, Roasted by Flames and Ice-Frosted Endgame. It was released in version 5.6 as an event and is unlocked at Adventure Rank 40 after Masquerade of the Guilty. It shows Escoffier's work ethic, her fondness for the restaurant she left, and her view of food.

The story is about ambition, inheritance and credit. Escoffier, Savanna and the hotel's founders each struggle with the legacy of one cake, and the plot turns on a staff member who sabotages the cook-off.

Plot: Escoffier returns for a cook-off against Savanna for the Codex Debord, which holds the founder's recipes. Escoffier loses after someone sabotages her cake. Savanna goes missing the next day and the party follows a map to a ruin where Monica, the real culprit, has her. At the ruin Monica wants the cake's secret ingredient, but it is gone, and Savanna and Escoffier hold a fair cook-off afterwards.

Shaped by Fame: Navia introduces the Traveler and Paimon to Savanna's overbearing management and to Firmin, whose injuries stopped his work. A candy wrapper from Monica says to find Escoffier in Fleuve Cendre. Navia explains that Escoffier is the former head chef who took the blame for an illegal substance, lumiline, in the food and spent a short time in the Fortress of Meropide. When she returned Savanna had taken over. Escoffier agrees to a cook-off proposed by the hotel's boss Vaneigem, with the Codex Debord as the stake. She tests the Traveler's cooking, scores Paimon's and Navia's dishes harshly and the Traveler's at 8 out of 10, and, needing capable assistants, takes the Traveler on.

Roasted by Flames: in a double-blind cook-off, Savanna wins. Savanna reads the codex and faints on finding no secrets in it. Escoffier tastes the cake and finds it was sabotaged during preparation; Monica apologises and claims that Savanna blackmailed her into making Escoffier lose; this later proves to be a cover for her own plan.

Ice-Frosted Endgame: Savanna is missing and has received threatening letters. A map found at her home matches the sites Modeste and Savelli travelled. The party follows it to a ruin where Monica has a knife at Savanna's neck. Monica wants the cake's secret ingredient, but the container is empty. Escoffier, Savanna and the Traveler subdue her and escape, and a final fair cook-off is held.

Shaped by Fame: Navia says business tripled at Fleuve Cendre once Escoffier joined it as a temporary chef. Navia explains the lumiline was a drug made from Lumitoile that heightened the senses but caused mood swings and nerve damage, and was banned quickly. The codex was handed to Escoffier as thanks for her service and only head chefs, current and former, may hold it. Escoffier says the founders Modeste and Savelli explored the world and made use of what they found, which shaped Fontainian cuisine, and that the Gateau Debord is rare because of one ingredient found on such an adventure.

Roasted by Flames: the judges unanimously agree that one cake is far below their standard. The other chefs explain that Savanna pushed herself even harder than them, working through the night. Savanna realises she is the problem and breaks down.

Ice-Frosted Endgame: Escoffier tells Savanna she will give her the scolding of her life. The ruin is a Remurian public bathhouse. Two Blubberbeasts guard the way, and Modeste's notes say they must be fed a good meal. Savanna saw through Monica's plan to poison the party's drinking water. She sets off explosives to cover her retreat. At the camp, journals show the ingredient came from the ruin.

The diaries: Savelli set up camp at the ruin and wrote that the ingredient cost Modeste his sense of taste. Modeste then died by his own hand, and sent Savelli a last letter. Savelli realised the truth and framed himself as the culprit to protect Modeste's legacy, erasing evidence. He emptied the jar so it could not harm later people. Monica, who believed Savelli had destroyed Modeste's reputation, breaks the jar in anger, which awakens two Praetorian Golems that attack her. She threatens Escoffier at gunpoint before Savanna knocks her out; the party leaves her behind.

Aftermath: Firmin forgives Savanna, saying the letters showed it was Monica who had laced his tea with lumiline. Savanna asks why her cake was not like Escoffier's and is told Monica sabotaged the ovens. Escoffier says she spent nearly three years creating her version of the cake. She insists on a fresh cook-off, and Savanna loses it. Escoffier says she left the hotel over the food-safety incident and because she felt the restaurant could no longer support her; she met a Liyue chef as adventurous as the founders, and used Romaritime Flowers on her cake. She says she believes the secret ingredient was lumiline, hyped only because sugar was less common then. A jar expert tells Navia the broken Remurian jar would have been priceless.

Revelations: Monica sabotaged the cake and plotted against Savanna. The founders' secret ingredient was found in a Remurian ruin.

Modeste lost his sense of taste to the ingredient and died. Savelli framed himself as the culprit to protect Modeste's legacy.

Monica's claim that Savanna blackmailed her was a cover. Savanna's harsh management came partly from pushing herself even harder than her staff.

Escoffier's view is that the cake's famed ingredient was only lumiline, with its fame owed to scarce sugar.

Characters: Escoffier, Navia, the Traveler and Paimon.

Savanna, the current head chef, and Monica, her subordinate who turns out to be the saboteur. Firmin, an injured chef. Vaneigem, the hotel's boss, and the customer Renaud.

Modeste and Savelli, the hotel's founders, appear through diaries and letters. Leone and Hilaire are other chefs.

Consequences: Monica is left at the ruin. The staff back Savanna as head chef and Escoffier reassures her that she has what it takes. Escoffier does not return as head chef but promises to visit the hotel from time to time to ensure its standards stay high.

Escoffier gives the Traveler a revised copy of her recipe. A broken relic is lost.

Placement: Unlocked at Adventure Rank 40 after Chapter IV Act V, Masquerade of the Guilty. Released in 5.6 as the event Treasured Above All.

288.content: The legendary cake of Hotel Debord, made to a recipe of its founder Modeste. Escoffier recreated it and restored the hotel's fame. It is made by three people. The secret ingredient is the story's central question, as Escoffier thinks it was lumiline while others thought it came from a ruin.

289.content: A book of the founding chefs' recipes and notes, held by current and former head chefs of the hotel. The original was given to Escoffier in thanks for her service. Savanna staked the right to it in the cook-off.

290.comment: Dulciaria Structura Chapter: Treasured Above All event rewards
290.content: The act ran as a limited event between 2025-05-07 and 2025-05-27 (GMT+8). Completing it during the event gave Primogems, ascension and level-up materials and Fontaine specialties, and low-rank players could unlock it through a Quick Start.

key: East of the Moon, West of the Sun
Proofs of the Cognoscenti quest series
Reed Miller's Great Treasure quest series
291.comment: East of the Moon, West of the Sun
291.content:
East of the Moon, West of the Sun (also: Proofs of the Cognoscenti quest series, Reed Miller's Great Treasure quest series): A Nod-Krai world quest series that begins in Version 6.0. Treasure hunters, many of them from the Snezhnayan city of Novokitezhgrad, are chasing the five Proofs of the Cognoscenti, legendary relics said to point to the Great Treasure of the thief Reed Miller. The Traveler and Paimon collect all five and find the treasure, learning in the process how the hunters' stories connect.

The series has four parts that can be done in any order: The Shoemaker's Children Go Barefoot, The Tale-Telling Heart, Whisper Beneath the Waves and Return to Sender. Once all four are complete, the final quest, The Raven's Legacy, starts automatically. Its title comes from a Norwegian fairy tale, "East of the Sun and West of the Moon" (wiki trivia).

Each quest is a self-contained story in a different corner of Nod-Krai (the Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau on Paha Isle, Blue Amber Lake on Lempo Isle, the Eye of Kratti, and a bunker near Piramida), and each leaves the Traveler with one Proof. Several characters share a history in Novokitezhgrad that is revealed bit by bit. The final quest is the series' pay-off, revealing what the Great Treasure actually is.

Plot: Four short adventures each yield a Proof of the Cognoscenti: a goblet won from a Fatui officer, a mask at a campfire by Blue Amber Lake, a feather from a ghost-haunted wreck, and a relic found in a doomsday bunker. Tolfin, a storyteller-merchant, leads the Traveler to his grandmother Hiljetta, who owns the fifth and tests the Traveler in a sparring match. The five Proofs open the Great Treasure site.

Each quest is a self-contained story. At the Fatui's Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau on Paha Isle, the Traveler and Paimon meet the thief-fan Netochka and beat the officer Raskolnikov for a Proof (Shoemaker's Children). At Blue Amber Lake, Tolfin sets a treasure hunt that exposes a family's guilty secret (Tale-Telling Heart). At the Eye of Kratti, a cave of shipwreck ghosts yields a feather (Whisper Beneath the Waves). In a doomsday bunker by Piramida the Traveler cleans up Abyssal contamination and defeats the Ultimate Calamity (Return to Sender). Finally Tolfin's grandmother Hiljetta spars with the Traveler, gives the last Proof, and the five Proofs open the Great Treasure site in Piramida, where a flashback shows the young Treasure Hoarders Relya and Silve (The Raven's Legacy).

The Shoemaker's Children Go Barefoot (Luna I, 6.0). At the Fatui's Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau, the Traveler and Paimon sneak in and meet Netochka, a thief-fan of Reed Miller from Novokitezhgrad. She is the daughter of a police chief, and the Fatui officer Poruchik Raskolnikov, who was once her father's student, has collected a Proof. The three fight through the facility, defeat Raskolnikov, and he lets them take the Proof, saying he does not want it drawing thieves to the Bureau.

The Tale-Telling Heart (Luna I). At a campfire at Blue Amber Lake, the merchant Tolfin offers the Traveler a hunt for the Proof left by his late friend Papa Wrench, who built a set of mechanical toys for a sick child named Tinet. Two travellers, Danyusha and Zhorik Shesternin, are present; Danyusha is Papa Wrench's daughter and Zhorik is his heir (Tolfin calls them Mr. and Mrs. Shesternin, but the exact relationship between the two is not clear). They also want the Proof. The Traveler clears a trial, finds spare parts underground and wakes the giant machine Colonel Iron Whale. The Proof, a mask, goes to the Traveler.

Whisper Beneath the Waves (Luna I). At the Eye of Kratti, near the fisherman Ilmari, the Traveler enters a hidden cave beneath the sea and passes through memories of ghosts from old shipwrecks. Throwing Kuuvahki dewdrops into the tree roots makes the tree glow and brings up a chest holding a feather, the Inscripta-Cognoscenti's Feather.

Return to Sender (Luna IV, 6.3). A recording leads the Traveler into a bunker at the "end of the apocalypse" by Piramida. Trapped in Abyssal contamination, the Traveler restores the purification system, learns what happened to its staff, defeats the Ultimate Calamity in the supervisor's office, and leaves with the Devocina-Cognoscenti's Sorrow.

The Raven's Legacy (Luna IV). In Piramida, Tolfin takes the Traveler to his grandmother Hiljetta, the "Black-Barrel Hag", who spars with them and gives the last Proof, the Memorata-Cognoscenti's Jest. The Traveler offers all five Proofs to a huge Weasel Thief statue and descends into a puzzle site. Under a heap of iron coins lies an old ship; when Paimon urges the Traveler to take the helm, a flashback begins to two young Treasure Hoarders, Relya and Silve, who take a governor's treasure from Bounty Island, plan to share it with street children in Snezhnograd, and leave a raven insignia to show who took it. Back with Tolfin, the Traveler receives "The First Iron Coin" and Tolfin names the raven's owner as Avrelian, the one remembered as Reed Miller.

The Shoemaker's Children: the first of Netochka's fixations is a book, The Legends of Reed Miller, Thief Extraordinaire, and she renames the party with codenames (Goldfinch for the Traveler, Snowy Owl for Paimon). She admits she knew Raskolnikov all along and tells them a woman named Hidimbi in Nasha Town "chose" her and sold her a thief's kit, which Paimon suspects was a scam. The final fight uses the Bureau's kuuvahki hammers against Raskolnikov's machinery.

The Tale-Telling Heart: A weasel thief steals the lift lever, and Tolfin's trained weasel thief Huginn catches it and later digs up Papa Wrench's journal pages. Tolfin later privately explains that he sent a message telling the Shesternins where a Proof lay because they had fallen into debt, and wanted to see whether Zhorik had changed in ten years; he says Papa Wrench had hoped he would forgive. Zhorik takes a flashy goblet to be the Proof and tosses the mask aside; when the Traveler shows him a photo, he flees.

Whisper Beneath the Waves: the cave holds the spirits of passengers and crew from at least three ships (Atlas, Fosegrin, Fortunate One). The Traveler reads diaries about twin sisters who travelled without their father, and an investigator's notes on two murder cases that he solved, ending with a note that a Mr. Shesternin failed to meet Chief Stalanov on deck while Zhorik denied knowing where he was.

Return to Sender: recordings tell of Senior Researcher Grazina, a supervisor named Morozov whom a dying maintenance worker accuses of sending his staff to die, and Professor Rotwang's plan; Grazina records that a man she calls Brahe Reed Miller quietly led the surviving children out to people who would protect them. The Ultimate Calamity thinks the world outside the sky has ended.

The Raven's Legacy: puzzle steps use three Weasel Thief statues, notices with riddles, and a huge hoard of Strange Iron Coins.

The Shesternin storyline stays unresolved on screen: Zhorik flees into dangerous terrain and Tolfin hints that other friends of Papa Wrench may deal with him. Netochka is found at Speranza in Nasha Town after her quest and says she misses Novokitezhgrad but is staying a while. Tolfin says he will visit Colonel Iron Whale from time to time and remains in Piramida for a while.

A message signed by Reed Miller at the hoard greets whoever has gathered the Proofs, says the treasure is right in front of them, and advises the finder to take their share quietly, remove his note and pretend nothing was found, so that people keep chasing the Proofs. A second note by Brahe says he deliberately spread rumours of Proofs and invented stories of failed treasure hunters, and mentions a "Prototype Iron Coin". After the flashback the Traveler digs up an item at the flashback site, the First Iron Coin, and Tolfin links the raven insignia to the family crest of Avrelian's noble academy classmate.

Revelations: The Great Treasure the Traveler finds is a vast pile of old iron coins above a buried ship, not a hoard of gold or modern Mora. Reed Miller founded the Treasure Hoarders and wrote that the hoard belongs to whoever gathers the five Proofs, but should be taken quietly.

Papa Wrench, the maker of Colonel Iron Whale, was Danyusha's father and was lost from the ship Fortunate One ten years earlier. Zhorik, his heir, is strongly implied to have pushed him overboard.

Tolfin and Hiljetta are grandson and grandmother, and both are Treasure Hoarders. Hiljetta wants to restore the Treasure Hoarders to their old role defending Elysium and helping the poor, and asks the Traveler to be heir to Reed Miller's dream; Tolfin says that golden age is gone and stages a show so that the Traveler's choice is theirs.

Tolfin says the man legend calls Reed Miller was Avrelian, who in the flashback goes by Relya and fights alongside Silve; it is said that before the Treasure Hoarders existed he stole from the rich with his military-academy friends. In Return to Sender (6.3), recordings tell of a "Mr. Brahe Reed Miller" who helped hide surviving children from a research bunker and who knew an old hunter and the new Frostmoon Scion priestess.
