Characters: The Traveler and Paimon; Tolfin (merchant-storyteller and Treasure Hoarder) and his weasel thief Huginn; Hiljetta, the Black-Barrel Hag; Netochka and Poruchik Raskolnikov; Danyusha and Zhorik Shesternin; Ilmari the fisherman.

Netochka is idealistic and dramatic, the child of a police chief; Raskolnikov is a rule-bound Fatui officer who insists on following orders to the letter but yields the Proof because keeping it would only draw thieves to the Bureau. Tolfin tells stories as a form of manipulation and kindness. Hiljetta is a gruff old fighter who rejects Tolfin's lightness. In the bunker, Grazina, Morozov and Rotwang appear only in recordings; the Ultimate Calamity is a corrupted monster that still follows a dead master.

Consequences: Each quest yields a Proof; the final quest ends the Great Treasure hunt. Raskolnikov stops searching for Proofs, Netochka stays in Nasha Town, and the Shesternin matter is left partly unresolved. Some quests unlock extra map content: the Viewpoint "Iron Whale's Dream" and Raskolnikov as a Local Legend.

The series gives backstory for the Treasure Hoarders, who today are scattered across Teyvat, and shows the bunker's link to Professor Rotwang's plans. Nothing else in the world changes.

Placement: Released as World Quests across 6.0 (Luna I, 2025-09-10) for the first three quests and 6.3 (Luna IV, 2026-01-14) for Return to Sender and The Raven's Legacy. They sit alongside the Song of the Welkin Moon Archon Quest chain but are not part of it; players typically complete them whenever they reach Nod-Krai.

292.content:
Echoes of a Forsaken Song (also: Forsaken Song quest, Amsvartnir lyre quest, Palaces of Times Bygone): Echoes of a Forsaken Song is a world quest at Amsvartnir, a lake in Wavechaser Plain, Nod-Krai, added in Version 6.3. After the Lunar Conflux Barrier at the lakeshore is melted, a lyre appears; when the Traveler plays it, only the player character hears music and a sorrowful song in an unknown language that the Traveler somehow understands. Seelie lead the Traveler and Paimon up through floating islands to a hidden ruin, the Royal Court of the Seelie, where a mural completes the song and a reward chest holds a handwritten note about a woman who befriended a northern wolf named Boreas.

The quest pays 350 Adventure EXP, 40 Primogems, 30,000 Mora, 4 Hero's Wit and 4 Mystic Enhancement Ore, unlocks a Teleport Waypoint and the Palaces of Times Bygone viewpoint, and grants the achievement Farewell Hope, With Hope Farewell Fear. Only the Traveler and Paimon appear; every other voice is the song and the note.

Plot: Near the centre of Amsvartnir, Paimon spots many Seelie circling above the lake and assumes treasure. Once the barrier is melted, a lyre can be played. Paimon hears nothing when she strums it and wonders if it is broken, yet the Traveler hears a desolate tune and a gentle song, and understands every word despite never having heard the language. When Paimon plucks the strings herself, the Traveler hears it again while she hears only silence.

The Seelie guide the pair upward. The Traveler rides a Moonlane to a floating island, reconnects Lakeside Prisms to break its seals, and a new verse of the song is heard at each stage. In the quest's wording, the verses move from asking why one should mourn what is lost, to a usurper on a throne of cruelty, to a golden city and the fall of the world's grandest glory, to a long decline afflicting the singer's unfortunate brethren.

After the last island, the Royal Court of the Seelie appears with the Seelie from the lake gathered there. A second lyre sits around a corner and is as silent as the first. In the ruins, the Traveler reconnects a last prism and touches a mural. The final verses speak of autumn insects and a chorus of exiles, of melodies and memories lingering in a foreign land, of the last singers playing a soft final tune, and of the first Seelie wandering a hall of angels. The Seelie then enter the mural and the quest ends, revealing many chests. Paimon credits the Seelie for knowing where the best goodies hide.

The wiki's step list is: follow the Seelie upward (riding the Moonlane), break the seals on the floating island (counted 1/4 to 3/4 across two islands), investigate the nearby area, break the seal on the ruins, break the seal, and examine the mural.

Gameplay details: following the Seelie to the next island unlocks a Teleport Waypoint, and completion gives two Precious Chests and one Luxurious Chest. The wiki lists the lyre music as the soundtrack Forsaken Hymn, whose Ancient Greek lyrics (English wiki translation) speak of a song like an autumn cicada, grief and memory remaining alone in exile, and a last singer seated in her sacred place. Those themes match the quest's final verses.

Revelations: - The Royal Court of the Seelie is hidden from mortal sight, and a song only the Traveler hears is the way in.
- The Luxurious Chest drops a readable note titled Ancient Handwriting. Its writer says she has sat alone in a temple that passers-by cannot see, grieving the afflictions of the land with only tiny spirits for company.

The note tells how brambles sprouted and a wild beast came from the north bearing ice and snow. It spoke no human words, but gazed at her as at heavenly light and listened to her singing without anger, even when she called it a stupid dog. She named it Boreas, meaning North Wind, and let it and its kin share her dwelling. After many days it began to speak, called her Mother, and said it would go south to make poor people's cities prosperous. She let it go and called its name one last time; the note trails off with "I remember...".

The wiki treats the writer as Koitar, whose memories were wiped by the Heavenly Principles as punishment for her rebellion, and the beast as Boreas, who became the Wolf of the North in Mondstadt's Four Winds. Neither identification is spelled out in the quest text itself.

Supporting context from the wiki: Koitar's page describes her as a former Archangel of Celestia who ruled Hyperborea and regained her power and wisdom through a chance meeting with Boreas. The Royal Court page cites weapon text (Etherlight Spindlelute) describing a lake beyond ancient palace ruins, a sacred forest, and a court of the Seelie hidden from mortals by day. Amsvartnir is also described there as the lake of that court.

Characters: The Traveler and Paimon are the only characters present. The singer and the writer of the note are unnamed in the quest; Boreas (Andrius) is named in the note. Seelie act as guides throughout.

Consequences: The Royal Court of the Seelie becomes explorable and holds further Ancient Handwriting notes (the wiki's location page lists three). The quest unlocks a waypoint and the Palaces of Times Bygone viewpoint; nothing in Nod-Krai's main plot changes.

Placement: Released in Version 6.3 as a standalone world quest at Amsvartnir, with no prerequisite quest listed beyond melting the Lunar Conflux Barrier at the start location. It has no fixed place in the main story; the memory it describes belongs to the distant past; its exact date is not given.

293.content:
Echoing Tales (also: Conch Retrospection, Echoing Conches, Summertime Sparkle event): The event needed Adventure Rank 21. There were 32 Echoing Conches in total: 5 when the islands were still submerged, 23 more after the second act of Midsummer Island Adventure raised the islands, and the last 4 after the third act. Collecting set numbers of conches unlocked rewards including Primogems, Hero's Wit, Mystic Enhancement Ore, character talent guides and Barbara's outfit "Summertime Sparkle". The recordings can be replayed from an event menu called the Conch Retrospection.

After Version 1.6 the island could no longer be visited, and the outfit moved to the Character Outfit Shop at 1,680 Genesis Crystals. The area returned in Version 2.8 with a different look under the Summertime Odyssey event, with its own conch event, Resonating Visions.

Plot: The Conch Retrospection is split into seven sets. The first, "Songs of a Distant Home", follows a family handing down an heirloom and a nursery rhyme ("five mountains hide the little village, two paths through the lonely forest, one river flowing down the middle, four winds bring the sound of joy") across generations of exile, until rising tides force them to leave the heirloom in the island's centre. The second, "Strangers in a Strange Boat", is two groups of stranded pirates bickering over a lost ship and a samurai puppet, afraid of their chief's anger. The third, "Unlucky Father", has a man attacked by hilichurls and rescued by an unseen helper. The fourth, "My 'Hero'", is a child's voice speaking to a silent figure the adults call a general. The fifth, "Grand Line", covers pirates and islanders working out how the fog moves and when the wind changes so they can sail out. The sixth, "Familiar Voices", is a set of recordings from the Midsummer Island Adventure cast, and the seventh, "Island Bygones", gives daily island life, the tide warnings and the choice to leave.

In "Island Bygones", a newcomer tells the islanders that Mondstadt, Liyue and Inazuma exist, and the islanders, who have been trapped for generations, do not know Liyue. An elder reluctantly agrees to trust a young guide's route, and the sentries sound the alarm as the tide rises. The fifth set includes a recorded insight that the fog follows a pattern and "a mirage" is mistaken for rock. Together they show how people on the Haar Islands, as the archipelago was once called, lived and left.

Set VI's items: Albedo says the island is part of a Mondstadt mountain thrown into the sea and landing upside down, probably by Barbatos; Kaeya asks Diluc whether it is time for hunting seabirds or collecting seashells, recalling a childhood outing; Klee and Barbara plan to catch fish quietly, with Barbara recalling her sister Jean as a fun, tortoise-keeping child; and Razor, hungry, mutters about fish and water. These conches only become collectable after the Midsummer Island Adventure quest "Dodo-King of the Sea: Lying in Wait"; before that, they only murmur about the waves.

Revelations: Two facts come from the conches themselves: the archipelago was formed from mountain tops split off and landing inverted (Albedo's remark in set VI, attributed to Barbatos), and its former inhabitants were cut off for generations by fog and tide. The wiki ties the pirates in set II to Ako Domeki's fleet, shipwrecked after a thunder event, and the samurai puppet to the figure the child calls "General", but the conches do not state this.

Characters: Only set VI uses named characters: Albedo, Kaeya, Diluc, Klee, Barbara and Razor, each in a short exchange. Sets I to V and VII use unnamed voices: a grandmother and child, a pirate crew, a father, a child talking to a "General", pirate and islander sailors, and islander elders and sentries.

Consequences: The event adds no plot beyond the voices; its lasting results are the outfit and the background to the Haar Islands later cited by the wiki. It unlocks nothing for later quests.

Placement: Released in Version 1.6 alongside Midsummer Island Adventure. Its recordings are read as background to that event's story, and the 2.8 Summertime Odyssey has a counterpart event, Resonating Visions.

294.content: In Echoing Tales an Echoing Conch is a collectable shell on the Golden Apple Archipelago that stores a spoken fragment of the past. The wiki lists 32 conches in seven sets. Before a conch is unlocked it only murmurs about distant waves. The later underwater Echoing Conch in Fontaine is a different mechanic.

key: five mountains hide the little village
295.comment: Echoing Tales: Nursery rhyme of the Haar Islands
295.content: Set I of the Conch Retrospection presents a nursery rhyme passed from grandmother to child across generations: five mountains hide the little village, two paths through the lonely forest, one river flowing down the middle, four winds bring the sound of joy. The set's final recording is titled "The Clan of Song, Scattered": the speaker orders everyone to higher ground and has to leave the heirloom in the centre of the island when the tide rises.

296.content: Summertime Sparkle is a 4-star outfit for Barbara, given at 24 conches in Echoing Tales and sold later in the Character Outfit Shop for 1,680 Genesis Crystals.

key: Song of the Welkin Moon Act II
297.content:
Elegy of Dust and Lamplight (also: Song of the Welkin Moon Act II, Luna I Act II): Act II of Song of the Welkin Moon, set in Nasha Town and around Nod-Krai. A phantom linked to the Wild Hunt is traced to Rerir, one of the Five Sinners of Khaenri'ah. He impersonates the Ratnik Sousi, who is found murdered with Flins blamed, and tries to use the Lightkeepers' kuuvahki cannon to regain strength. The Traveler, Flins and Ineffa blunt the shot, and Columbina pulls the group out of danger.

The act has five quests: Fulminations and Undercurrents, The Dark Side of Memory, One There Was, Who Hunted the Moon, The Ashen-White Order Burns and Rest Beyond Reach. It follows A Dance of Snowy Tides and Hoarfrost Groves and precedes A Nation That Doesn't Exist. It was released in version 6.0 (Luna I).

The act turns the Wild Hunt from a local menace into a named enemy. It also forces Columbina into the open, since the Moon Marrow the Traveler carries makes them a target, and it sets up the alliance against Rerir that is assembled in later acts.

Plot: The Traveler and Paimon help repair the cannon in Nasha Town and learn of a Wild Hunt phantom. Lauma and Columbina explain the Moon Marrow and identify Rerir. A false "Sousi" proves to be Rerir, the real Sousi is found dead and Flins is blamed. The group deduces that Rerir wants the cannon fired at himself, and it is fired at Starsand Shoal. Columbina teleports everyone out of danger. The act ends with Varka, who has been following Rerir, introducing himself to him.

The Traveler helps Aino's cannon repairs, meets Nefer, Lauma and Columbina, and learns the Wild Hunt's source is Rerir. Sousi is found murdered, a witness blames Flins, and the "Sousi" who helped with the repairs proves to have been Rerir; Rerir then manipulates the Lightkeepers' cannon at Starsand Shoal. Columbina rescues the group; the act ends with Varka, who has been trailing Rerir, introducing himself to him.

Fulminations and Undercurrents: in Nasha Town residents speak of a recent Wild Hunt incursion. The Lightkeepers ask the inventor Aino to repair the Boom and Blast Kuuvahki Cannon, and she agrees as long as she gets her sweets. With Ineffa and a Ratnik called Sousi, the Traveler and Paimon gather what is needed to fix it. Back at the Flagship tavern a private Banquet is under way. Entry needs the proper "channel", so the Traveler goes to the Curatorium of Secrets, where Nefer agrees to arrange an invitation in exchange for carrying medicine to Lauma. Jahoda, who mistakes salt for the medicine, fetches the right package. At the Banquet Nefer presents the Traveler as a Mondstadt mixologist. The Traveler questions Dobrawa about her encounter with the Wild Hunt, and the informant Korhonen tells Nefer that spots had been cleared before the Lightkeepers arrived, but he has never heard of the phantom. Nefer and the Traveler conclude the phantom is a recent sighting and a mastermind may stand behind it.

The Dark Side of Memory: the Traveler takes medicine to Lauma on Hiisi Island. Lauma uses the Moon Marrow to draw out one of the Traveler's memories, which shows only their spaceship crashing into Nod-Krai. A Luonnotar signals that Columbina wishes to speak, so the Traveler goes to Silvermoon Hall, where Columbina looks weakened. She says the Moon Marrow is a piece of Aria's remains, that her own power comes from the Frost Moon and that she does not want the marrow, because two moons cannot rise together. She recalls a man obsessed with the moons known only by the title Rächer of Solnari, and Paimon and the Traveler recognise one of the Five Sinners of Khaenri'ah, which Paimon takes to be Rerir. Columbina says Rerir was said to have fallen into the moon's reflection, a point of no return. She also helps the Traveler look again at their crashed ship, where they see their sibling outside it, and teaches a way to hide the marrow's presence.

One There Was, Who Hunted the Moon: Lauma decides to keep the enemy's identity from her people to avoid panic. Aino prepares concentrated kuuvahki for the cannon and reports that Sousi has been found murdered. The Lightkeeper Sieciech explains that a witness saw Flins kill him. The Traveler finds Flins just in time to save him from Rerir. Flins explains where his lantern came from and why he kept the abyssal fragment. Back at the scene the group notices Sousi's mechanical arm flashing a maintenance error code. They realise the Sousi who had helped repair the cannon was Rerir. Hintsa, the town mechanic, confirms the real Sousi never turned up for the work, so Rerir seems able to copy only external appearance. That night Flins tells the Traveler privately that he is a fae who turned his heart toward humanity, suffered loss and wished to die until the Lightkeepers' fearless fighting drew him in, and asks that it stay secret.

The Ashen-White Order Burns: a mob demands Flins, and Nefer drives them off. Rumours that the Wild Hunt can wear faces make townspeople accuse each other. At the Curatorium the group splits to handle incursions. With Flins the Traveler searches the Ratniks' library and, helped by spirits, learns that kuuvahki and abyssal energy are opposites in which the winner absorbs the loser. They infer Rerir wants the cannon fired at him. A Lauma ibis warns that the cannon is operating on its own aimed at Starsand Shoal. At the shoal Rerir reveals that he is the origin of the Wild Hunt, that he has been gathering fragments of his former body and that his heart is in Flins' lantern. In town Lauma calms barricading citizens while Aino and Ineffa work to interfere with the barrel. The shot is partly deflected by Flins, the Traveler's Moon Marrow shield and Ineffa, though part of the beam is corrupted and the Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau is damaged. A mysterious dome shields Hiisi Island. Rerir restores a part of his body but is enraged to find it incomplete. Sandrone and her robot Pulonia arrive, Pulonia is overcome, and Columbina teleports the group to Silvermoon Hall. Sandrone leaves rather than fight her former colleague, and Columbina privately realises her strength is not returning.

Rest Beyond Reach: the group cannot name Rerir's motive but rules out revenge. The Traveler finds Columbina walking on the rooftops of Nasha Town. She says she wishes to return to the moon, where she would find answers and "home". Elsewhere Rerir notices he is being followed and Varka introduces himself.

Details worth keeping apart: the Traveler's Moon Marrow shield and Columbina's concealment technique are two separate uses of the marrow. Rerir's lines at Starsand Shoal include that humans did not understand the powers they wielded. Columbina says her recent calculations had been significantly off, and Sandrone reminds her of the Fatui warrant against her.

The act depends on rumour as much as combat: the false murder charge, the mob at the Flagship and the spreading fear that anyone may be a Wild Hunt mimic all weaken Nasha Town before the cannon is fired. Information is gathered through social channels (the Banquet, the informant Korhonen, the Ratniks' library spirits) rather than only by fighting.

Revelations: The Wild Hunt's mastermind is Rerir, a Sinner of Khaenri'ah, and he is the origin of the Wild Hunt. The Moon Marrow is described by Columbina as a piece of Aria's remains.

Columbina says a moon marrow forms only when a moon is destroyed and its Moon Goddess dies, and that she has no marrow of her own. Rerir can copy only the outward appearance of people, and kuuvahki and abyssal energy are shown to be opposites. Flins is revealed to be a fae.

Columbina says Rerir's present Wild Hunt is far deadlier than past versions and suspects something is holding him back. The Traveler's memory shows their sibling outside the crashed ship, which the Traveler believes should have been impossible because they recall the sibling never leaving it.

Characters: The Traveler, Paimon, Lauma, Columbina, Flins, Nefer, Aino and Rerir are the main figures.

Others: Ineffa, Jahoda, Sandrone and Pulonia, Varka, the murdered Ratnik Sousi, and minor townspeople such as Valta, Dobrawa, Korhonen, Hintsa, Sieciech and Zvoni.

Consequences: Rerir regains part of his body and remains at large. Flins is cleared in the Traveler's eyes, though the town was briefly gripped by suspicion. Columbina is exposed and weakened, and Varka approaches Rerir and introduces himself. The next acts gather allies against him.

Placement: Song of the Welkin Moon Act II, after A Dance of Snowy Tides and Hoarfrost Groves and before A Nation That Doesn't Exist. Listed with Act I under version Luna I (6.0, released 2025-09-10).

298.comment: Elegy of Dust and Lamplight: Rerir impersonating Sousi
298.content: The Sousi who helped the Traveler repair the cannon was Rerir. The real Sousi had been killed in his office, and his mechanical arm flashed a maintenance error code that exposed the lie. A witness had seen "Flins" commit the murder, and the Lightkeepers initially suspected him. The group concluded Rerir copies only appearance.

299.comment: Elegy of Dust and Lamplight: Starsand Shoal cannon firing
299.content: Aino's cannon fires toward Starsand Shoal where Rerir stands, partly because he planned that kuuvahki would be converted by his abyssal energy. Flins, the Traveler's Moon Marrow shield and Ineffa limit the damage. Part of the beam is corrupted and Rerir restores some of his body.

300.comment: Elegy of Dust and Lamplight: Flins the fae
300.content: Flins tells the Traveler he is a fae who turned toward humanity, lost people and once wished to end his life, until the Lightkeepers' fearless fighting led him to join them. He kept an abyssal fragment in his lantern so others could not misuse it, and Rerir later says his heart is in it.

key: Enchanted Tales of the Mikawa Festival
As Though Caught in a Dream
301.comment: Enchanted Tales of the Mikawa Festival
301.content:
Enchanted Tales of the Mikawa Festival (also: Mikawa Festival event, As Though Caught in a Dream, As Though Beholding Illusions, As Though Surrounded by Thunder, As Though Kissed by Dew, Tanuki Game Award, The Doppelganger Incident): The festival is a revived youkai celebration. Teams pairing humans with bake-danuki build games: Thoma and his youkai helpers make Akitsu Harpastum, Sayu and Yoimiya make Bunshin Phantasm, and Kokomi, Mizuki and Gyoubu Koban make A Little Fox's Daydream. As contestants work, strange doppelganger rumours spread and people are found trapped in nightmares. The Tenryou Commission investigates quietly, Ei attends the festival in person at Miko's suggestion, and the cause turns out to be three frightened bake-danuki carrying a nightmare fragment from a horn buried five hundred years ago. A joint plan by the Traveler, Ei, Miko and Mizuki lures the fragment out and puts it to rest during the festival.

Requirements were Adventure Rank 30 and the Archon Quest "Ritou Escape Plan". The recommended story quests were Imperatrix Umbrosa Act II (Raiden Shogun), Tapirus Somniator Act I (Yumemizuki Mizuki), Dracaena Somnolenta Act I (Kokomi) and Carassius Auratus Act II (Yoimiya), plus Sayu's hangout and the World Quest Sacred Sakura Cleansing Ritual. The reward weapon was Tamayuratei no Ohanashi.

Plot: First Night. A letter from Miko brings the Traveler and Paimon to Tenshukaku, where Miko and the Shogun are arguing over a contract: a new Mikawa Flower Festival, an old youkai event of drink and games, now combining human invention with youkai arts and open to both peoples. The Traveler is chosen as neutral representative, having a deep connection to youkai and not being from Inazuma, and haggles the share of proceeds up to twenty percent. Fifty percent goes to the Shogunate. The plan is for attendees to build games in 48 hours. Miko wins over Ioroi, the Kakushigami of the bake-danuki, who is sealed in a statue in Chinju Forest, by playing on his pride, and three young bake-danuki, Kichiboushi, Shousei and Gyoubu Koban, join the Traveler. Miko feeds them a Kitsune Meal so they can speak with humans. Teams form: Thoma, whom Itto introduces to Hitotsume Kozou, Youko and Kappa, with Shousei; Sayu and Yoimiya with Kichiboushi; and Kokomi and Mizuki with Gyoubu Koban, who are discussing a new Aisa Bathhouse branch on Watatsumi Island and mean to use the contest as publicity. Kokomi sends Gorou back to Watatsumi Island to encourage islanders to attend. Ayaka volunteers to organise and Ayato oversees, while Miko adds a surprise: the theme will be "dreams" and the winner will receive the Tanuki Game Award, Mora and a sponsorship from Yae Publishing House. The Traveler is named chief judge. After play-testing and a night of food, the Traveler is attacked by a figure in Abyssal kairagi-like clothing and, after recognising a dream, hears thunder and wakes. Ei, on a cliff, wonders whether a Nightmare has returned to Inazuma. Elsewhere, Asari is left puzzled when Komura, who had been standing silent, appears beside him as though from nowhere.

Second Night. Rumours of doppelgangers spread. The Tenryou Commission has found a team of surveyors unconscious in a nightmare and traces of youkai power around Mt. Yougou. Sara and Heizou keep the investigation secret by order of the Shogun. Ei, whom the Traveler recognises at a glance, asks the Traveler to question the contestants without causing suspicion. Everyone passes: the Traveler tests Sayu and Yoimiya with shared memories and Thoma with an interview, while Kokomi vouches for Gyoubu Koban and says Mizuki left at night after a message, which turns out to be Miko's request for help. Miko then announces the Shogun's attendance; Sara and Heizou explain this will crack the culprit's composure. In the evening Mizuki gives the Traveler two Aisa Bathhouse coupons and shares her concern that Ei is hiding strain. The Traveler persuades Ei to come after midnight. In the bath Ei explains the old Nightmare: creatures that possess people and trap them in dreams. A strong enough victim does not fall asleep but wakes into a nightmare in which every precious thing seems an enemy. A person once trapped like this had to be struck down by Ei with Musou no Hitotachi, and she has no regrets. Miko and Mizuki, who arranged the bath to get her to talk, overhear. A woman named Rie reports seeing her own double in Inazuma City, then Haruto reports Kappa trapped in a nightmare. Heizou's reasoning, with the Traveler's help, shows that the doppelgangers and the nightmare are separate, that the aim is panic, and that "Kappa" is made of wood. The "Youko" and "Hitotsume Kozou" on site grow bake-danuki tails when frightened and flee with Tetsunosuke. In Chinju Forest they hide by transforming into bonfires and statues. The Traveler breaks each disguise with a leaf, Sara blocks their path, and the three bake-danuki, trapped in a nightmare, believe the Shogun sent humans to steal their land. The Traveler uses the power to purify the Abyss and sees their memory: a survey team (Kaga, Kiritani and Mizukawa) is at first ordinary, but the nightmare turns its words into threats, and then the real Hitotsume Kozou, Youko and Kappa fall unconscious. Ioroi, brought before the Shogun, recognises the three as Kinkaku, Ginkaku and Tetsunosuke who hid from a human named Kamuna Harunosuke after finding a horn full of youkai power. Mizuki suspects the horn holds a fragment of a nightmare. Ei says it is Mikoshi Chiyo's: a trusted lieutenant who raised her sword against the Shogun on Mt. Yougou while trapped in her own nightmare and was struck down, losing an arm and a horn. Miko proposes that the bake-danuki create a dreamscape that the fragment cannot tell from the real world, and Mizuki will craft a ritual. The Traveler and Ei will hold the fragment off until it takes effect.

Final Night. Ayato distributes ritual booklets, Sara adjusts security, and the contestants finish their games with help from friends: Itto and the Arataki Gang aid Thoma, Ayaka helps Sayu and Yoimiya, and Gorou and Swordfish II help Kokomi and Mizuki. Ei and the Traveler meditate. Ei says she will not use Musou no Hitotachi this time, and the Traveler promises she will not face it alone. At sunset the nightmare fragments appear on the Chinju Forest path and Ei draws them and the Traveler into the Plane of Euthymia. While they fight, voices of everyone outside chant "God of Thunder, heed our call", and the fragments weaken. A cutscene shows Chiyo's own memory: soldiers rouse her after fearing she was eaten by a beast, a nightmare makes the soldiers and two figures who call her 'Mother' (one named Mikoshi Nagamasa) look like monsters, and the Yumekui-Baku say it is beyond their skill. Ei cuts through the dream and takes her hand, and Chiyo wakes at a picnic with Makoto, Ei, Sasayuri and the Kitsune Saiguu, where Ei tells her that only sweet dreams await. In the present, Ei sits alone while Chiyo's horn fades. Night falls and the festival opens. The Traveler announces the best game (player's choice among the three) and Ei announces a special award for "most immersive game" to Kinkaku, Ginkaku and Tetsunosuke for their horror game, The Doppelganger Incident, and promises that no human will intrude on their peace without cause.

After-Night. Ei's thoughts: there were misunderstandings and hostilities, yet it ended as a celebration. Miko took Kinkaku and the others to Mizuki for a check-up. Kappa, Hitotsume Kozou and Youko recover and remember only a long dream. Itto drags friends to the Aisa Bathhouse again. In a game the Traveler beats Ayato, who the Traveler suspects lost on purpose so Ayaka could play. Outside, Aikawa Susumu says visitors tripled and the bathhouse has its best-ever result, second to Yae Publishing House, but Miko announces thirty percent of proceeds have gone to her house. Ei, watching from Tenshukaku, wishes everyone sweet dreams. Afterwards Kazuha, Kirara and Chiori can be found in the open world.

Details. Thoma explains that Akitsu Harpastum aims at everyone from children to the elderly, and that he is on holiday but helping the Yashiro Commission. Sara owns five Statues of the Almighty Narukami Ogosho and keeps that as a maximum so she can care for them properly. Kokomi privately calls Miko "Miss Fried Tofu With All the Frills". Mizuki and Miko are old acquaintances: Miko recalls racing Mizuki for the first piece of Fried Tofu at festivals when Miko was a kit and Mizuki a young baku, and Aisa Bathhouse's sales rivalry with Yae Publishing House (Aikawa Susumu calls it their 333rd sales contest) ends with the bathhouse in second place. The Aranara come up when Yoimiya says she considered putting them in her game.

Revelations: The Nightmare of five hundred years ago, according to Ei, trapped soldiers in dreams that even the Yumekui-Baku could not heal. Someone strong enough to resist became unable to tell dream from war and saw every cherished thing as an enemy. This was Mikoshi Chiyo, a lieutenant, called Torachiyo ("Chiyo the Tiger-Bite") by legend after she once tore apart a beast from beyond this world from within it. Tainted by darkness, she attacked the Shogun on Mt. Yougou and was struck down with Musou no Hitotachi, losing an arm, one horn and part of the mountain. The horn buried there carries a fragment of her nightmare. The three bake-danuki unearthed it while hiding from a human, used its power to hide, and have lived in its nightmare ever since, believing humans had come to destroy them.

The Shogunate's survey team was only checking for youkai on the land so it could avoid or negotiate with them, as the Shogun says. Paimon recalls that Ioroi was sealed after he stole a comb that turned out to be used for Sacred Sakura Daifuku, and Ioroi admits he lost a fight to the young human involved. Ei says the Shogun's body could keep working another hundred years, yet she does not deny that she carries a burden, and Mizuki, a clinical psychologist as well as a Yumekui-Baku, tells the Traveler that humans, youkai and archons share the same emotional strain.

Characters: The Traveler is festival representative and chief judge. Miko plots the event and plays the sly organiser, Ei joins as the Shogun and as herself, and Mizuki, who is both a baku and a clinical psychologist, handles nightmares. Teams: Thoma with Shousei and the youkai Hitotsume Kozou, Youko and Kappa, later helped by Itto, Shinobu and the Arataki Gang; Sayu and Yoimiya with Kichiboushi and later Ayaka; Kokomi, Mizuki and Gyoubu Koban, helped by Gorou and Swordfish II. Ayato and Ayaka organise. Sara and Heizou investigate. The bake-danuki Kinkaku, Ginkaku and Tetsunosuke are the culprits. Ioroi advises. Mikoshi Chiyo, Makoto, Sasayuri and the Kitsune Saiguu appear only in the cutscene.

Open-world cast after the quest: Kazuha enjoying the cherry blossoms on Mt. Yougou, Kirara on festival delivery for Komaniya Express, Chiori who came from Fontaine at Ayaka's invitation. Other NPCs: Senga, Wakana, Takitoh, Rie, Haruto, Inoue (stand-in vendor), Asari, Komura, Aikawa Susumu.

Consequences: The fragment is put to rest and Chiyo's horn fades in Ei's lap. The festival goes on. The bake-danuki learn that humans meant them no harm and receive the special award and Ei's promise. Kokomi and Mizuki's bathhouse collaboration remains a plan. Yae Publishing House profits from the proceeds. The Traveler's purification of the nightmare, which the Traveler calls a way of dealing with the Abyss, is what first wakes the bake-danuki.

Ioroi, still sealed in the statue, says the seal is almost spent and he can leave when he likes. Miko offers to release him.

Placement: Released in Version 5.4 as a Flagship Event, set in Inazuma after the Archon Quest "Ritou Escape Plan" and as a sequel in tone to the Version 3.3 Test of Courage (Akitsu Kimodameshi), where Miko's first Mikawa Flower Festival was held on a small scale. Characters refer back to that event, to the Sacred Sakura cleansing and to Sayu's hangout. Ei places the Nightmare in the aftermath of the dark disaster five hundred years ago.

Gameplay: Game mechanics, not in-world fact. Three modes unlock in sequence: Akitsu Harpastum: Dreams Doubled (return harpasta fired by Harpastum youkai), A Little Fox's Daydream (collect Fried Tofu by switching dreamscapes and altering terrain) and Bunshin Phantasm (use two doppelgangers to solve puzzles). Completing them gives Festival Stamps (15 in all) toward Tamayuratei no Ohanashi (Polearm), Primogems and a Crown of Insight. In the First Night fight the Traveler uses Parry and Veilbreak instead of skills and bursts. The Final Night fight is a boss battle with the Raiden Shogun as an ally, with "prayers" from the crowd weakening the fragments.

302.comment: Enchanted Tales of the Mikawa Festival: Mikoshi Chiyo
302.content: A trusted lieutenant of the Shogun five hundred years ago, said to have been swallowed by a tiger-bodied, serpent-tailed beast from beyond this world and to have torn it apart from inside. A nightmare made her see her subordinates, family and friends as enemies. She attacked the Shogun and was struck down, losing an arm and a horn. Ei says she would not like the nickname. A fragment of her nightmare lingers in the buried horn. She appears only in the cutscene memory near the end, where two figures call her 'Mother', one named Mikoshi Nagamasa.

303.comment: Enchanted Tales of the Mikawa Festival: Nightmare Fragment
303.content: Whatever remained of the old Nightmare in Mikoshi Chiyo's severed horn, which hates joy and every good thing. It travels through the ley lines, so it appears intermittently and never beyond Mt. Yougou, and Mizuki compares it to a jibakurei. It attacks the survey team, Hitotsume Kozou and his friends, and the Traveler. The Traveler breaks out of its dream when thunder sounds.

304.comment: Enchanted Tales of the Mikawa Festival: Kinkaku, Ginkaku and Tetsunosuke
304.content: Three bake-danuki who hid from a human, Kamuna Harunosuke, for five hundred years using the power of a horn they found, which kept them in nightmare. Under its influence they took the place of Hitotsume Kozou, Youko and Kappa at the festival, then fled into Chinju Forest when found out. After the Traveler purifies them, they realise the humans meant no harm, receive a special award and Ei's promise, and are looked after by Miko and Mizuki.

305.comment: Enchanted Tales of the Mikawa Festival: Ioroi
305.content: The Hidden Protector of the Grove, sealed in a statue in Chinju Forest as punishment for stealing a comb. He nags Miko, fears the Shogun (she nearly cut him in two when he tried to take a Naku Weed from the imperial garden), and warns the cubs against using external power. He calls the five hundred years of hiding a long game of hide-and-seek.

306.comment: Enchanted Tales of the Mikawa Festival: Kichiboushi, Shousei and Gyoubu Koban
306.content: Three young bake-danuki recruited by Miko, who uses a Kitsune Meal to let them speak. They call Paimon White Fur, the Traveler Yellow Fur, Miko Pink Fur and Yoimiya Orange Fur. Each joins a team and uses transformation to build sets. Kichiboushi works with Sayu and Yoimiya, Shousei with Thoma, Gyoubu Koban with Kokomi and Mizuki.

307.comment: Enchanted Tales of the Mikawa Festival: Tanuki Game Award
307.content: The prize for the winning team, with Mora and a sponsorship from Yae Publishing House to develop and promote the game across Inazuma. Ayaka organised its production at short notice. It sits at the winning booth afterwards.

308.comment: Enchanted Tales of the Mikawa Festival: Akitsu Harpastum
308.content: Thoma's game, a spiritual sequel to Akitsu Yuugei that combines it with Mondstadt's Ludi Harpastum: swing a racket to return balls. Thoma says that after leaving Mondstadt he could play Ludi Harpastum only in dreams, which is how he fits the theme.

309.comment: Enchanted Tales of the Mikawa Festival: Bunshin Phantasm
309.content: Sayu and Yoimiya's game, from Sayu's dream of making clones to do her work. Players place a hand on a board to enter a dreamscape, where body doubles help solve problems.

310.comment: Enchanted Tales of the Mikawa Festival: A Little Fox's Daydream
310.content: Mizuki, Kokomi and Gyoubu Koban's game: a fox travels between sweet dreams and nightmares in search of fried tofu, with a ramen stand at the end. Miko notices the fox resembles her.

311.comment: Enchanted Tales of the Mikawa Festival: The Doppelganger Incident
311.content: The scare in which people reported seeing their own doubles around Mt. Yougou and Inazuma City. An old Inazuma folk tale says people who meet their double are replaced by it within three days. Heizou deduces the doubles were separate from the nightmare and meant to cause panic. The culprits were the three bake-danuki. At the end the event honours the trio's "horror game" with a special award.

key: Towers of the Three Realms trials
312.content:
Erebos' Secret (also: Erebos Secret, The Three Great Martial Trials, Towers of the Three Realms trials): A version 2.4 world quest series in Enkanomiya. After the Traveler returns the Bloodbranch Coral to Tsuyuko, a shade named Eboshi, an auxiliary of Sangonomiya and one of the shrine maidens of Enkanomiya, offers a set of trials that lead to more of the island's secrets.

The series is a single quest, The Three Great Martial Trials, with three sub-quests: Yachimatahiko's Trial, Yachimatahime's Trial and Kunado's Trial. Each is held at a hidden tower that rises out of the fog. Once all three are passed, Eboshi tells the Traveler about the Bathysmal Vishaps, the Watatsumi Omikami, the time before the sun and moon, and the Dainichi Mikoshi.

In-universe, the trials tie into the Towers of the Three Realms, which the people of Byakuyakoku built to keep a border land stable. Eboshi is also called Erebos in Enkanomiya.

Plot: Eboshi, a translucent shade, meets the Traveler near the Serpent's Heart and proposes a trial path. Agreeing makes three new areas surface from the fog. At each the Traveler is tested, then returns to Eboshi for her explanations.

The Traveler is told to use the Emanant Skylights to reach each trial area, where a Jibashiri waits. The Traveler is recognised by the Jibashiri at all three places, then returns to Eboshi, who confers knowledge about the vishaps, the Watatsumi Omikami, the age before the sun and moon, and the Dainichi Mikoshi.

Starting the quest reveals three new subareas on the Enkanomiya map: Yachimatahiko's Locus, Yachimatahime's Locus and Kunado's Locus. Eboshi can be found east of the northwest-most waypoint of the Serpent's Heart and during Evernight.

Revelations: The Byakuyakoku Collection (as cited by the wiki) records that the people of Enkanomiya built the Towers of the Three Realms at the borders of Byakuyakoku, a land between the Human, Elemental (vishap) and Abyssal (Void) realms, to stabilise its tendencies and keep the realms in harmony. Because they are so important they are hidden with secret arts and can be summoned only by shrine maidens such as Eboshi and by the Vassals of Watatsumi.

The towers' ancient names have been forgotten; the three Loci carry later names.

Characters: The Traveler and Paimon; Eboshi.

Eboshi is a shade of Tokoyo, translucent like others of her kind, and the wiki lists Tsuyuko as her descendant. Three Jibashiri are met at the trials.

Consequences: The three Loci become accessible and Eboshi stays in Enkanomiya. The Traveler gains background on the vishaps, the Watatsumi Omikami and the Dainichi Mikoshi that sets up more of the island's story, including Hyperion's Dirge.

Placement: Released in Version 2.4 as an Enkanomiya world quest series. It requires From Dusk to Dawn in Byakuyakoku (handing the Bloodbranch Coral to Tsuyuko). Hyperion's Dirge has the same requirement, so the two can be done in either order.

The wiki notes her Enkanomiya name Erebos echoes the Greek Erebus, a personification of darkness, and her Narukami-style name Eboshi is the name of a traditional Japanese cap; these are etymological observations from the wiki, not in-game statements. Starting the series requires only the earlier Enkanomiya quest, and the rewards are of ordinary world-quest size.

313.content: Eboshi, also called Erebos in Enkanomiya, is a shade of Tokoyo living in Enkanomiya: a translucent humanoid without defining features. She describes herself as an auxiliary of Sangonomiya and one of the shrine maidens of Enkanomiya, and she offers the Traveler the three trials of Erebos' Secret.

314.content:
Everwinter Without Mercy (also: Chapter VII Act I, Snezhnaya Archon Quest Act I): Chapter VII Act I of the Archon Quest and the opening of the Snezhnaya story. The Traveler and Paimon cross into the frozen north, the supposed last stop on the road set by the Traveler's sibling. Paimon falls ill; the pair find a town short of fuel because of Project Stuzha, help an honest hunter expose a hoarding scheme, meet Harbingers Sandrone and Tartaglia, and are recruited into the secret group Rokot.

The act has four quests: Into the Wind, Into the Frigid North; Gunfire in the Silent Lands; Great Deeds on the Tundra; and Silence Alone is Disfavored. It moves from the wilds near the border to Sretomorozsk, then to Snezhnograd, its Veche and the Korolevskiy Theater. It introduces the Eye of Graeae, the Shadow Realm and the Exaiphanes Blade, and sets the nation's central problem: a state-wide cut in energy use called Project Stuzha. Released in version 7.0.

The act is a deliberate slow start. Rather than meeting the Tsaritsa, the Traveler learns the country from the bottom up: what the energy ration means for a town, how the Fatui and the Veche argue over it, and who works against both from the shadows. The Tsaritsa herself has gone east with her Druzhna to slay the monster behind the snowstorms, so while Paimon's illness keeps her resting, the Traveler sets out to understand the plan through the Harbingers, the Veche and the underground. The next act is Wraith's Nocturne.

Plot: The Traveler and Paimon leave for Snezhnaya after a farewell party hosted by Columbina. A gust separates them; the Traveler meets the Eye of Graeae, an ancient device, and finds Paimon asleep in a cabin where a stranger with star-shaped pupils tells them to look after her. In the town of Sretomorozsk the hunter Alyosha explains Project Stuzha and helps unmask a Kresnik Kristall thief. In Snezhnograd the Traveler meets Sandrone, Tartaglia and Odette, then is invited into the Rokot while investigating the project.

Across four quests the Traveler is separated from Paimon, meets the Eye of Graeae, and reaches Sretomorozsk, where Alyosha explains the Kresnik Kristall shortage caused by Project Stuzha and helps expose the officials hoarding fuel. The train journey onward is pulled into the Shadow Realm; later, in the Svetloledovka mine, the Traveler forms the Exaiphanes Blade. In Snezhnograd the Traveler meets Sandrone, Tartaglia and Odette, sees the Veche vote to continue Stuzha with 61 percent, learns from Mitya that the project needs a Stellar Linchpin energy source, and joins Rokot.

Into the Wind, Into the Frigid North: before leaving, the Traveler and Paimon are met by Columbina, who learned of their plans through Luonnotar and throws a farewell party on the Flagship; she also passes on a message from Sandrone, already in Snezhnograd, not to cause her trouble. Crossing into Snezhnaya, Paimon feels unwell but blames the cold. A powerful gust throws the Traveler off a bridge and separates them. In a wrecked train the Traveler meets the Eye of Graeae, which recognises them as a Descender and offers to find Paimon in return for a later favour. With its "Fab-Vision" they reach a cabin where Paimon sleeps beside a man the Traveler recognises as Khaenri'ahn by his star-shaped pupils; he gives no name, tells them to concentrate on Paimon's health and leaves. Paimon later says he was Pierro, Director of the Eleven Fatui Harbingers, and that he seemed to know her. Graeae suggests using the train; its knowledge of the current rails is out of date and it plunges off a cliff, but lands harmlessly within walking distance of a town.

Gunfire in the Silent Lands: in Sretomorozsk all businesses are shut and residents barely cope. Alyosha, a hunter, explains that the Tsaritsa's Project Stuzha reduces energy use so it can be redirected to crucial research, and Kresnik Kristall shortages leave many stoves cold. He takes them to a distribution where Shishkin calms an angry crowd. Alyosha lets Paimon rest in his home, and the Traveler offers the crashed but working train to reach a doctor in Snezhnograd. Suspecting Shishkin of skimming the town's Kristall, the Traveler, Alyosha and his dog Tugarin show that deliveries keep arriving carriages short of what the train carries, and find a hidden tunnel stocked with Kristall. Shishkin is exposed and, once more Kristall turns up in the mayor's house, the Fatui representative Polonsky has both arrested; he hints that Alyosha could suit Rokot, an organisation at odds with the Fatui. Alyosha delivers fuel to an elderly woman with dementia who, like him, has ties to the abandoned town of Alatyr, then works out who the Traveler is. He tells them the Tsaritsa and her Druzhna have gone east to kill the monster causing the snowstorms. As the train leaves, strange objects appear on it and everyone is pulled into the Shadow Realm, a place without wind, light or elemental energy. Graeae gives the Traveler a new outfit and weapons there, they escape just before the bubble sinks, and rest at Rankova Zorya while Graeae upgrades the train.

Great Deeds on the Tundra: in Snezhnograd Alyosha briefs the Traveler on local fae and sends them to Podvorye Restaurant, where Luneva examines Paimon and diagnoses a cold. Wanting to learn the Tsaritsa's plans without a direct approach to a Harbinger, the Traveler goes to Glupov to find Tartaglia but is stopped by Yuzhanin until Sandrone, interrupted at tea, takes over and arranges to meet at Torchlight Books. Zverev reports trouble at Svetloledovka; the Traveler accompanies Sandrone, rescues trapped miners and meets Odette, escapes a collapsing cavern, and draws on an unusual power to form the Exaiphanes Blade. Back in the city they meet Tartaglia, who is overworked by Veche duties, and discuss Project Stuzha's flaws; Odette is dismayed to learn the Traveler once duelled Signora and leaves. The Traveler uses the blade's Cryo power to empower the city's Statue of the Seven, then buys kristall in Zolnyy with Alyosha; Odette arrives and covers the costs through Fatui logistics. At the restaurant Sytin asks for identification, and the Traveler shows an Adventurers' Handbook. They ask Alyosha for Rokot leads and are told to meet him at the Korolevskiy Theater.

Silence Alone is Disfavored: at the theatre Kulish inspects them. A silent guard from the Armory Palace Special Assignments Battalion, Valeriy, stands nearby; Alyosha says he usually appears only when hunting a researcher named Mitya. They sit beside the irritable Chugunov and watch Vodyanitsa, the troupe's lead singer. Backstage she and Alyosha reveal themselves as Rokot members and say the Traveler has been approved by the president; members are anonymous, rarely meet and work as they see fit within the group's principles. The Traveler joins. Their target is Chugunov, boss of the Iskra Manufacturing Plant, suspected of illegal excess energy use. At Podvorye Restaurant Vodyanitsa questions Mitya, a respected energy expert, while the Traveler and Alyosha listen nearby. Mitya, whose scarf seems alive, admits he was distracted by Odette's dance, confirms the plant rumours, says Pulcinella now demands tracking of every Kristall batch, and reveals that the Armory Palace is seeking a new energy source drawn from Stellar Linchpins, burning vast amounts of Kristall; his scarf chokes him before he can say what it is for, and he leaves before Valeriy arrives. Paimon, still weak, feels a mysterious power seeming to come from the direction of the Armory Palace. At the Snezhnograd Veche, with Vodyanitsa and the reporter Mironova, Pulcinella presents energy figures and declares Project Stuzha will continue. Tartaglia argues that remote Fatui families receive fifteen percent less Kristall than Snezhnograd civilians, Pantalone replies that fairness is relative, and Sandrone steers the debate back to data. Stuzha passes with 61 percent, a narrower margin than before, and Chugunov surprisingly votes against. Vodyanitsa suspects coercion by "Lelek", the Rokot's most notorious member, who is obsessed with ending Stuzha and uses threats, coercion or bribery to change votes. Tartaglia and Sandrone share what the Fatui know (a highly skilled infiltrator who leaves threatening letters, with investigators split between human and fae explanations), and Sandrone floats the theory that Odette is Lelek, citing her father's death in the early stages of Project Stuzha and her mother's career ending with a broken leg. Tartaglia gives the Traveler his ticket to Odette's rehearsal of the ballet "Spirit Seeker" so they can talk to her while escorting his sister Tonia.

Sequence matters here. The party at the Flagship closes the Nod-Krai chapter of the Traveler's journey; Paimon's loss of her usual vitality opens the Snezhnaya chapter. The Kristall plot in Sretomorozsk is solved by evidence, not force, and ends with Polonsky showing awareness of Rokot. The Shadow Realm is the act's first combat-heavy set piece; the blade later used on the Statue of the Seven is formed separately, in the Svetloledovka mine. In Snezhnograd the story trades action for politics: Veche testimony, committee numbers, a reporter's slanted account, and the Fatui's honest uncertainty about their own intruder. Vodyanitsa explains that elites normally support Stuzha because ending it would make factories absorb the Tsaritsa's unchanged energy demand.

Names to keep straight: the town is Sretomorozsk, the mine town Svetloledovka, the fortress district Glupov, and the trading area Zolnyy. Paimon's diagnosis from Luneva is only a cold at this point; her later account of a mysterious power is the in-story hint that something else is wrong. The Traveler is repeatedly treated as an outsider until they show a Handbook or are vouched for by a Harbinger, which is how most access is gained. The Harbingers' attitudes to the Veche differ: Tartaglia, newly made a councillor through Capitano, is worn out by the work, while Sandrone dislikes its politics but takes part to speak for the subordinates under her command. Pulcinella chairs it.

Revelations: Snezhnaya is rationing energy under Project Stuzha, ordered by the Tsaritsa to free power for research. Pierro is in Snezhnaya and acts as though he knows Paimon. A covert network, Rokot, gives the disaffected false identities and an outlet, and is at odds with the Fatui.

The Eye of Graeae treats the Traveler as a Descender and promises help in return for a favour. Project Stuzha's research needs a new energy source from Stellar Linchpins and consumes huge amounts of Kresnik Kristall with little progress. Mitya is hunted by the Armory Palace's Special Assignments Battalion and is silenced when he starts to explain the purpose. The Veche vote on continuing Stuzha is narrowing (61 percent).

Rokot's rules: anonymous members, rare contact, freedom of method within shared principles, and an optional code of conduct. Alyosha and Vodyanitsa both belong, and Polonsky already suspects Alyosha. Fatui in remote areas receive less Kristall than Snezhnograd civilians, according to Tartaglia. Within this act, Sandrone's theory that Odette is "Lelek" is only speculation; later Chapter VII content confirms Odette operates in the Rokot as Lelek.

Characters: The Traveler and Paimon; the hunter Alyosha and his dog Tugarin; the Eye of Graeae; and Snezhnograd's Harbingers and Fatui: Sandrone, Tartaglia, Odette, Pierro.

Others include Columbina (farewell), Shishkin and Polonsky (Sretomorozsk), Luneva (doctor), Yuzhanin and Zverev (Glupov), Sytin (restaurant), Kulish and Valeriy (theatre security), Vodyanitsa and Chugunov, Mitya, Pulcinella and Pantalone (Veche), the reporter Mironova, and Tonia.

Consequences: The Traveler is a member of Rokot, has a working train and a Cryo blade, and plans to learn the real purpose of Project Stuzha from Odette. Paimon remains too weak to travel.

Shishkin and the mayor are sent to Snezhnograd for judgement. Chugunov's plant faces an investigation expected to take a week. The Traveler makes a first connection with Mitya through Vodyanitsa. The Statue of the Seven in Snezhnograd is awakened. The story continues in Wraith's Nocturne.

Placement: First act of Chapter VII, after the Nod-Krai content and the Song of the Welkin Moon story. Released in version 7.0.

The Archon Quest requires Adventure Rank 18 and completion of Prologue Act III. The wiki recommends Truth Amongst the Pages of Purana and the event quest Sunny Summer Fontinalia first. The Snezhnaya chapter was originally designated Act VI in the Teyvat chapter storyline preview, and became numbered Chapter VII after the Song of the Welkin Moon was added. Acts I and II arrived together in 7.0, and Acts III and IV in 7.1.

315.comment: Everwinter Without Mercy: Eye of Graeae
315.content: An ancient device the Traveler finds in a wrecked train near the Snezhnaya border. It recognises the Traveler as a Descender and agrees to help find Paimon in return for later help. It guides the Traveler with "Fab-Vision", gives them a new outfit and weapons in the Shadow Realm, and upgrades their train. Its picture of present-day Snezhnaya is out of date, which is why its first route ends off a cliff.

316.comment: Everwinter Without Mercy: Project Stuzha in Sretomorozsk
316.content: A policy of the Tsaritsa to lower energy use across Snezhnaya and redirect it to crucial research. In Act I it causes Kresnik Kristall shortages, closed shops and cold stoves in towns such as Sretomorozsk. The Veche votes on continuing it; at this point it passes with 61 percent. Elites normally back it because stopping would make factories absorb unchanged demand. The goal of the research is not stated.

317.content: A covert, anonymous organisation at odds with the Fatui that gives the disaffected false identities and an outlet for their frustrations. Alyosha and Vodyanitsa belong; the Traveler is accepted after Alyosha writes to the president on their behalf. Members rarely meet and may act as they wish within its principles. The Fatui's Polonsky knows of Rokot and says Alyosha is suited to it.

318.comment: Everwinter Without Mercy: Shadow Realm episode
318.content: Strange objects appear on the train leaving Sretomorozsk and its passengers are drawn into the Shadow Realm, a space without wind, light or elemental energy. They escape before the bubble sinks back. Later, in the Svetloledovka mine, the Traveler draws on an unusual power and forms the Exaiphanes Blade, which they use to empower the Statue of the Seven in Snezhnograd.

319.comment: Everwinter Without Mercy: Mitya at Podvorye
319.content: A respected energy expert and regular theatregoer who is hunted by Armory Palace guard Valeriy. His scarf seems alive and chokes him when he is about to explain what the new Linchpin-based energy source is for. He confirms excess energy use at the Iskra plant and Pulcinella's demand for strict tracking of Kristall batches.

320.content:
Fabulae Textile Chapter (Xingqiu) (also: Fabulae Textile Chapter, Xingqiu's Story Quest, Bookworm Swordsman): The Fabulae Textile Chapter is Xingqiu's Story Quest (Version 1.0), set in Liyue. In its one act, Bookworm Swordsman, the Traveler seeks the Liyue volume of the Teyvat Travel Guide and ends up helping Xingqiu defend a book collector, Chang the Ninth, from a merchant backed by the Fatui. Xingqiu defeats the merchant by cornering the market in Cor Lapis, and is revealed as heir of the Feiyun Commerce Guild.

The act has four quests: Justice, for Books' Sake; Know Thyself, Know Thy Enemy; Calm Before the Storm; and Justice Is Its Own Reward. It requires Adventure Rank 26 and Lisa's Story Quest, Troublesome Work. The Chinese title means roughly "Chapter of the Brocade".

The act is a character piece about Xingqiu's two sides: a bookish, kind swordsman who reads in the street, and a calculating merchant-heir with the resources to win without bloodshed. It shows his preference for a clever plan over brute force.

A strange bookmark left in the returned book is the last clue to Chang that Xingqiu helped him, which the act leaves implied.

Plot: **Justice, for Books' Sake.** At Wanwen Bookhouse in Liyue Harbor the owner, Jifang, has no Liyue volume of the Teyvat Travel Guide and suggests Chang the Ninth, a collector in Qingce Village. A passerby, Xingqiu, who has spent three years hunting the final volume of the Legend of the Shattered Halberd series, joins them. Chang's mining business has failed; he pawned most of his books, including the Travel Guide, but kept the rare sixth volume. The thug Changhu enters and says Gentry Maocai wants Chang's Cor Lapis stockpile at 30% of market price, threatening him if he refuses. Xingqiu steps in, naming himself a disciple of the Guhua Clan, which Changhu mocks as a fallen order. In thanks, Chang lends Xingqiu the book. Later Changhu returns with thugs and a Fatui Electro Cicin Mage, and Xingqiu drives them off with his sword and Hydro Vision. The Traveler suspects the Fatui are involved, and Xingqiu sends them to investigate Gentry while he finishes reading.

**Know Thyself, Know Thy Enemy.** Posing as a VIP client from Mondstadt, the Traveler and Paimon learn from Gentry's guard that he is meeting a client at Xinyue Kiosk. They eavesdrop and hear Gentry discuss an order with a Fatui agent, Javert, who offers help but urges him to finish quickly. They report to Xingqiu near Yujing Terrace, who gives them a letter written in a cipher for the Feiyun Commerce Guild.

**Calm Before the Storm.** At the Guild, Xu decodes the letter and agrees to help. Together at Liuli Pavilion they set the plan: force Gentry to desperation by buying every stock of Cor Lapis in Liyue. Xu supplies the Mora. The Traveler buys the ore from city merchants and Shizhuang the Strong in the Chasm, then visits Chang and offers market price, which relieves him; Paimon assures him Gentry's thugs will not return.

**Justice Is Its Own Reward.** At a Guild warehouse outside the city Xingqiu explains that, as the sole holder of Cor Lapis, he forces Gentry to come to him. Gentry arrives with Javert and tries to seize the ore by force, but they are beaten. Javert, judging the matter too costly, withdraws. Xu arrives and calls Xingqiu his lord, revealing him as heir of the Feiyun Commerce Guild. As punishment for intimidating Chang, Xingqiu triples the price on the stockpile, and Gentry pays it. Xingqiu asks the Traveler to return the borrowed book. Chang says his pawned books were all returned that morning and rewards the Traveler with the Liyue Travel Guide; a strange bookmark falls from the returned volume, hinting that Xingqiu was involved.

Remarks to keep. Xingqiu's plan relies on the Guild's resources rather than a duel: a market cornering that leaves Gentry no alternative. Chang is at first certain that Xingqiu had little to do with it, which the bookmark contradicts.

Revelations: Xingqiu is the heir of the Feiyun Commerce Guild and writes in a Guild cipher; the Guhua Clan is described by its enemies as having fallen from grace. A Fatui agent is involved in a Liyue ore deal, a recurring theme in early Liyue content.

Characters: Xingqiu, the Traveler and Paimon. Chang the Ninth, Jifang, Changhu, Gentry Maocai, Javert and Xu appear.

Xingqiu is bookish, principled and strategic. Chang the Ninth is a genial collector in financial trouble. Gentry Maocai is a ruthless merchant. Javert is a Fatui agent who cuts his losses.

Consequences: The Traveler obtains the Liyue Travel Guide and a lasting friendship with Xingqiu. Chang's business is rescued, and Gentry is forced to pay triple. Xingqiu's heirship becomes known to the people present.

Placement: Release order: 1.0. Story order: early Liyue content, after Lisa's Troublesome Work.

321.content: Act I of Xingqiu's Story Quest. Xingqiu and the Traveler foil the merchant Gentry Maocai's attempt to buy Chang the Ninth's Cor Lapis cheaply, by buying all the Cor Lapis in Liyue with Feiyun Commerce Guild funds.

322.content:
Fabulous Fungus Frenzy (also: Nilotpala Cup, Nilotpala Cup Beast Tamers Tournament, Beast Tamers Tournament): The event opens at Sumeru City, where a bulletin board advertises the first Nilotpala Cup, held at Port Ormos with the Amurta researcher Kautilya as organiser and the Fontaine businessman Elchingen as sponsor (sixty million Mora in prizes). The Traveler and Paimon sign up partly to keep an eye on the Fungi, learn from the guide Haniyyah, befriend Layla and meet Yae Miko, who has come with a writer from Yae Publishing House. As the rounds go on, the Traveler switches off a Wisdom Orb, finds that a Fungus still follows them freely, learns the tournament hides a deception, and in the finale exposes Elchingen's plot. The event ends with the tournament paused and Haniyyah caring for the remaining Fungi.

Requirements were Adventure Rank 30 and the Archon Quest A New Star Approaches; Akasha Pulses, the Kalpa Flame Rises and Yae Miko's Story Quest The Great Narukami Offering were recommended, with a Quick Start for those who had skipped them. The event is set while Sumeru is settling after the Archon Quest, and shows Fungi as something other than hostile monsters.

Plot: Act I, The Most Fantastic Tournament You've Never Heard Of?. The event notice at Sumeru City's southeast entrance promises the first Nilotpala Cup Beast Tamers Tournament. At Port Ormos, the rules say contestants may not use weapons or fight each other directly; Fungi registered to a Wisdom Orb may move around the arena and the main roads of the port but not Wikala Funduq, shops or restaurants, since many locals do not know about the tournament. The Corps of Thirty referees, and gross violations can bring Akademiya punishment. Kautilya, a senior Amurta researcher, promises the orb uses Amurta's "Intellectual Boost" technology and is absolutely safe. Elchingen's prize fund is sixty million Mora, with his whole fortune offered to whoever passes the Ultimate Trial if they take over hosting. Haniyyah, who tested the orb early on and worked among the Eremites taming Sumpter Beasts, teaches the Traveler to capture Fungi; her partner is a Pyro Fungus she calls Pyro-1. Paimon names the Hydro Fungus Bongo-Head. Layla, collapsing from exhaustion because she cannot sleep enough, hopes to reach the quarterfinals, since quarter-finalists may take home Fungi of their choice. Yae Miko explains that Yae Publishing House brought its writer Souka for inspiration for a novel on friendship and rivalry; Miko enters the tournament herself.

Act II, Nilotpala Cup: Debut Match. The Traveler beats Ajilenakh Dash's team; Layla and Miko also win. Miko leads them to a "training" session that turns out to be time spent bonding with their Fungi. Layla suggests Fungi can be tamed; switching off the orb makes Twirly-Whirly and Bongo-Head wander peacefully. Cries for help lead them to two children threatened by wild Fungi; Haniyyah drives the Fungi away, then says she plans to win the tournament and destroy every Fungus. A Corps of Thirty member is seen nearby, which the Traveler takes as a sign that Cyno is watching. Souka is the next opponent.

Act III, Dual Missions: Progress and Probe!. The Traveler defeats Souka. Layla has a meeting with the Almighty Merchant and Miko hands that task to the Traveler. At sunrise they photograph the Floral Jelly formula and meet the merchant, Dori, who gives them discarded scraps and agrees to ship Layla's order. They then beat Baron Bigfoot; Layla also wins, and Paimon begins gathering evidence for Miko.

Act IV, Unfathomable Defenses. The Traveler beats Hardy Two-Blades, whose rough handling of his Fungi upsets Paimon. Miko loses the semifinal to Haniyyah, so the Traveler faces Layla, who plays fair and loses, and then Haniyyah. Miko gives the Traveler a gohei blessing after receiving the evidence. The Traveler tracks Haniyyah with Elemental Sight; she tells why she hates Fungi and gives them her notebook. They learn Kautilya's setup is a deception and that Bongo-Head follows them of its own accord, since its orb was off.

Act V, The Strongest Opponent! The Biggest Crisis!. The Traveler defeats Haniyyah's team, with Pyro-1 holding back, and asks to keep Pyro-1. Elchingen then takes them to a hidden area where Fatui Skirmishers wait and uses the Wisdom Orb's backdoor command to seize Twirly-Whirly, Blitzara and Pyro-1. Bongo-Head, which was not controlled, repels them; Miko, Layla and Haniyyah arrive and the control is broken. Elchingen flees but Sido and the Corps of Thirty arrest him and Kautilya. Haniyyah apologises.

Act VI, Farewell, My Shroom Buddies. The Traveler and Layla see Miko off; she leaves Blitzara in their care. Haniyyah, who has taken the remaining orbs and Fungi, has renamed Pyro-1 as Kindlejoy, admits taming it brought her joy, and leaves to care for them in a place she found. Afterwards the Fatui agent Yurochka can be fought near Chatrakam Cave.

The Traveler's team in the final was Bongo-Head, Twirly-Whirly, Blitzara and one Fungus of the player's choice. Ten kinds of Fungi could be awakened during play: Floating Hydro, Dendro and Anemo; Whirling Electro, Cryo and Pyro; and Stretchy Pyro, Anemo, Geo and Electro. The in-world bulletin board reports thirty-two contestants after the preliminaries and sixteen in the next phase, with audience comments debating a points system and a "Floating Fungi Protection Association".

Revelations: Elchingen, the quiet Fontaine tycoon, is revealed as a Fatuus working for Il Dottore, who wants a Fungi army to cause havoc in Sumeru. The Wisdom Orb has a hidden backdoor command, and the rules disclaimers mention possible negative effects on the body. Kautilya's role as organiser is described by the Traveler's group as a deception, and the wiki summary says Elchingen throws him under the bus. Gentler Fungi follow people who treat them well, even without an orb.

Haniyyah's hatred of Fungi comes from terrible stories she grew up with, and Paimon argues she still felt compassion for her partner.

Characters: Traveler and Paimon (the "Golden Comet" and "Silver Companion" in Haniyyah's words), Haniyyah (beast tamer, ex-Eremite), Layla (Rtawahist student), Yae Miko (Yae Publishing House chief editor and Guuji), Souka (Yae author), Kautilya (Amurta researcher and organiser), Elchingen (sponsor), Balfour (staff member who distributes Floral Jelly), Dori (the Almighty Merchant), Sido (Corps of Thirty), Cyno (suspected observer), Yurochka (Fatui agent in the post-story), and opponents Ajilenakh Dash, Baron Bigfoot and Hardy Two-Blades. Fungi: Bongo-Head, Twirly-Whirly, Blitzara, Pyro-1/Kindlejoy.

Dori could be invited as a playable character after Act V by spending Mushroom Currency and Fungus Medals. Yanbei, Jutta, Najah, Thabit and Wafiq appear in the audience.

Consequences: Elchingen and Kautilya are taken away by the Corps of Thirty to face judgement. The tournament is put on hold until it can be run safely, with Haniyyah taking care of the Fungi, and the Traveler and Paimon, having technically passed the Ultimate Trial, are treated as hosts. Yurochka remains as a loose end near Chatrakam Cave.

Placement: Released in Version 3.2 as a Flagship Event, set after the Sumeru Archon Quest. Event quests are not part of the main storyline, and many in-world people did not know about the tournament, as its own rules state.

Gameplay: Game mechanics, not in-world fact. Three modes unlocked in sequence: Fungus Capture, Coruscating Potential and Special Training, plus a Championship Progress tab. Mushroom Currency and Fungus Medals bought rewards such as the Nilotpala Cup Tournament Stage, a Wisdom Orb model, Crown of Insight, materials and Mora; both currencies vanished when the event period ended, and the shop stayed open a week longer.

323.content:
A Fungi-commanding tournament held at Port Ormos. Contestants capture four Fungi, give them Floral Jelly and use a Wisdom Orb; weapons and direct fighting between tamers are banned, and the Corps of Thirty referees. The top eight win Mora, a title and the right to keep their ace Fungus.

It was initially unknown to many locals, hence the restrictions on bringing Fungi into Wikala Funduq, shops and restaurants.

324.content: A device developed for the tournament, using Amurta's "Intellectual Boost" technology, that registers and commands a Fungus. It has a hidden backdoor command that Elchingen used against the Traveler's Fungi; Bongo-Head, whose orb the Traveler had switched off, was unaffected.

325.content: A former Eremite beast tamer who tested the Wisdom Orb and guides the Traveler. She calls herself an illiterate nobody and plans to win in order to destroy all Fungi, including her partner Pyro-1. After the final she apologises and cares for the surviving Fungi, renaming Pyro-1 Kindlejoy.

326.content: Presented as a quiet Fontaine businessman who sponsored the tournament with sixty million Mora and offered his whole fortune to whoever passes his Ultimate Trial. He is later revealed as a Fatuus working for Il Dottore and is arrested by the Corps of Thirty.

327.content: The Amurta researcher who organises the Nilotpala Cup and whose disclaimer reserves interpretation of the rules to himself. He is exposed alongside Elchingen and arrested.

328.content: Fungi named in the event. Bongo-Head is the Traveler's Floating Hydro Fungus, named by Paimon; Twirly-Whirly is Layla's Floating Anemo Fungus; Blitzara is Yae Miko's Whirling Electro Fungus, named by Souka; Kindlejoy is Haniyyah's Pyro Fungus, formerly Pyro-1.

329.content:
Farewell, Archaic Lord (also: Chapter I Act II, Liyue Archon Quest Act II): Chapter I Act II of the Archon Quest, set in Liyue Harbor. With Rex Lapis dead and his body hidden by the Qixing, Childe introduces the Traveler and Paimon to Zhongli, a consultant at the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor, who offers to get them to the Geo Archon's vessel if they help him prepare the Rite of Parting.

The act has seven quests: An Organization Known as Wangsheng, Moonfinger, Three Poignant Perfumes, The Realm Within, Downtown, Guizhong and Zhongli's Treat. It is a long errand sequence through the harbor and surrounding countryside, and it ends when Ganyu delivers Ningguang's invitation to the Jade Chamber. Released in version 1.0.

Tonally it is light, with errands, misunderstandings and Zhongli's habit of leaving the Traveler to cover costs, set against a background of a murdered god. The recurring theme is Zhongli's insistence that the old rites be observed properly, in contrast to Childe's undisclosed agenda.

Plot: At Liuli Pavilion Childe introduces Zhongli, who says he can bring the Traveler to the Exuvia if they help with the Rite of Parting. They buy jade, make perfumes, borrow a bell from Madame Ping, order kites and workers, and get Everlasting Incense from Bubu Pharmacy. The act ends with Ningguang's invitation to the Jade Chamber.

**An Organization Known as Wangsheng.** At Northland Bank, Ekaterina tells the Traveler that Childe has found someone to break the stalemate and is waiting at Liuli Pavilion. Childe presents Zhongli as a consultant at the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor and a trusted contact of the Fatui. Zhongli explains that the parlor organises burials, that the age of the adepti is ending, and that the Qixing have broken tradition by not holding a memorial for a deceased adeptus. He asks the Traveler to help prepare the Geo Archon's last rites, the Rite of Parting, and the Traveler agrees; only by taking part can they again see the god's form. Zhongli says the Fatui are merely financial sponsors, that he does not know and does not wish to know what Childe gains from it, and that his own concern is that Liyue's traditions endure.

**Moonfinger.** The first item on Zhongli's list is Noctilucous Jade, paid for with mora from Childe. At the Jade Mystery the three inspect Shitou's samples. Zhongli tries to buy all three, but Paimon stops him, and he explains how to judge the jade by its Pyro affinity. Shitou chips thin samples which Zhongli says could be reinforced with Hydro. The trio use the Meaty Tribe's cooking pot in Dadaupa Gorge to test them (angering the tribe). The third sample is the best. When Zhongli explains the purpose, Shitou, saddened, sells it at half price, which the Traveler pays.

**Three Poignant Perfumes.** Zhongli, who treats the deicide as secondary to giving an archaic lord a proper farewell, sends them for silk flowers. Bolai gives them the flowers free once he learns the reason. After asking women around the city, the Traveler makes perfumes with help from Ying'er, and the three perfumes are offered at the Statue of The Seven outside the harbor.

**The Realm Within.** Zhongli needs the Cleansing Bell from Madame Ping but declines to go himself, claiming other business. At Yujing Terrace the pair find that Madame Ping's teapot is itself a domain, and that she is an adeptus; they recover the bell.

**Downtown.** Zhongli collects the kites he had commissioned from Granny Shan, one of the few who care for Liyue's old customs. Childe supplies mora to hire workers, and the Traveler negotiates with Tic, Tac and Toe. Childe then offers to let them keep the leftover mora in exchange for information, with access to the bank's vaults in return, and the Traveler reflexively refuses, which upsets him. Zhongli walks in unaware and names the next item: Everlasting Incense from Bubu Pharmacy.

**Guizhong.** At the pharmacy Qiqi asks for a prescription, and then offers the incense in return for hunting a cocogoat with the Guizhong Ballista on Mt. Tianheng. The ballista has been sabotaged by Treasure Hoarders who looted the area; the group repair it with parts from a nearby post and fight off the bandits, then discover there is no cocogoat, because Qiqi had actually meant coconut milk. Baizhu appears, thanks them for looking after Qiqi, and offers the incense for three million mora. Childe, amused, pays for it and sets up coconut milk supply for the pharmacy. Out of earshot, Ekaterina reports overhearing that the Qixing have taken over the Golden House (Paimon had let it slip), and Childe concludes that is where the Exuvia is hidden.

**Zhongli's Treat.** Zhongli invites the Traveler to dinner at Third-Round Knockout, a small tavern, where Iron Tongue Tian tells a story about Ningguang's Jade Chamber. Ganyu arrives, introduces herself as the Qixing's secretary at Yuehai Pavilion and Ningguang's special emissary, and passes on a letter inviting the Traveler to the Jade Chamber to "snip every one of these entwining dark threads". Zhongli tells them to go, calling it a rare honor, and to meet him at Dihua Marsh afterwards.

For most of the act Zhongli carries no mora of his own and relies on others to pay, a running joke that Childe's funds and the Traveler's generosity cover (he does bring mora for his own treat at Third-Round Knockout). The specific items on his list (jade, perfumes, kites, workers, bell, incense) are what the Rite of Parting requires, and Shitou and Bolai lower or waive their price once they learn what the purchase is for.

Revelations: The Qixing have hidden the Geo Archon's vessel, the Exuvia; Childe deduces that it is in the Golden House.

Zhongli is introduced as a funeral-parlor consultant who says the Geo Archon is also an adeptus; Madame Ping is an adeptus who keeps a domain inside her teapot; Ningguang, in her letter, speaks of cutting the "entwining dark threads" together with the Traveler.

The act does not explain why Zhongli avoids going to Madame Ping himself, or why he knows the rites so well; it leaves both unexplained.

Madame Ping's teapot domain shows the Traveler another adeptus living quietly near the harbor, after those met in Jueyun Karst and at Wangshu Inn.

Characters: Traveler and Paimon; Zhongli; Childe (Tartaglia); Ekaterina; Ganyu.

Also Hongru (Liuli Pavilion), Shitou, Bolai, Ying'er, Madame Ping, Granny Shan, Tic, Tac and Toe, Qiqi, Baizhu, Iron Tongue Tian, and Ningguang (appearing only through Ganyu's letter and the story).

Consequences: Everything needed for the Rite of Parting is gathered except the final pieces. The Traveler now has an invitation to the Jade Chamber and a rendezvous with Zhongli at Dihua Marsh, leading into Act III, A New Star Approaches.

Childe, from what Ekaterina overheard, believes the Exuvia is in the Golden House, and he has been put out by the Traveler's refusal to inform for him.

The Traveler's first impulse to refuse Childe's request is the act's one note of friction between them.

Placement: Chapter I Act II, after Of the Land Amidst Monoliths and before Act III, A New Star Approaches. Released in version 1.0.

330.comment: Farewell, Archaic Lord: Zhongli and the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor
