330.content: Zhongli presents himself as a Wangsheng consultant, says the parlor arranges burials so the dead pass in peace, and takes on the Rite of Parting to give Rex Lapis a proper farewell. Childe introduces Zhongli as a trusted associate of the Fatui and jokes that the parlor does not dabble in killing, "well, ostensibly".

331.content: The Geo Archon's vessel, which Zhongli says is traditionally called the Exuvia. Childe says the Tianquan Ningguang has forbidden anyone from accessing it; later, when Ekaterina reports overhearing that the Qixing have taken over the Golden House, Childe concludes the Exuvia is kept there.

332.content: A small harbor tavern with a resident storyteller, where Zhongli treats the Traveler to dinner. Iron Tongue Tian tells how Ningguang shreds her research and scatters the "paper snow" from the Jade Chamber, and Ganyu appears there to deliver the invitation.

333.content:
Felis Fuscus Chapter (also: Felis Fuscus, Lyney's Story Quest, The Forgotten Thief, The Phantom Thief's Reappearance, The Magician's Secret, The Truest Thing, The Interview, Phantom Weasel): Lyney's Story Quest, set in the Court of Fontaine. Ten years after a thief called the Phantom Weasel vanished, a poster announces the return. The Great Magician Lyney recruits the Traveler and Paimon as temporary assistants to find the culprit. They clear the name of Cesar, a dead stage magician wrongly branded the thief, expose his killer, and then learn the thief was someone else.

The chapter has one act, The Forgotten Thief, made of four quests: The Phantom Thief's Reappearance, The Magician's Secret, The Truest Thing and The Interview. It was released in version 4.0 and unlocked after As Light Rain Falls Without Reason. It also reveals how Lyney and Lynette came to learn magic from Cesar, and what they hid from him.

The plot is staged like one of Lyney's own shows: the real aim, restoring Cesar's name and drawing out the true culprit, is not what he first tells the Traveler.

Plot: Charlotte reports that the Phantom Weasel, a thief never caught ten years ago, is back. Lyney offers to investigate and has the Traveler and Paimon help look into Cesar's death. They find Cesar's former apprentice Lorenzo is hiding something, are attacked, and find Cesar's diary and workshop. Lorenzo admits he killed Cesar and was the Phantom Weasel. The next day Lyney performs Cesar's old trick at the Opera Epiclese and reveals Jemma was behind it. Jemma later turns herself in.

The Phantom Thief's Reappearance: Charlotte tells the Traveler that ten years ago the magician Cesar fell to his death during a performance and the Gardes found stolen goods among his belongings, so he was thought to be the thief. A poster at the Opera Epiclese announces the Weasel is back. Lyney offers help and says they should check whether Cesar faked his death, starting with his fiancee Jemma at the Poisson cemetery. Jemma hides something.

The Magician's Secret: at Hotel Debord the Traveler meets Lorenzo, a former magician and Cesar's apprentice turned businessman, who threatens Edmondo and storms out. Lyney leads them out of town, where pursuers attack and flee on discovering he is a Vision bearer. Jemma says she is threatened whenever she looks into Cesar's death. In the sealed workshop they find Cesar's diary about two children he agreed to train. Lyney confronts Lorenzo, who admits to sabotaging Cesar from jealousy and to being the Phantom Weasel, then is taken away by Gardes. Lyney holds a memorial for Cesar.

The Truest Thing: Lyney performs a show alone at the Opera Epiclese, and at the interval Lynette reveals Jemma was the real Phantom Weasel. The twins confront her privately. Jemma tells a sad history and does not confirm the facts. Lyney reveals that he, not Jemma, wrote the letter, to draw her out because the twins felt indebted to Cesar. He then performs the final act, Cesar's old trick, and vanishes in a sea of flowers. At the cemetery he tells the Traveler about his past with Lynette and Cesar.

The Interview: at the Steambird, Charlotte tries to interview the twins and says Jemma has turned herself in and admitted to being the real Phantom Weasel. Paimon notices Lyney is now using Rainbow Roses in his tricks, which Lynette notices. She says she had only been acting to distract Charlotte, and asks the Traveler to keep the Rainbow Rose Lyney gave them.

The Phantom Thief's Reappearance: Charlotte had been asking Abagnale about the Phantom Weasel before approaching the Traveler. The thief robbed rich and poor alike. Lyney is finishing a show when Charlotte spots him. Lynette at the cemetery has not seen Jemma yet; the group asks other visitors about her and Cesar.

The Magician's Secret: Edmondo says those who make an enemy of Lorenzo suffer misfortune. The pursuers say their tactics would not work on "the lady", which Lyney correctly takes to mean Jemma. In the workshop, the diary describes the children and the time spent with them, and Lyney confirms them to be himself and Lynette. Reading Cesar's notes on the trick, Lyney realised that someone sabotaged his play and caused his death. Lorenzo says he hated Cesar for his self-perceived poverty, for forbidding him to trick people out of Mora, and for entertaining crowds for free. He says he targeted the poor so he could hone his craft to steal more valuable items. Lyney suspects he also had feelings for Jemma, which Lorenzo denies. Bruno and Lori of the Gardes take him away. Lynette stays with Jemma. At the cemetery, Lynette says Lyney will host a magic show tomorrow.

The Truest Thing: the twins say the real Phantom Weasel worried about the Gardes, and, finding an aggravated pupil, used Lorenzo to kill Cesar and avoid dirtying her own hands. Jemma tells of her youth: parents lost young, betrayal and abuse, and a vow to hate all happiness and steal it. Lyney explains the letter was his, written because they felt indebted to Cesar and wanted his legacy restored. They tell Jemma she cared for Lorenzo and that her "truth" was gone now that he was arrested. Jemma asks about the secrets he and Lynette hid from Cesar and says he will end up like her; Lyney says he is nothing like her. In the finale he drops from the top of the opera, the same trick Cesar attempted, and vanishes into flowers while Charlotte watches.

At the cemetery Lyney explains that, after being taken in by Arlecchino, he and Lynette approached Cesar with an agenda in mind. He knew they had some talent but needed a professional to avoid plateauing. Cesar accepted readily, treated them well during ten days together, and asked why Lyney wanted to learn magic; Lyney said it was his passion and knew that was a lie. Lyney says selfishness and lies have followed them, but that they are grateful to have each other, unlike Jemma.

The Interview: Charlotte notes that Jemma turned herself in; she had also wanted to see Lorenzo one last time. Lyney gives his view of why Jemma turned herself in. Lynette's remark about the Rainbow Rose closes the act.

Revelations: Cesar was killed by his apprentice Lorenzo, and Cesar was not the Phantom Weasel. The thief was Jemma, who manipulated Lorenzo.

Lyney and Lynette studied under Cesar for ten days while hiding their real purpose, and the twins arranged the letter to flush Jemma out. Jemma later turns herself in and admits to being the Phantom Weasel.

Lyney's final act reprises the trick Cesar was attempting when he died. The twins' debt to Cesar is central to their motives.

The quest shows that the twins were taken in by Arlecchino before meeting Cesar and that they lied to him; the Story Quest does not detail the House of the Hearth.

Characters: Lyney, Lynette, the Traveler and Paimon.

Charlotte, Cesar (deceased), Jemma, Lorenzo, Edmondo, Abagnale, and the Gardes Bruno and Lori.

Arlecchino is referenced by Lyney as the one who took in him and Lynette.

Consequences: Cesar's name is cleared, Lorenzo is arrested and Jemma turns herself in as the real Phantom Weasel. Charlotte's article is overtaken by the news of Jemma's arrest.

Lyney begins using Rainbow Roses in his tricks and gives one to the Traveler, which Lynette notices.

Placement: Unlocked at Adventure Rank 40 after As Light Rain Falls Without Reason (Chapter IV Act II). Released in 4.0 on 2023-08-16. The wiki notes it is blocked at step 5 by Unfinished Comedy.

334.comment: Felis Fuscus Chapter: The Phantom Weasel
334.content: A notorious thief in Fontaine ten years before the Archon Quest who was never caught and robbed rich and poor alike. When the magician Cesar died, stolen goods were found among his things and he was blamed. His apprentice Lorenzo first confessed to being the Weasel after killing Cesar, but the twins revealed that Jemma was the real thief, using Lorenzo as a tool. She later turned herself in.

335.comment: Felis Fuscus Chapter: Cesar the magician
335.content: A stage magician who died in a fall during a performance ten years before the quest. He agreed to train Lyney and Lynette for ten days, not knowing their secrets, and was wrongly believed to be the thief. His diary and workshop helped Lyney prove he was sabotaged by Lorenzo.

336.content:
Film Notes (also: Film Notes World Quest series, "Outlander Brigade!", Mushounin, Xavier's second film): In "Outlander Brigade!" the Traveler finds Xavier midway through a troubled shoot at the Kamisato Estate's request, is offered the lead role, and plays two scenes of "When the Wind of Death Blew Towards the Blond Samurai" before the supporting actors walk out. Over a meal at Uyuu Restaurant, Rikuto's story of Seishimaru helps Xavier see what is wrong. In Mushounin, Koharu and Sasano are brought back and three new scenes are filmed at Komore Teahouse, Nazuchi Beach and a cliff on a small island east of Narukami Island.

The series is a light comedy about creative frustration and adds no wider Inazuma lore. The Traveler's real combat is used for the action scenes, and a Film Kamera recording area limits where they can stand during the shoots.

The quests are spread over several in-game evenings, since Xavier plans each location for the light. Koharu's remark that Keisuke lets Seishimaru take revenge in order to cool his temper leads Xavier to admit the story needs another possibility, which he says he may adjust.

Plot: Opening. Furuta, the Kamisato Estate's butler, tells the Traveler that Xavier, a young Fontainian, had received money from the Tenryou Commission for a film that the commission was not satisfied with, and then came to the Yashiro Commission, the body responsible for arts and the humanities, for help. Ayato agreed and sent Koharu, whom Furuta worries is not fond of Xavier.

The first shoot. Xavier reminds the Traveler of an earlier agreement that they would play the lead, and gives scripts for Act I, Scenes II and III. Sasano and Koharu are already weary after eleven takes. The script is Xavier's adaptation of a novel by Kayabuki Ikkei; Sasano recalls that Ikkei's manuscripts were always rejected by Yae Publishing House. In the story the two supporting characters sacrifice themselves so the lead can go on, which Sasano and Koharu find senseless. Xavier criticises stiff delivery and forgotten lines, and both actors quit.

Rikuto's advice. Xavier retreats to Uyuu Restaurant. Okazaki Rikuto, the owner, overhears the premise and remarks that a hero who charges into unwinnable fights with no hesitation seems hardly human. He tells a legend: Seishimaru's samurai parents were executed after an apparent error at work, and Seishimaru sought revenge on the Wakayama family who carried out the sentence, whose head was a childhood friend. Xavier decides to write a new script and asks to meet at Komore Teahouse the next day.

Mushounin. Koharu, apologetic after being reprimanded by Ayato for walking out, asks the Traveler to speak for her, and Sasano returns too. The new script, based on the Seishimaru legend, adds an original character, Yano Machiko. The first scene is shot in a private room at Komore Teahouse that Thoma helped Xavier borrow. The Traveler plays Seishimaru against Sasano as Wakayama Keisuke, and Koharu plays Machiko. In the scene the Traveler must follow the marked lines; going off-script makes Xavier call another take.

The second scene, at Nazuchi Beach in the evening, uses a gang of toughs (Yamada Hifumi, Yamamoto and Tanaka) as extras after the Traveler persuades them by fighting; Xavier later says he gave their characters their real names with their permission. The final scene, at sunset on a cliff, has Sasano play Wakayama Keisuke's younger brother Kojuurou, who confronts Seishimaru. The Traveler is asked to glide down the cliff on a wind glider rather than jump.

In the film's third act, Machiko tells Seishimaru that Keisuke is gone and urges him to let it go. Kojuurou says that Keisuke worked all year to settle the clan's affairs and calls Seishimaru's revenge on the executioner alone a coward's choice. Sasano warns the Traveler to pull punches in the fight scene because he is not a fighter.

Revelations: - Xavier's first script here is an adaptation of a novel by Kayabuki Ikkei, whom Sasano knows only as an author Yae Publishing House kept rejecting.
- Rikuto uses the Seishimaru legend to show a man whose revenge is aimed at someone who only followed orders, which pushes Xavier to rework the film.

Characters: Xavier (a Fontainian aspiring director), Koharu (a Kamisato household servant), Sasano (supporting actor), Furuta (Kamisato butler), Okazaki Rikuto (Uyuu Restaurant), Yamada Hifumi, Yamamoto and Tanaka (toughs turned extras in Mushounin), Paimon and the Traveler. Kamisato Ayato, Thoma and Kayabuki Ikkei are only mentioned.

Consequences: Both quests give Adventure EXP, Primogems, Mora and Hero's Wit; Mushounin also gives Mystic Enhancement Ore. The film is completed. Co-Op mode is locked during the shoots, and the Serenitea Pot is unavailable for part of the first quest.

Placement: Released in 2.8. It requires Omnipresence Over Mortals (the Inazuma Archon Quest) and "The Seventh Samurai", the earlier world quest featuring Xavier. It has no bearing on later Archon Quests.

337.content:
In-universe, Rikuto tells Xavier an Inazuman legend of Seishimaru, whose samurai parents were executed, and who sets out to take revenge on the Wakayama family that carried out the sentence. Xavier's "Mushounin" script retells it with film characters, including Wakayama Keisuke, who lets Seishimaru choose by a blind point between a sword and a temari ball whether they will fight or sever their bonds.

The film's third act has Keisuke's younger brother Kojuurou accuse Seishimaru of cowardice for blaming only the executioner.

338.content: Xavier is a theatrical Fontainian filmmaker working in Inazuma. He calls the Traveler his dear friend and says they were the first friend he made in Inazuma. He loves art over commerce but his scripts confuse his actors. In this series he works with funding and staff granted by Kamisato Ayato.

key: The Blazing Stars Ring in Fortune
The Stars Inscribe the Year's Wishes
339.content:
Fleeting Colors in Flight (also: Lantern Rite 2022, Version 2.4 Lantern Rite event, The Blazing Stars Ring in Fortune, Sky-Gazers, Land-Walkers, The Stars Inscribe the Year's Wishes, Flameplume Starflowers, Oceanic Defender event): The story is told in three parts: "The Blazing Stars Ring in Fortune" (Ningguang and Keqing introduce the fireworks show, and Zhongli suggests a storytelling approach to get Keqing to rest), "Sky-Gazers, Land-Walkers" (the gift round with Keqing, then the discovery that fireworks have been stolen from Qingce Village) and "The Stars Inscribe the Year's Wishes" (the trap for the thieves, the story at the Jade Chamber and the show itself). Along the way the adepti, Qiqi, Baizhu, Yanfei, Xingqiu and Chongyun appear. The mood is warm and humorous, with an underlying theme about balancing duty and rest.

The event is set shortly after the Jade Chamber's rebuilding and the defeat of Osial, which Paimon recalls in the opening; Keqing thanks Zhongli for his help in the Rite of Parting. Because it is a limited-time event, its scenes are known only to those who took part. It is the second Lantern Rite event, after the 2021 Lantern Rite.

The event continues threads from the Liyue Archon Quest: the adepti having handed Liyue Harbor to mortals, Ningguang and Keqing leading the Qixing, and Shenhe's recent arrival in Liyue Harbor. It also gives the first detailed look at how Keqing's drive affects those around her, a theme she herself admits at the finale.

Plot: Part I, The Blazing Stars Ring in Fortune: At Yujing Terrace Ningguang explains that the festival this year will include a fireworks show organised by the Ministry of Civil Affairs, with Keqing responsible. Keqing is seen revising plans, adding Qingce Village to the show's range and refusing to rest. Pengyi gives the Traveler a Launch Tube for designing fireworks. Ningguang worries about Keqing's long hours and asks the Traveler to help. At the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor and then Third-Round Knockout Zhongli advises that a story containing the message would work better than a lecture.

Part II, Sky-Gazers, Land-Walkers: Keqing asks the Traveler to introduce her to the adepti so she can deliver Qixing gifts. They visit Madame Ping, Cloud Retainer at Mt. Aocang, and Xiao at Wangshu Inn, and meet Qiqi and Baizhu on the way. Pengyi then reports that all the fireworks at Qingce Village have been stolen. The Traveler and Keqing follow footprints and meet Xingqiu and Chongyun, who have caught a Treasure Hoarder while escorting the Feiyun Commerce Guild's festival supplies. Keqing promises to find the stolen fireworks herself.

Part III, The Stars Inscribe the Year's Wishes: Keqing finds the stolen stash and waits with the Traveler for the hoarders to return. The Millelith's approach scares the hoarders into abandoning the fireworks; Keqing and the Traveler confront their leader Xingxiu and force a surrender. The Traveler meets Zhongli and Paimon invents a story with his help. At the Jade Chamber the Traveler tells Keqing a story of a chef who works himself to ruin, she recognises the message and admits she wishes she could slow time. The Fireworks Show begins, and everyone wishes each other a happy Lantern Rite.

Part I in more detail. Ningguang explains that fireworks were originally firecrackers, invented in Liyue to ward off beasts and signal other farmers, and that the festival uses them to honour the toughness of Liyue's ancestors. She says Jiangzhou, who planned the festival before, has moved departments because her father is old, leaving Ningguang as head organiser and Keqing in charge of the show. Keqing criticises the budget excuse from her subordinate Pengyi and tells him the budget must serve the goal. After Ningguang leaves, Paimon and the Traveler decide to consult Zhongli because he knows the people of Liyue best. At Third-Round Knockout he is eating with Hu Tao, Xiangling and Guoba. Zhongli says that as a mere consultant his words no longer carry weight, and that a story that touches on Keqing's daily life and friends would hit harder. Keqing arrives to ask the Traveler to take her to the adepti and agrees to watch the fireworks together afterwards.

Part II in more detail. At Madame Ping's, Yanfei (working through the festival) and Madame Ping thank her for gifts of seasonal goods, silk and flower seeds, and Madame Ping notes that Keqing designed the street decorations but has not seen them. At Mt. Aocang Cloud Retainer receives a Ministry-modified firework as a gadget, admires its design, and mentions Moon Carver, who has gone travelling because he cannot enter the city, and Mountain Shaper, who left to look for treasures. Ganyu is also visiting but leaves hurriedly when Cloud Retainer begins recalling her childhood. Shenhe brings food from the city because she has learned that people share food at Lantern Rite. Cloud Retainer tells them to look after each other and gives the advice used later: test your own work like a chef tasting his food, and take rest. At Wangshu Inn Qiqi and Baizhu are collecting digestive herbs for Bubu Pharmacy, and Xiao appears silently. He accepts the Qixing's gifts unwillingly, warns that karma is harmful to mortals and refuses to join the city fireworks. Pengyi then arrives with news of the theft in Qingce Village, and because the Millelith are short-handed Keqing refuses to ask the adepti, and says she will manage. Granny Ruoxin describes the theft. Xingqiu explains that he and Chongyun are escorting festival goods; Chongyun mistook the Treasure Hoarders for evil spirits (firecrackers were once used to drive away spirits), and Xingqiu agrees to guard Qingce Village.

Part III in more detail. Keqing returns with a lead: wagon tracks and fireworks packaging led her to the stash. A hoarder, Xiuyong, and leader Xingxiu plan to steal fireworks and later firecrackers to smuggle into the city, set them off during the opening ceremony and rob Liyue Harbor while the Millelith are distracted. The Millelith, having made the captured scout talk, arrive and the hoarders scatter. Keqing and the Traveler fight the remaining hoarders. Xingxiu surrenders on recognising the Yuheng. The Traveler delivers the prisoners to Qingce Village where Pengyi and Jingcheng of the Millelith are waiting. Everyone hears an explosion, which turns out to be Keqing accidentally lighting loose fireworks while searching the site.

At Third-Round Knockout Zhongli, who has been chatting with Yun Jin, hears the views the Traveler collected and helps shape the story. At the Ministry Jingcheng sends the Traveler and Keqing off together, and at the Jade Chamber the story is told. Then a messenger, Baishi, brings an imported-style outfit that Ningguang had her tailor make for Keqing, the fireworks begin, and the finale shows friends watching from the harbor.

Details of the story the Traveler tells. A talented chef opens a restaurant near the city gate, will not take on help, believes only he can turn good ingredients into fine dishes, never eats his own food, and in six months drives away his customers and closes the restaurant for good. Paimon built it from the advice they gathered: Cloud Retainer's remark that a chef who never tastes his own food courts trouble, Yanfei's saying that a rested worker is an efficient worker, and Xingqiu's habit of handing out work to the right people. Keqing calls the ending predictable but admits she knows the lesson in theory and loses sight of it when tasks are hers. She says she was once so impatient that colleagues left within three months, that she is getting better, and that she kept her promise to share the show.

Revelations: Keqing, privately, thinks Cloud Retainer is wary of mortal rule and wants a good first impression from the Qixing. Cloud Retainer asks Ganyu, Shenhe and Keqing to look out for one another, and tells Keqing that Ganyu forgets food and rest when busy and must be made to eat and sleep. Cloud Retainer says Moon Carver felt he could not simply roam into Liyue Harbor under the agreement that left the city to the Qixing, and went travelling instead. The Qixing now bear the daily running of Liyue.

Xiao recognises Keqing from the fight against Osial and says her swordplay is fierce. His post-quest line says the demons have retreated and humans are safe, which he thinks Pervases would have counted as a lifelong wish come true, and says that the fireworks can be seen from anywhere and that anyone who wants him can find him. Ganyu says she planned to go home but Ningguang told her to take a proper vacation.

Characters: Main: the Traveler, Paimon, Keqing, Ningguang, Zhongli. Others: Pengyi and Jingcheng (Ministry of Civil Affairs), Hu Tao, Xiangling, Guoba, Madame Ping, Yanfei, Cloud Retainer (Xianyun), Ganyu, Shenhe, Qiqi, Baizhu, Xiao, Verr Goldet, Granny Ruoxin, Xingqiu, Chongyun, Hongxing (guild attendant), Yun Jin, Kangsheng, Xingxiu, Xiuyong and the Treasure Hoarders. The finale cameo list includes Beidou, Xinyan, Smiley Yanxiao, Huai'an and Qiqi.

The 4-star Liyue characters who can be invited through Prosperous Partnerships are Xiangling, Beidou, Xingqiu, Ningguang, Chongyun, Xinyan, Yun Jin and Yanfei.

Consequences: The stolen fireworks are recovered, the thieves are handed to the Millelith and the show goes ahead. Keqing agrees to take a break and see it with the Traveler. Post-quest, Yun Jin is performing at Qingce Village at Granny Ruoxin's invitation, Xingqiu and Chongyun are lingering there, and the Traveler can speak with Zhongli, who spends the festival idly visiting Third-Round Knockout.

Placement: Released in Version 2.4 as a Flagship Event (with a Co-Op mode). It required Adventure Rank 28, the Archon Quest Chapter I Act III (A New Star Approaches) and Interlude Chapter Act I (The Crane Returns on the Wind). It follows the 2021 Lantern Rite and precedes later Lantern Rite events such as A Lanternlit Ode to the Silver Moon.

Gameplay: Game mechanics, not in-world fact. 25 January to 12 February 2022. Four challenge themes and a shop: Flameplume Starflowers (smelting and launching fireworks with the Launch Tube gadget, earning Affluence Talismans), The Great Gathering (recovering scattered materials in Guyun Stone Forest, including by sea on the Waverider, earning Immaculate Talismans), Wondrous Shadows (solving Shadow Lantern puzzles with Yuan Rong, earning Affluence Talismans) and Oceanic Defender (fighting Beisht, earning Conquest Talismans). Prosperous Partnerships exchanges 1,000 Affluence and 1,000 Conquest Talismans to invite a 4-star Liyue character; the Afterglow Market sells furnishings, a Crown of Insight and talent materials; and collecting enough talismans unlocks Ningguang's outfit Orchid's Evening Gown ("The Moon's Comely Brow"). The Launch Tube remains usable for launching after the event.

340.comment: Fleeting Colors in Flight: Fireworks Show
340.content: The Ministry of Civil Affairs' first big fireworks show at Lantern Rite, organised by Keqing with Ningguang as head organiser. Fireworks are placed across Liyue, including Qingce Village, and fired together at a chosen moment. Ningguang explains that fireworks descend from firecrackers used by Liyue's ancestors for warding off beasts and signalling. The best view is said to be from the Jade Chamber.

341.comment: Fleeting Colors in Flight: The fireworks theft
341.content:
Treasure Hoarders steal the fireworks placed at Qingce Village and elsewhere and stash them, planning to use them to cause a distraction on opening night and rob the harbor. Xingqiu and Chongyun catch one hoarder, Kangsheng, who insists he is mistaken. Keqing finds the cache and the Millelith corner the hoarders led by Xingxiu.

Xingxiu admits the hoarders had decided to steal firecrackers as well when they ran short of fireworks, since a loud bang alone would draw the Millelith away. The Feiyun Commerce Guild's capture of one hoarder makes the leader recall the rest of his gang, which leads to their meeting Keqing.

342.comment: Fleeting Colors in Flight: Keqing and the chef's story
342.content: Ningguang asks the Traveler to persuade Keqing to rest. Zhongli proposes a story, built from advice from Cloud Retainer, Yanfei and Xingqiu, about a chef who will not delegate or eat, falls ill and loses his customers. Keqing listens at the Jade Chamber, tells the Traveler the lesson is something she knows but forgets, and lets herself enjoy the show.

343.comment: Fleeting Colors in Flight: Gifts for the adepti
343.content: Keqing brings gifts from the Qixing to Madame Ping, Cloud Retainer and Xiao. Madame Ping receives seasonal goods, silk and flower seeds; Cloud Retainer receives a modified firework (chosen because she likes gadgets); Xiao is given food and declines to thank. Keqing hopes to give the adepti a good impression of mortal governance.

key: Flowers Resplendent on the Sun-Scorched Sojourn
344.comment: Flowers Resplendent on the Sun-Scorched Sojourn
344.content:
Flowers Resplendent on the Sun-Scorched Sojourn (also: Chapter V Act I, Natlan Act I, Natlan! A New Adventure): Act I of Chapter V is the Traveler's arrival in Natlan. The Traveler and Paimon meet Kachina of the Children of Echoes, follow her to the Stadium of the Sacred Flame, and meet Mualani and Kinich. They watch the Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame, a tournament that decides who fights the Abyss, and then visit Mualani's village, where the Traveler purges fresh Abyssal corruption from Mualani's gravely wounded friend Atea but cannot undo the old damage; she has only days to live.

Act I has three quests: "Natlan! A New Adventure", "Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame" and "Home of the Hot Springs". It requires Adventure Rank 40, and a quick start was offered from 5.0 until 6.0 to players who had completed "A New Star Approaches" (Adventure Rank 28). The Traveler cannot gain Pyro from the local Statue of The Seven, learns that Natlan's Pyro Archon is a human, and learns the basics of the tribes, Saurian companions, Ancient Names and the Ode of Resurrection.

The act is a tour of the nation's culture before the war story begins. It stages three tribes in turn (the Children of Echoes, the Scions of the Canopy and the People of the Springs), sets up the Pilgrimage's stakes and ends on Atea's approaching death; her talisman reaches Mavuika in Act II, and her passing is mourned in Act V.

A separate Version 5.0 event with the same name ("Flowers Resplendent on the Sun-Scorched Sojourn (Event)") is not the same as this Archon Quest act.

Plot: **Natlan! A New Adventure.** After a farewell from Charlotte, Navia, Clorinde and Furina at Romaritime Harbor, the Traveler and Paimon sail to Natlan and find a village in a canyon. Kachina is told by her teammates that they are leaving her for the Pilgrimage. The Traveler offers to help and she guides them around the village, to the black stone that represents the tribe's Wayob and to the chief, Pacal. At the stadium city they meet Mualani, Kinich and his companion K'uhul Ajaw. The Pilgrimage is open only to Natlanese, so the Traveler cannot join. The group has dinner at the Weary Inn.

**Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame.** Mavuika opens the tournament with an address to the contestants. The Traveler and Paimon watch from the stands as Kachina and Mualani clear the team stage. Two disqualified contestants, Tepexpan and Tamuin, threaten Kachina and are stopped. Kachina wins her one-on-one matches, including a duel with her friend Mualani, and earns a place in the Night Warden Wars with Chasca, Iansan, Kaiulani and Kibangu.

**Home of the Hot Springs.** Mualani takes the Traveler to her village, the People of the Springs. Atea explains that outsiders must acclimate in the artificial springs first. During the night the Abyss attacks. Atea has destroyed an Abyssal pylon but is gravely wounded. The Traveler purifies the Abyssal energy from her wounds, as they once did for Dvalin, but the damage is too deep to heal. At a party the next day Atea tells Mualani and the Traveler she has only a few days to live and gives the Traveler her talisman to hand to the Pyro Archon.

Detail from the first quest: at Natlan the Traveler follows human signs to the Children of Echoes' canyon, where Kachina's team leaves her. Kachina explains that her people can align themselves to a rhythm and that the Tepetlisaurs, such as her companion Ayo, are their Saurians. Pacal at first doubts the Traveler and Paimon and asks for proof of identity; he reads their Adventurers' Guild handbook and apologises, having heard of them. Kachina is unsure why the Wayob chose her for an Ancient Name. Kachina shows them the Statue of The Seven, learns the Traveler can use many elements, and explains that the Pyro Archon is human. The Saurian Toto offers a ride to the stadium city. Kinich explains the Pilgrimage's purpose: a test of who may fight the Abyss, with five people to earn the honour that round. Cival refuses to let the Traveler register, since Contending Fire, the fuel of the Sacred Flame, is made only in fights between Natlanese. He adds that the Ode of Resurrection works only on Ancient Name bearers and that those who fail against the Abyss die and have their Ancient Name forsaken and forgotten.

Detail from the second quest: Kachina defeats Nkunga and the more experienced Liliuo. Before the final, the ranking leaves Kachina and Mualani as each other's last opponent, and Mualani accepts either result; Kachina wins with a surprise attack.

Detail from the third quest: Mualani's village is a hot-spring resort; Atea is a good friend of Mualani and could no longer enjoy the springs after being impaled by an Abyssal monster. Chief Amina and her guards plan a party for Atea. After the attack Mualani and the Traveler destroy one pylon and follow the monsters to an abandoned spring, where Atea has already destroyed the second at the cost of severe injuries; she had been going there because she knew her end was near.

Fine detail: Paimon worries on the voyage that Natlan may have no human population because no Natlanese have been seen in other nations; the act shows the tribes living there. Kinich remarks that Kachina was ditched by teammates again, and says Mualani is a three-time veteran of the Night Warden Wars who has never needed to be resurrected, and that he has himself fallen several times and been brought to the Wayob's realm, the Night Kingdom. Mualani first asks whether the Traveler could join under special circumstances, expecting a refusal; if refused, she will pair with Kachina and Kinich will lead the team Mualani had gathered.

Revelations: - Natlan's Pyro Archon, Mavuika, is a human, and opens the Pilgrimage in person.
- The Pilgrimage produces Contending Fire, which fuels the Sacred Flame that keeps the Abyss from invading; the tournament also picks who fights in the Night Warden Wars.
- Ancient Names mark those chosen by the Wayob, and the Ode of Resurrection can revive only those who hold them; fallen bearers go to the Night Kingdom.
- Natlan has six tribes: the Children of Echoes, Scions of the Canopy, People of the Springs, Masters of the Night-Wind, Flower-Feather Clan and Collective of Plenty.

- The Traveler can purify Abyssal corruption, but cannot save deep injuries.

Characters: Kachina, Mualani, Kinich with K'uhul Ajaw, Pacal, Cival, Atea, Amina, Chasca and Iansan appear. Charlotte, Navia, Clorinde and Furina farewell the Traveler in Fontaine. Mavuika appears in person to deliver the Pilgrimage's opening address.

Consequences: Kachina becomes a Night Warden War fighter, Mualani and Kinich become the Traveler's guides, and Atea's talisman is left with the Traveler. Act II follows: the Night Warden Wars are won, but Kachina falls in battle and Mavuika cannot find her in the Sacred Flame.

Placement: Follows Chapter IV Act VI "Bedtime Story" and is the first act of Chapter V. It was released in 5.0 alongside Act II, with Acts III and IV in 5.1.

345.comment: Flowers Resplendent on the Sun-Scorched Sojourn: Atea's talisman
345.content: Atea is a respected member of the People of the Springs and a friend of Mualani; long unable to fight or enjoy the springs since being impaled by an Abyssal monster, she volunteers for night patrol and is gravely wounded destroying an Abyssal pylon. The Traveler cannot heal the old Abyssal contamination. Atea hands her talisman to the Traveler to give to the Pyro Archon.

346.comment: Flowers Resplendent on the Sun-Scorched Sojourn: Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame
346.content: The Pilgrimage is a tournament held in the Stadium of the Sacred Flame. Teams collect Contending Sparks before one-on-one duels. It produces Contending Fire, which keeps the Sacred Flame burning, and chooses the Natlanese who fight in the Night Warden Wars.

key: Fontaine Research Institute Chronicles World Quest series
Fontaine Research Institute, Stagnating in the Rubble
347.content:
Fontaine Research Institute Chronicles (also: Fontaine Research Institute Chronicles World Quest series, Fontaine Research Institute, Stagnating in the Rubble, Institute Survey Anchor quests): Fontaine Research Institute Chronicles is a world quest series added in version 4.1. After the explosion that wrecked most of the Fontaine Research Institute, the surviving staff recruit outside adventurers. The Traveler and Paimon go through a slow qualification review, then escort a senior researcher named Nacker into the floating ruins of the Central Laboratory. A reporter from The Steambird, Chronie, follows them.

The series is a comedy of paperwork and institutional self-protection wrapped around a real danger: unstable Arkhium left over from the experiment of Edwin Eastinghouse. It consists of one main quest, "Fontaine Research Institute, Stagnating in the Rubble", and two child quests that retrieve the last two Survey Anchors. It requires The Outlander Who Caught the Wind (the Fontaine prologue) to be completed.

The tone mixes bureaucratic satire with a serious thread: the Institute's public account of the disaster, its internal factions, and a journalist's attempt to get at the truth. The Traveler ends as an "Honorary Senior Researcher", but the quest leaves open who is lying about the missing core.

Plot: **Stagnating in the Rubble: the review.** At the Qualifications Review Representative Office Desnos, who manages recruitment, is being pestered by Recon Log Meks, and the Traveler defeats them. The forms are deliberately absurd. Raimondo later says the paperwork is mostly useful for weeding out "idiots" and is not what he really judges applicants by.

**Nacker and Chronie.** Nacker explains that the Institute was once the technological centre of the Court of Fontaine and that Edwin Eastinghouse, working on a gravity-lifting field generator powered by Arkhium, left roughly two-thirds of the Institute in ruins. He says Edwin would otherwise have been the next Director. Chronie, who has already tried to interview Choiseul, keeps cross-examining Nacker. She also raises that research materials are being sold off and asks who among the staff could do it. Nacker admits the Anchors are kept locked in a room because they were repeatedly stolen.

**The Survey Anchor.** The Anchors radiate Arkhium energy. Exposure makes Chronie violently ill, and the staff member Chalmet gives her medicine. Nacker has the Traveler operate an Energy Transfer Terminal and reach the Anchor through the radiation. Choiseul and Raimondo are astonished that it was done without instruments, since the Institute has only three complete sets.

**Dormitories and Clockwork Applications.** The child quests are short. In the dormitories Nacker explains that researchers think sleep is a waste of time and use the space to rest their brains by playing piano or reading. He also remarks that earlier applicants who tried the Anchor test used up a lot of antiemetics.

**To the ruins.** The group dives into allogravity-condensed water to reach the floating Central Laboratory ruins. Nacker takes the Traveler to the Experimental Field Generator that Edwin built. The thing that exploded earlier was not the Generator but the Arkhium ore that powers its Arkhium Kinetic Core. Nacker plans to use Raimondo's catalyst to turn inert Arkhium into stable Tri-State Arkhium and run the Generator at half speed so the ruins can land. He sends the Traveler to take photographs for his work record while Chronie waits elsewhere.

**The second explosion.** After the Traveler returns, another explosion occurs. Nacker has gone, and the Arkhium has overloaded while its cooling system is damaged. Raimondo and the Traveler fight a new wave of meka awakened by the energy, recover four condensing components and shut the Generator down. Raimondo explains that the Institute's Gravity Fields hold the Arkhium fragments together beneath the ruins and that this blast was a small rehearsal of a third great explosion.

**The two stories.** Raimondo claims Nacker stole the core and used the large Arkhium to draw attention, and that Nacker and other successors of Edwin sell information. In front of Chronie he calls the blast a "controllable hazard removal directional blast", but he also admits it was a small resonance of Arkhium fragments that someone must have piled up on purpose. Chronie rejects the Institute's account. The Traveler either sticks to Raimondo's request or tells Chronie the whole story; if told, she says she will report that the ruins can explode again and that the Institute tried to use the Traveler's credibility to blame Nacker. Either way, Choiseul gives the Traveler a certificate and trophy as Honorary Senior Researcher and poses for a group photo.

**Raimondo's account of Edwin (optional dialogue).** Raimondo calls Edwin a genius second only to the first Director, Alain Guillotin, but also an "inhuman monster" who cared about nothing but research. He says people under Edwin sold research assets, plagiarised results and used his name to scam others while Edwin ignored it as long as work advanced, and that Choiseul's reviews of Edwin's team were read as bureaucratic distrust. He says the Arkhium Kinetic Core was the fruit of his own joint research with Edwin, and that they split over a conservative plan versus a faster one after finding the large, very pure Arkhium chunk.

**Evidence about Nacker.** Raimondo says a blurry photo from Chronie shows Nacker working on the suppression device in a way not found in any procedure. This is the only concrete evidence given. Raimondo hopes Nacker and the core were destroyed so that the last trace of Edwin's influence is gone, then doubts it because most of the nearby fragments were spent ore waste that should not have exploded so violently.

**Gameplay and rewards (labelled as such).** The quest gives the achievements A Perfect Yesterday (reading a note in the Materials Office), Mired in Red Tape and This Ends Here, and the Honorary Senior Researcher Award. Afterwards the sky over the Institute region stays dark blue.

Revelations: - The Fontaine Research Institute of Kinetic Energy Engineering was once the technological centre of the Court of Fontaine. The explosion of Edwin Eastinghouse's Arkhium experiment destroyed most of it.
- The Central Laboratory ruins float, held up by a Gravity-Altering Field. The Institute plans to land them with an Experimental Field Generator running on a "Tri-State Arkhium".
- Survey Anchors measure Arkhium energy flow and are physically harmful to approach without instruments.

- The Arkhium under the ruins is held together by Gravity Fields and can resonate again. Raimondo calls a further blast a "third great explosion".
- The Institute has been selling off or losing research assets for some time, and Raimondo and Nacker each blame the other's circle.
- Alain Guillotin was the first Director of the Institute.

Characters: The Traveler and Paimon; Desnos, the recruiter; Nacker, a senior researcher who once worked under Edwin; Chalmet and Conjat, Institute staff; Raimondo and Choiseul, who run the new Institute; and Chronie, a political affairs journalist for The Steambird. Edwin Eastinghouse appears only through other people's accounts.

Chronie is relentless and likes to interview with evidence in hand, and she does not back down when the Institute stonewalls her. Choiseul is evasive and mostly repeats praise for the Institute. Raimondo is smooth and controlled, courteous but openly cynical about forms. Nacker is polite, blunt about the Institute's flaws and the least forthcoming about himself.

Consequences: The Traveler becomes an Honorary Senior Researcher. The ruins are made safer for the moment but can explode again. Nacker and the Arkhium Kinetic Core are missing. Chronie goes away with a story critical of the Institute, or with the full truth if the Traveler tells it.

Raimondo says Chronie will probably leave the Institute alone for a while once she has her story. The main quest has a follow-up, the world quest "An Expected Plan", which this entry does not cover.

Placement: Requires The Outlander Who Caught the Wind, the Fontaine prologue. Released in version 4.1. The two Anchor-retrieval quests are children of the main quest and are completed in either order.

348.comment: Fontaine Research Institute Chronicles: Edwin Eastinghouse's Arkhium experiment
348.content:
According to Nacker, Edwin Eastinghouse was developing a field generator powered by Arkhium that could lift an entire block of buildings. The Arkhium ore powering its Arkhium Kinetic Core exploded, leaving most of the Institute in ruins. The Generator itself survived. Raimondo says the core was the result of his own joint research with Edwin.

Raimondo and Edwin had trouble keeping the core powered and tried a mix of Pneumousia and Arkhium energy and chains of ore before finding a huge, inert and unusually pure Arkhium chunk. They disagreed about how fast to treat it. Raimondo calls Edwin a genius and a monster who wanted only results.

349.comment: Fontaine Research Institute Chronicles: Survey Anchors
349.content: Survey Anchors are Institute devices used to monitor the strength of Arkhium energy flows. Proper retrieval needs special instruments, and exposure makes people ill. The Institute locks them up because they kept being stolen. Retrieving an Anchor serves as part of the qualification review for outside applicants, and Nacker says it consumed a lot of antiemetics.

350.comment: Fontaine Research Institute Chronicles: Chronie of The Steambird
350.content: Chronie is a journalist in the political affairs section of The Steambird. She follows Nacker and the Traveler, asks pointed questions about Arkhium safety and the sale of research assets, and refuses to be fobbed off. She gets sick from Anchor radiation but keeps going.

351.comment: Fontaine Research Institute Chronicles: Raimondo and Choiseul
351.content: Raimondo and Choiseul are the co-administrators of the new Fontaine Research Institute. Raimondo, a Senior Technician, drives the Tri-State Arkhium plan and welcomes the Traveler as an Honorary Senior Researcher. Choiseul handles reviews and public statements and is evasive when Chronie presses him.

352.content:
For a Tomorrow Without Tears (also: Prologue Act II, Mondstadt Archon Quest Act II): For a Tomorrow Without Tears is Act II of the Mondstadt Prologue, the first Archon Quest chapter. After the Four Winds temples are cleared, the Traveler returns to Mondstadt, is made an Honorary Knight of Favonius and joins the bard Venti in a plan to cure the dragon Stormterror, who is really Dvalin, of the corruption the Abyss Order is exploiting. The plan needs the Holy Lyre der Himmel, which must be obtained, recovered from the Fatui and repaired with Dvalin's tears. At Starsnatch Cliff an Abyss Mage turns Dvalin against them and the lyre is broken.

The act is where Venti's identity as Barbatos, the Anemo Archon, comes into the open, where Jean and Diluc become active allies, and where the Fatui and Abyss Order stop being background threats. It requires Adventure Rank 10 and ends with the cliff confrontation that sets up Act III.

Plot: The act begins with Shadow Over Mondstadt. Near the Goth Grand Hotel the Traveler finds Jean refusing a masked Fatui diplomat, Anastasia, who offers to have the Fatui "put an end" to the dragon; Jean rebukes her for proposing to destroy one of the Four Winds of Mondstadt. Back at the Knights' headquarters, Lisa examines the crystal the Traveler picked up in the forest and finds that it gives off energy harmful to Vision users, so the Traveler pockets it again, keeping quiet about why. Jean names the Traveler an Honorary Knight.

Paimon recognises the presence that clung to the crystal in a boy running through the streets, and the party follows his footprints with Elemental Sight. The boy is Venti. He sings of Stormterror and the reason for the dragon's rampage, and recognises the Traveler. When the Traveler takes out the crystal it has been purified, so Venti realises the Traveler's power can save Dvalin. He sends them to the great tree at Windrise, where the Hero of Mondstadt is said to have ascended to Celestia. After the Traveler beats an Eye of the Storm, Venti explains that Dvalin is suffering from a degradation that the Abyss Order is exploiting. His own earlier attempt to cure the dragon had gone wrong when the Traveler's unexpected arrival left him poisoned, though he had since recovered.

Venti's remedy is the Holy Lyre der Himmel, kept at the Favonius Cathedral. He asks Sister Gotelinde for it, even telling her he is Barbatos, the Anemo Archon, and she takes him for a madman. The Traveler asks properly, but borrowing it needs papers signed by the Grand Master, the Seneschal and the community representative, since it is currently used only for Ludi Harpastum. The Traveler sneaks into the vault, but a Fatui Electro Cicin Mage teleports in and takes the lyre, and a guard spots the Traveler. Venti's wind carries the party to the Angel's Share, where Diluc, the owner, gives them a quiet table and misdirects the pursuing Knights.

Diluc, who recognises the Traveler as the new Honorary Knight and calls it a shame that they joined the Knights, agrees to help after Venti performs the situation for him. He arranges a meeting for the next night. There the party finds that Diluc has also brought in Jean, who is present privately rather than as Acting Grand Master, because she has little room to act officially. She backs the plan because she knows Dvalin's past. Diluc has interrogated some Fatui and learned that the lyre is not at the Goth Grand Hotel but at a stronghold outside the city.

The party takes the lyre after fighting through its guards; a Fatui Agent warns that Signora will end them. The lyre is in poor condition, so they collect Teardrop Crystals, which are Dvalin's tears, and use them to restore it fully. They then go to Starsnatch Cliff to summon Dvalin. Venti begins to play and speaks to the dragon, but a Cryo Abyss Mage appears beside Dvalin, tells him that Venti abandoned him and that Mondstadt has turned its back on him, and says the bard is deceiving him again. Dvalin, calling Venti Barbatos, accuses him of planning to have him slain, and flies off in rage; the lyre is ruined beyond repair. Afterwards Jean begins to say "Barbat-" and corrects herself to Venti, who replies that she has known his identity for some time and thanks her for still using his name. Diluc commits to finding the Abyss Mage through his own contacts, noting he has already killed one in a temple.

The act is made up of fifteen quests in this order: Shadow Over Mondstadt, Unexpected Encounter, That Green Fellow, Let the Wind Lead, Venti's Plan, Venti's New Plan, Wild Escape, Behind the Scenes, Chasing Shadows, State of the Holy Lyre der Himmel, then three that can be done in any order (Fallen Tears at the Thousand Winds Temple, Hidden Tears at Eagle's Gate, Stolen Tears at the Eclipse Tribe), then Crystal Tears and Reunion With the Dragon. Completing the last quest grants the achievement named after the act, and the player receives a Damaged Holy Lyre der Himmel item as a reward.

The closing cutscene shows the Traveler's sibling overlooking Stormterror's Lair while two Abyss Mages bow to them. After Dvalin flies past, the Cryo Abyss Mage that tricked him reappears behind them and addresses the sibling as "Your Highness", saying that when their homeland returns to this world they will revel in its glory. Nothing in this act identifies the homeland.

Revelations: - Venti is Barbatos, the Anemo Archon. He tells Gotelinde so (she does not believe him), Dvalin addresses him by that name, and Jean shows she has known for some time and keeps calling him Venti.
- Stormterror is Dvalin, one of the Four Winds, and has been degraded by something the Abyss Order manipulates. Jean already knows of Dvalin's past; the wider public treats Stormterror as a vicious dragon.
- The Teardrop Crystals are Dvalin's tears, and the Traveler can purify them.
- The Fatui are involved and hostile to Mondstadt's approach: a diplomat urges killing the dragon, a Fatui mage steals the Holy Lyre, and an agent invokes Signora.

- The Abyss Order is deliberately working on Dvalin, telling him that Venti abandoned him and that Mondstadt betrayed him. Venti's protest that it is not like that is cut off, so the act leaves open how Dvalin will take it.
- The Traveler's sibling is in Teyvat and is honoured as royalty by the Abyss Order's mages. The act shows this without explaining it.

Characters: Traveler: Honorary Knight, bearer of the power that purifies the crystals. Paimon: recognises Venti by his presence. Venti: bard and Anemo Archon, trying to heal his dragon friend. Jean: Acting Grand Master, constrained by office, acting privately with Diluc. Diluc: owner of the Angel's Share, who supplies information and shelter. Lisa: studies the crystal. Dvalin: the afflicted dragon, whose tears are the key material. Gotelinde: the Cathedral sister who refuses the lyre. The Traveler's sibling appears only in the final cutscene.

The Fatui are represented by the diplomat Anastasia, a Cicin Mage and an agent; Signora is named but absent. The Cryo Abyss Mage is the act's central antagonist and is dealt with in Act III.

Consequences: The Holy Lyre is destroyed and Dvalin flees, now believing he was betrayed. Diluc takes on the job of tracking the Abyss Mage. These lead directly into Act III, where an Abyss Mage is killed at the winery, the Lair is entered and Dvalin is finally purified.

Jean, Venti and Diluc become openly aligned, and the Fatui's interest in the lyre and in Venti sets up Signora's attack at the end of Act III.

Placement: Prologue Act II, after The Outlander Who Caught the Wind (Act I) and before Song of the Dragon and Freedom (Act III). Released with version 1.0. Requires Adventure Rank 10.

353.comment: For a Tomorrow Without Tears: Holy Lyre der Himmel Plot
353.content: The Holy Lyre der Himmel is a sacred instrument kept at the Favonius Cathedral and in this period used only for Ludi Harpastum. Borrowing it formally needs signatures from three authorities. After a Fatui mage takes it, the party recovers it in poor condition and repairs it with Teardrop Crystals, which are Dvalin's tears, but the Abyss Order's interference at Starsnatch Cliff destroys it.

354.comment: For a Tomorrow Without Tears: Starsnatch Cliff Confrontation
354.content: At Starsnatch Cliff, Venti plays the restored lyre to call Dvalin. Before the dragon can listen, a Cryo Abyss Mage turns him against Venti, calling the bard a deceiver. Dvalin flies off in a rage, the lyre is wrecked, and Diluc and Jean resolve to hunt down the mage.

key: From Dusk to Dawn in Byakuyakoku
355.comment: From Dusk to Dawn in Byakuyakoku
355.content:
From Dusk to Dawn in Byakuyakoku (also: Byakuyakoku world quest series, Enkanomiya world quest series): From Dusk to Dawn in Byakuyakoku is the World Quest series, added in version 2.4, that introduces Enkanomiya, a hidden realm beneath Inazuma whose old name is Byakuyakoku. The Traveler and Paimon come to recover the Bloodbranch Coral, pass through a gate with the Key of the Moon-Bathed Deep, and are drawn into a trial in the ruined kingdom. A helper named Enjou guides them, then proves to be an Abyss Order agent.

The series has two quests: The Entrance to Tokoyo and The Subterranean Trials of Drake and Serpent, the latter in three parts (The Trail of Drake and Serpent, The Heart of Ouroboros, Dreams in the Gaps). It is gated behind the earlier Enkanomiya quest The Still Water's Flow.

It works as the introduction to Enkanomiya's geography and vocabulary: White-night and Ever-night, Sinshades, the national treasures and the central tower. It is also the first place the Abyss Order is shown operating in Inazuma's hidden realm.

Plot: Back at the tower the Traveler finds Enjou gone. Aru explains that the Bloodbranch Coral had been absorbed by special Bathysmal Vishaps beneath the tower and must be recovered by defeating them. Aru adds that Enjou left in displeasure and that he has a special art that could make a Sinshade vanish, so Aru doubts he comes from Watatsumi and warns the pair to be wary of him.

After defeating the Vishaps below the tower, the Traveler meets Enjou, who explains he was after historical records from before the tower was built and admits he belongs to the Abyss Order. He reveals himself as an Abyss Lector and fights the Traveler. Beaten, he leaves, with a parting remark that Paimon may one day betray them; Paimon replies that he is trying to drive a wedge between her and the Traveler. On the surface the pair give the Bloodbranch Coral to Tsuyuko and warn her that the Abyss Order has infiltrated Enkanomiya. She calls this grave and says Madam Kokomi will soon have to face it, in connection with the Watatsumi Goryou Matsuri.

Quest-by-quest: The Entrance to Tokoyo covers the gate and the key. The Trail of Drake and Serpent covers the library, Enjou and the Golden Bridle; The Heart of Ouroboros the tower, Ever-night and Aru; Dreams in the Gaps the fragments, the Vishaps and the confrontation. This is a summary of the series page; individual quest dialogue was not read.

Revelations: - Enkanomiya's real name is Byakuyakoku; the ruin first reached was its library (Enjou's account).
- The Dainichi Mikoshi provides the realm's imitation of sunlight, called White-night, which is separate from the Ever-night.
- Sinshades are remnants of the thoughts of Byakuyakoku's former people.
- Enjou is an Abyss Lector of the Abyss Order.

- Bathysmal Vishaps beneath the tower had absorbed the Bloodbranch Coral.
- The Reins of Revival can make Ever-night spirits speak, and need the Golden Bridle and three fragments.

Characters: The Traveler, Paimon, Enjou (Abyss Lector, Abyss Order), Aru (a Sinshade) and Tsuyuko, who receives the Bloodbranch Coral. Madam Kokomi is mentioned only.

Consequences: Tsuyuko learns the Abyss Order has infiltrated Enkanomiya and expects Kokomi to have to deal with it. Enkanomiya's White-night and Ever-night cycle and its Sinshades are established for the later Enkanomiya quests.

Placement: Released in 2.4. In-game it follows The Still Water's Flow, a prior Enkanomiya quest that is not written as a separate entry here.

356.comment: From Dusk to Dawn in Byakuyakoku: Enjou
356.content: Enjou presents himself in Byakuyakoku as clerical staff assisting a trial, guides the Traveler to the Dainichi Mikoshi, then leaves. He is later revealed as an Abyss Lector of the Abyss Order who says he seeks records older than the tower. He is defeated in battle and departs, warning that Paimon might betray the Traveler.

357.comment: From Dusk to Dawn in Byakuyakoku: Reins of Revival
357.content: A national treasure of Byakuyakoku made of the Golden Bridle and three fragments hidden at The Narrows, The Serpent's Heart and the Evernight Temple. Restored, it can make the spirits of the Ever-night speak. Aru, a Sinshade at the Dainichi Mikoshi, assigns the Traveler to reunite it.

key: From One Case to Another World Quest series
358.content:
From One Case to Another (also: From One Case to Another World Quest series, Pakpaka Flying School mystery, Saurus Cracker case): From One Case to Another is a four-part Natlan world quest series added in version 5.2. At Pakpaka Flying School in the Scorchwind Trial Grounds, a young student named Taruka suspects the cheerful instructor Lamizana of plotting something dangerous around an upcoming air race. The Traveler, Paimon and the Little One investigate and end up uncovering a scheme to steal and sell Saurians.

The tone is comic. Almost everyone misreads everyone else: Taruka's suspicions are half right, the real villain is a travelling merchant, and the Traveler is briefly accused of being an accomplice. The quest uses the Saurian Indwelling feature for some stealth and tracking.

The story gives a view of daily life among the Flower-Feather Clan: flying lessons, training courses, races, and the closeness and friction between young riders and their Saurian partners.

Plot: **Incidents Are Ever Sudden.** Passing through a Recon Ring above the Scorchwind Trial Grounds brings the party to Pakpaka Flying School, where Temach introduces a training course with prizes. After the party passes it, the flashy instructor Lamizana gives out rewards, bickering with Taruka. Taruka asks the Traveler to investigate: he overheard Lamizana discussing something dangerous with an outsider, with phrases about being on time on race day and meeting at the north camp the next night.

**Beat the Clock: 24 Hours.** The party waits until the next evening, then uses an Iktomisaurus to sneak into the camp. They overhear two voices arranging a delivery of "goods" before the air race. Quilla, a travelling merchant, spots the Little One. A box of Saurus Crackers is knocked over elsewhere in the camp, drawing the Iktomisaurs, and the party slips away. Back at the school, Paran asks the Traveler to stand in for a contestant who has dropped out of the race against Taruka's sister Lliwa.

**An Air Race and an Alibi.** The Traveler races Lliwa. Lliwa's Saurian falters mid-race, and Taruka and his Qucusaurus Oberon go missing. Iktomisaurs attack Lamizana. He then confesses to a plan: he had arranged for young Saurians to stage a fake attack on Taruka at the finish line so that he could rescue the boy and impress Lliwa. Quilla suggests the real culprit is a Saurian trafficker named Hawka, mentions a blond youth with a white pet, and the group wrongly points at the Traveler and Paimon. The party escapes and goes back to the scene.

**Farewell, Final Saurus Cracker.** Following a scent, the party finds a letter from Hawka at Quilla's camp, revealing Quilla as the mastermind. They find Oberon in a cave; after he leaves, Quilla drops her "good merchant" act and sets her Saurian Furball on them. The Little One and Oberon win in a turn-based style fight. Taruka had already escaped by himself, Lamizana apologises, and the school offers its figurative open doors to the party.

Hawka's letter, found at the camp, is addressed to an unnamed recipient whom Paimon takes to be Quilla. It says the last batch of goods was good quality, some clients wanted more types of command, feed will be delivered on time, and asks the recipient to tell him if she makes progress with Paran, "that useless nephew of mine" so he can prepare a welcome. It also asks about a replacement for Soncoyoc. The Traveler learns from it that Quilla works with Hawka.

In the fight, Oberon hides Saurus Crackers under his wings to lure Furball off task. Oberon's added weight lets him block Furball's aerial escape. Quilla herself is useless in a fight and flees with Furball.

Details that matter in a scene: Taruka says his sister Lliwa is extremely competitive; Paran, who does most of the school's organising with his companion Carrewoof, comes from a family exiled from the tribe because of relatives' misdeeds. Taruka says people use that as an excuse to make things hard for him. Quilla deflects blame by describing a blond youth with a white pet, a description that happens to fit both the Traveler with Paimon and Paran with Carrewoof; Paimon points the second match out herself.

Gameplay notes (labelled as such): the stealth section lets the player pull Saurus Crackers from smudges on the walls to distract Iktomisaurs; co-op is disabled during Beat the Clock; The Punchy Saurian! and Every Contact Leaves a Trace are achievements. The Flower-Feather Clan reputation reward is 400.

Revelations: - Quilla, the apparently honest travelling merchant, is behind the scheme, as Paimon concludes from Hawka's letter and Quilla admits when cornered. She works with Hawka.
- Hawka, a Saurian trafficker, is Paran's uncle, who was exiled from the tribe long ago.
- Lamizana's "dangerous plan" was an ill-advised staged rescue to impress Lliwa; Quilla's group turned it into a real kidnapping.

- Hawka's letter treats trained Saurians, command sets and feed as goods supplied to clients.
- Taruka was never really in danger from the staged attack; he walked out of the camp himself once he learned the guards' patrol pattern.

Characters: Taruka (a young student at Pakpaka Flying School) and his Qucusaurus Oberon, his older sister Lliwa, Temach and Cisik of the flying school, the flashy Lamizana, the organiser Paran and his companion Carrewoof, the merchant Quilla and her Saurian Furball. Hawka appears only in his letter. Also the Traveler, Paimon and the Little One.

Consequences: Taruka and Oberon are safe, Lamizana apologises and offers compensation, and Quilla flees with Furball. Taruka asks the Traveler for the secret of getting along with young Saurians and says he wants to become the best adventurer of the Flower-Feather Clan and one day enter Ochkanatlan with Oberon.

Hawka and the wider trafficking network are not dealt with, so the case is only closed locally. Lliwa has not forgiven Lamizana for involving her brother, though they remain on good terms.

Placement: Released in version 5.2, with no required quest. The second part starts after waiting for the next evening; An Air Race and an Alibi begins when the player approaches the Tribal Totem Pole of the Flower-Feather Clan; the last quest starts automatically.

359.comment: From One Case to Another: Taruka
359.content: Taruka is a young student at Pakpaka Flying School who is protective of his sister Lliwa and doubtful of Lamizana. He is clever and articulate, tends to see conspiracies, and strictly manages the diet of his Qucusaurus Oberon. He asks the Traveler to investigate, escapes captivity on his own, and ends the series wanting to become the clan's best adventurer.

360.comment: From One Case to Another: Lamizana
360.content: Lamizana is a boastful, charming senior figure at Pakpaka Flying School, fond of giving advice and of feeding Oberon Saurus Crackers. His plan to look like a hero in front of Lliwa goes badly wrong, and he is quick to apologise at the end, offering compensation and accepting a threatened kick from the Little One.

361.comment: From One Case to Another: Quilla
361.content: Quilla poses as a well-travelled merchant who trades in many kinds of goods (Paran says she deals in a wide variety). She is in fact a villain working with Hawka. She admits it only when cornered, and is better at talking than fighting.

362.comment: From One Case to Another: Paran and Hawka
362.content: Paran runs much of the practical work at Pakpaka Flying School, with Carrewoof. His family was exiled from the tribe, which makes some people treat him badly. Hawka, his uncle, is a Saurian trafficker exiled long ago, who is trying to lure Paran into his scheme.

363.content:
Golden Slumber (also: Golden Slumber series, Lost in the Sands, Dreams Beneath the Searing Sand): A four-quest Great Red Sand world quest series from Version 3.1. The Traveler and Paimon find a lost research party in the desert: the scholar Tirzad, the merchant's associate Nachtigal, and the Eremite mercenaries Jebrael and his daughter Jeht. Exploring King Deshret's ruins with the machine Benben, they are hunted by the Eremite leader Samail, and Jebrael gives himself to the Golden Slumber to stop him.

The series examines the gap between the Akademiya's picture of King Deshret as a tyrant and the faith his people had in him. It centres on Jebrael's secret past in the Eremite group Thutmose, the murder of Jeht's mother, and the Golden Slumber, a collective dreamland within the king's throne room. It leads straight into The Dirge of Bilqis, which continues Jeht's story.

The quest requires only the Version 1.0 prologue quest The Outlander Who Caught the Wind, not any Sumeru Archon Quest. The series is the main window in the world quests onto the Eremites' pursuit of King Deshret's treasures and onto how those who worshipped him remember him.

Plot: Looking for Tirzad's missing party, the Traveler finds the group in a sinkhole and works with them to escape through ruins. They find a strange machine, Benben, which opens the sealed doors of the Khemenu Temple and a mural-hidden passage to the Mausoleum of King Deshret. Fatui and Eremites under Samail capture Benben, but the group recovers it. Samail pursues the Scarlet Sand Slate and Benben to the throne at Khaj-Nisut, where Jebrael enters the Golden Slumber to free the others and close the door.

Bonifaz, a Mondstadt merchant at Aaru Village, rented two Sumpter Beasts to the scholar Tirzad, who studies desert ruins with Nachtigal and two hired mercenaries. Contact stopped two days earlier, so the Traveler searches and finds the party at the bottom of a sinkhole with Jebrael and Jeht. Together they escape through a ruin, where Jeht finds the machine Benben, which makes Tirzad's Scarlet Sand Slate light up. Benben opens the Khemenu Temple and a mural-hidden passage to the Mausoleum of King Deshret, where a trap separates the group. Fatui and Eremites led by Samail take Benben; the group recovers it and Samail flees. At Khaj-Nisut, Samail uses Jeht as a hostage to force Jebrael to speak the prayer that opens the Golden Slumber. Samail enters and gains control of the building, so Jebrael follows to free the others and fades into the Slumber as the door seals. Jeht says she will go back to her father's original tribe, the Tanit.

Lost in the Sands: Contact by Dusk Bird stopped before the commission was posted. Jebrael is standoffish; Jeht welcomes help. Nachtigal has heatstroke from the fall; Tirzad is drunk after Jeht tells him Bonifaz and Nachtigal overcharged him for the Sumpter Beasts. In the ruin Tirzad says he owns the Scarlet Sand Slate because a relative abandoned her research to elope with a man she met in the desert. Jebrael criticises Tirzad's remark about the Akademiya's view of King Deshret so harshly that Tirzad faints in anger. Jeht names the machine Benben, and Tirzad entrusts the Slate to the Traveler.

An Introduction to Indoor Archaeology: At the oasis Jebrael tells the Traveler to keep the Slate safe and says he left the desert for a better path than seclusion. A mural of King Deshret leads Tirzad to call him a tyrant over insignificant subjects; Jebrael answers that Tirzad only repeats what the Akademiya says and knows nothing of the faith the people had in the king. Tirzad bumps the mural and a secret passage opens.

The Secret of Al-Ahmar: In the Mausoleum Jebrael says Ufairah would have loved to see it. The trapped door sends the Traveler to an unfamiliar ruin where Fatui and Eremites hold Benben. Samail knows Jebrael from Thutmose. Samail escapes the fight but leaves Benben, and Jeht and Tirzad demand the truth from Jebrael. The group then returns to the oasis.

Dreams Beneath the Searing Sand: The group rescues Nachtigal from Eremites and moves camp. At Khaj-Nisut the party passes three trials to reveal the whole city and reaches the throne room. Samail says Jebrael led them there only to enter the Golden Slumber; Jebrael warns it is a one-way trip. Inside, Samail says everyone joins a collective consciousness and loses individuality and urges Jebrael to join; Jeht's and the others' voices bring him back and he opens the door. He asks Jeht's forgiveness as he fades. Back at Aaru Village, Tirzad leaves to write his paper, and Bonifaz and Nachtigal stay. Jebrael had promised Tirzad to remain his bodyguard and help find King Deshret's secrets, something he and his wife had wanted to see together.

Small points. The commission can begin either by accepting Katheryne's Sumeru commission or by speaking to Bonifaz in Aaru Village. Tirzad's mercenaries are hired men separate from Jebrael and Jeht. Samail's leadership of the Eremites and his involvement with the Fatui is stated plainly in the Secret of Al-Ahmar quest. The series contrasts how the Akademiya teaches King Deshret with Jebrael's view of the faith the king's people had in him, and leaves the king's real nature unresolved.

Revelations: Jebrael was once a member of the Eremite group Thutmose and used his knowledge for it. Jeht's mother Ufairah, a researcher, was valuable to Samail for her knowledge of the desert and King Deshret. After Jeht was born, Jebrael began to doubt the morality of Thutmose's missions and planned to leave with his family, but Samail found out and killed Ufairah to make him stay. Samail was after King Deshret's treasures using Benben and the Scarlet Sand Slate, and the Fatui were working with the Eremites.

The Golden Slumber is described as a dreamland of King Deshret's knowledge, entered only through a prayer known to Jebrael, and entrants may never come back. The Akademiya's image of King Deshret as a tyrant is presented as secondhand opinion, countered by Jebrael's account of the faith his people had in him.

Characters: The Traveler, Paimon, Jeht, Jebrael, Tirzad, Nachtigal, Bonifaz, Samail and Benben.

Jebrael is a taciturn former Eremite who works as a mercenary; Jeht is his friendly daughter who later returns to the Tanit; Tirzad is a scholar with Akademiya assumptions; Nachtigal is Bonifaz's associate; Bonifaz is a Mondstadt merchant in Aaru Village; Samail is the Eremite leader and villain; Benben is the machine that opens the ruins. Katheryne issues the commission.

Consequences: Jebrael is lost to the Golden Slumber, and Samail is also taken into it. Jeht goes back to the Tanit and the story continues in The Dirge of Bilqis, where she buries her parents' remains in the Eternal Oasis. Tirzad writes his paper on King Deshret's ruins.

Placement: Released in Version 3.1 and set in the Great Red Sand. Requires only The Outlander Who Caught the Wind. The Dirge of Bilqis (3.4) can begin a Daily Reset after finishing Golden Slumber; Old Notes and New Friends is the other listed follow-up.

364.content: In the Golden Slumber series, Jebrael is a former Eremite of Thutmose who left after Samail murdered his wife Ufairah. Samail pursues King Deshret's treasures. At Khaj-Nisut both enter the Golden Slumber, a collective dreamland, and Jebrael sacrifices himself so that Jeht and the others escape.

key: Good Stuff, but Terrible Taste Continued
Alliance of Artists to Overthrow the Evil Organization
365.content:
Good Stuff, but Terrible Taste (also: Good Stuff, but Terrible Taste Continued, Salsa and the evil organization, Alliance of Artists to Overthrow the Evil Organization): The series is five regional quests (Belleau, Court of Fontaine, Central Beryl, Southeast Beryl and West Beryl) that can be done in any order, plus a follow-up, Good Stuff, but Terrible Taste - Continued, that unlocks after all five. Each regional quest starts by opening a chest after a nearby Water Volume Detection Crystal puzzle. The Traveler then moves one object under Salsa's direction to a spot that follows the natural lines of the scenery. The tone is gentle comedy about taste, art and a child's earnest, slightly muddled view of the adult world. Each quest gives Adventure EXP, 20 Primogems and Mora, and the regional ones also open a scenic viewpoint.

Across the five meetings Salsa gradually reveals herself: a painter-in-training whose parents work at the Fontaine Research Institute and are rarely home, who pretends to study for them, who forgets homework, and who treats her sketching trips as serious work. She names the Traveler and Paimon the first two members of an alliance she founds, and in the Continued quest she confronts Ubu over whether his work counts as art.

The wiki gives the requirement for every quest in the series as the first Fontaine Archon Quest, The Outlander Who Caught the Wind, so it can be started early in the region. The series name is a wiki label rather than an official umbrella title.

Plot: Opening. In the first meeting, Paimon wonders why a puzzle looks so strange and decides the Adventurers' Guild uses such puzzles to train rookies. A girl named Salsa interrupts, introduces herself as the future of Fontaine's art scene, and, hearing that the Traveler and Paimon are adventurers, fears they belong to the "evil organization" in green that has spoiled the scenery. When they offer help she recruits them to rearrange the objects.

The task. The camera moves to a fixed overhead view. Salsa explains that nature has its own flow of lines, for example the pattern of the flower bushes, and that the ugly objects look wrong because they break it. The Traveler lifts the object, tries a few spots (Salsa notes when a placement is no better than before) and puts it on a natural line. Salsa is delighted and speaks about points, lines and planes being in harmony.

Salsa across the meetings. She leaves hurriedly to get home before her parents return and says she pretends to study when they are back. In a later meeting she frets that she has a compulsion disorder she read about in a book, and Paimon and the Traveler suggest a doctor. In another she admits she had forgotten her homework and the interruption spared her a scolding. In the last she asks whether the battle will ever end, then founds the "Alliance of Artists to Overthrow the Evil Organization and Protect the Future of Fontaine", naming herself number zero and the Traveler and Paimon members one and two. In one meeting she also says she complained to Katheryne at the Guild and got only the stock phrase "ad astra abyssosque".

Continued. After all five are finished, a Hydro Elemental Monument sunk in the ground north of Echoes of the Deep Tides becomes a puzzle. Paimon, now fluent in Salsa's rules, has the Traveler lift it. The owner appears and accuses them of robbery: he is Ubu, a Guild adventurer and installation artist who made the objects and is angry that his "masterpieces" were rearranged. Salsa arrives and declares, as founder of her alliance, that she does not recognise them as art. Ubu argues that the artist defines what art is, and Salsa replies that an artist needs works people recognise. Paimon and the Traveler side with Salsa, noting that if no one understands his work it counts as a failure. Ubu leaves in distress, vowing not to give up. Salsa stays on, saying she finished her homework and will linger before going home. She remains in the area until the next daily reset, and the quest awards an achievement (Aesthetics of Ugliness).

Viewpoints. The five regional quests open, respectively, View From Mont Automnequi (Belleau), "Memories of Mont Esus" (Court of Fontaine), Fontaine Hot Springs (Central Beryl), The Seaside Village (Southeast Beryl) and Morning in the Beryl Mountains, Clear Weather (West Beryl). Which of the five meeting scripts plays depends on how many have already been completed, not on the region.

Revelations: - The strange objects are not traps or Guild training aids: Ubu, an adventurer, made them as installation art.
- Salsa's parents work at the Fontaine Research Institute and are often away; Salsa says that is why she can slip out to sketch.

- Salsa regards the Guild as an "evil organization" and its uniformed members as "evil green guys"; she is a child and the framing is comic. The Traveler is a Guild member but is exempted as a friend who "abandoned evil ways".
- Ubu insists the boundaries of art are set by the artist, a position the Traveler, Paimon and Salsa all reject.

Characters: Salsa is a quest-only child NPC, a would-be painter who describes herself as a great artist and insists she is not a small child; she calls Paimon "Lil' Miss". The wiki describes her as light-skinned with long blonde hair and purple eyes.
