Ubu is a quest-only adventurer in the Adventurers' Guild who describes himself as an installation artist and is touchy about criticism. Paimon and the Traveler appear throughout; Katheryne is mentioned only.

Salsa's parents are never seen. She quotes her father, who uses sayings such as that there is no trash that cannot be saved, only resources in the wrong place, and says he once forgot paperwork and was embarrassed for a week.

Consequences: Each quest gives Adventure EXP, Primogems and Mora, and the five regional ones unlock viewpoints. The Continued quest ends the series with the Hydro Monument raised and the argument between Salsa and Ubu unresolved. Neither Ubu's vow nor Salsa's alliance is followed up in the material read.

Salsa remains near the Hydro Monument until the next daily reset after the finale and can be spoken to, mentioning prospective alliance members she will vet.

Placement: Released in 4.0 with the Fontaine launch as optional world-quest content. The wiki gives the Archon Quest The Outlander Who Caught the Wind as the requirement, and the Continued quest follows the five regional ones. It has no bearing on the main plot.

key: The Whispers of the Crane and the White Rabbit
366.content:
Grus Nivis Chapter (Kamisato Ayaka) (also: Grus Nivis Chapter, Kamisato Ayaka's Story Quest, Ayaka's Story Quest, The Whispers of the Crane and the White Rabbit): Kamisato Ayaka's Story Quest. Ayaka finds the name Tsubaki in her late mother's notebook and asks the Traveler to help her find and visit Tsubaki, bringing a gift. The search leads to the discovery that Tsubaki was her mother's own secret persona, and Ayaka resolves to live without regrets.

The chapter has one act, The Whispers of the Crane and the White Rabbit, released in Version 2.0, with five quests: A Private Commission, Woven Wishes, Food From Afar, Lasting Promise and With You. It is a quiet story about friendship, grief and the freedoms Ayaka's rank has denied her.

The act also shows Ayaka as someone who has rarely had friends or been out in Inazuma in an ordinary way, and uses the Traveler's company to let her try ordinary things: shopping, a meal, a festival.

Plot: Ayaka asks the Traveler to accompany her to meet Tsubaki. She commissions a kimono and recovers stolen silk from ronin at Ritou, then tries to cook foreign food and fails, so the Traveler cooks instead. Following the notebook they find a hidden box under Tenshukaku and a second notebook, which shows Tsubaki and her mother were one person. Ayaka and the Traveler finish at a festival on Amakane Island.

A Private Commission. Ayaka tells the Traveler she found a note in her late mother's things naming Tsubaki, someone neither she nor Ayato had heard of. Custom requires a gift, and she would normally bring her brother but asks the Traveler instead.

Woven Wishes. Ayaka orders a kimono to her own design from Ogura Textiles & Kimonos, but the Sakoku Decree has cut off good Liyue silk. At Ritou, Kurisu of the International Trade Association says vagrants have stolen a silk shipment. Ayaka offers to help and, without revealing herself, drives off the ronin. Kurisu offers the silk free; Ayaka pays.

Food From Afar. At Kiminami Restaurant, the owner Anna tells the Traveler that Ayaka had few friends as a child because ordinary families feared her rank. An explosion follows from Ayaka's cooking attempt. The Traveler cooks Mushroom Pizza instead, and gives Anna the recipe. Ayaka thinks Tsubaki may be a fox envoy. She gives the Traveler a white heron hairpiece.

Lasting Promise. Following the notebook, they find a hidden box beneath Tenshukaku holding a second notebook. Ayaka learns her mother and Tsubaki were the same person, who had many wishes but was bound by duties to the clan and the commission.

With You. At Amakane Island's festival, Ayaka draws a prayer panel: she wants an Inazuma where everyone is happy, while the Traveler wishes to reunite with their sibling. Ayaka performs a dance to thank them.

Details. Ogura Mio is honoured by Ayaka's visit, and Ayaka whispers an additional request to Ogura. At Ritou, the ronin call Kurisu a worm and demand payment; Ayaka stops him paying. She is unconcerned that news of her intervention may spread because the ronin did not recognise her. She offers to have clothes tailored for the Traveler and Paimon, which the Traveler humbly declines. She asks what people in other nations wear, having never left Inazuma. She hopes to cook as well as the Traveler one day. Anna is happy Ayaka has made a friend and asks the Traveler to watch over her. On learning Anna spoke to them, Ayaka is sad because she knows she has few friends, until the Traveler and Paimon cheer her up.

The festival is nearly over when they arrive, and the merchants decide to stay open a little longer to keep Ayaka entertained. Ayaka decides, after reading the second notebook, to live each day without regrets. Before the search they collect the kimono and a second requested object from Ogura's shop.

Revelations: Tsubaki was Ayaka's mother herself; the name appears in her notebooks.

The notebooks show Ayaka's mother had many unfulfilled wishes because of her duties in the clan and the commission.

Ayaka does not know the truth when she sets out; she guesses Tsubaki is a fox envoy.

Characters: Kamisato Ayaka, the Traveler and Paimon.

Ogura Mio (Ogura Textiles & Kimonos), Kurisu (International Trade Association), Kiminami Anna (Kiminami Restaurant).

Ayato and Ayaka's late mother (as Kamisato Kayo and Tsubaki) appear only in conversation or the notebooks.

Consequences: Ayaka learns about her mother's hidden wishes and resolves to live without regrets. She forms a closer friendship with the Traveler, and gives them a white heron hairpiece.

Placement: Unlocks at Adventure Rank 30 after Chapter II Act I, The Immovable God and the Eternal Euthymia. Released in Version 2.0 and set during the Sakoku Decree, as Ayaka's difficulty in obtaining Liyue silk shows. No later acts exist as of 7.1.

367.content: A name found in a notebook belonging to Ayaka's late mother. Ayaka and the Traveler search for her, and discover that Tsubaki was her mother herself, who had many desires she could not fulfil because of her clan and commission responsibilities.

368.comment: Grus Nivis Chapter (Kamisato Ayaka): Ayaka's friendship
368.content: Anna, who runs Kiminami Restaurant, says Ayaka has been well regarded but had few friends because ordinary families avoided her out of fear. She is glad Ayaka now has the Traveler as a friend.

369.content:
Grus Serena Chapter (also: A Thousand Moonlit Miles, Xianyun's Story Quest, Grus Serena Chapter Act I): Grus Serena Chapter is Xianyun's Story Quest. In its one act, A Thousand Moonlit Miles, the adeptus formerly known as Cloud Retainer visits her disciples in human form, takes the name Xianyun, and helps the Traveler restore the memories of an elderly woman, Yuandai, who turns out to be a former crane in her care. It ends with Xianyun moving to Liyue Harbor.

It unlocks after The Crane Returns on the Wind at Adventure Rank 40. The tone is gentle and family-centred: a story of disciples, caring from a distance, and how adepti handle the passing of time among mortals.

Plot: Paimon visits Mt. Aocang and meets Cloud Retainer in human form. She goes to see Ganyu and Shenhe, takes the name Xianyun, and at Wanmin Restaurant meets Shuyu and her grandmother Yuandai, who has dementia. The group retraces Yuandai's past, then uses Xianyun's Suspensus Somnium Mechanism to restore her memory. Yuandai was a crane, Xianyun's follower, and reverts to her crane form. Shuyu becomes Xianyun's first disciple in the human world.

Xingqiu recalls a nameless heroine of chivalric novels who cleared spirits and bandits during a drought around fifty years ago and met an exorcist from Mt. Tianheng. The places tied to her are Wangshu Inn, Qingyun Peak and an area north of Jueyun Karst. At each, Yuandai recalls parts of her life, including the pills she took, and the group returns to Mt. Aocang for the device that helps her remember. Xianyun then moves to Liyue Harbor and sells some belongings, with Zhongli authenticating them.

**Leisurely Chatter.** Paimon decides to visit Cloud Retainer at Mt. Aocang and finds a woman at the table whom they realise is Cloud Retainer herself, in human form so that she can check on her disciples Ganyu and Shenhe without fuss. At Yuehai Pavilion Ganyu, speaking with Huixin, recognises her at once; Ganyu suggests she take a human name and she chooses Xianyun, with Ganyu explaining its meaning. Learning that Shenhe works at Wanmin Restaurant, they go there; Shenhe recognises her master immediately, which startles Xianyun, who had never shown her that form. During a break behind the restaurant Shenhe tells a story of her master losing a contest of flying machines to Moon Carver, and asks if Xianyun has ever felt lonely, which she declines to admit. At lunch, a girl called Shuyu shares their table with her grandmother Yuandai, who looks younger than expected and seems familiar to Xianyun. Shuyu explains that Yuandai's dementia has worsened and that her parents died young. Xianyun suggests retracing places from Yuandai's youth, and Shuyu says her father told her Yuandai was a martial-arts heroine.

**A Search for Secrets.** Xingqiu at Feiyun Commerce Guild recalls the nameless heroine and marks three sites. Shuyu wonders whether her late grandfather was the nameless exorcist, having once found a box of sigils, and privately tells the Traveler and Xianyun that a white crane once flew her to an adeptus's home and gave her a potion that cured a fever. Xianyun does not confirm that it was her. At Wangshu Inn Xiao teleports in, sensing a non-human presence, and is glad to find no trouble; he recalls fighting alongside her during the war and describes her as solemn and quiet then. Yuandai remembers having stayed at the inn to recover from an illness and being given Soul-Revitalizing Teapills by a merchant. North of Jueyun Karst, after Treasure Hoarders are driven off, she recalls staying in a house and then another, where Shuyu's father was born after she and her husband were chased by an unknown being in fog. At Qingyun Peak she points toward Mt. Aocang in fear.

**Lovely Dreams.** At Mt. Aocang Xianyun reveals the Suspensus Somnium Mechanism, which releases a gentle breeze and an adeptal tune that relaxes listeners. Under its influence Yuandai calls her Cloud Retainer and tells her story: once a long-lived wild crane who gained sentience and was taken in by Cloud Retainer, she admired the heroine tales and was given a potion of human mimicry lasting ten years. She fell in love with an exorcist from Mt. Tianheng and stayed with him past the potion's term, which led to her dementia. Ashamed, she left a letter and lived in seclusion. She now realises the merchant at the inn was Cloud Retainer in disguise. Xianyun confirms she was angry at the letter but, seeing his devotion, accepted the choice, and made the pills, and also healed Shuyu. Yuandai asks why she was not forced back; Xianyun says everyone must leave one day, but that she is welcome to return. As the medicine fades, Yuandai reverts to a crane without sentience and flies away. Shuyu asks to become Xianyun's disciple; Xianyun says she will move to Liyue Harbor, making Shuyu her first disciple in the human world.

Two days later at Chihu Rock, Xianyun argues with Shaozu over selling her items. His hired expert is Zhongli, who verifies the goods; Shaozu pays a deposit from Northland Bank, as the total is more than he can pay at once. Zhongli and Xianyun talk briefly about past and future before planning a dinner to introduce Shuyu to Ganyu and Shenhe.

While the Suspensus Somnium Mechanism runs, the Traveler dreams of their sibling and of travelling Teyvat together, and Xianyun notes they were not ready to wake. This is the quest's one touch on the Traveler's own search and is presented as a dream, not a revelation.

Revelations: - Yuandai was originally a long-lived wild crane, taken in by Cloud Retainer, not a human heroine.
- The merchant who gave Yuandai medicine at Wangshu Inn was Xianyun in disguise.
- Xianyun was also the white crane who helped the sick Shuyu.

- Xianyun says she had no need of human form after the war while living in the wilds.
- Yuandai's husband was an exorcist from Mt. Tianheng.

Characters: Xianyun (Cloud Retainer), Paimon and the Traveler; Ganyu, Shenhe, Xiao, Xingqiu, Zhongli; new characters Yuandai and Shuyu.

Supporting cast includes Huixin, Chef Mao, Madame Ping, Shaozu, Wenliu and Qingji. Xianyun is shown as warm, proud and bluntly practical, quietly caring for those she has taken in.

Consequences: Yuandai returns to her crane form and flies off, losing her sentience. Xianyun moves to Liyue Harbor and takes Shuyu as her first disciple in the human world, and adopts the name Xianyun in place of the title Cloud Retainer.

Placement: Released in Version 4.4 as Xianyun's Story Quest; requires The Crane Returns on the Wind (Interlude Chapter, Act I) and Adventure Rank 40. Xianyun's move to Liyue Harbor happens in this act.

370.comment: Grus Serena Chapter: Yuandai and Shuyu
370.content: Shuyu is a girl whose grandmother Yuandai has dementia. Yuandai was a long-lived crane taken in by Cloud Retainer, who took human form by a potion, married an exorcist from Mt. Tianheng and lived in seclusion. After her memory is restored she returns to crane form. Shuyu becomes Xianyun's first disciple in the human world.

371.comment: Grus Serena Chapter: Suspensus Somnium Mechanism
371.content: A device kept at Mt. Aocang that releases a soft breeze and an adeptal tune. It puts listeners in a relaxed, semi-hypnotic state that helps lost memories surface. Xianyun uses it on Yuandai and the Traveler.

372.content:
Hangout Event: Barbara (also: Barbara's Hangout Event, Wellspring of Healing, Barbara Hangout): Hangout Event: Barbara is a replayable, choice-driven story for Barbara, the Favonius Cathedral deaconess, added in Version 1.4. It has one act, Wellspring of Healing. The Traveler is asked to find Barbara, helps her avoid an overeager fan, tidies the Cathedral and shares a drink with her. It is lighthearted, low-stakes and has no effect on the main story.

Players need 2 Story Keys, Adventure Rank 26 and the Archon Quest Song of the Dragon and Freedom to start it. Different choices lead to five named endings. It is permanent, repeatable content, not a limited-time event.

The act is built around Barbara's popularity as a public figure in Mondstadt. Sister Victoria's concern at the start frames the day as the Traveler looking out for Barbara.

Some Hangout Events use a Heartbeat Value that can end the quest if it empties. In this act the notable hidden scoring is in the conversation with Albert (the quest Sudden Shouting), where small answers decide which of two branches follows.

Plot: After Victoria's request, the Traveler finds Barbara in Wolvendom. Hearing Albert approach, Barbara does not want to deal with him yet. The Traveler can chase Albert away, which is decided by a hidden score from the conversation. If it goes badly, Albert keeps searching and the day ends on an anticlimax (Untimely Enthusiasm). Otherwise Barbara goes to check on Tunner while the Traveler returns to the Cathedral, where Victoria asks them to clean it for Barbara.
Barbara then returns and offers the choice of drink. If the Traveler picks the new drink at The Cat's Tail, Barbara goes ahead and is swamped by a group of fans. Persuading each fan to leave her alone, or failing to, still ends with the two relaxing over drinks (A Holiday in Mondstadt).

If the Traveler picks the home-made Chilibrew instead, they must gather ingredients: Jueyun Chili and Sweet Flowers. The two can split up or stay together.
- Split up: the Traveler picks Jueyun Chili near Stone Gate while Barbara gathers Sweet Flowers in Whispering Woods. They meet in the Woods, where Barbara says she has been trailing Treasure Hoarders who were harassing a merchant. After they rescue Caishan, the merchant, he offers a Liyue Chilibrew or Sweet Flowers in exchange for Barbara's own recipe; the Liyue Chilibrew route leads to A Fiery Flavor From Liyue.
- Stay together: in Whispering Woods they meet a wounded man named Uwe. If the Traveler helps Barbara heal him on the spot, he is grateful, and Barbara can make her home-made Chilibrew (The Taste of Hard Work). If they instead take him to the Knights of Favonius, he tries to escape because he is a Treasure Hoarder; the Traveler defeats him and the day ends on Incompletely Cured.

The wiki's quest list for the act names: Sister Victoria's Vexation, The Church's Affairs, The First Chilibrew Ingredient, Knight and Deaconess, Ready for Battle!, The Second Chilibrew Ingredient, Healing Is My Job, Ulterior Motive...?, A Very Special Beverage and Sudden Shouting. A side branch, Temporary Relief From the Fanfare, covers the choice to wait out Albert deeper in the forest, where Barbara's reasons for joining the Church or picking herbs alone can come up in conversation (Of Wolfhooks Red). A separate answer there ends the event early.

Revelations: The act reveals very little lore. It is character material: Barbara is well known and sought out by admirers, and the Church sisters worry when she is away for long. It also shows that Wolfhooks from Wolvendom, Sweet Flowers from Whispering Woods and Jueyun Chili from Liyue are what go into her Chilibrew.

It also shows Treasure Hoarders operating in the Whispering Woods, near Mondstadt, and a Hoarder pretending to be an injured traveler.

Characters: Barbara, the Traveler and Paimon are the main characters. Sister Victoria, Albert (leader of the Barbara Fan Club) and Tunner appear early on.

Branch characters include the merchant Caishan, the wounded Uwe (a Treasure Hoarder), and fans at The Cat's Tail named Herman, Schulz and Susie.

Consequences: The Hangout Event has no lasting effect on the main story. Completing endings grants rewards (Adventure EXP, Primogems, Hero's Wit, talent or ascension materials and Barbara's special dish), and endings can be displayed as Lingering Moments in the Serenitea Pot mansion.

Hangout Events also award Memories of the Heart achievements, generally one for unlocking all endings. Each ending gives a different reward set, so replaying is expected.

Placement: Released in Version 1.4. It unlocks after Song of the Dragon and Freedom but sits outside the main-story timeline: a day in Mondstadt with no dated events.

Its structure (named endings, branching choices, rewards by number of endings reached) is shared with every other Hangout Event.

373.comment: Hangout Event: Barbara: Barbara Fan Club
373.content:
In Barbara's Hangout Event, Albert leads the Barbara Fan Club, a group of enthusiastic admirers who look for Barbara around Mondstadt. Barbara does not want to meet Albert in Wolvendom, so the Traveler either sends him away or leads her off. Later, fans at The Cat's Tail crowd Barbara until the Traveler persuades them to leave her in peace. They are portrayed as harmless and over-eager.

Albert's outcome depends on a hidden score from the Traveler's answers: a score of zero or higher leaves him still searching (Untimely Enthusiasm), while a negative one makes him more willing to be reasoned with.

374.content: Chilibrew is the drink at the center of Barbara's Hangout Event. Her home-made version needs Jueyun Chili and Sweet Flowers, which the Traveler and Barbara collect around Stone Gate and Whispering Woods. On another route the merchant Caishan gives them a Liyue Chilibrew in exchange. The ending for the home-made brew is The Taste of Hard Work, and the one for the Liyue version is A Fiery Flavor From Liyue.

375.comment: Hangout Event: Barbara: Barbara Hangout Endings
375.content: The five endings are: Untimely Enthusiasm (Albert keeps searching for Barbara after a failed conversation), A Fiery Flavor From Liyue (Caishan's Liyue Chilibrew), The Taste of Hard Work (home-made Chilibrew), Incompletely Cured (Uwe is revealed to be a Treasure Hoarder after being brought to the Knights) and A Holiday in Mondstadt (drinks at The Cat's Tail after dealing with the fans).

376.content:
Hangout Event: Beidou (also: When the Crux Shines Bright, Beidou Hangout Event, Beidou's Hangout): Beidou's Hangout Event, a replayable, choice-driven side story in which the captain of the Crux fleet invites the Traveler aboard the Alcor to celebrate the fleet's return from Inazuma. It has one act, When the Crux Shines Bright, and five endings, depending on which of three routes you take: sailor training, a quiet treasure hunt, or a day of business in Liyue Harbor. It unlocks after the Inazuma Archon Quest Omnipresence Over Mortals.

Unlocking needs two Story Keys, Adventure Rank 30 and the Archon Quest Omnipresence Over Mortals; it arrived in Version 2.3. The act holds five quests: A Special Guest (the hub), Life on the High Seas, Beneath the Surface, Guili Plains Treasure Hunt and Qingce Village Treasure Hunt. Hangout Events as a whole are replayable permanent content, so none of this is limited to a time window.

The tone is warm and crew-centred: Beidou reveals how she leads (trading favours, trusting specialists and keeping her crew's welfare in view) and, on one route, the harsh story of her childhood. Each ending is a "Memory" that can be displayed in the Serenitea Pot.

Plot: In A Special Guest the Traveler returns to the Alcor and is greeted by cheerful crew (Sea Drake, Furong, Huixing) who want to recruit them after hearing of the end of the Vision Hunt Decree. Beidou declines to let the crew press the Traveler, then offers a choice. Interested in sailor life, the Traveler goes to training; otherwise Beidou takes them aside to talk about a map she found.

**Sailor training.** Beidou explains that new recruits are split into the Shield of the Crux (survival, navigation, entertainment) and the Spear of the Crux (naval fighting and cargo deals). Choosing the Shield leads to Life on the High Seas; choosing the Spear leads to Beneath the Surface.

**Treasure hunt.** Beidou found a battered treasure map in an Inazuman pirates' wreck. She asks the Traveler to read it. Naming Guili Plains starts the Guili Plains Treasure Hunt; naming Qingce Village starts the Qingce Village Treasure Hunt.

**Life on the High Seas.** The Traveler learns from three crew: Yinxing (the ship's surgeon, who warns that the biggest danger to newcomers is underestimating the sea), Huixing (navigator, chart reading and the coloured distance lines on the supplementary chart) and Xu Liushi (lookout, who explains the warning signs of a waterspout). Beidou then quizzes the Traveler with three questions. Scoring zero or one sends them to Beneath the Surface instead; two or three correct answers pass them to the recreation programme. Because the regular photography teacher is ill, the Traveler becomes the teacher for the crew's photography class, and Beidou is cajoled into being the model. Choosing Yaoguang Shoal or the summit of Mt. Tianheng as a photo location ends the event without a Memory (Beidou prefers fun with her crew to a lifeless Kamera). Naming the abandoned fishing village near Wangshu Inn leads to the best-known story of the event (see the childhood entry). Depending on the pose chosen the event ends with Photography Class for Two or with the comedic Flirtatious ending.

**Beneath the Surface.** On old Skirmish Boats from the Alcor, Beidou sets a timed boat-handling course in the Sea of Clouds, then takes the Traveler to Liyue Harbor to show "the less official side" of the fleet's trade. Following coded phrases, the pair deal with two fishmongers and a warehouse owner, Mr. Iron Abacus. That night the Millelith arrive on a tip and search the goods, finding only potatoes, flour and correct paperwork. Beidou explains that she and the Traveler are both on the Ministry of Civil Affairs' watch list, so their visible presence acted as cover while her accountant Mora-Grubber ran the real, quiet transaction. A firework over the Domain of Guyun signals success. Beidou notes Ningguang is, in a sense, her business partner (Beidou fetches rare treasures Ningguang wants) and says she will say more if the Traveler ever finishes their journey. Ending: Once Everything Is Over.

**Guili Plains Treasure Hunt.** Treasure Hoarders led by Golden Alligator are already digging; they surrender at Beidou's name. Beidou honours first-come, first-served, offers to pay, and they hand it over as an apology, receiving an offer of honest port work in return. They later report back with a poem clue to a second cache, and the Traveler solves it by combining the ruins, the red-leafed tree and the time of day. The hoard is a Northland Bank cheque and a note left by an Inazuma-bound traveller for his elderly mother, who lives in a wooden house by the sea. Beidou has the former hoarders deliver the cheque as a government welfare payment, and the Traveler brings a Sakura Bloom as a keepsake from her son. Ending: Sakura Blooms Upon Guili Fell.

**Qingce Village Treasure Hunt.** In Qingce Village, Beidou is asked to settle three small disputes (a farmer and a neighbour over finches, a sunlit window and a tree planted by a dead father, and a farmer and a helper over a chest) before she can claim the chest. She resolves them with a mix of fair judgment, an offer to buy the finches, and promised payments from the Crux's village relief funds, depending on the Traveler's advice. At a village banquet she tells the Traveler why she trades in favours; they open the chest and find only rotten cabbage. Ending: Between Us.

**Qingce disputes in detail.** Ji is accused by Wenjing of letting a flock of wild finches destroy half her crops; the Traveler can hold him responsible (Beidou buys the finches and makes him compensate Wenjing) or call him innocent (Beidou pays from the Crux's relief fund, which Granny Ruoxin says is never used up). Pops Xing complains that a tree planted by Ren's late father blocks his sunlight; Ren says the tree was meant to suppress bad family luck and honours his father's dying wish, though he does not share the superstition himself. Beidou either has the tree moved with crew help and a gardener, or lets it stand with compensation for Pops Xing. Defu and Changping quarrel over a chest turned up while ploughing Defu's land; Beidou offers a legal expert from Liyue Harbor at her own cost, and when neither wants that, asks them to hand her the chest, promising the Crux's support in return.

**Guili poem.** The clue is a short verse about gazing at forsaken ruins while lying beneath a red-leafed tree whose crooked shadow marks the spot as dusk falls; the Traveler works out the vantage point and the shadow's direction rather than Golden Alligator, who admits he is not clever enough.

Revelations: Beidou, in her own words, was homeless and about five or six years old when she reached a fishing village near Wangshu Inn and was taken in by the village chief. After the chief fell ill and died the following winter and the catch shrank, the villagers blamed her and drove her out, citing her name: Beidou is the Northern Dipper constellation, whose Alcor star is read as an omen of death, and some villagers shouted that the Northern Dipper controls death. She tells the Traveler this at the empty village (known to its former residents as "Downriver"). The Traveler can answer that they too might be called cursed, and Beidou accepts the company: she will share the blame, as captain, for anyone who tries to scapegoat the Traveler.

Other established details: Beidou describes the Crux as an armed carrier that also trades, with some of that trade not entirely above-board; she says almost every confrontation in the fleet's history was settled by negotiation, that skirmish craft and armed crew are enough for most situations, and that the Alcor itself would open fire only in a fight to the death. She also mentions that Kazuha has led poetry, music and communal wind-listening sessions for the crew. Her philosophy of favours (an unseen net of mutual obligation that keeps a person from falling alone) is stated in the Qingce route.

Characters: Beidou (captain of the Crux; confident, generous, and fond of drinking) carries the event. The Traveler is the player-chosen guest, and many dialogue options colour the mood. Notable recurring Crux crew: Sea Drake, Furong, Huixing (navigator), Yinxing (surgeon), Xu Liushi (lookout), Juza (chief mate), Mora-Grubber (accountant). One-route characters include Golden Alligator and his Treasure Hoarders (Guili), the villagers of Qingce (Granny Ruoxin, Ji, Wenjing, Pops Xing, Ren, Changping, Defu), Mr. Iron Abacus, Nei and Wai, and the Millelith squad.

The wiki's trivia notes that Minamoto Kotomi stands, non-interactive, outside the wooden house during the delivery step; the dialogue itself speaks only of an old lady living there.

Consequences: Each ending is a self-contained "Memory"; no ending changes the open-world story or any other quest. Rewards scale with how many endings the player has unlocked (Primogems, Adventure EXP, Hero's Wit and other items). The Guili route establishes that the Crux will give former Treasure Hoarders a path to honest work, and the Qingce route that villagers treat the fleet as an ally whose members come from their villages.

Placement: Release order: 2.3 (hangout system introduced earlier in 1.4). Story order: set after the Traveler returns from Inazuma, so after the Archon Quest Omnipresence Over Mortals and after the Vision Hunt Decree has been abolished. Characters refer to the Traveler as the person who ended it and to the Liyue Harbor event as past.

377.comment: Hangout Event: Beidou: Beidou's Childhood and the Name Beidou
377.content: In the Life on the High Seas photography route the Traveler brings Beidou to the empty fishing village near Wangshu Inn. She says it was once called Downriver because the villagers came from a place called Upriver, who taught her fishing. At five or six she chased a stray dog that had snatched half a rice bun; the dog collapsed and died, and fishermen fed her, and the village chief took her in. A year or two later the chief died, the catch fell, and the villagers called her a bringer of bad luck and drove her out, shouting about the Northern Dipper and death. She learned her name was a constellation, with the Alcor as an omen of death, only then. She recounts it without self-pity.

378.content: A Treasure Hoarder leader who is digging for treasure on Guili Plains when Beidou arrives. He panics at her name, begs mercy for his men, and is spared. He and his crew choose to leave banditry for port work offered by the Crux, and later share a poem clue to a second treasure. He wants to join the Crux someday; Beidou says nothing is impossible if they earn her crew's respect.

379.comment: Hangout Event: Beidou: Mr. Iron Abacus and the Guyun Deal
379.content: Mr. Iron Abacus is the warehouse owner in Beidou's covert deal in Liyue Harbor. When the Millelith raid the meeting, they find only ordinary sacks, so Beidou's presence works as a decoy while her accountant Mora-Grubber runs the actual transaction. The event portrays the Crux as an armed carrier that also trades goods outside strict official channels.

380.comment: Hangout Event: Beidou: Beidou's Philosophy of Favours
380.content: In Qingce Village, Beidou says she is not an arbiter like Ningguang or Yanfei; her strength is trading favours. She argues that favours keep people connected and form an invisible net that catches anyone who falls, and that these bonds, not law, are what the Crux has survived on. She admits some of her solutions are "stupid" but says the point is that nobody leaves feeling cheated.

381.comment: Hangout Event: Beidou: Crux Training Staff
381.content: Yinxing is the Crux's surgeon and has Beidou's full authority to keep unfit recruits ashore. Huixing is the fleet's navigator, deciphering old charts with books Beidou obtains. Xu Liushi is the lookout, once a laughingstock for a drunken fall into the sea, and credits Beidou's judgment for his place. Juza is the chief mate who schedules the training. Together they show that Beidou lets each person master a role so the fleet does not rest on her alone.

382.content:
Hangout Event: Bennett (also: Bennett's Hangout Event, Fantastic Voyage, Bennett Hangout): Hangout Event: Bennett is a replayable, choice-driven story for the Adventurers' Guild member Bennett, released in Version 1.4, with one act, Fantastic Voyage. Bennett asks to adventure with the Traveler, and whichever outing they pick, his famously bad luck shapes the day. It is a comedy with no effect on the main story.

It requires 2 Story Keys, Adventure Rank 26 and the Archon Quest Song of the Dragon and Freedom. There are six endings. Permanent, repeatable content.

The three outings (around town, in the wilds, in ruins) each show a different side of his luck. The ruins routes also bring out how he copes with it: he leaves decisions to the Traveler, apologises for trouble he did not choose, and is delighted when something simply works.

The act is built from the quests Adventurous Acquaintance, Something... Other Than Adventure?, What Is This, a Day Trip?, Treacherous Thermadon and Expansive Eya.

Plot: Around town, Bennett needs materials. With Wind Comes Glory is out of stock, the Good Hunter turns them away because the cook, Sara, is busy with a meal order for a delegation from Snezhnaya, and Mondstadt General Goods seems to be offering 50% off everything. When Blanche finally appears she says the shop is closed and the promotion was for the day before (ending: Fruitless Anticipation).
In the wilds, Bennett suggests a stroll in a dandelion meadow. The dandelions have been stripped of seeds, a monster camp is empty and its chests hold only vegetables and a little Mora, and the weather turns into a thunderstorm. Jack arrives to take Bennett home because his dads have been asking for him, and the weather clears the moment he goes (Hasty Farewell).

In the ruins, the route depends on whether the two prepare food first.
- Food prepared: they make an Ominous Dish and go to the Deserted Ruins of Thermadon. A mechanism closes the door behind them, then jams. They meet Royce, another adventurer stuck there, who blames Bennett and then asks for food. If the Traveler lets Bennett share, Royce collapses from food poisoning (Taste Tester Royce). If not, Bennett eats the dish himself, hoping it will knock him out and let his bad luck lapse for a while (Ready to Make Sacrifices).
- No food: they go to the Deserted Ruins of Eya and find mechanisms. If Bennett operates one alone, they are trapped (No Wonder It's a Top-Class Commission). If the Traveler acts with him, they solve a series of puzzles and reach a Luxurious Chest, and Bennett is thrilled (Fortunate Outcome).

In Eya, Bennett is explicit that he is rarely lucky and defers the choice of mechanism to the Traveler. In a later room he says four people would be needed for the mechanisms, and explains that Benny's Adventure Team now exists only in name. Katheryne has not deregistered it out of sympathy, and Royce, Heckler and Jack were all former members who left because of his bad luck. In Thermadon, Royce tells the Traveler why he left: years of accidents such as ruins collapsing, lightning and a sudden explosion. Bennett apologises for the trouble he caused, and the Traveler can encourage him to look after himself instead of putting others first.

Revelations: The act confirms that Bennett's bad luck is a long-running, widely known fact, that Benny's Adventure Team has dwindled to Bennett alone, and that his former teammates left because of the danger, without bitterness.

Jack says Bennett's dads have all been asking for him, and Bennett says he wants Benny's Adventure Team's name known across Teyvat.

Characters: Bennett and the Traveler are the main characters.

Depending on the route: Sara, Blanche and the shops of Mondstadt (town); Jack (wilds); Royce (Thermadon ruins); Katheryne is mentioned in the Eya ruins.

Consequences: No lasting effect on the main story. Rewards are given per ending (Adventure EXP, Primogems, Hero's Wit, talent or ascension materials, Bennett's special dish), and endings can be shown as Lingering Moments in the Serenitea Pot.

Endings are independent of one another; none leads on to the next.

Placement: Released in Version 1.4. It unlocks after Song of the Dragon and Freedom but sits outside the main timeline, with no dated events.

Like other Hangout Events, it is a standalone day that does not alter the world.

383.comment: Hangout Event: Bennett: Benny's Adventure Team
383.content: In Bennett's Hangout Event, Bennett says Benny's Adventure Team is now a team only in name, because he is the only member left. Royce, Heckler and Jack were once part of it; they left because of the accidents that follow his bad luck. Katheryne has kept the team registered out of pity. Bennett hopes its name will one day be known all over Teyvat.

384.content: Royce is a former member of Benny's Adventure Team who left after repeated accidents. In the Thermadon ruins route he is trapped alongside Bennett and the Traveler, blames Bennett, then asks for food. If he eats the Ominous Dish he falls ill; if refused, he parts ways with Bennett, wishing him well.

385.comment: Hangout Event: Bennett: Bennett Hangout Endings
385.content: The six endings are: Fruitless Anticipation (the shop discount was yesterday's), Hasty Farewell (Jack takes Bennett home and the weather clears), Taste Tester Royce (Royce eats the Ominous Dish first), Ready to Make Sacrifices (Bennett eats it himself), No Wonder It's a Top-Class Commission (trapped in the Eya ruins) and Fortunate Outcome (the Eya puzzles are solved and a Luxurious Chest is found).

386.content:
Hangout Event: Chongyun (also: Signs of Evil, Chongyun Hangout Event, Chongyun's Hangout): Chongyun's Hangout Event, a replayable, choice-driven side story. The earnest young exorcist approaches the Traveler on Liyue Harbor's wharf asking whether they have seen any evil spirits. The one-act event, Signs of Evil, branches on whether the Traveler tells him his leads are far-fetched (popsicles, children and the Wanwen Bookhouse) or humours him (the Test of Courage at Wuwang Hill), and ends in one of six outcomes, none of which changes the wider story.

It was added in Version 1.4 with the Hangout Event feature and requires two Story Keys, Adventure Rank 26 and completion of the Archon Quest Song of the Dragon and Freedom. Its quests are Hard to Track, Distant Gaze, The Exorcist's Path, Popsicles and Their Curious Uses, For A Child's Smile, Test of Courage, The Bottom of Things, Sudden Discomfort, Ever Deeper, Killjoy and Independent Actions. The tone is gentle and comic: Chongyun takes everything seriously, and the humour comes from the gap between his earnestness and what the Traveler finds.

Because Chongyun's pure-yang constitution (managed with cold popsicles) shapes the event, many beats revolve around keeping his yang energy in check. All endings are Memories that can be shown in the Serenitea Pot.

Plot: In Hard to Track Chongyun explains that he is an exorcist, that all demons and monsters are "evil spirits" to those who practise exorcism, and that he protects Liyue's people from them. He praises the yakshas and says exorcists and yakshas have long guarded Liyue together, one openly and one in secret. He then lists several clues he has gathered, including a flyer for the Test of Courage at Wuwang Hill. The Traveler's choice here forks the event.

**Branch one: A Curious Gaze.** If the Traveler says the clues sound far-fetched, Chongyun grows dejected, his pure-yang energy heats him, and he eats a popsicle to cool down. A boy, Dalong, watches them. The boy admires the popsicle, saying he and his sister are poor and rarely eat snacks. Giving the boy one popsicle sends him off happy and the pair visit Wanwen Bookhouse to check Chongyun's clues (given by his friend Xingqiu), find them unreliable, and then follow a last snippet to Wuwang Hill. There they find strange smoke Chongyun says an evil spirit left, fight the hilichurls around it and cannot catch the spirit, but he counts the trip a success. Ending: Blessing in Disguise. Giving the boy both popsicles instead leaves Chongyun short; the Traveler helps him make more at Wanmin Restaurant. A cooling mix or sweet mix works. A "curious" mix with spicy ingredients sends Chongyun haywire and ends the event: Can't Beat This Heat. With good popsicles, they take some to Dalong and his sister Little Le, play hide-and-seek and share cold noodles. Ending: Idle Amusements.

**Branch two: To Take a Test of Courage.** If the Traveler humours him, they join the Test of Courage at Wuwang Hill, where couples are being frightened by staged scares. The staff (run by Zhouliang, with Fu San'er) are annoyed by Chongyun's questions. Drinking a potion can leave Chongyun suffering from unstable yang energy, requiring cooling recipes (Cryo Slime condensate or Cryo Whopperflower nectar) in Sudden Discomfort. In The Bottom of Things or Ever Deeper the Traveler learns the "ghost" is a staff member in costume, and in Killjoy must decide how to tell Chongyun. Telling him ends the route at Nothing Gained or Small Regrets, depending on the path.

**Independent Actions.** If, after being told it was all staged, the Traveler asks to investigate the strange mist found earlier, they split up. A girl ghost named Qianqian asks the Traveler to lead Chongyun away because his yang energy frightens her; she offers to scare off the troublemakers if he lets her go. While Chongyun argues with the staff about whether they are using ghosts for profit or running a scam, panic breaks out and the staff leave. Chongyun learns there is no evil spirit but a wandering ghost who scared the crowd to save him, and decides, if she harms no one, to pretend he never knew about her, stating that he will purge her if she ever does. Ending: Goodbyes.

**Quest tree (for reference).** Hard to Track forks into Distant Gaze (the far-fetched-clues branch) or Test of Courage. Distant Gaze leads to The Exorcist's Path (Wanwen Bookhouse, then Wuwang Hill, ending Blessing in Disguise) or to Popsicles and Their Curious Uses (mix choice; the curious mix ends at Can't Beat This Heat, the others go to For A Child's Smile and Idle Amusements). Test of Courage leads to The Bottom of Things (ending Nothing Gained), Sudden Discomfort (the Cryo recipes, which then continue to Killjoy) or Ever Deeper, which also goes to Killjoy. Killjoy ends at Small Regrets if the Traveler suggests heading back, or continues to Independent Actions (ending Goodbyes) if they suggest investigating the mist.

**Rewards.** Each ending gives Adventure EXP plus a rotating prize: Primogems, Hero's Wit, Guide to Diligence, Shivada Jade Fragments or Cold Noodles with Mountain Delicacies (Chongyun's special dish).

Revelations: The event establishes that Chongyun regards exorcist work as an ordinary job that simply must be done, that he respects the yakshas, and that in the Qianqian ending he weighs good and evil in each spirit rather than treating every ghost as an enemy. It also reaffirms that his pure-yang energy needs regular cooling to stay under control.

Qianqian is the ghost of a young child and is not shown to be malevolent; Chongyun's decision to spare her on his own responsibility is the closest the event comes to a character statement. The "Blessing in Disguise" ending carries his line that the sights and encounters along the way are as much a reward as catching a spirit.

Characters: Chongyun leads; the Traveler is the player guide. Dalong and Little Le are siblings, young children who say they are poor; Dalong hurries off to Chihu Rock with his popsicle. Zhouliang and Fu San'er run the Test of Courage at Wuwang Hill, with other staff and visitors (Uncle Jia, Lu Zheng, Dandan, Junjun, Chan'er) appearing in the scares. Xingqiu is mentioned as the friend who passed Chongyun the rumours.

Consequences: No ending changes any other quest or the wider story. Rewards scale with the number of endings unlocked; the six endings are Blessing in Disguise, Idle Amusements, Can't Beat This Heat, Nothing Gained, Goodbyes and Small Regrets.

Placement: Release order: Version 1.4, alongside the hangout system itself. Story order: it requires the Liyue Archon Quest Song of the Dragon and Freedom, so it takes place after Rex Lapis' apparent death and the Traveler's Liyue adventure. Nothing in the event depends on later story.

387.comment: Hangout Event: Chongyun: Test of Courage at Wuwang Hill
387.content: A staged "haunted" attraction at Wuwang Hill where visitors, often couples, are frightened by staff in costume. Chongyun hopes it hides a real evil spirit. The staff, led by Zhouliang, treat it as entertainment and resent being questioned; a real ghost, Qianqian, is present in one branch.

388.content: The ghost of a young child at Wuwang Hill. She fears Chongyun's pure-yang energy, which she believes could make her disappear, and she asks the Traveler to lead him away. After scaring off the staff, she is spared by Chongyun on the condition that she never harms anyone.

389.comment: Hangout Event: Chongyun: Dalong and Little Le
389.content: Dalong is a boy who approaches Chongyun and the Traveler hoping for a popsicle for himself and his sister Little Le; the siblings say they are poor and seldom get snacks. In the best path Chongyun plays hide-and-seek with them and serves cold noodles, and the children invite him to play more.

390.content: Chongyun keeps popsicles on hand to suppress his pure-yang constitution, which makes him run hot and can destabilise when he is stressed. The event lets the Traveler make cooling or sweet versions at Wanmin Restaurant from Mist Flowers and Qingxin, or Valberries and Sunsettias, while a spicy "curious" version backfires.

391.content:
Hangout Event: Diona (also: Diona's Hangout Event, The Cat and the Cocktail, Diona Hangout): Hangout Event: Diona is a replayable, choice-driven story for Diona, the bartender of The Cat's Tail, released in Version 1.5, with one act, The Cat and the Cocktail. The Traveler visits The Cat's Tail, where Diona is out of ingredients and exasperated with her drunken customers, and joins her either in finding the bar's missing cats or in hunting for ingredients for a new special cocktail. It is a comedy with no effect on the main story.

It requires 2 Story Keys, Adventure Rank 26 and the Archon Quest Song of the Dragon and Freedom. There are five endings. Permanent, repeatable content.

The act shows two sides of Diona: her dislike of drunkenness and of cats (she insists she does not understand why people like them), and the pride she takes as a bartender. It also gives a glimpse of her relationship with her father, Draff.

Its quest list is The Cat's Tail's Bartender, To Catch a Kitten, A Special Base Drink, The Shadow Over Dadaupa, Samachurl Herbal Soup, Special Cocktailing Condiments and Exchanging Pointers.

Plot: Cats branch: the Traveler helps Diona find three cats (Roger, Nelson and Paisley) around Mondstadt, using a cat toy for one and cat food for another. Depending on later choices the story ends either with the cats behaving unpredictably (The Unfathomable Felines) or with the cats coming home and The Cat's Tail starting a cat party (Cat Party).
Cocktail branch: Diona decides to use the herbal soup that samachurls make in Dadaupa Gorge as a base for a new cocktail. A hunter told her the soup smells overwhelming. She and the Traveler go to the gorge and meet Allan, a hunter who works with her father.

In Dadaupa Gorge, Diona's father Draff has wandered off drunk, believing he is hunting hilihounds and hilihogs. Which ending follows depends on how the Traveler handles it:
- Diona brews a concoction from the soup to sober Draff up, keeps the rest, and the day ends with her special cocktail back at The Cat's Tail (Diona's Special).
- The Traveler instead mixes the potent soup under Diona's guidance, and a whiff of it makes Draff retch. Diona remarks that it is the best ingredient for the worst possible drink and doubts it can be used in a cocktail ("I... Only Had... a Little...", whose tagline is that wine is fine in moderation).
Another route, Special Cocktailing Condiments, has Diona collecting fresh fish in Springvale and slime condensate near Dawn Winery for her cocktail, where she meets Connor and Elzer. In Exchanging Pointers she and Connor trade mixing tips and each speeds up their mixing in turn. The ending line has Diona telling Connor and Elzer to stop joking around (The Ultimate Special).

Draff, once sober, forgets what he did and promises to drink less. Diona says she has seen worse and lists earlier episodes: chasing dogs and calling them hilihounds, filling bottles from the town's spring water and drinking from them, and asking Myweiss to write a song about a hunter and his loyal hilihound. When Draff is sobered up she mutters a quiet thanks, then tells him not to drink so much. Allan was about to report to the Knights of Favonius if they had taken longer.

Revelations: Little lore is revealed. The act confirms that Diona thinks of herself as a professional bartender and is annoyed by adults who cannot control their drinking, that her father Draff drinks heavily and takes part in hunts with Allan, and that The Cat's Tail is a popular bar with resident cats.

Diona refers to the Kätzlein bloodline when a customer calls her a kitty, and her affection for her father shows through her irritation. The hangout does not explain why she dislikes cats.

Characters: Diona and the Traveler are the main characters.

Supporting characters include Margaret and Nimrod at The Cat's Tail, Draff and Allan in Dadaupa Gorge, the Dawn Winery's Connor and Elzer, and the cats Roger, Nelson and Paisley.

Consequences: No lasting effect on the main story. Rewards are given per ending (Adventure EXP, Primogems, Hero's Wit, talent or ascension materials, Diona's special dish), and endings can be shown as Lingering Moments in the Serenitea Pot.

The wiki notes that Jackie Lastra temporarily voiced Diona in the Hangout Event until Version 2.4, when Dina Sherman returned to the role.

Placement: Released in Version 1.5. It unlocks after Song of the Dragon and Freedom but sits outside the main timeline, with no dated events.

Like other Hangout Events, it is a standalone day that does not alter the world.

392.comment: Hangout Event: Diona: The Cat's Tail Bartender
392.content: In Diona's Hangout Event she works the bar at The Cat's Tail, which is known for specialty drinks and its cats. She refuses to compromise on her recipes: any drink made by her hands, she says, can only be a good one. Customers love the cocktails, which is why she is often out of ingredients.

393.comment: Hangout Event: Diona: Samachurl Herbal Soup
393.content: A strong-smelling soup made by samachurls in Dadaupa Gorge. Diona hears of it from an adventurer and wants it as a base for a cocktail. In the hangout it proves powerful enough to sober up Draff immediately, but Diona decides it is probably unusable in a drink.

394.content: The five endings are: Cat Party, The Unfathomable Felines, Diona's Special, "I... Only Had... a Little..." and The Ultimate Special.

395.content:
Hangout Event: Faruzan (also: A Confounding Conundrum, Faruzan Hangout Event, Faruzan Hangout, A Mysterious Senior...?, Essential Classic, Early Learning Mechanism, Wanderings of a Lonesome Shadow): Faruzan's Hangout Event, a single-act, branching side story added in Version 3.5. Tighnari asks the Traveler to help bring the veteran Haravatat researcher Faruzan to Pardis Dhyai for help with banned research, and the Traveler finds her cornered by Akademiya administrators over her lack of teaching or collaboration. Depending on the Traveler's choices the story becomes a reading course for Collei, a children's-toy collaboration with Kshahrewar and Acara Crafts, or a trip into the desert about a machine called the Ruin Wanderer, where Faruzan is reunited with an old companion. There are five endings.

The act is A Confounding Conundrum. It needs Adventure Rank 40, two Story Keys, and completion of the Archon Quest Akasha Pulses, the Kalpa Flame Rises and the story quest The Unanswerable Problems. It opens with A Mysterious Senior...? and then splits into three lines: Essential Classic, Early Learning Mechanism and Wanderings of a Lonesome Shadow.

It is where the player sees Faruzan's everyday friction with the present-day Akademiya, her relationship with Collei, and the fate of the machine she left behind a century earlier. As a Hangout Event it is permanent content, not a limited-time event.

Plot: Tighnari is waiting at Pardis Dhyai for Faruzan and sends Collei, who is nervous around her, with the Traveler to Sumeru City to find out why she is late. They find Faruzan being pressed by an Akademiya official, Nadwah, to either teach a course or join a collaborative project, because Haravatat students and other advisers have complained that she does neither. She puts the matter off, and the Traveler has a private word with Collei.

The player then chooses how to help. Either they help settle her Akademiya problem first, choosing between a Haravatat course and a Kshahrewar collaboration, or they find a pretext to take her to Pardis Dhyai. Helping with the course leads to Essential Classic, in which Faruzan founds a reading course for Collei as a public pilot, hunts for teaching material and learns how much taste in books has changed. Helping with the collaboration leads to Early Learning Mechanism, in which she designs a puzzle toy and a reference book for Acara Crafts. Taking the pretext route leads to Wanderings of a Lonesome Shadow, in which she repairs Collei's companion Karkata and is drawn into a desert mystery. Every route ends with a short ending scene; the five endings are Stories of the Past, Knowledge is Wealth!, The Gardener and the Nursery, Start Over, and "Welcome Back, Faruzan."

Nadwah explains the situation: Kshahrewar and Acara Crafts want Faruzan on a collaboration, and the other option is to teach a course; if she does neither the complaints may reach the sages. Faruzan suspects the complaints come from Haravatat colleagues and calls the metric unfair. She insists on being addressed as "Madam" and dislikes being called young, and Tighnari warns the Traveler of this beforehand. Collei explains that Faruzan's body stopped ageing while she was gone, so she looks as she did a hundred years ago.

If the Traveler asks about the Haravatat course, Faruzan describes her field as reading the carvings and documents of ruins to interpret their mechanisms; Nadwah says few students follow it and unexplored ruins are running out. The Traveler suggests teaching Collei to read, and that the course be public rather than held only for Akademiya students. Faruzan agrees, because the old Akademiya ignored the public, and goes with Nadwah to file the paperwork. In Essential Classic the group fills in the application with her, then searches Treasures Street for a text. Faruzan dislikes a modern light novel, tries to find a century-old series called Tales of Shahryar, finds a single stray volume in an antique shop, and learns from the storyteller Maddah that the series faded after its author kept extending it. Collei's liking for modern books leads Faruzan to choose a book Collei enjoys as the teaching material. This line ends with Stories of the Past.

If the Traveler asks about the Kshahrewar collaboration, Nadwah explains that the request comes from Acara Crafts and that a Kshahrewar representative, Anis, recommended Faruzan out of respect. In Early Learning Mechanism the group meets Anis and the shop owner Mamdouh at Port Ormos. Faruzan makes a paper prototype of a stacking puzzle called Pagoda Stack, and volunteer children play it; the minimum number of moves for seven layers is 127. At a launch conference she presents a reference book. If the Traveler urges a detailed, accurate book, the child audience is bored, but Kamal, Branch Master of Sumeru's Adventurers' Guild, offers an order of models and booklets for adventurers who cannot read, and the line ends in Knowledge is Wealth! If the Traveler urges a simple, playful book, the children are delighted and one says they want to build mechanisms; Faruzan realises with some dismay that this may not lead them to Haravatat, and the line ends in The Gardener and the Nursery.

If the Traveler chooses the pretext route, Faruzan claims that Tighnari wants her help with a fully automated irrigation system, which Nadwah accepts for the moment, and the group goes to Pardis Dhyai. There Tighnari shows a malfunctioning Karkata, a mechanical life form that Collei is fond of. Faruzan diagnoses a damaged Restitution Module and needs replacement parts, which sends her and the Traveler to the desert, where villagers speak of a "Ruin Wanderer" and an archaeologist named Raed keeps people away from his dig. Faruzan suspects a machine wreckage in the camp is the Wanderer and that Raed has swapped wreckage to deceive the Akademiya. At night the Wanderer attacks the camp; Faruzan recognises it as Tamimi, a machine from her own past, remodelled by her teacher and others so that it could search for her. It carries their last letters to her. Raed is exposed by his own logbook. Back at Pardis Dhyai the Traveler decides how much to tell Tighnari and Collei, which leads to either Start Over (the whole truth is shared) or "Welcome Back, Faruzan." (the Traveler keeps Tamimi a secret and Faruzan thanks them for it).

Smaller details. In Essential Classic Faruzan reads a modern light novel on sale at Treasures Street and finds it all fights and simple sentences; the bookseller is Farruq and the antique seller who has the single Tales of Shahryar volume is Derafsh. In Early Learning Mechanism the volunteer children include Qasit, Ruhi and Alia, and Mamdouh rewards them with Genius Invokation TCG cards. In Wanderings of a Lonesome Shadow Faruzan and the Traveler question villagers evacuated from Aaru Village, guarded by Raed's man Bakr, and learn that the Ruin Wanderer has been rumoured to be centuries old, which she rejects because she heard nothing of it a century ago. Ending rewards, in the wiki's order, vary: Stories of the Past and "Welcome Back, Faruzan." give Primogems and Guide to Admonition; Knowledge is Wealth! and Start Over give Hero's Wit and Vayuda Turquoise Fragments; The Gardener and the Nursery gives Primogems and Traditionally-Made Charcoal-Baked Ajilenakh Cake.

Revelations: Faruzan's old machine Tamimi spent roughly a hundred years searching for her until its Restitution Module wore out, carrying letters from her teacher and family. Raed, who leads the desert expedition, passed off other wreckage as the "Ruin Wanderer" in an attempt to mislead the Akademiya.

The letters let Faruzan remember her family and teacher clearly again and learn that they never gave up on her. She says she cannot repair Tamimi with her present abilities and that the replacement parts are better used to extend Karkata's life; she intends to revive Tamimi once she can reproduce the ancient creations.

Characters: Faruzan is proud, insists on "Madam", is affectionate toward Collei, scornful of the present Akademiya's priorities but respectful of Kshahrewar's methods. Collei is anxious around her but trusts the Traveler. Tighnari is the quiet organiser of the real task. Nadwah, Anis, Mamdouh, Maddah, Kamal and Raed are minor figures of the individual branches. Karkata and Tamimi are the machines.

Consequences: No branch changes Teyvat's main story. The event settles Faruzan's standing in the Akademiya for the player (course, collaboration or neither), shows her bond with the Traveler, and leaves Karkata repaired with parts from the desert. Whether Tighnari and Collei learn of Tamimi depends on the ending.

Placement: Released in Version 3.5. It requires the Sumeru Archon Quest Akasha Pulses, the Kalpa Flame Rises and is therefore set after Sumeru's main story. Describing Faruzan generally should not assume any single ending.

396.content: Tamimi is a machine from Faruzan's past. Her teacher and friends remodelled its Self-Repair function into Self-Learning so it could search for her and deliver letters. In the desert it was known as the Ruin Wanderer. After roughly a hundred years its Restitution Module was failing. Faruzan cannot yet repair it and uses the replacement parts for Karkata instead, promising to revive it later.

397.content: A puzzle toy devised by Faruzan for Acara Crafts: rings of different sizes are moved one at a time between poles and a larger ring may not sit on a smaller one. It follows the Tower of Hanoi puzzle. Seven layers need 127 moves.

398.comment: Hangout Event: Faruzan: Tales of Shahryar
398.content: A popular series from a hundred years ago, written by a Vahumana researcher who studied folk legends. Faruzan remembers it as a classic and cannot find it now; the storyteller Maddah says its author kept extending it instead of writing an ending and abandoned it. The more lasting Legend of Antara was the same author's original draft.

399.content:
Hangout Event: Gorou (also: The Canine General's Special Operations, Gorou Hangout Event, Gorou's Hangout Event): Hangout Event: Gorou is a branching, player-choice side story added in version 2.3 (Act I, "The Canine General's Special Operations"). Gorou, general of the Watatsumi Island resistance, spends a day on Narukami Island with the Traveler. He is rattled by Yae Miko's teasing, secretly answers readers' letters for a magazine under the pen name "Ms. Hina", and wants to recover a buried box of fallen soldiers' belongings. The tone is light and warm with one quietly sad thread. Five endings are possible.

The event needs two Story Keys and first requires the Archon Quest "Omnipresence Over Mortals" and the story quest "Warriors' Dreams Like Spring Grass Renewing". Everything starts from one scene near Yae Publishing House and fans out into five branches, each closing on a one-line ending card. The branches are alternate versions of the same day, not a continuous chronology.

Across branches the recurring beats are Gorou's discomfort with people who read him easily, his trust in the Traveler, his private worry about being a good leader, and post-war life on Watatsumi Island (soldiers moving on, the army slimmed down, closer contact with the Shogunate since the peace treaty).

Plot: The first choice splits the day. Telling Gorou to ignore Yae Miko leads either to the readers' letters (endings "The Smiling Send-Off" or "That's, Uh...") or to the box left on Nazuchi Beach (ending "Final Remembrance"). Offering to help him overcome his weakness leads to seeking advice or role-play training (endings "Tactical Retreat" and "Desserts Are the Best!").

Branch "What Shall We Do?" - Gorou goes to Watatsumi Island and asks soldiers for advice "for a friend". Shuuhei advises going through the motions and not hanging on a talker's every word; Miwa advises hiding what he really thinks. A Yae Publishing House clerk says Yae Miko personally picks the novels and rescued the magazine "That's Life" with a marketing plan. At the Grand Narukami Shrine they draw fortune slips (results randomised per player) and confront Yae Miko. Gorou's last tactic is to claim she is just like him and secretly wants her tail groomed; she answers that she has no tail. Ending: "Tactical Retreat".

Branch "Special Training" - they role-play difficult people. A merchant in Ritou fails because Gorou knows nothing of prices (Kokomi has always handled procurement); Fatui impressions are cut short by a real Fatui attack. The Traveler imitates Yae Miko in Inazuma City, but what unsettles Gorou is her knowing smile and sense that she sees through him, which the trusted Traveler lacks. The training fails; they buy cake instead and Gorou happily shares it. Ending: "Desserts Are the Best!".

Branch "Secret Identity" - Gorou asks the Traveler to scout Yae Publishing House, where the Ms. Hina Fan Club is waiting for the magazine to unveil Ms. Hina's "official likeness". The Traveler realises Gorou is Ms. Hina and decides not to tell him. The fans say Gorou strongly resembles Ms. Hina and take photos with him; the Traveler stalls him with an excuse about Yae Miko returning. Ending: "That's, Uh...", with Gorou sensing the Traveler is hiding something.

Branch "A Friend's Path" - after answering the letters together (one is from a resistance soldier torn between staying on Watatsumi Island and visiting his Narukami Island home), Gorou worries about losing touch with comrades. Soldiers tell him they rarely meet but would return at once if the island were in danger. A soldier, Hiroaki, asks to leave the resistance, crediting "Ms. Hina's" encouragement, and Gorou approves. Ending: "The Smiling Send-Off".

Branch "Ordinary Memorial" - Katheryne explains that the box Gorou buried at Nazuchi Beach is held because the Adventurers' Guild recovered it while investigating Treasure Hoarders who stole from Komore Teahouse. Guided by Taroumaru, whom Gorou can understand, they find the thieves hidden beneath Tenshukaku and defeat them. The box is returned, holding keepsakes of soldiers who died in the battle. Ending: "Final Remembrance".

Further detail by branch:

- Opening: Aratani of Yae Publishing House tells Yae Miko that a skilled artist has been engaged for work she ordered; she says she will check it and display it in front of the store. She wishes Gorou and the Traveler a good time on Narukami Island, remarking that much has changed. Gorou explains his errand: buying books for Kokomi and seeing a Shogunate-ruled area now that the two sides are in closer contact.
- "Special Training": Gorou wishes he were taller and bulkier so soldiers could follow him more easily on the field. He says cake is a luxury in the resistance, where special meals mean meat and wine, not dessert. A 100,000-Mora slice briefly tempts him until the Traveler admits no such cake exists.
- "A Friend's Path": Gorou recalls Kazuha telling him that bonds between people whose paths crossed never break. He fears distance will grow after parting; the soldiers' answer settles it. He does not want Hiroaki to leave without saying goodbye.
- "Ordinary Memorial": Taroumaru tells Gorou the gang has five members, the leader is Kousuke and his second is Yasuhisa. Kousuke offers half of everything they have saved as a bribe; Gorou refuses, then notes this is not a military camp so he need not be so heavy-handed.
- "What Shall We Do?": the fortune slips produce four different reactions (Great Fortune, Good Fortune, Misfortune, Great Misfortune); on Great Misfortune Gorou briefly suspects Yae Miko rigged the draw.
- The event pays Adventure EXP plus Primogems or enhancement materials depending on the ending.

Revelations: - Gorou writes the advice column of Yae Publishing House's magazine "That's Life" as "Ms. Hina". Readers see a gentle older-sister figure and write to him as a friend. He enjoys it: people in the army are reserved with a general, but letters remove that distance.
- Yae Miko oversees marketing for the magazine and rescued it from cancellation; she remains the final approver for the shop's books.
- Gorou does not realise the fan club's Ms. Hina is himself; he is never told in this event.
- The box Gorou buried held soldiers' everyday keepsakes, left for their families because weapons and armour were broken or hard to carry.

- Gorou can understand Taroumaru's barking, describing it as like a regional dialect: he catches the gist but not everything.
- Gorou finds Yae Miko hard to deal with because she towers over him, speaks cryptically and seems to see through him.

Characters: Gorou is the lead; the Traveler is his confidant. Yae Miko (Guuji of the Grand Narukami Shrine and chief editor of Yae Publishing House) teases him in the opening scene. Also present, depending on branch: Aratani and Kuroda of Yae Publishing House; Shuuhei, Miwa and other soldiers on Watatsumi Island; the soldier Hiroaki; the Ms. Hina fan club (Nobuhiro, Hiroshi, Yuka); Katheryne; Kozue of Komore Teahouse; the dog Taroumaru; and the Treasure Hoarders Kousuke and Yasuhisa.

Consequences: The event does not change the main story. Its value is characterisation: Gorou off the battlefield, shy, kind and a little overwhelmed by Inazuma's clever people.

The "Smiling Send-Off" and "Final Remembrance" branches deepen his sense of responsibility for the soldiers who followed him; the "Tactical Retreat" and "Desserts" branches keep him comic and warm.

Placement: Released in version 2.3. It is set after the Watatsumi Island war and the Archon Quest "Omnipresence Over Mortals", with Sangonomiya Kokomi governing and Gorou as her general. Watatsumi Island is at peace with the Shogunate, so Gorou can travel Narukami Island. No later-version content (6.x to 7.1) was found that revises the event.

400.comment: Hangout Event: Gorou: Ms. Hina Advice Column
400.content:
In Gorou's hangout, "That's Life" is a monthly Yae Publishing House magazine whose advice column is signed "Ms. Hina". Gorou writes it. The editors have staff copy each letter by hand and strike out names. Fans think of Ms. Hina as a gentle, understanding older sister who is weaker on romance questions, and a fan club formed. As recited by Nobuhiro, its rules are: do not pry into Ms. Hina's identity, make no controversial statements as club members, do not force the message on the uninterested, and keep improving oneself. Gorou has no idea the fans mean him.

Sample replies show his style: urging a lovestruck reader to seize the moment as on a battlefield, advising a cold-struck reader on rest and warmth, telling a neighbour-debt writer to demand repayment (or, in the softer option, to borrow a little in return). To the resistance soldier torn about home he writes "Narukami Island has changed. You should go back and visit."

401.comment: Hangout Event: Gorou: Nazuchi Beach Memorial Box
401.content: Gorou's buried box held water bottles, towels, knee guards and similar ordinary items, each marked with its owner's name, left by soldiers who expected to die in the Nazuchi Beach battle. He buried it hastily during the retreat. The Adventurers' Guild dug it up while investigating the theft of Taroumaru's reserve fund from Komore Teahouse by a five-person Treasure Hoarder gang led by Kousuke, hiding below Tenshukaku. After Gorou and the Traveler catch them, Katheryne returns the box and Gorou takes it to Watatsumi Island for the families. He tells himself that next time he must be stronger.

402.comment: Hangout Event: Gorou: Gorou and Yae Miko
402.content: Throughout the event Yae Miko teases Gorou about his tail and ears, clearly enjoying herself. Gorou's side is not fear of her power but discomfort at being read: her smile and unhurried gaze make him feel he has nowhere to hide. He says he can handle her in battle but not in everyday conversation. The Traveler's impersonation of her fails because he trusts the Traveler.

403.content:
Hangout Event: Kaeya (also: Kaeya's Hangout Event, Shenanigans and Sweet Wine, Kaeya Hangout): Hangout Event: Kaeya is a replayable, choice-driven story for Kaeya, the Knights of Favonius Cavalry Captain, released in Version 3.8, with one act, Shenanigans and Sweet Wine. The Traveler meets Kaeya far from home in Port Ormos in Sumeru, where he is on a Knights business trip, and spends the following days with him: watching and joining a theatre troupe, returning to Mondstadt, or going on to Liyue. It is a light, witty story with no effect on the main story.

It requires 2 Story Keys, Adventure Rank 35, and the Archon Quest Caribert plus the Story Quest Secret Pirate Treasure. There are five endings. Permanent, repeatable content.

This Hangout Event moves across three nations: Sumeru, Mondstadt and Liyue. The wiki notes that its Heartbeat Value stays at full and does not drop with any of the Traveler's choices. Its tone is playful, with glimpses of the people who care for Kaeya.

The act's quests are The Birdwatcher, All the World's a Stage, A Familiar Face in a Faraway Place, Reunion, Poems Dedicated to the Wind, An Ordinary Day for the Knights of Favonius, Fragrance of Wine, Taste of Home and Feathers Adrift in a Spring Breeze.

Plot: Opening: in Port Ormos Kaeya, travelling alone and bored, jokes about luring a Dusk Bird onto his shoulder, and greets the Traveler warmly. He proposes making his business trip a joint trip and, since the Knights count all expenses on a trip as travel expenses, treating it as a chance to live a little.
Stage branch (Questions): at Port Ormos a troupe is performing a drama about Prince Qubad, who rejects his father's war. When the actor playing Qubad is missing, Kaeya fills in, wearing Sailwind Shadow. He improvises, asks the audience if they believe in fate and throws the prop intaglio to the Traveler. The Traveler's answer shapes the scene, and Kaeya ends it by having the prince defy fate and leave. The ending is named Questions.
Mondstadt branches: if the Traveler declines to spend public money, Kaeya packs and they return to Mondstadt; he gives the Traveler a lamp as a souvenir. From there:
- A Boat Untethered: Kaeya, wanting to relax, takes the Traveler to the Cathedral plaza. Sister Grace has a problem, which the Traveler explains to Venti at the Angel's Share. A group including Barbara and Diona later gathers in the plaza to prepare a new song, and Kaeya hesitates to join; Venti gives him a poem and invites him to sing with everyone.
- The Grapes of Warmth: they visit Dawn Winery, where Kaeya teases Diluc and picks grapes with Tunner, who asks Kaeya and the Traveler to read a letter from his son, Guy.
- Our Sun: back at the winery, Kaeya and Adelinde, with the Traveler, share a home-cooked meal; Klee turns up to rescue Kaeya from a grounding.

Liyue branch (An Informant, or a Friend?): if the Traveler goes along with Kaeya's holiday trip, they go to Liyue Harbor. They meet Captain Wu, to whom Kaeya once gave unexpected help in Mondstadt (a Treasure Hoarder attack near Dawn Winery during a family trip). Captain Wu has been swindled by a con man who invoked a connection to Dr. Baizhu's master. Kaeya suggests reporting to the Ministry of Civil Affairs, but the Traveler wants to help. Kaeya devises a sting in which he poses as Albert Rich, a wealthy young lord from Mondstadt, with the Traveler as a disciple of the Guhua Clan, and the con man is exposed and taken away by the Millelith. Afterwards Kaeya asks Captain Wu whether he wants to be Kaeya's informant or his friend and tosses a coin, then declares him a friend.

In An Ordinary Day for the Knights of Favonius, Jean thanks him for his report and says a letter from the wine merchants' association in Sumeru credited his on-the-spot decisions with avoiding further losses from delays; Kaeya returns the leftover travel funds while the Traveler suspects he never meant to spend them. In Fragrance of Wine, he teases Diluc over a rumour about the winery's purchase of limited Northland Valberry Liquor. In Taste of Home, Adelinde tells him he has always been part of the Dawn Winery family. Klee, thinking Kaeya is in trouble with Jean, apologises for him; Kaeya says he has people to care for him now.
After the Port Ormos play, Kaeya says he might act full time if he ever left the Knights, and tells the Traveler that everyone is both actor and audience: if one dislikes the script, one can walk off the stage and join the audience.

Revelations: Little new lore is revealed. It adds personal detail: Kaeya's work for the Knights extends to travel, the Dawn Winery's staff think of him as family, and he says that people who owe him favours are either his friends or his informants.

Tunner remarks that something deep-rooted seems to bother Kaeya and that he guards his secrets closely, and asks the Traveler to look after him. Kaeya's remarks on the stage about an inept god who sets fathers against sons are framed as a figure of speech; he tells the Traveler not to take them literally.

The wiki notes that Kaeya's alias Albert Rich plays on his family name Alberich.

Characters: Kaeya and the Traveler are the main characters.

Mondstadt: Venti, Barbara, Diona, Sister Grace and the bards (Poems Dedicated to the Wind); Jean, Lisa, Albedo and Klee; Diluc, Elzer, Tunner, Adelinde and Connor at Dawn Winery. Sumeru: the theatre troupe including Darbil, Zabi and Tus. Liyue: Captain Wu, Guangzhi, Aunt Zhang and Mr. Bai.

Consequences: No lasting effect on the main story. Rewards are given per ending (Adventure EXP, Primogems, Hero's Wit, talent or ascension materials, Kaeya's special dish), and endings can be shown as Lingering Moments in the Serenitea Pot.

It does not add or resolve any plot threads about Kaeya's past.

Placement: Released in Version 3.8. It unlocks after the Archon Quest Caribert and the Story Quest Secret Pirate Treasure. The act sits outside the main timeline.

404.content: In Kaeya's Hangout Event, Albert Rich is the alias Kaeya uses in Liyue Harbor to pose as a wealthy, bored young lord from Mondstadt in order to bait a swindler. The wiki notes the name echoes Kaeya's family name, Alberich.

405.comment: Hangout Event: Kaeya: Prince Qubad play
405.content: In Port Ormos, a travelling troupe performs a drama about Prince Qubad, who refuses to let his father wage war and chooses exile instead. Kaeya takes over the missing role, improvises, and gives the Traveler the prop intaglio, Prince Qubad's Intaglio, when the Traveler first completes the quest. Tus, a caravan owner, praises the performance and invites Kaeya to visit his caravan.

406.comment: Hangout Event: Kaeya: Kaeya's Hangout Endings
406.content: The five endings are: Questions (the Qubad play), A Boat Untethered (Venti's poem), The Grapes of Warmth (Tunner's letter from Guy), Our Sun (the meal with Adelinde) and An Informant, or a Friend? (the Liyue sting).

key: The Pendulum of Weal and Woe
407.content:
Hangout Event: Kaveh (also: The Pendulum of Weal and Woe, Kaveh Hangout Event, Kaveh Hangout, The Sixth Proposal, A Refuge in the Sands, Past Mementos, Treasure and True Interest): Kaveh's Hangout Event, a single-act, branching side story added in Version 3.7. The Traveler finds the architect Kaveh depressed in a tavern after the sixth rejected design for a vague, stingy client, and follows him through one of several routes: a children's library in the desert village of Aaru, a hunt for sponsors with the merchant Dori, a locked box of his mother's mementos, or a scam that exploits his former classmate's architecture training centre. There are five endings.

The act is The Pendulum of Weal and Woe. It requires Adventure Rank 40, two Story Keys, and completion of the Archon Quest Akasha Pulses, the Kalpa Flame Rises and the story quest The Illusions of the Mob. The first quest, The Sixth Proposal, leads to three branch quests: A Refuge in the Sands, Past Mementos and Treasure and True Interest.

It is the main place where the Traveler sees Kaveh's private doubts about whether his art and his income can coexist, his past with his single mother, and how his friends, especially Alhaitham, Tighnari and Cyno, treat him. It is permanent content, not a limited-time event.
