Plot: In The Sixth Proposal Kaveh argues with a client, Badawi, who keeps asking for changes to a design in the desert. The Traveler meets him afterwards in a tavern, where Kaveh asks whether art is a divine gift or the product of one's own struggle and asks the Traveler to keep another secret. The Traveler then chooses what to do. Helping Kaveh convince the client leads to A Refuge in the Sands. Doing something else to clear his mind leads to Past Mementos. Elsewhere, when the talk turns to his money troubles, Kaveh remembers a former classmate who offers him a lucrative teaching job, which leads to Treasure and True Interest.

In A Refuge in the Sands the pair follow Badawi and learn that he is a former Eremite mercenary who has been disguising himself as a merchant because he feared being cheated; the building is a library for children in the desert, to be built at Aaru Village. The Traveler can propose a slightly different style, which sends the group to Aaru and ends in Blueprint for the Future, or a search for sponsors, which goes through Dori and ends in A Done Deal. In Past Mementos Kaveh digs out a box of his mother's old things and a locked notebook; the Traveler can look for her old acquaintances, ending in Leisurely Gathering after a dinner at Pardis Dhyai, or make a trip to places Kaveh loves, ending in Beneath the Stars. Treasure and True Interest ends in First Class.

In the tavern Kaveh admits that none of his projects since graduation has passed on the first review, and that his client has asked for changes that would destroy the design, such as turning the building into a single tall trunk. He says arguing with clients is bad for his reputation and asks the Traveler to add it to the secrets already being kept for him. Later he says that Alhaitham, whom he has argued with for years over his ideals, remains unconvinced.

Blueprint for the Future: Badawi and Kaveh clear monsters on the road to Aaru Village, with Kaveh as a trial character. Badawi talks about the short, hard lives of mercenaries and his wish to build the library before he dies, so that desert children can learn their letters. Kaveh says some people call him an idealist and that he wants everyone to lead a happy life. At the village, with Mehrak's help and answers from a villager, Setaria, he surveys erosion and wind, and the cost-heavy parts of the plan become insulation and ventilation, so he agrees to a plainer style to save money while compensating with layout, lines and colour. The ending text stresses that present suffering is nothing next to giving hope to future children.

A Done Deal: Dori introduces three merchants, Tippu, Rubab and Qasimi, who refuse to fund the project once they hear that most land around Aaru Village has already been bought up. Dori then reveals that she herself will pay, since she already owns the land, and Kaveh signs a contract, realising that she was the buyer all along. In the closing scene he insists on ordering the best food and drink to recoup his commission fees.

Past Mementos: The box holds a drawing Kaveh made at Port Ormos before he was five, a copy of his mother's blueprint with the door taller than the roof, and the locked notebook. His mother has since moved to Fontaine; his father died when he was young and she raised him alone. Wondrous Times: Kaveh and the Traveler find Professor Zaha Hadi, who remembers Kaveh's mother Faranak as a quiet, gifted student with many admirers who argued with clients before she met his father. Zaha Hadi's account leads to the password, and Kaveh reads that his parents chose his name together, and sees a photograph of a gathering that includes people he knows. The notebook ends with a message from his mother about forming ties outside one's work. Tighnari's dinner the next evening gathers Alhaitham and Cyno to discuss Collei's studies, and Kaveh drinks heavily while complaining about clients. The First Ideal: Kaveh brings the Traveler to places he loves, including the House of Daena, where Alhaitham appears and teases him about his habit of scribbling annotations in library books, and to the Port Ormos expansion he designed early in his career. The two end at a favourite desert site, where Kaveh says he wants to build things that move others and that he will try to define art for himself.

Treasure and True Interest: Alkami offers Kaveh work as a lecturer at his architecture training centre at three hundred thousand Mora per lecture. Kaveh discovers that Alkami's students are being led into debt on false promises of wealth, confronts him, resigns, and with the Traveler and Mehrak catches the moneylender Fakhr. Cyno takes them to the matra, who close the centre and investigate. In First Class Kaveh offers to keep teaching the remaining students real design and takes them out to look at buildings and draw their own ideas.

Smaller details. In A Refuge in the Sands, Kaveh recounts being cheated himself by a man he tried to help in the desert, who borrowed Mora repeatedly and then hired mercenaries to ambush him. The merchants Dori introduces are all friends or clients of hers. Kaveh refers to himself as the most famous architect in Sumeru and is called the Light of Kshahrewar by Alkami. Alhaitham appears in The First Ideal reading Kaveh's marginal notes. Faranak's notebook mentions a man with long ears among the friends of her husband.

Revelations: Kaveh is the son of a gifted architect, Faranak, who now lives in Fontaine; she left the locked notebook and her old things to him, and his father died when Kaveh was a child. Badawi, who commissions the library, used to be an Eremite mercenary. Dori already owned most of Aaru Village.

Kaveh says he knows how miserable living in debt is. He values his profession above comfort and accepts that this makes him stubborn with clients.

Characters: Kaveh is the lead; the Traveler and Mehrak accompany him. Badawi is the client and former mercenary. Dori is the merchant and creditor. Alkami is the exploitative former classmate. Zaha Hadi is a retired professor who taught his mother. Alhaitham, Tighnari and Cyno appear in the friendship-oriented routes, and Cyno in the training-centre case.

Consequences: No branch changes Teyvat's main story. Each ending settles one thread for the player: a library design for Aaru Village, funding through Dori, a closer link between Kaveh and his friends, a reflection on his art, or students freed from a debt scam.

Placement: Released in Version 3.7. It requires the Sumeru Archon Quest Akasha Pulses, the Kalpa Flame Rises and is set after Sumeru's main story. Describing Kaveh generally should not assume any single ending.

408.content: Badawi is the client of Kaveh's sixth proposal. He is an older former Eremite mercenary who hid his identity from Kaveh because he feared swindlers. He wants an affordable library for the children of the desert, placed at Aaru Village. He is stingy because he is saving the Mora himself.

409.content: A Kshahrewar graduate and former senior classmate of Kaveh who runs an architecture training centre. He pushes students into loans with a lender named Fakhr and promises a wealth that architecture rarely gives. After Kaveh and the Traveler expose him, the matra close the centre and investigate.

410.content: A locked notebook that Faranak left behind when she moved to Fontaine. Kaveh could not open it as a child. In the Wondrous Times branch he reads her diary and a message addressed to him about forming connections beyond one's art.

411.content:
Hangout Event: Kuki Shinobu (also: The Gang's Daily Deeds, Kuki Shinobu Hangout Event, Shinobu's Hangout Event): Hangout Event: Kuki Shinobu is a branching, player-choice side story added in version 2.7 (Act I, "The Gang's Daily Deeds"). After three Arataki Gang members are arrested for illegally posting flyers, deputy Kuki Shinobu bails them out and spends the day repairing the damage, with the Traveler as her improvised "Chief Advisor". Depending on choices, the day leads to a forced shift at the Grand Narukami Shrine, a reunion with her sister, a manhunt for runaway gang members, or a misunderstood job interview. It is a comic story about Shinobu's patience and her real attachment to the gang. Five endings are possible.

The event needs two Story Keys and first requires the Interlude "Perilous Trail" and the story quest "Rise Up, Golden Soul". The branches are alternatives of one day, not a continuous chronology. The running idea is that Shinobu fixes the gang's mess with law, bookkeeping and discipline, and that the "Gang Bylaws" she invents are how she hopes to make them behave.

Shinobu is never relaxed in this event: the shrine, her sister, the Tenryou Commission and even her own gang each press on a different part of her past or reputation. The gang, for its part, shows how much it relies on her and, in the last branch, how badly it fears losing her.

Plot: Shinobu's first plan is to scold the three and make them apologise. The Traveler's choices lead along five routes. Defending them sends everyone to the Grand Narukami Shrine, where the gang had posted flyers and met Yae Miko (ending "Unexpected Wages" or "Time For Some Secret Dealings..."). Proposing written rules sends Shinobu after the boys scattering through town (endings "Official Business!" or "Doom Arrives Just the Same"). Standing back lets her discipline them herself; the three then follow her, with the Traveler, to Uyuu Restaurant (ending "The Arataki Gang Community Service Chronicle").

Branch "To the Shrine" - Yae Miko, the shrine's Guuji, says the flyers insult the Shogun herself, and demands Shinobu serve as a shrine maiden for a day to make amends. If the Traveler urges Shinobu to play along, she agrees on conditions (one day only, and no shrine maiden outfit) and Yae Miko extends the offer to the Traveler. At the shrine Shinobu advises a visitor to avoid an investment scam, tells an editor blocked on ideas to travel, and makes omamori for an old woman whose granddaughter is leaving. The woman recognises her voice as that of a former shrine maiden. Shinobu admits she trained here briefly at her family's insistence, hated it, and wears her mask to avoid prying. Yae Miko pays them wages; the Traveler's envelope contains only a thin sheet, ending "Unexpected Wages".

If the Traveler instead refuses the shrine maiden role, Yae Miko tells Shinobu to remove the flyers from the mountain path with the shrine maiden already assigned: Shinobu's sister Miyuki. In "In the Aftermath" Shinobu tells Miyuki the Arataki Gang is a legitimate international organisation and the Traveler its Chief Advisor, until the gang members arrive and expose the truth. Shinobu admits she joined freely and is proud of the gang. Miyuki promises not to tell the family and asks Shinobu to carry out the dreams she once described. Ending: "Time For Some Secret Dealings...".

Branch "Gang Bylaws" - Mamoru, Akira and Genta scatter and Shinobu tracks them down: Mamoru on a bathhouse roof, Genta under a bridge where he took the spot used by local children, and Akira far outside the city. She recites Article 1 (do not damage property), Article 2 (do not bully small children) and, later, Article 3 (insubordination is punished by reciting all bylaws). Akira has fled far to the north and tries to hide in a crate. If the Traveler coaxes him out and takes him back, Shinobu runs "That'll Learn Them!", a classroom quiz where the trio must say which bylaws a hypothetical "John Doe" violated, and punishes wrong answers by making them copy out the rules three times. Ending: "Official Business!". If the Traveler instead helps him hide, Akira ends up caught between Kairagi smugglers and Fatui skirmishers; in "Temporary Escape" Shinobu and the Traveler defeat them and learn the Kairagi were fronting for the Fatui. Shinobu plans to pass that to the Tenryou Commission to offset the gang's past offences, but still says Akira needs hands-on training. Ending: "Doom Arrives Just the Same".

Branch "Key Decision" - Mamoru, Akira and Genta overhear Shinobu at Uyuu Restaurant with Kujou Sara and a woman named Norika, apparently interviewing for a Tenryou Commission job. They report to Itto, who panics, orders the flyers taken down and apologies made, and tells the Traveler to ask Shinobu for an interview. Shinobu gives the Traveler an "internship" apologising to shopkeepers, who report Itto has already apologised. Doushin Amano nearly arrests the gang again until Norika vouches for Shinobu. The gang gives Shinobu a farewell gift and confess hidden misdeeds, only for Norika to explain she is a Liyue-Inazuma merchant who hired Shinobu as a legal consultant for a first-aid supply deal. Shinobu then asks about their confessions and chases them. Ending: "The Arataki Gang Community Service Chronicle".

Further details:

- "Ways and Means": Shinobu tells the Doushin that Mamoru, Akira and Genta were posting flyers to reach "more people in need", and that she and the other gang members will remove them. The three had hung flyers on the Grand Narukami Shrine's mountain path and been caught by a "terrifying fox lady" they will not name. She lists past incidents: nearly summoning the fire brigade while roasting Lavender Melons, and a neighbourhood-angering "Great Singalong".
- If the Traveler backs away at the start, Shinobu disciplines the trio herself and the story continues at "Back to Business".
- The shrine maiden shift: visitors include Takuma, who is considering a 40 percent overseas-shipping scheme that Shinobu identifies as a Ponzi-style scam, and Hayato, a writer who asks the shrine for inspiration and is told to travel. The omamori scene involves Asami, a nearly blind old woman who refuses help up the mountain, and Inagi Hotomi and Maki of the shrine.
- Asked why she did not stay on, Shinobu says simply that she does not enjoy the work. She says separately that relying on gods for everything frustrates her, but that prayer sometimes is the only thing people can do.
- "Key Decision": Mamoru notes that a day's Shogunate pay could buy the gang a week of snacks; Itto replies that the gang's relaxed working environment compensates. His backup plan is a farewell gift of a Naku Weed bracelet bought at Tsukumomono Groceries. Doushin Amano recognises Itto from a flyer drawing.
- Rewards: Adventure EXP plus Primogems or enhancement materials per ending.

Revelations: - Shinobu, once a trainee at the Grand Narukami Shrine at her family's arrangement, quit because of the strict etiquette and constant monitoring at home. She later studied bookkeeping, worked as an editor and, by her own account, studied law in Liyue. She wears a mask so people do not pry.
- Shinobu has a sister, Miyuki, who works as a shrine maiden of the Grand Narukami Shrine (she mentions dealing with matters in Tatarasuna earlier), and who agrees to keep Shinobu's gang membership secret from their family.
- The Arataki Gang has no formal rules until Shinobu writes the Gang Bylaws in this event.
- The Kairagi group at the beach was handing supplies to Fatui skirmishers.

- Kujou Sara recommended Shinobu to Norika as a legal consultant, and a Police Station doushin notes that the gang's deputy has studied abroad and knows the law.
- Shinobu admits she dislikes the shrine, her family's expectations and Yae Miko's teasing, but is moved that the gang came to support her despite fear.

Characters: Shinobu is the lead; the Traveler is her "Chief Advisor". Arataki Itto and gang members Mamoru, Akira and Genta recur. Yae Miko and shrine staff (Inagi Hotomi, Maki) appear in the shrine branches, plus Shinobu's sister Miyuki. Tenryou Commission figures include Kujou Sara, Doushin Uesugi and Doushin Amano; Norika is a merchant. Shopkeepers Shimura Kanbei and Aoi, and a boy, Shouta, are apologised to.

Consequences: The event does not change the main story. It adds the Gang Bylaws as a running joke and shows Shinobu choosing the gang over her family's expectations. In the final branch it also shows her doing legal consulting work introduced by Kujou Sara.

Placement: Released in version 2.7. It is set after the Interlude "Perilous Trail". No content from 6.x to 7.1 was found that revises the event.

412.comment: Hangout Event: Kuki Shinobu: Gang Bylaws
412.content: Shinobu's improvised rulebook for the Arataki Gang: Article 1 - no damage to others' property; offenders repay the full loss through a gang loan, with their gang assets such as Onikabuto and Genius Invokation cards frozen until it is paid. Article 2 - no bullying small children; offenders apologise sincerely and are banned from gang activities such as Lavender Melon roasting until the victim forgives. Article 3 - when one gang member is in trouble, all come to help (in a later scene, insubordination is punished by reciting the bylaws from memory). Additional notes, such as Clause 36 of Article 2, are quoted in class. Shinobu runs a quiz as a deterrent.

key: Stick It to the Man flyer
413.comment: Hangout Event: Kuki Shinobu: Arataki Gang Flyer Incident
413.content: Itto designed flyers himself (his gang members call them avant-garde), including slogans like "Stick It to the Man, Join the Arataki Gang!" and "Arataki Numero Uno Itto: Ousting His Foes Like a Sumo Supremo!". Mamoru, Genta and Akira posted them around Inazuma City, the Grand Narukami Shrine path, Shimura's and Tsukumomono Groceries, and were arrested. The flyers are the cause of every branch of the event.

414.comment: Hangout Event: Kuki Shinobu: Shinobu and the Grand Narukami Shrine
414.content: Shinobu was once a trainee at the Grand Narukami Shrine; the placement was arranged by her family. She remembers nagging about etiquette and interrogations after each shift, and left to become anything but a shrine maiden. She finds it hard to refuse Yae Miko, who knows the history, and wears her mask partly to avoid being recognised there.

415.content:
Hangout Event: Layla (also: Ever Silent Stars, Layla Hangout Event, Layla Hangout, Drowsy Evening Star, The Wisdom Seelie, A Change of Pace, blessing from the stars): Layla's Hangout Event, a single-act, branching side story added in Version 3.6. The Traveler meets Layla, a worn-out Rtawahist student at the Akademiya who cannot finish her thesis and is secretly being helped by an unknown "blessing from the stars". Depending on the Traveler's choices they trace a legendary "Wisdom Seelie" through the House of Daena and Layla's old failures, help her prepare for her thesis defence, or take her out for a break. Some routes reveal that the helper is a second self who emerges when Layla faints from exhaustion. There are six endings.

The act is Ever Silent Stars. It requires Adventure Rank 40, two Story Keys and the Archon Quest Akasha Pulses, the Kalpa Flame Rises. It opens with Drowsy Evening Star and then branches into the Wisdom Seelie investigation (The Wisdom Seelie and its follow-ups) or a "change of pace" line (A Change of Pace, with The Helper and Fresh Air).

The event is the only extended look at Layla's life as a student: her fear that she does not belong at the Akademiya, her lack of sleep, and her kindness. It is permanent content, not a limited-time event.

Plot: At the Akademiya the Traveler meets Layla, who is rushing out of the House of Daena. She is behind on her thesis and has had little sleep for days. She explains that her homework and papers keep getting finished before their deadlines without her remembering, and she has been calling this a "blessing from the stars". She does not want to rely on it, but time is short and she hopes a rumoured Wisdom Seelie, who answers questions left in two astrology books, will help with the thesis. The Traveler can go with her to investigate the Seelie or suggest she rest.

In the Seelie investigation, the Seelie refuses to answer because it says she meant to copy its answer, and leaves a chain of riddles instead. The riddles lead to places from Layla's past failures. The Traveler can follow them to the end, which gives The Price to Pay and Its Returns, take a break to fight monsters, which gives Once Bitten, Twice Shy, or gather information from students, which leads to a night watch and That Which Remains Unspoken. In the "change of pace" line, the Traveler helps Layla borrow equipment, rehearse her thesis defence, or relax outdoors; these routes lead to A Matter of Course, The Stars' Expectations and A Moment of Respite.

Opening: Layla is still shaking from days without sleep. She calls herself a Rtawahist student "for now", fears the thesis will fail, and mentions the Seelie. She also remarks that she has not seen Twirly-Whirly for a long time; the event does not explain what that is. The Traveler can say that her effort matters as much as her results, or that she should rest.

The Wisdom Seelie: Rabah, a reader at the House of Daena, explains how to leave a letter in one of two astrology books and wait for a red stamp to appear as a reply. Layla leaves her question and receives a reply that refuses to answer for her and leaves hints "on the road of wisdom" instead. In Taking the Opposite Route the pair question the librarian Katayoun, a student Hunayn who saw a black shadow fall into the closed library one night, and a reader named Latifah who describes the Seelie as very strong, metal-bodied, able to freeze water and call meteors. In Compiling the Clues Layla reasons that the Seelie is a Rtawahist researcher studying the same subject, and the pair wait through the night at an observation site. In the end, as Layla's stress peaks she faints, and a calmer second Layla wakes. She is willing to answer questions: she entered the House of Daena by accident one night when a book had been left inside, put a student to sleep, and later answered questions to help other students; the legends have grown from that. She says she and Layla are "two sides of the same coin", that Layla's emotions are unstable, and that Layla already has the key data for her thesis, which she will organise for her. She asks the Traveler not to tell Layla. When Layla wakes she suspects she sleepwalked; whether the Traveler keeps the promise or not, the ending is That Which Remains Unspoken.

Further Investigation and One Final Step: the next hint points to Layla's arrival road, where she accidentally stepped on an Avidya Leopard's tail and lost the talisman her mother made. The second site is where she once ruined borrowed equipment during an observation attempt, and the third is a crossroads where she saw Treasure Hoarders robbing a family and ran for help rather than intervene. The final stop is Vimara Village, where Mundhir, the man she once helped, returns the lost package with a letter from the Wisdom Seelie encouraging her and giving her the missing summary for her thesis. Layla suspects she might be the Seelie but is mostly grateful. The ending is The Price to Pay and Its Returns.

An Exasperating Prank: if the Traveler chooses to rest, Layla insists on helping when monsters attack and joins as a trial character; afterwards she is out of breath but says her will is strong and resolves not to repeat her regrets. The ending is Once Bitten, Twice Shy.

A Change of Pace: at Puspa Cafe, Layla's classmate Munirah complains that Layla always seems on the verge of a breakdown even though she never misses deadlines. Layla says she cannot tell her classmates that something else helps her. If the Traveler offers to face the problem head-on, The Helper follows: Katheryne introduces the astrology collector Azzam, who will lend his equipment if Layla explains her research on the triple-orbit shift. In Thesis Defense Practice Layla practises the defence with the Traveler. If she keeps her composure she answers every question and decides she may no longer need the "blessing", which ends in A Matter of Course. If her hidden stress reaches its limit in the middle of an answer, the second Layla steps in and the line ends in The Stars' Expectations. In The Remaining Problem the second Layla appears while talking to Azzam, writes notes for the real Layla, explains that she must keep her existence secret, and says Layla's condition may worsen if she learns of her, which also leads to The Stars' Expectations.

Fresh Air and One Hearty Meal Later: instead, the Traveler takes Layla outside, where she cooks fruit and fish over a fire as she did as a child, remembers the home she left when she passed the Akademiya's admissions exam, swims a race at a lake and shouts from a mountain top. She says she studies astrology because the stars are beautiful, and this is why she calls the helper the "blessing from the stars". This ends in A Moment of Respite.

Smaller details. The books used for Seelie letters are Theoretical Astrology and A Quick Reference Guide to Astrology Cases. Layla says the Seelie is said to carry dozens of books and several pieces of astrology equipment. A Matter of Course rewards a keepsake called The Arrayed Stars Mirrored. Layla's thesis topic is the triple-orbit shift phenomenon and her adviser has put related methods into practice at Rtawahist. In her first thesis defence she froze, and Layla's practice questions include a trap about a "Great Machine" she has not prepared for. In Drowsy Evening Star a stress value tracked by the game changes how Layla responds in later scenes, which is why the same choice can lead to different endings.

Revelations: Layla's "blessing from the stars" is a second personality that takes over when she loses consciousness from anxiety and exhaustion. The Wisdom Seelie legend is a rumour that grew from its activity.

The second Layla describes herself as the shape Layla would take if rested and healthy, relies on Layla's own knowledge, and fears she would cease to exist if Layla's condition worsened. She never signs her notes. She believes in Layla and wants her to finish the thesis herself.

Characters: Layla is the lead, shy, apologetic and exhausted but determined. Her second self is poised and practical. Other characters include Rabah, Katayoun, Hunayn, Latifah, Mundhir, Munirah, Azzam and Katheryne; each appears in one or two branches only.

Consequences: No branch changes Teyvat's main story. The endings settle whether Layla learns of her other self, whether she gains confidence or keeps leaning on it, and whether she rests.

Placement: Released in Version 3.6, between Faruzan's and Kaveh's Hangout Events. It requires the Sumeru Archon Quest Akasha Pulses, the Kalpa Flame Rises and is set after Sumeru's main story. Describing Layla generally should not assume any single ending.

416.comment: Hangout Event: Layla: The Wisdom Seelie
416.content: A rumour in the House of Daena of a strong, metal-bodied Seelie that answers questions placed in astrology books. In Layla's Hangout Event the "Seelie" is revealed to be Layla's second persona. Students attribute abilities to it, such as freezing water and calling meteors, that are exaggerated tales of her night-time activity.

417.content: An astrology enthusiast and equipment collector whom Katheryne introduces. He lends his celestial equipment to Layla if she can explain her research to him.

418.content:
Hangout Event: Lynette (also: Lynette Hangout Event, Checks & Cats, Lynette hangout): Lynette's Hangout Event is a one-act, voiced, branching story in Fontaine released in Version 4.5. Its act, "Checks & Cats", is built from five quests (A Decision, Mask, Break, Detectives, Closure) and ends in one of five endings. The Traveler meets Lynette outside Hotel Debord just after the opening of her first-ever acting role, hiding from the reception with a stray cat she has named Bonnie. Whether she goes back to the party, helps the cat, or does neither decides the whole day. Throughout, the event leans on her established traits: she conserves social energy by switching between named "modes", she reads people through tells, and she is quietly devoted to her twin Lyney.

The act mixes character comedy with two full mysteries. The theatre branch is a small drama about a director, a sidelined understudy and an investor-driven publicity machine, resolved by Lynette and Lyney through a staged protest. The detective branch involves an animal-smuggling ring and, in its deepest path, brings back the Lefevere family, the aristocratic house that once abducted Lynette as a child. Which sub-quests the player sees depends on three fork points: the first choice at the hotel, the result of a card draw in the Detectives quest, and a late choice in Mask.

Mechanically, the event uses a Hangout Event structure (Story Keys, "hearts" for Lynette's energy, and skill-check style dice draws against a numbered deck), but this entry treats those only as the way branches are selected. The wiki act page records the unlock requirements as Adventure Rank 40, two Story Keys, and completion of "Masquerade of the Guilty" and "The Little Oceanid". The wiki treats this as the most recent Hangout Event as of Version 7.1, and lists only Act I.

Plot: **A Decision.** Outside Hotel Debord, Lynette tells the Traveler she has just accepted a leading role in a masked mime show, The Lost Puppet, directed by Merieux. She is playing a puppet, so no lines and no facial expressions are needed. The show opened well, but the reception afterwards drained her, so she left to enter "standby mode". She met a collared, hungry cat she named Bonnie, and cannot decide between returning to the party and finding Bonnie's owner. Lyney had Freminet build her a card-box device, the Fateometer, for such moments. Her first draw is botched when the box jams and the cards fall, so she hands the decision to the player. The Traveler can send her back to the reception (Mask), help Bonnie (Detectives), let the Fateometer decide, or suggest doing neither, which can end the event as "Standby Mode".

**Mask.** At the reception, reporters and critics pour praise on The Lost Puppet while Lynette answers in minimal stock phrases. She has a name for her power-saving conversation style, "tea party mode", but the interview burns far more energy than a normal tea party. Furina, also a guest, gives a more measured opinion and mentions that an earlier draft of the script was more complex. Back with her envelope containing the group photo, Lynette finds an anonymous letter telling her that she is a heartless puppet who has ruined the work and must give up the lead. Merieux blames a rival, but the investor Maloney lets slip that the role was first meant for the actress Gillian. Gillian, living in the Fleuve Cendre, confirms it. With the troupe's actor Jaiques, the group reads the original script and the official script side by side and finds that the original ending, a lone dance among ruins for dead companions, is far more demanding and moving than the simplified stage version. Lynette proposes that Gillian take the lead for the second half of the show at the Opera Epiclese.

**Mask, continued.** Two days later, Lynette and Gillian swap costumes and masks for the interval, so the critics file reviews after the first half praising Lynette's work, then see a different actress take the second half. When Merieux confronts them, Lynette announces she is quitting the lead role and Lyney arrives with a draft lawsuit, a contract and reimbursement money, an offer meant to force a choice. Lyney also reveals that other famous actresses had turned Merieux down before Lynette said yes, and that the troupe had chipped in for the money. Cyril, Jaiques and Gillian say plainly that Merieux had slid into the publicity-and-backroom-deal methods he used to despise. Merieux gives in, the second half runs with the original ending, and when Gillian removes her mask at the curtain call the audience, led from the balcony by Furina, applauds. Faced with angry critics, Lynette claims the actor swap was deliberate performance art, using the language of the show to explain the confusion, and secures a promise that Furina will write a review focused on Gillian.

**The letter.** After the show, Ginna, Gillian's younger sister, admits to having written the letter. In the "wait and see" path, Lynette suggests letting it go as a misunderstanding and gives Ginna a backstage job, which leads to the quest Break. In the alternative, Lynette claims not to remember anything, and the act ends with a new group photograph.

**Break.** A few days later the Traveler visits the opera house at Lynette's invitation. She is dozing in the audience, glad she no longer needs her energy-hungry modes, and says Merieux thinks Ginna is a promising actress with natural chemistry with her sister. Lynette says she would rather cheer on others from a quiet seat than seek fame herself.

**Detectives.** If Bonnie is helped, the pair post a notice at The Steambird, which the Traveler and Lynette are invited to follow up with tea the next day at Lynette's home. Later, a woman and the Humane Society director Bernard both turn up claiming the cat. The woman is the Gardes officer Elodie, who says Bonnie belongs to a suspect, the researcher Pierre Lefevere, in an investigation into a new drug called Imitation Sinthe. Lynette, who notices that Elodie's breathing stays calm when challenged, hears the family name with visible dread and tells the Traveler she was once kidnapped by the Lefevere head and rescued by Arlecchino. The twins then joined the House of the Hearth. Lyney had been avoiding her, and she realises he and Chevreuse, captain of the Special Security and Surveillance Patrol, were already working the case, and that he arranged the acting job to keep her busy. The group is merged into one team. A pendant bearing a Lefevere insignia for an illegitimate child, the Humane Society director Bernard's attempt to take the cat, and Lynette's reading of Bonnie's body language all point toward a secret base north of the Court of Fontaine. There they find equipment for a drug-making operation, special waterproof bags and barrels, and evidence of weighted floating barrels used for dead drops, from which the group concludes that animals were being used as carriers. At Lumidouce Harbor, travel logs show the Humane Society's repeated "overseas adoption" departures. The group confronts Bernard, who confesses to transporting animals for a partner he has never met. That partner, he says, is Pierre, but they only ever wrote letters and he has never met him.

**Fork.** In Falling Into Layers of Fog, Lynette enters "deduction mode" with the Traveler. If the Traveler fails the final check, they let the Gardes take Bernard away and go to rescue animals at the Humane Society (ending "Save the Kitty!"). If it succeeds, the Traveler stops Elodie from leaving, and Closure follows.

**Closure.** The Traveler and Lynette reason that a third person controlled both men: they were kept apart on purpose, Pierre was told to leave Bonnie and the pendant where the Phantom would find them, and Pierre was lured to his base and made to disappear. The third person is Elodie, who is revealed to be a Lefevere. Chevreuse and Lyney arrive with evidence that Elodie often swapped her port shifts to match smuggling activity. Elodie threatens to blow up the Humane Society with a crude device, but Lynette and the group subdue her, Bernard is knocked out, and the device turns out to be a toy. Over tea with Bonnie afterwards, Lynette explains that the cat's reluctance to approach Elodie raised her first strong suspicion (ending "Adventurers, Investigators, and Cats").

Revelations: - The anonymous letter in the Mask branch is the work of Ginna, Gillian's younger sister, not a professional intimidator or a rival troupe; Lynette judges her feeling to be indignant but not malicious.
- The detective branch discloses that Lynette was abducted by the head of the Lefevere family at a dinner party and rescued by Arlecchino, and that this is how the twins joined the House of the Hearth.
- The same branch shows Lyney working with Chevreuse as a consultant on a smuggling case without telling Lynette, and using the acting job to keep her away from a case that touches the Lefevere name.
- The Closure path names the mastermind of the smuggling ring as Elodie, a Gardes officer who is an illegitimate Lefevere descendant, planted in the Gardes before the family's fall and kept there afterwards.

- Merieux changed the script after investor pressure and chose Lynette because of her name; the original lead was Gillian. He is shown as sincere about his art but compromised by the publicity routine.
- Lynette explains that the Fateometer deck has twenty cards and that she sets the cutoff as she likes. She says she agreed to do the show only if she drew a 1, and later suspects that this draw was part of Lyney's plan to keep her busy (her own suspicion, not confirmed).
- Lynette says she has younger siblings and that Lyney has always been overprotective.

Characters: Lynette is the focus: her modes (standby, event, tea party, search, deduction, serious), her reluctance about fame, her talent for reading tells, and her protectiveness toward the weak. The Traveler is her main companion and the player's choices drive the story. Bonnie, a cat, appears throughout the story and is the thread connecting the branches.

- **Lyney:** Lynette's twin, who arrives in the theatre climax with legal paperwork and in the detective storyline as Chevreuse's consultant.
- **Chevreuse:** Captain of the Special Security and Surveillance Patrol, working with Lyney, who welcomes Lynette and the Traveler to the team.
- **Furina:** A guest at the Hotel Debord reception, attending as a theatre expert, who later applauds the audience reaction and agrees to review the show.
- **Mask troupe:** Director Merieux, actress Gillian and her younger sister Ginna, actors Jaiques and Cyril, investor Maloney, and the critics Corentin and Amaury. Argalia, Leone, and two reporters have small roles.
- **Detective cast:** Euphrasie (The Steambird), Gardes officer Elodie, port guard Chourei and the dog Girard, Humane Society director Bernard, and the researcher Pierre Lefevere, who is never seen.
- **Freminet:** Mentioned as the builder of the Fateometer.

Consequences: Each ending ends the day but not the characters' ongoing lives. Nothing in the event changes the main storylines of Fontaine. Depending on the branch, it leaves the Traveler with a closer bond to Lynette, a restored troupe (Gillian in the lead role), or a closed smuggling case.

Per the wiki's ending reward table, each ending gives Adventure EXP plus either Primogems and a book or food material, or Hero's Wit and Vayuda Turquoise Fragments. The Fateometer is listed as the reward of A Decision.

Placement: Released in Version 4.5, after the Fontaine Archon Quest chapters. It requires completion of 'Masquerade of the Guilty' and the story quest 'The Little Oceanid'. It is a side story and does not advance the main plot.

Because the event has five endings, there is no single canonical timeline. The recommended roleplay interpretation is that the Traveler experiences one of the branches and that Lynette remembers only the branch actually played.

419.comment: Hangout Event: Lynette: Endings of Hangout Event Lynette
419.content: The act has five endings. "A Roaring Success!" (Mask, with the late choice): a new group photo after the Gillian-led show. "A Seat in the Audience" (Break): Lynette relaxes in the audience. "Adventurers, Investigators, and Cats" (Closure): tea with Bonnie after the arrest. "Save the Kitty!" (Detectives): the Traveler and Lynette leave the case to the Gardes and go to rescue animals. "Standby Mode" (A Decision): the Traveler suggests doing neither task and the day is spent doing nothing.

420.content: A box of twenty numbered cards that Lyney had Freminet make for Lynette, so she can let a random draw decide things. The cutoff number is whatever she decides at the time. In the event she uses it for the question of whether to return to the reception or help Bonnie, but the box jams and the cards fall. The player receives it as a quest reward.

421.comment: Hangout Event: Lynette: The Lost Puppet
421.content: A masked mime show with no spoken lines and no facial expression, written and directed by Merieux and staged at the Opera Epiclese. Its protagonist is a dancing puppet who realises that her failing legs are the aging of her components. In the original script, she ends by dancing alone among ruins for her dead companions until her parts fail. In the commercial version, she is welcomed into a lavish stage and left uncertain about whether anyone will appreciate her. Lynette plays the lead in the first half of the opening run; Gillian takes it for the director's cut.

422.comment: Hangout Event: Lynette: Imitation Sinthe smuggling case
422.content: In the detective branch, a new drug that imitates Sinthe is made in a hidden base, carried in thin sealed bags swallowed by animals, floated in weighted barrels as dead drops and shipped abroad as "overseas adoptions" by the Humane Society. The researcher Pierre Lefevere and the director Bernard are made to appear as the culprits. In the Closure path, the Gardes officer Elodie is revealed as the coordinator who kept them apart and meant to sacrifice both.

423.content: A Gardes officer who introduces herself to Lynette and the Traveler as an investigator of the case. In the Closure path, she claims to be the last of the Lefevere family (Chevreuse names her a Lefevere), who hid her origin and used her post to organise the smuggling ring. She resents the family that made her an infiltrator, and her plan relies on blaming Pierre and Bernard.

424.content:
Hangout Event: Ningguang (also: The Jade Chamber's Returning Guest, Ningguang Hangout Event, Ningguang's Hangout): Ningguang's Hangout Event, a replayable, choice-driven side story set after the Liyue Harbor crisis. Short of staff because her three secretaries are running an auction, Ningguang asks the Traveler to cover as her assistant for a day. The Traveler either schedules a serious working day, or a day off, and the event ends in one of five outcomes: an auction that reclaims her lost treasures, a lunch-and-informants day, a chess-piece commission, a fishing-and-treasure outing, or a trip to Northland Bank.

It was added in Version 2.4 and requires two Story Keys, Adventure Rank 28 and completion of The Crane Returns on the Wind (Liyue's Archon Quest conclusion). It holds eight quests: The Jade Chamber Once More (hub), Time Off!, Endless Smoke, Starting From Zero, Liyue Millennial, Business as Usual, Auction Games and Exchanging Intelligence. It shows the private person behind her polished public image: her humble origins, her grief for the original Jade Chamber, and the care she takes of the children she uses as informants.

Hangout Events are replayable permanent content. Each ending is a Memory that can be shown in the Serenitea Pot. The tone leans on dry wit: Ningguang treats every outing as a business case, yet the closing beats of each route reveal her loneliness, her fear of being seen only as a profit-seeker and her wish to leave a legacy.

Plot: In The Jade Chamber Once More the Traveler arrives at the Jade Chamber to find Ningguang and her secretaries Baishi, Baiwen and Baixiao in need of a stand-in. The secretaries must run an important auction the next day, leaving Ningguang's day-to-day work without cover; she wants someone trusted who has no conflict of interest. Baishi briefs the Traveler: 133 unscheduled items, 17 of them high priority, including meetings with the Eight Trades, tax revisions, Keqing on land-conveyance deals and the guilds. The Traveler then drafts a schedule.

**Rigorous schedule.** Choosing a serious, well-ordered day leads to Business as Usual. The next morning the Traveler wakes Ningguang, has breakfast with her, collects her tailored clothes from Lanyang, and attends a lunch banquet at Liuli Pavilion with a businesswoman, Luo Qiao, who asks for advice on getting into the Luminescent Spine trade. Ningguang advises against it, saying the price far exceeds likely profit and the hype may be engineered. After the banquet the Traveler chooses between telling Ningguang her secretaries will be fine (Exchanging Intelligence) or going to check on them (Auction Games).

**Simple schedule.** Choosing a single day off sends the Traveler to Time Off! Baishi worries but agrees, noting Ningguang rarely rests. Next morning Ningguang can spend the day on something she never has time for (Liyue Millennial) or something she never has the chance to do (Starting From Zero or Endless Smoke).

**Liyue Millennial (ending: Unchanging Will).** Ningguang shows off her Liyue Millennial, a chess game of her own design with over thirty editions, and plans a new set based on the battle of Liyue Harbor against Osial and the Fatui. She wants a figurine of the Traveler, sold only to those who pre-order. The pair visit Ying'er at Scent of Spring for measurements, then Xingxi at Mingxing Jewelry to commission the piece. Ningguang says the set is meant to commemorate rather than profit. Back at the Jade Chamber she confesses she lied to Xingxi: sacrificing the Jade Chamber was not a calm calculation, and she grieved it like losing a lifelong companion. She says she is not always as strong as people think and would make the same choice again.

**Starting From Zero (ending: Fortunes Shared).** Ningguang wants to re-live her life before the Qixing. The first attempt, trying to sell unclaimed goods, fails because everyone defers to her rank, so they hunt treasure chests with the Traveler (Ningguang joins the party as a trial character), chase a Weasel Thief for Mora, and finally catch fish by hand and grill them on the shore. She talks about her mother, who disliked the idea of her starting a business, and her affection for fish. Ending: Fortunes Shared.

**Endless Smoke (ending: Feint and Riposte).** The pair visit Northland Bank, where Ekaterina is hostile and refers to the huge reparations Ningguang imposed after the Fatui's actions. Leaving, they sense someone watching, quietly study the crowd, and identify the follower (a blond man in Snezhnayan dress). Returning, they overhear Northland staff arranging a surveillance operation. Ningguang notes their reaction shows a guilty conscience, and vows to investigate by the book.

**Business as Usual to Auction Games (ending: The Weight of a Collection).** Ningguang hosts the auction herself and sells everyday objects from her own collection at huge prices to hand-picked bidders. She reveals that after the Jade Chamber fell many of her belongings were salvaged and passed through many hands; each bidder is in possession of one. She offers refunds in exchange for returns, since proving ownership through courts would take too long and she would not pay twice for her own property.

**Business as Usual to Exchanging Intelligence (ending: While the View Remains Good).** Ningguang collects a repaired comb from Mingxing Jewelry for one of her child informants. The informants (Zhizhi, Little Long and Nannan) report on boats in the harbour; Nannan falsely repeats a story about a Fontaine merchant buying Luminescent Spines because two men gave her a replacement comb. The men, Lao Ke and Big Xu, turn out to have gone into debt buying Luminescent Spines. Ningguang scolds them for using a child, but offers to buy their stock under a contract that recoups any premium. Nannan chooses for them to play hide-and-seek with the children. Ningguang then explains that she has taught the children observation and critical thinking, never business, and hopes her name will outlive her as a symbol rather than a person.

**Quest tree (for reference).** The Jade Chamber Once More forks on the schedule: the rigorous schedule leads to Business as Usual, then either Exchanging Intelligence or Auction Games; the one-day-off schedule leads to Time Off!, then Liyue Millennial, or a choice of Starting From Zero or Endless Smoke. Endless Smoke can be failed outright: talking to bystanders or naming the wrong follower costs hearts, and running out ends the event as the quarry flees.

**Rigorous schedule contents.** The Traveler's serious day plan is: get ready, lunch with Luo Qiao at Liuli Pavilion, meet three informants, a conference at Yuehai Pavilion in the evening, a light meal and any follow-up negotiation, and a return to the Jade Chamber. Baishi praises it as rigorous and well-structured.

**Banquet gossip.** At Liuli Pavilion Luo Qiao (textile businesswoman) repeats rumours that the Traveler is part of Ningguang's inner circle alongside the Crux's captain, which Ningguang waves off while praising the Traveler as a hero of Liyue.

Revelations: Ningguang's Jade Chamber sacrifice hurt her badly. She grew up in a humble family, worked odd jobs, and associates fish with childhood. She distrusts the Fatui-linked Northland Bank and knows her reparations demand still sours relations. She regards Beidou as a business partner who supplies rare treasures but also costs her investment opportunities.

Ningguang confirms she is willing to be seen as tight-fisted for strategy, that she values trust over profit in dealing with informants, and that her goal for the children is to leave them able to judge for themselves.

Characters: Ningguang and the Traveler lead. Her secretaries Baishi (daily schedule and image), Baiwen and Baixiao (experienced tasks) appear in the hub. Others by route: Gou San'er and Bolai (Starting From Zero), Ekaterina and Andrei of Northland Bank (Endless Smoke), Hongru and Luo Qiao (banquet), Lanyang (tailored clothes), Ying'er of Scent of Spring and Xingxi of Mingxing Jewelry (chess figurine), Xiaofei, Yingfeng and Little Bin (auction bidders), the children Zhizhi, Little Long and Nannan, and the merchants Lao Ke and Big Xu.

Zhizhi, Little Long and Nannan are young children who act as Ningguang's informants. The event stresses that she treats them protectively and that she is angry when others exploit them.

Consequences: Each ending is a Memory with no effect on later quests. Rewards scale with the number of endings completed (Primogems, Adventure EXP, Hero's Wit, Guide to Prosperity, Prithiva Topaz Fragments and Qiankun Mora Meat).

Placement: Release order: Version 2.4. Story order: after The Crane Returns on the Wind, the finale of the Liyue Archon Quest, since Ningguang refers openly to the Jade Chamber's sacrifice and the battle against Osial, and to Fatui reparations. It precedes any later Liyue material.

425.content: A strategy board game of Ningguang's own design, based on classical chess with different rules, pieces and boards. She has made over thirty editions, wants it to carry Liyue's culture, and plans a commemorative set of the battle for Liyue Harbor with limited-edition figurines.

426.comment: Hangout Event: Ningguang: The Jade Chamber Auction
426.content: In Auction Games Ningguang sells ordinary items from her private collection to hand-picked bidders at inflated prices. She explains that she was not trying to profit: after the Jade Chamber fell, many of her belongings were salvaged and resold, and every bidder holds one. She offers to refund them in exchange for the return of her property.

427.comment: Hangout Event: Ningguang: Luminescent Spine Speculation
427.content: A rumour that a Fontaine merchant will pay a premium for Luminescent Spines inflated their price. Ningguang warns Luo Qiao off, saying the current price is far above what the end product can earn, and later finds Lao Ke and Big Xu ruined by it.

428.content: Three children whom Ningguang treats as helpers and friends. She teaches them to observe, analyse and think critically but never business. When two merchants coach Nannan to lie, Ningguang is angry, gives Nannan the repaired comb (a gift from her mother, who has left Liyue Harbor), and lets Nannan decide the punishment.

429.content: In Endless Smoke Ekaterina greets Ningguang coldly, citing the reparations Ningguang imposed on the Fatui after the Liyue Harbor battle, which Northland Bank paid. After a brief visit the staff order surveillance of Ningguang, which she reads as a sign of guilt. She warns the Traveler that the bank is more than a commercial organisation.

430.content:
Hangout Event: Noelle (also: Noelle Hangout Event, Noelle's Hangout Event, Chivalric Training, Knightly Exam Prep, Maid-in-Training, Studious Maid): Noelle's Hangout Event is a two-act branching side story in which the Traveler spends time with Noelle, the Knights of Favonius' maid who dreams of becoming a knight. Act I (Chivalric Training) follows her small efforts to improve; Act II (Knightly Exam Prep) is about her anxiety over the Knights' selection exam. The Traveler's choices decide which of six endings each act reaches.

It is a Hangout Event, played with Story Keys. Each act is a tree of short quests: the Traveler's dialogue choices change what Noelle does, and some paths end in a failed hangout instead of an ending. The tone is warm and comic, with Noelle's earnestness, over-preparation and difficulty saying no driving most of the jokes. Nothing in it alters the main story.

Across both acts the theme is the same: Noelle measures herself against more accomplished Knights (Jean, Kaeya, Amber) and worries she is not ready, and the Traveler helps her see that the small, caring work she already does is part of the kind of knight she wants to be.

Plot: Act I: Noelle asks the Traveler for help with her "chivalric training". Act II: with the exam looming, she studies herself ragged until the Traveler steers her toward a trip to Liyue, a mock adventurer's exam, or practising knightly roles.

**Act I - Chivalric Training (summary-level).** Noelle asks the Traveler for guidance in the Knights' library. Paths lead to errands around Mondstadt and the merchant Alois, strength training, or a rest at Good Hunter and Beatrice's date problem, ending in a paper rose or a study of love books.

**Act II - Knightly Exam Prep.** After the Traveler returns from Liyue, Noelle is found cooped up in the library. She works for the Knights as a maid but must still pass the selection exam to become a knight, has failed it several times, and says it is about half a year away. She plans to sleep two hours less a day to study and nearly faints. The Traveler offers three routes: a change of scenery (Journey to Liyue), facing the stress by taking another exam (Adventurer's Entrance Exam), or imagining herself passing (Noelle Rides Out).

**Act I - Chivalric Training (summary-level).** Noelle meets the Traveler in the library of the Knights of Favonius Headquarters and asks for guidance. The Traveler can say it is fine not to be a knight, or ask where she wants to start. Telling her it is fine leads to small tasks around Mondstadt and to Alois, a travelling merchant who wants Mondstadt wine for Liyue; Noelle's heavy hospitality unsettles him and, depending on the Traveler's replies, he either confesses a scheme to copy Dandelion Wine and leaves, or leaves grateful without confessing. Asking about the training leads Noelle to say something feels lacking. If it is strength, they visit the training grounds, where she smashes every dummy but laments always losing to other Knights; the Traveler can blame inexperience (fights outside the city, then a rescue of Henning from a hilichurl camp) or insist on strength (a mining site where monsters and a rockfall appear and she clears them). If it is rest, they go to Good Hunter, where Beatrice asks for help getting Quinn's attention. A gift of Mondstadt Grilled Fish fails and Noelle goes back to the library to study books about love; a gift from With Wind Comes Glory leads to planning a date, which Beatrice settles at Cape Oath, and Noelle gives the Traveler a paper rose.

**Journey to Liyue.** Noelle, shy and self-conscious in Liyue, is repeatedly mistaken for a Knight of Favonius. At Wanmin Restaurant she insists on the local Black-Back Perch Stew, finds it extremely spicy and then learns the broth was not meant to be drunk. At Hanfeng's Ironmongers a Liyue boy, Dugu Shuo, suspects her of loitering, asks to see her greatsword and Geo Vision, and leaves declaring they will meet again. The Traveler then chooses the harbour or Third-Round Knockout.

**Adventurer's Entrance Exam.** Noelle asks Katheryne about a Guild ranking exam, but only members may take them. Katheryne sends her to Cyrus, the Mondstadt branch master, who is drafting an entrance exam and wants a trial run at top difficulty. It has three parts and passing two is enough: three knowledge questions, a survival dish (steak is praised; Mondstadt Grilled Fish is accepted less warmly), and defeating a Ruin Guard at Brightcrown Canyon within a time limit. A perfect score ends with Cyrus trying to recruit her; missing one part ends with Noelle returning to the library to study even more. Failing two parts is a failed hangout.

**Noelle Rides Out.** The Traveler asks what kind of knight she might become. Starting with an Outrider like Amber, she gathers fresh Valberries and Pyro Slime Condensate in the Stormbearer Mountains and makes a Baron Bunny, but it neither draws the hilichurls nor explodes, and she has to fight them herself. She concludes she is not suited to be an Outrider, and the Traveler offers two other models: Jean or Kaeya.

**While the Millelith Stands Guard.** At Liyue Harbor the Millelith soldier Sha'yin, who heard a Knight of Favonius was in Liyue, asks for help arresting Treasure Hoarders from Mondstadt near Stone Gate; he needs a Knight as a witness because the Millelith could not pursue them across the border. The Traveler, as an Honorary Knight, can qualify. Noelle asks to guard the escape route alone and succeeds, then asks the Traveler to stay a little longer and shares tea at a stall, saying she is less afraid of the exam. The ending is "Rest Amidst the Rocks".

**A Knight's Journey Through Liyue.** At Third-Round Knockout the storyteller Iron Tongue Tian wants Noelle as source material for a story called "A Knight's Journey Through Liyue". She agrees reluctantly because she is not an official Knight. She cleans out a hilichurl camp and fights the returning hilichurls while he takes notes, then helps him get a Chaos Device from a Ruin Guard as a "memento". His retelling is wildly exaggerated; the audience, including Qian and Guanhai, doubts it until he shows the part, and they then recognise Noelle. She flees. The ending is "The Maid-Knight's Tale".

**Substitute Acting Grand Master Noelle.** Modelling herself on Jean, Noelle helps Marjorie find a monocle imported from Sumeru, asking Mondstadt locals and following a flapping sound to a finch nest on a rooftop. Marjorie jokes that Noelle is like a second Jean; Noelle says she helps because she wants to, not because she is a maid, and that she may simply keep doing small things when she is a knight. The ending is "The One and Only Noelle".

**Noelle the Intelligence Operative.** Modelling herself on Kaeya, Noelle goes to the Angel's Share to gather intelligence, but Charles gives her a waitress shift. She serves a drunk regular, Payne, tries to sober him with dried fruit, clears the upper floor and works until late, forgetting the intelligence goal. Charles says her service made the night better and may hire waiting staff. The ending is "Work Made for a Maid".

Every Act II branch follows the same shape: Noelle starts with a plan to fix her nerves, the plan partly fails, and what helps is what she already does. The Traveler's choices mostly change how she answers; the Act II endings are "Rest Amidst the Rocks", "The Maid-Knight's Tale", "Perfect Score", "Points Deducted", "The One and Only Noelle" and "Work Made for a Maid". The six Act I endings are "A Cold Reception", "Goodbye, Miss Maid!", "A Defender's Will Is Their Strength", "A Maid Above Ground", "A Conundrum Called Love" and "Whisper of the Paper Rose". Each act's endings give Adventure EXP plus a mix of Hero's Wit, Primogems and materials.

Revelations: No main-story revelations. The event shows how Noelle sees herself and her exam.

Noelle has failed the Knights' selection exam several times and becomes anxious and blank when something unexpected happens in an exam. She works for the Knights as a maid and still needs to pass it to be an official Knight. She once got Amber to teach her to make Baron Bunnies, and finds she is not suited to being an Outrider.

She says she never dared imagine what kind of knight she would be, fearing disappointment, and by the end of Substitute Acting Grand Master Noelle decides she may simply keep doing what she does now. She says the Traveler's presence calms her during exams.

Characters: The Traveler and Noelle.

Mondstadt: Katheryne, Cyrus (branch master of the Adventurers' Guild), Charles, Payne, Marjorie, Alfry, Margaret, Raymond, Glory and Beatrice. Liyue: Chef Mao, Dugu Shuo, Sha'yin, Iron Tongue Tian, Qian and Guanhai. Act I: Alois, Henning and Quinn. Jean, Kaeya and Amber are discussed as models but do not appear in the Act II quests read.

Consequences: No lasting canon change; the event is a self-contained character study. The real exam is never taken.

Placement: Act I was released in Version 1.4 and Act II in Version 1.5. Act I requires the Mondstadt Archon Quest (Song of the Dragon and Freedom) and Act II follows the Liyue Archon Quest A New Star Approaches, since Noelle has just welcomed the Traveler back from Liyue. It is a side story with no fixed place in the in-world timeline.

431.comment: Hangout Event: Noelle: Knights of Favonius selection exam
431.content: In this event Noelle says she has failed the Knights of Favonius selection exam several times. It assesses knowledge, including a thesis on chivalry and Favonius bladework, and combat. She has already worked for the Knights as a maid for some time but must pass it to be an official Knight. The exam is described as about half a year off at the start of Act II and is never actually held.

432.comment: Hangout Event: Noelle: Adventurer's Entrance Exam
432.content: Cyrus, the Mondstadt Adventurers' Guild branch master, was drafting a new entrance exam when Noelle asked for a trial. It has knowledge, survival-cooking and Ruin Guard combat parts; passing two of three succeeds. Noelle never intended to join the Guild, and Cyrus tries to recruit her anyway.

433.comment: Hangout Event: Noelle: Black-Back Perch Stew
433.content: At Wanmin Restaurant, Chef Mao's signature stew is very spicy. Noelle insists on the local version rather than a milder one, finishes it with difficulty and learns afterwards that the soup is not normally drunk.

434.comment: Hangout Event: Noelle: The Maid-Knight's Tale
434.content: A storyteller at Third-Round Knockout turns Noelle's cleaning of a hilichurl camp and a Ruin Guard memento into an exaggerated legend. The audience half-believes it and recognises Noelle, who had wanted it corrected.

435.content: A Liyue boy who suspects Noelle of loitering at Hanfeng's Ironmongers, then asks to see her greatsword and Geo Vision. He hopes to get a Geo Vision himself one day.

436.comment: Hangout Event: Noelle: Baron Bunny (Noelle's attempt)
436.content: Noelle once got Amber to teach her to make Baron Bunnies. Her copy uses Pyro Slime Condensate and crushed Valberries but fails in the field, one reason she concludes she is not suited to be an Outrider.

437.comment: Hangout Event: Noelle: Marjorie's lost monocle
437.content: A fragile monocle imported from Sumeru goes missing from Marjorie's shop. Noelle and the Traveler trace a flapping sound to a finch nest on a rooftop and recover it without troubling the Knights.

438.comment: Hangout Event: Noelle: Waiting tables at the Angel's Share
438.content: Imitating Kaeya's intelligence work, Noelle ends up working a waitress shift for Charles, serving a drunk regular, Payne, and forgetting to gather intelligence. Charles says the customers were happier that night and talks of hiring waiting staff.

439.content:
Hangout Event: Sayu (also: Yoohoo Art: Seichou no Jutsu, Sayu Hangout Event, Sayu's Hangout Event): Hangout Event: Sayu is a branching, player-choice side story added in version 2.2 (Act I, "Yoohoo Art: Seichou no Jutsu"). Sayu, a young ninja of the Shuumatsuban who would rather nap than work, tells the Traveler she has been given a mission to ambush them, though she has no intention of doing it. Together they dodge her shrine-maiden supervisor Kano Nana, try to help Sayu grow taller, and uncover who forged the order. The tone is gentle and funny, with a tender thread about Sayu's absent sensei and her fear of disappointing people. Six endings are possible.

The event needs two Story Keys and first requires the Archon Quest "Omnipresence Over Mortals". The branches are alternate versions of the same few days, not a single timeline. Throughout, Sayu is portrayed factually as a child-like, sleepy, earnest ninja: she is anxious about her height, hides in disguises, and wants to be useful to someone she trusts.

The main emotional line is that Sayu feels everyone has hopes for her (Kano Nana, Kamisato Ayaka, her sensei) and fears she cannot meet them, so she retreats into sleep. The Traveler is allowed to treat her as a friend and a kind of stand-in for her sensei.

Plot: At Chinju Forest Sayu explains her grievance: she sleeps constantly to grow taller, yet has not grown, and the shrine maiden keeps assigning chores. The Traveler can tell her sleep alone will not help, advise on quality of sleep, or urge her not to neglect her work. The first two lead to hiding and eating schemes; the third leads to a day of ninjutsu training. In parallel the forged-order mystery resolves in one of two ways, depending on whether the Traveler thanks Kano Nana and drops the matter or keeps investigating.

Branch "Bottleneck Breaking" - Sayu tries to grow taller by eating. At Kiminami Restaurant she orders a large meal and struggles to finish it. Pushing on ("Hard Work Pays Off") leaves her ill after eating at Shimura's, until Kano Nana's voice makes her bolt and she falls; ending "Everything in Moderation". Instead, the Traveler suggests exercise after eating ("Exercise Follows Eating"); they chase Treasure Hoarders for Kiminami Anna, but a tall hoarder's hand lands on Sayu's head, which she considers disastrous for her growth. The Traveler takes her to a high place to comfort her, where she imagines being tall enough to pick fruit and swim in deep water. Ending: "Like Soaring Through the Skies".

Branch "Sleep Alone Can't Wait" - Sayu looks for better napping places. Her usual spot is overrun with Pyro Slimes; her backup spot has caltrop-like training devices set by the Shuumatsuban, which she and the Traveler clear away so kitsune are not hurt. She decides the safest place is the sakura tree at the Grand Narukami Shrine and sneaks in with the Traveler despite the Yashiro Commission staff there. Kano Nana nonetheless tracks her there, and Sayu dashes off. Ending: "Definitely No Work Today!".

Branch "Operation Substitution" - Kano Nana gives agility and live-combat ninjutsu training; Sayu demonstrates, then offers to teach the Traveler her "Twinjutsu". On a break by a tree with a rope marking her height from when her sensei left, Sayu reflects on how a tree grows, blooms and gives shade, and wonders whether she can fulfil everyone's hopes if she never grows tall. She brings the Traveler fruit and says they remind her of her sensei. Ending: "With the Trees".

Branch "Shuumatsuban Suspicions" - If the Traveler instead continues investigating the order, Sayu arranges a meeting with the Yashiro Commission's order courier, Ogawa. Ogawa believes Sayu completed the ambush; then the Traveler appears and he admits forging the order because the Kairagi were holding his daughter Kotomi hostage. The Traveler can have Sayu hold him and bring him to Kamisato Ayaka, who opens an investigation (ending "Little Sayu's Troubles"), or help him: they decoy the Kairagi, Sayu swaps places with Kotomi, the Tenryou Commission arrests Inou, and Kotomi calls Sayu "Ms. Ninja" (ending "The Best Rest").

Further detail:

- Opening: Sayu says she is a member of the Shuumatsuban, whose job includes handling matters that are "inconvenient" to superiors, "which sometimes includes ambushing people", and that she has been assigned such a task even though she is never given them. She blames the order for disrupting her sleep.
- Kano Nana tells the Traveler she has heard of them from Kamisato Ayaka. She says Sayu is "extremely loyal" and neglects duties but would never act presumptuously; "given her age", serious tasks are not assigned to her. She is exasperated by Sayu's habit of copying other people's phrasing.
- The Traveler can find the forged order's origin quickly by pretending the ambush succeeded: Sayu bags "evidence", sends it through the reporting crate and receives a new meeting place from Ogawa.
- In "Operation Substitution" the agility course gives rating lines based on how quickly the Traveler finishes (a fast mujina, an ordinary kitsune, or a slow turtle), recalling her sensei's scoring.
- Sayu says her sensei measured her height on a tree and tied a rope there; she feels the rope keeps rising with the tree. She did not ask her sensei's name, and cannot say how tall they were beyond being taller than her.
- "Shuumatsuban Suspicions" (Face-Off): Ayaka tells the Traveler that Sayu's sensei asked her to watch over Sayu, which is why she assigned Kano Nana. She says Sayu has been lost since the sensei's sudden departure, and that she wants to help but suspects Sayu keeps her at a distance. Sayu tells the Traveler she dislikes visiting Ayaka because the expectations press harder there.
- Rewards: Adventure EXP plus Primogems or enhancement materials depending on the ending.

Revelations: - Sayu is a member of the Shuumatsuban, the ninja corps that handles tasks for the Yashiro Commission, usually assigned errands such as carrying documents and organising tools rather than missions.
- Kano Nana is the Grand Narukami Shrine's shrine maiden and acts as Sayu's supervisor; Ayaka says Sayu's sensei asked her to watch over Sayu's progress, which is partly why she assigned Kano Nana.
- Sayu's sensei taught her ninjutsu and left suddenly; she never learned their name and is unsure what they were.
- The ambush order was forged by Ogawa, a Yashiro Commission courier, under coercion from the Kairagi who held his daughter.

- Sayu can transform into a ball and prefers to avoid fights, but is shown to be skilled in combat and stealth, and clever enough to stage a swap with the hostage.
- The Shuumatsuban's training devices are not marked for outsiders and endanger forest wildlife until Sayu and the Traveler clear them.

Characters: Sayu is the lead; the Traveler is her helper and eventual confidant. Kano Nana, the shrine maiden of the Grand Narukami Shrine, is her supervisor. Kamisato Ayaka appears in the "Shuumatsuban Suspicions" Face-Off scene. Ogawa (Yashiro Commission courier), his daughter Kotomi, the Kairagi leader Inou, Tenryou Commission member Aoki, and Kiminami Anna of Kiminami Restaurant also appear.

Consequences: The event does not change the main story. It deepens Sayu's characterisation: she is sleepy and avoidant but also caring, and moved by a child's thanks.

The rescue branches end with Sayu willing to help the Traveler with future work and with her wanting to be reachable; the troubled branches end with her struggling to cope with the weight of expectation.

Placement: Released in version 2.2. It is set after the Archon Quest "Omnipresence Over Mortals" and the Watatsumi war, with the Yashiro Commission and Shuumatsuban in normal operation. No content from 6.x to 7.1 was found that revises the event.

440.content: Sayu's sensei taught her ninjutsu, was patient and strong, and never pushed her to do more work. They measured her height on a tree with a rope marker and told her nothing is more satisfying than growing. They left suddenly for "important matters" and asked Ayaka to watch over Sayu. Sayu never asked their name and only half-remembers whether they described themselves as a ninja. She says the Traveler reminds her of them.

441.comment: Hangout Event: Sayu: The Forged Ambush Order
441.content: Ogawa, a Yashiro Commission official responsible for delivering orders to the Shuumatsuban, was forced by the Kairagi Inou to forge a Commission order for an ambush of the Traveler; his daughter Kotomi was taken. He assigned it to Sayu because she never completes confrontational jobs and Kano Nana oversees her. When the Traveler learns of the order, Kano Nana checks with the Yashiro Commission and confirms it did not come from them. In the helpful branch the Traveler and Sayu stage a fake ambush report, Sayu swaps places with the hostage, and the Tenryou Commission arrests Inou.

442.comment: Hangout Event: Sayu: Kano Nana and Sayu
442.content: Kano Nana is the shrine maiden of the Grand Narukami Shrine who also takes work from the Shuumatsuban. Sayu regards her as a "bane" because she always finds Sayu's napping places and turns them into training grounds. Kano Nana is stern but dutiful, protective of the Traveler's safety and cautiously proud of Sayu's real skills.

443.content:
Hangout Event: Shikanoin Heizou (also: Trap 'Em by Storm, Heizou Hangout Event, Shikanoin Heizou's Hangout Event, Heizou Talks Fraud, Ryuuji Case): Hangout Event: Shikanoin Heizou is a branching, player-choice side story added in version 2.8 (Act I, "Trap 'Em by Storm"). Ryuuji of the Bantan Sango Detective Agency commissions the Traveler to find the missing Tenryou Commission detective Shikanoin Heizou, who is actually investigating a feeling that something is missing on Watatsumi Island. Depending on choices, the Traveler follows him through a trade-smuggling case, a staged anti-fraud play with Arataki Itto, or the old "Ryuuji Case" murder. Five endings are possible.

The event needs two Story Keys and first requires the Archon Quest "Omnipresence Over Mortals", the story quest "Transient Dreams" and the story quest "Rise Up, Golden Soul". The branches are alternate paths, not one timeline. Heizou is shown as talkative and theatrical in public and more thoughtful and uncertain in private, with an intuition he trusts more than evidence.

The recurring themes are intuition against evidence, the limits of the law, and whether protecting someone from a painful truth is a kindness. Heizou treats the Traveler as a partner and, in the last branch, as the person he trusts to judge him.

Plot: If the Traveler agrees to investigate, the trade-smuggling case ("The Missing Thing") ends in "Memories Do Not Evaporate". Otherwise, Heizou goes back to the Police Station ("Report back"), where Kujou Sara makes the Traveler his temporary supervisor. There the Traveler picks a case file: the anti-fraud play "Heizou Talks Fraud" (endings "Free Onikabuto Lunch" and "The Three Undeceivables"), or one of the other two files, which sends the story to Sango's complaint letter and the "Long-Sealed Mystery" about the Ryuuji Case (endings "There's One Secret" and "The Famous Detective's Principles").

Branch "The Missing Thing" - Heizou and the Traveler find Sango Pearls and Crystal Marrow in the Nobushi camp. They ask Shibata at Sangonomiya Shrine, then Gorou, who admits the caravans were robbed and asks them to investigate the Ritou merchant Godot, because Watatsumi cannot easily investigate on Ritou. Heizou privately suspects Gorou of lying and follows the caravan leader Todoroki to Bourou Village, where wounded veterans (Tokuda and Masashi, who knew the Traveler as "Captain of Swordfish II") report seizing goods from bandits. Crates of medicinal herbs without tax clearance, with a torn bill naming a "Foreign Trade Association" Heizou has never heard of at Ritou, suggest smuggling. Captured thieves say pirates led by a woman with an eye patch took an earlier cargo, and Heizou concludes Todoroki is making a secret deal with pirates, with Gorou covering for him. The next morning at Sangonomiya Shrine, Heizou confronts Todoroki, who orders the veterans to arrest them until Gorou intervenes and admits misleading them. Todoroki explains the island cannot grow food or herbs, that buying from Ritou is heavily taxed, and that both his sons died, one of them for lack of medicine. Gorou says a new commodity tax bill would solve it. Heizou offers to stay on Watatsumi Island, as a reassurance, until the bill passes, and has Gorou promise not to lie to him or the Traveler again. His private conclusion is that what the island "lacked" was only apparent: he sensed the islanders' vitality. Ending: "Memories Do Not Evaporate".

Branch "Report back" - At the Police Station, Uesugi and Yoriki Owada greet Heizou; Sara scolds him for missing work and assigns the Traveler as his supervisor for the day. Heizou finds three case files: an approval for his anti-fraud event, "The Case of the Missing Eastern Express" (a lost dog) and "The Prince of Mischief in Hanamizaka". He is also served a complaint letter from Sango. Choosing the anti-fraud file starts "Heizou Talks Fraud"; choosing either of the others sends Heizou and the Traveler to Sango's detective agency about her complaint.

Branch "Heizou Talks Fraud" - Heizou needs two "scam artists" and one "mark" for a short play. He recruits Etsu (a former fraud convict doing community service at the Grand Narukami Shrine) and the elderly Mr. Iba (also caught in a fraud case; he agrees when Heizou mentions his granddaughter would attend) and, on Paimon's suggestion, Itto as the mark, bribing him with a photographed Emperor Onikabuto. In the play Itto plays "Doushin Arataki", who helps Etsu after her grandfather (Iba) loses money to notes posing as the Raiden Shogun, Ms. Hina and Itto himself. Etsu then begs for 500,000 Mora, offering a share of 10,000 Onikabuto; a prop cheque appears. Itto is tempted but asks whether a Doushin really earns so much, and the Traveler is asked to help him. If the Traveler helps, Itto spots that Etsu and Iba are the scammers ("Free Onikabuto Lunch"); otherwise he follows his heart and decides the cheque-carrying Doushin must be the criminal and refuses to hand it over ("The Three Undeceivables"). Heizou closes by explaining that scams cast wide nets. His promised Emperor Onikabuto prize for Itto turns out to be a non-moving figurine: in the Undeceivables branch he admits he was fooled by false advertising and Itto passes the figurine to the Traveler as a reminder.

Branch "Long-Sealed Mystery" - Sango demands that the Ryuuji Case be reopened. Years earlier, the head of the Police Station, Takatsukasa Isamu, died of poison. Ryuuji, his assistant, was arrested, and Sango, hired by the Takatsukasa Clan, identified the forensic doctor Shiroyama as the real killer. Shiroyama died by suicide before he could testify. Both convictions were signed by Kujou Sara. The Traveler reviews the case file with Heizou, identifies the motive (Isamu blackmailed Shiroyama with his pregnant wife) and the means (a toxin dissolved in the cold medicine rather than the fish-liver paste, as the autopsy suggests). Heizou then shows a torn research-log page: the poison works only when a particular cold medicine and the expensive fish-liver paste are combined, both harmless alone. Heizou says he found it in Kujou Takayuki's warehouse, that Shiroyama had worked for the Kujou Clan, and that Ryuuji only delivered the paste. He hid the truth to protect Ryuuji and asks the Traveler to decide whether to reveal it.
