Telling Sango and Ryuuji only that Shiroyama was guilty leads to "There's One Secret"; telling everything leads to "The Famous Detective's Principles", where Ryuuji is shaken but recovers the next day and Sango admits she now understands why Heizou left.

Further detail:

- Opening: Ryuuji, Sango's assistant, describes Heizou as lively and accurate at spotting bad actors, almost as if relying on a sixth sense. Sango, who dislikes Heizou, calls him an obstacle in her path. Ryuuji later says Heizou was once a detective at the agency before leaving. Ryuuji says Sango forbids him from acting friendly with Heizou in public.
- On Watatsumi Island Heizou explains that during the war Kujou Takayuki, then head of the Tenryou Commission, secretly sent him to investigate Watatsumi Island, and that he treated the trip as a paid vacation; he says Sangonomiya's soldiers have been watching him since. He teases Paimon about being a "Voice", meaning an external voice for the Traveler.
- "Complaint Letter Branch": Sango's complaint accuses Heizou of abusing his power to conceal the truth of the Ryuuji Case. Heizou says the case is solved and he has disclosed what he could.
- In "Heizou Talks Fraud", Heizou's cousin Kano Nana calls him a "brat" and tells the Traveler to discipline him; Etsu says the community-service deal he arranged was not the reduction she hoped for. Iba says Heizou knows how to get information from elders by being polite. Iba says criminals have a nickname for Heizou that makes him sound like a force of nature.
- In the Long-Sealed Mystery review, the clues include the autopsy report (Isamu was 41), Ryuuji's testimony, Shiroyama's testament, Isamu's threatening letter, the two convictions, the toxicology report (the toxin dissolves only in water and was not on any guild ledgers) and a blank page of the research log. The Traveler can raise doubts on points such as the International Trade Association's records. Heizou says Sara changed Ryuuji's sentence before signing it, from death to temporary incarceration pending trial, because the case had no confession or complete evidence.
- Ryuuji tells Chika, Isamu's young daughter, he is her "brother" because Isamu treated him like a son. The ending quote, "Some things will always be more important than the truth", is Heizou's principle.
- Rewards: Adventure EXP plus Primogems or enhancement materials depending on the ending; a furnishing, the Fabled Emperor Onikabuto, is awarded in the anti-fraud branch.

Revelations: - Heizou is a special detective of the Tenryou Commission (rank: Doushin) and cousin of the shrine maiden Kano Nana. Sango dislikes him; Ryuuji admires him.
- Watatsumi Island runs caravans to bring in food and medicinal herbs that its poor soil cannot grow; some of the goods are untaxed, so Gorou hid the truth from Heizou until the Traveler's presence made him reconsider. The Kanjou Commission is drafting a commodity tax bill that exempts needed goods.
- In the Ryuuji Case, Takatsukasa Isamu used Shiroyama's family as leverage; Shiroyama killed Isamu with a two-part poison that Ryuuji unwittingly helped deliver. Heizou's private conclusion is that Kujou Takayuki ordered it and planned to blame Ryuuji.

- Sara changed Ryuuji's conviction from death to temporary incarceration. Rumours blame her or the Kujou Clan; Heizou argues she acted from principle.
- Heizou has never heard of a "Foreign Trade Association" at Ritou and suspects smuggling.

Characters: Heizou is the lead; the Traveler and Paimon are his partner and supervisor. Ryuuji and Sango (Bantan Sango Detective Agency) open and close the main branches. Gorou, Todoroki, Tokuda, Masashi and Shibata appear on Watatsumi Island. Kujou Sara, Uesugi and Owada appear at the Police Station. Kano Nana, Etsu, Iba and Arataki Itto appear in the anti-fraud branch; Takatsukasa Chika, Isamu's daughter, in the Long-Sealed Mystery ending.

Consequences: The event does not change the main story. It shows Heizou's dual nature and adds background to the Kujou Clan, the Police Station and Watatsumi Island's trade difficulties. Whether the Ryuuji Case truth is revealed is a branch choice.

Placement: Released in version 2.8. It is set after the Watatsumi war and "Omnipresence Over Mortals", with the Sakoku Decree already ended. No content from 6.x to 7.1 was found that revises the event.

444.comment: Hangout Event: Shikanoin Heizou: Ryuuji Case
444.content: Years before the story, the head of the Police Station, Takatsukasa Isamu, died of poison. Ryuuji, his assistant, who regarded him as a foster father, was convicted within a week on a conviction signed by Kujou Sara and jailed. Sango's investigation then identified the forensic doctor Shiroyama, who died by suicide before he could be tried. Heizou's private reading: a harmless-looking cold medicine and an expensive fish-liver paste combined into a lethal poison; Shiroyama had once worked for the Kujou Clan, and Kujou Takayuki directed it. Ryuuji, who delivered the paste, does not know this. Sango believes Heizou is hiding something. Whether the truth is revealed depends on the player's choice.

445.comment: Hangout Event: Shikanoin Heizou: Watatsumi Island Trade Case
445.content: Watatsumi Island cannot grow enough food or medicinal herbs. To ease this Kokomi set up caravans under the farmer Todoroki, but Ritou's taxes are heavy. Nobushi and Treasure Hoarders prey on the caravans, and Todoroki also appears to buy scarce goods, including medicinal herbs, outside legal channels; a torn bill bears the name Foreign Trade Association, which Heizou does not recognise. Gorou concealed the arrangement from Heizou until the Traveler's presence and Heizou's offer to stay as a safeguard. A new commodity tax bill from the Kanjou Commission would exempt needed goods.

446.comment: Hangout Event: Shikanoin Heizou: Heizou Talks Fraud
446.content: Heizou's public-awareness play about scams. Etsu and Iba, both former fraud convicts, play the scammers; Arataki Itto plays a Doushin who must resist offers that are too good to be true. In the end Heizou's lesson is "Don't get greedy and you won't be needy; stay alert and you won't get hurt." The Tenryou Commission approved the project.

447.content:
Hangout Event: Thoma (also: A Housekeeper's Daily Chores, Thoma Hangout Event, Thoma Hangout): Hangout Event: Thoma is the branching Hangout Event for Thoma, the Kamisato Clan's housekeeper, added in version 2.2 and unlocked after Omnipresence Over Mortals. Thoma wants to thank the Traveler for helping during the Vision Hunt Decree by spending a day off with them. Depending on the Traveler's choices, the day ends in one of six endings: a housekeeping class, a knitting lesson, a vigil with a grieving ninja dog, sweaters for stray animals, a trip to Ritou, or a quiet scheme to rescue the Yashiro Commission from a price-gouging merchant.

It is a single act, "A Housekeeper's Daily Chores", made of ten quests in a decision tree. Requirements are Adventure Rank 30, two Story Keys and completion of Omnipresence Over Mortals. The event shows Thoma at ease: a cook, seamstress and animal lover, but also a capable fixer who settles the Yashiro Commission's problems through contacts and does not care much about reputation. As a Hangout Event it is optional, and only one route is played per run.

Two themes recur on every route. One is Thoma's calm attitude to the disdain of some Yashiro samurai: he calls it ordinary gossip, says he cares about the wellbeing of the Kamisato Clan, and says it is enough that those close to him know the real him. The other is his preference for sincere, simple bonds over transactional ones, which the stray animals, the ninken Inu Shoushou and the Traveler's gift of a Windwheel Aster each illustrate.

Plot: **Behind His Back.** At the Kamisato Estate, the Traveler overhears the samurai Kazumasa and Furusawa grumbling that men like Thoma are why the samurai spirit is declining, adding that he is from Mondstadt and wondering what Miss Kamisato sees in him. Thoma arrives yawning (the rain has kept him awake), realises what was said and brushes it off as the usual treatment of people who do not fit in. Agreeing with him leads to Host's Invitation; disagreeing sends the Traveler off to ask around the Yashiro Commission and leads to Unforeseen Circumstances.

**Host's Invitation.** Thoma, as host, asks whether the Traveler prefers staying in or going out. Staying in means Komore Teahouse. Going out offers the stray cats and dogs by a sakura tree in Hanamizaka, or a day in Ritou, where the two first met.

**Thanks for Your Hospitality!** At Komore Teahouse Thoma serves a home-cooked meal, insists his cooking is ordinary despite the odd hot pot game, and offers to mend loose threads on the Traveler's cape. The Traveler suggests a housekeeping class for the Yashiro Commission to win him respect. Thoma doubts it would change opinions of him but likes the idea of sharing life-maintenance skills. The Traveler then chooses to advertise widely or keep it inside the Commission.

**Start Spreadin' the News (Popular Class).** The Traveler gathers Lavender Melon, Fowl and Flour, and helps Thoma recruit through the shopkeeper Ogura Mio, the housewives Yuuko and Yuuri, and the elderly Nagano. Thoma presents it as open to all genders and ages with free trial lessons. On the day the room is full, including Kazumasa and Furusawa, brought by Yuuko. Thoma starts teaching and then notices the Traveler dozing.

**Small-Scale Changes (Alone Time).** Keeping it within the Commission, the Traveler asks Hirano and Furuta, the Kamisato Clan's butler. Furuta suggests a spring-clean of the Yashiro Commission as a demonstration, and Thoma, lent as a trial character, weeds and waters the grounds with the Traveler. Few people come to the class. Thoma is unbothered and teaches the Traveler to knit.

**Under the Same Shade.** Thoma takes the Traveler to strays he feeds whenever he visits Komore Teahouse. He says he has trained them not to be aggressive. He then mentions a Shuumatsuban ninja dog he has seen alone on the beach north of Konda Village, which bit him when he tried to pet it. The Traveler chooses to visit it or to give it time.

**Ninken by the Shore (The Sea Breeze Carries Memories).** Thoma and the Traveler find the dog, clear monsters nearby, and still cannot coax it to eat or leave. Kazuaki of the Shuumatsuban identifies it as Inu Shoushou and says its owner went out to sea on a dangerous mission and will not return. He hands over the owner's worn training kunai. With it, the dog is more affectionate, and Thoma and the Traveler resolve to remember the owner alongside it.

**Bits and Bobs for Cats and Dogs (New Clothes!).** Instead, the Traveler and Thoma photograph the strays so Thoma can estimate their sizes. He tells how he first came to feed them, knits sweaters overnight and dresses the animals with the Traveler. One sweater does not quite fit.

**A Trip for Two in Ritou (A Lingering Fragrance).** In Ritou Thoma shows the Traveler a Chuyu Trading Company branch, Sailing Breeze (a Mondstadt wine shop), the International Trade Association and a quiet lookout. He tells of his arrival from Mondstadt. After a merchant gives him sweets as repayment for a favour, the Traveler gives him a Windwheel Aster, which moves him far more. He gives the Traveler a Lucky Omamori in return.

**Unforeseen Circumstances (The Housekeeper's Other Side).** Asking staff about Thoma, the Traveler learns from Kiyoe that ceremonial implements for next month's festival sank in a storm and that the merchant Yuusaku is demanding extortionate prices. Yuusaku also holds a grudge against Thoma. Thoma meets him, fails to move him, and then quietly squeezes Yuusaku's trade and loan terms through his own contacts. A panicked Yuusaku arrives at the Commission offering to sell at half price. Thoma slips away to sweep the corridors.
**The Behind His Back exchange.** Thoma tells the Traveler he does not mind the gossip because it does no harm to the Kamisato Clan. If the Traveler objects, he says that as a housekeeper it is not his place to throw his weight around with other Yashiro staff, but invites serious suggestions.

**Cooking and housekeeping.** When the Traveler jokes about the hot pot game, Thoma says he added odd ingredients only for the game and cooks ordinary dishes normally. He names cleaning, cooking and mending as his strengths and argues that looking after yourself is needed to do your best at work. In class he argues housekeeping matters most in marriage, because otherwise one partner shoulders the other's burden.

**The Unforeseen Circumstances route.** Thoma takes the Traveler to Yasutake, the quartermaster of the Tenryou Commission, who is choosing Iron Ore suppliers. Thoma offers an assessment of the bidders (two veterans whose prices could be talked down to around 80 percent, a high-volume newcomer needing inspection, and a loan-funded latecomer he advises against). In return Yasutake asks for help with Iron Ore deliveries being stolen between Konda Village and Inazuma City, and the Traveler and Thoma escort a cargo balloon through three waves of monsters. Yasutake also mentions that Sakai had lent Yuusaku money. Thoma then secures some Noctilucous Jade for Sakai in exchange for Sakai pressing Yuusaku about his debt. Back at the Commission, Kazumasa and Furusawa, who were reluctantly preparing to beg, see Yuusaku apologise to Thoma.

**Ritou details.** At the Chuyu Trading Company, Qiuyue sells a Noctilucous Jade necklace and a Cor Lapis bracelet, and Thoma buys both after asking for a fair price for his friend from Liyue. At Sailing Breeze he says he never got to share a drink with his father at the Angel's Share and would love to meet its owner. The Ritou dialogue changes depending on whether the Traveler has completed Transient Dreams, the Raiden Shogun's story quest: before it, Ritou is still under the Sakoku Decree; afterwards the decree has been repealed and trade is recovering. Outside the International Trade Association, a merchant named Keiichi thanks Thoma with sweets from Yumeno Tennenan for a favour done through Kurisu.

**The animal story.** Thoma recalls first feeding the stray dog on a rainy day, after an obstinate Kamisato Clan elder refused to see him during a visit about the clan's new policies. He sat under a tree with the dog and shared a cold onigiri. He says powerful people expect him to read what they want, but with animals one onigiri makes friends for life.

**Requirements and rewards.** The event requires Adventure Rank 30, two Story Keys and completion of Omnipresence Over Mortals. Each ending gives Adventure EXP and a mix of Hero's Wit, Primogems, Warmth, Guide to Transience or Agnidus Agate Fragments, according to the wiki. A Trip for Two in Ritou also grants a Lucky Omamori. This is gameplay information, not lore.

**Gameplay notes.** Co-op is disabled during several quests. In Small-Scale Changes Thoma is lent as a trial character. Attacking the strays in Under the Same Shade ends the event. A wiki trivia note observes that the housekeeping classes appear to be followed up in a later Thoma story quest, Thoma: Training Exam.

**Branch map.** The choices produce six endings: Popular Class, Alone Time, The Sea Breeze Carries Memories, New Clothes!, A Lingering Fragrance and The Housekeeper's Other Side. The first two follow Thanks for Your Hospitality!, the next two follow Under the Same Shade, the fifth follows A Trip for Two in Ritou and the last follows disagreeing in Behind His Back.

Revelations: - Thoma grew up in Mondstadt. His father returned to Inazuma and stopped writing, so Thoma sailed to find him with Dandelion Wine as a gift. A storm sank the boat and he drifted to Inazuma on wreckage (Ritou route).
- Thoma's mother gave him the omamori his father had given her, just before he left Mondstadt (Ritou route).
- He feeds strays because simple bonds are what he values most. He describes himself to powerful people as an expendable servant boy who must always consider what they want.

- Thoma quietly handles disputes involving merchants for the Yashiro Commission using personal contacts rather than authority, and is trusted by figures such as Yasutake and Sakai.
- The Yashiro Commissioner, Kamisato Ayato, has allowed Thoma to inquire into Shuumatsuban matters in exceptional cases, though not to command them.
- The Shuumatsuban never discloses the identities of ninja who die on missions and does not commemorate them publicly.
- When he first arrived in Inazuma Thoma would stand on the beach looking out at the horizon.

Characters: Thoma (host) and the Traveler (guest). Also: the Yashiro Commission samurai Kazumasa and Furusawa, the shopkeeper Ogura Mio, the housewives Yuuko and Yuuri, the elder Nagano, the Kamisato servants Hirano, Furuta and Koharu, Kiyoe, Yuusaku, Yasutake, Sakai, Kazuaki of the Shuumatsuban and the ninken Inu Shoushou, Qiuyue, Kaede and Keiichi in Ritou, and Kurisu, mentioned in passing. Kamisato Ayato and Kamisato Ayaka are referred to but do not appear.

Consequences: No lasting change to the main story. Depending on the route, Thoma holds a first housekeeping class, adds the Traveler to those who remember an unnamed Shuumatsuban ninja, clothes strays for winter, gives the Traveler a Lucky Omamori, or settles a festival supply dispute at Yuusaku's expense.

Placement: Released in version 2.2 with the Hangout Event feature. It takes place after Omnipresence Over Mortals and refers back to the Vision Hunt Decree. Some Ritou dialogue differs if the Traveler has completed Transient Dreams. Nothing after version 7.1 is used.

448.comment: Hangout Event: Thoma: Thoma's housekeeping class
448.content: In two routes of Thoma's Hangout Event, he and the Traveler organise a housekeeping class at the Yashiro Commission headquarters, open to any gender or age. In the widely advertised route (Popular Class) a full room attends, including Kazumasa and Furusawa, brought by Yuuko. In the quiet route (Alone Time) few attend and Thoma teaches the Traveler to knit instead. These are route-specific outcomes.

449.content:
Inu Shoushou is a red Shiba ninken with a scar by one eye, in black stealth gear, who belonged to a Shuumatsuban ninja who left on a dangerous sea mission and did not return. It waits on a beach north of Konda Village and refuses food. Kazuaki gives Thoma the owner's blunt training kunai, and the dog becomes more affectionate when Thoma and the Traveler keep it company.

The Shuumatsuban pays for the dog's upkeep. Thoma talks of building a kennel and making winter clothes for it. The owner is never named.

450.comment: Hangout Event: Thoma: Thoma and the stray animals
450.content: Thoma feeds stray cats and dogs under a sakura tree in Hanamizaka whenever he visits Komore Teahouse. He says it began when a stray shared shelter with him on a rainy day after an elder turned him away. In the New Clothes! route he knits sweaters for them, naming Petal, Darko and Goldilocks.

451.comment: Hangout Event: Thoma: Thoma's trip to Ritou
451.content: On the Ritou route Thoma tours the town with the Traveler. He tells how he arrived from Mondstadt looking for his father, recalls the town's freer days, and praises the quiet lookout he visits every time. He buys a necklace and bracelet at the Chuyu Trading Company, accepts sweets from a grateful merchant, and is deeply touched by a Windwheel Aster from the Traveler, giving them a Lucky Omamori in return.

452.comment: Hangout Event: Thoma: Yuusaku and the ceremonial implements
452.content: Yuusaku is a merchant on Narukami Island who once sold the Yashiro Commission defective ceremonial goods, was exposed by Thoma, and was held by the Tenryou Commission. He bears a grudge and raised his prices when the Commission's festival shipment sank. In the Unforeseen Circumstances route Thoma privately cuts off Yuusaku's trade and loan terms until he apologises and offers to sell at half price.

453.content:
Hangout Event: Yun Jin (also: A Song That Knows Grace, Yun Jin Hangout Event, Yun Jin's Hangout): Yun Jin's Hangout Event, a replayable, choice-driven side story. Days before a major performance, the star of the Yun-Han Opera Troupe vanishes to a dangerous spot in search of inspiration, and the Traveler brings her back. The one-act event, A Song That Knows Grace, then branches: a thank-you night that ends in a tangle with fake reporters or in a relaxed meal and a photograph, or a crash course in acting from Yun Jin herself. There are five endings.

It was added in Version 2.4 and requires two Story Keys, Adventure Rank 28 and completion of The Crane Returns on the Wind. Its quests are Countryside Wandering (hub), After the Curtain Falls, Backstage Suspicions, Half a Day's Leisure and First Glimpse of Meaning. The title is a partial quotation of a Chinese saying about hearing a stringed song and understanding the deeper meaning, associated with the friendship of Bo Ya and Zhong Ziqi, according to the wiki's trivia.

Hangout Events are permanent, replayable content, and each ending is a Memory that can be displayed in the Serenitea Pot. The event gives a close look at Yun Jin's craft, her anxiety about her public image, and her habit of using theatrical skill to solve real problems.

Plot: In Countryside Wandering the Adventurers' Guild's Katheryne introduces Yunning, manager of the Yun-Han Opera Troupe, who is frantic: Yun Jin has left a note saying she has gone to Lingju Pass to find inspiration for the "Divine Maiden" play. The Traveler finds her there, defeats a Ruin Hunter threatening her, and learns why she went. Yun Jin was inspired by Shenhe's remarks about the divine damsel, whose real behaviour was less heroic than the opera shows, and wanted to feel genuine danger to deepen her portrayal. She admits she was close to a breakthrough and does not promise to stop, but returns. At the Guild, Yunning begs the Traveler to talk her out of dangerous practice. The Traveler's answer forks the event.

**Agree with Yunning (safety first).** Yun Jin promises to rehearse in safety and invites the Traveler to meet at the Heyu Tea House after her show. This leads to After the Curtain Falls.

**Side with Yun Jin.** She is delighted. Yunning, panicking, asks the Traveler to keep her busy until the next show, and when the Traveler is cast as a would-be student, Yun Jin agrees to give informal lessons, meeting at the bridge at Feiyun Slope. This leads to First Glimpse of Meaning.

**After the Curtain Falls.** After her performance, Yun Jin meets the Traveler. Two admirers, Maksim and Gentry Maocai, invite her to dinner; she declines, citing her plans with the Traveler. At the tea house two people who say they are from The Steambird (the editor Boyi and journalist Shiyun) corner her with questions that drift from theatre to her private life, to Snezhnaya and the Fatui. The Traveler either urges her to take the interview (Backstage Suspicions) or advises her to book it through her manager (Half a Day's Leisure).

**Backstage Suspicions.** Yun Jin senses something wrong and asks the Traveler to follow the pair. Shiyun and Boyi are quarrelling: Boyi is a fake editor planning a sensational piece, and Shiyun, bound by a harsh contract with ruinous penalty clauses, is reluctant. Failing the stealth section ends the event at A Shame That the Road Is Rocky. Succeeding, the Traveler delivers a letter and returns with Shiyun to the tea house, where Yun Jin plays along with the interview, then bluffs about the Millelith and legal scrutiny so that Boyi flees back to his headquarters, leading Yunning and the Millelith to him. Yun Jin invites Shiyun to submit an article to the real Steambird. Ending: And Few Friends You Shall Find.

**Half a Day's Leisure.** Declining the interview frees the evening. At Chihu Rock Yun Jin takes the Traveler to Chen the Sharp's barbecue stall for Grilled Tiger Fish and plays a "hot pot" guessing game with mixed leftovers of experimental drinks. She tells the Traveler she is not the same offstage as on, and the Traveler can say her offstage self is the cuter one (Commemorative Photo at Chen the Sharp's stall, then a photo at Feiyun Slope; ending Brought Together by Common Interests) or prefer the stage persona (she hands over a signed publicity picture; ending A Souvenir Without Sentiment Is of Little Worth).

**First Glimpse of Meaning.** Yun Jin teaches three acting methods, each tested with a scene from the Traveler's fight at the Jade Chamber: Immersive Performance (re-live the emotion; the Traveler fails to convey it), Well-Honed Performance (use familiar experience in place of unfamiliar events) and Meticulous Performance (choreograph the scene and rehearse it). The last is a timed exercise at a stage she builds to the north of Liyue Harbor, breaking red scarecrows while avoiding blue ones. She admits she saw through Yunning's scheme to keep her busy, hopes to put part of the Traveler into her portrayal of the divine damsel, and suggests the title "Mentor". Ending: The Cast Contemplates the Play's Meaning.

**Endings (for reference).** A Shame That the Road Is Rocky (stealth failed; the troupe must be more cautious), And Few Friends You Shall Find (the fake reporters are exposed), Brought Together by Common Interests (the shared photographs), A Souvenir Without Sentiment Is of Little Worth (the autographed picture) and The Cast Contemplates the Play's Meaning (the acting lessons).

**Small details.** At the tea house after her show, several regulars remark on the performance, including the silk dance she added to the divine damsel's entrance, which the false journalist Shiyun praises as crane-like. In the barbecue scene Yun Jin says she avoids Wanmin Restaurant's spicy stew because it is hard on her throat and prefers open-air dining. When asked to improve the divine-damsel portrayal she says the operatic tradition keeps the voices and faces of bygone heroes alive, and hopes the Traveler's will one day appear on a Liyue stage too.

Revelations: Yun Jin pursues realism: she joins in dangerous experience to understand a character, writes to performers from many nations, and calls acting her bread and butter. She cherishes the audience members who truly appreciate nuance. The tabloids once ran a story casting her as a diva after she left an interview, so Yunning now handles all interview requests. The troupe's rules forbid taking private gifts from patrons.

Yun Jin says she hopes to one day write an opera about the Traveler and that she can use their courage as a reference for the divine damsel. She also states she is not an expert in law, and her legal-sounding bluff in Backstage Suspicions is an act meant to lure Boyi into revealing himself.

Characters: Yun Jin and the Traveler lead. Yunning is the troupe's manager and a worrier. Katheryne appears at the Guild. Others by route: Maksim and Gentry Maocai (admirers), Boyi and Shiyun (self-declared Steambird staff), Chen the Sharp and Dongsheng (food stalls) and Shenhe (mentioned only).

Consequences: No ending alters the main story. Rewards scale with the number of endings unlocked (Primogems, Adventure EXP, Hero's Wit, Guide to Diligence, Prithiva Topaz Fragments and Cloud-Shrouded Jade). Within the event, Boyi's business is set to be investigated by the Millelith, and Shiyun is offered a chance to write for the real Steambird.

Placement: Release order: Version 2.4. Story order: after The Crane Returns on the Wind, since Yun Jin and others refer to the Traveler having defeated an ancient god and the Fatui at Liyue Harbor, and to the Jade Chamber battle.

454.content: The manager of the Yun-Han Opera Troupe. She is very protective of Yun Jin, anxious about risks to her health and the troupe's schedule, and insists all interview requests go through her.

455.comment: Hangout Event: Yun Jin: Boyi and Shiyun
455.content: Boyi poses as the editor-in-chief of The Steambird and Shiyun as his journalist. Shiyun is a new employee bound by an extortionate contract, who is sympathetic to Yun Jin. Boyi plans a sensational story from a false interview. Yun Jin and the Traveler trick him into leading them to evidence, and Yunning reports him to the Millelith.

456.comment: Hangout Event: Yun Jin: Chen the Sharp's Stall
456.content: A barbecue stall at Chihu Rock famous for Grilled Tiger Fish and frequented by Yun Jin. In the event Chen is experimenting with a milk tea he heard about from a Mondstadt merchant, and Yun Jin turns the leftover drinks into a guessing game.

457.comment: Hangout Event: Yun Jin: Yun Jin's Acting Methods
457.content: In First Glimpse of Meaning Yun Jin teaches three approaches: relive the real emotion, substitute familiar experiences for unfamiliar ones, or choreograph and rehearse every detail. She says all three are valuable and that she will use any method that improves her performance.

key: Her Foes Rage Like Great Waters...
Her Foes Rage Like Great Waters
Behold, the Sign Comes Like A Thief...
Make Bright the Arrows, Gather the Shields...
For Her Judgment Reaches to the Skies...
458.comment: Her Foes Rage Like Great Waters...
458.content:
Her Foes Rage Like Great Waters... (also: Her Foes Rage Like Great Waters, Behold, the Sign Comes Like A Thief..., Make Bright the Arrows, Gather the Shields..., For Her Judgment Reaches to the Skies...): Her Foes Rage Like Great Waters... is a three-quest world quest series in the Sumeru desert from version 3.4, set among the Tanit tribe. The Traveler, Paimon and their friend Jeht become the target of the Tanit matriarch Babel, who wants control of the Eternal Oasis and of the Traveler's jinni. Babel sends assassins, tells each side the other has joined the Fatui, and is finally confronted and killed by Jeht, who leaves the tribe behind.

The series follows Apocalypse Lost and Rejoice With Me, for What Was Lost Is Now Found. Its titles come from biblical passages on the fall of Babylon (Babel in the Hebrew Bible), and Babel the matriarch is its antagonist. It is a story about a manipulative adoptive mother, a daughter who chooses a friend over her tribe, and what Jeht does with the name of her real mother.

The series also records how Fatui dealt with the Tanit: the letters the Traveler finds show a Fatui desert expedition receiving a young woman from the tribe for experiments, after a pre-arranged ambush. The Fatui are a threat to Jeht in the middle part, then a plot device for Babel's lies.

Plot: **Behold, the Sign Comes Like A Thief...** Yuften, stuttering and anxious, says an outside party delivering Anahitian Blessing never arrived, and blames northerners who he says have been more active since Aderfi and Azariq left. The Traveler follows a trail of dropped goods: a cracked jar, an empty box with the tribe's symbol, a hilichurl camp that has no cart parts, and a rug with blotches on it. Paimon suspects the clues are laid out too neatly. Eremites, including one named Bouhanu, ambush them, saying they are friends of Jeht and have been commissioned to give the Traveler "hospitality". The Traveler decides to return to the tribe but not mention Jeht. Yuften tells them to report to Babel, who says the northerners have long tried to push into the tribe's lands, that traitors have been raiding for months, and that the Traveler will be safe among the Tanit while Jeht is brought to help. Babel thanks the Traveler for opening the Eternal Oasis and says it is central to the tribe's faith as the sovereignty of Nabu Malikata, the Queen of All Oases. She says the Oasis is guarded by Jeht, who she says guards her parents. When pressed, Babel insists the goddess "was" present even though the Traveler did not see her.

**Make Bright the Arrows, Gather the Shields...** The next day Babel says a captured northerner claims that Jeht revealed Tanit outposts and sent assassins after the Traveler. She asks the Traveler to bring Jeht back, whether she can prove her innocence or not. At the marked Fatui outpost, a soldier challenges the Traveler for a password; the passwords turn out to be mixed up. Documents say the Fatui's talks with the Tanit are over, that the tribe will hand over a young woman for experiments, and that the soldiers are being moved. The soldier Orest says Jeht was caged, tore the cage apart and killed a soldier, and was sedated with Electro bullets. Orest asks the Traveler to tell his superiors to give up, and goes. Letters at the next camp from a Fatui lieutenant, Ruslan Snezhevich, and captain, Zoya Snezhevna, show that a Tanit tribeswoman named Jeht was handed over, that the transfer code is "Red Ball Express", and that she is to be moved to a canyon.

**For Her Judgment Reaches to the Skies...** The Traveler follows the sound of fighting to a Fatui hideout in a cave, from which Fatui soldiers are fleeing in panic, and where Jeht is badly hurt. She attacks in a rage, believing the Traveler betrayed her, and they fight until she is down to a fraction of her strength. She says she did not betray the tribe, and the Traveler says the same. The assassins Nayram and Rezki, two Tanit Falcons who are like family to Jeht, then arrive to kill her; they are beaten. After they rest, Jeht and the Traveler find Babel at the entrance to a canyon. Babel says the Eternal Oasis is the tribe's hope, that outsiders must be kept away, that the Tanit will rebuild a nation of oases and challenge the god of Sumeru, and that she will be the Prophetess of Nabu Malikata. She asks Jeht to choose between the Tanit and the Traveler, offers her the succession, and Jeht refuses. Jeht lists the elders she says she removed on Babel's orders (Bleda, Gwaffah and Teyya), says her mother's name is Ufairah Hindi, and takes it as her own. Babel calls her the daughter of a traitor and of an outsider, names her father Jebrael, and sets the tribe on them. After the fight, Babel is wounded and dying. She says she has already sent word to the tribes that Jeht is a traitor and that she had planned to remove her. Jeht kills her. Outside the camp Jeht says she has nowhere to return to, then accepts the Traveler's suggestion that she can now call anywhere home. She says she has reclaimed her mother's name, parts from the Traveler with an embrace, and leaves with Benben.

After the series the Tanit Camps are empty. According to the wiki's gameplay notes a vault can be opened where Babel once stood, Jeht's tent carries a note saying she is out on business, and, after the Akasha Pulses, the Kalpa Flame Rises Archon Quest, an NPC named Tanjiyy comments on the aftermath. These are wiki-recorded notes.

The etymology notes record that each title is taken from the biblical chapters on the fall of Babylon, for example Jeremiah 51 and Revelation 16. The series also includes joke references, such as the passwords and the cry "shoot her", that are not plot-relevant.

Revelations: - Babel tells the Traveler and Jeht the other has joined the Fatui, in order to set them against one another. She wants to keep the Eternal Oasis and to be Prophetess of Nabu Malikata.
- Fatui documents say the Tanit agreed to hand a young woman over to the Fatui desert expedition for experiments, and to lure her into a pre-arranged ambush.
- Jeht says she has killed or removed several elders at Babel's command, and that her mother is Ufairah Hindi.

- Babel hopes to unite the desert tribes around the Oasis under her authority and, with Nabu Malikata's power, to topple the god of Sumeru. She wants to control the Traveler's jinni by removing her master.
- Babel's last words are that she sent word to other tribes that Jeht is a traitor, so that no one will accept her again.

Characters: The Traveler, Paimon, Jeht, Babel, Benben (a companion of Jeht who appears at the end), Yuften (a Tanit farmer), the Tanit Falcons Nayram and Rezki, Mendas (seen beside Babel), Eremite assassins including Bouhanu, and Fatui soldiers Orest, Ilyusha, Yevgraf, Lieutenant Ruslan Snezhevich and Captain Zoya Snezhevna. Mentioned: Professor Froderock, Lieutenant Muldoon, Ufairah Hindi, Jebrael, Aderfi, Azariq, Masseira.

Consequences: Babel is dead, the Tanit Camps are left deserted, and Jeht, now outside the tribe and expected to be called a traitor along the trade routes, takes her mother's name and goes her own way with Benben.

Jeht tells the Traveler she wants to share another adventure someday and hopes their paths will cross again. The Fatui expedition's attempt to take Jeht has failed, as the soldier Orest says in the second quest.

Placement: Requires Apocalypse Lost and Rejoice With Me, for What Was Lost Is Now Found. The wiki lists Apocalypse Lost directly before this series. Released in 3.4. The three quests follow each other, the second starting automatically after the first, and the third after the second.

keysecondary: Her Foes Rage Like Great Waters
459.comment: Her Foes Rage Like Great Waters...: Babel, matriarch of the Tanit
459.content: Babel is the matriarch of the Tanit, a desert tribe, and the adoptive mother of Jeht. She is courteous and tender in public, calls the Traveler "esteemed Master of the Jinni", and tells each side that the other has betrayed them. Her aim is control of the Eternal Oasis and of the goddess Nabu Malikata's legacy, with Jeht as her heir. She dies at Jeht's hand.

460.comment: Her Foes Rage Like Great Waters...: Jeht and Ufairah Hindi
460.content: Jeht is a Tanit whom Babel raised as her own daughter. In this series she refuses to kill the Traveler, says she is the daughter of Ufairah Hindi and Jebrael (an outsider mother and a father Babel calls a traitor), and chooses her mother's name over the tribe's. She leaves with Benben, saying that she is now the head of her own house.

461.comment: Her Foes Rage Like Great Waters...: Eternal Oasis in this series
461.content: Babel treats the Eternal Oasis as the central pillar of Tanit faith: whoever holds it claims the sovereignty of Nabu Malikata, the Queen of All Oases. Jeht says the goddess is long gone and cannot be revived. Babel says that she is absent only in appearance and will return. The Tanit say they are its defenders.

462.comment: Her Foes Rage Like Great Waters...: Fatui desert expedition in Her Foes Rage Like Great Waters
462.content: A Fatui desert expedition led by Captain Zoya Snezhevna and Lieutenant Ruslan Snezhevich received a young Tanit woman, Jeht, from the tribe for experiments, after a plan to ambush her. The transfer was code-named Red Ball Express. She escaped her captors, and the expedition's mission failed. Professor Froderock Fronkonsteen is the scientist the documents address.

key: Her Palace Collapses Into the Blizzard
An Ark That Used to Be a Soul
463.comment: Her Palace Collapses Into the Blizzard
463.content:
Her Palace Collapses Into the Blizzard (also: An Ark That Used to Be a Soul, Court of Eternal Bliss quest): Her Palace Collapses Into the Blizzard is a World Quest series in Snezhnaya, added in version 7.0, that contains a single quest, An Ark That Used to Be a Soul. It ends the hunt for the three missing fragments of the Eye of Graeae, the talking device the Traveler and Paimon call "Goggles". Once all three are recovered, the Traveler opens the door to the Court of Eternal Bliss at the Ruined Hvergelmir and learns what Goggles was built for.

It begins at the Ruined Hvergelmir in the White Birch Snowgrave area (Pale Crown Palace subarea) and requires the Archon Quest chapter "Gunfire in the Silent Lands" plus the three sibling series: Hesperides of Love and Hate, In the Dwelling of Life and On One Side a Palace, On the Other a Tomb. Each of those yields one Pebble, which together are the three power fragments. The finale is a two-phase boss fight against Aksinya and then the Primordial Human.

The series is the destination of a long mystery about who Goggles is. Its answer is deliberately bittersweet: the Eye's consciousness turns out to be the Key meant to complete the Belyi Tsar, and in the end the Traveler's party keeps only an empty, mechanical Eye of Graeae.

Plot: Having collected the three fragments, the Traveler and Paimon go to the door of the Court of Eternal Bliss at the Ruined Hvergelmir. Goggles explains that his maker, Aksinya, once of Hvergelmir (the research body of the Belyi Tsar), built him to guide a great power toward a "Tomorrow": a world without suffering, envy, or the line between humans and gods. He fears what recovering his last power may do to his purpose. The Traveler and Paimon tell him he can choose once he remembers everything. They open the gate by feeding Kresnik Energy to the Tsar's White Birch.

Inside, Goggles vanishes and Aksinya appears. She says he has gone where he belongs. He was never meant to take back an old body: he is the "Proto-Man", the Key that completes the Belyi Tsar into the true Primordial Human. The vessel is the still-living husk of the long-dead Tsar, a body Hyperborea tried to forge from the flesh of the Cryo Dragon Sovereign Nibelung. That experiment once dragged Hyperborea into the Shadow Realm and froze Snezhnaya, but the Tsar later awoke and accepted the role of the failed project's successor.

Aksinya states her goal: to spread the Shadow Realm over the world so that love and joy never fade and every moment feels as fulfilling as the first, ending desire, envy and change. The Traveler observes this means a world without change, and she agrees, since in her view time wears love away. When the Traveler and Paimon reject it, she says there will still be a place for them, and teleports away into the Shadow Realm, so the Traveler chases her while her ritual proceeds.

Beneath the White Birch they find a huge mechanical being. Aksinya gives them the now-empty Eye of Graeae as a "gift", saying Goggles' consciousness has become the core of the Velikan of Light, Svarod. The Primordial Human awakens and speaks as Goggles, with his memory complete. He says he deliberately split himself into fragments and encouraged Koshchei, Pavlina and Alvis to betray Aksinya, because he knew becoming the Primordial Human would set off an irreversible revolution of the world. He adds that Aksinya has left herself out of her own utopia, since someone who distrusts love cannot enter a realm of eternal love, and that she means to build it from her own corpse. Bound by duty and memory, he cannot simply refuse, so he asks the Traveler and Paimon to stop them both.

Before the fight he asks a question: if the Traveler's sibling became someone unrecognisable, what would the Traveler do? The Traveler answers that they would learn to love them again, however many times it took, and he calls this a wonderful answer. The fight has two phases, first Aksinya, then the Primordial Human, and the empty Eye of Graeae unexpectedly helps through a modified train and its "Final Protocol".

Defeated, the Primordial Human sheds the giant form and becomes a normal human body resembling the young Tsar. He and Aksinya fall together into the depths of the Shadow Realm. Aksinya admits defeat and reconsiders her philosophy: someone who truly believes in love should not fear losing it, since she could simply seek it again. He replies that loving the world begins with loving oneself, and that the best ending left to them may be the two of them, nameless, in a world "as small as a walnut shell".

Outside, the Traveler and Paimon slip away before anyone notices the Tsar's body is gone. Paimon repeatedly tries to "crack open" the Eye in case Goggles is hiding inside as in a story, but only a cold mechanical voice answers. Paimon reflects that he was brave to choose to stay with Aksinya, promises to stay loyal to the Traveler whatever happens, and hurries them out of the area.

Revelations: - Goggles (the Eye of Graeae's consciousness) is the "Proto-Man", a Key created by Aksinya at Hvergelmir to complete the Belyi Tsar into the Primordial Human.
- Hyperborea tried to forge the Tsar's body from the Cryo Dragon Sovereign Nibelung; the Tsar's husk was still living when the Traveler arrived.
- Aksinya intends to spread the Shadow Realm across the world as a changeless realm of lasting love.
- The Primordial Human says he engineered his own fragmentation and the betrayal of Aksinya by Koshchei, Pavlina and Alvis.

- The Velikan of Light, Svarod, is the giant form the Primordial Human takes in the fight.
- Aksinya's answer after the defeat changes: she concludes that believing in love means not fearing its loss.

Characters: - The Traveler and Paimon, who refuse a changeless world.
- The Eye of Graeae ("Goggles"), who becomes the Primordial Human and then leaves only a mechanical shell behind.
- Aksinya, Hvergelmir's former researcher and the Tsar's Court Jester, presented here as the series' antagonist, though sympathetic and ultimately self-doubting.
- The Primordial Human, the awakened Belyi Tsar's body with Goggles' mind in it.

- Koshchei, Pavlina and Alvis are mentioned only as the three the Primordial Human says he provoked into betraying Aksinya. Pavlina is the antagonist of Hesperides of Love and Hate, and Koshchei is mentioned in the Pale Crown Palace flashbacks as Zver's creator.

Consequences: The Traveler no longer has Goggles as a companion, only the empty Eye of Graeae. Aksinya's plan and the fight with the Primordial Human end there. After collecting all three fragments, Co-Op Mode (including the Serenitea Pot and Miliastra Wonderland access) is disabled until the quest is finished, as the wiki notes. Completing the quest awards the achievement "A Thousand Affections Caught in a Sigh" and the character avatar card of Aksinya.

The quest reuses the Eye of Graeae's gadget heavily in its mechanics: during the chase in the Shadow Realm the gadget is temporarily removed and ammunition is set to zero, then both return afterwards (wiki gameplay notes, game-mechanic information rather than story).

Placement: Story order: it is the capstone of the Snezhnaya Eye of Graeae arc and comes after the three sibling series, which can be done in any order. It also requires the Archon Quest "Gunfire in the Silent Lands". Release order: added in version 7.0 with the other Snezhnaya World Quest series.

The related Pale Crown Palace quests, "To Gaze Upon the Dreaming Pale Crown" and "The Stone Beasts, Like Ghouls Seated", belong to On One Side a Palace, On the Other a Tomb and set up the Tsar, Zver and Hvergelmir background used here.

464.comment: Her Palace Collapses Into the Blizzard: Proto-Man and the Primordial Human
464.content:
In Aksinya's account the "Proto-Man" is a Key, created at Hvergelmir to complete the Belyi Tsar into the Primordial Human. Goggles is revealed to be this Key. In the finale the Primordial Human appears as the giant mechanical Velikan of Light, Svarod, speaks with Goggles' restored memory, and asks the Traveler to stop both himself and Aksinya.

After he is defeated the giant form falls away and he becomes a human body that resembles the young Tsar, which then sinks into the Shadow Realm with Aksinya.

465.comment: Her Palace Collapses Into the Blizzard: Aksinya's Tomorrow
465.content: Aksinya's plan is to cover the world in the Shadow Realm so that love and joy never fade. In her view time erodes love, so this realm would hold every feeling at its first fullness, which also means ending desire, envy and change. The Traveler rejects this as a world without change. By the end she doubts her own reasoning.

466.content:
Hereafter (also: Hereafter: The Trail of Pervases, Hereafter: All is Well, Hereafter: Return to the Mountains, Pervases temple restoration quest): A small Version 2.4 Liyue series. The Traveler buys grilled tiger fish to honour the Yaksha Pervases, meets Xiao and the reformed Wang Ping'an, and helps rebuild Pervases's neglected temple over three days.

It requires the quest Butterfly's Dream, and each of its three quests (The Trail of Pervases, All is Well, Return to the Mountains) becomes available only after the daily reset. The series is a gentle follow-up to earlier encounters with Wang Ping'an, once called "Starsnatcher".

Thematically it is about remembrance of adepti who protected Liyue Harbor without seeking recognition, as Xiao says, and how ordinary people choose to honour them.

Plot: The Traveler and Paimon buy fish at Wanmin Restaurant, intending a third portion as an offering to Pervases. Near the temple they meet Xiao and rescue Wang Ping'an from attackers. Wang Ping'an plans to restore the temple. Over later visits the temple is repaired, with Millelith guarding the site, and he stays to write a book about the Vigilant Yaksha.

Paimon wonders why nobody maintains the temple of Yakshas who defended Liyue Harbor; Xiao goes quiet and then says they did not do their duty for recognition. After helping Wang Ping'an, the Traveler is told to return once work has begun. On the second visit workers are building and the Ministry of Civil Affairs has posted Millelith. Wang Ping'an fears deliveries may be attacked, so the Traveler defeats nearby Treasure Hoarders, who say they did not know the temple belonged to an adeptus and promise to leave it alone. Wang Ping'an then asks for Sandbearer Wood. On the final visit the temple is complete and the Traveler lights incense at the censer.

Paimon and the Traveler are unsure whether Wang Ping'an is sincere, which is why he asks them to come back and see the work for themselves. He says he will remain at the temple to compile his book about the Vigilant Yaksha, and welcomes the Traveler to offer incense any time.

Gameplay notes: the three quests are gated by the daily reset, so the restoration plays out over three days. The Treasure Hoarders' reaction (promising to leave an adeptus's temple alone for fear of the Adepti's judgment) is the series' only comment on how common Liyue folk regard the adepti.

Revelations: No major revelation. The series shows Wang Ping'an's change of heart and gives a glimpse of Xiao's attitude to remembrance.

Characters: The Traveler, Paimon, Xiao and Wang Ping'an, plus Millelith and Treasure Hoarders as background.

Xiao appears only at the start and is reserved: he says the Yakshas did not act for recognition. Wang Ping'an is a former thief shown rebuilding the shrine and writing about the Vigilant Yaksha.

Consequences: Pervases's temple is repaired and guarded, and Wang Ping'an stays as its keeper. The Traveler can offer incense there whenever they want.

Placement: Released in Version 2.4. It requires Butterfly's Dream and runs as a daily-gated trio of quests. The wiki notes a separate Fontaine quest called Hereafter..., unrelated to this one.

467.content:
Hesperides of Love and Hate (also: Through the Gates of Ivory, Procrustes' Iron Bed, Bell Ringing at Dusk, House of the Soulless, The Sun's Gilded Apple, Fellfrost Peak series): Hesperides of Love and Hate is a three-part Snezhnaya World Quest series added in version 7.0, set at the House of Hesperides on Fellfrost Peak. The Traveler and Paimon are invited to what is billed as a Snegovik wedding for Pavlina, the Snegurochka princess. It turns out to be a ritual meant to take a fragment of the Eye of Graeae's power from Ikhor, the "groom", and the house keeps looping each time a bell rings eight times.

The parts are "Through the Gates of Ivory", "Procrustes' Iron Bed" (with two sub-quests, "House of the Soulless" and "The Sun's Gilded Apple") and "Bell Ringing at Dusk". It runs concurrently with In the Dwelling of Life and On One Side a Palace, On the Other a Tomb, and one of its rewards is the Pebble of Freezing Heart, which unlocks An Ark That Used to Be a Soul.

Tone: a dreamlike gothic mystery, with bells, looping time, dolls and statues, set among Snegovik who live "for love" yet are soulless. It frames Pavlina as a sympathetic antagonist and gives Aksinya's own aims.

Plot: Through the Gates of Ivory. In a snowstorm the party climbs Fellfrost Peak and finds a lamp that eases the cold. A young man, Ikhor, tells them a woman he did not know told him to leave a house and he simply obeyed, because for him a strong wish must be granted. He lives at the House of Hesperides, home of Lady Pavlina, princess of the Snegovik and other fae, and says she is preparing a wedding, an important "ritual". The Eye of Graeae senses a piece of its body in him. He gives them a wedding invitation, since only guests may enter, and guides them through monsters to the door.

Inside, the host Aglaya welcomes them as guests, explains Larisa's earlier wedding and warns them away from forbidden rooms. After entertainments and a nap the party hears the bell strike eight and goes to the chapel with the Snegovik guests. Pavlina speaks of a people who were soulless and chased love because they longed for a soul, and calls Larisa's death the last page of a tragic chapter. She calls for Ikhor, who wears an icy collar, and he agrees to give "what we've been wishing for". As Pavlina raises her sword, Aksinya appears, objects, and turns Ikhor into a doll-like puppet. A portal to the Shadow Realm takes Aksinya and Pavlina away. The Traveler dreams of an endless wedding rehearsed again and again, wakes in a room, and learns from Paimon and the Eye that the ritual repeats because Pavlina can only draw the power bit by bit. Aksinya sends a message through the Eye saying she has trapped Pavlina for now, to take Ikhor's fragments away before the bell strikes eight, and that she will send a map.

Procrustes' Iron Bed. Aglaya acts as if she has not met them, because the loop has reset. Bells ring one to eight as time runs out, and the party must recover two fragments ("Severed Fragment of Ikhor") through the sub-quests: in House of the Soulless, a secret room, a cat and Snegurochka statues puzzle lead to a cellar; in The Sun's Gilded Apple, Paimon keeps the guard Ladon talking while the Traveler sneaks through the garden, where Larisa once worked, to the tree that holds a fragment. With both found, they reach the chapel and remove Ikhor's collar. Ikhor says the ritual has been set in motion and can neither be halted nor reversed, and chooses to become one with it. Pavlina then arrives, pierces him with her sword, and absorbs him as golden energy. The Snegovik attack the party as she escapes.

Bell Ringing at Dusk. The party fights through Snegovik and rides ice lifts and Rumbletwig branches to the Cloudborne Altar, above the clouds, where Pavlina is trying to widen the ritual. Aksinya frees herself from the Shadow Realm and fights beside the Traveler. After Pavlina is beaten, she and Aksinya talk. Pavlina says she cannot accept Aksinya's "tomorrow" because the fae and loveless would not be part of it, and she wants a way for beings born of artifice to find meaning in their lives. Aksinya replies that the love of one person is too small, and that a love capable of saving more lives is greater. Pavlina disintegrates into icy mist, leaving the completed union ritual without its offering; Aksinya gives the Traveler a piece of the Eye (a Pebble of Freezing Heart), explains that the Eye's body was made so that "life may transcend life itself", and says she shares the goal of helping the will in the Eye find its body.

Details. Aglaya's welcome mentions the rule that the ritual starts "when the clock strikes eight times", that a human woman once tried to reach the groom and was caught, and that the vow was sworn on the sword Larisa once held. In the chapel the Snegovik are divided: some praise Larisa, and some think Pavlina was tainted by human ways at Hvergelmir. Pavlina says humans who share their souls with the Snegovik become terrible creditors. Aksinya notes that the Snegovik, created without flesh and blood, are incomplete and can only be whole through love, by taking another's soul, and that this is why so many Snegovik love stories end in tragedy.

Revelations: - The "Snegovik wedding" is a ritual to take the soul or power of the loved one; Snegovik, created without flesh and blood, have incomplete souls.
- Ikhor is a fragment of the Eye of Graeae's power in a Prime Ice body. He and the Eye each call the other "me".
- Pavlina is one of the people who betrayed Aksinya (the Eye says this if the Traveler has seen the Pale Crown Palace series).
- Pavlina's aim is to give her people souls; Aksinya opposes her because she wants the power for the Eye.

- The House of Hesperides loops on a bell that strikes eight times; changes the Traveler makes in a cycle carry over.
- Aksinya says the Eye was built so that "life may transcend life itself", and that a number of fae were servants created by the Hyperboreans and never perfect.

Characters: - Pavlina, the Snegurochka princess and host.
- Ikhor, the gentle, wish-granting "groom".
- Aglaya, the polite hostess who tells the story of Larisa.
- Aksinya, the Eye's creator, fighting Pavlina from the Shadow Realm.
- The Eye of Graeae and Paimon, who guide the Traveler.

- Ladon, the garden guard who speaks of Larisa; Mesherskaya, who scouts guests in Svetloledovka and gives out the Invitation to the "Ritual"; the Snegovik attendants Saltykov and Safonov; Jack Frosts; and the dead Larisa, mentioned in speech but not seen.

Consequences: Pavlina's ritual is stopped before it can offer up Ikhor's power, and the Traveler receives the Pebble of Freezing Heart. Ikhor is gone and Pavlina has vanished into mist. This is one of the three fragments needed in Her Palace Collapses Into the Blizzard. Aksinya, if the Traveler has not yet met her, introduces herself as the Eye's maker and says that she shares its goal.

Placement: Story order: after the Snezhnaya Archon Quest chapter, one of three parallel series (with In the Dwelling of Life and On One Side a Palace, On the Other a Tomb) that all lead to Her Palace Collapses Into the Blizzard. Conditional dialogue changes depending on what the Traveler has already seen. Release order: version 7.0.

468.comment: Hesperides of Love and Hate: Pavlina's ritual
468.content: At the House of Hesperides, Pavlina holds a "wedding" at which Ikhor is to offer his soul so that the Snegovik can gain souls. The bell strikes eight times, the house resets, and each cycle lets Pavlina take a little more of the power in the Eye of Graeae's fragments.

469.comment: Hesperides of Love and Hate: Ikhor
469.content: Ikhor is a calm young man whose manner Paimon finds childlike, with a Prime Ice body who grants any wish he is asked for. He says he does not feel cold and calls the Eye of Graeae "me". Pavlina uses him as the sacrificial "groom" and, in Procrustes' Iron Bed, pierces him with her sword and absorbs him as golden energy.

470.comment: Hesperides of Love and Hate: Larisa
470.content: Larisa was a Snegurochka, described by Aglaya as the most beautiful of them. According to Aglaya her human husband betrayed her, she killed him, and the broken vow then took her own life. Her fury raised a blizzard that froze lightning in mid-fall. Pavlina called her a friend, and Ladon says plants thrived under her care in the garden.

471.content:
Historia Antiqua Chapter (also: Sal Flore, No Mere Stone, Zhongli's Story Quest): Historia Antiqua Chapter is Zhongli's Story Quest, in two acts. In Sal Flore he and the Traveler accompany two self-described archaeologists to the ruins of the god Havria and learn why the God of Salt really fell. In No Mere Stone, a missing-miners commission leads them to the sealed Azhdaha and his benevolent consciousness.

Both acts treat Zhongli as the former Rex Lapis living as a consultant. The chapter is about memory: how history is written, who preserves it, and what Morax feels when old friends and old gods resurface.

Plot: Act I: The Traveler meets Zhongli at the Pearl Galley with a Fatui archaeologist, Kliment, and a second, Wanyan. They search Guyun Stone Forest and Sal Terrae, open a sealed ruin, and Zhongli exposes both as treasure seekers. Wanyan is a follower of Havria who wanted proof that Morax killed her. Zhongli shows that Havria's own followers betrayed and killed her, then asks the Traveler to be a record of history. Act II: Zhongli helps investigate missing miners at The Chasm, finding that a small girl lured them for a corrupted Azhdaha, and that the expert Kun Jun is Azhdaha's benevolent consciousness.

Act I ends with Zhongli deciding to keep the truth in the Traveler, who has seen many worlds. He throws Havria's relics into the sea. Act II ends with Azhdaha re-sealed, the miners saved, and the benevolent half learning that Morax has stepped down as the Geo Archon. Zhongli also refuses to say what he knows of Khaenri'ah's fall.

**Act I: Sal Flore.**
*Shadow of Yore.* At the Pearl Galley the Traveler and Paimon find Zhongli and Liyue archaeologists debating the origin of the first Mora. A Fatuus, Kliment, who claims to be registered with the Ministry of Civil Affairs, says he hired Zhongli as a consultant; Wanyan joins. Zhongli asks that the Traveler come along, and Kliment gives in when told treasure is easy to find.

*Vortex's Wake.* In Guyun Stone Forest Zhongli says the place suits studying ancient gods because he sealed them there as Rex Lapis. Hydro Mimics guard a tablet with traces of divine power. The two archaeologists argue over each other's inexperience; a teacup is identified as Ningguang's and Kliment is warned not to sell it. Kliment heads for Sal Terrae.

*A Ruin Under Lock and Key.* Treasure Hoarders have already pilfered Sal Terrae. Wanyan knows of a sealed ruin; Zhongli finds a second mechanism with Electro monuments and, reciting a puzzle, lets the Traveler activate them in order to open it. Tired of their quarrels, Zhongli makes them sign a contract: they claim items alternately, and he will leave if it is broken. Wanyan adds a clause that they must judge the God of Salt's fate honestly, even if it harms Morax's image.

*Farewell, Sweet Salt.* Kliment takes a chalice that never runs out of salt; Wanyan's item is a ruler that, by its depth, produces endless salt. Kliment breaks the contract; Zhongli defeats him, confiscates the chalice and warns him off. Wanyan, who cannot manage archaeology basics yet knows Havria in detail, admits she is a follower who wanted proof that Morax killed the God of Salt. A broken sword is found; Zhongli says it was the weapon used to kill Havria. In an open chamber salinised statues include one in the pose of her killer. Zhongli explains that when her followers betrayed Havria, her power turned many of them to salt; the survivors fled to Liyue and Morax's care, then returned to break the sword in hopes of forgiveness, which her benevolence could not have required. Wanyan refuses to accept this and leaves; Zhongli confiscates the salt ruler.

*A Record of All Things.* At the top of Guyun Stone Forest Zhongli says that as Rex Lapis he wrote history with his own hands, but the incident showed him he needed another way. He tells the Traveler they were chosen because they have travelled many worlds and can retain Teyvat's history if the world is destroyed. He casts Havria's relics into the sea and offers to bring the Traveler along when he preserves Liyue's past.

**Act II: No Mere Stone.**
*Strange Sights, Stolen Souls.* At the Adventurers' Guild Katheryne passes on a commission from Uncle Dai, who needs workers and has an expert arriving. Paimon brings Zhongli from the Third-Round Knockout; Dai's expert, Kun Jun, shows a rare rock with water inside. Dai says he found Kun Jun by the roadside, and the group sets out for The Chasm.

*Truth in the Stones.* At the mine Dai explains that four miners (Long, Bold Cen, Brave Cen and Mao) vanished after a shift change. They took only pickaxes and baskets. Bravo had slept through it. Kun Jun, beside a Cor Lapis deposit, says he can see the memories of stones and reports that a young girl led the miners away. Zhongli discourages pursuit since six days have passed; Kun Jun says he seeks Dragonfall, which might restore his hazy memory.

*Shifting Earth and Lost Threads Come to Light.* At Lingju Pass Ling saw lifeless miners following a small blue-haired girl. After rescuing Wanyu from Pyro Slimes and Geovishap Hatchlings, they confirm the route toward Nantianmen, where a collapsed miner is found. Kun Jun gives the Traveler and Zhongli special stones, which Zhongli accepts hesitantly. Zhongli explains Dragonfall is forged by elemental reactions rather than heat and was mined out centuries ago, making Kun Jun's search strange. The Traveler and Paimon worry, but Zhongli advises watching.

*Amidst Chaos, the Rock Is Unmoved.* Kun Jun explains that stones keep only the most prominent memories. A tunnel under a huge tree holds the rest of the miners under a malevolent aura. The aura slips beneath Zhongli's stone barrier and becomes the girl; an attack redirected into the seal pulls the party into Azhdaha's domain. Azhdaha recognises Zhongli as Morax's vessel and calls him a betrayer. The pair subdue and re-seal him. Kun Jun then reveals himself as Azhdaha's benevolent consciousness. He tells how Azhdaha, a friend of humanity and the Geo Archon, suffered erosion and lost Morax's face; humans disturbing the Chasm's ley lines split him into a savage body and a kind consciousness. Morax failed to stop the erosion and, with the benevolent half, Mountain Shaper, Moon Carver and a third adeptus, sealed his friend. Afterwards Dai is found, Kun Jun asks to be taken to the harbor, and the benevolent half learns Zhongli has stepped down as the Geo Archon. He leaves Kun Jun's body. Zhongli recalls Azhdaha once wishing to see the surface and being given a form and sight by Morax, with a warning. The Traveler asks about the fall of Khaenri'ah; Zhongli declines, bound by a contract older than the Traveler's arrival.

The chapter's title in Latin means Ancient History; Zhongli's story chapter and Neuvillette's are, per the wiki, the only ones whose names do not match the character's constellation (Zhongli's is Lapis Dei). Per the wiki, Zhongli was the first character to receive a second act. The Act II wiki summary spells one quest title two ways, so minor naming details are unconfirmed.

Revelations: - Havria, the God of Salt, was betrayed and killed by her own followers, not by Morax; the survivors fled to Liyue and Morax protected them.
- Zhongli is the former Rex Lapis, and treats the Traveler as a keeper of memory.
- The little girl and Kun Jun are two halves of Azhdaha: a corrupted body and a benevolent consciousness.

- Azhdaha's erosion was worsened when humans disturbed the Chasm's ley lines.
- Zhongli knows of the fall of Khaenri'ah but is bound by a contract not to say.

Characters: Zhongli, the Traveler and Paimon; Act I adds Kliment and Wanyan (Havria appears only in the story told); Act II adds Uncle Dai, Kun Jun, Katheryne and Azhdaha.

Act II also includes Wanyu, Ling and the miners. Zhongli is shown as courteous and dry, a former archon who prefers contracts and records to force.

Consequences: Havria's relics are cast into the sea; Wanyan loses her proof and Kliment his chalice. Azhdaha is re-sealed with the miners saved, and the benevolent consciousness departs. The Traveler is treated by Zhongli as an ally for preserving Liyue's history.

Placement: Act I (Sal Flore) was released in Version 1.1, requires A New Star Approaches and Adventure Rank 40. Act II (No Mere Stone) requires Sal Flore and We Will Be Reunited, per the wiki. Zhongli is the former Geo Archon, so the Archon Quest's revelation precedes these acts.

472.content: In Sal Flore, Zhongli shows that Havria was benevolent and was killed by her own followers with a sword, after which many of them were turned to salt. Survivors fled to Liyue and Morax's care, later returning to break the sword. Wanyan, a follower, believed Morax was responsible; Zhongli corrects this.

473.content: Kun Jun is the stone-reading expert hired by Uncle Dai, who is later revealed to be Azhdaha's benevolent consciousness. He can see the memories of stones. His search for Dragonfall is a pretext for finding Zhongli and eventually helping to re-seal his own corrupted half.

key: Homeward, He Who Caught the Wind
Variations on the Song of the Dragon and Freedom
474.comment: Homeward, He Who Caught the Wind
474.content:
Homeward, He Who Caught the Wind (also: Homebound Anecdotes, For a Reunion Without Tears, Variations on the Song of the Dragon and Freedom, Alice's memory bubble event, Luna V Mondstadt event): Part I sends the Traveler and Paimon to Stormbearer Coast, where they walk through a Klee-themed version of the story's opening and meet Venti, Dvalin, Alice and Nicole. Part II has volunteers replay the Holy Lyre theft and chase, with Fatui roles played by Guild members and friends. Part III shows the bubble polluted by a nascent Abyssal power that makes Dvalin a corrupted threat, which Venti, Diluc, Jean, Varka and the Traveler must defeat before a bubble-world crisis becomes real. Afterwards Jean and the Knights realise home is wherever they are together.

The four event modes (Echoes of Memory, A Chat Over Fine Drinks, Lionfang's Radiant Onslaught and Favonius Falcon's Recon Log) cover the same welcome festival from different angles. The event lets Mondstadt's cast revisit old events with the Traveler.

Plot: Part I, Homeward, He Who Caught the Wind: Paimon and the Traveler read Jean's letter (the Wild Hunt threat in Nod-Krai is neutralised and the expedition is returning) and go to the beach across from Starsnatch Cliff, the spot where their journey began. They explore a Special Story Mode full of oddities (Jumpy Dumpty mines on a tree, a Klee version of the Statue of the Seven) and meet Venti and Dvalin, then Alice and Nicole. Alice and Nicole explain that the "bubble" is a world built from Venti's memories at the Knights' request, so returning knights can catch up on events they missed. The Traveler is asked to test it. Jean explains her plans for the reception and Varka turns up unexpectedly.

Part II, For a Reunion Without Tears: With Varka, Jean, Diluc, Venti and others, the Traveler enters the bubble for the Holy Lyre der Himmel sequence. Guild members and Knights play the Fatui, Fischl plays an Electro Cicin Mage who steals the lyre, and Amber, as gliding champion of the Fatui, runs it across Mondstadt. After the performance a banquet at the Cathedral follows, where Jean and Barbara discuss home, and Varka, Venti and the Traveler talk on top of the Anemo Archon Statue.

Part III, Variations on the Song of the Dragon and Freedom: The bubble has turned Abyssal. Inside, the Traveler's group finds Mondstadt overrun and the corrupted Dvalin beyond saving, and they must kill the bubble's Dvalin in Stormterror's Lair. The real Dvalin arrives and fights alongside them. Alice then explains the Abyss's nature, and Jean sends her to confinement for blasting fish.

Details. In Part I the Traveler discovers the discrepancies with Paimon's Spotter Kamera. Alice admits the odd statue was deliberate. Alice says Kleiner could not come because of trouble on "another planet" and the "border", and that Klee delighted in his call on the Dodocommunication Device. Jean recalls that she had to read two days of applications from volunteers. Varka says he left the group to arrive first, to spare Jean from planning a festival, then offers a meal at the Good Hunter's secret menu.

Part II details: Cyrus, Durin and Mona hold the three crests at the Fatui hideout in Fatui roles; Oz is an Electro Cicin; Albedo and Lisa watch from the quietest corner; Varka recovers from a hangover after drinks with Charles. At the banquet, Varka sits atop the Anemo Archon Statue and tells the Traveler he never thanked them. Venti says only the Pyro Gnosis remains free of the Tsaritsa and recalls how Signora reasoned about Morax's contract. Varka says the Knights still stationed in Nod-Krai will help if needed.

Part III details: the contaminated tears of Dvalin are gathered from the city, and Nicole's elemental devices offer support. The group sees Dvalin's tears as crystallised Abyssal power. They also learn from Alice that the bubble's unchosen events are the problem: when the original story's purification was removed, causal links produced an alternate version in which Dvalin broke his seal. Venti is prepared to kill the dragon in the fiction.

End of Part III: after Varka lands the final blow with both claymores, the bubble ejects everyone into the Grand Master's office and the real Dvalin crashes through a window into Cider Lake just as Klee enters, ready to play. The room is quickly repaired. The Knights celebrate at Diluc's wine, and Jean says she still has work to do, so Varka tells her to join later. Alice meets the Traveler in the library, thanks them for helping her keep her promise to Klee, and explains that the bubble is now looped and safe. Jean then tells Alice she must go to confinement.

Revelations: Alice and Nicole's bubble magic builds an interactive world from memories, but without safeguards it can develop causal knock-on effects; here the removal of the Traveler's Dvalin purification let a nascent Abyssal power take hold. Alice describes the Abyss's essence, according to the Hexenzirkel's view and Barbeloth's interpretation, as the hatred of "fates that will not come to pass". Alice also mentions that her friend Rhinedottir's decision to tap into the Abyss ended the possibility of a future in which she stayed pure.

Varka says he saw a prophecy through the Hexenzirkel's scryglass in which Venti sealed Dvalin, was injured, and the seal later failed. Alice says in real history the dragon-slayer from the story had already left for Nod-Krai, but declines to say what would have happened. Varka also tells the Traveler that their actions in Natlan reduced the Wild Hunt threat because two Abyssal powers might otherwise have joined forces.

Characters: The Traveler and Paimon; Jean (Acting Grand Master, in charge of the reception); Varka (Grand Master, returned early); Venti and Dvalin (Anemo Archon and his dragon); the Hexenzirkel mages Alice and Nicole (creators of the bubble); Klee; Diluc; Barbara, Amber, Mona, Fischl and Oz, Albedo, Durin, Mika, Lisa, Kaeya, Noelle and Rosaria in reenactment roles; Hertha, Cyrus, Charles and the event NPCs Hedwig and Horken in minor roles.

Clorinde visits Mondstadt in Echoes of Memory to exchange swordsmanship with Eula, and Razor, who refused Alice's attempt to take the sword for the bubble, guards its illusory copy.

Consequences: The bubble is stabilised and looped so the returning knights can experience it at leisure. Klee plays in it with Alice and Nicole. The Knights' welcome celebration is held in a modest form, Jean's worry that Varka would be upset about the celebration is eased, and Alice goes to solitary confinement for fish blasting at Starfell Lake. The event adds no new plot to the Archon Quest.

Placement: Released in Version 6.4 (Luna V) as a Flagship Event, requiring Adventure Rank 20 and the Prologue Act III "Song of the Dragon and Freedom"; the Archon Quest "True Moon" and the Lupus Majoris Chapter Act I are recommended for the best experience. It takes place in Mondstadt after Varka's expedition and the Nod-Krai crisis, with the Snezhnaya arc still ahead.

Gameplay: Game mechanics, not in-world fact. Four modes: Echoes of Memory (find discrepancies with a Spotter Kamera), A Chat Over Fine Drinks (prepare drinks at the Knights' stand), Lionfang's Radiant Onslaught (a battle-based stage play with a shadow of the Lionfang Knight) and Favonius Falcon's Recon Log (control a Recon Falcon). They award Windscape Splendor, which unlocks the weapon appearance "Phantasmal Gift: Star Omen", Primogems and a Crown of Insight.

475.comment: Homeward, He Who Caught the Wind: Alice and Nicole's memory bubble
475.content: A magic Alice and Nicole created at the Knights' request: a small world built from Venti's memories and reproduced by volunteers, where returning knights can relive the Traveler's adventures. It is unstable and must be debugged; Nicole offers hints by communication bubble. Without a purification step the bubble developed a nascent Abyssal power and had to be repaired, after which it was set to loop.

476.comment: Homeward, He Who Caught the Wind: Part III Abyssal Dvalin
476.content: In the alternate version of events the bubble creates, Dvalin broke free of a seal and is thoroughly corrupted, so purification would kill him. Venti, Varka, Diluc, Jean and the Traveler defeat him in the bubble's Stormterror's Lair. The real Dvalin joins at the end, and Varka delivers the final blow with the Abyssal core as the target.

477.comment: Homeward, He Who Caught the Wind: Varka's homecoming celebration
477.content: Varka asked that there be no grand reception, but Jean wanted the returning expedition to know they are still family. The compromise is a small Mondstadt-style festival with food, drink, sparring, glider shooting and the bubble. Varka thanks the Traveler for their help in Mondstadt and Natlan and sits with them on the Anemo Archon Statue.

key: fates that will not come to pass
478.comment: Homeward, He Who Caught the Wind: Unchosen fates
478.content: Alice's explanation that the Abyss is rooted in the hatred of the possibilities that were eliminated when something else happened; even trivial choices (a lunch order) cut off other versions of a person. She says the Hexenzirkel, and particularly Barbeloth, hold this view and that the bubble allowed some of these fates to come close to reality.

key: True Tales of the Violet Garden
The Strange Tale of Suikou's Tipsy Tincture
What the Blue Flowers Left Behind
A New Painting in Pale Scarlet
479.content:
Hues of the Violet Garden (also: True Tales of the Violet Garden, Legends of the Kasen, The Strange Tale of Suikou's Tipsy Tincture, What the Blue Flowers Left Behind, A New Painting in Pale Scarlet, The Palace, Dyed in Black, Irodori Anecdotes): Across four acts the Traveler greets guests as they arrive at Ritou's harbour: Albedo and Klee from Mondstadt, with Venti arriving by accident; Xingqiu with calligraphers and Theater Mechanicus players from Liyue; then Kazuha. Each guest finds an anonymous excerpt from the legend of the Five Kasen, and the excerpts and the guests' troubles gradually connect. A new light-novel volume goes missing, Xingqiu's signature trouble is solved, and Albedo paints the poets' portraits using the guests as models. The fourth act connects the story to the downfall of the Raiden Gokaden, five Inazuman forging schools, and an old failed sword commission. At the end Ayato admits he and Miko staged the hunt to help Kazuha find the truth.

Requirements were Adventure Rank 30 and the Archon Quest part "Ritou Escape Plan". The recommended story quests were Ayato's The Firmiana Leaf Falls, the Raiden Shogun's Transient Dreams and Kokomi's Warriors' Dreams Like Spring Grass Renewing. This was the first event with a Quick Start option for players who had not done them. The reward character was Xingqiu.

Plot: Act I. Katheryne tells the Traveler and Paimon of a commission from Yae Miko at Yae Publishing House. Miko explains that the Irodori Festival honours the Five Kasen poets with a modern twist: it showcases light novels and presents Inazuma's culture to the world, now that the Sakoku Decree is lifted. In Ritou, Ayato (as head of the Yashiro Commission) asks the Traveler, who is well travelled and knows Inazuma, to greet and guide foreign guests, and hands over a ship arrival schedule. The first ship from Mondstadt brings bards and then Albedo, invited as a special guest to paint the poets' portraits, and Klee, whom he brings along; Venti is not aboard as Paimon hoped.
