Albedo's contact, Mr. Hirayama, is missing, and at the Outlander Affairs Agency the editors panic: the new volume of A Legend of Sword by Zhenyu has gone missing and they plan to reprint. Locals also report a suspicious individual at a warehouse. At the warehouse Kujou Sara has caught Venti, who has come without his Invitation Pass. Venti was invited by Ayato but boarded a wine ship and fell asleep drinking, waking in a crate outside Sailing Breeze. Albedo concludes the thieves had inside access, planned for a while and were several. The invitation turns out to be in Venti's hat. Venti shows a paper about Suikou he found beside him, and Albedo decides to paint the portrait of Suikou with Venti as model.

Act II. The Traveler waits at the docks for the Liyue ship. Xu of the Feiyun Commerce Guild, who serves Xingqiu, and Xingqiu himself, the real author behind "Zhenyu", disembark; Xingqiu also has an excerpt, and Paimon bluffs that it is part of a poem hunt with a chance to be an artist's model. Xingqiu realises Albedo is the painter and is happy to meet his long-time collaborator in person. Albedo notices something off with him: Xingqiu did not object to Uyuu Restaurant over Shimura's, so he knew Shimura's is open-air and probably arrived earlier. The patrons at Uyuu report neat handwriting and rough weather; Xingqiu admits he lied. Venti announces that Kujou Sara has arrested the suspect, whom Xingqiu recognises as Onodera. Onodera explains that for the festival he planned to have authors sign copies of their new novels, forgot to tell them in advance, and Xingqiu, poor at calligraphy, came early to practise. The editors rearrange the schedule. Xingqiu asks to be Albedo's next model so that he remembers the lesson, and someone unseen overhears the group.

Act III. Kazuha arrives and gives the Traveler his own excerpt about seals, which Albedo can design and Kazuha, an experienced carver, can make. They propose it to Hirayama, and two other authors, Satomi and Kadenokouji Kenzaburou, agree. Ayaka and Venti bring a strange paper that reveals more writing when dipped in water, showing that Akahito was framed. Albedo uses Kazuha and Ayaka as the last models. Paimon wonders about Kuronushi, who was missing from the tale; Albedo and Venti explain he is hidden inside the other stories as the one who framed Akahito and blackmailed Aoi. Kazuha, silent, tells them the story reminds him of his family: the Raiden Gokaden were five Inazuman forging schools tied to the Yashiro Commission, and now only the Amenoma art remains because the Isshin Art was lost, with the Kaedehara Clan its descendants. His great-grandfather lost interest, his grandfather failed to revive the business, and the last clan property was seized in Kazuha's generation. Ayaka says three of the five schools were lost in a short time and some rumoured a plot to remove them. Kazuha says an incident in his great-grandfather's day nearly crippled both his clan and the Kamisato clan, and he wants to confirm something with someone before telling them.

Act IV. Kazuha has traced an old family servant. The Isshin Art had been asked to forge an important Goshintou from an ancient diagram, but all the smiths produced only defects. At the deadline the blade was not ready and the smiths fled in fear. Kazuha's great-grandfather and the Yashiro head tracked them to the coast, where they put up a fierce resistance and escaped, and the Kaedehara Clan was punished; the Kamisato head soon died of wounds. The Kamisato Estate's copy of the diagram, dipped in water, shows it was altered, so the failure was not a lack of skill. Kazuha says his grandfather also failed to forge it and left Inazuma after an argument. Albedo notes the wording of the diagram was odd, so the great-grandfather may have known the truth. At the Kujou Estate Sara allows the group to search the seized Kaedehara property in a warehouse behind the police station; Kazuha asks that it be sold and the money given to the poor, but finds in a dead bonsai pot a hidden compartment with a blank paper that reveals a letter when dipped in water. The letter tells how the great-grandfather, Kaedehara Yoshinori, and the Yashiro head found, at a spot on Narukami Island, an eccentric who had taken responsibility for the sabotage and quickly defeated the party. The eccentric asked whether Yoshinori knew of "Niwa" and, hearing that Yoshinori was a descendant, told him to let "her" know the name Kunikuzushi, and left. He threatened to destroy the rest of the Gokaden, so the two men never spoke of it. Ayaka suspects her ancestor kept the same silence so that their families could continue. Kazuha says he has no reason to act on past wrongs but would act if the eccentric made trouble now. Back in Ritou Albedo finishes the portraits and unveils a blank one for Kuronushi. Ayato admits that Miko and he planned the hunt: he wanted to see if Kazuha could find and accept the truth, and to give Kazuha and Ayaka someone to rely on. He tells the Traveler to splash water on the portrait when alone, which reveals the Balladeer's likeness. Ayato recalls that after the Kaedehara property was seized, someone broke into the warehouse and left with nothing; Sara pretended not to notice while a Shuumatsuban member watched; the intruder gave up without learning the bonsai pot's secret, and Ayato then found the papers.

Details. Venti's role as Suikou is the first of several portraits. The five poets are known only by their colours: green for Suikou, blue for Aoi no Okina, red for Akahito, white for Sumizome and black for Kuronushi. Venti is the basis for Suikou, Xingqiu for Aoi no Okina, Kazuha for Akahito, Ayaka for Sumizome, and the Balladeer (later called Wanderer) for Kuronushi.

Revelations: The old sword failure was sabotage. The forging diagram for a Goshintou had been altered so that even skilled Isshin smiths could not succeed, and the blame fell on the Kaedehara Clan. The saboteur was an eccentric who called himself Kunikuzushi, defeated the Yashiro head's party and warned that he would destroy the rest of the Raiden Gokaden if the story spread. Both families kept silent, which, as Ayaka says, let later generations exist. Ayato staged the poem hunt, partly on Miko's idea, so that Kazuha could find this out and so that the Kaedehara and Kamisato descendants could rely on each other.

The final portrait is the Balladeer, Scaramouche, and the wiki summary reads Ayato's account of the warehouse break-in after the seizure as Scaramouche's doing. The Five Kasen story itself is Ayato's invention, a way to guide Kazuha to the truth.

Characters: Albedo, Venti, Xingqiu, Klee, Kazuha, Ayaka and Ayato in the main acts, with Kujou Sara, Yae Miko and the Traveler. Event NPCs include Hirayama, Onodera, Zhenyu's editors, Xu of the Feiyun Commerce Guild, Satomi and Kadenokouji Kenzaburou, Asakawa, Fushizome, Kayabuki Ikkei and others. The Irodori Anecdotes also feature Itto, Gorou, Kokomi, Sayu, Thoma, Yoimiya and the Raiden Shogun.

The Irodori Anecdotes (Festival Deeds) are four side stories: A Story for You (Albedo, Klee, Miko), About That Time We Saved the Tanuki Photo Board (Itto, Thoma, with Arataki Gang members Akira and Genta), Buyer's Guide to the Statue of Her Excellency, the Almighty Narukami Ogosho, God of Thunder (Sara, the Shogun, Sayu) and Pen Pals, Book Reviews, and the Super Lucky General (Gorou, Kokomi, Miko).

Consequences: Kazuha learns the truth about his family's failure and chooses not to pursue old grievances. Ayaka learns that her ancestor kept the same secret. Ayato's two-sided purpose is explained to the Traveler. Xingqiu's signing problem is addressed with author seals. The Irodori Festival goes ahead, with the event's poems, themed challenges and floral courtyards.

Placement: Released in Version 2.6 as a Flagship Event and set in Ritou after the Archon Quest "Ritou Escape Plan". The recommended story quests are Ayato's The Firmiana Leaf Falls and Kokomi's and the Shogun's story quests. Scaramouche appears here only as the Balladeer in a portrait and in the letter's past history; his later story as Wanderer is not part of this event.

Gameplay: Game mechanics, not in-world fact. Four modes unlock in sequence: The Moon and Stars Inscribe (take pictures to fill Irodori poems), Theater Mechanicus (build mechanisms from Wondrous Sticks to defeat enemies), Clash of Lone Blades (duel martial artists using a Parry mechanic, without skills or bursts) and The Floral Courtyard (build furnishing arrangements to match flower themes). Completing the "Friendship in Writing" criteria invited Xingqiu as a playable character. Rewards included furnishings, recipes, Primogems and a Crown of Insight.

480.comment: Hues of the Violet Garden: Five Kasen
480.content: Legendary Inazuman poets who took turns each year to present a poem collection to the Shogun; their works are the reason for the Irodori Festival. The poets are known by colours (green Suikou, blue Aoi no Okina, red Akahito, white Sumizome, black Kuronushi) and little is reliably known of them. In this event Ayato devised the version of the legend that guides Kazuha.

481.comment: Hues of the Violet Garden: Raiden Gokaden
481.content: In Ayaka's account, the five best Inazuman forging schools, tied to the Yashiro Commission; today only the Amenoma art remains, the Isshin Art is lost although the Kaedehara Clan descends from it, and three schools vanished quickly, which fuelled rumours of a plot.

482.comment: Hues of the Violet Garden: Kunikuzushi
482.content: The name given by an eccentric who sabotaged the Kaedehara Clan's Goshintou in Yoshinori's day, asked about "Niwa", defeated the Yashiro head's party and told Yoshinori to pass his name to "her". The wiki identifies him with Scaramouche; the event only implies this through the Balladeer portrait.

483.comment: Hues of the Violet Garden: Irodori Festival
483.content: Held in Ritou in this event to honour the Five Kasen, show off modern light novels from Yae Publishing House and welcome foreign guests, with guides, poetry, performances and a flower display. Miko organises and Ayato helps as head of the Yashiro Commission.

484.comment: Hues of the Violet Garden: A Legend of Sword
484.content: A light-novel series by Zhenyu, a pen name of Xingqiu, illustrated by Albedo. Its latest volume disappears in Act I. Xingqiu has trouble signing copies in a neat hand.

485.content:
Hyperion's Dirge (also: Hyperion's Dirge Chapter, Narrow Inquiry, Temple Inquiry, Serpent's Heart Inquiry, Helios-Forger): A version 2.4 world quest series in Enkanomiya. A proud shade who calls himself Aberaku, Helios-Forger, says he built the Dainichi Mikoshi, the solar chariot that lit the sunless land, yet was imprisoned and his soul scattered. The Traveler recovers three fragments of it so that he can rest.

The fragments lie at the Narrows, the Evernight Temple and the Serpent's Heart. Once Aberaku is whole he remembers everything and tells how the light of the Dainichi Mikoshi drove off the Dragonheirs of the Depths, how nobles then used it to seize power through puppet Sunchildren, and how he was jailed for opposing that. As thanks he gives the Traveler the Divine Bridle, a badge of the Sunchild's office.

The series is a bitter portrait of a creator rewarded with prison. It is the main source for how the Sunchild system was kept in place by burning each Sunchild at a set age.

Plot: Aberaku introduces himself theatrically. Paimon asks about the Helios, and he explains it is the Dainichi Mikoshi. He asks the Traveler to find three pieces of his shattered soul.

At the Narrows he speaks of how his creation brought joy and saved the nation from the Bathysmal Vishaps and wonders why he cannot rest; his bones are enshrined here and monsters hold the fragment. At the Evernight Temple he says he was jailed on a child's orders but bears the child no hate, since the Sunchildren were only puppets, and that he was held in a high, dark, ice-cold place; his body and clothes were enshrined in several places to honour his work, which split his soul. The Traveler recovers his sacred crown. At the Serpent's Heart he says he was betrayed and left to rot after the Helios was made, and the Traveler wins back his sacred robes. Back with Aberaku, now whole, he tells the full story.

The series can be started with any one of its four quests. The introductory quest gives optional dialogue and is meant to be taken first, the three inquiries can run in any order and at once, and Hyperion's Dirge itself is finished last. In the Dainichi Mikoshi, Aberaku is first found in a hidden room under the central waypoint; afterwards he moves to the highest point of the structure.

Revelations: Byakuyakoku was terrorised by the Dragonheirs of the Depths until the light of the Dainichi Mikoshi drove them off. When peace came, greedy nobles led the people to worship the Mikoshi and proclaimed the rule of the Sunchild over the land, using the child as a puppet. Aberaku opposed this, was accused of high treason by the Sunchildren and imprisoned.

To stop the Sunchildren from realising they were manipulated, each was incinerated in a ceremony once they reached a certain age, as Aberaku confirms when Paimon wonders about this. The wiki profile, drawing on The Byakuyakoku Collection, names the Sunchild who imprisoned him as Rikoru.

Characters: The Traveler and Paimon; Aberaku, a shade.

Aberaku's original name is Abrax; his title is Helios-Forger. The wiki profile also calls him a sage enlightened by the Tokoyo Ookami. The Sunchildren are mentioned but not met.

The wiki notes that Abrax likely derives from Abraxas, a figure in Gnostic tradition; this is an outside observation. The inquiries require unsealing the Key Sigil seals before Aberaku appears at each location.

Consequences: Aberaku's soul is whole and he can rest, though his closing remark afterwards is that all his talent and ability came to nothing. The Traveler keeps the Divine Bridle.

Placement: Released in Version 2.4 with Enkanomiya as a world quest series. Like Erebos' Secret, it requires From Dusk to Dawn in Byakuyakoku, so either can be done first.

486.content: Aberaku no Mikoto, born Abrax, is the creator of the Dainichi Mikoshi (the Helios) in Enkanomiya. He was imprisoned by the Sunchild and died; his memories remain as a shade. The wiki profile says he lived about 6,000 years ago, was a pupil of Istoria, and travelled to Enkanomiya (then Delphi Pytho) shortly before the war of funerary flame, becoming trapped there.

487.content:
Ignis Purgatorius Chapter (also: Ignis Purgatorius, Arlecchino's Story Quest, When the Hearth-Flame Goes Out, The Child Who Doesn't Exist, Sea Breeze Rendezvous, Birds in a Cage, Into the Sunlight): Arlecchino's Story Quest, set in Poisson. A rumour of a 'phantom child' no one remembers has spread through the House of the Hearth, and Arlecchino has moved the whole House to the town to find her. Lyney, Lynette and Freminet secretly shelter the girl, Clervie, and the Traveler helps. Arlecchino reveals that Clervie was her friend, killed years ago in a duel, and the quest ends with Clervie being let go in peace.

The chapter has one act, When the Hearth-Flame Goes Out, of four quests: The Child Who Doesn't Exist, Sea Breeze Rendezvous, Birds in a Cage and Into the Sunlight. It was released in version 4.6 and is unlocked at Adventure Rank 40 after Masquerade of the Guilty. It shows the Harbinger as a ruthless and honest head of a household who rewrote the cruel rules she inherited.

The story is about loyalty inside a family built on fear. Lyney and his siblings risk their lives to protect one child, Arlecchino tests them, and the cost of her own survival becomes clear. It also sets up Project Stuzha as a looming threat to the House.

Plot: The Traveler and Paimon visit Poisson and find the House of the Hearth staying there. Freminet has been sheltering a girl named Clervie who no one else remembers. Lyney, Lynette and Freminet try to quietly resolve it. Arlecchino learns of it, warns the Traveler, then explains that Clervie died long ago. She lets the siblings duel her, allows the 'traitors' to leave with their memories erased, and releases Clervie at dawn.

The Child Who Doesn't Exist: in Poisson the Traveler meets Lyney, who says that Father has moved the family there during trouble elsewhere. Arlecchino says a rumour that a 'phantom child' is among the House has spread and she wants to find the culprit. Freminet leads the Traveler, Paimon and Lyney to Clervie, who has been following the House for about half a month. She says there were two rosters, one for an ideal candidate and one for execution, and that no one leaves the House alive. Lyney, Lynette and Freminet agree to find a way to grant her wish to go where the sun can shine.

Sea Breeze Rendezvous: the Traveler finds Arlecchino on the shore with Childe, who has come looking for Skirk and heard a rumour that she betrayed the House. She admits she is not a Fontainian and that duels in the House once ended in death. The siblings find that Clervie cannot go into sunlight and that her name is not on the execution roster. At night the Traveler and Paimon find Clervie leaving town and learn she fears being sent to Dottore.

Birds in a Cage: Arlecchino tells them she has known all along and orders them to Palais Mermonia. She says that betrayal is not tolerated, lets the Traveler off as a guest, and promises not to punish the siblings if Clervie is gone. At the Palais she gives Neuvillette a written proposal to withdraw her forces from Fontaine over time, and he accepts. Afterwards she agrees to let the guests stay, on condition that they help the House when the time comes.

Into the Sunlight: at ruins on Mont Esus East, Arlecchino tells her history. She decides to kill Clervie's shade again. Lyney begs her to stop and Lynette, Freminet and Chapleau back him. She duels the siblings, with the Traveler joining them, and wins easily. She then offers a potion of her flames that will erase the memory of the House, and the 'traitors' take it and leave. Clervie is told the truth, accepts it, and fades at dawn.

The Child Who Doesn't Exist: Lyney notices tension with some older members as he distributes supplies. Freminet lies to get food and cloth, and when Lyney sees through it he learns Freminet is hiding someone. Freminet says he could not hand her over, because he believed Clervie was the voice that helped him save Chapleau from poison. Lynette turns up unamused and joins the plan, threatening to tell Father otherwise. Asked who can vouch for her, Clervie names Perrie, whom the group has never heard of.

Sea Breeze Rendezvous: Childe says he enjoyed time with the children but would come for Arlecchino if she harmed them. She replies that her family is more complicated than he thinks, using Tonia and Teucer as examples. Lyney reports that Project Stuzha was a collaboration between Regrator and the Rooster, and that the House's acquisition of a Gnosis gave them a 'key' role that is dangerous for the House.

Birds in a Cage: Lyney says that when Arlecchino became a Harbinger Dottore proposed to work together; she turned down all but one plan. Neuvillette raises the Tartuffe assassination and asks if her proposal is sincere; she admits to nothing but says such incidents will be much less likely. A newsboy runs into the group and Arlecchino buys papers, seeing through Paimon's ruse.

Into the Sunlight: Arlecchino explains the House as a purgatory that made war orphans fight to be 'King', with the permanently injured given to Dottore or sent on dangerous missions. She tells Lyney she picked him as 'King' for his conviction and expects him to grow stronger.

Arlecchino's account in full: Clervie was the biological daughter of Crucabena ('Mother'), brought into the House at age six. She tried to change her mother and was supported only by Peruere ('Perrie'). Ten years later Peruere suggested killing Crucabena, but Clervie, who still saw her as her mother, refused. Concluding that death was the only escape, Clervie duelled Peruere and died. A year later Peruere killed Crucabena in the same place and revealed that Peruere was her real name, then took over the House and rewrote its rules. The old name brought back memories.

Aftermath: Lyney reports that those who wished to leave drank the potion while he, Lynette and Freminet declined it. Arlecchino says that with the weaker members removed the House is strong enough to turn against Project Stuzha when the time comes. She would have liked to tell Clervie she had seen the aurora of Snezhnaya, as they had promised each other, but left it unsaid before dawn would have wiped Clervie's memory. Two days later Lynette and Freminet are recovering at Hotel Bouffes d'ete; Lynette saw Filliol and the others in a cafe, living the life they wanted, with no memory of her.

Revelations: The 'phantom child' is Clervie, the daughter of the previous Harbinger Crucabena, killed in a duel with the young Arlecchino years ago.

Arlecchino, whose real name she says is Peruere, killed Crucabena and rewrote the House of the Hearth's rules. Before that, the House made orphans fight each other, and those who survived were hurt or given to Dottore. She is also not Fontainian.

Project Stuzha, a Pantalone-and-Pulcinella plan, is aimed at reining in the House now that it holds a Gnosis. Arlecchino has known of the siblings' plot from the start.

Her flames can erase memories of life in the House in those who drink them. A shade of everything she has consumed lingers in her blood and can take form.

Characters: Arlecchino, the Traveler, Paimon, Lyney, Lynette, Freminet, Clervie.

Childe, who visits Arlecchino on the shore. Neuvillette, who accepts her proposal at Palais Mermonia. Children of the House including Filliol, Chapleau, Tonia and Teucer, as well as Crucabena (in flashback).

Skirk, Regrator (Pantalone), the Rooster (Pulcinella) and Dottore are referred to but do not appear.

Consequences: Clervie is released and the 'traitors' who drank the potion leave the House with no memory of it. Lyney, Lynette and Freminet stay. Arlecchino and the Traveler part with an acknowledged bond, though she says they may be on opposite sides in future.

Arlecchino has agreed to withdraw her forces from Fontaine gradually and avoid special operations there unless absolutely necessary, in return for Neuvillette accepting her written proposal.

Placement: Unlocked at Adventure Rank 40 after Chapter IV Act V, Masquerade of the Guilty. Released in 4.6, so it follows the Fontaine Archon Quest in release order.

488.content: The 'phantom child' of the Ignis Purgatorius Chapter. As Arlecchino tells it, Clervie was Crucabena's daughter and the friend of the girl who became Arlecchino. She died in a duel with that friend after deciding death was the only escape from the House. A shade of her at age six was somehow formed from the shadows in Arlecchino's blood. She fades at dawn after being told the truth.

489.comment: Ignis Purgatorius Chapter: Potion of Arlecchino's flames
489.content: After the duel, Arlecchino offers any member who wishes to leave a potion made from her searing flames. Whoever survives it loses memories of the House, which in her words 'kills' that life so they can be released. Lyney, Lynette and Freminet each have a bottle available but decline it.

490.content:
Iktomi Spiritseeking Scrolls (also: Spiritseeking Scrolls, Night-Wind Letter, Vision of Ashen Desolation, The Spirit of Ah K'ulbatil): Iktomi Spiritseeking Scrolls was a limited-time flagship event of Version 5.2 (28 November to 16 December 2024) set among the Masters of the Night-Wind in Natlan. Ororon asks the Traveler for help when a spirit-duffer named Leyla loses his spirit during a clairvoyance attempt. With Citlali the Traveler recovers it and learns that a stranger called Kokuchuu was after the location of the vanished Mare Jivari.

Alongside the story the event offered three gameplay modes tied to clairvoyance (gathering roaming spirits, banishing disruptive foes and arranging fragments of a woven scroll). Its main reward was the sword Calamity of Eshu. Because it was an event, the story is canon but not known to every player or character.

Tone is comic and warm, built on the grandmother-and-grandson dynamic between Citlali and Ororon, but the plot pivots on a real issue: a tribe where spiritual talent is the norm and a young man who lacks it. It also hands the Traveler a map and a relic shard that point towards the Mare Jivari.

Plot: Ororon invites the Traveler to the Masters of the Night-Wind. Citlali has been blocking him from saving a comatose man, Leyla, whose spirit is lost after a clairvoyance session. Citlali joins in, reads Leyla's lingering visions, discovers they lead to Sanhaj's relic and the Mare Jivari, and calls his spirit home. The stranger behind it escapes.

The story runs over three volumes: Night-Wind Letter, Vision of Ashen Desolation and The Spirit of Ah K'ulbatil. Leyla, a man with no spiritual sensitivity, is physically present but spiritless. Citlali and Ororon first disagree over how to help him, then work together through two approaches: gathering roaming spirits, and reading the visions his body and a relic produce. The trail reveals that a stranger planted the relic as bait.

**Night-Wind Letter.** Ororon's letter asks the Traveler to visit the Masters of the Night-Wind. He asks them to distract Citlali with her favourite pastimes (drink, naps, light novels) so he can reach a cave where a man lies motionless. Citlali catches Ororon at the ritual site. She explains that Leyla is a "spirit-duffer", someone with no spiritual sensitivity, and that his spirit got lost. Because the tribe's healing methods depend on spiritual sensitivity, they cannot treat him directly. Citlali opposes Ororon's plan of using his own special constitution, which she considers too risky. Instead she proposes two approaches: gather the roaming spirits through a gateway to the Night Kingdom and hope to find Leyla's, and use Leyla's body as a medium for her own clairvoyance to learn what mystery he sought. The Traveler weaves the visions on the spiritloom, producing an image of Sanhaj Kompore, one of the six heroes and a Border Master. Citlali notes that his spiritual remains are still powerful.

**Vision of Ashen Desolation.** The roaming-spirit search fails to turn up Leyla. Citlali has learned from Leyla's parents that he had recently befriended an Inazuman-dressed stranger calling himself Kokuchuu. A flashback shows Kokuchuu proposing a "hypersensitization therapy" in which Leyla would immerse himself in spiritually rich objects. Citlali says the tribe once offered a similar treatment but outlawed it because of the risk and low success rate. She found a broken shard at their camp. Ororon senses it is tied to his ancient name. Using the shard as a medium, the visions show a flaming bow, confirmed as the weapon Sanhaj used in the Battle of the Mare Jivari, and then a map of the Mare Jivari's last known location in westernmost Natlan. Leyla's body reacts and a spirit approaches. Citlali needs two days to prepare the return.

**The Spirit of Ah K'ulbatil.** Citlali performs the rite with the ceremonial sword Calamity of Eshu, invoking the Ruler of Death and her title Ah K'ulbatil, and Leyla wakes. She scolds him, then credits Ororon for noticing something was wrong. Leyla insists he chose the method himself, though Kokuchuu supplied the relic. He admits he wanted not to be the odd one out in a talented tribe. Matla gives him a checkup. Then Citlali reveals she had left bait (the map and shard) in the cave and set a trap, which caught Kokuchuu. He slipped away, though she marked him so she can track him. She gives the shard and map to the Traveler. Leyla is surprised to find he can see through her illusion, and Citlali tells Ororon to teach him.

Citlali's reason for not holding Kokuchuu is that the cave is next to the hideout of a sleeping mad sage, and a fight could wake him. She also quietly admits the escape embarrassed her. After the quest the Traveler can offer her the light novels Ororon mentioned, and she tries to hide how pleased she is.

Revelations: Kokuchuu was after the location of the Mare Jivari, and Leyla was used as bait in a plan to get a real clairvoyant to examine Sanhaj's relic.

Sanhaj Kompore was one of the six heroes and a legendary Border Master of the Masters of the Night-Wind. According to Citlali, his border mastery turned the tide at the Battle of the Mare Jivari five hundred years ago: he summoned a miniature Night Kingdom and exploded it against the dark calamity, and he and Tenoch, leader of the tribal coalition forces, both died casting the spell. The bow shard is a relic of the weapon he used there.

The Mare Jivari, once a wasteland of ash, vanished from the world in recent decades. Citlali says the map points to a remote place in the far west of Natlan where few settlements stood before.

Characters: Citlali, Ororon, the Traveler and Paimon.

Leyla, a member of the Masters of the Night-Wind who lacks spiritual sensitivity; Matla, the tribe's witch doctor; and Kokuchuu, an Inazuman-dressed stranger who is listed under Enjou on the wiki. Leyla's parents appear only in report.

Consequences: Leyla recovers and begins training under Ororon. The Traveler keeps the shard and map. Citlali marks Kokuchuu and plans to follow him.

The shard and map are described as potentially useful if the Traveler later seeks the Mare Jivari. The event story does not resolve what Kokuchuu intends.

Placement: Released 28 November 2024 in Version 5.2 as a flagship event. It required Adventure Rank 20 and the Prologue Act III. Completing Chapter V Act IV, The Rainbow Destined to Burn, was recommended for the best experience. It takes place in the Masters of the Night-Wind territory in the Tezcatepetonco Range.

491.content: In the Masters of the Night-Wind a spirit-duffer is a person with no spiritual sensitivity: they cannot sense or command spirits and cannot cast the tribe's spells. Because the tribe's healing and problem solving all rely on dealing with spirits, ordinary treatments fail on them. Forcing a spirit-duffer into clairvoyance is possible but dangerous, and Leyla's case shows why.

492.content:
Kokuchuu is the name used by a stranger in Inazuman dress who befriends Leyla and proposes the dangerous hypersensitization therapy. Citlali judges that he used Leyla to get a clairvoyant to view Sanhaj's relic and learn where the Mare Jivari lay. He was never captured. In the quest he presents himself as a friendly helper.

The wiki lists the character as Enjou in the volume II cast. Treat the link as wiki-sourced rather than stated in dialogue.

493.comment: Iktomi Spiritseeking Scrolls: Sanhaj's bow shard
493.content: A broken shard of the bow Sanhaj used in the Battle of the Mare Jivari. It carries strong spiritual energy and was used as a medium by Leyla. Ororon feels it is connected to his ancient name. Citlali gives it to the Traveler together with a map of the Mare Jivari's last known location.

494.content: Kokuchuu's name for immersing a spirit-duffer in spiritually rich substances so they may glimpse spirits. Citlali says the Masters of the Night-Wind once offered a similar treatment but outlawed it, since it carried severe risk and rarely worked.

495.content:
Imperatrix Umbrosa Chapter (also: Imperatrix Umbrosa, Raiden Shogun's Story Quest, Ei's Story Quest, Reflections of Mortality, Transient Dreams): The Imperatrix Umbrosa Chapter is the Raiden Shogun's Story Quest. In Act I, Reflections of Mortality (Version 2.1), the Traveler brings Ei, the Electro Archon, out of her Plane of Euthymia to walk through Inazuma City. In Act II, Transient Dreams (Version 2.5), Ei confronts the memories of the catastrophe five centuries ago and her sister Makoto, defeats her own puppet in a duel and abolishes the Sakoku Decree.

Both acts take place after the Archon Quest Omnipresence Over Mortals. Act I has four quests: The Lonesome Euthymia, To Traverse the Mortal Plane, The Fabric of Constancy and To Hear Mortal Hearts. Act II has three: Cleansing Light, Farewell to the Past and Radiant Sakura. The chapter shows Ei beginning to take a living part in rule, and settles her relationship with the Shogun puppet.

The chapter is the personal sequel to the Archon Quest. The first act is about Ei learning that the present is not a threat to eternity; the second is about why she feared change and how Makoto's worldview survived in her. Its events also open Yae Miko's, Kazuha's and Ayato's Story Quests.

Plot: Act I, Reflections of Mortality. Thoma, Kamaji and Ippei are worried because the Shogun wants private time, the storms around Inazuma are advancing, and the Kujou Clan has lost control over its vassals after Kujou Takayuki's dealings with the Fatui and his poor health. Kamaji goes to see Takatsukasa Susumu. At the Grand Narukami Shrine, Yae Miko gives the Traveler a pass to see the Shogun, who at Tenshukaku does not recognise them and behaves strangely. Ei speaks through the puppet and takes them to her plane, saying she has disabled most of its functions because it clings to the old protocols she wants to change, and the puppet resists change so only Miko may see her. She says a small change to the Shogun could stop the storm. The Traveler asks about her view of Eternity, and Paimon suggests she take a walk.

Outside, Ei notes that the market has changed. She has no Mora because as an Archon she never shopped. At Tomoki's stall she tries Dango Milk, likes it, and her praise keeps him from dropping the product. At the Yae Publishing House she browses novels but cannot grasp fiction. She decides she should not hamper human lives for her pursuit of eternity. The Traveler takes a photo, and Ei is surprised that it shows only one person; they remind her she can exist in more than one form, like the puppet. She says Inazuma has changed a great deal and perhaps she held on too tightly.

Ippei reports that Kamaji has not returned from negotiations with the Takatsukasa Clan, who met at one of their own bases and not at the Commission. At the hidden base Ei and the Traveler find ronin guarding Susumu and his men and Kamaji. Susumu says it was for security; Kamaji says Susumu was pressing him to confess the Kujou Clan's crimes and claim the Takatsukasa had stood against injustice. Ei reminds them she chose the first Tenryou Commissioner by duel and that any replacement must beat her. Susumu and his retainers refuse out of fear, which Ei calls hypocrisy given Susumu's talk of giving his life. Kamaji challenges her, knowing he is outmatched, to atone for his father; he does not yield and the duel ends only when he collapses. She orders Susumu's party to look after him. Afterward she says the Shogun would have killed him and that she saw in his eyes he accepted that, and that Kamaji keeps the Kujou trait of honour. She will still punish the clan but gives them more time. Back at the shrine Miko says the Traveler may borrow the pass to visit Ei again.

Act II, Transient Dreams. At the Inazuma City Adventurers' Guild Katheryne passes on a Yashiro Commission request: rifthounds are attacking the Sacred Sakura. In the field Ei joins the Traveler. She says the rifthounds recall the cataclysm 500 years ago, which the Traveler recognises as Khaenri'ah's fall. The sakura's sap, which purifies filth in the Ley Lines, produces memories; tainted filth evokes aggressive ones. From the roots appear echoes: Kitamura, a samurai who warns that monsters roam and that both the Shogun and Kitsune Saiguu are gone, and Furuyama, a tea specialist from her entourage, who accepts the end of things as the Shogun taught. Ei says Saiguu led Inazuma's defence and died, and that she herself was too fixated on the past. Furuyama's attitude, she says, came from her sister Makoto.

At the Kamisato Estate they fetch a tea set, but by the time they return Furuyama has faded. Ei makes tea and tells how Makoto went to Khaenri'ah without telling her and was dying when Ei found her. Ei entered her consciousness to say goodbye, resolved on eternity, preserved the realm of Makoto's mind and took it home. Back in Inazuma she found the Sacred Sakura on Mt. Yougou, which she had never seen, though everyone else said it had always stood there. She believes Makoto's remnants made it and used its power against the monsters. Asked about the Traveler's sibling, she says she arrived too late to know.

Tracking the residue to a cave, Ei freezes while fighting. The roots call up three yoriki, Fujiki, Fukami and one unnamed, who fight the rifthounds and then say the Shogun gave them hope. Ei says she neglected her duties as an Archon and promises to be worthy. Under the Grand Narukami Shrine she opens a torii gate into Makoto's consciousness, where the puppet greets her. The puppet is rejecting her commands, believing her new views a sign of erosion. They duel, the puppet with Engulfing Lightning and Ei with Musou Isshin, and Ei expels the Traveler, telling them to ask Miko to govern in her stead.

Miko reopens the torii and sends the Traveler to the plane, where centuries have passed. The Shogun accepts a final duel. Ei wins, the Shogun finds she is not eroded, and Ei offers to make it her kagemusha, which it accepts, impressed and looking forward to a rematch. The Musou Isshin then releases a fragment of Makoto's consciousness. Makoto apologises for dumping rulership on Ei and not persuading her slowly, says she sensed what was coming in Khaenri'ah and had no time to wait, and left a fragment in the sword to wait for Ei to understand her view. She gives Ei a seed, which Ei plants in the past and becomes the Sacred Sakura, then bids her farewell. Back in the present, Ei looks at Inazuma, abolishes the Sakoku Decree and thanks everyone.

Revelations: - Ei has disabled most of the puppet Shogun's functions while she tries to change its old protocols.
- Ei can occupy the Shogun's body in the real world, and sees herself as one being with several forms.
- Ei has never dealt with Mora or shops, and enjoys Dango Milk.
- The Takatsukasa Clan tried to take the Tenryou Commission from the Kujou by pressuring Kamaji.

- Ei appointed the first Tenryou Commissioner by a duel, which the Kujou founder won.
- Ei says the Shogun puppet would have killed Kamaji in the duel; she holds back and he survives.
- Act II: Sacred Sakura sap purifies Ley Line filth and returns memories of the past.
- Act II: Makoto went to Khaenri'ah without telling Ei and died there; Ei resolved on eternity afterwards.
- Act II: A fragment of Makoto lived on in the Musou Isshin sword.
- Act II: Ei ends the Sakoku Decree.

Characters: - **Raiden Shogun**: the Electro Archon Ei and her puppet, the chapter's protagonist.
- **The Traveler and Paimon**: bring Ei into the city and then fight beside her.
- **Yae Miko**: Guuji who lends the pass, and governs for Ei when she retreats.
- **Thoma, Kujou Kamaji, Ippei**: Inazuman retainers and officials concerned for the Shogun.
- **Tomoki, Kuroda**: a stall owner and a publishing house editor.
- **Takatsukasa Susumu**: leader of the Takatsukasa plot.
- **Kitamura, Furuyama, Fujiki, Fukami**: memory echoes from the Sacred Sakura.
- **Makoto**: Ei's late sister, first Electro Archon.

Katheryne, Hirano and Takeshi have minor roles, and Kitsune Saiguu is present only through memory.

Consequences: Ei takes an active role in governing Inazuma. The Shogun puppet becomes her kagemusha. The Sakoku Decree is abolished. The Kujou Clan gets more time. Susumu and the Takatsukasa are checked.

Placement: Act I is Version 2.1; Act II, Transient Dreams, is Version 2.5. Both require Omnipresence Over Mortals and Adventure Rank 40; Act I is a prerequisite for the Kaedehara, Kamisato Ayato and Yae Miko chapters, and Act II is also required for Yae Miko's. Story order and release order match.

The puppet's later rematch is the subject of End of the Oneiric Euthymia, a separate quest.

496.content: The Shogun that Ei made to rule in her place. In Transient Dreams it turns against Ei, believing she is suffering erosion; after a duel in Makoto's consciousness it accepts that she is not, and becomes her kagemusha.

497.comment: Imperatrix Umbrosa Chapter: Furuyama and the memory echoes
497.content: Memories of the catastrophe 500 years ago that appear from the Sacred Sakura's roots. Furuyama, a tea specialist in Ei's entourage, accepts life's end as Makoto's teaching. Kitamura, Fujiki and Fukami are samurai who feared for Inazuma and take heart when Ei returns. They fade once the Ley Lines can no longer sustain them.

498.content: Takatsukasa Susumu tries to replace the Kujou Clan as Tenryou Commissioner by pressuring Kamaji at a hidden base guarded by ronin. Ei interrupts, says only someone who defeats her can hold the office, and Susumu backs down. Kamaji duels her instead.

key: In the Dwelling of Life world quest series
499.content:
In the Dwelling of Life (also: In the Dwelling of Life world quest series, Okurov quest series, Flamefeather Valley quest series, Nastya's quest): In the Dwelling of Life is a seven-part world quest series added in 7.0 in Flamefeather Valley, Snezhnaya. The Traveler and Paimon find a small girl named Nastya, who has branches growing from her head, asleep in a crate of loot, and escort her home to Okurov, a village sealed off from the outside world. There they learn that a "Doctor Moreau" has been leading the villagers into a ritual that turns people into a single eternal "Perfect Tree", and that the doctor is really the bio-alchemist Koshchei. Nastya chooses the ritual anyway, and the series ends with the Traveler recovering a fragment of the Eye of Graeae's power.

The series parts are: A Sprout Without a Gardener; Transplanted From "Yesterday" to "Tomorrow"; Down in the Dumps; Back on One's Feet; Forbidding Doors of Melancholy; To Rest in a Forgotten Field; and Chorus of Solace. Each title echoes a line from Nelly Sachs's poem "Chorus of the Consolers" (the final title echoes the poem's own title), according to the wiki's trivia; this is an observation of the title pattern, not an in-game statement.

It is a small-cast, unsettling story about a sealed village, and it runs at the same time as the first Snezhnaya Archon Quest chapter. Inside Okurov the Traveler plays in a third-person shooter style, per the wiki's Okurov trivia.

Plot: At the Morepesok train station, the Traveler and Paimon overhear Vinezka and her fiance Jary. Jary has been hired by criminals to blast open a tunnel to the abandoned town of Okurov, and Vinezka fears the local legend of a firebird that lures people into the valley and devours them. The Traveler takes the job. In the valley they defeat a Volkodlak gang led by "The Anvil" and find Nastya asleep in a crate; she lives in Okurov and speaks of a guardian called Zhara. She leads them through the tunnel toward her home. In the end Nastya enters the ritual, dissolves into glowing blue algae and joins the Perfect Tree.

In A Sprout Without a Gardener, The Anvil claims the "treasure" he stole from Okurov is inside the blocked tunnel and tries to enforce a hundred-times penalty on Jary. The "treasure" turns out to be Nastya, who fears she has been kidnapped by Volkodlak again, says she has slept in the dark for what felt like a short time, and clears the path with a magic hook. A newspaper in a wrecked carriage praises Okurov's warm weather, its exceptional doctor and its open-door policy; the air near the tunnel's end is unnaturally warm.

In the second quest, Nastya describes her town's belief that the assembly hall is the true home. She idolises "Doctor Moreau", whom she also calls "Doctor Birdie", who taught that becoming family means growing branches and leaves until everyone is the same. She calls outsiders "Badbugs", who in her telling are burned to feed the soil, and they play a game of "Catch the Bug" that she secretly uses to lead the party among hostile Leshy she regards as family. Then Zhara, a huge winged creature, attacks.

In Down in the Dumps, the party wakes in a flooded sewer. The Eye of Graeae explains that Zhara tries to preserve the status quo and that the transformations are linked to Koshchei the Deathless, one of the creators of its body. The party solves gate and valve puzzles, collects Red, White and Blue keys and escapes by lift. In Back on One's Feet, the party reaches Nastya, who is blocked from the assembly hall by a hostile neighbour, the Leshy "No-Nose" Ove, who has hidden the elevator's control wheel and locks children in his cellar. They retrieve the wheel from his house.

In Forbidding Doors of Melancholy, Nastya's idol Furiosa, a woman who grew branches after an experiment by the Doctor, warns that no one should reach the hall and fights the Traveler. Inside the Hall of Prayers, Nastya recalls reciting prayers for Zhara about a "firebird" becoming a "silent tree". Past the curtain relief of Zhara, a dial door asks for a "salt" to replace the "body of the past"; Nastya offers a twig from her own head after explaining the three steps of casting off soul (sulfur), will (silver) and body. Notes found beyond reveal that the Doctor is Koshchei and describe the "final ceremony". To Rest in a Forgotten Field takes the party past Zhara again and through glowing blue algae to the great tree where Nastya's "home" is, with another fight against Zhara.

Chorus of Solace opens after Zhara falls. Nastya tells the Traveler that "Doctor Moreau" and her late mother have welcomed her into the Perfect Tree and that she wants to see her mother's eyes once more. Paimon begs her to leave and the Traveler reminds her of the life waiting outside, but Nastya says her wish to be with her mother outweighs playing with friends or eating. The two respect the choice. She says she will tell her mother about them in the "world beyond eternity" and then disintegrates into blue algae.

The Eye of Graeae recovers the ritual's power, which has gathered as a crystal fragment inside a giant egg. Aksinya appears outside the tree, says she has kept Zhara from reviving, and introduces herself as the "Royal Jester" and creator of the Eye of Graeae's vessel. She says Koshchei succeeded in creating a form of eternity but could not hold onto his personal love, and that her goal matches the Traveler's: helping the Eye of Graeae regain its power and find its body. She leaves cryptically, and the Eye recalls that it, Aksinya and Koshchei created it within Hvergelmir.

Revelations: Okurov's "Doctor Moreau" is Koshchei the Deathless, a Snezhnayan bio-alchemist and former Hvergelmir member. His notes say the Perfect Tree grants great strength but regresses language, and that the "final ceremony" aims to turn the participants into embryos of a new, emotionless existence; pain, sorrow and individual love are to be cast off for eternal life, though the notes admit love might be the only thing that does not fade. The warm air, the blue algae and the Leshy are all products of this work. Zhara is Koshchei's guardian creature.

The wiki's Koshchei page, which should be read as medium confidence, says he took his share of the Eye of Graeae's power to Flamefeather Valley after the Eye's betrayal of Aksinya, joined Okurov under the alias "Doctor Moreau", and was himself dissolved into blue algae in the experiment. Furiosa and Ove, who realised the truth, tried to keep villagers away from the hall. Wiki trivia notes the alias and setting resemble H. G. Wells's The Island of Doctor Moreau.

Characters: Nastya, a child of Okurov who idolises "Doctor Birdie" and Furiosa; Koshchei (as Doctor Moreau); Zhara; the Leshy including Aunt LePuy and Ove; Furiosa; the Eye of Graeae; Aksinya; Vinezka and Jary; "The Anvil". The Traveler and Paimon escort Nastya throughout.

Nastya's mother, who has apparently already joined the tree, appears only through Nastya's words. Zhara can only be told apart from other constructs by its humanoid upper body and branch "mask" per the wiki. Nastya is a young child and should be portrayed as innocent and trusting, not as a villain.

Consequences: Nastya is gone, and the ritual's power is recovered as a crystal fragment for the Eye of Graeae, which helps its quest to rebuild its body. Aksinya now knows the Traveler and shares the Eye's goal. Koshchei is dissolved, and the experiment has ended in Okurov. The wiki says that visiting Nastya's home afterwards shows a young Juvenile Tree Segment named Shar living there with blue algae by the bed.

The series gives the Traveler their first long look at Hvergelmir's leftover work and at the relationship between Aksinya, Koshchei and the Eye of Graeae, which the Archon Quest develops later.

The Eye of Graeae, which already travels with the Traveler, is the main thread to keep: it wants its power and body back, and the crystal fragment from the Perfect Tree is a first step. Aksinya's statement that Koshchei failed to hold onto his personal love is the series' stated moral verdict on the experiment; Nastya's own choice is the human cost.

Placement: Released 7.0 as part of the Snezhnaya launch. The wiki lists it as concurrent with Archon Quest Chapter VII Act I quests "On One Side a Palace, On the Other a Tomb" and "Hesperides of Love and Hate", with "Her Palace Collapses Into the Blizzard" next. No separate prerequisite quest is stated for the world quest series.

For roleplay, the Traveler and Paimon know everything in this series from 7.0 onward, but characters elsewhere (Fatui, Druzhna, other Archon Quest figures) generally do not, since Okurov was sealed and most of its people are gone.

500.comment: In the Dwelling of Life: Okurov
500.content: Okurov is a hidden village in Flamefeather Valley, unlocked during the series. Its name references the 1908 novel The City of Okurov by Maxim Gorky, per the wiki. Its air is warm enough to help "pretty leaves" grow, its townsfolk see the assembly hall as home, and its Leshy residents include former villagers who did not complete the ritual. The way in is a collapsed rail tunnel leading from the Morepesok side, which Jary was hired to blast open.

501.comment: In the Dwelling of Life: Nastya
501.content: Nastya is a young child from Okurov with branches growing from her head, found asleep in a crate. She is cheerful, proud of being "the smartest child", loyal to the doctor and to Furiosa, and eager to see the world outside the valley for the first time while longing for her mother. Her choice at the end is shown as hers; the quest treats it as tragic and does not call her foolish.

502.comment: In the Dwelling of Life: Koshchei and Doctor Moreau
502.content: Koshchei is a Snezhnayan bio-alchemist and former Hvergelmir member who created the Aberrant Chimeric Monsters and later, as Doctor Moreau, led Okurov's villagers toward a state of eternal, unchanging life. The Eye of Graeae says it was created by him, Aksinya and a third party within Hvergelmir; by the series' end he has dissolved into the tree with the villagers. Aksinya says he achieved eternity but lost his personal love.

503.comment: In the Dwelling of Life: Zhara
503.content: Zhara is an Immortal Construct made by Koshchei, with a humanoid upper half, long blonde hair and branches masking her eyes. She guards Okurov from "Badbugs" (outsiders), attacks the Traveler twice and is subdued at the great tree. Aksinya stops her from reviving. The name echoes the Russian word for heat and the Firebird of folklore.

key: In the Footsteps of the Chosen of Dragons
In the Footsteps of the Chosen of Dragons World Quest series
Someday, We All Must Walk Alone
504.comment: In the Footsteps of the Chosen of Dragons
504.content:
In the Footsteps of the Chosen of Dragons (also: In the Footsteps of the Chosen of Dragons World Quest series, Little One side quests, Someday, We All Must Walk Alone): The series gathers the Little One side quests: A Saurian Lover's Ordinary Days, Feeling Like Fish Today!, Friends of Fire and Water (5.2), Gifts and Gifts in Return, Is "Intensity" Really the Key? (5.5), Lies and Promises, Lights, Kamera, Action!, Sauro-Vet's Dilemma (5.2), Special Friends, Stones, Coconuts, and Saurian Traffickers (5.2), Tepetlisaurus Hide-and-Seek, The Lone Isle Named Night (5.2), Treasures and Collectors, Waiting For Seeds to Sprout and Weighty Wings. They can be done in any order. Most are light errands that show Little One meeting other saurians and humans in Natlan. The final quest, Someday, We All Must Walk Alone (5.5), unlocks only after the main Little One quests are finished and a few hidden interactions around the map are completed. In it Little One takes a photograph with the Traveler and Paimon, then leaves on its own.

Natlan is a nation where humans and saurians live side by side, so the series is a long, warm look at that relationship through one individual. The wiki frames the whole chapter as the search for a cure for the Flamelord's Blessing, a mark on Little One's horn that Manqu says kills or maddens saurians as they grow. The main journey for that is carried by Between Pledge and Forgettance, Path to the Flaming Peaks and A Finale Emberforged.

The wiki's summary also says that after the cure Little One gets to enjoy freedom and a connection to its dragon roots, and that the Traveler receives a smaller, permanent saurian pet for the Serenitea Pot. The pet detail is a gameplay note: two daily server resets after the last quest, a Little Tepetlisaurus appears at the Rest Area where Little One used to be, according to the quest page.

Plot: The side quests share one setup. After Lost in the Woods, Little One travels with the Traveler and Paimon, and each quest starts from something Little One does or finds: catching fish, digging up a seed, meeting a group of alpacas, hiding among other Tepetlisauri, gifting its collected treasures, wanting to star in a film, or discovering a hidden chamber on the Isle of Night. Paimon narrates and mothers it; the Traveler handles the practical and puzzle work. Several quests take place in other tribes' territory, such as the Flower-Feather Clan range, and bring in local NPCs with their own saurian partners.

Someday, We All Must Walk Alone is the capstone. Once every Little One quest and a handful of unmarked puzzles are done, Little One leads the group back to the Rest Area where they first met, has found a Kamera, and sets up a group photograph. Afterwards it shows that it wants to go its own way. Paimon cries and makes the Traveler promise they will meet again; Little One tucks one photograph into its shell, nuzzles Paimon and the Traveler, and plods off.

Quest-by-quest hooks from the wiki quest descriptions: A Saurian Lover's Ordinary Days starts when the Traveler meets someone surrounded by three saurians; Feeling Like Fish Today! has Paimon fishing for Little One; Friends of Fire and Water rescues a Blubberbeast that befriends Little One; Gifts and Gifts in Return has Little One giving the Traveler its collected treasures; Is "Intensity" Really the Key? asks whether intensity or something else will beat the cold; Lies and Promises centres on a Yumkasaurus blocking a treasure; Lights, Kamera, Action! is a film starring Little One; Sauro-Vet's Dilemma begins with a Qucusaurus apparently attacking a human; Special Friends is about Little One making new friends; Stones, Coconuts, and Saurian Traffickers helps a merchant and his saurian; Tepetlisaurus Hide-and-Seek starts when Little One does not come back from playing; The Lone Isle Named Night is a hidden chamber on the Isle of Tozoz; Treasures and Collectors is the Saurian Relics Excavation Site; Waiting For Seeds to Sprout follows a strange seed; Weighty Wings is an injured saurian in the wild.

The final quest's prerequisites include essentially all of Natlan's Little One content: the A Finale Emberforged, Between Pledge and Forgettance, Chronicler of the Crumbling City, From One Case to Another, Lost Traveler in the Ashen Realm, Path to the Flaming Peaks, Shadows of the Mountains and Tale of Dreams Plucked From Fire chains, several single quests (including The Way Into the Mountain, The Road Ahead and Open Your Heart to Me), and three hidden interactions: an S-rank in Urubamba's Warrior's Challenge, a Kamera puzzle on Quahuacan Cliff, and a Secret Source Dragon Idol in the Sea of Shifting Sentience. Paimon guesses Little One got the Kamera from Akatanga, a would-be director from the Children of Echoes whom she recalls using his Kamera the wrong way round; Akatanga is also listed in Lights, Kamera, Action!.

Revelations: The series makes few story revelations of its own. It shows that Little One understands more than it can say and that it has quietly kept hold of keepsakes from the journey. In the closing quest Little One sets up the photograph and then departs; the narration says the Traveler recalls the mix of feelings in its eyes at the foot of the Sacred Mountain.

Because the final quest is gated behind A Finale Emberforged, anyone reading it has already seen that the Flamelord's Blessing was cleansed in the volcano and that the Sage of the Stolen Flame (Kukulkan) had darker plans. The farewell is therefore a human-scale epilogue to the larger Natlan story.

Characters: Little One is a young Tepetlisaurus with a red Flamelord's Blessing mark on its horn and a scarf from Paimon tied to its tail. It speaks only in growls and is treated as "he" by Paimon and the Traveler in several lines. It is energetic, curious, a hearty eater, and loyal. Paimon is protective and tearful at the parting; the Traveler is calmer but affected. Other quest NPCs include Icayo, Imix and Kulahaw, Linaha, Ma'chah and Yoleehe, Wayna, Mazkal, Qax, Quipia, and Akatanga, each tied to one quest.

Little One is the only recurring character; the wiki character lists show the rest as one-off figures, such as the saurians "Jade", "Marigold" and "Ripple" in A Saurian Lover's Ordinary Days and the alpacas of Special Friends.

Consequences: Completing Someday, We All Must Walk Alone ends Little One's time with the party. It gives the achievement Then You Will Be Free to..., the avatar "Till We Meet Again", 20 Primogems, a Photo With Travel Companions and Mora. After it the souvenirs in the Rest Area disappear, except for the Unhatched Saurian Egg.

Per the series summary, the Traveler also receives a smaller, permanent saurian pet in the Serenitea Pot, a Little Tepetlisaurus.

Placement: Most side quests released in 5.0 with Natlan; Friends of Fire and Water, Sauro-Vet's Dilemma, Stones, Coconuts, and Saurian Traffickers and The Lone Isle Named Night joined in 5.2; Is "Intensity" Really the Key? and Someday, We All Must Walk Alone arrived in 5.5. In story order the side quests can be done any time after Lost in the Woods, but the finale quest should be done after A Finale Emberforged and all other Little One content.

Between Pledge and Forgettance, Path to the Flaming Peaks and A Finale Emberforged supply the main emotional arc; this series is the optional companion.

key: Someday We All Must Walk Alone
505.comment: In the Footsteps of the Chosen of Dragons: Someday, We All Must Walk Alone
505.content:
Someday, We All Must Walk Alone is the final quest of the series. In the Rest Area where they first met, Little One shows the Traveler and Paimon a Kamera (a camera-like gadget), performs a move Paimon recognises as the Mighty Meaty Fireball, and takes a photograph with them. It then says goodbye. Paimon tearfully makes it promise to come find them if it needs help, and tells it to stay healthy and big. Little One nuzzles them and leaves.

Quest text hints at the Sage's role too: Paimon complains that the Sage never showed his face, and the Traveler thinks back to the feelings in Little One's eyes at the foot of the Sacred Mountain.

506.comment: In the Footsteps of the Chosen of Dragons: Kamera and the Mighty Meaty Fireball
506.content: Lights, Kamera, Action! is the quest in which the Traveler shoots a film starring Little One, and Akatanga appears in it. In the farewell quest Paimon recalls Akatanga as a would-be director who used his Kamera backwards and guesses Little One got its Kamera from him. Paimon also recognises a pose of Little One's as the Mighty Meaty Fireball, and the three say the phrase for the photograph. It is a light, comic detail contrasted with the parting.

507.content:
In the Mountains (also: In the Mountains world quest, Dragonspine frozen shards quest): A Dragonspine world quest from Version 1.2. Iris, an adventurer at the Dragonspine Adventurer Camp, complains of strange unmeltable ice blocking expedition routes. The Traveler thaws glowing shards from that ice, follows them up the mountain and opens the way to the summit.

The quest requires The Outlander Who Caught the Wind and starts by talking to Iris at the camp. Completing it opens the Frostbearing Tree offering system, the Peak of Vindagnyr domain and the Cryo Hypostasis boss, as game-side unlocks. It is a gameplay-driven quest with little dialogue lore.

Its story value is atmosphere and mystery: Dragonspine is shown as more hostile than anywhere else in Mondstadt, and the quest leaves its odd phenomena (a sealed windy cavern, ice that fire cannot melt, blue plants, a floating pillar) deliberately unexplained.

Plot: Iris tells the Traveler about hard ice that will not melt in fire and a cavern near the summit that breathes a strange powerful wind. The Traveler thaws a shard in the ice, sees a blue orb fly toward the summit, and later thaws two more. Reaching the top, they find a floating pillar and a hollow beneath it, and report back to Iris.

Iris suggests looking at a large slab of ice on the mountain's outer edge. When it is thawed with Scarlet Quartz, a blue orb flies off toward the summit and a new Frostbearing Tree grows. Paimon and the Traveler try to climb the summit cavern but are driven back by the cold and the air current, so they return to the camp. Iris explains that earlier expedition teams were turned back by the ice and that blue plants cluster near it, pointing to the Entombed City outskirts and Starglow Cavern. After thawing the other two shards the Traveler follows the road past a Statue of The Seven to the summit and sees a giant pillar. The three shards have frozen again on it, so the Traveler thaws them a second time. The ice under the pillar then shatters, revealing a large space below. Iris thanks them and promises to send explorers.

Details of the thawing: each shard needs a Scarlet Quartz effect, and the Warming Seelie lead the Traveler between the monuments and shards. The first two shards sit near the Entombed City outskirts and inside Starglow Cavern, where the wave fight is a timed challenge under falling icicles. The summit portion uses the Skyfrost Nail subarea. After the pillar is restored, Paimon can climb it and wonders whether it fell from the sky. Iris admits she saw something encased in the ice but could not melt it herself, and half-jokes that an adventure story would link the wind, ice and plants.

Game-side notes, kept separate from story: exactly enough Scarlet Quartz is provided at each stage, and any attack made with its effect melts a shard, not only Pyro. The second round of thawing needs only one hit per shard. A snowstorm and Ruin Guards or Ruin Graders guard parts of the Entombed City outskirts. Climbing the restored Skyfrost Nail gives a separate achievement, and Paimon's remark there is the only comment on the pillar's origin.

Revelations: No question is answered. The quest only establishes that the ice shards belong to a floating pillar at the summit (later called the Skyfrost Nail) and that a chamber lies beneath it.

Characters: The Traveler, Paimon and Iris.

Iris is an adventurer at the Dragonspine Adventurer Camp who organises expedition parties and warns the Traveler to prepare well before going up the mountain.

Consequences: Iris can resume organising expeditions now that the ice can be melted. The summit becomes reachable, and the Peak of Vindagnyr domain and Cryo Hypostasis become accessible as game features. The achievement for restoring the Skyfrost Nail is granted.

Placement: Released in Version 1.2 with the Dragonspine content. It follows The Outlander Who Caught the Wind in requirements and is a companion to the Dragonspine quest A Land Entombed, which uses the same mountain and ruins.

key: wooden house on the ice farewell
508.content:
In the Tranquility of Cycles (also: Chulkaturin's last quest, Chulkaturin's farewell, wooden house on the ice farewell): In the Tranquility of Cycles is a short 7.0 world quest in Snezhnaya's far north. It ends the story of Chulkaturin, an ancient fae who lives in a wooden cabin built on a floe of ice and refuses to set foot on Snezhnayan land. When the Traveler and Paimon return, the ice is melting and the cabin is about to sink. He declines to come ashore, thanks them, asks to be left alone, and the house sinks as the ice melts.

The quest is the third part of a chain begun in Ever Beneath the Waves and continued in The Sunken Ship Sailed Past, Ringing No Bells. Completing it grants the achievement "The Cherry Orchard Has Been Sold" (per the wiki).

Plot: The Traveler finds Chulkaturin's cabin tilted toward the sea. Paimon calls to him; he answers from inside and agrees that the ice is going, but will not leave. Rather than argue, the Traveler can try to persuade him, offer to pull him ashore or suggest rebuilding on ice, and he rejects each. He asks them to stop breaking the ice, stop towing the house and let him go, then asks for a last goodbye. The house makes no further answer.

In the earlier quests the Traveler cleared brash ice and towed the cabin toward shore in Ever Beneath the Waves, and in The Sunken Ship Sailed Past, Ringing No Bells helped him reach crates of materials so he could expand and reinforce it. Chulkaturin says he overloaded the floe himself in a wish to restore a measure of his people's former glory and dignity.

The cabin, he says, bears all his history and is his last place. Leaving would cut him from his roots; a new house would not be built from the snow poplars he grew up alongside, and new ice would not bear the weight of the past. He fears that on land, where the future is unpredictable, few of his choices would still be his own. He asks the Traveler for a last farewell instead of rescue.

At the close, the house gives no more answer and sinks quietly. For a long while the Traveler hears only a strange song hummed in an old, complex tongue, perhaps about snow poplars not yet felled and glories untarnished; it fades like ice melting into foam. The text ends: the ice melts away.

Revelations: Chulkaturin's earlier statements stand: he calls himself the last scion of old snowfield-dwelling nobility, a relic of an era that "still belonged to the fae", uprooted from the land over three hundred years ago, whose snow poplars were all cut down. This quest adds that he sees the past as inseparable from his life and that he would need to atone for it before he could start a new one. What he must atone for is not explained.

Characters: Chulkaturin, an old fae speaking from inside the cabin; the Traveler and Paimon. Chulkaturin addresses them as "shorebound travelers" and finally as friends.

His voice is formal, archaic and gentle. He thanks them repeatedly and never argues angrily. Paimon is the one who panics, pleads and offers practical alternatives.

Consequences: Chulkaturin and his house are gone from the ice. The Traveler's choice here is limited to how to say goodbye (the options in the wiki text are to plead, offer to help, or accept) and does not change the outcome.

Placement: Released in 7.0 as an ordinary open-world quest in northern Snezhnaya, available after completing The Sunken Ship Sailed Past, Ringing No Bells. It has no link to the Archon Quest.

For roleplay: Chulkaturin's refusal is a considered, calm choice, not despair spoken in anger; it is a quiet counterpart to other Snezhnaya stories about the weight of the past. Do not invent a name for the nobles' lost kingdom or a cause for its fall, because none is given.

509.comment: In the Tranquility of Cycles: Chulkaturin
509.content: Chulkaturin is an old fae who has lived 321 years in a wooden cabin on a floe, built from felled snow poplars, never setting foot on Snezhnayan land. He calls himself the last scion of old snowfield-dwelling nobility. He speaks in a courtly, archaic manner and addresses the Traveler and Paimon as "travelers by the shore". He asks them not to save him in the end and sinks with his home.

510.content:
In the Wake of Narcissus (also: Search in the Algae Sea, Savior's Wake, Waking from the Great Dream, Rowboat's Wake): In the Wake of Narcissus is a four-act Fontaine World Quest series added in version 4.2. It concludes the Narzissenkreuz storyline begun in Ann of the Narzissenkreuz and Ancient Colors. The Traveler, Paimon, Ann, Seymour and a hilichurl-bodied scholar called Caterpillar pursue the Narzissenkreuz Ordo, trace what happened to Mary-Ann, and reach the founder in the Primordial Sea.

The acts are Search in the Algae Sea, Savior's Wake, Waking from the Great Dream and Rowboat's Wake. The series is entered through the quest Initial Facts and its reward track is "In the Wake of Narcissus" in the Fontaine Reputation.

It is the quiet end of a storyline that began as a fairy tale: the "Narzissenkreuz Adventure Team", the "Holy Blade" and the "Princess" are shown to come from an orphanage-turned-cult, and the series chooses between the story being a delusion and the people inside it being real.

Plot: Act I, Search in the Algae Sea. The group deduce who Mary-Ann in Annapausis is, find the pieces of the Holy Blade in the Morte Region, and fight Jakob at the Tower of Gestalt, who dies when the Doomsday Clock strikes.

Act II, Savior's Wake. They descend and sink the Tower of Ipsissimus beneath the Ordo, leaving Caterpillar and Seymour behind.

Act III, Waking from the Great Dream. In the Primordial Sea the Traveler defeats Narzissenkreuz, and Ann forgives him.

Act IV, Rowboat's Wake. With Narzissenkreuz as guide they reach Mary-Ann in Annapausis, who chooses to live as herself; he fades, Seymour returns to Mamere and Caterpillar leaves.

Act I, Search in the Algae Sea. At the Narzissenkreuz Ordo the group compare notes. They reason that the Mary-Ann in the Annapausis is the Oceanid Lyris, former director of the Narzissenkreuz Institute orphanage, and that Ann came from her dream. In Annapausis they fight Al and Jak, who are under Mary-Ann's control, but cannot open the door to the real Annapausis; Mary-Ann's thoughts are heard instead. Caterpillar explains Narzissenkreuz and the Ordo's goals and proposes to find the real Holy Blade. In the Morte Region they find that three seals were already broken and Jakob has the elements, so they get the fourth, the Persona. They are carried to the Tower of Gestalt, where Jakob demands the Persona so Narzissenkreuz can obtain the Holy Blade and "save the world". After a battle he gives up the missing elements; the Holy Blade is forged. Ann refuses to absorb his persona and memories. The Doomsday Clock strikes twelve and crushes Jakob, who says Narzissenkreuz is returning.

Act II, Savior's Wake. The group descends the Tower of Ipsissimus beneath the Ordo, reading notes, an investigation log and a storybook with margin comments. They find a key, deal with dormant Gardemek meka, and activate a mechanism that sinks the tower to the seabed. Caterpillar and Seymour are held back; the Traveler, Paimon and Ann go on.

Act III, Waking from the Great Dream. In the "Genesis of a Certain Micro-Universe" in the Primordial Sea, the Traveler faces Narzissenkreuz, who offers to save as many as he can and demands the Holy Blade. He is defeated; he says he sensed changes in the "world-formula", calls the Traveler the person "equal to a world", and says the Holy Blade cut through the will around him. Ann forgives him. He admits his plan failed and says he wishes to return to the time before the Narzissenkreuz heroes set off.

Act IV, Rowboat's Wake. They return to the Ordo, where Caterpillar meets him and addresses him as "Master" with little warmth. Narzissenkreuz offers to guide them to the Kingdom Through the Looking-Glass. In Annapausis, Ann reshapes the world; they dodge Mary-Ann's bubble defences and break the "Will to Resist" with the Holy Blade. Narzissenkreuz is addressed by Mary-Ann as Rene. After a conversation she chooses to live as herself, and the Holy Blade loses its meaning. Narzissenkreuz fades after a talk with Caterpillar and Ann. Seymour is freed from his old orders, and returns to Mamere with Mary-Ann's blessing. Caterpillar leaves on his own path.
Act I details. Seymour's files on Lyris show she was the director of the Narzissenkreuz Institute, which the Traveler links to Mary-Ann. The group discuss Annapausis as the work of an Oceanid. Jakob says the Ordo's nodes are a response to the apocalypse and that the Seal of Chymical Marriage was an ancient Fontainian ritual to seal the source of life, that the five nodes still working are only part of the plan, and that "Rene" will return.

Act II details. The tower's theme is bells and gears, according to Caterpillar. The investigation log describes archaeological research on temple ruins and mentions a copy kept at the Institute of Natural Philosophy and the deciphering of Remurian script. Seymour estimates that 60% of the dormant Gardemeks will activate. After they sink the tower, Seymour rates his own survival chance at 100%.

Act III details. Narzissenkreuz says Director Lyris holds on to Mary-Ann and hopes only to retain the past. He addresses Ann as "Oceanid Ann" and asks if she would inherit his work; she declines. If the Traveler has completed Masquerade of the Guilty, his lines say the world "has been saved" rather than "is still fated to be saved".

Act IV details. Caterpillar and Seymour wait at the Ordo while the Traveler, Paimon, Ann and Narzissenkreuz go to Annapausis. Narzissenkreuz tells Ann to imagine the place without obstacles; Ann drains the water. At the barrier Mary-Ann begs them to go away: she wants to decay in peace. After the Will to Resist breaks, Ann shows her a treasure image; Mary-Ann says she cannot forgive "Narzissenkreuz" but can forgive "Rene". Narzissenkreuz suggests that Ann could merge with her or the Holy Blade could separate Lyris and the young Mary-Ann, but she refuses, accepting her past. In the Primordial Sea, Narzissenkreuz says he spent ten years holding on to his will, then built a universe within himself, and that Mary-Ann was right that it is warm there. The Sword of Narzissenkreuz is obtained as a reward.

Seymour, whose designer was Alain Guillotin, tells Mary-Ann his components were damaged at Elynas and have not been maintained. She tells him to follow what he wants, not orders, and he decides to return to Mamere. Mary-Ann and Ann plan to travel the world together.

Revelations: - The Mary-Ann of Annapausis is the Oceanid Lyris merged with Mary-Ann Guillotin; the Narzissenkreuz Institute was an orphanage run by the Oceanid Lyris.
- Narzissenkreuz is Rene, one of the circle around the Institute (Jakob lists Alain, Rene, Director Lyris, Mary-Ann and himself), who became the Ordo's master and tried to save the world from the apocalypse foretold in the prophecy.
- Ann is a being born from Mary-Ann's dream (Caterpillar's and the group's deduction, confirmed by Mary-Ann and Narzissenkreuz), and the adventure-team members are Oceanid-born shapes of that dream.
- The Holy Blade of Narzissenkreuz can be any object of significance, and it can separate a will from water.
- Jakob dies when the Doomsday Clock strikes, after reversing the Seal of Chymical Marriage.

- Caterpillar addresses Narzissenkreuz as "Master", resents how he was brought into being, and says he has long since seen the absurdities in the Master's theories.
- Jakob says the Ordo's aim is to unite all wills as one in a new world, to combat the apocalypse.
- The Persona is one of four elements required to forge the Holy Blade.

Characters: The Traveler, Paimon, Ann, Seymour, Caterpillar, Jakob, Al, Jak, Narzissenkreuz (Rene), Mary-Ann, and Mamere. Lyris and Alain Guillotin are discussed. Petit Chou and Al are mentioned as friends Ann may never see again.

Consequences: Jakob is dead, the Ordo's plan is broken and Narzissenkreuz fades in the Primordial Sea. Mary-Ann chooses to leave Annapausis and live as herself with Ann; Seymour returns to Mamere and Caterpillar goes off alone. The Traveler receives the Sword of Narzissenkreuz and the series' reward track.

The ending leaves open what the Ordo's remaining nodes mean and what Narzissenkreuz meant by the world-formula; these are not answered in this series.

Placement: Released in 4.2. Requires Initial Facts, which the wiki places after Mary-Ann's Story, Limner, Dreamer, and Robotic Dog and the Unfinished Comedy series. It is the last of the Ann/Seymour/Narzissenkreuz arcs.

511.comment: In the Wake of Narcissus: Narzissenkreuz (Rene)
511.content: In Waking from the Great Dream the Traveler faces Narzissenkreuz in the Primordial Sea, where he offers to save as many people as he can and demands the Holy Blade. After defeat he apologises to Ann. In Rowboat's Wake Mary-Ann calls him Rene. He spends the last of his power helping Ann and Mary-Ann and then asks to be left in the Genesis of a Certain Micro-Universe.

512.comment: In the Wake of Narcissus: Jakob's death and the Seal of Chymical Marriage
512.content: In Search in the Algae Sea the Traveler fights Jakob at the Tower of Gestalt. After the Holy Blade is forged he says he has reversed the Seal of Chymical Marriage and predicts Rene's return. The Doomsday Clock then strikes twelve and crushes him.

513.comment: In the Wake of Narcissus: Caterpillar
513.content: Caterpillar is a hilichurl-bodied scholar who helps the Traveler and Ann with deductions, jokes dryly, and counts himself among the "things that used to be human". He calls Narzissenkreuz "Master" but disagrees with his theories. He says he owes Lanoire the rest of a story, and at the end sets off alone.

514.comment: In the Wake of Narcissus: Mary-Ann (the Annapausis)
514.content: Mary-Ann in Annapausis is the fused form of the Oceanid Lyris and the human Mary-Ann Guillotin. She keeps the dream-world warm and tries to push visitors away, but accepts her past when Ann shows her a treasure image and when Rene appears. Afterwards she decides to live as herself and travel with Ann.

515.comment: In the Wake of Narcissus: Seymour's choice
515.content: Seymour is Alain Guillotin's creation, first met in Ancient Colors. In Rowboat's Wake Mary-Ann tells him his old orders are void and asks what he wants to do. He decides to return to Mamere, who is waiting in Merusea Village and plans an art trip with him.

516.content:
Incandescent Ode of Resurrection (also: Chapter V Act V, Natlan Archon Quest finale, Incandescent Ode): The act has five quests (Subterranean Ruins; As the Sun Rises and Sets; Journey of Stars and Flames; Where All Hopes Lie; When All Becomes a Monument) and requires Adventure Rank 40. It follows "All Fires Fuel the Flame"; the act's navigation lists "A Space and Time for You" and "Paralogism" as what comes next. The travel log recap frames it as the end of Natlan's millennia-long war against the Abyss, with the nation facing a hopeful future that its sacrifices have paid for.
