Within the act: Capitano appears in a dream, the Traveler is given the Ancient Name "Tumaini" (hope), the final battle with Gosoythoth is won, and the aftermath settles Mavuika's fate and points the Traveler toward Snezhnaya and Nod-Krai.

Plot: **Subterranean Ruins.** The Traveler dreams of the Night Kingdom and sees Capitano and Guthred leading "soldiers" toward a destined place; a rift shows on Capitano's chest.

**As the Sun Rises and Sets.** Mavuika, Xilonen and Citlali plan the descent, and the tribes hold a send-off feast. Ororon's ritual on the Traveler's dream identifies Guthred, and Mavuika confirms that Capitano is Thrain, a legendary hero of Natlan from five hundred years ago. Xilonen delivers the Ancient Name "Tumaini" and tests it at the Sulfurous Veins, where it draws in unusual numbers of souls that the group helps to the Night Kingdom.

**Journey of Stars and Flames.** The Traveler reveals the Ancient Name at the Stadium of the Sacred Flame, and Mavuika takes them into the Night Kingdom. They split: Mavuika seeks the enemy's core, the Traveler its lair, aided by departed allies and Guthred.

**Where All Hopes Lie.** Mavuika and the Traveler, empowered with Pyro by the Lord of the Night, destroy the dragon-formed Gosoythoth.

**When All Becomes a Monument.** After a ceremony honouring the Traveler, Ronova demands Mavuika's death at Ochkanatlan, and Capitano offers himself instead. See revelations and consequences.

Subterranean Ruins: Paimon suggests resting at the Weary Inn because the Ancient Name should soon be ready; the Traveler passes through a wall of light behind which souls are tormented.

As the Sun Rises and Sets: Mavuika will go to the deepest parts in three days, and if the Ancient Name is not ready she must go alone. The Traveler invites Mavuika to the feast at the People of the Springs. Kachina takes the Traveler on a walk that ends with helping the despondent saurian Ayo. At the Sulfurous Veins the group helps souls including Vichama, and Ayo is reunited with the spirits of his grandparents, who choose to stay with him.

Journey of Stars and Flames: departed allies include Atea, Mallko, Vichama, Bona, Cocouik and Chuychu. The heroes of 500 years ago bless the Traveler and the Lord of the Night sends seelies to guide them to Mavuika.

Where All Hopes Lie: Gosoythoth takes control of the Traveler while Mavuika is cast into a void that tries to sow doubt in her; she refuses it. The Sacred Flame goes out in Natlan, but Kachina steadies the crowd, and with their strengthened resolve the two win.

When All Becomes a Monument: Chasca presents a feathered crown on Natlan's behalf. Citlali tells the Traveler that Mavuika is still due to die as the price of restoring the Night Kingdom; at Ochkanatlan a rift of watching eyes appears and Ronova, the Ruler of Death, demands her death as payment.

Details of the feast and the dreams: Amina is overwhelmed by the quantity of supplies the tribes send, because the party grew into a collective send-off; she mentions that Atea, who would normally have handled logistics, died shortly after the attack on the tribe. Iansan recalls a dream of her saurian companion who died in the war. Ororon calls the Traveler's dream an outlier compared to those granted from the divine throne, and learns from the vision that Guthred's soul has persisted for hundreds of years and that Capitano's body holds an amalgamation of souls. Mavuika suggests Ororon ask Capitano directly. Mavuika also tells the Traveler she paints as a hobby, though duty rarely leaves her time.

Details of the Night Kingdom: at a pit stop the chiefs and friends wish the pair luck; Mavuika explains the enemy has a core that behaves like the tumors seen during the invasion. She meets a Cryo-aligned Abyss herald and then her sister Hine, who promises support. The Traveler is met by Atea and a group of Natlanese who stay behind to keep the Abyssal corrosion from the square behind them, because if it spread the Abyss could surge back into Natlan. Mallko and Vichama maintain a protective barrier against the fog. Bona realises Guthred is not from Natlan; Guthred says he is a story created by the Masters of the Night-Wind and so can manifest. The spirits can go no further because of the Ley Lines, and Chuychu, who also visited Chasca in dreams, provides an iktomisaurus and a qucusaur for the last stretch.

The act's ending: Ronova says she has no interest in Teyvat and names Mavuika's death as the price of using her power. Mavuika argues the Lord of the Night is still weak and the Abyss may return, so she means to put her life into the Sacred Flame again. Ronova accepts Mavuika's sacrifice as the death owed, but the Lord of the Night pauses, saying another wishes to take part in the ceremony and she must wait for him.

After the ceremony the Traveler leaves the feathered crown at a new monument for the fallen of the final battle. Back in the Speaker's Chamber, Mavuika writes a letter to her sister Hine and burns it so that it may be "sent" to her, telling her that Natlan is at peace. At the stadium, Sadigua tells children a story that includes the Traveler's deeds, and the Traveler and Paimon leave without interrupting. When they ask about their next journey, Mavuika reports that Capitano had asked the Tsaritsa to abolish his mission to take the Pyro Gnosis, and the request was granted; she still fears another Harbinger may try, and warns that entering Snezhnaya will place the Traveler in direct conflict with the Fatui. She adds that the Doctor's subordinates have been studying fragments in the sky, said to be Secret Source technology relics called Ancient Moon's Remnants, and that his stronghold lies in Nod-Krai, a land with a power said to predate the elements.

Revelations: - The Traveler's Ancient Name is "Tumaini" (hope); this is the first time in Natlan's history that an outsider has received one. Its power is so great that it attracts souls from beyond Natlan.
- Capitano is Thrain, the "Sentinel Knight" of Khaenri'ah and one of Natlan's legendary heroes of five hundred years ago.
- With Khaenri'ahn technology, Capitano's heart was modified to convert memories and souls from the Ley Lines into knowledge; after the catastrophe five hundred years ago he gave up that capacity and used his heart as a vessel for the souls of his comrades and many Natlanese. By merging his existence with the Lord of the Night he means to become master of the Ley Lines and change the rules so they can go home.
- Capitano, like many Khaenri'ahns, regards himself as innocent of what the Five Sinners of Khaenri'ah did, and wants revenge on Ronova for the curse of immortality by turning it into a paradox: if he gives his life for the Lord of the Night she receives the death she demands, yet his immortality negates that death.
- Guthred says he is a story created by the Masters of the Night-Wind.
- Ronova is called the Ruler of Death in the act's dialogue, and the watching rift above Ochkanatlan is attributed by Citlali to her.
- Capitano had asked the Tsaritsa to cancel his mission to take the Pyro Gnosis, and she agreed.

Mavuika's plan always involved her own death by the Sacred Flame; Citlali says she remains slated to die even after the war is won. The act shows her leaving the question of her own wishes unanswered when the Traveler asks. Her refusal of the void's doubts in the Gosoythoth fight is framed as her conviction that her fate is to end the war.

Characters: Mavuika, the Pyro Archon, leads the plan. Xilonen forges the Ancient Name and Citlali interprets the souls it draws. Kachina, Mualani, Kinich and Chasca represent the tribes, and Ororon's ritual reveals Guthred. Capitano, a Fatui Harbinger and Khaenri'ahn, appears in a dream and then at Ochkanatlan. The dead helpers include Atea, Vichama, Mallko, Bona, Cocouik and Chuychu. Gosoythoth is the final enemy; Ronova and Yohualtecuhtin, the Lord of the Night, appear at the end.

Consequences: Faced with the paradox, Ronova keeps the curse of immortality and relinquishes her demand for a death, telling Capitano to use it to fulfil his final wish. He sits on the Throne of the Primal Fire with the souls he carried, guiding them back to the Night Kingdom and, as Citlali puts it, granting the Lord of the Night eternal life by fusing his existence with hers. The Lord of the Night, grateful for the chance to live forever, apologises for having once thought so little of how long a life lasts, and returns to the Night Kingdom. Mavuika accepts that Natlan still needs a leader and lives; the five present pay respects to Capitano. Natlan is at peace, the Traveler is a celebrated hero, and Mavuika's briefing sends the Traveler toward Snezhnaya and Nod-Krai (the Song of the Welkin Moon chapter, beginning with the prelude "The Journey Home").

Ronova had already agreed to accept Mavuika's sacrifice for the Lord of the Night as her death, concluding her deal with Xbalanque from several thousand years ago. Capitano's challenge was to forsake one of her rules or let him trigger a paradox that could uproot the natural order; the cutscene narration says she relinquished the price of death to sustain the curse. The Lord of the Night explains that Natlan's Ley Lines could not connect to other nations, which is why Capitano's earlier attempts elsewhere failed and why he came to Natlan.

Placement: Chapter V, Act V; released in version 5.3 (the change history of the act and of all five quest pages lists 5.3). It follows "All Fires Fuel the Flame" and precedes the Song of the Welkin Moon chapter, whose prelude is "The Journey Home" (5.8). The act page lists "A Space and Time for You" and "Paralogism" as the next quests.

517.content:
Interlude Chapter (also: Interlude Archon Quest, Interlude Chapter Acts): The Interlude Chapter is a set of four self-contained Archon Quest acts. They do not form one story; each follows up on the quest that unlocks it. Act I, The Crane Returns on the Wind (Liyue), covers the rebuilding of the Jade Chamber and Shenhe. Act II, Perilous Trail (Liyue), sends a party into the Chasm after Xiao's lost comrade. Act III, Inversion of Genesis (Sumeru), deals with Scaramouche and Irminsul. Act IV, Paralogism (Mondstadt), is Albedo's trial during Windblume.

The chapter works as a place for stories that grew out of earlier main-story or region content but did not belong in the main chapters. Acts I and II revisit Liyue after the Chapter I finale, Act III follows the Sumeru Archon Quest, and Act IV returns to Mondstadt. The Traveler and Paimon are present throughout, and the Traveler's search for their sibling stays in the background rather than driving any act.

Released across several years: Act I in Version 2.4, Act II in 2.7, Act III in 3.3 and Act IV in 5.6. As of Version 7.1 these are the only four acts.

Acts: **Act I, The Crane Returns on the Wind (Version 2.4, Liyue).** Ningguang announces the rebuilding of the Jade Chamber and a contest to gather its materials. The Traveler befriends Shenhe, raised by the adeptus Cloud Retainer, and the sea monster Beisht attacks as the Chamber rises.

**Act II, Perilous Trail (Version 2.7, Liyue).** The Traveler, Yanfei, Yelan, Arataki Itto and Kuki Shinobu fall into a looping space beneath the Chasm where Xiao is searching for his fallen comrade Bosacius.

**Act III, Inversion of Genesis (Version 3.3, Sumeru).** The imprisoned Scaramouche enters Irminsul with the Traveler, learns Dottore's role in his past, and erases himself; he is later restored and given a new name.

**Act IV, Paralogism (Version 5.6, Mondstadt).** During Windblume, Albedo is tried for murder in a staged trial and then uses a Hexenzirkel trial to turn the young dragon Mini Durin into a human.

Quests per act: Act I has Jade Chamber Rising, Seagaze Sunset, Bygones Times Like Dust Passing and Where the Heart Finds Rest. Act II has The Unexpected Guest, Chasmic Maze, Danger All Around, End of the Line and At Tunnel's End, Light. Act III has The Night-Bird Falls at the Curtain's Call, A Dance of Destruction, The Kabukimono's Finale and As Though Morning Dew. Act IV has Crimes One and Two, The Hunger of Many and The Gardener.

Regions and focus shift each time: Act I is about Liyue's human government and the adepti, Act II about the Yaksha past and the Chasm's sealed depths, Act III about the Irminsul and the Fatui's manipulation of a puppet, and Act IV about Mondstadt's Knights, the Church and the Hexenzirkel. Each act has its own entry with the plot and revelations.

Requirements: Each act has its own unlock conditions on the wiki. Act I needs A New Star Approaches (Chapter I Act III). Act II needs A New Star Approaches plus Transient Dreams, Rise Up Golden Soul, Wherefore Did the Spiritstone Descend? and A Teapot to Call Home: Part I, with Adventure Rank 40. Act III needs Akasha Pulses, the Kalpa Flame Rises (Chapter III Act V) and A Strange and Friendless Road, with Adventure Rank 40. Act IV needs Inversion of Genesis and Traveler Observation Report with Adventure Rank 40.

Between Version 5.6 and the Version 6.0 update, the Quick Start function let a player at Adventure Rank 28 who had finished A New Star Approaches unlock Act IV directly. Act I's Adventure Rank requirement is not stated on the chapter page beyond A New Star Approaches.

Placement: The chapter sits beside the main Archon Quest chapters, not in sequence with them. The acts come in the order I to IV but each is timed by what it follows: Act I and Act II after the Liyue finale, Act III after Sumeru, and Act IV after Traveler Observation Report. The wiki notes that a long-time player caught up at Act I's release would play it after the Inazuma Archon Quest.

For Act IV, the project notes place it before Song of the Welkin Moon Act I; the act page itself does not say so.

Characters: Recurring through all four acts are the Traveler and Paimon. Each act brings its own cast: Shenhe, Ningguang, Xiao and Cloud Retainer in Act I; Yanfei, Yelan, Itto, Shinobu and Xiao in Act II; Nahida, Scaramouche and Dottore in Act III; Albedo, Jean, Kaeya, Hertha and the Hexenzirkel in Act IV.

Consequences: Act I shows Liyue handling a calamity as a community, and Shenhe begins to find her place among people. Act II tells Xiao what became of Bosacius. Act III frees Scaramouche from a false history and sets him on a path of his own. Act IV clears Albedo and gives Durin a new life as a human. None of the four acts changes the main Archon Quest plot.

518.content: The Interlude Chapter is a set of four unconnected Archon Quest acts: The Crane Returns on the Wind (Liyue, 2.4), Perilous Trail (Liyue, 2.7), Inversion of Genesis (Sumeru, 3.3) and Paralogism (Mondstadt, 5.6). Each follows up on the quest that unlocks it rather than continuing a single story.

key: The Night-Bird Falls at the Curtain's Call
519.content:
Inversion of Genesis (also: Interlude Chapter Act III, Interlude Act III, The Night-Bird Falls at the Curtain's Call, A Dance of Destruction, The Kabukimono's Finale, As Though Morning Dew): Interlude Chapter Act III. The defeated Scaramouche, held prisoner in Sumeru, joins the Traveler and Nahida in a trial run through Irminsul to look for hidden data on the Traveler's sibling. There he sees that Dottore engineered the tragedy of his past in Tatarasuna, and tries to erase himself from history.

The act has four quests: The Night-Bird Falls at the Curtain's Call, A Dance of Destruction, The Kabukimono's Finale and As Though Morning Dew. It was released in Version 3.3 and is unlocked at Adventure Rank 40 after Akasha Pulses, the Kalpa Flame Rises and the first act of the Acer Palmatum Chapter. It sits between Perilous Trail and Paralogism in the Interlude Chapter.

The act is a character study as much as a mystery: it pairs a scholars' ghost story about a puppet kabukimono with the real record held in Irminsul, and ends with the former enemy being given a future instead of a punishment. It also shows how a revision of Irminsul works and where it stops (it does not touch the Traveler).

Plot: Paimon and the Traveler visit Nahida and find Scaramouche in her sanctuary. Inside Irminsul he learns Dottore's role in his past and erases himself from Irminsul; the world forgets him, and the Traveler must find him and help Nahida restore his memories. He is then given a new name.

Four quests. The Night-Bird Falls at the Curtain's Call: two Akademiya scholars tell a ghost story about Tatarasuna, then Nahida, Scaramouche and the Traveler enter Irminsul, where he sees Dottore at work and erases himself. A Dance of Destruction: in Inazuma the Traveler checks what changed. The Kabukimono's Finale: Nahida confirms the erasure from a backup record, the Traveler finds him, and his memories are restored. As Though Morning Dew: he accepts a future and a name.

**The Night-Bird Falls at the Curtain's Call.** Looking for answers about Descenders, the Traveler and Paimon head for the Sanctuary of Surasthana and overhear the scholars Aqaba and Sawada arguing about a thesis topic, the Tatarasuna incident. Aqaba's teacher chose it because even Inazumans know little: the smith Mikoshi Nagamasa forged a fine blade, then threw it into the fire and killed Katsuragi for reasons unknown, and a kabukimono, an eccentric, was involved. Sawada has checked with a friend in government that the people in the records lived at the time, among them the official Niwa Hisahide, a distant relative of the Kaedehara clan and so a practitioner of the Isshin Art; he suspects a link to the clan's later decline. Aqaba reminds Sawada of the most important point, and Sawada reveals it: the kabukimono was not a human but a puppet. The Traveler recognises Scaramouche, and Paimon bluffs that the story is just a ghost tale. Soon after, Scaramouche walks by, and the Traveler and Paimon follow him into the sanctuary to warn Nahida, only to find him already inside.

Nahida explains she struck a deal with him to investigate Irminsul for her. He expected to be killed once the job was done. She argues he is too weakened to do anything drastic. He had learned of her own deal with Dottore, from which she gained valuable information she says she will disclose over time. After his defeat, she adds, Dottore and the others discarded him, so he needs a backup plan. She proposes that they cooperate; he refuses because the Traveler and Paimon distrust him, but she begins a trial run anyway. Even with most of his powers gone he can still connect to Irminsul, and his Harbinger connections may reveal data about the Traveler's twin that others are hiding from her. She asks the Traveler to supervise him and sends them into Irminsul.

Inside, they quarrel again until Nahida reminds them of the task. She opens a connection to the interior, they locate and attach to the heart of Irminsul, and Nahida speaks privately with the Traveler and Paimon, intending that he find answers for himself. The Traveler tells her about what they saw in Haypasia's vision, which Nahida confirms was the lie that made him who he is, and she admits the scholars got one thing right: Tatarasuna was sabotaged. Scaramouche, who has overheard, pulls up strange data.

The memory it shows: an official discusses the Tatarasuna furnace with Niwa, and deeper in Niwa talks with a man called Escher about using Crystal Marrow to forge Inazuman blades and make the area prosperous. Niwa then challenges Escher about the dangers, since workers are falling sick or dying; he has sent their friend the kabukimono to Narukami Island with a golden feather to seek an audience with the Shogun as a last hope. Niwa confronts Escher about his false identity, and Escher stabs him. Escher is Dottore, who wants to see what happens when a malevolent heart is placed into an unsuspecting puppet. Niwa's dying request is that if Dottore gives the puppet his heart, he tell him that both Nagamasa and Niwa see him as one of them. Dottore reports to Pierro that his task in Inazuma is done and introduces a puppet who could become their newest comrade if he proves useful, or be turned to dust if not. Scaramouche understands and rages; the Traveler and Paimon give him space, appalled at Dottore.

After he calms down he resumes searching and finds nothing about the twin, but does learn that when the sibling arrived in Khaenri'ah they lived for a time with Pierro, who served as a royal mage at the Khaenri'ahn court. He then raises a barrier to hide them from Nahida and asks for the Traveler's hand. He asks whether the past can be changed; the Traveler's hesitation reads to him as a yes, and he goes into the heart of Irminsul to erase himself from time so that Niwa and his friends can have a better fate. They cannot find him. Nahida reconnects, understands what happened, and takes them out while she deals with it herself. Paimon, panicking, talks about food to pass the time; when she wakes she no longer remembers Scaramouche, and the alarmed Traveler heads for Inazuma to see what has changed.

**A Dance of Destruction.** At the Amenoma Smithy, Amenoma Tougo tells them about the Raiden Gokaden: a catastrophe 400 years ago still happened, but Niwa and another smith purged the corruption in the furnace at the cost of their lives. The other smith's orphaned son grew up resentful of the world and passed only hatred to his descendants. About a hundred years ago the then-head of that family began killing Gokaden smiths and was killed by the Kamisato and Kaedehara clans. Relieved, the Traveler learns that Kazuha is fine, since Tougo had tea with him. At the Kamisato Estate, Hirotatsu and Furuta confirm that Ayato and Ayaka still lead the clan and its commission. At the Tatarigami furnace, Xavier tells them someone else worked on the furnace back then, which confirms that Dottore was present and sabotaged it. Xavier does not recall a kabukimono.

**The Kabukimono's Finale.** Back in Sumeru the scholars hand over their papers, which do not mention Scaramouche, and are astonished by what Tougo said. Nahida does not remember him either. She explains that he could have revised Irminsul by erasing himself, but because Irminsul holds no information on the Traveler, revisions do not affect them. She retrieves a record and confirms the Traveler's account: she had made a backup of his memories, which revisions cannot touch. She is unsure how the Harbingers are affected. At the Grand Bazaar the Traveler recalls Rukkhadevata saying that no one can erase themselves from existence, not even her, and realises he must still be alive. Overhearing a merchant scold an employee, they spot him and follow. Nahida catches up and shows him his past, and he eventually accepts it. As the flood of painful memory hits, Shouki no Kami emerges to attack; he composes himself, a newly descended Anemo Vision in hand, shields the Traveler from its blow, and the false god is defeated. The recovery succeeds and they leave the dream.

**As Though Morning Dew.** Nahida promises to keep sifting Irminsul for data on the Traveler's twin's travels. He asks why the Traveler went to Inazuma and, told it was to see what he had changed, decides to treat it as a favour he owes. Nahida urges him to look to the future and not the past; he agrees to help where he can. She says he should have a name, and at his request the Traveler picks one. He then wants revenge on Dottore for his manipulation; Nahida urges moderation, as he still needs time to compose himself. Before leaving he asks the Traveler to tell the Raiden Gokaden's descendants that he was responsible for their downfall, since they deserve to know, and says he will accept whatever punishment they choose. Back at the inn from earlier, the vase Paimon broke is still broken, and a strange voice tells them the fate of Teyvat cannot be changed so easily and that they should believe their own eyes.

Small details worth keeping: per the wiki trivia, the notes in Aqaba's essay are a transcription of the Rather Aged Notes found in Tatarasuna. Nahida treats the Irminsul visit as a supervised trial run of his access, and she chooses to let him discover answers for himself rather than tell him. The vase at the close shows the Traveler and Paimon still remembering a world that otherwise seems unchanged.

Revelations: Dottore, under the name Escher, sabotaged the Tatarasuna furnace, killed Niwa and picked the puppet Scaramouche as a future Fatui comrade. Scaramouche learns this inside Irminsul.

The Traveler's sibling once lived with Pierro for a time in Khaenri'ah, where he served as a royal mage. Irminsul can be revised by erasing a person from it, but the erasure does not alter the Traveler, and Nahida keeps a backup of Scaramouche's memories. Rukkhadevata told the Traveler that no one can erase themselves from existence, not even her.

Revision changes who did what rather than whether disaster happened: the furnace catastrophe still occurs 400 years ago and Niwa and another smith still die purging it, but the account of the kabukimono is gone. The closing voice implies that Teyvat's fate is not easily changed.

Characters: Traveler and Paimon; Nahida; Scaramouche (later the Wanderer).

Dottore (as Escher, in a recorded memory), Pierro (mentioned and reported to), Niwa Hisahide (in the memory), Amenoma Tougo, Hirotatsu, Furuta, Xavier, Aqaba and Sawada. Kazuha and the Kamisato siblings are discussed but do not appear.

Shouki no Kami appears as an attacker during his recovery. Katsuragi and Mikoshi Nagamasa are named in the scholars' story.

Consequences: Scaramouche has erased himself from Irminsul and the world forgets him, but he is restored through Nahida's backup, gains an Anemo Vision, receives a new name from the Traveler, and agrees to help the Traveler. Dottore is his target for revenge.

Nahida continues searching Irminsul for data on the Traveler's twin. The strange voice at the end sets up later events.

Placement: Third act of the Interlude Chapter, released in Version 3.3 between Perilous Trail (Act II) and Paralogism (Act IV). It requires the Sumeru Archon Quest through Chapter III Act V and the first act of the Acer Palmatum Chapter.

520.comment: Inversion of Genesis: Tatarasuna Furnace Memory
520.content:
Within Irminsul the Traveler and Scaramouche see a memory of Tatarasuna. Niwa Hisahide and a man called Escher discuss using Crystal Marrow in the furnace to make the area prosperous, but workers fall ill and die. When Niwa confronts Escher, Escher stabs him; he is actually Dottore, who wants to see a malevolent heart placed into the puppet, and he reports to Pierro that he has found a puppet who could become a comrade.

Niwa's last request is that, if Dottore gives the puppet his heart, he tell him that both Nagamasa and Niwa see him as one of them.

521.comment: Inversion of Genesis: Scaramouche Erases Himself
521.content:
After learning the truth, Scaramouche shields himself from Nahida's monitoring, asks the Traveler whether the past can be changed, reads the hesitation as a yes, and enters the heart of Irminsul to erase himself so Niwa and his friends can have a better fate. The world forgets him, though the Traveler, who is not recorded in Irminsul, remembers.

Nahida's backup of his memories allows his recovery. The Traveler, recalling Rukkhadevata's lesson that one cannot be erased completely, finds him near the Grand Bazaar.

522.content: After the erasure, the Traveler finds Inazuma's history changed in detail. A catastrophe in the furnace 400 years ago still occurred; Niwa and another smith purged it at the cost of their lives. The other smith's orphaned son nursed hatred that his descendants inherited, and around 100 years ago the head of that family began killing Raiden Gokaden smiths until the Kamisato and Kaedehara clans killed him. The Kamisato siblings still lead their clan.

523.comment: Inversion of Genesis: Naming the Wanderer
523.content: At the end of the act Nahida says he should have a name, and he asks the Traveler to choose one. He also asks the Traveler to tell the Raiden Gokaden's descendants that he caused their downfall and says he will accept their punishment.

524.content:
Invitation of Windblume (also: Invitation of Windblume event, Ode to Flower and Cloud, Missive of Cloud and Fog, Realm of Fog and Wind, Dream of Wind and Flowers, Peculiar Wonderland): Invitation of Windblume was a Version 1.4 flagship event (19 March to 5 April 2021) celebrating Mondstadt's Windblume Festival. With no commissions to take during the festival, the Traveler and Paimon become assistants to Venti, who is selling love-poem lessons to townsfolk, then trail a string of small festival errands (a missing admirer, a buried "threat", an alchemical flower, two friends locked in a temple). In the finale the Traveler is chosen as the year's Windblume Star and makes the formal flower offering to Barbatos.

The tone is light and community-minded: the event is a catalogue of how ordinary Mondstadters celebrate love and freedom, and it reuses well-known characters in small domestic roles. It is limited-time content and not universally known in-world.

Plot: Part I (Ode to Flower and Cloud). The Traveler and Paimon find that the Guild and townsfolk have no work for them during the festival. Flora, the florist, explains the Windblume Festival as a day of love and freedom and mentions how people dispute what a Windblume is: Flora favours the dandelion, while Quinn, the fruit seller, insists on the Windwheel Aster. Venti, running a poetry class in the plaza, enlists the two as assistants: the Traveler gives advice to townsfolk such as Marvin (a young man whose father opposes his sweetheart), Ellin (who wants to leave flowers for the Acting Grand Master) and Albert (head of Barbara's fan club) while Venti signals approval or caution. Kaeya enrols as a student on condition of homework and a fee of Applebloom Cider.

Part II (Missive of Cloud and Fog). Collecting homework, the Traveler runs an errand for Kaeya's drinking companion Nimrod, who wants help with a gift for his wife. Kaeya's own homework is a single line in the hilichurl tongue. At the Cathedral Barbara receives a note saying something precious to her has been stolen and buried; Rosaria calms her, the Traveler follows the map to a spot near Dawn Winery, defeats Treasure Hoarders, and digs up a box holding a gift of a Windblume from an admirer.

Part III (Realm of Fog and Wind). Sucrose and Timaeus cannot read an old alchemical recipe for a "Windblume", so the Traveler takes it to Albedo's camp on Dragonspine; his version produces a sweet flower and Sucrose claims a larger "Tetratanic Sweet Flower" is a true ancient recipe. Bennett's homework is missing because he and Razor were trapped on opposite sides of a mechanism at the Thousand Winds Temple, guarded by a Ruin Guard; once freed, Bennett recites his poem, which includes a flower name Razor suggested (Wolfhook). At Angel's Share Kaeya explains the Windblume Star: a rare honour, performed alongside the Acting Grand Master.

Part IV (Dream of Wind and Flowers). The Traveler is named Windblume Star, meets Jean in the plaza and offers a Windblume of their choice to Barbatos at the ceremony. Venti then takes them to Stormterror's Lair, where disorderly wind currents must be calmed. Venti closes by telling the Traveler that, in his view, Windblumes do not exist yet are all around, and that each citizen makes their own choice. Dvalin flies overhead at the end and finds the gift prepared for him.

Across the four parts the festival is shown as chiefly a time for sentiment between ordinary people, with the Knights mostly policing it (Lisa and Jean on patrol) and Kaeya covering Jean's desk work. Venti's poetry class is both a joke on his usual laziness and a genuine teaching moment: each student's letter is tailored to the recipient. The mystery items (Barbara's letter, Bennett and Razor's disappearance) turn out to have harmless explanations.

Part I's students are listed by Venti as Albert, Ellin, Marvin, Timaeus, Kaeya and Bennett. In Part II Lisa and Jean exchange banter about Lisa's habit of zapping brawlers, and Athos is a Knight who notes Kaeya covers the Acting Grand Master's paperwork. In Part III, Bennett says he and Razor were separated by an unexpected mechanism; Razor was not at fault. The Windblume Star's duties, as Kaeya describes them, include attending the Windblume Ceremony with the Acting Grand Master and making an offering on behalf of the people of Mondstadt.

Revelations: Nothing in the event changes the main story. It adds festival lore through dialogue: the Windblume Festival is a festival of love and freedom, the Windblume is a plant nobody can identify, and the Windblume Star is an honour for someone who has made great sacrifices or proved themselves over the festival period. Albedo judges the alchemical recipe, from a forgotten era, to be innovative in its thinking and worth trying. Venti's remark that Windblumes "don't exist, yet they are all around us" affirms the old Mondstadt custom of letting everyone pick their own flower.

The Windblume Ode item text, available from the event shop, retells the old legend of a flower that grew stronger in the winds and became a greeting among those who resisted a tyrant in his tower; it ties the plant to people resisting a tyrant who watched over them from a tower.

Characters: Venti, whose role as paid poetry teacher covers for his godhood and prompts Paimon's teasing, plays opposite Kaeya's mischief. Jean appears as Acting Grand Master and ceremony partner; Lisa, Barbara, Rosaria, Bennett, Razor, Sucrose, Timaeus, Albedo, Diluc and Katheryne have small parts. Townsfolk Flora, Quinn, Marvin, Ellin, Albert, Nimrod and Marjorie provide the festival colour.

Dvalin appears at the end of Part IV, flying over Stormterror's Lair.

Consequences: No lasting plot change. The event's weapon, Windblume Ode (a four-star bow), and its refinement material are obtained in the event shop.

Placement: Released in Version 1.4, event window 19 March to 5 April 2021, with the shop open until 12 April. The prerequisite is the Prologue Archon Quest (Song of the Dragon and Freedom) and Adventure Rank 20; the story takes place in Mondstadt at the time of that year's Windblume Festival.

Gameplay: Labelled game content: Festive Challenges (Bullseye Balloons, Floral Freefall, Ballads of Breeze) earned Festive Tour Tickets, and the Peculiar Wonderland activities earned Peculiar Collab Coupons.

525.comment: Invitation of Windblume: The Windblume Star
525.content: In Dream of Wind and Flowers Kaeya describes the Windblume Star as one of Mondstadt's greatest honours, normally given to someone who has made major sacrifices for the city or proved themselves over the festival. The Star attends the Windblume Ceremony with the Acting Grand Master and makes the people's offering to the Anemo Archon. The Traveler holds the title for that year.

526.comment: Invitation of Windblume: Venti's poetry class
526.content: During the event Venti charges fees (in Mora or alcohol) to teach festival-goers to write love poems. Kaeya enrols with a deal that Venti must grade his homework and be paid in Applebloom Cider; Albert, Ellin, Marvin, Timaeus and Bennett are the other named students. The Traveler and Paimon act as assistants who give advice while Venti signals with hand gestures. The class is a comic device in the event; it is not a recurring institution.

527.comment: Invitation of Windblume: Barbara's buried treasure
527.content: A note appears at the Cathedral claiming something precious to Barbara is buried near Dawn Winery. Barbara fears for her sister Jean; Rosaria stays composed, and when Treasure Hoarders are cleared the box proves to hold a Windblume and a note of admiration. Venti suspects a particular person but does not say.

key: Iridescent Arataki Rockin' for Life Tour de Force of Awesomeness
This Ain't Your Daddy's Iridescence Tour
528.comment: Iridescent Arataki Rockin' for Life Tour de Force of Awesomeness
528.content:
Iridescent Arataki Rockin' for Life Tour de Force of Awesomeness (also: Iridescent Arataki Rockin' for Life, Rock'n'Roll Tour, This Ain't Your Daddy's Iridescence Tour, Puppy Union, Xtreme Carnival Ensemble, Trillion Trinket Trawl, A Meeting of Melodies, Iridescence Tour Tickets): Dvorak's investors had cancelled his own plan for a music festival about the war, so he joins Itto in holding it with the Arataki Gang instead. Itto secures Watatsumi Island as the venue with Gorou's help, after asking Ms. Hina for advice by letter, and Kokomi supports the plan. The Traveler and Paimon fetch the supplies and music lovers needed to ready the stage over several days. At the party Itto and Paimon sing a new song about a reborn Onikabuto. Meanwhile Heizou finds traces of a wartime pet-rescue organisation, and Kokomi and Gorou privately discuss a secret joint operation with the Yashiro Commission. The Raiden Shogun, who has seen paper notes thrown towards Tenshukaku, attends with Miko.

Requirements were Adventure Rank 30 and the Archon Quest "Ritou Escape Plan". Itto's story quest "Taurus Iracundus Chapter: Act I" and the Shogun's "Imperatrix Umbrosa Chapter: Act II" were recommended. The reward character was Gorou, who could be invited, together with the weapon Nightwind Horn.

Plot: First Leg. An invitation letter from Itto in typically excitable style tells the Traveler about a new Fontainian friend who mentioned the Iridescence Tour, and asks them to come to Watatsumi Island for an even bigger party than the Drumalong Festival on Amakane Island. On Watatsumi Island Paimon admires the stage. Itto is talking with Dvorak about a legendary dog (Itto calls Dvorak "Jack-Attack"). Dvorak says that during the recent war between Narukami and Watatsumi, many animals were injured, among them a raven, a bake-danuki and a weasel thief, and that a dog like a ninken would appear out of nowhere in battle to carry the wounded to safety. He heard it in Ritou, where he was while the war was on, and meant to hold a music festival on that theme, but his investors cancelled after what they called an accident at sea; Dvorak thinks they saw poor returns and other risks. Itto offers to run it himself. He claims friends in high places, then lists them (Thoma, Kujou Sara, the three Commissions, Ayato, a fox lady, even the Shogun) in a way Paimon doubts. He says Gorou arranged the venue after Ms. Hina told him to ask the General of Watatsumi Island, and he did not know Gorou's role until then. Itto leaves to meet Gorou about the dog. Dvorak shows the Traveler the Jam Zone, where visitors can try instruments and scores from many regions including a horn from Fontaine, and the Roasted Lavender Melon Zone. At the stage Heizou and Shinobu arrive; Shinobu has been delivering invitations. Heizou brought two baskets of Lavender Melons: one from Sara, who declined to attend, and one from some Doushin and a few of Itto's former cellmates. Heizou promises to ask around Ritou about the dog but believes it is a local legend. Dvorak makes a checklist for the Traveler: invite more music lovers and gather materials to decorate the venue.

Glorious Finale. After the checklist is done, Dvorak says the party can start tomorrow. Itto, Shinobu and the Traveler talk: the dog search has stalled (Gorou and Itto's Gang found nothing), and Itto has thrown paper notes toward Tenshukaku, hoping the Shogun hands over the dog. Itto challenges Paimon to a song contest after Dvorak told him Paimon would perform. Friends gather. Kokomi and Gorou are there as supporters, saying the festival could attract tourists, and ask the Traveler if the mysterious Ms. Hina looks familiar. Thoma and Yoimiya, the latter supplying fireworks, discuss the dog; Thoma argues that if it was real, Watatsumi Island must have helped cover its tracks, since the Shogun's Army did not do rescues. Heizou says he suspects the Yashiro Commission and Sangonomiya were involved and is waiting for records from Yoriki Owada. Dvorak tells Paimon he rewrote the song for Itto by dropping the dog and writing about an Onikabuto. That night Itto and Paimon perform "I Got Reincarnated as an Onikabuto... And Flipped the World Upside Down", whose lyrics mention a raven shot through the heart, a bake-danuki, a weasel thief giving away his Mora, a General Crab reduced to a shell and an unagi, then promise rebirth as a beetle. Friends tease the result as a draw or ask who was most rock 'n' roll. Dvorak thanks everyone, and each guest gives their idea of the rock 'n' roll spirit. Thoma sees courage to grab life by the horns, Yoimiya sees world peace, Shinobu thinks of keeping the Gang safe, and Dvorak calls it hearing your own story in the music. Heizou has left a message. In the last scenes Kokomi tells Gorou the Puppy Union was a joint venture with the Yashiro Commission, a secret worth keeping but not the main aim, and that in an era of cooperation between Watatsumi and Narukami it may even help to be discovered. Miko, on a cliff, notes the rock was strong enough to stir lightning; Ei says she came because of the paper notes demanding she hand over a dog and an invitation delivered through Sara. They talk about Dvorak's songs commenting on the war: Ei says she cannot give him the answer he hopes for but that she will avoid another war, and Miko says everyone at the party would fight at her side if a bigger war came.

Details. Open-world notes show Ayato's gift of audio equipment, Thoma's tea stall from Komore Teahouse, Yoimiya's fireworks and a standing sign of Ms. Hina sent by the "Ramen Buddy" on the sign-in board, who by Itto's description is the fox lady, apparently Miko. Sayu appears in the open world as a Strange Daruma who complains she cannot grow taller. Langqing, Jifang's husband, comes from Liyue's Wanwen Bookhouse and later sells printed lyrics of the song with Dvorak's approval. Tomoki sells a "Rock 'n' Roll Dango Milk". Miko, appearing on day 4, jokes about Fortune Slips and guesses the dog was Taroumaru, the boss of Komore Teahouse, asking if he was saving only animals.

Revelations: Heizou's letters, left at the venue, trace the Puppy Union: a pet-treatment and pet-trade organisation registered with the International Trade Association during the war, whose emblem was a dog in a bamboo hat, which quickly dropped its registration after the war and was funded through at least six layers of transfers. Its hidden backers were the Foreign Trade Association, closely tied to Sangonomiya, and Komore Teahouse, with the Yashiro Commission behind the curtain. Kokomi and Gorou say it was a joint venture of Sangonomiya and the Yashiro Commission that saved some lives, including some on the Shogunate side.

A post-event message from Heizou and an item, the Puppy Union Admission Details, give a codename list of rescued 'pets'. Heizou says he has the evidence but is told by Yoriki Owada to keep it quiet. Kokomi says the secret only matters if someone with an agenda finds it, and could be turned to good use now that the two islands cooperate.

Characters: Itto leads the festival with Shinobu. Dvorak organises the music. Heizou investigates the dog story. Gorou and Kokomi help with the venue. Thoma, Yoimiya, Miko and the Raiden Shogun are guests. Sayu appears as a daruma in the open world, and Itto's gang members Mamoru, Akira and Genta appear in the cutscene.

Open-world and sub-event NPCs include Langqing, Tomoki, Yukio, Aoi, Charles, Flora, Linlang, Marjorie, Jifang and Xingxi.

Consequences: The festival is a success, the dog's story is not resolved, and Dvorak says the feeling matters more than the dog. Itto invites the Traveler to perform next time. The Shogun and Miko discuss avoiding war. Kokomi and Gorou keep their wartime secret.

Placement: Released in Version 4.6 as a Flagship Event and set in Inazuma after the Archon Quest "Ritou Escape Plan". It follows Itto's earlier Almighty Arataki Great and Glorious Drumalong Festival on Amakane Island, and continues the Iridescence Tour that began in Fontaine and reached Liyue during the Lantern Rite. Dvorak was previously in the Version 3.4 event The Exquisite Night Chimes. The war the legend refers to is the conflict between Narukami and Watatsumi Islands that Dvorak calls not long past.

Gameplay: Game mechanics, not in-world fact. Three modes unlock in sequence: Xtreme Carnival Ensemble (a rhythm performance, with the option to compose and share tracks), Trillion Trinket Trawl (collect items from Dvorak's list to build and decorate the venue) and A Meeting of Melodies (fill in missing notes of hummed tunes). Playing them earned Iridescence Tour Tickets (800 to invite Gorou, 1,000 for a Crown of Insight) and decorating the venue gave further tickets.

529.comment: Iridescent Arataki Rockin' for Life Tour de Force of Awesomeness: Dvorak
529.content:
A musician from Fontaine and one of the main organisers of the Iridescence Tour, who travels a lot. He appeared in Liyue's Lantern Rite and now helps Itto stage the rock festival on Watatsumi Island. He heard of the rescuing dog in Ritou while the war was on and wrote a song about it, then rewrites it for Itto as a song about an Onikabuto. He tells Paimon the point of rock is hearing your own story in the music.

The Puppy Union admission list includes an entry 'Unagi No. 9: Dvorak, 40 y/o'. The event never states what this means. The wiki reads it as Dvorak having been rescued during the war.

530.comment: Iridescent Arataki Rockin' for Life Tour de Force of Awesomeness: Iridescence Tour
530.content: An international music tour covering all seven nations, begun in Fontaine, that Itto adapts into his own rock festival with Dvorak. Xinyan's Lantern Rite concert in Liyue was an earlier stop.

531.comment: Iridescent Arataki Rockin' for Life Tour de Force of Awesomeness: Puppy Union
531.content: In the wartime story, a pet-treatment and pet-trade organisation registered in Ritou, with a dog in a bamboo hat as its emblem. Heizou traces its funding to Sangonomiya-linked and Komore Teahouse money. Kokomi and Gorou call it a secret joint venture with the Yashiro Commission that saved lives on both sides. Whether a single rescuing dog existed is left open.

532.comment: Iridescent Arataki Rockin' for Life Tour de Force of Awesomeness: I Got Reincarnated as an Onikabuto
532.content: The song Itto and Paimon sing at the finale. It names a raven, a bake-danuki, a weasel thief, a General Crab and an unagi, then promises rebirth as a beetle. Dvorak says it grew out of the dog story and describes it as soft rock. Heizou, Thoma and Yoimiya each read it differently.

533.comment: Iridescent Arataki Rockin' for Life Tour de Force of Awesomeness: Ms. Hina
533.content: A popular persona in Yae Publishing House's That's Life advice column. In this event Itto says she told him to ask Gorou for help with the venue, a standing sign of her arrives as a gift from a 'Ramen Buddy' (apparently Miko), and Gorou and Kokomi both feel her face is oddly familiar. The Traveler and Paimon keep quiet. According to the Gorou wiki page, Miko invented the pen name.

key: Khvarena of Good and Evil series
Girdle of the Sands Pari quest
534.content:
Khvarena of Good and Evil (also: Khvarena of Good and Evil series, The Hymn of Tir Yazad, Sign of Apaosha quest, Girdle of the Sands Pari quest): A seven-quest Sumeru world quest series from Version 3.6, set in the northern desert. The Traveler and Paimon meet Sorush, a Pari who believes she must sacrifice herself to remove the corrupting Sign of Apaosha, and help her gather five Great Songs of Khvarena. The Order of Skeptics' leader Nasejuna turns out to be using them, and the Pari's history from the cataclysm is revealed.

The series contrasts two ideas of duty: Sorush's wish to sacrifice herself and the Pari elder Zurvan's insistence that Pari fulfil their own duties. It also reveals that the Skeptics' own history was largely myth, that the Pari and Khaenri'ahn fighters including Dainsleif fought the Abyss together 500 years ago, and that Zurvan met Dainsleif.

It requires only the Version 1.0 prologue quest The Outlander Who Caught the Wind, not any Sumeru Archon Quest.

Plot: The Traveler finds a buried drum linked to an unfinished Adventurers' Guild commission about the Sign of Apaosha. Katheryne asks them to contact the isolated Order of Skeptics. They meet the Pari Sorush, who names the Traveler her Yasnapati. She must find two other Pari, Mihir and Rashnu, to earn the Twin-Horned Chaplet from the elder Zurvan, then gather five Great Songs for the Rite of Chinvat. Nasejuna betrays them at the last Song, and the group finally cleanses the tree Harvisptokhm.

The Splendorous Sky That Day: In Gavireh Lajavard the Traveler finds a drum and a note, and Katheryne explains the Akademiya wants the Sign of Apaosha, a strange phenomenon possibly tied to the cataclysm, investigated. After a fight with a Skeptic, Sorush appears and takes the party to Nasejuna, who says the Sign reflects the Abyss and corrupts the land, and that the Great Songs of Khvarena must be gathered for the Rite of Chinvat. Zurvan tells Sorush to prove herself by finding Rashnu and Mihir.

Asipattravana Itihasa: Mihir is found trapped by purple mist in Asipattravana Swamp, weakened by polluted energy. The group helps her complete a cleansing pilgrimage. Sorush and Mihir quarrel, but both agree Pari must do their duties themselves.

Awakening's Real Sound: In the Hills of Barsom Nasejuna tells the history of the Barsom and the Kory Drums, made in honour of Barsom's familiar, which has since stopped answering the Skeptics. The Traveler finds the carvings and drums, plays the ritual, and wakes Rashnu, who reveals she threw the drums away because they disturbed her sleep.

As the Khvarena's Light Shows: Zurvan refuses the chaplet because Sorush is not a Bloomguard, until Sorush prays to the Khvarena and grows one. The first Great Song is at Sunyata Lake; Nasejuna points out the rest. At the last Song, in a Khaenri'ahn factory he calls Dahri, Nasejuna reveals he has only pretended to worship Sorush and wants the Songs to release the Abyss's seal. The Traveler defeats him and an Abyss Herald, and he flees.

The Hymn of Tir Yazad: The group places the Songs at Tunigi Hollow and opens the path to the Harvisptokhm. Sorush sees a vision of the cataclysm, then in the Gaokerena collects Spenta Hearts and performs the Rite of Ab-Zohr, making a Flower of Sanctity bloom. The Sign of Apaosha vanishes and the tree regrows.

The Order of Skeptics was once allied with the Pari; the Kory Drums sealed that bond, but the Skeptics lost their traditions. Nasejuna's friend Aryadeva, a Skeptics elder who knows the traditions best, has left for Sumeru City to pursue light novels and Genius Invokation TCG, and Nasejuna calls him a ridiculous old geezer while relying on him. The wiki says Nasejuna learned of the Songs from documents from a scholar, and later says the history of the Order of Skeptics was all myth, while the accounted history of the Khaenri'ahns was more factual.

Zurvan reveals the Abyss Herald they fought was once a Skeptic who joined the Abyss Order after entering Khaenri'ahn ruins, and that Abyss monsters attacking the Vourukasha Oasis led her to seal it and other ruins with the Great Songs. She then tells the Traveler about 500 years ago: she rescued a masked swordsman with a ring, and they fought the Abyss together. Scholars from the rainforest led by a one-armed sage arrived, found machines and documents in a ruin, and used them to enter the Harvisptokhm, purifying the land and creating more Pari from a sea of flowers. The masked swordsman left with a golden-haired person; the sage disappeared into the ruins; the other scholars became the ancestors of the Skeptics. Zurvan asks the Traveler to give Dainsleif her regards, sure their paths will cross soon.

Mechanical and incidental details from the quests. The Kory Drum ritual uses three actions (attack, plunge attack and standing still) matched to leaf symbols on the musical scores; the three drums lie in the swamp's eastern cave, near Vourukasha Oasis and by the Gate of Zulqarnain, each with a Soul Bell trial. Rifthounds, remnants of past wars, attack at the Gray Gate cave. Mihir accuses Sorush of being swayed by Nasuraja, and Sorush's pride is hurt by Mihir's achievements. After Nasejuna's betrayal Sorush is embarrassed at being tricked for so long, and the Traveler and Paimon reassure her that she is valuable.

Revelations: Nasejuna feigned devotion to Sorush to take the Great Songs and release the Abyss's seal. The Skeptics' own histories are largely myth. The Sign of Apaosha is cleansed by the Rite of Ab-Zohr, not by Sorush's sacrifice.

500 years ago Pari, Khaenri'ahn warriors including a masked swordsman (Dainsleif) and a one-armed sage fought the Abyss together, and the Harvisptokhm was purified then. Zurvan sealed the Vourukasha Oasis and other ruins with the Great Songs after Abyss attacks.

Characters: The Traveler, Paimon, Sorush, Nasejuna, Zurvan, Mihir and Rashnu.

Sorush is a proud Pari who becomes the Traveler's partner and a Bloomguard. Nasejuna is the Skeptics' leader and the series' betrayer. Zurvan is the Pari elder who guards the Songs' secrets. Mihir and Rashnu are Pari: Mihir was stationed in Asipattravana Swamp to suppress corruption, Rashnu was asleep in the Hills of Barsom. Aryadeva, an absent Skeptic elder, is described but not met. Dainsleif and the one-armed sage appear only in vision and testimony.

Consequences: The Sign of Apaosha is gone and the Harvisptokhm has regrown. Nasejuna escapes. Zurvan expects the Traveler to meet Dainsleif soon. Sorush becomes a Bloomguard and gains confidence.

Placement: Released in Version 3.6 and set in the northern desert, in the Girdle of the Sands area. It is independent of the Archon Quest and requires only The Outlander Who Caught the Wind.

535.comment: Khvarena of Good and Evil: Nasejuna's Betrayal
535.content: In Khvarena of Good and Evil, Nasejuna leads the Order of Skeptics and presents himself as a guide to Sorush. At the Khaenri'ahn factory where the last Great Song lies, he reveals he only wanted the Songs to release the Abyss seal. He fights the Traveler with an Abyss Herald and flees.

key: King Deshret and the Three Magi
536.comment: King Deshret and the Three Magi
536.content:
King Deshret and the Three Magi (also: Chapter III Act IV, Sumeru Archon Quest Act IV, The Missing Village Keepers, Cry From the Eleazar Hospital, Secret of the Scorching Desert): The fourth act of Sumeru's Archon Quest. Village Keepers, scholars of the desert who tend its villages, are going missing, and rumours say King Deshret has returned. The Traveler, Paimon, Cyno, Candace, Dehya and Alhaitham of the Akademiya trace the kidnappings to an Akademiya-backed plot, find the buried ruins of King Deshret's civilisation, and learn that the sages mean to create a new god.

The act has three quests: The Missing Village Keepers, Cry From the Eleazar Hospital and Secret of the Scorching Desert. It pairs the Traveler with Cyno and Alhaitham in the desert, shows Dehya's standing among the Eremites, and uncovers the Akademiya's own plan for a god to replace Kusanali.

The act is the point where the sages' project stops being rumour: two of the people responsible are caught and confirm the plan to create a new god. It is also where the story discards the rumour that King Deshret is returning and replaces it with the story of what he did.

Plot: The Traveler, Cyno, Candace, Dehya and Alhaitham investigate the disappearance of Village Keepers around Aaru Village, where rumours say King Deshret is returning. Radical Eremites confess that a masked "envoy" gave them incense to lure the Keepers out, and Alhaitham, who stayed behind, leads the group to an abandoned Eleazar hospital where one Keeper is found. He reveals that the Akademiya's misinformation drives radicals to act and that it monitors Cyno through the Akasha, so the culprits have gone the opposite way, into the desert.

There Dehya bargains with the Eremite leader Rahman, offering her own arm as a pledge for her friends' honesty. After an earthquake the group falls into buried ruins of King Deshret, where Alhaitham reads the last priest Kasala's runes about Deshret's forbidden knowledge, Rukkhadevata's rescue of his people and Deshret's sacrifice. Rahman accepts the truth and returns the Keepers. The sages' agents Morghi and Judar then confirm that the Akademiya, prompted by Il Dottore, plans to create a new god, and the group resolves to oppose the sages.

In detail.

In Aaru Village the Traveler and Cyno question locals about the missing Village Keepers. Cyno overhears two men, Sharkan and Makan, speaking of King Deshret's revival, and frightens out of them that a radical group is behind the disappearances. At the house of a missing Keeper, the Traveler is nearly knocked out by incense; Cyno works out that someone lured Isak's grandfather away with it. Dehya takes the Traveler to Caravan Ribat to find her drinking friends among the Eremites. She tells the Traveler how she hates the Wall of Samiel, which the sages use to keep the desert people out of Sumeru. She has Zaki tell Delavar she has a spice deal for him; the meeting turns out to be an ambush by Delavar and Engur, who underestimate her and are easily defeated by her and the Traveler, then taken to the village. Candace questions them: a masked man claiming to be King Deshret's envoy gave them incense, and they were to meet him at a junction. Uncle Anpu suggests the man is linked to the Akademiya, which had asked for the Keepers back before.

Alhaitham, who stayed in the village, points out that the villager Shani lied. She heard screaming at night near an abandoned Eleazar hospital, Dar al-Shifa. There the group finds Razak, a Keeper, but evidence of a hasty withdrawal. Alhaitham explains the Akademiya's misinformation campaign spurs radicals to act unwittingly, so no blame reaches the sages, as at Port Ormos. When Cyno wonders how the Akademiya learned their plans, Alhaitham tells him Cyno himself is the leak, much to his anger: the sages knew his convictions and used the Akasha to predict his movements, so the culprits head where he would not go, the desert.

In the desert they find buried headsets, then Dehya arguing with the Eremite leader Rahman. Alhaitham offers himself as a hostage and Dehya offers her right arm to prove her friends' honesty; Rahman orders it cut off, then relents, seeing it as cutting his own fingers, and sets a fight for the next day. The next day Rahman has brought only one Keeper, and Dehya beats him quickly. An earthquake swallows them in sand, but Isak's grandfather shields them and they wake in ruins belonging to King Deshret, infused with the Dendro Archon's power. Alhaitham reads runes by the last priest Kasala. They state that Deshret's forbidden knowledge drove his people mad, Rukkhadevata gave them life, Deshret sacrificed himself so the knowledge would not return, and Rukkhadevata became a small child. Rahman accepts that his people have made an enemy of their savior, apologises, and returns the Keepers.

At Rahman's stronghold the culprits, Morghi and Judar, panic at the sight of Alhaitham and Cyno. They confirm that the sages plan to create a new god because Akademiya breakthroughs have dwindled since Rukkhadevata's death. Il Dottore proposed the plan; the dream samsara and the harvest of Divine Canned Knowledge from the mad scholars are part of it. Everyone agrees this is unacceptable and plans to crush the sages and rescue their true god.

Before leaving Aaru, Candace stays behind to handle the radicals while Cyno knocks them out so they cannot learn more; Dehya will not let Cyno join the visit to Caravan Ribat because he might frighten her friends. The headsets in the sand are recent. Alhaitham stakes himself as hostage and Dehya checks whether he will keep his promise and whether Rahman trusts her, which both do, before offering her arm.

Revelations: - The rumour that King Deshret is returning is a misinformation campaign aided by the Akademiya, which nudges radicals into acting while hiding the sages' involvement.
- The sages are working to create a new god after the decline in the Akademiya's breakthroughs; the plot was proposed by Il Dottore.
- The Akasha can predict a user's activity for the day, which let the sages monitor Cyno.
- King Deshret's ruins contain a record, by his last priest Kasala, of the forbidden knowledge that drove his people mad, of Rukkhadevata saving them, and of Deshret's self-sacrifice.
- The dream samsara and "Divine Canned Knowledge" harvested from mad scholars are parts of the sages' project.

The desert people who hate the Akademiya and the Dendro Archon learn that the god they regarded as an enemy had saved their ancestors.

Characters: Traveler and Paimon with Cyno, Candace, Dehya and Alhaitham. Rahman, leader of an Eremite band and Dehya's friend, is the main antagonist and then ally. Isak and his grandfather, a Village Keeper, Shani, Razak, Uncle Anpu, Zaki, Delavar, Engur, Sharkan and Makan appear. Morghi and Judar are the sages' agents. Tighnari is mentioned as Cyno's friend, and Dottore is named but absent.

Locals are visibly afraid of Cyno, which is why Dehya keeps him away from her friends; Alhaitham is the one who can read Deshret's runes.

Consequences: The group returns to the village with the Keepers and the captured culprits and begins planning against the sages. The story proceeds to Act V.

Labelled as later developments: in Act V Nahida and the Traveler use Setaria to learn more, and Dottore, named here only in passing, appears in person; the sages' plan to ascend Scaramouche (the Wanderer) as a new god is stopped, and Kusanali is freed.

Placement: Chapter III, Act IV. Released in Version 3.1. The previous act is Dreams, Emptiness, Deception; the next is Akasha Pulses, the Kalpa Flame Rises. Story order and release order match.

537.comment: King Deshret and the Three Magi: Kasala's runes
537.content: Kasala is the last priest of King Deshret, whose runes in the buried ruins tell how Deshret's forbidden knowledge drove his people mad, how Greater Lord Rukkhadevata used her power to give them life, and how Deshret sacrificed himself while Rukkhadevata reverted to a small child. Alhaitham deciphers the text.

538.comment: King Deshret and the Three Magi: Rahman and Dehya
538.content: Rahman leads an Eremite band and is Dehya's friend. He refuses to trust the Traveler's group and has Village Keepers hostage until Dehya offers her arm. He stops at the last second, saying that harming her would be like cutting off his own fingers. After the ruins, he apologises and promises to return the Keepers and share supplies.

539.comment: King Deshret and the Three Magi: Dar al-Shifa
539.content: The abandoned Eleazar hospital outside Aaru Village, where Shani heard screaming, hides a concealed entrance. The group finds the Keeper Razak, with signs of a hurried withdrawal.

540.comment: King Deshret and the Three Magi: The sages' new god plan
540.content: Morghi and Judar tell the group the sages plan to create a new god. Since Rukkhadevata's death the Akademiya's breakthroughs have been rare and in decline; Dottore proposed the new god, and the dream samsara and harvesting of Divine Canned Knowledge from mad scholars are part of the process.

541.content:
Labyrinth Warriors (also: Mystic Onmyou Chamber event, A Tricky Situation, Pushing On, Away With Obsessions and Falsehood, Path of the Taishou): The domain turns out to be a training ground built long ago by the onmyouji Kamuna Harunosuke so samurai, each paired with a shikigami, could hone their skill against monsters. The Fatui Harbinger Tartaglia joins the party inside, pursuing his own interests. By the end Shiki Taishou has full control of the chamber again, clears himself with the Tenryou Commission, and gives the Traveler a small replica of himself, Shiki Koshou. Xinyan was the event's reward character.

The event also doubles as a quiet character piece for Xinyan, whose rock 'n' roll becomes the way the party tests and then befriends Shiki Taishou, and for Tartaglia, who openly frames himself as a weapon who values the fight over any cause.

Plot: Part 1, A Tricky Situation. Katheryne points the Traveler to a Liyue musician who needs help renewing an expiring temporary travel permit. It is Xinyan, stranded when the Iridescence Tour she came to play in was cancelled. The Tenryou Commission is too stretched to process the permit: Kujou Sara explains that a nameless domain in Araumi is releasing strong monsters, and promises to see to the permit in exchange for help. After guarding the domain entrance, the party finds a moving paper figure, Shiki Taishou, the domain's overseer, who has lost much of his memory. Xinyan wins his trust with a rock song, and they enter together and meet Tartaglia, who joins them.

Part 2, Pushing On. The chamber rearranges itself. Sara contains escaped monsters and later gives Xinyan a long-duration permit and lodging. The Traveler, Paimon and Xinyan then return to Shiki Taishou secretly, rejoin Tartaglia and push deeper, fusing with replicas of Shiki Taishou to recover memory.

Part 3, Away With Obsessions and Falsehood. Shiki Taishou fuses with a powerful replica, recalls the chamber's origin and Harunosuke's last memory, and decides to keep guarding it. Tartaglia reveals his own investigation.

Part 4, Path of the Taishou. The Tenryou Commission accepts the original documentation and finds Shiki Taishou and the chamber innocent. He has restored it to a domain for honing martial skill and invites the party to try it.

Details of Part 1. The cancelled festival was pitched to Xinyan by a roadside recruiter as a famous Fontaine music event. She had asked Beidou to ferry her over early, and Xiangling had packed her a lunch. Xinyan offers to cover the party's other expenses with Mora Beidou gave her, if the permit fee is written off. Seeing the paper figure, she recalls the shikigami legends she collects for lyric ideas. Shiki Taishou describes hearing her song as wandering a misty path alone, wounded and afraid of what lay beyond, yet sensing someone waiting at the end. Paimon pictured people eating Grilled Fish, and Shiki Taishou then recalls grilling fish with faceless people by a fire, an answer Xinyan reads as a sign of understanding human feeling.

Details of Part 2. Tartaglia explains that he reached the domain by following monster tracks, calls it a combat training ground, and says plainly that he does not care about allegiance or right and wrong compared with the thrill of battle. Paimon doubts Shiki Taishou's sense of direction, since some doors in the chamber are false; he says he is guided by an overseer's intuition, and Xinyan points out there is no alternative to trusting him. In a memory fragment Shiki Taishou recalls a samurai ballad and the lead samurai calling Harunosuke 'Master Kamuna'. The Traveler openly asks whether Shiki Taishou would stand with them if Harunosuke proved a danger to Inazuma. He answers that his bond with the party is trust and with Harunosuke is responsibility, and does not promise.

Details of Part 3. Shiki Taishou says that Harunosuke founded an early form of onmyoudou after crossing the sea to study the arts of the adepti of Liyue, then created him as the template for all later replicas. When Shiki Taishou calls himself a weapon discarded by its owner, Tartaglia answers that he too is a weapon, chasing improvement rather than victory, and says sorrow and hesitation dull a blade; Xinyan counters that he need not abandon anything, only return to what he finds most important, as she has with rock 'n' roll, and Shiki Taishou resolves to continue. In the flashback, wounded samurai tell Harunosuke the outside situation is stabilising and ask whether the pursuit of 'ultimate attainment' should go on. Harunosuke says the targets no longer exist and those needing protection are safe, tells Shiki Taishou that giving him intelligence so he could know human emotion was the right decision, recites a line about rosy cheeks at morning and bleached bones by dusk, and sets out. After memory is restored, Tartaglia explains he came because he was looking for the Wanderer (Scaramouche in this event): the Fatui lost contact with him after he obtained a Gnosis. He says he will let that run a while longer and asks the Traveler what they will choose when they find it. Xinyan plays a second song and promises to visit, and Shiki Koshou is given to the Traveler.

Revelations: The Mystic Onmyou Chamber is a purpose-built training domain, not a source of evil. According to Shiki Taishou, Kamuna Harunosuke built it, and made him as its first shikigami, to defend Inazuma from the Abyss during the time of the cataclysm. Shikigami replicas were paired with samurai; they recorded the monsters defeated, and that data was fed back into the domain to create mirror monsters as training targets. Many samurai were wounded and many shikigami lost, and the Shogun's Army had already regained control of the situation, so Harunosuke disbanded the samurai and left, leaving Shiki Taishou to sleep inside.

Shiki Taishou says Harunosuke's drive began when the Abyss took someone important to him, and that he studied Liyue's adepti arts before founding early onmyoudou. Shiki Taishou also recalls that Harunosuke played chess with a Tenryou Commission Supreme Commander surnamed Kujou, whose given name he cannot remember.

Characters: The Traveler and Paimon are the protagonists. Xinyan, the Liyue rock musician, is the emotional centre of the cast. Kujou Sara represents the Tenryou Commission and appears in the first two parts. Tartaglia, a Fatui Harbinger, fights inside the chamber and pursues his own goals. Shiki Taishou, a polite, self-doubting paper shikigami, is the event's main new character. Katheryne gives the first commission, and Watanabe and Yata Kouki are named Tenryou Commission soldiers who briefly appear.

Shiki Taishou apologises easily and speaks formally; his eyes are Inazuman glyphs that change shape with his mood. Harunosuke appears only in a memory flashback, not in the present day.

Consequences: Xinyan receives a long-lasting travel permit and lodging in Inazuma from Kujou Sara and plans to keep visiting Shiki Taishou. The Tenryou Commission accepts Shiki Taishou's account, so the domain is left as a martial training ground that may go dormant if its charm magic runs out. The Traveler keeps Shiki Koshou, a replica that stays in contact with Shiki Taishou but cannot use shikifuda or charm magic outside the chamber. Tartaglia's inquiry about the Wanderer is left open.

The wiki notes that the chamber's final room was later reused as a setting in another quest (Silent Seeker of Knowledge).

Placement: Released in Version 2.2 and requires Adventure Rank 30 and completion of Archon Quest Chapter II Act III, Omnipresence Over Mortals. Inazuma is described as having stabilised by then. Tartaglia refers to the Wanderer as having gone missing with a Gnosis.

No source read gives the event a precise in-world date beyond following Chapter II.

Gameplay: Game mechanics, not in-world fact. The event was a solo roguelike-style domain. A player split their characters into a Combat party and a Support party, carried chosen shikifuda, and drew Charms in rooms called emplacements. Five trial stages unlocked every three days: The Ominous Demesne, The Brutal Divergence, The Vengeful Wood, The Echoes of Extinction and The Rending Absolution. Aged Tokens, earned in the first four stages, were spent in an event shop and, with enough accumulated, to invite Xinyan (Pyro) as a reward character.

542.content:
A domain in Araumi, Inazuma, first described as nameless by the Tenryou Commission. Built during the cataclysm by the onmyouji Kamuna Harunosuke as an ever-changing training ground where samurai fight monsters made of charm magic, which turn to paper charms when defeated. It slept after Harunosuke left, until an unknown power woke its monsters. Its rooms rearrange themselves, and some doors are false.

Shiki Taishou oversees it and says that if its charm magic runs dry he will let it lie dormant so power can build again. The wiki notes the Japanese name uses the term for the old Yin-Yang Bureau of Japan.

543.content:
Event-exclusive shikigami created by Kamuna Harunosuke to oversee the Mystic Onmyou Chamber. A small paper figure modelled on a samurai in dark armour. He wakes with amnesia, wants to prevent harm, fears he was created for evil, and recovers memories by fusing with replicas of himself. At the end he recalls a purpose of protection and chooses to keep guarding the chamber.

He calls himself a weapon abandoned by his master and struggles with purpose until Xinyan and Tartaglia each offer their own answer. Harunosuke says in the flashback that he gave him intelligence so he would understand human emotion.

544.content: A replica of Shiki Taishou made as a gift for the Traveler. Shiki Taishou can communicate with it wherever it goes, and the wiki says he can hear and see what it does. Outside the Mystic Onmyou Chamber it cannot use shikifuda or charm magic, but it can still protect its holder.

545.content: In this event Xinyan says she signed up for an Iridescence Tour stop in Inazuma, pitched to her by a roadside recruiter as a famous Fontaine festival, though nobody she knew in Liyue had heard of it. The tour was cancelled when the organisers ran into trouble at sea, leaving her temporary permit about to expire with no sponsor permit, which is the event's starting problem.

546.comment: Labyrinth Warriors: Tartaglia in the Chamber
546.content: Tartaglia followed monster tracks into the domain and enjoys the endless fighting. He tells the party he does not care about allegiance and calls himself a weapon seeking improvement rather than victory. At the end he reveals he is looking for the Wanderer, who has gone missing with a Gnosis, and leaves the matter for the Traveler to find out.

547.content:
Lagenaria Chapter (Baizhu) (also: Lagenaria Chapter, Baizhu's Story Quest, The Heart of Healing): The Lagenaria Chapter is Baizhu's Story Quest (Version 3.6), set in Liyue. In its one act, The Heart of Healing, a boy named Ayu seeks help for his sickly father, and Baizhu discovers that the man is being kept alive and poisoned by the remains of a dead god. The act also shows how Baizhu and Changsheng share life force, and what Baizhu hopes to achieve through immortality.

The act has three quests: The Search for a Physician, The Quest for a Cure and The Formula for a Miracle. It requires Adventure Rank 40, A New Star Approaches, Hu Tao's Yet the Butterfly Flutters Away and the Alatus Chapter's Butterfly's Dream. The Chinese title refers to the hanging gourd, a traditional emblem of physicians.

The act shows Baizhu's habit of paying for others' cures with his own body and the pharmacy's shared secret: Changsheng's power comes with a contract that has killed her earlier hosts young. It also brings in Hu Tao, whose family history with Baizhu's master gives context to her wariness of him.

Hu Tao's account of the rift, Xiao's warning about immortality, and Baizhu's own plan to become Changsheng's last host are linked pieces of the same theme: medicine, mortality and the cost of cheating death.

Plot: **The Search for a Physician.** At Bubu Pharmacy, Qiqi and Herbalist Gui are talking to a boy, Ayu, whose father is sickly and whose mother has not returned from gathering herbs. His father had left the house, the Millelith could not spare many people, and he came to the pharmacy. Baizhu arrives with Qiqi, says he knows Ayu's mother Jiangli and father as old acquaintances, and agrees to help. The Millelith suggest Jialiang may be near Luhua Pool. The group finds a man nearly walking off a cliff and someone stopping him; it is Hu Tao, who greets the Traveler warmly and Baizhu less so. Jialiang has memory loss. Baizhu says he has god remains inside him which, if not dealt with, would cause a major outbreak, but he has a duty to his patients, especially Jialiang, per his master's dying wish. He asks for a day. Hu Tao, invited to observe, tells the Traveler that the threat of dead gods has not been seen since the Archon War, though she was taught to recognise it, and that Baizhu's master was her grandfather's younger brother. When he went to Chenyu Vale they met a pharmacist, argued, and he left the family business. Her grandfather said the pharmacist had an ominous aura and that their medicine broke natural rules, and that Baizhu sought immortality. The next day Jialiang is well, but the Traveler finds Baizhu in poor health; he admits he did not cure Jialiang but transferred some of his life force to him through Changsheng's secret arts.

**The Quest for a Cure.** At Ayu's home in Qingce Village, Baizhu and Changsheng find a hidden compartment of poison, a minor offshoot used to manipulate and control, apparently Jiangli's doing. Eliminating the source will end Jialiang's trouble. They call Xiao, who is surprised to see Baizhu, and who confirms a dead god named Chi lies under the village. He declines to meddle in mortal affairs but offers aid if needed, and warns Baizhu that immortality may not be what he imagines. Gui reports that Jialiang has worsened, earlier than the three days Changsheng predicted. Baizhu stabilises him and then suffers his own symptoms. In private he tells the Traveler that Jiangli had used Chi's remains to treat her husband's underlying heart condition, which also harmed him. Jialiang, accepting death, asks to be brought to reunite with his wife. Baizhu agrees once he consents, and asks Qiqi to prepare medicine.

**The Formula for a Miracle.** In Qingce Village, Jialiang's symptoms flare as they approach a tunnel. The tunnel suggests Treasure Hoarders, though their tools are left behind, and a censer of monster-repelling incense stands inside. At the end they find a Geovishap and an unconscious Jiangli. Baizhu says the remains are killing her as they are him. Destroying them would kill Jialiang, who accepts it, having lived longer than he should and treasured his time with his family. Baizhu destroys the remains; Jiangli wakes, and Jialiang appears to die. He instead wakes at Bubu Pharmacy, with strange marks on his body. Baizhu reveals that Qiqi prepared an Elixir of Immortality to hold him on this side of the afterlife so that he could say goodbye when it expired. Hu Tao, exasperated at another "Qiqi", says she would have taken him to the parlor had she known. Jiangli privately warns Baizhu to use Changsheng's powers wisely, as she does not want him to die either. Changsheng tells the Traveler and Paimon that she and her host share a contract and all her previous hosts died young. Baizhu intends to break the cycle by learning the secret of immortality, so that he can be her final host while ensuring that no one else follows that fate. The family and Qiqi call them to share a meal.

Details worth keeping. Baizhu's reasoning for the day's grace was that he must try to save a patient even if the remains put the area at risk, and his secret technique is performed alone to avoid distraction. Changsheng at first says Jialiang should be fine for three days. Her contract with Baizhu means his illness and his handling of others' health are linked, and the transfer of life force from Baizhu to Jialiang uses her powers.

Revelations: Major for Baizhu's arc: he and Changsheng share a contract that has killed her earlier hosts young, and he seeks immortality to be her last host.
