A dead god named Chi lies beneath Qingce Village, and its remains are the source of Jialiang's illness and Jiangli's collapse. Hu Tao's grandfather's younger brother was Baizhu's master. All of this was revealed in Version 3.6.

Jialiang is briefly kept alive by an Elixir of Immortality as a stopgap, not a cure.

Characters: Baizhu, the Traveler and Paimon, with Changsheng, Qiqi, Hu Tao, Xiao, Herbalist Gui, Ayu, Jialiang and Jiangli.

Baizhu is calm, self-sacrificing and evasive about his own health; Changsheng is dry and protective; Qiqi prepares medicine; Hu Tao is wary but cooperative; Xiao appears briefly and warns Baizhu. Ayu is a worried child and is not described as anything beyond that.

Consequences: Jialiang's family is reunited and spared from the god remains, and Baizhu's secret about Changsheng is shared with the Traveler. Hu Tao and Baizhu remain uneasy but cooperative.

Placement: Release order: 3.6. Story order: after Chapter I of the Archon Quests, Hu Tao's Papilio Charontis Chapter and the Alatus Chapter's Butterfly's Dream.

548.comment: Lagenaria Chapter (Baizhu): The Heart of Healing
548.content: Act I of Baizhu's Story Quest. Baizhu and the Traveler find Ayu's father Jialiang poisoned by the remains of a dead god beneath Qingce Village, destroy them, and use an Elixir of Immortality to give the family time for a goodbye.

549.comment: Lagenaria Chapter (Baizhu): Baizhu and Hu Tao's Family History
549.content: In The Heart of Healing, Hu Tao says Baizhu's master was her grandfather's younger brother, who left the family business after meeting a pharmacist in Chenyu Vale. Her grandfather's version is that the pharmacist had an ominous aura and that their medicine broke natural rules, and that Baizhu sought immortality. It is a one-sided family account.

550.content:
Lantern Rite (2021) (also: Lantern Rite 2021, Version 1.3 Lantern Rite event, The Origin of the Lanterns, Currents Deep Beneath the Lanterns, Light Upon the Sea, Mingxiao Convergence): The event story is told in three parts, "The Origin of the Lanterns", "Currents Deep Beneath the Lanterns" and "Light Upon the Sea", which together make up the All That Glitters section. In the first the Traveler learns what Lantern Rite is and how Xiao Lanterns are made; in the second a stranger near the lantern materials turns out to be an unrelated, bumbling thief, after help from Xiao and Kaeya's informant; in the third the Traveler and the Wangshu Inn staff bring a miniature festival to Xiao, who still refuses to enter the crowded city. It is a lighthearted event with a gentle character study of Xiao at its core.

Because the event is limited-time, the 2021 story is canon but not universal knowledge: most people in Teyvat know the festival, not the Traveler's part in it. The giant lantern is dedicated to Skybracer, an adeptus who in Madame Ping's account gave his life holding up Mt. Tianheng. Xiao hears about this from the Traveler and does not go to see it, though the closing scene suggests he hears the wishes of the lanterns all the same.

Lantern Rite later returned as a flagship event (Version 2.4 with Fleeting Colors in Flight, and again in Version 6.3 with A Lanternlit Ode to the Silver Moon), each time with a different part of Liyue's celebration at its centre.

Plot: Part I, The Origin of the Lanterns: Verr Goldet of Wangshu Inn explains that Lantern Rite is held on the first full moon of the first month to honour the heroes of the past, and that the lanterns guide them home. She quietly asks the Traveler to try to bring Xiao along. In Liyue Harbor the Traveler meets festival organiser Wang'ya, eats Grilled Tiger Fish at Yi'nian's stall, hears Madame Ping's story of Skybracer, and learns from Jingming how to make a Xiao Lantern.

Part II, Currents Deep Beneath the Lanterns: the Traveler gathers rare Plaustrite (Azurite and Vermillionite), notices a suspicious figure near the lantern materials, reports it to the Ministry of Civil Affairs, clears hilichurls for the Millelith, and with Xiao's help and a tip from Kaeya's informant finds the "plot" to be a clumsy plan to steal the giant floating Plaustrite.

Part III, Light Upon the Sea: Xiao still declines to visit the city, so Verr Goldet, Huai'an and the Traveler build a small stall below Wangshu Inn, serve Almond Tofu and Grilled Tiger Fish and hold a miniature Lantern Rite for him. He eats with them, walks the Traveler partway to the city, and stops at its edge.

Part I in more detail. At the harbor a merchant, Bolai, makes a joke about buying Paimon and mentions that the lantern's lifting stone is the largest Plaustrite in twenty years. A girl called Changchang says she gave her ragdoll to the lantern because the doll wished to see the sky, and Jingming confirms that every contribution, even a symbolic one, is welcomed because the lantern is a community project. Jiangzhou explains that the Xiao Market exists to raise money for the lantern, with Mora and Plaustrite as the main donations, so no stall is meant to profit. Wang'ya sends the Traveler to Yi'nian with a Ministry document of tips from last year's festival, which Yi'nian says he will burn. The Traveler returns with the Xiao Lantern Wang'ya promised as a gift, and Paimon proposes making one for Xiao to cheer him up.

Part II in more detail. Wang'ya asks for the rarer types of Plaustrite; they are carved with wishes and donated. Back at the construction site beside the dock the Traveler and Paimon spot a man crouching near piles of paper, oil and wood, which Paimon fears are fuel for arson. Jiayi at the Ministry says a specialist, Xinghuo, is away at Guili Plains; the Traveler goes there, clears a hilichurl blockade, and Xinghuo, who has been chasing a thief, promises extra vigilance. Xiao then appears and leaves a symbol that he says the suspect dropped, warns the Traveler that the threat comes from the mortal world and so is theirs to handle, and says that if he intervened the streets might run red. Kaeya recognises the symbol as that of the Treasure Hoarders and arranges a meeting at Windrise with an informant, Nimrod. Nimrod doubts the Treasure Hoarders would risk so large a plan, and points out a branch that received an anonymous letter. At that camp Xiao appears from nowhere, which frightens the hoarders Bei'er and Crafty into handing over the letter. The two disguise themselves and go to the meeting place where the stranger turns out to be an apprentice thief hoping to impress the Treasure Hoarders. The Millelith take him away.

Part III in more detail. Verr Goldet and her colleague Huai'an are sure it would be easier to bring the festival to Xiao than Xiao to the festival. They pick a quiet spot below the inn, Huai'an builds a rough stall and decorates it with a Xiao Lantern, and Smiley Yanxiao cooks the food from the inn's pantry. When the Traveler brings Xiao down he is puzzled but eats with them. Afterwards he accompanies the party along the road toward the harbor at Paimon's request, stopping at the outskirts.

Minor beats. Paimon's order of Grilled Tiger Fish is explained as a way of honouring Pervases, who loved it. When the Traveler writes a wish on the Plaustrite it is for their sibling, a moment Paimon treats with tenderness and a promise to help look for them. Kaeya gives the password phrase "wine begets wisdom" for the informant, who then accepts a slightly wrong version because it is close enough. Xiao refuses to promise to attend but says he will answer a call for help at any time, and describes hearing "all cries for help, all prayers for peace, and all the wishes carried by the lanterns".

Revelations: Madame Ping's account of Skybracer: the giant lantern is shaped after him, a flamboyant adeptus whose antlers were made of the essence of Rex Lapis's power and were Liyue's hardest material. In the fateful battle between gods, mountains began to collapse onto villagers below, so Skybracer had a friend cut off his antlers and used them to prop up the mountain. He fought on until his blood ran out. Mt. Tianheng still stands because of this, and his blood became the Bishui River. She frames this as a story and says the point of Lantern Rite is that people come together instead of staying alone.

Xiao's inner conflict is the real revelation of the event. He says he dislikes the rabble because they are carefree and joyful, "nothing like me", and that after so long killing and carrying the burden of suffering he would only feel worse among them. Verr Goldet's description of the festival supplies the other half: the lanterns are believed to act as beacons guiding bygone heroes back to their homeland.

Nothing in the event identifies who first ties the symbol to the Treasure Hoarders beyond Kaeya's remark, and the event's "crisis" is resolved as a misunderstanding; the only real danger is the thief's incompetence. The Plaustrite is described as the main component of any Mingxiao Lantern, a floating stone, which is also the reason local gemstone merchants prize Azurite and Vermillionite so highly.

Characters: Main: the Traveler and Paimon, Xiao, Kaeya (by his advice and informant), Madame Ping (Skybracer's story), Verr Goldet and Huai'an of Wangshu Inn, Smiley Yanxiao (the inn's chef). Festival staff: Wang'ya (organiser), Jingming (lantern maker), Jiangzhou (Ministry planner), Yi'nian (food stall), Bolai (merchant), the child Changchang, Jiayi and Xinghuo (Ministry and Millelith). Treasure Hoarders: Bei'er and Crafty, plus a lone apprentice thief. Kaeya's informant: Nimrod.

Playable characters who take part in the Stand by Me mini-game, as invitable party members, are Beidou, Chongyun, Ningguang, Xiangling, Xingqiu and Xinyan; none of them appears in the story quests themselves.

Consequences: The thief is handed to the Millelith and the festival goes ahead. The quest line ends before the lantern's release; the event's Mingxiao Convergence cinematic shows the giant lantern and the Xiao Lanterns rising on Lantern Rite night. Xiao has eaten at a small festival of his own and walks with the Traveler to the city's edge, but never enters it; the closing thread is that he will hear any call for help. The Xiao Market closes after the event with its rewards (a Crown of Insight and the "Celebration: Lantern-Light" namecard).

Placement: Released in Version 1.3 as a Flagship Event and set during the first Lantern Rite after the Traveler arrives in Liyue. It required Adventure Rank 23, the Archon Quest Chapter I Act I (Of the Land Amidst Monoliths) and the first act of Xiao's Story Quest (Alatus Chapter), whose Adventure Rank requirement was lowered for the event. It precedes the 2.4 Lantern Rite (Fleeting Colors in Flight) and the 6.3 Lantern Rite (A Lanternlit Ode to the Silver Moon), both in the same series.

A similar earlier version of the event was run in the second closed beta; some leftover beta text survives in the tutorial (see uncertainties).

Gameplay: Game mechanics, not in-world fact. Event period 10 to 28 February 2021 (Xiao Market until 7 March), with the three story parts unlocking on 10, 14 and 18 February. Five sections: All That Glitters (the three quests above), Lantern Rite Tales (requests for Festive Fever and Primogems), Theater Mechanicus (a domain and mini-game earning Peace Talismans), the Xiao Market (spending Peace Talismans on materials, a Crown of Insight and the namecard Celebration: Lantern-Light) and Stand by Me (1,000 Peace Talismans invite one of six 4-star Liyue characters). Festive Fever progresses in three stages: We've Only Just Begun, Guests Flock From Afar, Glow of a Thousand Lanterns. During the event Xiao Lanterns could be crafted and released.

551.content:
Liyue's giant lantern, released into the sky on Lantern Rite night as a joint effort of the city's people and the Ministry of Civil Affairs. Its lift comes from a huge floating Plaustrite, the largest in twenty years in 2021, chained at the Xiao Market. The 2021 design honours the adeptus Skybracer, with a stag-like figure whose antlers were a source of pride.

Money and Plaustrite are donated by citizens, who often carve wishes into the stone. Even a symbolic gift such as a ragdoll is accepted, since contributions are believed to bring good luck.

552.content: Madame Ping describes Skybracer as a show-off, proud of his antlers, which were made from Rex Lapis's essence and were the hardest thing in Liyue. During a battle of the gods he gave them up, using the blood-soaked antlers as a wedge to hold up a collapsing Mt. Tianheng, and fought on until his life ran out. The Bishui River is said to be his blood. She tells the tale as a story whose truth the listener may decide.

553.comment: Lantern Rite (2021): Xiao's refusal and the small festival
553.content:
Xiao will not attend Lantern Rite, saying he dislikes crowds, and especially not at this time of year. The innkeepers and the Traveler instead set up a small stall with Xiao Lanterns, Almond Tofu and Grilled Tiger Fish below Wangshu Inn. He eats with them without enthusiasm, saying he does not understand human motives, and walks to the city's edge before turning back. He tells the Traveler he hears all calls for help in Liyue.

His stated reason, in the third part, is that carefree, joyful people are nothing like him and being among them would only remind him of the suffering he carries from slaying demons.

554.content: A suspicious man lingering near the lantern supplies is feared to be an arsonist. Trails lead via Xinghuo of the Millelith, a symbol left behind that Kaeya identifies as the Treasure Hoarders', and an anonymous letter in the hands of Bei'er and Crafty, to a meeting where the sender turns out to be an apprentice thief who only wanted to steal the giant Plaustrite by cutting its tethers and floating it out to sea. The Millelith arrest him.

555.content:
Leo Minor Chapter (Jean) (also: Leo Minor Chapter, Leo Minor, Master's Day Off, Jean's Story Quest): The Leo Minor Chapter is Jean's Story Quest, available since Version 1.0 and set in Mondstadt. Its single act, Master's Day Off, shows the Acting Grand Master worn down by the city's commissions. The Traveler and the other Knights quietly take the work off her hands and throw her a surprise party.

The act has four quests: When the West Wind Arises, then Margaret's Longing, Charles' Troubles and Sara's Worries (doable in any order), then Master's Day Off. It requires Adventure Rank 34 and the Trifolium Chapter's Act I, True Treasure. Its tone is warm and low-stakes, centred on how much the city relies on Jean.

Its central question is whether Jean measures up to Vennessa, the first Grand Master. The chapter answers through Jean herself: she is more a Dandelion Knight than a Lionfang Knight, working to protect the future Vennessa hoped for.

The chapter is a character study rather than a plot driver. Its only combat is a lone Abyss Mage that opportunistically tries to kill the exhausted Jean, and the Knights' party is the real climax. It also shows Diluc, usually distant from the Knights, lending his tavern for her sake.

Plot: **When the West Wind Arises.** In Mondstadt the Traveler and Paimon are asked by Sara of Good Hunter to send Jean a request to clear hilichurls from the road to Springvale, and by Charles of Angel's Share to have her send his quarterly tax records so Elzer can do the accounts. Margaret asks for help finding her cat, Prince. When the Traveler reports all this, Jean faints and Barbara tends to her. Kaeya passes the tasks on to the Traveler instead, saying he would rest easier if the Honorary Knight did them. Amber and Lisa take the original hilichurl and tax jobs.

**The three requests.** The Traveler protects Ernest's delayed delivery convoy from hilichurls, helps Sara with a flood of orders, and finds Prince; Venti explains that the cat took his astral strings, which cats are drawn to when rolled into a ball.

**Master's Day Off.** Barbara says Jean has gone to Windrise, where she always goes when troubled. There Jean admits she wants to be like Vennessa and fears her efforts fall short. An Abyss Mage appears, taunts her and flees; the Traveler helps Jean chase and defeat it. Swan then sends them to Angel's Share, where the Knights hold a surprise party. Jean learns the commissions were all done: Amber cleared the road, Lisa did the tax records and the Traveler recovered Prince and the strings. Kaeya reveals that the Traveler helped organise the party.

Diluc offered his tavern as the venue despite his reluctance to deal with the Knights, but says he is grateful for the work Jean does for the people. Afterwards Lisa tells the Traveler that Jean has gone upstairs to think alone. Jean thanks the Traveler for lifting her spirits, concludes she is a Dandelion Knight rather than a Lionfang Knight, and hopes the Traveler will keep helping the Knights.

Revelations: The city takes Jean's tireless work for granted; Charles admits so, then feels guilty when Paimon points out the pressure on her. Jean's habit of going to the great tree at Windrise when confused is established. Her closing view of herself is as a Dandelion Knight, preserving the future Vennessa hoped for.

The party shows that the other Knights, Amber, Lisa, Kaeya and Barbara among them, have been watching out for her.

Characters: Jean is the focus. The Traveler and Paimon do most of the legwork. Amber, Lisa, Kaeya, Barbara, Venti, Diluc, Charles, Margaret and Sara also appear.

Kaeya delegates cheerfully and is revealed as an organiser of the party alongside the Traveler. Lisa quietly handles the tax returns. Barbara looks after the fainted Jean and knows where she goes to think. Venti appears with Margaret and is the one whose strings Prince took.

Consequences: Nothing in the main story changes. The chapter deepens Jean's characterisation and shows the Traveler as a trusted helper of the Knights.

Placement: Release order: Version 1.0, alongside the other launch Story Quests. It follows the Trifolium Chapter's True Treasure.

556.comment: Leo Minor Chapter (Jean): Master's Day Off
556.content: Master's Day Off is Act I of Jean's Story Quest (Leo Minor Chapter, 1.0). Overwhelmed by Mondstadt's everyday requests, Jean is given a surprise party at Angel's Share by the Knights. She leaves with a clearer sense of her role as a Dandelion Knight carrying on Vennessa's hopes.

557.content:
Lepus Chapter (Amber) (also: Lepus Chapter, Amber's Story Quest, Wind, Courage, and Wings): The Lepus Chapter is Amber's Story Quest (Version 1.0), set in Mondstadt. In its one act, Wind, Courage, and Wings, Amber supervises the Traveler's exam for a gliding licence. The exam is interrupted by a hunt for a criminal named Raptor, whom Amber catches by leaping into a canyon on a wind current.

The act has five quests: Glide With the Wind, License to Glide, Mondstadt Glider, They Call Him Raptor and Outrider Style. It requires Adventure Rank 8 and the Prologue's Act I, The Outlander Who Caught the Wind. "Lepus" is Latin for hare or rabbit; the Chinese and Japanese chapter names mean "little rabbit".

The chapter is a light, comic introduction to Amber as the Knights' Outrider, showing her persistence and her love of gliding. It ends by setting up a friendly rivalry with the Traveler through the Wind Gliding Championship.

The act's main beats are a licence exam (two tests, then a modified final exam of bombing hilichurls), a case of mistaken identity involving the Knight Otto, and a chase from Springvale to Raptor's stronghold. The wiki notes the licence and championship hooks but the act does not otherwise change Mondstadt's situation.

Plot: **Glide With the Wind.** Amber asks how the Traveler's gliding is going and admits she forgot to mention that a licence is required in Mondstadt, though the Traveler has glided without one. She will oversee the exam, since she gave them the glider, and hands them a guidebook. The book she gave at first was her favourite storybook, by mistake.

**License to Glide, Mondstadt Glider, They Call Him Raptor.** After studying the real manual, the Traveler passes the first test and meets Amber at Favonius Cathedral. During the next test the Knight Otto orders the Traveler down and demands the licence, taking them for an accomplice of Raptor, a thief who stole a priceless artifact the Knights had set as bait and then escaped. Amber explains herself and offers to help. Raptor was last seen in Springvale, where one of the sisters had put an Anemo mark on the artifact. They find clues and then hilichurls attacking the merchant Farrah, who says a man dropped from the sky into a hilichurl camp with a heavy object and fled.

**Outrider Style.** Ambushed by hilichurls and Raptor's men, they find his stronghold. Amber changes the final exam so the Traveler must drop bombs on hilichurls along the way. At a canyon dead end Raptor tries to goad them into leaving; Amber jumps, a wind current carries her across, and she catches him, having reasoned that he could only escape if they left. At the Cathedral she gives the Traveler their licence and signs them up for the next Wind Gliding Championship, since nobody else can challenge her.

Revelations: No world-level revelations. The Knights set bait traps for thieves, hilichurl camps threaten roads near Springvale, and gliding in Mondstadt requires an official licence earned by exam.

Characters: Amber, the Traveler and Paimon. Otto, Raptor and Farrah appear.

Amber is both exam supervisor and partner, enthusiastic and stubborn. Otto is the over-zealous Knight who first threatens arrest; Raptor is the criminal who falls from the sky.

Consequences: The Traveler earns an official Mondstadt gliding licence and an entry in the Wind Gliding Championship. The chapter is also a prerequisite for Razor's Lupus Minor Chapter.

Placement: Release order: 1.0. Story order: early, after the first Prologue act and before Razor's chapter.

558.comment: Lepus Chapter (Amber): Wind, Courage, and Wings
558.content: Act I of Amber's Story Quest. Amber gives the Traveler the real gliding manual (her own favourite storybook was handed over by mistake), supervises their licence exam and catches the thief Raptor by jumping a canyon on the wind.

559.content:
Lepus Miles Chapter (also: Lepus Miles, Lohen's Story Quest, A Knight's Legacy, A Knight's Merit, A Knight's Pursuit, A Knight's Resolve): The Lepus Miles Chapter is Lohen's Story Quest, released in Version 6.6. It has one act, A Knight's Legacy, in three quests, set in Mondstadt. Lohen is due to receive the title Benevolent Knight from the ailing Adorno and command the 5th Company, but he is secretly helping Theodore use Ursa the Drake's flesh to prolong Adorno's life and to chase power himself. Adorno dies, and Lohen is punished.

The three quests are A Knight's Merit, A Knight's Pursuit and A Knight's Resolve. It follows the Archon Quest An Elegy for Faded Moonlight (Song of the Welkin Moon, Act IV) and requires Adventure Rank 40. Its tone mixes dark comedy (Lohen's "friendship fee" and his grisly "patrol methods") with a tragedy about obsession and mortality.

Its themes are what makes a knight (merit, conviction, or raw power), the lure of "extraordinary" power versus ordinary mortal life, and the shadow of Eroch's old betrayal over a new generation. Lohen's current struggle was sharpened by his defeat at Rerir's hands during the Nod-Krai expedition.

The chapter links the Nod-Krai arc to Mondstadt: Lohen's obsession is rooted in a childhood rescue from Eroch and Dottore's experiments, sharpened by being beaten by Rerir, and finally refused when Ursa's voice offers him the same kind of power. The wiki event description frames the question as whether a mortal who glimpses fate-rewriting power should submit or defy.

Plot: Kaeya tells the Traveler and Paimon that returning expedition knights are to be honoured, and that Lohen is expected to be named the Benevolent Knight and given command of the 5th Company. Lohen, who does not want either, pays them a "friendship fee" to pose as his friends while he visits Adorno at Dornman Port, and tells Adorno carefully disguised, grisly tales of his "training" and "patrols". Adorno takes him on a day of small kindnesses and a monster patrol, where Diluc says someone has cleaned up the monsters before them. In a test of the Simulation Training Bubble, Type 02, Lohen fights Adorno's memory of Rerir, loses control and is hurt; Adorno reveals that Lohen was a child saved from Eroch's experiments, and Sucrose notes unfamiliar power in him. Lohen and Theodore then pursue Ursa-tainted monsters, Adorno is badly hurt shielding a child, and Lohen swears to confess the next day. Instead Lohen, Theodore and Adorno vanish to a hidden lab, where Theodore has been using Ursa's flesh to make a serum to prolong Adorno's life and Lohen has been helping for his own pursuit of power. Adorno comforts both. Lohen draws the escaped monsters while Varka, Diluc and the Traveler destroy Ursa's remains, and he rejects Ursa's offer of power. Adorno dies; Jean confines Lohen, rescinds his commendation and buries the Benevolent Knight title.

**A Knight's Merit.** Kaeya tells the Traveler and Paimon that returning expedition knights, including Winfried, Leifhelm and Lohen, will get titles; Lohen is expected to be called the Benevolent Knight and to take command of the 5th Company, which would break Diluc's record as youngest Captain. Using Varka's name, Lohen summons them to the headquarters and pays a "friendship fee" for them to act as his friends when he visits Adorno, the retiring Captain, at Dornman Port. He tells Adorno gruesome, lightly disguised stories of his "group training" and "patrols" (drugged wine, traps, night raids and coercing captives), then admits that Rerir beat him in Nod-Krai. Adorno takes him through an ordinary day of candy for children, dogs and a lost cat, then a monster patrol. Diluc says someone cleaned up the monsters first. Adorno explains Ursa, Eroch and the Doctor's old plot. At the 10th Company's Simulation Training Bubble, Type 02, built from Alice's magic, Lohen asks to face the Rächer of Solnari from Adorno's memory. The test spirals, Adorno is strained, and Lohen is hurt. Adorno reveals that Lohen was one of the children saved from Eroch's experiments. Sucrose finds unfamiliar power in Lohen. Theodore, treating him, warns that they could be exposed.

**A Knight's Pursuit.** Lohen has left a note for Adorno promising to wipe out monsters. Diluc says the monsters fight each other and match no natural pattern; Varka explains Ursa's flesh and Eroch's old serum, and the Traveler tells them about the power sensed in Lohen. Lohen pursues a Geovishap Hatchling, then presses Theodore to use him as a test subject; it fails. A hatchling attacks Adorno while he is saving a child's cat, and he is badly hurt. Lohen swears on his honour to confess the next day. Theodore, at Adorno's bedside, hints at what he is about to do. Soon Adorno, Lohen and Theodore are gone.

**A Knight's Resolve.** Following Lohen's Cryo trail, Varka, Diluc, the Traveler and Paimon enter a hidden lab that looks like the work of one of Dottore's Segments, and a memory projection shows a captive being carried through it in a box. Lohen finds Theodore tending Adorno; flashbacks show how Lohen had offered himself as a subject and kept the Knights from noticing. Theodore completes a refined, high-concentration serum, which Lohen says would kill Adorno in his present state; Theodore ends up too weak to stand after using the highest concentration. Adorno, who has overheard everything, comforts both as he did when he first rescued them. Lohen takes the serum, crushes a vial to draw the restless monsters, and holds them while Varka, Diluc and the Traveler defeat Ursa. A voice tempts him with power; he stabs his own hand and rejects it. Adorno is later buried in Mondstadt. Lohen is confined; Jean rescinds his commendation, denies him promotion and buries the Benevolent Knight title with Adorno.

Further detail: at the ceremony Kaeya says Lohen's title was delayed by "personal reasons". Varka says Adorno's final wish is to see Lohen inherit the title, and the two had a pact: Adorno recommended Lohen for the expedition, and Lohen would reflect on what a virtuous knight is. and Lohen hurts himself trying to hold back his final blow. Sucrose says the bubble's parameters were normal but the energy released was neither elemental nor "Void Realm energy".

In the second quest Varka tells Diluc that he, Crepus and Eroch were once three young men who imagined their futures together: Crepus the rich young master who inherited the winery, Varka the rule-breaker who became Grand Master, and Eroch the one who got neither wealth nor power. In the third quest the three documents (notes, origins, scribbled lines) hint at an organisation's earlier plan to make Ursa's flesh a controllable asset.

In the lab, Theodore first restarted Eroch's experiments from hazy childhood memory, and Lohen discovered him later and joined in, wanting power. The serum helped Adorno get out of bed, but Lohen said it would kill Adorno in his present state. Theodore asks Lohen to destroy Ursa's flesh before he collapses. Lohen asks Varka for formal permission to attack and Varka orders him not to die.

At the grave Lohen chews bubblegum he made during confinement; he says Adorno liked giving sweets to children. His penalties were solitary confinement, loss of the commendation and no promotion; the 5th Company captaincy stays vacant for now. He says he will keep winning and still pursues power, and ends by asking the others not to grow old before he can shoulder everything alone.

Theodore, like Lohen, was a child rescued by Adorno; he has long wanted the Benevolent Knight title, which Adorno had meant to pass to Lohen. Lohen refuses Ursa's offer because he wants to remain master of what he wields, and states that forgetting why he pursues power would be true defeat. The epitaph on Adorno's grave pairs a couplet about not weeping at the grave with the line "Here rests the Benevolent Knight".

Revelations: - Lohen and Theodore were both children rescued by Adorno from Eroch and the Doctor's experiments.
- Ursa the Drake's flesh remained in a hidden lab, and Theodore restarted its serum experiments to prolong Adorno's life; Lohen joined for his own pursuit of power.
- Monsters carrying Ursa's mark appear near Dornman Port; they attack each other.
- Adorno, already ailing, dies after the lab episode and is buried with the Benevolent Knight title.
- Varka reports that Ursa was once an angel (hearsay), sealed by the first Grand Master Vennessa.

- The Simulation Training Bubble, Type 02, recreates memories as training; Sucrose and the 10th Company are testing it.
- The experiment site was concealed so well that the Knights never found it.
- Lohen was beaten by Rerir during the expedition and is haunted by the word "mortal".

- Lab documents suggest a hidden plan to seed fear in Mondstadt; authorship is unstated.

Characters: - **Lohen**: Vice Captain of the 5th Company, titled "Sharpest Arrow", the chapter's protagonist.
- **Adorno**: retiring Captain of the 5th Company, the Benevolent Knight.
- **Theodore**: trainee medic of the 8th Company, treating Adorno.
- **The Traveler and Paimon**: pretend friends, witnesses and fighters.
- **Varka, Diluc, Kaeya, Sucrose, Jean**: the Grand Master, a former Cavalry Captain, the current Cavalry Captain, a researcher working on the bubble, and the Acting Grand Master who sets the punishments.

Ursa the Drake, Eroch, Rerir and Dottore appear mostly as memories or reports. Winfried, Leifhelm, Ekbert, Lietzberg, Wernher and Porthos are minor knights; Max, Moricztill and Hannelore are Mondstadt locals.

Consequences: Ursa's flesh at the site is destroyed. Adorno has died by the closing scene. Lohen is placed in solitary confinement, his commendation is rescinded, he is denied promotion, and the Benevolent Knight title is buried with Adorno.

The 5th Company captaincy remains vacant for now. Theodore's penalty is left for Jean and the others.

Placement: Released in Version 6.6 ("Luna VII"). It requires An Elegy for Faded Moonlight, so it happens after the Nod-Krai expedition returns to Mondstadt. Story order and release order match. The chapter has no further acts as of 7.1.

A same-named event ran from 2026-06-09 to 2026-06-30, giving Primogems and materials for finishing the quest and offering a Quick Start to players at Adventure Rank 28 who had completed Chapter I, Act III (A New Star Approaches). Only these rewards were limited; the quest remains playable.

560.content:
The honorary title held by Adorno, earned when he rescued kidnapped children from Eroch's experiments. He wanted Lohen to inherit it with the 5th Company captaincy, and had once planned to leave the title to Theodore. After Adorno's death, Jean has the title buried with him.

Adorno himself says he never deserved it, as he failed to find Eroch's site or ease Lohen's trauma.

561.comment: Lepus Miles Chapter: Ursa's Flesh and Serum
561.content:
A serum drawn from the preserved flesh of Ursa the Drake. Eroch and a Doctor Segment first made it, Eroch's followers injected it and went mad, and Theodore later restarted production to prolong Adorno's life. Monsters carrying it fight one another and are far stronger than normal. Lohen takes a vial into the final fight as bait.

The flesh needs repeated stimulation to give high-concentration serum; overflow of its power changes nearby plants and monsters.

562.comment: Lepus Miles Chapter: Simulation Training Bubble: Type 02
562.content:
A memory-recreating magic bubble based on Alice's work and used to welcome the expeditionary force, now being tested by the 10th Company as a safe combat training aid. It recreates enemies from knights' memories.

In the quest it misbehaves when Lohen fights Adorno's recollection of Rerir, though Sucrose finds the bubble's parameters normal.

563.comment: Lepus Miles Chapter: Lohen's Friendship Fee
563.content: Mora that Lohen pays the Traveler and Paimon to pose as his friends when he visits Adorno. Paimon takes the payment readily. Lohen says he receives a special-missions allowance and has little use for it.

564.content:
Lightkeepers' Oath (also: Lightkeepers' Oath world quest, Oath Lantern quest): A Version 6.0 world quest on Paha Isle and Lempo Isle in Nod-Krai. If the active character is a Lightkeeper (Flins or Illuga), the Traveler can read the eight "Oath Lanterns" that lie abandoned around the islands. Each lantern has a line of the Lightkeepers' oath carved around its base, and each brings up the ghost of its former bearer. At the end, Flins explains what the oath is and what a masterless lantern means.

The quest has no fight and almost no dialogue until its last scene. Its worth is thematic: it shows how the Lightkeepers treat their oath and their lanterns, and how seriously Flins takes the memory of those who fell. Without a Lightkeeper active, a lantern is only "a dim lantern", described as the signature equipment of a Lightkeeper.

The quest is a good way to bring the full oath into a scene. Its lines are the same ones the Ratniki recite at the oath-taking in the Nightingale's Song story, so the quest gives an early, quieter look at words that later become a rallying cry.

Plot: With Flins or Illuga in the party, the Traveler touches an Oath Lantern and sees a line of the oath carved around its base. A ghost of a Lightkeeper appears. After the fourth lantern the rest are marked on the map. When all eight are read, Paimon suggests asking someone who knows the Lightkeepers, and they go to the Final Night Cemetery to find Flins.

Each lantern's inscription is one line of the oath. Together they run roughly: a vision of waves on the shore and a night sky devoured by silence; a declaration that whoever keeps the flame burning need not descend into that darkness; the Lightkeepers as those who shine the eternal light of hope into the endless snowy plains; a vow to use their bones and blood as fuel and make life greater than death; and lines about the winds awakening and leaves whirling, pale cheeks and burning eyes, freeing the heart from dreams of the living, and parting the snow-curtain of the sky to blast winter winds across the wasteland. The first three lanterns bring up female Lightkeeper ghosts and the later five male ghosts.

The third lantern has a hidden compartment with a yellowed note, written by a self-described humble Ratnik. The writer expects soon to be unable to speak of the lamp and asks whoever finds it to return it to the Lightkeepers.

At the cemetery, Flins greets the Traveler warmly "amidst the graves". The Traveler describes the lantern and its inscription. Flins identifies it as the oath everyone who joins the Lightkeepers swears. Each Lightkeeper normally carries a lantern of their own and gives up its care only when there is no other choice, so a masterless lantern marks a tragedy and fills him with sorrow. They knew this fate from the moment they swore. The one thing the living can still do is remember their oaths, and that was the dead's dearest wish: to bear and defend lanterns alight with eternal hope.

Gameplay notes: after Flins or Illuga touches a lantern, a papakha hat, a small knife and scattered blue petals appear around it. Some lanterns sit beside Tideseal Stones. The order in which the lanterns are visited does not matter; the quest begins once four have been inspected, and the remaining four are then shown on the map. Interacting with a lantern without a Lightkeeper active gives only the generic line. Rewards: Adventure EXP, 20,000 Mora and a small amount of Adventurer's Experience.

Step list: collect the eight Lightkeepers' Oaths (eight locations, any order), then talk to Flins at the Final Night Cemetery. In the Piramida story the Ratniki recite the first three lines of the oath and Illuga recites the vow about bones, blood and fuel to open the operation, which is how the quest text connects to Wind-Stirred Ripples.

Revelations: The quest reveals the content of the Lightkeepers' oath and that every Lightkeeper carries a lantern that stays with them for life. Flins explains the oath in his own words and shows that the order remembers its dead through their oaths.

It also shows that the islands hold the lanterns of Lightkeepers who died away from home. The note in the third lantern comes from a Ratnik who expected not to return the lamp himself, which fits Flins' remark that lanterns are abandoned only when there is no choice.

Characters: The Traveler and Paimon, with Flins as the one who explains. Illuga can be the active character instead of Flins. The lantern ghosts are unnamed.

Flins speaks in his usual courteous, slightly formal manner, but is solemn rather than playful. He treats the lanterns as memorials even though he names none of the dead.

Consequences: Completing the quest gives the rewards and changes nothing else in the world. It is characterisation and world texture rather than a plot step.

Placement: Introduced in Version 6.0 (Luna I), at the start of the Nod-Krai series. The wiki lists no prerequisite quest, only access to Nod-Krai and a Lightkeeper character as the active character, which means Flins or Illuga. The oath is quoted again in the Nightingale's Song world quests (6.3), so the quest can be read before or after them without conflict.

565.content: The Lightkeepers' oath is a set of lines every Lightkeeper swears on joining. In the Lightkeepers' Oath quest eight abandoned lanterns each carry a line, and Flins identifies "The winds awaken, the leaves whirl round" as part of the oath. Lightkeepers normally carry their own lantern and give up its care only when forced to. A masterless lantern marks a misfortune, and remembering the oaths of those who fell is all that can still be done for them.

key: Lost in a Foreign Land: Seeking
Fatui hideout in the Chasm quest
566.content:
Lost in a Foreign Land (also: Lost in a Foreign Land: Seeking, Katarina quest, Fatui hideout in the Chasm quest): A short Version 2.6 series in the Chasm's Underground Mines. The Traveler meets Katarina Snezhevna, a Fatui mage cut off from her supply line, and looks for her missing teammate Nikolay over three days.

The series is started by defeating a Fatui Electro Cicin Mage near the Glowing Narrows waypoint. It has two quests, Lost in a Foreign Land (day one) and Lost in a Foreign Land: Seeking (days two and three), and later steps wait for the daily reset.

It is a small portrait of Fatui loyalty and isolation: Katarina has been underground so long that she has never heard of the Traveler and does not know what has happened between the Fatui and Liyue.

Plot: Katarina invites the Traveler to her hideout and offers Fire-Water. She says everything the Fatui does prepares for a final battle against a common enemy and an inescapable long night. She later asks the Traveler to find Nikolay; the Traveler finds his insignia and diary scraps. On the last day Katarina has vanished, leaving a letter next to a Shadowy Husk.

On day one Katarina gives only her name, fights Floating Fungi alongside the Traveler and says to visit her hideout. She is out of black tea, sugar and milk, so she serves Fire-Water. She has not heard of the Traveler because her information comes through the Fatui supply line, which Paimon notes must have been cut off long ago. Awkwardly, she tells them to leave, then asks them to return. On day two she asks them to find Nikolay, who lured enemies away from the team. The Traveler finds his insignia and diary fragments describing a secret chamber with two exits and a swordsman in black, and a tunnel sealed by fallen rocks. Katarina says Nikolay would not flee; she hopes he fought to the end. If he is alive she would punish him as a deserter, and if dead she will be proud of him, in the spirit of the Fatui saying "If not us, then who."

She mentions that she was a good friend of Lyudochka, who looked after her while they grew up in the House of the Hearth, and guesses Lyudochka is doing well. On day three Katarina is gone from the hideout. The Traveler goes to the first diary spot and finds a letter from Nikolay that Katarina had carried because it smelled of Fire-Water, with a Shadowy Husk standing nearby.

Gameplay notes: the series gates on the daily reset (day one, then days two and three). Katarina's Fire-Water is offered twice, and the Fire-Water smell is why she kept Nikolay's letter, which the Traveler finds on the last day.

Revelations: No world-shaking revelation. It shows that some Fatui members are cut off from news and loyal to ideals of sacrifice, and hints at the Fatui's wider goal of facing a common enemy.

Characters: The Traveler, Paimon, Katarina Snezhevna, and by report Nikolay and Lyudochka.

Katarina is stern, proud and reticent about her mission. Nikolay is her missing teammate. Lyudochka, a friend from the House of the Hearth, appears only in her recollection.

Consequences: No lasting change to the world. Katarina's hideout is left empty and her fate is implied but not shown.

Placement: Released in Version 2.6 alongside the Chasm: Underground Mines content, in the same area as The Chasm Delvers. It is a small side story.

567.content:
Lost in the Snow (also: Dragonspine Joel quest, Joel's father quest): Joel is told to wait at the camp by a Knight of Favonius. The quest is a short search that ends without a reunion; the notes show that the father intended to keep his promise to bring Joel to see the snow. It leads on to the quest Snowy Silhouette: Hope and, later, links to the Version 2.3 event Shadows Amidst Snowstorms, where the father is found.

It requires finishing the Prologue's first act, The Outlander Who Caught the Wind, and starts at the Dragonspine Adventurer Camp. Completing it allows the hidden exploration objective "The Foxes' Affection".

Plot: Joel, a child waiting at the camp, explains that his father promised to take him to see the snow. When the agreed time passed, Joel came to Dragonspine alone, only to be told by a Knight that his father had gone up toward the summit. The Knight would not let him follow. Joel asks the Traveler to look for him, and recalls that his father meant to follow the Snow-Covered Path first, then visit the outskirts of the Entombed City, then try for the summit.

The first note, at a campsite on the Snow-Covered Path, is cheerful. The father says the weather and supplies are good, and mentions finding a book from the series "The Boar Princess" that Joel must have slipped into his bag; he wonders if it is bringing him luck. The second note, found under snow that has to be melted with Pyro, is from a western-slope campsite, where he decides to try for the summit and says he will turn back if anything goes wrong. The third, in a cave near the summit, is scribbled: a snowstorm came suddenly, he lost half of his supplies, and rocks collapsed to seal the entrance. He plans to climb down a cliff and jump the rest into deep snow, adds that supplies will last only a few days, repeats his promise to Joel, and asks anyone who finds the note to put food in a bowl for the foxes that kept him company.

The group feed the foxes, which stay hidden, and report to Joel. Whatever the Traveler says, Joel refuses to believe the worst. He insists his father is a great adventurer who must have reached safety, is resting, or has made camp, and he decides to keep waiting at the camp.

Details. The Traveler may tell Joel what was found or say nothing; either way he says he will wait. If told, he thinks his father may be resting or at a new camp at the summit. If told nothing, he thinks the Knight was mistaken. Either way he thanks the Traveler, gives a reward and ends with a worried line, wondering where his father is.

Gameplay detail: the second note requires melting snow with Pyro and the cave requires breaking a rock wall. Paimon notes that the third campsite has only the note and a feeding bowl. After completing the quest, the player can begin the hidden exploration objective "The Foxes' Affection".

Revelations: The father's three notes are the quest's entire evidence. The cheerful tone of the first gives way to danger in the third, and nothing in them says whether his climb down succeeded.

Epilogue: Later content (the Version 2.3 event Shadows Amidst Snowstorms) shows Joel's father, Joserf, found alive but with memory loss that leaves him recalling only Joel and Joel's mother. This quest itself never mentions that.

Characters: Joel, a child at the Dragonspine Adventurer Camp, who trusts that his father is safe; the Traveler and Paimon; and an unnamed Knight of Favonius, who told Joel to stay. The father appears only through his notes.

Consequences: Joel stays at the camp to wait. The Traveler receives rewards of 300 Adventure EXP, 40 Primogems, 2 Hero's Wit, 4 Mystic Enhancement Ore and 30,000 Mora, plus 100 reputation with Mondstadt (game rewards, not in-world).

The next quest in the series is Snowy Silhouette: Hope. The father's fate is not settled until the later event.

Placement: Added in Version 1.2, when Dragonspine became accessible. It is an optional Dragonspine world quest and not part of the Archon Quests. Later, the Version 2.3 event Shadows Amidst Snowstorms lists it as a prerequisite and resolves Joel's story.

568.comment: Lost in the Snow: Joel's father's notes
568.content: Joel's father left a trail of campsite notes on Dragonspine: cheerful ones at the Snow-Covered Path and the western slope, then a scribbled one in a cave near the summit, written after a snowstorm and a rockfall trapped him. He planned to climb down the cliff and jump into deep snow, and asked whoever read the note to feed the foxes that had kept him company.

key: Lost Traveler in the Ashen Realm
Lost Traveler in the Ashen Realm World Quest series
569.comment: Lost Traveler in the Ashen Realm
569.content:
Lost Traveler in the Ashen Realm (also: Lost Traveler in the Ashen Realm World Quest series, Bona's adventure, Jade of Return quests): Lost Traveler in the Ashen Realm is a four-act Natlan world quest series added in version 5.2. The Traveler, Paimon and the Little One enter the forbidden ruined city of Ochkanatlan to find the "Jade of Return", a treasure sought by countless adventurers. They are joined by an adventurer named Bona and a small green guide, Cocouik, and are hunted by a violent dragon.

The route leads from the city streets through the Core of Chu'ulel and an Altar of Primal Flame up to the sky-ship called the Tonatiuh. The legend of the Jade of Return turns out to be bait, the dragon is a corrupted former ruler, and what the party recovers is a second Golden Entreaty, one of the tokens needed to lift the Little One's curse.

The series is written as a story-within-a-story: the hero everyone is following (Bona) was herself following an earlier expedition, and the Traveler ends up completing an adventure that others began and failed.

Plot: **Act I, City Buried By Ash (Vaulting the Wall of Morning Mist).** Following a violent dragon, the party reaches Ochkanatlan, a ruin the Saurian Relics Association treats as forbidden. An explosion in the Vucub Caquix Tower drops them into the lower city. They find the notes of a nameless adventurer who came for the Jade of Return, meet a mysterious adventurer, and fight their way through Ashflow Street with the help of a small green guide whose rings of light can suppress Abyssal Blight. The dragon is shot down and driven off.

**Act II, A Dream of Gazing Upon the Distant Sky.** With Bona and Cocouik, the party looks for the Altar of Primal Flame so they can reach the Tonatiuh. Cocouik refuses to enter a ruin because of the Abyssal corruption inside. Below, the Traveler cleanses the Core of Chu'ulel and finds a second chunk of Pyrophosphorite wrapped in more of the nameless adventurer's notes. Offering both chunks on the Altar sends the group flying up through the clouds, and they land at the Tonatiuh.

**Act III, The Tonatiuh Quivers.** On the Tonatiuh the Traveler finds a stronger, flame-infused Pyrophosphorite that the Little One can handle, reunites with Bona and uses Firestones to break the rock holding the Jade of Return. The treasure is a Golden Entreaty. Bona then behaves oddly, the dragon snatches the Entreaty, and the group follows it. Cocouik helps the Traveler bring the dragon down, and a voice inside identifies itself as Och-Kan, former ruler of Ochkanatlan, asking for help against the corruption in his soul.

**Epilogue, The Chosen One's Promise.** The Traveler returns to the Tonatiuh and finds the Little One alive. Bona is nowhere to be seen. Paimon and the Traveler decide to keep the Golden Entreaty and carry it to the volcano.

Details worth keeping in a scene: the nameless adventurer's notes say the Abyss is no longer as frightening as when the writer was born, mention an "Aunt Liriwu", and describe the Core of Chu'ulel as the old heart of the city, where the tribe says a Sacred Lord once turned himself into the heart of the dragon city. The guide's repeated, wordless chirps are interpreted by Bona (she admits she is guessing), and the party eventually learns that following strict logic does not work in this place. Before the flight to the Altar, Bona says her Flower-Feather Clan background gives her plenty of flying experience, and she races ahead of the others out of excitement.

On the Tonatiuh the dialogue differs by player progress: if Between Pledge and Forgettance is complete, Paimon and the Traveler recognise the Jade of Return as a Golden Entreaty identical to the one found in the Sage's ruins; if not, Paimon says it looks like a food platter.

In the Moment of Awakening, the Traveler enters Och-Kan's memories. Kukulkan appears to him there and presses him to abandon human-centred ideals, accusing him of betraying dragonkind and Xbalanque's oath, and proposing to wake Huitzilopochtli by combining the Golden Entreaties. Och-Kan refuses. The memories also show Taika, with Copan, Titu and Legba, climbing the Tonatiuh and falling to a trap, and years later Taika's daughter Bona doing the same with Cocouik, though she managed to dismantle the trap.

Gameplay note, labelled as such: Act I lets the player control Cocouik for a Super Awesomesauce Laser sequence; the Little One and Bona fight alongside the player as an ally. These do not change the lore.

Revelations: - The "evil dragon" that attacks the party in Ochkanatlan is Och-Kan, the former ruler of the city, whose soul was corrupted by poison and who was turned into a dragon.
- The Jade of Return is a Golden Entreaty. Och-Kan says it can cleanse Natlan's Abyssal filth but at a cost, and that he and the Little One both bear the Flamelord's Blessing. Two Golden Entreaties must be brought to the sacred mountain to remove that blessing.
- The legend of the Jade of Return was fabricated by Kukulkan, as bait for a trap.

- Kukulkan wants to use the combined Golden Entreaties to activate Huitzilopochtli and bring about a new civilisation beyond both dragons and humans, even at great destruction. Och-Kan refuses and says he believes in humanity. Kukulkan warns he will return to claim Och-Kan's soul as part of an ongoing experiment.
- Och-Kan's memories are fragmentary, so he cannot fully explain the Entreaty's purpose.

Characters: The Traveler, Paimon, the Little One (a young Tepetlisaurus companion), Bona (a self-described adventurer of the Flower-Feather Clan), Cocouik (a small green guide), Och-Kan (the corrupted dragon), and Kukulkan (in memory scenes). Taika, Copan, Titu and Legba appear only in Och-Kan's memories.

Consequences: The party now holds a second Golden Entreaty and plans to take it to the volcano to help lift the Little One's curse. The unresolved question of Bona's nature remains, as does the matter of Kukulkan's plan.

A pair of goggles left near the damaged mural on the Tonatiuh can be found after the quest and update the nameless adventurer's notes. The Cornerstone of Stars and Flames is received at the end.

Placement: Released in version 5.2. The series page lists Between Pledge and Forgettance as the previous series and Path to the Flaming Peaks as the next. The dialogue changes depending on whether Between Pledge and Forgettance has been finished.

570.comment: Lost Traveler in the Ashen Realm: Bona
570.content: Bona describes herself as an adventurer of the Flower-Feather Clan who is chasing the Jade of Return. She is cheerful, impulsive and eager to prove herself, quick to claim she can read Cocouik's chirps and then admit she is guessing. According to Och-Kan's memories she is the daughter of Taika, who led an earlier expedition up the Tonatiuh. She disappears before the series ends and her nature is not explained.

571.comment: Lost Traveler in the Ashen Realm: Cocouik
571.content: Cocouik ("Coco" to Paimon) is a small green dragonspirit-like guide. Bona's notes say she woke it from the heart of the machine using Pyrophosphorite and named it after turquoise. It leads the party to the Altar of Primal Flame, and its rings of light can suppress Abyssal Blight. It is frightened of corrupted ruins. Och-Kan later retains memories of his time as Cocouik.

keysecondary: Dragon of the City of Flowing Ash
572.comment: Lost Traveler in the Ashen Realm: Och-Kan, the dragon of Ochkanatlan
572.content: Och-Kan appears first as the "evil dragon", the Dragon of the City of Flowing Ash, then speaks as the former ruler of Ochkanatlan. He says his soul was poisoned and turned into a dragon. Tribal legend says he oppressed his people to build the Tonatiuh, which attracted the Abyss; Bona notes that storytellers tell different tales about him. He refuses Kukulkan's plan.

573.comment: Lost Traveler in the Ashen Realm: Jade of Return
573.content: The "Jade of Return" is a legendary treasure that countless adventurers have sought in Ochkanatlan. In the series it is found sealed in a rock on the Tonatiuh and is a Golden Entreaty. Och-Kan's memories show the legend was invented by Kukulkan to lure people into a trap.

574.comment: Lost Traveler in the Ashen Realm: Altar of Primal Flame and the Tonatiuh route
574.content: The Altar of Primal Flame is a mechanism that sends travelers up to the Tonatiuh when offered Pyrophosphorite; the party offers two chunks to be safe. The Tonatiuh, a sky-borne vessel, looks to Paimon like a ball of yarn or snakes. Firestones, a variant of Pyrophosphorite found on the Tonatiuh, activate its own altar.

key: The Warm Rhythm of the Streets
The Reason We Are Gathered Here
575.content:
Lotos Somno Chapter (also: Lotos Somno, Nilou's Story Quest, To the Wise, The Warm Rhythm of the Streets, Show Canceled, The Reason We Are Gathered Here): The Lotos Somno Chapter is Nilou's Story Quest, released in Version 3.1, and as of 7.1 it has one act, To the Wise. After the Sabzeruz Festival, the Sumeru Akademiya orders the Zubayr Theater shut down and its stage demolished within 30 days. Nilou, backed by the troupe and the Traveler, stands up in a formal debate against the Akademiya's representative Sharif, and the confrontation turns into a quiet first step toward reconciliation between Sharif and his estranged daughter Inayah.

The act has three quests: The Warm Rhythm of the Streets, Show Canceled and The Reason We Are Gathered Here. It is a character piece about belonging and about how Sumeru's scholarly institutions treat art, not an adventure with combat set-pieces; the only fight is a brief rescue of Inayah from tigers outside the city. Nilou is shown nervous, kind and stubborn, and she is the one who has to carry the argument.

The quest follows the Archon Quest chapter in which the Sabzeruz Festival went ahead despite Akademiya interference, and it builds on that festival's success. Its central question is not only whether the theater broke the rules but what a place of belonging is worth against an institution that values intellectual output.

Plot: The Traveler and Paimon find Nilou in the Grand Bazaar with more donated goods than she can carry. They help her haul them to the Zubayr Theater, with help from the porter Farhad, and the troupe starts a small party celebrating the festival's success. Sharif interrupts and demands to speak to the manager, Sheikh Zubayr, saying the Akademiya has decided to shut the theater down and demolish its stage in 30 days because of repeated rule violations. Zubayr objects that nobody communicated with him properly. Nilou explains that the Akademiya judges the theater's shows not intellectual enough. Inayah, a troupe member who ran away from home, argues with Sharif and addresses him as father. The Traveler suggests settling the matter by debate, a normal way of resolving disputes in the Akademiya, and persuades a reluctant Nilou to represent the theater.

The troupe and locals talk about what the theater means to them. Inayah slips away, and Nilou guesses she blames herself for bringing Sharif to the theater. They search near an old camp outside the city and rescue Inayah from a pack of Rishboland tigers. Nilou convinces her the fault is not hers, and Inayah agrees to help at the debate. The Traveler points out what Nilou's case is missing: the theater is not only a stage but a place of belonging for the people there now and in future.

Two days later the debate is held, with Safwan of the Akademiya as adjudicator. The first topic, whether the theater is useful, ends inconclusive. On the second, Nilou argues that Zubayr met all legal and documentary requirements for running a theater, and Safwan rules that threatening demolition before the Akademiya's discussions was premature. Sharif then notes that the Akademiya could instead revoke the troupe's performance license, which catches Nilou off guard, and Safwan agrees. Nilou argues that the theater is a place of belonging, but Sharif replies that such bonds are formed through work, much as scholars share knowledge and then move on to other projects. Inayah steps onto the stage and tells her father he is too wrapped up in his own world to understand relationships. The audience sides with her, and Sharif says, almost to himself, that it is a relief, and leaves, with Safwan following. The debate ends without a clear verdict.

Afterwards Nilou thanks the Traveler for keeping her from losing her temper and tells them how she became a dancer: through hard work rather than natural talent, after being captivated as a child by a troupe's dancer who later became her teacher. She wonders what Sharif wanted to say but could not.

Two days after the debate, Nilou introduces Inayah as the troupe's newest member before a performance the Traveler and Paimon attend. Sharif tells them he is currently suspended at his own suggestion, because losing the debate hurt the Akademiya's image. He still does not understand the theater's purpose, but his curiosity is piqued. Nilou brings Inayah to him and the pair share an awkward moment; Sharif gives her a framed piece of amateur embroidery he made himself, showing he had not forgotten her gift. Nilou says reconciliation will take a while and that going slowly is a step in the right direction. She gives the Traveler a miniature replica of the theater made by the troupe, so they can keep the memory while travelling Teyvat, and says they are welcome back at any time.

Details of the debate worth keeping straight: Safwan swears an oath of impartiality before it starts, warns both sides to restrain their emotions after the first topic grows heated, and finds Sharif's licence argument well supported even while faulting the early demolition threat. The Traveler tells Nilou to calm down when she nearly lashes out, and afterwards observes that Sharif need not have agreed to a debate at all and could have used other measures against the theater.

Revelations: - The Akademiya's objection is that the theater's shows are not intellectual enough, and its tools are rule compliance and licensing.
- Inayah is Sharif's daughter; she did not get along with her parents and has lived at the theater.

- Nilou's skill as a dancer came from effort, not innate talent.
- Sharif gives Inayah a handmade embroidery as a sign he remembers her gift, though he struggles to say what he feels.

Characters: - **Nilou**: dancer of the Zubayr Theater, the act's protagonist, who must speak for the troupe.
- **The Traveler and Paimon**: advisers who propose the debate.
- **Sharif**: Akademiya official who issues the demolition order and argues the Akademiya's side. He is Inayah's father.
- **Inayah**: young troupe member, Sharif's daughter, estranged from her parents.
- **Sheikh Zubayr**: theater manager.
- **Safwan**: Akademiya scholar who adjudicates the debate.
- **Farhad**: a porter who helps carry the goods.

Other troupe members and local shopkeepers appear as supporters and give their views on what the theater means to them.

Consequences: The demolition is not carried out, Sharif suspends himself, and Inayah joins the troupe formally. The theater keeps its stage; the personal rift between Sharif and Inayah has only begun to heal.

Placement: Released in Version 3.1 and unlocked after Chapter III Act II of the Archon Quest and Adventure Rank 40. Story order and release order match. Only Act I exists as of 7.1.

576.comment: Lotos Somno Chapter: Zubayr Theater Dispute
576.content: After the Sabzeruz Festival, the Akademiya official Sharif orders the Zubayr Theater closed and its stage demolished within 30 days for ignoring Akademiya rules. Nilou argues the theater's case in a formal debate with Safwan as adjudicator. The demolition threat is ruled premature, and the debate ends without a clear winner.

577.comment: Lotos Somno Chapter: Sharif and Inayah
577.content: Sharif is an Akademiya official and Inayah's father. Inayah ran away from her parents and joined the Zubayr Theater. After the debate Sharif suspends himself and gives her a framed embroidery piece he made himself. Nilou expects reconciliation to be slow.

578.content:
Lupus Aureus Chapter (Cyno) (also: Lupus Aureus Chapter, Lupus Aureus, Cyno's Story Quest, Sands of Solitude, Oathkeeper, Golden Wolf Chapter): Cyno's Story Quest, in two acts. In Sands of Solitude (3.1) the Traveler helps the General Mahamatra track a ring smuggling Canned Knowledge out of the Akademiya, and learns it was part of a wider, hidden effort connected to a banned ruin, the Court of Desolation. In Oathkeeper (4.6) a blackmail letter to Cyno's old teacher leads back to the Temple of Silence, which wants the Hermanubis power Cyno carries.

Act I has three quests: Suspicious Smuggling Case, Chain of Interests and All Returns to Silence. Act II has five: The Mysterious Letter, After Repose, Footprints Sunken Beneath the Sands, Sage of Sages and The Dead Past is the Living Present. Cyno's friends Tighnari and Collei appear in both acts; the Traveler is a close helper, not a bystander.

The chapter explores Cyno's strict sense of duty in Act I, where the person he must stop is a man he respects, and his past in Act II, where the question is whether the power he carries belongs to him or to those who raised him in the Temple. Both acts end in understatement: Cyno plans to plant flowers for a fallen colleague, then spends time with his old teacher.

Plot: Act I: Nabil, a Matra, asks the Traveler for help with smuggled Canned Knowledge. Cyno is already investigating. Following Dori's tip about an auction in the desert, the group fights off hired Eremites and scorpions, presses a smuggler in Aaru Village, and traces the Matra seal on a shipment to Taj Radkani, Cyno's former superior. At the Court of Desolation Taj's resistance ends, the ruin collapses on him, and Cyno quietly rounds up the ring.

Act II: Cyno's old teacher Cyrus receives a blackmail letter. Its pattern leads to the Temple of Silence. The Temple's leader Bamoun wants Cyno's Ba Fragment transferred to his grandson Sethos. Cyno proposes a winner-take-all Rite of Duels, wins, and gives Sethos the leadership.

Act I - Sands of Solitude. Nabil tells the Traveler that smuggled Canned Knowledge is circulating. Cyno has already found the smugglers, and Dori's tip reveals the ring is really seeking the banned Court of Desolation. Hired Eremites and scorpions try to stop them, a tracker leads to a Kshahrewar researcher, and a Matra seal on a shipment points to Cyno's former superior Taj Radkani. At the Court, Taj shows he joined the ring to expose it, and the ruin collapses on him. Cyno then quietly arrests the rest.

Act II - Oathkeeper. Cyrus, Cyno's old teacher, is blackmailed. The paper's emblem is from the Temple of Silence, and Cyrus and Cyno head into the desert. At the Temple, Bamoun tells how Cyno and Sethos were given Ba Fragments of Hermanubis and demands Cyno's be handed to Sethos. Cyno proposes a Rite of Duels, wins, absorbs the second fragment, and appoints Sethos leader after Bamoun dies. Cyno shows the Traveler his hideaway at the Sanctuary of Surasthana.

Act-by-act detail.

Act I - Sands of Solitude. Suspicious Smuggling Case: Nabil tells the Traveler and Paimon that smuggled Canned Knowledge is circulating, while the Matra are short-staffed because Cyno is away. Cyno has already located the smugglers Amainu and Amenzu and their buyer Mutair; he warns them rather than arrests them. Paimon almost names Dori, who once sold Canned Knowledge to Cyno. Dori says she has already left the trade, and that the ring is really after information about the Court of Desolation, a banned ruin said to let people see beyond life and death, and that the mass dumping is a distraction. She sells them a desert survival kit and charges it to Cyno. Cyno explains the Court's origins and why research on it is banned. Leaving the outpost, they are attacked by the Eremite Jhuba, hired by the ring, and Cyno explains his wariness: an earlier ambush by mercenary remnants injured his superior Taj Radkani and ended Taj's field work.

Chain of Interests: scorpions raised by someone attack the group in the desert, and Cyno finds a tracking device on the Traveler, which he recognises as Kshahrewar handiwork. At the auction site they find only one smuggler, Bahari, who returned to loot what was left. Bahari takes them to Aaru Village; he sold Canned Knowledge to pay for his daughter Simin's chronic illness. The Matra seal on his shipment suggests insider help. Nabil and the Matra repository show that Murtada Radkani, Taj's only son, was jailed for researching the Court and died. Taj's own Eremite clothes were seen by Usem, and papers in his house reveal a wide, complex operation involving well-known figures. Cyno decides to confront Taj.

All Returns to Silence: at the Court of Desolation a short fight convinces Cyno that Taj has not truly betrayed the Matra. Taj admits that the ring had members inside the Akademiya and that the ban would have blocked a direct plan, so he joined it hoping Cyno would end the case. The ruin collapses with Taj in it. Four days later Nabil reports that a mysterious person captured the mercenaries and researchers on the list; the Matra, learning of Taj's sacrifice, acted. Cyno is seen with Tighnari, who gives him paralysing traps, and mentions Collei has been giving talks on the dangers of Canned Knowledge. Cyno plans to plant flowers for Taj.

Act II - Oathkeeper. The Mysterious Letter: Cyrus, a former Spantamad sage who taught Cyno and Lisa, got a letter demanding ten million Mora or his secret would be revealed. Cyno catches the writer, a sixteen-year-old student named Urraca with a gambling problem who overheard gossip at a tavern. The unusual pattern on the paper, however, points further. After Repose: Kaveh sketches it and Alhaitham recognises an emblem of the Temple of Silence. Cyrus has left, and Cyno has gone west after him, leaving a letter asking not to be followed. Naphis, Tighnari's master, urges the group to bring both back, noting the Akademiya's shameful history with the Temple.

Footprints Sunken Beneath the Sands: the group meets Cyno at Caravan Ribat, then goes to Thamud Oasis, where Sethos leads them into the Temple of Silence. Bamoun accuses Cyrus of betrayal and tells the history of the two Ba Fragments of Hermanubis implanted in Sethos and Cyno as children. Cyno refuses to hand his over. Sage of Sages: Cyno proposes a Rite of Duels, winner takes all. After the Traveler and Tighnari win their rounds, Cyno beats Sethos, who relinquishes his fragment; Cyno absorbs it and Bamoun dies. The Dead Past is the Living Present: Bamoun's wish makes Cyno leader of the Temple, but Cyno appoints Sethos in his place, and Sethos admits the duel was his and his grandfather's plan. Cyno shows the Traveler his retreat at the Sanctuary of Surasthana and meets Cyrus there.

Details from Act I. Nabil explains that taking too much Canned Knowledge causes health problems as well as being banned. Cyno keeps the tracking device rather than destroying it, because it might be useful later. Dori says she cashed out because a flat share was not worth it and new regulations made clients scarce, not out of conscience; Cyno does not ask where the tip came from. Utayba allows the repository search after reading Cyno's letter. Payam recalls a Kshahrewar researcher sending large shipments with little old equipment, under a Matra seal Taj told him to wave through. After the collapse, Cyno asks the Traveler to meet him at Caravan Ribat four days later while he handles the cleanup himself.

Details from Act II. Cyrus brought Cyno to Sumeru City after the trials in the Temple. Cyrus asks Cyno to bring Tighnari along to a meal at Lambad's Tavern, where Kaveh also drops by. The group camps with Tighnari and Collei in Gandharva Ville. Candace and Dehya briefly speak with Cyno at Caravan Ribat. Bamoun says the Temple's influence is fading without Hermanubis, that volunteers were rejected by the fragments, and that his two child candidates were his adopted grandson and a child whose parents accepted money. The three-phase plan was resonance, implantation, recovery and observation. He recognises Tighnari as a descendant of the Valuka Shuna. The duel is refereed by Duaenre. The Traveler faces a Grounded Geoshroom and Grounded Hydroshroom, and Tighnari two Primal Constructs. In the final round Cyno switches off Hermanubis' power mid-fight and so does Sethos.

Further details. Act I: Jhuba warns that others will come after Cyno. Nabil asks the Traveler to pass on his regards to the mysterious helper. In the closing scene Cyno asks whether the Traveler knows anything about someone billing him for survival packages, a nod to Dori's invoice. Act II: Tighnari, recalling Alhaitham's and Kaveh's remarks on desert tribes' honour customs, suggests facing the Temple on its own terms. A quick examination shows Bamoun is under heavy stress with only days to live. After the duel Bamoun, seeing the light as Hermanubis returning, dies. Sethos tells the group that, per Bamoun's wishes, anyone Sethos or Lesser Lord Kusanali deems worthy may study the knowledge the Temple holds, and that Bamoun had been pleased to meet a Valuka Shuna descendant. Cyno plans a report for Kusanali and invites Sethos to the rainforest to meet the other side. Back at the Akademiya, Naphis scolds Cyrus for recklessness, Faruzan is upset not to have been included, and Cyno has Collei distract her with an Akademiya tour. Tighnari gives Collei the password 'cup' for meeting at Puspa Cafe. Kaveh admires Cyno's decision to give up the leadership. At the Sanctuary of Surasthana, Cyno calls the Divine Tree his secret place to unwind. Cyrus and Cyno look at old photos taken by Lisa; Cyrus plans to postpone a visit to her because of a tomato-growing contest with Zaha Hadi.

Revelations: Cyno carries a Ba Fragment of Hermanubis, implanted in him as a child by the Temple of Silence.

The Canned Knowledge smuggling was a front for research into the banned Court of Desolation, aided by insiders in the Akademiya, and Taj Radkani joined it deliberately to expose it. The Temple of Silence is a surviving secret desert order whose leader, Bamoun, held two Ba Fragments of Hermanubis.

Cyno was one of two children chosen for fragments; Cyrus ended the experiment and took Cyno away. Sethos, Bamoun's adopted grandson, got the other fragment. Cyno remembers little of the Temple.

The duel was effectively staged by the Temple. Bamoun's goal was to unite both fragments in one person and to free his successor from the old order's burdens, a plan Sethos admits was shared with him. The Temple then opens its knowledge to those the Dendro Archon or Sethos approve. All of this is from the wiki summary and not independently confirmed.

Characters: Cyno, the Traveler and Paimon.

Act I: Nabil, the Matra Taj Radkani, Dori, the smugglers Amainu, Amenzu and Bahari, the Eremite Jhuba, Tighnari and Collei. Act II: Cyrus, Aarav, Urraca, Sethos, Bamoun, Tighnari, Collei, Kaveh, Alhaitham, Naphis, Candace, Dehya, Faruzan and Lisa (by photographs).

Minor named figures include Murtada Radkani (Taj's son, deceased), Simin, Utayba, Payam, Usem, Zaha Hadi, Fodil and the duel referee Duaenre.

Consequences: The smuggling ring is dismantled, with its mercenaries and Akademiya researchers arrested, and Taj Radkani dies in the Court of Desolation. In Oathkeeper Cyno absorbs the second Ba Fragment, Sethos leads the Temple of Silence, and Bamoun dies.

Cyno plans to plant flowers at the Court for Taj. The Temple of Silence is brought into contact with the Akademiya and the Dendro Archon, with an official delegation expected, and Sethos is invited to Sumeru's rainforest.

Placement: Act I unlocks at Adventure Rank 40 after King Deshret and the Three Magi (Chapter III Act IV) and was released in 3.1 on 2022-09-28. Act II unlocks after Akasha Pulses, the Kalpa Flame Rises (Chapter III Act V) and was released in 4.6 on 2024-04-24, so it takes place after Sumeru's Archon Quest even though it was released much later.

579.comment: Lupus Aureus Chapter (Cyno): Court of Desolation
579.content: A banned desert ruin said to let people see beyond life and death and, in legend, to revive the dead. The Akademiya forbids research on it. A smuggling ring used a Canned Knowledge trade to find people interested in it. It collapsed into quicksand at the end of Sands of Solitude.

580.content: Cyno's former superior in the Matra, injured in an earlier mission and removed from live work but still respected. After his only son Murtada died following a prison term for investigating the Court of Desolation, Taj joined the smuggling ring in secret to expose it, and died in the Court's collapse.

581.comment: Lupus Aureus Chapter (Cyno): Temple of Silence
581.content: A secret desert order tied to Hermanubis, whose influence was fading without its guide. Its leader Bamoun held two Ba Fragments and had them implanted in two children, one of whom was Cyno. After the Rite of Duels in Oathkeeper, Cyno holds both and Sethos leads the order.

key: To Those Who Embark on the Expedition
582.content:
Lupus Majoris Chapter (also: Lupus Majoris, Varka's Story Quest, To Those Who Embark on the Expedition): The act has three quests: "Triumphant Warrior", "Fated Warrior" and "Lonely Warrior". It is split between Mondstadt, where letters from Varka carry the plot, and Nod-Krai, where Varka gathers the Wolf Spirit fragments and fights Roland. It closes with Varka returning to Windrise among his friends.

The quest links Mondstadt's history of the Knights of Boreas (Ravenwood, Rostam, Roland and Varka himself) to the Abyss's attempt to reshape the wolf god Andrius, and shows that Varka's letters were also a device to anchor him.

Plot: Lohen brings Varka's letters from Nod-Krai to Mondstadt, and the Traveler learns from Boreas at Wolvendom that Roland, the Abyss's replacement for Rerir, has corrupted the remains of Andrius. Dvalin carries the Traveler to Nod-Krai. There Varka and his knights gather Boreas's Wolf Spirit fragments, and Roland swallows Varka in a duel. Inside the wolf Varka draws on the longings of Rostam, Ravenwood and the Wandering Knight, calls Andrius back to the Ley Lines and fights his way out, to wake at Windrise.

**Triumphant Warrior.** Venti, who has asked the Traveler about Nod-Krai, meets them at Starsnatch Cliff and remembers Varka fighting a Ruin Guard as a young man. They then see Lohen, Vice Captain of the Fifth Company, fighting a Ruin Guard at the Thousand Winds Temple. Lohen was sent from Nod-Krai to deliver ten letters from Varka and asks Venti to reply. Meanwhile Varka and his knights Winfried, Ekbert and Leifhelm destroy Wild Hunt stragglers near the Pillar of Embla. Varka finds a shard of Andrius and plants his claymore in front of it; it becomes a red wolf that asks whether the surface is still corrupt, and he readies for battle.

At Headquarters Lohen delivers letters to Jean, Lisa, Sucrose, Mika, Noelle, Eula and Amber and the Traveler volunteers to take Kaeya's. Jean explains that if Varka does not return she will become Grand Master and train his successor, and that the Boreas lineage has twice almost been wiped out. The Traveler delivers letters to Kaeya, Rosaria and Diluc at Angel's Share; Varka's note to Diluc apologises for Eroch's actions and asks if he will rejoin the Knights, which Diluc declines. Rosaria tells of Roland, a disciple of Rostam whom Boreas respected, known as the White Knight and later the Bloodstained Knight. At Wolvendom they meet a purple mist and the Wild Hunt, then Lohen, who admits the earlier meeting was a test that the Hunt had not copied them.
