They free Eggie from a stasis module, recover her name, repair the moon's Eye of Ibni-Belum, find the real Columbina, face a mad mega kuuhenki and finally enter a hidden base on the moon's far side.

Act I, Pioneers. At the Dunanna Forward Station the Traveler activates a ruined mechanism with Archaeolune Energy given by a Columbina who does not speak. It can only link to the Frost Moon. When the Traveler asks the figure to hold hands, as in Silvermoon Hall, it changes into a black kuuhenki. The Traveler chases it into a vast chamber with a spaceship and an alarm.

Act II, Visitors From the Stars. After a rough landing, Paimon and the Traveler find Eggie caught in a stasis module in a dragon energy station. She reads a terminal and remembers her name is Ninnin. They power three stations, activate the Eye of Ibni-Belum, and follow a lead to Ungien's Circle. There they reach the Space Lifeform Capture Station and find the real Columbina. A rampaging mega kuuhenki, Ungie, is calmed by removing Knotted Moonlight Vines. Columbina and Eggie learn what the dragons did there.

Act III, Project Moongazer. In a high-security base on the moon's far side, Eggie reads that the base was built for a "Lord of Darkness Who Returned From the Sea of Stars". Columbina vanishes. Records in Lusalim's laboratory show that Eggie carries the name of Ninnin, the artificial "daughter" of the researcher Lusalim, and was made to carry out the final step of Project Moongazer. The moon's core holds a recorded imprint of that original Nin-Kiggia.

Pioneers (Part 1): the false Columbina does not answer greetings; she walks to the Dunanna Forward Station, ignores their questions and gives the Traveler Archaeolune Energy so a machine can be activated. The room's centre becomes a model of the Three Moons with a large blue sphere.

Pioneers (Part 2): the pair land in escape pods, find Eggie hanging in a stasis module, and bring power to three small energy stations that feed the Eye of Ibni-Belum. The third station is already active, which Paimon thinks means Columbina has been there. Eggie asks to be called just Ninnin, and as she reads more terminals she grows more confident and quicker with the data, to Paimon's irritation.

Visitors From the Stars (Part 1): at Ungien's Circle, a biosphere under a large tree with a tall antenna, and at the Space Lifeform Capture Station, Eggie finds blueprints and records, while the group dodges flywheels and Archaeolune storms. Visitors (Part 2): Columbina is treating Maagees (called Maggie in the cast list) and asks the Traveler to hold Ungie's attention; schools of kuuhenki mimic jellyfish and whales to help. Eggie learns the history of Ungien, who flew the spaceship Moongazer toward a second signal, fused with a creature from deep space, and was later turned by his wife Maagees into the kuuhenki Ungie. Maagees was converted the same way by her student Lusalim.

Project Moongazer (Part 1): After reading the Stellar Blackbody message, Eggie says she does not have the memories the message implies and cannot explain why. Columbina senses an odd familiarity in the base. Records state the base's lowest levels reach a fissure into the moon's core. Part 2: the Traveler and Columbina descend, beat the guardian Warden of the Flame, meet Nin-Kiggia's recorded imprint, and return to the Eye so Eggie can transmit.

Dialogue notes: in Visitors Part 2 Columbina says she will take back the hat she gave Eggie if Eggie hides anything, and Eggie promises not to. In Pioneers Part 2, after reading terminals, Eggie briefly claims the Traveler is more rational and reliable than Paimon, which annoys Paimon.

The moon's inhabitants had protective systems beyond the facilities: the false sky; a miniature Lunar Veil on Ungien's Circle; and a failed full-scale Veil whose generator was pierced by an entity from beyond the stars. Columbina suspects the Descender destroyed Lusalim's lab, because a veil that hides the moon resembles the false sky, but since the other facilities survived, she thinks Lusalim traded his research to the ruler of the heavens.

Revelations: Eggie is a data-born lifeform, created to finish Project Moongazer from the merged information of the dragon researchers of the Frost Moon. The project's purpose is to send into space the message once carried by the Stellar Blackbody, a creature from beyond the stars: a message of hope that tells other civilisations they are not alone and may be in danger from a pitch-black annihilation spreading through the universe.

The researchers form a lineage. Ibni-Belum, the first Moongazer, designed the Eye that bears his name; Ungien and Maagees were later Moongazers; Lusalim was their student and Nin-Kiggia's creator and "father". Eggie is the newest life form born from the merged data of the researchers, and her nickname Ninnin is inherited from Nin-Kiggia, the final inheritor of the project.

A sealed segment of the transmission reveals a reply from the Traveler's sibling, sent thousands of years ago, thanking the moon's inhabitants for their courage and promising to find them once their own troubles are over. The Traveler learns only now that a reply existed, and says they once received a message too garbled to read.

According to the wiki's act summary, the moon's core is the launch silo of a weapon once reforged by a Dragon Lord of Darkness to fire on Teyvat, defeated by the Heavenly Principles. Nin-Kiggia's imprint says the Traveler has already met earlier reincarnations of the researchers (Ibni-Belum, Ungien and Maagees). Eggie's final broadcast lists the names of every Moongazer who came before her, then her body dissolves, leaving only her hat.

Characters: The Traveler, Paimon, Eggie (Ninnin), Columbina; recorded or remembered: Ibni-Belum, Ungien, Maagees (Maggie), Lusalim, Nin-Kiggia; the mega kuuhenki Ungie.

Eggie is quiet and mission-driven; Paimon fusses over her; Columbina is gentle, curious and protective, and she keeps her own sense of familiarity with the moon. The Frostmoon Scions are mentioned only in passing.

Consequences: Completing the series opens the Frost Moon map and its Ancient Moon's Remnant exploration system. Eggie is gone after sending her message. Columbina and the Traveler agree to hold a "Home-Returning Night" party with friends when the Traveler's journey ends.

Columbina's reading that the moon's veil resembles the false sky ties the story to the wider cosmology of the Heavenly Principles. Beneath the Lunar Sea, another Frost Moon world quest, explores one of the buried dragon facilities.

Placement: Released in Version 6.7 (Luna VIII, 2026-07-01), in the same version as Song of the Welkin Moon: Scherzo, and before the Snezhnaya content of 7.0. It is a world quest with no listed prerequisite; the Frost Moon is reached through the series itself.

key: One for the Foodies, Two for the Show
Three to Get Ready, and Here We Go
623.content:
Moonlight Merriment (also: Moonlight Merriment event, One for the Foodies, Two for the Show, Three to Get Ready, and Here We Go, Moonlight Seeker, Trail of Delicacies, Masterful Chefs competition): The story runs in two parts, "One for the Foodies, Two for the Show" and "Three to Get Ready, and Here We Go". Part I is a hunt for inspiration and for the history of the Stove God, which pulls in Keqing, Ningguang, Beidou and several other Liyue residents. Part II is the taste-testing, the final cook-off between Xiangling and Smiley Yanxiao, and the awakening of the statue. Alongside the story the event offered the Moonlight Seeker and Trail of Delicacies challenges and a limited claymore reward, the Luxurious Sea-Lord. It is warm, food-centred and light in tone, with one quiet and moving revelation at its end.

Because it was a limited-time event, the 2021 story is canon but not common knowledge in Teyvat: most people in Liyue know the festival and the competition, not the Traveler's part in it. The event's own requirements are Archon Quest Chapter I, Act III (A New Star Approaches), Trulla Chapter Act I (Mondstadt Gastronomy Trip) and Adventure Rank 28.

The Moonchase Festival has since been given a longer history in later canon (see its own entry). This entry covers only what the 2021 event says: the Stove God, the Guili Assembly, and the festival's unification by Rex Lapis in Madame Ping's telling.

Plot: Part I. Paimon pulls the Traveler to Wanmin Restaurant for a meal, where Xiangling explains that she has reached the Masterful Chefs competition of this year's Moonchase Festival (theme: "Feast of the Bounteous Land") and needs fresh ideas. They ask around the city for inspiration, and at Yujing Terrace find Beidou, Ningguang and Keqing around a strange large stone that was fished out of the sea. Nobody knows what is inside it. Keqing mentions her grandfather's research into Liyue traditions and the possibility that the Stove God is a figure separate from the Geo Archon, so the group goes to Qingce Village and then Wangshu Inn to dig through old texts. Along the way Smiley Yanxiao trades old texts for the Traveler's Satisfying Salad and turns out to be a rival entrant. Back in Liyue Harbor the adeptus Cloud Retainer appears to announce a showpiece of her own, a "supreme cuisine machine", and Keqing returns with a recipe from her grandfather's notes. Madame Ping, Xiangling's teacher, then explains the festival's history and the Stove God. The part ends with the stone beginning to crack.

Part II. With the competition narrowed to the finals, Xiangling collects more feedback. After Beidou and Xinyan, Paimon suggests someone who prefers mild food, and the Traveler calls Xiao, who has promised to come when his name is called. He praises the cooking and suggests easing the strong seasoning on the side dishes. The next day Xiangling and Yanxiao cook against each other, with Guoba cheering Yanxiao on when he falls behind. Xiangling wins. A downcast Keqing blames herself for having picked Yanxiao's Golden Shrimp Balls over Xiangling, and Xiangling reassures her. The statue has not changed, so Xiangling cooks the Chili-Mince Cornbread Buns from the recipe Ping had filled in. When Keqing eats them the stone cracks open and reveals a statue of Guoba as he once was.

Part I in more detail. Before narrowing the search, the group asks Hu Tao and Baizhu for opinions. At Qingce Village Xingqiu and Chongyun are present, and Xingqiu lets Keqing borrow her grandfather's texts, which place the Stove God at the Guili Assembly. At Wangshu Inn the old texts and Keqing's own information conflict on some points. A Treasure Hoarders skirmish near the Feiyun Commerce Guild warehouse is part of the quest steps. Xiangling comes to suspect that the Stove God may have been an adeptus, which is why she takes the group to Ping.

Part II in more detail. The cook-off is a timed contest in which the Traveler helps Xiangling make three dishes, Crystal Shrimp, Triple-Layered Consomme and Jueyun Chili Chicken. Afterwards the two chefs taste each other's dishes and part on good terms. Keqing eats the buns, a dish tied to her grandfather's research that she had wanted to taste; the nostalgia and longing of that moment is what Ping says resonated with the statue.

Minor beats. Guoba greets Ping warmly. The event also added world quests (the Contraption-Contrived Cooking Course in three parts, and The Many Matters of the Moonchase Festival). Event-only NPCs include Linyang (hints for Moonlight Seeker) and Sheng (in Part I). Many ordinary Liyue NPCs, among them Chef Mao, Huai'an, Nadia and Vlad, have temporary festival dialogue.

Revelations: Madame Ping's account of the festival and the Stove God, as told in the quest:
- Moonchase began as a rite of the adepti; ordinary people copied it, producing various local festivals. Rex Lapis later unified them under the Moonchase name to honour an old friend, the Stove God, Marchosius.
- Marchosius loved humanity. When the Guili Assembly was flooded and the people retreated south to Liyue Harbor through a storm, the adepti stayed by them and he cooked a flatbread with meat sauce. Centuries later, when disaster and plague returned, he placed all his power into the land to quell them, which left him much smaller and with greatly reduced wits. He told Ping and Rex Lapis about dishes that bring joy and the secrets of flame, then went into the mountains for a long slumber.
- When he awoke he ate Chili-Mince Cornbread Buns left on an offering table by a young woman in yellow. He did not remember the past, but was moved and followed her. He is now Guoba, who accompanies Xiangling.
- Ping says the real Stove God was never inside the statue; he has been with them all along.

Ping calls Marchosius the closest of all the adepti to the common folk and describes his sacrifice as a god "surrendering power to the soil". She suggests that Guoba, though diminished, is carefree and at rest. Keqing points out that Guoba recognised a dish he himself invented and approved of the cook.

Characters: Xiangling is the protagonist of the event: a chef from Wanmin Restaurant who is Madame Ping's student and Guoba's companion. Keqing drives the research into the Stove God through her grandfather's notes. Madame Ping holds the Stove God's history. Smiley Yanxiao is Xiangling's rival in the final. Cloud Retainer appears briefly with a showpiece of her own. Ningguang and Beidou appear at Yujing Terrace, with Beidou and Xinyan later giving taste feedback. Xiao tastes Xiangling's dishes at the Traveler's call. Zhongli appears at the end and greets Guoba as an old friend.

Hu Tao, Baizhu, Xingqiu, Chongyun, Ganyu and Qiqi also appear in Part I or the cinematic, as does Chef Mao, Xiangling's father, whose restaurant is the base for the preparations.

Consequences: No lasting plot consequence follows beyond the new understanding of who Guoba was. Xiangling resolves to take good care of him and let him eat, drink and enjoy himself. The Moonchase Festival continues as an annual occasion, and Guoba stays with Xiangling.

Placement: Released in Version 2.1 on 27 September 2021. The in-game requirements are Archon Quest Chapter I Act III (A New Star Approaches), Trulla Chapter Act I (Mondstadt Gastronomy Trip) and Adventure Rank 28. A story order is not stated; it is a self-contained festival-season story.

624.content: Masterful Chefs is the Moonchase Festival cooking competition organised by the Liyue Qixing. In the 2021 event Xiangling and Smiley Yanxiao reach the final. The Traveler helps Xiangling cook three dishes, Xiangling wins, and the two rivals taste each other's cooking on good terms. Moonlight Seeker and Trail of Delicacies were the event's challenge strands, unlocked in three waves from 27 September 2021, with rewards including the Luxurious Sea-Lord claymore.

625.content: In the Moonlight Merriment event, Madame Ping says Guoba is Marchosius, the Stove God, an adeptus who loved humanity and gave all his power to the land to protect Liyue from disaster and plague. His body shrank and his intellect declined. He cannot speak and remembers nothing of his earlier life, but recognises familiar flavours and old friends. The event shows a statue of him in his former form, revealed when Keqing eats a long-desired dish.

626.content:
Mushroom Realm Mystery (also: Collective of Plenty Tribal Chronicle, Ardent Land of Plenty, Orchard Repose, Field Fungal Traces, Sage Supreme, The Meaning of Courage, Smokeless War): The Tribal Chronicles chapter of the Collective of Plenty, which also serves as Varesa's story quest. The Traveler and Paimon meet Varesa near the Great Volcano of Tollan, visit her tribe and her family orchard, and notice strange mushrooms growing there that are surprisingly delicious. When the mushrooms begin to talk, the pair find they have been eating the remains of a fungi god, Bifrons, who is trying to recover enough power for a comeback. Varesa takes responsibility for keeping an eye on it.

The chapter has three acts: Ardent Land of Plenty, Orchard Repose and Field Fungal Traces. The first two are a gentle introduction to the Collective of Plenty's farms and food culture; the third turns the mushrooms into a mystery. It is told with a lot of humour about Varesa's appetite, and ends with the tribe turning the god's tool against it by simply feasting on it.

Beneath the comedy it is a story about being a hero. Varesa is very strong but has never moved past the team stage of the Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame because she cannot bring herself to fight her own people, and she worries about living up to a legacy. At the end she concludes that a hero is someone who makes the right choice at the right time.

Plot: Act I. Walking near the Great Volcano of Tollan, the Traveler and Paimon meet Varesa, a young woman of the Collective of Plenty. She offers to take them to her tribe and shows her strength on the way, smashing through rocks thrown by an eruption and dealing with some hilichurls. At the village she asks them to meet her at the arena.

Act II. Varesa shows them around the village. Iansan, who coaches Varesa, explains that Varesa has never passed the team stage of the Pilgrimage because she cannot fight her own people. At the family orchard Varesa calms her Tatankasaur guardian Vanana, explains that the area is ideal for growing fruit which the tribe sells to others, and mentions an upcoming food tournament for which the orchard supplies dessert fruit. While harvesting, Paimon spots mushrooms that Varesa says appeared when the orchard was planted. She cooks a simple meal of the harvest.

Act III. At the tournament, Varesa wins a special oversized challenge and mentions that she eats the orchard's mushrooms to balance flavours. Atolli, who cooks, says there are red and green ones and that the green ones are to be eaten at once, as someone from Sumeru advised. The Traveler eats a green mushroom, and a voice calling itself the Sage-Lord of Fungi addresses them as worthy devotees. Following its clues, they learn that the better the aroma of the cooked mushrooms the closer the god is to showing itself. The god mocks the heat of the grilled mushrooms as insufficient, so the tribe hunts for a hotter heat source and finds one in a Furnace Shell Mountain Weasel. With it the mushrooms' scent grows, the Traveler, Paimon and Varesa are drawn into a fungal realm, and they chase the Sage-Lord to its hiding place, learning that it is a weakened god named Bifrons, hoping to grow in power on a spread of spores.

**Ardent Land of Plenty (5.5).** Varesa introduces herself and demonstrates her abilities on the way to the tribe's village.

**Orchard Repose (5.5).** Iansan explains Varesa's training and the obstacle she has faced in the Pilgrimage. At the orchard Varesa tells the Traveler how she began her "eating journey" and why the mushrooms there are valued even though nobody planted them.

**Sage Supreme (5.5).** Iansan and Acatl tell the Traveler that when the Abyss attacked Natlan, the Collective of Plenty had their own struggles, which Iansan believes was an effort to stop them sending reinforcements elsewhere, and that Varesa helped defend the land. Acatl describes the "Guardians of Tollan": the volcano brings destruction but also the opportunity to grow crops. A "Varesa Challenge" was created after the Speaker's Chamber noticed a single person ordering food meant for a large group and investigated it for fraud; on seeing Varesa finish the entire portion, Mavuika let it be. Not even the Pyro Archon could finish the Varesa Challenge. The Traveler eats a green mushroom, hears the Sage-Lord, and meets mushrooms that turn into fungi when examined, one of which asks a riddle to which the Traveler answers with a bad pun, and that is taken as the right answer. A mushroom explains that being eaten forms a connection between the eater and the Sage-Lord.

**The Meaning of Courage (5.5).** The Sage-Lord returns to tell the group that the heat is a fraction of the devotion required, and mocks their intelligence. Varesa takes the Traveler to the volcano, where they defeat four Avatars of Lava and, after an eruption, a huge weasel whose armoured core Varesa extracts, thinking it hotter than ordinary cores. Varesa admits she is reluctant to make her own legacy, and the Traveler and Paimon reassure her that she is acting on her own will.

**Smokeless War (5.5).** The tribe uses the weasel's armour in a cooking rig. The green mushrooms start giving off mist and the Traveler, Varesa and Paimon are dragged into another realm where the Sage-Lord says they are worthy devotees and sends clones that are easily defeated. They follow it, jump down a well, and catch up. Varesa seizes it briefly and the group sees a memory: people had eaten so much of its clones that its power was nearly spent, but it could still control a single human, Chatraka, whom it ordered to carry it somewhere hot. At a volcano a volcanic eruption buried them both. The Traveler suspects the truth, and in the realm the Sage-Lord hides inside a statue; when they destroy it, it gives its name as Bifrons, a fungi god, and reveals that the green mushrooms were meant to spread spores so it could grow in power and take revenge on Sumeru for the Archon War. Paimon tells it the Archon War ended long ago, and Bifrons says it has heard about a war that was in fact against the Abyss, though it brushes this off as a lie. The Traveler deduces it is too weak and needs a host to control, and Bifrons threatens a Jadeplume Terrorshroom but is ignored.

Finer points. Back in reality, the tribe holds a huge feast with the green mushrooms, and Saurians and even Fatui join in. Bifrons demands that they stop and is bitten by a Tatankasaur whelp. Varesa thanks the Traveler for helping her become a hero in the story, and Paimon suggests finding someone who can help with Bifrons. At the Adventurers' Guild Katheryne turns out to have found Tighnari nearby; he is surprised to see the pair in Natlan but agrees to help once he hears about the Sage-Lord. When Varesa asks him about Bifrons's clones, he confirms there is one in the Chasm named Xamaran. Because it is not a green-cap mushroom and its link to Bifrons is likely weakened, he asks Varesa not to eat it, and she says she would never eat a friendly mushroom. The chapter's closing text says Varesa learned what it means to be a hero, that the god had so little divine power left that it posed little threat, and that Varesa offered to take responsibility and keep watch over it.

Revelations: The delicious mushrooms in Varesa's orchard are the remains of Bifrons, a fungi god with ties to Sumeru, so weakened by people eating its clones that it can only act through mushrooms and mind control a single host. The green ones are meant to carry its spores. Bifrons's plan is revenge on Sumeru for the Archon War, based on outdated information.

Bifrons says it gave followers sustenance in proportion to their contributions. The quest shows that a human, Chatraka, was once used by Bifrons to carry it somewhere hot and that both were buried by an eruption. One of Bifrons's clones, Xamaran, lives in the Chasm and, per Tighnari, is likely disconnected from Bifrons. The god's comic threat of a Jadeplume Terrorshroom goes unfulfilled.

Characters: The Traveler and Paimon are the viewpoint pair. Varesa is the heart of the chapter: a cheerful, enormously strong and hungry woman who is uncertain about her role as a hero. Iansan coaches her and Acatl explains the tribe's customs and history. Atolli is a cook who supplies Varesa with food. Bifrons is the villain, calling itself the Sage-Lord of Fungi. Tighnari arrives at the end as an expert on fungi.

Vanana is Varesa's Tatankasaur guardian at the orchard. Mavuika appears only in an anecdote about how the Varesa Challenge began. Katheryne arranges the introduction to Tighnari. Chatraka is Bifrons's former human host, seen in a memory.

Consequences: Bifrons is exposed as nearly powerless. Varesa takes responsibility for keeping an eye on it. Tighnari agrees to advise on Bifrons's clones. The Collective of Plenty celebrates with a feast built around the mushrooms. Varesa has learned what being a hero means. Xamaran is to be spared.

Placement: Release order: all three acts belong to Version 5.5, with the event running from 2025-03-26 to 2025-04-15. Story order: Acts I and II require only the Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame in the Archon Quest part Flowers Resplendent on the Sun-Scorched Sojourn, while the chapter and event pages require Incandescent Ode of Resurrection (5.3) for Act III. The event offered a Quick Start feature to unlock Act III for players who were behind on the Archon Quest.

627.content: A fungi god who calls itself the Sage-Lord of Fungi. Its power was nearly spent when people ate large amounts of its clones, and it could only control a single human, Chatraka, who carried it to a volcano where an eruption buried them. It lives on in the green mushrooms in Varesa's orchard, tries to recruit worthy devotees by being eaten, and plans revenge on Sumeru for the Archon War, unaware that the war ended long ago. It is exposed and mocked by the Traveler, Paimon and Varesa, and the tribe feasts on its mushrooms.

628.content: An oversized food challenge at the Collective of Plenty's food tournament that only people who have completed the normal challenge may try. It began when the Speaker's Chamber noticed that one person was ordering food meant for a large group, suspected fraud and investigated, and found Varesa eating the whole portion. Mavuika let it be. Not even the Pyro Archon could finish it.

629.content: A clone of Bifrons living in the Chasm. Tighnari confirms its existence and says it is not a green-cap mushroom and its connection to Bifrons has probably weakened, so he asks Varesa not to eat it, and she agrees.

630.content:
Nameless Bloodstained Monument (also: Nameless Bloodstained Monument world quest, Bloodstained Knight's final comrades quest): A Version 6.4 world quest on Ashveil Peak in Nod-Krai. With Varka as the active character, the Traveler touches a shadowy greatsword near the wolf-like enemy "The Homesick Lone Wolf" and is drawn into a sealed battlefield guarded by a shadow of Boreas. At its end Varka sees the memory of the last knights who followed the Bloodstained Knight Roland, and picks up their two greatswords.

The quest fills in what became of the knights of Favonius who left Mondstadt with Roland. They fought the cursed monsters of the north beside him until they died, and Roland used the power of Boreas to seal their battlefield so that their rest would not be disturbed. Varka, himself a knight of Mondstadt, treats the dead as comrades and carries their swords on.

The quest ties together three things the player may already know: the legend of the Bloodstained Knight, the Wolf of the North as a power Varka can sense, and the Knights of Favonius' own gaps in its records. It is a quiet, elegiac story rather than a mystery.

Roland's farewell is the emotional core. He believes he must walk his blood-soaked path alone, the knights insist they chose it, and in the end he seals them away to spare them further injustice, a choice Varka challenges by calling them back to fight.

Plot: The Traveler touches the shadowy greatsword, and Roland's voice tells them not to disturb the sleepers. Varka senses the Wolf of the North's power and also a hint of the Falcon of the West. Entering the domain, the party fights a shadow of Boreas, then sees the memory of Roland and his knights. Varka takes the swords of the fallen knights.

The quest begins when Varka is the active character and the player interacts with the greatsword behind the Homesick Lone Wolf. A voice, identified by the wiki as Roland's, whispers "do not disturb their peaceful slumber", and Varka comments on the power he feels there. He chooses to face the enemy. Inside the domain the area is sealed by a force that Varka suspects is a manifestation of Boreas, and he wonders who sealed it.

Mid-fight a distant voice recites lines about unyielding ice on an inscribed stele and a biting gale mourning the lost. The player can pick up flames of battle, which are the "unextinguished flame" of the knights, and the knights' heroic spirits indicate where to start. When Boreas's Shadow is weakened further, it is replaced by the Homesick Lone Wolf and its ancestral spirit while another voice urges, "continue your knightly journey".

After the fight Varka stands before two greatswords. He asks who left the wolf spirit there and what it guards, then holds out a hand and closes his eyes. Roland's spirit appears with several nameless knights and a pale-furred wolf. Roland says he has told them many times that this blood-soaked path is his alone and no one need follow. The knights answer that they simply happened to follow the same path "all the way from Mondstadt to Nod-Krai", revering a knight who saved them countless times, and that they would stand as witnesses even if only a few of them were left. The wolf howls. Roland says he has no right to deny them.

A black-screen scene shows the aftermath. The knights ask whether the cursed monsters are dead and whether the nearby residents are safe, then admit they lack the strength to see him to the end and tell him he must walk the rest of the road alone. Roland turns to Varka, says his sword could not protect them all and that in the end only one remains on the path, "perhaps the way it was always meant to be". He takes off his mask (his face is hidden from the camera) and says that these swords and the wolf spirit will serve as guardians so that dark aberrations never disturb the knights' eternal rest.

Varka reflects that the Knights of Favonius' records say some knights followed the Bloodstained Knight when he left, and that they were never mentioned again. He is moved that they died fighting monsters, a worthy end for true knights of Favonius, and asks whether this was truly all they wished. Roland reappears and says he will use the power Boreas left there to seal the battlefield, and that the little wolf will stand vigil outside, so the knights can enjoy eternal peace and be spared from witnessing the injustice of the world. He says goodbye to his final comrades.

The knights refuse to be left sleeping. Their voices say "no" twice, then "let us fight, once more". Varka answers that surely their wishes were not meant to wither in such a place, asks them to join him, lifts both greatswords and shouts "To battle!" in unison with their voices. The player receives the weapon Unbreakable: Durandarte. Varka's last words are that Roland really was on his own once they were gone. If the player touches the shadowy greatsword again after the quest, Roland says nothing audible and Varka challenges the shadow to show what it has.

Gameplay notes: from the second step the player enters a domain and is limited to Varka. Picking up flames of battle grants a temporary Pyro infusion. Food effects cannot be consumed during the challenge, and the domain can be re-entered after the quest to fight Boreas's Shadow again. Rewards: 40 Primogems, Unbreakable: Durandarte, Hero's Wit, Mystic Enhancement Ore and 30,000 Mora.

Revelations: The quest shows that some Knights of Favonius followed Roland out of Mondstadt and died fighting monsters in Nod-Krai, and that Roland used Boreas's power to seal their battlefield with a wolf spirit as guardian. It also answers Varka's question about the knights who vanish from the Order's records.

It shows how Roland saw himself: someone who walked alone because he thought he could not protect others, even as the knights insisted they had chosen their path. It gives a human reason for the wolf spirit on Ashveil Peak.

It does not say when the battle took place, who the knights were, or what Roland's face looked like. The quest also does not say what the Falcon of the West is beyond Varka's remark that he felt a hint of it.

Characters: Varka and Roland, the Bloodstained Knight. The nameless knights who followed him and a pale-furred wolf appear in the memory. The Traveler is present but the story belongs to Varka.

Varka is serious and respectful toward the dead; he speaks of the knights as "true Knights of Favonius" and refuses to let them rest if they still have something to fight for. Roland is weary and self-effacing: he says his sword could not protect everyone, and he wants his comrades at peace. The nameless knights are loyal and stubborn, and they joke about "fate".

The knights never give names, ranks or ages.

Consequences: Varka receives the two greatswords and the memory that goes with them, and the player gets the reward weapon. The domain stays available for repeat fights. No political or historical change follows.

Placement: Introduced in Version 6.4 (Luna V). The wiki lists no prerequisite quest, only Varka as the active character at the starting greatsword on Ashveil Peak. The Bloodstained Knight's earlier legend comes from Mondstadt content, which this quest extends.

631.comment: Nameless Bloodstained Monument: Roland and the nameless knights
631.content: In the Nameless Bloodstained Monument quest the memory shows several knights of Favonius who followed Roland from Mondstadt to Nod-Krai and died fighting cursed monsters. Roland says it is his blood-soaked path alone; they say they chose it. Roland later seals their battlefield with Boreas's power and a wolf spirit to guard it. Varka calls them back to fight and carries their greatswords.

632.comment: Nameless Bloodstained Monument: The Homesick Lone Wolf
632.content: "The Homesick Lone Wolf" is an enemy near Ashveil Peak in Nod-Krai. In the Nameless Bloodstained Monument quest the greatsword behind it opens a sealed battlefield, and Roland says a wolf spirit stands vigil outside so that no dark aberration disturbs the knights who died there.

key: Neko Is a Cat World Quest series
633.content:
Neko Is a Cat (also: Neko Is a Cat World Quest series, Restoration of the Asase Shrine, Cat in the Clouds): Because Neko believes Hibiki, the former head priestess, and Hibiki's friend Domeki will return, she wants the shrine restored. The Traveler cleans the grounds, mends a wooden shelf and the prayer rack, finds the cats who have wandered off, helps arrange a meal like the one Hibiki cooked, and recruits Ooshima Junpei, a stonemason from Tatarasuna, to carve a statue. The adventurers Taisuke and Etsuko, already on the island from Seirai Stormchasers, help along the way. Completing it earns the Cat in the Clouds achievement, new commissions and a viewpoint at the shrine gate.

The series is a gentle, humorous story with an undertone of sadness: Neko has waited a very long time and is not told that people have changed or gone. Her habit of describing Junpei as "the stone human" and not understanding salary or Mora keeps the tone light.

Follow-up content includes six daily commissions (A Fishy Flavor, Shadow of the Cat, Shrine Cleanup, The Cat's Trail, To Make Cat Ornaments and To Make a Cat Carving) and a world quest, The Narukami Trail, which needs four completions of certain commissions.

Plot: Opening. After Seirai Stormchasers, the Traveler returns to Asase Shrine. Neko is pleased that Taisuke and Etsuko visited and thinks it is because the repaired offering box draws people to the shrine, so she wants to repair more. The first quest, Shrine Cleanup, requires clearing dirt around the shrine; Neko remembers Hibiki, who was head priestess, received guests, cared for the shrine and named Neko. Domeki would visit to play with Hibiki and help clean.

The next days. The Traveler repairs the Prayer Rack with Taisuke and Etsuko, and Etsuko grows suspicious of Neko's motives, since the island's people long ago moved away. Neko answers that she needs to look after the shrine, or Hibiki will be sad when she returns, not knowing what became of her. The following day Neko asks for help finding cats that have wandered off. After that Neko recalls the dish Hibiki used to make for the cats; Kiminami Anna devises the Invigorating Kitty Meal, which Neko says is different but wonderful.

The statue. Neko remembers Hibiki once asking if she wanted a statue of herself and decides to have one built. Taisuke and Etsuko suggest looking for workers at Tatarasuna, where the Traveler meets Ooshima Junpei, who is baffled that a talking cat wants a statue of herself. He agrees but forgets to ask about pay while he is stunned by the speaking cat; over several days the Traveler fetches iron chunks and meat for him while Neko is puzzled by salary and Mora. During this time Neko asks the two adventurers about Hibiki and Domeki. They know nothing of Hibiki, and say that Domeki was a pirate with a bounty on his head; Neko, who remembers him playing with Hibiki, insists he must have been a good person.

Completion. In the last quest, Junpei leaves a little extra stone to chip off in Neko's presence, as statues of this sort deserve a formal finish. Neko says she only wants Hibiki, if she returns and loses her way, to see the statue and know where to go. At the final knock a cloud forms the shape of a cat. Neko believes it is Hibiki, and that the good thing Hibiki and Domeki promised would follow the statue has happened. She is certain that Hibiki, Domeki, Janome and the rest of Hibiki's friends will come back.

Neko lists what has been restored: the Offering Box, the Prayer Rack and now the statue. The final quest requires the player to leave Co-Op mode while it is active and rewards Adventure EXP, Primogems, Hero's Wit and Mora.

Revelations: - Neko named herself Provisional Head Priestess of the shrine while she waits; the real head priestess was Hibiki, who gave Neko her name.
- Neko still believes Hibiki and Domeki are alive and will return. The adventurers' remark that Domeki was a pirate is new to her.

- The wiki profile places Hibiki and Domeki some five centuries earlier, in the era of the Cataclysm, and has the island kept in near-constant storms afterwards. That background comes from Seirai Stormchasers and is not told in this series itself.

Characters: Neko (a talking black cat), the Traveler, Paimon, Taisuke and Etsuko (Adventurers' Guild members), Ooshima Junpei (stonemason), and Kiminami Anna (cook). Hibiki, Domeki and Janome are only remembered by Neko.

Consequences: The shrine is tidier and has a statue, Neko is happier and more certain of Hibiki's return, and the player earns the Cat in the Clouds achievement, new commissions and a viewpoint beside the shrine gate near the Teleport Waypoint.

Placement: Released in 2.1 and unlocked after Seirai Stormchasers (Part IV). Each following quest requires a daily reset before it can be accepted, so the series takes at least nine in-game days. It does not connect to the main Archon Quest.

634.content:
Neko is a talking black cat who guards Asase Shrine on Seirai Island and calls herself its Provisional Head Priestess. She was named by Hibiki for her habit of sleeping. She does not understand human money, and is determined that the shrine should be cared for until Hibiki returns.

Neko speaks of Hibiki with fondness and trusts that her promise of a good thing after the statue is finished has come true.

635.comment: Neko Is a Cat: Invigorating Kitty Meal
635.content: A dish designed by Kiminami Anna after Neko describes the meal that Hibiki used to make for her and the other cats. Neko says it differs from Hibiki's but tastes wonderful, and asks the Traveler to feed the other cats with it.

636.content:
Nereides Chapter (also: Nereides, Sigewinne's Story Quest, The Warmth of Lies, Beauty Expert, Switcheroo, Underground Crime, The Truth of What Was, Butterfly Dew): Sigewinne's Story Quest. On a holiday in the Court of Fontaine at the Duke's insistence, the head nurse of the Fortress of Meropide is drawn into a case: prisoners who seem to swap identities, and a new beauty lotion that is not what it seems. The Traveler helps her trace the potion behind it, and learns the story of why she kept a human face.

The chapter has one act, The Warmth of Lies, of four quests: Beauty Expert, Switcheroo, Underground Crime and The Truth of What Was. It was released in version 4.7 and is unlocked at Adventure Rank 40 after Masquerade of the Guilty and the Diluvies Chapter. It shows the medical, practical and sometimes scheming side of a character who is gentle but firm.

The theme is care and self-sacrifice. Sigewinne treats a thief and his dying mother with the same kindness, and the chapter ties the mystery to her own past choice to trade what her friend loved for a way to heal her.

Plot: Sigewinne tests a beauty lotion made by Rawat, and the Traveler sees an inmate's face melt away at the fortress infirmary. Serious offenders swap places with prisoners about to be released using a face-changing potion called Butterfly Dew. The Traveler, Sigewinne and the Marechaussee Phantom track the maker to a hidden plant and to his mother's house. The mastermind is revealed, and Sigewinne tells her own story at her teacher's grave.

Beauty Expert: the Traveler and Paimon find a beauty promotion in the Court of Fontaine and meet Sigewinne, who writes for a magazine run by a beauty association. Paimon asks if she is a half-Melusine; Sigewinne is not offended and says she chose long ago to keep a human form. She tells a story of a Melusine who befriended a human girl, was refused help by the girl's parents when she fell ill, went to a 'witch' for a potion that gave her a human form and lost what the girl loved about her, and then cured her. Sigewinne tests Rawat's lotion, then returns to Meropide to treat inmates. There a prisoner, Erick, claims to have seen his double; an inmate, Potton, has his face melt away. Sigewinne uses the Traveler to scare a child patient into taking his medicine, then prepares the inmates' meals.

Switcheroo: suspects arrested the day before now claim mistaken identity, and some prisoners due for release were swapped for serious offenders. Wriothesley orders a hold on releases, but some have already left. Sigewinne suspects a potion that even Melusines cannot detect. The party visits the Research Institute to ask after Rawat, then his mother's house, where Sigewinne treats a sick old lady and the Traveler finds a note pointing to a hidden laboratory.

Underground Crime: in the plant they find the escaped criminals, who argue with Potton about the potion. Potton traps the party and leaks gas; Sigewinne stalls him by saying she can make a better potion without Primordial Water and escapes. Back at Rawat's house, Potton claims to be Rawat, saying he used a potion to change his appearance because he was reviled as he was. Sigewinne lets him see his mother, who recognises only Sigewinne; he is taken away.

The Truth of What Was: the Butterfly Dew is taken off the market. Potton confesses to Morgane that he worked with a man called Vacher, and that after the flood cut the supply of Primordial Seawater the gang had turned to attacking people. Sigewinne takes the Traveler and Paimon to the grave of her teacher in the Morte Region and tells them about her past.

Beauty Expert: Sigewinne tells the Traveler that Melusines judge people by their cuteness. The Duke sends Erick to the ward for observation and Sigewinne handles the case while the Marechaussee Phantom deal with another matter. Her teacher, she says, was a human travelling doctor who frightened children into taking medicine and died long ago. She cooks inmates' meals from Slime Condensate, Xenochromatic Crystals and frog meat, finished by the Coupon Cafeteria, because inmates would refuse to eat food made in front of them.

Switcheroo: Erick fails the test Sigewinne set him earlier, which supports the swapping theory. Sigewinne goes with the Marechaussee Phantom, with Morgane's concern and Wriothesley's approval. Rawat's colleagues at the Institute show disdain for him, and Bognor says Rawat never got deep into conversations. The legal address Rawat registered his brand to was his mother's house.

Underground Crime: Sigewinne works out that the lotion contains remains of Fontainians dissolved before Neuvillette removed their sins, and that this is why the potion needed Primordial Water. Potton calls her out for using a similar potion herself and says they are the same; she argues otherwise.

The Truth of What Was: Neuvillette tells the Traveler, as relayed in the wiki summary, that Sigewinne was once an inmate at the fortress because she broke an ancient Fontainian law against forcibly changing a species into a human, a law he believes existed because Egeria wanted to keep the true origins of Fontainians a secret. Her teacher had discovered the truth too and left her a potion she could use. The Traveler and Paimon realise that her teacher was the 'witch' of the story. After her sentence Sigewinne chose to stay and became beloved there. She later received an invitation and reunited with her old friend, who recognised her in spite of her form. She had wanted to tell Potton the same but felt the warmth of his hand fade. She shows the Traveler an extra potion she made; she declines to use it herself and it is destroyed.

Revelations: Butterfly Dew, a potion that changes a person's face, was being sold by a gang as a lotion. Sigewinne's human appearance came from a similar potion she took to heal a friend.

Sigewinne's teacher was the 'witch' who gave her the potion. The lotion's key ingredient was Primordial Seawater, and the gang had hidden a production plant under a remote site.

The lotion originally depended on remains of Fontainians dissolved before Neuvillette removed their sins. The Marechaussee Phantom Melusines cannot detect the potion's effect.

As reported in the wiki summary, Sigewinne once served a sentence in the fortress for breaking a law about forced species change, and Neuvillette suspects Egeria's secret.

Characters: Sigewinne, the Traveler, Paimon.

Wriothesley and Neuvillette appear. Morgane, Ceasth and Odilon work for the Marechaussee Phantom. The inmates Erick and Potton, and the researcher Rawat, appear.

Luc, a child patient. Bognor and Rawat's colleagues at the Research Institute. The guards Lambersart, Courbevoie, Dupont and Wolsey. The seller Calcagni.

Consequences: Potton and the gang are arrested and the remaining Butterfly Dew is withdrawn from sale. Sigewinne keeps the secret of her own potion, and the extra potion she made is destroyed.

The Traveler learns the truth of Sigewinne's past and her friendship with a human girl that began it.

Placement: Unlocked at Adventure Rank 40 after Chapter IV Act V, Masquerade of the Guilty, and Diluvies Chapter Act I, The Remains of the Past Day. Released in 4.7. Wriothesley's earlier story in the fortress is the Cerberus Chapter.

637.content: A lotion sold in the Court of Fontaine under the name of Mr. Rawat of the Fontaine Research Institute. In truth it contains a potion that changes the user's face, allowing serious offenders to swap with prisoners about to be released. Its ingredient Primordial Water had become scarce after the flood. Potton, who used it to hide his looks, was part of the gang and worked with a man called Vacher.

638.content: A human travelling doctor who taught Sigewinne her skills and died long ago. She is buried in the Morte Region, where Sigewinne takes the Traveler. The story Sigewinne tells in the first quest casts her as the 'witch' who gave a potion to a Melusine, and, having discovered the truth about the law, left her a potion she could use.

639.content:
Nightingale's Song (also: Nightingale's Song world quest series, Prelude to the Night Vigil, Darradarljod, A Star Out of Time, Operation Clifftop): A Version 6.3 world quest series in Nod-Krai, in three acts. Illuga, the young captain of the Lightkeepers' Nightmare Orioles squad, is trying to stop a Wild Hunt outbreak spilling from Kipumaki Cliff, where an undying enemy called the "Professor" has been sealed for five hundred years. With the Traveler and Paimon he collects the sacred relics of the Torchforger, repairs the old seal and finally fires the Arrow of Terpikeraunas from Piramida. The enemy is destroyed, at a heavy cost.

The acts are Prelude to the Night Vigil (Wind-Stirred Ripples and Tower of Inversion), Darradarljod (When War Songs Rise, with three sub-quests called Focal Point of Ancient Array) and the final act A Star Out of Time (The Last Night, the First Light). The series is as much about the Lightkeepers and about Illuga's fear of failing those he leads as it is about the enemy.

Alia, a human woman from the Torchforger's era who lingers outside normal time at the Pillar of Embla, supplies much of the history. The series explains the Lightkeepers' relics (Silver Lampwick, Spiralblade, the Arrow of Terpikeraunas), the three-year-old disaster at Kipumaki Cliff, and a prophecy that the undying serpent will rise twice and be struck down a third time.

Title note: the wiki's etymology note says 'Darradarljod' is a skaldic poem in Old Norse, found in chapter 157 of Njals saga. The final quest also rewards an Avatar called the Arrow of Terpikeraunas.

Plot: At Piramida the Lightkeepers prepare an operation against the Wild Hunt at Kipumaki Cliff. The Traveler helps Illuga find the Silver Lampwick from Alia at the Pillar of Embla, joins his squad for the clifftop assault, and in the end helps load the Spiralblade into the great mead hall's giant arrow and fire it at the enemy's Cataclysm Egg. The Professor is killed with Alia's help, and the Lightkeepers celebrate and mourn.

Act by act: the Traveler meets Illuga and his squad and fetches the Silver Lampwick from Alia at the Pillar of Embla; the squad launches Operation Clifftop, loses Bjorn, repairs the old sealing array and recovers the Spiralblade; finally the Lightkeepers fire the Arrow of Terpikeraunas from Piramida, and Alia confronts the Professor at the tower's top.

Chapter I: Prelude to the Night Vigil. In Wind-Stirred Ripples, near Piramida, the Traveler meets two Ratniki, Anleifr and Rollon, whose broken-down Moonwagon is interrupted when Rollon is suddenly overcome by a vision of a great purple eye and attacks. After he is brought around, Anleifr explains the Wild Hunt outbreak at Kipumaki Cliff, the pioneering-age ruins there and how the Wild Hunt can seize minds. In Piramida the Ratniki gather for an oath-taking led by Illuga, who recites the Lightkeepers' vow and announces the mission, to set foot on the cliff they last approached three years earlier. The old Ratnik Nikita asks the Traveler to find the Silver Lampwick, one of the Torchforger's three sacred relics (the Sword, the Lamp and the Mirror) that can raise a barrier against the Wild Hunt. Flins then speaks with Nikita, warning that this is no ordinary Wild Hunt and that he has met the ancient enemy before.

In Tower of Inversion, a voice at Wavechaser Plain calls on the "heroes of the sublunary sphere" to ascend a tower. At the Pillar of Embla the Traveler is nearly hit by Abyssal attacks and Illuga shields them with his lantern. He explains that the Lampwick is held by Alia, said to be a fae. His companion bird Aedon reveals hidden kuuvahki paths. When the second barrier core is recharged, time shifts and Alia appears. She is no fae, she says, but an ordinary human of five centuries ago who fought beside Solovei, the Torchforger, and who is now stuck in a time seam. She tells them of the prophecy and asks them to cleanse the corrupted tower. The three barrier cores are restored, Alia gives them the Lampwick and then holds the tower alone against the Professor. Illuga invites the Traveler to join his squad.

Chapter II: Darradarljod. In When War Songs Rise the squad gathers at Cliffwatch Camp. Illuga tells the story of the camp, three years earlier, when the Wild Hunt's mist set Lightkeepers against one another. The Traveler and Paimon meet Anleifr, Rollon and Bjorn, who also lost people. The next morning "Operation Clifftop" begins. A fog-wrapped voice, the Scourge of Endless Decay, taunts Illuga about running away. At the altar the barrier cannot be redeployed because a great Evil Eye destroys it, so Bjorn proposes using the four-point sealing array left by the Torchforger and the first Moonchanter. Illuga carries the Lampwick to three Verdant Crests with the Traveler. They destroy the Evil Eye, but Bjorn, who had been defending a position, was killed by its attack. Illuga blames himself. The Scourge torments him with illusions, but his team arrives. They return the Sealing Blades to their scabbards in the chasm of endless decay, destroy the Scourge and recover the Spiralblade. A scuffle then takes place off-screen (the wiki transcript implies that Anleifr struck Illuga); Illuga does not punish him, admits he lost his composure, and the team reconciles. The Scourge has spoken of Professor Rotwang as its master who is already on his way.

Final Chapter: A Star Out of Time. In The Last Night, the First Light, they return to Piramida. Nikita, whom Illuga calls his old pops, reveals the great mead hall is the Arrow of Terpikeraunas, a bow and arrow forged by the Torchforger and the first Moonchanter, and that the Spiralblade is its missing arrowhead. While the Lightkeepers hold back the Abyss in the plaza, the Traveler and Illuga load the Spiralblade, fight a Serpent of All Evils and an Ultimate Calamity, activate three amplifiers and fire the arrow at the Cataclysm Egg above the Pillar of Embla.

Atop the Pillar of Embla the Professor, trapped by the Sampo Mill, mistakes Alia for Relya. He offers her an "Elysium" for the shamed and forgotten and calls her his chosen one. Alia answers that he used Relya from the beginning, spinning promises so that Relya would seize the Sampo Mill, and that his fall into thievery was also a trap devised with Grand Duke Alvis. She says she carries Relya's role and legacy and will take the name Reed Miller, names the Professor as Rauthvangi, mad monk and undying serpent, and says his story ends here. Both fade away.

The aftermath is a feast in the mead hall, led by Nikita, in honour of the fallen and the Traveler's help, and a visit the next day to Bjorn's grave south of Cliffwatch Camp, where Illuga says Bjorn completed his mission and that the Lightkeepers will go on, like the Winter Icelea, enduring cold and storm.

Quest-by-quest notes. Wind-Stirred Ripples unlocks the achievement The Winds Awaken, the Leaves Whirl Round (the oath line). Tower of Inversion rewards the Silver Lampwick plus chests. When War Songs Rise gives Illuga as a trial character and includes two fights against the Scourge of Endless Decay (as a Nightmare's Avatar and later as Pathfinder to the Bedeviled Sky). The Last Night, the First Light is in a special story mode with Illuga on the team and rewards the Arrow of Terpikeraunas Avatar and the achievement Si le grain ne meurt. Rewards across the quests include Primogems, Mora, Hero's Wit and Mystic Enhancement Ore; individual amounts vary.

Revelations: The Lightkeepers' relics, sealing array and Arrow of Terpikeraunas were all made five hundred years ago by the Torchforger Solovei and the first Moonchanter of the Frostmoon Scions. Alia is a human, not a fae. The Professor is an undying serpent who sought to ascend to an "Elysium" beyond the sky using the Sampo Mill, and who was already killed once by Alia.

The Pillar of Embla is the tower the Professor built to reach his Elysium. By the prophecy's count the Professor has fallen three times: first at Alia's hands, then sealed at Kipumaki Cliff by Solovei and the Moonchanter, and finally by the Lightkeepers and the Traveler with the Arrow. The nightingale Aedon was once Solovei's bird, adopted by Alia when Solovei meant to cast aside the Nightingale family name, and was carried through the Sampo Mill across five hundred years.

Alia says the prophecy is less a prediction than an earnest plea, since its giver was, like her, a person from the past; the wiki dialogue has the Traveler recall a similar remark from Aila. The Scourge says the Professor's plan has been tried and failed ten years ago and three years ago. The series does not explain the Cataclysm Egg beyond its being a doom hatching above the Pillar.

Characters: Illuga, young captain of the Nightmare Orioles; Alia; Flins; Nikita; the Ratniki Anleifr, Rollon, Bjorn, Egle, Vlaicu and Olav; Aedon the nightingale; the Professor and the Scourge of Endless Decay.

Illuga is dutiful and anxious about being responsible for others. Anleifr is brash, loyal and funny and a former treasure hunter who lost his wife; Rollon is calm and steady and the brother of Ivar; Bjorn has studied Frostmoon Scions texts he borrowed from the current Moonchanter and comes up with the plan for the sealing array. Nikita is a senior Ratnik, addressed as Starshyna, who directs the operation from Piramida and says his time is running out. Flins is theatrical but solemn about his friend Nikita. Alia is wry, kind and tired.

The Scourge of Endless Decay mocks and isolates its victims with illusions of the dead. The Professor speaks in grand promises.

Consequences: The Professor is destroyed and Bjorn's death is mourned. Illuga leans on his team more than before. The series ends with the Lightkeepers celebrating and with the loss that paid for it.

Placement: Released in Version 6.3 (Luna IV) as one of Nod-Krai's world quest series. The transcripts include alternate lines depending on whether Wind-Stirred Ripples or Tower of Inversion was done first, and some lines for players who have done other quests. Lightkeepers' Oath (6.0) quotes the same oath.

640.content: One of three sacred relics (the Sword, the Lamp and the Mirror) the Torchforger used five hundred years ago against the fiend of Kipumaki Cliff. It deploys a barrier against the Wild Hunt. Solovei entrusted it to Alia at the Pillar of Embla, and the Traveler receives it after cleansing the tower for Illuga.

641.content: A spiral-shaped sacred blade the Torchforger used to seal demons. The Evil Eye seized it, it fell into the underground ruins, and Illuga and the Traveler recover it in When War Songs Rise. It is later loaded into the Arrow of Terpikeraunas as its arrowhead.

642.content: A bow and arrow forged five hundred years ago by the Torchforger and the first Moonchanter, passed down by the Lightkeepers until the day it could be used. The great mead hall in Piramida is the arrow and the Spiralblade its missing arrowhead. It is fired from the lighthouse-cannon of Piramida at the Cataclysm Egg over the Pillar of Embla.

643.comment: Nightingale's Song: Alia of the Pillar of Embla
643.content: Called a fae in legend. She says she is an ordinary human of the Torchforger's age, an ally of Solovei, who killed the Professor the first time by casting herself into the Sampo Mill and who now lingers outside normal time. She guards the tower, hands over the Silver Lampwick, and holds the Professor back at the end, telling him she carries Relya's role and the name Reed Miller.

644.comment: Nightingale's Song: The Professor of Kipumaki Cliff
644.content: An undying enemy sealed beneath Kipumaki Cliff five hundred years ago. He sought to use the Sampo Mill and a tower to reach an "Elysium" beyond the sky. Alia calls him Rauthvangi, a mad monk and the undying serpent; a prophecy says he will rise twice and be struck down a third time. His servant the Scourge of Endless Decay names him Professor Rotwang.

645.comment: Nightingale's Song: Operation Clifftop and the Kipumaki Cliff disaster
645.content: Three years before the series, a Lightkeeper detachment camped on Kipumaki Cliff was drawn into a strange mist and turned on itself; Captain Olsson held on alone, died covering the retreat of Illuga and the badly injured Ivar, and the Wild Hunt spilled out and killed many civilians. The Lightkeepers rebuilt Cliffwatch Camp and held the line. In the series Illuga leads Operation Clifftop to seize the Clifftop Camp and begin the counterattack.

646.content: A Lightkeeper in Illuga's squad and a thoughtful tactician. He suggests using the Torchforger's four-point sealing array, having studied Frostmoon Scions texts lent by the present Moonchanter. He is killed by the Evil Eye while holding a position at Operation Clifftop, and Illuga blames himself. Anleifr and Rollon mourn him.

647.content: Illuga's investigation squad of the Lightkeepers. Its members in the series include Anleifr, Rollon and Bjorn, with Egle and Vlaicu in supporting roles and the Traveler and Paimon as temporary recruits. Illuga formally invites the Traveler to join in Tower of Inversion.

648.content: A source of power the Professor tried to seize to fuel his ascent. Alia ignited it with her own flesh and blood to stop him, and it later pulled the bird Aedon through five hundred years. The Professor says in the final scene that it turns its face from him again. What the Mill is, beyond this, is not explained.

649.content:
Noctua Chapter (also: Diluc's Story Quest, Darknight Hero's Alibi, Legend of the Darknight Hero): Diluc's Story Quest, set in Mondstadt. Rumours speak of a masked vigilante, the Darknight Hero, and the Traveler discovers it is Diluc. When the Abyss Order threatens the city and the Knights of Favonius start watching Diluc, the Traveler helps him fight in secret while giving him a public alibi.

The chapter has one act, Darknight Hero's Alibi, made of three quests: Legend of the Darknight Hero, Darknight Hero's Crisis and Darknight Hero's Alibi. It was part of version 1.0 and unlocks after Song of the Dragon and Freedom, the end of the Prologue.

The tone is comic rather than grim: much of the quest is a staged alibi in which Diluc is seen serving drinks while the Darknight Hero is elsewhere, and the secret is in practice already shared by the Traveler, Kaeya and his winery staff.

Plot: In Angel's Share, Charles tells the Traveler and Paimon about the Darknight Hero. They gather rumours, then find Diluc fighting an Abyss Mage in an alley and promise secrecy. The Abyss Order challenges the Hero; Diluc and the Traveler uncover its plan. To protect his identity from Huffman and Kaeya, they lure slimes to the city and arrange for Diluc to be seen behind the bar while he clears the horde.

Legend of the Darknight Hero: townsfolk describe the Hero as a wealthy Vision holder who works at night and is not a Knight. After waiting, the Traveler hears a commotion in a north alley and finds Diluc killing an Abyss Mage. He says he had planned his route to avoid the guards, asks them not to tell the Knights, and leaves. Huffman, a Knight, arrives a minute late.

Darknight Hero's Crisis: Huffman has a letter in which the Abyss Order declares war on the Hero, partly in cipher. Diluc, who has heard of the challenge at his winery, has found a stronghold; he and the Traveler infiltrate it and defeat Landrich, a Hydro Abyss Mage. Diluc uses his Vision on it to make it talk, and it reveals the attack is planned for the next night. Back in the city, Huffman says the Knights want to learn the Hero's identity. Kaeya orders him to keep an eye on Diluc, who has been seen working at the tavern.

Darknight Hero's Alibi: at the winery, Diluc is unsurprised by Kaeya's move. He has the Traveler gather Mist Flower Corolla; his staff had tried it to boost sales but it drew slimes with its elemental energy, which Diluc turns into bait. Diluc takes on the Abyss horde alone while the Traveler and Paimon keep Huffman in the tavern. When the slimes arrive, Diluc shames Huffman into helping defend the city and clears the horde at another gate, then returns to the bar before Huffman does.

Details of the alibi: the Traveler first sets a small amount of bait on the ground and slimes converge on the winery, where the group clears them. Later, in the tavern, Paimon declines Huffman's offer to pay for her drink as part of the plan, and a guard reports that a huge number of slimes are attacking, which Huffman takes to be the Abyss Order's secret weapon. On his return Huffman sees that the Traveler is unusually tired and asks the patrons whether Diluc left; they all say no. He leaves doubtful but does not press.

Diluc then tells the Traveler that the "patrons" are his winery staff. Kaeya steps out of the crowd, having watched to see how Diluc would react. Diluc dares him to expose him; Kaeya answers that it is not his style, so the secret stays. Diluc thanks the Traveler, pays them, and says they may ask him for help if needed.

Revelations: The Darknight Hero is Diluc.

Kaeya chooses not to expose him. The Abyss Order is using slimes as a weapon against Mondstadt.

Landrich gives away the planned attack under duress. Through Kaeya's orders to Huffman, the Knights treat the Hero as a figure to be monitored.

Characters: Diluc, the Traveler, Paimon and Kaeya.

Charles (in Angel's Share), Huffman (a Knight of Favonius) and Landrich, a Hydro Abyss Mage.

Connor receives the Mist Flower Corolla at the winery. Winery staff play the tavern patrons.

Consequences: The Traveler is now one of the few who know Diluc is the Darknight Hero, and Diluc says they can ask him for help. Huffman remains suspicious but without proof.

The slime bait trick is recalled by Paimon in the Astrolabos Chapter, which lists this act as a prerequisite.

Placement: Unlocked after Song of the Dragon and Freedom (Prologue, Act III); the wiki lists no Adventure Rank requirement. Released in 1.0.

650.content: The Darknight Hero is the rumoured vigilante of Mondstadt: a wealthy Vision-wielding fighter, not a Knight of Favonius, who acts at night against Abyss Order forces. Townsfolk do not know the Hero's identity. In the Noctua Chapter the Traveler learns it is Diluc, who keeps the secret with help from his winery staff and the Traveler.

651.content:
Of Ballads and Brews (also: Of Ballads and Brews event, Sounds From Afar, Bonds of Melody, Aroma of the Past, Weinlesefest event): Of Ballads and Brews was a Version 3.1 flagship event (29 September to 17 October 2022) set during Mondstadt's autumn Weinlesefest. The main story follows Razor, the wolf-raised boy, after the Knights of Favonius pass him a box his parents left behind. It holds a bottle of Thousand-Wind Wine, Mondstadt's oldest and rarest style. With the Traveler and Paimon, and with help from Klee, Bennett, Rosaria, Noelle, Sucrose, Diluc, Diona, Lisa, Kaeya and Venti, Razor brews his own bottle, buries it at Windrise, and drinks a toast at the festival's Windcoming Day.

Beside the story the event ran harvest-season activities (boar expulsion, a Knights' charity stall, gift hampers). The story is warm and family-themed, reusing known characters in small supporting roles.

Plot: Act I (Sounds From Afar). With the harvest season busy, the Traveler and Paimon finish Guild errands with Katheryne. Jean summons the Knights: a letter from Grand Master Varka, read aloud by Mika, says his expedition is going well, mentions that the Fatui Harbinger "the Captain" has helped rather than harmed them, and wishes everyone a good Weinlesefest. A private note for Lisa asks the Knights to give Razor a box his parents left. Told in Wolvendom, Razor is torn but decides to see his teacher Lisa. The box contains a woolen hand puppet, a part from a Ruin Guard and a bottle of Thousand-Wind Wine. Venti, consulted at the festival, can only offer a song and tells them to try brewing it themselves.

Act II (Bonds of Melody). Paimon and the Traveler read Venti's song as a clue: the wine should carry traits of the three organising institutions: an explorer's courage (Adventurers' Guild), a love tender and true (Church of Favonius) and a defender's will (Knights of Favonius). Klee, freed from confinement for the festival, joins to help Razor find his "mommy"; Bennett brings a Small Lamp Grass as the Guild's ingredient. After they rescue a fruit cart from hilichurls, Rosaria presents a Mist Flower Corolla for the Church and bluntly tells Razor that his parents' story may not be happy. At the Dawn Winery Diluc agrees, after Kaeya's persuasion, to supply a barrel.

Act III (Aroma of the Past). Noelle and Sucrose give the Knights' ingredient, a Sunsettia improved by Sucrose's bio-alchemy ("Quadruple-Sweetness Sunsettia"). At Angel's Share the group collects the barrel and Diona mixes the brew after a misunderstanding about Razor wanting to drink. Under the great tree at Windrise, Venti gives dandelion seeds as the last ingredient to capture the wind's memory and says Thousand-Wind Wine is the original dandelion wine, tasting different each time because people add what they like. They bury the barrel there; Razor promises to open it with everyone when he is grown. On Windcoming Day Venti sings "Thousand-Wind Wine"; the wind rises, and Razor, smelling his parents' bottle, sees a vision of two adventurers on a cliff, who decided to save it for their son and chose the name Razor.

Act II includes Rosaria's reasoning that the town's friendly people are too "sunny and bright" to give Razor a darker, more realistic perspective, and Paimon's observation that she is more thoughtful than she looks. Act III has Klee anxious that the Anemo Archon has not come; Paimon reassures her that Barbatos can appear in many forms, and Razor says he feels the Archon's blessing because he has grown and is no longer afraid.

The three ingredient sources come together as a patchwork of gifts: Bennett's lamp grass, Rosaria's flower, Noelle and Sucrose's fruit and Venti's seeds. Bennett and Klee also bring wines borrowed from Bennett's fathers and Albedo as an offering, which they hope will persuade the Archon to help Razor's cause. The vision of Razor's parents is brief and silent about their identity beyond their roles as adventurers who found the wine incomplete.

Revelations: Razor's parents left a box with a woolen puppet, a Ruin Guard part and a bottle of Thousand-Wind Wine, which the Knights have held for him. Thousand-Wind Wine is the first and rarest wine Mondstadt learned to make, and its character depends on whatever the brewer adds. A vision shows his parents as adventurers who called their wine unfinished and gave their son the name Razor. Details of their lives remain unknown.

Varka's request about the box reaches Lisa as a message on the back of his letter to the Knights; he is away on his expedition. Rosaria's remark, as the wiki summarises it, treats Varka as a father figure to both her and Razor.

Characters: Razor is the central figure; he is hesitant but warm. Klee and Bennett support him; Rosaria is blunt but kind; Lisa, his teacher, anchors the Knights' side; Noelle and Sucrose, Diluc, Diona and Kaeya provide the ingredients and logistics; Venti is the wine's guide and the singer of the closing song. Jean convenes the Knights and Mika reads Varka's letter.

Marcel, a merchant, asks for help finding his fruit cart in Act II. Draff hunts with Razor in Wolvendom in Act I. Other phases feature Clemens and Leah, who are not part of the Razor storyline.

Consequences: The bottle Razor brewed remains buried under Windrise's great tree, to be opened with his friends when he grows up. Razor now has his parents' bottle and a vision of them. No plot beyond the festival is affected.

Placement: Released in Version 3.1, 29 September to 17 October 2022, with the gift collection open until 24 October. The requirements were Adventure Rank 21, the Prologue Archon Quest and the Lupus Minor Chapter's first act. The story is set during Weinlesefest in Mondstadt and refers to Varka's expedition as still under way.

Gameplay: Labelled game content: the four phases were Autumn Crisis (expelling and capturing boars, including the Great Snowboar King), Highwind Trial (battling with Sublime Anemograna), Charity and Creativity (running a Knights' stall) and Fecund Blessings (finding gift hampers). Festive Fever points earned the Missive Windspear, a four-star polearm, and its refinement material.

652.comment: Of Ballads and Brews: Thousand-Wind Wine
652.content:
According to the event, Thousand-Wind Wine is the first and rarest wine that Mondstadters learned to make, and the many techniques involved mean each brew tastes different. Venti says it is the original dandelion wine, and that people have always been free to add what they like. In the event Razor's version takes an explorer's courage, a love tender and true, a defender's will and, last, dandelion seeds meant to capture the wind's memory.

The bottle left by Razor's parents is, in Lisa's reading, a bottle they brewed themselves.

653.comment: Of Ballads and Brews: Razor's parents' box
653.content: Varka asks that Razor be given a wooden box left by his parents. It holds a hand puppet of wool, a Ruin Guard part and a bottle of Thousand-Wind Wine. The bottle's smell later brings Razor a vision of two adventurers sharing the wine on a cliff, agreeing to save it for their son and giving him the name Razor. Their names and fate remain unknown.

654.comment: Of Ballads and Brews: Windcoming Day toast
654.content: At the festival market, everyone toasts after Venti performs "Thousand-Wind Wine". Klee is sad that no wind comes at first; later the breeze rises and Venti, winking at the Traveler, summons his powers. Townsfolk are shown spending time with families or remembering family figures.

655.content:
Of Drink A-Dreaming (also: Bartender Academy Week, Bartender's Academy Week, Angel's Share bartender event): Luka, who is running Bartender Academy Week, offers the Traveler and Paimon the run of the tavern's ingredients and unlimited refills as long as they are not wasteful, plus rewards when guests are happy. The bartender Charles teaches the basics and explains that beginners are no longer given alcoholic ingredients after an earlier student's mix knocked a customer out. Over three days friends from across Teyvat come to the counter, each with an order and a conversation, and a later Bartender Challenge tests the Traveler's skill. In the Afterword Luka offers them a job, which they decline to keep travelling together.

Requirements were Adventure Rank 28, the Interlude Chapter Act I The Crane Returns on the Wind, and Eula's Story Quest Aphros Delos Chapter Act I; during the event the Story Quest's Adventure Rank requirement was lowered to 28 and needed no Story Key. The event could not be completed in Co-Op Mode.

Plot: In the opening quest Luka greets the Traveler outside Angel's Share and pitches Bartender Academy Week, which is optional. Inside, Charles trains them on a first drink, warns that customers have special requests and says conversation matters as much as mixing. The Traveler then serves guests in seven Tavern Tales: Kaeya and Rosaria; Diluc; Jean and Lisa; Zhongli; Eula; Beidou and Ningguang; and Shenhe. After the event ends, Luka thanks them in the Afterword: business has boomed, most customers came for the Traveler, and he asks whether they would stay and work there.

When They Take Off Their Armor: Kaeya teases by ordering a Death After Noon, then asks for a large Moonlit Alley while Rosaria takes a small tea. Rosaria says tea reminds her of a church event she missed, when Sister Barbara saved her tea and dessert. Fine Wine From Yesterday: Diluc asks for a Gray Valley Sunset and says it was the first drink he ever mixed, when his father Crepus gave him ingredients with no instructions and he simply made a fruit punch. Dandelion, Rose, and Windwheel Aster: Lisa has dragged Jean to the tavern to relax; Lisa orders a medium extra-sweet Love Poem and Jean a medium coffee to keep her awake. Surrounded by the Aroma of Tea: Zhongli orders a strong Misty Garden and explains tea tasting to Paimon: look at the colour, smell, then sip.

Solid Ice, Soluble in Wine: Eula, after drinking at The Cat's Tail, orders a small Foamy Reef; Paimon has the Traveler water it down. Eula says her family name keeps her from being welcome in Mondstadt's taverns and asks how the Traveler makes so many friends. Docked on a Moonlit Night: Ningguang and Beidou, on a casual holiday, order a small sour Birch Sap and a large Dusk. Beidou teases Ningguang about having once sold fruit on the street and mentions her own ordinary fishing-village origins, and each invites the Traveler to bartend for them. Untainted Autumn Frost: Shenhe came after Zhongli gave her directions; puzzled by drink names, she is served a Snow-Covered Kiss and relates it to watching a sprout break through the soil. The Afterword ends with Luka inviting them back with friends.

Revelations: The Tavern Tales add small character moments rather than plot. Diluc recalls inventing Gray Valley Sunset as a boy; Rosaria's dislike of tea comes from a church memory; Eula admits she usually drinks alone because of her family name; Beidou teases Ningguang about her early days as a fruit seller, which Ningguang declines to dwell on; Zhongli puts his bill on the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor's tab; and Jean and Lisa discuss Jean's difficulty relaxing.

Diluc says his father gave no comment on the fruit punch at the time and notes he never thought about it afterwards. Jean concedes that learning to relax may be her biggest challenge and says she may come back. Eula says she wants to write down what the Traveler told her and Paimon predicts she may threaten them to forget it.

Characters: Luka (event-exclusive, runs the Academy Week) and Charles (bartender at Angel's Share) frame the event. The Tavern Tales guests are Kaeya and Rosaria, Diluc, Jean and Lisa, Zhongli, Eula, Beidou and Ningguang, and Shenhe. Paimon helps the Traveler throughout.

Each guest is written in character: Kaeya teasing, Rosaria dry and fond of drinks over talk, Diluc brief and a little wry, Lisa relaxed and Jean dutiful, Zhongli patient and traditional, Eula guarded until tipsy, Beidou and Ningguang friendly and competitive, and Shenhe literal and curious.

Consequences: The event does not change the main story. It leaves a standing invitation from Luka and Charles to visit Angel's Share, and Diluc says he wants to give the Traveler something once they have more bartending experience. Gameplay rewards include the furnishing Tavern Shaker: Grumous Oscillation and the namecard Celebration: Binge Vessel.

Placement: Released in Version 2.5, with entry after Interlude Chapter Act I and Eula's Aphros Delos Chapter Act I. The wiki does not date it in-world, so treat it as a light interlude with the Traveler and Paimon travelling together in Mondstadt.

Gameplay: Game mechanics, not in-world fact. Drinks are made from a foundation (Coffee, Tea or Juice) plus flavourings (Milk, Cocoa Paste, Fizzy Water, Caramel, Lemon, Mint); each basic recipe uses three ingredients and special requests add extra of the matching ingredient. A mixing minigame and a pouring-size check decide the result. On the fourth day the Bartender Challenge and further recipes unlock once all Tavern Tales are done.

The wiki lists 21 named recipes, among them Athenaeum, Barbatos' Boon, Birch Sap, Boreal Watch, Brightcrown, Caramel Pinecone, Dawning Dew, Dusk, Foamy Reef, Golden Eden, Gray Valley Sunset, Laughter and Cheer, Love Poem, Misty Garden, Moonlit Alley, Night of Swirling Stars, Scholar's Afternoon, Snow-Covered Kiss, Stroke of Night, Sweet Cider Lake and Tart Brilliance. Total rewards come to 420 Primogems and 460,000 Mora among other items.

656.comment: Of Drink A-Dreaming: Bartender Academy Week
656.content:
