In March 2022 Angel's Share, Mondstadt's tavern run by Dawn Winery, held a Bartender Academy Week hosted by Luka. Participants had access to the tavern's ingredients, with unlimited refills if they were not wasteful, and no alcohol for beginners. The Traveler and Paimon took part.

Charles trained them. Luka later said the week brought the best business he had seen and offered them jobs, which Paimon declined to keep travelling.

657.content: The seven Tavern Tales are the event's guest stories: When They Take Off Their Armor (Kaeya and Rosaria), Fine Wine From Yesterday (Diluc), Dandelion, Rose, and Windwheel Aster (Jean and Lisa), Surrounded by the Aroma of Tea (Zhongli), Solid Ice, Soluble in Wine (Eula), Docked on a Moonlit Night (Beidou and Ningguang) and Untainted Autumn Frost (Shenhe).

658.content: An event-exclusive NPC who organised Bartender Academy Week outside Angel's Share. He recruits the Traveler and Paimon, and later offers them jobs at the tavern.

key: Of Fading Flowers and Falling Feathers
659.comment: Of Fading Flowers and Falling Feathers
659.content:
Of Fading Flowers and Falling Feathers (also: Flower-Feather Clan Tribal Chronicle, The Wingless One of Tlalocan, The Night Before the Trial, Guns and Wings): The Flower-Feather Clan's Tribal Chronicles chapter and Chasca's story. The tribe's Qucusaur Rider trials have left many applicants "Wingless", and a merchant caravan arrives with Phlogiston Wings, jetpacks powered by phlogiston. When a wild qucusaur, Chasca's old "sister" Coya, starts attacking merchants, Chasca and the Traveler discover that a plot to harvest phlogiston from captive qucusaurs is being run by Allpa, a trusted member of the tribe.

The chapter has three acts, all released in Version 5.2: The Wingless One of Tlalocan, The Night Before the Trial and Guns and Wings, the last needing the Archon Quest act The Rainbow Destined to Burn. Guns and Wings has three quests: Tracks Through the Wilderness, Mortal Pursuit and Time for the Showdown. The chapter shows Chasca's mixed identity as a human raised by qucusaurs and her ties to her adoptive father Cusco and her qucusaur mother and sister.

The chapter weighs technology that replaces a bond with the qucusaurs against the bond itself: the Wings lower the bar for flight but are made from qucusaur phlogiston, and the people most hurt by the tribe's losses in the Abyss war are the ones most tempted to replace the riders' old ways.

Plot: In Act I Chasca keeps watch over Coyllur, a Qucusaur Rider applicant who failed her trial and is at risk of becoming one of the Wingless. The Traveler cheers her up by indwelling a qucusaur, and Chasca's adoptive father Cusco asks the Traveler to persuade Chasca to take care of herself. In Act II, before the retried trial, merchants led by Isidore arrive after being attacked by a qucusaur and show the Phlogiston Wings they carry. Chasca finds a bloodstained feather she recognises. In Act III the applicants try the Wings, a qucusaur attacks the merchants again, and Chasca recognises it as her "sister" Coya. They trace the wings to a hidden airborne workshop attributed to a man named Tepal and find that Allpa, who helps run the trials, is the mastermind. The workshop is destroyed and Coya, with whom Chasca had fallen out long ago, has forgiven her.

**The Wingless One of Tlalocan (5.2).** The Traveler and Paimon hear whistling in the Flower-Feather village and find Coyllur, who has just failed the Qucusaur Rider tests. Chasca explains that applicants must be skilled in combat and win a qucusaur's approval, and that those who fail too often give up and are called the "Wingless". The Traveler indwells a qucusaur to lift Coyllur's mood. Allpa announces the tests will be redone because the arena was not properly inspected. Chasca says she could tell the qucusaur was the Traveler because, being raised by qucusaurs, she knows they would not be so flustered. Cusco arrives; he says Chasca skips her checkups and has been different since Chuychu's death, and that he does not want to lose another daughter.

**The Night Before the Trial (5.2).** Chasca helps staff prepare the trial arena. A merchant, Isidore, begs for help after his caravan is attacked by a qucusaur. When they arrive Allpa is already there and says the qucusaur fled; the goods, the Phlogiston Wings, are undamaged. Chasca picks up a bloodstained feather that she appears to recognise.

**Tracks Through the Wilderness (5.2).** The applicants are now using the Wings, handheld-trackball jetpacks; Coyllur and Zhunan like them while Mukki feels they are cheating. Chasca wants to change the standards for Wing users, and Allpa says that would take too long after the tribe's losses in the invasion. The qucusaur returns and attacks the merchants; Chasca realises it is her sister Coya. Chasca's qucusaur "mom", Chimpu, tells them Coya had not visited in a while and brings them to Coya's nest on the edge of Ochkanatlan. Coya says humans have taken her child. Isidore's merchants ensnare Coya and Chimpu; during the fight Chasca throws his malfunctioning trackball into the sea, where it explodes. Isidore says a man named Tepal hired him and that the trackballs run on phlogiston drawn from qucusaurs. Allpa says Tepal was a Children of Echoes member who failed to become a rider.

**Mortal Pursuit (5.2).** Xilonen helps trace Tepal; his relative Puma says she had disowned him and hands over his tattered notes. They suggest his workshop is powered by a relic from Ochkanatlan, the balloon seen near the trial site. Mutota is exasperated that Och-Kan keeps sowing discord. The party seals all vents but the top one in the trial area so pressurised phlogiston catapults them into the workshop, with Coya following.

**Time for the Showdown (5.2).** In the workshop they free captive qucusaurs and learn from Puma's note that Tepal died long ago and someone used his name. The mastermind is Allpa, who, the wiki says, turned against qucusaurs on learning of her son's death and believed only humans should shape Natlan's future. She threatens a qucusaur chick, Chime, to make them surrender; Coya rams her, the relic becomes unstable and Chasca throws it away. It explodes and Coya shields Chasca, then collapses. The workshop is dismantled, part of it becomes a jail for Allpa and her lackeys, and Cusco tells Chasca to speak with Coya, who has forgiven her.

Finer points. The Wings were being tested as a new entry method, and Allpa told Chasca that changing the standards would take too long to put into practice. Chasca asked the party to hide when they reached Coya's nest, believing an unannounced human presence would make matters worse. Isidore believed Tepal wanted qucusaurs alive. After the explosion at the end Cusco examines Coya and says her old injuries, plus an outburst of energy, made her collapse; he adds that his wife had written from the Masters of the Night-Wind scolding him for his inaction. Mutota says he is upset the plot was not caught sooner, because many qucusaurs were hurt. Chasca's plan at the end tells Coya to act as in old times.

Revelations: The Phlogiston Wings are made with phlogiston drawn from captured qucusaurs. "Tepal" was a front; the real mastermind is Allpa, who helps run the trials; Tepal himself had died long before. Coya's attacks were defence of her stolen chick.

The wiki summary says Allpa had aimed to use unruly qucusaurs for production and to overthrow the chief, Mutota, with her lackeys. Puma's note and Tepal's disorganised journal are what exposed the deception.

Characters: Chasca is the lead and the chapter's emotional centre. Cusco is her adoptive father; Chimpu and Coya are the qucusaurs who raised her and her sister. Allpa is trusted organiser and villain, Mutota the tribe's chief, Coyllur, Zhunan and Mukki the applicants, Isidore the merchant, Puma Tepal's relative. Xilonen helps trace Tepal.

Chasca's behaviour mirrors the qucusaurs, which is how she notices the Traveler's indwelling; she tends to hide her own hurt behind duty. The chapter also puts weight on the death of Chuychu and its effect on Chasca and her tribe.

Consequences: Allpa and her followers are jailed in a part of the dismantled workshop. Captive qucusaurs are freed, though some drained of phlogiston still need rescue. Coya is injured saving Chasca but recovers, and the two reconcile. The tribe still has to decide how the Wings fit into the riders' future.

Placement: Released entirely in Version 5.2. Acts I and II need only the Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame quest, but Act III requires The Rainbow Destined to Burn, so it takes place after the Abyss invasion and Chuychu's death.

660.comment: Of Fading Flowers and Falling Feathers: Phlogiston Wings
660.content: A phlogiston-powered jetpack operated by a handheld trackball, brought to the Flower-Feather Clan by merchants. Using them, "Wingless" applicants can fly without a qucusaur. They are made with phlogiston drawn from captive qucusaurs.

661.comment: Of Fading Flowers and Falling Feathers: Qucusaur Rider Trials
661.content: The Flower-Feather Clan's entry test. Applicants need combat skill and the approval of a qucusaur; those who repeatedly fail may give up and are known as the Wingless.

662.comment: Of Fading Flowers and Falling Feathers: Allpa
662.content: A Flower-Feather Clan member who helps run the Qucusaur Rider trials and, after learning of her son's death (per the wiki summary), is revealed as the mastermind behind capturing qucusaurs for phlogiston. She is arrested after the workshop is destroyed.

663.comment: Of Fading Flowers and Falling Feathers: Coya and Chimpu
663.content: Chimpu is the qucusaur who raised Chasca; Coya is her qucusaur daughter, whom Chasca calls her sister. After Chasca was returned to human society they drifted apart; Coya attacked the merchants because humans took her chick, Chime. She forgives Chasca.

664.comment: Of Fading Flowers and Falling Feathers: Of Fading Flowers and Falling Feathers Event Window
664.content: The Tribal Chronicles event ran from 2024-11-20 to 2024-12-10 with extra rewards for completing the chapter. The story remains available.

665.content:
Of the Land Amidst Monoliths (also: Chapter I Act I, Liyue Archon Quest Act I): Chapter I Act I of the Archon Quest, set in Liyue. The Traveler and Paimon reach Liyue Harbor in search of the Geo Archon at the annual Rite of Descension, only to see Rex Lapis fall from the clouds apparently dead. Suspected by association, they are rescued by the Fatui Harbinger Childe and told to seek the adepti at Jueyun Karst.

The act has four stages: Rite of Descension, An Impromptu Change of Plan, three quests that can be done in any order (Wangshu, Moulder of Mountains, Custodian of Clouds), and Dust to Dust. It introduces Liyue's reverence for its god, the Liyue Qixing, the Millelith, the Fatui presence in the harbor, and the hidden adepti. Released in version 1.0.

Tonally it moves from festival to panic to a tour of Liyue's mountains, with a recurring contrast between Liyue, whose god is present, and Mondstadt, whose god is not. The adepti scenes turn on contract-like bargains (a sigil of permission, food offerings) rather than combat.

Plot: Venti has told the Traveler that Rex Lapis will appear in Liyue for the Rite of Descension. In Liyue Harbor the rite begins and Ningguang summons the god, but he drops lifeless onto the offering table and she orders the exits sealed. The Traveler is chased by the Millelith, rescued by Childe, and given a sigil to reach the adepti in Jueyun Karst.

**Rite of Descension.** Paimon explains that the Geo Archon is called Rex Lapis by Liyue's own people, since using the name Morax is considered impolite for outsiders. Locals such as Linlang, Guanhai and Bolai describe the yearly rite, in which the god gives guidance on Liyue's coming year, and send the pair to Yujing Terrace. They make wishes at the censers, then watch as Ningguang, who presides, calls the god down. As the clouds part, Rex Lapis's lifeless body crashes onto the offering table, and Ningguang declares that he has been killed and the exits must be sealed. The Millelith seize those who stood near the terrace. The Traveler tries to slip away but steps on a broken tile and is spotted. A Hydro user cuts down the guards and leads them off; he calls himself Childe, asks whether they met Signora in Mondstadt, and Paimon recognises him as a Fatui Harbinger. He says he had heard of their deeds in Mondstadt, kept his eye on them throughout the rite and so knows they did not do it, and sends them to the Northland Bank, where he gives them a Sigil of Permission and points them toward Jueyun Karst, the supposed home of the adepti.

**An Impromptu Change of Plan.** In Jueyun Karst the pair meet Moon Carver, who recognises the sigil. Millelith soldiers pursue them in, and Moon Carver tells the Traveler to see them gone; the Traveler fights them off. Told that Rex Lapis was killed at the rite and the Qixing are blaming onlookers, he is outraged, accepts that the accusation against the Traveler is unjust, and tells them to find Mountain Shaper and Cloud Retainer in the karst and the Conqueror of Demons, a guardian yaksha, at Wangshu Inn.

**Wangshu.** At the inn Xiao, the Conqueror of Demons, is irritable and leaves. The innkeeper Verr Goldet says he is an adeptus who likes almond tofu. The inn's chef is too frightened to cook because a ghost haunts the inn; the pair follow the ghost, which possesses a Ruin Hunter, and defeat it, and she agrees to stop haunting the chef as long as the Traveler keeps playing with her. With almond tofu and a salad they catch up with Xiao, who is shocked to hear of the death and explains that the ghost is a lingering innocent spirit he had asked the inn to look after.

**Moulder of Mountains.** On Mt. Hulao a man begs the adepti to spare his brother, who has been encased in amber. The Traveler frees the brother, and Mountain Shaper appears, angry that a "thief" was freed. It explains that it plants karst flowers to protect the mountain's calm, treats trespassers as thieves, and encases those who step on the flowers; it then learns of Rex Lapis's death.

**Custodian of Clouds.** At Mt. Aocang the pair lay out dishes at a stone table as offerings. Cloud Retainer lets them into its domain on condition that they cross its puzzles. On hearing of the death it is furious and vows to destroy Liyue for the crime; the Traveler calms it by framing the offered food as a contract, which it reluctantly accepts.

**Dust to Dust.** Back at Liyue Harbor, Childe tells them the Qixing will not let anyone pay respects to the Exuvia, because the killer is still unfound. He explains that the Geo Archon is also an adeptus, Prime of the Adepti and the God of Contracts, and that the adepti signed contracts to protect Liyue and may act if the Qixing fail. Paimon lets slip that the Traveler is looking for the Seven; Childe promises to find someone who can break the stalemate and tells them to stay alive until they next meet.

The three adepti quests can be done in any order, and Childe's closing lines differ slightly if the Traveler has not met all of them. The three adepti respond to the news in different ways: Xiao with shock, Mountain Shaper with concern for its mountain, and Cloud Retainer with threats that are talked down.

Revelations: Rex Lapis appears to have been assassinated at the Rite of Descension.

Childe is a Fatui Harbinger who had heard of the Traveler's deeds in Mondstadt and watched them throughout the rite. The adepti exist and are real. Rex Lapis is also an adeptus, the Prime of the Adepti, bound by contract with the other adepti to Liyue's protection. The Liyue Qixing are keeping the body out of sight.

Childe says the Qixing have always been overly suspicious of the Fatui and that he is no fan of Signora; later he trades what he knows about the Exuvia for the Traveler's report on the adepti, calling it a returning gift. The act does not say who is responsible for the death.

The wish-making at the censers, the sigil and the later food offerings all show the act treating offerings and agreements as the working currency between mortals and adepti.

Characters: Traveler and Paimon; Ningguang; Childe (Tartaglia); Moon Carver; Xiao.

Also Mountain Shaper, Cloud Retainer, Verr Goldet of Wangshu Inn, the inn's chef Smiley Yanxiao and its ghost, the brothers Li Ding and Li Dang on Mt. Hulao, and harbor locals including Linlang, Guanhai, Bolai, Ivanovich, Changshun, Gentry De'an, Fan Er'ye and Jifang. Venti is the one who sent the Traveler to Liyue.

Consequences: The Traveler is wanted by the Millelith and has accepted Childe's help; Childe promises to find someone who can break the stalemate over the Exuvia. The next act, Farewell, Archaic Lord, begins with that help.

The adepti now know of Rex Lapis's death and are angry, and the Traveler leaves with the sigil and the goodwill of the three they have met.

The act's last scene sets the Traveler's quest to find the Seven against the Exuvia's confinement: Paimon's slip means Childe now knows why they are in Liyue.

Placement: Chapter I Act I, after Song of the Dragon and Freedom (the Mondstadt story) and before Act II, Farewell, Archaic Lord. Released in version 1.0. The quest requires completing the Mondstadt story and Adventure Rank 23.

666.comment: Of the Land Amidst Monoliths: Rite of Descension
666.content: An annual ceremony at Yujing Terrace in which the Liyue Qixing's Tianquan, as presider, calls on Rex Lapis to give the year's economic guidance. Last year's request was made by the Yuheng, and Bolai recalls seventeen predictions from it. In the quest, the god falls dead.

667.comment: Of the Land Amidst Monoliths: Sigil of Permission
667.content: Childe hands over a sigil at Northland Bank, saying only that it keeps the adepti from harming its bearer. Moon Carver recognises it and says many seasons have passed since one was last seen.

668.comment: Of the Land Amidst Monoliths: Jueyun Karst adepti encounters
668.content: Moon Carver tells the Traveler to look for Mountain Shaper, Cloud Retainer and the Conqueror of Demons. Xiao is shocked and says he will seek out the other adepti, Mountain Shaper is mostly concerned with its flowers, and Cloud Retainer threatens Liyue before accepting a contract for the food offerings.

key: Old Notes and New Friends World Quest series
669.content:
Old Notes and New Friends (also: Old Notes and New Friends World Quest series, Dual Evidence, Soheil's Wish, Invisible Barrier, Hidden Mercenaries, Desert's Remembrance): Old Notes and New Friends is a world quest series in the Great Red Sand, Sumeru, added in version 3.1 as a follow-up to Golden Slumber. In Aaru Village the Traveler and Paimon meet two Vahumana researchers, Kalantari and Soheil. Soheil dismisses the Traveler's desert finds until the Traveler enters King Deshret's Mausoleum and brings back proof, then sends them to check the ruins in his old notes.

The series has two main quests, Dual Evidence and Soheil's Wish, and Soheil's Wish branches into three exploration quests: Invisible Barrier, Hidden Mercenaries and Desert's Remembrance. It is light in tone: the slates the Traveler brings back turn out to hold leave requests, a love poem and a fable, and the story pokes gentle fun at Akademiya paper-writing culture while also showing real pressure on its researchers.

The series follows on from Golden Slumber, where the Traveler helped the young researcher Tirzad on a desert expedition. Completing Dual Evidence permanently turns off the cyclone over the Mausoleum of King Deshret and opens Aaru's Shut for good.

Plot: Dual Evidence. Back in Aaru Village, the Traveler and Paimon are approached by Kalantari, a student of the Akademiya who has read Tirzad's new paper on the late period of Al-Ahmar's civilization, in which the two are thanked as a gift from the desert. Kalantari hopes to get inspiration for his own stalled paper and offers to hire them as guides. Before they can begin, the older researcher Soheil of the Usaibia family arrives with a Corps of Thirty escort, Hulwani, to send young scholars back: the sage fears they will alert the matra or damage the ruins, and Soheil says forty-six leave applications arrived after Tirzad's paper appeared. Soheil sends Kalantari home but stays himself, and tells the Traveler and Paimon that he suspects Tirzad invented his account. Stung, they find the stone slate Tirzad left glowing and head into the Mausoleum. They light the three ritual sites, activate the great device in the Great Hall of Truths, and defeat a Primal Construct at the top of the Mausoleum. They return with a new slate. Soheil's attitude flips, and he apologises on behalf of himself and his family.

Soheil's Wish. Soheil keeps the slate and, because the sage forbids researchers to enter the desert but has said nothing against gifts, hands the Traveler his old archaeology notes as a "present". The notes point to three places, and the Traveler brings back the slates found at each.

Dual Evidence in more detail. Kalantari is a student from a Port Ormos merchant family, who likes to say he is unlike researchers who cannot talk to people. Soheil calls the youngsters impetuous and doubts Tirzad's account for specific reasons: he has visited the desert in his youth and never found the Khemenu Temple or Khaj-Nisut named in the paper, and the sandstorm above the Mausoleum looks as it always did. The Traveler works through the slate's guidance: the new inscription says that to ascend to Aaru one must "peck three organs" and cross the underworld river as a falcon, so the Traveler clears the Place of Rebirth, the Place of Breath and the Place of Swallowing. These three ruins unlock the Great Hall of Truths, where four plinths open the way to a device and the slate asks for three embers of the sun to be burned. Lighting the three Primal Torches carries the Traveler to the roof, where a Primal Construct is defeated and a chest yields the Record of Aaru's Shut.

The three exploration quests. Invisible Barrier: the Traveler enters four transparent ruins marked in the notes, which Soheil had never been able to enter, and finds three slates. Soheil reads them as leave requests whose excuses resemble those of modern students, and plans a paper on the perception of days off in different societies. Hidden Mercenaries: near Lamb-Devourer Rock the notes describe Eremites of Thutmose appearing and vanishing. The Traveler follows a patrolling Eremite, overhears the password to a hidden door (Marg bar parvezravan), and reaches the secret base; the slate there is a love poem, which Soheil would send to the scholars of Haravatat for a paper on rhetoric and civilization. Desert's Remembrance: the Tomb of Carouses is a smaller version of the Mausoleum, and its slate is an animal fable that Soheil bends into a short paper on the retreat of sheep and environmental change.

Ending. After all three are done, Soheil explains why he wants to enter the Mausoleum himself: he wants to be a candidate to become a sage, who hold power over researchers. When Paimon quotes the line from his old notes about mockery being easier to bear than having no progress in knowledge, Soheil, who has forgotten writing it, asks to take his notes back, saying it is a pleasant reminder of when he was younger.

Soheil's Old Notes (an item given in Soheil's Wish) cover about forty-six days. The writer records a month recording everything outside the Mausoleum without entering, the legend that spring water would burst from a long-dried well and shatter the barrier, the discovery of four transparent ruins that repelled approach, and the cone-shaped Tomb of Carouses. On the 46th day an archaeology team was attacked by Eremites calling themselves Thutmose, led by two young men; one wanted to kill the party, the other stopped him. He decided to return to the Akademiya to face ridicule, hoped the second Eremite's axe would stay sharp, noted that sheep vanish near Lamb-Devourer Rock, and wrote that being mocked was not as painful as having no improvement in knowledge. The note also suggests Thutmose may hide in rock formations or a hidden cave. In the Thutmose base, Soheil remarks that Thutmose managed to rob him despite his precautions.

Smaller beats. Paimon wonders after Jeht and Tirzad when she arrives. Using Nahida's All Schemes to Know gives short private thoughts for Soheil and Hulwani at various points; Hulwani privately wants to return to Sumeru City. Soheil's change of attitude is abrupt enough that Paimon compares him to a Liyue storyteller. Soheil cannot go into the desert himself because of the sage's ban, and Hulwani eventually allows the Traveler to go because the ban applies to researchers.

Gameplay notes, labelled as such: Dual Evidence includes a boss fight (Field Annihilation Array) and a puzzle chain in each of three ruins. Invisible Barrier and Desert's Remembrance may be partly completed before the quest begins and the dialogue plays out as if new.

Revelations: - The Mausoleum of King Deshret can be entered and cleared by following a stone slate left from Golden Slumber; its inner structure includes the Great Hall of Truths and a roof reached by an elevator.
- The late-period records of Al-Ahmar's civilization have mostly been lost, so a complete slate is an unprecedented find for Vahumana, according to Soheil.
- Soheil's real motive is ambition: he wants a sage's seat, and he admits the gap between researcher and sage is like that between a hilichurl and a slime.

- Eremites of Thutmose are a group of Deshret believers who operate near Lamb-Devourer Rock and had a hidden base behind a password-locked door.
- The transparent ruins, the Thutmose base and the Tomb of Carouses each contain a stone slate whose text is mundane (leave requests, a love poem, a fable). Soheil does not draw any larger conclusion from them.
- A slate mentions Aaru in a construction-log style text, but no one confirms how this relates to Aaru Village.

Characters: The Traveler and Paimon; Kalantari, a student and Vahumana researcher (a quest-only NPC); Soheil Usaibia, an older Vahumana researcher; Hulwani of the Corps of Thirty; and mentions of Tirzad, Jeht and the sage. Thutmose Eremites appear in Hidden Mercenaries.

Consequences: The cyclone above the Mausoleum is permanently turned off and Aaru's Shut becomes permanently accessible. Soheil changes from scornful to grateful and gives the Traveler repeated gifts of friendship.

Placement: Requires Golden Slumber to be finished and the next day's reset. Released in 3.1. Dual Evidence comes first, then Soheil's Wish, which has three exploration quests that can be done in any order and may be done in advance.

670.comment: Old Notes and New Friends: Soheil
670.content:
Soheil Usaibia is an older Vahumana researcher of the Usaibia family. He was sent to Aaru Village to stop young scholars going into the desert, is dismissive of Tirzad's paper at first, then becomes warm once shown evidence. He covets a sage's position and openly says why. He is conscious of his age and the time left to him.

He keeps his dignity by relying on forms: he cannot enter the desert, but he can accept a "gift". His rediscovered old notes remind him of why he took up research.

671.comment: Old Notes and New Friends: Kalantari
671.content: Kalantari is a student of the Akademiya from a family of merchants in Port Ormos. He has read Tirzad's paper and wants help getting out of a creative block. He is friendly, talkative and gets sent back to Sumeru City by Soheil in Dual Evidence. He is a quest-only NPC.

672.comment: Old Notes and New Friends: Thutmose
672.content: Thutmose is a group of Eremites in the desert who describe themselves as fanatical believers in Deshret in Soheil's old notes. The notes record two young leaders, one aggressive and one merciful. In Hidden Mercenaries their base is a hidden location near Lamb-Devourer Rock behind a door that opens to a spoken password.

673.comment: Old Notes and New Friends: Mausoleum slates
673.content: Stone slates are the quest items of the series. The Scarlet Sand Slate gives instructions in stages for the Mausoleum. The slates in the transparent ruins, in the Thutmose base and in the Tomb of Carouses hold, respectively, leave requests, a love poem and a fable, according to Soheil.

674.content:
Omnipresence Over Mortals (also: Chapter II Act III, Sword, Fish, Resistance, Duel Before the Throne, The Omnipresent God): Omnipresence Over Mortals is the third act of Chapter II of the Archon Quests, set in Inazuma and released in Version 2.1. The Traveler joins the Watatsumi Army's Resistance as captain of a special unit, discovers that the Fatui are the Resistance's secret sponsor and are supplying life-draining Delusions, and loses the soldier Teppei to them. With Yae Miko's help, the Traveler exposes Kujou Takayuki's betrayal, defeats Signora in a duel before the Shogun, and then fights the Raiden Shogun in the Plane of Euthymia, where the true Ei agrees to abolish the Vision Hunt Decree.

The act has nine quests, from Sword, Fish, Resistance to Wishes. It combines the war's resolution, the unmasking of the Shogun as a puppet made by Ei, the death of Signora, and the loss of the Electro Gnosis to the Fatui. It ends by pointing the Traveler to Sumeru.

Plot: **Sword, Fish, Resistance.** Teppei takes the Traveler to Watatsumi Island to meet Sangonomiya Kokomi. She explains that she accepted an anonymous letter offering the Resistance supplies as long as it kept fighting the Shogunate, and that she doubted the sender's motives but had little choice because the island lacked resources. On the Vision Hunt Decree she says the attitude of the Tenryou Commission and of the Raiden Shogun does not add up. She makes the Traveler captain of a special operations unit, Swordfish II, and promises Teppei a combat role. After a first task the unit investigates vanishing supplies around Fort Mumei, staying at Bourou Village, where Teppei, now captain of a unit himself, praises the new sponsor's supplies.

**Those Who Yearn for the Gods' Gaze.** The Fort Mumei search finds nothing, but the area feels strange. Teppei arrives with greying hair and a cough, blaming a cold, and explains the Tatarigami, a phenomenon that appeared after the Raiden Shogun killed Orobashi, the god of Watatsumi Island, during the Archon War. He warns that it harms health. Back on Watatsumi Island the Traveler finds Kokomi and Gorou examining a secret weapon an officer handed in: a vitality-absorbing Delusion, which reveals the Fatui as the sponsor. Kokomi orders all users recalled. The Traveler realises Teppei's boosted strength came from a Delusion and rushes to him too late. Teppei, who now looks like an old man, dies in despair, and the Traveler swears revenge on the Fatui.

**Delusion.** Kokomi suspects the Fatui had local support and reluctantly gives the Traveler the suspected factory's location. Inside, the Traveler learns that the Delusions are made with Crystal Marrow collected by the Kanjou Commission, and finds a notice that a Resistance member, Nathan, is a Fatui mole. The Traveler confronts the Balladeer, a Fatui Harbinger who mocks the Resistance and shows that Inazuma has fallen for the Fatui's schemes. Provoked, the Traveler succumbs to the Tatarigami, falls unconscious and is found by Yae Miko.

**The Servant's Path.** The Traveler wakes in the Grand Narukami Shrine. Miko says Kokomi has resolved the factory crisis, and explains that the Shogun who runs Inazuma is a puppet made in the likeness of Ei, who is the true Raiden Shogun and lives inside her inner world, the Plane of Euthymia, pursuing eternity. The Traveler is the first person Ei has met since entering the Plane, and Miko believes this is the key to saving both Inazuma and Ei from a disastrous future. She trains the Traveler hard to survive the Electro Archon's attacks and plans to turn Kujou Sara against the Tenryou Commission by proving that her adoptive father Kujou Takayuki has betrayed the Shogunate. She invites Sara to the shrine, promising evidence if Sara returns alone in three days.

**Proof of Guilt.** The Traveler goes back to Komore Teahouse to meet Kamisato Ayaka and Thoma. Yoimiya supplies a distraction so the Shuumatsuban ninja Sayu can slip into the Tenryou Commission, and they obtain Takayuki's falsified, over-optimistic report on the war and his correspondence with the Fatui.

**Blind Loyalty, Reckless Courage.** Sara reads the documents, is furious and storms off to confront her adoptive father. Miko tells the Traveler that to meet Ei they must recreate the way they first met her, and gives them an omamori as a parting gift with vague promises about its use. The Traveler and Paimon join Sara and fight through Tenryou guards to Takayuki, who confirms everything and admits his selfish reasons for accepting the Fatui's proposals. Learning that Signora is meeting the Shogun at Tenshukaku, Sara runs there, and the Traveler follows.

**Duel Before the Throne.** At Tenshukaku the Traveler finds Sara defeated by Signora. Signora says Sara's Inazuman heritage spares her, but the Traveler, as Inazuma's most wanted criminal, has no such protection. The Traveler remembers that the winner of a duel before the throne receives a second chance, and challenges Signora with the Shogun's approval. The Traveler wins, and the Shogun executes Signora with Musou no Hitotachi, her most powerful technique. Shaken, the Traveler and Paimon are allowed to leave Tenshukaku alive.

**The Omnipresent God.** Outside, the Traveler meets Gorou's Resistance forces. The Shogun cuts space open behind the Traveler to execute them, but Kaedehara Kazuha resonates with the Masterless Vision of his late friend and uses its Electro power with his own Anemo Vision to block the technique and knock her back. The Resistance rallies and charges, and to save them from being slaughtered the Traveler attacks and is pulled into the Plane of Euthymia.

Ei has known about the Fatui's involvement all along: she judged Visions, meaning the pursuit of aspirations, a greater threat to eternity than a temporary war, so her inaction amounted to tacit approval. Their clash becomes a duel. Midway, Miko uses the omamori to enter the Plane and reminds the Traveler that they fight for those who want the Decree abolished. The light of human ambition from the confiscated Visions outside lights up the dark Plane, and the Traveler defeats Ei.

Ei explains why she seeks eternity: she lost close companions and her sister Makoto, and she saw the Heavenly Principles destroy Khaenri'ah. Miko persuades her that this vision of eternity causes too much suffering and loneliness, even for herself, pointing out that the Plane's sky had brightened with a predawn glow when Ei lit up on meeting her friend after so long. Ei agrees to abolish the Vision Hunt Decree but says she needs time to reconsider how she rules Inazuma.

**Wishes.** After the dust settles, Miko reveals she saved the Traveler from the Balladeer by giving him the Electro Gnosis. Ei had entrusted it to her before entering the Plane, knowing Miko would sell it for something of equal value, since Ei no longer needed it. As thanks, Miko answers the Traveler's questions: the Balladeer was Ei's prototype puppet, recruited into the Fatui and strengthened until he became the Sixth Harbinger; and in Sumeru, the Traveler's next stop, knowledge is managed as a resource, though she does not know whether that was Lesser Lord Kusanali's choice or the Sages'. She also speculates that the Traveler has no Vision because they have not yet found an ambition strong enough to receive one.

Revelations: The Shogun who governs Inazuma is a puppet; the true Ei is in the Plane of Euthymia. The Fatui sponsored the Resistance with Delusions that drain the lives of their users, using Crystal Marrow gathered by the Kanjou Commission, and Kujou Takayuki colluded with them. Signora is dead. The Balladeer is Ei's prototype puppet and the Sixth Harbinger. The Electro Gnosis passes from Ei through Miko to the Balladeer. Ei agrees to end the Vision Hunt Decree.

Ei's inaction during the war was a deliberate stance: she saw ambition, the thing Visions represent, as more dangerous to eternity than the war. Her motives include the deaths of her companions and of her sister Makoto and the fall of Khaenri'ah, and the Tatarigami around Watatsumi dates from Orobashi's death in the Archon War.

Characters: **Traveler and Paimon**: the Traveler becomes a Resistance captain, loses Teppei, breaks the Delusion factory, defeats Signora and Ei.
**Yae Miko**: the shrine's guide and Ei's old friend, who rescues, trains and pushes the plan, and in the end persuades Ei to relent.
**Sangonomiya Kokomi and Gorou**: lead the Resistance; Kokomi accepted the sponsor's supplies despite her doubts.
**Teppei**: grows in confidence with the Delusion's help and dies of its effects.
**Kujou Sara and Kujou Takayuki**: Sara is turned against her adoptive father when his betrayal is proved; he confesses selfish motives.
**Signora and the Balladeer**: Fatui Harbingers; she is executed, he is the Sixth Harbinger.
**Raiden Shogun and Ei**: the puppet Shogun and the true Electro Archon, who is defeated and persuaded.

Ayaka, Thoma, Yoimiya and Sayu are the allies who help obtain Takayuki's documents, and Kaedehara Kazuha is the one who blocks the Shogun's strike outside Tenshukaku.

Consequences: The Vision Hunt Decree is abolished, the Fatui's Delusion scheme collapses, and Signora is dead. The Traveler leaves with the Resistance's campaign effectively over; Ei says she must reconsider how she rules. The Electro Gnosis is in the Balladeer's hands. The Traveler is pointed toward Sumeru.

The next Archon Quest acts continue the Inazuma story in Requiem of the Echoing Depths and The Crane Returns on the Wind.

Placement: Released in Version 2.1 as the third act of Chapter II, after Stillness, the Sublimation of Shadow (2.0). Next in story order are Requiem of the Echoing Depths and The Crane Returns on the Wind. The act shares its name with the Chapter II title in some listings, so use "Act III" to be unambiguous. It requires Adventure Rank 30.

Further details: The act's Chinese title is Qian Shou Bai Yan, Tianxia Renjian and its Japanese title is Senju Hyakume no Ukiyo (a romanisation the wiki marks as assumed). The Chinese and Japanese titles refer to a thousand hands and a hundred eyes, which is not how the English title reads.

675.comment: Omnipresence Over Mortals: Swordfish II and the Fatui Sponsor
675.content: Kokomi accepted an anonymous letter's offer of supplies for the Resistance, with doubts about the sender. The Traveler is made captain of Swordfish II, a special operations unit. The sponsor turns out to be the Fatui.

676.content: Teppei uses a Fatui Delusion to gain combat strength, ages quickly, dismisses his symptoms as a cold and dies as an old man while the Traveler tries to reach him. His death drives the Traveler's personal vow against the Fatui.

677.comment: Omnipresence Over Mortals: The Delusion Factory
677.content: A Fatui plant that makes Delusions from Crystal Marrow collected by the Kanjou Commission. A notice there shows that Nathan, a supposed Resistance member, is a Fatui mole. The Balladeer is waiting inside.

678.comment: Omnipresence Over Mortals: Duel Before the Throne
678.content: At Tenshukaku the Traveler invokes the rule that a duel before the throne gives the winner a second chance, and challenges Signora. The Shogun approves. The Traveler wins, and the Shogun executes Signora with Musou no Hitotachi.

679.comment: Omnipresence Over Mortals: The Plane of Euthymia Confrontation
679.content: The Traveler defeats Ei in her inner world while the light of confiscated Visions brightens its darkness. Miko enters with the omamori, and persuades Ei, who lost companions and her sister Makoto, to abolish the Vision Hunt Decree.

680.comment: Omnipresence Over Mortals: Kazuha Blocks the Shogun
680.content: Outside Tenshukaku, Kazuha resonates with his late friend's Masterless Vision and combines its Electro power with his own Anemo Vision to block Musou no Hitotachi and push the Shogun back. It inspires the Resistance to charge.

681.comment: Omnipresence Over Mortals: The Electro Gnosis Sold
681.content: Ei gave her Electro Gnosis to Miko before entering the Plane, expecting Miko to sell it for something of equal value. Miko gave it to the Balladeer to save the Traveler.

key: On One Side a Palace, On the Other a Tomb
To Gaze Upon the Dreaming Pale Crown
The Stone Beasts, Like Ghouls Seated
682.comment: On One Side a Palace, On the Other a Tomb
682.content:
On One Side a Palace, On the Other a Tomb (also: To Gaze Upon the Dreaming Pale Crown, The Stone Beasts, Like Ghouls Seated, White Birch Snowgrave series): On One Side a Palace, On the Other a Tomb is a Snezhnaya World Quest series added in version 7.0, set in the White Birch Snowgrave. In two quests the Traveler and Paimon explore the Pale Crown Palace, the hidden former home and tomb of the Belyi Tsar, and the frozen mausoleum around it, where they recover one of the three missing fragments of the Eye of Graeae.

The quests are "To Gaze Upon the Dreaming Pale Crown" and "The Stone Beasts, Like Ghouls Seated". The series runs concurrently with In the Dwelling of Life and Hesperides of Love and Hate, and all three feed into Her Palace Collapses Into the Blizzard.

Most of the series is explored through flashbacks and environmental clues: it reveals what Hvergelmir was, why the Belyi Tsar's body is guarded, and how Zver came to be loyal to him. It introduces Aksinya's side of the Eye of Graeae story before the finale.

Plot: To Gaze Upon the Dreaming Pale Crown. The Eye of Graeae senses that one of the three pieces of its lost power lies inside the Pale Crown Palace. The palace was once the Belyi Tsar's private home and later his tomb, and the Eye also learns it was created there, in the hidden research facility Hvergelmir. The palace was a place where the Tsar welcomed humans alongside the fae, and where the flame of Kresnik was first kindled before it spread across what became Snezhnaya. After the Tsar died fighting the Abyss and waves of beasts around five hundred years ago, his remains returned to the palace and part of his body became the Tsar's White Birch.

The Stone Beasts, Like Ghouls Seated. With the Eye of Graeae, the Traveler and Paimon cross snow-covered ruins and royal halls, solving puzzles with statues and torches, and fight man-made monsters. A two-headed beast, "Zver", guards the Belyi Tsar's body and tells them to leave. Flashbacks show the Tsar, his servant Aksinya and the bio-alchemical work that produced Zver and other creatures. Zver was a failed prototype abandoned by its creator Koshchei; the Tsar saved it, gave it purpose and treated it as a loyal companion. Zver has guarded the corpse for centuries and hates those who wronged its master.

To reach the palace the Traveler summons a hidden railway and rides an old prototype train run by the Eye. In transit the Traveler is separated from Paimon and the Eye and enters a vision of Hvergelmir's past, where two researchers, Izmaylov and Azazel, cannot see them. The two are monitoring the Proto-Man, a being held in an egg that stays stable despite the darkness of the Font of the Shadow Realm. Izmaylov fears the newly ascended Tsaritsa's rumoured ban on alchemy will end Hvergelmir's bio-alchemy work and the Tsar's last aspiration. Azazel questions whether to continue after a previous disastrous experiment, and they leave the choice to superiors.

The Traveler explores the facility. A message from Pavlina asks the researchers to look after her cat, Lara, with a joking threat to whoever lets the cat grow parts of another animal. The Traveler finds Lara starving but unable to be fed except from her own bowl, finds Prime Ice that contains something, and reads research notes about prisoners, the Snegovik and the concept of "love". One researcher wonders whether loveless fae could use the technology to gain love. Another claims a certain power should have been theirs rather than part of Aksinya's aberrant dream. Behind a picture frame is a hidden laboratory with an alchemical apparatus; a note says Kresnik Kristall may help change matter and that separated things must be brought back together. The Traveler realises this means combining materials, grinds yellow crystal and Kresnik Kristall ore into powder and bottles it, and a new substance begins to form.

After Zver is beaten, it reveals that the Eye of Graeae is also a prototype, made to hold a "Key", and that its memories have been erased. It warns the Traveler that the Eye may not be as trustworthy as it seems. More flashbacks show Zver's bond with the Tsar and its defiance of Koshchei's orders. The Eye begins to suspect its identity is tied to the Tsar's legacy, though it cannot remember details until its power is whole.

At the ruins of Hvergelmir the party finds another fragment of the Eye's body, with a note from Aksinya explaining how it was recovered and hinting at a plan to rebuild the "sacred form" and begin a new era. They learn that collecting fragments is not enough: all must be brought to the "Court of Bliss" to restore the Eye.

Revelations: - The Pale Crown Palace was the Belyi Tsar's private residence and later his tomb, and is where the Kresnik flame was first lit; the Tsar's White Birch grew from part of his body.
- Hvergelmir is where the Eye of Graeae was created; researchers there studied a Proto-Man held in an egg.
- Zver was a rejected prototype of Koshchei's, saved and trusted by the Tsar.
- The Eye of Graeae is a prototype made to house a "Key", and its memories were erased.

- Hvergelmir's notes show experiments on prisoners and Snegovik and a research interest in whether loveless fae could gain love.
- Pavlina was linked to Hvergelmir: she is the author of the cat message, and the Hesperides series later shows her as one of the people who betrayed Aksinya.

Characters: - The Traveler and Paimon.
- The Eye of Graeae ("Goggles"), whose past the series starts to open up.
- Zver, the two-headed guardian of the Tsar's body.
- The Belyi Tsar and Aksinya, shown in flashback; Aksinya also leaves the note at Hvergelmir.
- Researchers Izmaylov and Azazel, seen only in a vision of Hvergelmir's past.

- Koshchei is the absent creator who abandoned Zver; the Tsaritsa is discussed by the researchers as newly ascended.

Consequences: The Traveler recovers one fragment of the Eye of Graeae (a Pebble), and the series establishes that all fragments must be brought to the Court of Bliss. Zver is left defeated but not shown as killed in the available summary.

The series is required, with Hesperides of Love and Hate and In the Dwelling of Life, to start An Ark That Used to Be a Soul in Her Palace Collapses Into the Blizzard.

Placement: Story order: it is one of three parallel series after the Snezhnaya Archon Quest chapter that unlock Her Palace Collapses Into the Blizzard. Release order: version 7.0 with the other Snezhnaya World Quest series. Players who finish it first will see different conditional lines in Through the Gates of Ivory; for example, Aksinya's appearance at the false wedding and the Eye's comments about Pavlina's betrayal refer back to the Pale Crown Palace.

683.comment: On One Side a Palace, On the Other a Tomb: Zver
683.content: Zver is a two-headed beast and man-made creature that guards the Belyi Tsar's body in the mausoleum below the Pale Crown Palace. Once an abandoned prototype of Koshchei, it was given purpose by the Tsar and has stayed loyal for centuries. It warns the Traveler away, is defeated in battle, and tells them the Eye of Graeae may not be trustworthy.

684.comment: On One Side a Palace, On the Other a Tomb: Hvergelmir (research facility)
684.content: Hvergelmir was the Belyi Tsar's bio-alchemy research organisation, hidden under the Pale Crown Palace. In the Traveler's vision, researchers Izmaylov and Azazel monitor a Proto-Man in an egg and fear that a ban on alchemy would end their work. The ruined site later holds a fragment of the Eye of Graeae and a note from Aksinya.

key: Origin of the Sequence world quest
685.content:
Origin of the Sequence (also: Origin of the Sequence world quest, Ia-Ilimmu No. 59 Storage Array quest): A Version 6.7 world quest in the Lunar Highlands of the Frost Moon. The Traveler and Paimon find a set of giant towers at the Nuur Stone Circle, repair a damaged ancient terminal and recalibrate a stone dragon idol. Finishing it unlocks the Ancient Moon's Remnant at the circle.

The terminal calls itself the Ia-Ilimmu No. 59 Storage Array and cannot recognise visitors because its central module is damaged or missing. It asks for Nin-Kiggia to be contacted for maintenance, and finally reports that its primary energy system is not connected. The quest ends with that unresolved error.

The quest is a short environmental story: no named living character appears, and what is learned is through a machine that is still trying to serve people who may no longer exist. A later quest, Within the Sequence, continues from here.

Plot: Paimon marvels at the giant towers and thinks they resemble the Frostmoon Scions' sanctum. The Traveler examines a terminal, follows its prompts to repair data nodes, and calibrates a Secret Source Dragon Idol that appears. Four glowing markers light up around the area.

On approach, the terminal checks for vital signs, tries an identification sequence and fails. A security check on the kernel also fails; it blames a damaged or missing central module and tells the visitor to contact Nin-Kiggia. It then switches to a "universal greeting", welcoming the visitor to the Ia-Ilimmu No. 59 Storage Array, which is used mostly to regulate the Engraving and store research resources. A critical component failure has left service dependencies broken; the terminal asks for a self-diagnostic command to restore critical data nodes. Paimon admits she did not follow most of this, and decides that a storehouse must hold treasure.

After the Traveler repairs the nodes, the diagnostic fails to run on schedule and manual path recalibration is needed. A Secret Source Dragon Idol appears. Paimon proposes climbing on its back and bopping it a couple of times to get it working, which the Traveler does. The terminal then reports repair complete and thanks them and lifts its lockdown. Four glowing markers appear nearby. A final error says the primary energy system is not connected and asks for Nin-Kiggia or an auxiliary power source.

Steps: investigate the giant tower; examine the terminal; follow the prompts to repair the data nodes; investigate the Secret Source Dragon Idol; examine the terminal again. Completing the quest unlocks the Hidden Exploration Objective Fragments of Ia-Ilimmu and the Ancient Moon's Remnant at the Nuur Stone Circle. Rewards: Adventure EXP, 40 Primogems, 30,000 Mora, Hero's Wit and Mystic Enhancement Ore.

The pre-quest scene, triggered on first approach to the Ancient Moon's Remnant, has a conditional variant in the wiki transcript (Paimon's first line differs); the wiki does not say what condition selects it. In the follow-up quest Within the Sequence (opened when the Remnant reaches level 5), the repaired terminal reports that the lockdown is lifted and addresses some visitors by titles such as Xiuhcoatl and rulers of Natlantea; that quest is covered separately.

Revelations: The quest establishes that this ancient array is numbered No. 59, called Ia-Ilimmu, tied to something called the Engraving, and designed to be maintained by Nin-Kiggia. The terminal calls the repairs a self-diagnostic and does not explain what the towers do beyond that.

Nin-Kiggia is the name of a data-based dragon-like lifeform created by the dragon researcher Lusalim, as the wiki describes her. The quest itself only says to contact her. For the larger story of the dragon researchers on the Frost Moon see Moon Gazing.

Characters: The Traveler and Paimon, plus the Ancient Terminal. Nin-Kiggia is only named, and does not appear.

Paimon supplies curiosity and a treasure-hunting attitude: she assumes a "storage" array means a storehouse. The terminal is polite, formal and fussy about titles and procedure, and repeatedly apologises for its limits.

Consequences: The Ancient Moon's Remnant at the Nuur Stone Circle becomes available, where Luna Sigils can be offered for rewards, and the Fragments of Ia-Ilimmu exploration objective is unlocked. The terminal remains partly broken because of its missing energy source.

Placement: Released in Version 6.7 (Luna VIII) with the Frost Moon area. Within the Sequence follows it, and the Moon Gazing series covers the wider setting. The wiki lists no formal requirement beyond reaching the Nuur Stone Circle.

686.comment: Origin of the Sequence: Ia-Ilimmu Storage Array
686.content: A damaged ancient installation at the Nuur Stone Circle in the Lunar Highlands of the Frost Moon. Its terminal calls it the Ia-Ilimmu No. 59 Storage Array, used to regulate the operation of the Engraving and to store research resources. After the Traveler repairs it in Origin of the Sequence, it still reports that its primary energy system is not connected and that Nin-Kiggia should be contacted.

687.content:
Orobashi's Legacy (also: Orobashi's Legacy: Prologue, Yashiori Island ward quests): Orobashi's Legacy is a six-part World Quest series on Yashiori Island, added in version 2.0. At Fort Fujitou the Traveler meets Kaji, who is studying why the island has endless rain and lightning. The cause is damaged ancient wards linked to the remains of Orobashi, a serpent god. The Traveler restores them across the island and the storm ends.

The parts are Prologue and Parts I to V. It requires the Archon Quest act A New Star Approaches, and the Ritou Escape Plan quest to reach its starting area. Finishing Part III opens the Formation Estate domain, and finishing Part V rewards the diagram for the Kitain Cross Spear.

Besides the puzzle chain, the series is where Orobashi's role in Yashiori Island's past and the origin of the Tatarigami phenomenon are explained to players. Completing each part clears the Tatarigami from its own area, so progress is visible across the island.

Plot: Each part clears the Tatarigami in its area. After the first three wards are repaired, Fort Mumei rises from the sea near Watatsumi Island. In Parts IV and V the Traveler and Kaji investigate it and find one last, larger ward guarded by a Maguu Kenki. The Traveler defeats the guardian and solves the final puzzle. The constant rain and storm over Yashiori Island stop. Kaji thanks the Traveler and goes on to the Kujou Encampment to continue his work.

This is condensed from the series overview; the individual part pages were not read in detail, and the page notes its own summary is incomplete.

Revelations: - The storm on Yashiori Island is a consequence of broken wards, not natural weather (Kaji's hypothesis, borne out by the quests).
- Orobashi's remains, scattered when the Raiden Shogun killed it, are the source of the Tatarigami.

- Orobashi sacrificed itself after learning something Celestia wanted hidden, and attacked Yashiori Island.

Characters: The Traveler, Paimon, Kaji (researcher), a Maguu Kenki as the final guardian. Orobashi and the Raiden Shogun appear in the history Kaji recounts.

Consequences: The storm and lightning over Yashiori Island cease and the Tatarigami are cleared from the repaired areas. Fort Mumei has surfaced near Watatsumi Island. Kaji leaves for the Kujou Encampment.

Placement: Released in 2.0 with Inazuma. Requires A New Star Approaches; Ritou Escape Plan is needed to reach the starting location.

688.content: A researcher the Traveler meets at Fort Fujitou, investigating the endless rain and lightning of Yashiori Island. He identifies the broken ancient wards as the cause and directs the Traveler to repair them. He moves on to the Kujou Encampment when the work is finished.

689.content: Ancient wards on Yashiori Island, linked to the remains of Orobashi, whose failure causes the storm. They are repaired by returning Rock Pillar Warding Stones and Rock Pillar Pearls to stone puzzles at Musoujin Gorge, Serpent's Head and Jakotsu Mine, with a last ward at Fort Mumei.

key: Awaken the Residual Pari in the Fravashi Trees
690.content:
Pale Fire (also: Pale Fire World Quest series, Awaken the Residual Pari in the Fravashi Trees, Fravashi Tree quests): Pale Fire is a world quest series in the Girdle of the Sands, Sumeru, added in version 3.6. Strange circular trees called Fravashi Trees hold the lingering remains of Pari who could not return home. With the Pari Sorush's help the Traveler awakens ten of them, collects the Plumes of Purifying Light they leave, and has the elder Zurvan explain what they are.

The series has a main quest, Pale Fire, and ten separate quests, one per tree, all named Awaken the Residual Pari in the Fravashi Trees, which can be done in any order. Doing any one of them unlocks Pale Fire, and completing all ten finishes it. The Traveler is formally addressed as Sorush's Yasnapati, and Zurvan asks them to help the Pari that have not yet returned.

The wiki's series summary is empty, so the account below comes from the Pale Fire quest and a sample Fravashi Tree quest. The Fravashi Trees quests share their dialogue structure, so what is described for one is a reasonable guide to the rest, though that is an inference rather than something checked tree by tree.

Plot: At each Fravashi Tree, a ring-shaped tree that Paimon at first takes for a door, Sorush speaks with scorn for the sight of her own kind clinging on. She explains that these trees are Pari who fought to the end against the defilement corrupting the land and, with their last strength, turned into trees; being tainted, they were rejected by the Vourukasha Oasis. Paimon insists the Traveler cannot leave them to suffer alone. Sorush wakes the residual Pari with her power. It lashes out at hidden enemies and the Traveler must defeat the monsters that appear (two waves in the example read, hilichurls and Abyss mages with mitachurl support). A Plume of Purifying Light floats out of the tree, the obsession within cleared away.

After the first tree, Pale Fire starts. If the Traveler has not yet done The Splendorous Sky That Day, a pop-up advises learning more about the Pari. The Traveler brings news to Zurvan, who explains what a Fravashi Tree and the Plume are and that offering the Plume to the Amrita Pool lets the Pari return to the Vourukasha Oasis. She names the ritual and the Yasnapati who performs it, and asks the Traveler to bring back every Plume. When all ten trees are awakened, Zurvan thanks the Traveler and Sorush and tells Paimon a story about visiting Oceanids.

Sorush's reaction varies depending on whether the Traveler has started As the Khvarena's Light Shows: before it, she calls the trees pathetic and says Pari should hope to spend their strength in a final stand; after it, her words are gentler and she says she can hardly bear the sight, and allows it might be their wish to guard the land. In both cases she says only a battle with no end is true eternity, and that a kind heart is one of Simurgh's noble qualities but not enough to survive in the desert. Paimon calls the trees' state lonely, and says that she would want to go home to everyone if trapped.

Zurvan's explanation is as follows. The being in the tree is a fragmented memory, like those in a Plume, which cannot return to the earth. If Heart of Amrita has been completed, Zurvan adds that Plumes of Purifying Light come from Simurgh's Khvarena and that Pari arose when Khvarena met Amrita, which is why they are called descendants of Khvarena. If the Traveler has completed In the End, the Forest Will Remember, she contrasts Pari, who are born from the Vourukasha Oasis and will return to it, with Aranara, who are born of the land. The god guarding the Oasis, she says, is rejected by the time flowing through the land, and so are the Pari; this is what they wish, because they exist to keep defilement from flowing into the land with them, and the Amrita Pool washes it away. She tells Paimon that humans who walked with Pari in ancient times purified scattered Pari and brought them to the Oasis, and that this bond gave rise to the title Yasnapati.

Final conversation. After all ten, Zurvan says the scattered Pari seem to have all returned and Sorush says she takes the praise as her due. If Khvarena of Good and Evil has not been done, Paimon says the giant hole will be fixed soon; if it has, she says the hole in the sky is already fixed. Paimon jokes that Pari, born from water, should be called "Hydri"; Sorush objects to the nickname. Zurvan is reminded of a distant past in which many Oceanids from foreign lands crossed the scorching, monster-ridden desert looking for their deceased god; finding no sign of one, and after seeing the Harvisptokhm, they dispersed. Their journey became a legend, and many outsiders have since followed the route; over time it came to be read as sacrificing oneself in pursuit of pure innocence. These pilgrimages continued for a long time after the Oasis was sealed. Zurvan muses that the journey may matter more than the destination, and that striving may mean more than a single sacrifice, which sets Sorush off ("Why does it always come back to me?").

Smaller points: the Fravashi Tree residual Pari speak in battle-boasting language ("Come forth and perish!") when woken. Gameplay: completing Pale Fire grants the achievement Homeward-Bound Spirits.

Revelations: - Fravashi Trees are Pari who exhausted their strength against the defilement of the land and were rejected by the Oasis as tainted.
- Plumes of Purifying Light let these Pari return to the Vourukasha Oasis when offered to the Amrita Pool.
- Humans who walked beside Pari once purified them in the desert; the Traveler as Sorush's Yasnapati takes on that role.

- Zurvan says the beings in the trees are best called fragmented memories, and that Plumes of Purifying Light come from Simurgh's Khvarena.
- The Order of Skeptics once did the purification rituals; according to Sorush, no one in the Order can do so now and the best they can manage is to keep the trees alive.
- Oceanids from foreign lands once crossed the desert seeking their dead god, which created the pilgrimage legend.

Characters: The Traveler and Paimon; Sorush, the Pari who calls the Traveler her Yasnapati and Paimon "Pale Floater"; Zurvan, the Pari elder at the Vourukasha Oasis; and a Residual Pari of the Forest in each tree.

Consequences: Ten Fravashi Trees are cleared and their Pari are able to return to the Vourukasha Oasis; the Oasis looks livelier. The Traveler is recognised as a Yasnapati by Zurvan.

Placement: Released in 3.6, located in the Girdle of the Sands, Sumeru (Gavireh Lajavard, with the Oasis as the hub). The trees are scattered in spots including Tunigi Hollow, Asipattravana Swamp, the Temir Mountains and Madinat al-Nuhas.

691.content:
A Fravashi Tree is a ring-shaped tree in the Girdle of the Sands that a Pari transformed into after exhausting its strength against defilement. Sorush says the Pari inside is stuck on obsessions of the past and has been rejected by the Oasis as tainted. Waking it triggers a short fight with spectral enemies and leaves a Plume of Purifying Light.

Zurvan says the contents are more truly fragmented memories than whole Pari. Ten of them are woken in the series, in places the wiki lists as North Tunigi Hollow, Northwest Tunigi Hollow, Asipattravana Swamp, East Tunigi Hollow, Hangeh Afrasiyab, Madinat al-Nuhas and the West Temir Mountains.

692.comment: Pale Fire: Plume of Purifying Light
692.content: The Plume is a glittering object that rises from a Fravashi Tree once its residual Pari is awakened. Zurvan says it carries memories that cannot return to the earth and comes from Simurgh's Khvarena; offered to the Amrita Pool, it lets the Pari return to the Vourukasha Oasis.

693.content: Yasnapati is a title Sorush uses for the Traveler. Zurvan says that in ancient times human warriors who walked with Pari held rituals to purify Pari scattered in the desert, and those with a special bond to Pari have been called Yasnapati ever since. Sorush instead credits the Order of Skeptics with the rituals.

694.content: A story Zurvan tells at the end of Pale Fire: long ago Oceanids from foreign lands crossed the desert in search of their dead god, found nothing, saw the Harvisptokhm and left. Their route became a legend for outsiders, who later read it as self-sacrifice in pursuit of pure innocence; pilgrims kept coming for a long time after the Oasis closed.

695.content:
Papilio Charontis Chapter (Hu Tao) (also: Papilio Charontis Chapter, Hu Tao's Story Quest, Yet the Butterfly Flutters Away): The Papilio Charontis Chapter is Hu Tao's Story Quest (Version 1.3), set in Liyue. In its one act, Yet the Butterfly Flutters Away, the Traveler meets the 77th Director of Wangsheng Funeral Parlor and helps her intern Meng find out whether his childhood friend, who died young, has become a vengeful spirit. The answer is a gentle one, and the act ends with a funeral at the border between life and death.

The act has four quests: The Mysterious Wangsheng Parlor, In Pursuit of a Phantom, Friendships, Wishes, and Regrets, and Perfect Send-Off. It requires Adventure Rank 40 and the Archon Quest Farewell, Archaic Lord. The Chinese chapter name means roughly "Chapter of the Guiding Butterfly".

The chapter is the standard introduction to how Hu Tao works: showy and irreverent on the surface, but careful, practical and compassionate about death. It also supplies the parlor's own account of its origins and of the "border" it works at. It is a prerequisite for Baizhu's Lagenaria Chapter, in which Hu Tao reappears.

Its tone mixes comedy (failed marketing, a staged exorcism, a Ley Line Monolith used as a monster lure) with a quiet ending about regret and the living friends left behind. The Traveler's own search for their sibling is mentioned only briefly, in the closing conversation.

Plot: **The Mysterious Wangsheng Parlor.** Meng, a new intern, flees from the Traveler and Paimon on Wuwang Hill. His boss, a young woman, tells him the "ghosts" are future clients. Paimon recalls that Zhongli works at the parlor as a consultant, which surprises the girl; she introduces herself as Hu Tao, the 77th Director, and tries a sales pitch that fails. She and Meng had come to the hill to hold a funeral after reports of strange activity. Taking the pair for adventurers, she asks them to act as intermediaries in a business deal with the Adventurers' Guild branch in Liyue Harbor, but the manager, Lan, is put off by her cheerful talk of death. Back at the parlor she plans a new marketing push and then, reminded by Meng of "Big G", takes the Traveler to meet three of Meng's friends: Little Wu, Mumu and Congzi. She later admits she had abandoned the marketing plan once the Guild deal failed; the visit was to see whether Big G's spirit was lingering near them, and she sensed nothing.

**In Pursuit of a Phantom.** Hu Tao explains that Big G was Meng's childhood friend and died in an accident, and that all three of the friends they met knew him. Meng fears Big G has turned vengeful, though Hu Tao says she rarely meets such spirits. Another man, Luocheng, bursts in convinced he is cursed by a demon. Hu Tao stages a mock exorcism at a Ley Line Monolith while the Traveler fights off hilichurls drawn to it. She then tells Luocheng the monolith merely attracts monsters, that he was pranked, and that he probably had an ordinary illness or was scared sick; she advises him to believe less in superstition. Big G then appears as a small spirit, in the form he had when he died.

**Friendships, Wishes, and Regrets.** At the parlor, Big G explains that he only wanted to check on his old friends. He had followed Luocheng back from Wuwang Hill, which explained Luocheng's nightmares, and had become lost in the unfamiliar city because of a poor sense of direction and a fear of heights. Hu Tao says a proper funeral needs keepsakes from his friends, and sends the Traveler to collect them without revealing why: extra-spicy Jueyun Chili Chicken from Little Wu, a toy box from Mumu, and Plaustrite Shards from Congzi for a Xiao Lantern. The friends say all five grew up on Wuwang Hill, lost their homes to a disaster, and moved to Liyue Harbor to stay near one another.

**Perfect Send-Off.** Hu Tao takes the group into the "border" between life and death, a place where Ley Lines run wild, and warns them to follow her instructions or she will have to erase their memories. While Meng and Big G say goodbye, she tells the Traveler how the parlor began as something like a doctor's office, how the Archon War tipped the balance toward death, and how the balance was repaired over many years. Big G leaves peacefully, reassured that his friends are well. Meng reveals that the two had wished to build careers, raise families and spend a Lantern Rite together, and Hu Tao gives him unpaid leave. She tells the Traveler she guessed from their reaction that they had not found what they sought, that she had asked the dead for news and found nothing worth following, and that she will keep looking. She adds that she has never seen any previous director in the border, so she knows they all died without regret.

Details worth keeping. Hu Tao's explanation of why she keeps panicky clients "in the dark" is that someone who is truly afraid needs something believable to bind the fear to, such as a ritual, so a trick is sometimes kinder than the plain truth. Her account of the parlor's history says that Yaksha karma gathered during the fighting against vengeful gods formed an ancient plague, that hysterical people read it as a curse from the gods, and that the founders of the parlor were those who realised that purifying the air and burning the diseased dead would halt it. After many years the plague was eradicated and the parlor has watched over the balance of life and death since. In the border she notes that the dead there are those who still envy the living or cannot let go.

Revelations: Minor lore: Wangsheng Funeral Parlor claims a founding role in ending an ancient plague born of accumulated Yaksha karma, and its directors tend the balance between life and death. The "border" between the living and the dead is a real, Ley-Line-disordered place that Hu Tao can enter with others. Spirits keep the form they had when they died.

Hu Tao says that no earlier director has been seen in the border, which she takes to mean they died without regrets. The Traveler's search for their sibling is mentioned, and the dead there offered nothing useful.

Characters: Hu Tao, the Traveler and Paimon. Meng, Big G, Luocheng, Little Wu, Mumu, Congzi, Lan and the Ferrylady appear. Zhongli is mentioned.

Hu Tao is playful and theatrical but conscientious, and she hides real care behind pranks. Meng is anxious, earnest and grieving. Big G is a gentle spirit with a poor sense of direction and a fear of heights. Zhongli is referred to as the parlor's consultant but does not appear in person.

Consequences: The Traveler and Paimon gain a friendly acquaintance with Hu Tao, who promises to keep looking for the Traveler's sibling. The chapter is also a prerequisite for Baizhu's Lagenaria Chapter, along with the Alatus Chapter's Butterfly's Dream.

Placement: Release order: 1.3. Story order: after Chapter I of the Archon Quests (Farewell, Archaic Lord). Hu Tao reappears in the Lagenaria Chapter (3.6).

696.comment: Papilio Charontis Chapter (Hu Tao): Yet the Butterfly Flutters Away
696.content: Act I of Hu Tao's Story Quest. The Traveler helps Hu Tao and her intern Meng discover that Meng's dead childhood friend Big G is a harmless spirit who only wished to see his friends again, then collects keepsakes for a farewell held in the border between life and death.

697.comment: Papilio Charontis Chapter (Hu Tao): The Border Between Life and Death
697.content: In the Papilio Charontis Chapter, Hu Tao leads the Traveler into a "border" that she says is an ordinary place most people never notice. There Ley Lines run chaotically and it feels near death. She says the dead still tied to the living world linger there, and she warns visitors to follow her instructions or risk having their memories erased.

698.content:
Paralogism (also: Interlude Chapter Act IV, Interlude Act IV, Crimes One and Two, The Hunger of Many): Interlude Chapter Act IV, set in Mondstadt as the Windblume Festival begins. Albedo is put on trial for murder, which proves a trap to expose an imposter made from the life force of the dragon Durin. Afterwards Albedo uses a Hexenzirkel trial to turn Mini Durin into a human.

The act has three quests: Crimes One and Two, The Hunger of Many and The Gardener. It follows Inversion of Genesis in the Interlude Chapter and is unlocked at Adventure Rank 40 after that act and Traveler Observation Report. It was released in Version 5.6. It resolves Albedo's long watch over the fallen Durin on Dragonspine.

The act turns a courtroom mystery into a defence of the city and then into an act of creation. Albedo, himself an artificial human made by Rhinedottir, chooses to give a new life to a dragon-born child rather than only destroy a threat. It is the prerequisite for Song of the Welkin Moon Act I, A Dance of Snowy Tides and Hoarfrost Groves.

Plot: Odd behaviour among Mondstadt's townsfolk and a murder trial of Albedo greet the Traveler on their return for Windblume. The trial is staged to flush out a copy of Hertha, monsters attack the city, and Albedo and the Hexenzirkel's Alice help him create a human Durin.

Three quests. Crimes One and Two: Albedo is tried for murder and the Traveler investigates, until a second Hertha exposes the first as a copy spawned by Durin's remains. The Hunger of Many: monsters attack the city, Albedo explains the trial was a trap, and the Hexenzirkel is called in. The Gardener: after a chessboard trial set by Alice, Albedo turns Mini Durin human at the start of Windblume.

**Crimes One and Two.** Paimon asks the Traveler to return for Windblume. In the city people act strangely: Beatrice avoids Quinn, Miles has been sleepwalking, and Donna talks about finding her ideal man instead of Diluc. Kaeya sends them to Knights of Favonius Headquarters, where they meet Eula and the captains Note and Skeiron, and Jean tells them Albedo is on trial, a case requiring both the Knights and the Church. Varka is away on his expedition to Nod-Krai, so Jean presides, with the deacon Dahlia as assessor, Hertha as prosecutor and Kaeya as defence. Witnesses claim to have seen Albedo dispose of a body, and Diluc reports a second disposal near Dragonspine; the evidence includes a femur and teeth and a letter. Jean finds Albedo guilty but allows an appeal. Rosaria sends the Traveler to Starsnatch Cliff, where Venti and Dahlia explain that Dahlia is also Barbatos' herald, and Venti gives them a Dodocommunication Device. Jean privately commissions the Traveler to investigate. In Albedo's office a hidden compartment points to a third site on Dragonspine, an empty pit with traces of non-human diggers. At the retrial the remains are tied to the missing hunter Hanselmann. Albedo admits to killing one person on Dragonspine, a near-identical double of himself who tried to eliminate him in secret (a failed Homunculus Project specimen abandoned in Durin's stomach), and says he was stationed on Dragonspine to watch Durin. A second Hertha then arrives, and the first is exposed as a copy: Durin's spawn can mimic people. The copy summons minions, the city is attacked, and Jean sends Skeiron's 3rd Company after it.

**The Hunger of Many.** Albedo reveals the trial was staged to draw out the imposter after the Knights spread word that the real Hertha had died. He says the other two people he killed had been consumed and replaced by the spawn. The Traveler and Albedo defend the city alongside Venti, who first hides his identity, Diluc, Kaeya, Barbara, Rosaria, Amber and Mika, and they find Eula worried about Klee, who returns to help against Ruin Machines. Venti senses a child's anger in the wind, which Albedo takes to be Durin's jealousy on learning, through Subject Two's emotions, that he is no longer Rhinedottir's only child. The source, Phonia, is found hiding nearby and is taken into custody; Jean questions her about being missing for over half a year. Albedo says he can save her if the plan proceeds. Albedo then explains the Tripartite Conference: the Knights and Church, the Anemo Archon and the Hexenzirkel, an arrangement Varka had secured. Alice answers a call and attends as a giant Dodoco.

**The Gardener.** In Albedo's office Mini Durin explains that he will take over the dead Durin's body to be reborn as a human, hoping his pure side can restrain the evil instincts. At the Imaginarium Theater Albedo asks Alice for two reagents: flesh of an immortal monster from Mare Jivari and part of an embryo left by Rhinedottir. Alice sets a chessboard trial and shrinks the group. In the second half Barbeloth turns the king and queen into the Ascended King and Sublimated Queen, whom the Traveler and Albedo defeat. Alice hands over the reagents. At Durin's Core on Dragonspine Albedo draws out its energy. Two days later the festival opens, Jean names Venti the Windblume Star, and while he sings Albedo's ritual turns Mini Durin human. Venti gives the Traveler a gift from the Hexenzirkel, a Wonderland Cosmosphere that will open itself when the time is right.
Details that matter in a scene: the first trial is closed-door because parts of the case are classified; Albedo's alibi for the first charge rests on Kaeya pointing to the long Dragonspine report he submitted the next day, which Hertha dismisses, and his alibi for the second on Sucrose, whose testimony fails because she had fallen asleep after midnight; the copy Hertha is exposed when the real Hertha asks where her longest scar is, something the Knights who fought beside her would know; Miles cannot answer, the scar is on her left arm, and Miles turns out to be one of the imposter's accomplices. Albedo says the plan took more than half a year to set up. The in-game recollection summarises the act as the Traveler uncovering the culprit as the fallen dragon, then Albedo and the Traveler reviving Durin in a new form.

Jean upholds the verdict in public although she privately believes Albedo innocent, and she is the one who quietly sets the Traveler to investigate. Albedo explains that acting on Durin's power makes the other spawn unstable. When Paimon asks whether the Wanderer approved of Durin's choice, Durin believes he did, since he was told to "get a move on". Albedo says he believes Rhinedottir would be proud of the outcome and that she had devoured Naberius, Ruler of Life, though he thinks the two are now one.

Revelations: The "murderer" Albedo is innocent of the disappearances; the strange behaviour and the Hertha accusing him come from imposters created from the dragon Durin's remains.

Albedo was stationed on Dragonspine to watch Durin, whose remains spawn mimics. Dahlia is secretly Barbatos' herald as well as an official of the Church. Mini Durin takes over the dead Durin's body to be reborn as a human with Albedo's alchemy.
