Albedo says Durin's jealousy comes from learning he was not Rhinedottir's only creation. He says Rhinedottir devoured Naberius, the Ruler of Life, a claim he shares in conversation and does not prove here.

Characters: Traveler and Paimon; Albedo; Jean; Kaeya; Venti; Dahlia; Durin (Mini Durin).

Also Diluc, Eula, Rosaria, Sucrose, Klee, Hertha and her imposter, Skeiron and Note, Alice, Barbeloth, Phonia, Amber, Barbara, Mika. Varka is voice-only by call and away at Nod-Krai.

Minor townsfolk include Beatrice, Quinn, Miles, Donna and the hunter Hanselmann, who is among the remains.

Consequences: Albedo is cleared, the city survives the attack, Phonia is held, and Durin starts a new life as a human. The Traveler receives a Hexenzirkel gift.

Albedo's Tripartite arrangement with the Anemo Archon and the Hexenzirkel is confirmed. The Wonderland Cosmosphere remains unopened at the act's end.

Placement: Interlude Chapter Act IV, following Inversion of Genesis. Released in Version 5.6; between 5.6 and 6.0 Quick Start could open it at Adventure Rank 28 after A New Star Approaches. Completing it is required to unlock Song of the Welkin Moon Act I, A Dance of Snowy Tides and Hoarfrost Groves.

699.content: The Knights and Church jointly try Albedo for murder and illegal disposal of remains. Hertha prosecutes, Kaeya defends, Dahlia assesses and Jean presides because Varka is away. It was a pretext arranged beforehand to lure out an imposter.

700.content: Durin's life force produces spawn that consume people and take their form; acting on that power destabilises the other spawn. Albedo killed two spawn that had consumed people and buried what remained. The double of Albedo he killed on Dragonspine was different: a failed Homunculus Project specimen abandoned in Durin's stomach.

701.content: A pact among the Knights and Church of Favonius, the Anemo Archon and the Hexenzirkel for times of need. Varka secured the Hexenzirkel's aid, and Alice joins the conference as a giant Dodoco.

702.comment: Paralogism: The Game Before the Gate
702.content: Alice shrinks the party to fight on a chessboard at the Imaginarium Theater. After the first half Barbeloth turns the king and queen into the Ascended King and Sublimated Queen, and the Traveler and Albedo defeat them to earn the reagents.

key: Path to the Flaming Peaks World Quest series
703.content:
Path to the Flaming Peaks (also: Path to the Flaming Peaks World Quest series, Nahuatzin's Leap): Path to the Flaming Peaks (5.5) has a single quest, Nahuatzin's Leap. The party rides a Spiritway to the Skyfire Circlet, climb to the top and jump into the volcano. The golden text that has been guiding Little One grows clearer as they approach. Paimon is nervous about the height and the gaseous phlogiston, and notes that a Qucusaur grabs a statue and dives into the crater before them. The leap takes the party into the Ancient Sacred Mountain, the area explored in the following chapters.

The series is a link between Lost Traveler in the Ashen Realm and Chronicler of the Crumbling City. Its wiki infobox places it after the former and before the latter. The quest can be triggered by reaching the Skyfire Circlet by any route; the intended route is a Spiritway from Tephric Ruins or Remnants of Tetenanco.

The name echoes Nanahuatzin, an Aztec god who sacrificed himself in fire; the wiki notes this as a real-world etymology, not an in-game statement. After the leap the following quest in the chain is The Frozen, Rekindling Land.

Plot: Riding the Spiritway, Paimon wonders what is inside the volcano and worries it will be full of liquid phlogiston. On the Skyfire Circlet, Little One sees golden words telling it to climb to the highest pinnacle, hurl itself into the Sacred Mountain's flames, break the golden seal and reveal the radiance of remnant flames. They feel clearer to it than before. Paimon suspects whoever is speaking is inside the mountain.

At the summit, Paimon recalls being told there is a lot of gaseous phlogiston at the volcano's mouth; an attempt to jump without preparation sends them back to a waypoint. A strange statue near the rim is seized by a Qucusaur, which dives into the crater. The Traveler realises they can pass through the gas as the Qucusaur does. Paimon is frightened but agrees; Little One joins in, and the three leap together.

If the Investigator of Ancient Ruins quest was done, Paimon links the statue to the one Kimosi said a Qucusaurus had stolen. The wiki notes that any character can complete the jump; the dialogue implies one has to negate the gas's HP loss, but the map access depends only on quest progress.

Revelations: The only story point is the confirmation that the golden voice leads Little One towards the Sacred Mountain and that the mountain's interior is reached from the Skyfire Circlet.

Characters: Little One, Paimon and the Traveler. Paimon provides the comic relief about weight and fear of heights; Little One responds with growls. Kimosi is mentioned in a conditional line. The golden-text speaker is unnamed here.

Consequences: Rewards are Adventure EXP, Primogems, Mora, Hero's Wit and Mystic Enhancement Ore. The leap opens the Ancient Sacred Mountain map, which the player can enter only through this quest.

Placement: Version 5.5. In story order it follows Lost Traveler in the Ashen Realm and The Way Into the Mountain (which can no longer be started once the leap is done) and precedes Chronicler of the Crumbling City and A Finale Emberforged.

704.comment: Path to the Flaming Peaks: Skyfire Circlet leap
704.content: The Skyfire Circlet is the high rim around the volcano's crater. Paimon recalls being warned about heavy gaseous phlogiston at the crater mouth. A Qucusaur that steals a statue and dives in shows the way: the party must move through the gas the same way as the Qucusaur does. Golden text tells Little One to climb to the circlet's highest pinnacle and leap.

705.content:
Pavo Ocellus Chapter (also: Kaeya's Story Quest, Secret Pirate Treasure, Kaeya's Troubles): Kaeya's Story Quest, set in Mondstadt. Kaeya says his pirate grandfather buried a legendary sword and asks the Traveler to find it before Treasure Hoarders do. The hunt follows map clues around Mondstadt, and at the end Kaeya reveals it was a ruse to lure out a Treasure Hoarder leader.

The chapter has one act, Secret Pirate Treasure, of three quests: Kaeya's Troubles, Mystery of the Arcadian Ruins and Kaeya's Gain. It belongs to version 1.0 and unlocks at Adventure Rank 5 after The Outlander Who Caught the Wind. The Traveler can solve the clues with or without Kaeya's help.

The quest shows Kaeya using a staged story to set up an arrest and then apologising, with a promise not to deceive the Traveler again. The wiki trivia notes that the chapter title is Latin for a peacock's eye.

Plot: After Stormterror's attack, Kaeya tells the Traveler his grandfather was a pirate who buried a sword from Celestia. Treasure Hoarders are active nearby. Following clues from an informant, the Traveler reaches the ruins, where Hoarder leader Izzard ambushes them. Kaeya arrives and reveals the treasure hunt was a trap.

Kaeya's Troubles: at Knights of Favonius Headquarters, Kaeya looks worried and leads the Traveler and Paimon to the courtyard. He says his grandfather, a pirate, buried a legendary sword from Celestia to avoid conflict among his fellows, and he fears local Treasure Hoarders will find the ruins. He suggests asking at the Adventurers' Guild.

Mystery of the Arcadian Ruins: no one at the Guild knows of the ruins. Kaeya says he found an informant who will only meet in Whispering Woods. They rescue her from monsters; she gives them a map with a riddle about three six-armed giants in the city in the lake, two guarding a statue and one the treasure. This points to the windmills of Mondstadt. A second riddle found at a windmill leads to a waterfall behind Springvale, where they find the map to the Arcadian ruins.

Kaeya's Gain: at the end of the ruins, Izzard ambushes the Traveler and Paimon. Kaeya arrives and reveals the treasure hunt was a ploy. Izzard flees and wakes a Ruin Guard, which the Traveler and Kaeya destroy before arresting him. Kaeya apologises for the deception and offers the Traveler the Harbinger of Dawn.

Details: the Guild visit turns up nothing, and Kaeya then reveals the informant. The second riddle describes a woman who does not love a man and a spring whose passion is only a front; the quest resolves it to the waterfall near Springvale. After getting the final map Paimon argues they should find the sword themselves. Izzard admires Kaeya's tactics but still refuses to be taken. If the Traveler completed the hunt without Kaeya's help, he is impressed by their skill and returns to headquarters to interrogate Izzard.

The first riddle quotes: "Three six-armed giants reside in the city in the lake. Two guard the statue, one, the treasure." The informant Vile gives the map only after being rescued, and Kaeya had arranged the meeting at Whispering Woods for confidentiality.

Revelations: The treasure hunt was a ruse to trap a Treasure Hoarder leader.

Kaeya admits he tricked the Traveler. The wiki summary does not confirm whether the sword exists or whether his grandfather was a pirate.

The plan was to lure the Hoarder crew out of hiding so they could be apprehended.

Characters: Kaeya, the Traveler and Paimon.

Izzard, a Treasure Hoarder leader, and the informant Vile.

Consequences: Izzard is captured and taken in for interrogation. Kaeya promises not to deceive the Traveler again and offers the Harbinger of Dawn.

The Traveler sees that Kaeya will use half-truths to reach a goal, a trait the quest leaves unexplained.

Placement: Unlocks at Adventure Rank 5 after Prologue Act I, The Outlander Who Caught the Wind, and takes place after Stormterror's attack on Mondstadt. Released in 1.0.

706.comment: Pavo Ocellus Chapter: Secret Pirate Treasure
706.content: In Kaeya's Story Quest, Kaeya claims his pirate grandfather buried a legendary Celestia sword in ruins near Mondstadt. The Traveler follows riddles about windmills and a waterfall behind Springvale to the ruins, only to learn that Kaeya was baiting a Treasure Hoarder leader, Izzard.

707.content:
Perilous Trail (also: Interlude Chapter Act II, Perilous Trail Archon Quest): Interlude Chapter Act II. After the Chasm is reopened, the Traveler and Paimon meet Yanfei, Yelan, Arataki Itto and Kuki Shinobu at the Chasm Nail. The ground gives way and the group is trapped in a chaotic underground space, where they find Xiao hunting for news of his lost brother-in-arms Bosacius. Together they escape, and Xiao learns what became of him.

The act has five quests: The Unexpected Guest, Chasmic Maze, Danger All Around, End of the Line and At Tunnel's End, Light. It is a small-cast Liyue story that pairs the Traveler with characters who rarely meet, and it resolves a long-standing Yaksha question. During its first run it was a time-limited event with a lowered Adventure Rank requirement; the permanent act is canon for all players with the prerequisites.

Most of the act is a survival puzzle in a space that ignores ordinary logic: no hunger, tiredness or passing of time as expected, illusions that prey on each character's worst fear, and passages that loop back to where they began. The solution comes from combining human knowledge (Yanfei's exorcist expertise, Yelan's resourcefulness, Itto's brute force) with Xiao's adeptal power.

Plot: Curious about the Chasm after the spiritstone incident, the Traveler and Paimon return to the Chasm Nail and run into Yanfei, then Itto and Shinobu, then Yelan. The ground collapses and the group falls into the Chasm's Bed, a looping space they cannot leave. Xiao, searching for Bosacius, helps them reach the surface with an ancient compass, nearly sacrificing himself.

Yanfei is at the Chasm Nail on secret business; Itto and Shinobu are chasing her (Shinobu came to Liyue for her Tongwen Academy certificate, which the Sakoku Decree had kept her from collecting). Yelan arrives and warns everyone off, Itto takes offense, and the ground collapses into the Chasm's Bed. There they meet Xiao, who is looking for Bosacius, and enter an illusion-filled domain that loops back on itself and keeps them from feeling hunger or time passing. Doors show each person's worst fear. Yanfei works out that it is an antlion's den of chaotic rules, they rescue Xiao from an illusion, and Itto punches open a new path. Treasure Hoarders and Fatui agents are beaten, Xiao ends a remnant of Bosacius' memory, and a Fantastic Compass lifts the group out. Xiao is hurled to safety and then rescued by Zhongli; Xiao and the Traveler agree those who died defending Liyue are heroes.

**The Unexpected Guest.** The Traveler and Paimon find Yanfei at the Nail, apparently on important and secret business. Itto, who is looking for her, arrives with Shinobu. Shinobu explains she came back to Liyue to collect a Tongwen Academy graduation certificate she had been unable to pick up when the Sakoku Decree kept her in Inazuma; Itto came along as an escort and ended up in a brawl with the Millelith until Yanfei sorted it out. Shinobu slyly points Itto at the wrong target. When the Traveler meets Yanfei below the Nail, a mysterious woman, Yelan, arrives and tells everyone to leave because the Chasm is dangerous. Itto takes offense at her tone, and as the two square up the ground cracks and everyone drops into the Chasm's Bed. They find a portal and extremely old Liyue rock around it, then meet Xiao, who says he is searching for someone and tells them to leave before he vanishes. With no alternative, they enter the domain.

**Chasmic Maze.** After clearing the domain the group is back where it began. Itto calls on Ushi to find the demon he believes responsible, but Ushi finds no exit. Yanfei notes the ceiling has sealed. Yelan advises them to prepare for a long stay. The Traveler tries calling Xiao by name, but he does not come.

**Danger All Around.** A day later Paimon feels as though twenty days have passed, while the Traveler feels one. None of them has felt hunger, thirst or fatigue. Yelan finds a hidden path behind illusory magic. In the domain beyond they hear Xiao struggling, and a puzzle opens a door through which a projection of Xiao warns them before being cut off. A door in a later passage shows the opener their deepest fear: Itto faces disapproving Inazuma townsfolk and beans, Shinobu an old conversation with her mother about becoming a shrine maiden, Yanfei a civil dispute, and the Traveler the Abyss that took their sibling. Yelan declines to open it, saying she would have to kill everyone inside because she works for Ningguang and knows many Liyue secrets. Paimon grows tired and hungry, which shows the domain is targeting weaknesses. Back at camp Yanfei theorises it is a chaotic space whose rules can be turned against it, and the group drags Xiao out just in time.

**End of the Line.** Xiao explains he is looking for his old comrade Bosacius, whom he suspects died in the Chasm. His description fits Yanfei's idea that the domain is an antlion's den that uses illusions to trap victims. Xiao offers to spend all his power to push the others to the surface and stay behind; they refuse. Itto, told of the argument by Ushi, punches a path open and exhausts himself doing it. The new route leads to a large Fantastic Compass. Treasure Hoarders, hired thugs sent after Yanfei over a past case, are driven off, and Fatui agents beyond the compass are easily dispatched. They meet Xiao and a remnant of Bosacius' memory, which confirms that he was the Nameless Yaksha of the Chasm battle. Xiao ends the remnant after a short fight. In a manifestation of the Abyss the Traveler chases an illusion of their sibling and finds only a second compass. Yelan discovers someone had used it before and tries to unlock it.

**At Tunnel's End, Light.** Yelan learns the compass held only information about Boyang's fate, which discourages the group. Paimon knocks the other compass over, and it reacts to Yelan's and Xiao's energy. Yanfei realises it is an exorcism catalyst combining human magic arts and adeptal power, and that it can carry the group to the surface, though as part of the illusion it cannot be taken out. A rising platform carries them upward while Xiao channels power and malevolent energy tries to drag them back down. Xiao's energy gives out and he throws the others to the surface; the platform shatters and he starts to fall, but a swirl of yellow energy rescues him: he had told Zhongli of his plan beforehand. Afterwards Yelan leaves, Yanfei offers Itto and Shinobu a tour of Liyue, and Xiao invites the Traveler to Pervases' temple, saying not knowing Bosacius' fate had always bothered him. He and the Traveler agree that those who died defending Liyue are heroes of history.

The pairing of characters shapes the tone. Itto and Shinobu supply comedy and an outsider view of Liyue, Yanfei supplies the explanation for the chaotic space, and Yelan stays guarded and professional while hinting at her ties to Ningguang. Xiao's plan to sacrifice himself is rejected by the whole group, and Zhongli's rescue is possible only because Xiao told him of his plan before setting out.

The Nail, the Chasm's Bed and the compasses tie into the Chasm's wartime history. According to the wiki's Bosacius history, the Fantastic Compass was brought to the Chasm by Boyang and Rongzhao as a space-manipulating catalyst needing power from both a mortal and an adeptus, and Bosacius and Boyang volunteered to be sealed with the invading monsters. The act shows traces of that sacrifice rather than narrating it in full.

Revelations: The Nameless Yaksha of the Chasm battle was Bosacius, Xiao's missing comrade, who died defending Liyue.

The Chasm's depths hold a chaotic, illusion-laden space (the Chasm's Bed), which the wiki notes long predates the cataclysm and which was used to seal the invading monsters. The Fantastic Compass is an exorcism catalyst blending mortal magic arts with adeptal power.

Another compass in the depths holds information about Boyang, who sealed himself in alongside Bosacius. Xiao told Zhongli of his search first and is saved by him at the end.

Characters: Traveler and Paimon; Yanfei; Yelan; Arataki Itto (with Ushi); Kuki Shinobu; Xiao; Zhongli (indirectly).

Bosacius appears only as a memory remnant. Ningguang is mentioned in connection with Yelan. Fatui agents and Treasure Hoarders appear as enemies.

Boyang is referred to through the compass; the Millelith are mentioned in Shinobu's backstory.

Consequences: Xiao finally knows what happened to Bosacius. Yanfei offers a Liyue tour to Itto and Shinobu, and Xiao invites the Traveler to Pervases' temple. The Chasm remains a dangerous place with more history below.

The act deepens Xiao's characterisation and the Yakshas' legacy without changing Liyue's political situation.

Placement: Second act of the Interlude Chapter, after The Crane Returns on the Wind and before Inversion of Genesis. Released in Version 2.7. It follows the Chasm world quest line (including the spiritstone) and the Traveler's search for their sibling continues in the background.

708.content: In Perilous Trail the Fantastic Compass is an exorcism catalyst combining human magic arts and adeptal power. A large version and a smaller one appear inside the Chasm's illusion space. Together they carry the group to the surface, but the compass is part of the illusion and cannot be taken out. According to the wiki's Bosacius history, it was brought to the Chasm by Boyang and Rongzhao in the original battle.

key: Forest Boar and the Little Witch event
709.content:
Phantasmal Pals (also: Little Hexenzirkel's Secret Base, Forest Boar and the Little Witch event): The story runs in three parts. In the first, Paimon and the Traveler meet Prune near Chinju Forest and learn that the little witches are looking after a talking Forest Boar named Popcorn, who turns out to be an imaginary friend. In the second, the Yumekui-Baku explain that Popcorn was warped by a nightmare fragment and the group collects the fragments. In the third, the nightmares are devoured, Popcorn is reunited with his now-adult human Homura, and Prune finally admits why she is searching for witches.

The tone is gentle comedy built around childhood imagination and the pressures of adulthood. The two themes the event returns to are that adults also need play and rest, and that a child pushed to grow up too fast can lose the same spark.

Plot: Part I, The Forest Boar and the Little Witch. After a run of hard events Paimon suggests relaxing at Aisa Bathhouse. Two passers-by mention a crazed Forest Boar near Chinju Forest and a child asking for a witch. Paimon drags the Traveler along. In the forest they meet Prune, who first claims to be Alice's friend on a "witch-related incident" and shows a mismatched set of witch's tools from Alice: a bell, a hammer and an old Spantamad textbook. The bell rings, a Cryo Whopperflower appears, and the Traveler fights it. A card nearby reads like a request for help from the Dough King, with a Forest Boar drawn on it. The bell rings again and leads to the Little Hexenzirkel's base, where Klee is playing with the boar, Popcorn. Qiqi, Sayu and Yaoyao, with Klee, introduce themselves, and Paimon joins by letting Klee give her an "introduction magic" title. Prune is invited but declines, saying she stopped playing pretend long ago. Over a tea party, the children explain that Popcorn is an imaginary friend found wandering angry and amnesiac, that he speaks of a human named Homura who needs help, and that he repeats a rhyme about bringing on the tear-bugs and booger-beasts. The meeting ends with plans to wait for the Dough King's report.

Part II, If You Should Forget the Entrance to Dreams. Next day Shion introduces the Dough King and explains that baku regulate emotions by devouring nightmares. A nightmare fragment found near Popcorn carries a signature identical to his, which explains why he is visible in the real world. Three more fragments sit at locations on a map; because devouring one now could destabilise the others, they must be gathered first. Prune tries to keep the children out of it but they come along. The party splits up to search a grove in Chinju Forest, an area east of Konda Village (where Kirara is found napping in a tree and Arataki Itto is playing hide-and-seek with the children), and a beach north of Konda Village, where the last fragment is guarded by Slimes. The quest ends with a meal at the base, during which Prune says she has an imaginary friend named Descartes.

Part III, The Magic That Never Fails. The baku eat the fragments, and Popcorn recovers his memories. He explains that Homura is now an adult worn down by work, who dreamed a nightmare when she finally rested; he tried to fight it from inside and was swept away. Shion warns that the baku sensed no effort by Homura to overcome the feelings in the fragments, a sign of emotional numbness. In Inazuma City the group watches Homura with her boss, and the little witches quote Popcorn's rhyme until Homura finds her voice and negotiates a better arrangement. Popcorn and the group then speak with her directly, and she and Popcorn reconcile. Prune confesses that she is a Witch Hunter, that she never was Alice's friend, and that Alice told her she had taken Descartes and that the only way to get him back was to defeat the witches. The little witches reassure her and she joins the Little Hexenzirkel. Descartes then reappears, along with every little witch's imaginary friend, and Alice speaks.

Small details. The event's launch quest requires the Chapter II Act I part "Ritou Escape Plan" and recommends the Archon Quest True Moon. Open-world dialogue in Part I points to the four minigames (see gameplay). In Part II, Kirara says she dozed in a tree after feeling a nearby spot was off, Prune pulls her tail by mistake and apologises, and Prune cites a book titled "Little-Known Creatures of Teyvat: Inazuma Edition" on nekomata and baku. When Itto turns up, the children hide in the Lavender Melon patch and Prune remarks that he seems the biggest kid of them all.

Revelations: Popcorn is an imaginary friend who became visible and unstable after contact with a nightmare fragment, a materialised accumulation of negative emotions. His human, Homura, is now an adult overworked in her first job; the baku say her failure to resist her own nightmare signals emotional numbness. Alice tells the Traveler and Paimon that she never captured Descartes: his existence was close to fading because Prune, a precocious child who grew up too fast, was losing her childlike innocence. Alice invented the quest to send Prune to Mondstadt and the little witches, and chose Mondstadt because freedom nurtures imagination and she wanted Klee to have someone else to play with.

Prune is a "Witch Hunter" and has been lying about being Alice's friend. She came to Mondstadt after being told to defeat all witches, then travelled overnight by boat to Inazuma following a trail.

Characters: Main: the Traveler and Paimon, Prune, Klee, Qiqi, Sayu and Yaoyao. Also: the Dough King (Kohaku), Hyakujitsuhaku Shion (a Yumekui-Baku), Popcorn, Homura, Homura's boss, Kirara, Arataki Itto, Alice (voice and finale appearance), and Descartes. Imaginary friends who appear in the finale include Dodoco (Klee), Gena (Sayu) and Yuegui and Tuantuan (the pair from the Yaoyao minigame), as well as Descartes.

The children are all minors and the event treats them as such: they are playful, protective of each other and curious. Prune is a child who acts like an adult and is the most defensive of the group. Alice appears only as a voice at the end of Part III.

Consequences: Popcorn returns to normal, is reunited with Homura, and she resolves to deal with her work situation more openly. Prune joins the Little Hexenzirkel and is reunited with Descartes. Alice makes the little witches' imaginary friends visible for the celebration. Players received the weapon appearance Super Awesome Magic Key, which stays available after the event, and the five imaginary friends and a group photo as event items.

Placement: Released in Version 6.6 ("Truth Amongst the Pages of Purana"), 22 May to 8 June 2026, Adventure Rank 30 and the Chapter II Act I part "Ritou Escape Plan" required. Prune mentions in passing that she has climbed rooftops in Nod-Krai and that she moved to Mondstadt not long ago (Klee's words). It is a stand-alone story, not part of an Archon Quest.

Gameplay: Game mechanics, not in-world fact. Four minigames: Dodoco's Bomb-Rally Ruckus (Klee, passing the Jumpy Dumpty), Gena's Great Escape (an endless runner with Sayu's imaginary friend Gena), A Little Walk Home (Yaoyao's Yuegui finding Tuantuan) and Fantasy Realm Performance (hunting training with Prune). Completing challenges earned Pals Synergy; reaching 900 gave the Super Awesome Magic Key and the final tier a Crown of Insight.

710.content: A talking Forest Boar who is the imaginary friend of a young adult named Homura, who works for a company in Inazuma City. He was found wandering, fast and angry, with patchy memory, after a nightmare fragment materialised him. He repeats a rhyme Homura wrote as a child and insists she is the best no matter what. After the baku devour the fragments he recovers his memory and goes back to her.

711.content: A children's club founded by Klee, with Sayu, Yaoyao and Qiqi as the other members, plus Paimon and later Prune. Yaoyao suggested the "Little" because they still have growing to do. Membership needs only an invitation from Klee, who can give each member an introduction magic that Alice taught her. The group meets in a secret base, shares snacks and toys, and treats the Hexenzirkel's real witches as models. Not to be confused with the Hexenzirkel itself.

712.content: The Dough King, also called Kohaku, and the baku Hyakujitsuhaku Shion (who speaks of patients at a clinic and is in charge while Mizuki is away) explain that Yumekui-Baku are dough-bodied youkai who help humans regulate their emotions by devouring nightmares. They cannot easily carry tools, so they ask the Traveler's group to bring them the fragments. The baku fast beforehand and prepare the fragments with seasoning.

713.content: A fragment is a materialised accumulation of negative emotions. Popcorn carries the same signature as the one found near him, and there are three more at locations in Inazuma. Because devouring one early could make the others more volatile, the group gathers all four before the baku eat them together.

714.content: Prune presents herself as a professional investigator and a friend of Alice, but admits at the end that she is a Witch Hunter whose imaginary friend, the puppy Descartes, was gone after she lost a debate to Alice. Alice later says she did not take Descartes and had created the whole task to help Prune. Prune joins the Little Hexenzirkel and Descartes returns.

key: Polkka Beneath the Moon's Oracle Chapter
The Mirrors, the Maze, and the Tsar
The Tale of the Gate Stone
715.content:
Polkka Beneath the Moon's Oracle (also: Polkka Beneath the Moon's Oracle Chapter, For a Green Island..., Gift of the Mirage, The Mirrors, the Maze, and the Tsar, The Tale of the Gate Stone, Echoes of an Unfinished Past): Polkka Beneath the Moon's Oracle is a Nod-Krai World Quest series on Hiisi Island, added in Version 6.0 (Luna I). Four quests can be done in any order: a flustered young Frostmoon priestess named Verna tries to calm unstable kuuvahki at Thunderclap Reef, an angler is puzzled by empty waters, a child hunts for pretty stones, and a self-styled master thief hunts a crab. Each leaves a stone fragment on a large rock that later flies to a pillar at the Sanctum of the Oathkeeper. The fifth quest opens a sealed sanctum and meets the recorded echo of Aila, the first Moonchanter.

The tone is comic on the surface (a priestess who "trusts science", a thief with borrowed bravado) with a quieter thread: a robed woman who speaks in riddles keeps appearing and, in the end, is explained by Aila's recorded blessing. The series is also the Traveler's first sustained contact with Frostmoon Scions customs outside the main Archon Quest.

The English title plays on "polkka", the Finnish form of the polka dance, as the wiki notes. The stones are the series' running mechanism: kuuvahki-charged fragments that, thrown at or fixed to large rocks, draw those rocks toward the sealed Court of the First Edict area.

Plot: For a Green Island... In Thunderclap Reef the Traveler and Paimon meet Verna, a priestess in a kuuvahki-resistant suit who is on a secret mission to calm the reef's unstable kuuvahki. Her plan, which she calls science, is to throw charged stone fragments at two huge rotating boulders. Her Kraka robots fetch the fragments but get stuck, so the Traveler retrieves them; the first attempt makes things worse before a third fragment is found. A robed woman waits there, calls the Traveler the hero of "Elysium", hands over the last fragment in a Moon Mirror, and says she will wait at the Court of the First Edict. A Frostnight Scion wakes and must be defeated; afterwards the third fragment is freed and the boulders fly toward the Sanctum of the Oathkeeper.

Gift of the Mirage. The angler Pekkani, who is not a Frostmoon Scion and has no kuuvahki power, is catching no fish and asks the Traveler to look under the water west of the Frostmoon Enclave. Fragments placed on a stone there raise a platform and make a big rock fly off; the fish return.

The Tale of the Gate Stone. In the Frostmoon Enclave a child named Kasha is looking for pretty stones to give a friend named Mai, an outsider girl of about her age. The Traveler finds a kuuvahki-affected stone that Kasha senses wants to join a large stone; placing it makes the large stone rise and fly to the same pillar.

The Mirrors, the Maze, and the Tsar. In a pit west of the Enclave a thief named Maite Veliu, who claims to be the heir of the legendary thief Reed Miller, recruits the Traveler to take a treasure from the Crab Tsar. The Traveler clears blocked passages with the help of rock crabs, breaks a Moon Mirror at the advice of the same robed woman, and defeats the Crab Tsar, which has been carrying a large stone. The stone flies away and the crab, ashamed, hides.

Echoes of an Unfinished Past. See below (this quest is unlocked after the other four).

Details of the Thunderclap Reef plan: after the first two fragments the kuuvahki turns to a violent "reversed chaotic" state with lightning, which Verna admits she mishandled. The robed woman greets the Traveler, who is addressed by her as the hero of "Elysium"; when Verna accuses her of being an impostor, the woman answers that masks only matter once someone sits in the seat. She says that "Via" (the wiki's tooltip reads Lovia; Verna takes it for her own name) has no place in a world where the "god" has been born, and invites the party to meet her at the Court of the First Edict, a place Verna says has been sealed for five hundred years.

Echoes of an Unfinished Past. Verna meets the Traveler again, unhelmeted, and has gathered more fragments from her Krakas. She plans to break the seal of the Court of the First Edict to trap the "impostor". At the Light-Bathed Platform a fragment sends the floating rock back to its pillar, which drops onto the lower one and draws the island's attention. A Moonlane leads into the Interstice of the Nearing Moon, where three pillars must be slid onto tracks. A mechanical voice runs an identity check, grants authority and asks for the seal to be lifted by hand; the final greeting depends on which Natlan quests the player has finished. Ehrnrooth, Krodo and Rahetar, other Frostmoon Scions, notice the intruders. Inside the Court of the First Edict, called the Sanctum of the Oathbearer in some lines, the party sees the Verdant Crest and the White Spring. A white kuuhenki leads to a recorded image of Aila, who speaks with an unnamed man later called Solovei. Aila shows awareness of the Traveler, explains she steered them there with the stones, and leaves a sword in the White Spring. Rahetar then leads Verna away to answer to the Lady Moonchanter for tampering with a sealed place.

Gift of the Mirage ends with Pekkani paying in assorted items he fished up and saying Mora is little use on Hiisi Island; he also grumbles about "that annoying bard" and a pet, a passing reference this series does not develop.

In The Mirrors, the Maze, and the Tsar, Maite says the Crab Tsar used to be gentle and could not pass through the mirrors until it picked up a stone about six months earlier, after which it grew cruel. She says she is a member of the Conch Gang gathering intelligence and rewards the Traveler with an IOU and her notes; she tells the Traveler to mention her name at the Speranza restaurant in Nasha Town, and that the Traveler must still settle bills with Katya. She describes the Conch Gang as a mutual aid group of like-minded young people and says her information on the Frostmoon Scions came from someone she calls Big Sis Hidimbi, who is still in Nasha Town. Maite also recalls being caught by a "naive little girl" among the Scions and released after telling stories; The Tale of the Gate Stone shows Kasha describing catching a girl called Mai, who tells her outside stories; the two accounts match closely but neither quest names the other's character.

Revelations: - The unstable kuuvahki at Thunderclap Reef worsened after two large stones fell from the sky; Verna says it has always been unstable since the first Moonchanter's time.
- The Court of the First Edict, a sacred site of the Frostmoon Scions, was sealed about five hundred years ago by Aila, the first Moonchanter.
- The robed woman is probably tied to Aila (see uncertainties). Aila's recording says its blessing only records awareness, and that she steered the Traveler with the fallen stones because the Traveler's thread would not catch in the loom of this world.

- Aila speaks of sealing the evil and corruption left by Lovia so the children of the faith are not stained, and calls this part of the preparation for the birth of a god. She says Lovia trusted her because she obeyed, and that she severed Lovia's thread when guided by the Lady of the Underworld.
- Solovei, speaking with Aila, says he came to help, thanks her, and wants to uncover a "mad monk" using years of secret correspondence with Lovia as evidence.
- Aila gives the Traveler a sword forged from Hyperborean moonlight by an apostle of the golden city, left in the White Spring as an apology, and hopes the Traveler is the hero meant to fell an undying serpent.
- Verna says Aila's name was struck from the record for blasphemy and is known only to senior priestesses.

- Players who have completed the Natlan Archon Quest will hear the final seal greet the Traveler as the ruler named in that quest line; those who have not hear a more generic greeting. This is conditional dialogue, so do not treat it as true for every Traveler.

Characters: Verna, a young priestess who misquotes scripture, trusts robots and blames "science" for her plans. Pekkani, an angler. Kasha, a child of the Frostmoon Enclave who tells stories borrowed from outside. Maite Veliu, a young thief and Conch Gang member. The Crab Tsar, a large crab. Aila, the first Moonchanter, seen as a recorded echo. Solovei, a voice speaking with Aila. Ehrnrooth, Krodo and Rahetar, Frostmoon Scions who pursue the intruders. Paimon and the Traveler throughout.

Verna says she is a direct apprentice of "Papa Wrench" and the best mechanic on Hiisi Island; her faction views technology with suspicion. Her Kraka robots (III, V, VII) are her own successors to an earlier original, Kraka I, whose story she says is long.

Consequences: The large stones are returned to the pillar at the Sanctum of the Oathkeeper, and the Court of the First Edict is opened for the first time in five hundred years. Verna is taken to answer to the Lady Moonchanter. The Traveler gains Maite's IOU and notes, and the final quest's reward list includes Moonweaver's Dawn, presumably the sword Aila left (the wiki does not state this outright).

The quest links the Traveler to Aila's longer thread, which other Nod-Krai stories continue (see the Moonchanter and Frostmoon Scions entries). Lauma, the current Moonchanter, is named by Verna as someone she will need to apologise to.

Placement: Released in Version 6.0 (Luna I, 2025-09-10) alongside the first Nod-Krai content. The four opening quests can be done in any order; Echoes of an Unfinished Past unlocks only after the other four. The wiki's chapter infobox uses the Song of the Welkin Moon chapter image.

716.comment: Polkka Beneath the Moon's Oracle: Verna and the Kraka robots
716.content: Verna (full self-styled name Vernadska) is a young Frostmoon priestess in a kuuvahki-resistant suit and helmet who forgets scripture, trusts "science" and builds small Kraka robots. She introduces herself with a grand ritual line, takes the Traveler for a moon-blessed saviour, and hides that she is acting alone and against her faction's wishes because most Scions distrust technology. Her plans frequently go wrong and she admits she is panicking only after pretending not to.

717.comment: Polkka Beneath the Moon's Oracle: Crab Tsar and Crab Tsar's Palace
717.content: The Crab Tsar is a large crab ruling a cave palace west of the Frostmoon Enclave. It was normally docile until it carried a fallen stone on its back; the stone made it aggressive toward smaller crabs and allowed it to pass through old Moon Mirrors. After the Traveler defeats it, the stone flies off and the crab hides in remorse. Maite calls the stone a "stone of desire", a name she says came from Hidimbi.

718.comment: Polkka Beneath the Moon's Oracle: Court of the First Edict
718.content: A sacred site of the Frostmoon Scions sealed five hundred years ago by Aila. Inside are the Verdant Crest, a tree said to have witnessed the Moon Maiden's birth, and the White Spring, where Aila left a sword. It can be opened by sliding three pillars onto tracks in the Interstice of the Nearing Moon. The wiki gives the in-quest names inconsistently, using Oathkeeper for the sanctum with the pillar and Oathbearer for the inner site.

719.comment: Polkka Beneath the Moon's Oracle: Aila's recorded blessing
719.content: In Echoes of an Unfinished Past the Traveler sees a recording of Aila made by a blessing that records awareness, so that a later "brave warrior" can overhear. Aila says past and future are one for her, that she grieves nothing about Lovia, and that she must seal Lovia's sins in the Court of the First Edict. She meets a man called Solovei, tells him he will leave soon, and declares him the hero meant to protect "Elysium" in a prophecy-like speech. The Traveler is separately invited to look for those of her bloodline.

720.comment: Polkka Beneath the Moon's Oracle: Maite Veliu and the Conch Gang
720.content: Maite Veliu is a young self-styled master thief who claims descent from the legendary thief Reed Miller and is a member of the Conch Gang. She talks big and gets scared easily, wants the Crab Tsar's treasure, and later pays back the Traveler with an IOU and notes. She mentions Katya in Nasha Town as the person the Traveler must settle bills with, and warns that the Frostmoon Scions are dangerous. Kasha's story of catching a girl called Mai fits her own account of being caught, though no quest says so outright.

721.content:
Pomum de Ambra Chapter (Emilie) (also: Pomum de Ambra Chapter, Emilie's Story Quest, Floral Debt, Blood Due): The Pomum de Ambra Chapter is Emilie's Story Quest (Version 4.8). Its single act, Floral Debt, Blood Due, takes the Traveler and Paimon to a flower exhibition in Port Ormos, Sumeru, where Emilie, a perfumer from Fontaine, is chasing rumours that the extinct flower "Auguste" has returned. A murder case follows that exposes the flower's dark origin.

The act has three quests named after perfume notes: Top Note: Floral Debt, Middle Note: Blood Due and Base Note: Auguste. It requires Adventure Rank 40 and completion of Masquerade of the Guilty, the Fontaine Archon Quest finale.

Thematically the chapter is about the stories and meaning people attach to objects such as flowers and scents, and what happens when a market, or a person, cannot let go of the past. It is a detective story with Emilie as the investigator.

The wiki notes that the "Perfume Mania" resembles the historical tulip mania and that the name Auguste resembles the Semper Augustus tulip; these are wiki observations, not statements by the game.

Plot: **Top Note: Floral Debt.** In Port Ormos the Traveler and Paimon meet Tighnari, who is helping with a flower exhibition. Paimon begins to sneeze and a stranger gives them incense that cures it: Emilie, a Fontaine perfumer. She explains the "Perfume Mania" of twenty years ago, when perfume prices soared. Only the perfume "Auguste" never fell back, because the flower it was named for went extinct when its flowerbeds burned. Rumours say Auguste has reappeared in Sumeru, and cheap counterfeits plague Fontaine's market, so Emilie has come to dispel the obsession. Her mentor Edgar, the exhibition's flower expert and creator of Auguste, is ill; she takes the group to a hotel to tell the rest.

**Middle Note: Blood Due.** The next day a guest, Lucien, is found dead in his room with no sign of forced entry; the only way in was through the room of his companion Sylvain. Emilie reasons that Sylvain's grief is genuine, though the sheriff Shyam fears he is the suspect. Sylvain confesses and reveals the truth about Auguste: it was produced by a Fatuus named Yelena using a Delusion, which wore down her body, and the flowers and perfume could harm people over long exposure. He hides the involvement of Yelena and Kirya. Edgar allows himself to be taken into custody. Emilie later finds that a Glaze Lily had been used to hide a sample of Auguste in a Slime Condensate mixture that releases scent at night, and concludes that the hotel was a trap laid by Kirya, who had been disguised as Edgar. Soon after, Edgar is reported attacked and missing.

**Base Note: Auguste.** The group chases Kirya into a domain and finds him drinking a large amount of Auguste in an attempt to end his life. He survives because the perfume was fake: Emilie had made a perfect Auguste accord from Rainbow Roses, Glaze Lilies and Cecilias, and the earlier commotion was meant to lower his guard so he would not turn to stronger measures that endangered Port Ormos. Kirya accepts his fate and Eremites take him away. A few weeks later Emilie invites the Traveler to Fontaine, where her new perfume "Yelena" is selling well. She says its flowers carry the meaning "forgetting the past and keep on living", which she believes is the legacy Yelena would have wanted. Kirya sends thanks and learns that Auguste could mean something else.

Backstory revealed along the way: Yelena did not want Kirya drawn into the matter, and when the group considered burning the evidence she did it herself, destroying the evidence and herself. She left Kirya the money, including the cuts owed to Lucien and Sylvain, who then went looking for him to get their share back.

Revelations: Auguste was created by a Fatuus, Yelena, with a Delusion, which wore down her body. The flowers and perfume were not dangerous in brief contact but could harm over the long term. The exhibition's flower expert "Edgar" and the schemer Kirya are the same man. The flower's extinction followed a fire in which Yelena died.

Characters: Emilie, the Traveler and Paimon, with Tighnari, Collei and Kirya (as Edgar). Yelena appears only through past events.

Emilie is the investigator and the emotional centre: precise with scents and people, and weary of the stories attached to her work. Tighnari and Collei assist on the Sumeru side. Kirya is both mentor and culprit. The sheriff Shyam, the Eremite Innam, the guests Sylvain and Lucien, and Oguz, Neriman and Sanjay appear in minor roles.

Consequences: Kirya is taken into custody by Eremites. For Emilie the myth of Auguste is closed and she releases a new perfume named after Yelena. The case has no world-level consequences.

Placement: Release order: 4.8. Story order: after Chapter IV Act V, Masquerade of the Guilty, though events happen in Port Ormos, Sumeru. This is not an Archon Quest.

722.comment: Pomum de Ambra Chapter (Emilie): Floral Debt, Blood Due
722.content: Act I of Emilie's Story Quest. In Port Ormos, Emilie and the Traveler investigate deaths linked to Auguste, a legendary flower and perfume created with a Delusion by the Fatuus Yelena, and catch the schemer Kirya.

723.content:
Prelude of Blancheur and Noirceur (also: Chapter IV Act I, Fontaine Archon Quest Act I): Chapter IV Act I of the Archon Quest, set in Fontaine. After leaving Sumeru, the Traveler and Paimon arrive in the Hydro nation, meet the Archon Furina, and are drawn into a courtroom drama as the defence attorney for the magician Lyney, accused after a stage trick ends with a man dead and an audience member missing.

The act has three quests: Soloist's Prologue, The City of Rains and Remembrance, and Lies Cast Shadows Under Gathered Lights. It introduces Fontaine's trial-centred society, the water-level prophecy, the Oratrice Mecanique d'Analyse Cardinale, the Fatui connection of Lyney and Lynette, and the investigators of the Spina di Rosula. Released in version 4.0.

Tonally it is a courtroom mystery. The Traveler's "duel" with the Archon is a legal contest, not a fight, and the verdict is swayed by audience opinion as much as by evidence. The act sets up threads that later acts follow: Childe's strange loss of control over his Hydro, the missing-women case, and the Fatui's interest in Fontaine's prophecy.

Plot: At the Caravan Ribat the Traveler says goodbye to Dehya and heads for Fontaine. Furina has them charged with a minor law, but Lyney rescues them with a stage trick. Later, during Lyney's show at the Court of Fontaine, a man dies and a woman vanishes; the Traveler defends Lyney, and the trial ends with the real events exposed.

**Soloist's Prologue.** Before leaving Sumeru, the Traveler and Paimon meet Dehya, who offers a mercenary escort to the border and is turned down. At the Romaritime Harbor the locals Rena and Etienne explain that the Court of Fontaine works like an opera house, that Neuvillette and the Oratrice have ended false charges, and that Furina can only be seen by appointment. The Traveler meets Lynette, who says an area tied to a past memory is now underwater and that "they will be, too", and then her brother Lyney. Furina arrives with her entourage, welcomes the Traveler in her role as Archon, and declares a "duel" in court; she then points to a law against releasing a flying object on the first three days of a month and names Paimon as the offending object. Lyney snaps his fingers and a red cord of energy binds Paimon to the Traveler, so Paimon counts as a balloon that arrived attached, and Furina drops the matter, amused. Lyney explains the prophecy of rising water and gives the Traveler Magic Pockets to hand to residents near the waterline. The pair help him chase a pickpocket at the harbour, and Charlotte joins them on the aquabus to the court.

**The City of Rains and Remembrance.** At the twins' home they meet Freminet. Rain falls, which Lyney says usually happens when a trial is held. At the Beaumont Workshop, Truand of the Confrerie of Cabriere picks a fight, and Childe (Tartaglia), now in Fontaine, beats him; but Childe's Hydro weapons vanish mid-fight, and he says he has felt something stir in him. He recounts his time in the Abyss and his teacher Skirk, mentions he has been sparring with Fontaine's Champion Duelists, and entrusts the Traveler with his Vision before a duel against Clorinde. At the Fountain of Lucine a voice is heard, and Lynette offers a theory about tears and the fountain. In the opera house the Traveler sits next to Neuvillette, whom Lyney introduces. During the show, Lyney's box trick goes wrong: the tank falls and crushes the box, and Neuvillette locks down the house. Cowell is found dead in the box and the chosen audience member has gone missing, apparently the latest victim in the disappearances of young women. Furina names Lyney a suspect, turns the case into her second "duel", and invites the Traveler to act as defence.

**Lies Cast Shadows Under Gathered Lights.** The Traveler gathers evidence, meeting the sceptical Esmond and Navia of the Spina di Rosula, with her associates Silver and Melus. Lyney and Lynette demonstrate the box trick, and the group explores the tunnel under the stage. At trial, Furina exposes the twins as members of the Fatui's House of the Hearth, and Lyney confirms it. After a recess in which Lyney gives his account, the defence argues that Cowell used Primordial Sea water to change form. Esmond reports that Cowell's bag held labelled tubes of that water and that he belonged to a drug-selling organisation; Vaughn then produces the same water from Lyney's belongings. Navia arrives with the missing woman, who reappears from the magic box at Lyney's snap. She gives her name as Liliane (the harbour thief, not "Halsey") and confesses: terrified when the machine picked her and Lyney spoke of the Fortress of Meropide, she forced her way out of a soaked box, smashed a vase over Cowell's head in the confrontation, put him in the box, and hid in a costume chest. The Oratrice returns "Not Guilty" for the twins. Vaughn, exposed as Cowell's accomplice for presenting false evidence, begins to confess but dissolves into water before naming the "Boss". Afterwards Lyney explains the twins' past and apologises for the deception; Navia and her associates invite the Traveler to a farewell meal at Hotel Debord.

Details worth keeping straight: the missing-persons case Charlotte mentions concerns young women vanishing over some twenty years; Navia found Liliane partly through the "extra macarons" Paimon swore she had not taken, which pointed to someone hungry and hiding in the opera house. Neuvillette also says the conduct of both Lyney and Liliane warrants further investigation, so the verdict is not a full clearing of everything. Lynette's cryptic remarks and the unexplained voice at the fountain are left unresolved in this act.

Structural note: each of the three quests ends on an escalation (the arrest threat, the crushed box, the exposed Fatui link), and each "duel" is rhetorical. The first is won for the Traveler by Lyney's technicality about whether Paimon counts as an object; in the second the Traveler's Primordial Sea hypothesis shifts the scales, but the case is only won when Navia produces Liliane. The audience's reaction is shown on a scale that visibly tilts during the trial, so persuasion of the crowd, not only logic, shapes how events are received in Fontaine's court.

Revelations: Lyney and Lynette belong to the Fatui's House of the Hearth.

The twins are orphans who joined the House of the Hearth under the Knave, Arlecchino, who believes in the prophecy of Fontaine and intends to try to use the Hydro Gnosis to save Fontaine before taking it to Snezhnaya. A drug-selling organisation uses Primordial Sea water, and its member Vaughn dissolves into water on trying to name the "Boss". Childe is in Fontaine and his Hydro Vision is behaving oddly.

Lyney's account of his history: after their parents died the twins lived on the streets, surviving on magic tricks Lyney learned by secretly watching an older street magician. An aristocrat took them in for Lyney's talent, then sent Lynette as a "gift" to an "eminent person" he met at a banquet. When Lyney broke into that person's mansion, the Knave had already killed him and rescued Lynette and several hidden orphan girls; she then offered Lyney a place in the House of the Hearth and also destroyed the noble who had first taken them in. Lyney says the Knave has the Tsaritsa's permission to use the Gnosis's power first, to find a way to break the prophecy. Childe also describes being taken as an apprentice by Skirk in the Abyss.

Characters: Traveler and Paimon; Furina; Neuvillette; Lyney and Lynette; Navia.

Also Dehya (farewell), Freminet, Clorinde (the Champion Duelist), Charlotte (reporter), Childe, Esmond, Cowell, Vaughn, Liliane, Truand, Estelle, Rena and Etienne, and Navia's associates Silver and Melus.

Consequences: Lyney and Lynette are acquitted but remain under suspicion for their Fatui ties. The Traveler has Childe's Vision in safekeeping. The act leads into Act II, As Light Rain Falls Without Reason, in which events around Childe unfold.

The disappearances case is not closed: Liliane is a thief and not the abductor, and Vaughn's dissolution leaves the "Boss" unnamed.

Placement: Chapter IV Act I, following Caribert (the end of Chapter III in Sumeru) and before Act II, As Light Rain Falls Without Reason. Released in version 4.0.

724.comment: Prelude of Blancheur and Noirceur: Furina's court duels
724.content: Furina frames her meeting with the Traveler as a "duel" in court. First she tries to arrest them over a law against flying objects; later she becomes prosecutor against the Traveler as Lyney's attorney.

725.comment: Prelude of Blancheur and Noirceur: The opera house incident
725.content:
During Lyney and Lynette's first show, Cowell dies in a crushed magic box and a woman vanishes; the Traveler later shows she is Liliane the thief, who hid after striking Cowell.

The Oratrice's verdict clears the twins, and Neuvillette says further investigation of Lyney and Liliane's conduct is still needed.

726.comment: Prelude of Blancheur and Noirceur: Primordial Sea water evidence
726.content: Tubes of Primordial Sea water in Cowell's bag point to a drug-selling organisation; Vaughn, who produced the same water from Lyney's belongings, dissolves into water before naming the Boss.

727.content:
Princeps Cretaceus Chapter (also: Albedo's Story Quest, Traveler Observation Report, The Rumored Alchemist): Albedo's Story Quest, set on Dragonspine. Sucrose asks the Traveler to help her master, the Chief Alchemist of the Knights of Favonius, with his research. Albedo, who believes the Traveler comes from another world, runs a series of experiments on their powers and nature, and ends the act with a quiet worry about himself.

The chapter has one act, Traveler Observation Report, of six quests: The Rumored Alchemist, The Genius Researcher and the Seed of Another World, then the First, Second, Third and Final Experiments (Elements, The World, Life, Withering Glory). It was released in version 1.2 and unlocks at Adventure Rank 40 after For a Tomorrow Without Tears.

Rosaria watches the experiments with suspicion, and warns the Traveler that Albedo may have hidden motives. The act is as much a portrait of Albedo as a curious researcher who finds little lasting satisfaction in answers as it is a Traveler study.

Plot: At Timaeus' alchemy store, Sucrose tells the Traveler her master Albedo needs help with an experiment on Dragonspine. Albedo concludes the Traveler is from another world and wants to see how life behaves outside Teyvat. Across five tests he examines their elemental ability, mind, cooking, movement and puzzle-solving. He decides they are much like an ordinary person of Teyvat, shows a flower grown from his otherworldly seed, and voices a private fear.

The Rumored Alchemist: Sucrose recognises the Traveler as the one who repelled Stormterror. She would like to study them herself, but says Albedo, a master alchemist consulted from across Teyvat, is troubled by an experiment, and is likely to reward help. He is on Dragonspine with Timaeus.

The Genius Researcher and the Seed of Another World: at the foot of the mountains the Traveler meets Barbara trying to bring Rosaria to choir practice; Rosaria refuses and is also looking for Albedo for a reason she will not share. They find Albedo sketching near a group of hilichurls, who attack; he finishes and explains alchemy until Rosaria leaves, bored. Recognising the Traveler as the Honorary Knight, he reasons their abilities mean they come from another world, and asks to experiment on how life functions outside Teyvat with a sample he has. Rosaria spies on them, wondering if he is a risk to Mondstadt.

The experiments: First, after a test against slimes, the Traveler drinks a potion extracting elemental power, with Starsilver Catalyst they find on the way to his mountain camp; Albedo remarks that peculiar people's essence differs from ordinary people's. Second, the Traveler tries and fails to break a pillar with their mind, cooks Sunshine Sprat, and finds an Anemo Crystalfly Extract and Electro Hypostasis Power with Elemental Sight; Albedo suspects Teyvat's natural laws affect them. Third, the Traveler jumps from a peak and crosses a lake; they are faster than the average Mondstadt citizen. Albedo says his interests are often fleeting because learning the truth gives him no satisfaction. Final: the Traveler solves a locked mechanism with Seelies, they find strange writing on a wall and Albedo copies it. Rosaria stops them, is persuaded the Traveler is no threat, sets up patrols and copies the script.

Further details: Albedo says everything will be as safe as possible and promises compensation. Rosaria is dismissive of the alchemy talk. In the Second Experiment, Albedo expects an elemental-imbued meal to be needed and is hungry himself, and finds nothing unusual in the dish. In the Final Experiment, the water has receded when the Traveler and Albedo examine the ruins at the south end of the mountain.

Back at camp, Albedo concludes the Traveler is like an ordinary person of Teyvat, though their participation has inspired his research; he blooms a flower from the otherworldly seed. He thanks them and invites them to return when he needs help.

As they leave, Albedo notices sediment growing in the vial that he had not seen before. He says he and the Traveler are of a "different sediment", worries he will lose control and destroy everything he holds dear, and asks whether he can rely on the Traveler to stop him if that time comes. Rosaria had warned the Traveler before leaving to be wary of him, believing there is more behind his kind surface.

Revelations: Albedo believes the Traveler is from another world and studies them for it.

He finds the Traveler ordinary in nature but not in effect on his work. Strange writing is found on the wall of ruins in the Dragonspine foothills.

Albedo's sample is an otherworldly seed that flowers during the report. His closing remarks about sediment and losing control are the main hint of his hidden concern.

The act does not explain either the script or the sediment.

Characters: Albedo, Sucrose, the Traveler and Paimon.

Rosaria, Barbara and Timaeus.

Hilichurls and slimes appear as opponents and test subjects.

Consequences: Albedo invites the Traveler back for future help. Rosaria starts patrols in the area and keeps a copy of the wall script, wary of Albedo.

Albedo's request that the Traveler stop him if needed is a promise left open here.

Placement: Unlocks at Adventure Rank 40 after Prologue Act II, For a Tomorrow Without Tears. Released in 1.2, with the Dragonspine content. The wiki trivia says that during the limited events The Chalk Prince and the Dragon and Shadows Amidst Snowstorms the requirement was lowered to Adventure Rank 20 with no story keys.

728.comment: Princeps Cretaceus Chapter: Traveler Observation Report
728.content: Albedo's series of tests on the Traveler on Dragonspine. He concludes the Traveler is like an ordinary person of Teyvat, though they come from elsewhere, and uses the otherworldly seed to bloom a flower. He ends by voicing a worry about losing control, and asks for the Traveler's help if it ever happens.

key: Prologue: The Outlander Who Caught the Wind
The Outlander Who Caught the Wind chapter
729.comment: Prologue: The Outlander Who Caught the Wind
729.content:
Prologue: The Outlander Who Caught the Wind (also: Mondstadt Archon Quest, The Outlander Who Caught the Wind chapter): The Prologue, "The Outlander Who Caught the Wind", is the first Archon Quest chapter and is set in Mondstadt. The Traveler and their twin are stopped on their way between worlds by an unknown god, who seals the sibling away and strips the Traveler of power. The Traveler later wakes, meets Paimon, and goes to Mondstadt to seek the Anemo Archon, only to find the city threatened by the dragon Stormterror. With the bard Venti, who is the Archon Barbatos, the Traveler frees the dragon Dvalin from the Abyss Order's corruption, and Venti loses his Gnosis to the Fatui Harbinger Signora. The chapter ends by sending the Traveler to Liyue.

The chapter has three acts: The Outlander Who Caught the Wind (Act I), For a Tomorrow Without Tears (Act II) and Song of the Dragon and Freedom (Act III), released in Version 1.0. It doubles as a tutorial for movement and combat and introduces the Knights of Favonius, the Fatui and the Abyss Order.

Plot: Opening and Act I. In the introductory quest Wanderer's Trail the twins, travelling from world to world, are confronted by an unknown god who calls herself the sustainer of heavenly principles and declares that "the arrogation of mankind ends now". The sibling is cubed and taken, and the Traveler is also sealed and left powerless. The Traveler awakes after an unstated time, and about two months before the story begins they save Paimon from drowning near Cape Oath. Paimon becomes their guide and suggests meeting the Seven to find the sibling. At Starfell Lake the Traveler activates an Anemo Statue of the Seven and sees a green dragon fly toward a forest. They find the dragon and a stranger trying to calm it, but the Traveler's power draws the dragon's attention, and the stranger leaves behind a crimson teardrop crystal. Amber, the Outrider of the Knights, offers to escort them to Mondstadt and gives them a Wind Glider. Stormterror, as locals call the dragon, then attacks, and the Traveler, helped unseen by the stranger, drives it off. Kaeya sends them to the Acting Grand Master, Jean, who asks them to deal with the Ley Line disruptions at the Four Winds' temples on Lisa's advice.

Act II. Back in the city, the Traveler is named an Honorary Knight after Jean rejects a Fatui diplomat who wants the dragon killed. Venti, who is the stranger from the forest, reveals that the dragon is Dvalin, one of the Four Winds, who is suffering and being exploited by the Abyss Order. Their plan to cure him needs the Holy Lyre der Himmel from the Favonius Cathedral. The Fatui seize it first; with the help of Diluc and Jean the party recovers it, repairs it with Dvalin's tears and summons the dragon at Starsnatch Cliff, but an Abyss Mage persuades him that Venti betrayed him, and the lyre is destroyed.

Act III. Diluc reports that an Abyss Mage has been killed at the winery and that its death released energy that was cutting Venti off from Dvalin. Venti breaks the barrier over Dvalin's hideout, the old Mondstadt of the tyrant Decarabian, and the party fights through hilichurls to a light actuator that Venti charges with Anemo power. The Traveler purges the corruption from Dvalin. Venti explains that he refused to order Dvalin to be free, since a command could not give freedom, and Dvalin leaves. Jean corrects the people's belief that the dragon appeared from nowhere.

At the same time the Knights beat back a coordinated hilichurl assault on the city. Kaeya, who stayed behind because he suspected the attack, intercepted Abyss Order infiltrators and learned from them that the Order is united under a single leader. Amber tells the Traveler that they will always be welcome in Mondstadt. At the Cathedral the Traveler gives Barbara the broken lyre; Venti makes it look repaired by magic and flees. Outside, a gust of cold freezes Venti and Paimon, Fatui Agents restrain the Traveler, and Signora, accompanied by two Cicin Mages, taunts Venti and rips his Gnosis from his chest. The Traveler is knocked out. Barbara finds them, and Venti leaves abruptly. Jean and the Traveler find him at the tree at Windrise, where he explains what a Gnosis is and who Signora is: the eighth of the Eleven Fatui Harbingers, who serve the Tsaritsa of Snezhnaya. Paimon realises the Tsaritsa is one of the Seven they are seeking. Venti says the Seven usually did not get along but respected each other, and that a certain catastrophe five hundred years ago severed relations completely. He sends the Traveler to Liyue, where the Geo Archon descends once a year for the Rite of Descension, and warns them to hurry.

Each act is a sequence of quests. Act I runs from Bird's Eye View through Unexpected Power, Forest Rendezvous, Wind-Riding Knight, Going Upon the Breeze, City of Freedom, Dragon Storm and Knights of Favonius, followed by optional Winds of the Past (Amber), Crash Course (Kaeya) and Sparks Amongst the Pages (Lisa). Act II lists fifteen quests, from Shadow Over Mondstadt to Reunion With the Dragon, including three tear quests (Fallen, Hidden, Stolen) done in any order. Act III runs Abyss Mage, Hurdle, Empty Abode, Light Guiding Ceremony, Calm Before the Storm, A Long Shot, When the Wind Dies Down and Ending Note. Act I requires completion of Wanderer's Trail, Act II requires Adventure Rank 10 and Act III requires Adventure Rank 18. Wanderer's Trail itself does not appear in the Archive's Travel Log.

The game's first closed beta differed in several ways, according to the wiki: the cataclysm was dated 100 years ago rather than 500, the Fatui hardly appeared, and Signora's ambush did not occur. These are development history, not canon.

Revelations: - The Traveler and their twin came from other worlds and were separated and sealed by an unnamed god; the Traveler has lost their power.
- Venti, the wandering bard, is Barbatos, the Anemo Archon.
- Stormterror is Dvalin, one of the Four Winds, who protected Mondstadt and was corrupted by the Abyss Order.
- The Fatui, acting through one of the Eleven Harbingers, will take a god's Gnosis by force. Signora removes Venti's.
- The Tsaritsa, the Cryo Archon, is one of the Seven and has broken from them since a catastrophe 500 years ago.

- The Abyss Order has a single leader, and the Traveler's sibling is shown overlooking Stormterror's Lair as Abyss Mages bow to them and speak of a homeland returning to the world (Act II). The Prologue explains none of it.
- The Prologue ends with the Traveler's goal set: meet the Seven, starting with the Geo Archon in Liyue.

Characters: Traveler and Paimon: protagonists. Venti: the Anemo Archon in disguise as a bard. Dvalin: the afflicted dragon of the Four Winds. Knights of Favonius: Jean (Acting Grand Master), Kaeya (Cavalry Captain), Amber (Outrider), Lisa (Librarian). Diluc: winery owner and informal ally. Barbara: Church of Favonius deaconess. Signora: Fatui Harbinger, the chapter's villain. The Cryo Abyss Mage and the Abyss Order are the dragon's corrupters. The Traveler's sibling and the unknown god appear in cutscenes.

Gotelinde, a sister at the Cathedral, refuses the lyre in Act II. A Fatui diplomat appears in Act II, and Fatui agents and Cicin Mages carry out the thefts and the ambush.

Consequences: Dvalin is freed and reconciled with Mondstadt; the people learn the truth of the dragon's attacks. The Traveler becomes an Honorary Knight. Venti loses his Gnosis, and the Fatui now hold it. The Traveler leaves for Liyue to seek the Geo Archon.

The Prologue establishes the Traveler's search, the role of the Fatui and Abyss Order as recurring forces, and the Gnosis as a god's power item, themes that carry through the later chapters. Chapter I continues in Liyue with Of the Land Amidst Monoliths.

Placement: The first Archon Quest chapter, released in Version 1.0 and in story order before Chapter I. Its acts must be played in sequence: Act I, Act II, Act III.

730.comment: Prologue: The Outlander Who Caught the Wind: Wanderer's Trail Opening
730.content: In the opening cinematic the Traveler and their sibling are stopped by a white-clad god who calls herself the sustainer of heavenly principles and declares that "the arrogation of mankind ends now". She seals the sibling, then the Traveler, who loses their power. The Traveler later meets Paimon, who becomes a guide. The god is not named on screen; the wiki and later content identify her as Asmoday.

731.comment: Prologue: The Outlander Who Caught the Wind: Venti's Gnosis Taken
731.content: After the Dragon is calmed, Signora ambushes Venti outside the Favonius Cathedral and rips out his Gnosis, then flees before the Knights arrive. Venti tells the Traveler and Jean what a Gnosis is and who Signora is, and sends the Traveler to Liyue.

key: Questioning Melusine and Answering Machine World Quest series
732.content:
Questioning Melusine and Answering Machine (also: Questioning Melusine and Answering Machine World Quest series, Vagrants and Scamps, The Red and the Black, Questions and Answers, Sir Arthur case, Talochard and Curve case): Questioning Melusine and Answering Machine is a three-act world quest series in Fontaine, added in version 4.2. The steambird mascot Sir Arthur has vanished from the office of the newspaper The Steambird. The Traveler and Paimon help the Melusine detective Talochard, of the Marechaussee Phantom, and her investigation mek Curve to find him.

The series is a mystery with a comic start and a bittersweet ending. Its acts are "Vagrants and Scamps", "The Red and the Black" and "Questions and Answers". It requires the story quest "A Fontainian Message" to be complete.

The missing bird leads to the editors of The Steambird, a gang of con artists, a Fatui intelligence officer and the legacy of the scientist Mosso Lombroso. The main emotional thread is the bond between Talochard and Curve.

Plot: Outside The Steambird's office the Traveler and Paimon settle an argument between the Melusine agent Talochard and the editor Jenck. Sir Arthur, the steambird, is missing. Euphrasie, the editor-in-chief, arrives with Curve, a Suppression Specialist Mek built by the scientist Mosso Lombroso, which the Marechaussee Phantom lets Talochard use for investigations. Clues lead from a drunk named Rocher to a boy, Kevin, and to a con-artist gang, the Elegant Tableware Confrerie, then to a Fatui officer who was hunting for Mosso's old research base and a threatening letter demanding Mosso's name be cleared.

The case turns out to hinge on a thirty-year-old scandal. Melo Lombroso, Mosso's granddaughter, reveals that Mosso staged his own disgrace to save Curve. A map hidden in a locket leads to Mosso's underwater base, where Jenck, who allied with the Fatui to take Euphrasie's post, triggers its self-destruction. Curve tells his first lie to get the others out and stays behind.

**Act I - Vagrants and Scamps.** Outside the offices of The Steambird the Traveler and Paimon settle an argument between Talochard, a Melusine of the Marechaussee Phantom, and the editor Jenck. Sir Arthur, the steambird, has gone missing. The editor-in-chief Euphrasie arrives with Curve, a Suppression Specialist Mek built by the scientist Mosso Lombroso, which belongs to the Marechaussee Phantom and which Talochard uses for special investigations. From clues at the scene the group draws up four suspects, with the drinker Rocher the strongest lead. They defeat the debt collectors who chase him, and find he did fall asleep by the office entrance but only saw a small figure running away. That figure was a troublesome boy, Kevin, who took a knife left at Sir Arthur's pedestal when a drunk man startled him. The knife is traced to the Elegant Tableware Confrerie, a group of con artists.

**Act II - The Red and the Black.** The group tracks the Confrerie and catches them by feeding them Talochard's unusual Poissonchant Pie. Their member "Intrepid Valberry" admits he left the knife as a warning after The Steambird exposed the Confrerie, and he sent for a locksmith at Fleuve Cendre, where he met a Fatui officer, Baulard, who wanted the same thing. Baulard is a peripheral intelligence officer tasked with finding Mosso Lombroso's research base. He had fed the paper intelligence on the Confrerie, and Jenck would not repay him with Steambird information about Mosso, so he tried to break in. At the office he found Sir Arthur gone and a letter signed "Crow or Blackbird?" demanding that The Steambird clear Mosso of his crimes. After dinner at Hotel Debord the group reconstructs the order of the visitors that night. The story behind the letter is an old one: thirty years ago The Steambird reported that Mosso had faked evidence for his lie-detector technology, and he was arrested and died in a duel rather than stand trial.

**Act III - Questions and Answers.** A second letter says Sir Arthur has been dismembered and gives three locations for the parts, saying they will be buried with the treasure in Mosso's base. Euphrasie suspects Mosso's granddaughter Melo Lombroso. The Traveler recovers the parts from three sites. At the last, Talochard, Curve and Kevin's mother Madeleine are fighting the Fatui. Madeleine and Kevin's father are both Fatui, and the father is Baulard, whose real name is Baulande. The group persuades him to hand over Sir Arthur's head, and he leaves with his family to escape the Fatui. Rocher reveals he is Melo's husband and denies she is behind the letters.

Melo has an alibi and denies knowing where Mosso's base is, but she reveals that the sensational articles about Mosso were submitted by Mosso himself. When Fontainians rioted over lie-detector technology being developed in Fontaine, he drew all attention to himself to save Curve, whom he saw as the culmination of his work. The Marechaussee Phantom took Curve in as evidence and left him in storage for thirty years until Talochard found him. A locket with a childhood photo of Melo reveals a map when held to the sunlight, leading the Traveler, Paimon, Talochard and Curve to Mosso's underwater research base and a letter from Mosso to the former editor-in-chief.

There Jenck and the Fatui arrive. Jenck is the mastermind: he allied with the Fatui to displace Euphrasie as editor-in-chief. He triggers the base's self-destruct. Curve says he can stop it if the Traveler removes his core and places it in the control panel, but doing so only opens the doors to the emergency room, and he stays behind. The Traveler, Paimon and Talochard escape as the base is destroyed. Curve had told his first lie, knowingly sacrificing himself.

**Clues and suspects (Act I).** The Traveler arrives as Talochard and Jenck argue outside the office, and Euphrasie turns up with Curve afterwards. The clues at the scene yield four suspects; the most reliable lead is Rocher, whose used wine bottle was left near the entrance, and the leads that follow include the boy Kevin and the Confrerie. Rocher's dog, called Lombroso, identifies his master's bottle. Kevin's mother Madeleine says she saw Kevin carrying a knife after he came back from the office, matching the knife found at Sir Arthur's pedestal. Kevin explains that his father's absence has made him act out.

**The reconstruction (Act II).** At Hotel Debord, after Talochard has tried to give up, the group acts out the scene in order. Rocher fell asleep first. Baulard came second, found the letter and the missing bird, and took the letter with him, which is why nobody at The Steambird knew about the demands. "Intrepid Valberry" came third and left the knife as a warning. Kevin came last and woke Rocher, grabbing the knife in panic. The group also learns that a "Boss" and "Intrepid Valberry" fight over the Confrerie's money.

**The case behind the case (Act III).** Kevin has turned over a new leaf by now and helps find Sir Arthur's wing with a dog, Baulande, who looks like Rocher's dog. Rocher discovers that the dog he has been calling Lombroso actually belongs to Kevin. At the second site "Intrepid Valberry" and "Boss" quarrel over treasure while Rocher begs for the part in the chest, and they agree to hand Sir Arthur's body over to the Traveler.

**Mosso's base and aftermath.** Jenck is found a few days later kneeling on the stage of the Opera Epiclese, apparently insane and with his tongue cut out, with a note apologising to the Traveler, Paimon and Talochard. The Traveler wonders if the Fatui Harbinger responsible is interested in machine intelligence. Talochard is anguished by Curve's loss and seeks revenge on Jenck, but the three cannot find him. Euphrasie adds a recorded commendation to the rebuilt Sir Arthur's voice library: Curve's analysis that Talochard would be the best agent in the Marechaussee Phantom.

**Talochard's character in the case.** Talochard is a Melusine agent who works for the Marechaussee Phantom on her own initiative on this case and blames herself for failing to identify a suspect. After the Confrerie episode she suddenly wants to give up and offers to take the Traveler and Paimon to dinner at Hotel Debord. She had rediscovered Curve in storage and been using him for special investigations.

**Mosso Lombroso's plan.** Melo says Mosso sacrificed his name to protect his work, and Curve was kept alive as the proof of it. The tale of 'falsified evidence' was therefore his own doing, published by The Steambird at his request. The letter from Mosso to the former editor-in-chief, found at the base, sets out the truth about the incident.
