**Gameplay note (labelled as such).** The investigation involves gathering clues, a scene reconstruction at the end of Act II, and fights against the Confrerie's debt collectors and the Fatui. These do not change the lore.

Revelations: - Sir Arthur's disappearance was not a random prank but connected to an old scandal: the thirty-year-old story that Mosso Lombroso had faked evidence for his lie-detector technology.
- That scandal was staged by Mosso himself. He had The Steambird publish the articles to draw public anger away from Curve and died in a duel instead of standing trial.
- Curve, the Marechaussee Phantom's investigation mek, sat in storage for thirty years before Talochard found him. His first lie lets the Traveler, Paimon and Talochard escape.

- The Fatui officer Baulard, whose real name is Baulande, was hunting for Mosso's research base on behalf of a Harbinger, and his wife Madeleine, also a Fatui member, and son Kevin were living in Fontaine.
- Jenck, an editor of The Steambird, allied with the Fatui to take Euphrasie's post as editor-in-chief and was the real mastermind. He is later found mentally broken at the Opera Epiclese.
- Rocher is Melo Lombroso's husband.

Characters: The Traveler and Paimon; Talochard, a Melusine of the Marechaussee Phantom; Curve, a Suppression Specialist Mek; Euphrasie, the editor-in-chief of The Steambird, and Jenck, an editor; the drinker Rocher and his dog; the boy Kevin and his mother Madeleine; the con artists "Intrepid Valberry" and "Boss"; the Fatui Baulard/Baulande; and Melo Lombroso, Mosso's granddaughter. Mosso Lombroso appears through letters and recollection. Sir Arthur is the missing steambird.

Talochard blames herself when the case stalls and is grief-stricken at the end. Curve's single lie, described by the quest as his first, is the key moment of the series. Jenck's motive is to replace Euphrasie as editor-in-chief. Baulande leaves with his family to escape the Fatui.

Consequences: Sir Arthur is rebuilt, with Curve's recorded commendation of Talochard added to its voice library. Curve is lost with the research base. Jenck is found ruined. Baulande and his family leave to escape the Fatui.

The truth about Mosso's staged downfall is learned by the Traveler, Talochard, Euphrasie and Melo. The wider public story is not shown changing.

Placement: Requires "A Fontainian Message". Released in version 4.2. Acts I to III are played in order over several in-game days.

733.comment: Questioning Melusine and Answering Machine: Talochard
733.content:
Talochard is a Melusine agent attached to the Marechaussee Phantom who takes up the case of the missing steambird on her own account. She works with the investigation mek Curve. She is hard on herself when the case stalls, and her Poissonchant Pie is described as unique, which the group uses to trap the Confrerie. This entry covers the case only.

After Curve's sacrifice she is grief-stricken and wants revenge on Jenck. Euphrasie later shows her a recording of Curve naming her the best agent in the Marechaussee Phantom.

734.comment: Questioning Melusine and Answering Machine: Curve
734.content:
Curve is a Suppression Specialist Mek built by the scientist Mosso Lombroso. Mosso's research was on lie-detector technology. Curve belongs to the Marechaussee Phantom and first lies at the destruction of Mosso's base, where he tells the group that his core can stop the self-destruct sequence. It can only open the door to the emergency room. He stays behind while the others escape.

Melo says Mosso saw Curve as the culmination of his research and ruined his own name to protect him. The Marechaussee Phantom held Curve as evidence for thirty years before Talochard found him.

735.comment: Questioning Melusine and Answering Machine: Sir Arthur
735.content: Sir Arthur is the steambird figure kept on a pedestal in the office of The Steambird. Its disappearance starts the case. Its parts are hidden at three places, and its head is held by Baulande. It is rebuilt after the case, with a voice library that contains Curve's commendation of Talochard.

736.comment: Questioning Melusine and Answering Machine: Jenck and Euphrasie
736.content: Euphrasie is the editor-in-chief of The Steambird. Jenck, one of her editors, helped the Fatui in order to take her post and set off the destruction of Mosso's base. He is later found broken and mute on the stage of the Opera Epiclese, with a note apologising to the Traveler, Paimon and Talochard.

737.comment: Questioning Melusine and Answering Machine: Baulard (Baulande)
737.content: Baulard, whose real name is Baulande, is a peripheral Fatui intelligence officer working for one of the Eleven Fatui Harbingers. He was searching for Mosso Lombroso's research base and took the first threatening letter from The Steambird's office. His wife Madeleine and son Kevin live in Fontaine. He hands over Sir Arthur's head and leaves with his family to escape the Fatui.

738.content:
Rapperia Chapter (also: Rapperia, Clorinde's Story Quest, Silent Night, Judgment Day, Hunters' Gathering, Buried Honor, Vanquishing Phantoms, Tabletop Troupe quest): Clorinde's Story Quest. She and Navia, both veterans of a local roleplaying club called the Tabletop Troupe, invite the Traveler, Furina and Lyney to play a new game about the Marechaussee Hunters. The script's author, Florian, has hidden a real purpose behind it, and the party ends up facing a real monster in a hidden vault and a church basement.

The chapter has one act, Silent Night, of four quests: Judgment Day, Hunters' Gathering, Buried Honor and Vanquishing Phantoms. It was released in version 4.7 and is unlocked at Adventure Rank 40 after Masquerade of the Guilty and The Little Oceanid. It shows the Champion Duelist's private life, her hobby as a Senior Game Master, and her private regard for the Hunters.

The theme is honour that goes unremembered. The Hunters chose obscurity, Florian could not accept it and was corrupted, and Clorinde, who is herself a Marechaussee Hunter, decides what to do about the treasure.

Plot: Clorinde and Navia recruit the Traveler for a game, Marechaussee Hunter: Judgment Day. Play begins in the Court of Fontaine and the party roleplays as Hunters. The party solves puzzles in an old vault, only to be attacked in the dark by a real Hunter, Florian, who is controlled by a monster. Clorinde calms him, and the party fights the Devorator in a church basement, with Florian offering himself as the target. Afterwards they learn the script was a cover.

Judgment Day: Navia and Clorinde, one player short, ask the Traveler to make a fourth. Lyney and Furina join, and Florian, the script manager, explains that the story is adapted from the real history of the Marechaussee Hunters, who hunted monsters with a swordsmanship passed down through generations. Clorinde will help by adding commentary.

Hunters' Gathering: the party roleplays as Hunters arriving in a hollow city that has sent a distress call. Players pick skills such as medicine, cooking and insight, and each can change how scenes go. They gather information, defeat monsters in a forest and find a chest.

Buried Honor: the next day the game moves to a set modelled on a prison, then a palace, and then to a hidden secret vault. The script seems to end, so Clorinde improvises. The party solves puzzles and collects three of four keys. In a darkened fight Clorinde defeats a 'guard', who turns out to be Florian. Florian says he is a descendant of Hunters, resented that his father died forgotten, and was driven by a voice. Clorinde reads it as a Devorator.

Vanquishing Phantoms: Florian asks to be the bait for the Devorator in the church basement. Clorinde accepts his request as a Champion Duelist. The monster takes him and he becomes a golem. The party defeats it by calling the names of the Marechaussee Hunters. Afterwards Florian explains and Clorinde forgives him.

Judgment Day: Clorinde says she keeps work and private life separate. In court she represents the law, but privately she is an ordinary person who feels anger and sadness. Furina notes she never saw Clorinde cry. Lyney says Clorinde is one of the few Senior Game Masters of the Troupe.

Hunters' Gathering: the game master describes a legend of monsters sent by demons and sorcerers against early humanity and the rebels who became the Hunters. Combat in the actual game is against Thundercraven Rifthound Whelps and a Praetorian Golem.

Buried Honor: the fourth key is Clorinde's, and Florian says he had followed her for a while but never found an opening, so he had lured her through her hobby. Florian says his family served as Hunters for generations and were charged with maintaining a seal. After his father died he neglected it and visited it only later, where his memory goes blurred. He says the Devorator tells him to eliminate the Hunters. He took the keys by theft, from his father, another Hunter and a third Hunter on the way home from a tavern. Clorinde tells him the sword is not special and the wielder's intention is what matters, and that his 'evil sorcerer' shows who he really wanted to fight.

Vanquishing Phantoms: the stone tablet in the vault records Hunters such as Este, who inherited the duties of the Golden Hunter, and Walter, an executioner who used many tricks. The party takes some of the weapons, which glow when monsters are near.

The tablet: the names and weapons of the Marechaussee Hunters of past ages were left by their comrades, so that Hunters would be remembered by each other and not by the public. Hunters worked in the dark and gave up wealth and fame, and revealed their identity rarely; stories of kills were told at night around a bonfire.

Wrap-up: Clorinde tells the others, after Florian recovers, that the script was never a real story and was a lure. She tells him he is more use to the city above ground than below, and that he must return two stolen keys and accept any terms the wronged Hunters set. Lyney and Navia, who noticed something was wrong when Clorinde told them to close their eyes, did not break the illusion for Furina. Clorinde chooses to leave the treasure as it is, saying every name on the tablet made the same choice, and she wants only to be known as a Champion Duelist. She ends by asking the Traveler whether a journey is meaningful if no one remembers it. The Traveler says the journey and the shared time still matter, and Clorinde says she will remember the answer.

Revelations: The script was a lure created by Florian, a descendant of Marechaussee Hunters, to get the last key from Clorinde. A Devorator was manipulating him.

The 'treasure' in the vault is a tablet of Hunters' names and their weapons. Clorinde herself is a Marechaussee Hunter, which she does not want publicised.

The Devorator is a monster of several centuries ago that amplifies a person's obsessions, and Hunters sealed it with a four-part key held by separate Hunters.

Clorinde's master left her a sword and an old key before disappearing; the key is similar to the Hunter keys.

Characters: Clorinde, Navia, Furina, Lyney, the Traveler and Paimon.

Florian, the script manager of the Tabletop Troupe and a descendant of Hunters. Este and Walter, Hunters named on the tablet.

Callas and Spina di Rosula members are mentioned in Navia and Clorinde's talk. Charlotte and Chiori are named as people Navia and Clorinde asked first.

Consequences: Florian offers to turn himself in to the Garde, but Clorinde judges that he has suffered enough and sends him to return the keys. The vault is left undisturbed, with its secret kept among the party.

The Devorator is defeated in the church basement by the party calling the Hunters' names and Clorinde's final blow.

Placement: Unlocked at Adventure Rank 40 after Masquerade of the Guilty and the Animula Choragi Chapter's The Little Oceanid. Released in 4.7. The setting spans the Court of Fontaine, the Fontaine Research Institute region and the Beryl Region.

739.content: A roleplaying club in the Court of Fontaine whose games let friends take part in a story. Clorinde and Navia are veteran members, and Clorinde is a Senior Game Master. Lyney is a casual member who is usually the game master of his own sibling games. Florian is a script manager who writes for the club.

740.content: A script manager of the Tabletop Troupe and the son of a Hunter. After his father died forgotten, bitterness and a Devorator drove him to steal Hunter keys and lure Clorinde to a hidden vault. Clorinde forgives him in the end, and he volunteers to be the Devorator's bait in a duel to restore his honour.

741.content: A monster active centuries ago that amplifies the desires and obsessions in people's hearts until they take over. Marechaussee Hunters sealed it away with a key in four parts. It reacts to the names of the Hunters of its own era.

742.content:
Requiem of the Echoing Depths (also: Chapter II Act IV, Liyue Chasm Archon Quest): Chapter II Act IV of the Archon Quest. The Traveler and Paimon investigate odd hilichurl activity in The Chasm, find the Inverted City, and meet Dainsleif again. Together they discover that hilichurls are gathering there to live out their last days, and stop the Abyss Order's attempt to amplify a pool that eases the Khaenri'ahn curse.

The act has four quests: In the Depths, an Unexpected Reunion; The Grave of the Guarded; Memories of Inteyvat; and The Black Serpent Knights' Glory. In it the Traveler asks Dainsleif directly about his background and about his past with their sibling, and it introduces Halfdan, one of his former subordinates. Released in version 2.6.

Coming after the sibling's appearance in Chapter I Act IV, the act shows the curse's effect on ordinary hilichurls and on cursed Black Serpent Knights, and states the Traveler's own position on the sibling's plan.

Plot: Yuehui, a miner, asks the Traveler to look into hilichurls in The Chasm. In the underground mines they find an Inverted City, and Dainsleif joins them. They learn that the hilichurls are gathering near a pool that weakens the curse, guarded by Black Serpent Knights. The Abyss Order tries to amplify the pool; Halfdan gives his life to delay it and the Traveler destroys the device.

In the Depths, an Unexpected Reunion: Paimon and the Traveler accept Yuehui's commission, suspect the Abyss Order, and go through the underground mines to an Inverted City that reminds them of the Defiled Statue. Dainsleif then steps out of a portal behind them, having pursued an Abyss Herald through it and lost it. The same thing happened when he last chased the Traveler's sibling into a portal. The Traveler asks about his background and about his relationship to the sibling: he says "Twilight Sword" was his title as captain of Khaenri'ah's Royal Guard five hundred years ago, and that the sibling was his travelling companion in a search for their fates, though they "did not make it to the journey's end together". He changes the subject to the Order's likely plans, and they continue inward.

The Grave of the Guarded: Dainsleif suspects the hilichurls have come to The Chasm to live out their last days, because the place seems to ease the curse of immortality laid on Khaenri'ahns in the cataclysm, though he does not know how. Two Black Serpent Knights, once his subordinates who lost their minds to the curse, attack; a third Knight only stares at Dainsleif and retreats. At the Inverted City he judges it older than Khaenri'ah. After the party defeats more Knights they find the Knights were protecting a group of dying hilichurls. The earlier Knight halts reinforcements with a silent order. Dainsleif believes it is Halfdan, a royal guard elite whom he ordered to tell all Black Serpent Knights to protect the people of Khaenri'ah at all costs; despite the curse eroding their minds, the Knights are still trying to carry out that order. The group climbs to the summit and finds a water pool, a relic of the ancient civilisation and the source of the area's curse-weakening effect, surrounded by strange devices. Halfdan arrives and urges them to follow.

Memories of Inteyvat: Halfdan leads them to a hilichurl camp where the Traveler finds an Inteyvat, Khaenri'ah's national flower. Touching it shows a vision of the sibling and an Abyss Herald discussing amplifying the pool's properties, lifting the curse from the gathered hilichurls and restoring "the homeland". Dainsleif calls this futile given the curse's reality-altering nature and expects only more suffering for the hilichurls. The Traveler chooses to help him stop it, holding that the sibling has no right to subject others to near-certain suffering for the slimmest chance of redemption. As they leave, the Order starts its plan, an Abyss Herald delays them, and after it falls the group rushes back to the device.

The Black Serpent Knights' Glory: they enter the chamber as an Abyss Lector activates the amplification device, which causes agonising pain to everyone cursed. Halfdan sacrifices himself to hold the device back temporarily, giving the Traveler time to defeat the Lector and destroy the mechanisms. Afterwards Halfdan's soul appears, speaks briefly with Dainsleif and passes on. Dainsleif leaves to recover and to investigate the Order's Loom of Fate project; the Traveler and Paimon report to Yuehui.

The act's emotional spine is Dainsleif's relationship to his former subordinates: the Knights have lost their minds but still serve his last order, and he is only recognised by one of them. The vision of the Inteyvat also gives the first sight of the sibling's stated aim in this period, centred on restoring "the homeland" by lifting the curse from the hilichurls.

Dainsleif says that the Knights' recognition of him ought to be impossible without "it", an unnamed thing he does not explain here. He suspects the Order has designs on The Chasm before he sees the amplification device, and he does not claim to understand how the pool works.

Revelations: Black Serpent Knights are former Khaenri'ahn soldiers who still guard their people; the Order wants to remove the curse from hilichurls by amplifying an ancient pool.

Dainsleif's title "Twilight Sword" is that of captain of Khaenri'ah's Royal Guard five hundred years ago, and the sibling was his travelling companion in a quest to find their fates. Hilichurls appear to gather at The Chasm to live out their last days because the place weakens the curse. The Inverted City is of an older civilisation than Khaenri'ah. The Abyss Order intends to remove the curse from the gathered hilichurls and "restore the homeland".

The Black Serpent Knights' loyalty traces back to Dainsleif's order to Halfdan to tell all Black Serpent Knights to protect Khaenri'ah's people at all costs. The Order is also pursuing a project called the Loom of Fate.

Characters: The Traveler, Paimon, Dainsleif and Halfdan.

Yuehui, a miner who commissions the investigation; the Traveler's sibling (seen in a vision); an Abyss Herald; an Abyss Lector; and other Black Serpent Knights. The hilichurls of The Chasm appear as people at the end of their lives.

Consequences: The amplification device is destroyed and Halfdan dies and passes on. Dainsleif goes to recover and to look into the Loom of Fate. The Traveler has stated openly that they oppose their sibling's plan.

Placement: Chapter II Act IV, following Omnipresence Over Mortals and The Crane Returns on the Wind and preceding Through Mists of Smoke and Forests Dark (Chapter III Act I, Sumeru). Adventure Rank 30 per the wiki. Released in version 2.6.

743.comment: Requiem of the Echoing Depths: Inverted City and the pool
743.content: In the depths of The Chasm's underground mines lies an Inverted City, which Dainsleif judges older than Khaenri'ah. At its summit is a water pool, a relic of the ancient civilisation, that weakens the curse of immortality on Khaenri'ahns. The Abyss Order's devices around it are meant to amplify this effect.

744.comment: Requiem of the Echoing Depths: Halfdan
744.content: Dainsleif identifies a Black Serpent Knight as Halfdan, a royal guard elite at the cataclysm whom he ordered to tell the Knights to protect the people of Khaenri'ah. Though cursed and mindless, Halfdan restrains other Knights and leads the party to the hilichurl camp. He sacrifices himself holding back the amplification device, and his soul speaks with Dainsleif before passing on.

745.comment: Requiem of the Echoing Depths: Inteyvat
745.content: The national flower of Khaenri'ah. In a hilichurl camp in The Chasm the Traveler touches one and sees a vision of their sibling and an Abyss Herald discussing the plan to amplify the pool and restore "the homeland".

key: Ritou Travel Permit World Quest series
746.content:
Ritou Travel Permit (also: Ritou Travel Permit World Quest series, Chisato's Letter): The quest follows Ritou Escape Plan, in which the Traveler secretly gets off Ritou with Chisato's help. The two belong to different institutions (the Hiiragi Clan leads the Kanjou Commission; Kamaji is a Kujou Clan member and a Tenryou Commission enforcer), and Kamaji worries that closeness between them could be exploited, so an outsider carries the letter.

The series is listed in the journal as a chapter, but contains only one quest. The wiki notes this as an oddity of presentation.

Plot: Chisato asks the Traveler to take her letter to Kamaji. The Traveler may first speak to Sanada, a Tenryou Commission subordinate who sends them to find Kamaji himself, walking near the bridge. Kamaji recognises the handwriting with relief and agrees to approve the permit as a personal favour to Chisato, but asks the Traveler to wait at Kiminami Restaurant while he prepares it.

At the restaurant Kiminami Anna hands over treats Kamaji had ordered. Kamaji says to her that they are a courtesy gift in return for tea Hiiragi Shinsuke once sent his father, a public-relations gesture. He tells the Traveler privately that his father, Kujou Takayuki, would not approve of contact with Chisato, and that he understands why, since a closeness between a Kujou and a Hiiragi could be exploited by others. He then gives the Traveler the Travel Permit, his own carefully worded reply and the snack box, and goes back to official duties, wishing he could deliver the gift himself. The Traveler returns to Chisato, who tells them to thank Kamaji rather than herself.

Before the Traveler goes in search of Kamaji, Chisato says she is counting on them; Sanada, if asked, is wary and will only direct the Traveler on once shown that the letter really is from Chisato. The quest rewards are Adventure EXP, 30,000 Mora, Hero's Wit and the Travel Permit, plus 100 Inazuma reputation.

Revelations: - The relationship between Chisato and Kamaji is a private romance between a Hiiragi and a Kujou, which Kamaji says could be taken advantage of by others given their positions.
- Kamaji's cover story for the gift (a return courtesy toward Shinsuke) is one he tells Anna; he is open about the real reason with the Traveler.

Characters: Hiiragi Chisato (daughter of Hiiragi Shinsuke, head of the Hiiragi Clan), Kujou Kamaji, Kiminami Anna, Sanada (minor), Paimon and the Traveler. Takayuki and Shinsuke are only mentioned.

Consequences: The Traveler receives a Travel Permit, which allows free entry to and exit from Ritou, plus Adventure EXP, Mora and Hero's Wit. Speaking to Chisato again afterwards, following a certain dialogue branch, gives a 4-star Storm Cage artifact once.

Placement: Released in 2.6, as a follow-up to Ritou Escape Plan, among the Inazuma world quests that follow the Traveler's arrival in Ritou under the Sakoku Decree. It is unrelated to the main Archon Quest beyond its setting.

747.content: The Travel Permit is the document Kujou Kamaji issues in Chisato's Letter. It lets the holder move freely into and out of Ritou, which the Sakoku Decree otherwise restricts. It is issued as a personal favour to Chisato and not as a general policy.

748.content:
Rosa Multiflora Chapter (Navia) (also: Rosa Multiflora Chapter, Navia's Story Quest, Braving the Tides Together): The Rosa Multiflora Chapter is Navia's Story Quest (Version 4.3), set in Fontaine after Masquerade of the Guilty. In its one act, Braving the Tides Together, she oversees the rebuilding of Poisson, faces former Spina di Rosula members who resent her father, and decides how to honour her parents' legacy.

The act has three quests: Shimmering Memories, Lost and Inherited and Yesterday's Tears, Tomorrow's Light. It requires Adventure Rank 40 and completion of Masquerade of the Guilty. The chapter's flower name is a wild rose, echoing Spina di Rosula, the organisation her parents led.

The chapter shows Navia as a leader who has lost her parents and her trusted attendants and still chooses support over grievance. Themes are inheritance, the cost of mistakes, and the difference between nostalgia for glory days and loyalty to people.

It links Navia's backstory to the old aquabus funding dispute that split the organisation, to the aftermath of the Confrerie of Cabriere and its Sinthe production being exposed, and to Poisson's recovery from the Primordial Sea flood.

Plot: **Shimmering Memories.** At the Court of Fontaine the Traveler and Paimon find Navia overworked, supervising Poisson's reconstruction without her attendants Melus and Silver. There is no aquabus line to Poisson, so they go by boat. There Florent, who has taken over some of Melus's duties, mentions a planned statue honouring Navia and her parents. Colter, having served his sentence in Meropide, arrives unaware that Melus and Silver have died or of Marcel's plot involving the Primordial Water. He asks about Romeuf and recalls the old quarrel: Romeuf wanted funds spent on Poisson, Callas backed the aquabus, and Romeuf left with his men on bad terms. Navia takes Colter to fetch a new uniform and shares macarons on an old road; something stirs in a bush behind them.

**Lost and Inherited.** In the town Navia notices they are followed, chases three men and defeats them. Their leader Martinat confirms they are Romeuf's men who were angered at seeing her drinking. She lets them go with a warning but asks Florent to increase security. The group stays at Fleuve Cendre and goes fishing; Navia speaks of her childhood immaturity, how Melus was hurt because of a mistake of hers, and how her mother's care inspires her own kindness. Meanwhile Martinat tells Colter the plan begins the next day.

**Yesterday's Tears, Tomorrow's Light.** Back in Poisson, Navia meets Adele and Coralie, and promises Adele a place in Spina di Rosula when she is old enough. Florent reports that Romeuf has brought explosives to bomb the Clementine Line so that the debris would fall on the town. During the evacuation Colter tries to attack Navia but Florent stops him. Colter says he blames her for ruining what the organisation meant, and that he had fallen out with Melus before learning he had died. Navia chooses to show trust and subdues him. The Traveler disables one set of explosives; another goes off, but Navia stops the falling debris. The Maison Gardiennage arrives and arrests Romeuf's followers, and Navia refuses to handle them privately as former members. She sympathises with Colter, dismisses him from the organisation but says he may return after his release, and says she will try to bring an aquabus to Poisson. After resting she asks the Traveler whether they see her as a partner; they confirm. Florent then shows her the statue design, an adult Navia standing with her parents.

Romeuf's faction held that Clementine, while pregnant with Navia, could no longer act as an impartial mediator, and so rejected the aquabus decision that Callas carried out after her death. Navia's remark that she did not want to lose another link to her parents explains her protectiveness of the Clementine Line.

Revelations: No world-level revelations. It deepens Navia's backstory, explains why Spina di Rosula split, and shows the state of Poisson after the flood.

Characters: Navia, the Traveler and Paimon. Florent, Colter, Romeuf and his men, Adele and Coralie appear.

Navia is portrayed as dutiful, generous and tired, willing to forgive but firm when people are endangered. Florent acts as her steady deputy; Colter is the sympathetic, embittered veteran; Romeuf is the rebel who left the organisation.

Consequences: Romeuf and his followers are arrested; Colter is dismissed but welcome to return; Navia plans an aquabus link for Poisson; and the town prepares a family statue.

Placement: Release order: 4.3. Story order: after Chapter IV Act V, Masquerade of the Guilty, in the aftermath of Fontaine's flood. This is not an Archon Quest.

749.comment: Rosa Multiflora Chapter (Navia): Braving the Tides Together
749.content: Act I of Navia's Story Quest. Navia and the Traveler foil Romeuf's plot to bomb the Clementine Line and bury Poisson, and she chooses to forgive Colter and carry her parents' legacy.

key: The Crack of Muskets Breaking the Silence
Fiction and Reality Inside and Outside the Frame
The Lone Isle Glimpsed Through Fog
750.content:
Roses and Muskets (also: Roses and Muskets Event Quest, The Crack of Muskets Breaking the Silence, Fiction and Reality Inside and Outside the Frame, The Lone Isle Glimpsed Through Fog, Where the Roses Bloom, The Two Musketeers' Triumph, The Two Musketeers film): Roses and Muskets is the Version 4.3 winter flagship event. The Traveler and Paimon help the Fontaine film producer Xavier make "The Two Musketeers" for the first Fontinalia Film Festival, with Ayaka, Ayato and Yoimiya as unpaid guest actors and Furina as director. While filming, Chevreuse of the Special Patrol investigates a murder that copies the original novel, and the resolution sets two siblings' grief for their murdered mother against Fontaine's law.

The story has four acts and an afterword: The Crack of Muskets Breaking the Silence, Fiction and Reality Inside and Outside the Frame, The Lone Isle Glimpsed Through Fog, Where the Roses Bloom and The Two Musketeers' Triumph. The event's reward was the claymore "Ultimate Overlord's Mega Magic Sword".

The event required Adventure Rank 20 and the Prologue Act III, and recommended Chapter IV Act V (Masquerade of the Guilty), Raiden Shogun's Imperatrix Umbrosa Chapter Act II and Furina's Animula Choragi Chapter Act I first. It introduced the Fontinalia Film Festival, organised by the Fontaine Film Association.

It is the origin of Musketeer Pictures, whose later productions appear in the Sunny Summer Fontinalia event.

Plot: Xavier loses his investor and cannot pay his cast, so Ayaka, Ayato and Yoimiya volunteer, and Furina is persuaded to direct. Chevreuse joins as the musketeer and asks the Traveler for help with a murder echoing the novel. While filming goes on, they trace the gun to Fleuve Cendre and a novelist's roses. At the wrap party Chevreuse stages a trap that exposes the investor Morris, who hired the killer of the novelist's mother. The film wins the festival.

**Act I.** In the Court of Fontaine Xavier cannot get funding for his film of "The Two Musketeers". Chiori has found actors from Inazuma, and Ayaka, Ayato and Yoimiya agree to work unpaid. Furina, offered a dessert and a Kamera demonstration, agrees to direct. Chevreuse, introduced by Chiori, joins and tells the Traveler about a murder that mirrors the novel.

**Act II.** Filming begins at Hotel Debord, with Chevreuse and Ayaka playing sisters Tulipe and Iris. Chevreuse, the Traveler and Paimon investigate gun parts through workshops and Fleuve Cendre.

**Act III.** The final scene is shot in one take. The trail leads to the novelist Baptiste, who confesses, then privately asks Chevreuse to kill the true mastermind.

**Act IV.** The film is stolen and recovered. At a beach party Chevreuse stages a fake murder to make the investor Morris confess; Morris hired the killer of Elisa, and Veronique, the prop manager, had killed the earlier victim.

**Afterword.** Xavier's film wins and Chevreuse hands the three to Wriothesley.

**Act I in detail.** The Traveler and Paimon learn of the Fontinalia Film Festival from The Steambird. At the plaza Xavier is pleading with a would-be investor, Morris, who cannot fund the film. Chiori reassures him: the actors she found do not care about Mora. Ayaka, Ayato and Yoimiya arrive by aquabus from the Clementine Line, and Ayato explains he and Ayaka already planned to work for free, because better ties between nations matter more than wealth. Paimon volunteers as clapperboard and Yoimiya as assistant. For a director the Traveler suggests Furina, who agrees on condition of full creative freedom after the Traveler brings her Fontinalia Mousse and a Kamera sample. Furina wants an expert on muskets, and Chiori brings Chevreuse. Chevreuse, who has just stopped a Sinthe sale (production halted after Marcel's arrest), joins gladly because she likes the book. She summarises the novel and asks for help with a recent murder.

**Act II in detail.** Furina, short on sleep, rewrites the script so the sister role is not overshadowed by an overbearing brother. With Ayato busy with the Palais Mermonia, his role goes to Chevreuse, so she and Ayaka play Tulipe and Iris. Veronique is the prop manager and Bonnot the lighting technician. Filming goes on until night. Chevreuse then tells the Traveler a Rainbow Rose was left at the scene, as in the novel. At Leschots Clockwork Workshop and Beaumont Workshop nothing stands out, but Estelle sells scrap parts to Fleuve Cendre. In the sewers they find someone cleaning up practice shots, buy information from Emerald, and learn from the bar owner that a gun left three days earlier was untouched. Chevreuse theorises the killer took the gun, copied it, killed a solitary man from the east side, and left the rose. The novelist has an alibi and no motive.

**Act III in detail.** Ayaka declines Furina's offer to stay as an actress because of her Yashiro Commission duties. Emilie reports that the rose is a rare cultivar grown only in Baptiste's garden. Baptiste admits to the murder but says he cannot reach the true mastermind, and asks Chevreuse in private to kill the culprit if she can, because twenty years have passed since his mother's death.

**Act IV in detail.** The cast notices Chevreuse is missing, and Morris returns. A Kamera breaks and the finished film disappears; Chiori finds it in the sewers, undamaged. After wrapping, Furina hosts a beach party. Yoimiya leads Morris into a building; Chevreuse stages the "murder", then reveals it as a trap with a recording. She arrests Morris for Elisa's murder and Veronique, the second musketeer, who aimed a gun at Morris. Morris admits an affair with Elisa, a maid in his family's estate, paying her to leave and end the pregnancy, and later hiring an assassin when she sent him photographs of their two children. Veronique recounts hiding with her brother beneath the floor as their mother died. Chevreuse refuses revenge killings but promises to inform Wriothesley. Afterwards Chevreuse tells the Traveler about her own childhood and her father's harsh training, and they arrive at Baptiste's house where the Rainbow Roses are in full bloom.

**Clues.** Chevreuse deduced that Baptiste could not have acted alone because he failed to reassemble the musket found in his garden, that his confession was a diversion, and that the sabotage came from the investor who hoped to sink the film. She found Veronique's name next to Baptiste's in the orphanage adoption records. Letellier and Turenna of the Special Patrol take the two into custody.

**Afterword in detail.** The Traveler finds Chevreuse in the Fortress of Meropide's Administrative Area, telling Wriothesley of the three she is bringing in. She asks him to give everyone the latest Steambird so Baptiste and Veronique are seen as heroes and Morris as the villain. Back at the festival Xavier's "The Two Musketeers" wins as Musketeer Pictures; Ayaka invites Chevreuse to Inazuma, Ayato confirms the storms around Inazuma have gone, and Furina carries the Furina Award reluctantly.

Revelations: The novelist Baptiste and the prop manager Veronique are siblings whose mother Elisa was murdered twenty years ago on the investor Morris's orders.

The "second musketeer" is Veronique, who killed the earlier victim and left a Rainbow Rose as in the novel. Baptiste's quick confession was a diversion that gave her a chance at Morris.

Morris signed on as an investor in order to sink the film and bury the story, and the missing film and mishaps were his sabotage. Chevreuse admits she hesitated when Baptiste first told her the truth.

Chevreuse says Fontaine is "the Nation of Justice" because it is built on laws, and that private revenge would start a cycle. She promises Morris will not lead a cushy life in the Fortress of Meropide; the Afterword shows Wriothesley making no promise.

Characters: Traveler, Paimon, Xavier, Furina, Chiori, Chevreuse, Ayaka, Ayato and Yoimiya.

Also Morris (the investor), Baptiste (the novelist), Veronique (prop manager), Bonnot (lighting), the extra Elain, Emilie, Wriothesley and the Special Patrol members Letellier and Turenna.

Furina agrees to direct only with full creative freedom. Chevreuse is calm and dutiful. Ayato keeps Inazuma's ties with other nations in mind, and Ayaka takes naturally to acting, saying that clearing her mind to become the character resembles her swordplay.

Consequences: Morris, Baptiste and Veronique are arrested and taken to the Fortress of Meropide. "The Two Musketeers" wins the festival, and the crew is credited as Musketeer Pictures.

The friendship between Ayaka and Chevreuse leads to a possible visit to Inazuma. Xavier and Musketeer Pictures return in the Sunny Summer Fontinalia event (6.7).

Placement: Released in Version 4.3 and run from 21 December 2023 to 8 January 2024 (server time), with the shop open until 15 January. Act II unlocked on 22 December, Act III on 23 December, Act IV on 24 December and the Afterword on 26 December. It is an event story set after Chapter IV Act V.

751.comment: Roses and Muskets: Fontinalia Film Festival
751.content: A film festival organised by the Fontaine Film Association; the entry with the highest score wins the Furina Award. The name stayed after Furina's abdication. The first winner was "The Two Musketeers" by Musketeer Pictures.

752.comment: Roses and Muskets: The Two Musketeers
752.content: A Fontainian novel by Baptiste about sisters Tulipe and Iris, whose mother Rain is poisoned by aristocrats; the sisters become the two musketeers and leave a Rainbow Rose on each victim. Xavier produced the film, Furina directed and Ayaka and Chevreuse starred. A real murder in Fontaine copied the novel's roses.

753.content: Twenty years before the event, Morris hired an assassin to kill Elisa, a maid who had borne his two children. She hid the children under the floorboards and fought on. The children are Baptiste and Veronique, who grew up in an orphanage.

754.content:
Ruins Exploration: Fieldwise Center (also: Ruins Exploration, Return From the Mysterious Realm, Headlong Into the Sands, Fieldwise Center): The story has two acts. In Return From the Mysterious Realm, Collei, now an Akademiya consultant for an outdoor survival and rescue agency, brings the Traveler to Gandharva Ville, where Layla and Djer describe being swept into the ruin and repeating strange phrases. In Headlong Into the Sands, a team of Cyno, Sethos, Tighnari, Alhaitham, Kaveh and Layla enters the ruin with the Traveler and Paimon, gathers stone slabs and notes, and meets Thoth. The event's home base is the Fieldwise Center, where players start the minigames.

Besides the mystery, the tone is light: Cyno's puns, Cyrus's tomatoes, Djer's fixation on Ajilenakh Nuts and Paimon's temporary persona as "Paimon Plus" run through both acts. The revelations are narrow: they affect Layla's ancestry and our picture of the Seven Pillars of King Deshret rather than the main story.

Plot: Act I, Return From the Mysterious Realm. Paimon, newly in "Paimon Plus" mode, goes to the House of Daena for books but diverts to greet Collei and Cyrus. Collei explains the new semester means more field research and the Akademiya wants an agency guiding students on outdoor survival and rescue; the Traveler joins as a helper. In Gandharva Ville, Tighnari treats Layla while Cyno and Sethos explain the incident. Sethos and members of the Temple of Silence rescued Djer from the desert, then found Layla at the same marked spot. Djer's account: he fell through quicksand into an undiscovered ruin, touched something, and was flooded with information until a voice said not to eat Ajilenakh Nuts and a cat guided him out; he also heard "there are those from Tulaytullah who still endure." Layla remembers nothing, and mentions that she sometimes sleepwalks. Sethos, Tighnari and Cyno agree to return to the site in two days. While Paimon fetches coffee, Layla's other self recounts what the first Layla saw: the device, the flood of information, the repeated question, and the cat that led her out.

Act II, Headlong Into the Sands. Alhaitham, Kaveh and Mehrak join Cyno, Sethos, Tighnari, Layla, the Traveler and Paimon. In the ruin the party must find broken slabs and other mechanisms; the Great Vayuvyastra is activated by attacking it. Three stone slabs (priests' records) show Thoth with other Pillars and with Goudarz and Makhaira. Mehrak helps Kaveh and Alhaitham clear dust from slabs with wind. Elsewhere the Traveler, Layla and others collect four Ragged Notes and assemble them into Ordered Notes. The notes describe a student who found the ruin and was trapped; his last page is signed Zandik. The team meets a cat who speaks as Thoth. He explains the questions he put to humans, relates what became of Goudarz and Makhaira, and says the device that harmed Layla and Djer was an old tool of King Deshret for measuring human brain power. He replaced the flood of information with simple repeating phrases to protect them, a side effect that will fade. He asks the Traveler to switch off the device.

Details. Kaveh and Alhaitham's team follows Mehrak. Thoth tells the Traveler they are special among the companions. Sethos observes that Thoth's slabs show the Pillars as colleagues of Hermanubis. Cyrus has waited in Aaru Village and later recounts that the Vahumana Darshan has a "mixed record" about the Ibis King. The post-quest vignettes show Cyno, Sethos and Tighnari planning a visit, Alhaitham and Kaveh arguing over dinner, and Layla meeting Nahida and Nilou under the stars.

Revelations: Thoth, the Ibis King and Scribe of Scribes among King Deshret's Seven Pillars, is imprisoned in Aaru with Sobek and Heryshaf and can occasionally speak through a cat. He explains that, when life became unbearable for the king, Deshret had him, Sobek and Heryshaf locked in Aaru, and that he could be freed if he found humans who gave the correct answers to three questions: what causes our rise and fall, what obliterates love and hate, and what determines truth and falsehood. The questions came from King Deshret, who received them from the Mistress of Flowers. Goudarz said conspiracy and betrayal and received the power to deceive; Makhaira said she had nothing left to lose and received the power to be loved. A third, unnamed woman was tested on the final question; because Thoth is still sealed, her answer must have been wrong. Thoth adds that a young man named Zandik, who lived several centuries ago, refused his third gift, and that Zandik's companion had blue hair and pointed ears, which means Layla is a descendant of Tulaytullah.

Thoth says Al-Ahmar insisted the Dendro Dragon Sovereign was one of the Pillars but she rejected it, which is why there were seven Pillars with one forever absent. He describes his relationship with Sobek and Heryshaf as chess companions. He admits he tricked Zandik by saying he could not leave without his companion: it is true that only Tulaytullah's descendants may come and go as they please, but anyone can in fact enter or leave, and Thoth made up the second half to stop Zandik leaving his tired companion behind. Thoth also says gifts of former ages, whether in blood or technology, are tools and not things to revere.

Characters: Main: the Traveler, Paimon, Collei, Layla, Cyno, Sethos, Tighnari, Alhaitham and Kaveh, with Mehrak. Also: Cyrus (Sumeru), Djer, Thoth (as the cat), and cameos by Nahida and Nilou. Trial characters are used inside the ruin (for example Layla in Act I and several allies in Act II).

Layla's other self appears in a conversation with the Traveler while Paimon is away. Nahida appears in a night-time vignette with Layla and Nilou at the end.

Consequences: Layla and Djer recover and Layla learns that her ancestry traces to Tulaytullah. The device that harmed them is left for the Traveler or Mehrak to switch off. Thoth remains in Aaru. Cyrus offers to ask friends for a star-related study topic for Layla.

Players who reached 750 Prep Progress could invite Collei to their party; the story shows her as an Akademiya consultant for the proposed survival and rescue agency.

Placement: Released in Version 6.1, 7 to 24 November 2025. Entry requires the Prologue Act III Song of the Dragon and Freedom; the Archon Quest An Elegy for Faded Moonlight and Cyno's Lupus Aureus Chapter are recommended. In an epilogue vignette Sethos says he has heard that the Hat Guy is taking care of something in Nod-Krai. It does not change main-story canon.

Gameplay: Game mechanics, not in-world fact. Three minigames: Mechanical Puzzle-Parsing Paradigm (guiding Puzzlepals with Miraculous Effects), Skillful Scouting (switching between Cuilein An-bot and Bar-drone Bunny on tracks) and Safe Engagement Training (trial objectives that grant buffs before fights). Completing them earned Prep Progress; 750 Prep Progress let players invite Collei to their party, and later tiers included Crown of Insight and a furnishing blueprint.

755.content: In this event the Ibis King speaks through a borrowed cat in the ruin beneath the desert. He is imprisoned in Aaru with Sobek and Heryshaf, is playful, proud of his chess record against his fellow prisoners, and treats ancient gifts as mere tools. He aided Layla and Djer by replacing overwhelming information with simple repeated phrases.

756.comment: Ruins Exploration: Fieldwise Center: Thoth's three questions
756.content: The three questions are: what causes our rise and fall, what obliterates love and hate, and what determines truth and falsehood. King Deshret gave them to Thoth, having received them from the Mistress of Flowers. Goudarz answered the first with conspiracy and betrayal and was given the power to deceive. Makhaira answered the second with vengeance and was given the power to be loved. The third person is not named.

757.comment: Ruins Exploration: Fieldwise Center: Zandik's notes
757.content: Four Ragged Notes found in the ruin are assembled into the Ordered Notes of a student who found an unrecorded ruin, complained about the Akademiya's attitude to the desert, and wrote about the Seven Pillars before being trapped. The last page is signed Zandik. Thoth later says Zandik was clever, mistrustful and narcissistic, declined his third gift, and was tricked into staying with his companion.

758.comment: Ruins Exploration: Fieldwise Center: Layla's lineage and the incident
758.content: Layla was caught in quicksand while stargazing, entered a ruin, touched a device, and was left repeating "How many moons are there in the sky?" with no memory of the event. Her other self remembers it. Thoth tells her that Zandik's companion looked like her, with blue hair and pointed ears, which marks her as descended from Tulaytullah.

key: Sacred Sakura Cleansing Ritual world quest series
759.content:
Sacred Sakura Cleansing Ritual (also: Sacred Sakura Cleansing Ritual world quest series, Hanachirusato quest series): Sacred Sakura Cleansing Ritual is a World Quest series on Narukami Island, added in version 2.0. At Konda Village the Traveler meets a masked shrine maiden, Hanachirusato, who asks for help carrying out the ritual that purges filth from the roots of the Sacred Sakura and the Thunder Sakura. The Traveler lifts five barriers and cleanses the Depths of Mt. Yougou.

The series has four quests: A Strange Story in Konda, Sacrificial Offering, Cleansing Defilement (with the sub-quest Tanuki-Bayashi in the Forest) and Yougou Cleansing. The starting area requires the Ritou Escape Plan quest.

It doubles as an in-world explanation of how the Sacred and Thunder Sakura cleanse Inazuma, and it ties the Grand Narukami Shrine's duties to the Electro Archon's watch over the land. Quest by quest: A Strange Story in Konda introduces Hanachirusato and the first barrier; Sacrificial Offering sends the Traveler to the shrines; Cleansing Defilement covers Araumi, the Kamisato Estate and Chinju Forest; Yougou Cleansing ends at the roots of the Sacred Sakura.

Plot: With all five barriers broken and the filth in each driven out, Hanachirusato and the Traveler go to the roots of the Sacred Sakura. She dispels the barrier over the Depths of Mt. Yougou, which drains its Electro pool, and the Traveler goes down to defeat the Miasmic Tumor. Afterwards she reveals that she is filth condensed from the memory of a Kitsune Saiguu. For the ritual to finish, all the filth must be cleansed, herself included. The two say goodbye and Hanachirusato dissipates.

The ritual as explained in the series: the Sacred Sakura and Thunder Sakura symbolize the Electro Archon's eternal watch and absorb filth into their roots, which are all interconnected and cannot purify themselves. Minor cleansings are done often to check the roots and set barriers that protect the roots from malicious people such as the Fatui and protect people from leaking filth. A major cleansing is needed every 60 years: the barriers are broken with wards, the filth condenses into "defilement incarnate" (harmless forms such as tofu boys in peaceful times, dangerous ones in troubled times), first for the Thunder Sakura roots and then for the central Sacred Sakura roots, where it forms a tumor. According to Hanachirusato's records, the Thunder Sakura almost withered several hundred years ago, monsters raged and the seas turned black, until someone performed the ritual. The shrine had planned this ritual, but Yae Miko called it off and told Inagi Hotomi to give the Memento Lens to a blonde-haired outlander.

Revelations: - Hanachirusato is filth condensed from the memory of the Kitsune Saiguu and ends by being cleansed with the rest (her own statement).
- The Sacred Sakura Cleansing Ritual must be performed regularly or the Sakura trees wither, which would be catastrophic for Inazuma.

- The major cleansing is due every 60 years and is split between the Thunder Sakura roots and the Sacred Sakura roots.
- Yae Miko arranged for the Traveler to perform it in place of the shrine.

Characters: The Traveler, Paimon, Hanachirusato, Inagi Hotomi (shrine staff), Ioroi (a sealed bake-danuki), and villagers of Konda. Yae Miko and the Kitsune Saiguu are referred to rather than present.

Consequences: The Sakura roots are purged of their accumulated filth for the time being. Hanachirusato dissipates at the end. The shrine's planned ritual is not needed.

Placement: Released in 2.0 with Inazuma. The Ritou Escape Plan quest is needed to reach the starting location. The Kitsune Saiguu is a historical figure covered separately.

760.content: A masked shrine maiden met at Konda Village who guides the Traveler through the Sacred Sakura Cleansing Ritual. She finally says she is filth condensed from the memory of the Kitsune Saiguu and must be cleansed too, and she fades away at the end of the series.

761.comment: Sacred Sakura Cleansing Ritual: Sacred Sakura Cleansing Ritual
761.content: A periodic rite normally led by the Grand Narukami Shrine to purge accumulated filth from the interconnected roots of the Sacred Sakura and the Thunder Sakura. Minor cleansings set protective barriers; a major cleansing, needed every 60 years, breaks the barriers so that filth takes physical form and is destroyed.

key: Another Home There May Yet Be
762.content:
Sapientia Oromasdis Chapter (Nahida) (also: Sapientia Oromasdis Chapter, Sapientia Oromasdis, Nahida's Story Quest, Lingering Warmth, Homecoming, Another Home There May Yet Be): Nahida's Story Quest, in two acts. In Lingering Warmth (3.2) the newly dream-free Sumeru City takes up dream-sharing, and Nahida and the Traveler uncover a man who has trapped other dreamers in an artificial dream built from his uploaded mind. In Homecoming (3.6) Nahida, uneasy about a forgotten duty, helps elemental fungi from a lost homeland and finds that the dragon Apep, damaged when forbidden knowledge was purged, is in danger of dying.

Act I has three quests: Dream of Awakening, Dream of Falling and Dream of Farewell. Act II has two: Where Lies the Path Home and What Shape Does the Self Hold. A follow-up, Another Home There May Yet Be, is unlocked afterward but is outside the act.

The chapter is Nahida's personal growth: learning to guide dreamers without erasing grief, and learning that being the Archon of Wisdom does not mean knowing what she has forgotten. It touches directly on the erasure of Greater Lord Rukkhadevata from memory, which only the Traveler recalls.

Plot: Act I: A group called A Moment of Dreams meets in Sumeru City. After one member sleepwalks, Nahida and the Traveler find that several dreamers are being lured into a shared dream. Its owner, a scholar who uploaded his mind to the Akasha before it was shut down, keeps it alive with others' Jnana energy and a recreated lost wife. Nahida ends it and arranges for his consciousness to return to his body.

Act II: Nahida has a vague sense of an unfinished duty. Elemental fungi from a lost homeland lead her to Apep, the Dendro Dragon, which harbours a void left by the purge of forbidden knowledge. With a Fire Seed and her own power she helps heal it.

Dream of Awakening: Pedrush invites the Traveler and Paimon to the interest group. Nahida appears as a surprise guest and answers dream questions. Ilman says he sees his dead wife each night and continues their talk; Nahida says this is rare. The Traveler thinks privately of Rukkhadevata. Ilman sleepwalks toward a cliff and is saved; Nahida warns him off the site. The headcount shows Kathya has gone to Chatrakam Cave.

Dream of Falling: Kathya dreams of Professor Aisha, an Amurta researcher who gave her a plant that she promised would bloom as proof of her return; Nahida says it never would. The Traveler and Paimon help tell her. Nahida takes the group into the dreams of Debbi, who has lost friends in a shipwreck, and Ilman's family, then to the dream's owner, who explains how he built a 'hyper-realistic' person, his wife Emira, and planted devices in others to feed her Jnana energy. Nahida exposes him. After his creation turns into a monster and is slain, he wishes to die; Nahida refuses and promises to return his consciousness to his body in a Knowledge Capsule.

Dream of Farewell: the sleepers wake. Nahida gives the Capsule to Sitt at the Akademiya for a patient at Bimarstan, then gives the group a speech about moving forward. To the Traveler she admits she felt a warm pull in the dream that she once knew and can trace only to her unnamed past.

Homecoming: Nahida shows the Traveler a Dendro-charged object she found in the Sanctuary of Surasthana. A Floating Hydro Fungus leads her to a collapsed elemental fungus; she revives it and learns its people are an ancient race twisted by the forbidden knowledge, that she once promised to bring them home, and that home is Apep. They clear a Withering Zone, find further fungi, and learn Apep now has a large void. Nahida realises her forgotten task was to tend it. What Shape Does the Self Hold: in the Chasm they cleanse a fungus with the Fire Seed, which the Geoshroom warns is unstable. At Apep's Resort in Hadramaveth, Apep first drives them off, then swallows them. The Seed shatters, and the fungi sacrifice themselves to restore the Heart of Oasis. Apep recovers and tells its story.

Details from Act I. Nahida is initially sulky when members hesitate to ask their Archon questions, and Paimon reassures them. Pedrush organises the headcount. Kathya's plant shows Aisha had cultivated it by special means, and the Traveler and Paimon break the news so Nahida does not have to. Debbi tells Nahida that Gaspar and Basimah died on a ship that struck a reef, which she learned from the newspaper The Steambird. The dream's owner says Emira was his first creation with it; he had grown close to her at the Akademiya, and she died of Eleazar complications; when Nahida shut the Akasha down he lost access to its energy and turned to other people's. The others realise they have slept too long and leave. In Dream of Farewell the dream's owner is identified as the Kshahrewar scholar Beynuni, who has been in Bimarstan since misusing the Akasha. Nahida says she will brief Cyno herself later.

Details from Act II. Nahida had been gathering hazy memories from Irminsul. The fungi can change appearance with the environment, and the Hydro fungus had a companion and a child. Paimon likens Apep to Dvalin; Nahida says Apep is older. Apep was ruler of Sumeru's once forested lands until a spike from the sky created the desert, and it never accepted the order that followed the Archon War. At Hadramaveth Apep calls both Nahida and King Deshret reliant on the heavens' glow, and warns that Buer will pay for knowing the truth. Nahida decides to use her own power in place of the shattered Seed, even though it might return her to a twig, before the fungi take her place. Apep admits its rage was amplified by corruption.

Apep's account: it and the other dragons sought forbidden knowledge to overcome the Heavenly Principles. Nibelung, who acquired it from a dark power outside Teyvat, led them against outsiders in a war that nearly destroyed the world; Nibelung died, but Apep kept collecting knowledge until the spike halted it. King Deshret, who gained forbidden knowledge from Nabu Malikata, was allowed to build his kingdom on Apep's land on condition that Apep would inherit that knowledge when he died. Apep consumed him as agreed but absorbed corruption instead, and saw it had fallen into a trap. It remains loyal to the Dragon King's cause and will watch Buer and humanity to see how life under the Heavenly Principles unfolds.

Aftermath: Nahida comforts the sad fungus Nur and finds elemental traces in her. In Another Home There May Yet Be she brings Nur and the Hydro fungi to a camp of Anemo fungi, apologises to the Traveler for nearly sacrificing herself, notices the fungi copying the elemental lifeform's farming, and resolves to monitor the camp.

Revelations: A scholar built a hidden shared dream from others' energy, and the dragon Apep is in danger of dying after the forbidden knowledge was purged.

Nahida's forgotten duty was to tend Apep and, with the fungi, to bring them home. The fungi's people are an ancient race corrupted by forbidden knowledge.

Nahida senses a 'warmth' from her past that she cannot explain, which the Traveler links to Rukkhadevata. Aisha's plant could never bloom.

Apep's history of Nibelung's war, King Deshret's pact and the trap it fell into, as told by Apep, who is an interested party. Apep's account is taken from the wiki summary and not independently confirmed.

Characters: Nahida, the Traveler and Paimon.

Pedrush and members of A Moment of Dreams, Ilman, Kathya, Debbi, the dream's owner and Emira, Sitt, and the dragon Apep. Cyno is mentioned as someone Nahida will brief.

Floating Hydro and Anemo fungi, including Nur, the Geoshroom, and Aranara helpers. Layth, Professor Aisha, Gaspar and Basimah appear only in references or dreams.

Consequences: The dream is broken and the dreamers wake; the scholar will face accountability. Apep is healed and wary. Nahida sets up a camp of fungi under her monitoring.

Nahida resolves to continue learning, including from the elemental fungi, and to reunite them with each other. The fate of the Fire Seed is that it breaks.

Placement: Both acts unlock at Adventure Rank 40 after Akasha Pulses, the Kalpa Flame Rises. Lingering Warmth was released in 3.2 on 2022-11-02 and Homecoming in 3.6 on 2023-04-12, so Act II follows Act I by several versions but takes place soon after the Sumeru Archon Quest.

763.comment: Sapientia Oromasdis Chapter (Nahida): Apep and the Fire Seed
763.content: The Dendro Dragon once ruled Sumeru's forests and was corrupted by forbidden knowledge. When Nahida purged it from Irminsul, Apep was left with a large void. The Fire Seed is a crystal Nahida and the fungi made to aid it. Its power, taken from Nahida, can heal Apep's Heart of Oasis, but it is unstable.

764.comment: Sapientia Oromasdis Chapter (Nahida): A Moment of Dreams
764.content: An interest group in Sumeru City where people share dreams, formed after the Akasha stopped. Nahida appears as a guest and guards dreamers against the shared dream.

key: Scenes from Life in Meropide World Quest series
765.content:
Scenes from Life in Meropide (also: Scenes from Life in Meropide World Quest series, Meropide daily-life quests, Fortress of Meropide world quests): Scenes from Life in Meropide is a series of twelve small world quests in the Fortress of Meropide, added in version 4.1. They are not chained together; each starts and ends on its own. The Traveler and Paimon do errands and favours for prisoners and guards, paid in Coupons, the fortress's currency, and glimpse the fortress's everyday routines, queues, jokes and regrets.

The quests unlock in batches. Seven become available during the quest "Game of the Rich", and access is also tied to finishing "Hereafter...". Three more open on the first daily reset after finishing "An Eye for an Eye" and the first seven, and the last two open on the next daily reset after those.

Mora is useless in the fortress, so Paimon is always chasing Coupons for the Rag and Bone Shop and the Coupon Cafeteria. The series is mostly comic, but several quests touch on regret, loneliness and the Fontaine Research Institute.

Plot: Each quest is a self-contained errand. In A Raw Deal the Traveler queues for the prisoner Decembre, who wants to post a birthday letter to his son, but he hands over the wrong letter. In Chit-Chat the Traveler negotiates for a study room on behalf of a scholar named Nakul. Dead End, Safe Operation, Treat the Symptoms and Unfinished Task are favours for Clynes, Caterpillar, the doctor Arderne and the photographer Nelly. Fists of Fury is a sparring bout, and Every Debt has a Creditor, Visible Hands and The Art of Negotiation involve guards and fortress bureaucracy. An Actor's Training and Memories close the series with a theatre rehearsal and a conversation with a former Institute researcher.

**A Raw Deal.** Decembre asks the Traveler to stand in the mail room queue because he must rush to the production zone after a safety incident. The queue is the slowest in the fortress, because the clerk, Lutz, embellishes letters as he types them. Other prisoners tell how "Unlucky Decembre" has failed three times. The letter turns out to be the wrong one: a gushing note signed "White Lily" to Monsieur Neuvillette, begging to see him again at her next trial. Decembre says a sick young woman gave it to him and that he paid the Traveler from his own pocket; the Coupons are less than a meal's worth.

**Chit-Chat.** Nakul wants a place to study with shelves, a table and a board, and the room he would like is unavailable. A similar room is occupied by someone who never opens the door. Nakul's earlier bodyguard Nizami hammered on it and failed. The Traveler negotiates through the door, hearing talk of "darkness" and a rival bidder, Carranza. The occupant never opens the door; depending on the offers made, he either agrees to deal only with Nakul in person or refuses, and Nakul pays the Traveler regardless.

**Dead End.** Galvaryet sends the Traveler to help Clynes with a Research Terminal at the Rift of Erosion that needs two people at once. It seals a rift connecting to the outside, which previously needed guards. Clynes lets slip that an advanced version is deployed at the Geode Mine Shaft.

**Fists of Fury.** Nizami, bored and holding Coupons he won from Roussimoff, asks for a spar and takes the Traveler to the Pankration Ring.

**Safe Operation.** Caterpillar and the Traveler open a passage to Supply Warehouse 1 to free Mitul, who was trapped by his associate Koblenz tinkering with a drive valve. Mitul, who sells health drinks, complains about competition from Fonta, pays in Coupons and offers a drink the Traveler declines on Caterpillar's advice.

**Treat the Symptoms.** The former doctor Lechlade believes the "yellow-green stones" from the Institute's Central Laboratory cause his headaches. The certified doctor Arderne says he is not seriously ill, having misdiagnosed a patient on the outside and become paranoid. Arderne sends Pure Water as a "health potion". It works.

**Unfinished Task.** Nelly, an amateur journalist and novice angler with a Kamera, wants a photo of the guard Grainville at work. The Traveler turns off a loudspeaker and reports a fault so Grainville walks past her. She is delighted with the result.

**Every Debt has a Creditor.** Galvaryet and the guard Maupoil cannot scrub a gear-shaped mark from a wall. The Traveler finds it is a Cipher Letter, a technology developed by Mr. Butor, a benefactor of Clynes, that Clynes uses hoping an old acquaintance might decode it. Clynes admits he drew it. The Traveler can say so or defer to him as a technical expert.

**Visible Hands.** Decembre returns offering a hundred Coupons for jobs. Maupoil says he swindles newcomers into commissions for a fraction of the real fee, takes him to solitary and asks the Traveler to drive Fontemer Aberrants from the Geode Mine Shaft, arriving afterwards to find the work already done.

**The Art of Negotiation.** After buying a book of that name, a note in it directs the Traveler to take a satisfaction survey at the Coupon Cafeteria's front desk. Paimon follows the book's advice with the clerk Monglane, who rushes the survey and fills it in as "satisfied". Completing it earns the achievement "Non-Zero-Sum Game". The wiki notes the title references a real-world book.

**An Actor's Training.** The two-person Tri-Coupon Troupe, Meilhat and Fourmon, rehearse "The Countess of Monte-Mer", a revenge drama about Juliette. Fourmon says he was sentenced at the Opera Epiclese. They ask the Traveler which ending is better: Juliette giving up revenge, or completing it and finding emptiness.

**Memories.** A loudspeaker plays odd broadcasts that lead the Traveler to Clynes. He says the fortress is simpler than the outside, that nothing outside is worth worrying about, and that he is content, though his friends are gone. He names Butor, who died of illness, Teilhard, who died when the Central Laboratory exploded, and a fired colleague he will not discuss. Completing it earns "The Superfluous Man's Account".

Revelations: - The fortress runs on Coupons, not Mora. Prisoners queue for mail, which is read and checked, and take small jobs and wagers.
- Clynes is a former Fontaine Research Institute researcher, and the quests refer to the Institute's accidents and its trouble with funding.
- Clynes says he can leave whenever he wants and chooses to stay.

- The Rift of Erosion once connected the fortress to the outside; a sealing device is used for it and a more advanced one at the Geode Mine Shaft.
- A Cipher Letter is a Butor-developed coding technique used at the Institute and known to few.
- Fonta and Pure Water compete as drinks inside the fortress.

Characters: The Traveler and Paimon, with prisoners and guards including Decembre, Nakul, Nizami, Clynes, Caterpillar, Mitul, Koblenz, the doctors Arderne and Lechlade, the amateur journalist Nelly and the guard Grainville, the guards Galvaryet and Maupoil, the clerk Monglane, and the Tri-Coupon Troupe's Meilhat and Fourmon.

Galvaryet is an official of the fortress who mentions her sister Galvana. Clynes is a technician and former Institute researcher who is deeply nostalgic. Decembre is a recurring swindler whose bad luck becomes a running joke.

Consequences: The quests have only small local effects: a stuck mark removed, a rift sealed, a photograph taken. They add a record of life in the fortress rather than change the main story.

Placement: Released in version 4.1. Availability comes in three batches tied to the archon quests "Game of the Rich", "Hereafter..." and "An Eye for an Eye", with the last quests opening after daily resets.

766.comment: Scenes from Life in Meropide: Coupons
766.content: Coupons are the currency used inside the Fortress of Meropide. Nakul says Mora is useless there. Prisoners buy food at the Coupon Cafeteria and goods at the Rag and Bone Shop with Coupons, and employ one another for errands.

767.comment: Scenes from Life in Meropide: Clynes
767.content: Clynes is a technician in the Fortress of Meropide who worked at the Fontaine Research Institute. He repairs devices, is the author of the Cipher Letter mark on the wall, and says he stays by choice. He mourns Butor, who died of illness, and Teilhard, who died in the Central Laboratory explosion, and says a fourth colleague was fired.

768.comment: Scenes from Life in Meropide: Decembre
768.content: Decembre is a prisoner nicknamed "Unlucky Decembre" for repeated failures at the mail room queue. He hands the Traveler the wrong letter, and later offers jobs to newcomers at a fraction of the real pay, for which Maupoil takes him to solitary.

769.comment: Scenes from Life in Meropide: Tri-Coupon Troupe
769.content: The Tri-Coupon Troupe is a two-person theatre group of prisoners, Meilhat and Fourmon, rehearsing "The Countess of Monte-Mer" and promoting it by loudspeaker. Fourmon says he was sentenced at the Opera Epiclese.

770.content:
Secret Summer Paradise (also: Veluriyam Mirage event, Bottleland event, An Invitation From Afar, Mirage Paradise in Crisis, Dreams and First Encounters): The Mirage is a glass-bottle world holding an amusement-park-like village. Idyia, who looks after it, welcomes visitors, and when the Traveler's group arrives the place is failing. Over three acts they gather four missing components for a spindle-like core (one from each of several residents), meet Sangonomiya Kokomi, Eula and Collei who are also there, and discover that Idyia is an Oceanid and that the residents are Hydro Eidolon copies of earlier visitors. The core is restarted with the help of Kokomi's relic, the Shinrou Casket.

Players who collected enough Fascinating Phenocrysts could invite Layla (Cryo) to the party, and Joyeux Vouchers collected in the Mirage could be exchanged for Kaeya's outfit "Sailwind Shadow", which was sold in the Character Outfit Shop after the end of 3.8. The event required Adventure Rank 18 and the Archon Quest Song of the Dragon and Freedom.

Plot: Act I, An Invitation From Afar! Jean asks the Traveler and Paimon to take Klee to Sumeru. Klee has been in solitary confinement at the Knights of Favonius headquarters and has just received her mother Alice's letter, which includes a "Magic Invite" that teleports its users anywhere, but only three times. Jean sends Kaeya with them. They first go to Gandharva Ville and find Collei, and Eula, who has come after hearing that one of her Lawrence cousins in Sumeru wants to restore the clan's honour. Following the invitation, Collei works out the target is somewhere in the desert; they teleport, cannot see anything, then call for help and enter a bottle, finding a magical world inside. They meet Idyia and Sangonomiya Kokomi, who is already there. Idyia is surprised to see guests and apologises that the domain has suddenly gone downhill. The group splits up to find the four missing components, getting the first one and then helping Ferdinand, Jeroney and Haddo, the caretakers of the cart area, to get it running again.

Act II, Mirage Paradise in Crisis! Next morning Eula, Collei and Idyia head for the fairgrounds where the manager, Maymunah, a Spantamad scholar, explains that the world was suddenly turned upside down. Something falling from the central hub knocked down the Crystal Light in the big tent and trapped Hydro Eidolons, and Lessig, a Lawrence clan man who tried to help, was also trapped. Everyone sets about fixing the fallen lights. Lessig refuses help; Idyia calms things with candy and Lessig admits his mistake. Maymunah says she came to the Mirage to run her own festival. The crystal is raised, the Eidolons freed, and Maymunah gives them a central hub component, a candy box. Kokomi says she is looking for the Shinrou Casket, lost long ago from Watatsumi Island, and all clues lead to the Mirage.

Act III, Dreams and First Encounters! Lessig confesses that he is the cause of the chaos: he touched a water orb, the domain's core, without knowing. The Traveler, Klee, Kaeya and Kokomi find the last component with Zosimos, a stage director, who will give it only after they perform his play. Klee, Kaeya and Kokomi act, the Traveler moves preprint props, and Zosimos is moved to receive costumes sewn for him by Idyia; he hands over a bottle-lamp. The group places the three components in the spindle-like core, but it does not move. Kokomi senses elemental energy in all the residents, deduces they are Hydro Eidolons that can take human form, and Idyia reveals she is an Oceanid. The residents are copies of previous human visitors, made by Idyia with the Streaming Projector to realise their wishes, and the components were gifts visitors left her. Kokomi proposes borrowing the Shinrou Casket from the core; Idyia wishes that everyone who came to the Mirage achieves what they truly wish for, and the casket glows and the hub turns again. Later at the top of the wheel Idyia tells Klee and the Traveler she comes there alone whenever a visitor leaves.

Details. In Act I the group uses the preprint (a 2D side-view puzzle entered through Streaming Projectors) to free a trapped Water Droplet that leads them to the town. Eula and Collei could not make much progress at first and planned to explore the northern jungle. Idyia explains that Ferdinand, Jeroney and Haddo were rescued from a sandstorm after setting out on an adventure. In Act II, Maymunah recalls helping her father with festivities at the Grand Bazaar and says she wanted to become her true self. In Act III, Zosimos wanted to write an epic story about a thief and a mage; Paimon and Idyia give honest criticism of the play. Idyia explains that the casket listens to wishes made by those who pray to it, building "shinki", which gives it power.

Revelations: Idyia is an Oceanid. The residents of the Veluriyam Mirage (Zosimos, Maymunah, the cart caretakers and others) are Hydro Eidolon replicas of previous human visitors, created to carry on the visitors' dreams. The central components are gifts from those visitors. Visitors cannot take what they make in the Mirage into the outside world; some were angry at that and destroyed everything, while others asked for a replica of themselves to stay. Kokomi's Shinrou Casket works through wishes people have prayed over it.

The wiki's Veluriyam Mirage page notes that Kaveh redesigned many buildings in the domain according to Idyia, and it is only "supposedly" in Sumeru.

Characters: Klee, Kaeya, the Traveler and Paimon; Jean (sends them), Alice (letter sender), Eula and Collei (already in the area), Sangonomiya Kokomi (seeking a lost relic), Idyia (host), Lessig (a Lawrence man, Eula's cousin), Maymunah (fairground manager), Zosimos (stage director), and the cart caretakers Ferdinand, Jeroney and Haddo.

Layla was the invitable reward character and Kaeya received an outfit. The wiki lists additional named event NPCs (Director-in-Chief, Engineer, Fake Playwright, Food Manager, Gretchen, Harum-Scarum, Hustler, Loafer, Mandora) in the event's character list.

Consequences: The central hub turns again and the Mirage returns to normal. Lessig offers to help maintain the domain. Klee gets the ride on the Choo-Choo Cart she wanted, and Idyia lets them enjoy the domain. Kokomi's search for the Shinrou Casket is only partly resolved on screen: the casket is borrowed from the core to help repair it.

Placement: Released in Version 3.8 as a Flagship Event, after the Sumeru Archon Quests (Song of the Dragon and Freedom is the entry requirement; Akasha Pulses, the Kalpa Flame Rises and some Story Quests are recommended with a Quick Start). Event quests are self-contained and not part of the main storyline.

Gameplay: Game mechanics, not in-world fact. Four mini-games unlocked in phases: Spino Blaster (water-cannon marksmanship), Sojourns of the Barking Fox (speed trials with a toy fox), Dance of Flashing Thought (combat challenges earning Honed Will) and Bing-Bang Finchball (launching Finchballs for score). The Choo-Choo Cart, preprints, Gleaming Lamps and Joyeux Vouchers are exploration features of the area.

771.content: A limited-time summer event area: a domain hidden within a bottle in the middle of the Sumeru desert. Rumour says those who enter are granted their heart's desire. It is run by Idyia and populated by Hydro Eidolons who copy past visitors. The wiki notes it is not treated as a normal Domain in gameplay.

772.content: An Oceanid and the caretaker of the Veluriyam Mirage, who looks after it and likes to spend time alone at the top of the wheel when a visitor leaves. She gives visitors candy and helps them restore the central hub, and in the finale wishes for all visitors to achieve their true wishes.

773.content: A relic lost long ago from Watatsumi Island that Kokomi seeks. It records the prayers of those who come to it, building "shinki" that gives it its power, and is used to restart the Mirage's central hub.

774.content: A man of the Lawrence clan, cousin to Eula, who came to the Mirage to restore the clan's honour but found nobody cared about it. He triggered the disaster by touching a water orb. After being trapped and reconciling with Eula he helps maintain the domain.

775.content: A cart ride in the Mirage looked after by Ferdinand, Jeroney and Haddo. Klee wishes to ride it to the top of the wheel at the end of the story.

776.content:
Seirai Stormchasers (also: Seirai Stormchasers Part I, Seirai Stormchasers Part IV, Warding Stones quest, Peculiar Pinion): A version 2.1 world quest series on Seirai Island, Inazuma. The Adventurers' Guild cannot explore the island because of constant storms. Katheryne sends the Traveler to help two adventurers, Etsuko and Taisuke, and the Traveler meets a talking cat who knows how to seal the Warding Stones that keep the storm at bay.

The series has four parts. The Traveler follows a cat's tracks to the Asase Shrine, repairs its Offering Box for the cat Neko, learns how to seal four Warding Stones, and seals them, two on the ground and two in the sky. A boss, the Thunder Manifestation, is fought on a platform of floating stones, and the Traveler finds a strange feather, the Peculiar Pinion.

Completing the series removes the Balethunder from the island, unlocks the Thunder Manifestation as a boss and awards an achievement of the same name. It is also the first meeting with Neko, who returns in later Inazuma quests.
