Plot: Katheryne says the guild's Seirai exploration is blocked by wild storms and suggests the Traveler help. On the island Etsuko explains that going toward the centre is too dangerous because of Balethunder, and that they have found broken stone structures they think are called Warding Stones.

Etsuko and Taisuke focus on the stones while the Traveler and Paimon follow strange cat tracks to a shrine in better shape and fairer weather than the rest of the island. There the cat Neko, who calls herself the provisional head priestess of the Asase Shrine, is worried about the damaged Offering Box, since Hibiki would grieve to see the shrine in a sorry state. She agrees to teach the Traveler about the Warding Stones in exchange for repairs, and describes the bird of most prodigious size the stones were meant to keep sealed.
The Traveler tells the adventurers (Taisuke is thrilled by the talking cat) and the group seals the first two stones. The other two prove puzzling until the Traveler realises they are in the sky, and goes up through a Phase Gate. Sealing them forms a huge platform from the floating stones, where the Traveler defeats a Thunder Manifestation and then finds the Peculiar Pinion.

Back on the ground the storm has passed. Taisuke cannot identify the Pinion and suggests posting a commission, and Etsuko plans to file the guild report, but Taisuke insists on visiting the Asase Shrine first. In Part IV the Traveler touches three paper-charm hangers and rotates the final Warding Stone; three chests that appeared on the floating rocks drop to sea level afterwards.

Revelations: The Warding Stones were made to seal a huge bird, and breaking them let the storm and the Thunder Manifestation loose. The wiki's profile of Neko, built on this and later material, says the wards were broken in the time of Asase Hibiki and Ako Domeki, when a Shogunate fleet attacked, after which Hibiki and Domeki vanished and the island stayed in storm for around 500 years. This series itself tells only part of that, through Neko's words.

The Peculiar Pinion's origin is not explained in the series.

Characters: The Traveler and Paimon; Katheryne; Etsuko and Taisuke of the Adventurers' Guild; the cat Neko.

Etsuko is a guild adventurer in the standard uniform and keeps Taisuke on topic. Neko is a large black cat with golden eyes who has lived for at least five centuries and styles herself provisional head priestess.

The wiki's Neko profile describes later events outside this series: Neko has a statue made by the artist Ooshima Junpei, takes a walk to find the island's village empty, and visits the Grand Narukami Shrine, where she admires its large offering box while insisting hers is better. These belong to Neko Is a Cat and are not part of the stormchasing.

Consequences: The storm clears and Seirai Island is open to exploration. Neko stays at the Asase Shrine, and her story continues in the quest Neko Is a Cat.

Placement: Released in Version 2.1. The wiki lists Ritou Escape Plan as its requirement. Part IV is followed by A Particularly Particular Author in the quest ordering.

777.comment: Seirai Stormchasers: Neko of the Asase Shrine
777.content: Neko is a talking black cat who calls herself the provisional head priestess of the Asase Shrine on Seirai Island. She waited for Hibiki's return at the shrine and keeps it as tidy as she can; she first helps the Traveler in Seirai Stormchasers.

778.content:
Shadows Amidst Snowstorms (also: The Snowy Past, The Shadows Deepen, A Secret Born From Ashes, Dragonspine winter camp event): Act I (The Snowy Past) starts from Paimon's wish for a fruit-juicing machine and moves up Dragonspine, where the Traveler joins a camp run by Cyrus. Act II (The Shadows Deepen) follows a group stuck on the mountain by bad luck, a night at Albedo's camp and a painting session, then an ambush by the impostor Albedo. Act III (A Secret Born From Ashes) is a story-telling session in which Paimon and Albedo share tales; Albedo's, which the Traveler takes to describe real events about the impostor, and the event ends with Joel's reunion and a last scene in Mondstadt that returns to the juicer joke.

The Fellflower is the event's boss. The event is a Dragonspine character-focus story for Albedo, with significant parts for Eula and Bennett, and is a milder winter counterpart to the earlier event The Chalk Prince and the Dragon.

Plot: Act I, The Snowy Past: Paimon asks the alchemists Timaeus and Sucrose to build a fruit juicer that keeps juice fresh; they say it is beyond alchemy and suggest Albedo, who had just left looking grim. On Dragonspine the Traveler finds Cyrus holding winter training with senior and junior adventurers. Amber has been entertaining Joel, whose father is missing, and Eula, who has never built a snowman, joins them. Cyrus has a spare instructor slot, because Fischl, originally invited, was busy elsewhere, and Eula takes it for the newcomer Gerald. The Traveler meets Albedo, who says he is on the mountain for quiet and to gather Starsilver for paint, and who invites them to learn painting at his camp. His camp has been burgled, his alchemy notes taken; the footprints lead to a cavern and Albedo goes on ahead alone. When the Traveler hears Bennett's voice, they find him caged in a Fatui camp and free him. Albedo has disappeared.

Act II, The Shadows Deepen: Back at Albedo's camp the Traveler and Paimon find Amber, Eula and Bennett have wandered the mountain for days, plagued by avalanches and ill luck. Albedo creates chairs by painting them, cooks dinner and paints Paimon's portrait with the Traveler. The next day an avalanche separates the party and Eula senses something is wrong. In a cutscene Albedo starts to make a Cryo Solar Isotoma and is run through by a second Albedo, who turns into a plant. Eula cuts the thing down, and Albedo explains it is an extremely rare mutated whopperflower and that Dragonspine's dragon-blood-saturated land makes strange life possible.

Act III, A Secret Born From Ashes: The Traveler and Paimon trade stories at Albedo's camp. Paimon tells a horror tale about whopperflowers that replace the people they eat. Albedo tells a longer story about Subject One, a synthetic human who blends in among people, and Subject Two, a failed experiment revived by a dragon's power on a snowy mountain, who copies Subject One and makes a Subject Three, intending to replace him. Albedo says it is just a story, but warns that monsters touched by Durin's blood are, like him, creatures of Rhinedottir. The group returns to the camp, where Cyrus and Pallad present Joserf, Joel's father, found without memory and recovering. A final scene in Mondstadt's alchemy shop shows Albedo again with the mark on his neck and a joke about burying fruit in Dragonspine's snow.

Details. In Act I, the Traveler's earlier quest Lost in the Snow is a prerequisite, and Gerald, a new adventurer, is paired with Eula. In Act II, Bennett's bad luck is a recurring subject: he flips Treasure Hoarder Insignias hoping to guess wrong and "use up" his misfortune, while Eula admits she does not usually believe in luck but concedes he makes the case. Albedo's chair-painting shows how his alchemy treats paintings as blueprints. Just before the ambush Eula tells the Traveler she senses that something has changed. Albedo says he once ground Mist Flowers into white paint to imitate the sparkle of snowflakes; it worked well but such works need careful storage.

Act III small details: Joserf was found by Reckless Pallad after Pallad fell down a slope; Joel recognised him and called him "Dad", at which Joserf began recovering memories of Joel and Joel's mother only. Joel says goodbye to Eula, who gives him powdered rime so his snowman never melts, and gives the Traveler and Paimon a packet too. Cyrus then scolds Pallad for his breaches of discipline.

Revelations: The "other Albedo" is a plant, not a human: Albedo identifies it as an extremely rare mutated whopperflower, and the event's boss is called the Fellflower. Albedo's second Act III story, framed as fiction, tells of two copies of a synthetic human; he says monsters touched by Durin's blood are creatures of Rhinedottir "just like me". When the Traveler protests that he is no monster he replies that he knows what he is and that he and the Traveler are both "different". In his story the copy erases the mark on its neck as a symbol of imperfection; in the final scene the mark on Albedo's neck briefly vanishes and returns, and the Traveler decides it was a prank.

Durin is described by Albedo as an artificially created life form whose remains make Dragonspine "a cradle of life's profoundest mysteries". Albedo also muses that creation might be arrogant and asks why creators are called gods; he feels a twinge of grief when thinking of the impostor.

Characters: Albedo (host, the target of the impostor), the Traveler and Paimon, Eula and Amber (Knights, present as helpers), Bennett (unlucky adventurer), Sucrose and Timaeus (alchemists, in Act I and III), and event NPCs Cyrus (Guild branch master), Reckless Pallad, Gerald (new recruit), Joel and his father Joserf. Fischl is mentioned as the original instructor who could not attend.

Eula is shown being called "Aunty" by Joel, who does not know what the Lawrence name means in Mondstadt; she is surprised and not displeased.

Consequences: Joel and Joserf leave Dragonspine together; the winter camp ends. The impostor is destroyed. The event's weapon reward was the sword Cinnabar Spindle. No further consequences are shown in the event.

Placement: Released in Version 2.3 as a Flagship Event; requirements were Adventure Rank 20, Prologue Act II, the Princeps Cretaceus Chapter Act I and Lost in the Snow. It is self-contained and not part of the Archon Quests.

Gameplay: Game mechanics, not in-world fact. Born of the Snow had players build Puffy Snowmen from components; Dragonspine Special Training offered Agility, Tracker and Combat training; Rise of the Fell Flower was a boss challenge against the Fellflower in which players hit Arcane Fruits back at it and picked up Arcane Essence. Rewards were exchanged for Snowstrider and Vanquisher's Emblems.

779.content: A very rare mutated whopperflower that took Albedo's appearance and tried to replace him on Dragonspine. Albedo says conditions there are far from typical because dragon blood seeped into the land and passed to monsters by the ley lines, speeding mutation. It is the event's boss: it summons Arcane Fruits and releases Arcane Essence.

780.comment: Shadows Amidst Snowstorms: Joel and Joserf
780.content: Joel is a boy living at the Dragonspine camp whose father had gone missing. In this event Reckless Pallad finds Joserf, who has lost most of his memory but recognises Joel and starts to recover. He survived hunting alone in a cave while his legs healed. They leave together.

781.content: Throughout the event Bennett believes his bad luck rubs off on others and apologises for avalanches and falls. Eula, Amber and the Traveler reassure him it is not his fault. He jokes that guessing a Treasure Hoarder Insignia flip wrongly uses up bad luck. A miracle of misfortune with Pallad ultimately helps reunite Joel with his father.

782.comment: Shadows Amidst Snowstorms: Albedo's painting and Paimon's portrait
782.content: Albedo teaches the Traveler to paint at his camp and uses painted blueprints to create chairs through alchemy. The Traveler's portrait of Paimon is poor; Albedo reworks it into a flattering image that Paimon hangs up. He says alchemy can create living beings with enough research.

key: Shadows of the Mountains World Quest series
783.content:
Shadows of the Mountains (also: Shadows of the Mountains World Quest series, Shadow Pin quests, Titu's Shadow Pin quests): Shadows of the Mountains is a two-quest Natlan world series added in version 5.0, set in Tequemecan Valley. A tribal storyteller named Titu is watching a giant stone pillar, the Greater Shadow Pin, and its three smaller Lesser Shadow Pins, which hold back the Abyss. The Traveler, Paimon and the Little One help restore them and then find out what is trapped beneath.

The series is told through a storyteller's lens. Titu keeps returning to how tales are shaped and warped, and the central reveal is that a villain from local legend was a hero. It ends with an act of mercy, not a victory.

The two quests are Beneath the Crystal Rock and Peace to the Slumbering. The second starts automatically after the first. Both give Children of Echoes reputation.

Plot: **Beneath the Crystal Rock.** At a sentry post in Tequemecan Valley the sentry Yukom is waiting for Titu to relieve him. The Traveler meets Titu beside the giant Shadow Pin. Titu explains that the Wayob are said in stories to have hung the pins to pin the shadow of the Volcano Lord, but in truth what is sealed beneath is the Abyss. Two of the three Lesser Shadow Pins have floated upward and the Iridescent Inscription, the language the ancient dragons used to wield phlogiston, has been squeezed out of them. The Traveler touches the inscription, breaks crystals to gather its power and fights Abyss-aligned monsters to push each pin back. The second pin's inscription has also been scattered and must be found in other places, with the Little One's nose pointing the way. Afterward the party asks Titu to tell the real story of the pins.

When all three Lesser Pins are set, the ground trembles. Black, Nightsoul-warped warriors appear, the Greater Shadow Pin falls into a deep cavity beneath it, and a hoarse voice cries out.

**Peace to the Slumbering.** Titu and the party climb down the hole. A tablet from Elder Traore explains that two Khaenri'ahn soldiers, Zephaniah and Irizar, guided the black flood to the seal site and stayed in it, and that the tribe's warriors sacrificed themselves with them. The Iridescent Inscription at the bottom is shattered into fragments and the party breaks the stones containing them while fighting Rifthounds. Voices behind the inscription reveal that more than two souls are locked in endless struggle with the Abyss. The Traveler unseals the inscription and defeats the two warriors, who thank them with their last words. In the Night Kingdom the Traveler and Paimon meet a beast with night-coloured fur who says the Night has forgiven them. Titu, relieved, plans to retell the story with the two soldiers as heroes and returns to take over Yukom's shift.

Titu's account of the old events, told in the first quest, runs thus. The mountains where the Children of Echoes live were once more complete and lovely. The Khaenri'ahn catastrophe damaged Natlan's delicate Ley Lines and the Night Kingdom, the totem poles dimmed and the Wayob could not hear the tribes. A dark tide of calamity reached the mountains, brought by two Khaenri'ahn soldiers. With the tribe's leader away at a lone island in the west resisting giant beasts, Elder Traore fought the Abyss. The warriors and Saurians fashioned giant stone nails out of solid phlogiston with the Iridescent Inscription, Traore leapt first into the dark pit, and the Abyss was sealed beneath the earth. Paimon notes this was about five centuries ago. Titu says even today the Children of Echoes, who mine solid phlogiston and gems, know to leave the phlogiston around the nails untouched.

Titu also explains the pun behind the name: a Shadow Pin is called that because it pins shadows.

Traore's tablet is a three-part blessing. He addresses it as elder, storyteller, and shield and spear of the tribe. The first blessing is for friends from afar, Zephaniah and Irizar, who he says would rather be called cowards or a thorn in the tribe's side than heroes and whom he nonetheless names heroes and brother-kin. The second is for the sacrificed warriors, illuminated by the Incandescent God and guided by Chief Sundjatta, and he prays to the spirit of Waxaklahun Ubah Kan, called a madman who stole fire from the throat of the great dragon, to block the Abyss's arcane magic with radiant glyphs. The third is for those who read it, reminding them that fortresses built from sacrifice cannot stand forever and that only an indomitable spirit is truly immortal.

Gameplay note, labelled as such: the challenges require indwelling a Tepetlisaurus or using a Children of Echoes character, and the Little One fights alongside the player in some steps. These do not change the lore.

Revelations: - The Shadow Pins are giant solid-phlogiston nails driven into the ground by the Children of Echoes ages ago, each carrying an Iridescent Inscription, to seal the Abyss. The "Volcano Lord's shadow" is a metaphor.
- The "evil Khaenri'ahn soldiers" of tribal legend, Zephaniah and Irizar, were sealed in with the Abyss and fought it for centuries; Traore's tablet calls them heroes.

- Titu says most tales in Natlan are embellished warnings in which rhetoric is metaphor.
- More souls than the two soldiers are locked with the Abyss; the Traveler hears the sound of countless hands pushing outward.

Characters: Titu (a Children of Echoes storyteller), Yukom (a sentry), the Traveler, Paimon and the Little One. Elder Traore, Zephaniah and Irizar, and the "Beast With Fur Like That of Night" appear through the inscription, boss fights and a vision. Sanhaj of the Masters of the Night-Wind is mentioned by Titu as a storyteller he reveres.

Consequences: The Greater Shadow Pin has fallen and the Abyss in the cavity is purified. The Iridescent Inscription is gone, the tormented voices fall silent, and Zephaniah and Irizar find rest. Titu intends to tell the tale of the golden-haired outlander, the flying white fairy and a small Tepetlisaurus, and to retell the soldiers as heroes.

Placement: Released in version 5.0, in Tequemecan Valley. Beneath the Crystal Rock begins by talking to Titu or by finishing a Lesser Shadow Pin challenge; Peace to the Slumbering follows automatically.

784.content: Titu is a Children of Echoes storyteller who also looks after the stone pillars. He is verbose, self-deprecating and keeps thinking in plots, joking that he is not a fighter. He says he loves heroes' stories most and tells them so that they are remembered. The quest has him come down into the cavity himself, because witnessing things through is a storyteller's duty. He is bad at turning up for his sentry shift, which annoys Yukom. Note that Titu is also the name of a member of Taika's expedition seen in Lost Traveler in the Ashen Realm; the quests do not say they are the same person.

785.comment: Shadows of the Mountains: Shadow Pins
785.content: Giant solid-phlogiston pillars: one large and three small. They seal the Abyss and are driven into the earth by Iridescent Inscription. When the Abyss presses, the inscription is squeezed out and the pin floats upward. The Children of Echoes know not to disturb the phlogiston near them.

786.comment: Shadows of the Mountains: Zephaniah and Irizar
786.content: Two Khaenri'ahn soldiers whom Natlan folklore remembers as villains who brought the Abyss to the valley. Traore's tablet names them as friends who guided the dark flood to the place of the seal and stayed behind it as promised. They are fought as Black Serpent Knights with hoarse, pained voices; Zephaniah worries about leading the tribe away, and Irizar says he does not want a certain person to see him as he is.

787.comment: Shadows of the Mountains: Elder Traore
787.content: Traore was the elder, storyteller and shield and spear of the Children of Echoes at the time of the sealing. According to Titu he was the first to leap into the pit. He left the Boundary Marker Inscription, a three-part blessing, and is remembered as a hero.

788.content: Yukom is a sentry in Tequemecan Valley who keeps waiting for Titu to relieve him from his post. He is tired and exasperated with Titu but worried when the earthquake strikes.

789.content:
Silvermoon Hall: Selenic Chronicles (also: Selenic Chronicles, Silvermoon Hall reputation quests, New Moon's Embrace): A reputation-style series of quests for Columbina, the Damselette, at Silvermoon Hall in Nod-Krai, added in Version 6.0 (Luna I). It is unlocked by the quest The Dark Side of Memory and is read through the Record-Keeping Kuuhenki. It consists of eighteen short quests in three parts, with small personal moments rather than world-changing plot.

Each completed quest gives the party the New Moon's Embrace effect for a time, and finishing groups of quests unlocks rewards. The series is a quiet companion to Columbina's role in the main Nod-Krai story: it shows her with her kuuhenki, a young painter and her memories of home.

The wiki's in-game quest blurbs describe moments such as a young painter introducing its goddess, a mechanic repairing her instrument, a board game that mirrors the tides of history, and her bringing Luonnotar back into the world, so the series reads as a gentle character portrait rather than an adventure.

Plot: The Traveler visits Silvermoon Hall now and then to meet Columbina. Each visit is a short quest; the next becomes available after seven daily resets.

Part I (six quests): The Dark Side of Memory, Her Past, The Artist By the Moon's Side (I), Moonlight Sonata, Homecoming's Faint Glow and May the Moonlight Connect Us. The official blurbs say she takes a beam of moonlight and gives the Traveler the "Moon Goddess's Favor"; that she claims to have "run away from home" yet seems to have fond memories of it; that a young painter tries to introduce its goddess; and that a genius mechanic repairs her broken instrument.

Part II (six quests): The Artist By the Moon's Side (II) and (III), The Moon Adorning the Night, Shifting Moonlight, Moonlight Sonata: Lingering Resonance and A Toast Beneath the Moon. The blurbs show the painter seeing the Moon Goddess at her most joyful, a board that mirrors the tides of history, kuuhenki to play with, echoes of past journeys, doubt over whether an art exhibition on the moon will take place, and the puzzle of what drink "that isn't too heavy" she would want.

Part III (six quests): Come Play With the Moon, The Homebound Moon, The Artist By the Moon's Side (IV), The Moon Adorning the Night: The Three Moons, Where Does the Moon Hide? and A Gift From Her. The blurbs say she brings Luonnotar back into this world, that "I am home," that the painter's strokes bring out a happiness that feels unfamiliar to her, and that the board becomes an extension of the future itself.

This file records only those official blurbs, not the quests' full scripts. Ambient idle scenes in Silvermoon Hall, per the wiki, include Columbina telling the kuuhenki fables (a bird and a whale, a lake that reflects a false moon, a seesaw as a lesson in giving something back) and wondering what Teyvat would look like from the moon above.

Revelations: The series is largely character material. Its blurbs imply that Columbina has a home she once left and now speaks of as home, and that Luonnotar can be brought back into the world by her, but the details belong to the Nod-Krai Archon Quest and are not reconstructed here.

The blurbs use spoiler-heavy wording ("I am home", the Three Moons) tied to the Archon Quest, so they should not be given to a character who has not seen that story.

Characters: Columbina, called the Damselette, her kuuhenki, the Traveler and Paimon. Part I also involves a young painter and a mechanic, and Part III involves Luonnotar, as named in the quest blurbs.

Idle dialogue shows Columbina as soft-spoken and unhurried, turning small observations into tales for the kuuhenki. She likes high places and sometimes appears behind the Traveler after the camera pans away. Her own entry carries her full portrayal.

Consequences: Completing a quest gives the New Moon's Embrace effect until the seventh daily reset: while in Nod-Krai, the party's Moonsign Level is Ascendant Gleam, and it cannot be switched off. Completing groups of quests unlocks rewards (Part I: From Here I Gaze, Blueprint: Cloud-Wrapped Moon and Blueprint: Blanket of Stars; Part II: Nod-Krai: Moonlight; Part III: Wings of the Silent Moon). These are gameplay items; they do not change the story.

Placement: Introduced in Version 6.0 (Luna I) with Nod-Krai. After each quest the player waits seven daily resets for the next. The Selenic Chronicles quests become unavailable when A Nocturne of the Far North starts (it begins automatically after Act IV, An Elegy for Faded Moonlight), and become available again after True Moon is completed.

790.comment: Silverwing in Pursuit of the Moon
790.content:
Silverwing in Pursuit of the Moon (also: Moonchase Festival 2026 event, Version 7.1 Moonchase event, World Food Fair event, Another Auspicious Moonlit Night Rolls Around, As One Might Stride Betwixt the Clouds (event), On White Wings Pierce Through Cloud and Fog, Having Met You, My Heart is Gladdened, Next Year's Moon, Just as Bright): This year's Moonchase is organised by Chenyu Vale's associations and replaces the Masterful Chefs contest with a World Food Fair featuring cooks from four nations. While the Millelith and the Lan clan's thaumaturges fight evil spirits stirred up by the festival, Lan Yan and the Traveler help Lan Junming, a remnant soul bound to a rattan figure with a seal he placed himself, recover his lost memory over several days: a poem, a Moon-Viewing Gathering, a promise made with Silverwing. Zhongli reveals what became of her, and Lan Yan performs a final art so that he can rest. Meanwhile, Xiangling, Escoffier and the food-street cooks solve a dispute over Wangxiao Cakes.

The story is told in a prologue ("Another Auspicious Moonlit Night Rolls Around"), three parts and an epilogue ("As One Might Stride Betwixt the Clouds", "On White Wings Pierce Through Cloud and Fog", "Having Met You, My Heart is Gladdened", "Next Year's Moon, Just as Bright") plus the Wondrous Anecdotes chapter. Recommended earlier quests include Dulciaria Structura Chapter Act I, Tapirus Somniator Chapter Act I and A Lanternlit Ode to the Silver Moon (6.3), which revives Zibai.

The event's title echoes the line "Through autumn skies, the windborne silverwing chases the moon" from a poem Hu Tao recounts at the Moon-Viewing Gathering, and the epilogue's title, "Next Year's Moon, Just as Bright", matches the closing promise of a yearly food duel. The event ends with the idea that Moonchase events change every year while food and friends remain.

Plot: Prologue: Xiangling invites the Traveler and Paimon to Yilong Wharf for the World Food Fair. Escoffier is there for Fontaine, Ningguang has come on official business and Lan Yan shows the Traveler around.

Part I: Lan Yan and the Traveler meet an old man repeating that "Moonchase ought not to be like this". He is a remnant soul in a rattan figure. Tracing Zibai from Baiju Guesthouse to Iron Tongue Tian's storytelling, they find her with Zhongli, and she identifies him as Lan Junming, the Wind Reader, and Zhongli suggests the Moon-Viewing Gathering at Wangshu Inn as the Moonchase he remembers.

Part II: Travelling toward Wangshu Inn they fight possessed monsters with Hu Tao, Xingqiu, Chongyun and Gaming. At the gathering Lan Junming remembers his promise to Silverwing.

Part III: They try to summon Silverwing but she does not come. Zhongli explains her fate, and Lan Yan performs a final art that frees Lan Junming's soul.

Epilogue: Ningguang thanks Lan Yan, swallows are calmer, and the Traveler enjoys the food street.

The five parts and the food chapter are described in separate entries.

Event gameplay is listed in the gameplay section. The three event world quests are Little Figure Exorcism, Battle Beneath the Spirit-Quelling Banner and Sigil Barrage Kaleidoscope.

Revelations: Lan Junming (the Wind Reader, also called Mad Lan) was a thaumaturge counted among the Eight Adepts. With the Red Runt (Wuwang Kid), whose Qihuang Arts he borrowed, he created a ward that repelled evil spirits. Silverwing, the Jade-Plumed Silverwing, carried sigils bearing the ward over Liyue so that he could draw on her adeptal power; each year at the Moonchase Festival the two promised to meet and renew the sigils. He used the forbidden Soul-Binding Art on himself to be able to keep the appointment. Silverwing, born from the spirit of heaven and earth, was embodied in swallows; losses on the long journeys wiped away her memory and mind, and in the end the swallows forgot their promise.

Lan Junming's remnant soul had awakened before, as Lan Yu's family stories suggest. At the end he learns that the failure was not his and is helped to leave. The ward and technique he created became the evil-dispelling art every Liyue thaumaturge now learns, and the Lan clan's tradition of teaching anyone who sincerely asks comes from him.

Lan Junming never married, according to Lan Yu, and the present Lan clan descends from his two brothers; he returned in later years to Chenyu Vale and taught them everything. Zhongli compares Silverwing's fate to the Ship of Theseus.

Characters: Main: the Traveler, Paimon, Lan Yan, Lan Junming (remnant soul), Zibai, Zhongli. Lan clan: Lan Yu (clan head) and other elders. Friends: Hu Tao, Xingqiu, Chongyun, Gaming, Xiangling, Guoba. Others: Ningguang, Escoffier, Lu Weng, Iron Tongue Tian, Jiangxue. Adepti: Cloud Retainer (Xianyun), Moon Carver, Mountain Shaper, Madame Ping, Xiao. Silverwing and Wuwang Kid appear only in memory.

Event listing on the wiki also includes Alphonse, Baofei, Carpe Diem, Da Xi'er, Dip Yeuk, Edler, Elowen, Eymen, Freda, Gaspard, Grandmaster Hanakado, Hautemontagne, Hyakujitsuhaku Shion, Isak, Jiewu, Kamal, Lan Ying, Lu Xiangxiang, Matsumoto, Mei Youyu, Mowang, Okazaki Erika, Okazaki Rikuto, Pain-Grocer, Pingxi, Roxane, Savanna, Shevirme, Shiba Murasaki, Shuyu, Vert Jr., Wenxun, Xi'er and Yaolu, who appear in the food street and open world.

Consequences: Lan Junming's remnant soul is released and returns to the Ley Lines. Lan Yan's art, completed at the pavilion east of Teatree Slope, suppresses evil spirits across Liyue, shortens the Millelith's operations and calms the swallows, which should return to nest in Chenyu Vale. Lan Yan finds a "responsibility" of her own, and her clan elders praise her. The Chenyu Vale Confectionery Guild president accepts a new Wangxiao Cake and funds more batches. Xiangling and Escoffier agree to hold a culinary duel at Yilong Wharf every year.

Placement: Released in Version 7.1 as a Flagship Event for the Moonchase Festival, running from 24 September 2026. Requirements were Adventure Rank 20 and the Prologue Act III (Song of the Dragon and Freedom). It takes place after the Frost Moon's return and the revival of Zibai in A Lanternlit Ode to the Silver Moon (6.3), who is by now living at Baiju Guesthouse, and the World Food Fair brings cooks from Mondstadt, Fontaine and Sumeru to Yilong Wharf.

Gameplay: Game mechanics, not in-world fact. Three modes: The Great Chase and Dispelling (steer a rattan figure to collect adeptal power and dispel evil energy), Banner Against the Dark (defeat enemies and damage a boss for a score) and Spiritshot Salvo (fire Spiritshots with Sigils and spells). Players can also take Festive Priorities and Wondrous Anecdotes quests. Accumulating Festive Cheer (up to 1,200) gives the sword Silver Light at 200, Primogems, Tea-Scented Tassel materials, a Crown of Insight and furnishing blueprints. The story is Festive Priorities; the Food Street chapter is the Wondrous Anecdotes.

key: Another Auspicious Moonlit Night Rolls Around
791.comment: Silverwing in Pursuit of the Moon: Prologue - Another Auspicious Moonlit Night Rolls Around
791.content: Xiangling writes inviting the Traveler to Yilong Wharf. Chenyu Vale's associations organise this year's Moonchase, and with the Lan clan's elders' agreement the Masterful Chefs contest has been replaced by a World Food Fair with representatives from Mondstadt, Fontaine and Sumeru as well as Liyue. Escoffier represents Fontaine. Ningguang says Moonchase has always been shaped by the people, that new customs are folded in and later called tradition, and that she is there on official business: around this time evil forces gather and possess monsters, so the Millelith have mobilised and the Lan clan's thaumaturges will help.

key: As One Might Stride Betwixt the Clouds
792.comment: Silverwing in Pursuit of the Moon: Part I - As One Might Stride Betwixt the Clouds
792.content:
Lan Yan, who chose the mystic arts as a hobby rather than a duty, shows Paimon and the Traveler around and mentions she is studying a swallow-related art. They meet an old man who keeps saying "Moonchase ought not to be like this", disliking the food street and calling Liyue changed. Lan Yan recognises the Soul-Binding Art, a forbidden clan technique that traps part of a soul in a rattan effigy. A seal blocks her from undoing it. He asks for help finding the Moonchase he remembers, which has nothing to do with cooking, and says Lan Yan's art steadies him. They think of Zibai at Baiju Guesthouse. At Iron Tongue Tian's, Zibai and Zhongli discuss the Moonchase Rite; Zibai recognises him as Mad Lan, the Wind Reader, Lan Junming. She says the technique was invented by Lan Junming himself, and the seal is his own work, so brute force would disperse his soul. Zhongli proposes a Moon-Viewing Gathering at Wangshu Inn in two days. Lan Junming accepts the title "Grandmaster".

Lan Yan explains that when a dignitary like Ningguang visits, many clan elders come and etiquette is strict, so she greeted one uncle and left. She also tells Paimon the clan rule that children choose whether the mystic arts are a duty or a hobby, which began when the founder, the Wind Reader, answered his descendants' dilemma with "Why not both?". Lan Junming himself asks that the elders not fuss over him.

key: On White Wings Pierce Through Cloud and Fog
793.comment: Silverwing in Pursuit of the Moon: Part II - On White Wings Pierce Through Cloud and Fog
793.content:
Two days later Lan Yan decides to walk the mountain paths with Lan Junming. Near Dihua Marsh they find Gaming, Hu Tao, Xingqiu and Chongyun besieged by possessed monsters; evil spirits born from fallen gods move from monster to monster. Lan Yan organises a spirit-quelling banner and rattan figures to sweep up the spirits. Lan Junming asks after a Tianheng Sect and a Yunlai Sect and finds the martial and thaumaturgic schools of Liyue unlike his memory. At Wangshu Inn Xiao and the fisherman Jiangxue (successor of Fish Creel, the Yunlai Angler) appear, and Xiangling and Smiley Yanxiao provide the Moon-Viewing Gathering's food. Hu Tao recounts a poetry contest in which Wuwang Kid beat Lan Junming with "Through autumn skies, the windborne silverwing chases the moon...". Lan Junming recalls Silverwing: during the Archon War he combined Qimen techniques with the Red Runt's Qihuang Arts to make a ward and inscribed it on sigils for her to carry. They promised to meet each year at Moonchase and renew the art, "seeing off the autumn swallow". The seal can only be lifted when the art is performed once more. They agree on a pavilion east of Teatree Slope two days later.

Lan Junming says the Eight Adepts first met by chance at a roadside tea stop; Hu Tao proposes a modern "New Eight" and several joke titles. Xiao says he remembers most Moon-Viewing Gatherings and that their customs have stayed the same for centuries. Jiangxue refuses to join because his ancestor ordered the family to avoid Mad Lan.

794.comment: Silverwing in Pursuit of the Moon: Part III - Having Met You, My Heart is Gladdened
794.content:
Lan Yu, head of the Lan clan, tells the story of his ancestor: unmarried, he brought his learning home and taught his brothers, and later Moonchase stories speak of a strange man appearing in Yilong Wharf each year. At the pavilion Lan Yan learns the swallow-pattern art that once called Silverwing and, with the Traveler, gathers adeptal energy to reveal the pattern on the water. Silverwing does not come. The art is weakening. The Traveler and Paimon ask the adepti at Mt. Aocang. Nobody knows where she is, except Zhongli, who explains that she was born from the spirit of heaven and earth and that the swallows were her embodiments. In the Archon War she flew between Chenyu Vale and Guyun Stone Forest, resting at Thousand Winds Temple, and swallows died on every trip. She lost pieces of her mind and memory with them, until the swallows forgot their promise to Lan Junming. He compares her to a ship all of whose parts have been replaced.

Lan Yan decides to tell Lan Junming the truth and lift the seal. She performs a recreated version of the art at night, while Lan Junming sings of his promise and of his love of the scenery he saw in her eyes. The seal opens, his remnant soul returns to the Ley Lines, and Zibai and Zhongli say he was a rare character who found peace.

Zhongli had tried to tell him before, but he could not let go. Lan Junming says he never wanted eternity, only to bid her farewell. Lan Yan answers that the art they made together now lives across Liyue in every thaumaturge's evil-dispelling art, and sings a farewell. He says Liyue was always like this and wishes them to find their own path.

795.comment: Silverwing in Pursuit of the Moon: Epilogue - Next Year's Moon, Just as Bright
795.content: Ningguang thanks Lan Yan before the Lan elders, saying that an unseen force suppressed the evil spirits across Liyue and let the Millelith finish early and go home for the festival. The elders praise her ability, and she says Hu Tao and Chongyun helped. Lan Yan is rescued from her elders by the Traveler. Zhongli says the swallows seem less frantic. The group goes to the food street. Lan Yan says Moonchase events change yearly but Xiangling and Escoffier will hold a yearly duel at Yilong Wharf, so good food and good friends are guaranteed.

796.comment: Silverwing in Pursuit of the Moon: Food Street Must Be Saved!
796.content: The Wondrous Anecdotes chapter with three quests: The Chefs From a Foreign Land, Deliciousness Knows No Borders and A Taste Beyond Time. The Fontainian chefs Savanna and Escoffier and Liyue's Smiley Yanxiao and Xiangling test each other's cooking until the president of the Chenyu Vale Confectionery Guild demands every stall sell Five-Nut Wangxiao Cakes. The cooks and friends team up to bake a better one, the Celestial Tea Crisp, using Glaze Lily nectar and tea extract. A taste of the authentic Five-Nut cake moves him because it recalls childhood and sharing food with family, but he judges the Celestial Tea Crisp a cut above and the Guild pays for more batches. Zibai, passing by, recalls Fullmoon Cakes she ate thousands of years ago.

797.comment: Silverwing in Pursuit of the Moon: Soul-Binding Art
797.content: A Lan clan technique that traps part of a person's soul in a rattan effigy to create a puppet the caster commands. Later generations banned it. Lan Junming used it on himself to leave a remnant soul able to keep a yearly appointment, adding a seal to bind the technique. The remnant soul slowly fades and can only be released when the art is performed once more.

798.comment: Silverwing in Pursuit of the Moon: Silverwing (Jade-Plumed Silverwing)
798.content: An adeptus born of the energy of heaven and earth whose living manifestations were Liyue's swallows. She carried Lan Junming's wards across the land during the Archon War and kept a yearly promise to meet him at Moonchase. The toll of the journeys wiped away her mind and memory, and the swallows now fly Liyue by instinct. The wiki counts her among the Eight Adepts.

key: Sea of Clouds, Sea of People
799.content:
Sinae Unicornis Chapter (Ganyu) (also: Sinae Unicornis Chapter, Ganyu's Story Quest, Sea of Clouds, Sea of People): The Sinae Unicornis Chapter is Ganyu's Story Quest (Version 1.2), set in Liyue. In its one act, Sea of Clouds, Sea of People, Ganyu, half qilin and half human, doubts whether she belongs in Liyue Harbor as a secretary to the Liyue Qixing or among the adepti. After training with the adepti and helping a colleague investigate tax fraud, she chooses to keep her post.

The act has three quests: The Illuminated Beast of the Sea of Clouds, A Secretary in a Sea of Humanity and A Pact That Crosses Time. It requires Adventure Rank 40 and the Archon Quest A New Star Approaches. The Chinese title means roughly "Chapter of the Immortal Qilin".

The act contrasts two "seas", the sea of clouds at Jueyun Karst and the sea of people in Liyue Harbor, as the places Ganyu feels adrift in. It shows how she is valued by ordinary people for a lifetime of service, and settles her choice without the Traveler deciding for her.

Beyond Ganyu's arc the act has side threads: the Fatui's low reputation in Liyue after Childe's release of Osial, a comic misunderstanding with a berry-picking Fatui skirmisher, and an Uncle Tian whose Qixing rank is a secret kept for his own comfort.

Plot: **The Illuminated Beast of the Sea of Clouds.** At Yujing Terrace the secretaries Baixiao, Baishi and Baiwen ask the Traveler to find Ganyu. She went to deliver a Qixing letter of respect and news to the adepti at Jueyun Karst and has not returned. They are overwhelmed by her workload. The Traveler finds her; Ganyu believes her qilin blood makes her unwelcome in Liyue and, seeing the secretaries doing her tasks, assumes she has been replaced. The Cloud Retainer tries to ease the tension by recounting Ganyu's childhood, which only embarrasses Ganyu into leaving. The Cloud Retainer then explains that she doubts relocating to Jueyun Karst would suit Ganyu's human side, but that Ganyu feels a separation from humans even among them, and has set a trial near Mt. Aocang at Ganyu's request. Ganyu passes it, then meets Xiao at Nantianmen. He is annoyed at her lateness, says her mixed heritage is the source of her inner conflict, and sets a second trial of defending a Ley Line monolith from wildlife. A pilgrim, Xin Cheng, then arrives seeking the adepti's blessing for good fortune. When it is clear that he wants material luck, Ganyu refuses a blessing and says he must make the effort himself. He leaves insulted, and his reaction deepens her doubts. The Traveler persuades her to return to the harbor, and she agrees, saying she will go back to Jueyun if it falls short.

**A Secretary in a Sea of Humanity.** In the harbor they meet Uncle Tian, whom Ganyu reveals is actually the Tianshu of the Qixing; he asks their discretion, enjoying the freedom of an unescorted stroll. He asks Ganyu to help his daughter Huixin, a junior secretary. Huixin has found tax irregularities at two rival shops, Second Life and Wanyou Boutique. Ganyu decides the best approach is to make the rivals expose each other. She tells Bolai of Wanyou Boutique that his shop's credit is not enough for Yuehai Pavilion orders, which angers him into demanding to read his rival Dongsheng's tax report, and he spots an undeclared furniture purchase from Fanmu Carpenters. At Qingce Village the carpenter Master Lu says the invoice is in a warehouse occupied by troublemakers. Ganyu suspects a Fatui Cryogunner Legionnaire in the fields below and attacks him, but he explains he only came to pick berries and that the village is of no interest to the Fatui. She apologises and suggests a complaint to the Ministry of Civil Affairs, but he says it would be ignored, since the Fatui's standing in Liyue is at rock bottom after Childe released Osial. The warehouse troublemakers turn out to be hilichurls. With the invoice, Huixin, Ganyu and the Traveler confront Dongsheng, who confesses; learning that Bolai tipped them off, he exposes Bolai's own misdeeds too. Ganyu tells Huixin that this method of turning opponents on each other was a long-standing tactic of Tian's, and Huixin invites the three to Xinyue Kiosk.

**A Pact That Crosses Time.** Huixin says she has admired Ganyu all her life from her father's stories, and that her own daughter has become a secretary in turn. Because the work is harder than she expected, she asks Ganyu to help her daughter in about twenty years. Ganyu realises that people care about her and that she has been a living witness to Liyue Harbor and its people. She decides to stay with the Qixing, returns to Yujing Terrace to relieve the grateful secretaries, and thanks the Traveler and Paimon for helping her overcome her inner conflict. She hopes to travel with them again, though Paimon points out how swamped she is.

Remarks to keep. The Cloud Retainer expresses worry rather than a demand. Xiao tells Ganyu that only she can measure her own effort, signals a harder training schedule, then leaves her to deal with the pilgrim. Ganyu's handling of the audit (work out motive, exploit rivalry, then confirm with paper evidence) is presented as a working example of her competence as a secretary.

Revelations: Minor: Uncle Tian is the Tianshu of the Liyue Qixing, though few know it. Ganyu feels set apart from both adepti and humans, more strongly than others realise. The Fatui's reputation in Liyue is poor after Childe released Osial.

Characters: Ganyu, the Traveler and Paimon. Baixiao, Baishi, Baiwen, the Cloud Retainer, Xiao, Xin Cheng, Uncle Tian, Huixin, Bolai, Dongsheng, Master Lu and a Fatui skirmisher appear.

Ganyu is dutiful and self-doubting; the secretaries are harried and fond of her; Xiao is brusque but takes her training seriously; Huixin looks up to her; Tian is relaxed and shrewd.

Consequences: Ganyu stays at her post as the Qixing's secretary and deepens her trust in the Traveler. The act also gives a first look at the Cloud Retainer's and Xiao's attitudes toward her.

Placement: Release order: 1.2. Story order: after Chapter I of the Archon Quests (A New Star Approaches).

key: Sea of Clouds Sea of People
Illuminated Beast of the Sea of Clouds
800.comment: Sinae Unicornis Chapter (Ganyu): Sea of Clouds, Sea of People
800.content: Act I of Ganyu's Story Quest. Ganyu doubts whether she belongs among humans or adepti, takes trials from the Cloud Retainer and Xiao, assists Huixin with a tax investigation, and decides to continue working for the Qixing.

801.content: A junior secretary and Uncle Tian's daughter, who has admired Ganyu all her life through her father's stories. In this act she investigates tax irregularities at Second Life and Wanyou Boutique with Ganyu's help, and asks Ganyu to look after her own daughter, also a secretary, in about twenty years.

802.content:
Sol Invictus Chapter (Mavuika) (also: Sol Invictus, As the Blazing Sun, Mavuika's Story Quest): Mavuika's Story Quest, set the day after the war with the Abyss ends. The Wayob warn that the first Pyro Archon, Xbalanque, is returning to Natlan. During the Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame, now reworked as a friendly tournament, Mavuika finds Xbalanque living in the body of a boy named Mausau, duels him in a spirit arena and wins, and declines his offer of life force to meet someone from the Night Kingdom.

The chapter has a single act, As the Blazing Sun, released in Version 5.3 and requiring the Archon Quest act Incandescent Ode of Resurrection. Its quests are After the Peace, A New Pilgrimage and Hearken, Ye Who Have Returned. It is a calm, comic follow-up to the war and shows Mavuika at ease in peacetime with the Traveler and the tribes.

The act is about what a warrior is for once the war is won. Xbalanque, who laid down the rules for the long war, meets the Archon who finished it; Mavuika's refusal of the revival offer says she wants the past kept as memory rather than relived.

Plot: Citlali wakes the Traveler and Paimon the morning after the war and brings them to Mavuika, who says the Wayob in the Night Kingdom have told Citlali that Xbalanque is returning. Mavuika has turned the Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame into a friendly competition and hopes it will draw him out. She and the Traveler visit the tribes, then the tournament runs at the Stadium of the Sacred Flame and Kinich wins it. Mavuika identifies Xbalanque in the crowd inside the body of a boy called Mausau, speaks to him privately, and agrees to a duel in a spirit arena. She wins narrowly. She declines his gift of life force, they ride her Flamestrider together, and at day's end he departs; Mausau wakes remembering a dream.

**After the Peace.** At the Speaker's Chamber, Citlali relays what the Wayob said and Mavuika explains the reworked Pilgrimage. At the People of the Springs, Kinich, Ajaw, Mualani and Kachina have no leads. At the Masters of the Night-Wind, Citlali asks them to check on Ororon, who is setting a trap for Xbalanque with a young qucusaur named Cacucu. Xilonen is asleep to avoid work. At the Flower-Feather Clan, Chasca takes them to Iansan, who is planning the tournament course.

**A New Pilgrimage.** Iansan's course is tested, and a dormant Secret Source Automaton wakes and attacks Mavuika, who defeats it. Mavuika treats the Traveler to a huge meal in the Scions of the Canopy and takes them to the stadium on her Flamestrider. The tournament has several events; Kinich wins and Ajaw alone does not congratulate him. In the crowd Mavuika spots Xbalanque in the body of Mausau, a young boy from the tribes.

**Hearken, Ye Who Have Returned.** Xbalanque, a joker, introduces himself as "Lanque" and explains that the child is asleep in a happy dream and is unharmed. He says he once prayed to the Ruler of Death as a mortal, struck a bargain to share her strength and let Natlan run on new rules, and bet on winning the long war; his visit is the prize. He asks how the war was won and Mavuika summarises it. He wishes to fight her. In a spirit arena of the sun they duel until the flame goes out, and he declares her the winner. He offers his remaining life force to revive someone she misses; she declines. He relays a message from her family and comrades. After riding her Flamestrider across Ochkanatlan and the People of the Springs, he leaves Mausau's body. At a feast with signal flames, Kinich is toasted, and Mausau, awake, says he dreamed of being very strong and decides to train.

Finer points. Xbalanque says the borrowed body had less than a third of his usual strength, and that he failed to reach the final 32 in the tournament. He jokes about the trouble he had after waking, with a fishing line, a trap and a coach who made him double his warm-up. He calls Mavuika the inheritor of his Ancient Name "Kiongozi" (Leader). After he leaves, Mavuika notes she can no longer sense Xbalanque's soul. Mavuika says that the signal flames at night let tribes light a path for those returning. She asks the Traveler to introduce her to the other Archons one day. Afterward the Traveler wonders aloud how she knew what they were going to say, and she answers that the night is young.

Revelations: Xbalanque can return, but only for a single day and only inside a living body. His deal with the Ruler of Death let Natlan follow its own rules for the long war. Mavuika's family, comrades and friends who died are said to still call to her and watch over her from the winds.

Xbalanque tests Mavuika's strength not only of body but also of spirit, and judges that the inheritance of Ancient Names has proven its worth. The scene confirms that Mavuika has chosen not to use the means that could bring a person back briefly.

Characters: Mavuika leads the story; the Traveler and Paimon accompany her. Xbalanque is the visitor. Citlali, Kinich, Ajaw, Mualani, Kachina, Ororon, Xilonen, Chasca and Iansan appear as the heroes of their tribes, and Mausau is the boy whose body Xbalanque borrows.

Iansan organises the tournament; Ajaw keeps mocking Mavuika; Ororon sets a trap for Xbalanque; Xilonen sleeps through the early search. Mausau remembers the experience as a dream.

Consequences: Kinich wins the reworked Pilgrimage. Xbalanque leaves at the end of the day and Mausau resolves to train for the next tournament. Mavuika has again chosen to keep the dead in memory.

Placement: Released in Version 5.3 as a Story Quest. It requires the Archon Quest act Incandescent Ode of Resurrection and Adventure Rank 40, and is set right after the war with the Abyss ends.

803.content: The first Pyro Archon returns for one day in the body of a boy named Mausau, enters the Pilgrimage tournament, and duels Mavuika in a spirit arena. He loses narrowly, offers his remaining life force, and leaves at dusk. Mausau is left unharmed.

804.content: A boy who takes part in the Pilgrimage tournament and, unknown to him, is possessed by Xbalanque. He wakes after the feast remembering a very vivid dream and decides to train for the next Pilgrimage.

805.content: Braziers that Natlan sets up to guide people home at night. Those returning light them themselves, and the light shows the tribe that the person has made it back.

806.comment: Sol Invictus Chapter (Mavuika): As the Blazing Sun Event Window
806.content: The Story Quest event ran from 2025-01-01 to 2025-01-21 with extra rewards for completing the chapter via Story Key. The story remains available afterwards.

key: Song of the Dragon and Freedom
807.comment: Song of the Dragon and Freedom
807.content:
Song of the Dragon and Freedom (also: Prologue Act III, Prologue: Act III, Dvalin purification act): The act opens with the Abyss Order's mage dealt with at the winery, which frees Venti to dispel the barrier over Stormterror's Lair. Inside the lair, an old structure from Decarabian's Mondstadt, the group activates a light mechanism that Venti imbues with Anemo energy, and the Traveler purges Dvalin of the corrupting energy. Dvalin asks why Venti never asked for his protection, and flies away reassured. Jean explains the misunderstanding to the people.

Meanwhile hilichurls and Abyss infiltrators attack the city; Amber and the Knights hold, and Kaeya intercepts infiltrators. After Barbara receives the Holy Lyre der Himmel, a Fatui ambush freezes Venti and takes the Anemo Gnosis from him: Signora, the Eighth Harbinger, tears it out of his chest. Venti then explains the Gnosis, Signora's rank and the Tsaritsa, and advises the Traveler to meet the Geo Archon in Liyue at the Rite of Descension.

Thematically the act is about freedom: Venti declined to command Dvalin because obedience given on an order would not be freedom. The cost to Venti is high, since the Fatui exploit the quiet moment after the victory to take the Gnosis.

Plot: **Preparation.** With the Abyss mage killed at the winery, Venti can dispel the barrier over Stormterror's Lair, and he and the Traveler go in to cleanse Dvalin.

**Dvalin purified.** The Traveler catches up with Dvalin and purges the corrupt energy. Dvalin protects the group and asks Venti why he did not ask for protection. Venti says he did not want him to obey the Abyss Order, nor to obey Venti either; an order to be free would not be true freedom. Dvalin leaves, assured that no one is after him. Jean tells the people that the dragon had not attacked for no reason.

**The city.** The Knights repel a hilichurl attack on Mondstadt while Kaeya intercepts Abyss Order infiltrators; Amber wishes the Traveler luck on their journey to meet the Seven.

**The Gnosis.** At the Cathedral Jean introduces the deaconess Barbara, who asks for the lyre. The Traveler hands over a damaged one and Barbara panics; Venti repairs it and Barbara leaves with it. Venti says he only used magic to make it appear fixed and runs off. Outside a cold gust freezes Venti and Paimon. Fatui Agents restrain the Traveler; Signora and two Fatui Cicin Mages arrive, and Signora, after trading insults with Venti, rips out his Gnosis and leaves before the Knights arrive. An agent strikes the Traveler unconscious.

**Aftermath.** Barbara finds them but her healing does not help Venti, who leaves. Jean guesses his purpose; the Traveler stays silent for her sake. They find Venti at the great tree in Windrise, where he explains the Gnosis, Signora as the eighth of the Eleven Fatui Harbingers, and the Tsaritsa, the Archon of Snezhnaya who is also one of the Seven. He says the Seven used to respect each other but a catastrophe five hundred years ago broke the relationship, and advises heading to Liyue to see the Geo Archon at the Rite of Descension.

Fuller account of two stretches. **Preparation.** Diluc brings word of the Abyss Order, having killed one of its operatives before. Venti admits he is the weakest of the Seven because of long absences and so depends on Mondstadt's people. Diluc's men track the Abyss mage to the winery; it dies and dissipates the energy that had cut Venti off from Dvalin. Venti learns the nature of the barrier on the ruins and says he can dispel it. Jean thinks they may have to kill Dvalin; Venti insists the plan to cleanse him still works because the Traveler can purify the Teardrop Crystal. **The lair.** At Stormterror's Lair hilichurls, manipulated by the Abyss Order, attack and are repelled. Venti dispels the barrier. The ruins turn out to be part of old Mondstadt from the time of the tyrant Decarabian; Venti refuses to say more. The group activates a light actuator, and Venti infuses it with Anemo energy. **The city.** Amber reports that during the fight she and other Knights repelled a coordinated hilichurl attack. She is annoyed at Kaeya's absence, but at the Good Hunter tavern Kaeya says he suspected the attack and stayed to intercept Abyss Order infiltrators; he learned from them that the Order has a single leader. Amber asks the Traveler's plans; Paimon says they will travel Teyvat to meet the Seven, and Amber wishes them well. She reminds them Jean wants them at the Cathedral about the lyre.

The wiki lists the act's quests as Abyss Mage, Hurdle, Empty Abode, Light Guiding Ceremony, Calm Before the Storm, A Long Shot, When the Wind Dies Down and Ending Note. It requires Adventure Rank 18 and awards 200 Mondstadt reputation.

Small details: Jean and Venti note that hilichurls tend to avoid elemental areas, and Diluc says the Abyss Order is manipulating the hilichurls at the lair only to stall the party. Venti says outright that his power has waned from his absences. The Traveler is struck by an agent only after Signora orders her subordinates to flee before the Knights arrive. Venti later tells the Traveler he wants them to move quickly, since the Geo Archon descends only once a year.

Revelations: - The ruins that Dvalin took refuge in are part of old Mondstadt from Decarabian's time.
- Dvalin was cleansed of the Abyss Order's corruption and was not to blame for the attacks on the city. He wanted to know why Venti never asked him for help.
- The Anemo Gnosis was taken from Venti by Signora, the Eighth of the Eleven Fatui Harbingers.
- Venti reluctantly explains what the Gnosis is, and Paimon realises that the Tsaritsa of Snezhnaya, who gave the Harbingers their power, is one of the Seven.
- Kaeya learns that the Abyss Order has a single leader.

The sibling's relationship to the Abyss Order is not explained here. The seeds of the Fatui-Seven conflict and the cataclysm five hundred years ago are only named, not explained, and are pursued in later chapters.

Characters: Traveler and Paimon; Venti (the Anemo Archon, Barbatos, who has by now revealed his identity); Dvalin, cleansed of the corruption; Jean (Acting Grand Master); Diluc (brings word of the Abyss Order; his people track the Abyss mage); Amber and Kaeya (the defence of the city, the tavern conversation); Barbara (receives the lyre); Signora (antagonist) with two Fatui Cicin Mages and Fatui Agents.

Consequences: Dvalin is free of the Abyss Order's influence and the dragon crisis ends. Venti loses the Anemo Gnosis to the Fatui, and the Traveler is set on the road to Liyue to meet the Geo Archon at the Rite of Descension, leading directly into Chapter I.

Jean clears up the people's misunderstanding about Dvalin. When Venti walks away after the attack, Jean appears to understand his intentions, and the Traveler keeps quiet for her sake.

Placement: Third and last act of the Prologue (release 1.0). It follows For a Tomorrow Without Tears and leads into Chapter I Act I, Of the Land Amidst Monoliths, set in Liyue.

808.comment: Song of the Dragon and Freedom: Signora takes the Anemo Gnosis
808.content: After the Dvalin episode Signora, the Eighth Fatui Harbinger, ambushes Venti outside the Favonius Cathedral with Fatui Agents and Cicin Mages. A freezing wind immobilises Venti and Paimon; she insults him, then pushes her arm into his chest and removes his Gnosis. The Traveler is struck unconscious. Barbara later finds them, but Venti walks away.

809.comment: Song of the Dragon and Freedom: Dvalin purified
809.content: In the lair, the Traveler purges the Abyss-Order corruption from Dvalin, who asks Venti why he never requested his protection. Venti answers that commanded freedom would not be freedom. Dvalin flies off, and Jean explains to Mondstadt that the dragon had been misunderstood.

810.comment: Song of the Dragon and Freedom: Kaeya on the Abyss Order's leader
810.content: While others fight at the ruins, Kaeya stays in the city to counter a suspected diversion and intercepts Abyss Order infiltrators. He learns that the Order has one leader. Amber thinks he abandoned duty for a drink.

811.content:
Song of the Welkin Moon (also: Welkin Moon chapter, Song of the Empty Moon, Nod-Krai Archon Quest, Luna Archon Quest): The chapter runs from a prelude in Natlan (version 5.8) through ten acts (6.0-6.6). It follows the Traveler's search for clues about their spaceship while Nod-Krai is threatened by the Wild Hunt, by Rerir, and by Fatui who have moved in under Dottore and Sandrone. Columbina, the weakened Moon Goddess, is the emotional centre: friends restore her strength and her name, and she in turn helps them. Dottore then steals the power of the three moons and attacks Nod-Krai and, ultimately, Sumeru's Irminsul, with Sandrone's death and Dottore's end as the cost. It was never officially called Chapter VI.

The chapter links the Traveler's own origin to Nod-Krai, since their spaceship crashed there, and ties Nod-Krai's moons, the Hyperborean past and the Khaenri'ahn Cataclysm together. Its closing acts shift to Sumeru and the fate of Irminsul.

Plot: **Prelude: The Journey Home (5.8).** In Natlan the Traveler and Paimon find Ineffa, an automaton looking for them, and learn of a message from Varka telling them to come to Nod-Krai.

**Acts I-II (6.0).** In Nasha Town they meet Flins, Lauma, Aino and Nefer. A Moon Marrow ends up carried by the Traveler, and a shape-shifting phantom linked to the Wild Hunt is traced to Rerir.

**Acts III-IV (6.1).** Rerir, one of the Five Sinners of Khaenri'ah, attacks Columbina. Allies recover the Iridescent Marrow with Arlecchino's help, delve into Rerir's past, and cast him out of Teyvat.

**Acts V-VI (6.2).** Columbina is fading; she is given a name, enjoys Moon-Prayer Night and is lost after Dottore's ambush (Act VI has its own entity).

**Acts VII-VIII (6.3).** Dottore captures the Traveler; Columbina recovers help in the moon's reflection and returns to defeat him; Sandrone dies.

**Acts IX-X (6.6).** In Sumeru, Nahida and her allies stop an Irminsul crisis traced to Dottore.

Fuller account of each stage, condensed from the wiki summaries.

**Prelude.** Ineffa washes ashore in Natlan, carrying a cryptex for the Traveler. With Chasca, Ifa and Xilonen the Traveler learns her core comes from Natlan's Secret Source while the rest is not Natlan-made; memories of her past flicker, and an entity in her mind calls her a traitor for daring to seek a place to belong. In a Secret Source facility she learns she is the benevolent half split from the Eleventh Lord, one of the Thirteen Sovereign Lords; fighting the Lord's hostile self, she builds a new core and gains an Electro power that the Eleventh Lord recognises as a Moon Wheel. The cryptex holds Varka's letter asking the Traveler to meet him at a tavern called the Flagship.

**Act I.** Ineffa leaves Natlan with the Traveler and Paimon. In Nasha Town the Traveler feels kuuvahki, the moons' primordial power, and recognises it as like the power they felt on landing, suggesting their spaceship is nearby. They meet Aino, Flins, Lauma of the Frostmoon Scions, and Marionette, a Harbinger, who warns them off Fatui business. After a Wild Hunt attack, Lauma's Moon Marrow is stored in the Traveler's body; she tells the tribe the truth about their faith and some members leave.

**Act II.** With Nefer, Jahoda and Aino the Traveler pursues a phantom that can impersonate others. Columbina recalls a man titled the "Rächer of Solnari", from which the Traveler and Paimon identify the enemy as Rerir, one of the Five Sinners; Columbina had been told he fell into the moon's reflection. Flins is accused of killing the Ratnik Sousi, but the "Sousi" seen earlier had been Rerir in disguise.

**Act III.** Rerir attacks Columbina, who is hurt shielding Jahoda, and the Wild Hunt hunts them. Varka rescues the group and Nefer is hired. Columbina and the Traveler go to the Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau, where Rerir later disables Sandrone's automaton Pulonia. Arlecchino, present only in a personal capacity as Columbina's friend, opens a portal to a domain where they take the Iridescent Marrow; her hands are corrupted by the Abyss in forcing the way out.

**Act IV.** Albedo, a young Durin and Dainsleif join the group. Rerir's past emerges: a Khaenri'ahn under King Irmin who was engaged to Tholindis and was ordered to eliminate his own fiancee. In the battle that follows, Albedo and Durin siphon Rerir's power into Columbina, and Columbina flicks Rerir through a moon gate held open by Dainsleif, throwing him out of Teyvat. Sandrone mentions the Lord-Artificer, Alain Guillotin.

**Act V.** About two months after arrival, Moon-Prayer Night approaches. Columbina plans to return to the moon but is fading because the world rejects a being with no accepted name; Alice says her true name must be found, and Nicole explains the rejection and how to open the Hyperborean ruins. Phantoms from Hyperborea appear across Nod-Krai and the ruins' gate opens, but Columbina is too weak to follow.

**Act VI.** See quest.melting-moonlight-in-the-morning-mist.

**Act VII.** A few days after the ambush, a Fatuus passes on word that Arlecchino and Sandrone are going to Dottore's far-north facility. There Dottore, using an artificial Moon Marrow, overpowers the group, captures the Traveler and curses the others so that leaving Nod-Krai would trigger it. Dottore replaces the Frost Moon in the sky with an artificial one and Nod-Krai begins evacuating. Holding the Traveler, Dottore accidentally leaves them frozen for over a month and offers to restore their status as a Descender. In the moon's reflection, Columbina re-enters the past and creates Luonnotar to help.

**Act VIII.** Wanderer rescues the Traveler. Columbina meets the three Moon Sisters, who lend her their authorities and then face the end in their own time. Sandrone's world-formula, run partly through Wanderer's core, brings Columbina back. Dottore becomes the "Heretic of the False Moon". Sandrone dies saving the Traveler. Columbina arrives as the Trilune Goddess and, with the Traveler and friends, destroys his artificial Moon Marrow and Dottore. Afterwards a new League of Nod-Krai's factions is formed, and Columbina takes the Traveler to their spaceship on the Frost Moon and gives them a gift: the lifting of some of Teyvat's restrictions on how they use the elements.

**Act IX.** Collei's letter and Nicole's premonition warn Sumeru that identities will be switched. Irminsul stops recording and processing properly; Nahida takes over the load and collapses. Sumeru City is evacuated to Caravan Ribat and civilians later moved on to Aaru Village, while scholars search the Temple of Silence; the Seven Pillars of King Deshret agree to open Aaru.

**Act X.** Nahida plans to overload Irminsul with the Akasha System. She obtains Mavuika's Pyro Gnosis through the Traveler. Dottore, working inside a new Irminsul tree, is helped by Pantalone. Nahida uses the Gnosis to burn the corrupted tree; Dottore's remaining Segments drag him into the flames and he dies, naming Pantalone as Feofan. Aaru takes over Irminsul's recording role, the Pyro Gnosis disappears, and Collei has the god remains removed by Liloupar.

Details worth keeping separate: the two Moon Marrows Dottore stole from Columbina before building his artificial Moon Marrow; the Thirteen Sovereign Lords are artificial intelligences built from Secret Source technology, as Citlali says in the prelude; Flins reveals he is 600-700 years old and lived through the Cataclysm in Nod-Krai; Pulcinella's letter to Nahida apologises for Dottore's actions; and the wiki's Act X summary treats Dottore's death as final.

Revelations: - Nod-Krai is soaked in kuuvahki, the primordial power of the moons, and the Traveler's spaceship crashed there.
- The Moon Goddess is Columbina; Rerir is a Khaenri'ahn who served King Irmin and was sent out of Teyvat in Act IV.
- Dottore built an artificial Moon Marrow and a false moon and was destroyed in Act VIII; his larger experiment moved to Sumeru's Irminsul.
- The Heavenly Principles placed the Traveler's spaceship on the Frost Moon.

The Moon Sisters (Aria, Canon and Sonnet) were imprisoned by Nibelung and lend their authorities to Columbina. Irminsul is destroyed by Nahida using the Pyro Gnosis in Act X, ending the corruption but leaving Aaru as the new recording system.

Details that matter for later portrayals: Dottore knew Wanderer's erased identity as Scaramouche and said so in Act X; Pulcinella's letter says Dottore killed Sandrone; Nicole is treated as an angel whose identity is kept quiet, and she reveals that the god remains in Collei come from Nabu Malikata.

Characters: Traveler and Paimon; Columbina (the Moon Goddess); Lauma and the Frostmoon Scions; Ineffa and Aino; Flins; Nefer and Jahoda of the Curatorium; Varka (Mondstadt's Grand Master and Knight of Boreas); Sandrone and Arlecchino of the Fatui; Rerir (antagonist); Dottore (antagonist); Dainsleif, Albedo and Durin; Nicole and Alice of the Hexenzirkel; Wanderer, Nahida and the Sumeru allies in Acts IX-X.

Consequences: The Frost Moon is back in Teyvat's sky, Columbina lives on Hiisi Island, Nod-Krai forms a joint League, and Dottore and Sandrone are dead. Sumeru keeps functioning under Aaru; Irminsul has been burned, and the Pyro Gnosis has gone.

Nicole warns that the disaster has made Teyvat easier for the Abyss to detect. The expedition from Mondstadt starts returning home in waves, and Varka writes to Jean about the Fatui's disunity.

Placement: Released as a prelude in 5.8 and Acts I-X across Luna I-VII (6.0-6.6), the chapter follows Chapter V (Natlan) and precedes Chapter VII (Snezhnaya), which opens in 7.0. Story order matches release order.

The chapter's version labels are Luna I (6.0) for Acts I-II, Luna II (6.1) for III-IV, Luna III (6.2) for V-VI, Luna IV (6.3) for VII-VIII, and Luna VII (6.6) for IX-X.

812.comment: Song of the Welkin Moon: Rerir
812.content: A Khaenri'ahn, one of the Five Sinners, who served King Irmin and was once engaged to Tholindis. He attacks Columbina and the Moon Marrows in Acts III-IV, is cast out of Teyvat through a moon gate in Act IV, and is later met in the moon's reflection.

813.comment: Song of the Welkin Moon: Dottore's false moon
813.content: Dottore ambushes Columbina's return to the moon, steals the power of the three moons, replaces the Frost Moon in the sky with a false one, and is destroyed by Columbina and the Traveler in Act VIII.

814.comment: Song of the Welkin Moon: Columbina restored
814.content: Columbina, the weakened Moon Goddess, lives at Silvermoon Hall and is saved by friends who give her a name, a festival farewell and, in Act VIII, the return of her full power. Afterwards she lives with the Frostmoon Scions on Hiisi Island.

815.comment: Song of the Welkin Moon: Sumeru Irminsul crisis
815.content: Dottore's experiment corrupts Irminsul. Nahida takes the strain, Sumeru City is evacuated, and the Seven Pillars help open Aaru as a replacement. The Pyro Gnosis burns the corrupted Irminsul.

key: The Shining Warriors Take the Stage
816.content:
Soulblazers' Snowbound Journey (also: Dragonspine International Cross Country Challenge, The Shining Warriors Take the Stage, Now's No Time for Tears, Go, Fietena, Go!): The story has three parts. In The Shining Warriors Take the Stage, the Traveler and Paimon reach the Dragonspine camp, meet Amber and Heinz of the organizing committee, and discover that Varesa and Xilonen are competing with Alrani, Tang Yigang and Minnie as the Soulblazers. In Now's No Time for Tears, the Traveler is initiated into the Legion, trains with the team, and helps convince Minnie's parents to let her race. In Go, Fietena, Go!, Yigang falls ill, the Traveler runs in his place, and Minnie leaves the race to help an injured rival.

The event is a light, warm story about fandom, mutual encouragement, and the gap between a young person's ambitions and their parents' worries for her health. It carries almost no wider lore beyond the comic series and its link to Natlan's history.

Plot: Part I, The Shining Warriors Take the Stage. The Traveler reads the letter from the Dragonspine International Cross Country Challenge Organizing Committee and goes to Dragonspine. Amber and Heinz (Field Officer, 1st Company, Knights of Favonius) give them VIP tickets; Amber asks them to borrow a Soulblazer comic for her. At the Natlan-Sumeru camp, Alrani and Tang Yigang quote The Soulblazer Saga in ceremonial tones and are disappointed that Paimon is not moved. Xilonen translates: Legion of Soulblazers means comic-book fan club. She is vice captain on Varesa's team, standing in for Nepecha, who loves the series but cannot take part in extreme sports; she also wants merchandise for Nepecha. Varesa and Minnie are training; Varesa says she and Minnie had only written letters and traded illustrations before meeting in person. Minnie wants to see more of the world but is unsure she is tough enough, and mentions a deal with her parents: train hard and get a good race time.

Part II, Now's No Time for Tears. The morning after, Varesa has finished the comics and explains the series is a 12-volume adaptation of Natlan's history with a focus on the heroine Fietena. She then holds an initiation ceremony using a Fietena mask she made, and the Traveler and Paimon join the Legion; the creed is shouted aloud. Xilonen insists on rehearsing the relay stages, so the Traveler runs the course with either Varesa or Xilonen and Minnie while monsters near the track are cleared. Minnie explains her situation: her parents oppose her wish to move abroad as an assistant comic artist or prop maker. She is the youngest in her family, was a sickly child, and her parents want a stable career. The team spends the afternoon at the Mondstadt Library, where Lisa checks out books, then lunches at Good Hunter. Minnie confides that she keeps quitting and returning to art. Her brother Patton and then her parents Sherilyn and Moritz arrive; Moritz says this race will be her last. Xilonen steps in: she tells the parents that her student Nepecha and many others admire Minnie's art and presents a group painting. She compares art to a bard's career, and Varesa assures them Minnie is sturdier than they think.

Part III, Go, Fietena, Go! The next morning Yigang has a fever and is bedridden under a medic's care. Xilonen asks the Traveler to run in his place. The referee Draff opens the race; the teams include The Sand Blasters, Lightning Strike, The Sunset Squadron, The Frostbite Friends, Dragonspine Must Be Scaled, The Mild Hunt and the Soulblazers. The order is Xilonen, the Traveler, Varesa and then Minnie. The Soulblazers fall behind early, but near the end Minnie sees an exhausted Inazuman runner, Kenzou of Lightning Strike, in trouble, and takes him to the finish line, by which point the other teams have finished. The organizing committee, in agreement with Kenzou's team, says the Soulblazers would have ranked much higher and awards a special honorary medal for putting lives first. Moritz and Sherilyn then keep their deal.

Details. The course features a Statue of The Seven at the baton hand-off between the Traveler and Varesa. The final stretch includes a fight against a Frostarm Lawachurl and Cryo Hilichurl Shooters, with a trial party that includes Amber. The comics mentioned include Soulblazer 6: Shadow of Tenebrium and a standalone special, Fietena VS Abyss Lector: Battle of the Meat Feasters. Moritz proposes making the trip abroad a family visit to the Yae Publishing House. Alrani leads a group photo posed like Fietena and Mavuika in volume 2, and the Soulblazers promise to return for the next challenge. Five Snowrealm Visitors side quests (from the Yae Publishing House, the Spark Knight and others) are accessed from the world.

Revelations: The Soulblazer Saga is a 12-volume comic series published by the Yae Publishing House. According to Varesa it is an entertainment adaptation of Natlan's history in which Fietena and a group of fellow warriors fight the Abyss. Fan communities of the series span Mondstadt, Natlan and Sumeru through letters and pen friends. Minnie's parents' objections come from worry about her health and her future; they relent once she meets the deal.

Xilonen says she is related to Nepecha and has known her only a short time. Minnie's brother Patton works at the tavern and had heard of the Traveler's exploits.

Characters: Main: the Traveler, Paimon, Varesa, Xilonen, Minnie, Alrani, Tang Yigang. Also: Amber, Heinz, Lisa, Draff (the referee), Sara, and Minnie's family (Patton, Sherilyn and Moritz); the Inazuman contestant Kenzou; Fietena, Mavuika and others appear only in the comic sequence.

Minnie is a young person and a determined runner; she has artistic and prop-making talent. Varesa and Xilonen are competing as captain and vice captain of the Soulblazers team.

Consequences: Minnie's family allows her to travel abroad on the condition that she is careful. The Soulblazers earn an honorary medal. The event ends with plans to return for the next cross country challenge; Alrani also brings Amber a copy of a Soulblazer comic.

Players who reached 200 Blazing Spirit received the bow Rainbow Serpent's Rain Bow; the final tier added a Crown of Insight and a Soulblazer: Fietena item.

Placement: Released in Version 6.2 ("A Nocturne of the Far North"), 19 December 2025 to 5 January 2026. Entry requires Prologue Act III, Song of the Dragon and Freedom; the Tribal Chronicles A Prayer for Blessings, Told to Crested Peaks and Mushroom Realm Mystery are recommended. It takes place in Mondstadt and Dragonspine and does not affect main-story canon.

Gameplay: Game mechanics, not in-world fact. Four minigames: Snowtrace (a hide-and-seek mode with Snowstorm and Cold mechanics), Frontier Recon (piloting the Saury-Saury Scout), Jade Pitching (throwing snowballs at snowman targets) and Trial of Valor (choosing Battle Souls in combat). Challenges earned Blazing Spirit.

817.comment: Soulblazers' Snowbound Journey: Legion of Soulblazers
817.content:
A fan club for the comic The Soulblazer Saga. Alrani and Tang Yigang use dramatic tenets drawn from the series; Varesa says its real purpose is to share life's joys and get rid of life's woes. The members in this event are Alrani, Tang Yigang, Minnie, Varesa, and Xilonen as stand-in for Nepecha; the Traveler and Paimon are inducted in Part II.
