Alrani is an aspiring herbad of the Akademiya struggling with a thesis. Tang Yigang collects Soulblazer books and mecha action figures from the Yae Publishing House. Varesa leads the group as captain.

818.comment: Soulblazers' Snowbound Journey: The Soulblazer Saga
818.content: A long-running comic series with 12 volumes in the main series and spinoffs, including an armoured-mecha spinoff, Armored Assault. The central heroine is Fietena, a warrior who becomes a commander and who fights alongside friends; the Pyro Archon also appears in it. Varesa says it adapts Natlan history for entertainment.

819.comment: Soulblazers' Snowbound Journey: Dragonspine International Cross Country Challenge
819.content: A relay race on Dragonspine. Teams include The Sand Blasters, Lightning Strike, The Sunset Squadron, The Frostbite Friends, Dragonspine Must Be Scaled, The Mild Hunt and the Soulblazers, run by an organizing committee that includes Amber and Heinz of the Knights of Favonius. Draff is the referee.

820.content: Minnie, the youngest in her family and a sickly child, promised her parents that if her team is ranked in the race they must take her ambition of working with comics seriously. The parents are loving but anxious; Xilonen persuades them with a group painting from Nepecha's fans. Minnie stops mid-race to help an injured runner, and her father says she achieved what she set out to do, so the parents honour the deal.

key: Liyue Celebrates and Eight Adepts Face a Hidden Calamity
821.content:
Springtime Charms (also: Springtime Charms event, Swirling Butterflies, Lantern Rite 2025, Liyue Celebrates and Eight Adepts Face a Hidden Calamity, Sanctification of Tao Dou): Alongside the story the event offered four festival activities (Immortal Combat, Drills by Lamplight, Custom Gift Envelopes and Festive Travel Journal) whose Festive Fever points unlocked Xiangling's outfit "New Year's Cheer" and a choice of 4-star Liyue character. The narrative runs in four "stanzas" under the heading Swirling Butterflies. It ends warmly: Hu Tao lives, the fetor is contained, Yun Jin performs the rite as a stage piece, and the adepti gather over tea to talk about Hu Tao.

The event places Hu Tao, Lan Yan, Xiao, Ningguang and Yelan at the centre, shows how Hu Tao's family history shapes her work as funeral director, and makes the Traveler's inability to be linked to the ley lines plot-relevant.

Plot: First Stanza, Liyue Celebrates and Eight Adepts Face a Hidden Calamity: at Wangsheng Funeral Parlor Hu Tao (in a new outfit from Xiangling) says only that she is busy. The Traveler meets Lan Yan, a young woman from Chenyu Vale, and hears the legend of Tao Dou, a tree god of the Archon War. Several people who visited Qingce Village collapse, including Timaeus and the patriarch of the Feiyun Commerce Guild, and Baizhu suspects one cause for all of them.

Second Stanza, The Funeral Parlor Has No Master, Yujing Terrace Calls the Troops: Hu Tao has not returned and Qiqi is missing after gathering herbs, with Wuwang Hill the lead. With Xiao's help the Traveler breaks into the "border" and finds Hu Tao, Lan Yan and Qiqi. Back in Yujing Terrace it is revealed that Hu Tao and Ningguang plan a Sanctification of Tao Dou to purge the fetor.

Third Stanza, Qimen Arts and the Rite of Homa, the Spirits are Calmed and Life Restored: friends take positions at the gates of the array (Terrain at Dihua Marsh, Repose at Qingce Village, Initiation at Liyue Harbor, Death at Wuwang Hill, plus the Gate of Injury in the Chasm). Hu Tao herself must be the obscured person at the centre of the rite. The Traveler cannot be linked to the ley lines, goes after Hu Tao anyway, finds the Gate of Death and pulls her out of the border.

Final Stanza, The Sanctification of Tao Dou: with the crisis contained, Yun Jin performs the rite as a stage piece at Yilong Wharf, and short epilogue scenes follow.

First Stanza detail: Hu Tao had been meeting An Su, a butler of the Feiyun Commerce Guild, and then slipped out; she asks the Ferrylady to follow up the funeral arrangements. An Su fears Lan Yan has cursed the patriarch because he saw her with a rattan figure like the one he later found in the patriarch's room. Chongyun, brought by Xingqiu as an exorcist, feels a cold presence but no malice and suspects a "fetor of death." Baizhu finds Timaeus and the patriarch afflicted alike, links the cases to Qingce Village and says he had sent Qiqi to gather herbs there. Lan Yan leaves a rattan doll behind in her rush after Hu Tao. Zhongli reads the Guyan Sigil on the doll as an upstanding, auspicious sign and gives the Traveler a Rex Lapis fortune coin, which he says is only a replica from a vendor.

Second Stanza detail: Gaming mentions delivering funeral goods to the Feiyun home at Yilong Wharf. At Wuwang Hill Yelan warns the pair away, shows them Qiqi's herb basket and takes them to Yiyan Temple, where Ningguang and Beidou are talking. Xiao is reluctant to involve the Traveler but relents, destroys the fetor and temporarily shares his senses. Inside the border the Traveler breaks Lan Yan's protective illusion, Hu Tao keeps the fetor-laden Qiqi awake by startling her, and Xiao leads everyone out and takes Qiqi to Bubu Pharmacy. Ningguang explains that the Qixing have found four of eight gates. Hu Tao tells the Traveler, at the parlor, that about a dozen years ago a border incident at Wuwang Hill killed her father when he slipped while using the Art of Homa and that her grandfather, who dealt with the aftermath, did not live to sixty. She shows a photograph of them. Lan Yan separately explains that her own grandfather's fortune-telling, disturbed by the fetor, pointed to the funeral parlor.

Third Stanza detail: Lan Yan's cousin in the main family branch finds no definitive answer on why the central person must be obscured, but suspects a rule of the mountains and land. Her workaround is rattan Hu Tao figures linked to the ley lines, held by those who know the truth, in the hope that the fetor blast aimed at Hu Tao is spread among them. Hu Tao brings the Traveler along to hand out fortune coins, quietly gives the coin to Zhongli to return, and tells him that if she fails to come back he would be the 78th Director; he declines. When the rite runs, the figures are overwhelmed, Hu Tao completes it and her doll darkens. In the border she reaches a copy of the parlor where her father and grandfather greet her but say her time has not come; a plum branch falls into her hand before the Traveler pulls her out. The Traveler wakes two days later at Bubu Pharmacy; Hu Tao thanks them for saving her life.

Final Stanza detail: Xiao tells Yelan he should have taken the assignment, and she replies that she was posted at the Chasm and would have been a liability. Beidou and Ningguang talk at Yiyan Temple. Keqing tells Ganyu that Xianyun and the other adepti most likely left the anonymous information the Qixing used. At Mt. Aocang, Cloud Retainer, Zhongli and other adepti gather for tea and talk about Hu Tao.

Gameplay: Immortal Combat (rattan figures duelling with falling blocks), Drills by Lamplight (a team drill using Secret Stratagems), Custom Gift Envelopes (filling envelopes to companions' wishes, tied to seven world quests numbered 1 to 7) and Festive Travel Journal (visiting festive toy sites around Liyue Harbor). Festive Fever thresholds were 300, 600, 900, 1,200 (invite a character in Lantern-Lit Gathering) and 1,500 (Xiangling's outfit and a Crown of Insight). Selectable characters were Beidou, Chongyun, Gaming, Lan Yan, Ningguang, Xiangling, Xingqiu, Xinyan, Yanfei, Yaoyao and Yun Jin. The outfit was later sold in the outfit shop. These are game mechanics, not in-universe canon.

Revelations: The fetor sickening Liyue is connected to the earlier Wuwang Hill disaster, in which Hu Tao's father died using the Art of Homa. The Sanctification of Tao Dou is traditionally believed to require a death, because the Lone Butterfly sacrificed herself in the original rite; Hu Tao argues a scaled-down version only needs the central person to withstand a huge blast of fetor. The Traveler is invisible to the ley lines, which is why the Traveler cannot be the obscured one. No Abyss involvement is sensed.

Hu Tao concealed the connection to Wuwang Hill from Ningguang and the Qixing, and Lan Yan suspected her of keeping the truth bottled up. Hu Tao expected she might die and said so to Zhongli.

Characters: Hu Tao is the focus, shown at her most serious beneath her jokes. Lan Yan, a Chenyu Vale rattan-figure maker, is introduced here. Ningguang and Keqing coordinate the Qixing side; Baizhu and Qiqi handle the sick; Xiao and Yelan guard borders and gates; Zhongli quietly supports Hu Tao and the Traveler. Xiangling, Xingqiu, Chongyun, Gaming, Yun Jin, Ganyu, Xianyun and Beidou have smaller roles.

Consequences: Hu Tao survives, the fetor is contained and the sick recover. Ningguang's worry that a greater power may be behind the fetor is left open. Hu Tao's friends see how heavily her family history weighs on her.

Placement: Released in Version 5.3 for the 2025 Lantern Rite. Requirements: Adventure Rank 20 and the Prologue Act III. Recommended first: the Archon Quest Incandescent Ode of Resurrection and the Story Quests Lagenaria Chapter Act I (Baizhu) and Papilio Charontis Chapter Act I (Hu Tao). Because the event runs in Liyue Harbor, its quests can interfere with those Story Quests' character appearances.

822.comment: Springtime Charms: Sanctification of Tao Dou
822.content: In Springtime Charms the Sanctification of Tao Dou is a rite to purge fetor, built on a Seven-and-Eight-Gates Array. The array master picks one of eight gates to subdue the evil by using the ley lines to obfuscate themselves, removing themselves from the lines and carrying the evil with them. The traditional reading is that the person dies, because the Lone Butterfly sacrificed herself; Hu Tao leads a scaled-down version in which she must withstand a huge blast of fetor.

823.content: Lan Yan is a young woman from Chenyu Vale who makes rattan figures. In Springtime Charms her grandfather's divination was disturbed by the fetor, and she seeks out Hu Tao. With help from a cousin in the main family branch she links Hu Tao's rattan dolls to the ley lines.

key: In the Name of the Resistance
824.content:
Stillness, the Sublimation of Shadow (also: Chapter II Act II, Amidst Stormy Judgment, In the Name of the Resistance): Stillness, the Sublimation of Shadow is the second act of Chapter II of the Archon Quests, set in Inazuma and released in Version 2.0. It has only two quests. In the first, the Traveler tries to save Thoma from becoming the hundredth person stripped of a Vision under the Vision Hunt Decree, and is crushed in a duel by the Raiden Shogun. In the second, the Traveler and Paimon, now wanted criminals, find the Watatsumi Army's Resistance, help defend it from the Shogun's Army under Kujou Sara, and are invited to Watatsumi Island by Sangonomiya Kokomi.

The act is where the Traveler becomes Inazuma's most wanted criminal and a participant in the war rather than a visitor. It requires two Story Quest openers, one from the Grus Nivis Chapter and one from the Carassius Auratus Chapter, and by number of quests it is the shortest Archon Quest act in the game.

Plot: **Amidst Stormy Judgment.** The Traveler and Paimon return to Komore Teahouse to hear about their next operation from Kamisato Ayaka and Thoma, but Thoma is missing. Ayaka arrives with news that the Tenryou Commission has taken him to the Statue of the Omnipresent God as the hundredth victim of the Vision Hunt Decree, to be marked with a public ceremony attended by the Raiden Shogun. Ayaka is ready to storm in alone, but the Traveler and Paimon point out that any direct action by her would endanger the Yashiro Commission's neutrality, and persuade her to let them go instead.

At the ceremony the Shogun sees the Traveler use Electro power without a Vision. She calls the Traveler an exception and the enemy of eternity, then draws them into an alternate dimension and easily incapacitates them. Thoma distracts her at the critical moment and escapes with the Traveler and Paimon. The Shogun orders the Traveler's arrest and says she will strike twice next time.

**In the Name of the Resistance.** Thoma sends the pair west to the Watatsumi Army, which leads the resistance against the Decree, while he hides at Komore Teahouse inside Yashiro Commission territory. The Resistance's location is secret, so the Traveler has to find it. On the way through the war zone they save a lone soldier, Teppei, from Shogunate troops. He takes them to General Gorou, warning that the Resistance is at a disadvantage because the Shogun's Army has Kujou Sara's leadership. Gorou, impressed by what the Traveler did at the ceremony, welcomes them.

Teppei shows the Traveler around the camp and the Traveler helps some soldiers. A sudden attack by the Shogun's Army makes Teppei suspect a traitor in the camp, but he is persuaded to use his logistics skill to reinforce the weak points instead, and he does so while complaining that he cannot contribute on the battlefield or make a name for himself.

When the Traveler returns to report, Gorou has gone to the front to meet the Shogun's Army, which Kujou Sara leads in person. She says she has come only for the Traveler, and Gorou refuses to hand them over. Sara proposes a fight of honor, a ceremonial contest in which each side's finest warrior represents it before battle. Gorou explains that a win can raise a weaker side's morale, that Sara's real motive is to capture the Traveler if they lose, and that they need not accept. The Traveler accepts and wins consecutively, which heartens the Resistance, and the two armies clash. As the Shogun's Army gains ground, Sangonomiya Kokomi, the Resistance's leader, arrives with surprise mercenary reinforcements that include Beidou and Kaedehara Kazuha. Sara orders a retreat, and Kokomi invites the Traveler to Watatsumi Island to plan the counterattack.

Revelations: The Raiden Shogun treats the Traveler's Electro power without a Vision as a threat in itself, and shows that she can overpower the Traveler almost without effort. The Resistance is led by Kokomi, the Watatsumi Army's leader, and the Shogunate's forces are commanded in the field by Kujou Sara. Yashiro Commission neutrality limits what Ayaka can do openly.

The Shogun's phrase "strike twice" sets up her next encounter with the Traveler in the following act, and the Traveler's survival here depends on Thoma's distraction, not on their own strength.

Characters: **Traveler and Paimon**: now criminals in Inazuma, they move from the Kamisato side of events to the Resistance's side.
**Kamisato Ayaka and Thoma**: Ayaka is held back by her commission's neutrality; Thoma is the intended hundredth victim and is saved by the Traveler, then lies low at Komore Teahouse.
**Raiden Shogun**: appears in person at the ceremony, defeats the Traveler in an alternate space and orders their arrest.
**Teppei**: a Resistance soldier rescued by the Traveler, who guides them and wishes to prove himself.
**Gorou**: the Resistance's commanding general, who refuses to give up the Traveler.
**Kujou Sara**: leads the Shogun's Army against the Resistance and challenges the Traveler to a fight of honor.
**Sangonomiya Kokomi**: the Resistance's leader, who arrives with reinforcements and invites the Traveler to Watatsumi Island.

Beidou and Kaedehara Kazuha appear among the mercenary reinforcements Kokomi brings, so they enter the story as fighters hired for the Resistance rather than as members of the Watatsumi Army.

Consequences: The Traveler and Paimon are wanted by the Shogunate, so they join the Resistance. The Shogun's Army retreats from this clash. The way is open for Act III, in which the Traveler meets Kokomi on Watatsumi Island and becomes active in the Resistance's operations (see Omnipresence Over Mortals).

Placement: Released in Version 2.0 as the second act of Chapter II, following The Immovable God and the Eternal Euthymia and followed by Omnipresence Over Mortals (Version 2.1). The act requires the player to have completed Act I of the Grus Nivis Chapter (The Whispers of the Crane and the White Rabbit) and Act I of the Carassius Auratus Chapter (Dreamlike Timelessness).

Further details: By number of quests (two), this is the shortest Archon Quest act in the game. Its Chinese and Japanese titles both translate roughly as "Stillness & Nothingness, the Shattering of Mirage", which differs from the English wording.

825.comment: Stillness, the Sublimation of Shadow: The Hundredth Vision Hunt Victim
825.content:
Thoma is seized by the Tenryou Commission to be the hundredth person whose Vision is confiscated under the Vision Hunt Decree, in a public ceremony at the Statue of the Omnipresent God where the Raiden Shogun appears personally. The Traveler and Paimon intervene because Ayaka cannot without compromising the Yashiro Commission's neutrality.

The ceremony fails to go as planned: the Shogun's attention turns to the Traveler's Electro, Thoma helps the Traveler escape, and the Decree's centrepiece event ends with the Traveler becoming a fugitive.

826.comment: Stillness, the Sublimation of Shadow: Fight of Honor
826.content: A ceremonial contest before battle in which each side puts forward its best warrior. Gorou explains that a win can give a weaker side a boost in morale. Sara offers it intending to capture the Traveler if they lose. The Traveler's consecutive wins encourage the Resistance.

827.comment: Stillness, the Sublimation of Shadow: Teppei at the Resistance Camp
827.content: Teppei is the Resistance soldier the Traveler rescues from Shogunate troops. He guides the pair, shows them the camp and reinforces its weak points when an attack makes him suspect a traitor. He is frustrated that his logistics work does not let him fight. His fate unfolds in the next act and is not part of this act.

828.content:
Submerged Dragon, Soaring Phoenix (also: Zhangsun Jijing's Raincutter challenge, Plumwatcher Piles challenge): A Version 6.5 world quest set in Luyang Academy, the painting gallery inside the Temple of Space. The Traveler meets Zhangsun Jijing, a Guhua Clan swordsman, and passes three small agility trials he sets.

The Traveler restores a painting on the boat with Dex and then talks to the figure who leaps about inside it. He explains that no rain falls in this realm, so he cannot practise his master's Raincutter sword arts, and trains his lightfoot technique instead. He asks the Traveler to show their skill on the Plumwatcher Piles, then through roof-leaping, then in the air.

The quest is a light, humorous interlude with no plot revelations of its own. It unlocks Zhangsun as an open-world NPC at Luyang Academy and grants an achievement on completion.

Plot: At Luyang Academy the Traveler restores the painting on the boat with Dex, the Temple of Space guide, and sees an ink blot on a pillar. Touching it brings out Zhangsun Jijing, a Guhua Clan sword practitioner. He is polite and formal, and asks why he was called; Paimon says they were only curious about his jumping.

He says he was practising lightfoot techniques because rain never falls in the realm, so he cannot train the Rain Cutter arts his master taught him. He recalls the Great Master Guhua, who sharpened his agility on stone piles and reached the peak of his art, and asks the Traveler for a demonstration. Paimon, jokingly addressed as the master of the Paimon Clan, is amused.

There are three trials, each with a timed Geo-particle goal. First the Traveler steps over the Plumwatcher Piles, then performs the Leaping Techniques (roof-running and wall-scaling, which Zhangsun says the ancient Guhua masters used to scale city walls), and finally the Cloud-Striding Techniques, a legendary secret art said to have let Guhua tread the air and rise through purple haze. Paimon suggests the Wind Glider as the nearest equivalent.

Each trial ends with Zhangsun praising the Traveler. When the Traveler jokes that the leaping skills sound like a burglar's, Zhangsun answers that if thieves may hop walls to escape justice while those upholding it cannot, the wicked would simply slip away. After the final trial he says gliding is not truly treading on air but that it inspired him anyway, and thanks the Traveler.

The wiki lists three chests as rewards for the trials (common, exquisite and precious) and quest rewards of Adventure EXP, 30 Primogems and 35,000 Mora. These are gameplay details.

The trials escalate: seven Geo particles in 90 seconds on the Plumwatcher Piles, 38 in 90 seconds across the roofs, and 55 in 90 seconds in the air. The quest's start step is to climb a pillar and interact with the ink blot after restoring the painting. The Plumwatcher Piles, Leaping Techniques and Cloud-Striding Techniques are the three Guhua skills Zhangsun asks to see.

Revelations: Little is revealed. Zhangsun says he is a disciple of the Guhua Clan, that his master passed down the Rain Cutter arts, and that his sect's ancient masters mastered roof-running, wall-scaling and, by legend, walking on air. He is hampered by the absence of rain in the Temple of Space. The Plumwatcher Piles are an exact copy of the ones in front of Wangshan Hall on Mt. Lingmeng, the Guhua Clan's base (wiki trivia).

The wiki profile for Zhangsun says he is one of the Uplifted, people preserved as living memories in the Temple of Space, and was known as the Rainbearer before. It also says he had been turned into an ink blot by Melanta before the Traveler freed him. These come from the profile page rather than the quest text read here.

Characters: Zhangsun Jijing: earnest, courteous and formal, speaks in a stilted martial-arts register, and treats the Traveler as a fellow practitioner. The Traveler and Paimon supply the lighthearted tone. Dex's ability to restore paintings starts the quest. Guhua is mentioned only as the revered founder figure of the clan.

Zhangsun's appearance per the wiki: a burly man with dark blue hair and gray eyes, a blue shirt under a striped gray vest, dark baggy trousers, brown shoes and a large straw hat on his back. His idle line complains that the clouds never release any rain.

Consequences: Completing the quest unlocks the achievement "Where Now Lies the Raincutter's Hidden Light?" and lets players find Zhangsun at Luyang Academy afterward. There is no wider effect on the story.

Placement: Released in Version 6.5 (Luna VI, 2026-04-08), set in the Temple of Space at Luyang Academy. The wiki states it requires completing Long Live Life, part of the A Long Day in the Mountains chapter, which opens the academy. The quest has no place in a main story sequence.

829.comment: Submerged Dragon, Soaring Phoenix: Zhangsun Jijing
829.content: Zhangsun Jijing is a Guhua Clan disciple and open-world NPC at Luyang Academy in the Temple of Space. Known as the Rainbearer, he trained in the Raincutter sword style and cannot practise it fully because it never rains there. He asks the Traveler to demonstrate lightfoot, leaping and gliding skills in Submerged Dragon, Soaring Phoenix. The wiki describes him as one of the Uplifted preserved as living memories in the Temple of Space.

830.comment: Submerged Dragon, Soaring Phoenix: Plumwatcher Piles
830.content: The Plumwatcher Piles are the stone pillars on which the Guhua Clan trains lightfoot techniques. The set at Luyang Academy copies exactly the ones in front of Wangshan Hall on Mt. Lingmeng. In the quest, Zhangsun calls them the pride of Guhua, and he says Great Master Guhua once honed his agility on them.

key: Summertide Scales and Tales Event Quest
The Story Begins in a Forest Without Rain
They Once Walked the Starry Sky
Until the End of the World
831.content:
Summertide Scales and Tales (also: Summertide Scales and Tales Event Quest, The Story Begins in a Forest Without Rain, They Once Walked the Starry Sky, Until the End of the World, Simulanka storybook event): Summertide Scales and Tales is the Version 4.8 summer flagship event. A strangely bound book sends the Traveler and Paimon into Simulanka, a fairytale world of paper animals and toy people made by three goddesses, where Nilou, Navia and Kirara are also stranded and the Wanderer turns out to be the prophesied Hero. The "evil dragon" they must face is a lonely child named Durin, whose curse they lift by blessing him.

The story runs in three Pages and an Appendix (Afterword): The Story Begins in a Forest Without Rain, They Once Walked the Starry Sky, Until the End of the World and Afterword. It is a self-contained fairytale pastiche, light comedy until Durin's memories are shown. The event's reward character was Kirara.

The event required Adventure Rank 18 and the Prologue Act III, and recommended the Interlude Chapter Act III (Inversion of Genesis) and Chapter IV Act V (Masquerade of the Guilty) first. Kirara's outfit Phantom in Boots was earned through the event's Excerpts of Bliss.

The Afterword leaves a hook for Teyvat: a flashback line says the child of a creator named "R" will one day rise from the dead, and Albedo asks the Wanderer to be ready to help if Dragonspine's Durin awakens.

Plot: The Traveler and Paimon open a mysterious book and wake in Simulanka. In the Forest of Blessings Nilou has become the prophesied Forest Fairy and Grandpa Almond believes the Traveler is the Hero. After restoring the Calligraphy Tavern's Magic Tonic they travel to Constellation Metropole, where Navia is King, and on to the end of the world to face the dragon. There the Wanderer, the real Hero, learns the dragon's story, and everyone's blessings turn him into a small, harmless Mini Durin.

**Page I.** In the Forest of Blessings the paper folk are fading because the Calligraphy Tavern, source of their Magic Tonic (ink), closed after a dragon attacked. Nilou, dressed as the Forest Fairy, learns that magic here is made of words, brews new Tonic, brings a paper hamster to life as Padisarah and reopens the Tavern.

**Page II.** By the Maritime Express the party reaches Constellation Metropole, where Navia is King. The city's tracks (a gift of the Goddess of Prophecy that rewinds people out of danger) are failing and the dragon has stolen its stars. They recover the stars and ride the Aerial Express to hang them back.

**Page III.** The Wanderer, the real Hero of Simulanka, leads them to the dragon's lair. The dragon's memories show a lonely child. After the Wanderer names him Durin, everyone's blessings shrink and uncurse him.

**Afterword.** Two days later friends from Teyvat holiday in Simulanka, and Mini Durin leaves with the Wanderer to visit Teyvat.

**Page I in detail.** The Traveler and Paimon wake on the Cliff of Prophecy among paper plants and talking origami frogs. Almond explains that three goddesses created Simulanka and that an evil dragon came down in black mist, ravaged the forest and left its paper dwellers with the Fading Disorder, losing colour and memory. Nilou cannot use her Vision here. The group helps the Tavern's workers (reconnecting pipes, steadying the singer Stream's rhythm, positioning the bartender Citrus), and Paimon discovers the Tonic is ink. Nilou senses an empty space under the Tavern, a giant ink bottle, and brews the Tonic from sunsettias, snapdragons and Nilotpala Lotuses. Almond regains his memory and recalls the prophecy: the Hero from another world will descend on the Cliff of Prophecy and restore peace.

**Page II in detail.** The conductor Wheel drives the Maritime Express. Kirara is found asleep in a carriage after waking in Simulanka the day before. In the city of toy people, the Goddess of Prophecy's gift freezes or rewinds residents who are about to come to harm, but it now triggers too often, monsters are invading and the Hero is expected. Navia shares the prophecy "push the gear that connects up to the starry sky... I shall dance, and return the tracks beneath my people's feet back to the stars". Many fear losing the protection, and Navia wants the citizens to choose for themselves. The party clears monsters from the castle, recovers scattered stars, retrieves the magic thread from a frightened "conservative radical" whom Navia lets go, and asks the goddess's statue questions. It answers only about the dragon and the gear.

**Page III in detail.** A broken track throws the party off the train into a hallucinatory fog and the Wanderer catches them. He carries a "Hero's Sword" he cannot discard, had been seeking a way out rather than obey the voice telling him to save the dragon, and gives them a Fell Dragon's Scale that turns things to toy blocks. In the lair the dragon's attacks show his memories: a woman's voice naming a newborn, the child seeing his reflection and frightening the capital, his mother M telling him she will become a star and to be kind, and a flying squirrel girl whose mother calls him a kidnapper. The Wanderer, alone in the black mist, tells him nobody else defines who he is and says the name Durin.

**After the memories.** Durin's curse turned everything he touched to toy blocks and left barren footprints, and his wish to the Goddess of Fate was "to never have been born at all". Navia reads the star-taking as longing: M had told him she would become a star in Simulanka. Through a hole the Wanderer leads the party to M's study, where an old journal and a yellowed letter explain the world's makers (see revelations). Nilou asks whether Durin truly wants to live beside the people, blesses him as a dweller of the Forest, and Navia, Kirara, the Wanderer and the Traveler add theirs. Durin becomes small and no longer transforms things at a touch. Alice, appearing as a talking street lamp, welcomes the guests and explains that the boat at the Broken Sea or the giant bookmark at the Cliff of Prophecy would have taken them home all along.

**The Metropole.** A toy man tells the party "Push the gear, and the 'tracks' will disappear. We're not ready yet." Bleufond and Bleucher are rescued from falling blocks by the rewind gift in Page II. In the lair the dragon grows two extra heads and its breath bars the party's elemental skills, so toy bombs must be thrown into its open mouths.

**Afterword in detail.** Kaeya and Jean came by invitation from Alice and are at the Tavern, where Paimon tricks Kaeya into ordering the House Special (ink). Klee ran off at once, Albedo is watching over her and Fischl and Oz join in. Collei is sketching tree-houses, and Mona is scrying the Goddess of Prophecy's statue. Mini Durin and the Wanderer have built houses by the giant footprints and Durin has apologised to the Metropole with toytanium and plant oil. Albedo asks the Wanderer to consider helping if Dragonspine's Durin returns. The group names a small paper boat "The Durin". Klee calls Mini Durin her big brother because their mothers were friends. Collei mentions that something interesting is happening in Sumeru that Tighnari is working hard on, and the wiki lists An Odd Textual Mystery as the next quest. Post-quest NPC dialogue has Nahida teasing the Wanderer about his new friend.

Revelations: The "evil dragon" is Durin, a child created and then left alone, and Simulanka was made by three friends who loved M's stories.

Durin's mother M created him with a name that would tie him to a "real-world namesake's" sad fate, hoping a happier ending would be possible in a storybook. His fear and loneliness, not malice, caused his rampages.

Simulanka's creators are Alice (Goddess of Creation), B (Goddess of Prophecy, who maps fates and wanted her own statue) and M (Goddess of Fate, a Hexenzirkel mage who wrote the tales and told Durin her life would be shorter than a fairytale). The journal says Alice overruled M's wish to be "A" and gave her "M" for her middle name, and that Alice made M's origami frogs speak. M's letter says that, according to A, the Goddess of Fate in Simulanka will go on granting wishes after M is gone. The guests' blessings changed Durin's body: in this world words carry magic.

The Wanderer says Durin too was "betrayed" and "hated by people", and he alone reaches him. Mona scries that Simulanka's fate is a projection of Teyvat's, as if the world were a reflection in a mirror or lake, and recognises the Goddess of Prophecy's statue as her own master in youth. B tells M a secret: "R's child will one day rise from the dead", which the Wanderer relays to Albedo. Albedo notes that Dragonspine's Durin shows signs of slowly gathering vitality and hopes whatever wakes will not be an "evil dragon". Alice says she sent the book to the Traveler and Paimon, and the others each held a copy of M's tale when Durin made his wish.

Characters: Traveler, Paimon, Nilou (the Forest Fairy), Navia (King of Constellation Metropole), Kirara (the Nekomata-in-Boots), Wanderer (Hero of Simulanka) and Durin (Mini Durin).

Locals include Almond, Citrus, Stream, Firecracker, Padisarah, Wheel and the toy guards Montagne and Bizerte. The goddesses are Alice, B and M. Afterword guests are Kaeya, Jean, Klee, Albedo, Collei, Mona, Fischl and Oz.

Navia is addressed as "Your Majesty" but acts like a partner. Kirara is teased as the "Nekomata-in-Boots" and frightens the paper animals. The Wanderer is blunt, hates the Hero title and mocks the voice that gave him orders, yet stays by Durin. Other locals: Chestnut, Ginkgo, Cedule, Bleufond, Bleucher and Olivier.

Consequences: Durin becomes the small dragon Mini Durin, no longer cursed, and sets out to make amends. The Traveler, Nilou, Navia, Kirara and the Wanderer can leave through the Broken Sea boat or the Cliff of Prophecy's bookmark. The Wanderer promises to bring Mini Durin to Teyvat on the boat "The Durin".

Albedo's request ties the fairytale to Dragonspine, and the later Paralogism quest features a dragon from Simulanka.

Placement: Released in Version 4.8 on 17 July 2024 (UTC+8) and run until 28 August 2024. Page II unlocked on 19 July, Page III on 21 July and the Appendix on 23 July. It is an event story rather than an Archon Quest, though Navia (president of Spina di Rosula) takes a leading role.

832.content: Simulanka is a storybook world created by three goddesses: Creation (Alice), Prophecy (B) and Fate (M). The Forest of Blessings is home to paper-folded animals who drink Magic Tonic (ink) to keep their colour. Constellation Metropole is a clockwork city of toy people ruled from a castle with an Astral Garden at its peak, with a statue of the Goddess of Prophecy. At the end of the world lies the Broken Sea and the dragon's lair. Players can leave Simulanka via the Broken Sea boat or the giant bookmark at the Cliff of Prophecy.

833.comment: Summertide Scales and Tales: Durin of Simulanka
833.content: Durin is the dragon created by M, who gave him a name tied to a sad real-world namesake. He grew up lonely, frightened the capital, took the Metropole's stars because they reminded him of his mother, and lived behind the waterfall while others sheltered at the Broken Sea. The Wanderer, Nilou and the others blessed him, shrinking him into Mini Durin; he now apologises, rebuilds and befriends Klee, who calls him her big brother because their mothers were friends.

834.comment: Summertide Scales and Tales: Magic Tonic and the Fading Disorder
834.content: In the Forest of Blessings the paper residents' colours and memories fade unless they drink Magic Tonic, which is made from sunsettias, snapdragons and Nilotpala Lotuses brewed into ink at the Calligraphy Tavern. Nilou realises the Fading Disorder is ink running dry. A giant ink bottle sits under the Tavern, and Nilou's blessing reopens it.

835.comment: Summertide Scales and Tales: The Goddesses of Simulanka
835.content: Alice made the world habitable and made origami frogs talk, B (Barbeloth) mapped every fate and has her statue in the capital, and M wrote the fairytales. M expected a short life. Mona recognises the Goddess of Prophecy's statue as her own master.

key: Like Rhyme and Song, the Summer Reverie
836.content:
Summertime Odyssey (also: Golden Apple Archipelago event, Summertime Odyssey event, The Golden Apple Vacation Returns, Immernachtreich Apokalypse, Like Rhyme and Song, the Summer Reverie): The invitation traces back to Alice, with Venti secretly in on it. The archipelago has been seeded with a Fatui experiment, a machine named Cognitive Mimicry, which warps minds; the Fatui who tested it went mad, but the protagonists' stronger wills shaped their hallucinations into stable mirages. The story visits Kazuha's regrets over his clan, Xinyan's struggle to be a musician, Mona's burden as an astrologer and Fischl's relationship with her "Immernachtreich" fantasy. At the end the machine is repaired and switched off, and a mysterious voice, implied to be the future Dendro Archon, speaks to the Traveler.

Players who collected Iridescent Flotsam during the event's challenges could invite Electro Fischl ("Prinzessin der Verurteilung!") as a character reward. The story returns to the archipelago first visited in the earlier event Midsummer Island Adventure, and its closing voice points ahead to Sumeru.

Plot: Act I, The Golden Apple Vacation Returns!: Fischl, Mona, Xinyan, Kazuha, the Traveler and Paimon travel to the archipelago after Fischl receives an anonymous letter (really Alice's) offering her a land to restore her kingdom. On arrival, Kazuha and the Traveler find a strange Fatui machine.

Act II (Kazuha): a bonsai pot belonging to the Kaedehara family opens a domain recreating Kazuha's childhood. Act III (Xinyan): a vine-covered drum on the Broken Isle opens a domain of her memories and turns the island into an instrument again. Act IV, Immernachtreich Apokalypse (Fischl): Fischl's imagined kingdom, its three-volume book and her double. Act V, The Ancient Azure Stars (Mona): a star-chasing mirage through her years as an astrologer.

Act VI, Like Rhyme and Song, the Summer Reverie: the party finds the Fatui researcher Persikov, recovers the cores of his machine "Cognitive Mimicry", repairs and disables it, and hears the unseen voice a second time.

Act I details: Katheryne tells the Traveler and Paimon that Fischl wants to see them, and Mona suspects Alice, who also made the Dodocommunication Device that Venti gives the Traveler. Venti admits he knew the plan; Xinyan and Kazuha, in Mondstadt by chance, are invited. At the archipelago Fischl and Mona race, Xinyan makes camp, and the Fatui (led by Persikov) say their machine was a failed energy generator.

Act II: The group's boat has become sentient and talks to a squirrel; Paimon names it Miitoboru. Kazuha's mirages show his father telling him to abandon the family craft, the clan dissolving after the Raiden Gokaden incident, his wandering, receiving a Vision and fleeing Inazuma on the Alcor under the Vision Hunt Decree. He realises he wants to keep the family's bonsai tradition alive.

Act III: Xinyan's mirage shows her mother and others discouraging her music and a surprise birthday gathering with Xiangling and Yun Jin; her wish is to perform with someone completely unexpected. A note by Albedo says the island is a giant instrument. The group revives a flower called Blazing Heart with Glacial Spring Water and a second, Frozen Soul, lets them dredge the mountains so Xinyan can perform. Mona admits she had already warned Fischl of the Fatui, and the trail leads to Twinning Isle, where Fischl behaves oddly.

Act IV: A raven statue and the book "Hymn of the Holy Land" are found abandoned. In the mirage the group learns of Fischl's childhood name Amy and of her parents first playing along, then telling her to give up fairy tales. Immernacht Fischl, a double, claims the Immernachtreich is a tomb for those who cannot face reality and tries to trap them, until the real Fischl accepts her insecurities and reclaims it. A hijacked call delivers the unseen voice, which says the mirages are humans' "deep dream".

Act V: Mona's mirage on Minacious Isle follows a star through her miserable early years of divination, a prediction of an adventurer's death within two years (he refused to quit adventuring), and a home filled with expensive astrology equipment. She decides she cannot change fate but can seize her destiny while still guiding others. Kazuha proposes that the machine reacts to willpower, so the strong-willed produce stable mirages.

Act VI: Persikov, drunk and ranting, is snapped out of madness. His manuscripts say the machine alters brains, is modelled on a god's power and lost its crystalline cores. The party refits them. Mona says the mirages persist, but she senses no ill intent. The voice says it was curious about a power related to it and helped design the experience; a Dendro symbol appears.

In Act VI Kazuha slams Persikov to the ground to bring him to his senses. His papers record that the Fatui did not support his research but let him test it on a deserted island with junior soldiers; it broke after a couple of days, he left his subordinates in a cave and searched for the cores himself, and succumbed to the device. After the repair two Fatui arrive no longer affected. Venti, called afterwards, says the journey has served its purpose if they had an unforgettable experience. In Act IV, raven-statue guards refuse the party at first and the final volume's castle is the toy castle Fischl once smashed in a tantrum; in Act V the group needs an Asterism Shard to reopen a pool.

Revelations: Fischl's imagination is part of herself, not a flaw: Oz says Immernacht Fischl and the child Amy are two sides of the same person. Kazuha admits a wish to continue his clan's bonsai tradition. Mona decides destiny cannot be rewritten but can be seized. The Fatui machine and the unseen voice are separate causes of the mirages, and the voice's Dendro symbol foreshadows Sumeru.

The wiki notes that the voice's timbre matches that of a Sumeru teaser at the Version 2.8 Special Program, and later Sumeru content names Nahida. Within the event the entity's identity remains an inference.

Characters: The Traveler and Paimon, Fischl (and her raven Oz), Mona, Kazuha, Xinyan and Venti (by communicator). Alice and Klee are involved offstage. Persikov leads a hapless Fatui group. Raven statues of the Immernachtreich include one named Arnold, and Immernacht Fischl is the boss-like double of Fischl. The sentient boat, named Miitoboru by Paimon, appears.

Albedo is present only through a note he left on the Broken Isle, and Xiangling and Yun Jin appear in Xinyan's mirage.

Consequences: The machine is switched off; the mirages remain for a while. Fischl feels secure in her imagination, Kazuha and Xinyan and Mona each resolve a private regret, and the group enjoys the rest of the holiday. The voice's final words suggest a future meeting.

Placement: Released in Version 2.8 as a Flagship Event; players needed Adventure Rank 32 and the Chapter II Prologue (Autumn Winds, Scarlet Leaves), with Mona's Beyond This World's Stars recommended. It was set before Sumeru's release in Version 3.0.

Gameplay: Game mechanics, not in-world fact. Gameplay combined Surfpiercer boat challenges and five Phantom Realm challenges (Misty Hills, Foggy Vales; The Islands' Stirring Strings; Immernachtreich Keep; Temple of the Star Latitudes; and Initial Exploration/Direct Strike), with Iridescent Flotsam exchanged for materials and for Fischl's invite.

837.content: A limited map of islands reached by a Dodoco-themed device outside Mondstadt. In the 2.8 event it holds Pudding Isle, the Broken Isle, Twinning Isle and Minacious Isle, a Fatui camp and the mirage domains. It is also where the Midsummer Island Adventure took place.

838.content: A Fatui machine designed by the researcher Persikov, said to be modelled on a god's power and able to alter brains. After it broke, its crystalline cores were lost. Those weak in willpower hallucinate and go mad; Kazuha, Xinyan, Mona and Fischl instead shaped stable mirages. The group retrieves the cores and fixes it.

839.content: Fischl's imagined kingdom, here a domain with raven statues, narration and a three-volume book. It shows the child Amy and her parents' changing response to fairy tales. Immernacht Fischl, her double, calls it a tomb for those who cannot face reality, but the real Fischl reclaims it.

840.comment: Summertime Odyssey: The unseen voice on the Dodocommunication Device
840.content: Alice's prototype communicator, handed to the Traveler by Venti. In Acts IV and VI an unknown voice takes over the connection, says the mirages are the "deep dream" of humans and that it may meet the Traveler in another place; a Dendro symbol appears. The wiki treats this as implying the Dendro Archon Lesser Lord Kusanali, but the event does not say so.

841.content:
Sunny Summer Fontinalia (also: Sunny Summer Fontinalia Story Quest, Should We Meet Again, Those We Have Lost, Those We Have Kept, A Homecoming film, Luna VIII summer event): Sunny Summer Fontinalia is the Version 6.7 (Luna VIII) summer event and its three-act story quest. At Fontaine's Fontinalia Film Festival the Traveler and Paimon help Xavier's Musketeer Pictures film a story about Columbina, who is visiting Fontaine while searching for her lost best friend. On the borrowed ship Wingalet they find Sandrone alive again, calling herself Miss Guillotin, and help her reach her dead creator Alain Guillotin's flooded home, resolve the "anomalies" in her core and mend an old Fontaine wound.

The acts are Should We Meet Again, Those We Have Lost and Those We Have Kept. The event itself was an aquarium-management game (Operation Deep-Dive Treasure, Kaleido-Catch, Curio Ledger) rewarding the character Charlotte and her outfit Hurlock Variations. The story quest stays playable after the event ended.

The event required Adventure Rank 20, a Fontaine Statue of The Seven and the Prologue Act III, and recommended Act X of Song of the Welkin Moon (Truth Amongst the Pages of Purana) first. Version 6.7 also released Sandrone as a playable character.

The quest follows directly on the Nod-Krai finale: Sandrone's survival, Columbina's return and the Moon Sisters are treated as shared background.

Plot: Xavier rewrites his festival film around Columbina and borrows the Wingalet from Wriothesley, but its renter, Miss Guillotin, is Sandrone. She tells the Traveler and Paimon that Alain's final gift revived her. They dive for Alain's home, find her creator's formula, and Sandrone faces her inner "anomaly". She then puts a corrupted mass of wandering souls to rest, reunites with Columbina, and the film gets its happy ending.

**Act I, Should We Meet Again.** Xavier is looking for a new subject after Columbina wanders into his auditions. Chiori and Furina support the rewrite, and Wriothesley lends the Wingalet. Aboard are Citlali (front desk worker) and Sandrone (the ship's renter, using Alain's family name). Sandrone tells the Traveler and Paimon that Dottore destroyed her core in Nod-Krai and that Alain's built-in "Final Gift" rebooted her when a Stellar Linchpin appeared. She wants to find Alain's home, now underwater, and the Traveler offers to dive with her while the crew films.

**Act II, Those We Have Lost.** The party locates the Hidden Dwelling and finds Alain's letter, a formula for meeting her inner "anomaly", and a handwritten note from her earlier years. Sandrone, with the Traveler and Paimon witnessing, faces her own grief and accepts it.

**Act III, Those We Have Kept.** Sandrone destroys the Tower of Gestalt's accumulation of wandering souls, reunites with Columbina on camera, and the film gets its ending. At a party aboard the Wingalet friends gather, and Wriothesley keeps the aquarium.

**Act I in detail.** The Traveler and Paimon meet Chiori, Furina and Xavier in the Court of Fontaine. Columbina says she travelled alone after asking Nefer and Lauma for advice, and she tests friendship by punching people's arms ("Hya!"), including Wriothesley and, later, Neuvillette. Chevreuse arrives to say the Duke has agreed to let well-behaved inmates leave under supervision for the festival. Learning that the festival has booked up every good location, Wriothesley shows Xavier the Wingalet, which he has brought to the surface. In the cabin the party finds Citlali in pajamas, working the front desk for room and board: she came to Fontaine for the premiere of a light-novel adaptation, could not sleep at her hotel near the Opera Epiclese, and found every other room booked. The renter is Sandrone, who has applied for a fishing permit and business licence under the name Guillotin so she can search for the home without applying to excavate underwater ruins. She keeps her presence quiet. Charlotte's crew (director Lepine-Pauline, with Chevreuse, Navia and Emilie in the cast) is shooting "Great Detective Hurlock" on the same deck, and Xavier names the Traveler "chief lighting and Kamera specialist" for "A Homecoming".

**Act II in detail.** Sandrone and the Traveler take samples from several sites to find the entrance. While Furina and Charlotte's crews shoot on the Wingalet, Sandrone has to hide in a box for a scene. Hearing the detective scene about machines having no heart, she recalls Alain asking whether she recognised her own heart. Inside the Hidden Dwelling the party sees her garden, workbench, a photograph from the days when Alain and Rene were still together at the Institute of Natural Philosophy, a Pagoda Stack puzzle game she played as a child, and a box that holds a Multidimensional Algorithmic Core, a letter and photographs. Alain's letter says a person should be born twice, once into life and once into the soul, and gives her a formula for facing the "anomaly" within. In an inner mirror space, the "anomaly" (her emotions) recalls the tea parties with Columbina, Tartaglia, Capitano, Signora and Arlecchino, Columbina's farewell, and the loss of Pulonia. Sandrone smashes the mirror and embraces the anomaly, saying they were always one.

**Act III in detail.** Citlali pinpoints the Tower of Gestalt, in the Morte Region, as the source of resentful, severed souls. Sandrone refuses to call in Neuvillette because of the diplomatic mess, drains the tower and, with Citlali's ritual, calls the corrupted mass. When negotiation fails she runs the numerological array in reverse ("Reversion"), separating the souls so they can return to the Ley Lines. Afterwards Columbina pulls Sandrone to a lunar space and the two embrace, then are teleported in front of Xavier's Kamera; the take becomes the film's ending. At the premiere "Great Detective Hurlock" wins the Furina Award. Sandrone and Columbina visit Alain's grave, and a party on the Wingalet follows, with Neuvillette, Wriothesley, Sigewinne, Baptiste and Veronique, Lyney, Lynette, Freminet, Escoffier, Navia, Clorinde and others. Arlecchino arrives for tea with Sandrone and Columbina, and Sandrone plays the mechanical piano.

**Act I extras.** Sandrone says Alain Guillotin lived in seclusion after leaving the Institute, that she is the Seventh of the Fatui Harbingers, and that the Traveler offered to come along because they were worried about her condition. Sandrone says Columbina's senses rely on kuuvahki: strong in Nod-Krai, but elsewhere about as wide as ordinary sight unless she uses her abilities, which is how Sandrone has been avoiding her. Charlotte, Chiori and Furina discuss new awards at the festival, including Best Director, Best Costume Design and Best Kamera Operation.

**Act II extras.** In the dwelling's Pagoda Stack game the Traveler can match Sandrone's fewest-move solution, which impresses her. She reads a note she wrote as a child, "Her Highness the Clockwork Princess, Unraveller of All Reason", and blames it on Pulonia. Sandrone says she created Katheryne only as a superficial imitation of Alain's work and that some mechanics of her own core remain mysterious to her. In the aquarium she has told Paimon the fish all swam away because the old her stopped caring, and the Traveler and Paimon's care changes her view.

**Act III extras.** After the premiere Clorinde and Navia discuss Alain's legacy (founder and first director of the Fontaine Research Institute, inventor of pneuma-ousia annihilation energy), and Navia realises the Guillotin name seems familiar. Alain's headstone reads "Founding Director of the Research Institute of Kinetic Energy Engineering, White Cavalier of Protection, Lord-Artificer". Lyney and Lynette try to borrow Citlali's Tzitzimitl helpers for their magic show.

Revelations: Sandrone survived the Nod-Krai battle; Alain Guillotin prepared a built-in "second chance" that triggered when a Stellar Linchpin appeared.

The Stellar Linchpin let her core reboot and repair. Pulonia, the other half of Alain's work, is beyond repair, though some of its algorithms and the numerological array were imported into her body. A formula Alain left lets her meet and accept her inner "anomaly", the clash of her emotions and logic.

Sandrone's account of the Stellar Linchpin is that it is a rare form of Vision linked in Fatui research to the Third Descender, whose remains the Heavenly Principles used to create the Gnoses. She says it channels elemental power with an extra, otherworldly quality. Sandrone supposes the Final Gift exists because Alain, who often spoke to her about wishes, thought she might one day wish for something enough to give up her life. The Multidimensional Algorithmic Core stores information that only she and Pulonia can access.

Sandrone explains that the Narzissenkreuz Ordo's Rene and Jakob severed souls in their research before Rene awakened; those souls could not return to the Ley Lines and corrupted over time. A query to the numerological array tells Sandrone that only one living Moon Goddess remains, and she takes this to mean Columbina made it back; later she says Columbina is now merged with the Moon Sisters. Columbina has not told Xavier, because Nefer and Lauma both advised against it.

Characters: Traveler, Paimon, Columbina, Sandrone (Miss Guillotin), Citlali, Furina, Chiori, Xavier and Wriothesley.

Charlotte, Chevreuse, Navia, Emilie, Clorinde and Lepine-Pauline appear in the film crews. Act II features Alain Guillotin in flashbacks, and Tartaglia, Capitano, Signora and Arlecchino appear in Sandrone's memories of tea parties. The finale party adds Neuvillette, Sigewinne, Lyney, Lynette, Freminet, Escoffier, Ninette, Veronique and Baptiste.

Citlali is embarrassed and defensive about her pajamas, and gruff but kind. Columbina is polite, curious and devoted to Sandrone. Sandrone is sharp-tongued and dislikes bureaucracy, but admits she missed everyone.

Consequences: Sandrone resolves her "anomalies", reunites with Columbina and the Fatui circle, and visits Alain's grave. The Wingalet's aquarium remains, since Wriothesley asks to keep some installations for the inmates at the Fortress of Meropide. Xavier's "A Homecoming" does not win the Furina Award, which goes to "Great Detective Hurlock".

The Hidden Dwelling stays accessible after the quest. Sandrone says she will bring gifts to the House of the Hearth and hopes to meet in Nod-Krai or Snezhnaya. Columbina wants to keep seeing Sandrone but not return to the Fatui.

Placement: Released in Version 6.7 (Luna VIII) on 1 July 2026 as a flagship event running to 11 August 2026 (UTC+8). It is a permanent story quest in Fontaine (the event page notes it can still be accepted after the event). It follows the Nod-Krai events and precedes the version 7.0 Snezhnaya story.

842.content: A large vessel kept at the Fortress of Meropide, brought up to the Court of Fontaine for the festival and rented out for extra income. Its maintenance is done by inmates. Sandrone rented it as captain and turned it into an aquarium that Wriothesley keeps afterward.

843.comment: Sunny Summer Fontinalia: Hidden Dwelling and Alain's Final Gift
843.content: The Hidden Dwelling is Alain and Sandrone's old home, now underwater, with a garden, workbench, water-insulating sluice gates, a fireplace and a puzzle table. Alain's built-in "Final Gift" revived Sandrone and left a Multidimensional Algorithmic Core, a letter and a soul-mapping formula.

844.comment: Sunny Summer Fontinalia: Stellar Linchpin (Sandrone's account)
844.content: According to Sandrone, a Stellar Linchpin is a rare kind of Vision, linked by Fatui research to the Third Descender, whose manifestation seems to fix impurities from his remains in place. It lets its user channel elemental energy with an unusual power from beyond Teyvat.

845.comment: Sunny Summer Fontinalia: Wandering souls at the Tower of Gestalt
845.content: A mass of resentful, severed souls had gathered at the Tower of Gestalt in the Morte Region and was fusing with evil beings. Sandrone reversed her world-formula to separate the souls and returned them to the Ley Lines, saying she did it to fulfil Alain's wish to repair things with his friend Rene.

846.comment: Sunny Summer Fontinalia: A Homecoming and Great Detective Hurlock
846.content: "A Homecoming" is Musketeer Pictures' festival film about a woman searching a foreign land for her lost friend, directed by Furina with Columbina as the lead. "Great Detective Hurlock", directed by Lepine-Pauline with Charlotte as the lead, adapts a popular light novel and wins the Furina Award.

key: The Surprise That Awaits Us All
A Curtain Call for a Colorful Summer Night
847.content:
Sunspray Summer Resort (also: Sunspray Summer Resort Story Quest, To a Carefree Vacation, The World Is Your Canvas, The Surprise That Awaits Us All, A Curtain Call for a Colorful Summer Night): Sunspray Summer Resort is a Natlan story quest released in Version 5.8 alongside a limited-time flagship event (30 July to 18 August 2025). The Traveler and Paimon holiday at the new Easybreeze Holiday Resort with Bennett, Mualani and Chasca, later joined by Venti. During the holiday Bennett meets the spirits of his birth parents.

The quest has four parts: To a Carefree Vacation!, The World Is Your Canvas!, The Surprise That Awaits Us All! and A Curtain Call for a Colorful Summer Night! The event offered four gameplay modes and rewards such as Bennett's outfit Adventures in Blazing Hue and the claymore Flame-Forged Insight. Unusually, the story quest stays playable after the event ended.

The tone is light holiday comedy until Part III, which turns to Bennett's origins as the child of a retired Natlan adventurer team.

The story assumes the Traveler's heroism in Natlan as shared background (Incandescent Ode of Resurrection is recommended) and spends little time on the Archon plot.

Plot: Bennett, Mualani, Chasca and the Traveler test the new resort. After rest, painting and challenges, a blurred photograph leads Bennett to an Abyssal domain, where Venti helps him reach the spirits of his parents. A party on Tete Isle and a quiet farewell follow.

**Part I, To a Carefree Vacation!** The Traveler and Paimon receive a letter inviting them to the resort's trial operation, with food, lodging and entertainment covered. Bennett, whose luck has unexpectedly improved, greets them with a friendly Asha companion. Mualani and Chasca arrive by sea. The group tries the Dreambow Drift, buys candles for a "sun" offering at a market stall, eats at Huha Hill and holds a bonfire ritual in which each makes a wish. Bennett wishes the land healing and his dads in Mondstadt health.

**Part II, The World Is Your Canvas!** The group tackles three areas of the resort (Colorfall Cliffs, Guiztli Ridge and Wavey Bay), then visits Tete Isle, where the Traveler acts as DJ on a dance-off stage Xilonen designed and the group colours the stage with the Asha.

**Part III, The Surprise That Awaits Us All!** After the challenges the group collects a prize, then finds the album's photos have blurred and the last shows four unknown people in tribal outfits. Bennett names them as Tecpatl's Flintblades, a famed adventurer team. A rift leads to a fiery domain with an Abyssal presence where a voice mocks Bennett. Venti shields the others, and a candlelit prayer brings a memory and then the spirits of Bennett's parents, Aroni and Macani. They speak outside the domain, then join the grand opening of Tete Isle, where Mavuika appears on stage.

**Part IV, A Curtain Call for a Colorful Summer Night!** The group paints their part of the resort and takes a photograph. Bennett decides to stay in Mondstadt. Venti then tells the Traveler about Istaroth and the Mare Jivari.

Revelations: Bennett was born in Natlan to a retired adventurer couple, and the spirits of his parents are now Asha.

His parents, Aroni and Macani, belonged to Tecpatl's Flintblades. When Abyssal monsters attacked the team in the Mare Jivari, his mother stayed behind to save him. The Mondstadt adventurers who raised him gave him the name Bennett, which means "blessed". The parents lost their memories as Asha, and the album's photos were taken by Aroni.

Mavuika tells Bennett the domain was an Abyssal simulation of the Mare Jivari. Venti says that 500 years ago he blew the Mare Jivari into another timeline to stop corruption spreading, making it the "Windless Land". Some souls could not escape, and others merged with Monetoo to become Asha. Mavuika opened a rift between the simulated and real Mare Jivari that let him bring them back.

Venti says he received part of Istaroth's power and authority when he met her at the Thousand Winds Temple, and ties the Mare Jivari's corruption to Time itself. He has brought memories of the dead to Bennett before. Bennett's luck will worsen again far from Natlan's ley lines, but he feels the holiday has readied him for it.

Characters: Traveler, Paimon, Bennett, Mualani, Chasca and Venti.

Also Mavuika, Rhythmos, resort staff such as the candle seller Nataba and Ukucha (who gives out the challenge prize), the Asha, and Bennett's parents Aroni and Macani. Ororon and Ifa are at the resort checking on the health of saurian staff and aphids, and Xilonen designed the stage.

Consequences: Bennett makes peace with his past and chooses to return to Mondstadt. The group takes a commemorative picture with the cry "Lucky star!"

The quest adds to what is known of the Mare Jivari and the link between Asha and lost souls.

Placement: Released in Version 5.8 on 30 July 2025 (UTC+8) as a flagship event with timed phases. The event required Adventure Rank 18 and the Prologue Act III. After the event ended the story quest remained available at the Easybreeze Holiday Resort. It does not appear in the Archive's Story Quests list.

848.comment: Sunspray Summer Resort: Easybreeze Holiday Resort
848.content: A newly opened holiday resort in Natlan staffed by locals, with Asha as its mascots. It held a trial operation and invited the Traveler. Areas include Huha Hill, Colorfall Cliffs, Guiztli Ridge, Wavey Bay and Tete Isle.

849.content: Aroni and Macani belonged to Tecpatl's Flintblades, a Natlan adventurer team that retired when two members had a baby. After Abyssal monsters attacked in the Mare Jivari, Aroni stayed behind to save the child. Both later lost their memories as Asha. In Part III they briefly appear to Bennett and say they are proud of him.

850.content:
Swords and Secrets (also: Vesna's world quest, Vesna's sword spirits, Ancient Sword Esoterica quest, Druzhna Special Dispatch Order quest): Swords and Secrets is a lighthearted 7.1 world quest starring Vesna, Commander of the Druzhna. After a rare Liyue "manual" teaches her to make sword spirits, they escape and start causing trouble around Snezhnaya. The Traveler and Paimon help her hunt them down over seven days. The manual is revealed at the end to be an unfinished work of fiction from Yae Publishing House. The reward is the Druzhna Special Dispatch Order.

It unlocks after White Night, Like a Dream Upon Waking, and takes seven real-time days because one part opens each day. Completing it gives Primogems, 30,000 Mora, Hero's Wit, Guide to Glory, the cosmetic Construct Appearance Flutterwing and the Druzhna Special Dispatch Order, which makes a sword spirit fly beside Vesna when she is in her Coursing state. The tone is comedic, and the cast of sword spirits are caricatures of cultivation tropes.

Plot: Vesna's flying sword turns out to be one of several sword spirits she accidentally created while following a book bought from a rare-book dealer. Each has "mastered" a different cultivation art, and each is caught in turn. The last, a Greater Sword Spirit with two Volkodlak followers, makes a last stand on the Everfrozen Earth, and Vesna ends up sparing its group and giving them a second chance.

Day 1: A person named Blyushko shouts that a thief has struck at Sadov-Arbat; the Traveler chases a flying blue-green blur to Vesna, who admits it is one of her creations. She had bought an ancient manuscript from Liyue about people who cultivated mind and body to command flying swords, and tried the method; the sword spirits flew off, and one stole the second half of her copy of the "Ancient Sword Esoterica". She does not want to send the Druzhna because the unit is stretched and she hopes to clean it up quietly.

Days 2-5: Vesna makes a "Divine Sense Compass", which Paimon points out has nothing to do with divine sense because she uses her own elemental energy. Spirits found: the Master of Potions, who brewed an "immortal elixir" that turns out only to be sweet; the Master of Body, tricked into staying in a cauldron until it passes out; the Master of Sigils, who paints a portrait of the one person Vesna fears, which she defaces and glues in place; and the Master of Artifacts, a machine body based on a Landcruiser which the party defeats in battle.

Day 6: The compass points to the Korolevskiy Theater, where Vodyanitsa and Odette have noticed an unseen watcher. During a rehearsal Vesna finds a shy Master of Sound hiding behind the curtains. A larger Greater Sword Spirit with two Volkodlak followers, "Second of the Pack" and "Third of the Pack", appears while the Master of Sound cowers behind it, and challenges Vesna to settle matters at a proper place, on the frozen river instead of the theater.

Day 7: The Traveler, Vesna, Odette and Vodyanitsa ambush the pair on the Everfrozen Earth. Danica, who followed them, appears and tells Vesna to end the farce. The Greater Sword Spirit sends its two followers away by spell and flees, but they return, and the Master of Sound, its "Disciple Four", gives it its power. Vesna acts the villain, retrieves the Master of Sound, revives it, and reveals her reason: unchecked wishes lead to disaster, and "guiding every fae" needs more than a gang of misfits. She sentences the group to study at the Druzhna garrison and to return the stolen half of the manual, and keeps the Master of Sound as a recruit.

Danica explains afterwards that Vila forge magical weapons by merging elemental energy with their own consciousness, so each sword spirit embodies a wish of Vesna's. She says the younger Vesna often declared she would guide lost fae onto the right path, and that she mellowed once she understood laws and discipline.

Revelations: The "Ancient Sword Esoterica" is not a real cultivation manual. A cutaway shows Mr. Nine at Yae Publishing House, with a collaborator, discussing a draft work of fiction whose author and researcher disagree over whether to keep its adepti hierarchy consistent; the draft was only circulated within the publisher and shelved. Vesna had bought the books in a clearance lot of Yae Publishing House stock. Post-quest, the Greater Sword Spirit admits it could not read all of the Liyue script and took gaps as hidden mysteries.

The sword spirits' personalities are Vesna's own repressed wishes (Danica's explanation). The two Volkodlak followers were roadside robbers for only a few days before the Greater Sword Spirit set them straight, so they have little record; Vesna lets them go. The "Divine Sense Compass" is ordinary elemental sensing; the incantation ("Spirit, roam the eight reaches!") was theatrical.

Characters: Vesna (Commander of the Druzhna), Danica (Her Majesty's head housemaid), Odette and Vodyanitsa of the Korolevskiy Theater, Blyushko, the Greater Sword Spirit and its followers "Second of the Pack" and "Third of the Pack", the Masters of Potions, Body, Sigils, Artifacts and Sound, Mr. Nine, the Traveler (Cryo) and Paimon.

Vesna is playful, impulsive and quick to cut corners, yet carries real responsibility and a firm sense of justice. Danica is stern and dry; she watches over Vesna's affairs. The Greater Sword Spirit is dramatic and speaks in cultivation-novel verses, but is loyal to its followers.

Consequences: Vesna's escaped sword spirits are all recaptured; the Master of Sound stays at her side, and the Greater Sword Spirit and its followers now help with Druzhna paperwork, in the Greater Sword Spirit's words, having laid down weapons and taken up the pen. Vesna learns the manual was fiction and the Druzhna avoid a larger scandal. The dispatch order gives her a sword spirit companion.

The Greater Sword Spirit says that guiding every fae onto the proper path is harder than it thought, which echoes Vesna's own history. Vesna and Danica's exchange also hints at how Vesna keeps much of her true self in check to set an example for the Druzhna.

Placement: Released in 7.1 (the first patch version after Snezhnaya's launch in 7.0), unlocked by completing White Night, Like a Dream Upon Waking. One part is available per day for seven days. Some dialogue changes after A Rekviem for the Underworld. A trial Vesna and Traveler (Cryo) are used in some steps.

851.comment: Swords and Secrets: Vesna's sword spirits
851.content: Vesna's sword spirits are semi-sentient flying swords she created while experimenting with a manual; each is drawn to a different "art" such as potions, body tempering, sigils, artifacts or sound. They are comic, grandiose and easily thwarted, and each embodies a wish of Vesna's. All are recaptured by the end, and the Master of Sound stays with her.

852.comment: Swords and Secrets: Ancient Sword Esoterica
852.content: A Liyue-style manuscript describing Sword Immortals who cultivate body and mind, command flying swords and nurture sword spirits. Vesna bought it cheaply from a rare-book dealer who had bought a clearance lot from Yae Publishing House; it is actually an unfinished novel by Mr. Nine, never printed.

853.comment: Swords and Secrets: Druzhna Special Dispatch Order
853.content: A quest reward item usable only by a player who owns Vesna; once used, a small green sword spirit flies beside Vesna whenever she is in her Coursing state, and cannot be turned off.

key: Tale of Dreams Plucked From Fire
elixir that can cure all injuries
854.comment: Tale of Dreams Plucked From Fire
854.content:
Tale of Dreams Plucked From Fire (also: Tracer No Tracing, Seeker No Finding, Chikya's treasure hunt, elixir that can cure all injuries): Both quests are lighthearted and character-driven. Chikya, a self-described Phlogiston Usage Tutor, uses ancient woven scrolls to lead the party past Phlogiston Engravings and Spiritdoors, relying on the Traveler's ability to read phlogiston directly. The goal she names, a cure-all elixir, is not what she finds; the Sage's gift is a spring that grants a chosen hero the power to wield phlogiston. Chikya herself, who cannot use phlogiston because of an old Abyss-related injury, gets nothing from it except a little back relief.

The series doubles as a short history lesson on how humans learned phlogiston, told from Chikya's partisan viewpoint, and as a small character study of someone who knows everything about a power she cannot use.

Plot: Tracer No Tracing. The quest begins in the Underground Lava River beneath the Ameyalco Waters Statue of the Seven, either by talking to Chikya or by defeating a Secret Source Automaton: Hunter-Seeker at the end of a hallway. Chikya's back seizes up as she meets the party, and she introduces herself with a joke about giving a fake name. She says she hunts treasure: an "elixir that can cure all injuries" described in a secret scroll, which she offers to split. She explains Phlogiston Engraving, a language of patterns that imitates how dragons controlled phlogiston, and says analysing one door would take her a day. The Traveler reads it directly with phlogiston and learns that an Unveiling Script is needed; the party finds one (a Koholasaurus can retrieve it) and the door half-opens. Deeper in, past a Spiritdoor and Spiritway among lava, they find a clay ring with phlogiston patterning that opens the way to the Upper Sanctum. This door needs three Unveiling Scripts, one of which is already lit, and the party gathers the rest. Chikya waits because of her back, and a Fluid Avatar of Lava guards one of them. They ride the Spiritway to the surface.

Seeker No Finding. Chikya admits she left her tribe without telling friends or family. At the Upper Sanctum, floating islands held up by phlogiston, she asks the Traveler to activate mechanisms while she consults her memory of the scrolls. Touching Iridescent Inscriptions makes them vanish, each with a short message. After a Spiritway trial, a previously hidden island appears at the centre. At a large stone tablet only the Traveler and Little One notice faint words and a golden pattern. Reaching out to it triggers a fight with Avatars of Lava. Afterwards the water in the spring is full of phlogiston and warm.

Chikya's scroll-reading gets partial credit. She correctly predicts the Spiritdoor and the existence of the trial, but doubts her memory when the mechanisms do not match her expectations, until the hidden central island shows she remembered correctly. In the first quest she is easily distracted by banter and quizzes the party, including on the name of the sage who stole the "flaming seed" of phlogiston. The ride back on the Spiritway is her first, and she suggests the Pyro Archon should install them everywhere.

Practical details. An optional note on a crate near the start records someone's failed attempts at the same cure: grinding Embercore Flower cores, applying powdered Iktomisaur claw-shell, bathing in the People of the Springs' hot springs ten times, and finally the trial of Xbalanque and the Sage of the Stolen Flame. It is not identified as Chikya's, though it suggests she is one of several seekers. The first quest awards the achievement "Like Floating Silk..." and the second gives "Hidden... Ahead" and "Not All Treasure Is Silver and Gold".

Revelations: - The Sage's gift at the Upper Sanctum is a hot spring that fills with phlogiston, which grants a chosen hero the ability to wield phlogiston; it is not a medical cure-all.
- When Paimon accuses her of knowing this, Chikya does not deny it: she says no single elixir could heal every injury and admits she tricked Paimon, framing it as a lesson.
- Chikya cannot use phlogiston at all, which is rare in Natlan. She blames a grave Abyss-related injury from early childhood.

- Per Chikya, tribespeople who could not already use phlogiston only ever learned by passing the trial, and the spring did nothing for her.
- The Iridescent Inscriptions at the Upper Sanctum are both the key and the trial: touching them reveals the hidden central island.
- Chikya says the Phlogiston Chiselith found across Natlan were modelled on the mechanisms of the Upper Sanctum.

Characters: Chikya is the main non-player character: a talkative woman of the Masters of the Night-Wind who looks after old woven scrolls and teaches children about phlogiston, with chronic back pain and a habit of awarding or deducting points for the Traveler's answers. Little One, the Tepetlisaurus companion, reacts and sometimes seems to sense where a Script is. Paimon asks the questions and gets teased. The Traveler is the one who reads and activates phlogiston.

Chikya is jokingly proud of her expertise, wants friends, and feels regret over not being able to use phlogiston. She dislikes being called "Aunt" and prefers "Big Sis". She mentions a friend who drifted away after a joke about swimming in lava. Her age and full background are not given.

Consequences: Chikya stays to rest in the spring and says that her back hurts less than after the People of the Springs' baths, though her real goal is still far off. The first quest rewards 250 Adventure EXP, 30 Primogems, 20,000 Mora, 2 Hero's Wit and 3 Mystic Enhancement Ore; the second gives 300 Adventure EXP, 40 Primogems, 30,000 Mora, 2 Hero's Wit, 3 Mystic Enhancement Ore and an Iridescent Inscription Fragment. Both grant 200 reputation with the People of the Springs.

No later quest in the sources continues Chikya's story. She remains optimistic and plans to go back to poring over scrolls for a cure and to face a scolding for leaving home.

Placement: Released in Version 5.0 as a Toyac Springs world quest series, starting at the Underground Lava River beneath Ameyalco Waters. Seeker No Finding follows Tracer No Tracing directly. No prerequisites are listed for either.

855.comment: Tale of Dreams Plucked From Fire: Chikya
855.content: Chikya is a Masters of the Night-Wind woman who tidies and studies ancient woven scrolls and calls herself a Phlogiston Usage Tutor. She cannot use phlogiston because of a severe childhood injury linked to the Abyss, which fuels both her scholarship and her regret. She is chatty, self-mocking and optimistic, wants to be called "Big Sis", and left her tribe without telling anyone to go on this hunt.

856.comment: Tale of Dreams Plucked From Fire: Phlogiston Engraving and Unveiling Scripts
856.content: In Chikya's account, Phlogiston Engraving is a language of patterns humans developed by imitating how dragons controlled phlogiston, after the Sage of the Stolen Flame stole its seed. Doors with engravings open when the required Unveiling Scripts, themselves engravings, are integrated. Scholars like Chikya can read them by comparing patterns over about a day; someone able to use phlogiston can read the meaning directly.

857.comment: Tale of Dreams Plucked From Fire: The Upper Sanctum trial
857.content: Called Hanan Pacha in the Natlan tongue, the Upper Sanctum is a group of floating islands held up by phlogiston and described by Chikya as a pure land of peace made by the first human to use phlogiston. The trial involves activating mechanisms and Iridescent Inscriptions with phlogiston, riding Spiritways and revealing a hidden central island, where a battle against Avatars of Lava closes the trial.

key: Encounter in the Realm of Dreams
858.content:
Tapirus Somniator Chapter (Yumemizuki Mizuki) (also: Tapirus Somniator, Yumemizuki Mizuki's Story Quest, Dream Eater's Melancholia, Encounter in the Realm of Dreams, Crisis at the Aisa Bathhouse, A Deceit Called Happiness, Descendant of Nightmares): The Tapirus Somniator Chapter is Yumemizuki Mizuki's Story Quest, released in Version 5.4, and as of 7.1 it has one act, Dream Eater's Melancholia. The Traveler meets Mizuki, a yumekui-baku who works as a clinical psychologist at the Aisa Bathhouse in Inazuma City, and helps her when a rival clinic draws away her patients. The rival's cheer turns out to have an inhuman source: a nightmare monster.

The act has five quests: Encounter in the Realm of Dreams, Crisis at the Aisa Bathhouse, A Deceit Called Happiness, Descendant of Nightmares and an Afterword. Much of it takes place in dreams. It is partly a comedy of bathhouse therapy and rivalry, and partly a study of what it costs Mizuki to digest other people's nightmares.
