Thoma then brings them into the Kamisato circle. Ayaka sends them to help three people who lost their Visions, and after seeing the harm first-hand the Traveler agrees to help the resistance by freeing the craftsman Masakatsu from the Tenryou Commission.

At Komore Teahouse Thoma jokingly poses as the dog Taroumaru and explains that the earlier tests were needed to see whether they could "change the lightning". He takes them to the Statue of the Omnipresent God, where the seized Visions are set into the structure. When the Traveler touches it they hear the wishes of the Visions' owners. At the Kamisato estate Ayaka, speaking from behind a screen, asks them to join the resistance. They again refuse, so she compromises: visit three people whose Visions were taken, and she will arrange a meeting with the Shogun.

The three visits take up the middle of the act. In Konda Village a Visionless samurai, Tejima, has forgotten why he stayed there; the Traveler helps him recover the memory that he was waiting for a lover, and he decides to keep waiting. In Inazuma City, a Tenryou Commission samurai, Kurosawa Kyounosuke, has forgotten the monthly emergency rations he gave to neighbours and is accused of withholding them; the Traveler finds that he had run up debts to a grocer, Aoi, to feed people, and he is left unsure whether he is good or bad. The third is Domon, a master of the Meikyou Shisui Art who seems possessed after losing his Vision. Lady Yae of the Grand Narukami Shrine finds he is not possessed: the Vision's aspirations had been covering the memory of what he had destroyed. Anzai, the senior disciple of Domon's old master whom Domon surpassed, has given up his own ambitions and urges Domon to pass his on to his students.

Back with Ayaka, who now meets them openly, the Traveler agrees to help. Ayaka explains the resistance's work, including making fake Visions to hand over in place of real ones. Their craftsman, Masakatsu, has been arrested. The Traveler meets Yoimiya at Naganohara Fireworks, who has been fooling the confiscators with a fake, and goes with her to the holding cells. Yoimiya sets off a firework "gift" to distract the guards, Kujou Sara arrives and reprimands the guards for torturing Masakatsu, then spots the rescuers and lets them go because he needs urgent care, while warning she will bring him back when he is recovered. The act ends with a group hot pot game at the teahouse, after Thoma mentions the Tenryou Commission has been tasked with a "ceremony".
Details of the middle quests. The Crystal Marrow scam works as a cycle: Keijirou's group buys all the Marrow and passes it to Werner, who sells the excess back to the association at a profit while being paid very little. Werner is afraid to confront the president, and tells the Traveler to deliver a ledger that Keijirou was burying. Harrison, an association member, demands more of Keijirou and names the commissioner aloud, which draws Katsuie into the scene.

Kurosawa's IOU box is the key evidence: the Treasure Hoarders who had been robbing him found only IOUs addressed to Aoi of Tsukumomono Groceries. Aoi says she would have accepted his prized sword as payment but he refused. He had threatened the men with that sword while feeling unable to follow through. Domon's disciple Junya is on high alert and hired Grand Narukami shrine maidens, one of whom, Inagi Hotomi, found no demon.

The act's three Vision stories show three different effects of confiscation: lost purpose (Tejima), lost sense of right and wrong (Kurosawa) and a return of suppressed guilt (Domon). The Traveler resolves none of them by force, only by helping someone remember or reframe. Kurosawa's account that the Raiden Shogun was disappointed by his "slacking" is told by him, not shown, so why he in particular lost his Vision is known only second-hand.

The act title is rendered by the wiki as roughly "The Immovable Narukami and the Eternal Paradise" in Chinese and Japanese, with Narukami as the Electro Archon's title.

Revelations: Thoma is a Kamisato Clan attendant, not just Beidou's business partner. Ayaka and the Kamisato resistance run fake-Vision operations against the Vision Hunt Decree. The Visions set into the Statue of the Omnipresent God are seized Visions, and the Traveler can hear their owners' aspirations. Lady Yae explains that a Vision gives aspirations and that losing it can bring back what those aspirations hid.

Kujou Sara, an enforcer of the decree, reprimands the guards for torturing Masakatsu and lets his rescuers go, though she says he will be brought back. Chisato reports that an arrogant-sounding woman visited and conspired with her father to keep the Traveler in Ritou.

Characters: The Traveler and Paimon are guests of Thoma and Ayaka. Beidou delivers them to Ritou. Thoma guides and tests them. Ayaka backs the resistance from behind the scenes and at first asks for help from behind a screen. Hiiragi Shinsuke and Chisato represent the port's authorities and the quiet dissent inside them. Lady Yae and Kujou Sara appear briefly, on different sides of the decree. Yoimiya is a firework maker who helps with the rescue.

Minor figures with their own small arcs: Kurisu (association president), Werner and Keijirou (the Marrow scam), Tejima, Kurosawa Kyounosuke, Aoi, Domon, his disciple Junya and his former fellow disciple Anzai, and Masakatsu.

Consequences: The Traveler stops refusing and commits to the resistance. Masakatsu is freed but Sara has said she will bring him back. The Tenryou Commission is tasked with a "ceremony", which the next act (Stillness, the Sublimation of Shadow) picks up.

Placement: Chapter II Act I, added in version 2.0. It follows Chapter I's final act (Autumn Winds, Scarlet Leaves) and precedes Stillness, the Sublimation of Shadow. Story order equals release order.

892.comment: The Immovable God and the Eternal Euthymia: Crystal Marrow tax scam
892.content: In Confessions of an Outlander the Kanjou Commission switches the International Trade Association's tax from Mora to Crystal Marrow, which nearly none of them knew. Scarcity pushes up both the price and the taxes. The Traveler traces the cycle to a corrupt officer, Keijirou, and a pressured merchant, Werner.

893.comment: The Immovable God and the Eternal Euthymia: Three Vision bearers
893.content: Ayaka's test: the Traveler helps Tejima of Konda Village, Kurosawa Kyounosuke of Inazuma City and the swordmaster Domon, each of whom has lost something with their Vision.

894.comment: The Immovable God and the Eternal Euthymia: Masakatsu's rescue
894.content: Masakatsu, the craftsman who makes the resistance's fake Visions, is held by the Tenryou Commission. The Traveler and Yoimiya break him out as Sara looks on and lets them go.

key: Song of the Welkin Moon Prelude
Song of the Welkin Moon: Prelude
895.content:
The Journey Home (also: Song of the Welkin Moon Prelude, Song of the Welkin Moon: Prelude): The act has three quests (Flamelets; Smoldering; Searing) and requires Adventure Rank 40. It follows "A Space and Time for You" and leads into "A Dance of Snowy Tides and Hoarfrost Groves". The Traveler is still struggling with what they have learned about their sibling. A sealed cryptex found beside Ineffa holds a message for the Traveler; her memories are blocked, and her core turns out to be linked to a Sovereign Lord of the ancient Secret Source. The act ends with Varka's letter pointing the Traveler to Nod-Krai and to a tavern called The Flagship.

Plot: **Flamelets.** At the Flower-Feather Clan, Chasca explains that Secret Source automatons have been attacking people nearby. The Traveler and Paimon help and find Ineffa on the shore, unconscious and surrounded by automatons; she is a machine, and she calls out for the Traveler and Paimon before waking. Beside her is a cryptex marked with a crude picture of the Traveler and Paimon. Xilonen, at the Children of Echoes workshop, finds the cryptex built from materials of many nations and cannot safely open it. Ineffa cannot recall her past, but cleans the workshop with a broom form of her arm, and malfunctions at an image of the first Baraka, firing Electro; Kinich arrives, and the caravan merchants who were looking for her explain that she is Ineffa, made by Aino, and that they come from Nod-Krai, where Fatui activity had stirred tension between religious groups.

**Smoldering.** The Traveler gives Ineffa a flower sent by the merchant's daughter Adieta, which triggers a memory of a woman who tells her to find a new place to belong across the sea. Ineffa asks Chasca what home means. Citlali explains the Thirteen Sovereign Lords, artificial minds made with Secret Source technology, and suspects Ineffa's core is the Eighth Lord, then the hostile Eleventh Lord. Ineffa disassembles attacking automatons and learns that the Fatui, led by a regiment connected to the Harbinger Sandrone ("Marionette"), forced them. The merchant Zhuoxin is revealed to be tied to the Fatui as an informant, and Ineffa is drawn into ruins that lead to the Lord's territory.

**Searing.** Beneath the ruins is the Temple of Cascading Colors. The Eighth Lord reveals that Ineffa is the benevolent half of a split Eleventh Lord; the malevolent half manipulated events to reclaim the core. Fatui under Velimiru chase them inside. Ineffa crushes the Eleventh Lord's core; when Velimiru revives her, Ineffa creates a new core, gains a Moon Wheel, and the group destroys her. The group escapes; the cryptex opens to a message from Varka.

Opening details: Ifa has examined a qucusaur Chasca brought; Ifa warns against forcing the cryptex open in case it self-destructs. While the group heads to Xilonen, a mysterious man watches them from above. Chasca expected Xilonen to be napping, but Xilonen has just dealt with an automaton issue with Mavuika and assumes the group has come about the same thing. Ineffa answers that she is not from Fontaine or Mondstadt despite liking Fontaine pastries and resembling a maid; Xilonen finds clockwork knee joints and a core from the Secret Source, but other materials from beyond Natlan. Xilonen identifies the poster as the first Baraka, a machine-breaker who tried to help humanity, killed herself when Och-Kan went insane, and whose workshop Ixquieh burned so Och-Kan could not use it against humanity; Chasca adds that her friend Lianca saved some of her work. When Ineffa malfunctions, a voice in her mind calls her a traitor for seeking a place to belong. Kinich explains that the merchants hired him to find her and that not every job he takes involves hunting. The merchants named in the act include Zhuoxin, Asimu and Aamu, who left Nod-Krai when the Fatui's actions there, described as pulling the moon down, threatened the Frostmoon Scions; Ineffa's amnesia worsened as they neared Natlan. Ajaw acts unnaturally cowed by Ineffa.

Middle details: three tribal children, Yatlan, Capac and Kotimy, are playing with Ineffa's small robot when Adieta tells them her family is returning to Liyue, her father Zhuoxin's hometown. Ineffa thanks Adieta in person before the family leaves for Liyue Harbor. Citlali says Kinich put Ajaw in timeout for three days. The Eighth Lord was close to Lianca and ruled the territory of today's tribe, but was executed by the other lords for raising Lianca; a curse makes any pro-human goodwill cause her crippling pain. The group later learns Citlali and Xilonen privately believed Ineffa might be the hostile Eleventh Lord who went mad and vanished after Xiuhcoatl was defeated, and might have to be taken out; Chasca stops this, saying she trusts Ineffa. Secret Source Automatons attack Zhuoxin's family while Fatui led by Velimiru watch; a voice tells Velimiru he is playing with fire, and he orders a retreat. The automaton says the Fatui seized its privileges, mentions the Mirror of the Dawning Morn and asks Ineffa to return the Eighth Lord's memory; Zhuoxin says he heard in Nasha Town that the Fatui regiment is run by Sandrone. Ineffa's small robot reports that Zhuoxin's picture was found at a Fatui stronghold.

Closing details: the ruins hold the Temple of Cascading Colors, built by Administrator 1; a service bot calls Ineffa Administrator 3, and Administrator 2 later sealed the facility. Zhuoxin, who says he spied for the Fatui for over ten years, is promised the waiver of a debt to the Northland Bank in exchange; he refuses a final device built to control Secret Source mechanisms. The Eighth Lord, who has waited more than two thousand years for Ineffa's return, tells her that the temple is where she was reborn, that the curse was one Ineffa placed on herself, and that after the war, defeated and stranded, the Eleventh Lord split into one personality that sought revenge on humanity and one that sought a new home; the latter became Ineffa, and the former, she says, perished. That account proves incomplete: the malevolent self survived and reveals that it manipulated events from the start; Lianca had caught on and imprisoned it in the facility for trying to destroy the benevolent self. When the Eleventh Lord is destroyed, she recognises Ineffa's Moon Wheel as made by the usurper and the three gods who abandoned them. After the group escapes, Aamu slaps Zhuoxin, and Chasca offers the family shelter at her tribe. In Varka's message, he thanks the Traveler for protecting Mondstadt in his absence, warns that the Abyss Order and the Fatui are making trouble in Nod-Krai along with struggles among other factions, and asks them to meet at The Flagship. Ineffa explains that a Moon Wheel works like a Vision but is more a power source than a mere elemental power, and plans to stay in Natlan for now but offers to return to Nod-Krai with the Traveler later.

The wiki summary also notes the act's quick-start entry through "A New Star Approaches" and a matching event, "The Journey Home (Event)". Details not in the main plot above: Kinich calls Ajaw out for acting timid, and Ajaw retorts that Kinich is the one who sent him into a stupor; the Fatui agents in the temple include an Anemoboxer Vanguard and a Fatui Agent, and named Fatui in the confrontation are Velimiru, Fajeyi and Gulebu. The service bot refers to a Secret Source Dragon Idol that carries the group down to the central zone. The Eleventh Lord is said to have lured Ineffa so she could reclaim the core, declaring that they will all have a new home, buried underground until the end of time. Velimiru, who turns out not to be human, briefly revives her with a replica core before she is finally destroyed. Ineffa's small robot takes part in the defence by raising a barrier on the Fatui.

Revelations: - Ineffa is an automaton whose core comes from the Secret Source's Sovereign Lords. According to the Eighth Lord, she is the benevolent half of the Eleventh Lord, split off after the ancient war; the hostile half survived separately and manipulated events to regain the core.
- The Thirteen Sovereign Lords were artificial minds created by the Pyro Sovereign with Secret Source technology, per Citlali (as relayed in the act summary).
- The Fatui regiment active in Natlan is said to be led by Sandrone ("Marionette") and to be interested in ancient history for "inference".
- According to the horrified Eleventh Lord, a Moon Wheel is something built by the usurper and the three gods who abandoned the Sovereign Lords; Ineffa gains one, appearing as an Electro Vision, when she creates a new core. Ineffa later describes it as working like a Vision but serving more as a power source.

Citlali's guesses change within the act: first the Eighth Lord, then the Eleventh Lord. Each guess is a reasonable inference from the automatons' behaviour and is not confirmed until the Eighth Lord speaks.

Characters: Ineffa is the central figure: an amnesiac maid-like automaton, made by Aino. Chasca of the Flower-Feather Clan, Xilonen, Citlali and Kinich help her; Mavuika is mentioned and appears at the end. Ajaw reacts oddly to her. Zhuoxin and his family are Nod-Krai merchants who guide the plot. The Fatui side is led by Velimiru, with Sandrone as the Harbinger behind the regiment. The Eighth Lord, who has waited for her and guides her through the temple, is an ally; the antagonist is the surviving malevolent half of the Eleventh Lord, Ineffa's own other self. Varka appears through his letter.

Consequences: Ineffa is no longer in the dark about herself and now has an Electro Moon Wheel. She stays in Natlan for the near term but is willing to travel to Nod-Krai with the Traveler. Zhuoxin's family is given shelter in Chasca's tribe. The Traveler holds Varka's message asking for a meeting at The Flagship in Nod-Krai and has learned about the Fatui and Abyss Order trouble there, leading into "A Dance of Snowy Tides and Hoarfrost Groves".

Placement: The prelude of the Song of the Welkin Moon chapter, released in version 5.8 per the wiki change history. Story-wise it sits between "A Space and Time for You" (Natlan, after the end of Chapter V) and "A Dance of Snowy Tides and Hoarfrost Groves"; it takes place in Natlan, before the crossing to Nod-Krai.

896.content:
The Last Survivor of Tenochtzitoc (also: Tenoyollotzin quest, Easybreeze Holiday Resort world quest, Lavawalker's Resolution quest): Behind the comedy are three threads: Enjou's search for the vanished Mare Jivari, Citlali's pursuit of him, and the legend of Tenoch, who let himself be eaten by Bakunawa to defeat it. The party learns that Papar was never the one speaking; Enjou, disguised in the costume, was reciting a script, then fled when Citlali arrived. Citlali and the Traveler follow Enjou's map to a cave and a woven scroll that opens a hall with memorial seats for the six heroes and Tenoch, and Enjou takes the chance to follow. Citlali binds a part of her spirit into Enjou in exchange for Papar's safety, and the Traveler fights Bakunawa with Enjou's body speaking for her. Enjou leaves them with a keepsake and a short, unreliable account of who he is.

The quest is the first of the post-summer 5.8 content to link the Mare Jivari investigation to the Masters of the Night-Wind and to the Muratans, and it leaves Enjou's motives and loyalties open. It also gives the Traveler an item of Enjou's, Lavawalker's Resolution, and begins a series of investigative reports on Bakunawa that can be collected again after waiting 72 hours.

Gameplay and side details: the Local Legend "The Last Survivor of Tenochtzitoc" disappears from his usual location from step 3 and is replaced by a notice sign. The quest rewards 450 Adventure EXP, 50 Primogems, 50,000 Mora, 5 Hero's Wit, 4 Mystic Enhancement Ore, the three Investigative Reports, Someone's Tattered Notes (I) and Lavawalker's Resolution, plus an Iktomi Scroll: Map for those who skipped The Spirit of Ah K'ulbatil. It grants the achievement "Until the Day That the Fires Turn Me Into Ashes" and the avatar The Scholar Who Crossed the Mare Jivari.

Plot: Tenoyollotzin. Near Wavey Bay, Paimon and the Traveler meet a Pipilpan-costumed man reciting a story about "Tenoyollotzin", Wanjiru and a snaggletoothed child. He treats Paimon as the insolent child and attacks. When his HP drops to 30 percent, Pucli stops the fight, and explains that the man is Papar, an on-site actor in the resort's Tenochtzitoc theme. Papar has been acting erratically and chanting a script. Pucli sedates him with a blowpipe dart, and with the party's help decides to look for a shaman while he looks into rumours of hidden spirits.

Leyla. The party finds Leyla, a young Masters of the Night-Wind shaman on holiday, and brings him to the spot where Papar first spoke. Using a ring of carrots as a divination medium, he sees an Asha on a swing, three Asha gathered around a woven scroll, then three fallen Asha in a burning wasteland approached by a man in a kimono. He reads this as Asha being connected to Papar's behaviour and gives the party his carrots, whose juice makes invisible Asha visible.

Asha and Citlali. Overnight Pucli reports that workers building the resort complained of missing materials and rippling water near the huts. The party finds and paints three hidden Asha, then meets Citlali, who has come for the man seen in Leyla's vision. She names him as Kokuchuu, who also used the alias Sanka, and Paimon identifies him as Enjou of the Abyss Order. Citlali has marked him with a spirit trace so she can sense him nearby. Back at the huts "Tenoyollotzin" suddenly calls Citlali an old lady. Citlali tears off the costume and finds nobody inside; Enjou had been in it. He watches from a cliff and complains that she is more of a nuisance than he is.

The cave. The party collects three investigative reports from Enjou's camp (on Bakunawa, the Mare Jivari and a secret cave). They follow Enjou's redrawn map to a cave behind a waterfall, where a woven scroll too old to work is revived by the Asha, who recognise Sanhaj's relic. It sends them to a hall unfamiliar to Citlali, where her connection to the Wayob is cut.

The hall. Memorial seats bear inscriptions to Tupac, Menilek, Sundjatta, Tenoch (whose remains are buried here), Wanjiru, Sanhaj Kompore (also buried here) and Burkina. Sanhaj's seat is empty. When the party places his relic on it, the central seat glows and the Traveler and Paimon vanish. Citlali stays behind to avoid trapping everyone and is met by Enjou, who followed through the same scroll. They trade barbs. Enjou offers Papar's safe return for passage to the Mare Jivari, and Citlali sets conditions (no vandalism, no harm to plants, protect the Traveler and Paimon) and has Itzpapa pin him while she splits part of her spirit into him.

The realm. The Traveler and Paimon arrive in a Night Kingdom-like place where the Wayob link is missing but the Abyss is still present. After a short trek they reach what looks like the Mare Jivari and find Enjou speaking in Citlali's voice, with her spirit attached to him. She gives them Sanhaj's ritual sword, the Calamity of Eshu, which she borrowed from the chief before leaving. Enjou argues for killing the beast ahead, which he identifies as Bakunawa's "permeation", saying that it will otherwise eat them and then spread into Natlan. Using the Calamity of Eshu, the Traveler blocks claw swipes, severs the creature's arms from its head and interrupts a charged attack with Soulshard Rain until it falls.

Aftermath. Enjou tries to scavenge, and when Citlali's voice stops him he tells his tale of a divided kingdom and Tenoch's people, drives her spirit out, and says that without Bakunawa's power the Traveler cannot enter the true Mare Jivari. He gives the Traveler a flower that glows in flames and walks deeper in. Citlali's voice returns briefly to ask for his real name and he promises to give it one day. Back in the hall Citlali says she will report to Mavuika, and that tablets behind the hall name former Pyro Archons. Papar is safe, sleeping off Aphimead on Tete Isle after Enjou befriended him as a tourist called "Hayne".

Details. Citlali's pursuit differs by branch: if the player has not done The Spirit of Ah K'ulbatil, Citlali says she got Sanhaj's relic and a map from a previous encounter with Enjou and gives them to the Traveler; if they have, she asks the Traveler to produce the items they were left earlier. In both cases she tells them that Enjou once tried to use Leyla for information about the Mare Jivari until Ororon stepped in. A throwaway joke has Citlali define "Ororon" in the Night-Wind Dictionary as a cultisham, a shaman who cultivates vegetables.

Revelations: - Bakunawa appeared in western Natlan about five hundred years ago with other Abyssal monsters, devouring the tribespeople of Tenochtzitoc. Citlali says it could not be killed, as its parts regrow and seek each other out.
- Tenoch let Sanhaj engrave phlogiston on his body to release border spells, then allowed himself to be eaten. With his body as offering, Sanhaj summoned a miniature Night Kingdom in Bakunawa's belly. The resulting clash among the Abyss's power, the Lord of the Night and Tenoch's spirit shattered the monster; some believe it never truly died.
- The Mare Jivari is described by Pucli as a land west of Tenochtzitoc born from the Abyssal invasion, where warriors became dust and souls were bound to it, until it vanished about twenty years ago. Asha appeared around then and are said to be "ashes" blown from it as well as "benevolent souls".

- The Investigative Report: Bakunawa describes it as an out-of-control creation of "Gold" whose immortality is not from the power of "Life" but a more transcendent Abyssal power. The Mare Jivari report says all records of its disappearance were erased and cites an ancient legend of a troupe wandering through "the blazing Mare Jivari" thousands of years ago, raising the possibility of a temporal disruption.
- Citlali says the hall was likely made by former Pyro Archons five hundred years ago to contain Bakunawa. Tablets mention a blocked Mare Jivari, holding back the Black Tide, an absent Kiongozi, and a Wind-Worn Booklet by Cochanina about sealing the borders across generations.
- Enjou says his remembered places (Vindagnyr, the Sunchildren, Gurabad, Moshiri Ceremonial Site, Remuria, the Vucub Caquix Tower and others) do not belong to him, and that the Abyss Order is not his home.

- Enjou claims in his story that Tenoch's people wielded Anemo, that their burial place was called the "Windless Land", and that kin who left 500 years earlier became the Muratans in Mondstadt. He frames the tale around a king (Xbalanque), his steadfast follower (Och-Kan), a civil war and two exile groups. These are presented as his account.
- A short note from Isaja reads "Task complete. Now I sing!", a more recent booklet in the hall.

Characters: Enjou drives most of the plot, charming, evasive and flexible about his principles. Citlali is protective, sharp-tongued and comically hostile to him, calling herself Granny Itztli. Pucli is the worried resort supervisor and childhood friend of Papar. Papar is the actor, never really present. Leyla is the young shaman who treats Ororon as his master and Citlali as a great shaman, and calls the Traveler "Master Gramps/Granny". Paimon and the Traveler carry the investigation.

Enjou masquerades as Papar's friend "Hayne" and as the costume's occupant; Citlali learns this only after the fight. Itzpapa and Citlalin, Citlali's spirit companions, assist her in the hall. The historical figures Tenoch, Sanhaj, Wanjiru, Menilek, Burkina, Sundjatta and Tupac appear in script, inscriptions and legend; Xbalanque and Och-Kan appear only in Enjou's tale.

Consequences: Enjou disappears into the deeper realm and Citlali's spirit trace on him is consumed by a strange power. Citlali plans to consult Mavuika, asks the party to keep the hall secret for now, and warns them not to go deeper. The Traveler keeps the Calamity of Eshu only for the duration of the visit and gets Lavawalker's Resolution, a flower from Enjou. Papar is found safe. The Mare Jivari mystery is unresolved.

After completion, Bakunawa can be fought again 72 hours later to yield Someone's Tattered Notes (II), and again 72 hours after that for Corroded Tattered Notes (III).

Placement: Released in 5.8. It requires completing A Curtain Call for a Colorful Summer Night! and begins in Wavey Bay at the Easybreeze Holiday Resort. The Spirit of Ah K'ulbatil, the earlier Leyla quest, changes some dialogue but is not required. There is no previous or next quest listed in the infobox.

897.comment: The Last Survivor of Tenochtzitoc: Papar
897.content: Papar is a resort actor who plays the hero Tenoch under the honorific "Tenoyollotzin", the honored heart of Tenochtzitoc. Pucli says he and Pucli are close friends whose mothers are friends, and that Papar has recently recited a script and acted erratically. The behaviour was really Enjou in the costume. Papar himself was drugged with Aphimead and left sleeping on Tete Isle, unharmed.

898.comment: The Last Survivor of Tenochtzitoc: Pucli
898.content: Pucli is the entertainment supervisor at the Easybreeze Holiday Resort. He sedates the "Tenoyollotzin" actor with a blowpipe, apologises constantly to guests, and worries mostly about facing Papar's mother. He explains the Asha and the Mare Jivari to the party.

899.comment: The Last Survivor of Tenochtzitoc: Asha
899.content: In Tenochtzitoc culture, per Pucli, "Asha" means both "benevolent soul" and "ashes" blown from the Mare Jivari. People believe they are Monetoo with a soul and treat them as more approachable. They appeared roughly when the Mare Jivari vanished. They follow the party out of affection for Sanhaj's relic and unlock the old woven scroll.

900.comment: The Last Survivor of Tenochtzitoc: Bakunawa
900.content: Bakunawa is a mountain-sized Abyssal beast that devoured Tenochtzitoc's people about five hundred years ago. It regrows from its pieces and was shattered only after Tenoch's sacrifice and Sanhaj's border spell. In the quest the party fights what Enjou calls its "permeation", a possibly partial form that has an immortality unlike other creations of "Gold" and a power Enjou says can corrupt time.

901.comment: The Last Survivor of Tenochtzitoc: Enjou's parting account
901.content: After the fight Enjou claims to know the history of lost places and the people of Tenochtzitoc, says he serves the Abyss Order but that it is not his home, and asks where the Traveler's home is. His story of exiles and the Muratans is deliberately told to distract Citlali, and whether any of it concerns himself is left open.

key: The Moon-Bathed Deep World Quest series
902.content:
The Moon-Bathed Deep (also: The Moon-Bathed Deep World Quest series, Goshou Rocks seals quest): The series has six quests: the opening The Moon-Bathed Deep and then "Eye of Watatsumi", "Fang of Watatsumi", "Fin of Watatsumi", "Tail of Watatsumi" and "Heart of Watatsumi". Tsuyuko of the Sangonomiya Shrine wants the barrier to Enkanomiya opened so that a Jade Coral Branch can be fetched for a ritual meant to halt the Holy Soil bleaching of the island. The Traveler gathers a Spirit Pearl from each of the first four seals, then opens the Heart with Tsuyuko and obtains the key. The series ends with the descent to Enkanomiya still waiting on the Divine Priestess's approval and the right spirit-vein flow, and leads into The Still Water's Flow.

Tone: Tsuyuko is cheerful, self-aware about asking outsiders for help and openly sceptical of folklore, so the series mixes shrine tradition with a practical worry about Watatsumi's land. "The Moon-Bathed Deep" is also the name of the pool under the Sangonomiya Shrine that serves as the entrance to Enkanomiya, which is unlocked during The Still Water's Flow.

Plot: Tsuyuko at Mouun Shrine. During their travels in Inazuma the Traveler and Paimon reach Watatsumi Island. Tsuyuko, a Sangonomiya Shrine maiden, immediately asks for help, saying a divination promised that help would arrive whenever she was in trouble. The Traveler and Paimon are unimpressed by the manner of asking but hear her out.

The problem. She explains that the deep pool opposite the shrine leads to Enkanomiya, and that Watatsumi tradition holds the people's ancestors once lived there. Because the island's spirit is said to be drawn toward the depths, the soil is bleaching into Holy Soil and may one day turn to a pale desert. The remedy is a ritual using a Jade Coral Branch left by the Omikami, which means breaking the barrier and diving to Enkanomiya. Taking such a branch could weaken the suppression of the Dragonheir of the Depths, so the matter is risky.

The commission. For now Tsuyuko asks only that the Traveler visit the Goshou Rocks, five barrier nodes set by the founding clergy and the Omikami: the Eye on the island to the west, the Fang on the northwest coast, the Fin on the north coast and the Tail on the eastern shoal. The Heart is opened with the four Spirit Pearls. She admits the rite for breaking the seals is mostly forgotten, that the Divine Priestess has no time for a grand ceremony, and that an outlander is a convenient person to take the risk.

The four seals. These quests can be done in any order. Each has a nearby stone tablet whose weathered text hints at the solution.
- Eye: the tablet speaks of the Omikami's envoy with three eyes. The Traveler uses Elemental Sight to find three elemental orbs and dispels them; specters and slimes are drawn by the released energy.
- Fang: the tablet speaks of provoking battle and taking the spoils. The Traveler defends a Ley Line Monolith against five waves of hilichurls, Nobushi and Treasure Hoarders.
- Fin: the tablet speaks of two retainers greeting each other like scale and fin. The Traveler turns fish statues on discs to face each other and activates a Mysterious Pillar.
- Tail: the tablet demands slow, quiet, pious movement along the lights. The Traveler lights six Electric Lamps with an Electrogranum, then Fatui skirmishers ambush them.

The Heart. Back at the Sangonomiya Shrine, Tsuyuko joins the Traveler and Paimon. Using the four Spirit Pearls they open the seal to the Heart, a water cave where, Tsuyuko says, the Omikami once stayed and where now only the sound of water remains. The fish-statue puzzle appears on several platforms, now with Hydro Mimics emerging after each alignment and three more waves after the last. When it is solved, water gathers into the Key of the Moon-Bathed Deep.

Afterwards. Tsuyuko, briefly lost in thought, says the key is needed to open the entrance to Enkanomiya and that legend claims it was forged from the Omikami's spilled blood. They still need the Divine Priestess's approval and the right spirit-vein flow before descending. She thanks them with the lasting friendship of the shrine and says she expects to meet them again when it is time.

Tsuyuko's explanations to the Traveler (extra dialogue at the shrine). She says the Goshou Rocks are named for the skeleton of an envoy of the Omikami, over which the clergy placed a seal; on the island's map the western bulge is the Eye and the south-eastern extension is the Tail, and she admits she finds the explanation hard to accept too. She also gives her own view of Holy Soil, drawn from knowledge gained at the Sumeru Akademiya: seawater encroaching on land leaves salts that leach nutrients away, while the Jade Coral Branches replenish the missing elements. Tradition says the shrine's suppression and the Omikami's power inherited by the Divine Priestess keep the Holy Soil from spreading across the rest of the island.

Gameplay details, labelled as such. The Eye, Fang, Fin and Tail are independent of each other. The Fang can be done in Co-Op mode and its monolith timer shortens with each kill. The Heart has three platforms done in any order, then a fourth with three waves of Hydro Mimics. Players note a Latin inscription, Ad Virtutem, on the seals. Completing the series grants the achievement The Same Moonlight and rewards of Primogems, Mora and Hero's Wit; the Heart also gives Mystic Enhancement Ore, Inazuma reputation and the key itself. A Precious Chest near the Heart contains furnishing blueprints.

Revelations: - The deep pool opposite the Sangonomiya Shrine is the entrance to Enkanomiya, and the Watatsumi people claim descent from those who lived there, in Byakuyakoku.
- The island's soil bleaching (Holy Soil) is tied in tradition to Enkanomiya drawing on the island's spirit; Tsuyuko offers a sober alternative explanation.
- The Goshou Rocks are five seal nodes, four of which yield Spirit Pearls that open the fifth.

- Tsuyuko's account: Byakuyakoku survived on the faint light of the Dainichi Mikoshi against the Dragonheir of the Depths, until the Watatsumi Omikami defeated it a few thousand years ago and led the people to dry land, where Sangonomiya was founded; the underwater land was then renamed Enkanomiya.
- According to records Tsuyuko cites but does not trust, the Spirit Pearls answer someone pure and the key comes together only for a person whose heart is as clear as water.

Characters: Tsuyuko, the Traveler and Paimon. The Divine Priestess (Sangonomiya Kokomi) is discussed but does not appear.

Tsuyuko is courteous and rueful about imposing, with a taste for tours, folklore and digressions. Enemies met are Fatui skirmishers at the Tail and, elsewhere, hilichurls, Nobushi, Treasure Hoarders, specters, slimes and Hydro Mimics.

Consequences: The Traveler holds the Key of the Moon-Bathed Deep and has earned the goodwill of the Sangonomiya Shrine. The barrier to Enkanomiya stays in place until the Divine Priestess approves and the spirit veins flow correctly. The next quest in the chapter is The Still Water's Flow.

The Jade Coral Branch ritual is still pending at the end of the series.

Placement: Released in Version 2.1 as part of the Watatsumi Island content. It requires completing the Archon Quest A New Star Approaches and, to reach the starting location, Ritou Escape Plan. It is followed by The Still Water's Flow, which opens the way into Enkanomiya.

903.content:
The Goshou Rocks are five barrier nodes called the Eye, Fang, Fin, Tail and Heart, set up by the founding Sangonomiya clergy with the Omikami to separate Watatsumi Island from Enkanomiya. Four hold Spirit Pearls and the fifth opens only when all four are given. Tsuyuko says the ritual for breaking them is mostly forgotten, and the stone tablets beside each are barely legible.

Per Tsuyuko the seals were placed on the skeleton of an envoy of the Omikami, which explains the body-part names. The Eye is on the island to the west, the Fang on the northwest coast, the Fin on the north coast and the Tail on the eastern shoal.

904.content: A Sangonomiya Shrine maiden who used to give guided tours to visitors of Watatsumi Island. She asks the Traveler for help, is sceptical of folk legend, and mentions knowledge gained at the Sumeru Akademiya. She trusts her fortune slips and says she is sure the Traveler will return when it is time to descend to Enkanomiya. She has no separate entry in this archive; here she is the series' quest giver.

905.comment: The Moon-Bathed Deep: Key of the Moon-Bathed Deep
905.content: The key forms from water in the Heart of Watatsumi after the final seal is broken, and is needed to open the entrance to Enkanomiya. Tsuyuko says legend has it forged from the Omikami's spilled blood, though she does not usually believe such records. The Spirit Pearls are the four items from the Eye, Fang, Fin and Tail seals that open the Heart.

906.comment: The Morn a Thousand Roses Brings
906.content:
The Morn a Thousand Roses Brings (also: Chapter III Act II, Sumeru Archon Quest Act II, The Coming of the Sabzeruz Festival, The Arrival of the Sabzeruz Festival, The Continuation of the Sabzeruz Festival, The Samsara of the Sabzeruz Festival, The Causality of the Sabzeruz Festival, The Empty Illusions of the Sabzeruz Festival): The second act of Sumeru's Archon Quest. During the Sabzeruz Festival in Sumeru City, the Traveler and Paimon find the same day repeating. A mysterious girl named Nahida restores their memories, tells them it is a "samsara" and that the real Dunyarzad, a gravely ill festival-lover, weakens with each cycle, and asks them to break it. The loop turns out to be a collective dream built by the Akademiya's Akasha, and it ends only when the dreamer at its centre, Nilou, realises she is dreaming and performs the Dance of Sabzeruz.

The act has eight quests: The Coming, The Arrival, The Continuation, The Samsara, The Causality, The Empty Illusions and The End of the Sabzeruz Festival, plus the denouement Dawn. It is the point at which the story shifts from a puzzle about a missing god to a direct clash with the Akademiya, and where Nahida is first revealed to be Lesser Lord Kusanali, the Dendro Archon.

The act is structured like a time-loop mystery: each quest is one more repeated day, and the Traveler's progress is made by testing a theory per day and carrying the result forward through recorded messages, since memories reset.

Plot: During the Sabzeruz Festival in Sumeru City, the Traveler and Paimon help the ailing festival-lover Dunyarzad and the bodyguard Dehya. Grand Sage Azar and his secretary Setaria shut the festival down just before Nilou's Dance of Sabzeruz, and the morning then repeats. The Traveler follows a strange girl to the Bimarstan and meets Nahida, who restores their memories, explains the "samsara" and shows that the real Dunyarzad is fading with every loop. With Dehya's help they test theories day by day (terminal removal, memory erasure, leaving the city) and use recorded messages to learn that the Akasha harvests users' dreams and that the samsara is a collective festival dream.

The real Dunyarzad's consciousness vanishes and Nahida leaves to save it. The Traveler identifies Nilou as the dream's host; she realises she is dreaming, dances the Dance of Sabzeruz as the dream dissolves, and everyone wakes. In the denouement Nahida, speaking through Katheryne's puppet, is revealed as Lesser Lord Kusanali, shut in the Sanctuary of Surasthana for five hundred years, and says the words "World... forget me" came from Rukkhadevata.

In detail.

The Traveler and Paimon return to the Grand Bazaar and tell Dunyarzad about their trouble at Port Ormos. She lets them rest, then guides them around the festival venues (including Vihar's stall, where visitors pick a mystery box of Yalda Candy flavours). Eremite mercenaries try to seize Dunyarzad for ransom, and Dehya holds them off alone, ending up hurt because she is not yet used to a new greatsword, having sold her old one to fund the festival. Resting, Dunyarzad admits she was born with Eleazar, that it is now terminal, and that she is giving everything to the festival so she will have no regrets. They hurry back for the Dance of Sabzeruz, but Grand Sage Azar and his secretary Setaria shut the festival down in front of Nilou, citing legal violations and banning public art performances from the next Jnagarbha Day. Elsewhere, a beeping sound is heard, and Khajeh says the project is entering its most critical phase.

The morning then repeats. The Traveler feels déjà vu, finds an unfamiliar-looking snack tastes familiar, sees Dunyarzad seem a little weaker than before, and watches Azar and Setaria close the festival again. The project's "Jnana Energy" output is noted to be dropping.

On the third day the Traveler has memorised the mystery boxes, abandons the festival to chase a strange girl and ends up in the Bimarstan, where a second Dunyarzad lies in bed. The girl, Nahida, restores their memories of the loops and explains that only they, thanks to their Dendro-linked constitution, can perceive her. The bedridden Dunyarzad is the real one, fading with each cycle while Nahida slows her illness. Nahida cannot simply tell them the cause without, as she puts it, literally blowing their minds, so they must find it themselves. They recruit Dehya, who cannot see Nahida but senses Dunyarzad's aura and believes them, and she correctly deduces that the sages are using the Akasha to cause the samsara, suspecting they are extracting knowledge from its users to make one massive collective brain. Taking their terminals off does not help: they hear the beep and lose consciousness. Khajeh warns that casualties are likely, and Azar decides to continue.

The next days eliminate theories. Removing the terminal fails; so does the idea that memories are simply erased, because Dehya's training dummy shows details the sages could not recreate for every loop. The pair conclude they are not in the real world and test leaving the city. Their memories of leaving vanish each time, so Nahida modifies the Traveler's Akasha Terminal to record messages. The recordings reveal that the Akasha gathers its wisdom by taking its users' dreams, which arise in a phase of sleep with heavy brain activity, and that the sages' claim that dreams are harmful is a cover. The samsara is a shared dream of the festival in which users keep "waking" to a new day while their emptied dreams are harvested. The Traveler also works out that Nahida is Lesser Lord Kusanali.

The real Dunyarzad's consciousness can no longer withstand the harvesting and vanishes; the one in the festival is a puppet. Nahida leaves the city to find a way to rescue Dunyarzad. The Traveler's first guess at the dream's host is wrong, but a book of folk legends the puppet Dunyarzad compiled for them leads to the remembered Dance of Sabzeruz. When the Traveler interrupts Azar and Setaria confronting Nilou, they stop responding, as they are only puppets. True purple padisarah flowers confirm that Nilou is the host. Linking it to the tale of the First Sage, Nilou realises she is dreaming, begins to wake, and dances the Dance of Sabzeruz while the dreamscape dissolves and Dunyarzad's spirit appears in the crowd. The Traveler and Paimon wake up free, remove their terminals, and find Dunyarzad alive at the Bimarstan with Katheryne.

In the denouement, that "Katheryne" is Nahida, speaking through the Snezhnayan puppet's Akasha Terminal because she has been unable to leave the Sanctuary of Surasthana for five hundred years. She explains how she saved Dunyarzad's consciousness and answers some of the Traveler's questions as thanks. She says the words "World... forget me" were left by Greater Lord Rukkhadevata, whose consciousness was contaminated by something dangerous, and that the Traveler encountering them without going mad gives her hope of curing Irminsul. The sages removed their terminals to prevent leaks; she means to look into how and punish them if necessary. Exhausted, she leaves Katheryne's body, and the real Katheryne wakes confused away from her post.

Details that matter in play: Dehya's left arm is bandaged after the first mercenary fight and the injury is gone in the Samsara quest, which is how the Traveler tells that a loop has changed; the injury is one of few in-game model changes. In the fourth quest Dehya forgets the previous loop but finds her new greatsword oddly familiar, raising false hopes. The wiki notes that a later quest gives the total as 168 cycles, roughly five and a half months of days. The quests' Chinese titles are, per the wiki, likely references to chapter titles of the visual novel Steins;Gate, and the act title echoes a quatrain of Omar Khayyam's Rubaiyat.

Revelations: - The Akademiya's Akasha runs on harvested dreams; the sages' public line that dreams are harmful is a falsehood that hides this.
- The Sabzeruz samsara is a shared dream built from the minds of Akasha users in Sumeru City. Its host, the person who must realise they are dreaming for it to break, is Nilou.
- Nahida is Lesser Lord Kusanali, the Dendro Archon, imprisoned in the Sanctuary of Surasthana for five hundred years and able to act only through an Akasha Terminal.
- The words "World... forget me" were left by Greater Lord Rukkhadevata, and forbidden knowledge contaminated her consciousness.

Dunyarzad was born with Eleazar, and its terminal stage motivates her devotion to the festival. The Akademiya's top figures (Azar, Setaria, Khajeh) are shown to know about the project and to accept casualties; Azar calls the sacrifices trivial relative to the goal.

Characters: Traveler and Paimon drive the investigation. Nahida appears as a girl only they can see, and later possesses Katheryne's body. Dunyarzad, a young woman with a terminal illness, is the emotional centre; a real and a puppet version both appear. Dehya is the Traveler's reluctant ally and bodyguard to Dunyarzad. Nilou is the festival's dancer and the unwitting dream host. Azar (Grand Sage) and Setaria (his secretary) shut the festival down; Khajeh is heard discussing the project's progress with Azar. Vihar runs a stall, and Eremite mercenaries attack the group.

Azar and Setaria are puppets inside the dream, not the real sages. The real Setaria, a desert-born prodigy, is developed in later acts.

Consequences: In Act III (Dreams, Emptiness, Deception), Nahida, again speaking through Katheryne, says she wants to resolve matters with the sages before turning to Irminsul and The Withering. Dunyarzad recovers in the real world but remembers nothing of the loop except Nilou's dance.

Labelled as later consequences: in Act V, Nahida removes the contaminated remnants of Rukkhadevata from Irminsul and shuts the Akasha down; with the forbidden knowledge gone, Eleazar disappears and Dunyarzad is cured, and she attends the victory feast with Dehya. Earlier, in Act III, Setaria is pushed to reveal that the story of King Deshret's resurrection was an Akademiya misinformation campaign, and she agrees to work against the sages.

Placement: Chapter III, Act II. Released in Version 3.0 (the Sumeru launch). The previous act is Through Mists of Smoke and Forests Dark; the next is Dreams, Emptiness, Deception, then King Deshret and the Three Magi and Akasha Pulses, the Kalpa Flame Rises. Story order and release order match.

907.comment: The Morn a Thousand Roses Brings: Dunyarzad and the real and puppet selves
907.content: Dunyarzad is a festival enthusiast who donated heavily to revive the festival and says she wants no regrets when her terminal Eleazar claims her. In the samsara there are two of her: a bedridden real one at the Bimarstan whose consciousness is eroded each cycle, and a puppet who repeats the festival day and keeps the loop going. The puppet gives the Traveler a book of folk legends and echoes a line the real Dunyarzad once said, which points to the dance she most wanted to see. After the samsara the real Dunyarzad is found alive, remembering only the dance.

908.comment: The Morn a Thousand Roses Brings: Dance of Sabzeruz and Nilou
908.content: The Dance of Sabzeruz is the festival's central performance, which Nilou is forbidden from giving by the Grand Sage. In the dream, Nilou is the host; once she connects a tale of the First Sage to her situation, she realises she is dreaming, and her performance of the dance as the dream dissolves ends the loop. The purple padisarah flowers present in the dream are the clue that she is the host.

909.comment: The Morn a Thousand Roses Brings: Dream harvesting
909.content: The Traveler's recorded messages show that the Akasha works by taking users' dreams during the active phase of sleep, and that the sages' talk of dreams being harmful is a lie. Jnana Energy output is tracked by the project and dips as the loops continue. Taking the terminal off does not stop the samsara. The sages, per Nahida, later remove their own terminals so nothing leaks.

910.comment: The Morn a Thousand Roses Brings: Nahida's first appearance
910.content: Nahida first appears as a small girl only the Traveler and Paimon can see, because of their Dendro connection. She deliberately withholds answers to protect their minds. In the denouement she is revealed to be Kusanali, imprisoned in the Sanctuary of Surasthana for five hundred years; she speaks through Katheryne's puppet body. She calls the Traveler's immunity to the forbidden knowledge a hope for curing Irminsul.

key: The Outlander Who Caught the Wind
911.comment: The Outlander Who Caught the Wind
911.content:
The Outlander Who Caught the Wind (also: Prologue Act I, Prologue: Act I, Stormterror crisis Act I): This is the first act of the Prologue chapter of the Archon Quest. After an unknown entity seals the twins' powers and separates them, the Traveler wakes in Teyvat, rescues Paimon from the sea near Cape Oath and decides to seek the Seven in the hope that one of them can help find the lost sibling. In Mondstadt's wilds they touch an Anemo Statue of The Seven, see the dragon Stormterror, are escorted by the Outrider Amber, and are taken to the Knights of Favonius, who ask them to tackle the disrupted Ley Line energy around the Four Winds' temples. The act doubles as the game's tutorial for movement and combat.

Narratively the act sets up three threads that the next two acts pay off: the stranger who keeps appearing near the dragon, the red teardrop crystal the Traveler is left with, and the Knights' handling of the crisis under Jean, who leads as Acting Grand Master because, as Kaeya explains, the Grand Master is away leading an expedition.

Plot: **Opening.** As the Traveler and their twin are about to leave a world, an unknown being confronts them. In the fight it seals the sibling, then the Traveler, and the Traveler's abilities are locked away. The Traveler eventually wakes in Teyvat after an undisclosed length of time.

**Meeting Paimon.** Near Cape Oath the Traveler fishes Paimon out of the water. She becomes their companion and guide and suggests contacting the Seven to find the missing sibling.

**The dragon and the stranger.** At Starfell Lake the Traveler touches the Anemo statue and both see a green dragon flying toward a forest. In the forest they find the dragon and a stranger trying to calm it. Because of a reaction triggered by the Traveler's new powers the dragon notices them; the stranger flees, leaving a crimson teardrop crystal that the Traveler takes.

**Amber and the glider.** Outside the forest the scout Amber, Outrider of the Knights of Favonius, offers to escort them to Mondstadt after clearing a nearby hilichurl camp, which the Traveler and Paimon help with. Impressed, she gives them a Wind Glider.

**Stormterror attacks.** After a test flight the dragon, which the locals call Stormterror, rampages and raises storms. The Traveler, helped without knowing it by the stranger, drives it off.

**The Knights.** Kaeya, Cavalry Captain, notices the fight and sends the newcomers to Acting Grand Master Jean at the Knights' headquarters. Jean asks them to handle Ley Line disruption at three of the Four Winds' temples, as advised by Lisa, the librarian. After the temples are dealt with Paimon proposes returning to headquarters.

The wiki lists the act's quests as Bird's Eye View, Unexpected Power, Forest Rendezvous, Wind-Riding Knight, Going Upon the Breeze, City of Freedom, Dragon Storm and Knights of Favonius, followed by three optional character quests that may be done in any order: Winds of the Past (Amber), Crash Course (Kaeya) and Sparks Amongst the Pages (Lisa). Together with the preceding Wanderer's Trail it forms the opening tutorial.

Extra detail: Wanderer's Trail is the act's formal prerequisite. In the Knights of Favonius quest Lisa explains that the dragon whips up its storms by drawing power from the abandoned Four Winds' Temples, and Jean sets the objective of dealing with three of the four, after which three optional quests with Amber, Kaeya and Lisa can be done in any order. The stranger's identity and the dragon's name are held back until the next act. The Chinese title translates as "The Foreigner Who Catches the Wind".

Revelations: - The Traveler and their twin travel between worlds and were intercepted and sealed by an unnamed entity before arriving in Teyvat.
- The Traveler's powers are sealed; Paimon is introduced as the one who guides them.
- The dragon terrorising Mondstadt is known locally as Stormterror and its attacks are powered by disrupted Ley Line energy.
- A stranger (later revealed as Venti, in the next act) tries to calm the dragon; the red crystal he leaves matters later.

In this act the Traveler does not yet know that the dragon is Dvalin, one of the Four Winds. That identification and the stranger's identity belong to the next act (see quest.for-a-tomorrow-without-tears).

Characters: Traveler and Paimon (protagonists), Amber (Outrider, the first Knight they meet), Kaeya (Cavalry Captain who notes the fight), Jean (Acting Grand Master), Lisa (Librarian, advises on the temples), Venti (the unnamed stranger seen near the dragon) and the dragon Stormterror, Dvalin. The sibling and the sealing entity appear only in the opening.

Consequences: The Traveler is accepted by the Knights as an ally in the dragon crisis and has a Wind Glider for travel. The act hands over the crystal and the open questions of the stranger and dragon to Act II.

Placement: First act of the Prologue (release 1.0), directly followed by For a Tomorrow Without Tears and Song of the Dragon and Freedom. It is entered after the Wanderer's Trail prelude.

912.comment: The Outlander Who Caught the Wind: Stormterror (Act I view)
912.content: In Prologue Act I the green dragon is known to Mondstadt's people only as Stormterror, a rampaging storm-bringer. The Knights do not yet connect it to the Four Winds. It attacks after the Traveler tests the glider, and is driven off with help from the unnoticed stranger. Its true identity as Dvalin is explained in the following acts.

913.comment: The Outlander Who Caught the Wind: Amber's Wind Glider gift
913.content: After the Traveler and Paimon help Amber clear a hilichurl camp, she gives them a Wind Glider, which lets them travel by air. A test flight is interrupted by Stormterror's attack.

914.content:
The Rainbow Destined to Burn (also: Chapter V Act IV, Natlan Archon Quest Act IV): The act has six quests: Beneath the Secret Source, As One We Watch the Setting Sun, The Surging Darkness, Despair Engulfs the Heavens, No One Fights Alone and A Fuel Named "Fate". It follows Act III, Beyond the Smoke and Mirrors, and precedes Act V, All Fires Fuel the Flame. It requires Adventure Rank 40. It is the point where Natlan's war with the Abyss becomes open, nation-wide fighting, and where the six Ancient Name bearers of Mavuika's plan are finally assembled.

Thematically the act sets two answers to hopeless odds against each other: Capitano's insistence on whatever maximises survival, even at the price of using a Gnosis-like source of power, and Mavuika's refusal to give her people a victory that would make their lives meaningless. The act also explains Natlan's Ley Line problem, the nature of the Lord of the Night and Capitano's backstory in Natlan.

Plot: Mavuika, Xilonen, Kinich and the Traveler raid a Fatui base and shut down the Source Mechanism that Capitano and Ororon activated; Ororon's Ancient Name appears and the Lord of the Night explains Natlan's Ley Lines. Mavuika refuses her offer to rebuild them at the cost of her life, and Capitano agrees to join the fight. The Fatui are welcomed into the alliance and the Lord of the Night makes the Pilgrim's Chronicle for the Traveler. The Abyss then launches a nation-wide invasion; Chuychu dies and Chasca's Ancient Name appears, completing the six heroes, and Mavuika leads the six in a ritual declaring a Night Warden War. The defenders then counter-attack, and Mavuika destroys the rift and drives the Abyss into the Night Kingdom, then plans to go there alone while Citlali warns that she is still fated to die.

Quest by quest.

**Beneath the Secret Source.** In the Speaker's Chamber Mavuika reports that Capitano has been located. Citlali tells her what she learned from Ororon's memories: his plan, with Capitano, to activate a Source Mechanism is as dangerous as using a Gnosis, and must be stopped. Mavuika, Xilonen, Kinich with Ajaw, and the Traveler plan an attack: Kinich and Ajaw draw off the Fatui in a frontal assault while Xilonen leads the others through a tunnel to the device. Ororon starts the Source Mechanism and is suddenly overtaken by an unknown presence which Capitano subdues, while the Traveler turns the device off. Ororon, in his own memory space, resists a Khaenri'ahn soul named Guthred and his Ancient Name appears, revealing the hero Sanhaj as the fifth bearer. The Lord of the Night, Yohualtecuhtin, speaks from the cavern, explains the Source Mechanism and Natlan's Ley Lines, and offers to rebuild them at the cost of her existence. Mavuika refuses and Capitano reluctantly agrees to cooperate, lending his troops and aid.

**As One We Watch the Setting Sun.** Mavuika welcomes the Fatui into the alliance. Capitano explains how he found the Source Mechanism and why he knew of the Gnosis' power, and Mavuika says her opinion has not changed. Xilonen and Citlali visit the Lord of the Night about giving the Traveler an Ancient Name, which will cost the Name Engraver her life, and about Mavuika's foreseen death; the Lord creates the Pilgrim's Chronicle, a parchment recording the Traveler's deeds in Natlan. The Abyss attacks again.

**The Surging Darkness.** The Abyss, sensing the change in Ororon, intensifies attacks across Natlan. Mavuika sends the heroes to their tribes and the Traveler to handle matters nation-wide by hot air balloon. At a checkpoint near the stadium, a surge around the Sacred Flame drops pylons that release Abyssal hilichurls and riftwolves, and Mavuika briefly subdues the rift with the Gnosis.

**Despair Engulfs the Heavens.** The invasion begins to overwhelm Natlan. The Traveler sees the dead of both humans and Saurians, helps defend a camp in the Sulfurous Veins and investigates a tumour-like object that has fallen from the sky. Tumours fall across the nation, the evacuation of the Children of Echoes is helped, and the Traveler finds Chasca and Chuychu. Chuychu, contaminated by Abyssal energy, wakes after the Traveler purifies it but dies of her wounds after saying goodbye. In her grief Chasca's Ancient Name appears, bearer Menilek, making her the sixth hero. With all six heroes (Mualani, Kinich, Xilonen, Iansan, Ororon and Chasca) gathered at the heart of the stadium, Mavuika, invoking her name Haborym, declares a Night Warden War, extending the Ode of Resurrection to all Natlanese.

**No One Fights Alone.** The heroes destroy the tumours and defend the stadium from attempts to extinguish the Sacred Flame, and Mavuika destroys the rift. Her blast briefly exposes a "false sky", which no one pays attention to.

**A Fuel Named "Fate".** At a feast at the Weary Inn, Mavuika says the Abyss has been forced deep into the Night Kingdom and that she will go there alone to finish it. She tells the Traveler she regrets not saving Chuychu. Citlali warns the Traveler that using Ronova's power still means Mavuika is fated to die. Mavuika explains that the Traveler is the only known person resistant enough to the Abyss to accompany her, but only if their Ancient Name is complete; Paimon would have to stay behind. Elsewhere Capitano speaks to the Lord of the Night, aware that Mavuika's use of Ronova's power will cost her life, and says he has his own final foe to face.
Further details. In Beneath the Secret Source, Kinich and Xilonen advise against fighting Capitano again because Mavuika has lost the power to fuel the Sacred Flame; she is determined to destroy the Source Mechanism regardless. The entity inside Ororon addresses Capitano as "Commander" and is upset that he still cares about others even when it costs him. In his memories, Guthred insults Ororon and plans to take his body once he dies; Ororon, who feels he has never done anything meaningful, refuses, and his Ancient Name "Bidii" (devotion) appears. Mavuika commends him for enduring pain with a damaged soul.

The Lord of the Night says the Source Mechanism is the source of Natlan's old Ley Lines. When the Descender and the dragons fought, Natlan's Ley Lines were badly damaged; to stabilise them she rebuilt a similar network from the old fragments, the Night Kingdom. The dragons tried to strengthen the lines by pouring power into the device but could not navigate their intricate structures. She says that she was once worshipped as a "lord", that before her kind died out they were known as Angels, and that they are better known in their devolved form as Seelie. Capitano, who says he is a survivor of Khaenri'ah who personally witnessed the horrors of the Abyss, argues that false hope should be ignored; Mavuika argues that a future in which the Abyss returns is worse for later generations. Ororon, his life rekindled, says he wants a life with meaning, Xilonen agrees, and Capitano concedes, giving his subordinates and direct assistance.

In As One We Watch the Setting Sun, Capitano says that he tracked three scholars, Aberewaa, Bosomtwe and Cuxtal, and combined their research to find the Source Mechanism, because the Fatui were not getting the Gnosis. After Khaenri'ah became unsalvageable he fled with his platoon to Natlan, which was suffering a similar fate, and met the chief of the Masters of Night-Wind, Ayizu, who treated him with respect though many blamed Khaenri'ah. He fought beside Ayizu, who on his deathbed told him the secret of the Gnosis. Mavuika does not recognise him and assumes the mask is why; Capitano says his flesh still rotted despite his curse. He knows Dainsleif only by name and last saw him travelling with the Traveler's sibling, and so did not want to harm the Traveler. He admits he meant to use the Gnosis to save Natlan and then, if it survived, give it to the Tsaritsa. Mavuika explains that when all six heroes unite they will use a power Xbalanque gained from Ronova, a god older than the Archons with power over death. She expects the Abyss to attack harder.

In the Lord of the Night's exchange with Citlali, she distinguishes the fate of someone's death from death itself, and says the Traveler can only affect whether Mavuika dies soon or not. She adds that humanity's creator looked on humans favourably. Citlali says she hopes to find a way to keep the Lord of the Night alive after the war, which the Lord thanks her for but says cannot be done.

In Despair Engulfs the Heavens, Chimalli declares a Sulfurous Veins base lost and lets his soldiers retreat or support the Children of Echoes; they choose to fight. Maztla's group believes the tumours came from a "sky-demon" above, and Pacal orders a full evacuation of the Children of Echoes. Kinich reports that tumours have fallen across the nation and that the Flower-Feather Clan is hit hardest. The Scions of the Canopy are seen overrun during the Traveler's balloon journey.

Details of the end of the act. Mavuika promises Chuychu a worthy funeral, and the fallen are given a moment of silence at Xilonen's suggestion. Mavuika tells the Traveler she would go alone rather than risk the Traveler lacking the Ode of Resurrection, but would welcome a true Ancient Name bearer at her side. Capitano's last scene hints that the Ruler of Death also sent him on a long journey.

Revelations: - The Source Mechanism is the origin of Natlan's Ley Lines; the Night Kingdom was built by the Lord of the Night from fragments of the old network after the war between the Descender and the dragons.
- The Lord of the Night, Yohualtecuhtin, belongs to an extinct kind once called Angels; Seelie are their devolved descendants.
- Ororon's Ancient Name is Bidii ("devotion"), tied to the hero Sanhaj; Chasca's is tied to Menilek. Together they complete the six heroes of the plan.
- Capitano is a survivor of Khaenri'ah who fled to Natlan and fought alongside the Masters of Night-Wind chief Ayizu, who told him the secret of the Gnosis.
- Mavuika's plan relies on a power gained by Xbalanque from Ronova, a god with power over death, and Citlali believes this means Mavuika is still fated to die.
- The Name Engraver's life is consumed in forging an Ancient Name.

- A "false sky" is briefly exposed when Mavuika destroys the rift, unremarked by the characters at the time.
- Another soul tried to use his damaged soul as refuge; the Lord of the Night does not know its origin.

Characters: Mavuika, Il Capitano, Ororon, Citlali, Xilonen, Kinich and Ajaw, Chasca and Chuychu, Kachina, Iansan, Pacal, the Lord of the Night, Paimon and the Traveler. Mualani is seen with Kachina tending to people after the alliance meeting, and both Mualani and Iansan take part in the six-hero ritual. Chimalli and Maztla appear as minor soldiers and villagers, and the figures Guthred, Sanhaj and Menilek appear through Ancient Name or memory sequences.

Consequences: The Fatui and Natlan form a joint front against the Abyss, with Capitano lending troops. The invasion is broken, the Abyss is driven into the depths of the Night Kingdom and Chuychu is dead. Mavuika decides to enter the Night Kingdom alone, and the Traveler is asked to help her if their Ancient Name can be completed. The next act, All Fires Fuel the Flame, continues from here.

The act's cost is borne by named people: the dead among the Saurian and human defenders, and Chuychu, whose death gives Chasca her Ancient Name. The Pilgrim's Chronicle keeps a record of the Traveler's deeds in Natlan.

Placement: Chapter V, Act IV, released in Version 5.1. Follows Beyond the Smoke and Mirrors (Act III) and precedes All Fires Fuel the Flame (Act V). The 5.1 event of the same name is a separate limited-time event.

915.comment: The Rainbow Destined to Burn: Source Mechanism and the Night Kingdom
915.content: The Source Mechanism is a device found in a Fatui-held cavern, the source of Natlan's original Ley Lines. Ororon activated it for Capitano's plan. The Lord of the Night, Yohualtecuhtin, says it could let her rebuild the Ley Lines at the price of her own existence, and Mavuika refuses to use it.

916.comment: The Rainbow Destined to Burn: Chuychu's death
916.content: In Despair Engulfs the Heavens Chuychu is found contaminated by Abyssal energy. The Traveler purifies it, but she dies of her wounds after saying goodbye to Chasca. Chasca's grief triggers her Ancient Name, making her the sixth hero.

917.comment: The Rainbow Destined to Burn: Capitano's past in Natlan
917.content: Capitano says he is a survivor of Khaenri'ah who fled to Natlan with his platoon, was treated respectfully by Masters of Night-Wind chief Ayizu, and fought alongside him. Ayizu told him the secret of the Gnosis on his deathbed. Capitano wanted to use it to save Natlan and then give it to the Tsaritsa.

918.content:
The Soft Song She Sang (also: Everfrozen Earth lighthouse quest): The Soft Song She Sang is a short Snezhnaya World Quest added in version 7.0, set on the Everfrozen Earth coast. It is the last part of the story of the giant snow figure first met in "A Great Heart Fettered by Slender Chains". The Traveler and Paimon thaw the ice around a lighthouse lamp, the giant lights it, and a ghostly young woman appears in its beam. The giant then walks out into the sea.

The quest is entered directly after "Like a Labyrinth Imprisons Her Servants", which ends with the giant kneeling before the lighthouse. It is quiet and nearly wordless: almost all of its meaning comes from a cutscene and from Paimon's reflections afterward. It rewards Adventure EXP, Primogems and Mora, a Luxurious Chest and an achievement (game-mechanics information).

It is best treated as an epilogue to a love story that canon only hints at: a giant who wanted to return to a promised place and a young woman who may or may not have waited. The quest leaves her nature unexplained on purpose.

Plot: Continuing from the previous quest, Paimon notices the giant is trying to light the lighthouse, but the whole building is covered in ice. The Traveler approaches the lighthouse, climbs to the top and uses a Basic Heat Source to melt the ice and snow around the lamp room.

A cutscene follows. A glowing energy in the giant's chest forms an orb that travels to the lamp, and the lamp ignites, throwing a spotlight on the island. The ghost seen earlier appears inside the light and climbs the lighthouse. The giant stands and faces her. She clasps her hands in a prayer pose while he stares into space. Then he turns and walks away into the distant sea, the blizzard stills, and the ghost becomes an ice statue.

Afterward Paimon comments that the giant was chained up, but this lighthouse was where he always wanted to be. She notes that the young woman was only human and should not have lived so long, and asks what the shadow really was. The Traveler can suggest that the girl's own wish gave it form, or that it was made from the Snegovik's wishes. Paimon follows both thoughts: that the shadow may have lasted because the girl held on to her wish to see him, or that she never managed to wait for him and the shadow was a figment of his imagination, so that he gained his world at least there. Paimon watches him walk beneath the waves, says she has a feeling they will not see him again, and calls out goodbye, unsure if he can hear. The Traveler tells her he will.

Post-quest dialogue. A statue of a young woman in prayer stands where the ghost froze. Interacting with it gives only a short description: she may be praying that her beloved returns safely from the battlefield, or that they appear at the place they promised to meet. Completing this exchange unlocks a separate achievement (game-mechanics information).

Revelations: - The giant's long wait ends at the lighthouse. Lighting it is treated as the fulfilment of what he wanted.
- The ghostly woman is shown only as an apparition. Her nature is left for the player to interpret.

- The statue text ties the ghost to a prayer about a loved one at a battlefield, matching the war background that the previous quest mentions for the giant.

Characters: - The Traveler and Paimon.
- The snow giant, named Donskoy elsewhere in the quest chain, who does not speak in this quest.
- An unnamed ghostly young woman who becomes an ice statue.

- Pavlina and the other voices of the previous quest do not appear here.

Consequences: The giant leaves the land and wanders into the sea. The blizzard around the lighthouse stops. No effect on any named living character is shown.

Placement: Story order: the third and last quest in the snow giant chain: "A Great Heart Fettered by Slender Chains", then "Like a Labyrinth Imprisons Her Servants", then this quest. Release order: version 7.0, all Everfrozen Earth World Quests. It does not depend on the main Archon Quest.

919.comment: The Soft Song She Sang: The Soft Song She Sang
919.content: The Soft Song She Sang is the end of the Everfrozen Earth snow giant chain. A lighthouse lamp is thawed, a ghostly young woman appears in its beam, and the giant walks into the sea. Its tone is elegiac, and the apparition is deliberately unexplained.

920.comment: The Soft Song She Sang: Snow giant at the lighthouse
920.content: By the end of the chain, the giant has crossed the tundra to a lighthouse on an island in the north. The previous quest implies he had promised to meet a girl there, and the lighthouse lamp is lit by energy from his chest. He then walks away beneath the waves, probably for good.

key: vessel of the Welkin Moon quest
921.content:
The Unmanned Vessel (also: Unmanned Vessel, vessel of the Welkin Moon quest): A three-quest Frost Moon world quest series from Version 6.7 (Luna VIII). In each, the Traveler boards a silver ship, the vessel of the Welkin Moon, which plays a memory of three sister moon goddesses, Aria, Canon and Sonnet, from the distant past.

The scenes are conversations aboard the ship: the sisters adopting human forms, Sonnet skipping duties to play on the surface, and a quarrel over whether to defy the ruler of the age as dragons and humans suffer. The Traveler only watches.

The series gives a rare personal look at the Three Moons as characters: Canon is exacting and dislikes ambiguity, Aria is amused and teasing, and Sonnet is playful but angry at suffering. It also touches their view of the Heavenly Principles and of the Abyss.

Plot: Quest (I) begins at the Bubble Pool, where a silver ship waits. Quest (II) begins at the Golden Hall and includes a fight. Quest (III) begins at Nuur Stone Circle. In each the Traveler boards the vessel and a memory plays.

(I) At the Bubble Pool, the Traveler hears voices calling a stainless child to ride the silver ship back to "Mother." Boarding the ship, with Floating Ooze and Moonglow Frostfin Whales as help, triggers a memory in the Moonheart Gap. Canon and Aria meet in human forms; Aria teases her sister for being sentimental, and Sonnet wants to sneak out and play with the people on the surface. Canon mentions that Istaroth wants to discuss the world's gravitational potential and time laws with her, and Aria remarks on a certain feeling about how Istaroth views the Descender.

(II) In the Golden Hall the Traveler may read the Chanson of the Boatman, a prayer by a man named Euthyphro of Arcadia to the goddess Prusmene, asking to be saved from his "dread master." After defeating Lusa, the Blighted Newborn, and touching the transit station, the Traveler boards. In the memory Canon scolds Sonnet for skipping work to play with humans; Sonnet points to the Moon Envoy who now shares her work; and Aria teases Canon for dancing at a human festival, then reminds her that the Envoy's name is Zibai.

(III) The Traveler rides a lift at the Ancient Moon's Remnant in Nuur Stone Circle, then investigates a glowing spot where a boat arrives and boards it. This memory is darker. Sonnet is angry at the ruler's harsh "order" that has killed dragons and humans alike and asks why they stand by. Aria says their mission is only to preserve the world until their King returns, and that even a painful order is better than "pitch-black silence." Canon admits the cruelty, wants to save whoever can be saved, asks Sonnet not to defy the order openly while the world is fragile, and quotes Istaroth's word "hope."

Rewards: (I) unlocks a precious chest; (II) unlocks two exquisite and one luxurious chest and, through its hidden objective, the viewpoint The Boatman's Song-House. The wiki notes that the "silver shining ship" in (I) was previously mentioned in the Boatman's song in an earlier quest.

Revelations: The three moon goddesses appear as sisters who chose human forms to respond to those who prayed to them. They serve a King who left and who told them that life across the sea of stars are allies against the darkness. Their present ruler is a "new master", which the dialogue links to the Heavenly Principles.

Sonnet is the one most moved to resist the ruler's cruelty; Aria and Canon argue for patience. Canon has met Istaroth. A Moon Envoy named Zibai was sent to share Sonnet's work.

The memory also says the sisters were entrusted with a city of dragons and watched human civilisation on the surface, and that terrible losses to both occurred under the ruler. The Chanson of the Boatman, by a believer in Prusmene, concerns a Primordial One that wants to return all dreams to the earth; treat it as in-world scripture by one believer, not neutral narration.

Characters: Traveler, Paimon and the three moon goddesses Aria, Canon and Sonnet.

Canon speaks formally and finds ambiguous human words hard (she cannot parse "endearing"). Aria is warm and teasing and wants Canon to remember people's names. Sonnet is energetic, impatient with duty, and fiercely protective of the living. Istaroth and Zibai are mentioned, not seen.

Consequences: No lasting world change. The quests give chests and memory scenes. Their value is lore: they supply the moon goddesses' personalities and positions on the fate of the world.

Placement: Released in Version 6.7 (Luna VIII) with the Frost Moon map as Lunar Highlands content. The memories themselves are set in the distant past. The wiki lists the three quests as concurrent and does not give a fixed play order.

key: The Very Special Fortune Slip World Quest series
922.content:
The Very Special Fortune Slip (also: The Very Special Fortune Slip World Quest series, Shuumatsuban Operations, The Replacement's Secret, Where the Dandelions Find Rest, Gendou Ringo's Strange Fortune Slips): The series is unlocked by a hidden exploration objective (Gendou Ringo's Strange Fortune Slips, named by fans) in which Ringo's odd fortune slips send the Traveler against Fatui agents.
