After Omnipresence Over Mortals, the three quests are Shuumatsuban Operations, The Replacement's Secret and Where the Dandelions Find Rest (the last needs Adventure Rank 40 for its quest domain). In order, the Traveler gathers intelligence from three disguised Fatui, tails the impostor with elemental powder to a meeting with the Teacher, takes her mission and finds her a hiding place, and finally frees Momoyo from the Fatui and talks Lyudochka out of leaving Inazuma.

The quests combine spy comedy with an emotional core. Lyudochka is a House of the Hearth orphan who loves Inazuma and hates being a fraud, and who comes to admit what she actually wants. The Traveler acts alongside Paimon and the dry, impatient Momoyo, and the shrine's fortune slips are first a code and then a gift.

Momoyo's replacement means that for the whole series the shrine maiden the public sees is not the real Gendou Ringo. The Shuumatsuban's codes mention "Iron Rats" for themselves, "General Crabs" for the Kanjou Commission, and "Sun Crabs" for the International Trade Association, among other words, on the partly legible Fatui Code Sheet. Momoyo says Sayu helped copy the sheet, and jokes that the water stains are saliva.

Plot: Prelude (hidden exploration objective). Over four real-world days, the Traveler draws a fortune slip, hands over the bamboo slip with the phrase "in the middle of a hazy night," and receives a "Strange Fortune Slip" assigning them a target. These are Fireblade Mourisu (a Fatui Pyro Agent), "Mousey Maki" (a Kairagi), Nobushi and shogunate samurai in a cave under Inazuma City, and a final location in a cave near Jakotsu Mine that leads to a safehouse. The wiki gives the objective's name as unofficial.

Shuumatsuban Operations. A passer-by slips a note with pictures of a shuriken and a metal gate into the Traveler's pocket outside the Adventurers' Guild. It leads to the safehouse, where Gendou Ringo, now using the codename Momoyo, gives them a mission. The Fatui have gone quiet, and the one at the shrine has not been in contact. Momoyo's team has found three undercover Fatui, and gives the Traveler a Fatui Code Sheet to pose as their comrade. They are Buzuleac, a Sumeru merchant at Ritou's south dock, Fujita, a merchant in Inazuma City, and Tae, a woman working at the hot springs. The Traveler has to pick the right responses to earn their trust. If they get it wrong the spy grows suspicious; if they reveal their allegiance they must fight. Together the three reveal that the replacement is named Lyudochka and that her superior, "the Teacher", will give her an assignment at Watatsumi Island that night. Momoyo hands over a bamboo slip dusted with elemental powder so she can be tailed with Elemental Sight.

The Replacement's Secret. At the Grand Narukami Shrine the Traveler pretends to be an ordinary visitor and hands the dusted bamboo slip to the false Ringo. Her manner is nervous when the Traveler uses the old hazy-night phrase, and she answers that no such thing exists at the moment. She gives them a Modest Fortune (the Special Fortune Slip). When she leaves the shrine at night, the Traveler follows the powder trail to a meeting with the Teacher, Efim Snezhevich. He accuses Lyudochka of stalling and of not actually having the trust of the supposed Shuumatsuban members, and hands her written final instructions. Efim says that, with Signora dead in Inazuma, it is the right time to repay Arlecchino's kindness, and that chaos is the best soil for them.

Lyudochka, once alone, spots the Traveler and attacks, but Paimon says she did not seem to be fighting in earnest. She says she infiltrated the shrine only to reach the Shuumatsuban, learned that her supposed targets were the Traveler and Paimon, and kept stalling because she could not tell the Teacher the plan had failed, and because shrine life was like a dream. Her new order is "to poison": she and others must poison Watatsumi Island and expose themselves as a shrine maiden and as Tenryou Commission soldiers, to provoke conflict between the Shogunate and Watatsumi and give the Fatui an opening. She explains that "Snezhevich" and "Snezhevna" are surnames given to the orphans in Arlecchino's orphanage, that Efim is also a Snezhevich, and that his casual attitude toward more orphans being made disgusts her. The Traveler offers help, Lyudochka hides at Yae Publishing House's back room, where she once worked as a proofreader under a pseudonym, and gives them the written final instructions.

Back at the safehouse Momoyo recognises the importance of the instructions, but is first reluctant to save a Fatuus. She then asks for eight Raw Meat, four White Iron Chunks, three Sea Ganoderma and a set of clearly identifiable clothes to build a dummy corpse of Lyudochka, which takes a full day to make. Lyudochka's clothes are her Fatui uniform.

Where the Dandelions Find Rest. The safehouse has been raided by the Fatui, and Momoyo is gone, though she left a trail of elemental powder. In a cell beneath an abandoned house on Mt. Yougou the Traveler takes a key from Fatui junior leaders, who discuss that the Teacher was summoned back to Snezhnaya yet the Watatsumi operation continues, and that he had not reported it to Arlecchino. Momoyo is hurt: elemental powder got into one eye when the box was shot. She says the Teacher was fooled by the dummy and that Lyudochka will no longer need to live in fear, and the Shuumatsuban will deal with the poisoning plot.

Lyudochka has left Yae Publishing House when the Traveler returns, leaving a letter and a purse of Mora for them and Momoyo; she is leaving Inazuma, because she does not think she deserves to stay. Momoyo says that her eye was an occupational hazard, that Lyudochka can keep the name "Gendou Ringo" (which Momoyo gave herself on a whim) and that Yae Miko, the Guuji, had thought the impostor well suited to shrine work. At Ritou, the Traveler gives Lyudochka the Special Fortune Slip, whose words say to fly like seeds on the wind and one day become what you hope to be. She breaks down, and admits she always wanted to be a real shrine maiden who could bring people joy. She takes the name Gendou Ringo, and gives the Traveler a fortune slip of her own, "Lyudochka's Fortune Slip", as a blessing.

Momoyo also explains that Sayu is passing news to the Shuumatsuban, and says she was taken in as an orphan by Momoka, who let her join. After the series, Momoyo's dialogue (per the wiki) reveals Efim follows the directives of the previous Knave.

Revelations: - The shrine maiden of the Grand Narukami Shrine seen by the public since earlier events is a Fatui impostor named Lyudochka, not the real Gendou Ringo, who is a Shuumatsuban ninja now using the name Momoyo.
- The Fatui cell led by "the Teacher" planned to poison Watatsumi Island and have their agents exposed as shrine maiden and Tenryou Commission soldiers, to reignite conflict between the Shogunate and Watatsumi Island.

- The Teacher is Efim Snezhevich, and the Snezhevich and Snezhevna names mark orphans raised in Arlecchino's House of the Hearth.
- Efim ordered the operation without reporting it to Arlecchino, according to his own subordinates.

- The Shuumatsuban faked Lyudochka's death with a prepared dummy to protect her from Efim.

Characters: The Traveler and Paimon; Gendou Ringo (Momoyo); Lyudochka Snezhevna (the impostor); Efim Snezhevich (the Teacher); Buzuleac, Fujita and Tae (disguised Fatui); Aratani (Yae Publishing House); Pavel and Ilyin (Fatui junior leaders); Riku (who saw the impostor leave the shrine); Mikawa Akane, Yae Miko and Sayu in supporting roles. Arlecchino, Signora and Momoka are only mentioned.

Consequences: The Watatsumi poison plot is exposed and the Shuumatsuban moves against it; Lyudochka stays in Inazuma and becomes the shrine's Gendou Ringo; Momoyo (the real Ringo) loses sight in one eye and stays in the shadows. The series gives Adventure EXP, Primogems, Hero's Wit, Mora, Mystic Enhancement Ore and quest items.

The impostor stays at the shrine afterwards, under the name Gendou Ringo, and invites the Traveler to call her that. Efim appears to have left Inazuma, and Momoyo means to catch his remaining operatives.

Placement: Released in 2.4. The Hidden Exploration Objective Gendou Ringo's Strange Fortune Slips and Omnipresence Over Mortals (the Inazuma Archon Quest) are required to start Shuumatsuban Operations. It follows the end of the Vision Hunt Decree and the Tenryou Commission's loss of cover for the Fatui, and is part of the Inazuma world quest storyline around the Shuumatsuban.

923.comment: The Very Special Fortune Slip: Lyudochka
923.content: Lyudochka Snezhevna is a House of the Hearth orphan who infiltrated the Grand Narukami Shrine in place of Gendou Ringo, hoping to reach the Shuumatsuban. She stalled her Teacher's orders rather than harm the Traveler, and in this series is persuaded to stay and become the real Gendou Ringo. See her own entry for her later life.

924.comment: The Very Special Fortune Slip: Momoyo
924.content: Momoyo is the codename the Shuumatsuban ninja Gendou Ringo uses while the Fatui impostor holds her shrine post. She is gruff and sarcastic but helps the Traveler, builds the dummy corpse, loses use of one eye in the elemental powder accident and gives Lyudochka her blessing to use the name Gendou Ringo.

925.comment: The Very Special Fortune Slip: Fatui Code Sheet
925.content: A water-stained sheet given by Momoyo. It lists the Fatui's coded phrases, such as "Fellow countrymen who've forgotten their homeland" for self-identification, "hiking" for being on a mission and "sunbathing" for lying low, plus animal names for factions. The Traveler has to use it to pass as a Fatuus in conversation with the three spies.

key: The Wild Fairy of Erinnyes World Quest series
926.content:
The Wild Fairy of Erinnyes (also: The Wild Fairy of Erinnyes World Quest series, Pahsiv quests, Foggy Forest Path quest, Within the Depths of Erinnyes, Teardrop Key quests): The Wild Fairy of Erinnyes is a world quest series in Erinnyes Forest, Fontaine, added in version 4.2. The Traveler and Paimon meet Pahsiv, a Melusine who speaks only a few words at a time and lives alone in the forest. She needs help to collect three Teardrop Keys and protect "the root" of Erinnyes from a "purple thing".

The series has three quests that can be done in any order, "Foggy Forest Path", "Wilting Weeping Willow" and "Furious Mouth of the Spring", each of which yields a Teardrop Key, and a finale, "Within the Depths of Erinnyes". The finale restores the dying great willow. Furious Mouth of the Spring requires The Outlander Who Caught the Wind.

The tone is gentle and puzzling. Pahsiv's speech is built from a handful of words that Paimon slowly learns to read, and the mystery of who she is and who the "visitor" is never gets answered.

Plot: **Foggy Forest Path.** Someone has scratched out most of the inscriptions on the stone tablets at Marcotte Station; one fragment survives about "clear dew" singing on the Foggy Forest Path. The Traveler follows the path, solves three Harmonious Reed Pipe puzzles and examines the altar. A drop of water appears on the altar.

**Wilting Weeping Willow.** At the Weeping Willow of the Lake, a huge tree that looks like a wilting waterfall, the Traveler uses local creatures to clear polluted mats and solves a Harmonious Reed Pipe puzzle to activate an altar whose inscription is mostly scratched out except for the word "foam". The altar yields a key. Paimon's guess that the drop of water might be a way to contain the Demon King is a joke, not lore.

**Furious Mouth of the Spring.** A vishap lies by a spring altar and wakes enraged. Pahsiv stops it by stroking its head, and it coughs up a key. Pahsiv calls the vishap the "blue thing" and says it was guarding the key and was knocked out when the "purple thing" stole it.

**Meeting Pahsiv.** The first conversation is Paimon decoding words: "Pahsiv" turns out to mean yes and "Melusine" no. Pahsiv likes the name Paimon gives her. If the Traveler asks about rewards, she does not grasp the word, and she does not seek payment. She says she is not from the Court of Fontaine or Merusea Village but from Erinnyes. Paimon asks who the visitor is and learns it is named "that visitor", who teaches Pahsiv language and wisdom and works to protect Fontaine.

**The finale.** Pahsiv tells Paimon that Erinnyes works like an information system: willows collect, fog handles, springs send, and the root is the centre of the water veins. The visitor senses evil through them. The purple thing is trying to destroy the root, and Pahsiv scratched the tablets to hide the way. It found another route. After the Traveler enters the passage Pahsiv says the blue thing fought the purple thing and was badly hurt.

**Pahsiv's help.** Pahsiv touches the Traveler's stomach with her palm and the Traveler feels warmth and enhancement. She is tired afterwards. When Rifthounds charge from a glowing formation she runs off; a vishap joins to help. After the water carries the Traveler out, Pahsiv returns, says she went for a box, and offers a chest. She learns "thank you". Paimon wants to return to teach her more words and notes that she acts more like a wild fairy.

**Aftermath in the world (labelled as gameplay).** The willow leaves in the area turn bright blue, young Primordial Bathysmal Vishap hatchlings appear along the river, and the local legend "Mageblade Corrouge" appears where the tumour was. The achievement "Semnai Sans Shadow" is for fully clearing the finale area.

Revelations: - A Melusine called Pahsiv lives in Erinnyes Forest and guards it. Her home is the forest, not a Melusine settlement.
- The altars at Marcotte Station, the Weeping Willow of the Lake and the spring each hold a Teardrop Key and are linked to a door under a fountain that leads to the Roots of Erinnyes.
- Erinnyes Forest is described by Pahsiv as an information system run through its water veins, which an unnamed "visitor" uses to sense danger.

- A "purple thing" corrupted the roots; a vishap that tried to stop it was injured.
- Someone scratched the stone inscriptions at Marcotte Station. Pahsiv says she did it, to hide the way to the root from the purple thing.

Characters: The Traveler and Paimon; Pahsiv, the Melusine who lives in Erinnyes; the vishap of the spring, which Pahsiv calls the "blue thing"; and two bystanders at Marcotte Station, Keratry and Remaudiere, who appear in the finale. Keratry sees the hole in the fountain and credits his brother's magic, and Remaudiere goes along with it. The "visitor" and the "purple thing" are mentioned, never shown.

Pahsiv speaks in short fragments and uses her own name for yes. She never asks for reward but accepts a chest she finds. Paimon is delighted by her and promises to teach her more words.

Consequences: The root of Erinnyes is cleansed, the great willow recovers, and Pahsiv leaves. The Traveler and Paimon say they will visit and teach her more words.

The threat behind the purple thing is not removed. These quests resolve only the damage to the root.

Placement: Released in version 4.2. The three key quests may be done in any order; "Within the Depths of Erinnyes" unlocks after the Traveler holds all three keys. Furious Mouth of the Spring requires The Outlander Who Caught the Wind.

927.comment: The Wild Fairy of Erinnyes: Pahsiv
927.content:
Pahsiv is the name Paimon gives to a Melusine met in Erinnyes Forest. She speaks in a few words at a time, does not understand rewards, and treats the forest as her home and duty. She calms a furious vishap with a touch, helps the Traveler fight the corruption at the roots and then slips away. Her origin and her relationship to the "visitor" are not explained.

She uses "Pahsiv" for yes and "Melusine" for no, and calls the vishap the "blue thing" and the force behind the corruption the "purple thing". She did not know about the Court of Fontaine or Merusea Village as places where Melusine live.

928.comment: The Wild Fairy of Erinnyes: Teardrop Keys
928.content: The three glittering drops of water found at altars in Erinnyes Forest. Inserted into three statues in the square of Marcotte Station, they open a door beneath the fountain that leads to the Roots of Erinnyes.

929.comment: The Wild Fairy of Erinnyes: Roots of Erinnyes
929.content: The roots of the great weeping willow lie deep beneath Marcotte Station and are the centre of Erinnyes' water veins. In the finale they are choked with filth that the Traveler destroys. When they recover, the tree above is visibly restored.

930.content:
Thelxie's Fantastic Adventures (also: Thelxie's Fantastical Adventures, Water Imp's Conjecture, Prince's Country, Miraculous Crown): The event began as a Fontaine Fishing Association commission about vanished fish and rumours of a Water Imp. It turned out that the "imp" was Freminet's test penguin, and the story became a gentle, sad tale about Loneliness Syndrome, grief and the way fantasy can help someone say goodbye. It required Adventure Rank 20 and the Archon Quest Song of the Dragon and Freedom; finishing Masquerade of the Guilty first was advised. Because it was a limited event, not every player has seen it.

Three story parts (Water Imp's Conjecture, Prince's Country, Miraculous Crown) unlocked on 23, 25 and 27 November 2023. Three gameplay modes accompanied them: Motherboard Troubleshooting (circuit puzzles), Record of the Search for Glory (finding marked spots with the Echoing Conch) and Purgation Counterstrike (timed combat using Thelxie's abilities). Players collected Thelxie's Badges (100 available; 80 invited Freminet).

Plot: Act I, Water Imp's Conjecture. Delaroche, from the Fontaine Fishing Association, explains that the fish around Erinnyes have vanished. Local stories blame a Water Imp called Thelxie, said to look like a snake-haired woman or a penguin, and a child is rumoured to have walked into the water, lured by a voice. In the waters near Erinnyes Forest the Traveler and Paimon meet Freminet in his diving helmet. He is building a mechanical penguin named Thelxie on commission and had been taking it to the water each day for testing, which explains the "penguin" and, he assumes, the child in the rumour (himself diving). Thelxie has no language module and answers only simple commands and keywords. After debugging its motherboard and collecting shells and coral for its toy weapon, they meet Freminet's client Zuria Destree. She says her son loves the Water Imps rather than fearing them, sneaks to the shore to befriend them and has built a detailed imaginary world of them. He was diagnosed at age 8 with Loneliness Syndrome, a rare illness after which a patient can no longer tell fantasy from reality. Doctors advised "guiding" the fantasy, so Zuria is drawing a picture book and wants to act out Thelxie's story at the Water Imp Kingdom, an underwater ruin in Salacia Plain. Freminet privately warns the Traveler that the illness can be fatal in the worst cases, and says he saw many such cases while at the House of the Hearth under its previous director.

Act II, Prince's Country. Two days later Thelxie has a sword and shield. Zuria draws the first page, and at the ruins Paimon plays the Guardian Goddess while the others are Prince Thelxie's companions, fighting the monsters that have taken the kingdom. The coronation cannot happen because the crown is unfinished, so Zuria draws page two with the monsters fleeing with the crown. Freminet goes to the city for parts and hopes that anyone in a dark place may see something beautiful.

Act III, Miraculous Crown. The crown is ready but Zuria does not arrive. Delaroche, worried by the lack of news, has learned that the boy in the rumour was Lescot Destree, aged eight: about a month before, fishermen saw him tie heavy shells to himself and walk into open water. His mother fell ill and left the Court of Fontaine. At her home her doctor Jalacan says Zuria has now caught the same illness through grief and is sedated after a breakdown. Freminet takes her picture book to finish it with a happy ending. They "reclaim" the crown in the ruins, and Zuria draws the last page as Paimon and Freminet narrate the coronation. The Traveler, wearing Freminet's helmet, hears Zuria speaking with Lescot through Thelxie; he asks for a lullaby so he can return in peace to his dreams. Three days later Zuria returns to the city, plans an exhibition of picture books about the illness with her doctor, and gives the Traveler a copy.

Revelations: The vanished fish and the Water Imp rumours have a mundane cause (Freminet's testing), but the child who walked into the water was real: Zuria's son Lescot, who died a month earlier. Zuria's commission was her own way of coping.

Zuria is herself afflicted by Loneliness Syndrome after her loss, and the picture book is the "guidance therapy" her doctor proposed. Her recovery and the final conversation are left ambiguous.

Characters: Freminet (the diver building Thelxie; his own entry carries his biography), the Traveler and Paimon, Delaroche of the Fontaine Fishing Association, Zuria Destree (an artist and the client), her late son Lescot, her doctor Jalacan, and Thelxie the mechanical penguin.

Delaroche appears as a worried client and later a worried friend. Freminet is the emotional anchor: he understands the illness from his time at the House of the Hearth and insists on finishing the story with a happy ending.

Consequences: Zuria says goodbye to her son, returns to the city and works with her doctor on an exhibition of picture books on the illness. Freminet could be added to the player's party as a reward.

Freminet's event reward was "Yearning for Unseen Depths" Freminet (Cryo). The Traveler keeps a copy of the picture book.

Placement: Released in Version 4.2 and set in Fontaine after the Archon Quest chapters that lead up to Masquerade of the Guilty. It is self-contained and does not change the main story.

Tone note for scenes: the event is quiet and compassionate, with humour from Paimon's goddess role and Thelxie's limited responses. Canon gives Lescot's age (8) and the one-month gap but no cause beyond the account above, and treats his death with restraint; portray it the same way.

931.content:
Three Realms Gateway Offering (also: Aphotic Diffusal, The Bunkoku Enigma, Bokuso Box, Sankai Michiae-no-Matsuri): The event story follows the Traveler and Paimon down to Enkanomiya after Kokomi's own investigation shows that the darkness is empowering monsters and has brought strange armoured creatures called Shadowy Husks. A shrine maiden in a snake mask, Tsumi, protects the Dainichi Mikoshi with a Sentou ceremony and gives the Traveler a device, the Bokuso Box, that gathers light and drives darkness back. By collecting Aphotium Ore and Tokoyo Legumes, defeating Husks for their gems and relighting three Towers of the Void, the Traveler weakens the darkness. In the aftermath Enjou claims the vishaps are behind the crisis and that Tsumi is one of them, while Kokomi suggests another reading of who Tsumi may be.

Requirements were Adventure Rank 30, the Archon Quest Chapter II Act II "Stillness, the Sublimation of Shadow" and the World Quest "Erebos' Secret". The related world quest The Bunkoku Enigma was unlocked by finishing the Aftermath quest.

Plot: The Eve. Paimon proposes visiting Kokomi at the Sangonomiya Shrine. Kokomi, speaking with Ueno, explains that after the Watatsumi Goryou Matsuri used the Bloodbranch Coral, the soil only stopped bleaching and did not recover, which was not expected. She sent the Stingray III division into Enkanomiya, which found a lasting darkness that empowers local monsters and brings Shadowy Husks, plus a shrine maiden in a snake mask who performed a Sentou ceremony to shield the Dainichi Mikoshi. Kokomi orders Swordfish I to help with the evacuation and gives the Traveler a Fragmented Accessory, to be used when a hard decision comes. In the Dainichi Mikoshi the soldiers show their worry about Tsumi; one of them, Imaizumi, says her pupils are like a snake's, a mark the islanders associate with the Vassals of Watatsumi. The Traveler and Paimon decide to work with her anyway. Tsumi says the darkness comes from three towers at the corners of Enkanomiya's triangular border and hands over the Bokuso Box, a device found in the Dainichi Mikoshi that collects light and clears darkness in a small radius. She tells them an Abyss adherent caused the situation, and the Traveler and Paimon recognise who she means.

Parts I to III. By gathering Aphotium Ore and Tokoyo Legumes across Enkanomiya and defeating the Husks near each tower to obtain their gems, the Traveler restores the Towers of the Void one after another. The three quests are tied to the Narrows, Evernight Temple and the Serpent's Heart, with the towers in the loci of Yachimatahiko, Yachimatahime and Kunado. The quests can be completed in any order.

Aftermath. Tsumi says the darkness under the Dainichi Mikoshi is unusual and she has located the Abyss adherent. The Traveler finds Enjou, who is surprised they sided with Tsumi, suggests a fight so the Traveler can let off steam, and loses. He then tells a story. According to an old Enkanomiyan legend, after the Bathysmal Vishaps were defeated a line of them evolved to look like humans except for their pupils, the Vishap-people, who infiltrated Enkanomiya's higher ranks. He says Tsumi is one and is using the Traveler for revenge. He claims he made an alliance with the vishaps, promising darkness so their elites could enter the Dainichi Mikoshi and rescue captive kin, in return for safe passage for the Abyss Order and help rebuilding the towers, but they did not know abyssal darkness poisons elemental beings and felt betrayed. He says that once the Mikoshi's power is used to suppress the Sangacorallia and protect the vishaps, the source of the Bloodbranch Coral will be cut off. He tells them how to dispel the darkness with a mechanism in each of the three areas and leaves a gift, an accessory piece matching Kokomi's. Tsumi is gone when the Traveler returns, and most of the soldiers have been evacuated. The Traveler activates the three mechanisms with the Bokuso Box, descends into the Mikoshi, and holds off the vishap elites there. Tsumi waits above, wishing to destroy the Dainichi Mikoshi so the vishaps will not suffer again. The Traveler gives her the two fragments, which she assembles into a pendant of three entwined snakes that has been with her as long as she can remember. She says she grew up among vishaps, who taught her language and writing, and decides to return to them rather than stay on Watatsumi Island. She leaves the Mikoshi standing and warns that the vishaps will return.

Details. Tsumi says she found the methods and tools for the Sentou ceremony in the Dainichi Mikoshi and that she can read human writing. The wiki notes the Bokuso Box's upgrades give corrosion resistance and, later, the ability to disperse stronger darkness; the Sentou Trials in the Narrows, Evernight Temple and the Serpent's Heart give extra Light Realm Sigils (see gameplay).

Revelations: Kokomi explains the three pendants. When the Watatsumi Omikami reorganised the court and reformed Enkanomiya, three matching pendants were given to the Dainichi Mikoshi, the Sangonomiya line and the Vassals of Watatsumi, so that commoners, officials and the divine vassals would hold one another accountable. Only the commoners have flourished since, while the other two bloodlines declined. The Vassals of Watatsumi were the familiars of the serpent god. Over time they came to look just like humans, except for their pupils. When the Watatsumi Omikami spent its power creating Watatsumi Island, it weakened and no more Vassals were born. The records mention only the last one, who was hoped to become a bridge between vishaps and humans and vanished as an infant at the Enkanomiya border after an attack by vishaps with her guardian shrine maiden. Most believe she died; some believe vishaps raised her. Kokomi says nothing outright connecting this child to Tsumi.

Kokomi adds that Vishap-people and Reptilians are fiction with no evidence in Sangonomiya's classified documents. Now that she understands how the Bloodbranch Coral works, she plans to look for another way to counter the bleaching soil so the islanders no longer disturb the vishaps. She also hopes Tsumi will find where she belongs, since the Watatsumi people owe the Vassals a debt, now that the vishaps and islanders no longer dispute territory.

Characters: Kokomi (Divine Priestess of Sangonomiya) gives the quest and the first accessory fragment. Tsumi, a masked shrine maiden with snake-like pupils, is the ally. Enjou is the Abyss adherent behind the darkness. Paimon and the Traveler carry out the work. Soldiers Imaizumi and Ueno and others from the Watatsumi Army appear in the Dainichi Mikoshi.

The Eve lists Enomoto, Tsuyuko, Yabe and Imaizumi among the NPCs. In The Bunkoku Enigma Yabe and the afterimage of Koyanagi appear.

Consequences: The darkness is repelled and most evacuees are safe. Enjou disappears again. Tsumi returns to the vishaps who raised her and warns they will come back. Kokomi decides not to rely on the Bloodbranch Coral again if she can avoid it. The event unlocked The Bunkoku Enigma and a battle challenge, The Call of Ice and Thunder, against the Bathysmal Vishap elites.

The Fragmented Accessory pieces Kokomi and Enjou provide form a pendant with Tsumi. The Traveler gives away both pieces, and Paimon feels slightly guilty about handing over what was Kokomi's.

Placement: Released in Version 2.5 as a Flagship Event, set in Enkanomiya and on Watatsumi Island after the Archon Quest Chapter II Act II and the world quest Erebos' Secret, and after Kokomi's use of the Bloodbranch Coral in the Watatsumi Goryou Matsuri. The reward weapon was the Oathsworn Eye. The Bunkoku Enigma could not be completed after Version 2.5.

Gameplay: Game mechanics, not in-world fact. The Bokuso Box has 15 upgrade levels bought with Light Realm Sigils, raising Corrosion Resistance (to protect against accumulating Corrosion) and unlocking exploration effects such as marking nearby ores, chests and challenges. Bokuso Arts add combat boosts for the event. Sentou Trials, Corrupted Waypoints, Illusory Platforms and Stairways, and the Rite of Diffusal (restoring sealed waypoints with Aphotium Ore and Tokoyo Legumes) are the exploration systems. The Call of Ice and Thunder is a Normal, Hard and Extreme challenge against vishap elites. The Oathsworn Eye (Catalyst) was the main reward.

932.comment: Three Realms Gateway Offering: Bokuso Box
932.content: A light-gathering device Tsumi found in the Dainichi Mikoshi. It clears the Void's darkness within a small radius and, through upgrades paid for with Light Realm Sigils, strengthens its holder against the corrosion. It also powers the three mechanisms Enjou left for dispelling the darkness in the Dainichi Mikoshi. It disappears from the inventory after the event.

933.content:
A shrine maiden in a snake mask who protects the Dainichi Mikoshi with a Sentou ceremony. Her pupils are like a snake's, which makes some islanders think of the Vassals of Watatsumi. She grew up among vishaps, who taught her to speak and read. Enjou says she is a Vishap-people; Kokomi says that is fiction and hints she may be the lost last Vassal. She leaves with the vishaps after the Traveler helps her assemble a pendant.

She can read human writing and learned the Sentou ceremony from texts in the Dainichi Mikoshi. She tells the Traveler she wants the Mikoshi destroyed so the vishaps will suffer no more, then decides against it.

934.comment: Three Realms Gateway Offering: Vassals of Watatsumi
934.content: In Kokomi's account the first familiars of the Watatsumi Omikami, a half-human, half-snake kind said to have helped the islanders resist the Bathysmal Vishaps. Over time they looked fully human except for their pupils. No more were born after the god exhausted itself making Watatsumi Island. Only the last is mentioned in the records, as an infant who disappeared.

935.content: An old Enkanomiyan legend repeated by Enjou: after the Bathysmal Vishaps lost, some evolved to imitate the victors and became indistinguishable from humans except for their pupils. Kokomi says there is no evidence for them and calls them fiction. Do not treat them as established canon.

936.comment: Three Realms Gateway Offering: Dainichi Mikoshi
936.content: In this event the shelter in Enkanomiya where wounded soldiers and islanders gather, where Tsumi tends them and where the Bokuso Box and the Sentou ceremony texts are found. Enjou claims the vishaps want to rescue captive kin from beneath it. Tsumi considers destroying it and does not.

937.comment: Three Realms Gateway Offering: The Bunkoku Enigma
937.content: A world quest unlocked after the Aftermath. Yabe, who patrols near the Dainichi Mikoshi and likes mysteries, finds a stone slate and asks the Traveler to solve the Bunkoku Puzzle of eight slates and a sliding-tile mechanism. Beneath is a hidden chamber guarded by defiled spirits (a Mysterious Samurai). The afterimage of Koyanagi, who believes he attacked his friend while possessed, is found there. Yabe afterwards sums up the solution as ordinary elemental effects that kill the excitement. The story of Bunkoku, a traitor minister of Byakuyakoku, is told only in Yabe's partial version.

key: Through Mists of Smoke and Forests Dark
938.comment: Through Mists of Smoke and Forests Dark
938.content:
Through Mists of Smoke and Forests Dark (also: Chapter III Act I, Sumeru Archon Quest Act I): Chapter III Act I of the Archon Quest, the opening of the Sumeru story. The Traveler and Paimon cross into Sumeru's rainforest looking for the Dendro Archon, experience a strange vision of a great white tree, and are taken in by the Forest Rangers Tighnari and Collei. Their search for a way to meet the Archon leads them to Sumeru City and then to Port Ormos, where they join the Akademiya scholar Alhaitham in tracking a stolen Akademiya item.

The act has seven quests: A Forest of Change; Further Observation; Chronic Illness; Silent Seeker of Knowledge; The Trail of the God of Wisdom; Lost in Prosperity; and Ever So Close. It introduces the Withering, the illness of Irminsul and the Dendro Archon's link to it, Collei's illness, Sumeru's two Dendro Archons, the Akasha System and the Akademiya, and it sets up the Sabzeruz Festival that the next act develops. Released in version 3.0.

The act is a slow, clue-gathering opening rather than a crisis. Each stop gives the Traveler a piece of Sumeru: the rainforest and its rangers, the scholars' reliance on the Akasha, the neglected cult of Lesser Lord Kusanali, and the extremist Eremites of the desert who dispute the old order. Its closing moment (a captured man repeating the words from the vision) links the Akademiya's secret item to Irminsul.

Plot: After leaving The Chasm, the Traveler and Paimon enter the Sumeru rainforest to ask the Dendro Archon about their sibling. A scholar's incense sends the Traveler into a vision of a glowing white tree; Tighnari and Collei take them to Gandharva Ville. The pair learn of the Withering and of two Dendro Archons, one dead, one living in Sumeru City who nobody can show them how to meet. They follow a theft from the Akademiya to Port Ormos and help Alhaitham recover a Divine Knowledge Capsule from the Eremite leader Mizri, who goes berserk.

In outline: (1) in the rainforest the Traveler is knocked into a vision of Irminsul and wakes in Gandharva Ville; (2) Collei, who knows Amber, explains Sumeru's two Dendro Archons; (3) Collei's illness and a Withering Zone show what Irminsul's disease does, and Tighnari admits the vision was real; (4) in Haypasia's cave an Aranara's dream shakes the Traveler, and the Akademiya tries to recruit Tighnari; (5) in Sumeru City nobody can say how to meet Kusanali, but Dunyarzad, Dehya and Nilou lead to the Sabzeruz Festival and to a robbery of an Akademiya convoy; (6) at Port Ormos the pair meet Alhaitham and win Dori's trust; (7) they stop Mizri, who is carried off repeating the words of the vision.

A Forest of Change: The Traveler and Paimon emerge from the tunnel at Cinnabar Cliff into the rainforest. They try to ask a passing scholar, Haypasia, for directions and are ignored; they follow her, she lights incense in a cave, and the Traveler faints. In a vision they see a huge glowing white tree under a red sky and hear a woman's voice murmur "World... Forget me...". They wake in Gandharva Ville, where the Forest Rangers Tighnari and Collei brought them. Tighnari calls the vision a hallucination, and the Traveler suspects he is not being truthful.

Further Observation: Tighnari lets the pair walk Collei's patrol route while he and the rangers take a harder one. Collei explains that Sumeru has had two Dendro Archons: Greater Lord Rukkhadevata, who died in the cataclysm, and the current Archon, Lesser Lord Kusanali, who was found afterwards and now lives in the Sanctuary of Surasthana in Sumeru City. Collei knows little else because she spent much of her life away. She recognised the Traveler at once: she is a close friend of Amber and lived in Mondstadt for a time, and Amber's letters told her about the Stormterror affair. She defends Tighnari when Paimon criticises how he talks to her. When Paimon touches her in a joking moment, Collei panics, tries to play it down, then flees to her bed.

Chronic Illness: Next morning the pair find Collei bedridden. She was born with Eleazar, a disease endemic to Sumeru that brings a slow, painful death; the Fatui Harbinger Dottore once suppressed her symptoms, but the experiments left her traumatised and averse to touch. They offer to gather ingredients for her medicine with Tighnari, but detour when a Withering Zone forms on a ranger route; only elemental-ability users can resist one, so Tighnari and the Traveler handle it. Tighnari explains that the Withering comes from a disease in Irminsul, the great tree whose roots are the ley lines and which absorbs the memories the lines gather. The Dendro Archon is called the God of Wisdom because her consciousness is linked to it directly. The Aranara, Rukkhadevata's familiars, told Tighnari's ancestors this but cannot cure it. Back in the village, a Dusk Bird brings a plea from Haypasia for food and water. Tighnari now trusts the Traveler with Sumeru's fate and says the incense had connected them to Irminsul, so the vision was a memory stored there. He sends them with emergency rations to Haypasia, whose training involves reaching Irminsul.

Silent Seeker of Knowledge: In Haypasia's cave the Traveler stumbles on an Aranara, which casts a dream on them. The dream voices their doubts about their journey and their sibling through a conjured Abyss Herald they cannot defeat. After waking they find the Aranara had been looking after the unconscious Haypasia, and they revive her with fruit and then cook for the three of them. Haypasia explains that reaching Irminsul is very difficult and that many Akademiya researchers have lost their minds touching its divine knowledge. It took her three years, and the same day she first saw the Aranara. She notes a contradiction: Aranara control dreams, yet adult Sumeru residents cannot dream, which the Sages say is Rukkhadevata's way of shielding people from the disorder of dreams. Back in Gandharva Ville, Sage Khajeh and aides try to recruit Tighnari to a secret Akademiya project; even the mention of his teacher, Sage Naphis, does not move him. Tighnari then sends the Traveler to an acquaintance, Rohawi, in Sumeru City.

The Trail of the God of Wisdom: At Sumeru City's entrance the pair receive Akasha Terminals under a new policy, but neither the Akasha, Rohawi, Katheryne nor the Corps of Thirty advisor Asfand can say how to meet the Archon. The Akademiya values Kusanali less than Rukkhadevata, so nobody questions her absence. Dunyarzad, a follower of Kusanali, approaches them; her bodyguard Dehya arrives to take her home but relents on seeing her resolve. Dunyarzad wants to revive the Sabzeruz Festival, an obscure celebration of Kusanali's birthday, as thanks for the Archon's help during a childhood illness. They meet Nilou, who will perform the festival's Dance of Sabzeruz, once danced by the Goddess of Flowers. Nilou longs for real Padisarahs, a purple flower that went extinct when the Goddess died; Rukkhadevata made her own version in the goddess's memory but never matched the colour. Katheryne, on a break at the bazaar, chats informally with them. Dehya then brings a lead from Asfand: an Akademiya convoy at Aaru Village was robbed, Grand Sage Azar is alarmed, and the item (classified, but tied to "the Akasha, knowledge, and even the gods") is somewhere in Port Ormos.

Lost in Prosperity: At Port Ormos the pair learn that extremist Eremite groups such as Ayn Al-Ahmar are spreading word that King Deshret, whom they believe Rukkhadevata betrayed, will return. They witness a dispute between Ayn Al-Ahmar and an Akademiya man, Alhaitham, who agrees to fight them in a few days. The Traveler persuades him to cooperate. He names the missing item as a Knowledge Capsule, used to obtain knowledge beyond the Akasha's limits, but will tell them more only after they pass a test: becoming customers of the merchant Dori, who refuses to deal with anyone from the Akademiya. Given a large sum and told not to haggle, they earn her trust and return.

Ever So Close: Alhaitham and the Traveler explain their interests to each other. The item is a Divine Knowledge Capsule, which Alhaitham wants to study to learn what "divine knowledge" means. With Dori's help they learn that Ayn Al-Ahmar's leader, Mizri, holds it, and plan to use the scheduled fight to get access. Mizri goes berserk after using it and turns on his own people; Alhaitham ends the fight by cutting Mizri's link to his Akasha Terminal, and the Matra take Mizri away. As he is led off, Mizri mutters "...World ...Forget me...". Afterwards each hides something: Alhaitham that he took the Capsule from Mizri, the Traveler that they heard those words in the vision. Alhaitham compares Mizri's state to researchers driven mad by Irminsul and concludes the Capsule gives neither divine knowledge nor power. He knows nothing about Kusanali either, so the Traveler and Paimon return to Sumeru City for the Sabzeruz Festival, and Alhaitham is left debating whether to deal with the Capsule or file a report for the Sages.

Structure: the first three quests are set in the rainforest and ground the act in the Forest Rangers and the Withering; the next two bring the Traveler to the Akademiya's world and Kusanali's neglected following; the last two form a self-contained investigation in Port Ormos. The Traveler's failure to find any official route to the Archon is itself the act's argument: the city that prizes knowledge has no answer about its own god.

Tone: Collei's reaction to touch and the Traveler's dream-induced doubts about the sibling are the two personal threads, played quietly against the political ones (the Akademiya's recruiting, Eremite rumours).

Revelations: Sumeru has had two Dendro Archons, Greater Lord Rukkhadevata (dead) and Lesser Lord Kusanali (alive, in Sumeru City). A disease in Irminsul called the Withering harms the rainforest and worsens Collei's illness.

Irminsul absorbs the memories gathered by the ley lines, and the Dendro Archon is called the God of Wisdom because her mind is directly tied to it. Burning the right incense can connect a mind to Irminsul, so the Traveler's vision was a stored memory. Many Akademiya researchers have gone insane touching Irminsul's divine knowledge. Sumeru adults cannot dream, which the Sages say is Rukkhadevata's protection; the Aranara, meanwhile, can induce dreams. Extremist Eremites expect King Deshret's return. The Akademiya's stolen Divine Knowledge Capsule drove Mizri berserk, and Mizri repeated the words heard in the vision.

Collei and Amber write to each other, and Collei knows of the Traveler through Amber. Dottore earlier suppressed Collei's Eleazar symptoms through experiments. The Akademiya is running a secret project it wants Tighnari for. Alhaitham privately holds the Capsule and is undecided whether to report it.

Characters: The Traveler, Paimon, Tighnari, Collei and Alhaitham.

Haypasia, Rohawi, Sage Khajeh (and his subordinates), Dunyarzad, Dehya, Nilou, Katheryne, Asfand of the Corps of Thirty, Dori, and Mizri of Ayn Al-Ahmar. Sage Naphis, Grand Sage Azar, Greater Lord Rukkhadevata, Lesser Lord Kusanali and Dottore are mentioned; Aranara, Dusk Birds and the Matra also appear.

Consequences: The Traveler and Paimon are accepted by the Forest Rangers and have learned of Irminsul and the Withering, but have not yet met the Dendro Archon. Mizri is in the Matra's custody, Alhaitham keeps the Capsule, and the pair head back to Sumeru City for the Sabzeruz Festival, which opens the next act.

Placement: Chapter III Act I, following Requiem of the Echoing Depths (Chapter II Act IV) and preceding The Morn a Thousand Roses Brings. Adventure Rank 35 per the wiki. Released in version 3.0 (2022-08-24). The opening of Sumeru's story. Irminsul and Dottore, both introduced here, return in much later content, notably Truth Amongst the Pages of Purana (Song of the Welkin Moon Act X, Version 6.6), in which the corrupted Irminsul is burned and Dottore dies.

939.comment: Through Mists of Smoke and Forests Dark: Irminsul vision and Mizri's words
939.content: Incense lit by the scholar Haypasia connects the Traveler's mind to Irminsul, showing a glowing white tree under a red sky and a woman's voice saying "World... Forget me...". Tighnari later explains this was a real memory stored in the tree. Mizri, leader of the Eremite group Ayn Al-Ahmar, uses the stolen Divine Knowledge Capsule, turns violent, and mutters the same words when taken away. Alhaitham decides the Capsule gives neither divine knowledge nor power.

940.comment: Through Mists of Smoke and Forests Dark: The Withering and Eleazar
940.content: A Withering Zone is an area of decay that appears across Sumeru's rainforest; only people with elemental abilities can resist it. Tighnari traces the Withering to a disease in Irminsul and notes that Zones are appearing faster and also worsen Eleazar symptoms. Eleazar is a Sumeru-endemic illness that kills slowly and painfully; Collei was born with it. Not even the Aranara know a cure for Irminsul.

941.comment: Through Mists of Smoke and Forests Dark: Collei and the Forest Rangers
941.content: Gandharva Ville is the rangers' village in the rainforest. Tighnari leads patrols and shields Collei from the harsher routes; Collei, who is touch-averse because of past experiments, still shows warmth and humour. Her friendship with Amber of the Knights of Favonius begins the act's link between Sumeru and Mondstadt.

942.comment: Through Mists of Smoke and Forests Dark: Aranara dreams and the dreamless adults
942.content: In Haypasia's cave an Aranara casts a dream on the Traveler as a distraction, using a conjured Abyss Herald to voice their doubts about their quest and their sibling. Haypasia points out the oddity that Aranara command dreams while adult Sumeru residents cannot dream; the Sages say this is Rukkhadevata's protection against the disorder of dreams. The cause is not resolved in this act.

943.comment: Through Mists of Smoke and Forests Dark: Sabzeruz Festival and Nilou
943.content: Dunyarzad, thanking the Archon for her help during a childhood illness, wants to revive the Sabzeruz Festival, an obscure celebration of Lesser Lord Kusanali's birthday. Nilou will perform the Dance of Sabzeruz, formerly danced by the Goddess of Flowers. Nilou wishes for real Padisarahs, a purple flower extinct since the Goddess died; Rukkhadevata's own version never matched the colour.

944.comment: Through Mists of Smoke and Forests Dark: Alhaitham and Port Ormos
944.content: At Port Ormos extremist Eremite groups spread word that King Deshret will return. Alhaitham of the Akademiya is pursuing the stolen Capsule and arranges a fight with Ayn Al-Ahmar, using the Traveler as an ally. He first sends the pair to become customers of the merchant Dori, who refuses to trade with Akademiya affiliates. Both sides hide a secret from each other at the end.

945.content:
Through the Mists (also: Tsurumi Island world quest series, Maushiro quest series): Through the Mists is a daily-gated World Quest series on Tsurumi Island, added in version 2.2. The author Sumida commissions the Traveler to find a Maushiro on the fog-shrouded island, where a child named Ruu and his people seem to live though their civilisation vanished long ago. The Traveler learns the island is locked in a curse from the Thunderbird Kapatcir and helps end it.

The series has four quests: A Particularly Particular Author, Octave of the Maushiro, The Sea of Fog and the Rite of the Trees and The Sun-Wheel and Mt. Kanna. Each needs the daily reset after the previous one. A follow-up quest, The Saga of Mr. Forgetful, and several hidden exploration objectives (such as Una's Longing and Rero's Joke) follow. It requires Seirai Stormchasers.

It is the sequel in feeling to Seirai Island's story: it reuses the Peculiar Pinion found there and explains the thunderbird connection to the Raiden Shogun's earlier killing of Kapatcir. Finishing the series grants the achievement Thunder Is Forever and a viewpoint near Mt. Kanna.

Plot: Now asked to investigate further, the Traveler goes to Ritou and learns from Kama that his ancestors came from Tsurumi Island. The full story emerges: as conditions on the island worsened, Ruu offered himself as a sacrifice to Kapatcir, enraging the Thunderbird, who cursed the island and its people to re-live the ceremony and its destruction forever. Believing that the Perches are the key, the Traveler destroys them all, which brings a crimson lightning storm. Ruu, who thought the ceremony would please Kanna Kapatcir, is upset and runs off.

Returning with Kama, the Traveler uses the Peculiar Pinion to glimpse the Thunderbird's memories, and finds Ruu at the Autake Plains. Kama tells him his ancestors lived happily after leaving and only regretted not returning for him. The Traveler suggests the ceremony may not be what Kapatcir wanted and shows Ruu the memory of when he first sang for her. At Mt. Kanna they defeat a Thunder Manifestation, and learn the curse will lift only when Kapatcir hears Ruu's song again. Because the Raiden Shogun killed Kapatcir, the Traveler and Paimon say she moved to Seirai Island; the Pinion's power carries Ruu there and his song lifts the curse.

Back on Tsurumi the land is cleansed. Ruu thanks the Traveler, apologises for his mistake, and is keen to see the outside world later; for now he chooses to rest on the island, and with the promise kept and the loop ended the series implies he will soon pass on. The Traveler reports to Sumida. Gameplay notes: fog clears towards the end of each quest and returns the next day; during the last quest the fog and lightning turn red (cosmetic only).

Revelations: - Tsurumi Island's civilisation is gone; the people the Traveler meets are illusions of the past repeating a cursed ceremony.
- Kama's ancestors came from Tsurumi Island.
- The Thunderbird Kapatcir cursed the island after Ruu offered himself as a sacrifice.

- The Thunderbird's feathers were the original Maushiro.
- The Raiden Shogun had killed Kapatcir; the Traveler and Paimon told Ruu she had moved to Seirai Island to spare him the truth.
- The curse could only end when Kapatcir heard Ruu's song again.

Characters: The Traveler, Paimon, Sumida (author), Kama (boatman of Ritou), Ruu (child of Tsurumi Island), the tribal priest and other illusory islanders, and Kapatcir (Thunderbird, seen in memory).

Consequences: The curse on Tsurumi Island is lifted, the fog returns daily as ordinary scenery, and new interactables open for exploration. Ruu is released from his loop. Sumida's commission ends.

Placement: Released in 2.2. Requires Seirai Stormchasers (Seirai Island, 2.0) and reuses the Peculiar Pinion obtained there.

946.content: A child of Tsurumi Island who, in the time loop, keeps the ceremony going to calm the Thunderbird. He once offered himself as a sacrifice to Kapatcir. With the Traveler's help he reaches Seirai Island, sings for her, and ends the curse.

947.content: Originally the feathers of the Thunderbird. Sumida asks the Traveler to find one for her novel; it keeps vanishing on Tsurumi Island until the Peculiar Pinion reveals where Kama's illusion had buried it.

key: To the Stars Shining in the Depths
948.comment: To the Stars Shining in the Depths
948.content:
To the Stars Shining in the Depths (also: Chapter IV Act III, Fontaine Archon Quest Act III): Chapter IV Act III of the Archon Quest, in Fontaine. With Childe jailed and then vanished, Neuvillette secretly sends the Traveler and Paimon into the Fortress of Meropide on false charges to find out what happened to him.

The act has four quests: A Tea Party Most Thorny, Fortress of Meropide, The Proscribed, Hidden in Plain Sight, and Lost in Deep Seas. It follows Act II (As Light Rain Falls Without Reason), in which Childe was apprehended, and introduces the prison's economy of Credit Coupons, its "hidden rules", the Duke Wriothesley and the head nurse Sigewinne. Released in version 4.1.

The tone shifts from courtroom drama to prison investigation. The act advances the search for Childe, but the Traveler only reaches the flooded pipe exit by the end; what lies beyond it is left for the next act.

Plot: Neuvillette arranges for the Traveler and Paimon to be imprisoned in the Fortress of Meropide so they can quietly look into Childe's disappearance. Inside, they meet Wriothesley, Sigewinne and Lyney's group, learn of the prison's hidden rules, and discover that Childe escaped through the pipes.

**A Tea Party Most Thorny.** Days after settling in with the Spina di Rosula, the Traveler is told by Isadora that Neuvillette wants to meet at Palais Mermonia. A flashback shows the Knave asking Furina for a meeting; Neuvillette advises refusing because Childe has been detained in the Fortress of Meropide, but Furina agrees, trusting his help. The Knave thanks them for the House of the Hearth's children being better off and asks for Childe's custody, which Neuvillette refuses because the trial has ended. He also says the prison lies outside the court's jurisdiction, and proposes that someone else investigate on her behalf, which she reluctantly accepts. Back in the present, Neuvillette reveals that Childe has since disappeared from the prison and was not seen outside. He asks the Traveler to investigate from inside, and will arrange false charges to get them in. He gives them the Fruity Trio cake. Paimon eats it and orders heavily at Cafe Lutece; Charlotte, whom they meet there, asks them to gather information on Wriothesley, titled "Duke", for her stories, and pays for the meal. At the prison gate the charges are read out: eating cake meant for Furina, with a sentence of 45 days.

**Fortress of Meropide.** Deakin guides them and explains Credit Coupons, the prison's currency. At the entrance they see many Gardemeks and Wriothesley, who takes over the tour. They glimpse Lyney, who pretends not to know them, and finish at the infirmary with head nurse Sigewinne. Later, Lyney and Lynette (who got in with a staged "theft", alongside Freminet) say the prison hides a secret and that the Knave confirmed Furina does not hold the Hydro Gnosis, though they do not know how. They should focus on the "forbidden zone". Vidoc warns the Traveler about "hidden rules". That night the Traveler dreams of Childe's time in the prison.

**The Proscribed, Hidden in Plain Sight.** The next day they explore the facilities and learn two rules: three straight days of work leads to mystery meat, and betting on both fighters in a match is forbidden. They conclude that these rules are not directly related to Childe and rest.

**Lost in Deep Seas.** Vidoc warns them to avoid the pipes late at night because of rumours of cannibals who turn victims into other "forms", then goes missing, and others nearby refuse to talk. Fielding confirms strange sounds on monthly pipe-cleaning days. A second dream shows the Traveler that Childe used the pipes. They find the three men from earlier, who admit the rules were a pretence to protect Childe: they first despised him, then followed him after he proved his strength. He left after hearing "that voice" again, and the entrance he used is flooded. The Traveler has Lyney ask Freminet to help with the dive.

The prison arc quietly cross-references earlier acts: Lyney explicitly avoids hiding secrets again after the opera-house trial; Neuvillette cannot use the court to investigate because the fortress sits outside the court's jurisdiction, though he knows the administrator personally. The charges and the 45-day sentence are a cover, and Charlotte is told only a minor offence. Fielding's information comes from colleagues, and the pipe sounds are tied to scheduled cleaning days.

Quest-by-quest function: the first sets the political stakes and cover story; the second maps people and rules; the third gathers rule trivia without progress on Childe; the fourth finds the escape route. The act ends before the Traveler learns where Childe went.

Revelations: Childe has escaped the prison via the pipes after hearing a voice.

The Fortress of Meropide hides a "forbidden zone" and operates outside the court's jurisdiction. The Knave has confirmed Furina does not have the Hydro Gnosis. The prison's "hidden rules" were partly invented to protect Childe.

The Knave sought custody of Childe and was refused because the trial had concluded; since the prison is outside the court's jurisdiction, she reluctantly accepted Neuvillette's proposal of a third-party investigation.

Characters: Traveler and Paimon; Neuvillette; Wriothesley; Sigewinne; Lyney, Lynette and Freminet.

Also Furina and the Knave (Arlecchino) in flashback, Isadora, Charlotte, Childe (in dreams and by reference), Deakin, Vidoc, Fielding, and the three prisoners who helped Childe.

Consequences: The Traveler finds Childe's escape route, which leads to a flooded passage. The investigation continues in the next act, Cataclysm's Quickening.

Freminet is recruited to help dive the flooded pipe.

Placement: Chapter IV Act III, after As Light Rain Falls Without Reason and before Cataclysm's Quickening. Requires Adventure Rank 40 per the wiki. Released in version 4.1.

949.comment: To the Stars Shining in the Depths: The Fortress of Meropide
949.content: A prison outside the court's jurisdiction, with its own currency of Credit Coupons. The Duke Wriothesley runs the tour; Sigewinne is head nurse.

950.comment: To the Stars Shining in the Depths: Hidden rules of Meropide
950.content: Rules the Traveler discovers include mystery meat after three days of work and no betting on both fighters. Some were a pretence to protect Childe.

951.comment: To the Stars Shining in the Depths: The Knave's request to Furina
951.content: The Knave asks Furina for a meeting and Childe's custody; Neuvillette refuses custody but offers a third-party investigation.

952.content:
Tournament of Glory in Bloom (also: Bloomflower Trials event, Saurian Treasure Seeker event, For Our Saurian Companion, Medicine Born of Guilt, Spell of Unity): The story is told in three parts: For Our Saurian Companion, Medicine Born of Guilt and Spell of Unity. Milray, a juvenile Tepetlisaurus who fought the Abyss in the war, has a rare phlogiston-related illness. The sauro-vet Ifa of the Flower-Feather Clan says the cure needs Ocean Zephyrs and Sacred Flame Crystals. The six chiefs and the Pyro Archon Mavuika agree to hold the Bloomflower Trials again, with exhibition matches in which the Traveler fights alongside, then against, the tribes' champions. Investigating a rumor that the Crystals "beguile human hearts", the group learns that the last Trials, centuries ago, ended in greed and bloodshed, and that Ifa's ancestor lost a Qucusaur companion called Antu. Antu's spirit still lingers. With the cooperation of everyone, they stage a harmless performance, the Spell of Unity, to give it peace while Milray is cured.

Requirements were Adventure Rank 20, the Prologue Archon Quest Song of the Dragon and Freedom, and, for the best experience, Mavuika's Story Quest Sol Invictus Chapter Act I. The event offered two gameplay modes alongside the story, the Bloomflower Trials (war games between the tribes) and Saurian Treasure Seeker (a route-planning mini-game with young saurians).

Plot: Part 1, For Our Saurian Companion: the Traveler and Paimon find the Children of Echoes gathered around Milray. Ifa, a vet from the Flower-Feather Clan, says the young saurian used too much phlogiston in the war, and the cure needs Ocean Zephyrs and a pure form of the Sacred Flame called Sacred Flame Crystals. Biram knows from scrolls that the Crystals were once obtained through the Bloomflower Trials, a joint combat exercise of the six tribes not held for centuries. The chiefs agree to revive it, with voluntary entry and new rules. Milray tells the Traveler, while indwelt as a saurian, that the Crystals are dangerous and can turn friends into enemies, a warning he heard from a mysterious Qucusaur. Mavuika approves the plan but finds the rumor implausible. The tribes' champions compete to recruit the Traveler, who joins an exhibition match on the side of the Scions of the Canopy, People of the Springs and Children of Echoes, capturing the Collective of Plenty, Masters of the Night-Wind and Flower-Feather Clan bases. A hot-spring party follows, at which Kachina seems troubled.

Part 2, Medicine Born of Guilt: Kachina admits she feels hollow and left behind after achieving her dream of joining the Night Warden Wars; the Traveler reassures her that others feel this way. With Citlali they search old woven scrolls at the Masters of the Night-Wind and find only that the last Trials were held to save an ailing saurian, failed, and caused a rupture between a Flower-Feather chief and his younger brother. Naiyan, Milray's friend, describes the Qucusaur as "light and floaty". Ifa is followed by a ghostly Qucusaur, which leads the group to a buried box of scrolls written by the younger brother, Nampole, Ifa's ancestor. They show how Nampole's companion Antu fell ill, how Nampole asked the tribes to take part in a scaled-down Trials while he went to find Ocean Zephyrs, and how his brother, the chief Imara, used the contest to hoard Crystals. The tribes turned on each other, Imara spent the Crystals on tribal research instead of Antu's cure, and Antu died, ashamed and believing the Crystals themselves had poisoned people's hearts. Nampole spent his life healing saurians, which Ifa's family calls "medicine born of guilt".

Part 3, Spell of Unity: Antu's spirit does not know the truth, and Ifa judges that telling it would only wound it. The Traveler, Ifa, Citlali, Kachina and friends instead plan a play in which the group pretends the Crystals have bewitched them into quarrelling, then lets Antu "cleanse" them with a Spell of Unity. Mavuika, Xilonen, Ororon (who makes smoke and light effects), Mualani and Kinich (director) join. After the second half of the exhibition match, the performance goes ahead, with Mualani, Citlali and Xilonen turning real grievances into comic arguments, and Mavuika reading prepared lines. Antu casts the spell, the "evil" fades and the squabbling stops. Ifa then mixes the medicine, Milray recovers, and Antu sees the Night Kingdom, where Nampole is waiting, waves goodbye and joins him. A feast follows, and Kachina decides she wants to bake sweets to share. Later, Ifa visits Nampole's hill to speak to his ancestor.

Revelations: The Bloomflower Trials were an ancient joint contest of the six tribes that produced Sacred Flame Crystals. The last one ended in greed, violence between tribes and a scandal that all six tribes wished to forget, which is why the scrolls say little. Sacred Flame Crystals are not supernatural corrupters; they are another form of the Sacred Flame, far less miraculous than once believed. Ifa's family tradition of veterinary medicine grew from his ancestor Nampole's guilt over Antu.

Citlali and Biram note that the Crystals were once thought to enhance warriors, but turned out to be nearly identical in essence to ordinary Sacred Flame. Mavuika says the rules of the Ode of Resurrection have been fuelled by the Sacred Flame for ages without ill effect. In Part 3 she keeps the surplus Crystals for future use. The Qucusaur spirit, once Antu, kept lingering after death, possibly hibernating in a cave near the Remnants of the Secret Source, until the war's end let Ley Lines recover and the way to the Night Kingdom open.

Characters: Event-exclusive characters: Milray (young Tepetlisaurus), Naiyan (his friend, a companion saurian), Antu (Qucusaur spirit), Nampole and Imara (the brothers of the past), Ballo (event organiser) and Vinesh (runs the Saurian Expedition Supply Station). Ifa and his assistant Cacucu, a Qucusaur who translates for saurians, are central. The champions of the six tribes (Mualani, Varesa, Kinich, Kachina, Chasca and Citlali) are the trial characters, with Ororon, Iansan, Xilonen and the chiefs also appearing. Charlotte of Fontaine appears as a reporter covering the contest.

Kachina is the emotional focus of the middle part, wrestling with uncertainty about her future. Ororon is the newly arriving character of the event and is introduced as one of the Masters of the Night-Wind; he provides the black mist illusion in the play. Ajaw, Kinich's companion, ruins arguments by appointing himself referee. Mavuika attends but declines to compete so as not to spoil others' fun.

Consequences: Milray recovers and the Bloomflower Trials conclude successfully. Mavuika announces that, without arguments or scheming, all six tribes worked together. Antu's spirit finds peace. Kachina decides to pursue baking, and the chiefs are shown relaxing together. The event adds no new lasting lore beyond this history of the Trials and Ifa's family. Players who completed the stages could invite Ororon, and the event paid out 960 Primogems in total.

Placement: Released in Version 5.5 as a Flagship Event, after the Natlan Archon Quest content. The wiki does not give an exact story position; the event assumes the war against the Abyss has ended and the Ley Lines have recovered. Treat it as a post-war interlude shared by the Traveler and Paimon.

Gameplay: Game mechanics, not in-world fact. The event had three phases (28 March, 30 March and 1 April, 2025). In the Bloomflower Trials, the Traveler plays a six-part series of offensive and defensive battles, each with a required trial character: Offensive battles use ritual items to break barriers around enemy camps, defensive battles protect a flag. Saurian Treasure Seeker has the player steer young Tatankasaurus and Koholasaurus whelps through six stages collecting Grainfruit and avoiding hilichurls, magma and watchtower patrols. To invite Ororon, players had to clear all offensive stages, earn Bronze or better on all other stages, and complete the collection and infiltration stages.

The six trials are Attack From the Waterway (Mualani, offense), Crush the Enemy Head-On (Varesa, defense), Traverse! Infiltrate!! Surprise!!! (Kinich, offense), Like Towering Mountains and Sturdiest Stone (Kachina, defense), Air Supremacy and Close Support (Chasca, offense) and Dynamic Defense (Citlali, defense). The treasure stages are Twinkle Twinkle Little Fruit, The Truth of Churlish Treasure, Don't Panic! In the Volcano, Eyes of Ire, Aye?, Saurians, Water, and Fire and An Ending to Treasure. The quests Let the Bloomflower Trials Begin! (Ballo) and Go Go Saurian Expedition! (Vinesh) unlock the two modes.

953.comment: Tournament of Glory in Bloom: Bloomflower Trials
953.content:
An ancient contest in which the six tribes of Natlan fought together in organised war games, producing a purer form of Sacred Flame called Sacred Flame Crystals. The last one held, many centuries ago, collapsed amid greed and violence, and the tradition was forgotten. In Version 5.5 the tribes revive it as a voluntary tournament, with main matches between two tribes and exhibition matches between three and three, to cure a sick young saurian.

The Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame later supplied enough Sacred Flame to make the Trials unnecessary.

954.comment: Tournament of Glory in Bloom: Sacred Flame Crystals
954.content: A rarer, purer form of the Sacred Flame produced through the Bloomflower Trials. They were once believed to give warriors great power but turned out to be little different from ordinary Sacred Flame, though they can treat certain chronic phlogiston-related illnesses. A rumor that they "beguile human hearts" arises from a young Qucusaur's misunderstanding of greed; Mavuika and Citlali find no evidence for it.

955.comment: Tournament of Glory in Bloom: Milray
955.content: A young Tepetlisaurus of the Children of Echoes who joined the war against the Abyss despite his age and was awarded a Warrior's Medal. Overuse of phlogiston left him with a rare condition that nobody had managed to cure. He is cured by Ifa's medicine in the event, and his friends include Naiyan and Antu.

956.comment: Tournament of Glory in Bloom: Antu and Nampole
956.content: Antu was the Qucusaur companion of Nampole, a scholar-healer of the Flower-Feather Clan, and fell ill centuries ago; Nampole organised a small Bloomflower Trials to obtain Crystals while his brother, the chief Imara, hoarded them for the tribe. Antu died believing the Crystals were evil, and Nampole wrote the story down. In the present Antu's spirit befriends Milray and Naiyan and is given peace through the Spell of Unity.

957.comment: Tournament of Glory in Bloom: Ifa
957.content: In this event Ifa, a veterinary doctor from the Flower-Feather Clan, diagnoses Milray and discovers that his family's tradition began with his ancestor Nampole. His father taught him that their skills were "medicine born of guilt". He designs the Spell of Unity plan and cures Milray.

958.comment: Tournament of Glory in Bloom: Spell of Unity
958.content: A harmless staged play devised by Ifa and Citlali in which the Traveler and friends pretend the Sacred Flame Crystals have made them quarrel, until Antu "cleanses" them. It lets the Qucusaur's spirit feel it has undone its past mistake, and allows it to rejoin Nampole in the Night Kingdom.

959.content:
Trifolium Chapter (Klee) (also: Trifolium Chapter, Trifolium, True Treasure, Klee's Story Quest): The Trifolium Chapter is Klee's Story Quest (Version 1.0), set in Mondstadt. Its single act, True Treasure, starts from a tavern rumour about who is Mondstadt's strongest fighter and ends with the Traveler helping Klee after her buried "treasure" goes missing. Klee learns an Abyss Mage was not a playmate, and Jean again confines her to the Knights of Favonius' solitary room.

The act has three quests: Who Is Mondstadt's Strongest Fighter?, The Mystery of the Girl in Red's Treasure and A Very Volatile Treasure. It requires Adventure Rank 32 and the completion of Diluc's Darknight Hero's Alibi and Razor's The Meaning of Lupical. The tone is comic, but the middle of the act has Klee reacting with horror to the death of the Abyss Mage.

The chapter shows how the Knights treat Klee: Jean has shielded her from the Abyss Order, but she is a Knight and is cared for despite the trouble she causes. The act ends with Jean asking the Traveler to keep an eye on her.

The act's three quests move from rumour (a tavern debate), to a chase (the Abyss Mage in the Whispering Woods), to consequences (Jean's office and the confinement room), so it can be used in a scene as a single arc: gossip leads to danger, which leads to a lesson that Klee only partly absorbs.

Plot: **Who Is Mondstadt's Strongest Fighter?** At night the Traveler and Paimon return to Diluc's tavern, Angel's Share, where Patton laments that he cannot join in on the current fad. The patrons give different answers, including Stanley, Diluc as the Darknight Hero, and Jean, while Six-Fingered Jose says it is a little girl who blew up the Stormbearer Mountains. Unable to settle the question, the pair ask Jean at Knights of Favonius Headquarters. She cannot answer either, but reports an Abyss Mage lurking near the city and warns them to be careful.

**The Mystery of the Girl in Red's Treasure.** Leaving Jean's office, they bump into a small girl who drops a parchment of "survival" rules. She is Klee, who recognises the Traveler as the Honorary Knight, and tells them the treasure she buried in the Whispering Woods, with a large marker, has gone missing. In the woods Paimon spots the Abyss Mage Jean mentioned. Klee calls it "Mr. Fluffball" and thinks it is only pretending to be a villain, whatever Paimon says about the Abyss Order. After a chase it retreats to its stronghold. Inside, the Traveler and Klee clear slimes and hilichurls and reach the mage, which says it has deduced from gossip that Klee is the strongest in Mondstadt and tries to use her "treasure" against them. Klee warns it not to set off the bomb; the mage reads this as fear, ignores her, and detonates it too early, killing itself. Klee, horrified that she broke one of her survival rules, runs off.

**A Very Volatile Treasure.** Back at headquarters, Klee is frantically apologising to Jean for hurting someone. Jean does not understand until the Traveler and Paimon explain that the person was an Abyss Mage. Jean apologises for never having told Klee about the Abyss Order, and partly because the problem has resolved itself, allows her to attend the next Ludi Harpastum, to Klee's delight. The celebration is cut short when Jean suspects Klee meant to blow up the fish in Starfell Lake, and Klee resigns herself to solitary confinement. Jean tells the pair that Klee is a Knight, that they care for her despite the trouble, and asks the Traveler to watch over her. In the confinement room nearby, Klee says she is reflecting on her actions while also developing another bomb to show off at the next Ludi Harpastum.

Revelations: Klee's first encounter with the Abyss Order: Jean had not told her about it, and she is horrified at the Abyss Mage's death and believes she has hurt someone. The act presents Klee as a Knight of Favonius whom Jean and the Order protect and discipline, not only as a troublemaker.

Jean's reaction in the confinement scene shows she knows Klee's habits well enough to guess the Starfell Lake plan in advance.

Characters: Klee, Jean, the Traveler and Paimon. Diluc, Patton, Stanley and Six-Fingered Jose appear in or are discussed in the Angel's Share scene. An unnamed Abyss Mage, nicknamed Mr. Fluffball by Klee, is the antagonist.

Klee thinks of the Abyss Mage as a playmate and keeps a list of survival rules she takes seriously. She is explosive and impulsive, and affectionate toward Jean. Jean is protective and strict. Diluc appears only through the tavern rumour about the Darknight Hero.

Consequences: Klee is allowed to attend the next Ludi Harpastum but ends in solitary confinement again after Jean guesses her plan for Starfell Lake. Jean entrusts the Traveler with looking out for Klee, and Klee is already planning a new bomb for the festival.

Placement: Release order: 1.0, with the other launch Story Quests. Story order: after the Prologue, and not before the Traveler has finished Diluc's Noctua Chapter and Razor's Lupus Minor Chapter. The act page's Adventure Rank requirement is 32.

960.content: Act I of Klee's Story Quest. A rumour about Mondstadt's strongest fighter leads the Traveler to Klee, whose buried treasure is missing. They chase an Abyss Mage in the Whispering Woods, which kills itself by detonating its own bomb. Jean explains the Abyss Order to Klee and, after guessing Klee's Starfell Lake plan, confines her again.

key: Song of the Welkin Moon Act VIII
961.content:
True Moon (also: Song of the Welkin Moon Act VIII, The First Sliver of Moonlight, Descending Moon, Welkin Moon's Homecoming): Act VIII of the Song of the Welkin Moon Archon Quest, released in Version 6.3. The Traveler and their allies rescue Columbina from the moon's reflection, fight Dottore, the self-styled "Heretic of the False Moon", and bring the Frost Moon down into Teyvat. Sandrone dies shielding the Traveler from him, and afterwards Columbina goes to live among the Frostmoon Scions of Nod-Krai.

The act has three quests: The First Sliver of Moonlight, Descending Moon and Welkin Moon's Homecoming. It resolves the Nod-Krai confrontation with Dottore, answers where Columbina has been, and closes with farewells, a new joint League and a meeting with Columbina outside the Silvermoon Hall, where she rarely met the Traveler before.

It is the climax of the Nod-Krai chapter: the Moon Sisters' prison, Rerir's and Tholindis' sides of an old story, and Sandrone's long-planned world-formula all converge in one battle. Teyvat's sky now holds the real Frost Moon, where the Heavenly Principles had placed the Traveler's spaceship.

Plot: Dottore pressures the Traveler to serve him; they refuse and are rescued by the Wanderer. Columbina, trapped in the moon's reflection, wins the help of the three Moon Sisters and sacrifices her body to return. In the final battle Sandrone dies, the Frost Moon is pulled into Teyvat, and Columbina and the Traveler defeat Dottore.

**The First Sliver of Moonlight.** In Dottore's realm the Traveler refuses his offer, even after he lowers his demands, because they will not kill innocents and become like Rerir. They try to strike first but Dottore survives and overpowers them. The Wanderer cracks the dome with an alchemical signal and rescues them, giving up a chance at revenge on Dottore. Back at the curatorium the Traveler shares what Dottore said. Nefer reveals that Columbina is still alive, trapped in a space that flows backwards, and Nicole recounts the origin of the Moon Sisters.

**Descending Moon.** Sandrone adds a channel to the Dodocommunication Devices so the group can follow her progress. Dottore's forces besiege Nasha Town and are repelled, then Dottore arrives in a new form and tears the false sky open, pulling everyone into a vast arena above the clouds. He separates Flins, Lauma and Nefer into pocket spaces and offers the Traveler a last chance to join him. Pulonia and Sandrone interrupt, but both are overpowered. Sandrone takes the blow meant for the Traveler and is killed after telling Dottore to go to hell.

With her formula seemingly frozen at 90 percent, Dottore gloats. Then the formula advances: the Frost Moon appears through the gash. Arlecchino, Varka and Nicole drag the moon into Teyvat, shattering the false sky. Columbina's body, which had been dispersed as moonlight over Nod-Krai, and her spirit, carried to Luonnotar, join the Trilunar Authority on the Frost Moon, and she descends with her eyes open for the first time. With the Traveler she retakes the Iridescent Marrow, frees her friends and destroys Dottore's artificial Moon Marrow. Afterwards she cradles Sandrone's body.

**Welkin Moon's Homecoming.** The Frost Moon stays above Teyvat, people return to Nod-Krai and a new League is formed by the region's factions.
