The Traveler says farewell to Arlecchino and the Wanderer at the port, meets Columbina on Hiisi Island, and visits their spaceship on the Frost Moon. Columbina gives the Traveler a Moon-Prayer Blossom and eases some of Teyvat's restrictions on them.

Inside the reflection, Columbina meets Rerir, who now speaks calmly, has no wish to fight and admits her plan to siphon his power was ingenious. He says Dottore revived him, timing it to her weakness, and asks her to carry a message to Tholindis. Tholindis, once a moon marrow researcher, explains that she tried to enter the reflection to change her past mistakes and was torn apart, leaving only her soul. She wanted to prevent Irmin from meeting the Traveler's sibling. Columbina then meets Sonnet, the youngest of the Three Moons, and her elder sisters Canon and Aria, who are held in a prison made by Nibelung.

Outside, the Wanderer, Sandrone, Albedo and Durin prepare. The Wanderer offers his core so that Sandrone's equation can be computed directly in the ley lines, accepting that he might be reset or lost.

Details of the descent into the past: Columbina asks the sisters whether they ever escaped (they always returned to the prison), and demonstrates kuuvahki, which none of them know. They realise she wants to borrow their authorities against Dottore, which could tear her apart and still not let her leave alive. Her plan is to leave part of her soul in the future, "die" in the prison and scatter her body as moonlight across the Nod-Krai of the past, to be reassembled by a signal in the future. Nefer, using Luonnotar, watches this past at the risk of her sight, but Columbina bears that cost for her. Canon asks why Columbina keeps her eyes closed; she answers that she wanted to avoid the lies she saw everywhere, and Canon makes her promise to open them in the future. Transferring their powers to her makes the sisters mortal, and at their request she sends them back to face their end together in their own time.

In the arena, the plan Sandrone had laid out was that her formula would handle about 90 percent of the work (the link to Columbina) and the remaining 10 percent was bringing the moon down by any means. The Wanderer's Irminsul core, hidden inside Pulonia, finalised the formula. Arlecchino evacuated civilians beforehand, and Varka asked Nicole to extend her agreement to cover Nod-Krai in order to stall Dottore.

Welkin Moon's Homecoming in more detail: in Nasha Town, Jahoda greets the Traveler and Paimon, Aino and Ineffa help distribute food for the Frostmoon Scions, and Tarno addresses the crowd. At the port, Arlecchino and the Wanderer say Columbina mourned Sandrone alone for a long time, and Arlecchino credits the Traveler's friendship with Columbina's growth; Columbina comforted others even while grieving. On Hiisi Island, the older Frostmoon Scions are timid around Columbina while the children are curious. The Traveler returns the friends' greeting card she left behind when she fled into the reflection. On the ship, the flight logs show it passed Teyvat once long ago; the Traveler dons an outfit left in a cabinet, and says Teyvat is their home even if it differs from what they knew. Varka's letter to Jean notes a temporary alliance with a more benevolent Harbinger and his continued wariness of Rooster, Regrator and Jester.

Revelations: - Columbina survived and was held in a backwards-flowing space; Rerir was revived by Dottore and has recovered his composure.
- The Three Moons (Canon, Aria, Sonnet) were imprisoned by Nibelung and were aware of what was coming.
- Sandrone deliberately placed the real formula inside Pulonia and a false one in herself, fooling Dottore.
- The Heavenly Principles placed the Traveler's ship on the Frost Moon, and the ship passed Teyvat once thousands of years before the crash-landing.

- The Frost Moon is now permanently visible in Teyvat, and the disaster has made Teyvat easier for the Abyss to detect, per Nicole.
- Columbina shares impressions of Snezhnaya: major cities are built around enormous heat sources called Kresnik's Torch, and she mentions the term Mistilteinn in connection with Project Stuzha. She describes the Tsaritsa as clear yet unfathomable, like ice over a frozen lake, and warns that Jester, Regrator and Rooster are not united (Regrator and Rooster dislike each other in private).

Characters: Columbina is the central figure, supported by the Traveler and Paimon. Dottore is the antagonist; Sandrone is the pivotal sacrifice. The Wanderer, Albedo and Durin work beside Sandrone; Nefer, Flins, Lauma and Jahoda act from the curatorium and Nasha Town; Arlecchino, Varka and Nicole bring down the moon. Rerir, Tholindis, Sonnet, Canon and Aria appear inside the moon's reflection. Aino, Ineffa, Illuga and Tarno appear in the aftermath.
Jahoda takes over the curatorium at Nefer's request under an earlier agreement. Nicole and Alice offer help, and Nicole later reports that the border disturbance has been handled. Pulonia, Sandrone's construct, carries the Wanderer's Irminsul core.

Consequences: Dottore is destroyed. Sandrone dies, and per her verbal will Arlecchino takes her core and Pulonia's to the Fontaine Research Institute while her notes go to the House of the Hearth, with one book delivered to the Traveler's room on the Flagship. Columbina is not to be told. The Tsaritsa revokes the Palestar Edict, Columbina's arrest warrant, and Columbina moves in with the Frostmoon Scions on Hiisi Island, hoping to attend the next Moon-Prayer Night openly. A new League of Nod-Krai factions is set up, with Flins urging Illuga to represent the Lightkeepers. The Wanderer returns to Sumeru to help Nahida with Dottore's fallout. Varka writes to Jean that the expedition will come home in waves.

Columbina has given the Eternal Moon Marrow to Lauma and the Iridescent Moon Marrow to Arlecchino, and will return part of the Frost Moon to Nod-Krai as kuuvahki. She also lifts some of Teyvat's limits on the Traveler's use of the elements.

Placement: Act VIII of Song of the Welkin Moon, following A Traveler on a Winter's Night and preceding As All Falls to Emptiness. Released in Version 6.3 (Luna IV), which also introduced Columbina.

Story order and release order coincide for this act. The wiki lists an Adventure Rank requirement of 40.

962.comment: True Moon: Dottore's Defeat at the False Sky
962.content: In Descending Moon, Dottore takes a new form as the "Heretic of the False Moon", opens a gash in the false sky and isolates the Traveler's allies. After Sandrone's death he is overcome when Columbina arrives with the Traveler, retakes the Iridescent Marrow, frees her friends and destroys his artificial Moon Marrow with a beam of lunar energy.

963.comment: True Moon: Sandrone's Death and Will
963.content: Sandrone steps in front of a killing strike meant for the Traveler and dies, mocking Dottore to the end. She had hidden the real formula in Pulonia and kept a false one in herself. Her will asks Arlecchino to carry her core and Pulonia's to the Fontaine Research Institute and keep her notes at the House of the Hearth, and not to tell Columbina.

964.comment: True Moon: Columbina's Return from the Reflection
964.content: In the moon's reflection Columbina meets Rerir, Tholindis and the Three Moons. The sisters transfer their authorities and are returned to their own time as mortals. Columbina disperses her body as moonlight over past Nod-Krai and is reconstituted when the Frost Moon is pulled down.

965.content:
Trulla Chapter (Xiangling) (also: Trulla Chapter, Trulla, Mondstadt Gastronomy Trip, Xiangling's Story Quest): The Trulla Chapter is Xiangling's Story Quest (Version 1.0). Although Xiangling is from Liyue, the act, Mondstadt Gastronomy Trip, takes place mostly in and around Springvale, Mondstadt. The Traveler helps the travelling chef gather ingredients for a cook-off, and they revive a hunter frozen for centuries.

The act has six quests: Little Chef on a Hunt, Cooking Appointment, Secret Ingredient, Lucky Find, Present From the Past and Cooking Showdown. It requires Adventure Rank 12 and the Prologue's The Outlander Who Caught the Wind. The tone is light, with food as the central theme and Xiangling's refusal to be limited to conventional ingredients as the running joke.

Beneath the comedy the act sets out Xiangling's values: she cares about customers' happiness, not Mora, and treats any ingredient as potential food. The frozen hunter Olaf gives the chapter an unusual emotional beat about a lost era and a forgotten taste.

The act mixes small-town rivalry (Springvale's hunters and cooks against Xiangling's improvisation) with a Liyue-to-Mondstadt round trip for ingredients, and the discovery in a cave of a hunter and a boar species frozen in the same incident.

Plot: **Little Chef on a Hunt.** In Springvale's forest the Traveler and Paimon meet Xiangling, who is drooling over wild boars she cannot catch. The Traveler hunts them and she cooks a snack she invented on the spot. Allan, a hunter, arrives and scolds them for hunting in the boars' own habitat, which hurts the hunters' trade. Xiangling apologises and goes with Allan to see the chief, Draff.

**Cooking Appointment.** Draff receives Xiangling warmly because of her reputation as a chef in Mondstadt and Liyue, and hopes her dishes will promote Springvale's meat. Xiangling will not tie herself to specific ingredients, and storms off when Draff reacts badly to her idea of using Slime Condensate. Drawn by the smell of Brook's cooking, she argues with Brook over adding the pungent Qingxin flower, which Brook calls overkill, and declares a cook-off. If Xiangling wins, Brook must stock her dish; if Brook wins, Xiangling must promote Brook's dish at Wanmin Restaurant. Xiangling leaves for Liyue to gather ingredients.

**Secret Ingredient.** The Traveler and Paimon catch up with her in Liyue and help gather Lotus Heads and Jueyun Chilis. She is still unsatisfied until she recalls a place she has not visited. At a cave entrance they find a shivering man, and Xiangling has the Traveler make Radish Veggie Soup. Warmed, he says he was tracking a boar in the ruins when a Cryo Regisvine froze him. Xiangling realises the Regisvine is what her dish needs and charges in; the man asks the Traveler to protect her.

**Present From the Past.** In the ruins they defeat the Cryo Regisvine. Xiangling finds a boar with special markings, identified as a species hunted to extinction for its prized meat, and the Traveler suggests it was cryopreserved for at least 300 years. Back in Springvale, the man is bewildered that none of his friends or family are there; the Traveler concludes he was frozen along with the boar. Draff asks his name, Olaf, recognises it and realises Olaf is his ancestor.

**Cooking Showdown.** Brook brings in Siegfria as an assistant, so Xiangling has the Traveler and Paimon help: they fetch a wild radish and wash it in the lake, clear nearby slimes, and cook Jade Parcels as a side for the extinct boar. After tasting both meals Draff declares Xiangling the winner. Brook suggests the extinct boar made the difference, which alarms Draff given its value. Xiangling replies that Mora does not interest her, only her customers' happiness. Olaf mourns that he cannot taste the food of his time, and Xiangling promises to recreate the flavour with modern ingredients. She thanks the Traveler, says she will return to Liyue (with detours), and promises a meal and lessons on her unorthodox recipes at Wanmin Restaurant.

Revelations: A hunter named Olaf and a boar of a species hunted to extinction were preserved by a Cryo Regisvine in a cave. Draff is Olaf's descendant. The Traveler infers the preservation lasted at least 300 years.

Characters: Xiangling, the Traveler and Paimon; Draff, chief of Springvale; Allan, Brook, Siegfria and Olaf.

Xiangling is enthusiastic, hungry for new ingredients and stubborn about her methods, but she accepts correction when she has made a mistake, as with the hunting. Draff is hospitable but traditional about local produce. Brook is a rival cook with firm views on balance.

Consequences: Xiangling wins the cook-off and leaves for Liyue, with a standing invitation for the Traveler to eat and learn at Wanmin Restaurant. Olaf is reunited with a descendant in Draff, and learns he can still taste something like his era's cooking.

Placement: Release order: 1.0, with the other launch Story Quests. Story order: after the Prologue's The Outlander Who Caught the Wind, with an Adventure Rank 12 requirement.

966.content: Act I of Xiangling's Story Quest. In Springvale, Xiangling quarrels with the chief Draff, challenges the cook Brook to a cook-off, hunts a Cryo Regisvine for her dish, and wakes a hunter named Olaf, frozen with an extinct boar, who turns out to be Draff's ancestor. She wins the cook-off.

key: Truth Amongst the Pages of Purana
Song of the Welkin Moon Act X
Of Myriad Paths, Flux, and Dissolution
967.comment: Truth Amongst the Pages of Purana
967.content:
Truth Amongst the Pages of Purana (also: Song of the Welkin Moon Act X, Of Myriad Paths, Flux, and Dissolution, Luna VII Archon Quest): Act X of Song of the Welkin Moon, released in version 6.6 as the Sumeru climax of the Nod-Krai-and-Sumeru Archon chapter. Irminsul has been corrupted by Dottore's experiment, which now grows a vast tree over Sumeru City. Nahida, the Traveler, the Wanderer, the Seven Pillars and Sumeru's friends overload Irminsul through the Akasha System, then burn it down with the Pyro Gnosis, and Dottore dies with it.

The act has four quests: Darkness Looming; A Tower Unto Wisdom and Folly; Truth Amongst the Pages of Purana; and Your Past Is Like a Garden. It is the Sumeru plot's resolution, closing threads that began in Chapter III: Irminsul's disease, the Akasha System, King Deshret's legacy and Collei's god remains. The act's title is initially shown as Of Myriad Paths, Flux, and Dissolution and is replaced during Darkness Looming.

Irminsul is destroyed in this act, not repaired: Aaru, the Deshret-era system re-opened in Act IX, takes over its work of collecting and storing information. The Traveler, being unaffected by Irminsul, walks out through the barrier around the sealed nation and back in with the Pyro Gnosis; because Irminsul cannot record them, Dottore cannot learn of the meeting through it (Mavuika, connected to the Night Kingdom, is likewise unrecorded while in Natlan). The act ends with a calm epilogue and a diplomatic letter from Snezhnaya.

Plot: The Seven Pillars of Deshret and the scholars Kaveh and Alhaitham prepare to use Aaru, while Nahida learns that her attacker entered Irminsul through death and that Dottore's experiment has raised a huge Irminsul tree in Sumeru City. In a secret meeting at the Natlan border she asks Mavuika for the Pyro Gnosis, which the Traveler carries back. The next day they overload Irminsul through the Akasha, the Traveler and the Wanderer go inside to face Dottore, and Nahida burns the tree with the Gnosis. In an epilogue Collei, now a full ranger, has the god remains removed by the jinn Liloupar.

In outline: (1) Darkness Looming: the Pillars hand Aaru to the scholars, Nahida learns her attacker entered Irminsul through death, and a huge Irminsul tree rises in Sumeru City, tied to Dottore; (2) A Tower Unto Wisdom and Folly: a chess trial opens Aaru, and at the Natlan border the Traveler fetches the Pyro Gnosis from Mavuika; (3) Truth Amongst the Pages of Purana: Irminsul is overloaded through the Akasha, the Traveler and Wanderer face Dottore inside it, and Nahida burns it with the Gnosis while Dottore is dragged to death; (4) Your Past Is Like a Garden: Sumeru recovers, Snezhnaya sends a letter, the Gnosis has vanished, and Collei has her god remains removed.

Darkness Looming: Kaveh gives the Seven Pillars a draft; Alhaitham's rudeness irritates Bennu, but Sobek and Thoth talk him down and Bennu hands over Aaru's mainframe with a warning. Thoth shows Kaveh and Alhaitham the system and asks them to close their eyes as he chants, letting them see more of its structure. Apep delivers Nahida to the mausoleum, having flung off the pests that tugged her tail; they are Aranara riding with the Pari Sorush, who then falls and is caught by the Traveler. The Aranara Arabalika reports seeing two suspicious Nara at Caravan Ribat. Nefer poses as a lost merchant to bait the spy, Qanafiya of the Corps of Thirty, and Cyno intercepts. Wanderer and Paimon scout the meeting place and Wanderer, finding no contact, senses a problem. Nahida reports that her attacker entered Irminsul through death, a danger she could not have blocked, and a huge Irminsul tree rises in Sumeru City. She links it to Dottore and sets out a new plan.

A Tower Unto Wisdom and Folly: Cyno, Sethos and Wanderer take apart Primal Constructs for parts. Kaveh and Alhaitham find a chessboard trial that will override Aaru and clear it. The Traveler goes to the sealed Natlan-Sumeru border and meets Mavuika, with Nahida speaking through a manifestation; Nahida explains that only the Traveler, who cannot be recorded, was sent so that Dottore, who has access to Irminsul's knowledge through the ley lines, would not learn the plan. Nahida asks to claim ownership of the Pyro Gnosis, not merely borrow it; Mavuika agrees. The Traveler walks through the barrier, absorbs the Gnosis through their command of Pyro, and walks back.

Truth Amongst the Pages of Purana: The Akasha System is used to overload Irminsul and stop the tree from growing. Dottore, inside Irminsul, is amused. In Sumeru City Pantalone, the hooded man seen since Gurabad, learns that his spy was caught; he and Dottore speak of Segments, debts and Northland Bank. Cyno, Dehya, Candace, Jeht, Rahman and Rana fight into the city as a distraction while Tighnari, Wanderer, Paimon and the Traveler climb the Divine Tree to the Sanctuary of Surasthana. Cyno exposes the Pantalone stalling them as an immaterial decoy. The Traveler and Wanderer enter Irminsul, guided by Nicole's voice, until Dottore appears in person and reveals he knows Wanderer's erased identity as Scaramouche. While the Wanderer distracts Dottore, the Traveler places Nahida's trinket in the ley lines and the world's information is redirected to Aaru. Nahida enters Irminsul and blocks Dottore's attack. Dottore drops the three into the depths, Nahida calls the Pyro Gnosis out of the Traveler, and in the presence of the Shades Ronova, Istaroth and Naberius she gains their permission to destroy the corrupted tree. The Gnosis burns Irminsul's roots; Dottore tries to drag the Traveler down but his own Segments drag him into the fire. Outside, he bids Pantalone farewell, calling him by his real name, Feofan, and Nahida says they will not meet again.

Your Past Is Like a Garden: Sumeru begins to rebuild. The Pillars Thoth and Heryshaf stay in the Temple of Silence. Collei is made a full Forest Ranger but still needs treatment. Nahida explains the Gnosis took seven days and nights to burn Irminsul, that Aaru now does Irminsul's job without lasting damage, and that Nicole's dependence has been transferred to it. Naphis brings a letter from Pulcinella apologising for Dottore, noting the Harbinger Sandrone's death, and promising relief supplies. In Natlan, Nahida tells Mavuika the Pyro Gnosis has vanished. In Mondstadt, at Windrise, Liloupar asks Collei whether she wishes to have the god remains removed; Collei agrees, Liloupar absorbs them and fades, and Collei says she has said goodbye to her old self.

Darkness Looming, details: Nahida thanks the Seven Pillars after learning the attacker entered through death; Heryshaf says the attacker feels familiar. The plan assigns roles: Kaveh and Alhaitham continue on Aaru, Cyno provides material support, Wanderer and Sethos deliver it, Dori, Faruzan, Collei and Nicole build an energy amplifier, and the Traveler goes to the border. Aranara tell Nahida their home stands firm and she tells them they must show themselves to humans, or call her name if frightened. Paimon admits to Wanderer that she feels useless; he says he knows the feeling and that there are two choices, staying or moving forward.

A Tower Unto Wisdom and Folly, details: Cyno, Sethos and Wanderer dismantle several Primal Constructs, including an Algorithm of Semi-Intransient Matrix of Overseer Network, and bring the parts to the scholars. After the trial, Alhaitham asks for a greater range and Thoth's side agrees. Before the operation everyone shares last thoughts with friends. Mavuika says she had wondered about handing the Gnosis to someone who needed it more; she asks for no more detail for tactical security.

Truth Amongst the Pages of Purana, details: Nahida asks the Pillars to bring her to the Eternal Oasis, and Thoth asks Nefer for the chessboard he gave her, revealing a new function. Pantalone informs Dottore that his last backup is in the ley lines and they are even for his fees; Dottore says Pantalone's life has been thanks to him. Pantalone mentions the crushing defeat of Dottore's other half in Nod-Krai; Dottore dismisses it. Dottore tells the Wanderer he has no intent to restore the erased information but that his regrets would never be absolved. Nicole's guidance is cut off before Dottore appears. Dottore says his supply of elixirs, which Pantalone depends on, will end with him.

Your Past Is Like a Garden, details: Sethos, Dehya and Candace part at Caravan Ribat. The Pillars decline to move their statues into the Temple of Silence out of respect for Hermanubis. Alhaitham and Kaveh return to repair the damage to their home. Dori complains of a loss to Nefer, who reunites with Katayoun. The Traveler and Paimon eat at Lambad's Tavern, then meet Nahida and Wanderer at the Sanctuary of Surasthana; Wanderer leaves to run errands. Nahida agrees to the Akademiya's feasts if there are no tomatoes. Nahida, the Traveler and Mavuika lie on grass atop a Natlan cliff. Two days later Collei, Tighnari and Cyno go to Mondstadt; Sucrose, Albedo, Amber and Nicole are there. Nicole is happy to grant wishes for her friends.
Gameplay note from the wiki: the quest is a Special Story Mode with trial parties (Cyno/Candace/Dehya in the city, Tighnari/Wanderer/Traveler (Pyro) at the Sanctuary, and Wanderer with the Traveler inside Irminsul). On the map the red mist of the corrupted ley lines over central Sumeru clears after the first step.

Revelations: Dottore's experiment has made Irminsul a deliberate weapon; the corrupted tree is destroyed with the Pyro Gnosis, with the Shades' consent, and Aaru replaces it.

Nahida's attacker entered Irminsul through death, which cannot be guarded against except by blocking all souls' free access to the ley lines. The Irminsul tree that rose in Sumeru City is a new stage of Dottore's experiment. Dottore has direct access to Irminsul's knowledge through the ley lines, so the plan had to bypass recording. The Traveler is not recorded by Irminsul and can pass the barrier. Dottore has deduced that the Wanderer's erased past is that of Scaramouche. The three Shades Ronova, Istaroth and Naberius can grant the keeper permission to destroy Irminsul. Irminsul took seven days and nights to burn.

Pantalone, the Ninth Harbinger, has been the hooded man seen since Act IX. In his farewell Dottore addresses Pantalone by his real name, Feofan ("Goodbye, Feofan"). Collei's god remains came from Nabu Malikata (Act IX). Pulcinella's letter says Dottore also killed the Harbinger Sandrone.

Nahida argues that Irminsul exists to protect humanity, so humanity's survival (and her own as a protector) outweighs the tree. Naberius agrees she has herself become a great tree.

Characters: The Traveler, Paimon, Nahida, Wanderer, Dottore and Pantalone.

The Seven Pillars (Thoth, Heryshaf, Sobek, Bennu, Shesepankh, Apep and Hermanubis's representative Cyno), Kaveh, Alhaitham, Cyno, Nefer, Nicole, Tighnari, Collei, Dehya, Candace, Sethos, Jeht, Rahman, Rana, Dori, Faruzan, Mavuika, Sorush and the Aranara, Qanafiya of the Corps of Thirty, Ronova, Istaroth, Naberius, Liloupar, Naphis and, in the epilogue, Sucrose, Albedo and Amber.

Layla, Katayoun and Nilou appear briefly; Pulcinella and Sandrone are named in the closing letter.

Consequences: Irminsul is burned; the Akasha-linked system Aaru now collects and stores the world's information without lasting harm. Dottore is presented as dead. The Pyro Gnosis is gone. Collei no longer carries the god remains. Sumeru begins to rebuild and Snezhnaya sends a carefully worded apology and relief supplies, which Nahida and Naphis agree to watch.

The act is followed in release order by Chapter VII, Everwinter Without Mercy (7.0), in Snezhnaya.

Placement: Song of the Welkin Moon Act X, after As All Falls to Emptiness (Act IX) and before the Snezhnaya chapter. Released in 6.6 (Luna VII, 2026-05-20). Adventure Rank 40 per the wiki. The title also names Chapter III in a storyline preview, which is a different thing.

968.comment: Truth Amongst the Pages of Purana: Irminsul's destruction
968.content: In this act Nahida, as Irminsul's keeper, gets the three Shades' consent and ignites the roots of the corrupted Irminsul with the Pyro Gnosis, which burns for seven days and nights. Aaru takes over its role in storing information, with Nicole's reliance transferred too. Nahida argues that humanity's survival matters more than the tree.

969.comment: Truth Amongst the Pages of Purana: Dottore's end
969.content: Dottore, inside Irminsul, confronts the Traveler and Wanderer in person and reveals he knows the Wanderer's erased identity as Scaramouche. When Nahida burns the tree he tries to drag the Traveler down, but his Segments drag him into the flames. As he fades he asks Pantalone how he will live longer without the elixirs, considers the experiment concluded and bids Pantalone farewell by his real name, Feofan. Nahida tells him they will not meet again.

970.comment: Truth Amongst the Pages of Purana: Pantalone in Sumeru
970.content: The hooded man of Act IX is revealed to be Pantalone, Ninth Fatui Harbinger, whom Dottore calls by his real name, Feofan. He supports Dottore, stalls the city's defenders with an immaterial decoy, and is left unconcerned about his death when Dottore's elixirs end.

971.comment: Truth Amongst the Pages of Purana: Mavuika and the Pyro Gnosis
971.content: Mavuika meets the Traveler at the sealed Natlan-Sumeru border while Nahida speaks through a manifestation, and agrees to let Nahida claim ownership of the Pyro Gnosis instead of merely borrowing it. The Traveler absorbs it and carries it across the barrier. After Irminsul burns, Nahida tells Mavuika the Gnosis has disappeared without a trace; Mavuika accepts it.

972.comment: Truth Amongst the Pages of Purana: Collei's god remains
972.content: Collei is promoted to full Forest Ranger and still needs treatment for her god remains, which Act IX showed came from Nabu Malikata. At Windrise in Mondstadt, the jinn Liloupar asks whether she wants them removed. Collei agrees, wanting a normal life, and Liloupar absorbs them and fades. Collei says she has said goodbye to her old self.

973.comment: Truth Amongst the Pages of Purana: Pulcinella's letter
973.content: Naphis brings Nahida a letter from Snezhnaya in which Pulcinella apologises for the trouble Dottore caused, mentions that Dottore had also killed Sandrone, and promises to punish his subordinates. Relief supplies are already on the way. Nahida and Naphis agree it is diplomatically airtight and that Snezhnaya must be watched.

974.content:
Umbrabilis Orchis Chapter (Yelan) (also: Umbrabilis Orchis Chapter, Umbrabilis Orchis, Calculated Gambit, Yelan's Story Quest): Yelan's Story Quest, released in Version 2.7 and consisting of one act, Calculated Gambit. Uncle Tian, the Tianshu of the Liyue Qixing, is ready to retire, and Yelan is helping him assess three candidates. Investigating their backgrounds with the Traveler, she finds that the apparently ideal candidate, Zhiyi, has been propped up by a Fatui scheme. She feigns choosing him, lets him lower his guard, then catches him with the Fatui's ambassador at the Qingxu Pool ruins.

The chapter name is Latin, "Umbrabilis Orchis", roughly "Shadowy Orchid"; the Chinese title means the same, since "shadowy guest" is an old name for the orchid, and it is a nod to Yelan. Calculated Gambit has three quests: Seven-Star Selection, Candidature Analysis and Foregone Conclusion. It requires Adventure Rank 40 plus the Interlude Chapter act Perilous Trail and the Sinae Unicornis Chapter act Sea of Clouds, Sea of People. The Chinese act title echoes a saying from the board game Go, that a game is won at the point where an opponent's advance is cut off.

The story is an investigation told as a game of deception. Yelan deliberately plays out a false verdict, and the Traveler serves as her second pair of eyes, tailing suspects and noticing details such as a cold floral scent. The chapter shows her cunning, her dry humour and her preference for the thrill of her present work over high office.

Plot: In Liyue Harbor the Traveler and Paimon meet Huixin, daughter of Uncle Tian, who says her father is thinking of stepping down as Tianshu. At the Yanshang Teahouse Tian explains how the succession works and introduces Yelan, who is assisting him as an assessment official. Yelan says she would like the post herself, and Tian agrees she may have it if no candidate proves worthy. The candidates are Qianwei, clever but arrogant; Mingbo, nervous; and Zhiyi, who seems flawless. Yelan checks their backgrounds. Her informants report that Qianwei and Mingbo have faults but are decent people, while Zhiyi's reputation is suspiciously polished: tales of cruelty toward him in youth, kindness to those who disliked him, and a recent turn from bad rumours to good. Yelan connects a rumour of treasure in some ruins beneath Qingxu Pool with newcomers at the Blackcliff Forge who keep apart from the other workers. Rain lets her follow their footprints to an abandoned camp, where she and the Traveler catch a cold, floral scent that the Traveler recognises as Snezhnayan, pointing at the Fatui. She announces Zhiyi as the winner to make him complacent, has him followed, and learns of an ambassador, Yusupov, heading to the Qingxu Pool. Beneath the pool she and the Traveler overhear Zhiyi and Yusupov celebrating, and Yelan then confronts Zhiyi with the Millelith.

**Seven-Star Selection.** Zhiyi admits that Tian personally tutored all three candidates. When he brings Tian a fish soup recipe, improved with seasonings he added, the recipe becomes a detail Yelan later uses. Yelan calls in her informants Wenyuan and Shanghua; the third, Wupei, is missing, so she looks into Zhiyi herself with the Traveler and Paimon, beginning with the broker Bolai on the docks.

**Candidature Analysis.** Bolai says Zhiyi's parents died when he was young and he was treated cruelly, yet he supported the family of someone who had disliked him once that person fell on hard times. The Traveler tails Zhiyi to Linlang, where he buys wineware, then to the south wharf, where Uncle Sun and Uncle Gao say he is no real fisherman and has no Mora. Dugu Shuo says Zhiyi's reputation, bad in rumour, turned positive only a few months earlier. At Blackcliff Forge, Iron Shoulder praises some newcomers' skill but says they refuse to drink with the other workers. When Wupei finally appears and says Zhiyi fell overboard and no one had interacted with him, Yelan mentions the fish soup, which Wupei has never heard of, and decides to claim Zhiyi as the winner as a trap.

**Foregone Conclusion.** At Yuehai Pavilion Yelan announces Zhiyi, to Qianwei's open anger and Mingbo's disappointment. Zhiyi suggests that his rivals work with him after his appointment, then leaves, giving her subordinates the slip. They find that he bought strong liquor at Xinyue Kiosk and the wineware at Xigu Antiques, and Yelan sends them to watch Fatui officials. That night Wenyuan reports that Yusupov has gone alone toward Qingxu Pool. Yelan, the Traveler and Paimon enter the underground ruins by an emergency exit, solve a statue puzzle, and overhear Zhiyi and Yusupov celebrating. Yusupov collapses from poison Zhiyi put in his drink; he says the Fatui will hunt Zhiyi, who answers that his subordinate Theofan, who wanted Yusupov's post, already knew about the plot.

Finer points. Yelan wanted Theofan as a source of information about the Fatui operation, and Zhiyi's reference to him is how his involvement surfaces. When she confronts Zhiyi with her subordinates and the Millelith, he first claims to have been working undercover; Yelan answers that this makes no sense after he has just confessed. Zhiyi admits poisoning Tian and promises to use his status to protect them, but gives up when she and the Traveler say he has betrayed Tian's trust. Qianwei and Mingbo, shaken, resolve to keep working.

Revelations: Zhiyi, the front-runner for Tianshu, is a Fatui agent, and Tian has been poisoned by him. The Fatui, working through the ambassador Yusupov, wanted a figure inside the Liyue Qixing and a treasure said to be hidden in the ruins beneath Qingxu Pool. Yelan's informants had not interacted with Zhiyi, and his glowing reputation had been built recently.

The scheme was also betrayed from within: Zhiyi poisoned Yusupov at the celebration, and his subordinate Theofan had been waiting for Yusupov's post. The Fatui's higher ranks were involved too, since Harbinger Regrator stepped in and took Theofan away with the information Yelan wanted. The quest never explains the ruins' treasure.

Characters: Yelan leads the investigation. The Traveler and Paimon follow and observe. Uncle Tian is the ageing Tianshu, Huixin his daughter. Qianwei, Mingbo and Zhiyi are the candidates. Wenyuan, Shanghua and Wupei are Yelan's informants. Yusupov is the Fatui ambassador, Theofan his subordinate.

Bolai, Linlang, Uncle Sun, Uncle Gao, Dugu Shuo, Iron Shoulder and Qiping are Liyue Harbor residents questioned on the way. Baizhu treats Tian after the poisoning. Regrator is mentioned, not shown.

Consequences: Zhiyi is taken into custody. Tian is treated by Baizhu for the poison and is shocked by the betrayal. Tian offers Yelan the Tianshu post, but she says she was joking, as she would miss the thrill of her present job. Qianwei and Mingbo agree to keep working hard. Theofan is removed by Regrator before Yelan can question him.

Placement: Release order: all three quests came out together with Version 2.7. Story order: it needs the Interlude Chapter act Perilous Trail and the Sinae Unicornis Chapter's Sea of Clouds, Sea of People, so it takes place in Liyue after those events. Adventure Rank 40 is also required.

975.content: Zhiyi is a Tianshu candidate who seems the best of three. His kindness charmed Uncle Tian but was part of a Fatui scheme; he is arrested after Yelan's trap. He poisoned Tian and Yusupov.

976.comment: Umbrabilis Orchis Chapter (Yelan): Qianwei and Mingbo
976.content: The other two Tianshu candidates. Qianwei is clever and arrogant, quick to anger; Mingbo is reliable but anxious and unambitious. Yelan's report says Qianwei has pioneering ideas with weak detail, and Mingbo struggles to win people over. Both are shaken by Zhiyi's betrayal and resolve to continue working.

977.content: A Fatui ambassador who leads the scheme to plant Zhiyi near the Tianshu. Zhiyi poisons him at the celebration beneath Qingxu Pool, and he says the Fatui would kill him for failing.

978.comment: Umbrabilis Orchis Chapter (Yelan): Wenyuan, Shanghua and Wupei
978.content: Yelan's informants. Wenyuan and Shanghua check on the candidates; Wupei was missing at first and later said that Zhiyi had fallen overboard and no one had interacted with him.

979.content: Uncle Tian, the Tianshu, is old and wants a successor. He gives the assessment of candidates to Yelan, and sets no time limit. If none prove worthy, he agrees Yelan may take the post.

980.content:
Unfinished Comedy (also: Caterpillar's Story: Prologue, Game of the Rich, An Eye for an Eye, Hereafter..., Coupon Millionaire, Lanoire's escape from Meropide): Unfinished Comedy is a Fontaine World Quest series from version 4.1, set in the Fortress of Meropide. A prisoner called Caterpillar, who looks like a boy but says he is not a child, wants to get a young girl named Lanoire out of the fortress and back to her family. She was born inside and has no papers. The Traveler and Paimon join the plan, win a contest called Coupon Millionaire, and help the pair escape.

The series has three quests, played in order: Game of the Rich, An Eye for an Eye, and Hereafter... It requires The Outlander Who Caught the Wind to have been completed, and begins when the Traveler is caught by the fortress searchlights, enters through the dormitory pipes, or teleports in once the fortress is unlocked during To the Stars Shining in the Depths. The Fontaine Reputation menu lists it as "Caterpillar's Story: Prologue", and its name echoes a 1957 Chinese film, The Unfinished Comedy.

The tone starts as a comic prison farce full of paperwork, Coupons and competing schemes, and darkens when Caterpillar changes shape and Noailles shows how far he will take the rules. Its centre is Caterpillar's wish to be more human through compassion, set against a fortress that treats people as case files.

Plot: **Game of the Rich.** The Traveler and Paimon are taken to reception in the Fortress of Meropide. The receptionist Monglane records them and sends them to the prisoner Darcy, who takes them to the guard Estienne. Estienne has invented a game called Coupon Millionaire: whoever earns the most Coupons wins a supervised job outside, under the sun. A small girl, Lanoire, says she will win because her friend Cater told her so, and a stricter new guard, Noailles, breaks up the crowd. The Traveler follows Lanoire around the fortress, meets Caterpillar and learns that she was born here, that her mother Agnes died of a long illness, and that she has family outside but no proof of identity. Caterpillar proposes using the game as an exit. The Traveler and Paimon join his team, the Kids Team, over several days of commissions.

**An Eye for an Eye.** The team wins and Estienne takes them outside at night, but Noailles intercepts them with Gardemeks. Caterpillar turns into an Anemo Hilichurl Rogue to fight. Noailles offers a deal, breaks it, and takes everyone back. Estienne and the guard Maupoil help them leave a second time, and the Traveler opens the Geode Mine Shaft's sealed passage. Noailles follows and is beaten, and Estienne takes him into custody. The group leaves.

**Hereafter...** Caterpillar leads Lanoire and the Traveler along a hidden path to a house with a garden of purple flowers at the foot of the mountains to the southeast. Earnshaw, her grandfather, takes her in. Caterpillar stays outside and tells Lanoire the first part of a story about a mage's apprentice and a little fish.

**Game of the Rich in more detail.** The rival teams are Darcy's, the researchers Genevieve and Poiret, Rave's, and the Kids Team. Other prisoners such as Henaff, Delassaux and Nizami are seen around them. Monglane's records for Caterpillar are missing. When Noailles questions him, Caterpillar says he was sentenced for a task done under a master's orders, and gives an account that makes Noailles abandon the question and turn instead to a misused loudspeaker. Paimon senses something is wrong; Caterpillar admits he made Noailles "certain" of one plain fact, and says such tricks have limits. Rave later offers to team up and calls Caterpillar a monster in human skin; Noailles interrupts. Caterpillar says Rave once tried to have him taught a lesson. On the first two nights Caterpillar tells Lanoire a story about a girl in a giant's garden who is lured over the wall by a witch needing purple flowers and cannot return; Lanoire says she dislikes it. On the third night Lanoire tells her own version, in which the witch makes a deal and everyone is happy. At the final tally Genevieve's team has handed its Coupons to Rave, giving Rave 8,250. Caterpillar's team reaches 2,003,480, because he spent a long-saved hoard of Coupons to hire many workers, and he says the rules allow it. Estienne names Caterpillar, the Traveler and Paimon the winners.

**An Eye for an Eye in more detail.** Outside the walls Lanoire sees no walls, only sky, and takes the moon for something that would hurt her eyes if it were the sun. Noailles arrives with Gardemeks, calls them all criminals even if their records are missing, and Estienne is attacked too. After the Anemo transformation, Noailles accepts Caterpillar's offer to return to the fortress in exchange for Lanoire leaving, then says no one makes deals with monsters and takes all of them back. In the fortress Caterpillar answers the Traveler's questions: he came more than four hundred years ago, belonged to the Narzissenkreuz Ordo, and was a hilichurl to whom the master Narzissenkreuz gave speech and intelligence. He says he helps Lanoire out of compassion, which he practises by imitating how a human would act, and that he believes his own sins can never be absolved. Maupoil lets them out. The four cross the Production Zone by drawing guards away with a searchlight and the Rochelle Loudspeaker, then reach the Geode Mine Shaft, where a research terminal needs two people at once and a note warns that a Flying Energy Thief hunts anyone carrying an energy storage device. The Traveler and Paimon collect three energy devices while Caterpillar and Lanoire hold the terminals. Noailles catches up there without Gardemeks and is defeated. Estienne arrives, says Noailles used the Gardemeks without authorisation, and tells the group not to come back.

**Hereafter... in more detail.** Caterpillar tells Lanoire the goodbye is only temporary, and tells Paimon that children quickly forget, so she will forget him. Lanoire asks whether the characters at the end of a story ever meet again. Earnshaw learns what happened to Agnes from the Traveler and Lanoire, says Lanoire's home is now with him, and asks them to invite Caterpillar to visit. Caterpillar says they will meet again, then offers to tell the Traveler more about the Ordo.

**Ways in.** The Traveler can reach the fortress by being caught by the searchlights, by sneaking in through the broken piping, or by teleporting there. During Game of the Rich, at certain Coupon steps, the twelve small quests of Scenes from Life in Meropide unlock.

**Caterpillar and the Traveler.** If An Artist Adrift has been completed, Paimon links the name Caterpillar to the painter Julien in Sumeru. Caterpillar says Julien already had the skill and that he only gave him "certainty". This is the series' only link to that quest.

**The stories.** The mage's apprentice tale told in Hereafter... has a teacher who forbids the apprentice to go out and a fish separated from its family in the sea. The series does not say whether any of the stories are Caterpillar's own memories.

**The contest.** Genevieve criticises the vague rules and proposes restarting with clearer ones; when the others will not, she gives up her team's Coupons, and says she has been in the fortress before for striking someone in anger. Rave says it is a matter of honour. Estienne says the game would have been more exciting if everyone used the rules to the full.

Revelations: - Lanoire was born inside the Fortress of Meropide. She is the granddaughter of Earnshaw, and her mother Agnes died of a chronic illness in the fortress.
- Caterpillar is not a child. He has been in the fortress for over four hundred years.
- Caterpillar is a hilichurl who can change how he looks; his real form is an Anemo Hilichurl Rogue.

- Caterpillar says he was taught speech, memory and intelligence by Narzissenkreuz and served in the Narzissenkreuz Ordo, whose plan, he says, failed. He says the ceremonial Holy Blade of Narzissenkreuz no longer exists.
- Caterpillar says he can make pure-hearted people "certain" of a statement, with limits and unpredictable results.
- Estienne could take Lanoire out himself, but chooses not to break the rules at that personal cost.
- The Geode Mine Shaft has an exit to the outside, sealed with a two-person locking mechanism. Arkhium mining there stopped after the Fontaine Research Institute accident.

- Earnshaw had not read Agnes' letters; he learns the truth only through the Traveler, and his idle lines afterwards show regret about not reading them sooner.

Characters: Caterpillar ("Cater"), Lanoire ("Skylark" in the fortress), the guards Estienne, Noailles and Maupoil, the receptionist Monglane, Earnshaw, the Traveler and Paimon. Prisoners seen include Darcy, Genevieve, Poiret, Rave, Henaff, Delassaux, Nizami and Alvard. Clynes, Galvana and Galvaryet appear in support.

Caterpillar speaks politely and calmly and is protective of Lanoire, who says he has never lied to her. Lanoire is trusting and curious, and calls the guards "evil sorcerers" or "good sorcerers". Estienne is easy-going, bends rules, and calls himself a small fry who will not take large risks. Noailles is rigid and punitive, and believes anyone can be a criminal regardless of age.

Consequences: Lanoire lives with Earnshaw in the Court of Fontaine Region, near Mont Esus. Caterpillar leaves, and goes on to the 4.2 Narzissenkreuz Ordo quests, where he travels with the Traveler, Ann and Seymour. After the series the searchlights outside the fortress no longer react to the Traveler.

The follow-up World Quest Happy Birthday (4.2) shows Caterpillar visiting Lanoire in his hilichurl form, telling her the end of the apprentice's story, and asking her never to approach anyone who looks like him.

Placement: Released in version 4.1, with the Fortress of Meropide. In story order it sits just before the 4.2 In the Wake of Narcissus series, which Hereafter... leads into.

981.content: Caterpillar, called Cater by Lanoire, is a prisoner in the Fortress of Meropide who appears as a white-haired boy. He says he is not a child. His real form is an Anemo Hilichurl Rogue; he says he is a hilichurl whom the mage Narzissenkreuz taught to speak and think. He says he has been imprisoned for more than four hundred years for his part in his master's plan. He helps Lanoire out of what he calls compassion, copying what a human would do.

982.content: Lanoire is a young girl born inside the Fortress of Meropide, nicknamed Skylark by the prisoners. She has no official identity there. Her mother Agnes died, and Caterpillar and Estienne have looked after her. She loves stories, flowers pressed in books and the Tasses Ragout. After the series she lives with her grandfather Earnshaw and the three dogs Prince, Princess and Hero.

983.content: Estienne is an easy-going guard in the Fortress of Meropide who invents the Coupon Millionaire game to decide who is sent on outside jobs. He bends rules, dislikes Noailles' rigidity, and helps Lanoire and Caterpillar get out. He says he would not take Lanoire out himself, because he would pay too high a price.

984.content: Noailles is a new, rule-bound guard in the Fortress of Meropide. Darcy says he dislikes Fonta and wants to close the Pankration Ring. He tries to recreate Caterpillar's lost records, calls the fugitives criminals whatever their documents say, uses Gardemeks without permission and breaks the deal he offered Caterpillar. He is beaten at the Geode Mine Shaft and taken into custody by Estienne.

985.content: Earnshaw is Lanoire's grandfather, a broad white-haired man who lives at the foothills of Mont Esus in the Court of Fontaine Region, in a house with a purple-flower garden. His daughter Agnes left after a quarrel and sent letters that he did not read. He cares for her three dogs, makes Tasses Ragout and takes Lanoire in at the end of the series.

986.content: Coupon Millionaire is a game Estienne runs in the Fortress of Meropide. Teams earn Coupons however they like, and the winner gets a supervised job outside the walls. The contest has few rules, which Genevieve criticises. The Kids Team, made up of Caterpillar, Lanoire, the Traveler and Paimon, wins with 2,003,480 Coupons, thanks to a stash Caterpillar saved earlier and used to hire helpers.

987.comment: Unfinished Comedy: Geode Mine Shaft Escape
987.content: The Geode Mine Shaft is the route the group uses out of the Fortress of Meropide. A locking mechanism there can only be opened by two people at once, and its terminal needs energy storage devices that attract a Flying Energy Thief, a trial device that disables whatever carries one. Noailles confronts the group here.

key: What the Skies Conceal, the Water Reveals
988.content:
Unreconciled Stars (also: Unreconciled Stars event, Fading Star event, Unknown Star, The Crisis Deepens, What the Skies Conceal, the Water Reveals, Where Ancient Stars Align): Unreconciled Stars was a Version 1.1 flagship event (16-30 November 2020, with the final act released on 26 November). Meteorites fell across Mondstadt and Liyue, and anyone who touched one fell into a deep sleep, dreaming of climbing a freezing mountain. The Adventurers' Guild sends the Traveler and Paimon out with the self-styled "Prinzessin der Verurteilung" Fischl and her raven Oz; they later gain the astrologist Mona. The trail leads to Leonard, an adventurer from about two thousand years ago who never climbed Pilos Peak, and to a Fatui Harbinger who is also hunting the meteorites.

The event is mostly an investigation story told with Fischl's theatrical speech and Oz's patient translation. It was limited-time: Fischl was the event's reward character, and the story is canon but not common knowledge for characters who were not present.

Plot: Act I (Unknown Star). Katheryne briefs the Traveler and Paimon: a meteor shower covered the countryside of Mondstadt and Liyue, and anyone who touches a meteorite sinks into sleep. Fischl and Oz are assigned as partners, since the Guild advises adventurers to travel in pairs. At Springvale the victims mumble about cold and rest, one remembers a snowy mountain path, and a villager asks for help finding a boy who ran to the nearest impact site. Fischl's Vision glows near the meteorite shards; clearing the shards wakes some sleepers, so the group concludes the meteorites are the cause.

Act II (The Crisis Deepens). Meteorites keep falling faster than they can be cleared. The search for a missing Dawn Winery delivery worker takes the party to Liyue, where the Millelith have turned Wangshu Inn into a relief station. A wandering Inazuman swordsman helps them briefly and leaves. At the inn Fatui skirmishers appear at the last meteorite and warn that a Harbinger is nearby. Fischl declares the sleep a curse and asks for someone expert in undoing curses; Katheryne names the travelling astrologist Mona.

Act III (What the Skies Conceal, the Water Reveals). Mona's hydromancy shows that the meteorites came from someone's constellation. At Qingce Village the party learns that the sleepers all dream of an enormous snowy mountain and feel compelled to climb it, as though the wish were put in their heads. Mona reads the name "Leonard". The Inazuman stranger returns and Mona abruptly teleports everyone away; the stranger is revealed to be the Fatui Harbinger Scaramouche, who had hoped to strike down the Traveler and orders his soldiers to keep researching the meteorites.

Act IV (Where Ancient Stars Align). Fischl and Oz step back to tend the growing number of sleepers. A book in the Mondstadt Library, "Of Mountains and Seas", written by Leonard, is half illegible until Mona reconstructs it: Leonard lived about two thousand years ago and never reached the top of Pilos Peak. Mona reasons that the mountain was levelled when Barbatos cleared the ice and is now Musk Reef. The party finds Scaramouche there, shaken, and he leaves after announcing that the stars are a lie. After fighting off his Fatui, they destroy the meteorite core, and Leonard's spirit speaks one last time before the sleepers can wake.

Fischl's guesses run ahead of the evidence throughout: she names a mountain demon's curse in Act I, a cold mountain in Act I and II, and a "curse of unanswered longing" in Act II. Paimon and Mona later wryly conclude she may use the wrong method but reach the right answer. Mona's reading in Act III is deliberately incomplete: she gets the name Leonard first and the context only from the book.

In Act I Paimon points out that the Guild's "travel in pairs" advice already describes a party of four. In Act II the Dawn Winery workers Ben and Fritz are separated; Ben is rescued from monsters, and Fritz, whose cart was hit by a meteorite on the road between Dihua Marsh and Stone Gate, is found asleep by the Inazuman stranger and the Millelith. The stranger tells the party he is "a vagrant from Inazuma" and leaves quickly when the Millelith arrive. In Act III the party tracks sleepers' dream details at Qingce Village: a patient who wakes demands home cooking (a Qingce Stir Fry) before telling them about the dream.

Revelations: The meteorites are fragments of Leonard's constellation, brought down from the sky, and the sleepers dream of climbing the mountain he failed to climb. Leonard was an adventurer who died without summiting Pilos Peak and instead put his efforts into designs for flying devices, the "Wings of Incompletion". The meteorites radiate elemental energy that lulls people into a hypnosis-like sleep, and a core meteorite contains a crystal holding his spirit. Pilos Peak no longer exists as a mountain: it is the small island Musk Reef.

A Fatui Harbinger is investigating the meteorites. He walks out of the shared dream on his own strength and says he has found that the stars and sky are a gigantic hoax. Mona, who was taught to speak of a "false sky" in astrology, takes the claim seriously rather than dismissing it.

In his last words Leonard says that where legs fail, tools might carry people, and where tools fail, wings might, and that "against the unknown, humanity stands as one". The event itself closes by tying this to gliding: Paimon remarks that the people of Mondstadt can now glide, and that anyone can now reach the former peak by boat.

Characters: Fischl and Oz lead the investigation by volume rather than method; Oz translates and keeps the party grounded. Mona supplies the astrology and an ego to match. Paimon asks the questions; the Traveler does the legwork. Katheryne dispatches them. The Harbinger Scaramouche (disguised as an Inazuman vagrant in Acts II and III) is the antagonist. Leonard appears only as a spirit in a cutscene.

Ben, Fritz, Adelinde and Draff appear as Dawn Winery and Springvale locals. Millelith officers staff the relief stations at Wangshu Inn and Qingce Village. The event also names Edna, Joyce, Adler, Allan and Hartman among the Springvale villagers.

Consequences: The victims wake when the core is destroyed. Fischl's event reward quest (the "Prinzessin's Pact") makes her obtainable. The Harbinger leaves Musk Reef after saying the sky is a hoax; the event does not follow up on his claim.

Placement: Released in Version 1.1 on 16 November 2020 and available until 30 November 2020 (final act released 26 November). It follows the Prologue Archon Quest (Mondstadt chapter) in release order and has no formal story prerequisite beyond Adventure Rank 20. In story terms it takes place with Scaramouche still a serving Harbinger; the event states no exact date relative to the Prologue.

Gameplay: Labelled game content, not story: players collected meteorite shards for Fading Star's Might, cleared meteorite remains in Meteorite Strike Zones, and ran the Star of Destiny "Fallen Star" challenge for Fading Star's Essence. Three optional "Meteoric Wave" quests followed each of the first three phases.

989.comment: Unreconciled Stars: Leonard and Pilos Peak
989.content:
In the Unreconciled Stars event Mona reconstructs a damaged book, "Of Mountains and Seas", by Leonard, an adventurer who lived about two thousand years ago. By forty he had conquered every domain of the world except Pilos Peak, which defeated him. Near the end of his life he put his hope into flying devices he called the Wings of Incompletion. Pilos Peak itself no longer exists above the sea; it is the small island of Musk Reef, which Mona matches to the legend that Barbatos cleared the ice and snow and reshaped Mondstadt.

The Mondstadt Library holds the book; the event connects Leonard to gliding only through Paimon's closing remark, not through any stated history of the glider.

990.comment: Unreconciled Stars: Scaramouche and the stars are a lie
990.content: In the event the Sixth Fatui Harbinger, Scaramouche (codename the Balladeer), first poses as a vagrant from Inazuma, then commands Fatui soldiers to keep researching the meteorites. He had planned to strike down the Traveler during the event. At Musk Reef he has been through the shared dream and says the stars and sky are a hoax, mentions "the Jester" with irritation, and leaves. Later canon identifies the Wanderer as this same person after he erased his identity from Irminsul (Version 3.3 playable); this event itself stays in Scaramouche's Fatui period.

991.content: Fischl introduces herself to the Traveler and Paimon in Act I as Prinzessin der Verurteilung from the Immernachtreich, with the raven Oz as her familiar. Oz openly translates her style ("Mein Fräulein means to say: hello"). By Act IV she steps aside to tend sleepers and tells the Traveler, out of her usual style, that she enjoyed their conversations, since most Guild adventurers only talk to her for Oz's scouting reports. Her character details belong in her own entry.

992.content:
Upstream Variations (also: Upstream Variations (Quest), Vodyanitsa's handwritten ticket quest, Happy-Quacky Phonograph Ducky quest): Upstream Variations is a World Quest series added in version 7.1. It is played over seven real-time days, one short scene per day, around Vodyanitsa, the principal soprano of the Korolevskiy Troupe. Over meals and visits she tells the Traveler and Paimon about a childhood friend who turned her tickets into social currency, and about the hollow feeling of singing to people who do not listen. The Traveler gives her a necklace-sized recording device, and she ends the week cheerful.

The quest is unlocked by completing "Wraith's Nocturne" and raising the Tidesong Cavern Meeting Point to Construction Level 2. The wiki notes that completing "White Night, Like a Dream Upon Waking" first gives the best experience. Completing it gives a special reward, the Happy-Quacky Phonograph Ducky, which gives Vodyanitsa a new decorative appearance (game-mechanics information). It also gives Primogems, Mora and talent materials.

Its tone moves from teasing comedy to a quietly sad centre on Day 2 and Day 5, and back to comedy at the end. It shows a more fragile Vodyanitsa than the cheerful one met in earlier content, and gives Odette, Alyosha, Ineffa, Aino and Escoffier supporting roles.

On the wiki, the event menu was noted to play one of several short vocal sound effects. This is a minor user-interface detail.

Plot: Day 1. At Podvorye Restaurant in Snezhnograd the Traveler and Paimon find Vodyanitsa at a table with only tea, sighing about a meeting with a "friend". She says food tastes like wax when she has to talk to that person, and meeting at a restaurant lets her pretend to eat instead. She orders a huge meal, then tells a story: a banquet in her honour, thrown by Lishnaya, head of a Snezhnayan guild, who praises the performance with exaggerated flattery. Vodyanitsa explains that Lishnaya was once a small girl who loved opera and worked part-time at the theater. Vodyanitsa gave her handwritten tickets, and the girl used to watch from behind the curtain. She stops the story there, gives the Traveler a blank notebook made at Maryyushka's Antykvariat with tickets inside, and says to bring it to the theater.

Day 2. The ticket is handwritten, so the theater policy sends the Traveler and Paimon backstage to watch from the wings. There Vodyanitsa continues. Lishnaya stopped using the backstage ticket, missed a performance with an excuse, and Vodyanitsa learned that a wealthy merchant sat in the seat she had saved. She says Lishnaya used the tickets to make powerful friends and is now part of the Zapolyarny elite. Vodyanitsa still thinks of her as a friend, because she does not like giving up on things that belong to her. She speaks of flower baskets from people who never come, and of the Water Imps' voices that she hears in the empty theater. Her tone turns bitter, then she suddenly asks if she scared them, claims a Water Imp named Xenia was speaking through her, and plays a prank. She offers a meal on her tab at Podvorye and says to meet at Sadov-Arbat. Alone, she repeats a lament as if answering voices, and names two Water Imps, Xenia and Paraskeva.

Day 3. At Sadov-Arbat, Vodyanitsa has finished shopping. Two fans, Malinina and Rozhdestvensky, hover outside; she overhears them from a distance, invites them in and gives them signed tickets. She tells the Traveler she keeps handwritten tickets in her pocket and always gives them to people who like her singing but cannot get a seat. In another flashback, she tells Lishnaya the ticket will always be valid. She says others tried to bribe her, resold tickets on the black market, or used them to pretend to have connections. She asks if the Traveler will trade their ticket; the Traveler and Paimon say no, and propose a meal as thanks.

Day 4. At Podvorye the Traveler meets Escoffier and her sous-chef Savanna, who are asking the owner, Nefedov, to let them cook in return for taking ingredients. Escoffier says she guessed the Traveler's next stop would be Snezhnaya after reading about events in Nod-Krai in The Steambird. Vodyanitsa recalls tasting Hotel Debord's new cake on a visit to Fontaine and calls it dry and gritty, which upsets Savanna. Savanna explains that customers buy cakes to show off, not to eat them, and that the kitchen staff are losing heart. Vodyanitsa says it is like singing an aria to an audience that is not listening. Escoffier tells Savanna she must balance being a head chef with being a baker. Vodyanitsa suggests they bake a cake for Odette, the prima ballerina, and a montage shows Fontainian dishes made from Snezhnayan ingredients.

Day 5. The Traveler finds Vodyanitsa and Odette on the theater stage. Odette notes Vodyanitsa has been off for five days and asks if the voices are back; Vodyanitsa calls them not real. Vodyanitsa plans a special performance for those who hold handwritten tickets, and to declare that some tickets are invalid. While she is backstage, Odette tells the Traveler and Paimon why: Vodyanitsa knows many songs written by Water Imps and keeps the songs alive by performing them. When other singers were taught them, the shows sold poorly, so Vodyanitsa used her fame to bring people in. Odette adds that Vodyanitsa fears being forgotten. She then says she overheard it all while Vodyanitsa talked in her sleep.

Day 6. At Sadov-Arbat, Ineffa delivers the Happy-Quacky Phonograph Ducky, a small wearable phonograph that Aino built after the Traveler wrote to her. It has limited recording space and the memory must be replaced, which Aino wants paid in ice cream, which Ineffa rations. Ineffa has also come to look for Jahoda, and the exchange changes slightly depending on whether the Traveler has seen the Jahoda anecdote. An interlude follows from Vodyanitsa's point of view: she walks through Snezhnograd, hears fans' ambition and thinks of being forgotten, and later sits alone in her room. The Traveler and Paimon arrive at her window with food and the gift. The Traveler promises to listen and to remember any song, and mentions a director friend and actors who would give her songs attention. Vodyanitsa accepts, then asks for the Traveler's most sincere singing and drags everyone out for a Whopperflower hunt.

Day 7. The night's Whopperflower hunt ended with only a photograph of a Whopperflower, and Vodyanitsa gave the party medicine against colds. At the theater she then gives a performance for a small audience, mostly handwritten-ticket holders, with a few tickets sold to the public. Afterward she is cheerful, says the ducky is full of songs, including recordings of Paimon's and the Traveler's songs from the night before, and threatens to release them. She says that because the Traveler promised to listen, they will be a regular, and the handwritten ticket never expires. Characters in the audience react: Vesna and Danica discuss the fae, Odette says a Water Imp's song is the most sincere sound, Mitya and Valeriy comment, Alyosha with Tugarin listens, Escoffier and Savanna react, Aino and Ineffa discuss the rule against recording devices in the theater and Vodyanitsa's ticket for them, Arlecchino praises the performance and says Tartaglia missed it on another mission, and Sandrone, as Marionette, jokes that Columbina has heard the songs. Leaving the theater after talking to everyone ends the quest.

Revelations: - Vodyanitsa, a Water Imp, hears the voices of the dead Water Imps in the empty theater and keeps their songs alive through performance.
- She is hurt that many fans treat her handwritten tickets as status symbols, not invitations to listen.
- Her friendship with Lishnaya was real, and the break came when Lishnaya used a ticket for business.
- The Traveler promises to listen to and remember Vodyanitsa's songs, which ends the quest on a hopeful note.

- Odette watches over Vodyanitsa; she says she learned the reason for Vodyanitsa's sadness only by overhearing her talk in her sleep.
- The Happy-Quacky Phonograph Ducky is named by Aino, who likes ducks, and looks like Vodyanitsa's own necklace.
- Arlecchino and Sandrone are present as audience members in the final scene and treat the performance respectfully.

Characters: - Vodyanitsa, the central character, presented as sociable and teasing in public and lonely in private.
- The Traveler and Paimon.
- Odette, the prima ballerina, who explains Vodyanitsa's motives.
- Lishnaya, a guild head, in flashbacks.

- Escoffier and Savanna, Fontaine chefs at Podvorye (Day 4).
- Ineffa and Aino, who deliver and designed the ducky (Day 6), with Jahoda mentioned.
- Staff and audience members, including Vzdykhalov, Buturlina, Nefedov, Yevlena, Malinina, Rozhdestvensky, Avreliya, Scheffield, Burnaya, Agarova, Arkady and Taisia, plus final-scene appearances by Vesna, Danica, Mitya, Valeriy, Alyosha with Tugarin, Arlecchino and Sandrone.

Consequences: Vodyanitsa gains a recording device and a promise from the Traveler to hear her songs. She plans to keep performing the Water Imps' music. The Traveler's handwritten ticket remains valid and now gives access to regular shows. Ineffa and Aino also receive tickets.

Vodyanitsa's decorative appearance changes when the ducky is used (game-mechanics information). The quest provides a notebook item, "Vodyanitsa's Special Notebook".

Placement: Story order: after "Wraith's Nocturne" (a prerequisite). It is recommended after "White Night, Like a Dream Upon Waking". Release order: version 7.1. It shares the Korolevskiy Theater setting with "Variations on Belyi and Chernyi", where Odette plans a schedule; Vodyanitsa and Odette appear in both.

993.content: Vodyanitsa gives out tickets she writes by hand to people who love her singing but cannot get a seat. They are valid for nearly any show: the holder sits in an empty seat if there is one, otherwise backstage. She meant them as invitations to listen, but some people tried to bribe her, resold them for large sums, or used them to pose as connected. She plans to declare some tickets invalid.

994.content: Vodyanitsa has memorized every song a Water Imp performed at the Korolevskiy Theater and sings them at special shows. She says she hears Xenia and Paraskeva, two departed Water Imps, in the empty hall. Odette says that to Vodyanitsa, those voices never really disappeared. Whether they are real is left open.

995.content: Lishnaya is the head of a Snezhnayan guild and a member of the Zapolyarny elite. As a girl she loved opera, worked part-time at the theater and was Vodyanitsa's friend. Vodyanitsa says she later used her tickets for networking and to impress a wealthy merchant. Vodyanitsa has not given up on her.

996.content: A small wearable phonograph built by Aino at the Traveler's request, brought by Ineffa. It looks like Vodyanitsa's necklace and has limited recording space. Aino named it after her love of ducks and wanted ice cream for each replacement memory.

key: Valor's Afterglow: The Faint Light Remembered
997.content:
Valor's Afterglow (also: Valor's Afterglow: Return by Sundown, Valor's Afterglow: The Faint Light Remembered, Zhiqiong's Letter quest, Zhiqiong's departure): A three-part Version 2.6 world quest series in The Chasm: Underground Mines. After The Chasm Delvers, the young cartographer Zhiqiong still works for the exploration team. The Traveler helps her place measuring beacons, rescues her when she is trapped in the dark mud, and finds the letter she leaves when she goes deeper alone.

It requires The Chasm Delvers and is released as three quests on consecutive days: Valor's Afterglow, Return by Sundown, and The Faint Light Remembered. Its theme is what drives ordinary mortals without Visions to risk their lives for the chance of being remembered.

Zhiqiong's reasoning is voiced through her talk with the Traveler about Stanley's lost friend, through Jinwu's and Muning's worry, and through her long farewell letter. The series ends with her gone and the camp's members unsure whether they were right to hold her back.

Plot: Part 1, Valor's Afterglow (Day 1). The Chasm is now safer, so Zhiqiong asks the Traveler to help place five measuring beacons built by Jinwu. The beacons track the dark mud and gather data for the scholar Khedive to analyse. The Traveler returns with her to the camp and is thanked. If the Traveler talks to her again, she explains why she is so stubborn and reckless: adventurers are drawn to danger, and she hopes to be remembered as one who faced The Chasm.

Part 2, Return by Sundown (Day 2). Jinwu is distraught: Zhiqiong went to retrieve the beacons and has been away five or six hours. The Traveler searches the beacon sites and finds her south of the Stony Halls, trapped in the dark mud and attacked by monsters. After clearing the monsters, the Traveler carries her to the camp. Khedive gives her medicine, and the Traveler brings her Jinwu's soup. Zhiqiong apologises and asks the Traveler to come back later.

Part 3, The Faint Light Remembered (Day 3). Zhiqiong has vanished from the camp, insisting on leaving. Jinwu and the Traveler go up to tell Muning, who learns she has gone and organises a search party. After the quest, the Traveler finds her abandoned camp in the southwest corner of The Glowing Narrows with her letter and a Frostglaze Crystal. The letter says she will follow a path deeper. Back at camp, Jinwu reads it and admits she cannot judge Zhiqiong.

In Part 1 Zhiqiong asks whether Stanley's friend who did not return is truly dead, or "alive" because adventurers still remember him. She says she would rather leave an impression even in failure than be forgotten. She also says she does not adventure for anyone else, or even for herself. She describes mortals without Visions, in a world ordered by the gods, refusing to go quietly, and quotes a saying she heard from a senior from Sumeru who heard it from the Eremites: someone not afraid of dying so that they might truly live.

In Part 2 Zhiqiong, half-conscious, murmurs that Jinwu should not be disappointed, and speaks of a golden city, a black watchtower and envoys having left. Paimon dismisses it as nonsense. Jinwu reflects that she has watched many young people treat adventure as noble only to find it too late to regret, and wonders whether she even has the right to stop her.

In Part 3 Muning reveals that the Ministry of Civil Affairs had decided, because her maps were so useful to Huishan Hall, to invite Zhiqiong to become a formal consultant and guide. He argues that dreams should not come before life, and says he had hoped she had forgotten her unrealistic dreams of adventurers like Roald and Stanley. He admits he wondered whether asking the Traveler to come to The Chasm had reignited her drive.

Gameplay details per the wiki: Parts 1 and 2 each give Adventure EXP, 30 Primogems and 30,000 Mora (plus Hero's Wit), and Part 3 gives a smaller reward. The sites for the beacons are around the dark mud, and in Part 2 she is found at the beacon site south of the Stony Halls; the other sites need not be checked once she is found. Her letter includes a hand-drawn map.

Revelations: Zhiqiong's motives are laid out: she wants to be remembered, to put her own mortal names on the unmapped places of The Chasm, and to show how far someone not chosen by the gods can go. Her letter also questions how the gods and the Traveler regard ordinary mortals and their labour, asked at a time when Rex Lapis had only just left Liyue.

The letter describes what she saw: stone halls crawling into the dark, purple mud gushing like lava, translucent azure crystals floating in the air, damaged stone tablets carved with maps of ancient places. She left half-finished names on her map as a parting gift. It also gives each team member a personal farewell, thanks the Traveler, and says she is not blessed with a Vision and that Khedive may be right that the Chasm's secrets are beyond mere mortals.

Characters: Zhiqiong: young, headstrong cartographer-adventurer who admires famed adventurers and keeps going despite injury. Jinwu: a veteran of the mines who builds the beacons and looks after the young adventurers, gruff and caring; she gave up on becoming great and feels she cannot judge. Khedive: a scholar of the team (Zhiqiong calls his terminology Sumeru jargon) who analyses the data and gives Zhiqiong medicine. Muning: a Ministry of Civil Affairs official at the surface who sees her as a friend and is angered by her risk-taking. Paimon and the Traveler: support her, rescue her, and disagree on whether to stop her.

Her letter also names Clitopho, a former Treasure Hoarder, whom she apologises to for her earlier distrust; and wishes Leonard, Stanley and Roald as her adventuring models. Wiki trivia notes that Stanley's story, as revealed in the later quest Should You Be Trapped in a Windless Land, is not quite as Zhiqiong believed. The real Stanley died in the Mare Jivari, and his friend Hans Archibald took on his identity so he would not be forgotten. Zhiqiong's remarks in this series do not reflect that.

Consequences: Zhiqiong's camp stays in The Glowing Narrows permanently. Collecting her letter gives the achievement "Valor's Afterglow" and unlocks a new viewpoint, The Court of Pillars. Her story is left open: the team does not know whether she will return.

Placement: Released in Version 2.6 as a direct follow-up to The Chasm Delvers. Each part is unlocked after the daily reset following the previous one. Release and story order match. Her letter says Rex Lapis has only just left, which places the series shortly after his departure from Liyue.

998.content: A quest item found in a camp in the southwest corner of The Glowing Narrows after The Faint Light Remembered. Zhiqiong addresses Jinwu, Khedive, Clitopho, Muning and the Traveler, asking questions about how the gods see mortals, and announces she will go deeper into The Chasm to mark it on her map with names that belong to mortals. The item text notes a slightly bitter scent of Qingxin.

999.content: Jinwu is a long-serving miner at the Chasm exploration team's camp. She builds the measuring beacons, cooks the soup for Zhiqiong, and watches over the young adventurers. She says she gave up on becoming great and has grown used to ordinary days, so she feels she cannot judge Zhiqiong's choice.

1000.content: Muning is a Ministry of Civil Affairs official who helped Zhiqiong get her post in The Chasm. He is Zhiqiong's friend and, when she leaves, organises the Millelith search party. He tells the Traveler that the Ministry had decided to invite her as a formal consultant and guide.

key: Variations on Belyi and Chernyi: Schedule
1001.content:
Variations on Belyi and Chernyi (also: Variations on Belyi and Chernyi: Schedule, Odette's schedule quest, Black Snow Swan schedule quest): Variations on Belyi and Chernyi is a Snezhnaya World Quest series added in version 7.0 and set at the Korolevskiy Theater. The Traveler and Paimon become Odette's temporary managers for two weeks. Odette is the troupe's prima ballerina, and she is about to premiere the ballet "Black Snow Swan" while also taking on a Fatui monster-clearing mission. The player fills in a schedule of hunts, rehearsals, fan meetings and rest, and the result decides one of five endings.

The quest is unlocked by raising the Korolevskiy Theater Meeting Point to Construction Level 2. It consists of a short setup quest and a longer "Schedule" quest. The planner affects Odette's inner sense of self ("Self-Identity"), how others see her ("External Recognition") and her energy (game-mechanics information); the wiki says that tasks matter more than points for the ending. The series grants Primogems, Mora and talent materials, and the Schedule quest grants a "Black Snow Swan Archive" item.

Its real subject is Odette's divided life: a ballerina in the spotlight and a member of the Fatui who was recruited as a child. Her desire for both external praise and self-approval is the answer she reaches in the best ending.

In several scenes, the "Black Snow Swan" ballet mirrors Odette. It tells of a swan whose feathers are a different colour from the flock, who finally stops trying to fit in and flies higher than any white swan.

Plot: Setup. At the theater the Traveler and Paimon see a poster for "Black Snow Swan" and overhear Vodyanitsa trying to talk Odette out of taking a Fatui monster-hunting mission only two weeks before the premiere. Odette insists she can do both, and has applied knowing the schedule. Vodyanitsa makes her agree to let someone else plan her time. Odette chooses the Traveler, citing trust built when they were trapped in the theater and familiarity with the Fatui, while Vodyanitsa objects that she has known Odette much longer and says she would schedule too much rest. The Traveler is given the planner. The premiere is in two weeks and the Fatui mission assessment is in one.

Schedule. Each day the player chooses a type of activity: monster hunt, dance rehearsal, fan meeting, rest or relaxation. Special scenes appear depending on the choice (see below). Week one ends with the Fatui mission examination and week two with the performance.

Monster hunt. Odette is clearing monsters from an area she used to practise dancing in as a child. She says she loves dancing in nature and that she wanted the area to stay peaceful, but also that she hoped it would help her interpret the Black Snow Swan, a role she practised as a child and never performed. As a child it was her least favourite role, she says, because she did not want to be like the swan, yet her real life came to resemble it. She tells the story's ending: the swan stops trying to fit in, lives proudly alone and flies into the clouds. In another scene she says that she hated joining the Fatui as a child, because it took time from dance, and that her father's death and her mother's pain destroyed her family's happiness.
