1036.content: The top-ranked guide of the People of the Springs, who boasts of having been to the mysterious island alone and of having found rare crystals in an underground ruin. He turns Viramdra away as unskilled, then recommends Mualani to him, which Nuu suggests was because he thought she could not reach the island and so could not expose him. Nuu says Koolau never completed the trip, though Koolau denies it.

1037.comment: Where the Springs Return: Nuu's Choice
1037.content: Nuu is Mualani's teacher. He reached the mysterious island long before her and, with his companions, chose to tell no one so that the legend could keep inspiring young guides. He gives Mualani a talisman made from an unusual Spinel Fruit that turns out to match the fruit growing in the underground cave, and takes it back after she completes the journey. He tells her that a guide's duty is to deliver clients safely, not to prove anything.

1038.comment: Where the Springs Return: The Island Scam
1038.content: A small ring of tribespeople, including Kaulu and Kaeho, who sold tourists fake guided trips to the mysterious island, with photos and gear sold at inflated prices and receipts written in ink that faded. They claimed the fees as travel expenses so that the money was hard to prosecute, and used false names. Amina asked the Traveler and Paimon to pose as victims and gather evidence. Kaulu was caught after his fake island reveal.

key: A Commission From the Curatorium of Secrets
Return Home, Children of the Desert
1039.content:
Where Waves Meet the Reef (also: Nod-Krai Trade Expo event, A Commission From the Curatorium of Secrets, Encirclement of Bullets and Silk, Toys for the Children, Return Home, Children of the Desert, Tales of Many): The expo's one firm rule is that there must be no violence. The Traveler registers three headline exhibitors (Beidou, Navia with Clorinde, and Aino with Ineffa), then brokers a deal in which Yelan and Chevreuse may run their sting provided they do nothing that wrecks the expo and the Traveler takes part in every operation. The sting catches a ring of agents, but it also exposes Ashvapati, a Sumeru-born former Akademiya researcher who, by his own account, once designed weapons for a desert Eremite band that were turned against that band. He had lured the investigators to Nod-Krai to reach the man he blames, Sennedjem.

The story ends without bloodshed and with a public trial for the arms dealers. A cutscene shows the Alcor-class No. 2 shooting down Ashvapati's rockets as a firework display, and Dori sells the children a gemstone said to grow an oasis. Players who earned enough Joint Exhibition Popularity could invite Anemo Jahoda ("Windthreading Shadow") to their party. The event also included three minigames and a large set of optional open-world "Tales of Many" character interactions.

Plot: Part I: Nefer hires the Traveler and Paimon to help Jahoda coordinate the Nod-Krai Trade Expo, whose one rule is no violence. They bring in Beidou (selling an upgraded Guizhong Ballista), Navia with Clorinde (a Fontaine pneuma and ousia relay device) and Aino with Ineffa (blueprints for the Thwack 'n Smack Defense Bots). Yelan and Chevreuse reveal that their goods are bait for the same international arms ring; Nefer lets them proceed so long as the expo's protected deals are not disturbed and the Traveler joins every operation.
Part II: Yelan, Chevreuse and their allies trap the ring's buyer aboard the Flagship while the other agents are rounded up. The Traveler subdues the buyer and Chevreuse corrals a runaway agent.
Part III: Beidou's prototype ballistas vanish. The trail leads to Ashvapati, the guild member guarding three orphaned children, whose letter confesses a past as an Akademiya exile who designed weapons for a desert Eremite band that were turned against it.
Epilogue: Ashvapati lures Sennedjem, the man he blames, to a meeting and plans to die with him under a salvo of rockets. Beidou's ship turns the rockets into fireworks, Sennedjem is arrested, Ashvapati is spared charges but expelled from the guild, and Dori sells the children a gemstone that grows an oasis.

Full account by part.
Part I, A Commission From the Curatorium of Secrets: A letter from Nefer brings the Traveler and Paimon to the Curatorium of Secrets in Nasha Town. She explains that Nasha Town grew out of a lawless black market and that the annual Nod-Krai Trade Expo is meant to be the largest "legal" black market in Teyvat. Jahoda, organising for the Voynich Guild, is overwhelmed, so the Traveler is hired for participant coordination. Nefer's only demand is that no violence happen at the expo. Three guests must be fetched: Beidou, captain of the Crux fleet, selling an upgraded Guizhong Ballista from her second ship, the Alcor-class No. 2 (Yelan has hitched a ride on that ship); Navia of the Spina di Rosula, selling a Fontaine Research Institute relay device that releases pneuma and ousia energy, with Clorinde as bodyguard and Chevreuse also in town; and Aino with Ineffa, selling blueprints for the Thwack 'n Smack Defense Bots. At the venue a bully pushes the children Ati, Neb and Raya aside over their booth, Jahoda faces him down, and the children's guardian Ashvapati, a guild member, turns up. After the expo opens, Yelan and Chevreuse separately question Aino and then reveal to the Traveler that they are both hunting the same arms ring, and that their goods are bait. The Traveler takes them to Nefer, who suspected as much. Yelan reports that bandits on Liyue's border have recently got a mysterious weapon, and Chevreuse that gangs in Fontaine are being armed. Nefer agrees to let them work as long as anything illegal happens outside the expo's protected deals and the Traveler is part of every step.
Part II, Encirclement of Bullets and Silk: Two days later a ring agent approaches Beidou and Navia's stalls and, after haggling, proposes a private deal away from the guild. Yelan, Chevreuse, Beidou, Navia and Clorinde plan a coordinated takedown: Yelan, with the Traveler as hidden backup, meets the buyer aboard the Flagship and stalls him while Chevreuse and Navia's local Spina members round up the other agents. The Traveler subdues the buyer; Chevreuse shoots obstacles to corral a fleeing agent and traps him by breaking a guild signboard; all twenty agents are accounted for. Tarno then summons the Traveler back to the venue.
Part III, Toys for the Children: Jahoda reports that Beidou's prototype ballistas have been stolen from storage. The children say they cannot reach Ashvapati and that he had steered them to Beidou's booth. At the Curatorium, Nefer recalls a band of Eremites who gained advanced weapons about a decade ago, sold them to the highest bidder, and were destroyed by their own creations; the children come from such a band. After Yelan locates Ashvapati's hideout, the group finds a cargo manifest of the same kind that had set both Liyue and Fontaine on the trail, a display ballista, and a letter addressed to them. In the letter Ashvapati confesses. He says he was a Kshahrewar researcher expelled from the Akademiya for taking forbidden texts, was saved from dying in the desert by an Eremite chief, Khaemwaset, and made toys for the oasis children. A newcomer named Sennedjem persuaded him to build a lure that turns Ruin Drakes into weapons, then sold the designs to the oasis's enemies. When the camp burned Ashvapati saved only three children and has raised them since while hunting Sennedjem.
Epilogue, Return Home, Children of the Desert: Ashvapati poses as Sennedjem's contact, using the old meeting signal, to lure him to the rendezvous while the authorities hold his agents, and raises a barrier around them intending to die with him under a salvo of rockets. Yelan argues that weapons made for peace-keeping can later become toys, as fireworks did, and that people are the ones who do evil. Beidou's ship fires on the rockets and turns them into fireworks. Sennedjem and his men are taken into Maison Gardiennage custody. Chevreuse declines to charge Ashvapati in exchange for Nefer dropping any claim over the broken signboard; Nefer ejects Ashvapati from the Voynich Guild for the rules he broke but urges him to take the children back to Sumeru. Dori sells them a gemstone made by the mage Alice that grows an oasis, priced for "whatever keeps the kids happy", which she sets as what the children earned at the expo.
Details of Part I: Jahoda is delighted to learn that the Traveler will cover participant coordination, and promises Nod-Krai Hot Dogs as thanks. She warns that Beidou and Navia must not be offended. Beidou says her ballista can be guided by remote control from far away and jokes that it is antique compared to what Liyue's Millelith use. Navia, represented as the Spina's president, jokes about being called top dog of the criminal underworld, and Clorinde remarks that Nod-Krai is chaotic. Chevreuse, on official business for the Special Security and Surveillance Patrol, notes that she must bend rules in a lawless place. Ineffa explains the craftshop's dessert budget is separate from research funds because overspending on desserts had caused research shortages in at least 47 cases. When Yelan and Chevreuse realise they are using the expo as bait for the same target, Chevreuse says she has looked into the Curatorium head and does not want her to know their plans, while Yelan guesses that Nefer arranged the Traveler's role precisely so they would come to her.
Details of Part II: Beidou fields the children's curious questions about her ballista, promises them a look at it in action after the expo, and Ashvapati remarks that he is envious that Liyue children can treat a warship as a playground. The ring agent suggests moving the deal somewhere the Voynich Guild cannot take its cut; Beidou, who is registered with the expo, sends a proxy. Yelan deduces from the buyer's wish for disassembly and discreet crates that the ring resells at ports such as Yilong Wharf and Lumidouce Harbor. Clorinde reveals that Navia has quietly won over Nod-Krai gangs who owed the Spina favours, and Navia laughs at being called boss. The Maison Gardiennage's reputation for firm interrogation is joked about by both investigators.
Details of Part III: Navia tells the children their uncle cannot be judged by what he made but only after asking why, a process Fontaine's courts are built for, and promises they will have a chance to ask him. Chevreuse and Yelan agree that the cargo manifest, the one slip in an otherwise untraceable operation, being in Ashvapati's hideout shows he laid the trail himself, and that he was acting alone. His letter praises them for removing more than half the gang within a day. In the flashback Khaemwaset refuses Ashvapati's offer to upgrade weapons because his scimitar is enough and the oasis is safely remote; he suggests toys for the children instead. Sennedjem's group had earlier abandoned the oasis after a sandstorm and returned when no band would take them. When Ashvapati left the arms deal after learning how they were being used, Sennedjem's men sold to the oasis's old enemies, in his words as an excuse to raise the price.

Further details: Jahoda announces over the loudspeaker that registration is complete and the expo is open. When the Traveler brings Yelan and Chevreuse to Nefer, she greets them by origin (Miss Yelan of Liyue and Miss Chevreuse of Fontaine) and asks only that she hear the real story afterwards. The sting stops short of the leader because the ring's head is not at the expo; the epilogue shows the person collecting the goods to be Sennedjem, who in his own words lives in Fontaine's Vasari Passage as a respected benefactor. The children's own expo earnings are counted as payment for the gemstone, a detail Dori calls a way for them to say they bought back their home through their own work. In the finale cutscene the bully who harassed the children returns, is startled by one of Aino's bots and sent off by Jahoda, Aino and Ineffa. The wiki lists a trivia note that Liben is shown with a short beard in the firework cutscene although he has only a moustache.

Revelations: The mastermind of the arms ring is Sennedjem, a former Eremite who sold weapons to the very band that had sheltered him, and who now poses as a Fontaine philanthropist. Ashvapati, the children's guardian and a Voynich Guild member, is a former Kshahrewar researcher who designed those weapons and tracked Sennedjem for years; he lied to the guild about almost everything but his desert origins. He planned to die with Sennedjem but is talked down. Nefer's home is the desert too, she says, and she hopes his story shows another way of life there; she names Lesser Lord Kusanali as a reason the Sumeru of today is changing.

Yelan's remarks that fireworks began as weapons against evil forces and wild beasts frame the event's theme: weapons and toys can be the same technology in different times, and the real question is who uses them and why. Chevreuse's verdict is that Ashvapati's crime lay not in researching weapons but in failing to use his skill to protect those he loved.

Characters: Nefer, who runs the Curatorium of Secrets, hires the Traveler and Paimon. Jahoda is the harried Voynich Guild manager and the event's reward character. Beidou, Navia, Clorinde, Chevreuse and Yelan carry the investigation, and Aino and Ineffa supply the defense bots. Ashvapati, Ati, Neb and Raya form the central family, and Dori is the Sumeru merchant who helps resolve it. Sennedjem is the antagonist, and Khaemwaset, Ashvapati's rescuer, appears only in flashback. Tarno is a messenger, and the ring's agents are nameless.

Ashru appears with Nefer at the Curatorium. Other exhibitors on the roster include Liben, Lakkaberry, Wislawa, Nkrumah, Fassbender, Gongmiao, Huoxiang, Fengyun, Seahawk, Stone Stool and Zhiyao. The optional Tales of Many bring in Chasca, Citlali, Flins, Illuga, Alice, Nicole, Diluc and Varka.

Consequences: The ring's agents and Sennedjem are taken into custody by Fontaine's Special Security and Surveillance Patrol (Maison Gardiennage) to face a public trial; Yelan considers her objective met. Ashvapati is not charged by the Fontaine authorities and is expelled from the Voynich Guild by Nefer, who urges him to take the children back to the desert. He accepts the oasis gemstone for the children. The expo ends as an unusually memorable one in Nefer's judgement.

Placement: A Version 6.5 (Luna VI) flagship event, running 27 April to 14 May 2026 in three phases (27 April, 29 April and 1 May). Players needed Adventure Rank 20 and the Prologue Act III quest Song of the Dragon and Freedom; the Archon Quest True Moon was recommended first. The story is set in Nod-Krai and mentions Sumeru under Lesser Lord Kusanali. The Part I side quests are concurrent, and Parts II and III each begin two in-game days after the previous part.

Gameplay: Game mechanics, not in-world fact. The event had three minigames, each unlocked by one of the Part I side quests: Thwack 'n Smack Defense Bots (a defense game using Aino's bots, tied to the Aino and Ineffa side quest), Pneumousia Barrage Countermeasure (an experimental shield that absorbs same-alignment projectiles, tied to Navia), and Fire Support Assault (guiding a Guizhong Ballista, tied to Beidou). Completing challenges raised Joint Exhibition Popularity, which could be spent toward an invitation to Jahoda; rewards included up to 970 Primogems and a Crown of Insight. Optional Tales of Many interactions unlocked as the story progressed.

1040.comment: Where Waves Meet the Reef: Nod-Krai Trade Expo
1040.content:
An annual market held on the shoreline southeast of Nasha Town once shipping routes reopen, organised by the Voynich Guild and billed as the biggest "legal" black market in Teyvat. The town began as an unregulated black market, and the expo preserves that spirit of unrestricted trade. The guild takes a cut from seller and buyer and promises safety to all, so violence is forbidden, but deals struck outside the expo are not protected. This 6.5 edition was unusually large.

Exhibitors included weapons makers (Beidou's ballista, the Spina's pneuma and ousia relay), toys and blueprints from the Krumkake Craftshop, a Natlan seller offering "Wayob fragments", a Fatui sergeant selling scrap muskets, a Mondstadt wine vendor, a curio dealer, and Dori with goods from the Hexenzirkel.

1041.comment: Where Waves Meet the Reef: Ashvapati and Sennedjem
1041.content: Ashvapati is a Voynich Guild member and guardian of Ati, Neb and Raya. By his own letter he is an expelled Kshahrewar scholar who was taken in by the Eremite chief Khaemwaset and built toys for children until Sennedjem, a trader who had left the oasis and then returned, convinced him to design Ruin Drake lures. Sennedjem sold the designs to enemies of the oasis, the camp was burned, and Ashvapati saved only three children. Sennedjem later became a rich arms supplier and, by his own claim, a Fontaine philanthropist. All of this is told by Ashvapati and Sennedjem themselves.

1042.comment: Where Waves Meet the Reef: Ati, Neb and Raya
1042.content: Three orphaned children, raised by Ashvapati, who run a toy booth at the expo. Neb loves building mechanisms and wants an Aino bot blueprint; Ati prefers practical purchases such as clothing; Raya hopes everyone can stop arguing. Jahoda promises to look after them. They are not involved in the arms ring, and in the end they ask Ashvapati to remain their uncle even after learning the whole truth.

1043.comment: Where Waves Meet the Reef: Yelan and Chevreuse joint operation
1043.content: Yelan of Liyue's Ministry of Civil Affairs and Chevreuse of Fontaine's Special Security and Surveillance Patrol come to Nod-Krai after the same international arms-trading network, each carrying a trap product (Beidou's ballista as the bait). After Nefer's mediated deal they pool intelligence: the Traveler must be included in every move, and the expo's own rules must not be broken. They capture twenty agents and the buyer without casualties, then pursue Ashvapati as the best lead. Afterwards each returns to their duties; Chevreuse praises working together.

1044.comment: Where Waves Meet the Reef: Dori's oasis gemstone
1044.content: A gemstone made by the mage Alice which, planted in the ground, grows a spring and then an oasis even in a desert. At the expo Dori sells it for the price Alice set, "whatever keeps the kids happy", which she fixes as what Ati, Neb and Raya earned. In the Tales of Many, Alice and Nicole test a pricing scheme paid in virtues like courage and kindness rather than Mora, which sold little.

1045.content:
Whirling Waltz (also: Whirling Waltz Event, Chevalmarin Film Fantasyland event, Eclectic Escapades, Movie Masterpieces, Mellow Manor): Whirling Waltz is the Version 5.6 spring flagship event. After overhearing old friends at a Court of Fontaine newsstand, the Traveler and Paimon are invited to run the Chevalmarin Film Fantasyland, a film-themed amusement park. Friends from across Teyvat arrive as visitors and consultants, and the story is told in light, character-focused Friendly Encounters rather than a quest chain.

The park has three attractions: Eclectic Escapades, Movie Masterpieces and Mellow Manor, plus a Theme Restaurant run by the chef Escoffier. The player upgrades attractions, hires staff and chooses theme dishes to raise revenue. The event's reward was the bow Sequence of Solitude.

It required Adventure Rank 20, a Fontaine Statue of The Seven and the Prologue Act III, and recommended Incandescent Ode of Resurrection, Animula Choragi Chapter Act I, Dulciaria Structura Chapter Act I, Mushroom Realm Mystery Act III and a Fontaine world quest first. Many staff members are callbacks to earlier quests and events.

The park is named after Surintendante Chevalmarin, a friend of Furina's, and carries themed zones for Fontaine, Natlan and Sumeru.

Plot: The Traveler and Paimon manage the Chevalmarin Film Fantasyland. As the park grows, Varesa from Natlan sets up a fruit stall, Sigewinne and Lynette become consultants for Mellow Manor and Eclectic Escapades, Dehya's mercenary band partners with them, and Furina becomes consultant for Movie Masterpieces and invites the Traveler and Paimon to co-direct a film with Escoffier.

**Varesa.** The Natlan orchard owner comes to promote her fruit after a letter from Escoffier. She goes shopping for clockwork parts for Iansan's gym equipment, tries Movie Masterpieces and then opens the Vibrant Orchard stall.

**Sigewinne.** The Fortress of Meropide's head nurse likes animated films and shows them to inmates. She becomes Mellow Manor's consultant after being called away to treat an inmate who tried to copy a film recipe.

**Lynette and Lyney.** Lynette arrives alone because Lyney is exhausted from watching a director's horror films. They coax him to the park, and Lynette consults for Eclectic Escapades.

**Dehya.** She was a guest star in a Fontaine adventure film, and the Blazing Beasts agree to pass desert commissions to the Traveler and Paimon.

**Furina.** The park's patron surveys visitors and becomes consultant for Movie Masterpieces.

**Varesa in detail.** She says Escoffier's order for her restaurant led to a chance to promote her orchard's fruit. In the Collective of Plenty she leaves a price list, a scale and a coin jar and no money ever goes missing, but Paimon warns Fontainians may not trust unattended stalls. Coach Iansan wants Fontainian clockwork meka parts to improve her gym equipment, and Varesa offers to teach Paimon beginner exercises. She plays Movie Masterpieces, loves the homages to films and comic-book heroes, and asks to be told about any future event so she can help design levels.

**Sigewinne in detail.** She heard about the park from Navia at the Beauty Association. Under the Fortress's new rules, well-behaved inmates can spend Credit Coupons on up to three films a week, and Sigewinne runs the projector herself. She has shown "My Neighbor Kokoro" and the long-running "Dom and Cherry". An inmate attempted the fictional "Magical Mouse Munchies" from three days of welfare meals and gave himself unfamiliar food poisoning; Giustina fetches her, and she returns once the patient is stable. She resolves to speak to Furina and Neuvillette about preventing copycat accidents.

**Lynette and Lyney in detail.** The siblings were invited by a director known for psychological horror. Lyney watched all of the director's films, and lost three nights of sleep. Lynette dislikes jump scares, enjoys Eclectic Escapades and likes watching guests' faces as they fall. She is also looking at animals for magic acts: Freminet's blubberbeasts and the obedient squirrels "Father" has praised. Lyney recovers at Mellow Manor and gets a new idea for an interactive magic show with a moving stage.

**Dehya in detail.** Dehya and fellow Blazing Beasts were cast in an action film; she was dismissed after wrecking half a set, while Uncle Scimitar became a star when the lead actor improvised shooting him instead of a sword fight. At the bar The Rusty Rudder she orders drinks, tells the Traveler they could be hired swords too and offers commissions for the region west of the Hypostyle Desert, north of the Desert of Hadramaveth, east of Ardravi Valley and south of the Ashavan Realm. She gives the Blazing Beasts' motto "We Protect, You Prosper!" and says she will send letters to Adventurers' Guild branches.

**Furina in detail.** She says she was first asked to approve plans for what she expected to be a small event, praises the Traveler and Paimon and says she suggested to several directors that they be named "Pioneers of the Film Industry". She says the park bears the name of her dear friend Surintendante Chevalmarin, so she runs a visitor survey and, wanting others to shine, declines to perform herself. At a dessert tasting she proposes a dramatic film about Escoffier's cooking and invites the Traveler and Paimon to direct it with her.

**Attractions.** Eclectic Escapades is a diving and gliding circuit collecting Adventure Coins, with six themed courses based on invented films such as "Journey to the Secret Sea" and "The Clockwork Express". Movie Masterpieces are action challenges with a time-slowing ability, based on invented films such as "The Champion Duelist", "RainbowEye" and "Doctor When". Mellow Manor is an animal enclosure where Cuddly Anemo Slimes, Good Little Hydro Fungi, Voracious Squirrels, Huge Golden Finches, Languorous Blubberbeasts, Placid Alpacas and Contented Capybaras are arranged for satisfaction.

**Business levels.** The park unlocks Mellow Manor at Business Level 2, a Natlan zone (Fire Tribe) at 4, a Sumeru zone (Eremite Camp) at 9 and a Fontaine zone (Classic High Street) at 14. The Theme Restaurant's dishes give temporary bonuses.

**Callbacks.** Staff include Helene, Melies and Petit Lumiere, who ran the three modes of Roses and Muskets, plus Jala, Miss Gardemetiquette and Basima the Fifth from the Dodoco, Lil' Fungi and Bing-Bang Finchball events. The wiki infers from his name and outfit that the staff member Captain Ferment O'Juice is Alphonse, a chef seen in Escoffier's character teaser.

Characters: Traveler, Paimon, Furina, Escoffier, Varesa, Sigewinne, Lynette, Lyney and Dehya.

Also Giustina, Iansan, Uncle Scimitar and Freminet (mentioned in dialogue), plus many staff recruited at the Staff Center.

Varesa is cheerful and trusting, Sigewinne warm and conscientious, Lynette dry and fond of calm films, Lyney sleep-deprived and playful, Dehya relaxed and practical and Furina theatrical but sincere.

Consequences: No lasting plot change is shown. Dehya's offer of Blazing Beasts commissions and Furina's plan for a film with Escoffier are left open.

Placement: Released in Version 5.6 and run from 9 May to 26 May 2025 (server time) in three phases (9, 11 and 13 May). It is a standalone event set in Fontaine, after the Fontinalia film festival of Roses and Muskets. The next Fontaine summer event, Sunny Summer Fontinalia, comes in Version 6.7.

1046.content: A film-themed amusement park in Fontaine named after Furina's friend Surintendante Chevalmarin. Its attractions are Eclectic Escapades, Movie Masterpieces and Mellow Manor. The Traveler and Paimon work as managers; Escoffier cooks for the Theme Restaurant.

1047.content: Dehya's mercenary band passes far-flung, high-pay, high-risk commissions in the region west of the Hypostyle Desert, north of the Desert of Hadramaveth, east of Ardravi Valley and south of the Ashavan Realm to the Traveler and Paimon, who will receive notice by letters through the Adventurers' Guild.

1048.comment: Whirling Waltz: Fortress of Meropide film screenings
1048.content: Under the Fortress's new regulations, well-behaved inmates can spend Credit Coupons to watch films up to three times a week. Sigewinne runs the projector and has shown animated films such as My Neighbor Kokoro and the long Dom and Cherry series.

key: White Night, Like a Dream Upon Waking
1049.comment: White Night, Like a Dream Upon Waking
1049.content:
White Night, Like a Dream Upon Waking (also: Chapter VII Act III, Snezhnaya Archon Quest Act III): Chapter VII Act III of the Archon Quest. The Tsaritsa Anastasya, back in Zapolyarny Palace after killing the monster behind the snowstorms, suspends Project Stuzha because of a curse of death. The Traveler finally meets her, learns why she wants the Gnoses, and helps a Seal of Life plan that draws out Rhinedottir.

The act has three quests: Light and Shadow, Intertwined; Sparks Converging Upon the Tundra; and One Move Left to Make. It places the Traveler in the Tsaritsa's court for the first time, shows her daily memory-recording habit and the sealed relic left by the Third Descender, introduces Vesna's authority over life, and ends with a theft in the Northland Bank vault. Released in version 7.1.

The act answers why the energy rationing paused but not why the Tsaritsa hoards Gnoses: she wants enough power to face the Heavenly Principles, which could destroy Snezhnaya with a Celestial Nail. Against the curse of death she sets a plan to harvest memory-bubbles called Seals of Life, a plan that is also bait. The next act is A Rekviem for the Underworld.

Plot: Tartaglia tells the Traveler and Paimon that suspending Project Stuzha has lightened the Veche, and arranges an audience. Danica, the Tsaritsa's head maid and personal attendant, tests the Traveler over a game of Mora. At court Anastasya cancels all investigation of the Traveler and speaks to them privately. Pierro and Mitya show a plan to counter the curse using Vesna's power over life. When Seals of Life go missing from Northland Bank, the Traveler and Vesna find a creature stealing them, and Rhinedottir arrives, as the Tsaritsa had intended.

Across three quests the Traveler is tested by Danica, attends the Tsaritsa's court, hears why she seeks the Gnoses and sees the seal left by the Third Descender. Pierro's Mirror of Remembrance reveals Ronova's collaboration with Rhinedottir, and Vesna's power of life inspires the Seal of Life collection. When seals are stolen from Northland Bank, the Traveler and Vesna find a creature of the Ruler of Life, and Rhinedottir arrives, as the Tsaritsa had planned.

Light and Shadow, Intertwined: at Glupov Tartaglia explains the mood after Stuzha's suspension and agrees to help file for an audience. At Podvorye Restaurant the Traveler is approached by Danica, who has read many reports on them and wants to see what sort of person they are. She names Capitano, who fought alongside the Traveler in Natlan, as her mentor and calls his passing an enormous loss for Snezhnaya, then proposes a Mora game he taught her, in which she tries to land a coin on the table and the Traveler must stop it. Vesna ends the game, saying it troubles guests, and pays for the meal.

The next day, at Zapolyarny Palace, the Traveler joins their first court session. The Tsaritsa wants only good manners. She hears from Pulcinella that civilian disruption was low, with a few corruption cases to review, and has the House of the Hearth's extra entries checked with the 3rd Druzhna Company. She tells Mitya and Pierro that she accepts their report: work on Project Mistilteinn stays halted until Ronova is dealt with. Mitya says none of their weapons can seriously harm the Ruler of Death, and Pantalone notes that any sign of progress triggers a mass death; Sandrone suggests moving the research materials to the Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau in Nod-Krai, but Mitya says the curse afflicts them directly and will follow them anywhere. Anastasya assures them the problem will be overcome and leaves it to Pierro. She tells the Traveler they are a formidable adversary she respects, and orders all investigations of them to stop and grants unrestricted access to the palace.

In her office, Anastasya asks about the Pyro Gnosis. The Traveler says it burned with Irminsul; she answers that, as part of the Third Descender's remains, it cannot stay among the Ley Lines long and will be ejected. Why does she want the Gnoses? To gain the power to face the Heavenly Principles. Snezhnaya has always been hostile land, forcing its people to grow quickly in military and economic strength, and so they have pushed to the edge of what the Principles allow and have long been at risk of a Celestial Nail. In a hidden basement she shows a large crystalline structure, a seal the Third Descender left, watched over by her predecessor the Belyi Tsar and undetected by the Principles. It reacts only to Gnoses, so she thinks all seven must be gathered to open it, though she does not know what it holds. Asked about her own authority, she says it is "love", but she will not use or identify with it because the love granted by the Heavenly Principles was false. The Traveler recalls Venti's similar words about freedom. Danica then reports that Pierro wishes to see her.

Pierro says their experiment is ready. Before leaving, Anastasya finishes the day's memory recording with a transcription prism; he explains that she believes memory cannot be completely trusted, and that a transcription prism, like a Stellar Linchpin, contains the Third Descender's power and so is free from certain laws of Teyvat. At the Armory Palace Mitya and Vesna wait. Pierro presents a large prism, the Mirror of Remembrance, or Svetovid Stone, a recent Armory Palace innovation. Mitya's soul now bears the mark of the Ruler of Death, and Anastasya reveals Vesna's secret: during the Hyperborean era the former Archangel stole a small portion of the Ruler of Life's power, which after changing hands was entrusted to the Vila, and Vesna inherited it with the blood of the first Vila. Memory fragments extracted with the prism show that Ronova had worked with Rhinedottir, "killing" without permission by exploiting a gap in the Heavenly Principles' monitoring cycles while Rhinedottir revived them before the Shades could catch it. Sandrone and Pantalone suggest using Vesna's small authority of life against death. Vesna extracts a "Seal of Life" from herself, a bubble holding an impactful memory that could defy death if enough are gathered. Everyone agrees; Vesna takes bubbles from all of them and notes the Tsaritsa has no happy memories. Mitya is told to assist Sandrone in researching how life force can be used to fight the Ruler of Death. Pantalone then voices concerns to Anastasya, and she agrees to listen.

Sparks Converging Upon the Tundra: Danica, given a few days off, apologises to the Traveler for her test, tidies their room and makes hot milk. She says she has worked as a maid for about three years and two months, though the Postelnitskaya family has served the Tsaritsa for three generations; her father was a travelling mercenary, the Tsaritsa persuaded her mother and grandmother to let her seek adventure abroad, and she returned when her homeland needed her. She hints that this was an act of love on the Tsaritsa's part. Two days later news that Seal of Life collection is under way has leaked, and many people are eager to help. Councilor Belozersky stumbles through questions. Pantalone explains that donation was obligatory for government officials and nobles, hence the Druzhna, while the public may donate at Northland Bank for compensation. Alyosha, Odette and Vodyanitsa volunteer. Vesna is overworked; Pevtsova, whom the Traveler had saved from monsters earlier, says the people of Svetloledovka will help. After harvesting seals there the party returns to Snezhnograd by train, during which the Traveler senses a presence that vanishes.

One Move Left to Make: Odette's subordinate reports that Seals of Life may be stolen, with the suspect targeting the frail and elderly. Alyosha is made up as an old man and, at Central Station, approaches Avaz, who questions him; if Alyosha convinces him, Avaz names a price in Mora and a meeting in two days before Alyosha seizes him, while failure leaves Avaz fleeing and caught by the Traveler. Back at the theatre Avaz threatens to report them to the Veche but, with Alyosha's rifle aimed, admits that as a Northland Bank employee he noticed seals missing from the vault and hints that a Harbinger, Pantalone, is responsible. The Traveler tells Anastasya, who sends Avaz to Fatui Internal Affairs and rules out Pantalone's direct role. With Vesna the Traveler goes to Northland Bank on the pretext of a withdrawal. Deep vaults require a train; Vesna disables an employee and takes his radio and keycard, and the pair infiltrate, take clearance cards, trigger an alarm and defeat guards before reaching Pantalone's office, where he expected them. He defends himself: before he was a Harbinger there were no state-owned banks in Snezhnaya, humans and fae kept separate rules and customs, and the Fatui unified them and founded the Northland Bank. Another alarm leads them to the vault where a creature of the Ruler of Life, the False Horned Steed, is draining the seals through portals. Pantalone activates turrets, Vesna revitalises the seals, and the Traveler subdues the creature. It rises again and charges Vesna, but Anastasya freezes it. Rhinedottir arrives, stops her, lets the beast (her own failed experiment) flee, and reclaims from Vesna the stolen "morsel" of power. At a snap of her fingers all seals return to their owners. It emerges that the collection was meant to force Rhinedottir to appear: Pantalone's concerns had been that mass collection would alert the Ruler of Life, and he had the Northland Bank spread the news so she could not ignore it. Rhinedottir says she had foreseen that Anastasya would try to win her over as her conflict with Ronova escalates, and refuses to help fight Ronova. Anastasya says she has information on Asmoday and offers to meet in seven days; Naberius judges this as placing the ball on their side, and Rhinedottir agrees. At Podvorye Restaurant Vesna says she is content to lose the power, which belonged to the Ruler of Life. Pantalone returns a beacon crafted from the sample of that power she had lent the bank, saying the Ruler of Life is uninterested in reclaiming every last morsel so long as no further large-scale collection is attempted, and that this was Her Majesty's design; he refuses to lend Vesna a train car, citing her insufficient credit. Lyney, Lynette and Freminet arrive but the Traveler lets them get on with their work.

The structure mirrors Act I's political tour in a more exclusive setting. The first quest is almost all conversation and ritual: court etiquette, Danica's test, the office, the sealed relic, the memory recording, the Mirror of Remembrance. The second shifts to community response: how Snezhnaya reacts when asked to give a memory for the Tsaritsa. The third is an investigation that ends in a staged confrontation, with the Tsaritsa already ahead of everyone. Details worth keeping straight: the Tsaritsa's name in court is Anastasya; the Mirror of Remembrance and the transcription prism are different objects; the Seal of Life is a bubble holding one strong memory, extracted from a person by Vesna.

The act is careful about who makes each claim. The history of Vesna's power (stolen by the former Archangel, passed down the Vila line) is Anastasya's explanation in the Armory Palace. The account of Ronova and Rhinedottir comes from fragments played back through the Mirror of Remembrance. Anastasya's reason for gathering Gnoses is her own, given privately to the Traveler. Pantalone's account of Northland Bank is his own, and Avaz's accusation is later shown to miss the real thief. The bait plan is revealed only after the fact: Pantalone raised the risk of alerting the Ruler of Life and proposed the leak, and he says the returned beacon was part of Her Majesty's design.

Revelations: Project Stuzha is on hold because of the curse of death. The Tsaritsa wants all seven Gnoses to unlock a seal left by the Third Descender and to gain strength against the Heavenly Principles. Her authority is love, which she refuses to use.

The Tsaritsa records every day with a transcription prism because she does not trust memory; like a Stellar Linchpin, the prism holds the Third Descender's power and is free from certain laws of Teyvat. Vesna carries the Ruler of Life's authority, via the first Vila. Ronova used a loophole in the Heavenly Principles' monitoring cycles with Rhinedottir's help to kill and revive without being caught. Seals of Life are memory bubbles that could resist death.

Snezhnaya's growth has brought it to the limit the Heavenly Principles allow, so a Celestial Nail is a standing threat. The sealed crystal in the basement was watched by the Belyi Tsar and reacts only to Gnoses. Collecting Seals of Life was bait to force Rhinedottir to appear; Anastasya offered her information on Asmoday and a meeting in seven days. The Tsaritsa has no happy memories.

Danica's family, the Postelnitskayas, has served the Tsaritsa for three generations. Capitano was Danica's mentor (Vesna also studied under him). Pantalone says that despite endless accusations against him, the Tsaritsa still trusted the Northland Bank to keep the Seals of Life. Pyro Gnosis, according to Anastasya, will be ejected from the Ley Lines because it is part of the Third Descender's remains.

Characters: The Traveler, Paimon, Tartaglia, Danica, Vesna, the Tsaritsa Anastasya, Pierro, Mitya, Pantalone, Sandrone, Rhinedottir and Naberius.

Others: Pulcinella (court report), Alyosha, Odette and Vodyanitsa (volunteers), Councilor Belozersky, Pevtsova of Svetloledovka, the suspect Avaz, and Lyney, Lynette and Freminet (briefly, at the end). Capitano is mentioned. Ronova and Asmoday are discussed but absent.

Consequences: The Traveler gains unrestricted access to Zapolyarny Palace. Project Mistilteinn waits on a way to counter the curse of death. Rhinedottir has agreed to meet the Tsaritsa again in seven days.

All seals go back to their owners; Pantalone returns to Vesna a beacon made from a sample of her power. Avaz is handed to Fatui Internal Affairs. The act leads directly into A Rekviem for the Underworld.

Placement: Third act of Chapter VII, between Wraith's Nocturne and A Rekviem for the Underworld. Released in version 7.1.

The act requires Adventure Rank 18; its place in the chain is Act II, then Act III, then Act IV. Acts I and II are 7.0 content and Acts III and IV are 7.1 content.

1050.comment: White Night, Like a Dream Upon Waking: Court at Zapolyarny Palace
1050.content: At the Traveler's first court session the Tsaritsa Anastasya hears reports from Pulcinella and Mitya, halts Project Mistilteinn until Ronova is dealt with, and orders all investigations of the Traveler to end. She asks the Traveler for the Pyro Gnosis, explains her aim to face the Heavenly Principles, shows a seal left by the Third Descender, and states that her authority is love but she refuses to use it.

1051.comment: White Night, Like a Dream Upon Waking: Mirror of Remembrance
1051.content: A massive prism in the Armory Palace used to extract memory fragments for review. Through it Pierro shows that Ronova collaborated with Rhinedottir. It is distinct from the transcription prism with which Anastasya records each day because she distrusts her own memory.

1052.comment: White Night, Like a Dream Upon Waking: Seal of Life
1052.content: A bubble holding an impactful memory, extracted by Vesna through her small authority of life, that could defy death if enough are gathered. Donation is obligatory for officials and nobles and voluntary for the public through Northland Bank. The collection draws a thief, a creature made by the Ruler of Life, and ends with Rhinedottir restoring every seal.

1053.comment: White Night, Like a Dream Upon Waking: Vault confrontation at Northland Bank
1053.content: Vesna and the Traveler infiltrate the bank's deep vaults, meeting Pantalone, who had anticipated them. The False Horned Steed drains the seals through portals until the Tsaritsa freezes it. Rhinedottir lets it escape and reclaims the stolen power. The Tsaritsa offers her information on Asmoday and a meeting in seven days.

1054.comment: White Night, Like a Dream Upon Waking: Danica
1054.content: The Tsaritsa's head maid and trusted personal attendant, from the Postelnitskaya family, which has served the Tsaritsa for three generations. She tests the Traveler with a Mora game taught to her by her mentor Capitano, and later apologises and brings hot milk. The Tsaritsa persuaded her mother and grandmother to let her travel abroad (her father was a mercenary) before she returned when her homeland needed her.

1055.content:
Windblume's Breath (also: Windblume's Breath event, Windblume 2023 event, Floral Pursuit, Ballads of Breeze, Breezy Snapshots): The event's in-game blurb frames it as the honeyed scents of the Windblume Festival wafting on the wind again, a festival of romance in the city of freedom, with a note found by accident leading the Traveler on another fantastical journey. Floral Pursuit introduces "Floral Chess", a new game created by the Mondstadt Adventurers' Guild; Ballads of Breeze has seven songs and a score editor; Breezy Snapshots has nine photo requests for a photobook. Rewards include Primogems, a Crown of Insight and the Claymore Mailed Flower.

The event is canon but was only available for a limited time, so not every character in a roleplay setting will have taken part in it; treat it as an optional, festival-time memory. The Mailed Flower's item text ties the weapon to the Windblume and to a "nameless shepherd" telling stories of the wind, linking the event's reward to the festival's old meaning.

Plot: No continuous storyline is documented. Each segment is a self-contained activity. Floral Pursuit is a six-stage challenge (Ordered, Inverted, Observant, Obstructing, Shimmering and Pursuing Wind), unlocking daily from 3 March, in which the player collects Bloom Balloons while avoiding Ersatz Balloons. Ballads of Breeze unlocks one song per day, and Breezy Snapshots has three sets of three photo requests from Fassben.

Floral Pursuit mechanics fit its stages: Galeblessings charge an "Ersatz Dispeller" skill that destroys Ersatz Balloons for a short time, Gatherblessings widen the collection range, bookcases can be shifted to open paths (Obstructing Wind) and darkened areas must be lit with light sources (Shimmering Wind). Co-op play was allowed.

Breezy Snapshots sends the Traveler to Mondstadt City's main gate and square, Cider Lake, Dadaupa Gorge, Stormterror's Lair, a viewpoint at Whispering Woods, the Snow-Covered Path on Dragonspine, a Dragonspine panorama and Wyrmrest Valley. The commissioner's comments are informal: he wants a cover photo of the city gate with its bouquets and carpets, mentions the festival crowds, jokes that a request sounds like a Guild commission, and says Cyrus has often told him not to rush to Dragonspine. After seeing the Dragonspine photos he says he should adjust his own planned photo trip.

One request has a subject at Cider Lake who says they are not photogenic and is embarrassed to be photographed. The requests attach conditions to each shot (time-of-day windows, a Mondstadt character, a Pyro character, an Elemental Skill in use, an idle animation, a subject spanning one or two photo points), but these are gameplay constraints rather than story.

Revelations: The event reveals nothing new about the main story. Its only lore weight is the Mailed Flower's text: the Windblume as a symbol, once lost to time, now a sign of love and gladness in times of peace, with a legend of a nameless shepherd who handed out "flowers" and an account that a noble took Ludi Harpastum away.

The Windblume Festival's wider background is covered in its own entry: Windblumes are offered to Barbatos and loved ones, and the festival's origins lie in the rebels against Decarabian using "Windblume" as a code word.

Characters: The Traveler and Paimon take part. Fassben the Adventurer is the commissioner of Breezy Snapshots. Cyrus is named in his remarks. The Mondstadt Adventurers' Guild created the Floral Chess game used in Floral Pursuit. No other named characters have verified roles.

Consequences: No lasting consequences for the story. The Mailed Flower, a four-star Claymore with the passive Whispers of Wind and Flower and Elemental Mastery as its second stat, could be earned during the event. Collei's Windblume and a Windblume Kamera were also among the rewards.

Placement: Released in Version 3.5 as a Flagship Event, requiring Adventure Rank 18 and the Prologue Act III "Song of the Dragon and Freedom". For the best experience, Chapter III Act V "Akasha Pulses, the Kalpa Flame Rises" and Albedo's "Princeps Cretaceus Chapter" Act I were recommended; the Quick Start option let players without them enter anyway. It follows the earlier Windblume event "Invitation of Windblume" (Version 1.4), whose title is also a Ballads of Breeze song.

Gameplay: Game mechanics, not in-world fact. Ballads of Breeze has seven songs, one unlocked per day from 3 March 2023: Invitation of Windblume, Contemplation in Snow, Dance of Aphros, Caelestinum Finale Termini, Caprice of the Leaves, Winding Through Avidya and Bard's Adventure, each on Normal, Hard and Pro. Players can edit, save (up to 50 slots) and share scores, and choose between the Windsong Lyre, Floral Zither and Festive Drum interface styles. Currencies were Festive Tickets (songs and photos) and Floral Coupons (Floral Pursuit), exchanged in an event shop for a Crown of Insight, refinement material, talent books, weapon materials, Mystic Enhancement Ore and Mora.

1056.content: A Windblume's Breath activity in which the Traveler collects Bloom Balloons and evades Ersatz Balloons across six daily-unlocking stages. It is described as Floral Chess, a new game made by the Mondstadt Adventurers' Guild.

1057.content: The event's seven-song rhythm performance mode, with a score editor, Windsong Lyre, Floral Zither and Festive Drum interface styles, and shareable scores.

1058.content: Fassben the Adventurer is making a photobook of Mondstadt for the festival and asks the Traveler to photograph set locations with a Kamera. The nine requests, in three sets, cover Mondstadt, Dadaupa Gorge, Stormterror's Lair and Dragonspine.

key: Winds Beneath the Tower of Silence
1059.comment: Winds Beneath the Tower of Silence
1059.content:
Winds Beneath the Tower of Silence (also: Dornman Port lighthouse ghost quest): A light world quest at Dornman Port, Windrest Peak. The old lighthouse's alarm keeps flashing, the keeper Winslow is terrified of ghosts, and the tavern regular Odolf asks the Traveler to investigate the ruins under the tower. The cause is an Eye of the Storm drawn by a tampered mechanism.

It begins at the group of regulars by the Devil's Cut tavern and ends at the lighthouse base. The quest requires Song of the Dragon and Freedom and was released in Version 6.5. It mixes mild humour with a small moral about honesty.

The quest also uncovers why the alarm doors misbehave: they are all linked to the alarm mechanism, so wind and flashing lights lock doors and open them. It unlocks a teleport waypoint in the Knights of Favonius Ruins and an achievement about someone else owing an apology.

Plot: At the tavern the regulars say the lighthouse alarm keeps flickering and that locals whisper of the ghosts of old knights. Odolf, who lives nearby, asks the Traveler to help Winslow. They enter the ruins beneath the lighthouse, block drafts, solve the alarm doors, survive a cave-in, and defeat an Eye of the Storm. Odolf then tells Winslow the ghosts have calmed down.

Lennart and Matthew tell the story: Winslow first shouted that the Abyss had come, the Knights searched several times and found nothing, and the alarm still flickered. Odolf, back from a business trip in Snezhnaya, wants to check for himself. Winslow, panicking, has locked the main doors, so Odolf leads the Traveler through another entrance known only to locals. In the ruins the Traveler pushes crates and breaks a rock pile to block wind currents that trip the alarm, fights Hydro and Electro Slimes in a cemetery, and glides over a gate with Anemograna. A strong wind falls from above: an Eye of the Storm. After it is defeated the alarm stops. Odolf tells the shaken Winslow that the wind was the unhappy fallen knights, now soothed, and covers a loud cave-in with a story about "super spiritual arm wrestling". Winslow says he has been tending the graves, and Odolf encourages him to keep doing so.

Earlier, Winslow bolts at the sight of Paimon, shouting about a white ghost, and later says the locals have always pushed him away. Odolf recalls that when Winslow wanted to move the "damp, horrible" things below out to the fields beyond the port, the locals tried to stop him, and he warned that there would be consequences. In the ruins the Traveler finds many old tombstones, eroded but recently tended. Odolf's reward is the preparation he mentioned; he says adventuring is not his strength and invites the Traveler back to the tavern.

Steps in the ruins: block the first wind current with a crate to open a door, close a main control switch that drops the floor into a cemetery, fight Hydro and Electro Slimes, then use Anemograna to pass a gate whose alarms flash faster. The ending dialogue gives the pun-heavy "ghost negotiation expert" title to the Traveler. Odolf reports he had been in Snezhnaya on business, a detail with no wider story use here.

Revelations: The "ghost" is Odolf's own doing.

In the optional post-quest talk, Odolf confesses he adjusted the alarm mechanism and added a lure for elemental creatures, meaning only to frighten Winslow a little so he would give up moving the old graves of knights who died fighting the Abyss. He thought a few Anemo Slimes would drift away, then left on business to Snezhnaya, and the lure instead drew an Eye of the Storm. He did not want Winslow to end up so frightened.

Odolf says he thanked Barbatos when the Traveler arrived. Had they not, he would have tried to drive the creature away himself or told the Knights the truth. He fears Winslow would explode at the truth and might even smash the tombstones. He quotes his own line that an open heart and a clear conscience keep out all evils and admits he did not live up to it. The Traveler can raise the guess that the ghost was Odolf himself, and he does not deny it.

Characters: The Traveler, Paimon, Odolf, Winslow, Lennart and Matthew.

Odolf is a local who talks in flowery proverbs and knows the lighthouse's secrets; Winslow lives at the old lighthouse and is anxious and prickly; Lennart and Matthew are tavern regulars, with Lennart staying out of it after too much drink. The Knights of Favonius appear only as having searched the ruins before.

Consequences: The alarm stops, Winslow calms down and keeps cleaning the graves, and Odolf's secret stays between him and the Traveler. A teleport waypoint in the Knights of Favonius Ruins opens.

Placement: Released in Version 6.5 (Luna VI, 2026-04-08), set in Windrest Peak and requiring Song of the Dragon and Freedom. It is a stand-alone local story with no bearing on the main plots.

1060.content:
Within the Sequence (also: Within the Sequence world quest, Ia-Ilimmu Storage Array terminal): A very short Version 6.7 world quest at Nuur Stone Circle on the Frost Moon. When the Ancient Moon's Remnant there reaches level 5, the Traveler examines an ancient terminal that greets them with the titles of old Natlan rulers.

It follows Origin of the Sequence, which repaired the terminal. It has one step, no combat and no named NPC. The wiki treats the name as unofficial.

Its only point is atmosphere and a small mystery: why the machine addresses the visitor like Natlantean royalty, and how many cycles have passed.

Plot: The Traveler raises the Ancient Moon's Remnant to level 5 and then examines the terminal. It runs a self-diagnostic, reports that lockdown is lifted and says an unreadable number of cycles has passed.

The terminal's greeting varies. Variants welcome the Master of Flame and Wisdom, Xiuhcoatl, and his companion, the Sovereign Ruler of Natlantea, either Ix Raq'lapuj Chue'q Buluk or Ix Uxul Tz'ib Bolon, or greet only one of them. It then gives a general welcome to "friends from afar" to its data array.

In Origin of the Sequence the terminal could not identify visitors and asked that Nin-Kiggia be contacted for maintenance. Here it says the lockdown is lifted. The elapsed-time count displays as "ERROR".

Revelations: The quest answers nothing. It shows that this storage array, labelled No. 59 Ia-Ilimmu in the prelude, recognises Xiuhcoatl and Natlantean sovereigns by title, a link between the Frost Moon works and Natlantea that the quest does not explain.

Characters: The Traveler only; the ancient terminal speaks. Xiuhcoatl and the Natlantean sovereigns are named but absent.

Consequences: Completing the quest unlocks the achievement The Inner Light. No other change to the world is recorded.

Placement: Released in Version 6.7 (Luna VIII) as Frost Moon content. It follows Origin of the Sequence and requires the Ancient Moon's Remnant at Nuur Stone Circle to be raised to level 5.

The quest infobox gives the start location as Nuur Stone Circle in the Lunar Highlands of the Frost Moon. The prelude quest rewards 350 Adventure EXP, 40 Primogems and 30,000 Mora and unlocks the hidden objective Fragments of Ia-Ilimmu; this quest itself lists no item rewards.

1061.content:
Wraith's Nocturne (also: Chapter VII Act II, Snezhnaya Archon Quest Act II, Curse of Death theater incident): Wraith's Nocturne is Act II of Chapter VII, the Snezhnaya Archon Quest. At a rehearsal of the ballet "Spirit Seeker" in the Korolevskiy Theater, a blizzard traps the audience, among them Odette, who is secretly the saboteur "Lelek", the Fatui Alyosha and the singer Vodyanitsa. Each night two people die without a mark, and the Traveler relives each death in a dream of climbing a spiral staircase. The cause is the Curse of Death of Ronova, Ruler of Death. In the end Pierro explains why Paimon was taken to the Armory Palace.

The act follows Everwinter Without Mercy and precedes White Night, Like a Dream Upon Waking. It was released in version 7.0 and requires Adventure Rank 18. It has five quests: The White Curtain Falls, Lelek's Confession, Winter's Mysterious Silence, Wraith's Nocturne (the quest) and Mistilteinn.

Plot: The Traveler attends the theater hoping to find Tonia, Tartaglia's sister, and to ask about Lelek. A blizzard seals everyone in. Two people die each night, the Traveler dreams of each death beforehand, and gradually the dead turn out to be ghosts or fellow victims of the Curse of Death. Ronova reveals herself, is driven off, and everyone wakes with no memory. The Traveler then rescues Paimon from the Armory Palace, where Pierro explains the curse and Project Mistilteinn.

Trapped by the blizzard, the group finds two dead on the first morning and Odette admits she is Lelek. Further deaths follow each night; the cast discover that Shram and the girl called Tonia (really Ptashka) are ghosts, that Mitya has died without knowing it, and that Alyosha is Ronova in disguise. Ronova kills Odette and Chugunov, is struck by the Traveler and Mitya, and vanishes, and everyone wakes with no memory. In the Armory Palace, Pierro shields Paimon from Ronova and explains the Curse of Death and Project Mistilteinn.

The White Curtain Falls. The Traveler arrives at the Korolevskiy Theater, where the usher Kulish checks their ticket, and recognises faces from earlier in the chapter: the merchant Chugunov, Mitya and Valeriy, the Armory Palace officer escorting him. They watch a rehearsal of the classic ballet "Spirit Seeker", during which the lights flicker once. Afterwards a staff member, Dymov, calls everyone onstage for a group photo and the Traveler finds Tonia, but a snowstorm bars the doors. Dymov goes out for blankets and does not return, and Alyosha goes out alone and comes back warning that the storm is too severe. Vodyanitsa and Odette emerge from backstage and agree the group will shelter there. That night the Traveler is woken by Mitya on a spiral staircase while a black mist pursues them and two merchants, Soboleva and Torgov. The mist engulfs the two merchants and the Traveler faints at the top.

Lelek's Confession. The Traveler wakes to find Soboleva and Torgov dead without wounds. Chugunov insists Lelek did it to frighten him, since he voted against Project Stuzha. Vodyanitsa doubts it fits Lelek's methods. The Traveler, who suspects Odette is Lelek, shares this privately with Vodyanitsa and Alyosha, and Odette, defended by Vodyanitsa, admits it and then publicly confesses onstage. The group sets Lelek aside to find the real killer. On the second night the singer Vodyanitsa unconsciously sings a nervous melody that the mercenary Shram understands, and Valeriy organises night watches. Odette tells the Traveler how she trained under Signora and why she joined the Fatui. The Traveler falls asleep and dreams the staircase again with Kulish and Rampana, who are taken by the mist, and Odette tells them this is only the beginning.

Winter's Mysterious Silence. Kulish and Rampana are found dead, as the dream foretold. Chugunov blames Odette again, and Mitya suggests the cause may be supernatural. Searching, the group finds Vodyanitsa's diary, a logbook showing one extra person who never had a ticket, and a report that the theater is haunted, with a note reading "Death is near". By elimination the extra person is Shram. His talk of fae and human "factions" proves he is a ghost from over four hundred years ago, who died protecting his water imp girlfriend in the theater. Vodyanitsa, who was a child then, tells him what became of her. He apologises for the harm he has caused and walks into the storm. Odette tells the Traveler that she thought she saw Mitya dead in the Armory Palace a week earlier. The third staircase dream ends with Valeriy staying behind.

Wraith's Nocturne. Valeriy is found dead at his post. Mitya notes that only one person died this time and proposes that the nightly toll matches the number of dead in the building. Odette says Mitya is himself dead, which he cannot remember, and he leaves into the storm. Tonia and Vodyanitsa comfort the Traveler, who misses Paimon, and Vodyanitsa sings a water imp requiem. In the next dream she acts as the Traveler's "Guardian Angel" against a spirit that looks like Tonia, and then stays behind. She is dead in the morning. The Traveler asks Tonia about Teucer and her confusion confirms a suspicion; Chugunov admits that Tonia is a ghost of a girl who had Frostblight, and that he saw his own late daughter Iskra in her. Tonia gives her real name, Ptashka, and leaves. That night Mitya returns, having followed Vodyanitsa's requiem back, with a red eye carved into his palm. The Traveler recognises it as Ronova's mark and the group deduces that "Alyosha" is her. Ronova drops the disguise, kills Odette and Chugunov with a snap of her fingers, explains the Curse of Death, says that the ley lines took as many souls each night as there were lingering dead, and that the ancient angels' modifications to the theater's ley lines hindered them from accepting ordinary souls and capped how many they could receive each day; she also says Teyvat's ley lines would not accept a Descender's soul. The Traveler and Mitya strike her and she vanishes, leaving a sky of watching eyes before everyone wakes in their seats.

Mistilteinn. Everyone has forgotten the dream, and Mitya no longer recognises the Traveler until he sees the carved eye and recalls that he must return to the Armory Palace. Valeriy's questions let the group recover their memories. The Traveler and Odette go to Podvorye Restaurant to check on Paimon and learn from Tartaglia's guards that Pierro came himself and took her away. They hurry to the Armory Palace; on the way the curse triggers again and Odette uses her Cor Ignis to wake the Traveler faster. Inside the palace everyone is dead again. Ronova appears in her true form and tries to take Paimon, Pierro blocks her, and the Traveler's attack only scratches her. Paimon wakes, hardly any time having passed for her. Pierro explains the curse and Project Mistilteinn, and the act closes with the aftermath in Snezhnograd.

Pierro and Mitya explain that Project Mistilteinn is a weapon against Celestia and that its energy had been making Paimon ill, so Mitya cancelled it with another form of energy. Pierro adds that over five hundred years ago in Khaenri'ah he used a technology upon the heavens and Paimon descended from Celestia in response; he offered her to Irmin as a gift, who took no interest, and he now sees her as the only sane thing that survived that era of insanity, and so worthy of protection. Mitya explains that the Curse of Death blocks Snezhnaya's technological progress: when a moment of breakthrough occurs, all life nearby is taken, and the revived forget what happened while dead; the theater incident was triggered by Mitya thinking of a breakthrough for his experiment during the performance. Pierro says the Tsaritsa and the Fatui aim to challenge the Heavenly Principles. The Traveler chooses to side with them to keep Paimon safe from Ronova, and Pierro shows the two the secret weapon. Project Mistilteinn is paused until Ronova is eliminated.

In the aftermath Chugunov orders the Iskra Manufacturing Plant shut down permanently. Odette visits Signora's tomb in the Sanctuary of Grief, where a vision of Signora and a conversation about the Cor Ignis, Arlecchino, and memory and forgetting lead her to dance for Signora and to keep going as both ballerina and Fatuus. In Snezhnograd the Traveler and Paimon meet Tartaglia, who apologises for Pierro's misunderstanding and introduces his sister Tonia. A crowd then cheers the Tsaritsa's return from fighting a monster, with the Druzhna, its commander Vesna and the head housemaid Danica around her. She returns without a word to Zapolyarny Palace, where Pierro and the others bow to her.

Deaths by night as the wiki summarises them: Soboleva and Torgov on the first, Kulish and Rampana on the second, Valeriy alone on the third, and Vodyanitsa on the fourth, with Shram, Ptashka and Mitya each leaving of their own accord. Mitya reads the falling toll as matching the number of dead already in the theater. Patch notes show that 7.0 had a Mitya Elemental Type icon display error in a cutscene (it should show the Electro Stellar Linchpin), fixed in 7.1, along with collision fixes and Travel Log text corrections; none affect story content.

Revelations: - Odette is Lelek, and publicly admits it in the theater; she trained under Signora.
- Ronova, the Ruler of Death, has been manipulating the theater through a Curse of Death, and her symbol is a red eye.
- Some of the people in the theater were not alive: Shram, a water imp's boyfriend from over four hundred years ago, and "Tonia", whose real name is Ptashka, a girl who had Frostblight. Mitya had also died earlier at the Armory Palace without remembering it.
- The Curse of Death is triggered by moments of technological progress that could threaten the Heavenly Principles, killing everyone nearby; the revived forget what happened.
- A Descender's soul cannot be carried into the ley lines.
- The Fatui, with the Tsaritsa, intend to challenge the Heavenly Principles.

- Project Mistilteinn is an anti-Celestia weapon whose energy sickened Paimon, a being of Celestia.
- Pierro claims he caused Paimon, a creation of Celestia, to descend to Khaenri'ah over five hundred years ago and presented her to Irmin, who was uninterested. Paimon lacks any Celestia power or authority, according to Ronova.
- The Traveler chooses to side with Pierro to protect Paimon.

Characters: Traveler: dreams each death, wakes after dying, and joins the Fatui's side to protect Paimon. Paimon: absent in the theater, missed by the Traveler, then the object of Ronova's and Pierro's interest. Odette: a ballerina and secret Lelek, trained under Signora. Alyosha: a Fatui whose appearance Ronova wears. Vodyanitsa: the singer and the Traveler's "Guardian Angel". Mitya: a researcher tied to Project Mistilteinn, dead without realising, whose carved eye proves decisive. "Tonia" / Ptashka: a ghost girl who answered to the name Tonia, believing her own brother had chosen it as a code name; she is not Tartaglia's sister. Valeriy: an Armory Palace officer escorting Mitya, who organises watches. Chugunov: a merchant who knew Tonia was a ghost. Ronova: the Ruler of Death. Pierro: arrives at the end. The Tsaritsa, Vesna and Danica appear in the closing scene.

Other theater staff and guests who die or vanish include Kulish, Rampana, Soboleva, Torgov, Dymov and Shram. Tartaglia appears only in the epilogue.

Consequences: The Curse of Death is understood and the Traveler has now met Ronova in person. Project Mistilteinn is paused until Ronova can be dealt with. Odette and Chugunov survive; Chugunov shuts down the Iskra Manufacturing Plant. The Traveler allies with Pierro, and the Tsaritsa returns to Zapolyarny Palace.

Ronova states she has no immediate interest in Descenders but warns the Traveler against meddling in Snezhnaya's affairs. These threads lead into White Night, Like a Dream Upon Waking.

Placement: Chapter VII Act II, after Everwinter Without Mercy (Act I) and before White Night, Like a Dream Upon Waking. Released in version 7.0 with Act I. Requires Adventure Rank 18.

1062.comment: Wraith's Nocturne: The Korolevskiy Theater Incident
1062.content:
During a "Spirit Seeker" rehearsal a blizzard trapped the audience, and each night two people died with no wounds. Some of the people present were ghosts. The Traveler experienced the deaths as spiral-staircase dreams chased by a black mist. It ended when Ronova revealed herself, was struck by the Traveler and Mitya, and everyone woke in their seats with no memory.

Ronova says the ley lines took as many souls each night as there were lingering dead, and that the angels' old alterations to the theater's ley lines limited how many souls they could receive each day. Mitya's carved red eye was the clue that kept him from forgetting.

1063.content: In the theater a girl who answered to the name Tonia was actually a ghost: a child ill with Frostblight whose brother Razyk had snuck her out of hospital to see a show, where she fell asleep. When the Traveler said her brother had sent them and called her Tonia, she assumed her brother had chosen it as a code name. Chugunov knew and treated her as his late daughter Iskra. She tells the Traveler her real name is Ptashka and leaves. The real Tonia, Tartaglia's sister, is introduced in the epilogue.

1064.content: A mercenary who understands Vodyanitsa's water imp song, found to be a ghost from over four hundred years ago who died in the theater protecting his water imp girlfriend. He apologises for the deaths he caused and leaves into the storm.

1065.content: The curse is triggered by moments of technological progress that could threaten the Heavenly Principles; it kills everyone nearby temporarily, and they forget what happened on revival. Armory Palace personnel had suffered unexplained temporary memory loss, which Mitya mentions as a hint. In the theater it was triggered by Mitya's thoughts during the ballet. Ronova, Ruler of Death among the Four Shades, says she wanted to watch a play about death and was hampered by the angels' changes to the theater's ley lines.

1066.comment: Wraith's Nocturne: Paimon's Explanation at the Armory Palace
1066.content: Pierro had Paimon brought to Mitya because Project Mistilteinn's energy was harming her. He says that over five hundred years ago in Khaenri'ah he used a technology upon the heavens and she descended from Celestia in response; he gave her as a gift to Irmin, who showed no interest. The act's account is Pierro's own and Paimon does not remember it.

key: Scions of the Canopy Tribal Chronicle
1067.content:
Yupanqui's Turnfire (also: Scions of the Canopy Tribal Chronicle, A Mysterious Visitor From Huitztlan, A Hero's Rite, Kinich's Deal, I, Flame Bearer, The Last Turnfire Night): The Tribal Chronicles chapter of the Scions of the Canopy, which also serves as Kinich's story quest. The tribe holds Turnfire Night to honour the hero Burkina and his Saurian companion Kongamato, who fought the Abyss, and to keep the Abyssal energy still within Kongamato stable. This year the ritual is in trouble, and the tribe wants the Saurian hunter Kinich to bear the flame. The Traveler is drawn into the matter, and Kinich solves it his own way through a deal with an Abyss Lector.

The chapter has three acts: A Mysterious Visitor From Huitztlan, A Hero's Rite and Kinich's Deal. It unlocks after the Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame in the Archon Quest. The chapter title refers to the Turnfire, the ritual flame; a book called "Yupanqui's Turnfire" also appears in Act III.

The conflict is between two ways of dealing with Kongamato. The tribe's elder Trinidad plans a ritual that would drain the Abyssal energy even though it would probably kill Kongamato, while the elder Wayna wants it kept alive as a source of the tribe's history, pride and faith. Kinich chooses a third option, sealing Kongamato inside a Beastly Rift obtained by dealing with an Abyss Lector, and then has to improvise when his plan is broken in front of the whole tribe.

Plot: Act I. At the foot of Coatepec Mountain the Traveler and Paimon meet two children of the Scions of the Canopy, Huni and Toba, who are looking for baby Yumkasaurs and were told by a man named Sanka that helpers were coming. Ajaw is already with the Yumkasaur whelp Pocchi and explains that the babies' mother was overcome by Abyssal energy, attacked her tribe and her young, and died. The children say they had been telling Sanka stories about their tribe, including that Kinich is the current Turnfire bearer, when he fled. Learning that the visitors know Kinich, the children point them to the village.

Act II. In the village Trinidad, Huni's father, first doubts the visitors but warms to them when Huni says they ate with Kinich. He explains Turnfire Night, honouring Burkina and Kongamato, and the current crisis: five months after the last ceremony Kongamato has shown signs of instability, and in its rage it attacked Trinidad's own Saurian companion Nanna, whom the tribe believes died. The tribe had hoped Kinich would be the flame-bearer but he named a price, which they took as a refusal, so Trinidad asks the Traveler to take that place. At the same time Kinich and Ajaw confront Sanka. The Traveler completes a stage of the ritual at the summit of Coatepec Mountain while Kinich watches in secret.

Act III. Kinich asks the Traveler to find out what Trinidad's ritual really involves, then explains his own plan. Over the next day the chapter shifts to a search for Ponche's stolen book, a ruins mural and a meeting in a cave where Kinich reveals he has struck a deal with Sanka, who is really the Abyss Lector Enjou. On Turnfire Night Kinich produces the Beastly Rift device, Trinidad destroys the device in a panic, and Kongamato wakes and has to be calmed by the Traveler and Kinich using Kinich's Ancient Name.

**A Mysterious Visitor From Huitztlan (5.0).** The Traveler and Paimon find the children at the foot of Coatepec Mountain. Ajaw tells them to question suspicious outsiders because the taint of the Abyss still lingers there. The children describe the stranger, Sanka, who tried to learn about Kinich and fled after distracting them when the Traveler arrived.

**A Hero's Rite (5.0).** Trinidad tells the Traveler that Turnfire Night honours Burkina and Kongamato. The Abyssal energy keeps Kongamato alive unnaturally long compared with other Yumkasaurs but is highly sensitive, and the ceremony keeps it at stable levels. Five months after the last ceremony it shows signs of failure. Sanka tells Kinich and Ajaw that he was tired of watching them from afar and let them catch up because he did not feel like running, and offers to negotiate. Kinich tells him to state his real purpose before he names his own price. The Traveler performs part of the rite quickly and Trinidad plans to recommend them as the flame-bearer.

**Kinich's Deal (5.0).** Trinidad intends the Traveler to purify the energy out of Kongamato, which would likely kill it. Wayna tells them he supports the Traveler's taking part but not Kongamato's death. On a walk Kinich says he knew Trinidad's plan, reveals that he gave Ajaw a teacher, and explains that he found a Beastly Rift while chasing riftwolves. He proposes to clear a rift of its inhabitants and put Kongamato inside so it can threaten no one, while admitting the plan has many flaws.

**I, Flame Bearer (5.0).** To take attention off Kinich, the Traveler and Paimon help Thiago, who has seen a mural of a human and a Saurian in ruins infested by riftwolves, and Ponche, whose book "Yupanqui's Turnfire" was taken by the Treasure Hoarder Matthias, who threw it away. Sanka finds the book in a cave and reads it aloud to Ajaw; when he mentions that all bearers of the Turnfire name die horribly, Ajaw takes interest and agrees to a deal with Sanka. Ponche thinks he has a solution that needs Kinich. Kinich shows the Traveler his reading of Burkina's memories: Kongamato killed Burkina and wishes to die, which the tribe cannot allow. The next day they open a Beastly Rift and an Abyss Lector steps out, remarking that he had delivered more than promised. Paimon recognises Enjou. Kinich had already traded the rift for being left alone in his historical research, and says Ajaw's apparent betrayal was bait. Enjou says he is a lowly clerk and not part of the inner circle, then departs. Kinich suspects he is busy with debts.

**The Last Turnfire Night (5.0).** The Traveler completes the ritual with Kinich's guidance. At Kongamato's lair, Trinidad asks the Traveler to purify the energy, but Kinich produces Enjou's device, which the tribe recognises as a Beastly Rift, and Wayna relents when Kinich says Kongamato will be fine. Trinidad, thinking the Traveler is in league with Kinich, smashes the device while Kinich is distracted. The energy collapses, Kongamato wakes and Kinich orders the tribe out, while Trinidad runs to the Turnfire and is caught by Kongamato's fire. The Traveler and Kinich fight it until it begs to be put out of its misery. Kinich uses his Ancient Name to build invisible walls between Kongamato and the Sacred Flame, tells it that it must live with the shame of its past, and it agrees on condition that Kinich uses its ruined body to train heroes until the Abyss is gone from Natlan.

Finer points. The Beastly Rift plan puts Kinich on the same side as a member of the Abyss Order against the expectations of Paimon, who is horrified by the apparent collusion; Kinich says he had wanted the Traveler to learn about the Abyss Order, which is why he had Enjou in reach. Enjou denies that he roused Kongamato. On the day after the incident Wayna reports that the elders have recovered Trinidad, who is expected to recover from severe burns, and that a transparent shell formed around Kongamato. Kinich thanks the Traveler for the Kongamato matter and says he owes them a favour; the Traveler objects that he already captured Enjou, but Kinich says Enjou gave away nothing of value. When Paimon calls them friends, Kinich cannot accept that for free and says he would do anything for them if needed. Elsewhere Enjou meets Toba and Huni, apologises for deceiving them, and says he enjoys the tribe's extreme sports after being struck by a bungee jumper falling out of the sky and learning of the practice. He says he then reunited with a friend who had missed her family and brought her to them. Huni turns round and finds Nanna, her family's Saurian companion, whom the tribe had believed dead, pressing her face against hers.

Revelations: Kinich bears the Ancient Name Malipo; from the memories he has of Burkina, he concludes that Kongamato killed Burkina and wants to die, and that the tribe's honour for it hides this. Sanka, the stranger who pumped the children for stories about Kinich, is Enjou, an Abyss Lector who admits to being only a clerk in the Abyss Order. The Turnfire ritual is not a normal ceremony of respect but a means of stabilising Abyssal energy in Kongamato, and the elders disagree on whether to destroy it.

The tribe's version of the Turnfire legend says its bearers die horribly, which Sanka reports to Ajaw. At the story's end a transparent shell surrounds Kongamato, and the elders cannot say whether the Sacred Flame or the Turnfire produced it. Nanna, whom the family believed Kongamato had killed, is alive and is brought back to them by Enjou.

Characters: The Traveler and Paimon are the viewpoint pair. Kinich, the Saurian hunter who names a price for every job, drives the plot and keeps his reasoning to himself until late. Ajaw, bound to Kinich by contract, sides with Sanka for part of the story but the betrayal is bait. Trinidad is a worried elder whose companion Nanna is hurt; Wayna is another elder who values Kongamato as tribal heritage. Huni and Toba are children of the tribe. Enjou, under the alias Sanka, is the Abyss Lector.

Thiago, Ponche, Matthias and the baby Yumkasaur Pocchi have minor roles. Burkina and Kongamato are not present as characters except through the tribe's story and Kongamato's actions.

Consequences: Kongamato survives and agrees to remain in its ruined state to train future heroes. Trinidad is badly burned but expected to recover. Kinich owes the Traveler a favour and says he will do anything for them in future. Enjou leaves, Nanna is returned to Huni's family, and the Beastly Rift plan is spent. The tribe records the story of Malipo's manifestation, preserved by a scholar of Ancient Names.

The chapter's closing text says the tale will be passed on until it becomes an enigmatic relic of a past era, to be unearthed again by later seekers of knowledge, a point about how legends outlive the events behind them.

Placement: Release order: all three acts came with Version 5.0; the wiki gives the event window as 2024-09-17 to 2024-10-08. Story order: the chapter requires only the Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame in the Archon Quest part Flowers Resplendent on the Sun-Scorched Sojourn, and the wiki lists the Inazuma quest From Dusk to Dawn in Byakuyakoku as a recommended earlier quest for Act I. Trinidad recognises the Traveler from the Stadium of the Sacred Flame.

1068.content: A ceremony of the Scions of the Canopy that honours the hero Burkina and his Saurian companion Kongamato, both of whom fought the Abyss. Burkina died and Kongamato was left with Abyssal energy that lets it live unnaturally long but is highly unstable, so the ritual flame, the Turnfire, is used to keep that energy stable. In the year of the chapter, five months after the last ceremony, Kongamato showed signs of instability and its rage hurt Trinidad's Saurian companion Nanna, whom the tribe believed it killed.

1069.content: The Yumkasaur companion of the hero Burkina, afflicted by Abyssal energy in the fight that killed him. It lives unnaturally long, and the tribe treats it as a source of history, pride and faith. Kinich believes it killed Burkina and wishes to die. After the Last Turnfire Night it agrees to live with its shame and allow Kinich to use its ruined vessel for training future heroes, and a transparent shell forms around it that the elders interpret as insulation against Abyssal energy.

1070.content: Two elders of the Scions of the Canopy. Trinidad, Huni's father, wants the Abyssal energy purged from Kongamato even though it would probably kill it, and is badly burned when he rushes to the Turnfire. Wayna endorses the Traveler's participation but refuses to let Kongamato be killed, and afterwards reports the elders' interpretation of the shell around it.

1071.content: Kinich's plan to contain Kongamato. He discovered Beastly Rifts, hidden spaces opened by the Abyss, while hunting riftwolves. In exchange for being left alone in his historical research, the Abyss Lector Enjou, who had been using the alias Sanka, supplied one. The plan was to clear a rift and put Kongamato in it. Trinidad smashed the device on Turnfire Night, and the problem was then settled by Kinich's Ancient Name instead.
